The English translation of the Skanda Purana, the largest of the eighteen major puranas containing over 81,000 Sanskrit metrical verses. The earliest version of the Skanda Purana probably existed before the 5th century CE and thus preserves an enormous amount of history and information regarding Hindu tradition in an encyclopedic format.

Subjects covered by this Purana include cosmogony (creation of the universe), mythology (itihasa), genealogy (vamsha), dharma (virtuous lifestyle), festivals (yatra etc.), geography, gemology, etc. But another significant feature is the inclusion of a tremendous amount of pilgrimage guides (Tirtha Mahatmya).

The Skanda Purana is also spelled as Skandapurāṇa (स्कन्दपुराण) or Skanda-purāṇa (स्कन्द-पुराण). Skanda is the name of a son of Shiva and Parvati. He is also known as Kartikeya and Murugan.

# The Skanda Purana. Part 7

## Book 7 - Prabhāsa Khaṇḍa

## Section 1 - Prabhāsa-kṣetra-māhātmya

## Chapter 1 - Queries of Sages

## \|\| 1.1.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*yaścādyaḥ puruṣaḥ purāṇa iti yaḥ saṃstūyate sarvataḥ someśaḥ surasaṃyutaḥ kṣititale yairvīkṣito hīkṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*te tīrtvā vitatāṃtaraṃ bhavabhayaṃ bhūtyā'bhisaṃbhūṣitāḥ svargaṃ yānavaraiḥprayānti sukṛtairyajñai yathā yajvinaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Obeisance to Śrī Gaṇeśa

Now begins the Prabhāsa Khaṇḍa. The first section is called: Prabhāsa-kṣetra-māhātmya (The greatness of the sacred place called Prabhāsa) Om. Obeisance to the Supreme Soul (Paramātman), the highest and the most excellent Puruṣa. Om. Obeisance to the gods Hari, Hara and Hiraṇyagarbha (Brahmā). Obeisance to (Sages) Vyāsa, Vālmīki, Śuka and Parāśara.

1\. The Lord (Śiva) is proclaimed and eulogized everywhere, the primordial PURUṢA and the eternal ancient being. The devotees of Śiva by whom the Lord of Umā, accompanied by Suras has been viewed on the earth by their own eyes, cross

the extensive terrible ocean of worldly existence and become embellished with prosperity just as Yajvans (performers of sacrifices) proceed to heaven (Svarga) through excellent aerial chariots on account of those well-performed Yajñas.

## \|\| 1.1.2 \|\|

*prasaradbindunādāya śuddhāmṛtamayātmane \|*  
*ṣaḍtriṃśattattvadehāya namaścinmātramūrtaye \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Obeisance to the Supreme Being, the embodiment of pure consciousness and knowledge. His body is constituted of thirty-six categories\[1\] (from Parama Śiva down to the element earth). His soul is (consists of) pure, immortal nectar. He is the expanding Nāda (vibrating spiritual sound) and Bindu .

## \|\| 1.1.3 \|\|

*amṛtenodarasthena mriyante sarvadevatāḥ \|*  
*kaṃṭhasthita viṣeṇāpi yo jīvati sa pātuḥ vaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Despite the presence of Amṛta within the belly, all the Devas die. But despite the presence of poison (Halāhala) in his throat, Lord Śiva continued to be alive. May that Lord Śiva protect you all.

## \|\| 1.1.4 \|\|

*satrānte sūtamanaghaṃ naimiṣeyā maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*purāṇasaṃhitāṃ puṇyāṃ papracchū romaharṣaṇam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. At the conclusion of the Satra (Sacrifice of a long duration) the great sages of Naimiṣa forest asked the blemish-free Sūta Romaharṣaṇa about the meritorious Purāṇa Saṃhitā:

## \|\| 1.1.5 \|\|

*tvayā sūta mahā buddhe bhagavānbrahmavittamaḥ \|*  
*itihāsapurāṇārthe vyāsaḥ samyagupāsitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. “O highly intelligent Sūta, holy Lord Vyāsa, the foremost among the knowers of Brahman, has been perfectly served and propitiated by you for the sake of acquiring the Itihāsa and the Purāṇas.

## \|\| 1.1.6 \|\|

*tasya te sarvaromāṇi vacasā harṣitāni yat \|*  
*dvaipāyanasyānubhāvāttato'bhū romaharṣaṇaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Due to the exalted majesty and dignity of Dvaipāyana, and on account of his words all your hairs stood on ends through delight and you became known as Romaharṣaṇa.

## \|\| 1.1.7 \|\|

*bhavantameva prathamaṃ vyājahāra svayaṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*munīnāṃ saṃhitāṃ vaktuṃ vyāsaḥ paurāṇikīṃ kathām \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. It was to you that the Lord of the sages himself propounded the ancient legend, the Purāṇasaṃhitā.

## \|\| 1.1.8 \|\|

*tvaṃ hi svāyaṃbhuve yajñe sutyāhe vitate hariḥ \|*  
*saṃbhūtaḥ saṃhitāṃ vaktuṃ svāṃśena puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. When the Yajña pertaining to Svayaṃbhū (Brahmā) was being elaborately performed, on the Sutyāha (the day when Soma Juice is extracted), Hari, the Supreme person manifested himself by a part of himself in your form, for propounding the Purāṇasaṃhitā.

## \|\| 1.1.9 \|\|

*tasmādbhavantaṃ pṛcchāmaḥ purāṇe skandakīrtite \|*  
*prabhāsakṣetramāhātmye brāhmī yātrā śrutā purā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The Brāhmī Yātrā (religious pilgrimage pertaining to Brahmā) has already been heard by us, in the context of Prabhāsa-Kṣetra-Māhātmya (the greatness of the sacred place called Prabhāsa) in the Purāṇa propounded by Skanda.

## \|\| 1.1.10 \|\|

*adhunā vaiṣṇavīṃ raudrīṃ yātrāṃ sarvārthasaṃyutām \|*  
*vaktumarhasi cāsmākaṃ purāṇārthaviśārada \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Now, O holy Sir, O Purāṇa specialist, it behoves you to expound the Yātrā pertaining to Viṣṇu and Rudra along with all the themes thereof.”

## \|\| 1.1.11 \|\|

*munīnā vacanaṃ śrutvā sūtaḥ paurāṇikottamaḥ \|*  
*praṇamya śirasā prāha vyāsaṃ satyavatīsutam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On hearing the words of the sages, Sūta, the most excellent one among those conversant with Purāṇas, bowed down his head to Vyāsa, the son of Satyavatī and said:

## \|\| 1.1.12-16 \|\|

*romaharṣaṇa uvāca \|*  
*śrīvatsāṃkaṃ jagadyoniṃ harimoṃkārarūpiṇam \|*  
*aprameyaṃ guruṃ devaṃ nirmalaṃ nirmalāśrayam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*haṃsaṃ śuciṣadaṃ vyoma vyāpakaṃ sarvadaṃ śivam \|*  
*udāsīnaṃ nirāyāsaṃ niṣprapañcaṃ nirañjanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*śūnyaṃ biṃdusvarūpaṃ tu dhyeyaṃ dhyānavivarjitam \|*  
*asti nāstīti yaṃ prāhuḥ sudūre cāntike ca yat \|\| 14 \|\|*

*manogrāhyaṃ paraṃ dhāma puruṣākhyaṃ jaganmayam \|*  
*hṛtpaṃkajasamāsīnaṃ tejorūpaṃ nirindriyam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*evaṃvidhaṃ namaskṛtya paramātmānamīśvaram \|*  
*kathāṃ vadiṣye dvividhāṃ dviśarīrāṃ tathaiva tu \|\| 16 \|\|*

Romaharṣaṇa said:

12-16. After bowing down to the Supreme Soul, the Almighty Lord, I shall propound the story with two Vidhās (modes of narration) and two Śarīras (bodies, i.e. units). Śrīvatsa marks his chest. He is the source of origin of the worlds. He is Hari with OM as his form. He is incomprehensible and unmeasurable. He is the Lord-preceptor. He is free from impurities. His resort is free from impurities. He is Haṃsa (pure spiritual being), Śuciṣad (abiding in the purest essence). He pervades the entire firmament. He is Śiva, the bestower of all things, Udāsīna (indifferent), free from worldly ties and physical extension. He is unsullied. He is the vacuity (Śūnya). He is of the form of Bindu (point whence the universe evolves). He is worthy of being meditated upon. He is one without (beyond) meditation. They say that he is and he is not, that he is far-off and also very close. He is the greatest refulgence worthy of being comprehended through the mind. He is called Puruṣa who is identical with Jagat (Universe). He is seated in the lotus of the heart. He is in the form of fiery splendour. He is devoid of Indriyas (sense-organs).

## \|\| 1.1.17 \|\|

*divyabhāṣāsamopetāṃ vedādhiṣṭhānasaṃyutām \|*  
*pañcasaṃdhisamāyuktāṃ ṣaḍalaṃkārabhūṣitām \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The story is couched in the celestial language. It has the Veda for its basis. It has five Sandhis (divisions, joints such as Mukha, Pratimukha etc.). It is embellished with six ornaments (figures of speech).

## \|\| 1.1.18 \|\|

*saptasādhanasaṃyuktāṃ rasāṣṭaguṇaraṃjitām \|*  
*guṇairnavabhirākīrṇāṃ daśadoṣavivarjitām \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. It possesses seven Sādhanas (means of achieving objectives). It is coloured (brightened) with the eight Rasas and Guṇas. Further, the nine Guṇas can be seen spread over throughout. It is free from ten defects.

## \|\| 1.1.19 \|\|

*vibhāṣābhūṣitāṃ tadvadekāyattāṃ manoharām \|*  
*pañcakāraṇasaṃyuktāṃ catuṣkaraṇasammatām \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. It is embellished with Vibhāṣās (alternatives). Similarly it is completely converging into a single purpose. It is pleasing to the mind. It has the five Kāraṇas (purposes). It is approved by the four Karaṇas (means of achieving objects).

## \|\| 1.1.20 \|\|

*punaśca dvividhāṃ tadvajjñānasaṃdohadāyinīm \|*  
*vyāsena kathitāṃ puṇyāṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ pāpanāśinīm \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. It is further divided into two aspects. It bestows successive waves of knowledge (consciousness). Listen ye all to the meritorious story narrated by Vyāsa. It is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.1.21 \|\|

*yāṃ śrutvā pāpakarmāpi gaccheddhi paramāṃ gatim \|*  
*duḥkhatrayavinirmuktaḥ sarvātaṅkavivarjitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. On hearing it even a man of evil actions attains the greatest goal. He will be relieved of the three types of miseries. He shall be freed from all distressing worries.

## \|\| 1.1.22 \|\|

*na nāstike kathāṃ puṇyāmimāṃ brūyātkadācana \|*  
*śraddadhānāya śāntāya kīrtanīyā dvijātaye \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Never should one narrate this meritorious story to a Nāstika (atheist). It should be propounded to a twice-born one who is quiescent and faithful.

## \|\| 1.1.23 \|\|

*niṣekādiḥ śmaśānānto mantrairyasyodito vidhiḥ \|*  
*tasya śāstre'dhikāro'sti jñeyo nānyasya kasyacit \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. It should be known that only he is entitled to hear (or read) this scripture and none else, for whom the consecratory rites beginning with Niṣeka (impregnation by dropping the semen within the womb) and ending with obsequial rites at the cremation ground, are enjoined with relevant Mantras.

## \|\| 1.1.24 \|\|

*catuḥpakṣāvadātasya viśuddhirbrāhmaṇasya ca \|*  
*sadvṛttasyādhikāro'sti śāstre'sminvedasammate \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The purity of a Brāhmaṇa is the purity in all the four sides (his father and mother, wife’s father and mother). To this scripture approved by the Vedas, all men of good conduct are entitled.

## \|\| 1.1.25-26 \|\|

*yathā surāṇāṃ pravaro devadevo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*nadīnāṃ ca yathā gaṃgā varṇānāṃ brāhmaṇo yathā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*akṣarāṇāṃ tu sarveṣāmoṃkāraḥ prathamo yathā \|*  
*pūjyānāṃ tu yathā mātā gurūṇāṃ ca yathā pitā \|*  
*tathaiva sarvaśāstrāṇāṃ pradhānaṃ skandakīrtitam \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Just as Maheśvara, the Lord of Devas, is the most excellent one among Suras, just as Gaṅgā is the greatest of all rivers, just as Brāhmaṇa is the greatest of all castes, just as Oṃkāra is the foremost among all Akṣaras (syllables), just as mother is the greatest among those worthy of adoration, just as father is the greatest (most respectable) of all elders, so also the Purāṇa narrated by Skanda is the most important of all scriptural texts.

## \|\| 1.1.27 \|\|

*purā kailāsaśikhare brahmādīnāṃ ca sannidhau \|*  
*skāndaṃ purāṇaṃ kathitaṃ pārvatyagre pinākinā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The Skanda Purāṇa was formerly narrated by the Pināka-bearing Lord (Śiva) in front of Pārvatī, in the presence of Brahmā and others on a peak of Kailāsa.

## \|\| 1.1.28 \|\|

*pārvatyā ṣaṇmukhasyāgre tena nandigaṇāya vai \|*  
*nandinā tu kumārāya tena vyāsāya dhīmate \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. It was then narrated by Pārvatī to Ṣaṇmukha (Skanda), by him to the Gaṇa Nandin and to Kumāra by Nandin and by him to the intelligent Vyāsa.

## \|\| 1.1.29 \|\|

*vyāsena me samākhyātaṃ bhavadbhyo'haṃ prakīrtaye \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. It was narrated to me by Vyāsa and I shall propound it to you all.

## \|\| 1.1.30 \|\|

*yūyaṃ sadbhāvasaṃyuktā yataḥ sarve maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*tena me bhāṣituṃ śraddhā bhavatāṃ skandasaṃhitām \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. You are all endowed with good mental attitude. You are all great sages. Hence I am sincerely eager to propound the Skanda Saṃhitā to you.

## Chapter 2 - Merit in Gifting Purāṇa Texts

## \|\| 1.2.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kathāyā lakṣaṇaṃ brūhi guṇadoṣānsavistarān \|*  
*ārṣeyapauruṣeyāṇāṃ kāvyacihnaparīkṣaṇam \|*  
*kathaṃ jñeyaṃ mahābuddhe śrotumicchāmahe vayam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: This religious incentive to gift Purāṇa manuscripts has resulted in the preservation and spread of these ancient texts.

The sages said:

1\. Describe the characteristic features of Kathā (story) and its good merits and demerits in detail. How should one assess the distinctive characteristics of the composition of sages and those of ordinary persons? How should it be understood, O highly intelligent one? We wish to hear.

## \|\| 1.2.2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atha saṃkṣepato vakṣye purāṇānāmanukramam \|*  
*lakṣaṇaṃ caiva saṃkhyāṃ ca uktabhedāṃstathaiva ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

2\. Now I shall succinctly describe the due order of the Purāṇas, their characteristic features, number and the differences mentioned.

## \|\| 1.2.3 \|\|

*purā tapaścacārogramamarāṇāṃ pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*āvirbhūtāstato vedāḥ saṣaḍaṃgapadakramāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Formerly the Grandfather of Amaras (Devas) performed a severe penance. Then the Vedas along with the six Aṅgas, Padas (words) and Kramas (special manners in the recitation of Vedic passages) manifested themselves.

## \|\| 1.2.4-7 \|\|

*tataḥ purāṇamakhilaṃ sarvaśāstramayaṃ dhruvam \|*  
*nityaśabdamayaṃ puṇyaṃ śata koṭipravistaram \|\| 4 \|\|*

*nirgataṃ brahmaṇo vaktrādbrāhmaṃ vaiṣṇavameva ca \|*  
*śaivaṃ bhāgavataṃ caiva bhaviṣyaṃ nāradīyakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*mārkaṇḍeyamathāgneyaṃ brahmavaivartameva ca \|*  
*laiṅgaṃ tathā ca vārāhaṃ skāṃdaṃ vāmanameva ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kaurmyaṃ mātsyaṃ gāruḍaṃ ca vāyavīyamanantaram \|*  
*aṣṭādaśaṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-5a. Then the entire range of the Purāṇas containing all the sacred texts and extending to a hundred crores (of verses) manifested themselves. The Purāṇa constituted of eternal sounds and words is meritorious. They (the Purāṇas) came out of the mouth of Brahmā.

5b-7. They are: (1) Brahmapurāṇa, (2) Viṣṇu Purāṇa, (3) Śiva Purāṇa, (4) Bhāgavata Purāṇa, (5) Bhaviṣya Purāṇa, (6) Nāradīya Purāṇa, (7) Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, (8) Āgneya Purāṇa, (9) Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa, (10) Liṅga Purāṇa, (11) Varāha Purāṇa, (12) Skanda Purāṇa, (13) Vāmana Purāṇa, (14) Kūrma Purāṇa, (15) Matsya Purāṇa, (16) Garuḍa Purāṇa, (17) Vāyavīya Purāṇa, and then (Padma Purāṇa) is called the eighteenth Purāṇa that is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.2.8-9 \|\|

*ekameva purā hyāsīdbrahmāṇḍaṃ śatakoṭidhā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tato'ṣṭādaśadhā kṛtvā vedavyāso yugeyuge \|*  
*prakhyāpayati loke'sminsākṣānnārāyaṇāṃśajaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Formerly there was only one Brahmāṇḍa (?Purāṇa) consisting of a hundred crores (of verses). In every Yuga, Vedavyāsa, the direct partial incarnation of Nārāyaṇa, divides it into eighteen Purāṇas and propounds it to the world.

## \|\| 1.2.10 \|\|

*anyānyupapurāṇāni muninā kathitāni tu \|*  
*tāni vaḥ kathayiṣyāmi saṃkṣepādavadhāryatām \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Others, Upapurāṇas, also were narrated by that sage. I shall mention them briefly to you. May they be listened to and understood.

\[List of Upapurāṇas\]

## \|\| 1.2.11-15 \|\|

*ādyaṃ sanatkumāroktaṃ nārasiṃhamataḥ param \|*  
*tṛtīyaṃ skāndamuddiṣṭaṃ kumāreṇānubhāṣitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*caturthaṃ śivadharmākhyaṃ sākṣānnandīśabhāṣitam \|*  
*durvāsasoktamāścaryyaṃ nāradoktamataḥ param \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kāpilaṃ mānavaṃ caiva tathaivośanaseritam \|*  
*brahmāṇḍaṃ vāruṇaṃ cānyatkālikāhvayameva ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

*māheśvaraṃ tathā sāṃbaṃ sauraṃ sarvārthasaṃcayam \|\| \|*  
*parāśaroktaṃ paramaṃ mārīcaṃ bhārgavāhvayam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*etānyupapurāṇāni kathitāni dvijottamāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

11-15. The first one is that narrated by Sanatkumāra. Thereafter is the Narasiṃha. The third one is indicated as Skanda (or Nanda) which is recounted by Kumāra (Skanda). The fourth one is called Śivadharma directly proclaimed by Nandīśa. Then the wonderful one narrated by Durvāsas. Thereafter what is narrated by Nārada. Then Kāpila and Mānava. Then what is narrated by Uśanas. Then Brahmāṇḍa. The next one is Varuṇa. Then the other one called Kālikā. Then Māheśvara, Sāṃba and Saura having the collection of all topics. What is narrated by Parāśara is great. Then Mārīca. Then what is called Bhārgava. These are the Upapurāṇas mentioned, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.2.16 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*purāṇasaṃkhyāmācakṣva sūta vistaraśaḥ kramāt \|*  
*dānadharmamaśeṣajña yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

The sages said:

16\. O Sūta, kindly mention the number of the Purāṇas in detail and due order, O Sūta, O knower of distinct features of Dāna and Dharma.

## \|\| 1.2.17 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*idameva purāṇe'sminpurāṇapuruṣastadā \|*  
*yaduktavānsa viśvātmā manave tannibodhata \|\| 17 \|\|*

Suta said:

17\. That immanent soul of the universe narrated to Manu this alone. The ancient Puruṣa mentioned this in this Purāṇa. Understand what he said:

## \|\| 1.2.18 \|\|

*purāṇaṃ sarvaśāstrāṇāṃ brahmāṇḍaṃ prathamaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*anantaraṃ ca vaktrebhyo vedāstasya vinirgatāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa is the most ancient of all scriptural texts. Thereafter the Vedas came out of his mouth.

## \|\| 1.2.19 \|\|

*purāṇamekamevāsīttasminkalpāntaretathā \|*  
*trivargasādhanaṃ puṇyaṃ śatakoṭipravistaram \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. There was only one Purāṇa in that Kalpāntara. It was the means of achieving the three aims (i.e. Virtue, Wealth and Love). It is meritorious and extended to a hundred crore (of verses).

## \|\| 1.2.20-23 \|\|

*vinirdagdheṣu lokeṣu kṛṣṇenānantarūpiṇā \|*  
*sāṅgāṃśca caturo vedānpurāṇanyāyavistaram \|\| 20 \|\|*

*mīmāṃsāṃ dharmaśāstraṃ ca parigṛhyātmasātkṛtam \|*  
*matsyarūpeṇa ca punaḥ kalpādāvudakārṇave \|\| 21 \|\|*

*aśeṣameva kathitaṃ brahmaṇe divyacakṣuṣe \|*  
*brahmā jagāda ca munīṃstrikālajñānadarśanaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*pravṛttiḥ sarvaśāstrāṇāṃ purāṇasyābhavattataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

20-23. When all the worlds were completely burned, at the time of Pralaya, Kṛṣṇa, in the form of the infinite one, collected together the four Vedas along with their Aṅgas, the Purāṇas, the detailed texts of Nyāya, Mīmāṃsās and Dharmaśāstra and retained them within himself. At the beginning of the next Kalpa, he, assuming the form of a fish in the vast ocean, told the entire tract of lores to Brahmā, endowed with divine vision. Brahmā endowed with the knowledge and vision of the three divisions of time (past, present and future) narrated it to all sages. Thereafter, all the scriptures and Purāṇas became current.

## \|\| 1.2.24 \|\|

*tataḥ kālakrameṇāsau vyāsarūpadharo hariḥ \|*  
*aṣṭādaśapurāṇāni saṃkṣepsyati yugeyuge \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then in due course, Hari in the form of Vyāsa, will summarize and propagate the eighteen Purāṇas.

## \|\| 1.2.25 \|\|

*caturlakṣapramāṇāni dvāparedvāpare sadā \|*  
*tadāṣṭādaśadhā kṛṣṇā bhūrloke'sminprabhāṣate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Always in every Dvāpara Yuga, the Purāṇas extended to four hundred thousand (verses). Kṛṣṇa expounds them in eighteen different forms (texts) on the earth.

## \|\| 1.2.26 \|\|

*adyā'pi devaloke tu śatakoṭipravistaram \|*  
*tadartho'tra caturlakṣaḥ saṃkṣepeṇa niveśitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Even today, in the celestial world, it extends to a hundred crores (of verses). The essence thereof is summarized into four hundred thousand (verses) (in this world).

\[Mahāpurāṇas: Extent, Contents\]

## \|\| 1.2.27 \|\|

*purāṇāni daśāṣṭau ca sāṃprataṃ tadihocyate \|*  
*nāmatastāni vakṣyāmi saṃkhyāṃ ca munisattamāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Now these are the eighteen Purāṇas, O excellent sages. I shall mention their names and the number (of verses) too.

## \|\| 1.2.28 \|\|

*brahmaṇā'bhihitaṃ pūrvaṃ yāvanmātraṃ marīcaye \|*  
*brāhmaṃ taddaśasāhasraṃ purāṇaṃ tadihocyate \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The entire thing mentioned earlier to Marīci by Brahmā is called Brahma Purāṇa. It contains ten thousand (verses).

## \|\| 1.2.29 \|\|

*likhitvā tacca yo dadyājjaladhenusamanvitam \|*  
*vaiśākhyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ ca brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. He who copies it in writing and makes a gift of it along with Jaladhenu on the Full-Moon day in the month of Vaiśākha is honoured in the world of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.2.30 \|\|

*etadeva yadā padmamabhūddhairaṇmayaṃ jagat \|*  
*tadvṛttāṃtāśrayāṃtaṃ tatpādmamityucyate budhaiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. When this universe was a golden lotus, the incidents therein were collected together and that Purāṇa is called Padma Purāṇa by learned men.

## \|\| 1.2.31 \|\|

*pādmaṃ tatpañcapañcāśatsahasrāṇīha paṭhyate \|*  
*tatpurāṇaṃ ca yo dadyātsuvarṇakamalānvitam \|*  
*jyeṣṭhe māsi tilairyuktaṃ so'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The Padma Purāṇa contains fifty-five thousand verses. He who makes a gift of it along with a golden lotus and gingelly seeds in the month of Jyeṣṭha, obtains the merit of a horse-sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.2.32 \|\|

*vārāhakalpavṛttāntamadhikṛtya parātparaḥ \|*  
*yatrāha dharmānakhilāṃstaduktaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ viduḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Based on the incidents of the Vārāhakalpa, the Lord, greater than the greatest, recounted all the virtues and holy rites. They know that Purāṇa as Vaiṣṇava (Viṣṇu) Purāṇa.

## \|\| 1.2.33 \|\|

*caritairañcitaṃ viṣṇostalloke vaiṣṇavaṃ viduḥ \|*  
*trayoviṃśatisāhasraṃ purāṇaṃ tatprakīrtitam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. This Purāṇa is beautified through the activities of Viṣṇu. This is proclaimed as the Purāṇa consisting of twenty-three thousand verses.

## \|\| 1.2.54 \|\|

*yatrāgniliṅgamadhyasthaḥ prāha devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*dharmārthakāmamokṣārthānāgneyamadhikṛtya ca \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. He who makes a gift of it along with Ghṛtadhenu on the bright full-moon day in Āṣāḍha attains the region of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 1.2.35 \|\|

*śrutakalpaprasaṅgena dharmānvāyurathābravīt \|*  
*yatra tadvāyavīyaṃ syādrudramāhātmyasaṃyutam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Vāyu recounted the holy rites and virtues in the context of Śrutakalpa as the background. This Purāṇa is Vāyavīya Purāṇa. It contains Rudramāhātmya also.

## \|\| 1.2.36 \|\|

*caturviṃśatisāhasraṃ nānā vṛttāntasaṃyutam \|*  
*dharmārthakāmamokṣaiśca sādhuvṛttasamanvitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. It consists of twenty-four thousand verses and many events are recounted in it. Virtue, wealth, love and salvation are dealt with along with the good conduct of the well-behaved.

## \|\| 1.2.37 \|\|

*śrāvaṇyāṃ śrāvaṇe māsi guḍadhenusamanvitam \|*  
*yo dadyāddadhisaṃyuktaṃ brāhmaṇāya kuṭumbine \|*  
*śivaloke sa pūtātmā kalpamekaṃ vasennaraḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He who makes a gift of it on the Full-Moon day in the month of Śrāvaṇa along with Guḍadhenu and curd to a Brāhmaṇa burdened with a large family, shall become a purified soul and he will live in Śivaloka for the period of a Kalpa.

## \|\| 1.2.38 \|\|

*punaḥ saṃjāyate martyo brāhmaṇo vedavittamaḥ \|*  
*vedavidyārthatattvajño vyākhyātattvārthavittamaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. He is reborn as a man once again. He will be a Brāhmaṇa, the most excellent one among those conversant with the Vedas. He will be an expert in the Vedic lore and the principles and meanings thereof and be the foremost among scholars of the themes and principles of writing glosses.

## \|\| 1.2.39 \|\|

*yatrādhikṛtya gāyatrīṃ varṇyate dharmavistaraḥ \|*  
*vṛtrāsuravadhopetaṃ tadbhāgavatamucyate \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. That Purāṇa is called Bhāgavata where Dharma is described on the basis of Gāyatrī. The killing of the demon Vṛtra is also contained in it.

## \|\| 1.2.40 \|\|

*sārasvatasya kalpasya madhye ye syurnarāmarāḥ \|*  
*tadvṛttāntodbhavaṃ puṇyaṃ puṇyodvāhasamanvitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. It also contains the events about men and Devas who live in the Sārasvata Kalpa. It is holy and there is meritorious description of marriages too.

## \|\| 1.2.41 \|\|

*likhitvā tacca yo dadyāddhemasiṃhasamanvitam \|*  
*paurṇamāsyāṃ prauṣṭhapadyāṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. He who copies it and makes a gift of it on the Full-Moon day in the month of Bhādrapada along with a gold replica of a lion attains the greatest goal.

## \|\| 1.2.42 \|\|

*aṣṭādaśasahasrāṇi purāṇaṃ tatprakīrtitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. It is glorified as a Purāṇa containing eighteen thousand verses.

## \|\| 1.2.43 \|\|

*yatrāha nārado dharmānbṛhatkalpāśrayāṃstviha \|*  
*pañcaviṃśatsahasrāṇi nāradīyaṃ taducyate \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. That is Nāradīya Purāṇa in which Nārada expounds Dharma as current in Bṛhatkalpa. It consists of twenty-five thousand verses.

## \|\| 1.2.44 \|\|

*tadiṣe pañcadaśyāṃ tu yo dadyāddhenusaṃyutam \|*  
*uttamāṃ siddhimāpnoti iha loke paratra ca \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. He who copies it and makes a gift of it on the Full-Moon day in the month of Àśvina along with a cow attains the highest Siddhi in this world and in the next. He obtains all his cherished desires. No doubt need be entertained in this respect.

## \|\| 1.2.45 \|\|

*yatrādhikṛtya śakunīndharmādharmavicāraṇam \|*  
*purāṇaṃ navasāhasraṃ mārkaṇḍeyaṃ taducyate \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. That which contains discussion about Dharma and Adharma with reference to (and in consultation with) birds is called the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa. It contains nine thousand verses.

## \|\| 1.2.46 \|\|

*parilikhya ca yo dadyātsauvarṇakarisaṃyutam \|*  
*kārtikyāṃ pauṇḍarīkasya yajñasya phalabhāgbhavet \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. He who copies it and makes a gift of it along with a gold replica of an elephant on the full-moon day of the month of Kārttika, attains the merit of the Pauṇḍarīka Yajña.

## \|\| 1.2.47 \|\|

*yattadīśānakalpasya vṛttāntamadhikṛtya ca \|*  
*vaśiṣṭhāyā'gninā proktamāgneyaṃ tatpracakṣate \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. What is narrated to Vasiṣṭha by Agni taking into account (and with reference to) the events of Īśānakalpa is called Āgneya Purāṇa.

## \|\| 1.2.48 \|\|

*likhitvā tacca yo dadyāddhemapadmasamanvitam \|*  
*mārgaśīrṣe vidhānena tiladhenuyutaṃ tathā \|*  
*tacca ṣoḍaśasāhasraṃ sarvakratuphalapradam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. He who copeis it and makes a gift of it along with a golden lotus and Tiladhenu (cow made of gingelly seeds) in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa in accordance with the injunctions, obtains the merit of all Kratus. It (the Purāṇa) contains sixteen thousand verses.

## \|\| 1.2.49-50 \|\|

*yatrādhikṛtya māhātmyamādityasya caturmukhaḥ \|*  
*aghorakalpavṛttāntaprasaṃgena jagatpatiḥ \|*  
*manave kathayāmāsa bhūtagrāmasya lakṣaṇam \|\| 49 \|\|*

*caturdaśasahasrāṇi tathā pañcaśatāni ca \|*  
*bhaviṣyacaritaprāyaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ tadihocyate \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. In the context of the events of Aghorakalpa, the Four-faced Lord of the universe explained to Manu the characteristics of all the Bhūtas (living beings, elements, spirits) on the basis of the greatness of Āditya. It is called Bhaviṣya Purāṇa because mostly future events are described. It contains fourteen thousand five hundred verses.

## \|\| 1.2.51 \|\|

*tatpauṣamāsi yo dadyātpaurṇamāsyāṃ vimatsaraḥ \|*  
*guḍakumbhasamāyuktamagniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. He who is free from jealousy and makes a gift of the Purāṇa on the full-moon day in the month of Pauṣa along with a pot of jaggery, shall obtain the merit of Agniṣṭoma.

## \|\| 1.2.52-53 \|\|

*rathaṃtarasya kalpasya vṛttāntamadhikṛtya ca \|*  
*sāvarṇinā nāradāya kṛṣṇamāhātmyasaṃyutam \|*  
*proktaṃ brahmavarāhasya caritaṃ varṇyate'tra ca \|\| 52 \|\|*

*tadaṣṭādaśasāhasraṃ brahmavaivartamucyate \|*  
*purāṇaṃ brahmavaivartaṃ yo dadyādbrāhmaṇottame \|*  
*māghamāse paurṇamāsyāṃ brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. With reference to the events of the Rathantara Kalpa, the story of Brahma-Varāha along with the greatness of Kṛṣṇa was narrated by Sāvarṇi to Nārada. It is called Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa. It contains eighteen thousand verses. He who makes a gift of Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa to an excellent Brāhmaṇa on the full-moon day in the month of Māgha, is honoured in the world of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.2.54-55 \|\|

*yatrāgniliṅgamadhyasthaḥ prāha devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*dharmārthakāmamokṣārthānāgneyamadhikṛtya ca \|\| 54 \|\|*

*kalpaṃ tallaiṅgamityuktaṃ purāṇaṃ brahmaṇā svayam \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. Lord Maheśvara staying in the middle of a. fiery Liṅga expounds (the Puruṣārthas) Virtue, Wealth, Love and Salvation in the context of Āgneya Kalpa. It is called Liṅga Purāṇa by Brahmā himself.

## \|\| 1.2.56 \|\|

*tadekādaśasāhasraṃ phālgunyāṃ yaḥ prayacchati \|*  
*tiladhenusamāyuktaṃ sa yāti śivasātmyatām \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. It contains eleven thousand verses. He who makes a gift of it on the full-moon day in the month of Phālguna along with Tiladhenu attains identity with Śiva.

## \|\| 1.2.57 \|\|

*mahāvarāhasya punarmāhātmyamadhikṛtya ca \|*  
*viṣṇunā'bhihitaṃ kṣoṇyai tadvārāhamihocyate \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. With reference to the greatness of Mahāvarāha Viṣṇu expounds (virtue etc.) to the Earth. It is called Varāhapurāṇa.

## \|\| 1.2.58 \|\|

*mānavasya prasaṃgena dhanyasya munisattamāḥ \|*  
*caturviṃśatsahasrāṇi tatpurāṇamihocyate \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. O excellent sages, it is in the context of Dhanya (a blessed one), the son of Manu. That Purāṇa contains twenty-five thousand verses.

## \|\| 1.2.59 \|\|

*kāñcanaṃ garuḍaṃ kṛtvā tiladhenusamanvitam \|*  
*paurṇamāsyāmatho dadyādbrāhmaṇāya kuṭumbine \|*  
*vārāhasyaprasādena padamāpnoti vaiṣṇavam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. A devotee should make a gold replica of Garuḍa and give it along with Tiladhenu to a Brāhmaṇa of a large family. He attains the region of Viṣṇu with the favour of Varāha.

## \|\| 1.2.60-61 \|\|

*yatra māheśvarāndharmānadhikṛtya ca ṣaṇmukham \|*  
*kalpe tatpuruṣe vṛtte caritairupabṛṃhitam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*skāṃdaṃ nāma purāṇaṃ tadekāśīti nigadyate \|*  
*sahasrāṇi śataṃ caikamiti martyeṣu paṭhyate \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. It is with reference to the religious practices of (the followers) of Maheśvara and with special reference to the Six-faced Lord. It describes in details the events which happened in Tatpuruṣa Kalpa. That Purāṇa called Skanda is said to consist of eighty-one thousand one hundred verses. It is thus recited among mortals (people).

## \|\| 1.2.62 \|\|

*parilekhya ca yo dadyāddhemaśūlasamanvitam \|*  
*śaivaṃ sa padamāpnoti makaropagame raveḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. He who copies it and makes a gift of it along with a trident made of gold when the Sun enters Capricorn, attains the region of Śiva.

## \|\| 1.2.63 \|\|

*trivikramasya māhātmyamadhikṛtya caturmukhaḥ \|*  
*trivargamabhyadhāttattu vāmanaṃ parikīrtitam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. With reference to the greatness of Trivikrama as the basis, the Four-faced Lord expounds the three aims of life. It is glorified as Vāmana Purāṇa.

## \|\| 1.2.64 \|\|

*purāṇaṃ daśasāhasraṃ kaurmakalpānugaṃ śivam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. This Purāṇa contains ten thousand verses. It is a Śaiva Purāṇa consisting of (the events of) Kaurmakalpa.

## \|\| 1.2.65 \|\|

*yaḥ śaradviṣuve dadyāddhemavastrasamanvitam \|*  
*kṣaumāvṛtaṃ yutaṃ dhenvā sa padaṃ yāti vaiṣṇavam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. He who makes a gift of it on the autumnal equinox along with gold and garments, covered with a silk cloth and accompanied by a cow, attains the region of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 1.2.66-68 \|\|

*yacca dharmārthakāmānāṃ mokṣasya ca rasātale \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ kathayāmāsa kūrmarūpī janārdanaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*indradyumnaprasaṃgena ṛṣīṇāṃ śakrasannidhau \|*  
*saptadaśasahasrāṇi lakṣmīkalpānuṣaṅgikam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*yo dadyādayane kaurmaṃ hemakūrmasamanvitam \|*  
*gosahasrapradānasya sa phalaṃ prāpnuyānnaraḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

66-68. In Rasātala, in the presence of Indra and sages, Janārdana, in the form of a Tortoise expounded the greatness of (the Puruṣārthas, viz.) Virtue, Wealth, Love and Liberation, in the Lakṣmīkalpa in the context of the interlude of Indradyumna. It (Kūrma Purāṇa) consists of seventeen thousand verses. He who makes the gift of the Kūrma Purāṇa along with a gold replica of tortoise, shall obtain the merit of gifting a thousand cows.

## \|\| 1.2.69-70 \|\|

*śrutīnāṃ yatra kalpādau pravṛttyarthaṃ janārdanaḥ \|*  
*matsyarūpī ca manave narasiṃhopavarṇanam \|\| 69 \|\|*

*adhikṛtyābravītsaptakalpavṛttaṃ munivratāḥ \|\| \|*  
*tanmātsyamiti jānīdhvaṃ sahasrāṇi catudarśa \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. For the propagation of the Vedas at the beginning of a Kalpa, Janārdana assumed the form of a Fish and expounded to Manu the events of seven Kalpas in the course of the description of Narasiṃha. O sage of holy rites, know this as the Matsya Purāṇa. It contains fourteen thousand verses.

## \|\| 1.2.71 \|\|

*viṣuve haimamatsyena dhenvā kṣaumayugānvitam \|*  
*yo dadyātpṛthivī tena dattā bhavati cākhilā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. If anyone makes the gift (of this Purāṇa) covered with a silk cloth on the day of equinox along with a gold replica of a fish and a cow, it is as though the entire earth has been gifted by him.

## \|\| 1.2.72 \|\|

*yadā vā garuḍe kalpe viśvāṇḍādgaruḍo'bhavat \|*  
*adhikṛtyābravītkṛṣṇo gāruḍaṃ tadihocyate \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. In Garuḍa Kalpa, Garuḍa came out of Viśvāṇḍa (Cosmic Egg). Kṛṣṇa expounded this Purāṇa on that as the basis. It is called Garuḍa Purāṇa.

## \|\| 1.2.73 \|\|

*tadaṣṭādaśa caikaṃ ca sahasrāṇīha paṭhyate \|\| \|*  
*svarṇahaṃsasamāyuktaṃ yo dadyādayane pare \|*  
*sa siddhiṃ labhate mukhyāṃ śivaloke ca saṃsthitim \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. It is recited in (i.e. consists of) nineteen thousand verses. He who makes a gift of it along with a gold replica of a swan in the latter Ayana (i.e. Southern transit) \[If pare is taken to mean “the great”, then the Ayana will be the Northern\] one achieves the principal Siddhi and a stay in Śiva Loka.

## \|\| 1.2.74 \|\|

*brahmā brahmāṇḍamāhātmyamadhikṛtyābravītpunaḥ \|*  
*tacca dvādaśasāhasraṃ brahmāṇḍaṃ dviśatādhikam \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Brahmā again expounded the greatness of the Cosmic Egg. That is Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa containing twelve thousand two hundred verses.

## \|\| 1.2.75 \|\|

*bhaviṣyāṇāṃ ca kalpānāṃ śrūyate yatra vistaraḥ \|*  
*tadbrahmāṇḍaṃ purāṇaṃ tu brahmaṇā samudāhṛtam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. A detailed description of the future Kalpas is found therein. That Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa is narrated by Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.2.76-78 \|\|

*yo dadyāttu vyatīpāta ūrṇāyugasamanvitam \|*  
*rājasūyasahasrasya phalamāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*hemadhenvāyutaṃ tacca brahmalokaphalapradam \|*  
*caturlakṣamidaṃ proktaṃ vyāsenādbhutakarmaṇā \|\| 77 \|\|*

*idaṃ lokahitārthāya saṃkṣiptaṃ dvāpare dvijāḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

76-77a. A man who makes the gift of that Purāṇa along with two woollen cloths, attains the merit of a thousand Rājasūyas. If the gift is accompanied by a gold replica of a cow, it bestows the region of Brahmā.

77b-78. Thus (the whole range of Purāṇas) was spoken by Vyāsa of miraculous deeds in four hundred thousand verses briefly in Dvāpara, O Brāhmaṇas, for the sake of the benefit of all the worlds.

## \|\| 1.2.79 \|\|

*idamadyāpi deveṣu śatakoṭipravistaram \|*  
*upabhedānpravakṣyāmi loke ye saṃpratiṣṭhitāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. The same tract of literature called Purāṇa among the celestial beings extends to a hundred crores.

\[Upapurāṇas: Extent and Contents\]

Now I shall narrate the different Upapurāṇas that have been established in the world.

## \|\| 1.2.80 \|\|

*pādme purāṇe yatproktaṃ nārasiṃhopavarṇanam \|*  
*taccāṣṭādaśasāhasraṃ nārasiṃhamihocyate \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. The description of Narasiṃha has been included in Padma Purāṇa. It contains eighteen thousand verses. It is called Nārasiṃha (Upa) Purāṇa.

## \|\| 1.2.81 \|\|

*nandine yatra māhātmyaṃ kārtikeyena varṇitam \|*  
*loke nandipurāṇaṃ vai khyātametaddvijottamāḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. (The text) wherein the greatness (of the Lord) has been described by Kārttikeya to Nandin has become well-known in the world as Nandi Purāṇa, O excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.2.82 \|\|

*yatra sāmbaṃ puraskṛtya bhaviṣyati kathānakam \|*  
*procyate tatpunarloke sāṃbameva munivratāḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. O Brāhmaṇas of holy Vratas, that Upapurāṇa of Sāṃba is famous in the world and the story therein pertains to Sāṃba.

## \|\| 1.2.83 \|\|

*evamādityasaṃjñaṃ tu tatraiva paripaṭhyate \|*  
*aṣṭādaśabhyastu pṛthakpurāṇaṃ yacca dṛśyate \|*  
*vijānīdhvaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhāstadetebhyo vinirgatam \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Thus the Āditya Upapurāṇa is mentioned there itself. It is seen as separate from the eighteen Upapurāṇas, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, know that it has been taken out of these.

## \|\| 1.2.84 \|\|

*pañcāṅgāni purāṇasya cākhyānamitaratsmṛtam \|*  
*sargaśca pratisargaśca vaṃśo manvantarāṇi ca \|*  
*vaṃśānuvaṃśacaritaṃ purāṇaṃ pañcalakṣaṇam \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. There are Five Aṅgas (limbs or sections) of the Purāṇa. They are: Sarga (creation), Pratisarga (subsidiary creation), Vaṃśa (the royal lineage), Manvantaras (the periods of the rule of Manus), Vaṃśānuvaṃśa Carita (the description of the dynasties of Sages etc.). Thus a Purāṇa has five characteristics.

## \|\| 1.2.85 \|\|

*brahmaviṣṇvarkarudrāṇāṃ māhātmyaṃ bhuvanasya ca \|*  
*saṃhāraśca pradṛśyeta purāṇaṃ pañcalakṣaṇam \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Another interpretation: the five characteristics are the description of the greatness of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Arka (the Sun god) and Rudra and the annihilation of the universe. All these five are seen in a Purāṇa.

## \|\| 1.2.86 \|\|

*dharmaścārthaśca kāmaśca mokṣaśca parikīrtyate \|*  
*sarveṣvapi purāṇeṣu tadvirūḍhe ca yatphalam \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. In all the Purāṇas virtue, wealth, love and salvation as well as the benefit contained in them have been explained.

## \|\| 1.2.87 \|\|

*sātvikeṣu ca kalpeṣu māhātmyamadhikaṃ hareḥ \|*  
*rājaseṣu ca māhātmyamadhikaṃ brahmaṇo viduḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. In the Sāttvika Kalpas the greatness of Hari is supreme. They know that the greatness of Brahmā reigns supreme in the Rājasa Kalpas.

## \|\| 1.2.88 \|\|

*tadvadagre ca māhātmyaṃ tāmaseṣu śivasya hi \|*  
*saṃkīrṇe ca sarasvatyāḥ pitṝṇāṃ ca nigadyate \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Similarly the greatness of Śiva is to be found in the Tāmasa Kalpas. In a Purāṇa of a mixed nature, the greatness of Sarasvatī and Pitṛs is narrated.

## \|\| 1.2.89 \|\|

*caturbhirbhagavānviṣṇurdvābhyāṃ brahmā tathā raviḥ \|*  
*aṣṭādaśapurāṇeṣu śeṣeṣu bhagavāñchivaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Among the eighteen Purāṇas, Lord Viṣṇu is extolled in four (Purāṇas), Brahmā and Ravi each in two and Lord Śiva in the remaining ones.

## \|\| 1.2.90 \|\|

*vedavanniścalaṃ manye purāṇaṃ vai dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*vedāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ sarve purāṇe nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, I think that Purāṇa is steady (unchangeable) like the Vedas. All the Vedas are established in the Purāṇas. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.2.91 \|\|

*bibhetyalpaśrutādvedo māmayaṃ cālayiṣyati \|*  
*itihāsapurāṇaistu niścalo'yaṃ kṛtaḥ purā \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. The Veda is afraid of the men of insufficient knowledge of the lore and feels: “Oh! This man will move and dislodge me.” It (Veda) has been rendered firm and steady formerly by means of Itihāsas and Purāṇas.

## \|\| 1.2.92 \|\|

*yanna dṛṣṭaṃ hi vedeṣu na dṛṣṭaṃ smṛtiṣu dvijāḥ \|*  
*ubhayoryatra dṛṣṭaṃ ca tatpurāṇeṣu gīyate \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. What is not seen in the Vedas, O Brāhmaṇas, what is not seen in the Smṛtis and what is not seen in both of them is being sung about in the Purāṇas.

## \|\| 1.2.93 \|\|

*yo veda caturo vedānsāṃgopaniṣado dvijaḥ \|*  
*purāṇaṃ naiva jānāti na ca sa syādvicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. A Brāhmaṇa who knows all the four Vedas along with their Aṅgas and the Upaniṣads, but who does not know the Purāṇa is not learned.

## \|\| 1.2.94 \|\|

*aṣṭādaśapurāṇāni kṛtvā satyavatīsutaḥ \|*  
*bhāratākhyānamakarodvedārthairupabṛṃhitam \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. After composing the eighteen Purāṇas, the son of Satyavatī (Vyāsa) wrote the narrative (epic) of Bhārata rendering it strengthened through the topics of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.2.95-97 \|\|

*lakṣeṇaikena tatproktaṃ dvāparānte mahātmanā \|*  
*vālmīkinā ca yatproktaṃ rāmopākhyānamuttamam \|\| 95 \|\|*

*brahmaṇā vihitaṃ yacca śatakoṭipravistaram \|*  
*āha tannāradāyaiva tena vālmīkaye punaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

*vālmīkinā ca loke tu dharmakāmārthasādhakam \|\| 97 \|\|*

95-97. It was propounded by the noble soul by means a hundred thousand verses at the end of Dvāpara.

Brahmā composed the story of Rāma in a hundred crores of verses. He spoke (transmitted) it unto Nārada and through him to Vālmīki and Vālmīki narrated the excellent story of Rāma that enables one to achieve virtue, wealth and love in this world in one-fourth of a Lakṣa of verses i.e. in twenty-five thousand verses.

## \|\| 1.2.98 \|\|

*evaṃ sapādāḥ pañcaite lakṣāḥ puṇyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*purātanasya kalpasya purāṇe tu vidurbudhāḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Thus these twenty-five thousand verses are glorified as meritorious. Learned men understood everything about the ancient Kalpas from the Purāṇa.

## \|\| 1.2.99-100 \|\|

*itihāsapurāṇāni bhidyante kāla gauravāt \|*  
*skāndaṃ tathā ca brahmāṇḍaṃ purāṇaṃ laiṅgameva ca \|\| 99 \|\|*

*vārāhakalpe viprendrāsteṣāṃ bhedaḥ pravartate \|*  
*aṣṭādaśaprakāreṇa brahmāṇḍaṃ bhinnameva hi \|\| 100 \|\|*

99-100. In accordance with the demands of the age (Kāla) the Itihāsas and Purāṇas differ, O leading Brāhmaṇas. Different versions of the Purāṇas, Skanda, Brahmāṇḍa and Liṅga are current in the Vārāha Kalpa. Indeed Brahmāṇḍa is different in eighteen ways.

## \|\| 1.2.101 \|\|

*aṣṭādaśapurāṇāni tena jātāni bhūtale \|*  
*laiṅgamekādaśavidhaṃ prabhinnaṃ dvāpare śubham \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Therefore, the Purāṇas came to be eighteen in the world. The splendid Liṅga Purāṇa was divided into eleven different sections in Dvāpara.

\[Khaṇḍas of the Skanda Purāṇa\]

## \|\| 1.2.102 \|\|

*skāndaṃ tu saptadhā bhinnaṃ veda vyāsenadhīmatā \|*  
*ekāśītisahasrāṇi śataṃ caikaṃ tu saṃkhyayā \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. The intelligent Vedavyāsa has divided the Skanda Purāṇa into seven Khaṇḍas. The number of verses in the Skanda is eighty-one thousand one hundred.

## \|\| 1.2.103 \|\|

*tasyā'dyo yo vibhāgastu skandamāhātmyasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*māheśvaraḥ samākhyāto dvitīyo vaiṣṇavaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. The first Book or Khaṇḍa is called Māheśvara Khaṇḍa. It contains the greatness of Skanda. The second one is remembered as Vaiṣṇava Khaṇḍa.

## \|\| 1.2.104 \|\|

*tṛtīyo brahmaṇaḥ proktaḥ sṛṣṭisaṃkṣepasūcakaḥ \|*  
*kāśīmāhātmyasaṃyuktaścaturthaḥ paripaṭhyate \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. The third one is mentioned as Brahma Khaṇḍa. It briefly expounds the creation (of the universe). The fourth one is cited as one containing the greatness of Kāśī (Kāśī Khaṇḍa).

## \|\| 1.2.105 \|\|

*revāyāḥ pañcamo bhāgaḥ sojjayinyāḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhaḥ kalpo nāgaraśca tīrthamāhātmyasūcakaḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. The fifth one is glorified as describing the greatness of Revā along with that of Ujjayinī. The sixth one is Nāgara Kalpa (Khaṇḍa). It indicates the greatness of the Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.2.106 \|\|

*saptamo yo vibhāgo'yaṃ smṛtaḥ prābhāsiko dvijāḥ \|*  
*sarve dvādaśasāhasrā vibhāgāḥ saṃprakīrtitāḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. O Brāhmaṇas, this seventh book is remembered as Prābhāsika (Khaṇḍa). Each of these Books is glorified as containing twelve thousand verses (approximately).

## \|\| 1.2.107 \|\|

*asminprābhāsikaḥ sarvo varṇyate kṣetravistaraḥ \|*  
*tīrthānāṃ caiva māhātmyaṃ māhātmyaṃ śaṃkarasya ca \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. In this Prābhāsika Khaṇḍa all the details of holy spots, greatness of the Tīrthas and greatness of Śaṅkara are explained.

## \|\| 1.2.108 \|\|

*anyeṣāṃ caiva devānāṃ māhātmyaṃ ca prakīrtyate \|*  
*iti bhedaḥ purāṇānāṃ saṃkṣepātkathito dvijāḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Of course the greatness of the other Devas too is mentioned.

Thus, O Brāhmaṇas, the different Purāṇas are succinctly told.

## \|\| 1.2.109 \|\|

*imamaṣṭādaśānāṃ tu purāṇānāmanukramam \|*  
*yaḥ paṭheddhavyakavyeṣu sa yāti bhavanaṃ hareḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. One who reads this enumeration of the eighteen Purāṇas at the time of the offering of Havyas and Kavyas goes to the abode of Hari.

## \|\| 1.2.110 \|\|

*idaṃ pavitraṃ hi yaśonidhānamidaṃ pitṝṇāmapi vallabhaṃ ca \|*  
*idaṃ ca deveṣvamṛtāya nityamidaṃ mahāpātakahṛcca puṃsām \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. This is indeed the storehouse of renown. This is a favourite of the Pitṛs. This gives satisfaction to the Devas always, like nectar. This destroys great sins of men.

## Chapter 3 - Queries Made by Devī

## \|\| 1.3.1-3 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kathito bhavatā sargaḥ pratisargastathaiva ca \|*  
*vaṃśānuvaṃśacaritaṃ purāṇānāmanukramaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*manvantarapramāṇaṃ ca brahmāṃḍasya ca vistaraḥ \|*  
*jyotiścakrasvarūpaṃ ca yathāvadanuvarṇitam \|*  
*śrotumicchāmahe tvattaḥ sāṃprataṃ tīrthavistaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

*pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni pāpaghnāni śubhāni ca \|*  
*tāni sūtaja kārtsnyena yathāvadvaktumarhasi \|\| 3 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-3. The regular creation and the counter-creation (or subsidiary creation) have been mentioned by Your Holiness. So also the story of the main dynasties and races (of sages) (Genealogies of kings and sages), the order or sequence of the Purāṇas, the extent of Manvantaras, the magnitude of the cosmic egg and the nature of the circle of the luminaries have been described factually.

Now we wish to hear from you the details of the Tīrthas. O Sūtaja, It behoves you to describe entirely and factually all the auspicious and evil-destroying Tīrthas on the earth.

## \|\| 1.3.4-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*idaṃ pṛṣṭaṃ purā devyā kailāsaśikharottame \|*  
*nānādhātuvicitrāṃge nānāratnasamanvite \|\| 4 \|\|*

*nānādrumalatākīrṇe nānāpuṣpopaśobhite \|*  
*yakṣavidyādharākīrṇe hyapsarogaṇasevite \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

4-5. This same question was formerly asked by the Goddess on the excellent peak of Kailāsa that possesses different kinds of gems. It is variegated due to various kinds of minerals. It is full of all types of trees and creepers. It shines with all sorts of flowers. Yakṣas, Vidyādharas and groups of celestial damsels frequent it.

## \|\| 1.3.6-9 \|\|

*tatra brahamā ca viṣṇuśca skandanandigaṇeśvarāḥ \|*  
*caṃdrādityau grahaiḥ sārdhaṃ nakṣatradhruvamaṇḍalam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*vāyuśca varuṇaścaiva kubero dhanadastathā \|*  
*īśānaścāgniriṃdraśca yamo nirṛtireva ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

*saritaḥ sāgarāḥ sarve parvatā uragāstathā \|*  
*brāhmyādyā mātaraścaiva ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 9 \|\|*

6-9. There were present there the following: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Skanda, Nandin, the leading Gaṇas, the Moon, the Sun along with the Planets, the Galaxies of Stars, the group of Stars round the Pole-star, Vāyu, Varuṇa, Kubera the bestower of wealth, Īśāna, Agni, Indra, Yama, Nirṛti, the Rivers, all the Oceans, Mountains, Serpents, Brāhmī and other Mothers, sages, ascetics, the Tīrthas in their personified forms, the holy places and shrines as well as Dānavas, Asuras, Daityas, Piśācas, Bhūtas (evil spirits) and Rākṣasas.

## \|\| 1.3.10 \|\|

*mūrtimaṃti ca tīrthāni kṣetrāṇyāyatanāni ca \|*  
*dānavāsuradaityāśca piśācā bhūtarākṣasāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. There was a divine throne there, a hundred Yojanas (a Yojana=12 Kras) in extent. Its refulgence was like that of ten million Suns. It was adorned with jewels and pearls.

## \|\| 1.3.11 \|\|

*tatra siṃhāsanaṃ divyaṃ śatayojanavistṛtam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. It was decorated with lotuses and lilies. It was resorted to by Siddhas and Kinnaras. By means of millions of its white umbrellas, it covered up all the regions and quarters.

## \|\| 1.3.12 \|\|

*lakṣāyutasahasraiśca rudrakoṭibhirāvṛtam \|*  
*tanmadhye sarvatobhadraṃ siṃhadvāraiḥ sutoraṇaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. In the center thereof, there was a Sarvatobhadra (temple-like structure with doors on all sides) with ornamental gates. It was surrounded by thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands and millions of Rudras.

## \|\| 1.3.13 \|\|

*svacchamauktikasaṃkāśaṃ prākāraśikharāvṛtam \|*  
*nandīśvaramahākāladvārapālagaṇairvṛtam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. It was covered with peaks and ramparts shining with crystal-clear pearls. There were sentries like Nandīśvara, Mahākāla and others.

## \|\| 1.3.14 \|\|

*kiṃkiṇījālamukharaiḥ satyatākairalaṃkṛtam \|*  
*vitānacchatrakhaṃḍaiśca muktādāmapralaṃbitaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. It was adorned with excellent banners producing resonant sounds with tiny tinkling bells. There were awnings and pieces of umbrella-like stretches with pearl strings hanging down.

## \|\| 1.3.15 \|\|

*ghaṃṭācāmaraśobhāḍhayairdarpaṇaiścopaśobhitam \|*  
*kalaśairdvāravinyastaratnapallavasaṃyutaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Its beauty was enhanced by means of mirrors having the lustre of hanging bells and chowries. Big pots had been placed at the entrances and were decorated with tender sprouts and jewels.

## \|\| 1.3.16 \|\|

*citritaṃ citraśāstrajñai ratnacūrṇaiḥ samu्jvalaiḥ \|*  
*svastikaiḥ patravalyādyairliṃgodbhavalatādibhiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Experts in the science of ornamental decorations had embellished it with shining powders of jewels. There were Svastika-shaped fittings embellished with creeper-like designs above the Liṅga-like fittings.

## \|\| 1.3.17 \|\|

*śatasiṃhāsanākīrṇaṃ vedikābhiśca śobhitam \|*  
*āsīnai rudravṛndaiśca rudrakanyākadambakaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. In the assembly hall there were hundreds of thrones and refulgent altars. Groups of Rudras and Rudra-girls were seated there.

## \|\| 1.3.18 \|\|

*lakṣapatradalāḍhyaiśca śvetapadmaiśca bhūṣitam \|*  
*apsarobhiḥ samākīrṇaṃ puṣpaprakaravistṛtam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. It was adorned with white lotuses with hundred thousands of petals. Flowers had been scattered all round and the Apsarās had occupied all those places.

## \|\| 1.3.19-20 \|\|

*dhūpitaṃ dhūpavarttībhiḥ kuṃkumodakasecitam \|*  
*vaṃśavīṇāmṛdaṃgaiśca gomukhairmukhavādanaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*śaṃkhabherīninādena dundubhidhvanitena ca \|*  
*garjadbhirgaṇavṛndaiśca meghasvanitanisvanaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Saffron waters were sprinkled. The place was fumigated with incense sticks. The entire area resounded with the sounds of the notes of flutes, lutes, Gomukhas and Mṛdaṅga drums, mouth organs, the sounds of conchs and Bherī drums, Dundubhi (war drums) etc. The roaring groups of Gaṇas filled the place (as if) with the sounds of rumbling clouds.

## \|\| 1.3.21 \|\|

*gaṇānāṃ stotraśabdena sāmavedaraveṇa ca \|*  
*prekṣaṇīyairmahānādairgeyahuṅkāraśobhitam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. There was the sound of the prayers of the Gaṇas along with chanting of Sāman. They were handsome to look at and their voice was at its highest pitch. Now and then, gruff sounds came out of them laconically in the midst of their songs.

## \|\| 1.3.22 \|\|

*vṛṣanarditaśabdena gajavājiraveṇa ca \|*  
*kāṃcīnūpuraśabdena samākīrṇadigaṃtaram \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. All the quarters were filled with sounds of bellowing of bulls, neighing and trumpeting of horses and elephants and tinkling of girdles and anklets.

## \|\| 1.3.23-24 \|\|

*sarvasaṃpatkaraṃ śrīmacchaṃkarasyaiva maṃdiram \|*  
*vaṃśa vīṇāmṛdaṃgaiśca nāditaṃ tatra tatra ha \|*  
*ṛgvedo mūrtimāṃścaiva śakranīlasamadyutiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*divyagandhānuliptāṃgo divyābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*saṃsthitaḥ pūrvatastasya dīpyamānaḥ svatejasā \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. The palatial abode of Śaṅkara was glorious with all rich equipments. It was resonant here and there with the notes and sounds of flutes, lutes and Mṛdaṅgas.

In the eastern wing (of the hall) was the personified form of Ṛgveda with the lustre of sapphire embellished with divine ornaments and smeared with divine unguents. It was refulgent with self-luminosity.

## \|\| 1.3.25 \|\|

*uttareṇa yajurvedaḥ śuddhasphaṭikasannibhaḥ \|*  
*divyakuṇḍaladhārī ca mahākāyo mahābhujaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Yajurveda who resembled the lustre of pure crystal was present in the northern wing. He had a huge body with large arms and he wore divine earrings.

## \|\| 1.3.26 \|\|

*sthitaḥ paścima digbhāge sāmavedaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*raktāṃbaradharaḥ śrīmānpaprarāgasamaprabhaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The eternal Sāmaveda was present in the western wing. He was glorious in red robes having the lustre of ruby.

## \|\| 1.3.27-32 \|\|

*sragdāmadhārī citraśca gītabhūṣaṇabhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*athavāṃ'janavacchayāmaḥ sthito dakṣiṇatastathā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*piṃgākṣo lohitagrīvo harikeśo mahātanuḥ \|*  
*itihāsaṣaḍaṃgāni purāṇānyakhilāni ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

*vedopaniṣadaśchando mīmāṃsāraṇyakaṃ tathā \|*  
*svāhākāravaṣaṭkārau rahasyāni tathaiva ca \|\| 29 \|\|*

*etaiḥ samanvitaiścaiva tatra brahmā svayaṃ sthitaḥ \|*  
*śaktirūpadharairmantrairyogaiśvaryasamanvitaiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*sahasrapatrakamalairaṃkitaiḥ surapūjitaiḥ \|*  
*pūjitairgaṇarudraiśca brahmaviṣviṃdravaṃditaiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*cāmarākṣepavyajanairvījitaiśca samantataḥ \|*  
*śobhitaśca sadā śrīmāṃścaṃdrakoṭisamaprabhaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

27-28a. Atharvaveda wore a garland. He appeared with the embellishments of Gīta (Music) and ornaments.

He was as dark-complexioned as collyrium. His eyes were reddish-brown and the neck red. The hairs were greenish and the body was huge.

28b-30a. God Brahmā was himself present there along with these: Itihāsas, all the Purāṇas, the six Aṅgas, Upaniṣads, Chandas, Mīmāṃsā, Āraṇyakas, Svāhākāra, Vaṣaṭkāra and the (their) esoteric secrets.

30b-32. Lord Śiva shone there with the eternal glorious refulgence of ten million moons. In a respectful way, he was attended upon by Suras who worship the Mantras in the form of Śaktis endowed with supreme Yogic powers, by means of thousand-petalled lotuses. He was adored by Rudras and Gaṇas. He was respectfully bowed to by Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Indra who served him with moving of fans and waving of chowries.

## \|\| 1.3.33 \|\|

*jñānāmṛtasutṛptātmā yogaiśvaryaprasādakaḥ \|*  
*yogīṃdramānasāṃbhoja rājahaṃso dvijottamaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. His (Śiva’s) soul is perfectly contented with nectarine (spiritual) knowledge. This excellent Dvija (Twice-born one i.e. Parama Haṃsa) who shines in the lotus-like hearts of Yogins enlightens them with rich Yogic powers and supernatural achievements.

## \|\| 1.3.34 \|\|

*ajñānatimiradhvaṃsī ṣaṭtriṃśattattvabhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*sarvasaukhyapradātā ca tatrāste caṃdraśekharaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. There stays the Moon-crested Lord, the destroyer of the darkness of ignorance, embellished with thirty-six Tattvas, giving happiness to all.

## \|\| 1.3.35 \|\|

*tasyotsaṃgagatā devī taptakāṃcanasaprabhā \|*  
*pūjito yoginīvṛndaiḥ sādhakaiḥ surakinnaraiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The goddess with the refulgence of heated gold is seated on his lap. He is adored by the groups of Yoginīs and the Suras and Kṛnnaras who are the aspirant devotees.

## \|\| 1.3.36 \|\|

*sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpūrṇā sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā \|*  
*yogasiddhipradā nityaṃ mokṣābhyudayadāyinīm \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. She is endowed with all excellent characteristic features and embellished with all kinds of ornaments. She is the perpetual bestower of Yogic powers and of the worldly prosperity and salvation.

## \|\| 1.3.37-38 \|\|

*saubhāgyakadalīkandamūlabījaṃ ca pārvatī \|*  
*devasya mukhamālokya vismitā cārulocanā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*ānaṃdabhāvaṃ saṃjñāya ānandāsrāvilekṣaṇam \|*  
*uvāca devī madhuraṃ kṛtāṃjalipuṭā satī \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Pārvatī is the root of origin of all spiritual felicity with wonder. She looked at the face of the Lord whose eyes were bedimmed with tears of joy displaying the state of enjoyment of bliss. Smilingly Goddess Satī of charming eyes, spoke these sweet words with the palms joined together in veneration:

## \|\| 1.3.39 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*janmakoṭisahasrāṇi janmakoṭiśatāni ca \|*  
*śodhitastvaṃ jagannātha mayā prāṇanaciṃtayā \|\| 39 \|\|*

The Devī said:

39\. O Lord of the worlds, you have been sought by me, with the anxiousness for living in the course of hundreds and thousands of crores of lives.

## \|\| 1.3.40 \|\|

*arddhāṃga saṃsthayā vāpi tvadvaktradhyānakāmyayā \|*  
*tathāpi te jagannātha nāṃto labdhvo maheśvara \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O Lord of the worlds, though I have occupied half of your person with a desire to meditate on your countenance, O Lord, I have however not achieved the perfect realization of it.

\[Devī’s prayer:\]

## \|\| 1.3.41 \|\|

*anantarūpiṇe tubhyaṃ devadeva namo'stu te \|*  
*namo vedarahasyāya namo vedaiḥ stutāya ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O Lord of Devas, of infinite forms, obeisance to you. Obeisance to you who are the secret of the Vedas, Obeisance to one who is eulogized by the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.3.42 \|\|

*śmaśānaratinityāya namo gaganacāriṇe \|*  
*jyeṣṭhasāmarahasyāya śatarudrapriyāya ca \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Obeisance to you who loves to stay in cremation ground perpetually. Obeisance to the Lord moving about in the sky. Obeisance to the secret of the Jyeṣṭha Sāman. Obeisance to the Lord fond of Śatarudra prayer.

## \|\| 1.3.43 \|\|

*namo vṛṣakṛtāṃkāya yajurvedadharāya ca \|*  
*brahmāṃḍakoṭisaṃlagnamāline gaganātmane \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Obeisance to the Lord who adopted bull as his emblem, to the Lord who holds the Yajur-veda. Obeisance to the Lord wearing the garland wreathed out of crores of Cosmic Eggs, to the Lord identical with the sky (or the soul of the sky).

## \|\| 1.3.44 \|\|

*maṇicitritakandāya namaḥ sarvārthasiddhaye \|*  
*namo vedasvarūpāya dvija siddhipriyāya ca \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Obeisance to the Lord with the neck appearing variegated with jewels. Obeisance to the one who has achieved all objectives. Obeisance to the one who is the real form of the Vedas, to the one who likes the spiritual achievement of the twice-born.

## \|\| 1.3.45 \|\|

*puṃstrīvikārarūpāya namaścaṃdrārddhadhāriṇe \|*  
*namognaye sahomāya ādityavaruṇāya ca \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Obeisance to the one in the form of transformation of man and woman. Obeisance to the one wearing the crescent moon. Obeisance to Agni with Homa, to Āditya and Varuṇa.

## \|\| 1.3.46 \|\|

*pṛthivyai cāṃtarikṣāya vāyave dīkṣitāya ca \|*  
*saṃyogāya viyogāya dhātre kartre'pahāriṇe \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Obeisance to Pṛthivī and also to the Space, to the Wind, to the Dīkṣita (the initiated one). Obeisance to Saṃyoga (Contact) and to Viyoga (Separation), to Dhātṛ (Creator), Kartṛ (Doer), Apahārin or destroyer.

## \|\| 1.3.47 \|\|

*pradīptaśūlahastāya brahmadaṇḍadharāya ca \|*  
*namaḥ patīnāṃ pataye mahatāṃ pataye namaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Obeisance to the Lord with the brilliant trident in the hand, to the one who holds the Brahma-Daṇḍa (the staff of Brahmā). Obeisance to the Lord of Lords. Obeisance to the Lord of the great.

## \|\| 1.3.48 \|\|

*namaḥ kālāgnirudrāya saptalokanivāsine \|*  
*tvaṃ gatiḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ bhūtānāṃ pataye namaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Obeisance to Kālāgnirudra (Rudra, the Fire of destruction), the inhabitant of the seven worlds. You are the ultimate goal of all the living beings. Obeisance to the Lord of goblins.

## \|\| 1.3.49 \|\|

*namaste bhagavanrudra namaste bhagavañchiva \|*  
*namaste parataḥ śreṣṭha namaste parataḥ para \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O holy Lord Rudra, obeisance to you. O holy Lord Śiva, obeisance to you. Obeisance to you, the greater than the greatest. O Lord, O one greater than the greatest, obeisance to you.

## \|\| 1.3.50 \|\|

*jihvācāpalyabhāvena khedito'si mayā prabho \|*  
*tatkṣantavyaṃ maheśāna jñānadivya namo'stu te \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. O Lord, you have been pained by me due to the fickleness of my tongue. O Maheśāna, that should be pardoned. Obeisance to you, O Lord endowed with the divine knowledge.

## \|\| 1.3.51 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*mamotsaṃgasthitā devi kiṃ tvaṃ sāsrāvilekṣaṇā \|*  
*adyāpi kimapūrṇaṃ te tatsarvaṃ karavāṇyaham \|\| 51 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

51\. O goddess, you are on my lap. Why should your eyes be turbid with tears? What is it that is yet incomplete in regard to you. I shall make it full.

## \|\| 1.3.52 \|\|

*varaṃ bravīhi bhadraṃ te stavenānena suvrate \|*  
*dadāmi te na saṃdehaḥ śokaṃ tyaja maheśvari \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Mention the boon. Welfare unto you. By this prayer (I am pleased), O lady of holy vows. I will give you (everything) undoubtedly. O Maheśvarī, share off your sorrow.

## \|\| 1.3.53 \|\|

*niṣkale sakale devi sthūle sūkṣme carācare \|*  
*na tatpaśyāmi deveśi yattvayā rahitaṃ bhavet \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O goddess, you are one with Kāla and one without Kalā. O goddess of Devas, I do not see anything without you in the whole universe consisting of mobile and immobile beings whether gross or subtle.

## \|\| 1.3.54 \|\|

*ahaṃ te hṛdaye gauri tvaṃ ca me hṛdi saṃsthitā \|*  
*ahaṃ bhrātā ca putraśca baṃdhurbhartā tathaiva ca \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. O Gaurī, I am abiding in your heart. You are stationed in my heart. I am your brother, son, kinsman and husband.

## \|\| 1.3.55 \|\|

*tvaṃ tu me bhaginī bhāryā duhitā bāṃdhavī snuṣā \|*  
*ahaṃ yajñapatiryajvā tvaṃ ca śraddhā sadakṣiṇā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. You are my sister, wife, daughter, kinswoman and daughter-in-law. I am the performer of Yajña and the Lord of Yajña. You are Śraddhā (faith) and also the Dakṣiṇā.

## \|\| 1.3.56 \|\|

*oṃkāro'haṃ vaṣaṭkāraḥ sāmāhamṛgyajustathā \|*  
*ahamagniśca hotā ca yajamānastathaiva ca \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. I am Oṃkāra and Vaṣaṭkāra. I am Sāman, Ṛk and Yajus. I am Agni, Hotṛ and Yajamāna.

## \|\| 1.3.57 \|\|

*adhvaryurahamudgātā brahmāhaṃ brahmavittathā \|*  
*tvaṃ tu devyaraṇī caiva patnī tu parikīrtyase \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. I am Adhvaryu, Udgātṛ and Brahmā. I am the knower of Brahman. O Devī, you are Araṇi (the stick from which sacrificial fire is produced by attrition). You are glorified as Patnī (wife of the performer of a sacrifice).

## \|\| 1.3.58 \|\|

*svāhā svadhā ca suśroṇi tvayi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*ahamiṣṭo mahāyajñaḥ pūrvo yajñastvamucyase \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. O lady of excellent hips, you are Svāhā and Svadhā. Everything is established in you. I am the desired great Yajña duly performed. You are said to be Pūrvayajña (the earlier Yajña).

## \|\| 1.3.59 \|\|

*puruṣo'haṃ varārohe prakṛtistvaṃ nigadyase \|*  
*ahaṃ viṣṇurmahāvīryastvaṃ lakṣmīrlokabhāvinī \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. O fair lady, I am Puruṣa. You are mentioned as Prakṛti. I am Viṣṇu of great vigour and exploits. You are Lakṣmī, the promoter of the welfare of the worlds.

## \|\| 1.3.60 \|\|

*ahamindro mahātejāḥ prācī tvaṃ parameśvarī \|*  
*prajāpatīnāṃ rūpeṇa sarvamāhaṃ vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. I am the highly refulgent Indra. You are the great goddess Prācī (the East). I am stabilized as omniformed through the forms of Prajāpatis.

## \|\| 1.3.61 \|\|

*teṣāṃ yā nāyikāstāstvaṃ rūpaistaistairavasthitā \|*  
*divaso'haṃ mahādevi rajanī tvaṃ nigadyase \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. You have become established in the different forms of their spouses. O great goddess, I am Divasa (day) and you are mentioned as Rajanī (night).

## \|\| 1.3.62 \|\|

*nimeṣo'haṃ muhūrtaśca tvaṃ kalā siddhireva ca \|*  
*ahaṃ tejo'dhikaḥ sūryastvaṃ tu saṃdhyā prakīrttyase \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. I am Nimeṣa (Moment) and Muhūrta (period of forty-eight minutes). You are Kalā and Siddhi (achievement). I am the highly refulgent Sun. You are glorified as Sandhyā (Twilight).

## \|\| 1.3.63 \|\|

*ahaṃ bījadharaḥ śreṣṭhastvaṃ tu kṣetraṃ varānane \|*  
*ahaṃ vanaspatiḥ plakṣastvaṃ vanaspatirucyase \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. I am the sower of seed, the most excellent one. O lady of excellent countenance, you are the Kṣetra (field). I am the Plakṣa tree. You are mentioned as Vanaspati.

## \|\| 1.3.64 \|\|

*śeṣarūpadharo nitye phaṇāmaṇivibhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*revatī tvaṃ viśālākṣi madavibhramalocanā \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. O eternal one, I have assumed the form of Śeṣa, adorned with a jewel on the hood. O Viśālākṣī (goddess of large eyes), you are Revatī with the eyes of inebriated graceful charms.

## \|\| 1.3.65 \|\|

*mokṣo'haṃ sarvaduḥkhānāṃ tvaṃ tu devi parā gatiḥ \|*  
*apāṃ patirahaṃ bhadre tvaṃ tu devi saridvarā \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. I am salvation, the release from all sorrows. O goddess, you are the greatest goal. O fair lady, I am the Lord of Waters. O goddess, you are the most excellent one of the rivers.

## \|\| 1.3.66 \|\|

*vaḍavāgnirahaṃ bhadre tvaṃ tu dīptiḥ prakīrtitā \|*  
*prajāpatirahaṃ karttā tvaṃ prajā prakṛtistathā \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. O fair lady, I am the submarine fire. You are glorified as the coruscant splendour. I am Prajāpati and the Doer. You are Prajā (subject) and the Prakṛti.

## \|\| 1.3.67 \|\|

*nāgānāmadhipaścāhaṃ pātālatalavāsinām \|*  
*tvaṃ nāgī nāgarājo'haṃ sahasraphaṇabhūṣitaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. I am the Lord of the serpents staying in the nether regions. You are the Nāgī and I am the king of Nāgas adorned with a thousand hoods.

## \|\| 1.3.68 \|\|

*niśākaravaraścāhaṃ śreṣṭhā tvaṃ rajanīkarī \|*  
*kāmo'haṃ kāmado devi tvaṃ ratiḥ smṛtireva ca \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. I am the excellent Niśākara (the Moon). You are the excellent Rajanīkarī (cause of night). I am Kāma, the bestower of love, O goddess. You are Rati and Smṛti (memory).

## \|\| 1.3.69 \|\|

*durvāsāścāpyahaṃ bhadre tvaṃ kṣamā samacāriṇī \|*  
*lobhamohatapaścāhaṃ tvaṃ tṛṣṇā tāmasī smṛtā \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. O fair lady, I am Durvāsas. You are Kṣamā (forgiveness) acting impartially. I am Tapas (penance) performed with delusion and covetousness. You are remembered as the thirst (desire) overwhelmed by dark traits.

## \|\| 1.3.70 \|\|

*kakudmānvṛṣabhaścāhaṃ yogamātā tapasvinī \|*  
*vāyurapyahamavyaktastvaṃ gatirmanasūdanī \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. I am Bull with a big hump. You are the saintly Yogamātā (Mother of Yogic feats). I am the unmanifest Vāyu (Wind). You are the movement that animates the mind.

## \|\| 1.3.71 \|\|

*ahaṃ mocayitā lobhe nirmamā tvaṃ yaśasvini \|*  
*nayo'haṃ sarvakāryeṣu nītistvaṃ kamalekṣaṇā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. I am the releaser in the case of covetousness. O lady of renown, you are Nirmamā (free from the feelings of mine-ness or possession). I am circumspection in regard to all tasks. You are the lotus-eyed Nīti (Judicious policy).

## \|\| 1.3.72 \|\|

*ahamannaṃ ca bhoktā ca oṣadhī tvaṃ nigadyase \|*  
*ahamagniśca dhūmaśca tvamūṣmā jvālameva ca \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. I am food and its enjoyer. You are mentioned as Oṣadhī (medicinal herb). I am Agni and smoke. You are the heat and flame.

## \|\| 1.3.73 \|\|

*ahaṃ saṃvarttako meghastvaṃ ca dhārā hyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ munīnāṃ rūpeṇa tvaṃ tatpatnī prakīrtitā \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. I am the Saṃvartaka (occurring at the time of ultimate annihilation) cloud. You are the many-sided downpour. I am in the form of the sages. You are glorified as the wives of those sages.

## \|\| 1.3.74 \|\|

*ahaṃ saṃsārakarttā vai tvaṃ tu sṛṣṭirvarānane \|*  
*ahaṃ śukrāsthiromāṇi tvaṃ majjā balameva ca \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. O lady of excellent countenance, I am the creator of the worldly existence and you are the creation. I am semen, bone and hairs. You are marrow and strength.

## \|\| 1.3.75 \|\|

*parjanyo'haṃ mahābhāge tvaṃ vṛṣṭiḥ parameśvari \|*  
*ahaṃ saṃvatsaro devi tvamṛtuḥ parikīrttitā \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. O highly blessed lady, I am Parjanya (cloud). O great goddess, you are Vṛṣṭi (downpour of rain). O goddess, I am Saṃvatsara (year). You are glorified as Ṛtu (season).

## \|\| 1.3.76 \|\|

*ahaṃ kṛtayugo devi tvaṃ tu tretā nigadyase \|*  
*yugo'haṃ dvāparaḥ śrīmāṃstvaṃ kaliḥ parameśvari \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. O goddess, I am Kṛtayuga. You are mentioned as Tretā. I am the glorious Dvāpara. O great goddess, you are Kali.

## \|\| 1.3.77 \|\|

*ākāśaścāpyahaṃ bhadre pṛthivī tvamihocyase \|*  
*ahamadṛśyamūrtiśca dṛśyamūrtistvamucyase \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. O fair lady, I am Ākāśa (Sky). You are mentioned as Pṛthvī (Earth). I am one of unmanifest form. You are mentioned as one of manifest form.

## \|\| 1.3.78 \|\|

*varado'haṃ varārohe maṃtrastvamiti cocyase \|*  
*ahaṃ draṣṭā ca śrotā ca tvaṃ dṛśyā śrutireva ca \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. O beautiful lady, I am the bestower of boons. You are mentioned as Mantra. I am the seer and the hearer. You are the seen and the act of hearing.

## \|\| 1.3.79 \|\|

*ahaṃ vaktā ramayitā tvaṃ vācyā parameśvari \|*  
*ahaṃ śrotā ca gātā ca tvaṃ gītirgeyameva ca \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. I am the speaker and the Ramayitṛ (one who delights). O great goddess, you are what is spoken. I am the listener and the singer. You are the music and song.

## \|\| 1.3.80 \|\|

*ahaṃ trātā ca gandhaśca tvaṃ tu nighrāṇameva ca \|*  
*ahaṃ sparśayitā kartā sparśyastvaṃ sṛṣṭameva ca \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. I am the Ghrātṛ (one who smells) and the scent. You are the act (or organ) of smelling. I am Sparśayitṛ (one who touches) and the creator. You are the Sparśya (that which is to be touched) and the Sṛṣṭa (what is created).

## \|\| 1.3.81 \|\|

*ahaṃ sarvamidaṃ bhūtaṃ tvaṃ tu devi na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*sraṣṭā'haṃ tava deveśi tvaṃ sṛjasyakhilaṃ jagat \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. There is no doubt, O goddess, that you and I constitute this visible range of living beings. O goddess of Devas, I am your creator. You do create the entire universe.

## \|\| 1.3.82 \|\|

*tvayā mayā ca deveśi otaprotamidaṃ jagat \|*  
*ekadhā daśadhā caiva tathā śatasahasradhā \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. O goddess of Devas, this universe is woven together in every direction (period?) by you and me once, ten times, hundred times, thousand times.

## \|\| 1.3.83 \|\|

*aiśvaryeṇa tu saṃyuktau sarvaprāṇi vyavasthitau \|*  
*ahaṃ tvaṃ ca viśālākṣi satataṃ saṃpratiṣṭhitau \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. O large-eyed lady, you and I are always established as controllers in all the living beings. We are in close contact with all supernatural powers.

## \|\| 1.3.84 \|\|

*krīḍāmi krīḍayā devi tvayā sārddhaṃ varānane \|*  
*tvaṃ dhṛtirdhāriṇī lakṣmīḥ kāṃtā matprakṛtirdhruvam \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. O goddess of excellent countenance, I divert myself with you in all sports. You are certainly Dhṛti (fortitude, that which holds), you are Lakṣmī (glory) that sustains and holds, my beloved and my Prakṛti.

## \|\| 1.3.85 \|\|

*ratiḥ smṛtiḥ kāmacārī mama cāṃganivāsinī \|*  
*devi kiṃ bahunoktena prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. You are Rati (pleasure), Smṛti (memory), Kāmacārī (moving as you like) and one who is always present in my limbs. O goddess, why speak much? You are greater than my own vital airs.

## \|\| 1.3.86 \|\|

*varaṃ varaya devaśi yatkiṃcinmanasi sthitam \|*  
*tatte dadāmi tuṣṭo'haṃ yadyapi syātsudurllabham \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. O goddess of the Devas, choose your boon, whatever is present in your mind. I am pleased and I shall give the same to you even if it be very difficult to get.

## \|\| 1.3.87 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*dhanyāhaṃ kṛtapuṇyāhaṃ tapaḥ sucaritaṃ mayā \|*  
*yattvayā'haṃ jagannātha harṣadṛṣṭyā'valokitā \|\| 87 \|\|*

The Devī said:

87\. O Lord of the universe, I am blessed. I am one who has performed meritorious deeds. Penance has been performed by me very well inasmuch as I have been looked upon by you with a pleased eye.

## \|\| 1.3.88 \|\|

*yadi tuṣṭo'si me deva varaṃ dātuṃ mamecchasi \|*  
*tanme kathaya deveśa sāṃprataṃ tīrthavistaram \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. O Lord, if you are pleased with me, if you wish to grant me a boon, then, O Lord of Devas, tell me now the details of all holy spots.

## \|\| 1.3.89 \|\|

*pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni pāpaghnāni śivāni ca \|*  
*tāni deveśa kārtsnyena yathāvadvaktumarhasi \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Whatsoever holy spots, conducive to welfare and destructive of sins, are spread all over the earth, O Lord of Devas, it behoves you to narrate them entirely.

## \|\| 1.3.90 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi tīrthamāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*sarvapāpaharaṃ nṛṇāṃ puṇyaṃ devarṣisatkṛtam \|\| 90 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

90\. O goddess, listen, I shall expound to you the greatness of the Tīrthas. It is excellent and destructive of all sins of men. It is meritorious and honoured by the celestial sages.

## \|\| 1.3.91 \|\|

*tīrthānāṃ darśanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ snānaṃ caiva sureśvari \|*  
*śravaṇaṃ ca praśaṃsaṃti sadaiva ṛṣisattamāḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. O goddess of Suras, visit to a Tīrthas is excellent. So also is ablution performed therein. Excellent sages always praise the listening to (the glory) thereof.

## \|\| 1.3.92 \|\|

*pṛthivyāṃ naimiṣaṃ tīrthamaṃtarikṣe ca puṣkaram \|*  
*kedāraṃ ca prayāgaṃ ca vipāśā cormilā tathā \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. The following are the Tīrthas on the earth: Naimiṣa, Puṣkara in the sky, Kedāra, Prayāga, Vipāśā (Bias) and Urmilā (all on the earth),

## \|\| 1.3.93 \|\|

*karṇaveṇā mahādevī caṃdrabhāgā sarasvatī \|*  
*gaṃgāsāgarasaṃbhedastathā vārāṇasī śubhā \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Karṇaveṇā (probably Kṛṣṇāveṇī), Mahādevī, Candrabhāgā (Chinab), Sarasvatī, the confluence of Gaṅgā and the ocean, and the splendid Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 1.3.94 \|\|

*arghatīrthaṃ samākhyātaṃ gaṃgādvāraṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*himasthānaṃ mahātīrthaṃ tathā māyāpurī śubhā \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Ardha Tīrtha (Semi-Tīrtha), Gaṅgā Dvāra, the Mahā Tīrtha, is a place of (plenty of) snow and the auspicious Māyāpurī (Hardwar, U. P.).

## \|\| 1.3.95 \|\|

*śatabhadrā mahābhāgā sindhuścaiva mahā nadī \|*  
*airāvatī ca kapilā śoṇaścaiva mahānadaḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Śatabhadrā is highly blessed and esteemed. Sindhu is a great river. So also is Airāvatī (Rāvī—De), Kapilā (Narmadā, near its source) and the great Nada i.e. Śoṇa.

## \|\| 1.3.96 \|\|

*payodhiḥ kauśikī tadvattathā godāvarī śubhā \|*  
*devakhātaṃ gayā caiva tathā dvārāvatī śubhā \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Kauśikī (Kosī) is a vast storehouse of waters. Similarly Godāvarī is splendid. Devakhāta, Gayā and Dvārāvatī (Dwarka, Gujarat) are splendid.

## \|\| 1.3.97 \|\|

*prabhāsaṃ ca mahātīrthaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Prabhāsa is a great Tīrtha that is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.3.98 \|\|

*evamādīni tīrthāni yāni saṃti mahītale \|*  
*tāni dṛṣṭvā tu deveśi punarjanma na vindate \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. If a person visits these and similar other Tīrthas that abound on the surface of the earth, O goddess of Devas, he is never reborn.

## \|\| 1.3.99 \|\|

*tisraḥ koṭyo'rdhakoṭī ca tīrthānāmiha bhūtale \|*  
*saṃjātāni pavitrāṇi sarvapāpaharāṇi ca \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. There are three and a half crores of Tīrthas on the earth. They are holy and destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.3.100 \|\|

*gaṃtavyāni mahādevi svadharmasya vivṛddhaye \|*  
*aśakyāni śivānyevaṃ gaṃtuṃ caiva sureśvari \|*  
*manasā tāni sarvāṇi gaṃtavyāni samāhitaiḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. O great goddess, they should be visited for the purpose of augmenting one’s own piety. O goddess of Suras, if it is difficult to go to all these auspicious (Tīrthas), they can all be resorted to mentally by (devotees) with concentration and purity of mind.

## \|\| 1.3.101 \|\|

*\|devyuvāca \|*  
*bhagavanprāṇinaḥ sarve sarvopadravasaṃkulāḥ \|*  
*alpāyuṣaḥ sadā baddhā vyāmohairmaṃdirodbhavaiḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

The Devī said:

101\. O holy Lord, all the living beings are overwhelmed by all sorts of harassments and tortures. Their span of life is short and they are fettered down. They are faced with delusions regarding holy shrines.

## \|\| 1.3.102 \|\|

*tretāyāṃ dvāpare caiva kiṃ nu vai dāruṇe kalau \|*  
*tasmātteṣāṃ hitārthāya tattīrthaṃ tvaṃ prakīrtaya \|*  
*yena dṛṣṭena sarveṣāṃ tīrthānāṃ labhyate phalam \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. If this is the case even in Tretā as well as Dvāpara.then it is still more so in the terrible age of Kali. Hence for the sake of their welfare, do glorify that (one) Tīrtha which accords, when visited, the benefit of all the Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.3.103 \|\|

*evamuktastu pārvatyā prahasya parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*uvāca parayā prītyā vācā madhurayā prabhuḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. On being told thus by Pārvatī, Lord Parameśvara laughed joyously and spoke these sweet words:

## \|\| 1.3.104 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tvameva hi carāḥ prāṇāḥ sarvasya jagatoraṇiḥ \|*  
*tvayā virahito devi muhūrtamapi notsahe \|\| 104 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

104\. You alone are the moving vital airs of the entire universe. You are the source of origin of the universe even as the Araṇi (attrition stick) is that of the fire. O goddess, I cannot bear to be separated from you even for a Muhūrta (short while).

## \|\| 1.3.105 \|\|

*śivasya ca tathā śakteraṃtaraṃ nāsti pārvati \|*  
*na tadasti mahādevi yanna jānāsi śobhane \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. O Pārvatī, there is no difference between Śiva and Śakti. O splendid great goddess, there is nothing that you do not know.

## \|\| 1.3.106 \|\|

*tvayā vinā'haṃ na kvāsmi na tvaṃ devi mayā vinā \|*  
*caṃdracaṃdrikayoryadvadagneruṣṇatvameva hi \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. I am nowhere without you, O goddess and you without me. Our relation is like that of the Moon and moonlight or of fire and warmth.

## \|\| 1.3.107 \|\|

*tava devi mamāpīha nāsti caivāṃtaraṃ priye \|*  
*sarvaṃ caiva sureśāni yathāvatkathayāmyaham \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. O beloved one, there is no difference between you and me. O goddess of Suras, I shall state everything factually as it is (exists).

## \|\| 1.3.108 \|\|

*rahasyānāṃ rahasyaṃ tu gopanīyaṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*nāstikāya na dātavyaṃ na ca pāparatāya ca \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. This is the secret of secrets and it should be guarded carefully. It should not be imparted to an atheist nor to one engrossed in sinful activities.

## \|\| 1.3.109 \|\|

*dātavyaṃ bhakti yuktāya svaśiṣyāya sutāya vā \|*  
*pūrvameva mayā khyātaṃ sārātsārataraṃ priye \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. It should be imparted to one endowed with devotion, one’s own disciple or son. O my beloved, the essence of all essences has already been narrated by me.

## \|\| 1.3.110 \|\|

*tīrthopaniṣadaḥ khyātā liṃgopaniṣadastathā \|*  
*yogopaniṣado devi pūrvaṃ vai kathitāstava \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. The well-known Tīrthopaniṣads as well as the Liṅgopaniṣads and the Yogopaniṣads have been narrated to you before.

## \|\| 1.3.111 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*leśenāpi na siddhyaṃti kāṃkṣamāṇāḥ paraṃ padam \|*  
*yonīrbhramaṃto dṛśyaṃte narā nāstikavṛttayaḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:

111\. Those who desire the greatest region do not attain it despite all pain and strain. Men of atheistic predilections are seen roaming through Yonis (births after births in different wombs).

## \|\| 1.3.112 \|\|

*tīrthavratāni sevante pratyayo naiva jāyate \|*  
*mohitaṃ tu jagatpūrvaṃ mithyājñānena śaṃkara \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. They resort to Tīrthas and observe Vratas but they do not have faith and belief. O Śaṅkara, the entire universe has already been deluded through false knowledge.

## \|\| 1.3.113 \|\|

*kiṃ te phalaṃ suraśreṣṭha jagadvyāmohane kṛte \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. What do you gain, O most excellent one among Suras, by creating this universal delusion?

## \|\| 1.3.114 \|\|

*sārātsārataraṃ nātha tava prāṇapriyaṃ hi yat \|*  
*tanme kathaya deveśa priyāhaṃ yadi te prabho \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. O Lord of Devas, if I be your beloved, do mention to me the essence of the essential thing, that which is pleasing to your own vital airs.

## \|\| 1.3.115 \|\|

*ityuktaḥ sa tayā devyā śrīkaṃṭhaḥ suranāyakaḥ \|*  
*prahasyovāca bhagavāngaṃbhīrārthamidaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. On being requested thus by the goddess Śrīkaṇṭha, the leader of Suras, laughed loudly and spoke these words of profound import:

## \|\| 1.3.116 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇuṣvāvahitā bhūtvā pṛṣṭo'haṃ yastvayā'dhunā \|*  
*niṣphalaṃ tatpravakṣyāmi vastutattvaṃ yathāsthitam \|\| 116 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

116\. Listen attentively now to what I have been asked in regard to its fruitlessness. I shall mention everything as it is factually.

## \|\| 1.3.117 \|\|

*pūrvamuktāni tīrthāni yāni te surasuṃdari \|*  
*tisraḥ koṭyo'rddhakoṭī ca brahmāṃḍe sacarācare \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. O beautiful lady among Suras, earlier three and a half crores of Tīrthas in the Cosmic Egg consisting of mobile and immobile beings, have been described to you.

## \|\| 1.3.118 \|\|

*teṣāṃ ca gopitaṃ tīrthaṃ prabhāsaṃ caiva suvrate \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. The well-guarded Prabhāsa Tīrtha is among them, O lady of excellent holy vows.

## \|\| 1.3.119 \|\|

*evamuktaṃ mahādevi prabhāsaṃ kṣetramuttamam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā saṃskārarahitāḥ kalau pāpena mohitāḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. O great goddess, the excellent holy spot of Prabhāsa has been thus extolled, but those who are deluded by sins and those who are devoid of religious purificators, rites and cultural refinement in Kali Age (do not benefit) even if they visit this Kṣetra.

## \|\| 1.3.120 \|\|

*rājasāstāmasāścaiva pāpopahatacetasaḥ \|*  
*paradāraparadravyaparahiṃsāratā narāḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*
