120\. They are of Rājasa and Tāmasa traits. Their minds have been assailed by sins.These men are engrossed in (acquiring) wealth and womenfolk of others. They also indulge in injuring others.

## \|\| 1.3.121 \|\|

*udvegaṃ ca paraṃ yāṃti pratapyaṃti yatastataḥ \|*  
*ātmasaṃbhāvitā mūḍhā mithyājñānena mohitāḥ \|*  
*varṇāśramaviruddhaṃ tu tīrthe ku्rvanti ye'dhamāḥ \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. They undergo great excitement and worry. They become distressed everywhere. They are deluded but they think very high of themselves. They are fascinated with improper and false knowledge. They are base men who do not hesitate to perform rites in the Tīrthas even when they are contrary to the injunctions regarding the Varṇas and the Āśramas.

## \|\| 1.3.122 \|\|

*tīrthayātrāṃ prakurvaṃti daṃbhena kapaṭena ca \|*  
*tīrthe mṛtā na sidhyaṃti te narā varavarṇini \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. They undertake pilgrimage with hypocrisy and deceit. O lady of excellent complexion, they do not get any benefit even if they die in a holy Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.3.123 \|\|

*etadarthaṃ mayā devi tīrthāni vividhāni ca \|*  
*liṃgāni caiva suśroṇi gopitāni prayatnataḥ \|*  
*na siddhidāni deveśi kalau kalmaṣakāriṇām \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. It is for this purpose, O goddess of excellent hips, that these diverse Tīrthas and Liṅgas have been concealed and guarded by me. O goddess of Devas, they do not bestow Siddhis in Kali Age on those who perform sinful activities.

## \|\| 1.3.124-125 \|\|

*ye narāstu jitakrodhā jitalobhā jiteṃdriyāḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāścādambhamatsarāḥ \|\| 124 \|\|*

*madbhāvabhāvitā devi tīrthaṃ sevaṃti suvratāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ caiva hitārthāya kathayāmi yaśaśvini \|\| 125 \|\|*

124-125. O goddess of great renown, I shall now mention for the benefit of those good men among Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas and Śūdras who have conquered the sense-organs, anger and covetousness, who are devoid of hypocrisy and jealousy and who are sanctified by devotion to me and who resort to the Tīrtha and perform holy rites.

## \|\| 1.3.126 \|\|

*prabhāsamiti vikhyātaṃ kṣetraṃ trailokyavaṃditam \|*  
*tatkṣetraṃ naiva jānaṃti mama māyāvimohitāḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. The holy spot well-known as Prabhāsa is honoured by all the three worlds. Those who are deluded by my Māyā do not know that holy spot (its real nature).

## \|\| 1.3.127 \|\|

*parohaṃ tvekacittaiśca bahujanmabhirarcitaḥ \|*  
*te vidaṃti paraṃ kṣetraṃ prabhāsaṃ pāpanāśanam \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. If I, the great Being, have been adored with single-minded devotion in the course of many births, those people know that great Prabhāsa Kṣetra that is destructive of sins.

## \|\| 1.3.128 \|\|

*madbhāvabhāvitā devi mama vrataniṣeviṇaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ prabhāsikaṃ kṣetraṃ viditaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. There is no doubt, O goddess, that the holy place of Prabhāsa has been fully comprehended by those who are sanctified through devotion to me and who resort to holy vows and rites pertaining to me.

## \|\| 1.3.129 \|\|

*yamaiśca niyamairyuktā ahaṃkāravivarjjitāḥ \|*  
*teṣāmarthe vadiṣyāmi tava praśnaṃ sudurllabham \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇvindradevānāṃ purāṇaṃ kathitaṃ mayā \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. Those who observe Yamas and Niyamas, those who are devoid of egotism (are to be benefitted). For the sake of those people, I shall clarify the question to which answer is very difficult to get. This ancient truth has been already revealed to Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra and the Devas by me.

## \|\| 1.3.130-131 \|\|

*so'haṃ devi vadiṣyāmi karṇaṃ dehi varānane \|*  
*pṛthivyāmapi sarveṣāṃ tīrthānāṃ surasuṃdari \|\| 130 \|\|*

*ekaṃ me vallabhaṃ tatra prabhāsaṃ kṣetramuttamam \|*  
*tasmiṃścaiva mahākṣetre tīrthaiḥ somena pūjitaḥ \|*  
*varāṃstasmai pradāyātha sadaikāṃte sthito hyaham \|\| 131 \|\|*

130-131. Now I shall tell you, O lady of excellent countenance. Pay heed to it. O beautiful lady among Suras, among all the Tīrthas all over the earth the excellent Prabhāsa kṣetra is the dearest one to me. In that holy spot, I was worshipped by Soma (Moon). After granting him all the boons, I stayed here always in seclusion.

## \|\| 1.3.132 \|\|

*tena guhyaṃ kṛtaṃ sthānaṃ tava devi prakāśitam \|*  
*tatra me yogayuktasya divyaṃ liṃgaṃ babhūva ha \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. Therefore, the holy place that was kept secret, O goddess, has been revealed to you. There from me engrossed in Yoga, the divine Liṅga emerged.

## \|\| 1.3.133 \|\|

*divyatejassamā yuktaṃ vahnimekhalamaṃḍitam \|*  
*lakṣamātrasthitaṃ śāṃtaṃ durnirīkṣyaṃ tu mānavaiḥ \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. It has divine refulgence. It is adorned by a fiery ring (around it). It is quiescent and has been there as mere focus point of concentration. It is very difficult to be perceived by men.

## \|\| 1.3.134 \|\|

*icchājñānakriyākhyāśca tisro vai śaktayaśca yāḥ \|*  
*tasmālliṃgātsamutpannā jagatkartṛtvahetave \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. For the purpose of creation of the universe the three Śaktis viz. Icchā (Volition), Jñāna (Knowledge) and Kriyā (Activity) have originated from that Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.3.135 \|\|

*tasmiṃlliṃge layaṃ yāti jagadetaccarācaram \|*  
*punastenaiva saṃbhūtaṃ dṛśyate sacarācaram \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. This universe consisting of mobile and immobile beings gets dissolved in that Liṅga. Further the whole thing appears originating from it.

## \|\| 1.3.136 \|\|

*guhyaṃ caiva tu saṃbhūtaṃ na kaścidveda tatparam \|*  
*janmābhyāsena talliṃgaṃ jñāyate bhuvi mānavaiḥ \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. It has originated secretly. No one knows that great thing. By practice throughout the different births, it becomes known to men on the earth.

## \|\| 1.3.137 \|\|

*kṣetraṃ prabhāsikaṃ proktaṃ kṣetrajño'haṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tatra someśanāmāhamasminkṣetraṃ varānane \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. The holy place is called Prābhāsika. There is no doubt about this that I am the Kṣetrajña (the Soul, Knower thereof). In this holy spot I am named Someśa, O lady of excellent countenance.

## \|\| 1.3.138 \|\|

*mamāṃśasaṃbhavā ye ca asminkṣetre samudbhavāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ tu viditaṃ liṃgaṃ pūrvakalpe tu bhairavam \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. Those who are born in this holy place are born from the parts of mine. This Liṅga was known to them even in the earlier Kalpa as Bhairava (Liṅga).

## \|\| 1.3.139 \|\|

*anyairapi yugairdevi idaṃ liṃgaṃ sudurlabham \|*  
*ghore kaliyuge pāpe viśeṣeṇa ca durlabham \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. O goddess, this Liṅga is rarely accessible even in the other Yugas. In the sinful, terrible Kali Yuga, it is all the moreso.

## \|\| 1.3.140 \|\|

*anyannidarśanaṃ tatra tatpravakṣyāmi pārvati \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. O Pārvatī, I shall give another example in that connection.

## \|\| 1.3.141 \|\|

*kalau yuge mahāghore hetuvādaratā narāḥ \|*  
*vadiṣyaṃti mahāpāpāḥ sarve pākhaṇḍasaṃsthitāḥ \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. In the excessively terrible Kali Yuga, men are prone to indulge in arguments and disputation. Those great sinners abiding by heresy will all say thus:

## \|\| 1.3.142-143 \|\|

*mithyā caitatkṛtaṃ sarvaṃ mūrkhaiścāpi prakīrtitam \|*  
*kva kṣetraṃ kva prabhāvaśca kutra vai santi devatāḥ \|\| 142 \|\|*

*sarvaṃ cāpi tathālīkaṃ mūḍhaiścāpi prakīrtitam \|\| 143 \|\|*

142-143. “All these things have been done falsely. It is glorified by fools. Where is the holy spot? What is its power? Where are the deities? Everything is false and glorified by deluded ones.”

## \|\| 1.3.144 \|\|

*evaṃ mūrkhā vadiṣyaṃti prahasiṣyanti cāpare \|*  
*nārakā nāstikā lokāḥ pāpopahatacetasaḥ \|*  
*siddhiṃ naiva prayāsyaṃti saṃprāpte tu kalau yuge \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. Thus the foolish ones will say. Others will laugh. The non-believers, the people destined to fall into hell, get their minds overwhelmed by sins. At the advent of Kali Age, they will never gain Siddhi.

## \|\| 1.3.145 \|\|

*tīrthe caiva mṛtā ye tu śivanindāparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*tiryagyoniprasūtāśca dṛśyante sarvayoniṣu \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. Those who habitually censure Śiva and die in the Tīrtha, appear as persons born in all the lower strata of beings.

## \|\| 1.3.146 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇāddevi tīrthe caiva suduḥkhitāḥ \|*  
*dṛśyante yugamāhātmyātsatyaśaucavivarjitāḥ \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. It is on account of this, O goddess, that there are persons in great misery. Due to the great evil power of the Yuga, they are seen as persons devoid of truthfulness and purity.

## \|\| 1.3.147 \|\|

*idaṃ hi kāraṇaṃ proktaṃ kṣetrāṇāṃ caiva gopane \|*  
*etatte kathitaṃ sarvaṃ siddhiryena sudurllabhā \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. This is the reason why holy spots are kept guarded and concealed. Thus everything has been mentioned to you, as to how Siddhi has become very difficult to achieve.

## \|\| 1.3.148 \|\|

*yugeyuge tu tīrthāni kīrtitāni sureśvari \|*  
*teṣāṃ me vallabhaṃ devi prabhāsaṃ kṣetrameva ca \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. O goddess of Suras, Tīrthas are glorified in every age. Among them, O goddess, Prabhāsa Kṣetra alone is very dear to me.

## \|\| 1.3.149 \|\|

*ityetatkathitaṃ devi rahasyaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*kṣetrabījaṃ mahādevi kimanyatparipṛcchasi \|\| 149 \|\|*

149\. Thus, O fair lady, the sin-destroying secret has been divulged—the very seed in the form of the holy spot. O great goddess, what else do you wish to ask?

## \|\| 1.3.150 \|\|

*idaṃ mahāpātakanāśanaṃ ye śroṣyaṃti vai kṣetramahāprabhāvam \|*  
*te cāpi yāsyanti mama prabhāvāttriviṣṭapaṃ puṇyajanādhivāsam \|\| 150 \|\|*

150\. Those who listen to the great power of holy spots, the narration that destroys great sins, will attain, by my power, the heavenly region, the abode of meritorious persons.

## Chapter 4 - The Extent of Prabhāsa Kṣetra

## \|\| 1.4.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ munīndrāḥ kathite prabhāve śaṃkareṇa tu \|*  
*punaḥ papraccha sā devī kṛtāṃjalipuṭā satī \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1\. When the efficaciousness was narrated by Śaṅkara thus, O leading sages, goddess Satī kept her palms joined together in reverence and asked again:

## \|\| 1.4.2-3 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*devadeva jagannātha kṣetratīrthamaya prabho \|*  
*prabhāsakṣetramāhātmyaṃ vistarātkathayasva me \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kathaṃ tuṣyasi martyānāṃ kṣetre tatra vicetasām \|*  
*japtaṃ dattaṃ hutaṃ yaṣṭaṃ tapastaptaṃ kṛtaṃ ca yat \|*  
*prabhāse tu mahākṣetre kasmāttatrākṣayaṃ bhavet \|\| 3 \|\|*

The Devī said:

2-3. O Lord of Devas, O Lord of the worlds, O Lord identical with the sacred places and holy rivers, do narrate in detail to me the greatness of Prabhāsa Kṣetra. How will you get pleased with men of confounded and wicked nature in the holy spot? Wherefore do Japa, Dana, Homa, Yajña and Tapas performed there become rites of everlasting benefit?

## \|\| 1.4.4 \|\|

*jātyaṃtarasahasreṣu yatpāpaṃ pūrvasaṃcitam \|*  
*tatkathaṃ kṣayamāpnoti tanmamācakṣva śaṃkara \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O Śaṅkara, do tell me how the sin accumulated earlier in the course of thousands of births gets dissolved.

## \|\| 1.4.5 \|\|

*yadi prabhāsaṃ sarveṣāṃ tīrthānāṃ pravaraṃ matam \|*  
*kimanyairbahubhistatra karttavyaṃ tīrthavistaraiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. If Prabhāsa is considered the most excellent of all the Tīrthas, of what avail are the numerous other Tīrthas?

## \|\| 1.4.6 \|\|

*ekaṃ yadi bhavettīrthaṃ mano niḥsaṃśayaṃ bhavet \|*  
*bahutve sati tīrthānāṃ mano vicalate nṛṇām \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. If the Tīrtha is confined to one holy spot the mind will be free from doubts. When there is the multiplicity of Tīrthas the minds of men begin to waver.

## \|\| 1.4.7 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaṃ parityajya tīrthajālaṃ savistaram \|*  
*prabhāsasyaiva māhātmyaṃ kathayasva sureśvara \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Hence, O Lord of Suras, leave aside the entire mess of Tīrthas, and their details, and mention the greatness of Prabhāsa alone.

## \|\| 1.4.8 \|\|

*kṣetrapramāṇaṃ sīmāṃ ca kṣetrasāraṃ hi yatprabho \|*  
*vaktumarhasi tatsarvaṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O Lord, it behoves you to narrate everything such as the extent of the holy spot, its boundary and its essential features etc. My curiousity is intense.

## \|\| 1.4.9 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi kṣetrāṇāṃ kṣetramuttamam \|*  
*sarvakṣetreṣu yatkṣetraṃ prabhāsaṃ tu priyaṃ mama \|\| 9 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

9\. O goddess, listen. I shall describe the most excellent of all Kṣetras. The Prabhāsa Kṣetra is the dearest Kṣetra unto me.

## \|\| 1.4.10 \|\|

*prabhāse tu parā siddhiḥ prabhāse tu parā gatiḥ \|*  
*yatra saṃnihito nityamahaṃ bhadre nirantaram \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The greatest Siddhi is achieved at Prabhāsa. One attains the greatest goal at Prabhāsa. O fair lady, it is the place where I am permanently stationed.

## \|\| 1.4.11 \|\|

*tasya pramāṇaṃ vakṣyāmi sarvasīmāsamanvitam \|*  
*kṣetraṃ tu trividha proktaṃ tatte vakṣyāmyanukramāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. I shall mention its extent along with all the boundaries. The holy spot comprises three distinct sections which I shall mention in due order.

## \|\| 1.4.12 \|\|

*kṣetraṃ pīṭhaṃ garbhagṛhaṃ prabhāsasya prakīrtyate \|*  
*yathākramaṃ phalaṃ tasya koṭikoṭiguṇaṃ smṛtam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. They are the Kṣetra, the Pīṭha and the Garbhagṛha (sanctum sanctorum) of Prabhāsa which I mention. The efficacy of each of the three is crore times more than the preceding one.

## \|\| 1.4.13 \|\|

*kṣetraṃ tu prathamaṃ proktaṃ tacca dvādaśayojanam \|*  
*pañcayojanamānena kṣetrapīṭhaṃ prakīrtitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The Kṣetra is mentioned at the outset. It extends to twelve Yojanas (1 Yojana =12 Kms.). It is well-known. The Pīṭha of the Kṣetra measures five Yojanas.

## \|\| 1.4.14 \|\|

*garbhagṛhaṃ ca gavyūtiḥ karṇikā sā mama priyā \|*  
*kṣetrasīmā pravakṣyāmi śṛṇu devi yathākramam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The Garbhagṛha is in the form of a pericarp very dear to me. It extends to a Gavyūti (six kms.). I shall tell you about the frontiers of the Kṣetra in due order. O goddess, listen.

## \|\| 1.4.15 \|\|

*āyāmavyāsataścaiva ādimadhyāntasaṃsthitam \|*  
*pūrve taptodaka svāmī paścime mādhavaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In length and breadth the frontiers are fixed at the beginning, middle and end. Taptodakasvāmī is to the east and Mādhava is to the west.

## \|\| 1.4.16 \|\|

*dakṣiṇe sāgarastadvadbhadrā nadyuttare matā \|*  
*evaṃ sīmāsamāyuktaṃ kṣetraṃ dvādaśayojanam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The ocean is to the south and the river Bhadrā is on the north. The Kṣetra with these boundaries extends to twelve Yojanas.

## \|\| 1.4.17 \|\|

*etatprābhāsikaṃ kṣetraṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|*  
*tanmadhye pīṭhikā proktā pañcayojanavistṛtā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. This is the Prābhāsika Kṣetra destructive of all sins. The Pīṭhikā is mentioned as stationed in the middle and it extends to five Yojanas.

## \|\| 1.4.18-19 \|\|

*nyaṃkumanyapareṇaiva vajriṇyāḥ pūrvatastathā \|*  
*māheśvaryā dakṣiṇataḥ samudrottaratastathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*āyāmavyāsataścaiva pañcayojanavistaram \|*  
*pīṭhametatsamākhyātamatho garbhagṛhaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. The Pīṭha is mentioned as extending to five Yojanas lengthwise and breadthwise. It is beyond Nyaṅkumanya and to the east of Vajriṇī. It is to the south of Māheśvarī and to the north of the ocean. Now listen to the description of the Garbhagṛha.

## \|\| 1.4.20 \|\|

*dakṣiṇottarato yāvatsamudrā tkauraveśvarī \|*  
*pūrvapaścimato yāvadgomukhāccāśvamedhikam \|*  
*etadgarbhagṛhaṃ proktaṃ kailāsānmama vallabham \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Kauraveśvarī extends from south to north upto the ocean. Āśvamedhika extends from east to west upto Gomukha. This is what is called Garbhagṛha and it is dearer to the than Kailāsa.

## \|\| 1.4.21-22 \|\|

*atrāntare tu deveśi yāni tīrthāni bhūtale \|*  
*vāpīkūpataḍāgāni devatāyatanāni ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

*sarāṃsi saritaścaiva palvalāni hradāstathā \|*  
*tāni medhyāni sarvāṇi sarvapāpaharāṇi ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Whatever Tīrtha is in between these two, O goddess of Devas, on the earth all the tanks, wells and lakes and all the shrines of the deities, the lakes and the rivers, the puddles and the whirlpools—all these are holy. All of them are destructive of all the sins.

## \|\| 1.4.23 \|\|

*yatra tatra naraḥ snātvā svargaloke mahīyate \|*  
*kṣetrasya prathamo bhāgo medhyo māheśvaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. By taking his holy bath anywhere (in the area) a man is honoured in the heavenly world.

The first part of the Kṣetra is in the highly sacred Māheśvara (pertaining to Śiva).

## \|\| 1.4.24 \|\|

*dvitīyo vaiṣṇavo bhāgo brahmabhāgastṛtīyakaḥ \|*  
*tīrthānāṃ koṭirekā tu brāhme bhāge vyavasthitā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The second part pertains to Viṣṇu and the third one is Brahmā’s part. A crore Tīrthas are well-established in the part pertaining to Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.4.25 \|\|

*vaiṣṇave koṭirekā tu tīrthānāṃ varavarṇini \|*  
*sārddhakoṭistu saṃproktā rudrabhāge ca madhyataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O lady of excellent complexion, there are a crore Tīrthas in the part of Viṣṇu. It is said that there are one and a half crores in the middle part pertaining to Rudra.

## \|\| 1.4.26 \|\|

*evaṃ devi samākhyātaṃ tatkṣetraṃ hi tridaivatam \|*  
*guhyādguhyataraṃ kṣetraṃ mama priyataraṃ śubhe \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Thus, O goddess, that holy spot has been described as having three divinities. O splendid lady, this holy spot is the greatest secret of all secrets and very dear to me.

## \|\| 1.4.27 \|\|

*tisraḥ koṭyo'rddhakoṭiśca kṣetre proktā vibhāgataḥ \|*  
*yātrā tu trividhā jñeyā tāṃ śṛṇuṣva varānane \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thus the assignment of the regions for the three and a half crores of Kṣetras (Tīrthas) has been explained.

The Yātrā (religious procession) should be understood as threefold. Listen to it, O lady of excellent countenance.

## \|\| 1.4.28 \|\|

*raudrī tu prathamā yātrā vaiṣṇavī ca dvitīyikā \|*  
*brāhmī tṛtīyā saṃkhyātā sarvapātakanāśinī \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The first Yātrā is Raudrī (pertaining to Rudra). The second one is Vaiṣṇavī (concerning Viṣṇu). The third is reckoned as Brāhmī. It is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.4.29 \|\|

*brāhme vibhāge saṃproktā icchāśaktirvarānane \|*  
*kriyā ca vaiṣṇave bhāge dvitīye tu prakīrtitā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. It is mentioned, O lady of excellent countenance, that the Icchāśakti (power of volition) is in the part pertaining to Brahmā. The Kriyāśakti (power of action) is glorified in the second part pertaining to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 1.4.30-33 \|\|

*raudre bhāge tṛtīye tu jñānaśaktirvarānane \|*  
*yadi pāpo yadi śaṭho yadi naiṣkṛtiko naraḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*nirmuktaḥ sarvapāpebhyo madhyabhāge vasettu yaḥ \|*  
*himavaṃtaṃ parityajya parvataṃ gaṃdhamādanam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*kailāsaṃ niṣadhaṃ caiva merupṛṣṭhaṃ mahādyutim \|*  
*ramyaṃ triśikharaṃ caiva mānasaṃ ca mahāgirim \|\| 32 \|\|*

*devodyānāni ramyāṇi naṃdanaṃ vanameva ca \|*  
*svargasthānāni ramyāṇi tīrthānyāyatanāni ca \|*  
*tāni sarvāṇi saṃtyajya prabhāse tu ratirmama \|\| 33 \|\|*

30-31a. O lady of excellent countenance, the Jñānaśakti (the power of cognition) is in the third part pertaining to Rudra.

Even a sinful man, a rogue or a person of the worst character shall become rid of all sins if he stays in the middle part.

31b-33. My great interest centres round Prabhāsa after leaving aside Himavān, mountain Gandhamādana, Kailāsa, Niṣadha, the lustrous Merupṛṣṭha, the charming Triśikhara (three-peaked one), the great mountain Mānasa, the beautiful parks of the Devas, the Nandana garden, the beautiful regions of heaven and all the Tīrthas and shrines.

## \|\| 1.4.34 \|\|

*yastatra vasate devi saṃyatātmā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*trikālamapi bhuṃjāno vāyubhakṣasamo bhavet \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O goddess, if a person stays there with restrained soul and concentration of mind, he shall be considered on a par with the one living with air alone as diet, even if he takes food thrice a day.

## \|\| 1.4.35 \|\|

*vighnairāloḍyamāno'pi yaḥ prabhāsaṃ na muṃcati \|*  
*sa muṃcati jarāṃ mṛtyuṃ janmacakramaśāśvatam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Despite being shaken by obstacles, if a man does not leave Prabhāsa, he actually frees himself from old age and death and the transient cycle of births and deaths.

## \|\| 1.4.36 \|\|

*janmāṃtaraśatairdevi yogo vā yadi labhyate \|*  
*mokṣasya ca sahasreṇa janmanāṃ labhyate na ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O goddess, Yogic power may be obtained perhaps in the course of hundreds of births. But salvation cannot be obtained even after a thousand births.

## \|\| 1.4.37 \|\|

*prabhāse tu mahādevi ye sthitā kṛtaniścayāḥ \|*  
*ekena janmanā teṣāṃ mokṣo naivātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. But, O great goddess, those who continue to stay in Prabhāsa with determination shall undoubtedly attain liberation in the course of a single birth.

## \|\| 1.4.38-39 \|\|

*prabhāse tu sthitā ye vai brāhmaṇāḥ saṃśitavratāḥ \|*  
*mṛtyuṃjayena saṃyuktaṃ japaṃti śatarudriyam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*kālāgnirudrasāṃnidhye dakṣiṇāṃ diśamāśritāḥ \|*  
*jñānaṃ cotpadyate tatra ṣaṇmāsābhyaṃtareṇa tu \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. If the Brāhmaṇas of praise-worthy holy vows permanently residing in Prabhāsa perform the Japa of Śatarudriya together with Mṛtyuñjaya Mantra, in the very presence of Kālāgnirudra and resort to the southern quarter, they will get perfect knowledge within six months.

## \|\| 1.4.40 \|\|

*śivastu procyate vedo nāmaparyāyavācakaiḥ \|*  
*tasya cātmasvarūpaṃ tu śatarudraṃ prakīrtitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Śiva is extolled in the Veda under his name as well as synonyms. But the form of his soul is glorified as Śatarudriya.

## \|\| 1.4.41 \|\|

*kalpeṣu vedāśca punaḥpunarāvartakāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*maṃtrāścaiva tathā devi muktvā tu śatarudriyam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O goddess, Smṛtis say that the Vedas and the Mantras are repeated in every Kalpa but Śatarudriya is not.

## \|\| 1.4.42 \|\|

*īḍyaṃ caiva tu maṃtreṇa māmeva hi yajaṃti ye \|*  
*prabhāsakṣetramāsādya te muktā nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Those who resort to Prabhāsa Kṣetra and worship by means of this Mantra me alone who am worthy of being adored, are liberated souls. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.4.43 \|\|

*samaṃtro'maṃtrako vāpi yastatra vasate naraḥ \|*  
*so'pi yāṃ gatimāpnoti yajñairdānairna sādhyate \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. A man may stay there with or without (the repetition of) the Mantras, but the goal that he attains cannot be attained through Yajñas and Dānas.

## \|\| 1.4.44 \|\|

*asmikṣetre svayaṃbhūśca sthitaḥ sākṣānmaheśvaraḥ \|*  
*rudrāṇāṃ koṭayaścaiva prabhāse saṃvyavasthitāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. In this holy spot, Maheśvara abides directly as the self-born deity. Crores of Rudras are established in Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.4.45 \|\|

*dhyāyamānāstathoṃkāraṃ sthitāḥ someśadakṣiṇe \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. They are stationed in the south of Someśa, meditating on Oṃkāra.

## \|\| 1.4.46 \|\|

*brahmāṃḍodaramadhye tu yāni tīrthāni suvrate \|*  
*someśvaraṃ gamiṣyaṃti vaiśākhasya caturdaśī \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O lady of excellent holy vows, all the Tīrthas, present in the Cosmic Egg will flow on to Someśvara on the fourteenth day of Vaiśākha.

## \|\| 1.4.47 \|\|

*manobuddhirahaṃkāraḥ kāmakrodhau tathā'pare \|*  
*ete rakṣaṃti satataṃ someśaṃ pāpanāśanam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The mind; intellect and ego, Kāma and Krodha as well as others always guard Someśa, the destroyer of sins.

## \|\| 1.4.48 \|\|

*na sā gatiḥ kurukṣetre gaṃgādvāre tripuṣkare \|*  
*yā gatirvihitā puṃsāṃ prabhāsakṣetravāsinām \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The goal that has been indicated as accessible in the case of men residing in the Prabhāsa Kṣetra is not (obtained) in Kurukṣetra, Gaṅgādvāra and Tripuṣkara.

## \|\| 1.4.49 \|\|

*tiryagyonigatāḥ sattvā ye prabhāse kṛtālayāḥ \|*  
*kālena nidhanaṃ prāptāstepi yāṃti parāṃ gatim \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Animals of lower species also that have their abodes in Prabhāsa and die in due course (there) attain the greatest goal.

## \|\| 1.4.50-53 \|\|

*tadguhyaṃ devadevasya tattīrthaṃ tattapovanam \|*  
*tatra brahmādayo devā nārāyaṇapurogamāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*yoginaśca tathā sāṃkhyā bhagavaṃtaṃ sanātanam \|*  
*upāsate prabhāsaṃ tu madbhaktā matparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*aṣṭau māsānvihāraḥ syādyatīnāṃ saṃyatātmanām \|*  
*eke ca caturo māsānaṣṭau vā niyataṃ vaset \|\| 52 \|\|*

*prabhāse tu praviṣṭānāṃ vihārastu na vidyate \|*  
*atra yogaśca mokṣaśca prāpyate durlabho naraiḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

50-53. That Tīrtha of the Lord of Devas is a penance grove that (should) be kept as a closely guarded secret.

There the Devas including Brahmā with Nārāyaṇa as the leader, Yogins and Sāṅkhyas and my devotees adore the eternal Lord having me as the greatest refuge at Prabhāsa.

Recluses of controlled souls have to go about for eight months. A few roam about for four months and stay behind for eight months. In the case of those who have entered Prabhāsa, they have no (need of) religious tour (Vihāra). Yoga and Mokṣa (salvation) which are rare are attained by men here.

## \|\| 1.4.54 \|\|

*tasmātprabhāsaṃ saṃtyajya nānyadgacchettapovanam \|*  
*prabhāsaṃ ye na sevaṃte mūḍhāste tamasā vṛtāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Hence one should not leave Prabhāsa and go to another penance grove. Those who do not resort to Prabhāsa are deluded and overcome by darkness of ignorance.

## \|\| 1.4.55-56 \|\|

*viṇmūtraretasāṃ madhye saṃbhavaṃti punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobho daṃbhaḥ staṃbho'tha matsaraḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*nidrā taṃdrā tathā'lasyaṃ paiśunyamiti te daśa \|*  
*ete rakṣaṃti satataṃ someśaṃ tīrthanāyakam \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. They are repeatedly born amidst faeces, urine and semen (i.e. in the wombs of mothers). These ten, viz. Kāma (love), Krodha (anger), Lobha (covetousness), Daṃbha (hypocrisy), Staṃbha (arrogance), Matsara (rivalry), Nidrā (sleep), Tandrā (lethargy), Ālasya (sloth) and Paiśunya (backbiting, depravity), always protect Someśa, the leader of the Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.4.57 \|\|

*na prabhāse mṛtaḥ kaścinnarakaṃ yāti kilbiṣī \|*  
*yāvajjīvaṃ naro yastu vasate kṛtaniścayaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. No sinner dying in Prabhāsa falls into a hell, if a man resolutely stays there as long as he lives (during his life time) (He attains this benefit).

## \|\| 1.4.58-59 \|\|

*agnihotraiśca saṃnyāsairāśramaiśca supālitaiḥ \|*  
*tridaṃḍairekadaṃḍaiśca śaivaiḥ pāśupatairapi \|\| 58 \|\|*

*etairanyaiśca yatibhiḥ prāpyate yatphalaṃ śubham \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ labhyate devi śrīsomeśvarayātrayā \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. The great benefit that is obtained by Śaivas, Pāśupatas (devotees of Śiva, Paśupati), by Sannyāsins known as Tridaṇḍins, Ekadaṇḍins and such other Sannyāsins, performers of Fire-worship (Agnihotrins), can be attained by means of performance of pilgrimage to Śrī Someśvara.

## \|\| 1.4.60 \|\|

*eko hyarcayate liṃgaṃ tapasyati tathāparaḥ \|*  
*tayormadhye tu śreṣṭho yaḥ someśaṃ ca prapūjayet \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. He who adores Someśa is on a par with the best among those who worship a Liṅga and who perform a penance.

## \|\| 1.4.61 \|\|

*yattadyoge ca sāṃkhye ca siddhāṃte paṃcarātrike \|*  
*anyaiśca śāstrairvijñeyaṃ prabhāse saṃvyavasthitam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Whatever is to be known in Yoga, Sāṅkhya, Pañcarātra Siddhānta and other scriptures has been well-established in Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.4.62 \|\|

*liṃge caiva sthitaṃ sarvaṃ jagadetaccarācaram \|*  
*tasmālliṃge sadā devaḥ pūjanīyaḥ prayatnataḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The entire universe consisting of the mobile and immobile beings is stationed in the Liṅga. Hence the Lord has always to be assiduously adored in the Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.4.63 \|\|

*mamaiva sā parā mūrtiḥ śrīsomeśākhyayā sthitā \|*  
*tena caiṣā tmanātmānamārādhanaparo hyaham \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. It is my supreme form that is stationed by the name Śrīsomeśa. Through it alone I am engrossed in propitiating my own Ātman (soul) through the Ātman.

## \|\| 1.4.64 \|\|

*anekajanmasāhasrairbhramamāṇastu janmabhiḥ \|*  
*kastāṃ prāpnoti vai muktiṃ vinā someśapūjanāt \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Who roaming through thousands of births is able to attain liberation without the adoration of Someśa?

## \|\| 1.4.65 \|\|

*yatkiñcidaśubhaṃ karma kṛtaṃ mānuṣabuddhinā \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ vilayaṃ yāti śrīsomeśvarapūjanāt \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Whatever inauspicious and evil act has been committed through the petty intellect of a human being shall get entirely destroyed through the adoration of Someśvara.

## \|\| 1.4.66 \|\|

*anekajanmakoṭībhirjaṃtubhiryatkṛtaṃ hyagham \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ nāśamāyāti śrīsomeśvarapūjanāt \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. The sin that has been committed by creatures in the course of crores of births, gets perished by the adoration of Śrī Someśvara.

## \|\| 1.4.67 \|\|

*tīrthāni yāni loke'sminsevyaṃte pāpamokṣibhiḥ \|*  
*tāni sarvāṇi śuddhyarthaṃ prabhāse saṃviśaṃti hi \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. All the Tīrthas resorted to by those who get rid of their sins, themselves enter Prabhāsa for their own purification.

## \|\| 1.4.68 \|\|

*yo'sau kālāgnirudrastu procyate vedavādibhiḥ \|*  
*so'yaṃ bhairavanāmnā tu prabhāse saṃvyavasthitaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. He who is called Kālāgnirudra by the expounders of the Vedas, has become established in Prabhāsa by the name Bhairava.

## \|\| 1.4.69 \|\|

*janānāṃ duṣkṛtaṃ sarvaṃ kṣetramadhye vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*bhairavaṃ rūpamāsthāya nāśayāmi sureśvari \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. O goddess of Suras, I have assumed the form of Bhairava, settled in the centre of the holy spot, and thus destroy the entire evil (acts) of the people.

## \|\| 1.4.70 \|\|

*jagatsarvaṃ caritvā tu sthito'haṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*tena bhairavanāmāhaṃ prabhāse saṃvyavasthitaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. I have wandered all over the world of mobile and immobile beings. Still I am steady and established. Hence I am well-established at Prabhāsa by the name Bhairava.

## \|\| 1.4.71 \|\|

*agninā yatra taptaṃ tu divyābdānāṃ caturyugam \|*  
*meghavāhanakalpe tu tatra liṃgaṃ babhūva ha \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. In the Meghavāhana Kalpa, Agni performed penance for a period of four Yugas according to the reckoning of divine years. At that place a Liṅga originated.

## \|\| 1.4.72 \|\|

*agnimīḍeti vedoktaprabhāvaḥ surasuṃdari \|*  
*kālāgnirudranāmā ca devaiḥ sarvairudāhṛtam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. O beautiful lady of Suras, he is one whose prowess has been extolled by the words of the Vedas, agnimīḍe etc. (I praise Agni—RV. L.l-17). The Liṅga was addressed by all the Devas by the name of Kālāgnirudra.

## \|\| 1.4.73 \|\|

*agnīśāneti deveśi nāmatritayamucyate \|*  
*kalpekalpe tu nāmāni kathituṃ naiva śakyate \|*  
*asaṃkhyatvācca kalpānāṃ brahmaṇā ca varānane \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. O goddess of Devas, Agni, Īśāna and Kālāgnirudra, these three names are oft-repeated. O lady of excellent countenance, since the Kalpas and Brahmās are innumerable, the names (of the Lord) in every Kalpa cannot be mentioned.

## \|\| 1.4.74 \|\|

*evaṃ caiva rahasyaṃ ca mahāgopyaṃ varānane \|*  
*snehānmahatyā bhaktyā ca mayā te parikīrtitam \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Thus it is a very great secret, O lady of excellent countenance. It has to be kept strictly concealed. But due to your great affection for me and the excess of devotion, it has been glorified by me to you.

## \|\| 1.4.75-79 \|\|

*ekatastu jagatsarvaṃ karma kāṃḍe pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*yajñadānatapohomaiḥ svādhyāyaiḥ pitṛtarpaṇaiḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*upavāsairvrataiḥ kṛtsnaiścāṃdrāyaṇaśataistathā \|*  
*ṣaḍrātraiśca trirātraiśca tīrthādigamanaiḥ paraiḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*āśramairvividhākārairyatibhirbrahmacāribhiḥ \|*  
*vānaprasthairgṛhasthaiśca vedakarmaparāyaṇaiḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*anyaiśca vividhākārairlokamārgasthitaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*na tatpadaṃ paraṃ devi śakyaṃ vīkṣayituṃ kvacit \|\| 78 \|\|*

*yāvanna cārcayeddevi someśaṃ liṃganāyakam \|*  
*līlayā vāpi tairdraṣṭuṃ tatpadaṃ durlabhaṃ param \|\| 79 \|\|*

75-79. The entire universe is established in Karmakāṇḍa (mass of rituals), which includes Yajña, Dāna, Tapas, Homa, Self-study of the Vedic texts, offering libations to ancestors, fasts, holy vows, the whole range of the hundreds of Cāndrāyaṇas, Ṣaḍrātras, Trirātras, visiting pilgrim centres etc. By means of these holy rites, people of the various stages of life such as celibate students, householder, Vānaprastha, etc. devoted to the holy rites laid down in the Vedas should ordinarily hope to earn merits. So also is the case of other people engaged in the auspicious rites of the layman. But, O goddess, unless one adores Someśa the leader of the Liṅgas, none can attain that great region. They cannot even espy it. It is extremely difficult to attain.

## \|\| 1.4.80-83 \|\|

*pūjito yairjagannāthaḥ someśaḥ kila bhairavaḥ \|*  
*tiryagyonigatā ye tu paśupakṣipipīlikāḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*antarjjalagatā ye tu kṛmikīṭapataṃgakāḥ \|*  
*sthāvarā jaṃgamāścānye manuṣyāḥ paśavaḥ striyaḥ \|\| 81 \|\| \|*  
*bālā vṛddhāstathā ṣaṇḍhāḥ śvānagarddabhavāyasāḥ \|*  
*caṃḍālāḥ puṣkasāḥ śūdrā mlecchā ye'nye viyonijāḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*antarjjalagatā ye tu kṛmikīṭapataṃgakāḥ \|*  
*sthāvarā jaṃgamāścānye manuṣyāḥ paśavaḥ striyaḥ \|\| 8 \|\| \|*  
*bālā vṛddhāstathā ṣaṇḍhāḥ śvānagarddabhavāyasāḥ \|*  
*caṃḍālāḥ puṣkasāḥ śūdrā mlecchā ye'nye viyonijāḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*mūrkhāstu paṇḍitāścāpi ye cānye kutsitā bhuvi \|*  
*te sarve muktimāyāṃti prabhāse ye mṛtāḥ śubhe \|\| 83 \|\|*

80-83. If the Lord of the universe, Bhairava Someśa is worshipped, all those attain salvation, those who die in Prabhāsa, O fair lady. They may be animals and birds of the lowest species, even ants, worms, insects, locusts etc. under water, the mobile and immobile beings, men, beasts, women, boys, girls, old men and women, eunuchs, dogs, donkeys, crows, Cāṇḍālas, Śūdras, Puṣkasas, other people of base births, fools, scholars, all despicable persons etc.

## \|\| 1.4.84 \|\|

*kālānalasya rudrasya kālarājena cāgninā \|*  
*dagdhāste jantavaḥ sarve prabhāse ye mṛtāḥ śubhe \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. O auspicious lady, all those creatures that die in Prabhāsa are burnt by the fire of Kālānala Rudra, by the Kālarāja fire.

## \|\| 1.4.85 \|\|

*durllabhaṃ tu mama kṣetraṃ prabhāsaṃ devi pāpinām \|*  
*na tatra labhate mṛtyuṃ pāpātmā lokavaṃdite \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. O goddess, my holy spot Prabhāsa is difficult of access to sinners. O lady honoured by people, a sinful soul does not get the opportunity to die there.

## \|\| 1.4.86 \|\|

*mayā dakṣiṇabhāge ca vighneśaḥ saṃpratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*uttare daṇḍapāṇistu kṣetrametacca rakṣati \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. In the southern side, Vighneśa has been installed by me. Daṇḍapāṇi protects this holy spot in the northern side.

## \|\| 1.4.87 \|\|

*tathānye gaṇapāḥ sarve madājñāvaśavartinaḥ \|*  
*kṣetraṃ rakṣaṃti deveśi teṣāṃ nāmāni me śṛṇu \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Other Lords of Gaṇas also, subject to my behest, guard this holy spot, O goddess of Devas. Listen to their names:

## \|\| 1.4.88-90 \|\|

*mahābalastu caṇḍīśo ghaṃṭākarṇastu gomukhaḥ \|*  
*vināyako mahānādaḥ kākavaktraḥ śubhekṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*ekākṣo dundubhiścaṃḍastālajaṃghastathaiva ca \|\| 88 \|\|*

*bhūmidaṃḍaśca caṃḍaśca śaṃkukarṇaśca vaidhṛtiḥ \|*  
*tālacaṇḍo mahātejā vikaṭāsyo hayānanaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

*hastivaktraḥ śvānavaktro biḍālavadanastathā \|*  
*siṃhavyāghramukhāścānye vīrabhadrādayastathā \|\| 90 \|\|*

88-90. Mahāhala, Caṇḍīśa, Ghaṇṭākarṇa, Gomukha, Vināyaka, Mahānāda, Kākavaktra, Śubhekṣaṇa, Ekākṣa, Dundubhi, Caṇḍa, Tālajaṅgha, Bhūmidaṇḍa, the fierce Śaṅkukarṇa, Vaidhṛti, Tālacaṇḍa, Mahātejas, Vikaṭāsya, Hayānana, Hastivaktra, Śvānavaktra and Biḍālavadana. There are others with faces resembling those of lions, tigers etc. including Vīrabhadra.

## \|\| 1.4.91 \|\|

*vināyakaṃ puraskṛtya deva devaṃ kaparddinam \|*  
*ekādaśa tathā koṭyo niyutāni trayodaśa \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Keeping Vināyaka at their head, they guard the Lord of Devas, Kapardin. They number eleven crores and thirteen million.

## \|\| 1.4.92-93 \|\|

*arbudaṃ ca gaṇānāṃ ca prabhāsaṃ kṣetramāśritāḥ \|*  
*dvāridvāri pracaṃḍāste śūlamudgarapāṇayaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

*prabhāsakṣetraṃ rakṣaṃti devadevasya vai gṛham \|*  
*na kaścidduṣṭabuddhyā tu praviśediti saṃsthitiḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

92-93. An Arbuda (one hundred million) of the Gaṇas have occupied the Prabhāsa Kṣetra. They are very fierce. They stand at every door with tridents and Mudgaras in their hands. They guard Prabhāsa Kṣetra, the abode of the Lord of Devas. They see to it that no one enters it with evil intention.

## \|\| 1.4.94 \|\|

*śatakoṭigaṇaiścāpi pūrvadvāri tu saṃvṛtaḥ \|*  
*aṭṭahāso gaṇo nāma prabhāsaṃ tatra rakṣati \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. The Gaṇa named Aṭṭahāsa is surrounded by a hundred crores of Gaṇas in the eastern doorway. He protects Prabhāsa there.

## \|\| 1.4.95 \|\|

*kālākṣo bhīṣaṇaścaṃḍo vṛto'ṣṭādaśakoṭibhiḥ \|*  
*ghaṃṭākarṇagaṇo nāma dakṣiṇaṃ dvāramāśritaḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Kālākṣa is terrible and fierce. He is surrounded by eighteen crores of Gaṇas. The Gaṇa named Ghaṇṭākarṇa has occupied the southern gate.

## \|\| 1.4.96 \|\|

*paścimadvāramāśritya sthitavānviṣṭaro gaṇaḥ \|*  
*daṇḍapāṇiḥ sthitastatra devadevasya cottare \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. The Gaṇa named Viṣṭara has occupied the western doorway. Daṇḍapāṇi is stationed in the northern doorway of the abode of the Lord of Devas.

## \|\| 1.4.97 \|\|

*yogakṣemaṃ vahannityaṃ prabhāse bhāvitātmanām \|*  
*bhīṣaṇākṣastathaiśānyāmāgneyyāṃ chāgavaktrakaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. He looks after the Yogakṣema (acquisition and preservation i.e. maintenance) of all purified souls in Prabhāsa. Bhīṣaṇākṣa is in the north-east and Chāgavaktraka is in the south-east.

## \|\| 1.4.98-99 \|\|

*nairṛtyāṃ caṃḍanādastu vāyavyāṃ bhairavānanaḥ \|*  
*nandī caiva mahākālo daṇḍapāṇirvināyakaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

*eteṅgarakṣakā madhye śatakoṭigaṇairvṛtāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ rakṣaṃti bahavo hyasaṃkhyeyā gaṇeśvarāḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

98-99. Caṇḍanāda is in the south-west and Bhairavānana is in the north-west.

Nandin, Mahākāla, Daṇḍapāṇi and Vināyaka are the bodyguards stationed in the middle, surrounded by a hundred crore Gaṇas. Thus innumerable leading Gaṇas guard everywhere.

## \|\| 1.4.100 \|\|

*kalikalmaṣasaṃbhūtyā yeṣāṃ copahatā matiḥ \|*  
*na teṣāṃ tadbhavedgamyaṃ sthānamardhendumaulinaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. That holy spot of the Crescent-moon-crested Lord is not approachable to those persons whose minds are overwhelmed by the outcome of the evils of Kali Age.

## \|\| 1.4.101-102 \|\|

*gaṃdharvaiḥ kinnarairyakṣairapsarobhistathoragaiḥ \|*  
*siddhaiḥ saṃpūjya deveśaṃ someśaṃ pāpanāśanam \|\| 101 \|\|*

*antardhānaṃ gatairnityaṃ prabhāsaṃ tu niṣevyate \|*  
*saptalokeṣu ye santi siddhāḥ pātālavāsinaḥ \|*  
*pradakṣiṇaṃ te kurvaṃti someśaṃ kālabhairavam \|\| 102 \|\|*

101-102. Prabhāsa is resorted to by Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Yakṣas, Apsarās and serpents and Siddhas who remain invisible. They adore Someśa, the Lord of Devas, the destroyer of sins. Siddhas of the seven worlds and those who reside in Pātāla circumambulate Someśa Kālabhairava.

## \|\| 1.4.103-106 \|\|

*pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni puṇyānyāyatanāni ca \|*  
*lākuliṃ bhārabhūtiṃ ca āṣāḍhiṃ daṇḍameva ca \|\| 103 \|\|*

*puṣkaraṃ naimiṣaṃ caiva amareśaṃ tathāparam \|\| \|*  
*bhairavaṃ madhyamaṃ kālaṃ kedāraṃ kaṇavīrakam \|\| 104 \|\|*

*haricaṃdrastu śaileśastathā vastrāṃtikeśvaraḥ \|*  
*aṭṭahāsaṃ mahendraṃ ca śrīśailaṃ ca gayā tathā \|\| 105 \|\|*

*etāni sarvatīrthāni devaṃ someśvaraṃ prabhum \|*  
*pradakṣiṇaṃ prakurvaṃti tatra liṃgaṃ stuvaṃti ca \|\| 106 \|\|*

103-106. All theTīrthas and holy shrines of the earth circumambulate Lord Someśvara and eulogize the Liṅga there. The Tīrthas are Lākuli, Bhāvabhūti, Āṣāḍhi, Daṇḍa, Puṣkara, Naimiṣa, Amareśa, another Bhairava, Madhyama, Kāla, Kedāra, Kaṇavīraka, Haricandra, Śaileśa, Vastrāntikeśvara, Aṭṭahāsa, Mahendra, Śrīśaila and Gayā.

## \|\| 1.4.107 \|\|

*brahmā janārdanaścānye ye devā jagati sthitāḥ \|*  
*agniliṃgasamīpasthāḥ saṃdhyākāle stuvaṃti ca \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. Brahmā, Janārdana, and the other Devas stationed in the universe come near the Agni Liṅga at the time of dusk and eulogize.

## \|\| 1.4.108 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭikoṭisahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭikoṭiśatāni ca \|*  
*sarve someśvaraṃ yāṃti māghakṛṣṇacaturddaśīm \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Sixty crores of thousands and sixty crores of hundreds of these go to Someśvara on the fourteenth day in the dark half of the month of Māgha.

## \|\| 1.4.109-110 \|\|

*tasminkāle ca yo dadyātsomeśe ghṛtakambalam \|\| 109 \|\|*

*ghṛtaṃ rasaṃ tilāndugdhaṃ jalaṃ caṃdrādhivāsitam \|*  
*ekatra kṛtvā kāśmīramityetadghṛtakaṃbalam \|\| 110 \|\|*

109-110. At that time a devotee should offer the Ghṛtakaṃbala to Someśa, i.e. they are to collect together all these: Ghee, Rasa (juice), gingelly seeds, milk, water rendered fragrant with camphor and Kāśmīra (saffron).

## \|\| 1.4.111 \|\|

*śivarātryāṃ tu karttavyametadgopyaṃ mama priyam \|*  
*evaṃ kṛte ca yatpuṇyaṃ gadituṃ tanna śakyate \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. This has to be done on the Śivarātri day. This is a secret and it is my favourite. It is impossible to reckon the merit that accrues when this is done.

## \|\| 1.4.112 \|\|

*tatra dakṣiṇabhāge tu svayaṃ bhūtavināyakam \|*  
*prathamaṃ pūjayeddevi yadīcchetsiddhimātmanaḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. If one desires one’s siddhi, O goddess, one should adore at the outset Bhūtavināyaka himself in the southern side.

## \|\| 1.4.113 \|\|

*ūṣarāṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ prabhāsakṣetramūṣaram \|*  
*pīṭhānāṃ caiva pīṭhaṃ ca kṣetrāṇāṃ kṣetramuttamam \|*  
*sandehānāṃ ca sarveṣāmayaṃ saṃdeha uttamaḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Of all Ūṣaras (arid regions) the Prabhāsa Kṣetra is the greatest Ūṣara (arid land). It is the most excellent of all Pīṭhas and Kṣetras. Of all Sandehas this is the greatest of Sandeha (?).

## \|\| 1.4.114 \|\|

*ye kecidyoginaḥ saṃti śatakoṭipravistarāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ kṣetre prabhāse tu ratirnnānyatra kutracit \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. There are hundred crores of Yogins. They have great interest only in Prabhāsa Kṣetra and nowhere else.

## \|\| 1.4.115-116 \|\|

*liṃgādīśānabhāge tu saṃsthitā surasundari \|\| 115 \|\|*

*mayā yā kathitā tubhyamumā nāma kalā śubhā \|*  
*sā satī procyate devi dakṣasya duhitā purā \|\| 116 \|\|*

115-116. O beautiful woman of Suras, the splendid Kalā named Umā, about whom I have already mentioned, is established on the north-east of the Liṅga. O goddess, she is called Satī and she was the daughter of Dakṣa formerly.

## \|\| 1.4.117 \|\|

*dakṣakopāccharīraṃ tu saṃtyajya paramā kalā \|*  
*himavaṃtagṛhe jātā umānāmnā ca viśrutā \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. Being angry with Dakṣa, the greatest Kalā abandoned her body and was reborn in the abode of Himavān. She became well-known by the name Umā.

## \|\| 1.4.118 \|\|

*tena devi tvayā sārddhaṃ tatrasthā varadāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*navakoṭyastu cāmuṃḍāstasminkṣetre sthitāḥ svayam \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. Therefore, O goddess, they remained there along with you. They are remembered as the bestowers of boons. Nine crores of Cāmuṇḍās are stationed in that holy spot.

## \|\| 1.4.119 \|\|

*caitre māsi sitāṣṭamyāṃ tatra tvāṃ yadi pūjayet \|*  
*eka viṃśatijanmāni dāridryaṃ tasya no bhavet \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. If a devotee adores you there on the eighth day in the bright half of the month of Caitra, he will not meet with poverty in the course of twenty-one rebirths.

## \|\| 1.4.120 \|\|

*amā somena saṃyuktā kadācidyadi labhyate \|*  
*tasyāṃ someśvaraṃ dṛṣṭvā koṭiyajñaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. If the Amā (New-Moon) united with Monday is attainable at any time, a devotee should visit Someśvara. Thereby he attains the benefit of a crore of Yajñas.

## \|\| 1.4.121 \|\|

*etatkṣetraṃ mahāguhyaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|*  
*rudrāṇāṃ koṭayo yatra ekādaśa samāsate \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. This holy spot is something to be treated as a great secret. It is destructive of all sins, since it is the place where eleven crores of Rudras are collectively present.

## \|\| 1.4.122 \|\|

*dvādaśātra dineśānāṃ vasavo'ṣṭau samāgatāḥ \|*  
*gandharvayakṣarakṣāṃsi asaṃkhyātā gaṇeśvarāḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. Twelve Dineśas (Ādityas, Sun-gods) and eight Vasus arrive here. There are innumerable prominent Gaṇas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas and Rākṣasas.

## \|\| 1.4.123-126 \|\|

*umāpi tatra pārśvasthā sarvadevaistu saṃstutā \|*  
*nandī ca gaṇanātho yo devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

*mahākālasya ye cānye gaṇapāḥ saṃti pārśvagāḥ \|*  
*gaṃgā ca yamunā caiva tathā devī sarasvatī \|\| 124 \|\|*

*anyāśca saritaḥ puṇyā nadāścaiva hradāstathā \|*  
*samudrāḥ parvatāḥ kūpā vanaspataya eva ca \|\| 125 \|\|*

*sthāvaraṃ jaṃgamaṃ caiva prabhāse tu samāgatam \|*  
*anye caiva gaṇāstatra prabhāse saṃvyavasthitāḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

123-126. Umā too who is eulogized by all the Devas is present very near at the side. There is Nandin, the leader of Gaṇas of the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas. There are other leading Gaṇas who stand by the side of Mahākāla. There are the rivers Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī and other sacred ones, Nadas and Hradas. There are oceans, mountains, wells and trees. All the mobile and immobile beings have arrived at Prabhāsa. Other Gaṇas too are stationed there at Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.4.127 \|\|

*na mayā kathitāḥ sarva uddeśena kvacitkvacit \|*  
*bhaktyā paramayā yukto devadevi vināyakam \|*  
*tṛtīyaṃ pūjayettatra vāṃchetkṣetraphalaṃ yadi \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. All have not been mentioned by me. At random I have mentioned a few here and there. If one desires the benefit of the sacred place, O goddess of Devas, one should worship the third Vināyaka there with great devotion.

## \|\| 1.4.128 \|\|

*dvādaśaivaṃ tathā cāṣṭau catvāriṃśacca koṭayaḥ \|*  
*nadīnāmagnitīrthasya dvāre tiṣṭhaṃti bhāmini \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. Thus, O beautiful lady, at the entrance to the Agni Tīrtha there are stationed twelve, eight and twenty-four crores of rivers.

## \|\| 1.4.129 \|\|

*nirmālyalaṃghanaṃ kiṃcidajñātādyadi vai kṛtam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ vilayaṃ yāti agnitīrthasya darśanāt \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. If the (sin of) Nirmālya Laṅghana (i.e. over-stepping flowers and other leavings of adoration of God) has been committed unknowingly, the entire sin is washed off on visiting the Agni Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.4.130 \|\|

*devi kiṃ bahunoktena kṣetrametanmahāprabham \|*  
*na te varṇayituṃ śakyaṃ kalpakoṭiśatairapi \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. Of what avail is talking too much, O goddess? This holy spot is highly refulgent. It is impossible to describe it adequately to you eveṇ in the course of hundreds of crores of Kalpas.

## \|\| 1.4.131 \|\|

*ye cāṃtarikṣe bhuvi ye ca devāstīrthāni vai yāni digaṃtareṣu \|*  
*kṣetraṃ prabhāsaṃ pravaraṃ hi teṣāṃ someśvaraṃ devi tathā variṣṭham \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. Prabhāsa Kṣetra is the greatest of all the Tīrthas in the various quarters and of all the deities in the atmosphere, or on the earth. So also, O goddess, Someśvara is the greatest deity.

## \|\| 1.4.132 \|\|

*ye cāṃḍajāścodbhijāścaiva jīvāḥ sasvedajāścaiva jarāyujāśca \|*  
*devi prabhāse tu gatāsavo'tha muktiṃ paraṃ yāṃti na saṃśayo'tra \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. All the types of living beings such as the oviparous, viviparous, sweat-born ones and plants (coming out breaking through the ground) attain salvation if they meet with death at Prabhāsa. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.4.133 \|\|

*iti nigaditametaddevadevasya citraṃ caritamidamaciṃtyaṃ devi te śaṃkarasya \|*  
*kalikaluṣavidāraṃ sarvaloko'pi yāyādyadi paṭhati śṛṇoti stauti nityaṃ ya ittham \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. Thus the wonderful story of the Lord of Devas has been narrated. O goddess, the incomprehensible deeds of Śaṅkara have been narrated to you. He who reads, listens to this and eulogizes the Lord, all these people will attain salvation, destroying into smitherens the sins of Kali.

## Chapter 5 - Sages and Devas Residing in Prabhāsa Kṣetra

## \|\| 1.5.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityevamukte vipreṃdrā śaṃkareṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*punaḥ papraccha sā devī harṣasaṃpūrṇamānasā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1\. O leading Brāhmaṇas, when this was narrated by the noble-souled Śaṅkara, the goddess became extremely delighted in her mind and asked again:

## \|\| 1.5.2 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*devadeva jagannātha sarvaprāṇahitāya vai \|*  
*prabhāsakṣetramāhātmyaṃ vistarādvada me prabho \|\| 2 \|\|*

The Devī said:

2\. For the sake of the welfare of all living beings, O Lord of Devas, O Lord of the universe, do tell me in detail the greatness of the Prabhāsa Kṣetra.

## \|\| 1.5.3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*anyaddṛṣṭāṃtarūpaṃ te kathayāmi yaśasvini \|*  
*yena sṛṣṭaṃ mahādevi kṣetrametanmama priyam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

3\. O renowned one, I shall give you another example as to why, O great goddess, this holy spot, a favourite of mine, has been created.

## \|\| 1.5.4 \|\|

*yā gatirdhyāyatāṃ nityaṃ niḥsaṃgānāṃ ca yoginām \|*  
*saivaṃ saṃtyajatāṃ prāṇānprabhāse tu parā gatiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The great goal (region) that Yogins who are devoid of any attachment attain by constant meditation, is attained by those who give up their life at that holy place Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.5.5 \|\|

*anekakalpasthāyī ca mārkaṃḍeyo mahātapāḥ \|*  
*so'pi devaṃ virūpākṣaṃ prabhāse tu sadā'rcati \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Mārkaṇḍeya also, the great ascetic whose span of life extends to many Kalpas, always worships Lord Virūpākṣa at Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.5.6 \|\|

*aṭitvā sarvatīrthāni prabhāsaṃ naiva muṃcati \|*  
*durvāsāśca mahātejā liṃgasyārādhanodyataḥ \|*  
*na muṃcati kṣaṇaṃ devi tatkṣetraṃ śaśimaulinaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Though he wanders over all the Tīrthas, he never leaves Prabhāsa. Durvāsas of excessive splendour endeavours to propitiate the Liṅga. O goddess, he does not forsake that holy place of the Moon-crested Lord even for a moment.

## \|\| 1.5.7-10 \|\|

*bharadvājo marīciśca muniścoddālakastathā \|*  
*kratuścaiva vasiṣṭhaśca kaśyapo bhṛgureva ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

*dakṣaścaiva tu sāvarṇiryamaścāṃgirasastathā \|*  
*śuko vibhāṃḍakaścaiva ṛṣyaśṛṃgo'tha gobhilaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*gautamaśca ṛcīkaśca agastyaḥ śaunako mahān \|*  
*nārado jamadagniśca viśvāmitro'tha lomaśaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*anye ca ṛṣayaścaiva divyā devarṣayastathā \|*  
*na muṃcaṃti mahākṣetraṃ liṃgasyārādhanodyatāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-10. Similarly, Bharadvāja, Sage Marīci, Uddālaka, Kratu, Vasiṣṭha, Kaśyapa, Bhṛgu, Dakṣa, Sāvarṇi, Yama, Aṅgiras, Śuka, Vibhāṇḍaka, Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, Gobhila, Gautama, Ṛcīka, Agastya, the great Śaunaka, Nārada, Jamadagni, Viśvāmitra, Lomaśa and many other sages as well as celestial sages never leave the great holy spot. They endeavour to propitiate the Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.5.11 \|\|

*ahaṃ tatraiva tiṣṭhāmi liṃgārādhanatatparaḥ \|*  
*na muṃcāmi mahākṣetraṃ satyaṃsatyaṃ varānane \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. I stay there itself eager (in watching their) propitiation. I never leave that great Kṣetra, O lady of excellent countenance. It is the truth, nothing but the truth.

## \|\| 1.5.12 \|\|

*sarvatīrthāni deveśi mayā dṛṣṭāni bhūtale \|*  
*prabhāsena samaṃ kṣetraṃ naiva dṛṣṭaṃ kadācana \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O goddess of Devas, all the Tīrthas on the earth have been seen by me. A Kṣetra on a par with Prabhāsa was never seen.

## \|\| 1.5.13 \|\|

*devi ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi yājñavalkyapuraskṛtāḥ \|*  
*japaṃ kurvaṃti rudrāṇāṃ candrabhāgāṃ vyavasthitāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O goddess, sixty thousand devotees with Yājñavalkya at the head, stay at Candrabhāgā. They perform Japa of the Rudra Mantras.

## \|\| 1.5.14 \|\|

*catvāriṃśatsahasrāṇi ṛṣīṇāmūrddhvaretasām \|*  
*devikātaṭamāśritya japaṃti śatarudriyam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Forty thousand sages of absolute celibacy perform the Japa of Satarudriya on the banks of Devikā (a local rivulet).

## \|\| 1.5.15-17 \|\|

*koṭayaścaiva paṃcāśanmunīnāmūrddhvaretasām \|*  
*umāpatiṃ samāsādya liṃgaṃ tatraiva saṃsthitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*rudrāṇāṃ koṭi jāpyaṃ tu kṛtaṃ tatraiva taiḥ purā \|*  
*koṭistatraiva saṃsiddhāstasmiṃlliṃge na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*śataṃ caiva sahasrāṇāṃ deveśaṃ śaśibhūṣaṇam \|*  
*pūjayaṃti mahāsiddhā mama kṣetraniṣeviṇaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. Fifty crores of the sages of perfect celibacy have resorted to the Umāpati Liṅga stationed there itself. Formerly, the Japa of the Rudra Mantras was performed by them a crore times there itself.

A hundred thousand great Siddhas who stay in that holy place of mine worship the Moon-crested Lord of Devas.

## \|\| 1.5.18 \|\|

*vedāṃteṣu ca yatproktaṃ phalaṃ caiva maharṣibhiḥ \|*  
*tatphalaṃ sakalaṃ tatra caṃdrabhūṣaṇadarśanāt \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. By visiting Gandrabhūṣaṇa there, one gets entirely that benefit which has been mentioned by great sages in the Vedāṇtas.

## \|\| 1.5.19 \|\|

*agnitīrthe ṛṣīṇāṃ tu koṭiḥ sāgrā sthitā śubhe \|*  
*rudreśvare smṛtaṃ lakṣaṃ kaṃparddīśe tathaiva ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O splendid lady, more than a crore of sages are staying at Agni Tīrthā. It is remembered that a hundred thousand have settled in Rudreśvara. So also in Kapardīśa.

## \|\| 1.5.20 \|\|

*ratneśvare sahasraṃ tu ṛṣīṇāmūrddhvaretasām \|*  
*arkasthale mahāpuṇye koṭiḥ sāgrā sthitā śubhe \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. A thousand sages of extraordinary celibacy arc stationed in Ratneśvara. In the highly meritorious Arkasthala, O splendid lady, more than a crore are stationed.

## \|\| 1.5.21 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭiścaiva sahasrāṇi tatra siddheśvare sthitāḥ \|*  
*sapta caiva sahasrāṇi mārkaṃḍeye tu saṃsthitāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Sixty thousand are stationed there in Siddheśvara. Those who are stationed in Mārkaṇḍa number seven thousand.

## \|\| 1.5.22-23 \|\|

*sarasvatyāṃ brahmakuṇḍe'saṃkhyātā munayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*daśārbudasahasrāṇi koṭitritayameva ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

*ṛṣayastatra tiṣṭhaṃti yatra prācī sarasvatī \|*  
*brahmahatyā gatā yatra śaṃkarasya ca tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Innumerable sages are remembered as stationed in Sarasvatī and Brahma Kuṇḍa. Ten thousand Arbudas and three crores of sages stay at the place where there is Prācī Sarasvatī. It was there that Śaṅkara’s sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter perished in a moment.

## \|\| 1.5.24 \|\|

*kāyaḥ suvarṇatāṃ prāpa kapālaṃ patitaṃ karāt \|*  
*jñātvaivaṃ śaṃkinā pūrvaṃ kṛtaṃ tatra mahātapaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. His (Śaṅkara’s) body became golden and the skull fell down from his hand. After knowing this Śaṅkin performed a great penance there.

## \|\| 1.5.25 \|\|

*tuṣṭaḥ śrīśaṃkaro devo liṃga vāsavareṇa tu \|*  
*koṭiyajñaphalaṃ snāne prācyāṃ liṃgasya pūjane \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Lord Śrī Śaṅkara became pleased and blessed him with the boon of staying in the Liṅga. By having ablution in Prācl and worshipping the Liṅga one acquires merit of a crore of Yajñas.

## \|\| 1.5.26 \|\|

*piṃḍe gayāśataguṇamamāsomayute dine \|*  
*bhūtāyāṃ piṃḍadastatra kulakoṭiṃ samuddharet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. If a ball of rice is offered on a New-Moon day, the benefit is a hundred times more than that at Gayā. One who offers balls of rice there on the Bhūta day (i.e. fourteenth lunar day) shall redeem a crore of the members of his family.

## \|\| 1.5.27 \|\|

*ye cātra malanāśāya nimaṅkṣyaṃti ca mānavāḥ \|*  
*daśagodānajaṃ puṇyaṃ teṣāmapi bhaviṣyati \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. If men take a plunge here for quelling the dirt (of sins) they will earn the merit of gifting ten cows.

## \|\| 1.5.28-29 \|\|

*pādena vā krīḍamānā jalaṃ lipsaṃti ye narā \|*  
*teṣāmapi śrāddhaphalaṃ vidhivatsaṃbhaviṣyati \|*  
*tatra liṃgāni pūjyāni śūlabhedādikāni tu \|\| 28 \|\|*

*evaṃ vikalpya liṃgāni aśvamedha phalāni tu \|*  
*darśanenāpi sarveṣāṃ sparśāddhi dviguṇaṃ phalam \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. The merit of a Śrāddha performed in accordance with the injunctions of the scriptures will accrue to those also who play about iṇ the waters with the feet in water. By viewing it too all will attain merit. By touching they get twice the merit. The Liṅgas beginning with Śūlabheda should be considered to give the merit of a horse-sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.5.30 \|\|

*evaṃ tuṣṭo jagannāthaḥ sthitaḥ prācīvane dhruvam \|*  
*mano'pi ye kariṣyaṃti snānadāneṣu kā kathā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thus the Lord of the universe who is pleased is certainly stationed in the forests of Prācī. Even those who think mentally (of visiting etc.) are benefitted. Still more so in the case of those who perform Snāna and Dana.

## \|\| 1.5.31 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tuṣṭo jagannāthaḥ śaṃkaro nīlalohitaḥ \|*  
*triṃśatkoṭigaṇastatra prācīṃ rakṣaṃti sarvataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Nīlalohita, Śaṅkara, the Lord of the worlds is pleased with them. Thirty crores of Gaṇas guard Prācī all round.

## \|\| 1.5.32 \|\|

*mahāpāpasamācāraḥ pāpiṣṭho vā'ti kilbiṣī \|*  
*ghuṇākṣaramiva prāṇānprācyāṃ muktvā śivaṃ vrajet \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. A great sinner, one of evil conduct, a person of great misdeeds may by a happy chance meet with death in Prācī. He will attain Śiva.

## \|\| 1.5.33 \|\|

*dadhikaṃbaladānaṃ tu tatra deyaṃ dvijottame \|*  
*kathitaṃ pāpaśamanaṃ sārātsārataraṃ dhruvam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The offering of Dadhikaṃbala (adoration of Śiva with cover of curds) should be made there by excellent Brāhmaṇas. It is said to certainly suppress sins. It is the most efficacious of all essential things.

## \|\| 1.5.34 \|\|

*adhunā saṃpravakṣyāmi hiraṇyāśca mahodayam \|*  
*durvāsasā tapastaptaṃ tatra sūryaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Now I shall explain the great efficacy of Hiraṇī. The Sun-god was installed there and penance was performed by Durvāsas.

## \|\| 1.5.35-37 \|\|

*koṭirekā tu tatraiva ṛṣīṇāmūrddhvaretasām \|*  
*caturviṃśatitattvānāmadhiko balarūpadhṛk \|\| 35 \|\|*

*yatra tiṣṭhati deveśi bhṛgukoṭisamanvitaḥ \|*  
*anyatra brāhmaṇānāṃ tu koṭyā yacca phalaṃ labhet \|\| 36 \|\|*

*brahmasthāne tathaikena bhojitena tu tatphalam \|*  
*evaṃ jñātvā mahādevi tatra tiṣṭhāmi nirvṛtaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. There too, there are a crore of sages of perfect celibacy.

O goddess of Devas, the deity who has power more than that of twenty-four Tattvas stands there accompanied by a crore of Bhṛgus.

If a single person is fed in Brahmasthāna, one gets the same benefit as by feeding a crore of Brāhmaṇas elsewhere. O great goddess, this I am aware of and hence I stay there extremely pleased.

## \|\| 1.5.38-39 \|\|

*koṭirbhirdevaṛṣibhirdevaiḥ saha samāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*tīrthāni tatra tiṣṭhaṃti aṃtarbhūtāni vai kalau \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tatra kṣetre mahāramye yatra someśvaraḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*mama devi gaṇau dvau tu vibhramaḥ saṃbhramaḥ paraḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. I am surrounded by a crore of celestial sages and Devas.

In Kali Age, Tīrthas stay there latent (merged underneath) in the holy spot of great beauty where Someśvara is stationed. I have, O goddess, two Gaṇas there—Vibhrama and Saṃbhrama.

## \|\| 1.5.40 \|\|

*tau cātra kṣetrasaṃsthānāṃ lokānāṃ bhramavibhramaiḥ \|*  
*yojayaṃti sadā cittaṃ vikalpānaikyasaṃkulam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. These two make the minds of the people residing in the Kṣetra excited and deluded due to ignorance. They are disunited and are in a dilemma.

## \|\| 1.5.41 \|\|

*vināyakopasargāśca daśa doṣāstathā pare \|*  
*evaṃ kṣetraṃ tu rakṣaṃti pāpināṃ duṣṭacetasām \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. There are then the Vināyakas, Upasargas (troubles) and ten other defects. They guard the Kṣetra from evil-minded sinners.

## \|\| 1.5.42 \|\|

*daṃḍapāṇiṃ tu ye bhaktyā paśyaṃtīha narottamāḥ \|*  
*na teṣāṃ jāyate vighnaṃ tatra kṣetranivāsinām \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. If the residents of the Kṣetra visit the deity Daṇḍapāṇi with devotion, they are excellent men and they will not meet with obstacles.

## \|\| 1.5.43-44 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrā vai varṇasaṃkarāḥ \|*  
*akāmā vā sakāmā vā prabhāse ye mṛtāḥ śubhe \|\| 43 \|\|*

*caṃdrārddhamaulinaḥ sarve lalāṭākṣā vṛṣadhvajāḥ \|*  
*śive mama pure divye jāyaṃte tatra mānavāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. O splendid lady, those who die at Prabhāsa, whether Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras, or of mixed castes, whether they have desires or not, they become identical with Śiva. All of them will have the crescent-moon for the coronet. They will have eyes in the forehead. They will be bull-bannered. Those men are born (or become) so in the splendid divine Śivapura of mine.

## \|\| 1.5.45 \|\|

*yastatra vasate vipraḥ saṃyatātmā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*trikālamapi bhuṃjāno vāyubhakṣasamo bhavet \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. A Brāhmaṇa staying there with mental concentration and purity, may be taking food thrice a day. But he is on a par with one who subsists on air only.

## \|\| 1.5.46-47 \|\|

*meroḥ śakyā guṇā vaktuṃ dvīpānāṃ ca guṇāstathā \|*  
*samudrāṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ śakyā vaktuṃ guṇāḥ priye \|\| 46 \|\|*

*ādidevasya deveśi maheśasya mahāprabhoḥ \|*  
*śakyā naiva guṇā vaktuṃ varṣākoṭiśatairapi \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. O my beloved, the good qualities of Meru can be narrated. So also the good qualities of the continents. The good qualities of all the oceans can be enumerated. But, O goddess of Devas, one cannot enumerate the good qualities of the primordial Lord Maheśa, the great Lord, in hundreds of crores of years.

## Chapter 6 - Greatness of Someśvara (Soma-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.6.1-3 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*atyadbhutaṃ mahādeva māhātmyaṃ kathitaṃ mama \|*  
*apūrvaṃ devadeveśa kadācinna śrutaṃ mayā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*brahmāṃḍe yāni liṃgāni kīrtitāni tvayā mama \|*  
*teṣāṃ prabhāvenādhikyaṃ someśe tatkathaṃ vada \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kiṃ prabhāvo mahādeva kṣetrasya ca sureśvara \|*  
*tanme brūhi sureśāna yāthātathyaṃ mamāgrataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

The Devī said:

1-3. The extremely miraculous greatness has been narrated to me. This is unprecedented, O Lord of the chiefs of Devas. Never has it been heard by me before.

Of all the Liṅgas in the Cosmic Egg which have been extolled by you to me, how is it that Someśa has become extremely pre-eminent?

O great Lord, O Lord of Suras, is it the power of the holy place? Hence, O Lord of Suras, narrate it factually to me.

## \|\| 1.6.4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi rahasyaṃ paramaṃ tava \|*  
*prabhāsakṣetramāhātmyaṃ someśasya varānane \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

4\. O lady of excellent countenance, hereafter I shall narrate in detail the greatest secret, the greatness of Someśa and Prabhāsa Kṣetra.

## \|\| 1.6.5-6 \|\|

*tīrthānāṃ paramaṃ tīrthaṃ vratānāṃ paramaṃ vratam \|*  
*jāpyānāṃ paramaṃ jāpyaṃ dhyānānāṃ dhyānamuttamam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*yogānāṃ paramo yogo rahasyaṃ paramaṃ mahat \|*  
*tattehaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi śṛṇu hyekamanā priye \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Of all the Tīrthas, it is the greatest Tīrtha; of all the Vratas it is the greatest Vrata; of all the Jāpyas (Mantras to be muttered) it is the greatest Jāpya; it is the most excellent one of all meditations; it is the greatest Yoga among all Yogas; it is the greatest secret. I shall expound it to you. O my beloved, listen to it with concentrated attention.

## \|\| 1.6.7 \|\|

*someśaṃ paramaṃ sthānaṃ paṃcavaktrasamanvitam \|*  
*etalliṃgaṃ na muṃcāmi satyaṃsatyaṃ mayoditam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Someśa is the greatest holy shrine. The Liṅga has five faces. I never leave it. It is the truth. The truth has been mentioned by me.

## \|\| 1.6.8 \|\|

*yacca tatparamaṃ devi dhruvamakṣayamavyayam \|*  
*someśaṃ tadvijānīhi mā vikalpamanā bhava \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Whatever is the greatest, the most permanent, everlasting and immutable, do know it to be Someśa. Do not get confused in mind.

## \|\| 1.6.9-10 \|\|

*nirbhayaṃ nirmalaṃ nityaṃ nirapekṣaṃ nirāśrayam \|*  
*niraṃjanaṃ niṣprapaṃcaṃ niḥsaṃgaṃ nirupadravam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*talliṃgamiti jānīhi prabhāse saṃvyavasthitam \|*  
*apavargamavijñeyaṃ manoramyamanāmayam \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Know that Liṅga in Prabhāsa as one that is above fear, free from impurities, eternal, independent, not having (needing) another support, unsullied, devoid of ramifications, free from attachment and devoid of torments. It is well-established at Prabhāsa. It is the final beatitude, incomprehensible, pleasing to the mind and devoid of ailments.

## \|\| 1.6.11 \|\|

*nityaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ devaṃ makhaghnaṃ sarvatomukham \|*  
*śivaṃ sarvātmakaṃ sūkṣmamanādyaṃ yacca daivatam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. That is the eternal, the cause of the universe, the destroyer of (Dakṣa’s) sacrifice, Lord with faces everywhere (in all directions), the auspicious subtle (principle) identical with all, the primordial deity.

## \|\| 1.6.12 \|\|

*ātmopalabdhivijñeyaṃ cittaciṃtāvivarjitam \|*  
*gamāgamavinirmuktaṃ bahiraṃtaśca kevalam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. It is comprehensible only through self-realization. It is devoid of mental worries. It is devoid of birth and death. It is pure and absolute both within and without.

## \|\| 1.6.13 \|\|

*ātmopalabdhiviṣayaṃ stutigocaravarjitam \|*  
*niṣkalaṃ vimalātmānaṃ prakaṭaṃ jñānadīpakam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. It is the object of self-realization. It is beyond the ken of eulogy. It is partless, the soul devoid of impurities. It is the manifest illumination of perfect knowledge.

## \|\| 1.6.14 \|\|

*talliṃgamiti jānīhi prabhāse surasuṃdari \|*  
*nirāvakāśarahitaṃ śabdaṃ śabdāṃtagocaram \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Know that the Liṅga at Prabhāsa is of such a nature, O beautiful goddess. It is devoid of space-lessness. It is sound that is perceptible when all (other worldly) sounds cease.

## \|\| 1.6.15 \|\|

*niṣkalaṃ vimalaṃ devaṃ devadevaṃ surātmakam \|*  
*hetupramāṇarahitaṃ kalpanābhāvavarjitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. It is unsullied and free from impurities. It is the Lord, the Lord of Devas. It is the soul of Suras. It is beyond reasoning. It is beyond the perview of imagination.

## \|\| 1.6.16 \|\|

*cittāvalokaviṣayaṃ bahiraṃtarasaṃsthitam \|*  
*prabhāse taṃ vijānīhi praṇavaṃ liṃgarūpiṇam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. It is the object of mental view. It is stationed both within and without. Know it to be Praṇava in the form of Liṅga at Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.6.17 \|\|

*aniṣpaṃdaṃ mahātmānaṃ nirānaṃdāvalokanam \|*  
*lokāvalokamārgasthaṃ viśuddhajñānakevalam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The great soul is stable (unmoved by any pulsation or variation), beyond all perception of bliss. It is the pure and perfect knowledge on the path of survey of the world(?).

## \|\| 1.6.18 \|\|

*vidyāviśeṣamārgasthamanekākārasaṃjñitam \|*  
*svabhāvabhāvanāgrāhyaṃ bhāvātītamalakṣaṇam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. It is stationed on the path of special spiritual knowledge (?). It is designated by its innumerable forms. It can be comprehended through the concept of its own existence (?). It is beyond existence and characterization.

## \|\| 1.6.19 \|\|

*vākprapaṃcādirahitaṃ niṣprapañcātmakaṃ śivam \|*  
*jñānajñeyāvalokasthaṃ hetvābhāsavivarjitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. It is devoid of (beyond) development, display etc. of words. It is Śiva free from identity with the worldly units. It is stationed under the survey of knowledge and the knowable? It is devoid of fallacious reasoning.

## \|\| 1.6.20 \|\|

*anāhataṃ śabdagataṃ śabdādigaṇasaṃbhavam \|*  
*evaṃ someśvaraṃ viddhi prabhāse liṃgarūpiṇam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. It is present in the Śabda in the mystic (Yogic) Cakra named Anāhata. It originates from the groups of Śabda (sound) etc(?). Know Someśvara to be thus. It is in the form of a Liṅga in Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.6.21 \|\|

*śabdabrahmagataṃ śāntaṃ sa śabdāṃtagamāspadam \|*  
*sarvātirikta viṣayaṃ sarvadhyānapade sthitam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. It is quiescent. It is present in Śabdabrahman. Its place (resort) is beyond the ken of words. It is the object of that which surpasses everything. It is present in the path of meditation of all (?).

## \|\| 1.6.22 \|\|

*anādimacyutaṃ divyaṃ pramāṇātīta gocaram \|*  
*adhaścordhvaṃ gataṃ nityaṃ jīvākhyaṃ dehasaṃsthitam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. It is beginningless. It is divine and unswerving. It is the object of that which is beyond all valid testimony. It exists both above and below. It is stationed in the body and so is called Jīva.

## \|\| 1.6.23 \|\|

*hṛdādidvādaśāṃtasthaṃ prāṇāpānodayāstagam \|*  
*agrāhyamindriyātmānaṃ niṣkalaṃkātmakaṃ vibhum \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. (In Yogic meditation) it is stationed at the end of twelve Aṅgulas which is the extreme reach of the breadth both within (the heart) and outside (when exhaled). It is present at the rise (beginning) and end of Prāṇa and Apāna (inhalation and exhalation). It is identical with the soul (power) of sense- organs yet it is imperceptible (beyond the grasp of senses). It is blemishless and all-pervading.

## \|\| 1.6.24 \|\|

*svarādivyaṃjanātītaṃ varṇādiparivarjitam \|*  
*vācāmavācyaviṣayamahaṃkārārddharūpiṇam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. It is beyond Svara (vowels) etc. and Vyañjana (consonant). It is beyond letters of alphabet etc. It is not the object of oral expression. It is in the form of half of Ahaṃkāra (?).

## \|\| 1.6.25 \|\|

*apratarkyamanuccāryaṃ kalanākālavarjitam \|*  
*niḥśabdaṃ niścalaṃ saumyaṃ dehātītaṃ parātparam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. It is beyond the reach of logical argumentation or imagination. It cannot be expressed orally. It is devoid of time and act of reckoning. It is devoid of sound and movement. It is gentle. It is beyond the body, greater than the greatest.

## \|\| 1.6.26 \|\|

*bhūtāvagraharahitaṃ bhāvābhāvavivarjitam \|*  
*avijñeyaṃ paraṃ sūkṣmaṃ pañcapañcādisaṃbhavam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. It is beyond the grasp of (five) elements (or living beings). It is beyond existence and non-existence. It is extremely subtle and incomprehensible. It originates from the five pentads etc.

## \|\| 1.6.27 \|\|

*aprameyamanaṃtākhyamakṣayaṃ kāmarūpiṇam \|*  
*prabhavaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ bījāṃkurasamudbhavam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. It is immeasurable. It has infinite names (or it is designated as infinite). It is everlasting. It can assume any form it likes. It is the source of origin of all living beings. It originates like a sprout from seed.

## \|\| 1.6.28 \|\|

*vyāpakaṃ sarvakāmākhyamakṣaraṃ paramaṃ mahat \|*  
*sthūlasūkṣmavibhāgasthaṃ vyaktāvyaktaṃ sanātanam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. It is pervasive. It has all desired names. It is imperishable and extremely great. It is present in the setup of the subtle and the gross. It is both manifest and unmanifest. It is eternal.

## \|\| 1.6.29 \|\|

*kalpakalpāntarahitamanādinidhanaṃ mahat \|*  
*mahābhūtaṃ mahākāyaṃ śivaṃ nirvāṇabhairavam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. It is devoid of great periods of time called Kalpa and ends of Kalpas. It is great without beginning and end. It is the great element. It has a huge body. It is auspicious and Nirvāṇabhairava (terrific though quiescent).

## \|\| 1.6.30 \|\|

*evaṃ sadāśivaṃ viddhi prabhāse liṃgarūpiṇam \|*  
*yogakriyā vinirmuktaṃ mṛtyuṃjayamanādimat \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Understand Sadāśiva thus in the form of the Liṅga at Prabhāsa. He is devoid of yogic activity. He is the conqueror of Mṛtyu (death) and has no beginning.

## \|\| 1.6.31 \|\|

*sarvopasargarahitaṃ sarvatovyāpakaṃ śivam \|*  
*avyaktaṃ parato nityaṃ kevalaṃ dvaitavarjitam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He is devoid of all torments. He is Śiva who pervades everything all round. He is unmanifest and eternal, more than the greatest. He is absolutely one without any duality.

## \|\| 1.6.32 \|\|

*ananyatejasākrāṃtaṃ prabhāsakṣetravāsinam \|*  
*bhūrisvayaṃprabhaprakhyaṃ sarvatejo'dhikaṃ haram \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. It is not overwhelmed by another refulgence for the residents of Prabhāsa Kṣetra. He has excessive self-luminosity and refulgence. He is Hara who surpasses the splendour of all.

## \|\| 1.6.33 \|\|

*śaraṇyaṃdevamīśānamoṃkāraṃ śivarūpiṇam \|*  
*devadevaṃ mahādevaṃ paṃcavaktraṃ vṛṣadhvajam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. He is Lord Īśāna worthy of being the refuge. He is Oṃkāra in the form of Śiva. He is Mahādeva, the Lord of Devas. He is five-faced and bull-emblemed.

## \|\| 1.6.34 \|\|

*nirmalaṃ mānasātītaṃ bhāvagrāhyamanūpamam \|*  
*sadā śāṃtaṃ virūpākṣaṃ śūlahastaṃ jaṭādharam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. He is free from impurities. He is beyond the ken of the mind. He can be comprehended through Bhāva (emotion, devotion). He is incomparable. He is always quiescent. He is the trident-armed Virūpākṣa (Three-eyed Lord) having matted hairs.

## \|\| 1.6.35 \|\|

*hṛtpadmakośamadhyasthaṃ śūnyarūpaṃ nirañjanam \|*  
*evaṃ sadāśivaṃ viddhi prabhāse liṅgarūpiṇam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He is stationed in the middle of the lotus (the Yogic plexus) of the heart. He is void-formed and unsullied. Understand Sadāśiva thus in the form of the Liṅga at Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.6.36 \|\|

*yo'sau parātparo devo haṃsākhyaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*nādākhyaḥ suvrate devi so'sminsthāne sthitaḥ svayam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. That Lord who is greater than the greatest is glorified by the name of Haṃsa and by the name of Nāḍa. He is stationed in this holy spot, O goddess of excellent holy vows.

## \|\| 1.6.37 \|\|

*etadādisvarūpaṃ ca mayā yogabalena tu \|*  
*vijñātaṃ devi gaditaṃ divyamātmānamātmanā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. This primordial form, the divine form of the Ātman has been comprehended by me through the power of Yoga and this divine (form of the) soul has been narrated to you, O goddess.

## \|\| 1.6.38 \|\|

*ṛgvedasthastu pūrvāhṇe madhyāhne yajuṣi sthitaḥ \|*  
*aparāhṇe tu sāmastho hyatharvastho niśāgame \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. He is stationed in the Ṛgveda in the forenoon. He is stationed in the Yajus in the midday. He is stationed in the Sāman in the afternoon. He is stationed in the Atharvan at the beginning of night.

## \|\| 1.6.39 \|\|

*vedāhametaṃ puruṣaṃ mahāṃtamādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt \|*  
*tameva viditvā na bhavettu mṛtyurnānyaḥ paṃthā vidyate vai janānām \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. I know this great Puruṣa of the brilliance of the sun beyond darkness. Death will not overtake if one knows it. There is no other pathway for the people.

## \|\| 1.6.40 \|\|

*itīritaste tu mahāprabhāvaḥ someśaliṃgasya kṛtaikadeśaḥ \|*  
*vṛtaṃ na cābdairbahubhiḥ sahasrairvaktuṃ ca kenāpi mukhairna śakyam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Thus the great power of Someśaliṅga has been partially narrated to you. The deity cannot be extolled even by one endowed with many thousands of mouths in the course of many (innumerable) years.

## \|\| 1.6.41 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ śūdro'pīdaṃ paṭhedyadi \|*  
*nirmuktaḥ sarvapāpebhyaḥ sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. A Brāhmaṇa, a Kṣatriya, a Vaiśya and even a Śūdra will become rid of all sins if he reads this. He shall attain all desires.

## Chapter 7 - The Appearance (Origin) of Somanātha

## \|\| 1.7.1-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ tatra tadā devī śrutvā māhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*harṣotkaṃṭhitayā vācā punaḥ papraccha śaṃkaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

*devyuvāca \|*  
*devadeva jagannātha bhaktānugrahakāraka \|*  
*samastajñānasaṃpanna namaste'stu maheśvara \|\| 2 \|\|*

*namo'stu vai tripuraprahartre mahātmane tārakamardanāya \|*  
*namo'stu te kṣīrasamudra dāyine śiśormunīndrasya samāhitasya \|\| 3 \|\|*

*namo'stu te sarvajagadvidhātre sarvatra sarvātmaka sarvakartre \|*  
*namo bhavāyāstu namo'bhavāya namo'stu te sarvagatāya nityam \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-4. After hearing the excellent greatness there, the goddess asked Śaṅkara once again with words coming (profusely) through the throat due to eagerness and delight:

## \|\| 1.7.5 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*kiṃ devi pṛcchase'dyāpi sarvaṃ te kathitaṃ mayā \|*  
*saṃdigdhamasti kiṃciccetpunaḥ pṛcchasva bhāmini \|\| 5 \|\|*

The Devī said:

O Lord of Devas, O Lord of the worlds, O conferor of blessings unto the devotees, obeisance to you, O Maheśvara, richly endowed with all knowledge.

Obeisance to the noble-souled one, to the slayer of the Tripuras, to the suppressor of Tāraka. Obeisance to you who bestowed the ocean of milk on the child (viz. Upamanyu) of the leading sage endowed with perfect concentration and mental purity.

Obeisance to you, the creator of all the worlds. O Lord identical with all everywhere! Obeisance, to the creator of all. Obeisance to Bhava (the origin of all). Obeisance to Ābhava (having no birth). Obeisance to you, the eternal one, to you who are omnipresent.

Īśvara said:

5\. O goddess, what do you ask? Everything has been narrated by me. If still you have any doubts, you may ask, O beautiful lady.

## \|\| 1.7.6 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*someśvareti yannāma kasminkāle babhūva tat \|*  
*kiṃ nāmāgre'bhavalliṃgaṃ nāma kiṃ bhavitā'dhunā \|\| 6 \|\|*

The Devī said:

6\. When did that name Someśvara come into existence? At what time did it take place? What name did it have first? What will be the name of the Liṅga now?

## \|\| 1.7.7 \|\|

*evaṃ yasya prabhāvo vai noktaḥ pūrvaṃ tvayā vibho \|*  
*anyeṣāṃ tīrthadevānāṃ māhātmyaṃ varṇitaṃ tvayā \|*  
*na tvīdṛśaṃ tu kathitaṃ śrīsomeśasya yādṛśam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O Lord, he whose power is such, has not been described by you before. The greatness of the other deities of the Tīrtha has been described by you. Nothing like the greatness of Śrīsomeśa has been expounded.

## \|\| 1.7.8 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*pūrvamevāhamevāsaṃ sparśaliṃgasvarūpavān \|*  
*na ca māṃ tattvato veda janaḥ kaścidiheśvari \|\| 8 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

8\. I was in existence even formerly in the form of Sparśa Liṅga. O goddess, none of the men here knew me in my real form.

## \|\| 1.7.9 \|\|

*mahākalpe tu sañjāte brahmaṇaḥ prati saṃcare \|*  
*nāmabhāvaṃ bhavedanyaddevi liṃge punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. In the great Kalpa when the Pratisañcara (re-absorption into the origin) of Brahmā took place the name of the Liṅga too originated. This shall be different and occur again and again.

## \|\| 1.7.10 \|\|

*atītaṃ brahmaṇāṃ ṣaṭkaṃ saptamo'yaṃ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*varttate yo'dhunā devi śatānanda iti śrutaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Six Brahmās have passed away. The present Prajāpati who is well-known as Śatānanda is the seventh one, O goddess.

## \|\| 1.7.11 \|\|

*asminbrahmaṇi deveśi saṃjāte hyaṣṭavārṣike \|*  
*tadā kālātsamārabhya someśa iti viśrutaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. When this Brahmā became eight year old, O goddess of Devas, from that time onwards I became well-known as Someśa.

## \|\| 1.7.12 \|\|

*atīteṣu ca deveśi brahmasuptalayādanu \|*  
*babhūvuryāni nāmāni tāni tvaṃ śṛṇu pārvati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O Pārvatī, listen to those names that occurred in the periods that elapsed after the sleep and dissolution of Brahmās.

## \|\| 1.7.13 \|\|

*ādyo viraṃcināmāsīdyadā brahmā pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*mṛtyuñjayastadā nāma somanāthasya kīrtitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. When the first grandfather Brahmā called Viriñci existed, the name Mṛtyuñjaya of Somanātha was glorified in that period.

## \|\| 1.7.14 \|\|

*dvitīyo'bhūdyadā brahmā padmabhūriti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*tadā kālāgnirudreti nāma proktaṃ śubheṃ'bike \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. When the second (incumbent) Brahmā well-known by the name Padmabhū became Brahmā, the Liṅga (Somanātha) was called Kālarudrāgni, O auspicious lady.

## \|\| 1.7.15 \|\|

*tṛtīyo'bhūdyadā brahmā svayaṃbhūriti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*amṛteśeti devasya tadā nāma prakīrtitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. When the third one well-known as Svayaṃbhū became Brahmā, the name of the Lord was glorified as Amṛteśa.

## \|\| 1.7.16 \|\|

*caturtho'bhūdyathā brahmā parameṣṭhīti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*anāmayeti devasya tadā nāma smṛtaṃ śubhe \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. When the fourth one well-known as Parameṣṭhin became Brahmā, O auspicious lady, the name of the Lord was remembered as Anāmaya.

## \|\| 1.7.17 \|\|

*paṃcamo'bhūdyadā brahmā surajyeṣṭha iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*kṛttivāseti devasya nāma proktaṃ tadāmbike \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. When the fifth one remembered as Surajyeṣṭha became Brahmā, O Aṃbikā, the name of the Lord was mentioned as Kṛttivāsa.

## \|\| 1.7.18 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭhaścābhūdyadā brahmā hemagarbha iti śrutaḥ \|*  
*tadā bhairavanātheti nāma devasya kīrtitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. When the sixth one well-known (by the name) Hemagarbha became Brahmā, the Lord was glorified as Bhairavanātha.

## \|\| 1.7.19 \|\|

*ayaṃ yo varttate brahmā śatānaṃda iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*somanātheti devasya vartate nāma sāṃpratam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The present Brahmā is remembered as Śatānanda and the name of the Lord now is Somanātha.

## \|\| 1.7.20 \|\|

*ataḥ paraṃ caturvaktro brahmā yo bhavitā yadā \|*  
*prāṇanātheti devasya tadā nāma bhaviṣyati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Hereafter when the future Brahmā will be known as Caturvaktra, the name of the Lord shall be Prāṇanātha.

## \|\| 1.7.21 \|\|

*atītā ye vidhātāro bhaviṣyaṃti ca ye'dhunā \|*  
*tāvattadvarttate nāma yāvadanyoṣṭavārṣikaḥ \|*  
*saṃdhyāsaṃdhyāṃśabhedena viṣṇvanaṃtasanātanāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. In the case of Brahmā of the past and those of the future, the respective name continues till the other one is eight years old. With reference to the difference of Sandhyā and Sandhyāṃśa (Twilight of Yugas and part of twilight between Yugas) they are Viṣṇu, Ananta and Sanātana.

## \|\| 1.7.22 \|\|

*evaṃ nāmāni devasya saṃkṣepātkīrtitāni me \|*  
*vistarātkathituṃ naiva śakyaṃte kālagauravāt \|\| 22 \|\|*
