43\. O great goddess, that spot of mine is dearer to me than even Kailāsa. There too even an area extending to a Gocarma (150 Hastas by 150 Hastas) is to be guarded as secret, O Lady of excellent countenance.

## \|\| 1.11.44 \|\|

*akathyaṃ devadeveśi tava snehātprakāśitam \|*  
*etatprābhāsikaṃ kṣetraṃ prabhayā dīpitaṃ mama \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Ordinarily it should not be mentioned. But it has been revealed (to you) out of love for you. This Prābhāsika Kṣetra is illumined by my refulgence.

## \|\| 1.11.45-47 \|\|

*tena prabhāsamityuktamādikalpe varānane \|*  
*dvitīye tu prabhā labdhā sarvairdevaiḥ savāsavaiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*mama prabhābhā deveśi tena prābhāsikaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*prabhāvavanto deveśi yatra saṃti mahāsurāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*athavā tena lokeṣu prabhāsamiti kīrtyate \|*  
*prathamaṃ bhāsate devi sarveṣāṃ bhuvi tejasām \|*  
*tīrthānāmāditīrthaṃ yatprabhāsaṃ tena kīrttitam \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. Therefore, O lady of excellent countenance, it is called Prābhāsika in the first Kalpa. In the second (Kalpa) my Prabhā (Bhā, refulgence) was obtained (seen) by all the Devas including Vāsava, O goddess of Devas. Therefore it is remembered as Prābhāsika, It is the place where the great Suras are Prabhāvavantaḥ \[=Prabhāvavat?\] (influential, powerful). Therefore it is glorified as Prabhāsa in the worlds. O goddess, the first among all the refulgences i.e. the first Tīrtha among all the Tīrthas shines. Hence it is glorified as Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.11.48 \|\|

*prakṛṣṭaṃ bhānurathavā bhāsito viśvakarmaṇā \|*  
*yatra sākṣātprabhāpāto jātaḥ prābhāsikaṃ tataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Or since Bhānu (the Sun) prakṛṣṭam bhāsitaḥ i.e. is made to shine all the more by Viśvakarman and the fierceness of brilliance was lessened there, therefore it is Prābhāsika.

## \|\| 1.11.49-50 \|\|

*athavā dakṣasaṃśaptenendunā niṣprabheṇaca \|*  
*tatra devi prabhā labdhā tena prābhāsikaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*proddadhe bhāratī devī hyaurvāgniṃ vaḍavānalam \|\| 49 \|\|*

*athavā tena deveśi prabhāsamiti kīrtyate \|*  
*prakṛṣṭā bhāratī brāhmī viproktā śrūyate'dhvani \|*  
*sadā yatra mahādevi prabhāsaṃ tena kīrtitam \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. Or, O goddess, Prabhā (lustre) was regained there by the Moon who had been cursed by Dakṣa and therefore had become lustreless. Therefore, it is remembered as Prābhāsika.

Goddess Bhāratī lifted up the Vaḍavāgni (submarine fire). Therefore, O goddess of Devas, it is glorified as Prabhāsa.

Since the ‘Prakṛṣṭa Bhāratī’ (i.e. the most excellent Vedic text) is always heard on the pathways, O great goddess, therefore it is glorified as Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.11.51 \|\|

*prollasadvīcibhirbhāti sarvadā sāgaraḥ priye \|*  
*tena prabhāsa nāmeti triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O my beloved, the ocean always shines there with brilliant waves. Therefore, the name Prabhāsa became well-known in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.11.52 \|\|

*pratyakṣaṃ bhāskaro yatra sadā tiṣṭhati bhāmini \|*  
*tena prabhāsa nāmeti prasiddhimagamatkṣitau \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O lady of great lustre, there the sun always stands perceptible. Therefore, it gained renown in the earth as Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.11.53 \|\|

*prakṛṣṭaṃ bhāvināṃ sarvaṃ kāmaṃ tatra dadāmyaham \|*  
*tena prabhāsanāmeti tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. To those who meditate perfectly I grant all desires there. Therefore, the Tīrtha became well-known in all the three worlds by the name Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.11.54-55 \|\|

*kalpabhedena nāmāni tathaiva surasundari \|*  
*niruktabhedairbahudhā bhidyaṃte kāraṇaiḥ priye \|*  
*prabhāsamiti yannāma dātavyaṃ niścalaṃ smṛtam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*aptattve saṃsthitaṃ devi viṣṇorādyakalevare \|*  
*iti te kathitaṃ devi saṃkṣepātkṣetrakāraṇam \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. O my beloved, O beautiful lady of the Suras, the names differ due to the difference in the Kalpas as well as due to the etymological explanations. There are many reasons thereof.

But whatever name has to be given is remembered as the name Prabhāsa.

O goddess, it is well-established in the aqueous principle, the first body of Viṣṇu. Thus, O goddess, the cause of origin of the name of the Kṣetra has been explained to you succinctly.

## \|\| 1.11.56 \|\|

*punaste kathayāmyadya yatpṛcchasi varānane \|*  
*tadbrūhi śīghraṃ kalyāṇi yatte manasi vartate \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. O lady of excellent countenance, I shall explain further whatever you ask. Hence, O woman of excellent countenance, tell me quickly whatever is in your mind.

## \|\| 1.11.57 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*asminkalpe yathā jātaṃ kṣetraṃ prābhāsikaṃ hara \|*  
*tanme vistarato brūhi utpattiṃ kāraṇaṃ tathā \|\| 57 \|\|*

The Devī said:

57\. O Hara, tell me in detail how the Prābhāsika Kṣetra originated in this Kalpa and the cause of it’s origin.

## \|\| 1.11.58 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi yathāvatkṣetrakāraṇam \|*  
*yacchrutvā mānavo bhaktyā mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

58\. Listen, O goddess, I shall duly explain the origin of the holy spot which, if a man listens to with devotion, will rid him of all sins.

## \|\| 1.11.59 \|\|

*ādikṣetrasya māhātmyaṃ rahasyaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*kathayiṣye varārohe tava snehena bhāmini \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. O beautiful lady, O fair one, I shall narrate the greatness of the primordial Kṣetra which is to be kept a secret and is destructive of sins. Out of love for you I shall narrate.

## \|\| 1.11.60-62 \|\|

*asminkalpe tu yaddevi ādāveva varānane \|*  
*svāyaṃbhuve manau tatra brahmaṇaḥ sṛjataḥ purā \|\| 60 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇāllocanājjātaḥ pūrvaṃ sūrya iti priye \|*  
*tataḥ kālāntare tasya bhārye dve ca babhūvatuḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*tayostu rājñī dyaurjñeyā nikṣubhā pṛthivī smṛtā \|*  
*saumyamāsasya saptamyāṃ dyauḥ sūryeṇa ca yujyate \|\| 62 \|\|*

60-62. In this Kalpa in the first Manvantara of the Svāyaṃbhuva Manu, when Brahmā was engaged in creation earlier, the sun was born of his right eye, O my beloved. In due course he had two wives. One of them should be known as Dyau (Heaven) the Queen. The other is remembered as Nikṣubhā, Earth. On the seventh day in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, Dyau gets herself united with Sun.

## \|\| 1.11.63 \|\|

*māghamāse tu saptamyāṃ mahyā saha bhavedraviḥ \|*  
*bhūścādityaśca bhagavāngacchate saṃgamaṃ tadā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. On the seventh day in the month of Māgha Ravi shall be in the company of Earth. Then Bhūḥ and Āditya have their union.

## \|\| 1.11.64 \|\|

*ṛtusnātā mahī tatra garbhaṃ gṛhṇāti bhāskarāt \|*  
*dyaurjalaṃ sūyate garbhaṃ varṣāsvāsviha bhūtale \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Fresh after her bath in the Ṛtu (menstrual cycle) Earth conceived from Sun. During the rains Dyau gives birth to water flowing over Earth.

## \|\| 1.11.65 \|\|

*tatastrailokyavṛttyarthaṃ mahī sasyāni sūyate \|*  
*sasyopayogātsaṃhṛṣṭā juhvatyāhutibhirdvijāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Then for the sustenance of all the three worlds, Earth gives birth to vegetation and food-grains. Brāhmaṇas become delighted by making use of the vegetation. They begin to offer libation to fire.

## \|\| 1.11.66-68 \|\|

*svāhākārasvadhākārairyajaṃti pitṛdevatāḥ \|*  
*niḥkṣudhaḥ kurute yasmādgarbhauṣadhisudhā'mṛtaiḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*martyānpitṝṃśca devāṃśca tena bhūrnikṣubhā smṛtā \|*  
*yathā rājñī ca saṃjātā yasya ceyaṃ sutā matā \|\| 67 \|\|*

*apatyāni ca yānyasyāstāni vakṣyāmyaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*marīcirbrahmaṇaḥ putro mārīcaḥ kaśyapaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

66-67a. They begin to worship Pitṛs and Devas by uttering the words Svāhā and Svadhā (at the time of offering libations).

67b-68a. I shall narrate to you completely how she became a queen, whose daughter she was, and who were her children. Since Bhūḥ renders human beings, Pitṛs and Devas free from hunger through the medicinal herbs from her womb, and nectar, it is remembered as Nikṣubhā.

I shall explain fully how Rājñī (Queen) became so, how the sons were born etc.

68b. Marīci is the son of Brahmā and Kaśyapa is remembered as Mārīca (son of Marīci).

## \|\| 1.11.69 \|\|

*tasmāddhiraṇyakaśipuḥ prahrādastasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*prahrādasya suto nāmnā virocana iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. From him was born Hiraṇyakaśipu. Prahlāda was his son. The son of Prahlāda is remembered by the name Virocana.

## \|\| 1.11.70 \|\|

*virocanasya bhaginī saṃjñā yā jananī tu sā \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipoḥ pautrī diteḥ putrasya sā smṛtā \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Virocana’s sister is the mother of Saṃjñā. She is remembered as the granddaughter of Hiraṇyakaśipu, son of Diti.

## \|\| 1.11.71 \|\|

*sā viśvakarmaṇaḥ patnī prāhlādī procyate budhaiḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. That daughter of Prahlāda is mentioned as the wife of Viśvakarman by learned ones.

## \|\| 1.11.72 \|\|

*atha nāmnātirūpeti marīciduhitā śubhā \|*  
*patnī hyaṃgirasaḥ sā tu jananī ca bṛhaspateḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. There was a splendid daughter of Marīci, Atirūpā by name. She was the wife of Aṅgiras and the mother of Bṛhaspati.

## \|\| 1.11.73 \|\|

*bṛhaspatestu bhaginī viśrutā brahmavādinī \|*  
*prabhāsasya tu sā patnī vasūnāmaṣṭamasya vai \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Bṛhaspati’s sister Viśrūtā was an expounder of Brahman. She was the wife of Prabhāsa, the eighth one among Vasus.

## \|\| 1.11.74 \|\|

*prasūtā viśvakarmāṇaṃ sarvaśilpavatāṃ varam \|*  
*sa caiva nāmnā tvaṣṭā tu punastridaśavārddhakiḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. She gave birth to Viśvakarman, the most excellent one among artists and craftsman. By the name of Tvaṣṭṛ, he became the Architect of Devas.

## \|\| 1.11.75 \|\|

*devācāryasya tasyeyaṃ duhitā viśvakarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*sureṇuriti vikhyātā triṣu lokeṣu bhāminī \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. The daughter of the preceptor of Devas is well-known in all the three worlds as Sureṇu. She became the wife of Viśvakarman.

## \|\| 1.11.76 \|\|

*prahrādaputrī yā proktā bhāryā vaṣṭustu sā smṛtā \|*  
*tasyāṃ sa janayāmāsa putrīstā lokamātaraḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. The daughter of Prahlāda who has been mentioned earlier is remembered as the wife of Tvaṣṭṛ. He begot of her the daughters (called) Lokamātaraḥ \[=Lokamātṛ?\] (Mother of the worlds).

## \|\| 1.11.77 \|\|

*rājñī saṃjñā ca dyaustvaṣṭrī prabhā saiva vibhāvyate \|*  
*tasyāstu valayā chāyā nikṣubhā sā mahīyasī \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. She is known as Dyau, Saṃjñā, Rājñī, Tvaṣṭrī and Prabhā. Valayā is her shadow. She is noble-minded Nikṣubhā.

## \|\| 1.11.78 \|\|

*sā tu bhāryā bhagavatī mārtaṃḍasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*sādhvī pativratā devī rūpayauvanaśālinī \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. She was a chaste divine lady and wife of the noble-souled Mārtaṇḍa. She was endowed with beauty and youth.

## \|\| 1.11.79-80 \|\|

*na tu tāṃ nararūpeṇa bhāryāṃ bhajati vai purā \|*  
*ādityasyeha taptatvaṃ mahatā svena tejasā \|\| 79 \|\|*

*gātreṣvapratirūpeṣu māsikāṃtamivābhavat \|*  
*saṃjñā ca raviṇā dṛṣṭā nimīlayati locane \|*  
*yatastataḥ saroṣo'rkaḥ saṃjñāṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 80 \|\|*

79-80. He did not approach her in the form of a man. Āditya blazed with his fiery refulgence. That refulgence scorched her unrivalled limbs. On being looked at by Ravi, Saṃjñā used to close her eyes. Hence Sun got angry and spoke these words to Saṃjñā:

## \|\| 1.11.81 \|\|

*raviruvāca \|*  
*mayi dṛṣṭe sadā yasmātkuruṣe netrasaṃkṣayam \|*  
*tasmājjaniṣyase mūḍhe prajāsaṃyamanaṃ yamam \|\| 81 \|\|*

Ravi said:

81\. Whenever I am seen, you close your eyes. Hence, O foolish woman, you will give birth to Yama, the restrainer of the subjects.

## \|\| 1.11.82 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tataḥ sā capalā dṛṣṭiṃ devī cakre bhayākulā \|*  
*vilolitadṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvā punarāha ca tāṃ raviḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

82\. Thereupon, the terrified lady made her eyes tremulous. On seeing her with tremulous eyes, Ravi said to her again:

## \|\| 1.11.83 \|\|

*raviruvāca \|*  
*yasmādvilolitā dṛṣṭirmayi dṛṣṭe tvayā punaḥ \|*  
*tasmādvilolāṃ tanayāṃ nadīṃ tvaṃ prasaviṣyasi \|\| 83 \|\|*

Ravi said:

83\. Since, on seeing me you made your eyes tremulous, you will give birth to a daughter, an unsteady river.

## \|\| 1.11.84 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tatastasyāstu saṃjajñe bhartṛśāpena tena vai \|*  
*yamaśca yamunā ceyaṃ prakhyātā sumahānadī \|*  
*tṛtīyaṃ ca sutaṃ jajñe śrāddhadevaṃ manuṃ śubham \|\| 84 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

84\. Then, due to the husband’s curse, Yama and the well-known great river Yamunā were born of her. She gave birth to a third son, the auspicious Manu Śrāddhadeva.

## \|\| 1.11.85 \|\|

*sāpi saṃjñā ravestejo golākāraṃ mahāprabham \|*  
*asahantī ca sā citte cintayāmāsa vai tadā \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Unable to endure red-hot iron-ball like refulgence of Ravi, Saṃjñā began to think within her mind:

## \|\| 1.11.86 \|\|

*kiṃ karomi kva yāsyāmi kva gatāyāśca nirvṛtiḥ \|*  
*bhavenmama kathaṃ bhartā kopamarkkaśca neṣyati \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. ‘What shall I do? Where shall I go? Where will I get relief? How can it be that my husband Arka does not get angry?’

## \|\| 1.11.87 \|\|

*iti saṃcintya bahudhā prajāpatisutā tadā \|*  
*bahu mene mahābhāgā pitṛsaṃśrayameva ca \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. After thinking thus in various ways, the daughter of the Patriarch, the highly esteemed lady, approved of the plan of resorting to her father.

## \|\| 1.11.88-89 \|\|

*tataḥ pitṛgṛhaṃ gantuṃ kṛtabuddhiryaśasvinī \|*  
*chāyāmayīmātmatanuṃ pratyaṃgamiva nirmitām \|\| 88 \|\|*

*sammukhaṃ prekṣya tāṃ devīṃ svāṃ chāyāṃ vākyamabravīt \|\| 89 \|\|*

88-89. After deciding to go to her father’s house, the lady of great renown looked at her own reflection (Chāyā), which appeared to be made similar to her in every limb. Seeing that divine being in front of her, her own Chāyā, she spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.11.90 \|\|

*saṃjñovāca \|*  
*ahaṃ yāsyāmi bhadraṃ te svakaṃ ca bhavanaṃ pituḥ \|*  
*nirvikāraṃ tvayā tvatra stheyaṃ macchāsanācchubhe \|\| 90 \|\|*

Saṃjñā said:

90\. Welfare unto you. I am going to the abode of my father. O splendid one, at my bidding you should stay here without any change (in behaviour).

## \|\| 1.11.91 \|\|

*imau ca bālakau mahyaṃ kanyā ca varavarṇinī \|*  
*saṃbhāvyā naiva cākhyeyamidaṃ bhagavate tvayā \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. These two sons of mine and this girl of excellent complexion should be well looked after. This should not be mentioned by you to my Lord.

## \|\| 1.11.92 \|\|

*pṛṣṭayāpi na vācyaṃ te tathaitadgamanaṃ mama \|*  
*tenāsmi nāmasaṃjñeti vācyase tatpratiṣṭhayā \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Even when asked, this departure of mine should not be divulged by you. If you are to be addressed by my name Saṃjña behave accordingly (as if you are Saṃjña) to carry out my part.

## \|\| 1.11.93 \|\|

*chāyovāca \|*  
*ā keśagrahaṇāddevi ā śāpānnaiva karhicit \|*  
*ākhyāsyāmi mataṃ tubhyaṃ gamyatāṃ yatra vāṃchitam \|\| 93 \|\|*

Chāyā said:

93\. Unless and until I am caught hold of by my tresses, until I am cursed, I will not mention your secret. You may go wherever you desire.

## \|\| 1.11.94 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*ityuktā sā tadā devī jagāma bhavanaṃ pituḥ \|*  
*dadarśa tatra tvaṣṭāraṃ tapasā dhūtakalmaṣam \|\| 94 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

94\. On being told thus, the great lady went to her father’s abode. There she saw Tvaṣṭṛ who had washed away all sins by means of penance.

## \|\| 1.11.95 \|\|

*bahumānācca tenāpi pūjitā viśvakarmaṇā \|*  
*varṣāṇāṃ ca sahasraṃ tu vasamānā piturgṛhe \|*  
*tasthau pitṛgṛhe sā tu kiṃcitkālamaniṃditā \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. For a thousand years she stayed in the abode of her father. Due respect was paid by Viśvakarman. The uncensured lady still continued her stay in the abode of her father.

## \|\| 1.11.96 \|\|

*tatastāṃ prāha cārvaṃgīṃ pitā nāticiroṣitām \|*  
*stutvā tu tanayāṃ premṇā bahumānapuraḥsaram \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Not long after that stay, the father said to the lady of beautiful limbs. He praised his daughter with affection and consideration.

## \|\| 1.11.97 \|\|

*viśvakarmovāca \|*  
*tvāmeva paśyato vatse dināni subahūnyapi \|*  
*muhūrtārddhasamāni syuḥ kiṃ tu dharmo vilupyate \|\| 97 \|\|*

Viśvakarman said:

97\. My dear, on seeing you even many many days appear as though half a Muhūrta. But thereby there is violation of Dharma.

## \|\| 1.11.98 \|\|

*bāṃdhaveṣu ciraṃ vāso nārīṇāṃ na yaśaskaraḥ \|*  
*manorathā bāṃdhavānāṃ nāryā bhartṛgṛhe sthitiḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Continued stay with kinsmen is not conducive to the reputation of a woman. Her stay in her own husband’s house is what is desired by all the relatives of a woman.

## \|\| 1.11.99 \|\|

*sā tvaṃ trailokyanāthena bhartrā sūryeṇa saṃyutā \|*  
*piturgṛhe ciraṃ kālaṃ vastuṃ nārhasi putrike \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. You are united in wedlock with your husband Sūrya, the Lord of the three worlds, O my dear daughter, it does not behove you to stay in the abode of your father for a long time.

## \|\| 1.11.100 \|\|

*tattvaṃ bhartṛgṛhaṃ gaccha dṛṣṭo'haṃ pūjitāsi me \|*  
*punarāgamanaṃ kāryaṃ darśanāya śucismite \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Hence do go to your husband’s place. You have seen me and have been duly honoured by me. You should come again, O lady of pure smiles, to see me.

## \|\| 1.11.101-105 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*ityuktā sā tadā pitrā gacchagaccheti sā punaḥ \|*  
*saṃpūjayitvā pitaraṃ vaḍavārūpadhāriṇī \|\| 101 \|\|*

*meroruttaratastatra varṣaṃ yaddhanuṣākṛti \|*  
*uttarāḥ kuravo loke prakhyātā ye yaśasvini \|\| 102 \|\|*

*tatra tepe tapaḥ sādhvī nirāhārā'śvarūpiṇī \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare devi tasyāśchāyā vivasvataḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

*samīpasthā tadā devī saṃjñāyā vākyatatparā \|*  
*tasyāṃ ca bhagavānsūryo dvitīyāyāṃ divaspatiḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

*saṃjñeyamiti manvāno rūpaudāryeṇa mohitaḥ \|*  
*tasyāṃ ca janayāmāsa dvau putrau kanyakāṃ tathā \|\| 105 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

101-105. On being told thus by her father, “Do go! Do go! repeatedly, she. duly took leave of her father with due veneration.

She assumed the form of a mare. There is a Varṣa (continent) to the north of Meru. It has the shape of a bow. O lady of renown, it is well-known in the world as Uttara Kuru.

The chaste lady in the form of a mare, abstained from food and performed penance there.

In the meantime, her Chāyā, the divine lady, wished to abide by her own promise to Saṃjñā and stayed near Vivasvān (Sun).

Lord Sūrya, the Lord of the heaven, became enamoured of her exalted beauty. He begot of this second wife two sons and a daughter.

## \|\| 1.11.106 \|\|

*pūrvaṃ yastu manostulyaḥ sāvarṇistena so'bhavat \|*  
*yaḥ sūryātprathamaṃ jātaḥ putrayoḥ surasundari \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Of the two sons, O beautiful lady of Suras, he who was born first from Sun became similar to Manu. Therefore, he became (known as) Sāvarṇi.

## \|\| 1.11.107 \|\|

*dvitīyo yo'bhavaccānyaḥ sa graho'bhūcchanaiścaraḥ \|*  
*kanyā 'bhūttapatī yā tāṃ vavre saṃvaraṇo nṛpaḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. The second son who was born became the planet Śanaiścara (Saturn). The girl was Tapatī whom King Saṃvaraṇa wooed.

## \|\| 1.11.108 \|\|

*tāpīnāma nadī ceyaṃ viṃdhyamūlādviniḥsṛtā \|*  
*nityaṃ puṇyajalā snāne paścimodadhigāminī \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. This river named Tāpī rose from the foot of Vindhya. Her waters are always auspicious for a bath. She flowed into the western ocean.

## \|\| 1.11.109-111 \|\|

*anyā caiva tathā bhadrā jātā putrī mahāprabhā \|*  
*saṃjñā tu pārthivī chāyā ātmajānāṃ yathākarot \|\| 109 \|\|*

*snehaṃ na pūrvajātānāṃ tathā kṛtavatī satī \|*  
*lālanādyupabhogeṣu viśeṣamanuvāsaram \|\| 110 \|\|*

*yathā sveṣvanuvarteta na tathānyeṣu bhāminī \|*  
*manustu kṣāṃtavāṃstasyā bhaviṣyo yo hi pārvati \|\| 111 \|\|*

109-111. This daughter of great refulgence was extraordinarily blessed and prosperous.

The Pārthivī (Earthy) Chāyā did not show the same affection as Saṃjñā had shown towards her children by means of fondling and feeding well. The lady did not behave towards the others as she did towards her own children. O Pārvatī, the future Manu continued to forbear this behaviour of hers.

## \|\| 1.11.112 \|\|

*merau tiṣṭhati so'dyāpi tapaḥ kurvanvarānane \|*  
*sarvaṃ tatkṣāṃtavānmāturyamastasyā na cakṣame \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. O lady of excellent countenance, he (Manu) continues to stay on Meru even today performing penance. He was patient with his mother forbearingly but this was not the case with Yama.

## \|\| 1.11.113-114 \|\|

*bahuśo yācamānastu chāyayā'tīva kopitaḥ \|*  
*sa vai kopācca bālyācca bhāvino'rthasya vai balāt \|\| 113 \|\|*

*tāḍanāya tataḥ kopātpādastena samudyataḥ \|*  
*tathā punaḥ kṣāṃtimatā na tu dehe nipātitaḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

113-114. He used to beg for his requirements (of food or eatables) many times. Due to his childishness and anger as well as due to the inevitability of the destiny, the foot was raised by him to kick her but, due to forbearance, he did not place his foot on her person.

## \|\| 1.11.115 \|\|

*padā saṃtarjayāmāsa chāyāṃ saṃjñāsuto yamaḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. Yama, the son of Saṃjñā, threatened Chāyā with his foot.

## \|\| 1.11.116 \|\|

*taṃ śaśāpa tataśchāyā kruddhā sā pārthivī bhṛśam \|*  
*kiṃcitprasphuramāṇoṣṭhī vicalatpāṇipallavā \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. The earthy Chāyā became excessively angry. With lips throbbing slightly and the sprout-like hands moving, she cursed:

## \|\| 1.11.117 \|\|

*chāyovāca \|*  
*pituḥ patnīmamaryāda yanmāṃ tarjayase padā \|*  
*bhuvi tasmādayaṃ pādastavādyaiva patiṣyati \|\| 117 \|\|*

Chāyā said:

117\. O Amaryāda (one who transgresses the bounds of propriety), you threaten me, your father’s wife, with your foot. Hence this foot of yours will drop down today itself.

## \|\| 1.11.118 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*yamastu tena śāpena bhṛśaṃ pīḍitamānasaḥ \|*  
*manunā saha dharmātmā pitre sarvaṃ nyavedayat \|\| 118 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

118\. Tormented much in his mind due to that curse, Yama, the righteous Soul, intimated everything to his father along with Manu.

## \|\| 1.11.119 \|\|

*yama uvāca \|*  
*tātaitanmahadāścaryaṃ na dṛṣṭamiha kenacit \|*  
*mātā vātsalyamutsṛjya śāpaṃ putre prayacchati \|\| 119 \|\|*

Yama said:

119\. Dear father, this is indeed highly surprising. It has never been seen by anyone that a mother gives up her maternal affection and heaps a curse on her son.

## \|\| 1.11.120 \|\|

*snehena tulyamasmāsu mātādya naiva varttate \|*  
*visṛjya jyāyaso yasmātkanīyaḥsu bubhūṣati \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. Mother does not behave impartially with us. Ignoring the seniors, she tends to become more affectionate towards the juniors.

## \|\| 1.11.121 \|\|

*tasyā mayodyataḥ pādo na tu dehe nipātitaḥ \|*  
*bālyādvā yadi vā mohāttadbhavānkṣaṃtumarhati \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. Due to childishness, it may be, or due to delusion, I lifted up my foot against her, Of course. But it was restrained from touching her. You may be pleased to forgive me.

## \|\| 1.11.122 \|\|

*śapto'haṃ tāta kopena tayā suta iti sphuṭam \|*  
*ato na mahyaṃ jananī sā bhavedvadatāṃ vara \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. This is clear that I, a son, have been cursed by her in anger. Hence, O foremost one among the eloquent ones, she is obviously not mother.

## \|\| 1.11.123 \|\|

*nigurṇeṣvapi putreṣu na mātā nirguṇā bhavet \|*  
*pādaste patatāṃ putra kathametattayoditam \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. A son may be unmannerly but the mother ought not to be bereft of consideration for him. How did she manage to utter, “Son, your foot shall drop down.”

## \|\| 1.11.124 \|\|

*tava prasādāccaraṇo na patedbhagavanyathā \|*  
*mātṛśāpādayaṃ me'dya tathā ciṃtaya gopate \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. O Lord of rays, O holy Sir, with your favour, let not the foot fall down as a result of this curse of my mother. Think out means to this effect.

## \|\| 1.11.125 \|\|

*raviruvāca \|*  
*asaṃśayaṃ mahatputra bhaviṣyatyatra kāraṇam \|*  
*yena te hyāviśatkrodho dharmajñasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

Ravi said:

125\. Dear son, undoubtedly there must be a strong reason in this matter, since you, a noble-souled one conversant with Dharma, got enraged.

## \|\| 1.11.126 \|\|

*sarveṣāmeva śāpānāṃ pratighāto'pi vidyate \|*  
*na tu mātrābhiśaptānāṃ kvacicchāpanivarttanam \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. There is a remedy too in the case of all curses, but there is no redemption to those cursed by mother.

## \|\| 1.11.127 \|\|

*na yuktametanmithyā tu kartuṃ māturvacastava \|*  
*kiṃcitte saṃvidhāsyāmi putrasnehādanugraham \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. It is not proper to make your mother’s words false and so ineffective. But out of my filial affection for you, I will try to bring about some blessings.

## \|\| 1.11.128 \|\|

*kṛmayo māṃsamādāya prayāsyaṃti mahītalam \|*  
*kṛtaṃ tasyā vacaḥ satyaṃ tvaṃ ca trāto bhaviṣyasi \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. Worms will scrape up some flesh from your leg and go down to the earth. Thereby her words will be true and you will also be not affected.

## \|\| 1.11.129-131 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*ādityastvabravīcchāyāṃ kimarthaṃ tanayeṣu vai \|*  
*tulyeṣvapyadhikaḥ sneha ekatra kriyate tvayā \|\| 129 \|\|*

*nūnaṃ na caiṣāṃ jananī tvaṃ saṃjñā kvāpi sā gatā \|*  
*vikaleṣvapyapatyeṣu na mātā śāpadā bhavet \|\| 130 \|\|*

*api doṣasahasrāṇi yadi putraḥ samācaret \|*  
*prāṇadrohe'pi nirato na mātā pāpamācaret \|*  
*tasmātsatyaṃ mama brūhi mā śāpavaśagā bhava \|\| 131 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

129-131. Āditya said to Chāyā, “When all the children are equal, why should partiality be shown towards one?

Certainly you are not the mother of these children. That Saṃjñā has gone away somewhere. Even in the case of her defective children, a mother does not utter a curse.

A son may commit thousands of blunders and misdeeds. He may even threaten her life. But the mother should not react sinfully. Hence tell me the truth. Do not get cursed (by me).”

## \|\| 1.11.132-134 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*taṃ śaptumudyataṃ dṛṣṭvā chāyāsaṃjñā dinādhipam \|*  
*bhayena kaṃpatī devī yathāvṛttaṃ mahāsatī \|\| 132 \|\|*

*sā cāha tanayā tvaṣṭurahaṃ saṃjñā vibhāvaso \|*  
*patnī tava tvayā patyā patiyuktā divākara \|\| 133 \|\|*

*itthaṃ vivasvataḥ sā tu bahuśaḥ pṛcchato'nyathā \|*  
*na vācā bhāṣate kruddhaḥ śāpaṃ dātuṃ samudyataḥ \|\| 134 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

132-134. On seeing the Lord of the Day ready to curse the Reflection (Shadow) of Saṃjñā, she trembled with fear. She narrated what had happened.

## \|\| 1.11.135 \|\|

*śāpodyatakaraṃ dṛṣṭvā sūryaṃ chāyā vivasvataḥ \|*  
*kathayāmāsa tatsarvaṃ saṃjñāyāḥ suviceṣṭitam \|\| 135 \|\|*

The great chaste fair lady said: “I am the daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ, O Vibhāvasu (Sun), O Divākara (Sun), I have my husband in you.”

Though Vivasvān (Sun) asked many times, she said only thus and not otherwise. He became angry and got ready to curse her.

135\. On seeing Sun ready to curse, Chāyā told everything regarding Saṃjñā’s well designed act to Vivasvān.

## \|\| 1.11.136 \|\|

*tacchrutvā bhagavānsūryo jagāma tvaṣṭurālayam \|*  
*tataḥ saṃpūjayāmāsa tadā trailokyapūjitam \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. On hearing it Lord Sun went to the abode of Tvaṣṭṛ. He honoured (Sun) who is adored by all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.11.137 \|\|

*nirdagdhukāmaṃ roṣeṇa sāntvayāmāsa pārvati \|*  
*bhāsvaṃtaṃ nijayā dīptyā nijagehamupāgatam \|*  
*kva saṃjñeti ca pṛcchantaṃ kathayāmāsa viśvakṛt \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. O Pārvatī, when the Sun-god came to his house and intending to burn down him (Viśvakarmā) with his dazzling refulgence demanded, “Where is Saṃjñā”? He (Viśvakarmā) pacified him and told:

## \|\| 1.11.138-140 \|\|

*viśvakarmmovāca \|*  
*āgataiva hi me veśma bhavatā śrūyatāṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*vikhyātaṃ tejasā'ḍhyaṃ ta idaṃ rūpaṃ suduḥsaham \|\| 138 \|\|*

*asahantī tataḥ saṃjñā vane carati vai tapaḥ \|*  
*drakṣyase tāṃ bhavānadya svabhāryāṃ śubhacāriṇīm \|\| 139 \|\|*

*rūpārthaṃ carate'raṇyaṃ caraṃtī sumahattapaḥ \|*  
*mataṃ me brahmaṇo vākyādyadi te deva rocate \|*  
*rūpaṃ nirvarttayāmyadya tava kāṃtaṃ divaspate \|\| 140 \|\|*

138-140. “Let my words by heard by you. Indeed she came to my abode. Unable to endure this fiery, well-known refulgence of yours, Saṃjñā performs penance roaming about in the forest.

You will see your wife of auspicious activities today itself, performing a great penance for the sake of (your) excellent form.

This I became aware through the words of Brahmā, O Lord, if it is approved of by you, O Lord of heaven, I shall make your refulgence attractive.”

## \|\| 1.11.141 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*yato hi bhāsvato rūpaṃ prāgāsītparimaṃḍalam \|*  
*tatastatheti taṃ prāha tvaṣṭāraṃ bhagavānraviḥ \|\| 141 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

141\. Since Bhāsvān’s earlier form was of the nature of an orb, Lord Hari (the Sun-god) said to Tvaṣṭṛ, “So be it”.

## \|\| 1.11.142 \|\|

*viśvakarmātvanujñātaḥ śākadvīpe vivasvatā \|*  
*bhṛ mimāropya tattejaḥ śātanāyopacakrame \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. On being permitted by Vivasvān, Viśvakarman placed him on a lathe and prepared to whet his refulgence in Śākadvīpa.

## \|\| 1.11.143 \|\|

*bhramatā'śeṣajagatāmadhibhūtena bhāsvatā \|*  
*samudrā draviṇopetāścukṣubhuśca samantataḥ \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. While Bhāsvān, the Lord of all living beings, began to whirl, the oceans along with all the materials within became agitated all round.

## \|\| 1.11.144 \|\|

*bhramatā khalu deveśi sacaṃdragrahatārakam \|*  
*adhogati mahābhāge babhūvākṣiptamākulam \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. O highly esteemed goddess of Devas, everything including Moon, the planets and the stars was pulled (by Sun) who was whirling. They began to fall down and become upset.

## \|\| 1.11.145 \|\|

*vikṣiptasalilāḥ sarve babhūvuśca tathā nadāḥ \|*  
*vyabhidyaṃta tathā śailāḥ śīrṇasānunibaṃdhanāḥ \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. The waters in all the rivers were thrown up. The mountains split with all their peaks and ridges broken up.

## \|\| 1.11.146 \|\|

*dhruvādhārāṇyaśeṣāṇi dhiṣṇyāni varavarṇini \|*  
*bhrāmyadraśminibaddhāni adho jagmuḥ sahasraśaḥ \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. O lady of excellent complexion, all the heavenly abodes having the support of Dhruva went down in their thousands when the rays that bound them together snapped in the course of their whirling.

## \|\| 1.11.147 \|\|

*vyaśīryaṃta mahāmeghā ghorārāvavirāviṇaḥ \|*  
*bhāsvadbhramaṇavibhrāṃtabhūmyākāśamahītalam \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. When the sky and the surface of the earth became shaky as Bhāsvān whirled the massive clouds became shattered producing terribly loud thunders.

## \|\| 1.11.148 \|\|

*jagadākulamatyarthaṃ tadā'sīdvaravarṇini \|*  
*trailokye sakale devi bhramamāṇe maharṣaryaḥ \|*  
*devāśca brahmaṇā sārddhaṃ bhāsvaṃtamabhituṣṭuvuḥ \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. Then, O lady of excellent complexion, the whole universe became extremely confounded and chaotic. O goddess, as the entire range of the three worlds whirled the great sages and Devas eulogized Bhāsvān along with Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.11.149-150 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*ādidevo'si devānāṃ jātametatsvayaṃ tava \|*  
*sargasthityaṃtakāleṣu tridhā bhedena tiṣṭhasi \|\| 149 \|\|*

*svasti te'stu jagannātha gharmavarṣahimākara \|*  
*iṃdra āgamya taṃ devaṃ likhyamānamathāstavīt \|*  
*jaya deva jagatsvāmiñjaya deva jagatpate \|\| 150 \|\|*

Devas said:

149 -150. You are the primordial Lord of Devas. This entire universe was born of you. You stand in three different forms at the times of creation, sustenance and annihilation. Hail unto you, O Lord of the universe, who are the source of heat, rain, shower and cold (i.e. three seasons, Summer, Rains and Winter).

Indra came and eulogized that Lord as he was being whetted: “Be victorious, O Lord, O Lord of the universe, be victorious, O master of the universe.”

## \|\| 1.11.151 \|\|

*ṛṣayaśca tataḥ sapta vasiṣṭhātripurogamāḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭuvurvividhaiḥ stotraiḥ svasti svastīti vādinaḥ \|*  
*vedoktibhirathāgryābhirvālakhilyāśca tuṣṭuvuḥ \|\| 151 \|\|*

151\. Then the seven sages with Vasiṣṭha, and Atri as leaders, eulogized with different kinds of prayers. They began to say loudly, “Hail! Hail!” Then the Vālakhilyas eulogized with the excellent words of the Vedas:

## \|\| 1.11.152 \|\|

*vālakhilyā ūcuḥ \|*  
*namasta ṛksvarūpāya sāmarūpāya te namaḥ \|*  
*yajuḥsvarūparūpāya sāmnāṃ dhāmaga te namaḥ \|\| 152 \|\|*

Vālakhilyas said:

152\. Obeisance to you in the form of Ṛks. Obeisance to you of the form of Sāmans. Obeisance to you having the form comprising Yajus Mantras. O Dhāmaga (one who has occupied the abode) of Sāmans, obeisance to you.

## \|\| 1.11.153 \|\|

*jñānaikarūpadehāya nirdhūtatamase namaḥ \|*  
*śuddhajyotiḥsvarūpāya trimūrtāyāmalātmane \|\| 153 \|\|*

153\. Obeisance to one whose sole form and body is perfect knowledge. Obeisance to one who has quelled darkness (or ignorance). Obeisance to one whose form is the pure refulgence. Obeisance to one who is personified Trinity. Obeisance to the Ātman free from impurities.

## \|\| 1.11.154 \|\|

*variṣṭhāya vareṇyāya sarvasmai paramātmane \|*  
*namo'khilajagadvyāpirūpāyānaṃtamūrttaye \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. Obeisance to the most excellent one, Obeisance to one who is to be considered the most excellent one. Obeisance to the Supreme Ātman identical with all. Obeisance to one whose form pervades the entire universe. Obeisance to one of endless forms.

## \|\| 1.11.155 \|\|

*sarvakāraṇabhūtāya niṣṭhāya jñāna cetasām \|*  
*namaḥ sūryasvarūpāya prakāśālakṣyarūpiṇe \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. Obeisance to one who has become the cause of all. Obeisance to one stationed as knowledge in the minds. Obeisance to one in the form of the Sun. Obeisance to one whose form is very difficult to look at due to the dazzling brilliance.

## \|\| 1.11.156 \|\|

*bhāskarāya namastubhyaṃ tathā dinakṛte namaḥ \|*  
*sarvasmai hetave caiva saṃdhyājyo tsnākṛte namaḥ \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. Obeisance to you, Bhāskara (Creator of brilliance). Obeisance to Dinakṛt (the cause of day). Obeisance to the entire cause of all. Obeisance to the creator of twilight and moonlight.

## \|\| 1.11.157 \|\|

*tvaṃ sarvametadbhagavañjagacca bhramatā tvayā \|*  
*bhramatyāviśvamakhilaṃ brahmāṃḍaṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*tvadaṃśubhiridaṃ sarvaṃ spṛṣṭaṃ vai jāyate śuci \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. O Lord, you are all this universe. When you whirl everything in the universe, the entire Cosmic Egg including mobile and immobile beings moves. On being touched by your rays all this becomes purified.

## \|\| 1.11.158 \|\|

*kriyate tvatkarasparśairjalādīnāṃ pavitratā \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. Through the contact with your rays purification of waters etc. is brought about.

## \|\| 1.11.159 \|\|

*homadānādiko dharmo nopakārāya jāyate \|*  
*tāta yāvanna saṃyogi jagadetattvadaṃśubhiḥ \|\| 159 \|\|*

159\. O father, as long as this universe does not come into contact with your rays, the holy rites of Homa, Dāna etc. do not come to help (i.e. prove efficacious).

## \|\| 1.11.160 \|\|

*ṛcaste sakalā hyetāstathā yāni yajūṃṣi ca \|*  
*sakalāni ca sāmāni nipataṃti tvadaṃgataḥ \|\| 160 \|\|*

160\. All these Ṛks, all the Yajus Mantras, and all the Sāmans fall from your person.

## \|\| 1.11.161 \|\|

*ṛṅmayastvaṃ jagannātha tvameva ca yajurmayaḥ \|*  
*yataḥ sāmamayaścaiva tato nātha trayīmayaḥ \|\| 161 \|\|*

161\. O Lord of the universe, you are Ṛṅmaya (full of Ṛks, identical with Ṛks). You alone are Yajurmaya (full of Yajus, identical with Yajus). You are Sāmamaya and therefore, O Lord, you are Trayīmaya (identical with the three Vedas).

## \|\| 1.11.162 \|\|

*tvameva brahmaṇo rūpaṃ paraṃ cāparameva ca \|*  
*mūrttāmūrttaṃ tathā sūkṣmaṃ sthūlaṃ rūpeṇa saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 162 \|\|*

162\. You alone are the forms of Brahman viz. Para (the greatest) and Apara (the least); Mūrta (embodied), Amūrta (disembodied), Sthūla (gross) and Sūkṣma (subtle). You abide in all these forms.

## \|\| 1.11.163 \|\|

*nimeṣakāṣṭhādimayaḥ kālarūpakṣaṇātmakaḥ \|*  
*prasīda svecchayā rūpaṃ svaṃ tejaḥ śamanaṃ kuru \|*  
*tvaṃ deva jagatāṃ hetorduḥkhaṃ sahasi duḥsaham \|\| 163 \|\|*

163\. You are identical with the units of time such as Nimeṣa, Kāṣṭhā etc. You are the forms of Kāla such as Kṛṣṇa etc. Be pleased and change your form. Subdue your refulgence willingly. O Lord, for the sake of the worlds, you endure unbearable pain.

## \|\| 1.11.164 \|\|

*tvaṃ nātha mokṣiṇāṃ mokṣo dhyeyastvaṃ dhyāyatāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ gatiḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ karmakāṃḍanivartinām \|\| 164 \|\|*

164\. O Lord, you are salvation unto those yearning for salvation. You are the most excellent Dhyeya (object of meditation) of those who regularly meditate. You are the goal of all living beings who desist from Karmakāṇḍa (rituals).

## \|\| 1.11.165 \|\|

*śaṃ prajābhyo'stu deveśa śanno'stu jagatāṃpate \|\| 165 \|\|*

165\. O Lord of Devas, let there by happiness and prosperity unto the subjects. O Lord of the worlds, let us have happiness and welfare.

## \|\| 1.11.166 \|\|

*tvaṃ dhātā visṛjasi viśvameka eva tvaṃ pātā sthitikaraṇāya saṃpravṛttaḥ \|*  
*tvayyaṃte layamakhilaṃ prayāti caitattvattonyo na hi tapanāsti sarvadātā \|\| 166 \|\|*

166\. You are the creator. You alone create the universe. You are the protector ardently engaged in its sustenance. All this universe will get dissolved in you at the end. O Tapana (Burning One), there is no one other than you who bestows everything.

## \|\| 1.11.167 \|\|

*tvaṃ brahmā hariharasaṃjñitastvamindro vitteśaḥ pitṛpitaraṃbupaḥ samīraḥ \|*  
*somo'gnirgaganamahādharādirūpaḥ kiṃ na tvaṃ sakalamanorathapradātā \|\| 167 \|\|*

167\. You are Brahmā. You are termed Hari and Hara. You are Indra. You are the Lord of Wealth (Kubera). You are Pitṛpati, Aṃbupa (Varuṇa), Wind-god, Soma (Moon), fire, one having the forms of sky, great mountain etc. Are not you the bestower of all desires?

## \|\| 1.11.168 \|\|

*yajñaistvāmanudinamātmakarmmasaktāḥ stuvanto vividhapadairdvijā yajaṃti \|*  
*dhyāyantaḥ savinayacetaso bhavantaṃ yogasthāḥ paramapadaṃ prayāṃti marttyā \|\| 168 \|\|*

168\. Brāhmaṇas assiduously engaged in their respective duties eulogize you with diverse kinds of Padas (words, songs, prayers) and perform Yajñas everyday. Men engaged in Yogic practice meditate on you with humility in their minds and attain the greatest goal (Mokṣa).

## \|\| 1.11.169 \|\|

*tapasi pacasi viśvaṃ pāsi bhasmīkaroṣi prakaṭayasi mayūkhairhlādayatasyaṃśugarbhaiḥ \|*  
*sṛjasi kamalajanmā pālayasyacyutākhyaḥ kṣapayasi ca yugāṃte rudrarūpastvamekaḥ \|\| 169 \|\|*

169\. You scorch and cook the universe, protect it, reduce it to ashes and make it manifest. You delight the universe with your rays filled with water. You create as the Lotus-born (Brahmā). You protect with the name Acyuta. At the end of the Yuga, you annihilate everything in the sole form of Rudra.

## \|\| 1.11.170 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*likhamānastato bhānuṃ viśvakarmā prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*udbhūtapulakaḥ stotramidaṃcakre vivasvataḥ \|\| 170 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

170\. Even as he scraped and whetted Bhānu (Sun) Viśvakarman, the patriarch, experienced horripilation. He eulogized Vivasvān thus:

\[Viśvakarman’s Prayer:\]

## \|\| 1.11.171 \|\|

*vivasvate praṇatajanānukampine mahātmane samajavasaptasaptaye \|*  
*satejase kamalakulālibaṃdhave sadā tamaḥpaṭalapaṭāvapāṭine \|\| 171 \|\|*

171\. Obeisance to Vivasvān who shows mercy on the people who bow down. Obeisance to the noble-souled one who has seven horses of equal speed. Obeisance to the brilliant one, the kinsman of the clusters of lotuses and bees. Obeisance to the destroyer of the curtain of darkness.

## \|\| 1.11.172 \|\|

*pāvanātiśayasarvacakṣuṣe naikakāmaviṣayapradāyine \|*  
*bhāsurāmalamayūkhamāline sarvabhūtahitakāriṇe namaḥ \|\| 172 \|\|*

172\. Obeisance to the Lord who surpasses all in sanctity, who has an eye on everyone (is all-seeing); who bestows many objects of desire, who has a number of shining rays devoid of impurities, and who does everything conducive to the welfare of all living beings.

## \|\| 1.11.173 \|\|

*ajāya lokatrayabhāvanāya bhūtātmane gopataye vṛṣāya \|*  
*namo mahākāruṇikottamāya sūryāya vastuprabhavālayāya \|\| 173 \|\|*

173\. Obeisance to the excellent Lord of rays who is unborn, who is the conceiver and creator of the three worlds, who is the soul of the living beings, who is the most excellent of all compassionate ones. Obeisance to Sūrya, the source of origin and dissolution of all objects.

## \|\| 1.11.174 \|\|

*vivasvate jñānabhṛte'ntarātmane jagatpratiṣṭhāya jagaddhitaiṣiṇe \|*  
*svayaṃbhuve nirmalalokacakṣuṣe surottamāyāmitatejase namaḥ \|\| 174 \|\|*

174\. Obeisance to Vivasvān who possesses perfect knowledge, who is the immanent soul, who is the support of the universe, who desires the welfare of the universe, who is self-born, who is the eye of the world and free from impurities, who is the most excellent of all Suras and whose refulgence is unlimited.

## \|\| 1.11.175 \|\|

*kṣaṇamudayācalabhālitārcciḥ suragaṇagītigariṣṭhagītaḥ \|*  
*tvamuta mayūkhasahasravajjagati vikāsitapadmanābhaḥ \|\| 175 \|\|*

175\. In a moment you shine on the top of Udayācala (Mountain where the Sun rises) even as the groups of Suras sing about you in excellent songs. You are like the Lotus-navelled Lord in the world covered with thousands of rays.

## \|\| 1.11.176 \|\|

*tava timirāsavapānamadādbhavati vilohitavigrahatā \|*  
*mihiravibhāsatayā sutarāṃ tribhuvanabhāvanamātraparaḥ \|\| 176 \|\|*

176\. O Mihira (Sun), your physical form assumes red hue due to the inebriation resulting from the drinking of the liquor of darkness. By your refulgence you are intent on sanctifying the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.11.177 \|\|

*rathamāruhya samāvayavaṃ ruciravikalitadivyahayam \|*  
*satatamaribale bhagavaṃścarasi jagaddhitabaddharasaḥ \|\| 177 \|\|*

177\. You ride on a chariot of symmetrical parts having divine shining horses, not at all defective. O Lord, you always move among the hordes of enemies because of your interest in the welfare of the universe.

## \|\| 1.11.178 \|\|

*amṛtamayena rasena samaṃ vibudhapitṝnapi tarppayase \|*  
*arigaṇasūdana tena tava praṇatimupetya likhāmi vapuḥ \|\| 178 \|\|*

178\. You propitiate the Pitṛs of Devas too with the nectareous juice. O destroyer of enemies, therefore, I bow down to you and whet and scrape your body.

## \|\| 1.11.179 \|\|

*śubhasamavarṇamayaṃ racitaṃ tava padapāṃsupavitratamam \|*  
*natajanavatsala māṃ praṇataṃ tribhuvanapāvana pāhi rave \|\| 179 \|\|*

179\. O Ravi fond of the people who bow down, O sanctifier of the three worlds, I bow down to you. I am dejected. Make me one with splendid complexion and one rendered very holy through the dust from your feet. Oh, protect me.

## \|\| 1.11.180 \|\|

*iti sakalajagatprasūti bhūtaṃ tribhuvanabhāvanadhāmahetumekam \|*  
*ravimakhilajagatpradīpabhūtaṃ tridaśavaraṃ praṇato'smi devadevam \|\| 180 \|\|*

180\. Thus, I bow down to Ravi, the most excellent one among Devas. You are Lord of Devas. You are a light unto the whole of the world. You are the progenitor of the entire universe. You are the sole cause of the refulgence that creates the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.11.181 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*hāhāhūhaśca gandharvo nāradastuṃbarustathā \|*  
*upagātuṃ samārabdhā gāṃdharvakuśalā ravim \|\| 181 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

181\. Those who were expert in the art of music such as Gandharvas, Hāhā and Hūhū as well as Nārada and Tuṃburu, began to sing in praise of Ravi.

## \|\| 1.11.182-188 \|\|

*ṣaḍjamadhyamagāṃdhāragrāmatrayaviśāradāḥ \|*  
*mūrchanābhiśca tānaiśca suprayogaiḥ sukhapradam \|\| 182 \|\|*

*saptasvaravinirvṛttaṃ yatitrayavibhūṣitam \|*  
*saptadhātusamāyuktaṃ ṣaḍjāti triguṇāśrayam \|\| 183 \|\|*

*caturgītasamāyuktaṃ catuvarṇasamutthitam \|*  
*caturvarṇapratīkāraṃ saptālaṃkārabhūṣitam \|\| 184 \|\|*

*tristhānaśuddhaṃ trilayaṃ samyakkālavyavasthitam \|*  
*citte citte ca nṛtye ca raseṣu layasaṃyutam \|\| 185 \|\|*

*caturviṃśadguṇairyuktaṃ jagurgītaṃ ca gāyanāḥ \|*  
*viśvārcī ca ghṛtācī ca urvaśyatha tilottamā \|\| 186 \|\|*

*menakā sahajanyā ca raṃbhā cāpsarasāṃ varā \|*  
*caturvidhapadaṃ tālaṃ triprakāraṃ layatrayam \|\| 187 \|\|*

*yatitrayaṃ tathā'todyaṃ nāṭyaṃ caiva caturvidham \|*  
*nanṛturjagatāmīśe likhyamāne vibhāvasau \|\| 188 \|\|*

182-188. While Vibhāvasu (Sun), the Lord of the worlds, was being scraped, the songsters sang elaborately. They were experts in the three Grāmas such as Ṣaḍja, Maḍhyama and Gāndhāra. Their songs caused pleasure through Mūrchanās and Tānas well produced. The seven notes of the gamut evolved them and embellished them with the three Yatis (pauses). The seven Dhātus, six Jātis and the three Guṇas were at the basis. The four types of Gīta rose out of the four Varṇas. The four Varṇas (Vargas) were duly repulsed. The seven Alaṅkāras embellished the songs. There was the purity of the three Sthānas. The three Kālas were perfectly set up. In every mind and dance item the Rasas and the Layas were in harmony.

The most excellent Apsarās such as Viśvācī, Ghṛtācī, Urvaśī, Tilottamā, Menakā, Sahajanyā and Raṃbhā duly danced the four types of Padas with three kinds of Tālas and Layas as well as Yatis. There were Ātodyas (musical instruments) and the Nāṭya was of four types.

## \|\| 1.11.189 \|\|

*bhāvānbhāvaviśāradyaḥ kurvantyo vidhivadbahūn \|*  
*devadundubhayaḥ śaṃkhāḥ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 189 \|\|*

189\. These Apsarās were experts in depicting many Bhāvas. There were sounded hundreds of Devadundubhīs (drums) and thousand of conchs.

## \|\| 1.11.190 \|\|

*anāhatā mahādevi nedire ghananisvanāḥ \|*  
*gāyadbhiścaiva gaṃdharvairnṛtyadbhiścāpsarogaṇaiḥ \|\| 190 \|\|*

190\. They sounded without being played and their sounds resembled the rumblings of clouds while Gandharvas sang and groups of Apsarās danced.

## \|\| 1.11.191 \|\|

*avādyaṃta tatastatra veṇuvīṇādijharjharāḥ \|*  
*paṇavāḥ puṣkarāścaiva mṛdaṃgapaṭahānakāḥ \|\| 191 \|\|*

191\. Veṇus (flutes), Viṇās (lutes), Jharjharas (drums and cymbals) and various kinds of drums like Paṇava, Puṣkara, Mṛdaṅga, Paṭaha and Ānaka were sounded.

## \|\| 1.11.192 \|\|

*tūryavāditraghoṣaiśca sarvaṃ kolāhalīkṛtam \|*  
*tataḥ kṛtāṃjalipuṭā bhaktinamrātmamūrttayaḥ \|\| 192 \|\|*

192\. There was a lot of confused sounds from the different musical instruments of Tūrya and Vāditra.

All the people joined their palms in veneration and bowed down humbly due to devotion.

## \|\| 1.11.193 \|\|

*tataḥ kalakale tasminsarvadevasamāgame \|*  
*saṃvatsaraṃ bhramasthasya viśvakarmā ravestataḥ \|\| 193 \|\|*

193\. All the Devas had assembled and there was clangorous hubbub. Viśvakarman kept Ravi on the lathe for a year.

## \|\| 1.11.194 \|\|

*tejasaḥ śātanaṃ cakre stūyamānasya daivataiḥ \|*  
*devaṃ cakre samāropya bhrāmayāmāsa sūtrabhṛt \|\| 194 \|\|*

194\. Even as he was being eulogized by Devas, he continued the whetting and scraping. Sūtrakṛt (i.e. Tvaṣṭṛ) made the Lord get on to the wheel and whirled him.

## \|\| 1.11.195 \|\|

*mṛtpiṃḍavatkulālasya saṃspṛśankṣuradhārayā \|*  
*pataṃgasya stavaṃ kurvanviśvakarmā divaspateḥ \|\| 195 \|\|*

195\. This was like the work of a potter with a lump of clay. Viśvakarman continued to scrape with the sharp edge of his chisel even as he eulogized Pataṅga (Sun), the Lord of heaven.

## \|\| 1.11.196 \|\|

*tejasaḥ ṣoḍaśaṃ bhāgaṃ maṇḍalasthamadhārayat \|*  
*śātitaṃ tasya tattejo yāvatpādau varānane \|\| 196 \|\|*

196\. A sixteenth part of the fieriness of the solar disc was scraped off even upto the feet, O lady of excellent countenance.

## \|\| 1.11.197 \|\|

*yattasya ṛṅmayaṃ tejastatprabhāse'patatpriye \|*  
*yajurmayena deveśi bhāvitā dyaurmahāprabhoḥ \|\| 197 \|\|*

197\. The part of the fieriness comprising Ṛks fell over Prabhāsa Kṣetra, O my beloved.O goddess of Devas, heaven was sanctified by the refulgence comprising Yajus Mantras of the great Lord.

## \|\| 1.11.198 \|\|

*svargaṃ sāmamayenāpi bhūrbhuvaḥsvaritisthitam \|*  
*tatastaistejaso bhāgairdaśabhiḥ paṃcabhistathā \|\| 198 \|\|*

198\. Svarga was sanctified by the part comprising Sāman songs. Thus Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ and Svaḥ were set up. Then the refulgence was split into sixteen parts. Out of the first fifteen parts, the following were made.

## \|\| 1.11.199-201 \|\|

*tena vai nirmitaṃ cakraṃ viṣṇoḥ śūlaṃ harasya ca \|*  
*mahāprabhaṃ mahākāyaṃ śibikā dhanadasya ca \|\| 199 \|\|*

*daṇḍaḥ pretapateḥ śaktirdevasenāpatestathā \|*  
*anyeṣāṃ ca surāṇāṃ ca astrāṇyuktāni yāni vai \|\| 200 \|\|*

*yakṣavidyādharāṇāṃ ca tāni cakre sa viśvakṛt \|*  
*tataḥ ṣoḍaśamaṃ bhāgaṃ bibhartti bhagavānraviḥ \|*  
*tattejo ravibhāgaśca khastho vicarati priye \|\| 201 \|\|*

199-201. The discus of Viṣṇu, the highly refulgent huge trident of Hara, the Śibikā (palanquin) of Kubera, the staff of Pretapati (Yama), Śakti of Devasenāpati (Kārttikeya) and the various weapons of the other Devas as well as Yakṣas and Vidyādharas—all these were made by Viśvakarman. Thus Lord Ravi now had only a sixteenth of his early brilliance. It is this brilliant light that is seen in the sky as of Ravi, O my beloved.

## \|\| 1.11.202 \|\|

*iti śātitatejāḥ sa śvaśureṇātiśobhanam \|*  
*vapurdadhāra mārttaṃḍaḥ puṣpabāṇamanoramam \|\| 202 \|\|*

202\. On being whetted thus by his father-in-law with the excess of refulgence scraped off, Mārtaṇḍa (Sun) had a very splendid body, as charming as that of the Flower-arrowed One (i.e. Kāmadeva).

## \|\| 1.11.203 \|\|

*tataḥ surūpa dhṛgbhānuruttarānagamatkurūn \|*  
*dadṛśe tatra saṃjñāṃ tu vaḍavārūpadhāriṇīm \|\| 203 \|\|*

203\. Bhānu (Sun) with a lovely body went to Uttarakuru region. There he saw Saṃjñā in the form of a mare.

## \|\| 1.11.204 \|\|

*apāpāṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ tapasā niyamena ca \|*  
*sā ca dṛṣṭvā tamāyāṃtaṃ parapuṃso viśaṃkayā \|*  
*jagāma saṃmukhaṃ tasya aśvarūpadharasya ca \|\| 204 \|\|*

204\. She was free of sins of all living beings due to her penance and restraint. On seeing him coming in the form of a horse, she had the suspicion of his being another male and so went forward facing him.

## \|\| 1.11.205 \|\|

*tataśca nāsikāyoge tayostatra sametayoḥ \|*  
*nāsatyadasrau tanayāvaśvavaktrau vinirgatau \|\| 205 \|\|*

205\. Their union thereupon was through the nose (of Saṃjñā) Two sons, Nāsatya and Dasra, with horse-faces were born.

## \|\| 1.11.206 \|\|

*retasonte ca revantaḥ khaḍgī chatrī tanutrabhṛt \|*  
*piturgṛhyottamaṃ so'śvaṃ jātamātraḥ palāyata \|\| 206 \|\|*

206\. At the culmination of the coitus Revanta the son appeared with a sword, umbrella and coat of mail. As soon as he was born he seized the excellent horse of his father and fled.

## \|\| 1.11.207 \|\|

*sa tasminsakṛdārūḍhastamaśvaṃ naiva muṃcati \|*  
*tatorkeṇa samādiṣṭau daṃḍanāyakapiṃgalau \|\| 207 \|\|*

207\. Once he mounted the horse he never left it. Thereupon Daṇḍanāyaka and Piṅgala were commanded by Arka (Sun):

## \|\| 1.11.208-209 \|\|

*aśvaṃ pratyānayadhvaṃ me mā balācchidrato'syatu \|*  
*pārśvasthau tiṣṭhatastasya aśvacchidrābhikāṃkṣiṇau \|\| 208 \|\|*

*na ca cchidraṃ labhete tau tasyādyāpi mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*agre gacchati revaṃte pṛṣṭhagau daṇḍapiṃgalau \|\| 209 \|\|*

208-209. “Both of you, do bring back the horse to me not using force but through a loophole (i.e. by cunning device).” Though they stood at his side waiting for the loophole in regard to the horse, till today they did not find a loophole in regard to the noble-souled one. While Revanta went ahead Daṇḍa and Piṅgala closely followed.

## \|\| 1.11.210 \|\|

*uttarebhyaḥ kurubhyastu nirgatau vegavattarau \|*  
*dakṣiṇaṃ bhārataṃ prāptau yatra kṣetra prabhāsikam \|\| 210 \|\|*

210\. They had speedily come out of Uttarakuru region and had come to the south of India where there was the holy spot Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.11.211 \|\|

*atyarthaṃ vegakhinnau tau sa ca revaṃtako'pi hi \|*  
*prasvinnagātraḥ socchvāso revaṃtastatra saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 211 \|\|*

211\. They as well as Revantaka were weary and distressed due to the rapidity. Gasping for breath with profuse perspiration all over the body, Revanta stationed himself there.

## \|\| 1.11.212 \|\|

*muhūrtena samākrāntaṃ lakṣayojanamaṃḍalam \|*  
*uttarāddakṣiṇaṃ devi revatena mahātmanā \|\| 212 \|\|*

212\. O goddess, from north to south a distance of a hundred thousand Yojanas was traversed in a Muhūrta by the noble-souled Revanta.

## \|\| 1.11.213 \|\|

*svinnagātrastato devi prabhāse samavasthitaḥ \|*  
*daṇḍapiṃgalakasaṃyukto hyaśvārūḍhaḥ sa tiṣṭhati \|\| 213 \|\|*

213\. With profuse perspiration all over the body, O goddess, he stationed himself in Prabhāsa, riding the horse and accompanied by Daṇḍa and Piṅgala.

## \|\| 1.11.214 \|\|

*sāvitryā nairṛte bhāge nātidūre vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*rājñīputro yato devi rājā bhaṭṭārakastataḥ \|\| 214 \|\|*

214\. He is stationed to the south-west of Sāvitrī not very far. Since he was the son of Rājñī (Queen), O goddess, he was called Rājabhaṭṭāraka.

## \|\| 1.11.215 \|\|

*loke khyātiṃ samāyāti rājabhaṭṭāriketi ca \|*  
*guhyabhaṭṭārakatve ca revaṃto viniyojitaḥ \|\| 215 \|\|*

215\. He has earned fame in the world as Rājabhaṭṭāraka. Revanta was employed in the post of Guhyabhaṭṭāraka (a venerable person as a confidant).

## \|\| 1.11.216-218 \|\|

*evamabhyetyāha tato bhagavāṃllokatāpanaḥ \|*  
*tvamapyaśeṣalokasya pūjyo vatsa bhaviṣyasi \|\| 216 \|\|*

*araṇye ca mahādāve vairidasyubhayeṣu ca \|*  
*tvāṃ smariṣyaṃti ye marttyā mokṣyante te mahāpadaḥ \|\| 217 \|\|*

*kṣemamṛddhiṃ sukhaṃ rājyamārogyaṃ kīrtimunnatim \|*  
*narāṇāmatituṣṭastvaṃ pūjitaḥ saṃpradāsyasi \|\| 218 \|\|*

216-218. Then Lord Sun, the scorcher of the worlds, approached him and said thus: “O dear one, you will also become a person worthy of the adoration to all the worlds.

Whether in a forest or in a great forest-fire or during danger arising from the enemies and robbers, if men remember you they will become liberated from the great disaster.

On being adored by men you will become greatly pleased and bestow on them prosperity, welfare, happiness, kingdom, health, fame and advancement.”

## \|\| 1.11.219 \|\|

*aśvinau devabhiṣajau kṛtau pitrā mahātmanā \|*  
*dharmadṛṣṭiryamaścāsau samo mitre tathā'hite \|\| 219 \|\|*

219\. Aśvins were made the physicians of Devas by their noble-souled father. Yama had pious and righteous outlook. He was impartial towards friends and enemies.

## \|\| 1.11.220 \|\|

*tato niyogaṃ taṃ cāsya cakāra timirāpahaḥ \|*  
*yamunāṃ ca nadīṃ cakre kalindāntaravāhinīm \|\| 220 \|\|*

220\. Then the destroyer of darkness employed him likewise. He made Yamunā, the river flowing through the Kālinda mountainous region (near the source of Yamunā).

## \|\| 1.11.221 \|\|

*chāyāsaṃjñāsutaścāpi sāvarṇistu mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*bhāvyaḥ sonāgate kāle manuḥ sāvarṇikoṣṭamaḥ \|\| 221 \|\|*

221\. Sāvarṇi, the highly esteemed son of Chāyā Saṃjñā, shall (in the future) become the eighth Manu, Sāvarṇika.

## \|\| 1.11.222-225 \|\|

*merupṛṣṭhe tapo ghoramadyāpi carati prabhuḥ \|*  
*bhrātā śanaiścarastasya graho'bhūcca priye dhruvam \|\| 222 \|\|*

*evaṃ tebhyo varāndattvā revaṃtasyāpi bhāskaraḥ \|*  
*punarnāma niruktaṃ sa revaṃtasyākarotpramuḥ \|\| 223 \|\|*

*evaṃgacchatyasau yasmātsaṃjñāyāḥ śāṃtidaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*aśvānāmādhipatye tu bhānunā ca niyojitaḥ \|\| 224 \|\|*

*kṣemeṇa gacchate'dhvānaṃ yastu pūjayate pathi \|*  
*sukhaprasādyo marttyānāṃ sadā ca varavarṇini \|\| 225 \|\|*

222-225. The Lord is performing a terrible penance on the top of Meru even today. His brother Śanaiścara became a planet, O my beloved.

After giving them boons thus and also to Revanta, Lord Bhāskara further explained his name. The son of Saṃjñā, a bestower of peace on her, goes like this. He was employed as the commander of horses by Bhānu. He who adores him on the path, traverses the way safely. O lady of excellent complexion, he can be easily propitiated always by men.

## Chapter 12 - Creation of Yameśvara (Yama-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.12.1-2 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*yā saṃjñā sā smṛtā rājñī chāyā yā sā tu nikṣubhā \|*  
*rājṛ dīptau smṛto dhātū rājā rājati yaḥ sadā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*adhikaṃ sarvabhūtebhyastasmādrājā sa ucyate \|*  
*rājapatnī tu sā yasmāttasmādrājñī prakīrtitā \|\| 2 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-2. She who was Saṃjñā was remembered as Rājñī and she who was Chāyā was Nikṣubhā. The root √rājṛ (Rāj) is remembered as meaning Dīpti (Shining). Rājā is one who shines always. He is superior to all living beings. Hence he is called Rājā. Since she was the wife of a Rājā she is glorified as Rājñī.

## \|\| 1.12.3 \|\|

*kṣubha saṃcalane dhāturniścalā tena nikṣubhā \|*  
*bhavaṃti hyathavā yasmātsvāṃgīyāḥ kṣudvivarjitāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The root √kṣubh is used in the sense of agitation. Since (the earth) is motionless it is called Nikṣubhā. Or (it may be thus) since members of her family shall be devoid of Kṣut (hunger).

## \|\| 1.12.4-7 \|\|

*chāyā tāṃ viśate divyā smṛtā sā tena nikṣubhā \|*  
*sāṃprataṃ vartate yo'yaṃ manurloke mahāmate \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tasyānvavāye jātastu śaṃkhacakagadādharaḥ \|*  
*yamastu mātrā saṃśapto hīnapādo dharātale \|\| 5 \|\|*

*prabhāsakṣetramāsādya cacāra vipulaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*varṣāṇāmayutaṃ sāgraṃ liṃgaṃ pūjitavānpriye \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tuṣṭaścāhaṃ tatastasya varāṇāṃ ca śataṃ dadau \|*  
*adyāpi tatra deveśi yameśvaramiti śrutam \|*  
*yamadvitīyāyāṃ dṛṣṭvā yamalokaṃ na paśyati \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-7. Chāyā the divine enters it (the earth). Hence it is remembered as Nikṣubhā.

The (Lord) holding conch, discus and club is born in the family of (that king) who is the Manu in the world now, O highly intelligent one.

On being cursed by his mother, Yama became deficient of foot. He came to Prabhāsa Kṣetra on the earth and performed elaborate penance. O my beloved, he adored the Liṅga for more than ten thousand years. Becoming pleased, I granted him a hundred (i.e. a number of) boons. O goddess of Devas, Yameśvara is well-known there even today. One who visits it on the Yamadvitīyā day never sees Yama’s world.

## Chapter 13 - Origin of Arkasthala

## \|\| 1.13.1-2 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*yadā bhramisthaḥ savitā takṣitaḥ kṣuradhārayā \|*  
*śvaśureṇa mahādeva jāmātā prītipūrvakam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tattejaḥ śātitaṃ bhūri prabhāse yatpapāta vai \|*  
*tadabhūtkiṃ tadā deva prabhāsātkathayasva me \|\| 2 \|\|*

The Devī said:

1-2. O great Lord, Savitṛ stationed on the lathe was whetted and scraped by his father-in-law lovingly. The particles of fieriness of the son-in-law fell in Prabhāsa profusely. O Lord, what was it transformed into at Prabhāsa? Do tell me.

## \|\| 1.13.3-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi sūryamāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*yacchrutvā mānavo bhaktyā mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dehāvatāro devasya prabhāse'rkasthalasya ca \|*  
*purāṇākhyānamācakṣe tava devi yaśasvini \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

3-4. O goddess of great renown, I shall narrate to you the ancient ancedote \[anecdote?\], the physical incarnation of Lord Arkasthala in Prabhāsa.

Listen, O goddess, I shall expound the excellent greatness of Sūrya. If a man listens to it with devotion, he is liberated from all sins.

## \|\| 1.13.5-6 \|\|

*śākadvīpe mahādevi bhramisthasya tadā raveḥ \|*  
*varṣāṇāṃ tu śataṃ sāgraṃ takṣyamāṇe vibhāvasau \|\| 5 \|\|*

*yadādya bhāgajaṃ tejastatprabhāse'patatpriye \|*  
*patitaṃ tatra tattejaḥ sthalākāraṃ vyajāyata \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. O great goddess, Ravi was fixed on the lathe in Śākadvīpa for more than a hundred years. While Vibhāvasu (Sun-god) was being whetted and scraped, O my beloved, particles of his fiery splendour fell down in Prabhāsa, which took the shape of a Sthala (holy ground).

## \|\| 1.13.7 \|\|

*jāṃbūnadamayaṃ devi tatpūrvamabhavatkṣitau \|*  
*tiṣyamāhātmyayogena śailībhūtaṃ ca sāṃpratam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O goddess, earlier it was completely of gold on the earth, but due to the (evil) influence of the Kali Age it has become a mere rock now.

## \|\| 1.13.8 \|\|

*tatra cārkamayaṃ rūpaṃ kṛtvā devo divākaraḥ \|*  
*utpannaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ hitāya dharaṇītale \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Actuated by a desire for welfare of all beings on the earth, Lord Divākara assumed the form of Arka and manifested himself.

## \|\| 1.13.9 \|\|

*hiraṇyagarbhanāmeti kṛte sūryeti kīrtitam \|*  
*tretāyāṃ savitānāma dvāpare bhāskaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Though actually named Hiraṇyagarbha he is glorified as Sūrya in Kṛta age. In Tretā his name was Savitṛ. He is remembered as Bhāskara (in Dvāpara).

## \|\| 1.13.10 \|\|

*kalau cārkasthalonāma triṣu lokeṣu kīrtitaḥ \|*  
*avatīrṇamidaṃ devi svayameva pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. In Kali Age he is glorified in all the three worlds by the name Arkasthala. The deity was self-installed soon after the incaranation.

## \|\| 1.13.11 \|\|

*yadā svārociṣo devi dvitīyo'bhūnmanuḥ purā \|*  
*tasminkāle'vatīrṇo'sau devastatra divākaraḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O goddess, formerly the second Manu was Svārociṣa. Lord Divākara took the incarnation at that time.

## \|\| 1.13.12-14 \|\|

*bhaktimukti prado devi vyādhiduḥkhavināśakṛt \|*  
*tasya tejodbhavairvyāptaṃ reṇubhiḥ pañcayojanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇottarato devi pañcapūrvāpareṇa tu \|*  
*uttareṇa samudrasya yāvanmāheśvarī nadī \|\| 13 \|\|*

*nyaṃkumatyāścāparato yāvadeva kṛtasmaram \|*  
*etadvyāptaṃ mahādevi tattejoreṇubhiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. O goddess, the deity is the bestower of worldly pleasures and salvation. He is the destroyer of ailments and misery. The particles of his fiery splendour spread over in an area of five Yojanas from south to north and five Yojanas from east to west. It extends to the north of the ocean upto Māheśvarī Nadī (river) and to the west of Nyaṅkumatī upto Kṛtasmara, O great goddess. This area was completely overspread by the auspicious particles of his fiery splendour.

## \|\| 1.13.15 \|\|

*tasya sūkṣmā prabhā yā tu āditejoviniḥsṛtā \|*  
*tayā vyāptaṃ mahādevi yāvaddvādaśayojanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O great goddess, twelve Yojanas were covered by it. Its subtlest refulgence issued forth from the primordial splendour.

## \|\| 1.13.16 \|\|

*uttare bhāskarasutā dakṣiṇe saritāṃ patiḥ \|*  
*pūrvapaścimato devi rukmiṇīdvitayaṃ smṛtam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. To the north is the daughter of Bhāskara (i.e. the local river Yamunā). The ocean is to the south. To the east and west are the two Rukmiṇīs.

## \|\| 1.13.17 \|\|

*etasminnantare devi sauraṃ tejaḥ prasarppitam \|*  
*tena pāvitryamānītaṃ kṣetraṃ dvādaśayojanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Within this area, O goddess, the solar splendour has spread. Thereby the holy spot extending to twelve Yojanas, was rendered sacred.

## \|\| 1.13.18 \|\|

*tasya madhyasya yanmadhyaṃ tadgṛhaṃ mama sundari \|*  
*tejomaṇḍalamadhyasthaṃ mama sthānaṃ maheśvari \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The middle of its centre is my abode, O beautiful woman. O great goddess, my holy spot exists in the centre of the refulgent solar zone.

## \|\| 1.13.19 \|\|

*cakṣurmaṃḍalamadhye tu yathā devi kanīnikā \|*  
*pūrvapaścimato devi gomukhādā'śvamedhikam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O goddess, it is like the pupil in the middle of the eye. From the east to the west, O goddess, it extends from Gomukha to Āśvamedhika.

## \|\| 1.13.20 \|\|

*dakṣiṇottarato devi samudrātkauraveśvarīm \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare kṣetre kṣetrajño'haṃ varānane \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. From the south to the north it extends from the ocean to Kauraveśvarī. In the holy spot in the midst of all these I stay as Kṣetrajña (Soul), O lady of excellent countenance.

## \|\| 1.13.21 \|\|

*yasmādarkasya tejobhirbhāsitaṃ mama tadgṛham \|*  
*tasmātprabhāsanāmeti kalpe'sminprathitaṃ priye \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Since that abode of mine is illuminated by the refulgence of Arka (Sun), it has become well-known by the name Prabhāsa in this Kalpa, O my beloved.

## \|\| 1.13.22 \|\|

*tatra paśyati yaḥ sūryamarkkarūpaṃ narottamaḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ sūryaloke mahīyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. An excellent man who sees Sūrya in the form of Arka there, shall be rid of all sins. He is honoured in the world of Sun.

## \|\| 1.13.23 \|\|

*sa snātaḥ sarvatīrtheṣu tena ceṣṭaṃ mahāmakhaiḥ \|*  
*sarvadānāni dattāni pūrvajāstena toṣitāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. It is as though he has had his ablution in all the Tīrthas and performed great Makhas (Yajñas). All the Dānas have been offered by him and the ancestors have been propitiated by him.

## \|\| 1.13.24 \|\|

*arkarūpī yataḥ sūryastatra jāto mahītale \|*  
*tasmāttyājyaḥ sadā cārko bhojane'tra na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Since the Sun was born in the world there in the form of Arka (the plant Calotropis gigantea), so in the course of taking food there, a leaf of Arka plant should always be avoided.

## \|\| 1.13.25 \|\|

*yo dṛṣṭvārkasthalaṃ marttyaścārkapatreṣu bhuṃjati \|*  
*gomāṃsabhakṣaṇaṃ tena kṛtaṃ bhavati bhāmini \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. After a visit to Arkasthala, if a man takes food on Arka leaves, it is as though cow’s meat has been eaten by him, O beautiful lady.

## \|\| 1.13.26 \|\|

*bhakṣito bhāskarastena sa kuṣṭhī jāyate naraḥ \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena cārkapatrāṇi varjayet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. It is as though Bhāskara (the Sun-god) has been eaten by him. That man becomes a leper. Hence all efforts should be made to eschew the leaves of Arka (from food).

## \|\| 1.13.27-29 \|\|

*yātrāyāṃ prathamaṃ devi dṛṣṭo yenārkabhāskaraḥ \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā mahiṣīṃ dadyādbrāhmaṇāya vipaścite \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tāmravarṇaṃ raktavastraṃ tatastuṣyati bhāskaraḥ \|*  
*tasya caiva tu sāṃnidhye vahnikoṇe vyavasthitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*nātidūre mahābhāge siddheśvaramiti smṛtam \|*  
*sarvasiddhipradaṃ devi liṃgaṃ trailokyapūjitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

27-28a. If a pilgrim visits Arkabhāskara for the first time, O goddess, he should, after the visit, give a she-buffalo to a learned Brāhmaṇa. The buffalo may be copper-coloured. It should be offered along with a red cloth. Thereby Bhāskara becomes pleased.

28b-29. In the vicinity thereof, O highly esteemed one, not very far off in the south-eastern corner, there is the Liṅga remembered as Siddheśvara, O goddess, this Liṅga bestows all Siddhis. It is adored by all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.13.30 \|\|

*jaigīṣavyeśvaraṃnāma pūrvaṃ kṛtayuge'bhavat \|*  
*kalau siddheśvaramiti prasiddhimagamatpriye \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Formerly in Kṛtayuga it was known by the name Jaigīṣavyeśvara. O my beloved, it becomes well-known as Siddheśvara in Kali Age.

## \|\| 1.13.31-33 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā manujo devi sarvasiddhimavāpnuyāt \|*  
*tatraiva devadeveśi nātidūre vyavasthitam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*sūryadakṣiṇanairṛtye pātālavivaraṃ priye \|*  
*maṃdehā rākṣasā yatra tathā śālakaṭaṃkaṭāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*sūryasya tejasā dagdhāḥ pātālamagamanpurā \|*  
*kalau taddvāramevāsti na pātāle gatiḥ priye \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. On seeing the deity, O goddess, a man attains all the Siddhis.

O goddess of the chiefs of Devas, there is a crevice leading to Pātāla. It is not far from it. It is to the south and south-west of the deity Sun.

On being scorched by the brilliance of the Sun, the Rākṣasas named Mandehas and the Śālakaṭaṃkaṭas went to Pātāla. O my beloved, in Kali Age only the crevice exists but there is no passage leading to Pātāla.

## \|\| 1.13.34 \|\|

*yoginyastatra rakṣaṃti brāhmyādyā mātarastathā \|*  
*māghekṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ rātrau mātṛgaṇānyajet \|*  
*balipuṣpopahāraiśca tataḥ siddhirbhaviṣyati \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Yoginīs and Mothers Brāhmī etc. guard that place. One should worship the groups of Mothers at night on the fourteenth lunar day in the dark half of the month of Māgha, by means of oblations and floral offerings. Thereby Siddhi is achieved.

## \|\| 1.13.35 \|\|

*iti hi sakaladharmabhāvahetorharakamalāsanaviṣṇusaṃstutasya \|*  
*tanuparilikhanaṃ niśamya bhānorvrajati divākaralokamāyuṣoṃ'te \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Thus, by listening to the story of the whetting of the body of Bhānu, eulogized by Hara, Brahmā and Viṣṇu, one goes to the world of Divākara at the close of one’s life. Indeed Bhānu is the cause of all holy rites and feelings.

## Chapter 14 - Creation of Siddheśvara (Siddha-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.14.1-5 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*yadetadbhavatā proktaṃ māhātmyaṃ sūryadaivatam \|*  
*tanme vistarato brūhi devadeva jagatpate \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kathamarkasthalo bhūtaḥ prabhāsakṣetrabhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*pūjanīyo mahādevaḥ samyagyātrāphalepsubhiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ke maṃtrāḥ kiṃ vidhānaṃ tu keṣu parvasu pūjayet \|*  
*jaigīṣavyeśvaro bhūtvā hyabhūtsiddheśvaraḥ katham \|*  
*tanme kathaya deveśa vistarātsarvameva hi \|\| 3 \|\|*

*pātāle vivaraṃ tatra yoginyastatra kiṃ purā \|*  
*tathā mātṛgaṇaścaiva kathametadabhūtpurā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*etatsarvamaśeṣeṇa dayāṃ kṛtvā jagatpate \|*  
*mamācakṣva virūpākṣa yadyahaṃ te priyā hara \|\| 5 \|\|*

The Devī said:

1-5. What has been narrated by you as the greatness of the deity Sun, may be further expounded in detail, O Lord of Devas, O Lord of the worlds.

How did Arkasthala, the ornament of Prabhāsa Kṣetra, take shape? The great Lord has to be worshipped by those desirous of the benefits of a perfect pilgrimage.

What are the Mantras? What is the procedure of worship? What are the Parvas (festive occasions) during which one should offer worship? How did the deity become Siddheśvara after having been Jaigīṣavyeśvara originally. O Lord of Devas, narrate this to me in full detail.

How was the crevice leading to the nether world created formerly? How did the Yoginīs and the groups of Mothers come there? O Lord Virūpākṣa, O Hara, O Lord of the worlds, have mercy on me and describe everything to me, if I am your beloved.

## \|\| 1.14.6 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā devi kathayāmi samāsataḥ \|*  
*siddheśvaro hyabhūdyena jaigīṣavyeśvaro haraḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

6\. You have put a pertinent question, O goddess. I shall narrate briefly how Jaigīṣavyeśvara Hara became Siddheśvara.

## \|\| 1.14.7-8 \|\|

*pūjāvidhānaṃ vistīrya tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu \|*  
*āsīdasminkṛte devi sarva jñānaviśāradaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*putraḥ śatakalākasya jaigīṣavya iti śrutaḥ \|*  
*prabhāsakṣetramāsādya sa cakre duścaraṃ tapaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Listen even as I expatiate upon the procedure of worship.

O goddess, in this Kṛta Yuga there was a son of Śatakalāka well-known by the name Jaigīṣavya. He was an expert in all the lores (branches of knowledge). He came to Prabhāsakṣetra and performed a very difficult penance.

## \|\| 1.14.9 \|\|

*atiṣṭhadvāyubhakṣaśca varṣāṇāṃ śatakaṃ kila \|*  
*ambubhakṣaḥ sahasraṃ tu śākāhāro'yutaṃ tathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He stood for a hundred years with air alone as the sole intake, a thousand years with water constituting his diet and ten thousand years with green vegetables for his food.

## \|\| 1.14.10 \|\|

*cāṃdrāyaṇasahasraṃ ca kṛtaṃ sāṃtapanaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*śoṣayitvā mitāhāro digvāsāḥ samapadyata \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A thousand Cāndrāyaṇas were performed and Sāntapana thereafter. With meagre intake of food, he dried up his body and became Digvāsas (nude).

## \|\| 1.14.11 \|\|

*pūrve kalpe svayaṃ bhūtaṃ mahodayamiti śrutam \|*  
*sa liṃgaṃ devadevasya pratiṣṭhāpyārcayannapi \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. There is a Liṅga well-known as Mahodaya which was self-born in the previous Kalpa. He installed this Liṅga of the Lord of Devas and worshipped it.

## \|\| 1.14.12 \|\|

*bhasmaśāyī bhasmadigdho nṛtta gītairatoṣayat \|*  
*japena vṛṣanādaiśca tapasā bhāvitaḥ śuciḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He used to lie in holy ash. He smeared his body with the holy ash. He propitiated the deity with dances and songs. He performed Japa and made sounds like the bellow of a bull. By means of penance he sanctified himself and remained pure.

## \|\| 1.14.13 \|\|

*tamevaṃ toṣayāṇaṃ tu bhaktyā paramayā yutam \|*  
*bhagavāṃśca tamabhyetya idaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Even as he was endowed with great devotion and propitiated the Lord thus, the Lord came to him and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.14.14 \|\|

*jaigīṣavya mahābuddhe paśya māṃ divyacakṣuṣā \|*  
*tuṣṭo'smi varadaścāhaṃ brūhi yatte manogatam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. “O Jaigīṣavya of great intellect, look at me with your divine vision. I am pleased with you. I shall grant you boons. Tell me whatever you cherish in your mind”.

## \|\| 1.14.15 \|\|

*sa evamukto devena devaṃ dṛṣṭvā trilocanam \|*  
*praṇamya śirasā pādāvidaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. On being told thus by the Lord, he looked at the Threeeyed Lord, bowed down to his feet and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.14.16 \|\|

*jaigīṣavya uvāca \|*  
*bhagavandevadeveśa mama tuṣṭo yadi prabho \|*  
*jñānayogaṃ hi me dehi yaḥ saṃsāranikṛntanam \|\| 16 \|\|*

Jaigīṣavya said:

16\. O Holy Lord, O Lord of the chiefs of Devas, if you are pleased with me, impart to me Jñānayoga that cuts off (the bonds of) worldly existence.

## \|\| 1.14.17 \|\|

*bhagavannānyadicchāmi yogātparataraṃ hitam \|*  
*tvayi bhaktiśca nityaṃ me devyāṃ skande gaṇeśvare \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O Holy Lord, there is nothing more beneficial than Yoga and I do not wish for anything else. Let me have permanent devotion unto you, Skanda, Gaṇeśvara and the goddess.

## \|\| 1.14.18 \|\|

*na ca vyādhibhayaṃ bhūyānna ca tejo'pamānatā \|*  
*anutsekaṃ tathā kṣāṃtiṃ damaṃ śamamathāpi ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Let there be no fear of ailments nor insult to (my) brilliance. Grant me absence of haughtiness, forbearance, restraint and quiescence.

## \|\| 1.14.19 \|\|

*etānvarānmahādeva tvadicchāmi trilocana \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O Lord, O great Lord, O Three-eyed One, I wish for these boons from you.

## \|\| 1.14.20 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*ajaraścāmaraścaiva sarvaśokavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*mahāyogī mahāvīryo yogaiśvaryasamanvitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

20\. You shall be immortal, free from old age and free from all griefs. You shall be a great Yogin of great power. You will become endowed with Yogic supernatural powers.

## \|\| 1.14.21 \|\|

*prabhāvāccāsya kṣetrasya guhyasya mama śāśvatam \|*  
*yogāṣṭaguṇamaiśvaryaṃ prāpsyase paramaṃ mahat \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. By the power of this well-protected holy spot of mine, you will attain the eight Yogic powers such as Aṇimā, Laghimā etc.

## \|\| 1.14.22 \|\|

*bhaviṣyasi muniśreṣṭha yogācāryaḥ suviśrutaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O most excellent sage, you will become a well-known Yogācārya (Master of Yoga).

## \|\| 1.14.23 \|\|

*yaścedaṃ tvatkṛtaṃ ligaṃ niyamenārcayiṣyati \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto yogaṃ divyamavāpsyati \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He who regularly worships this Liṅga consecrated by you, shall be liberated from all sins. He will attain the divine Yoga.

## \|\| 1.14.24 \|\|

*jaigīṣavyaguhāṃ cemāṃ prāpya yogaṃ karoti yaḥ \|*  
*sa saptarātrādyuktātmā saṃsāraṃ saṃtariṣyati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He who comes to this cave of Jaigīṣavya and practices Yoga shall become a liberated soul in seven days. He shall cross the ocean of worldly existence.

## \|\| 1.14.25 \|\|

*māsena pūrvajātiṃ ca janmātītaṃ ca vetsyati \|*  
*ekarātrāttanuṃ śuddhāṃ dvābhyāṃ tārayate pitṝn \|*  
*trirātreṇa vyatītena tvaparānsapta tārayet \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Within a month he will begin to recollect the previous birth and everything that has happened before. Within a single night he will get a pure body. Within two days he will be able to redeem the Pitṛs and when three nights elapse, he will redeem seven succeeding generations.

## \|\| 1.14.26 \|\|

*punaśca tava viprarṣe ajeyatvaṃ ca yogibhiḥ \|*  
*icchato darśanaṃ caiva bhaviṣyati ca te mama \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Further, O Brāhmaṇa sage, you will become invincible to other yogins. You will have my vision whenever you wish.

## \|\| 1.14.27 \|\|

*iti devo varāndattvā tatraivāṃtaradhīyata \|*  
*etatkṛtayuge vṛttaṃ tava devi prabhāṣitam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. After granting the boons thus, the Lord vanished there itself. This is what happened in Kṛta Yuga. It is thus explained to you, O goddess.

## \|\| 1.14.28-30 \|\|

*tretāyuge mahādevi dvāpare'pi tathaiva ca \|*  
*kaliyugapraveśe tu vālakhilyā maharṣayaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*asminprābhāsike kṣetre sūryasthalasamīpataḥ \|*  
*ārādhayaṃto deveśaṃ guhāmadhyanivāsinam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi ṛṣayaścorddharetasaḥ \|*  
*varṣāyutaṃ tapastaptvā siddhiṃ jagmustadātmikām \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. O great goddess, the same happened in Tretāyuga as well as Dvāpara. After the advent of Kaliyuga, the great sages, Vālakhilyas numbering eighty-eight thousand, came to this Prābhāsika Kṣetra. Near Sūryasthala they propitiated the Lord of Devas who resided in the middle of the cave. Practising strict celibacy these sages performed penance for ten thousand years and attained the Siddhi in the form of identity with the Supreme Soul.

## \|\| 1.14.31 \|\|

*tataḥ siddheśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ kalau khyātaṃ varānane \|*  
*yadā somena saṃyuktā kṛṣṇā śivacaturdaśī \|*  
*tadaiva tasya devasya darśanaṃ devi durllabham \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Therefore, O lady of excellent countenance, it became well-known in Kali Age as Siddheśvara Liṅga. O goddess, rare indeed is the vision of that Lord on Śivacaturdaśī—the fourteenth lunar day in the dark half which has conjunction with the Moon.

## \|\| 1.14.32 \|\|

*brahmāṃḍaṃ sakalaṃ dattvā yatpuṇyamupajāyate \|*  
*tatpuṇyaṃ labhate devi siddhaliṃgasya pūjanāt \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. By worshipping the Siddhaliṅga, O goddess, one gets that merit which accrues from donating the entire Cosmic Egg.

## Chapter 15 - Origin of Pāpanāśana

## \|\| 1.15.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tasyāgneye tu deveśi aruṇena pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*dhanuṣāṃ ca traye tatra siddhaliṃgasamīpataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sūryasārathinā tatra liṃgaṃ devipratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*kalau pāpaharaṃnāma darśanātpāpanāśanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*caitramāsa trayodaśyāṃ śuklāyāṃ varavarṇini \|*  
*pūjayedvidhivadbhaktyā pauṃḍarīkaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. To the south-east thereof, O goddess of Devas, there is the Liṅga installed by Aruṇa, the charioteer of Sūrya. It is very near the Siddhaliṅga, say three Dhanus (12 Hastas) away. It dispels the sins in Kali Age by mere vision. It’s name is Pāpanāśana.

A person should worship it duly with great faith and devotion, O lady of excellent countenance, on the thirteenth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Caitra. He shall obtain the fruit of the Pauṇḍarīka Yajña.

## Chapter 16 - Origin of Sunandā and Other Mother Goddesses

## \|\| 1.16.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*pātālavivarasyāpi māhātmyaṃ śṛṇu sāṃpratam \|*  
*pūrvapṛṣṭaṃ mahādevi brahmaṇā viśvakarmaṇā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tamobhāve samutpanne jātāstatraiva rākṣasāḥ \|*  
*sūryasya dveṣiṇaḥ sarve hyasaṃkhyātā mahābalāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*te tu dṛṣṭvā mahātmānaṃ samudyaṃtaṃ divākaram \|*  
*te dhūmrapramukhāḥ sarve jahasuḥ sūryamaṃjasā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*asmākamaṃtakaḥ ko'yaṃ vidyate pāpakarmakṛt \|*  
*ityūcurvividhā vācaḥ sūryasyāgre sthitāstadā \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Now listen to the greatness of the Pātālavivara (Crevice leading to the nether worlds). O great goddess, this was already asked earlier by Brahmā, the creator of the Universe.

When there arose prevalence of darkness, Rākṣasas were born there too. They were innumerable, very powerful. All of them hated Sūrya.

They had Dhūmra as their leader. On seeing the noble-souled Divākara (Sun) rising, all of them immediately laughed at him: “Who is this perpetrator of evil deeds who may be our destroyer?” Standing before Sūrya, they spoke these and various other similar words.

## \|\| 1.16.5 \|\|

*iti śrutvā tadā devaḥ krodhasphuritādharaḥ \|*  
*rākṣasānāṃ vacaścaiva bhakṣyamāṇo divākaraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On hearing this, the Lord got angry and his lips throbbed. Divākara appeared to swallow the words of the Rākṣasas.

## \|\| 1.16.6 \|\|

*tataḥ krodhābhibhūtena cakṣuṣā cāvalokayat \|*  
*sa krūrarakṣaḥkṣayakṛttimiradvipakesarī \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Like a killer lion, the destroyer of darkness wanted to annihilate the cruel Rākṣasas. He looked at them with wrathful eyes.

## \|\| 1.16.7 \|\|

*mahāṃśumānkhagaḥ sūryastadvināśamaciṃtayat \|*  
*ajānannaṃtataśchidraṃ rākṣasānāṃ divaspatiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Sūrya traversing the sky with great rays thought of killing them, but the Lord of heaven did not know the weak point of the Rākṣasas till the end.

## \|\| 1.16.8 \|\|

*sa dharmavicyutāndṛṣṭvā pāpopahatacetasaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ saṃciṃtya bhagavāndadhyau dhyānaṃ prabhākaraḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then he saw these ones fallen from Dharma, having minds overwhelmed with sins. After considering this, Lord Prabhākara began to meditate.

## \|\| 1.16.9 \|\|

*ajānaṃstejasā grastaṃ trailokyaṃ rajanīcaraiḥ \|*  
*tataste bhānunā dṛṣṭāḥ krodhādhmātena cakṣuṣā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The Rajanīcaras (demons) came to know that the three worlds were swallowed (pervaded) by the splendour. Then they were looked at by Bhānu with eyes (as if) burning with anger.

## \|\| 1.16.10-11 \|\|
