*nipeturaṃbarabhraṣṭāḥ kṣīṇapuṇyā iva grahāḥ \|*  
*rākṣasairveṣṭito dhūmro nipatañchuśubheṃ'barāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

*arddhapakvaṃ yathā tālaphalaṃ kapibhirāvṛtam \|*  
*yadṛcchayā nipetuste yaṃtramuktā yathopalāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Slipping down from the sky they fell like the planets with dwindling merit. Dhūmra surrounded by the Rākṣasas falling down from the sky, shone like a half ripe Tāla fruit surrounded by monkeys. They fell automatically like stones released from a machine.

## \|\| 1.16.12 \|\|

*tato vāyu vaśādbhraṣṭā bhittvā bhūmiṃ rasātalam \|*  
*jagmuste kṣetramāsādya prabhāsaṃ varavarṇini \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thereafter, they fell further, dislodged and carried off by the wind. After reaching Prabhāsa Kṣetra, they pierced through the earth and went to the nether worlds, O lady of excellent complexion.

## \|\| 1.16.13 \|\|

*yatra cārkasthalo devaḥ sarvasiddhipradāyakaḥ \|*  
*tatsānnidhyasthitaṃ devi pātālavivaraṃ mahat \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. It is there that Lord Arkasthala, the bestower of all Siddhis, is present. O goddess, the great Pātāla cavity is in its vicinity.

## \|\| 1.16.14-15 \|\|

*anyāni koṭiśaḥ saṃti tāni luptāni bhāmini \|*  
*kṛtasmarātsamārabhya yāvadarkasthalo raviḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*devamāturvaraṃ prāpya siddhayo'ṣṭau vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare devi sūryakṣetramudāhṛtam \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. There were crores of other cavities but, O beautiful lady, they had become lost. Beginning with Kṛtasmara and ending with Arkasthala with the Sun as the deity in between these two, O goddess, is the holy place of Sūrya. Attaining the boon from Devamātṛ (i.e. Aditi) the eight Siddhis had set up there.

## \|\| 1.16.16 \|\|

*sūryasya tejaso devi madhyabhāgaṃ hi tatsmṛtam \|*  
*sarvaṃ hemamayaṃ devi nāpuṇyastatra vīkṣate \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. It is remembered, O goddess, as the middle part of the splendour of Sūrya. It is fully golden. No one without merit sees the place, O goddess.

## \|\| 1.16.17 \|\|

*vivarāṇāṃ śataṃ caikaṃ sparśāścaiva tu koṭiśaḥ \|*  
*tatra saṃti mahādevi siddheśastu prarakṣati \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O great goddess, a hundred and one cavities and crores of Sparśa gems (philosopher’s stones) are there, and Siddheśa guards them.

## \|\| 1.16.18 \|\|

*idaṃ kṣetraṃ mahādevi priyaṃ sūryasya sarvadā \|*  
*sūryaparvaṇisaṃprāpte kurukṣetrādhikaṃ priye \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O great goddess, this holy spot is always dear to Sūrya. O my beloved, in the Sūrya Parva (festival day of Sun), it is more efficacious than Kurukṣetra.

## \|\| 1.16.19 \|\|

*brāhmī caiva hiraṇyā ca saṃgamaśca mahodadheḥ \|*  
*etattrisaṃgamaṃ devi koṭitīrtha phalapradam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Brāhmī, Hiraṇyā and the confluence of the great ocean, these three meeting places together, bestow the fruit of visiting Koṭitīrthas (a crore of Tīrthas).

## \|\| 1.16.20 \|\|

*devamātā ca tatraiva maṃkīśastatra tiṣṭhati \|*  
*nāgasthānaṃ nagasthānaṃ tatraiva samudāhṛtam \|1 \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The Devamātā and Maṅkīśā are there. So also it is cited that Nāgasthāna (holy spot of Nāgas) and Nagasthāna (holy spot of the mountains) are also there.

## \|\| 1.16.21 \|\|

*iti saṃkṣepataḥ proktamarkasthalamahodayam \|*  
*rākṣasānāṃ ca saṃpātādabhūcca vivaraṃ yathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Thus the great origin of Arkasthala has been narrated. It is also explained how the cavity came into existence due to the fall of Rākṣasas.

## \|\| 1.16.22 \|\|

*anyāni tatra deveśi luptāni vivarāṇi vai \|*  
*evaṃ tu prakaṭaṃ tatra dṛśyate'dyāpi bhāmini \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O goddess of Devas, the other cavities there have become lost but this is clearly manifest even today, O beautiful woman.

## \|\| 1.16.23-24 \|\|

*śrīmukhaṃ nāma taddvāraṃ rakṣyate mātṛbhiḥ priye \|*  
*varṣamekaṃ caturddaśyāṃ niyamādyastu pūjayet \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tatra mātṛgaṇāndevi sunaṃdādyānvidhānataḥ \|*  
*paśupuṣpopahāraiśca dhūpadīpaistathottamaiḥ \|*  
*viprāṇāṃ bhojanairdevi tasya siddhirbhaviṣyati \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. That cavity named Śrīmukha is guarded by the Mothers, O my beloved. A devotee should worship the groups of Mothers beginning with Sunaṇḍā in accordance with the injunctions on every fourteenth lunar day for a period of one year, through the offerings of animals and flowers and excellent incense and lights. Brāhmaṇas should be fed. O goddess, he will achieve Siddhi.

## \|\| 1.16.25-27 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena tatrārkasthalasaṃnidhau \|*  
*pūjayenmātaraḥ sarvā yadīcchetsiddhimātmanaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*etāstu mātaro devi sunaṃdāgaṇanāmataḥ \|*  
*khyātiṃ yāṃti prabhāse tu kṣetresminvaravarṇini \|\| 26 \|\|*

*etatsaṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ pātālottaramadhyataḥ \|*  
*tacchrutvā mucyate devi sarvāpadbhyo narottamaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-27. Hence, if one desires achievement of Siddhis by oneself, one should assiduously worship all the Mothers. All these Mothers become famous by the name Sunandāgaṇa in this Prabhāsa Kṣetra, O lady of excellent complexion. It is to the north and middle of Pātāla. It has been briefly told. On hearing it an excellent man becomes rid of all dangers.

## Chapter 17 - Procedure of Worship (of the Sun-God)

## \|\| 1.17.1-5 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*atha pūjāvidhānaṃ te kathayāmi yaśasvini \|*  
*arkasthalasya devasya yathā pūjyo narottamaiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sarveṣāmeva devānāmādirāditya ucyate \|*  
*ādikarttā tvasau yasmādādityastena cocyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

*nādityena vinā rātrirna divā na ca tarpaṇam \|*  
*na dharmo vai na cādharmo na saṃtiṣṭheccarācaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

*ādityaḥ pālayetsarvamādityaḥ sṛjate sadā \|*  
*ādityaḥ saṃharetsarvaṃ tasmādeṣa trayīmayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ārādhanavidhiṃ tasya bhāskarasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*kathayāmi mahādevi vedoktairmaṃtravistaraiḥ \|*  
*taṃ śṛṇuṣva varārohe sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-5. O lady of great renown, now I shall tell you the injunctions regarding the worship of the Lord of Arkasthala as to how he should be adored by excellent men.

Āditya (Sun) is called the primordial one among all the Devas. Since he is the Ādikartā (first creator) he is called Āditya.

Without Āditya there is neither day nor night, no libation, no holy rite, no unrighteousness and no living beings whether mobile or immobile exist.

Āditya protects everything always. Āditya creates. Āditya annihilates everything. Hence he is identical with Trayī (Triad).

O great goddess, I shall tell you the procedure of the worship of the noble-souled Bhāskara by means of the extensive Vedic Mantras. O beautiful lady, listen to it. It is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.17.6 \|\|

*mūrttisthaḥ pūjyate yena vidhānena maheśvari \|*  
*dvādaśātmā yathā sūryastatte vakṣyāmyaśeṣataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. I shall tell you fully, O great goddess, how Dvādaśātman (i.e. Sun) is to be adored duly as (incorporated in) an icon.

## \|\| 1.17.7 \|\|

*mukhaśuddhiṃ ca kṛtvā'dau snānaṃ kṛtvā viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*vastraśuddhiṃ deha śuddhiṃ kṛtvā sūryaṃ spṛśettataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. At the outset one should cleanse the mouth, Then one takes the bath. After wearing washed clothes and with purified body one should touch Sūrya (i.e. the idol of the Sun-god).

## \|\| 1.17.8 \|\|

*dantakāṣṭhavidhānaṃ tu prathamaṃ kathayāmi te \|*  
*madhūke putralābhaḥ syādarke netrasukhaṃ priye \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. First I shall explain the procedure for cleansing the mouth through Dantakāṣṭha (a twig used as toothbrush). If Madhūka tree is used (i.e. a twig thereof), there shall be the acquisition of a son. O my beloved, if Arka twig is used, it is good for the eyes.

## \|\| 1.17.9 \|\|

*vaktṛtvaṃ vai badaryā ca bṛhatyā drurjjanāñjayet \|*  
*aiśvaryaṃ ca bhavedbilve khadire ca na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. By using Badarī twig, one shall attain eloquence, by using Bṛhatī twig one defeats wicked people. If a Bilva twig is used, there shall be good fortune. Undoubtedly so with Khadira twig also.

## \|\| 1.17.10 \|\|

*rogakṣayaḥ kadambe tu arthalābho'timuktake \|*  
*marutāṃ yāti sarvatra āṭarūṣakasaṃbhavaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. By using a Kadamba twig ailment is reduced; by using Atimuktaka twig there is acqusition \[acquisition?\] of wealth. If Āṭarūsaka twig is used, one receives greater respect.

## \|\| 1.17.11 \|\|

*jātipradhānatāṃ jātāvaśvattho yacchate yaśaḥ \|*  
*śriyaṃ prāpnoti nikhilāṃ śirīṣasya niṣevaṇāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. If a Jāti twig is used, one attains chiefship of one’s community; Aśvattha yields fame; by resorting to Śirīṣa one gets all glory.

## \|\| 1.17.12 \|\|

*priyaṃguṃ sevamānasya saubhāgyaṃ paramaṃ bhavet \|*  
*abhīpsitārthasiddhiḥ syānnityaṃ plakṣaniṣevaṇāt \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Conjugal felicity shall be attained by one using a Priyaṅgu twig. By resorting to a Plakṣa twig always, one attains what one desires.

## \|\| 1.17.13 \|\|

*na pāṭitaṃ samaśnīyāddaṃtakāṣṭhaṃ na savraṇam \|*  
*na corddhaśuṣkaṃ vakraṃ vā naiva ca tvagvivarjjitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. One should never use a twig if it is split, damaged, crooked, or dried in the upper part or if the bark is peeled off.

## \|\| 1.17.14 \|\|

*vitastimātramaśnīyāddīrghaṃ hrasvaṃ ca varjayet \|*  
*udaṅmukho vā prāṅmukhaḥ sukhāsīno'tha vāgyataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. One should chew the twig a Vitasti (i.e. a span or 12 Aṅgulas) long, neither more nor less. One should sit comfortably facing the north or the east. One should remain silent while chewing.

## \|\| 1.17.15 \|\|

*kāmaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ hṛdaye kṛtvā samabhimantrya ca \|*  
*maṃtreṇānena matimānaśnīyāddantadhāvanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. One may have some specific desire cherished in the heart, in which case one should recite the following Mantra. An intelligent (householder) shall chew the twig always in this manner.

## \|\| 1.17.16 \|\|

*varaṃ dattvā'bhijānāsi kāmaṃ caiva vanaspate \|*  
*siddhiṃ prayaccha me nityaṃ dantakāṣṭha namo'stu te \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. “O Dantakāṣṭha (toothbrush twig), obeisance to you. O Vanaspati (tree or plant), you have granted me the boon. Hence you know my desire. Grant me the full Siddhi (accomplishment of desire) always.”

## \|\| 1.17.17 \|\|

*trīnvārānparijapyaivaṃ bhakṣayeddaṃtadhāvanam \|*  
*paścātprakṣālya tatkāṣṭhaṃ śucau deśe vinikṣipet \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. After repeating the above Mantra three times, one should begin to Chew the twig. After cleansing the mouth, the twig is washed and kept in a clean place.

## \|\| 1.17.18 \|\|

*daṃtakāṣṭhena deveśi na jihvāṃ parimārjayet \|*  
*pṛthakpṛthaktadā kāryaṃ yadīcchedvipulaṃ yaśaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O goddess of Devas, the tongue should not be cleaned by means of this twig. If one desires good reputation, one should do these two acts separately..

## \|\| 1.17.19 \|\|

*aṃgulyā daṃtakāṣṭhaṃ ca pratyakṣaṃ lavaṇaṃ ca yat \|*  
*mṛttikābhakṣaṇaṃ caiva tulyaṃ gomāṃsabhakṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Cleansing the teeth with finger, taking in salt by itself directly and eating mud—all these are on a par with eating cow’s meat.

## \|\| 1.17.20 \|\|

*mukhe paryuṣite nityaṃ bhavatyaprayato dvijaḥ \|*  
*tasmācchuṣkamathārdraṃ vā bhakṣayeddaṃtadhāvanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. If the mouth remains stale (i.e unwashed) a Brāhmaṇa always becomes impure. Hence one must use a dry or damp tooth-brush twig.

## \|\| 1.17.21 \|\|

*varjite divase caiva gaḍūṣāṃścaiva ṣoḍaśa \|*  
*tattatpadmasugandhairvā mukhaśuddhiṃ ca kārayet \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. On days when Dantakāṣṭha is prohibited one must gargle sixteen times with sixteen mouthfuls of water. One should cleanse mouth with water rendered fragrant by means of lotus.

## \|\| 1.17.22 \|\|

*mukhaśuddhimakṛtvā yo bhāskaraṃ spṛśati dvijaḥ \|*  
*trīṇi varṣasahasrāṇi sa kuṣṭhī jāyate naraḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A Brāhmaṇa who touches (the idol of) Bhāskara without cleaning the mouth, becomes a leper for three thousand years.

## \|\| 1.17.23 \|\|

*evaṃ vastrādi saṃśodhya tataḥ snānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*śucau manorame sthāne saṃgṛhyāstreṇa mṛttikām \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. After washing clothes etc. a person should take his bath. A lump of clay should be extracted from a clean pleasing spot with the Astra Mantra repeated.

## \|\| 1.17.24 \|\|

*sānusvārokārayuto hakāraḥ phaṭsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*anenāstreṇa saṃgṛhya snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The letter “H” along with the letter “U” and Anusvāra \[Ṃ\] and Phaṭ is called Astra Mantra (i.e. Huṃphaṭ). One should gather a lump of clay by repeating this Mantra and then take bath.

## \|\| 1.17.25-26 \|\|

*bhāgatrayaṃ tu saṃśuddhaṃ tṛṇapāṣāṇavarjitam \|*  
*ekamastreṇa cālabhya tathānyaṃ bhāskareṇa tu \|\| 25 \|\|*

*aṃgaiścaiva tṛtīyaṃ tu abhimaṃtrya sakṛtsakṛt \|*  
*japtvāstreṇa kṣipeddikṣu nirvighnaṃ tu jalaṃ bhavet \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. The lump of clay should be without grass blades or gravel. Three parts thereof are made. One part is to be rubbed well repeating the Astra Mantra; another part with the Bhāskara Mantra. The third part is to be charged with the ancillary Mantras once each. After uttering the Astra Mantra, the clay is to be thrown in different directions. Now the water has become free from impediments.

## \|\| 1.17.27 \|\|

*sūryatīrtha dvitīyena tṛtīyena sakṛtsakṛt \|*  
*guṃṭhayitvā tataḥ snāyādravitīrthena mānavaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. A man should cover (ritualistically) the Sūryatīrtha with the second and third parts once each. Then he shall take his bath in the Ravitīrtha.

## \|\| 1.17.28 \|\|

*tūryaśaṃkha ninādena dhyātvā devaṃ divākaram \|*  
*snātvā rājopacāreṇa punarācamya yatnataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The sounds of musical instruments and conch should be thought of when the devotee meditates on Lord Divākara. After the bath, the Ācamana rite is performed again with royal ostentatiousness.

## \|\| 1.17.29-30 \|\|

*snānaṃ kṛtvā tato devi maṃtrarājena saṃyutam \|*  
*harephau biṃdu lakṣmīśca tathā'nyo dīrghayā saha \|\| 29 \|\|*

*mātrayā rephasaṃyukto hakāro biṃdunā saha \|*  
*sakāraḥ savisargastu maṃtrarājo'yamucyate \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. The bath is performed along with the utterance of the Mantrarāja\[2\]. The mantrarāja is as follows: Letters “H” and “R” along with Bindu (dot) and Lakṣmī. Then the vowel is lengthened. The letter “S” with the Visarga. Ultimately OM HRĪṂ HREṂ SAḤ becomes the Mantrarāja.

## \|\| 1.17.31 \|\|

*tatastu tarppayenmaṃtrānsarvāṃstāṃstu karāgrajaiḥ \|*  
*tulanādūrdhvato devānsavyena ca munīṃstathā \|*  
*pitṝṃścaivāpasavyena hṛdbījena pratarpayet \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Then the devotee propitiates all the Mantras with the fīngers.The Devas are to be meditated on the point where all the finger dps converge. The sages are to be meditated on the left side (Savya) and the Pitṛs should be propitiated anticlockwise (Apasavya).

## \|\| 1.17.32 \|\|

*yadgītaṃ pravaraṃ loke akṣarāṇāṃ manīṣibhiḥ \|*  
*ekonaviṃśaṃ mātrāyā akṣaraṃ tatprakīrttitam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Akṣara (Imperishable) is that which is sung about by learned men as the most excellent of all letters. It has nineteen Mātrās.

## \|\| 1.17.33 \|\|

*evaṃ snātvā vidhānena saṃdhyāṃ vaṃdedvidhānataḥ \|*  
*tato vidvānkṣipetpaścādbhāskarāyodakāṃjalim \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. After taking the holy bath thus in accordance with the injunctions, the person should offer the Sandhyā prayers duly. Then the learned devotee offers water with palms joined together (as a cup) to Bhāskara.

## \|\| 1.17.34 \|\|

*japecca tryakṣaraṃ maṃtra ṣaṇmukhaṃ ca yadṛcchayā \|*  
*maṃtrarājeti yaḥ pūrvaṃ tavākhyāto mayā priye \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Then he should perform the Japa of the three-syllabled and six-faced Mantra casually (or as he pleases). O beloved, this has already been mentioned to you as Mantrarāja.

## \|\| 1.17.35 \|\|

*paścāttīrthena maṃtrāstu saṃhṛtya hṛdaye nyaset \|*  
*maṃtrairātmānamekatra kṛtvā cārghaṃ pradāpayet \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Afterwards the person concentrates the mantras and ritualistically touches the heart with the Tīrtha (holy water). Through the Mantras, he concentrates in the soul and offers the Arghya.

## \|\| 1.17.36 \|\|

*raktacaṃdanagaṃdhaistu śuciḥsnāto mahītale \|*  
*kṛtvā maṃḍalakaṃ vṛttamekacitto vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The devotee remains clean after the bath. He makes a circular diagram on the ground by means of sweet scents and red sandal-paste. He then sits there with mental concentration.

## \|\| 1.17.37 \|\|

*gṛhītvā karavīrāṇi tāmre saṃsthāpya bhājane \|*  
*tilataṃdulasaṃyuktaṃ kuśagandhodakena tu \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Karavīra flowers are placed in a copper vessel, scented water is poured into it and gingelly seeds, Kuśa grass and raw rice-grains are put into it.

## \|\| 1.17.38 \|\|

*raktacaṃdana dhūpena yuktamarghyopasādhitam \|*  
*kṛtvā śirasi tatpātraṃ jānubhyāmavaniṃ gataḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The materials of worship are fumigated with incense and red sandal. The devotee places that pot on his head and kneels down on the ground.

## \|\| 1.17.39 \|\|

*mūlamaṃtreṇa saṃyuktamarghyaṃ dadyācca bhānave \|*  
*mucyate sarvapāpaistu yo hyevaṃ vinivedayet \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. He then offers the Arghya to Bhānu (the Sun-god) uttering the Mūla Mantra. He who makes this offering is rid of all sins.

## \|\| 1.17.40 \|\|

*yadyugādisahasreṇa vyatīpātaśatena ca \|*  
*ayanānāṃ sahasreṇa yatphalaṃ jyeṣṭhapuṣkare \|*  
*tatphalaṃ samavāpnoti sūryāyārghya nivedane \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. By offering Arghya to the Sun, one obtains that benefit, O goddess, which one gets by offering Arghya in Jyeṣṭha Puṣkara in the course of a thousand Yugādis, a hundred Vyatīpātas and a thousand Ayanas (transits of the Sun).

## \|\| 1.17.41 \|\|

*dīkṣāmaṃtravihīno'pi bhaktyā saṃvatsareṇa tu \|*  
*phalamargheṇa vai devi labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. There is no doubt about it, O goddess, that even if one be without the initiation and utterance of the Mantra, the devotee obtains the benefit through the Arghya, if offered with devotion for a year.

## \|\| 1.17.42 \|\|

*yaḥ punardīkṣito vidvānvidhinārghyaṃ nivedayet \|*  
*nāsau saṃbhavate bhūmau pralayaṃ yāti bhāskare \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. In the case of a devotee who is learned and has due initiation, if he offers Arghya to the Sun, he is not reborn on the earth, even when Bhāskara gets dissolved.

## \|\| 1.17.43 \|\|

*iha janmani saubhāgyamāyurārogyasaṃpadam \|*  
*acirāllabhate devi sabhāryaḥ sukhabhājanam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Along with his wife, O goddess, he attains ere long happiness in this very birth, conjugal felicity, long life, riches and freedom from illness.

## \|\| 1.17.44 \|\|

*evaṃ snānavidhiḥ proktaḥ sauraḥ saṃkṣepatastava \|*  
*hitāya mānavendrāṇāṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Thus for the sake of the welfare of good men, the procedure regarding holy bath for the propitiation of the Sun god has been succinctly told to you. It is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.17.45 \|\|

*athavā vedamārgeṇa kuryātsnānaṃ dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*yadyevaṃ mantravistāre hyaśakto dīkṣayā vinā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Or, an excellent Brāhmaṇa who is unable to perform the Snāna-rite with elaborate utterance of Mantras without the requisite Dīkṣā (initiation) can perform Snāna following the Vedic procedure.

## \|\| 1.17.46 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*atha pūjāvidhānaṃ te kathayāmi yaśasvini \|*  
*vedamārgeṇa divyena brāhmaṇānāṃ hitāya vai \|\| 46 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

46\. Now, O lady of good renown, I shall tell you the procedure regarding the Pūjā (worship) in accordance with the holy Vedic way. It is conducive to the welfare of Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.17.47 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃbhṛtasaṃbhāraḥ puṣpādipraguṇīkṛtaḥ \|*  
*tata āvāhayedbhānuṃ sthāpayetkarṇikopari \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. After the devotee has gathered together all the requisite things and has arranged in proper order the flowers etc. he should install the deity Bhānu on the Karṇikā and invoke him.

## \|\| 1.17.48 \|\|

*upasthānaṃ tu vai kṛtvā maṃtreṇānena suvrate \|*  
*udutyaṃ jātavedasamiti maṃtraḥ saṃparikīrtitaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. For the Upasthāna (waiting on the deity for the prayers to begin) the Mantra, beginning with udutyam jātavedasam (RV I.50.1) is to be used. This is the Mantra glorified, O lady of good holy rites.

## \|\| 1.17.49 \|\|

*agniṃ dūteti maṃtreṇa anenāvāhya bhāmini \|*  
*ākṛṣṇena rajasā maṃtreṇānena vā'rcayet \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The deity is to be invoked by. the Mantra beginning with agniṃ dūta etc. O lady of beauty, and adored by the Mantras beginning with ākṛṣṇena rajasā etc. (RV I.35.2)

## \|\| 1.17.50 \|\|

*haṃsaḥ śuciṣaditi maṃtreṇānena pūjayet \|*  
*apatyeteti mantreṇa sūryaṃ devi prapūjayet \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The Pūjā should be performed with the Mantra beginning with haṃsaḥ śuciṣaṭ (RV IV.40.5.). Special Pūjā should be performed with the Mantra beginning with apatye tāyavo vathā (RV I.50.2) etc., O goddess.

## \|\| 1.17.51 \|\|

*adṛśramasya caitena sūryaṃ devi samarccayet \|*  
*taraṇirviśvadarśeti anena satataṃ japam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The excellent Samārcana of Sūrya should be performed, O goddess, with the Mantra beginning with adṛśramasya (RV I.50.3.) etc. There must be constant Japa with the Mantra beginning with taraṇir viśva darśa etc. (RV I.50.4).

## \|\| 1.17.52 \|\|

*citraṃ devānāmudeti bhadrāṃ devo sadārcayet \|*  
*vibhūtimarccayennityaṃ yenā pāvaka cakṣasā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Bhadrā Devī should always be adored with the Mantras beginning with citraṃ devānām udagāt (RV 1.115.1). Vibhūti (glory) should always be adored with the Mantra beginning with yenā pāvaka cakṣasā etc. (RV I.50.6)

## \|\| 1.17.53 \|\|

*vidyāmepirajaspṛthvityanena vimalāṃ sadā \|*  
*amoghāṃ pūjayennityaṃ maṃtreṇānena suvrate \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Vimalā should always be adored with the Mantra beginning with vidyām eṣi rajaspṛthu etc. (RV I.50.7), O lady of excellent holy rites. Amoghā should always be worshipped with the same Mantra.

## \|\| 1.17.54 \|\|

*sapta tvā harito'nena siddhidāṃ sarvakarmasu \|*  
*vidyutāmarcayeddevaṃ sapta tvā haritena ca \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Siddhidā (The bestower of Siddhis) in all the holy rites should be worshipped with the Mantra beginning with sapta tvā haritaḥ (RV I.50.8) etc. With the same sapta tvā haritaḥ, one should worship the Lord of Vidyuts (Lightning).

## \|\| 1.17.55 \|\|

*navamīṃ pūjayeddevīṃ satataṃ sarvatomukhīm \|*  
*mantreṇānena vai devi udvayantamitīha vai \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. With the Mantra beginning with ud vayam tamasas pari (RV I.50.10) etc. one should worship the ninth goddess Sarvatomukhī always, O goddess.

## \|\| 1.17.56 \|\|

*udyannadya mitramahaḥ prathamamakṣaraṃ japet \|*  
*dvitīyaṃ pūjayeddevi śukeṣu me harimeti vai \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The first Bījākṣara should be repeated after uttering the Mantra beginning with udyannadya mitramahaḥ (RV I.50.11). The second should be adored, O goddess, with the Mantra śukeṣu me harimānam (RV I.50.12).

## \|\| 1.17.57 \|\|

*udagādayamādityo hyanenāpi tṛtīyakam \|*  
*tatsaviturvareṇyeti caturthaṃ parikīrtitam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. With the Mantra beginning with udagādayam ādityaḥ etc. (RV I.50.13) one should worship the third Bījākṣara. It is glorified that the fourth Bījākṣara should be worshipped with the Mantra beginning with Tat Savitur Vareṇyam etc. (RV III.62.10).

## \|\| 1.17.58 \|\|

*mahāhivo mahāyeti pañcamaṃ parikīrtitam \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartata ṣaṣṭhaṃ bījaṃ prakīrtitam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. It is proclaimed that the fifth should be adored with the Mantra beginning with mahāhivo mahāyā etc. With the Mantra beginning with hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartata (RV X.1.1) etc. the sixth one should be adored.

## \|\| 1.17.59 \|\|

*savitā paścātātsavitā saptamaṃ varavarṇini \|*  
*evaṃ bījāni vinyasya ādityaṃ sthāpayecchubhe \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. O lady of excellent complexion, the seventh Bīja should be adored with the Mantra beginning with savitā paścāttāt savitā (RV X.36.14) etc. After performing the rite of Nyāsa thus, O splendid lady, Āditya should be installed.

## \|\| 1.17.60 \|\|

*ādityaṃ sthāpayitvā tu paścādaṅgāni vinyaset \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. After installing Āditya, the devotee should perform the Nyāsa of the Aṅgas.

## \|\| 1.17.61 \|\|

*āgneyyāṃ hṛdayaṃ nyasya aiśānyāṃ tu śiro nyaset \|*  
*nairṛtyāṃ tu śikhāṃ caiva kavacaṃ vāyugocare \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The Nyāsa of the heart is in the south-east, that of Śiras in the north-east, that of Śikhā (tuft of hair) in the south-west and that of Kavaca (coat of mail) in the north-west.

## \|\| 1.17.62 \|\|

*astraṃ diśāsu vinyasya svabījena tu karṇikām \|*  
*amosi prāṇiteneti anena hṛdayaṃ yajet \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. After the Nyāsa of the Astra in the quarters the Karṇikā (pericarp) should be adored with its Bīja. One should perform the Pūjā of the Hṛdaya with the Mantra beginning with amosi prāṇitena (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra)

## \|\| 1.17.63 \|\|

*śirastu pūjayeddevi āyuṣyaṃ varcaseti vai \|*  
*gāyatryā tu śikhāṃ pūjya nairṛtyāṃ tu vyavasthitām \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. One should worship the head, O goddess, with the Mantra beginning with āyuṣyam varcaseti vaī etc. (RV, Khila X. 128.2). Śikhā set up in the south-west should be worshipped with the Gāyatrī Mantra.

## \|\| 1.17.64 \|\|

*jīmūtasyeva bhavati pratyekaṃ kavacaṃ yajet \|*  
*dhanvannāgā dhanvaneti anenāstraṃ sadā'rcayet \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. One should worship kavaca separately with the Mantra beginning with jīmūtasyeva bhavati etc. (RV VI.75.1.) The Astra should always be adored with the Mantra beginning with dhanvannāgā dhanvanā etc. (RV VI.75.2.).

## \|\| 1.17.65 \|\|

*netraṃ tu pūjayeddevi aśvinā tejaseti ca \|*  
*hyataḥ pūrvataḥ somaṃ dakṣiṇena budhaṃ tathā \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Netra (eye) should be worshipped, O goddess, with the Mantra beginning with aśvinā tejasā etc. (Vājasaneyī Saṃhitā 20.80). Externally the Nyāsa of Soma (Moon) is in the east, that of Budha in the south.

## \|\| 1.17.66 \|\|

*paścimena guruṃ nyasya uttareṇa ca bhārgavam \|*  
*āgneyyāṃ maṅgalaṃ nyasya nairṛtyāṃ tu śanaiścaram \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Guru (Jupiter) should be placed (Nyāsa) in the west, the Nyāsa of Bhārgava is in the north. The Nyāsa of Maṅgala is in the south-east and that of Śānaiścara is in the south-west.

## \|\| 1.17.67 \|\|

*vāyavyāṃ tu nyasedrāhuṃ ketumīśānagocare \|*  
*āpyāyasveti mantreṇa devi somaṃ sadārcayet \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The Nyāsa of Rāhu is in the north-west and that of Ketu is in the north-east. One should always worship Soma with the Mantra beginning with āpyāyasva etc. (RV I.91.16.17). The Pratīka is common to both.

## \|\| 1.17.68 \|\|

*udbudhyadhvaṃ mahādevi budhaṃ tatra sadārcayet \|*  
*bṛhaspateti mantreṇa pūjayetsatataṃ gurum \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. O great goddess, Budha should be always worshipped there with the Mantra beginning with udbudhyadhvam etc. (RV X.101.1). Guru should always be adored with the Mantra beginning with bṛhaspate etc.

## \|\| 1.17.69 \|\|

*śukraḥ śuśukvāniti ca bhārgavaṃ devi pūjayet \|*  
*agnirmūrddheti mantreṇa sadā maṃgalamarcayet \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. O goddess, Bhārgava should be worshipped with the Mantra beginning with śukraḥ śuśukvān etc. One should always adore Maṅgala (Mars) with the Mantra beginning with apnirmūrdhā etc. (RV VIII.44.16).

## \|\| 1.17.70 \|\|

*śamagniritimantreṇa pūjayedbhāskarātmajam \|*  
*kayānaścitretimantreṇa devi rāhuṃ sadā'rcayet \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. One should adore the son of Bhāskara (i.e. Saturn) with the Mantra śam agni (RV VIII.18.9) etc. O goddess, one should always worship Rāhu with the Mantra kayā naścitrā (RV IV.31.1).

## \|\| 1.17.71 \|\|

*ketuṃ kṛṇveti ketuṃ vai satataṃ pūjayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*bāhyataḥ pūrvataḥ śukraṃ dakṣiṇena yamaṃ tathā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. A sensible man should always worship Ketu with the Mantra beginning with ketum kṛṇvanti (RV I.6.3). etc. Externally the following deities are installed: Śakra in the east, Yama in the south.

## \|\| 1.17.72 \|\|

*aiśānyāmīśvaraṃ viṃdyādāgneyyāmagnirucyate \|*  
*naiṛteti virūpākṣaṃ pavanaṃ vāyugocare \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Īśvara should be known in the north-east, Agni in the south-east, Virūpākṣa in the south-west and Pavana in the north-west.

## \|\| 1.17.73 \|\|

*tamuṣṭavāma iti vai hyanenendramathārcayet \|*  
*udīratāmavareti sadā vaivasvataṃ yajet \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. One should adore Indra with the Mantra beginning with tamuṣṭavāma etc. and one should always worship Vaivasvata (i.e. Yama) with the Mantra beginning with udīratām avara etc.

## \|\| 1.17.74 \|\|

*tattvāyāmīti mantreṇa varuṇaṃ devi pūjayet \|*  
*indrāsomāvata iti mantreṇa dhanadaṃ yajet \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. O goddess, one should always worship Varuṇa with the Mantra beginning with tattvāyāmi (RV I.24.11) etc. and worship Dhanada with the Mantra beginning with indrāsomāvata.

## \|\| 1.17.75 \|\|

*pāvakaṃ pūjayeddevi agnimīḷe purohitam \|*  
*rakṣohaṇaṃ vājineti virūpākṣaṃ sadārcayet \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. O goddess, one should worship Pāvaka (Fire) with the Mantra beginning with agnim īḷe purohitam (RV I.1.1). etc. and worship Virūpākṣa with the Mantra beginning with rakṣohaṇam vājinā (RV X.87.1). etc.

## \|\| 1.17.76 \|\|

*vāyavāyāhi mantreṇa vāyuṃ devi sadārcayet \|*  
*yathākramamimāndevi sarvānvai pūjayedbudhaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. O goddess, one should always worship Vāyu with the Mantra beginning with vāyavāyāhi etc. A sensible man should always worship these Devas in this order.

## \|\| 1.17.77-79 \|\|

*bāhyataḥ pūrvato devi indrādīnāṃ samantataḥ \|*  
*raktavarṇaṃ mahātejaṃ sitapadmopari sthitam \|\| 77 \|\|*

*sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyuktaṃ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitam \|*  
*dvibhujaṃ caikavaktraṃ ca saumyapañcakadhṛkkaram \|\| 78 \|\|*

*varttulaṃ tejabiṃbaṃ tu madhyasthaṃ raktavāsasam \|*  
*ādityasya tvidaṃ rūpaṃ sarvalokeṣu pūjitam \|*  
*dhyātvā saṃpūjayennityaṃ sthaṃḍilaṃ maṇḍalāśrayam \|\| 79 \|\|*

77-79. Externally the adoration of Indra etc. from the east etc. should be performed thus all round:

Āditya’s Rūpa (form) should be meditated upon on the ground where the mystic diagram (Maṇḍala) is drawn. It is red in colour and highly brilliant. It is stationed on a white lotus. It has all the characteristic features and is adorned with all ornaments. It has two arms and a single countenance. The hands hold Saumya Pañcaka. The radiant disc is circular and is stationed in the centre. The cloth is red in colour. This form of Āditya is adored in all the worlds.

## \|\| 1.17.80 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*maṇḍalasthaḥ suraśreṣṭha vidhinā yena bhāskaraḥ \|*  
*pūjyate mānavairbhaktyā sa vidhiḥ kathitastvayā \|\| 80 \|\|*

The Devī said:

80\. The procedure of the adoration of Bhāskara as stationed in the Maṇḍala (mystic diagram) has been mentioned by you. You have explained how he should be worshipped devoutly by men, O Suraśreṣṭha.

## \|\| 1.17.81 \|\|

*pūjayedvidhinā yena bhāskaraṃ padmasaṃbhavam \|*  
*mūrttisthaṃ sarvagaṃ devaṃ tanme kathaya śaṃkara \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. O Śaṅkara, tell me how one should duly worship Bhāskara, the omnipresent Lord stationed in (represented as) the idol and arising from the lotus.

## \|\| 1.17.82 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*sādhusādhu mahādevi sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi suvate \|*  
*śṛṇuṣvaikamanā devi mūrtithaṃ yena pūjayet \|\| 82 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

82\. Well! Well! O great goddess of good holy rites, I have been well asked. O goddess, listen attentively. I shall tell you how to worship the Lord stationed in an idol.

## \|\| 1.17.83 \|\|

*iṣetveti ca mantreṇa uttamāṃgaṃ sadārcayet \|*  
*agnimīḷeti mantreṇa pūjayeddakṣiṇaṃ karam \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. The Uttamāṅga (head) should always be worshipped with the Mantra beginning with ise tvā etc. The right hand should be worshipped with the Mantra beginning with agnim īḷe etc. (RV I.1.1).

## \|\| 1.17.84 \|\|

*agna āyāhi mantreṇa pādau devasya pūjayet \|*  
*ājighreti ca mantreṇa pūjayetpuṣpamālayā \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. The feet of the Lord should be worshipped with the Mantra beginning with agnā ā yāhi etc. One should adore the deity with flower garland with the Mantra beginning with ājighra etc.

## \|\| 1.17.85 \|\|

*yogeyogeti mantreṇa muktapuṣpāṃjaliṃ kṣipet \|*  
*samudrāgaccha yatproktamanena snāpayedravim \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Handfuls of loose flowers should be scattered with the Mantra beginning with yoge yoge (RV I.30.7) etc. The devotee bathes Ravi with the Mantra samudrāgaccha etc.

## \|\| 1.17.86 \|\|

*imaṃ me gaṃgeti yatproktamanenāpi ca bhāmini \|*  
*samudrajyeti mantreṇa kṣālayedvidhivadravim \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. O beautiful lady, the deity can be bathed with the Mantra beginning with imaṃ me gaṅge etc. also. The bathing rite (with medicinal herbs) is to be duly performed with the mantra beginning with samudrajyā etc.

## \|\| 1.17.87 \|\|

*sinīvālīti mantreṇa snāpayecchaṃkhavāriṇā \|*  
*yajñaṃ yajñeti mantreṇa kaṣāyaiḥ parirakṣayet \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. One should bathe with water from a conch with the Mantra beginning with sinivālī etc. Uttering yajñam yajñena etc. ointments and unguents are smeared over the idol.

## \|\| 1.17.88 \|\|

*snāpayetpayasā devi āpyāyasveti maṃtrataḥ \|*  
*dadhikrāvṇeti vai dadhnā snāpayedvidhivadravim \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. O goddess, one should bathe the deity with milk uttering the Mantra beginning with āpyāyasva. One should duly bathe Ravi with curds uttering the mantra dadhikrāvṇa etc.

## \|\| 1.17.89 \|\|

*imaṃ me gaṃgeti yatproktamanenāpi ca bhāmini \|*  
*samudrajyeti maṃtreṇa snānamauṣadhibhiḥ smṛtam \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. It can also be done, O beautiful lady, with the Mantra beginning with imaṃ me gaṅge etc. It is remembered that the bathing with herbal medicines is performed with the Mantra samudrajyā etc.

## \|\| 1.17.90 \|\|

*udvartayettato bhānuṃ dvipadābhirvarānane \|*  
*mānastoketi maṃtreṇa yugapatsnānamācaret \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Then one should anoint the body of the (Sun) deity with perfumes etc. uttering Dvipadas (two-footed verses etc.) The simultaneous bath with several liquids shall be performed with the Mantra beginning with manastoke etc.

## \|\| 1.17.91 \|\|

*viṣṇorarāṭamantreṇa snāpayedgaṃdhavāriṇā \|*  
*sauvarṇena tu maṃtreṇa arghyaṃ pādyaṃ nivedayet \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. One should bathe with scented water with the Mantra viṣṇo rarāṭa etc. and offer Arghya and Pādya with the Sauvarṇa Mantra.

## \|\| 1.17.92 \|\|

*idaṃ viṣṇurvicakrame maṃtreṇārghyaṃ pradāpayet \|*  
*vedosīti ca maṃtreṇa upavītaṃ pradāpayet \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. The Arghya is offered with the Mantra idam viṣṇur vicakrame etc. Upavīta (sacred thread) is offered with the Mantra vedosi etc.

## \|\| 1.17.93 \|\|

*bṛhaspateti maṃtreṇa dadyādvastrāṇi bhānave \|*  
*yena śriyaṃ prakurvāṇaḥ puṣpamālāṃ prapūjayet \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. One shall offer garments to Bhānu uttering the Mantra bṛhaspate etc. One shall adore with flower garland with the Mantra yena śriyam prakurvāṇaḥ.

## \|\| 1.17.94 \|\|

*dhūrasīti ca maṃtreṇa dhūpaṃ dadyātsaguggalam \|*  
*samiddhoṃjanamaṃtreṇa aṃjanaṃ tu pradāpayet \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Dhūpa (Incense) is offered with Guggala uttering the Mantra dhūrasi etc. One shall offer Añjana (collyrium) with the Mantra beginning with śamiddhoñjana etc. (Vāj. Saṃhitā 29.1).

## \|\| 1.17.95 \|\|

*yuṃjāna iti maṃtreṇa bhānuṃ rocanamālabhet \|*  
*ārārttikaṃ ca vai kuryāddīrghāyutvāya vai punaḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. One should rub Bhānu with Rocana (Yellow pigment) uttering the Mantra yuñjāna etc. For the sake of longevity Ārārtika (waving of lights) is offered.

## \|\| 1.17.96 \|\|

*sahasraśīrṣā puruṣaḥ sūryaṃ śirasi pūjayet \|*  
*śaṃbhavāyeti maṃtreṇa ravernetre parāmṛśet \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. The Sun is worshipped at the head uttering the Mantra sahasraśīrṣā puruṣaḥ (RV X.90.1) etc. The eyes of Ravi should be wiped (or touched) with the Mantra śambhavāya.

## \|\| 1.17.97 \|\|

*viśvataścakṣurityevaṃ bhānordehaṃ samālabhet \|*  
*śrīśca te lakṣmīśceti sarvāṃge pūjayedravim \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. The whole body of Bhānu is rubbed with the Mantra viśvataścakṣuḥ etc. Ravi is worshipped in all the limbs with the Mantra srīśca lakṣmīśca etc.

## \|\| 1.17.98 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|\|*  
*atha merormahādevi aṣṭaśṛṃgasya suvrate \|*  
*pūjāvidhānamaṃtrāṃste kathayāmi samāsataḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

98\. Now, O great goddess of holy rites, I shall briefly tell you the Mantras relevant to the adoration of the eight-peaked Meru.

## \|\| 1.17.99 \|\|

*aṣṭaśṛṃgaṃ mahādevi anena vidhinā'rcayet \|*  
*prathamaṃ pūjayenmadhye maṃtreṇānena suvrate \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. O great goddess, the Aṣṭaśṛṅga (eight-peaked mountain) is to be adored in this manner. One shall adore the first peak in the middle by the following Mantra, O lady of good holy rites.

## \|\| 1.17.100 \|\|

*mahāhivomahāyeti nānāpuṣpakadaṃbakaiḥ \|*  
*trātāramiṃdramaṃtreṇa pūrvaśṛṃgaṃ sadārcayet \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Uttering the Mantra mahāhivomahāya etc. diverse kinds of flowers are offered. One should always adore the eastern peak with the Mantra trātāram indra etc. (Vāj. Saṃhitā 8.46).

## \|\| 1.17.101-102 \|\|

*tamuṣṭavāmeti maṃtreṇa pūjayetsurasundari \|*  
*agnimīḷe purohitamāgneyaṃ śṛṃgamarcayet \|\| 101 \|\|*

*āgneyyā caiva gāyatryā athavānena pūjayet \|*  
*yamāya tvā makhāya tvā dakṣiṇaṃ śṛṃgamarca yet \|\| 102 \|\|*

101-102. O beautiful lady of the Suras, Pūjā should be performed unto him uttering the Mantra tamūṣṭavāma etc. One should adore the south-east peak with the Mantra agnim iḷe purohitam (RV I.1.1). It can be adored either with Āgneyī Gāyatrī or this Mantra. One should adore the southern peak with the Mantra yamāya tvā makhāya tvā etc. (Vāj. Saṃhitā 37.11).

## \|\| 1.17.103 \|\|

*udīratāmavarepyathavānena pūjayet \|*  
*āyaṃ gauriti maṃtreṇa nairṛtyaṃ śṛṅgamarcayet \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. The Pūjā can also be done with the Mantra udīratām avare etc. or with this Mantra. One should adore the southwestern peak with the Mantra beginning with āyaṃ gauḥ.

## \|\| 1.17.104 \|\|

*rakṣohaṇaṃ vājinaṃ vā pūjayedasurāṃtikam \|*  
*iṃdrāsomā ca yo maṃtro hyathavā tena pūjayet \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. Asurāntika can also be worshipped with the Mantra rakṣohaṇam vājinam vā (RV X.87.1) etc. or with the Mantra indrāsomā ca vo etc.

## \|\| 1.17.105 \|\|

*abhi tvā sūra nonviti caiśānaṃ śṛṃgamarcayet \|*  
*yenedaṃ bhūtamiti vā athavānena pūjayet \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. One should worship the north-eastern peak with the Mantra beginning with abhi tvā sūra nonuma. etc. (RV VII.32.22) or the Mantra beginning with yenedam bhūtam etc. (Vāj. Saṃ 34.4.)

## \|\| 1.17.106 \|\|

*namostu sarpebhya iti merupīṭhaṃ sadā'rcayet \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavarttateti punarmadhye sadārcayet \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. One shall always adore Merupīṭha uttering namostu sarpebhyaḥ etc. Again one should always adore in the centre with the Mantra hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgre etc. (RV X.121.1.).

## \|\| 1.17.107 \|\|

*savitā paścātāditi vai pūjayetpuṣpa mālayā \|*  
*trikālamarcayeddevi pradadyādarghyamādarāt \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. One should offer flower garland uttering the Mantra savitā paścāttāt etc. (RV X.36.14) The Arcanā should be performed thrice a day, O goddess, and the Arghya is offered with great respect.

## \|\| 1.17.108 \|\|

*mātā rudrāṇāṃ duhitā vasūnāṃ pūrvāhne caiva pūjayet \|*  
*madhyāhne pūjayeddevi tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. In the forenoon, the Pūjā is performed uttering the Mantra mātā rudrāṇām duhitā vasūnām etc. (RV VIII.101.15). O goddess, at midday, the Pūjā is done with the Mantra beginning with tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam etc. (RV I.22.20).

## \|\| 1.17.109 \|\|

*haṃsaḥ śuciṣaditi vā aparāhṇe sadārcayet \|*  
*evaṃ bhānuṃ grahaiḥ sārddha pūjayedvaravarṇini \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. In the afternoon the Pūjā is offered with the Mantra beginning with haṃsaḥ śuciṣat (RV IV.40.5.) etc. Thus, O lady of excellent complexion, one should adore Bhānu along with the planets.

## \|\| 1.17.110 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*yāni puṣpāṇi ceṣṭāni sadā bhāskarapūjane \|*  
*kāni coktāni deveśa kathayasva prasādataḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

The Devī said:

110\. O Lord of Devas, do me this favour of telling me the names of the flowers always recommended in the adoration of Bhāskara. What are the flowers mentioned in this connection?

\[Sub-Chapter: Puṣpādhyāya (Chapter on flowers)\]

## \|\| 1.17.124 \|\|

*kiṃ tasya na bhavelloke yaścaibhiścārcayedravim \|*  
*upalipyālayaṃ yastu kuryānmaṃḍalakaṃ śubham \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. If one worships Ravi with all these, what is it that he will not get. The devotee should smear and plaster the shrine and draw the auspicious Maṇḍalaka.

## \|\| 1.17.125 \|\|

*ekenāsya bhavedartho dvābhyāmārogyamaśnute \|*  
*tribhistu sarvavidyāvāṃścaturbhirbhogavānbhavet \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. If one such Maṇḍalaka is drawn, one shall attain wealth. With two such, one attains normalcy of health. With three, one acquires all lores, and with four, one shall enjoy all pleasures.

## \|\| 1.17.126 \|\|

*paṃcabhirvipulaṃ dhānyaṃ ṣaḍbhirāyurbalaṃ yaśaḥ \|*  
*saptamaṇḍalatārī syānmaṃḍalādhipatirnaraḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. Through five, one attains plenty of food grains; through six, Longevity, strength and fame; and one who draws seven Maṇḍalas, shall become a Maṇḍalādhipati (a sovereign).

## \|\| 1.17.127 \|\|

*ghṛtadīpapradānena cakṣuṣmāñjāyate naraḥ \|*  
*kaṭutailasya dīpena svaṃ śatruṃ jayate naraḥ \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. By offering a light with clarified butter, a man becomes one with good vision. A man offering light with mustard oil defeats his enemy.

## \|\| 1.17.128 \|\|

*tailadīpapradānena sūryaloke mahīyate \|*  
*madhūkatailadīpena saubhāgyaṃ paramaṃ labhet \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. By offering light with gingelly oil, one is honoured in the world of the Sun. One will attain great Saubhāgya (conjugal felicity) through the light with Madhūka oil.

## \|\| 1.17.129 \|\|

*puṣpāṇāṃ pravarā jātī dhūpānāṃ vijayaḥ paraḥ \|*  
*gandhānāṃ kuṃkumaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ lepānāṃ raktacaṃdanam \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. Jāti is the most excellent one of all flowers. Vijaya (yellow myrobalan) is the greatest among the incenses. Kuṃkuma (saffron) is the most excellent of all sweet scents. Red sandal-paste is the most excellent one of all unguents.

## \|\| 1.17.130 \|\|

*dīpadāne ghṛtaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ naivedye modakaḥ param \|*  
*etaistuṣyati deveśaḥ sāṃnidhyaṃ cādhigacchati \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. Among light offerings that of clarified butter is the most excellent. Among food offerings, sweetmeat is the best. The Lord of Devas becomes pleased with all these and grants Sānnidhya (proximity).

## \|\| 1.17.131-135 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃpūjya vidhi vatkṛtvā pitṛpradakṣiṇām \|*  
*praṇamya śirasā devaṃ tatra cārkasthalaṃ priye \|\| 131 \|\|*

*sukhāsīnastataḥ paśyedraverabhimukhe sthitaḥ \|*  
*ekaṃ siddhārthakaṃ kṛtvā haste pānīyasaṃyutam \|\| 132 \|\|*

*kāmaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ hṛdaye kṛtvārkasthalasannidhau \|*  
*pibetsatoyaṃ taddevi hyaspṛṣṭaṃ daśanaiḥ sakṛt \|\| 133 \|\|*

*evaṃ kṛtvā naro devi koṭiyātrāphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*brahmā viṣṇurmahādevo jvalano dhanadastathā \|\| 134 \|\|*

*bhānumāśritya sarve te modante divi suvrate \|*  
*tasmādbhānusamaṃ devaṃ nāhaṃ paśyāmi kañcana \|\| 135 \|\|*

131-135. After duly adoring thus, the devotee circumambulates the Pitṛs and bows down to the deity. Facing Ravi, he sits comfortably and surveys Arkasthala (the region). He then should put a grain of white mustard in water taken on the palm. Wishing for whatever he has in the heart in the presence of Arkasthala, he should drink that water once, O goddess, without letting the teeth touch it.

## \|\| 1.17.134-135 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛtvā naro devi koṭiyātrāphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*brahmā viṣṇurmahādevo jvalano dhanadastathā \|\| 134 \|\|*

*bhānumāśritya sarve te modante divi suvrate \|*  
*tasmādbhānusamaṃ devaṃ nāhaṃ paśyāmi kañcana \|\| 135 \|\|*

134-135. By doing thus, O goddess, the man attains the benefit of a crore pilgrimages. O lady of excellent holy rites, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Mahādeva, Jvalana (Fire-god) and Dhanada (Kubera) resort to Bhānu (the Sun-god) and all of them rejoice in heaven. Hence Ido not see any deity on a par with Bhānu.

## \|\| 1.17.136 \|\|

*iti kṛtvā mahādevi punarbhānau pradakṣiṇam \|*  
*kuryānmantreṇa deveśi saptakṛtvo varānane \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. After the performance of all these, O great goddess of excellent countenance, the devotee circumambulates Bhānu seven times again uttering the Mantras.

## \|\| 1.17.137-140 \|\|

*tamuṣṭavāma iti ṛkprathamā parikīrtitā \|*  
*etonvindraṃ stavāmeti dvitīyā parikīrtitā \|\| 137 \|\|*

*iṃdra śuddho na āgahi tṛtīyā parikīrtitā \|*  
*indraṃ śuddho hi no rayiṃ caturthī parikīrtitā \|\| 138 \|\|*

*asya vāmasyeti śubhe pañcamī parikīrtitā \|*  
*tribhiṣṭvaṃ deva iti vai ṣaṣṭhī ca parikīrtitā \|\| 139 \|\|*

*daśa sāmāni vai yāni pravarāṇi manīṣibhiḥ \|*  
*gītāni sāmagairnityaṃ saptamīṃ taistu kārayet \|\| 140 \|\|*

137-140. The Mantras to be uttered during the circumambulation: For the first, the Ṛk beginning with taṃuṣṭavāma (RV VIII.96.6) etc. the second with the Ṛk beginning with etonvindram stavāma (RV VIII.95.7). The third is indramśuddho na āgahi (RV VIII.95.8) and the fourth is indraśuddho hi no rayim. O splendid lady, the fifth one is asya vāmasya (RV I.164) etc. The sixth one is tribhiṣṭvam deva. The devotee makes the seventh circumambulation chanting all the ten Sāmans sung about by the learned men following the Sāman Śākhā as the greatest.

## \|\| 1.17.141-144 \|\|

*tāni te kathayāmyadya daśa sāmāni sundari \|*  
*huṃkāraḥ praṇavodgīthaḥ prastāvaśca catuṣṭayam \|\| 141 \|\|*

*pañcamaṃ praharo yatra ṣaṣṭhamāraṇyakaṃ tathā \|*  
*nidhanaṃ saptamaṃ sāmnāṃ saptasiddhimiti smṛtam \|\| 142 \|\|*

*pañcavidhyamiti proktaṃ hrīṃkārapraṇavena tu \|*  
*aṣṭamaṃ ca tathā sādhyaṃ navamaṃ vāmadevakam \|\| 143 \|\|*

*jyeṣṭhaṃ tu daśamaṃ sāma vedhase priyamuttamam \|*  
*eteṣāṃ devi sāmnāṃ vai jāpyaṃ kāryaṃ vidhānataḥ \|\| 144 \|\|*

141-144. O beautiful lady, I shall tell you those ten Sāmans, Huṃkāra, Praṇava, Udgītha, Prastāva are the first four. The fifth one is Prahara and the sixth one is Āraṇyaka. The seventh of the Sāmans is Nidhana remembered as Saptasiddhi. The eighth one is the Pañcavidhya uttered along with Hrīm and Praṇava. The ninth one is Sādhya and Jyeṣṭha Vāmadevaka is the tenth Sāman excellent and dear to Vedhas (Brahmā). The Japa of all these Sāmans should be performed in accordance with the injunctions.

## \|\| 1.17.145 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhasāmaparaṃ caiva dvitīyaṃ gadataḥ śṛṇu \|*  
*na ca śrāvyaṃ dvitīyaṃ tu japtavyaṃ muktimicchatā \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. Listen to my explanation of another Jyeṣṭha Sāman, the second. It should not be (loudly) chanted. The Japa should be performed by one who wishes for salvation.

## \|\| 1.17.146 \|\|

*tajjāpyaṃ paramaṃ proktaṃ svayaṃ devena bhānunā \|*  
*jāpyasya viniyogo'sya lakṣaṇaṃ ca nibodha me \|*  
*stobhasāraṃ śvāsalīnamoṃkārādi smṛtaṃ budhaiḥ \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. That Jāpya is mentioned as the greatest by Lord Bhānu himself. The application and the definition of the Jāpya are being mentioned. Even as I expound it, listen and understand. Stobha (a division in the Sāman text) is its essence. Aukāra etc. get merged in the breath. It is remembered so by learned men.

## \|\| 1.17.147 \|\|

*ūrbhānuśca tathā dharmaṃ dharmaḥ satyaṃ hyṛta tathā \|*  
*dharmaṃ ye dharmavaddharme dharme vai nidhanaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. (Obscure—Urbhānu, dharmam, Dharma, Satya, Ṛta, dharmaṃ ye, dharmavaddharme, dharme vai dhanaṃ gatāh). (These are the allusions to the different passages.)

## \|\| 1.17.148 \|\|

*yadebhiśca yajecchabdairucitaṃ sāmagairdvijaiḥ \|*  
*jāpyaṃ caitatparaṃ proktaṃ svayaṃ devena bhānunā \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. With these words one should worship. It is so practised by the Brāhmaṇas following Sāman Śākhā. This Jāpya has been mentioned as the greatest by Lord Bhānu himself.

## \|\| 1.17.149 \|\|

*etadvai japyamānastu punarāvartate na tu \|*  
*sarvarogavinirmukto mucyate brahmahatyayā \|\| 149 \|\|*

149\. One who performs the Japa of this is never reborn in the world. Rid of all ailments he is liberated from the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter.

## \|\| 1.17.150 \|\|

*ājyadohādyadoheti jyeṣṭhasāmno'pi lakṣaṇam \|\| 150 \|\|*

150\. Another characteristic of the Jyeṣṭha Sāman is ājyado hādyado ha etc.

## \|\| 1.17.151 \|\|

*iti saṃpūjya deveśaṃ tataḥ kuryātparāṃ stutim \|*  
*ṛgbhirve paṃcabhiścaiva śṛṇuṣvaikamanāstu tāḥ \|\| 151 \|\|*

151\. After worshipping the Lord of Devas thus, another prayer is recited by means of five Ṛks. Listen to them attentively.

## \|\| 1.17.152 \|\|

*ukṣāṇaṃ pṛśnimiti vai prathamā parikīrtitā \|*  
*catvāri vākparīti vai dvitīyā parikīrtitā \|\| 152 \|\|*

152\. The first proclaimed is that which begins with ukṣāṇam pṛsnim \[pṛśnim?\] etc. (RV 1.164.43). The second one is the Mantra beginning with catvāri vāk parimita etc. (RV I.164.45).

## \|\| 1.17.153 \|\|

*iṃdraṃ mitraṃ tṛtīyā tu ṛkcaiva parikīrtitā \|*  
*kṛṣṇaṃ niyānaṃ hi tathā caturthī parikīrtitā \|\| 153 \|\|*

153\. The third Ṛk proclaimed is idam mitram etc. The fourth one proclaimed is kṛṣṇam nīyānam hi etc. (RV I.164.47).

## \|\| 1.17.154 \|\|

*dvādaśaprathama iti paṃcamī parikīrtitā \|*  
*yo ratnavāhītyanayā kirīṭaṃ yojayedraveḥ \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. The fifth one proclaimed is dvādaśa prathama etc. Uttering the Ṛk beginning with yo ratnavāhī etc. the devotee puts the crown on Ravi.

## \|\| 1.17.155 \|\|

*gatehanāmityanayā avyaṃgaṃ bhāskaraṃ nyaset \|*  
*anena vidhinā devi pūjayedvidhivadravim \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. With the Ṛk beginning with gatehanām etc. the devotee performs the Nyāsa (concluding rite of the adoration) of the unmutilated (idol of) Ravi. Thus, O goddess, one should duly worship Ravi in accordance with this procedure.

## \|\| 1.17.156 \|\|

*ityeṣa te mayā khyātaḥ pratimāpūjane vidhiḥ \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. Thus the entire procedure for the worship of the idol has been described to you by me.

## \|\| 1.17.157 \|\|

*anenavidhinā yastu satataṃ pūjayedravim \|*  
*sa prāpnotyadhikānkāmāniha loke paratra ca \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. He who always worships in accordance with this procedure, attains most of his desires in this world as well as in the world hereafter.

## \|\| 1.17.158 \|\|

*putrārthī labhate putraṃ dhanārthī labhate dhanam \|*  
*kanyārthī labhate kanyāṃ vidyārthī vedavidbhavet \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. One who seeks a son gets a son. One who seeks wealth gets wealth. One who seeks a daughter gets a daughter. One who seeks learning becomes fully conversant with the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.17.159 \|\|

*niṣkāmaḥ pūjayedyastu sa mokṣaṃ yāti vai dhruvam \|*  
*asya kṣetrasya māhātmyādarkasūryaprabhāvataḥ \|\| 159 \|\|*

159\. By the greatness of this Kṣetra and by the power of Sun-god at Arkasthala, one who worships without any specific desire certainly gets liberation.

## \|\| 1.17.160 \|\|

*anyatra brāhmaṇānāṃ ca koṭinā yatphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*arkasthale tathaikena bhojitena tu tatphalam \|\| 160 \|\|*

160\. By feeding one Brāhmaṇa in Arkasthala, the benefit gained is the same as is obtained elsewhere by feeding a crore of Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.17.161 \|\|

*snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ sūryaparvaṇi yatkṛtam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ koṭiguṇitaṃ sūryakoṭiprabhāvataḥ \|\| 161 \|\|*

161\. Snāna, Dāna, Japa, Homa—all these performed in Sūrya Parva have the benefit increased a crore times, by the power of Sūryakoṭi (Arkasthala).

## \|\| 1.17.162 \|\|

*māghamāse naro yastu saptamyāṃ ravivāsare \|*  
*kṛṣṇapakṣe mahādevi jāgaraṃ śraddhayā'caret \|*  
*arkasthalasamīpe tu sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 162 \|\|*

162\. A man who faithfully performs the rite of Jāgara (religious vigil) on the seventh lunar day on Sunday in the dark half of the month of Māgha, in the vicinity of Arkasthala, attains the greatest goal, O great goddess.

## \|\| 1.17.163 \|\|

*gośatasya pradattasya kurukṣetre ca yatphalam \|*  
*tatphalaṃ samavāpnoti tatrārkasthaladarśanāt \|\| 163 \|\|*

163\. By visiting Arkasthala one attains that benefit which one obtains by making the gift of a hundred cows in Kurukṣetra.

## \|\| 1.17.164 \|\|

*arkasthalaḥ pūjanīyastatra sthāne nivāsibhiḥ \|*  
*japāpuṣpairarkapuṣpai rogibhistu viśeṣataḥ \|\| 164 \|\|*

164\. Arkasthala should be worshipped through Arka flowers and Japā flowers by the permanent residents of that holy spot, especially the sick ones.

## \|\| 1.17.165 \|\|

*na ca patrorṇakusumairna caivonmattasaṃbhavaiḥ \|*  
*na cāmrātakajaiḥ puṣpairarcanīyo divākaraḥ \|\| 165 \|\|*

165\. Divākara should not be worshipped with flowers like Patrorṇa, Unmatta and Āmrātaka.

## \|\| 1.17.166 \|\|

*āmrātakasya kusumaṃ nirmālyamiva dṛśyate \|*  
*apratyagraṃ bahiryasmāttasmāttatparivarjayet \|\| 166 \|\|*

166\. A flower of Āmrātaka is looked upon as Nirmālya (used up for worship and kept aside). Since it is not fresh externally, it should be avoided.

## \|\| 1.17.167 \|\|

*nāvijñātaṃ pradātavyaṃ na mlānaṃ na ca dūṣitam \|*  
*na ca paryyuṣitaṃ mālyaṃ dātavyaṃ bhūtimicchatā \|\| 167 \|\|*

167\. If one desires prosperity, one should not offer a garland of flowers, if it is not from known (familiar) variety. If it is faded, defiled or stale, it should not be offered.

## \|\| 1.17.168-169 \|\|

*devamullocayedyastu tatkṣaṇātpuṣpalobhataḥ \|*  
*puṣpāṇi ca sugandhāni bhojakenetarāṇi ca \|\| 168 \|\|*

*brahmahatyāmavāpnoti bhojako lobhamohitaḥ \|*  
*mahārauravamāsādya pacyate śāśvatīḥ samāḥ \|\| 169 \|\|*

168-169. If a man makes the sweet-smelling flowers disappear from the idol of the Lord immediately due to greed for flowers, and in the case of the regular priest any flower, the priest enamoured and covetous incurs the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter. He falls into Mahāraurava and is cooked there for many years.

## \|\| 1.17.170 \|\|

*hanta te kīrttayiṣyāmi dhūpadānavidhiṃ param \|*  
*pradānāddevadevasya yena dhūpena yatphalam \|\| 170 \|\|*

170\. Oh, I shall now explain to you, the procedure for offering incense. I shall tell you which incense yields which fruit on being offered to the Lord of Devas.

## \|\| 1.17.171 \|\|

*sadārcane ca dhūpena sāmīpyaṃ kurute raviḥ \|*  
*pradadyātsakalaṃ kāmaṃ yadyadicchati mānavaḥ \|\| 171 \|\|*

171\. If Lord Ravi is offered incense always, he stays nearby and bestows all desires, whatever the man may wish for.

## \|\| 1.17.172 \|\|

*tathaivāgurudhūpena nidhiṃ dadyādabhīpsitam \|*  
*ārogyārthī dhanārthī ca nityadā guggalaṃ dahet \|\| 172 \|\|*

172\. If Aguru incense is offered, the Lord bestows the desired treasure. One who seeks health and wealth should always burn Guggala.

## \|\| 1.17.173 \|\|

*piṃḍātadhūpadānena sadā tuṣyati bhānumān \|*  
*ārogyaṃ ca svayaṃ dadyātsaukhyaṃ ca paramaṃ bhavet \|\| 173 \|\|*

173\. Bhānumān is always pleased with the offering of Piṇḍāta incense. He himself grants freedom from ailments. Thus there will be greatest happiness.

## \|\| 1.17.174 \|\|

*śrīvāsakasya dhūpena vāṇijyaṃ sakalaṃ labhet \|*  
*rasaṃ sarjarasaṃ caiva dahato'rthāgamo bhavet \|\| 174 \|\|*

174\. Through the incense of Śrīvāsaka one gets the monopoly of trade. One who burns Sarjarasa incense shall get wealth.

## \|\| 1.17.175 \|\|

*devadāruṃ ca dahato bhavatyannamathākṣayam \|*  
*vilepanaṃ kuṃkumena sarvakāmaphalapradam \|\| 175 \|\|*

175\. One who burns Devadāru gets everlasting food-grains. Smearing with Kuṃkuma (saffron) as unguent yields all desires.

## \|\| 1.17.176 \|\|

*iha loke sukhī bhūtvā akṣayaṃ svargamāpnuyāt \|*  
*caṃdanasya pralepena śriyamāyuśca viṃdati \|\| 176 \|\|*

176\. Remaining very happy in this world, he shall attain everlasting heavenly pleasures. By the unguent of sandal-paste one gets fortune and longevity.

## \|\| 1.17.177 \|\|

*raktacandanalepena sarvaṃ dadyāddivākaraḥ \|*  
*api rogaśatairgrastaḥ kṣemamārogyamāpnuyāt \|\| 177 \|\|*

177\. The unguent with red sandal is very efficacious. Divākara grants everything. Even if one is affected by hundreds of ailments, one gets happiness and welfare and health.

## \|\| 1.17.178 \|\|

*gatigaṃdhaṃ ca saubhāgyaṃ paramaṃ viṃdate naraḥ \|*  
*kastūrikāmardanakairaiśvaryamatulaṃ labhet \|\| 178 \|\|*

178\. By offering (powder or) unguent of musk, one gets unparalleled prosperity, good goal, scents and highest conjugal felicity.

## \|\| 1.17.179 \|\|

*karpūrasaṃyutairgaṃdhaiḥ kṣmādhipādhipatibhavet \|*  
*catuḥsamena gaṃdhena sarvā nkāmānavāpnuyāt \|\| 179 \|\|*

179\. Through scents together with camphor one becomes an emperor. If all the four types of scents are offered, one realizes all one’s desires.

## \|\| 1.17.180 \|\|

*etatte kathitaṃ devi sūryamāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*savistaraṃ mayā khyātaṃ kimanyatparipṛcchasi \|\| 180 \|\|*

180\. Thus, O goddess, the excellent greatness of Sūrya has been described to you in detail by me. What else do you wish to ask?

## \|\| 1.17.181 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*yadyevaṃ bhagavānsūryaḥ sarvatejasvināṃ varaḥ \|*  
*sa kathaṃ grasyate deva saiṃhikeyena rāhuṇā \|\| 181 \|\|*

The Devī said:

181\. O my Lord, if, in this way, Lord Sūrya is the most excellent of all luminaries, why is he swallowed by Rāhu, the son of Siṃhikā?

## \|\| 1.17.182 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu daivi pravakṣyāmi sarva pāpapraṇāśanam \|*  
*kāraṇaṃ grahaṇasyāpi bhrāṃtervicchedakārakam \|\| 182 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

182\. Listen, O goddess, I shall explain the cause of an eclipse. It destroys all sins and resolves all illusions and mistakes.

## \|\| 1.17.183 \|\|

*rāhurādityabiṃbasyādhastāttiṣṭhati bhāmini \|*  
*amṛtārthī vimānastho yāvatsaṃsravate'mṛtam \|\| 183 \|\|*

183\. O beautiful lady, Rāhu is (positioned) beneath the disc of the Sun. He seeks nectar and so is stationed in an aerial chariot till the liquid nectar drops down.

## \|\| 1.17.184 \|\|

*biṃbenāṃtarito devi ādityagrahaṇaṃ hi tat \|*  
*na kaścidgrasituṃ śakta ādityo dahati dhruvam \|\| 184 \|\|*

184\. He is therefore hidden by the disc. It is the solar eclipse. No one can swallow him. Āditya certainly burns (all).

## \|\| 1.17.185 \|\|

*brahmādayastamarcaṃti sa ādiḥ sarvanākinām \|*  
*ādityadehajāḥ sarve tathānye devadānavāḥ \|\| 185 \|\|*

185\. Those beginning with Brahmā worship him (the Sun-god). He is the primordial one among all heaven-dwellers. All other Devas and Dānavas are born of the body of Āditya.

## \|\| 1.17.186 \|\|

*ādikarttā svayaṃ yasmādādityastena cocyate \|*  
*prabhāse saṃsthito devaḥ sarvapātakanāśanaḥ \|\| 186 \|\|*

186\. He is called Āditya because he is the first and primordial agent. The Lord, the destroyer of all sins, is stationed in Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.17.187 \|\|

*bhuktimuktiprado devo vyādhiduṣkṛtanāśakṛt \|*  
*tatra siddhāḥ purā devi lokapālā maharṣayaḥ \|\| 187 \|\|*

187\. The Lord is the bestower of worldly pleasures and salvation. He is the destroyer of ailments and evil deeds. There in the holy spot, O goddess, the guardians of the world and great sages became Siddhas.

## \|\| 1.17.188-192 \|\|

*siddhā vidyā dharā yakṣā gaṃdharvā munayastathā \|*  
*dhanado'pi tathā bhīṣmo yayātirgālavastathā \|\| 188 \|\|*

*sāṃbaścaiva tathā devi parāṃ siddhimito gatāḥ \|*  
*idaṃ rahasyaṃ deveśi sūryamāhātmyamuttamam \|\| 189 \|\|*

*na deyaṃ duṣṭabuddhīnāṃ pāpināṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*na nāstike'śraddadhāne na krūraṃ vā kathaṃcana \|\| 190 \|\|*

*imāṃ kathāmanubrūyāttathā nā'sūyake śive \|*  
*idaṃ putrāya śiṣyāya dharmiṇe nyāyavartine \|\| 191 \|\|*

*kathanīyaṃ mahābrahma sūryabhaktāya suvrate \|*  
*arkasthalasya devasya māhātmyamidamuttamam \|\| 192 \|\|*

188-192. Siddhas, Vidyādharas, Yakṣas, Gandharvas, sages, Dhanada (Kubera), Bhīṣma, Yayāti, Gālava and Sāṃba attained the great Siddhi from this place.

O goddess of Devas, this, the excellent greatness of Sūrya, is a great secret. It should not be divulged to people of wicked intellect and sinners in particular. This story should be told neither to an atheist nor to one who has no faith, nor to a ruthless man at any cost.

If one is not ardently devoted to Śiva, it is not to be passed on to him. This story should be told to a son, to a disciple, to a righteous one and to one who abides by justice.

The great Brahman should be mentioned to a devotee of Sūrya and to one of good holy rites. This greatness of the Lord of Arkasthala is excellent.

## \|\| 1.17.193 \|\|

*yaḥ śrāddhe śrāvayeddevi brāhmaṇānsaṃśitavratān \|*  
*tasyānaṃtaṃ bhaveddevi yaddānaṃ puruṣasya vai \|\| 193 \|\|*

193\. He who recites this to Brāhmaṇas at the time of Śrāddha, to persons of esteemed holy rites, shall attain infinite bliss as though through a Dana.

## \|\| 1.17.194 \|\|

*brahmādayastamarcaṃti sa ādiḥ sarvanākinām \|*  
*ādityadehajāḥ sarve tathānye devadānavāḥ \|\| 185 \|\|*

194\. Where this is being glorified, there will be affluence always. Yātudhānas become terrified. They do not violate that Śrāddha.

## \|\| 1.17.195 \|\|

*paṃktipāvanatāṃ yāṃti ye'pi vai paṃktidūṣakāḥ \|*  
*sutavāñjanmavāṃśca syātsarvakāmamanoramaḥ \|\| 195 \|\|*

195\. If a person has been earlier declared a Paṅktidoṣaka

i.e. a defiler of a row at meals, he will become holy and esteemed. He will beget sons. He will become charming and possessor of all desired objects.

## \|\| 1.17.196 \|\|

*pravāsibhirbaṃdhuvargaiḥ saṃyujyeta sadā naraḥ \|*  
*naṣṭaiḥ saṃyujyate cārthairaparaiścāpi ciṃtitaiḥ \|\| 196 \|\|*

196\. A man who has been away in alien lands will become reunited with kinsmen. He will regain the lost wealth and other things that caused him worry.

## \|\| 1.17.197 \|\|

*rakṣyate yāginībhiśca priyaiśca na viyujyate \|*  
*upaspṛśya śucirbhūtvā śṛṇuyādbrāhmaṇaḥ sadā \|*  
*sarvānkāmāṃśca labhate nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 197 \|\|*

197\. He is protected by Yoginīs. He is not separated from dear ones. A Brāhmaṇa should listen to the story after sipping water rìtualistically and becoming clean. He will get all desired things. No doubt should be entertained about this.

## \|\| 1.17.198 \|\|

*vaiśyaḥ samṛddhimatulāṃ kṣatriyaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ \|*  
*vaṇijaścāpi vāṇijyamakhaṃḍaṃ śatasaṃkhyayā \|*  
*labheyuḥ kīrtanādasyāḥ sūryotpattervarānane \|\| 198 \|\|*

198\. O lady of excellent countenance, by the glorification of the origin of Sūrya, a Vaiśya gets unlimited prosperity, a Kṣatriya becomes Lord of the earth. Merchants will flourish hundred times more in their trading activities.

## \|\| 1.17.199-200 \|\|

*śūdrāścaivābhilaṣitānkāmānprāpsyaṃti bhāmini \|*  
*apamṛtyubhayaṃ ghoraṃ mṛtyuto'pi mahābhayam \|\| 199 \|\|*

*naśyate nātra saṃdeho rājadvārakṛtaṃ ca yat \|*  
*sarvakāmasamṛddhātmā sūryaloke mahīyate \|\| 200 \|\|*

199-200. O beautiful lady, Śūdras will attain all desired objects. All fear of premature death and terrible death due to accidents perishes. There is no doubt that what is done at the royal palace gets nullified (i.e. complaints against a devotee do not stand. He is acquitted). Richly endowed with all desired objectives, he is honoured in the world of the Sun.

## \|\| 1.17.201 \|\|

*ityetatkathitaṃ devi māhātmyaṃ sūryadaivatam \|*  
*arkasthalaprasaṃgena kimanyacchrotumicchasi \|\| 201 \|\|*

201\. Thus, O goddess, the greatness of the deity Sun has been narrated in the context of Arkasthala. What else do you wish to hear?

## \|\| 1.17.202 \|\|

*sthānaṃ śāśvatamojasāṃ gatirapāṃ dīpo diśāmakṣayaḥ siddherdvāramapāvabhedi jagatāṃ sādhāraṇaṃ locanam \|*  
*haimaṃ puṣkaramaṃtarikṣasaraso dīptaṃ divaḥ kuṇḍalaṃ kālonmānavibhāvanākṣatalayaṃ biṃbaṃ raveḥ pātu vaḥ \|\| 202 \|\|*

202\. May the Solar Disc protect you all. It is the permanent abode of vigour. It is the goal unto waters, eternal light unto the quarters. It is the gateway to Siddhis. It destroys obstacles, dangers. It is the common eye for all the worlds. It is the golden lotus in the lake of the vast firmament. It is the brilliant earring unto heaven. It is the means of reckoning the time. It has no destruction nor has it any boundary.

## Chapter 17 - Puṣpādhyāya (Chapter on flowers) \[Puṣpa-adhyāya\]

## \|\| 1.17.111 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi puṣpā dhyāyamanuttamam \|*  
*yena cārkasthale devi śīghraṃ tuṣyati pūjitaḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

\[Note: These verses are extracted from Chapter 17: Procedure of Worship (of the Sun-God).\]

Īśvara said:

111\. Listen, O goddess, I shall expound the excellent Puṣpādhyāya (Chapter on flowers) \[puṣpa-adhyāya\]. O goddess, on being worshipped duly, Arkasthala, the Lord, becomes pleased thereby.

## \|\| 1.17.112 \|\|

*mālatīkusumaiḥ pūjā bhavetsāṃnidhyakārikā \|*  
*mallikāyāśca kusumairbhogavāñjāyate naraḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. The Pūjā performed with Mālatī flowers causes the Sānnidhya (proximity to the Lord). If the adoration is through Mallikā flowers, the man becomes an enjoyer of pleasures.

## \|\| 1.17.113 \|\|

*saubhāgyaṃ puṃḍarīkaistu bhavatyarthaśca śāśvataḥ \|*  
*kadaṃbapuṣpairdeveśi paramaiśvaryamaśnute \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Worship with Puṇḍarīka flowers causes conjugal felicity and permanent wealth. Through Kadaṃba flowers, O goddess of Devas, one attains the greatest Aiśvarya (glory, power).

## \|\| 1.17.114 \|\|

*bhavatyakṣayamannaṃ ca bakulai rarcane raveḥ \|*  
*madārapuṣpakaiḥ pūjā sarvakuṣṭhavināśinī \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. If worship of Ravi is performed through Bakula flowers, one acquires everlasting food-grain. Adoration through Mandāra flowers destroys all types of leprosy.

## \|\| 1.17.115 \|\|

*bilvasya patrakusumaimahatīṃ śriyamaśnute \|*  
*arkasrajā bhavatyarthaḥ sarvakāmaphalapradaḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. Through the flowers and leaves of Bilva, one attains the greatest fortune and wealth. Through a garland made of Arka flowers, one acquires wealth that yields the fulfilment of all cherished desires.

## \|\| 1.17.116 \|\|

*pradadyādrūpiṇīṃ kanyāṃ pūjito bakulasrajā \|*  
*kiṃśukairarcito devi na pīḍayati bhāskaraḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. On being worshipped with Bakula garland, Lord Bhāskara shall bestow a beautiful daughter. On being adored with Kiṃśuka flowers, he desists from troubling the devotees.

## \|\| 1.17.117 \|\|

*agastikusumaistadvadānukūlyaṃ prayaccha ti \|*  
*karavīraistu deveśi sūryasyānucaro bhavet \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. On being adored with Agasti flowers the Lord becomes favourable. O goddess of Devas, by adoring with Karavīra flowers, one becomes a follower (servant) of Sūrya.

## \|\| 1.17.118 \|\|

*śatapatrasrajā devi sūryasālokyatāṃ vrajet \|*  
*bakapuṣpairmahādevi dāridyaṃ naiva jāyate \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. O goddess, through a garland of Śatapatra one attains Sūryasālokyatā (sharing the same world as that of Sūrya). O great goddess, through Baka flowers poverty is ever averted.

## \|\| 1.17.119 \|\|

*ṛtukusumena gandhena samabhyarcya divākaram \|*  
*catuḥsamudramaryādāṃ sa bhuṃkte pṛthivīmimām \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. By worshipping Divākara through the seasonal flowers and scents, one enjoys this earth with the four oceans as its boundary.

## \|\| 1.17.120 \|\|

*yaḥ sūryāyatanaṃ bhaktyā gairikeṇopalepayet \|*  
*prāpnuyānmahatīṃ lakṣmīṃ rogaiścāpi pramucyate \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. One who devoutly plasters the shrine of Sūrya with Gairika (red chalk) shall attain great fortune and is rid of ailments.

## \|\| 1.17.121 \|\|

*aṣṭādaśeha kuṣṭhāni ye cānye vyādhayo nṛṇām \|*  
*pralayaṃ yāṃti te sarve mṛdā yadyupalepayet \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. If the shrine is smeared with clay, all the eighteen types of leprosy and many other ailments of men get cured completely.

## \|\| 1.17.122 \|\|

*vilepanānāṃ sarveṣāṃ kuṃkumaṃ raktacaṃdanam \|*  
*puṣpāṇāṃ karavīrāṇi praśastāni varānane \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. Of all unguents Kuṃkuma and red sandal-paste are the best. Of all flowers, O lady of excellent countenance, Karavīras are the most praiseworthy.

## \|\| 1.17.123 \|\|

*nātaḥ parataraṃ kiṃcidbhāsvatastuṣṭikārakam \|*  
*yādṛśaṃ kuṅkumaṃ jātī śatapatraṃ tathā'guruḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. Nothing is more pleasing to Bhāsvān than Kuṃkuma (flowers), Jāti, Śatapatra and Agaru.

## Chapter 18 - The Birth of Moon-God

## \|\| 1.18.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti proktā tadā devī śaṃkareṇa yaśasvinī \|*  
*punaḥ papraccha vipreṃdrāḥ kṣetramāhātmyavistaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1\. O leading Brāhmaṇas, on being told thus by Śaṅkara, the goddess of great renown further asked him about the details of the greatness of the Kṣetra.

## \|\| 1.18.2 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*adya me saphalaṃ janma saphalaṃ ca tapaḥ prabho \|*  
*devatvamadya me jātaṃ tvatprasādena śaṃkara \|\| 2 \|\|*

The Devī said:

2\. O my Lord, today my birth has become fruitful. My penance too has borne fruit. O Śaṅkara, with your favour, divinity has been attained.

## \|\| 1.18.3 \|\|

*adyāhaṃ kṛtakalyāṇī jñānadṛṣṭiḥ kṛtātvayā \|*  
*adya me bhūṣitau karṇau kṣetra māhātmyabhūṣaṇau \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Today I have become one who has done an auspicious act. Wisdom-eye has been granted by you. Today my ears have become adorned with the ear-ornaments in the form of the greatness of the Kṣetra.

## \|\| 1.18.4 \|\|

*adya me tejasaḥ piṃḍo jāto jñānaṃ hṛdi sthitam \|*  
*adya me kulaśīlaṃ ca adya me rūpalakṣaṇam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Today my brilliance has become a solid entity as knowledge has been fixed in the heart. Today my decorum and nobility, beauty and characteristics have become well-defined.

## \|\| 1.18.5 \|\|

*adya me bhrāṃtirucchinnā tīrthabhramaṇasaṃbhavā \|*  
*prabhāse niścalaṃ jātaṃ mano me mānināṃ vara \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Today my delusion about the pilgrimage to holy places has become dispelled. O most excellent one among honoured ones, my mind has become steady in regard to Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.18.6-7 \|\|

*ārādhito mayā pūrvaṃ tuṣṭo me'dya sureśvaraḥ \|*  
*vahninā veṣṭitā sāhamekapādena saṃsthitā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tattapaḥ saphalaṃ tvadya jātaṃ me bhaktavatsala \|*  
*prabhāsakṣetramāhātmyamadya me prakaṭīkṛtam \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. The Lord of Suras was propitiated by me earlier. Today the Lord has become pleased. I was surrounded by fire (in Pañcāgni penance). I have been standing on a single foot. That penance has become fruitful today. O Lord to whom devotees are favourites, the greatness of Prabhāsa Kṣetra has been revealed to me today.

## \|\| 1.18.8 \|\|

*punaḥ pṛcchāmi deveśa yāthātathyaṃ vada prabho \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. I am asking you again, O Lord of Devas. O Lord, do tell me the exact facts.

## \|\| 1.18.9 \|\|

*adyāpi saṃśayo nātha tīrthamāhātmyasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*anyatkautūhalaṃ deva kathayasva maheśvara \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Still, O Lord, I entertain doubts regarding the greatness of the Kṣetra and the Tīrtha. O Lord Maheśvara, do tell me if there is any other interesting thing.

## \|\| 1.18.10 \|\|

*ayaṃ yo varttate deva caṃdraste śirasi sthitaḥ \|*  
*kasyāyaṃ kathamutpannaḥ kasminkāle vada prabho \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Here this Candra (Moon) is on your head. Of whom is he born and how? At what time? Do tell me, O Lord!

## \|\| 1.18.11-12 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*asminkāle mahādevi vārāha iti viśrute \|*  
*parārddhe tu dvitīye'sminvartamāne tu vedhasaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dvitīyamāsasyādau tu pratipadyā prakīrtitā \|*  
*vārāheṇoddhṛtā tasyāṃ tathā cādau dharā priye \|*  
*tena vārāhakalpeti nāma jātaṃ dharātale \|\| 12 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

11-12. This is the period (Kalpa) well-known as Vārāha. The second Parārdha of Brahmā is current now. At the beginning of the second month, this is the Pratipad (first lunar day). Lord Varāha (the divine Boar, Viṣṇu) redeemed and lifted up Dharā (the Earth) on this day, O my beloved. Therefore, this Kalpa came to be known by the name Vārāha Kalpa on the Earth.

## \|\| 1.18.13-14 \|\|

*tasminkalpe mahādevi gate saṃdhyāṃśake priye \|*  
*prathamasya manoścādau devi svāyaṃbhuvasya hi \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kṣīrode mathyamāne tu daivatairdānavairapi \|*  
*ratnāni jajñire tatra caturddaśamitāni vai \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. In that Kalpa, O great goddess, O my beloved, the Sandhyāṃśa (twilight period i.e. interregnum of two Kalpas) has passed. The first Manu Svāyaṃbhuva was reigning, O goddess. The Ocean of Milk was being churned by Devas and Dānavas. Gems, fourteen in number, were born (recovered) therefrom.

## \|\| 1.18.15 \|\|

*teṣāṃ madhye mahātejāścaṃdramāstattvasaṃbhava \|*  
*so'yaṃ mayā dhṛto devi adyāpi śirasi priye \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Among them the highly refulgent Candra is one born of the Tattva (eternal entities, principles). O goddess, O my beloved, he was held and kept on the head by me where he still continues to be.

## \|\| 1.18.16 \|\|

*viṣe pīte mahādevi prabhāsasthasya me sadā \|*  
*bhūṣaṇaṃ muktaye devairmama caṃdraḥ kṛtaḥ purā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O great goddess, when the poison (Halāhala) was swallowed by me while I was stationed in Prabhāsa, Candra was formerly made my ornament for the relief (from the effects of poison).

## \|\| 1.18.17 \|\|

*śaśinābhūṣito yasmāttenāhaṃ śaśibhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*tatra sthāne sthito'dyāpi svayaṃbhūrliṃgamūrttimān \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Since I have been adorned with the Moon (Śaśī), I came to be known as Śaśibhūṣaṇa (Moon-ornamented). Even today I am stationed in that holy spot in the form of Svayambhūliṅga.

## \|\| 1.18.18 \|\|

*sarvasiddhipradātā ca kalpasthāyī sadā priye \|*  
*ityetatkathitaṃ devi kimanyatparipṛcchasi \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. I am the bestower of all Siddhis, O my beloved. I continue to stay through the duration of the Kalpa. Thus it has been narrated, O goddess; what else do you wish to ask?

## Chapter 19 - Incarnations of Śrī Viṣṇu

## \|\| 1.19.1 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*yadyevaṃ sakalaścaṃdraḥ kathaṃ na vidhṛtastvayā \|*  
*antabhāve kalānāṃ tatkāraṇaṃ kathaya prabho \|\| 1 \|\|*

The Devī said,:

1\. If it is so, O Lord, why was the Full-Moon with all its digits not worn by you? Tell me the reason for (liking) the last part of the digits.

## \|\| 1.19.2-5 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*amā ṣoḍaśabhedena devi proktā mahākalā \|*  
*saṃsthitā paramā māyā dehināṃ deha dhāriṇī \|\| 2 \|\|*

*amādipaurṇamāsyaṃtā yā eva śaśinaḥ kalāḥ \|*  
*tithayastāḥ samākhyātāḥ ṣoḍaśaiva prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*amā sūkṣmā parā śaktiḥ sā tvaṃ devi prakīrtitā \|*  
*pralayotpattiyogena sthitāḥ kālakramoditāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ṣoḍaśaiva svarā ye tu ādyāḥ sṛṣṭayaṃtakāḥ priye \|*  
*kālasyāvayavāste ca vijñeyāḥ kālavedibhiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

2-5. Amā (New Moon) is mentioned as the Mahākalā (greatest digit as distinguished) in sixteen types (of Kalās), O goddess. It is the greatest Māyā and the supporter of the bodies of the embodied ones.

Beginning with Amā and ending with Paurṇamāsī (Full-Moon) there are sixteen Kalās pertaining to the Moon. They are called Tithis (Lunar days). The sixteen Kalās are thus glorified.

Amā is the greatest and subtlest Śakti. O goddess, it is acclaimed that you are that Śakti.

There are sixteen primordial Svaras (Notes). They are mentioned in the due order of time units, beginning with creation (of the world) and ending with its annihilation. O my beloved, they should be known by the experts on time as units of time.

## \|\| 1.19.6-8 \|\|

*truṭirlavo nimeṣaśca kalā kāṣṭhā muhūrtakam \|*  
*rātryahaḥpakṣamāsāśca ayanaṃ vatsaraṃ yugam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*manvataraṃ tathā kalpaṃ mahākalpaṃ ca ṣoḍaśa \|*  
*kalā visarjanī yā tu jīvamāśritya vartate \|\| 7 \|\|*

*sā sṛjatyakhilaṃ viśvaṃ viṣuvadvayasaṃyutam \|*  
*tathā saṃvaraṇī yā tu viśvaṃ saṃharate priye \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. They are Truṭi, Lava, Nimeṣa, Kalā, Kāṣṭhā, Muhūrtaka, Rātri (night), Ahaḥ \[Ahan?\] (day), Pakṣa (fortnight), Māsa (month), Ayana, Vatsara (year), Yuga, Manvantara, Kalpa and Mahākalpa the sixteenth. Kalā Visarjanī (the creative one) is based on the Jīva (the individual soul). It creates the entire universe, the two Vīṣuvas (equinoxes) being included. Kalā Saṃvaraṇī (that which conceals and covers), O my beloved, annihilates the universe.

## \|\| 1.19.9 \|\|

*netrapātāccaturbhāgastruṭikālo nigadyate \|*  
*tasmācca dviguṇaṃ viddhi nimiṣaṃ tanmaheśvari \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. A fourth of the winking time is called Truṭi. Understand, O Maheśvarī, that Nimiṣa is twice that (Lava is included in between).

## \|\| 1.19.10 \|\|

*nimiṣaistriṃśadbhiḥ kāṣṭhā tābhirviṃśatibhiḥ kalā \|*  
*viṃśatikalo muhūrtaḥ syāddinaṃ paṃcadaśaistu taiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thirty Nimiṣas make a Kāṣṭhā and twenty Kaṣṭhās \[Kāṣṭhās?\] make one Kalā. A Muhūrta consists of twenty Kalās and fifteen Muhūrtas make a Dina (day).

## \|\| 1.19.11 \|\|

*dinamānā niśā jñeyā ahorātraṃ dvayādbhavet \|*  
*taiḥ paṃcadaśabhiḥ pakṣo dvipakṣo māsa ucyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Night is of the same duration as Dina (day) and these two together make one Ahorātra (night plus day=24 Hours). Fifteen Ahorātras make one Pakṣa (fortnight). Two Pakṣas together make what is called Māsa (month).

## \|\| 1.19.12-13 \|\|

*māsaiścaivāyanaṃ ṣaḍbhirvarṣaṃ syādayanadvaye \|*  
*catvāriṃśacca lakṣāṇi lakṣāṇāṃ tritayaṃ punaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*viṃśatiśca sahasrāṇi jñeyaṃ sauraṃ caturyugam \|*  
*caturyugaikasaptatyā manvaṃtaramudāhṛtam \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Six months make one Ayana and two Ayanas make one Varṣa (year). Four million three hundred twenty thousand years should be known as one Caturyuga according to the solar reckoning. Seventy-one Caturyugas can be cited as constituting one Manvantara.

## \|\| 1.19.14 \|\|

*aiṃdrametadbhavedāyuḥ samāsāṃtaṃ ca kīrtitam \|*  
*caturdaśendraiḥ pralīnaiḥ kalpaṃ brahmadinaṃ bhavet \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. This period along with the end of a month is acclaimed as the span of life of Indra. The period covered by the lives of fourteen Indras constitutes a Kalpa and it shall be one day of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.19.15 \|\|

*rātriśca tāvatī caiva caturyugasahasrikā \|*  
*anena dinamānena śatābdaṃ jīvati priye \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The same period of a thousand Caturyugas constitutes his Rātri (Night) of Brahmā. O my beloved, he (Brahmā) lives for a hundred years calculated thus.

## \|\| 1.19.16 \|\|

*mamaiva nimiṣārddhena sahasrāṇi caturddaśa \|*  
*vinaśyaṃti tato viṣṇorasaṃkhyātāḥ pitāmahāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Along with half of a Nimiṣa pertaining to me, fourteen thousand Viṣṇus and unlimited number of Pitāmahas (Brahmās) die.

## \|\| 1.19.17 \|\|

*evaṃ krameṇa deveśi samutpannamidaṃ jagat \|*  
*śaśisūryavibhāgena citrarūpamanaṃtakam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O goddess of Devas, this universe is created (and maintained) in this order. The reckoning may be lunar and solar; the universe is infinite and variegated.

## \|\| 1.19.18 \|\|

*kalā devi yadādyaṃtamanādimajamavyayam \|*  
*tadānvitaḥ śaśī tasyāmadhomukhamavasthitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O goddess, the Kalā is unborn, beginningless and immutable and Śaśin (Moon) is established therein with face down and accompanied by it.

## \|\| 1.19.19 \|\|

*evaṃ kṣayodayaṃ jñeyaṃ caṃdrārkābhyāmavasthitam \|*  
*sṛṣṭikramaṃ mayā proktaṃ saṃhāramadhunā śṛṇu \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Thus the waxing and waning of the Moon and the Sun should be known. It is the order of creation that has been narrated by me. Now listen to the annihilation.

## \|\| 1.19.20-23 \|\|

*mahākalpaṃ hataṃ kalpaiḥ kalpaṃ manvaṃtarairhatam \|*  
*māsaṃ pakṣāhataṃ kṛtvā taṃ cāhorātribhājitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*ahorātraṃ muhūrtena muhūrtaṃ tu kalāhatam \|*  
*kalāṃ kāṣṭhā hatāṃ kṛtvā kāṣṭhāṃ nimiṣabhājitām \|\| 21 \|\|*

*nimiṣaṃ ca lavairhatvā lavaṃ truṭivibhājitam \|*  
*tadatītaṃ praśāṃtaṃ ca nirvikāramalakṣaṇam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tasya ceyaṃ parā māyā kalā śirasi dhāritā \|*  
*sā śaktirdevadevasya viśvākārā parā priye \|*  
*mohayitvā tu saṃtānaṃ saṃsārayati pārvati \|\| 23 \|\|*

20-23. Mahākalpa is struck (becomes extinct) by passing away of Kalpas constituting it and a Kalpa is destroyed by Manvantaras. Māsa gets annihilated by Pakṣas and that (Pakṣa) is divided through Ahorātras. This Ahorātra is divided by Muhūrta and a Muhūrta is struck down by Kalās. Kalā is made extinct through Kāṣṭhās and Kāṣṭhā is divided through Nimiṣas. Nimiṣa is ended through Lavas and the Lava is divided by means of Truṭi. Thus that (which is beyond that) remains quiescent, sans characteristics and devoid of aberrations. The Kalā thereof, the great Māyā has been held over the head. O my beloved, it is the Śakti of the Lord of Devas. It has the form of the universe. O Pārvatī, it deludes the Santāna (series, progeny) and makes it undergo worldly existence.

## \|\| 1.19.24 \|\|

*evametajjagaddevi utpattisthitilakṣaṇam \|*  
*yatraivotpadyate kṛtsnaṃ punastatraiva līyate \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thus this universe, O goddess, has its characteristics of origin and sustenance. The entire universe gets dissolved wherein it is born.

## \|\| 1.19.25 \|\|

*seyaṃ māyāmayī śaktiḥ śuddhāśuddhasvarūpiṇī \|*  
*caṃdrarūpā sthitā sā tu tava devi prakāśayet \|\| 25 \|\|*
