25\. Such is the Śakti in the form of Māyā, It’s features are Śuddha (pure) and Aśuddha (impure). To you, O goddess, it reveals itself as staying in the form of Candra (Moon).

## \|\| 1.19.26 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*paṃcāgninopasantaptā varṣakoṭīranekadhā \|*  
*tattapaḥ saphalaṃ jātaṃ me'dya deva jagatpate \|\| 26 \|\|*

The Devī said:

26\. I performed penance in which I got myself scorched by five fires for many crores of years. O Lord, O Lord of the universe, that penance has become fruitful today.

## \|\| 1.19.27 \|\|

*sṛṣṭiyogo mayā jñātaḥ saṃhāraśca maheśvara \|*  
*candrotpattisvarūpaṃ ca kalāmānaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The Sṛṣṭiyoga (process of creation etc.) is understood by me, O Maheśvara, and that of the annihilation too (is understood). The origin of the Moon and the magnitude of Kalā also (is understood).

## \|\| 1.19.28 \|\|

*adhunā mama deveśa sandeho hṛdi saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*kautūhalaṃ paraṃ deva kathayasva maheśvara \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Now, O Lord of Devas, there is a doubt in my mind. O Lord Maheśvara, my curiosity is very great. Do tell me.

## \|\| 1.19.29 \|\|

*amṛtādeva saṃbhūtaḥ sarvāhlādakaraḥ śaśī \|*  
*priyaśca tava deveśa vallabhaścaṃdramāstathā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Śaśin (Moon) that delights everyone is born of nectar. O Lord of Devas, this Candramas is your dear favourite.

## \|\| 1.19.30 \|\|

*caṃdre ca cadi ityeṣa hlādane dhāturiṣyate \|*  
*śuklatve cāpatattve ca mayā tveṣa vibhāvyate \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. In regard to the word Candra, the root generally taken is √cad ‘to delight’, but I think it means whiteness and aqueousness.

## \|\| 1.19.31 \|\|

*sarvauṣadhīnāmadhipaḥ pitṝṇāṃ prīṇanaṃ param \|*  
*tadāśrayaśca tvadbhaktastva tsevātatparaḥ śaśī \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Śaśin is the Lord of all herbs. He pleases the Pitṛs much. He is your devotee. He is eager to serve you. He has resorted to you.

## \|\| 1.19.32-33 \|\|

*tathāpi sakalaṃko'yaṃ kautukaṃ kurute mama \|*  
*devi brahmāṃḍasaṃghaṭṭamālāmaṃḍitaśekharaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*śīrṣe tava niviṣṭasya kaṣṭaṃ caṃdrasya cedyadi \|*  
*tarhi nātha na śocyā vai saṃsāre duḥkhabhāginaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. You are the Lord whose crest is embellished by groups of Cosmic Eggs coming into clash with one another. Yet he has a stigma despite being established on your head. This arouses my curiosity. If such a Candra too has to suffer, then why should a miserable one in the world be bewailed and pitied.

## \|\| 1.19.34-37 \|\|

*na cāsti triṣu lokeṣu na caitatsaṃbhaviṣyati \|*  
*yatra śakto bhavatkartuṃ duḥkhasyāsya ca saṃkṣayam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*sarveṣāṃ vartate śaṃkā yathā mama maheśvara \|*  
*utpannaṃ kāraṇaṃ kiṃtadyena somasya lāṃchanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*kimetatkāraṇaṃ deva kathayasva maheśvara \|*  
*amṛte saṃbhavo yasya kathaṃ tasyāpi lāṃchanam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*priyaśca tava deveśa lāṃchanaṃ cāpi tiṣṭhati \|*  
*kautūhalaṃ paraṃ deva tattvaṃ me vaktumarhasi \|\| 37 \|\|*

34-37. A parallel instance is not seen in all the three worlds, nor can it be so. This is a case where you can bring about an end to this. (Yet you do not do so.) In this regard, O Maheśvara, everyone has a grave doubt as it is in my case. What is the cause of the origin of the stigma in the Moon? O Lord Maheśvara, do tell me what caused it. How comes it that one who has issued forth from nectar has a stigma? He is your favourite, O Lord of Devas, yet the stigma continues to be there. My curiosity is great, O Lord. It behoves you to tell me the truth.

## \|\| 1.19.38 \|\|

*evamuktaḥ sa pārvatyā devadevo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*uvāca paramaprītaḥ premṇā śailasutāṃ prabhuḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. On being enquired thus by Pārvatī, Maheśvara, the Lord of Devas, became highly pleased. He spoke to the Daughter of the Mountain lovingly:

Īśvara said,:

## \|\| 1.19.39 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*kiṃ te devi mahāśaṃkādyotpannā varavarṇini \|*  
*mamopari na karttavyā nirudvignā bhava priye \|*  
*pitustava prabhāvena lāṃchanaṃ śaśino'bhavat \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O goddess of excellent complexion, how is it that a great doubt such as this has occurred to you? No aspersion should be cast on me. O my beloved, do not be agitated. It is due to the power of your father (i.e. Dakṣa) that Śaśin contracted this stigma.

## \|\| 1.19.40 \|\|

*bhāvitvātkarmaṇo devi dakṣasyājñāvyatikramāt \|*  
*samaṃ varttasva bhāryābhirityuktaḥ śaśalāṃchanaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O goddess, it is due to the inevitability of the destined Karma. The Moon was told: “You should be impartial in regard to all your wives.” Since the Moon transgressed this command of Dakṣa (he had to incur this curse).

## \|\| 1.19.41 \|\|

*tadvākyamanyathā cakre tataḥ śaptaḥ śaśī priye \|*  
*idaṃ pṛṣṭaṃ tu yaddevi tvayā lāṃchanakāraṇam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O my beloved, Śaśin did do something against his words (of advice).So he was cursed. And, O goddess, it is this that you have asked me, the cause of the stigma (on the Moon).

## \|\| 1.19.42 \|\|

*kalpekalpe pṛthagbhāvaṃ kāraṇairasti bhāmini \|*  
*asaṃkhyātaṃ ca tadvaktuṃ śakyaṃ naiva mayā priye \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. In every kalpa, O beautiful lady, there is difference due to various reasons. It is numberless and hence cannot be narrated. O my beloved, it cannot be mentioned by me.

## \|\| 1.19.43 \|\|

*asaṃkhyeyāścandramasaḥ saṃbhavaṃti punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*vinaśyaṃti ca deveśi sarvamanvantarāntaram \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Innumerable Moons come into existence again and again and they perish. In every Manvantara this happens, O goddess of Devas.

## \|\| 1.19.44 \|\|

*asaṃkhyātāśca kalpākhyā asaṃkhyātāḥ pitāmahāḥ \|*  
*harayaścāpyasaṃkhyātā eka eva maheśvaraḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Innumerable are those (periods) called Kalpa. The Pitāmahas (Brahmās) are innumerable and Haris too are innumerable. But Maheśvara is one and only one.

## \|\| 1.19.45 \|\|

*koṭikoṭyayutānyatra brahmāṇḍāni mama priye \|*  
*jalabudbudavaddevi saṃjātāni tu līlayā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Like formations of bubbles in water, O my beloved, crores and ten thousand crores of Brahmāṇḍas (Cosmic Eggs) issue forth from me in my sport.

## \|\| 1.19.46 \|\|

*tatratatra caturvaktrā brahmāṇo harayo bhavāḥ \|*  
*sṛṣṭāḥ pradhānena tadā labdhā śaṃbhostu saṃnidhiḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. In different places (Cosmic Eggs), four-faced Brahmās, Haris and Bhavas are created by the Pradhāna (Māyā). Then the proximity to Śaṃbhu was obtained.

## \|\| 1.19.47 \|\|

*layaṃ caiva tathānyonyamādyaṃtaṃ prakaroti ca \|*  
*sargasaṃhārasaṃsthānāṃ karttā devo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. He (Maheśvara) brings about the mutual merger and dissolution of beings as well as the beginning and end. Lord Maheśvara is the agent of creation, annihilation and sustenance.

## \|\| 1.19.48 \|\|

*sarge ca rajasā pṛktaḥ sattvasthaḥ paripālane \|*  
*pratisarge tamoyuktaḥ so'haṃ devi tridhā sthitaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. I get combined with Rajas at the time of creation. I am established in Sattva while maintaining it. I am united with Tamas during the annihilation (of the world). Thus I abide in three forms.

## \|\| 1.19.49 \|\|

*tasmānmāheśvaro brahmā brahmaṇo'dhipatiḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*sadāśivo bhavedviṣṇurbrahmā sarvātmako hyataḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Hence Brahmā is the son of Maheśvara. Śiva is the Lord, master of Brahmā. Sadāśiva may become Viṣṇu and Brahmā, because he is Sarvātmaka (the immanent soul of all, identical with all).

## \|\| 1.19.50 \|\|

*sa eva bhagavānrudro viṣṇurviśva jagatprabhuḥ \|*  
*asminnaṇḍe tvimelokā antarviśvamidaṃjagat \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. He alone is Lord Rudra and Viṣṇu, the Lord of the entire universe. These worlds are in this Cosmic Egg, this world is within the universe.

## \|\| 1.19.51 \|\|

*candrasūryagrahā devi brahmāṇḍe'sminmanasvini \|*  
*saṃkhyātuṃ naiva śakyante ye bhaviṣyaṃti ye gatāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O goddess, O highly intelligent one, it is impossible to count the Moons, Suns and Planets which are (now) in existence, and those that have come and gone and those which are as yet to come.

## \|\| 1.19.52 \|\|

*asminvārāhakalpe tu vartamāne manasvini \|*  
*ṣaḍatītā mahādevi rohiṇīpatayaḥ purā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. In the present Vārāha Kalpa, O intelligent lady, six Moons have already come and gone in the Cosmic Egg.

## \|\| 1.19.53 \|\|

*saptamo'yaṃ mahādevi vartate'mṛtasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*dakṣaśāpena yo devi saṃkṣīṇo dṛśyate'dhunā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O great goddess, the present one issued forth from nectar and is seen now weak and wearied due to the curse of Dakṣa and is the seventh one.

## \|\| 1.19.54-56 \|\|

*atha dvitīye saṃprāpte parārddhe caiva vedhasaḥ \|*  
*tasya triṃśattime kalpe pitṛ kalpeti viśrute \|\| 54 \|\|*

*svāyaṃbhuveṃ'tare prāpte tasyādau tvaṃ satī kila \|*  
*tasminkāle mahādevi yobhūddakṣaḥ pitā tava \|\| 55 \|\|*

*prāṇātprajāpaterjanma tasya dakṣasya kīrtitam \|*  
*asminmanvantare devi dakṣaḥ prācetaso'bhavat \|\| 56 \|\|*

54-56. In the second Parārdha of Brahmā, the thirtieth Kalpa was well-known as Pitṛkalpa, In the beginning of the Svāyaṃbhuva Manvantara therein, you were (known as) Satī. O great goddess, the Dakṣa who was then your father was born of Prāṇa, the patriarch. But in this Manvantara, O goddess, Dakṣa was born of Pracetas.

## \|\| 1.19.57 \|\|

*aṃguṣṭhāddakṣiṇāddakṣo bhaviṣyatyadhunā priye \|*  
*yugeyuge bhavantyete sarve dakṣādayo dvijāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Now, O my beloved, Dakṣa will be born of the right Aṅguṣṭha (thumb). All the Brāhmaṇas beginning with Dakṣa are born in every Yuga.

## \|\| 1.19.58 \|\|

*punaścaiva vinaśyanti vidvāṃstatra na muhyati \|*  
*tasyāpamānāttvaṃ devi dehaṃ tatyaktha vai purā \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. They will again die. A sensible man does not become deluded thereby. O goddess, on being insulted by him (Dakṣa) formerly you abandoned your body.

## \|\| 1.19.59 \|\|

*tāvadviyukto'haṃ devi tvayā mukto'bhavaṃ purā \|*  
*yāvadvarāhakalpasya cākṣuṣasyāntaraṃ priye \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Thus bereaved of you formerly, O my beloved, I was separated from you till the Cākṣuṣa Manvantara of the Vārāhakalpa.

## \|\| 1.19.60 \|\|

*ekaviṃśo manuścāyaṃ kalpe vārāhasaṃjñake \|*  
*kalpekalpe mahādevi bhavennāmāntaraṃ tava \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. This is the twenty-first Manu (i.e. beginning from Svāyaṃbhuva of Pitṛkalpa and ending with Cākṣuṣa of Vārāha Kalpa) in the Kalpa called Vārāha. O great goddess, in every Kalpa you will have a different name.

## \|\| 1.19.61 \|\|

*asminkalpe tu vārāhe himavattapasārjjite \|*  
*saṃbhūtā pārvatī devi cākṣuṣasyāṃtare gate \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. In this Vārāha Kalpa, O goddess, you became Pārvatī obtained by Himavān through his penance, when the Cākṣuṣa Manvantara has passed off.

## \|\| 1.19.62 \|\|

*brahmaṇo dinamekaṃ tu ṣaṇmāsena tavāvadhiḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ viyuktā mayā sārddhaṃ dakṣakopena bhāmini \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. O beautiful lady, due to the anger of Dakṣa you had to be separated from me for the duration of a day of Brahmā. Your span of life is the period of his six months.

## \|\| 1.19.63 \|\|

*tava krodhena ye śaptā ṛṣayo vai mayā purā \|*  
*te'pi devi tvayā sārddhaṃ jātā vaivasvateṃtare \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. O goddess, the sages who were formerly cursed by me out of my anger in your case, are also born along with you in the Vaivasvata Manvantara.

## \|\| 1.19.64 \|\|

*bhṛguraṃgirā marīcistu pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ \|*  
*atriścaiva vasiṣṭhaśca aṣṭau te brahmaṇaḥ sutāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. They are the eight sons of Brahmā, viz. Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras, Marīci, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Atri and Vasiṣṭha.

## \|\| 1.19.65 \|\|

*dakṣasya yajñe te śaptāḥ pūrvaṃ svāyaṃbhuventare \|*  
*jātā devi punaste vai kalpesmiṃścākṣuṣe gate \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Formerly, in the Svāyaṃbhuva Manvantara they had been cursed at the time of the Yajña of Dakṣa. O goddess, they are reborn in this Kalpa after the Cākṣuṣa Manvantara has elapsed.

## \|\| 1.19.66-67 \|\|

*devasya mahato yajñe vāruṇīṃ bibhratastanum \|*  
*brahmaṇo juhvataḥ śukramagnau pūrvaṃ prajepsayā \|\| 66 \|\|*

*ṛṣayo jajñire pūrvaṃ sūryabiṃbasamaprabhāḥ \|*  
*pitustava samīpaṃ te varaṇāya tava priye \|*  
*prasthāpitā mayā pūrvaṃ tattvaṃ jānāsi suvrate \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. Adopting the Vāruṇī body in the course of his Yajña, the great Lord Brahmā performed the Homa of his Śukra (semen) with a desire to get progeny.

Then the sages with the refulgence of the solar disc were born again. O my beloved, in order to woo you, they were sent by me to your father (Himavān). I hope you remember it, O lady of holy vows.

## \|\| 1.19.68-69 \|\|

*atha kiṃ bahunoktena vacmi te praśnamuttamam \|*  
*dvitīye tu parārddhe'sminvarttamāne ca vedhasaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*śvetakalpātsamārabhya yāvadvārāhagocaram \|*  
*samatītāśca ye candrāstāñchṛṇuṣva varānane \|\| 69 \|\|*

68-69. Why digress with profuse verbosity? I shall give reply to your excellent question. In the present second Parārdha of Brahmā beginning with Śveta Kalpa and ending with the Vārāha Kalpa, many Candras have come and gone. O lady of excellent countenance, listen to them.

## \|\| 1.19.70 \|\|

*catuḥśatāni deveśi ṣaḍviṃśatyadhikāni tu \|*  
*gatāni śītaraśmīnāṃ saptaviṃśo'dhunā priye \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. O goddess of Devas, four hundred and twenty-six Moons have come and gone. O my beloved, the present one is the four hundred twenty-seventh.

## \|\| 1.19.71-73 \|\|

*vaivasvateṃ'tare prāpte yaścāyaṃ vartate'dhunā \|*  
*tretāyuge tu daśame dattātreyapuraḥsaraḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*saṃjāto rohiṇīnātho yo'dhunā varttate priye \|*  
*tasyotpattiprasaṃgena viṣṇormānuṣasaṃbhavān \|\| 72 \|\|*

*dehāvatārānvakṣyāmi prāraṃbhātprathamānpriye \|*  
*pañcamaḥ paṃcadaśyāṃ sa tretāyāṃ tu babhūva ha \|\| 73 \|\|*

71-73. The Moon who is present now is born in the tenth Tretāyuga of Vaivasvata Manvantara along with Dattātreya. In the context of the origin of the Moon, I shall describe the human incarnations of Viṣṇu. O my beloved, I shall describe (later) the earlier physical incarnations. The fifth incarnation was in the fifteenth Tretā Yuga.

## \|\| 1.19.74-77 \|\|

*māṃdhātā cakravarttitve tasyotathyapuraḥsaraḥ \|*  
*ekonaviṃśatretāyāṃ sarvakṣatrāṃtako'bhavat \|\| 74 \|\|*

*jāmadagnyastathā ṣaṣṭho viśvāmitrapuraḥsaraḥ \|*  
*caturviṃśe yuge rāmo vasiṣṭhena purodhasā \|\| 75 \|\|*

*saptamo rāvaṇasyārthe jajñe daśarathātmajaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭame dvāpare viṣṇuraṣṭāviṃśe parāśarāt \|\| 76 \|\|*

*vedavyāsastato jajñe jātūkarṇyapuraḥsaraḥ \|*  
*tatraiva navamo viṣṇuraditeḥ kaśyapātmajaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

74-77. He was Māndhātā, the emperor, along with Utathya (as preceptor).

In the nineteenth Tretā Yuga was born Jāmadagnya who was the slayer of all Kṣatriyas. It was the sixth incarnation with Viśvāmitra as the leader (teacher?).

In the twenty-fourth (Tretā) Yuga, Rāma was born with Vasiṣṭha as Priest. That was the seventh incarnation. He was the son of Daśaratha and the incarnation was for (the slaying of) Rāvaṇa.

Viṣṇu was born as Vedavyāsa, the eighth incarnation. It was in the twenty-eighth Dvāpara and he was born of Parāśara with Jātūkarṇya as the leader (priest).

The ninth incarnation of Viṣṇu was also then born as the son of Aditi and Kaśyapa.

## \|\| 1.19.78-80 \|\|

*devakyāṃ vasudevāttu brahmagargapuraḥsaraḥ \|*  
*ekaviṃśatamasyāsya dvāparasyāṃśasaṃkṣaye \|*  
*naṣṭe dharme tadā jajñe viṣṇurvṛṣṇikule svayam \|\| 78 \|\|*

*kartuṃ dharmavyavasthānamasurāṇāṃ praṇāśanaḥ \|*  
*pūrvajanmani viṣṇuḥ sa pramatirnāma vīryavān \|\| 79 \|\|*

*gotreṇa vai caṃdramasaḥ saṃdhyāmiśre bhaviṣyati \|*  
*kalkirviṣṇuyaśānāma pārāśaryapratāpavān \|\| 80 \|\|*

78-80. He was born of Devakī and Vasudeva with Brahmagarga as leader (priest, preceptor). It was in the twenty-first Dvāpara towards its close. When Dharma was spoiled Viṣṇu was born in the Vṛṣṇi dynasty. He was born in order to establish Dharma. He destroyed the Asuras.

He who was the powerful one named Pramati will be born as Kalki in the Gotra of Candramas, (with) the name of Viṣṇuyaśas. He will have the exploit of Pārāśarya (Vyāsa).

## \|\| 1.19.81 \|\|

*daśamo bhāvyasaṃbhūto yājñavalkyapuraḥsaraḥ \|*  
*anukarṣaśca vai senāṃ hastyaśvarathasaṃkulām \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. He will be the tenth incarnation. He is not yet born. With Yājñavalkya as the priest he will be dragging (taking with him) an army full of elephants, horses and chariots.

## \|\| 1.19.82 \|\|

*pragṛhītāyudhairviprairbhṛśaṃ śatasahasraśaḥ \|*  
*niḥśeṣāñchūdrarājñastāṃstadā sa tu kariṣyati \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. He will be accompanied by hundreds and thousands of fully armed Brāhmaṇas. He will exterminate all the Śūdra kings

## \|\| 1.19.83 \|\|

*pākhaṃḍānmlecchajātīṃśca dasyūṃścaiva sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*nātyarthaṃ dhārmikā ye ca brahmabrahmadviṣaḥ kvacit \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Thousands of heretics, barbarian tribes and robbers will be slain including the haters of Brāhmaṇas and the Vedas, those who are not very religious and pious.

## \|\| 1.19.84 \|\|

*pravṛttacakro balavāñcchūrāṇāmaṃtako balī \|*  
*adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ pṛthivīṃ vicariṣyati \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. The powerful hero will move about on the earth remaining invisible to all living beings. He will establish his sovereignty. The mighty one was (will be) a destroyer of many brave enemies.

## \|\| 1.19.85 \|\|

*mānavasya tu soṃ'śena devasya bhuvi vai prabhuḥ \|*  
*kṣapayitvā tu tānsarvānbhāvinārthena noditān \|*  
*gaṃgāyamunayormadhye niṣṭhāṃ prāpsyati sānugaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. With a part of Mānava Deva (Lord and incarnation of Manu) he will undermine all those already so destined. Along with his followers he will disappear in the middle of Gaṅgā and Yamunā.

## \|\| 1.19.86 \|\|

*tato vyatīte kalkau tu sāmātye sahasainike \|*  
*nṛpeṣvapi ca naṣṭeṣu tadātvapraharāḥ prajāḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. When Kalki passed away along with his ministers and army, when all the kings were also slain, the subjects became helpless (leaderless).

## \|\| 1.19.87 \|\|

*rakṣaṇe vinivṛtte ca hatvā cānyonyamāhave \|*  
*parasparahatāstāśca nirākraṃdāḥ suduḥkhitāḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Succour and protection having been denied they (people) began attacking one another and continued killing one another in fights. They were highly miserable and lamented much.

## \|\| 1.19.88 \|\|

*kṣīṇe kaliyuge cāsmindaśavarṣasahasrake \|*  
*sa saṃdhyāṃśe tu niḥśeṣe kṛtaṃ vai pratipatsyati \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. When this Kaliyuga of thousand years according to the divine reckoning becomes diminished and when it becomes extinct along with the Sandhi (intervening period) Kṛta Yuga will begin.

## \|\| 1.19.89 \|\|

*yadā caṃdraśca sūryaśca tathā tiṣyabṛhaspatī \|*  
*ekarāśau sameṣyaṃti prapatsyati tadā kṛtam \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. When the Sun and the Moon as well as Jupiter come to the same zodiac with the Puṣya Star, Kṛṭa Yuga will set in.

## \|\| 1.19.90 \|\|

*abhijinnāma nakṣatraṃ jayaṃtīnāma śarvarī \|*  
*muhūrto vijayo nāma yatra jāto janārddanaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. When Janārdana was born the constellation was Abhijit, the night was Jayantī and the Muhūrta was Vijaya.

## \|\| 1.19.91 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*noktaṃ yathāvadakhilaṃ bhṛguśāpaviceṣṭitam \|*  
*pūrvāvatārānme brūhi noktapūrvānmaheśvara \|\| 91 \|\|*

The Devī said:

91\. The entire (story of incarnation) has not been narrated as it happened as a result of the curse of Bhṛgu. O Maheśvara, narrate to me the earlier incarnations not yet mentioned.

## \|\| 1.19.92-94 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*yadā tu pṛthivī vyāptā dānavairbalavattaraiḥ \|*  
*tataḥ prabhṛti śāpena bhṛgunaimittikena ha \|\| 92 \|\|*

*jajñe punaḥpunarviṣṇuḥ karttuṃ dharmavyavasthitim \|*  
*dharmānnārāyaṇaḥ sādhyaḥ saṃbhūtaścākṣuṣeṃtare \|\| 93 \|\|*

*yajñaṃ pravartayāmāsa sa ca vaivasvateṃ'tare \|*  
*prādurbhāve tadā tasya brahmā cāsītpurohitaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

92-94. When the earth was occupied by highly powerful Dānavas, Viṣṇu took birth again and again with the curse of Bhṛgu as an ostensible cause. He took the incarnation in order to establish piety (Dharma).

Nārāyaṇa should be realized through Dharma (piety). He was then born in the Cākṣuṣa Manvantara. He propagated Yajña in the Vaivasvata Manvantara. At the time of his manifestation, Brahmā became his priest.

## \|\| 1.19.95 \|\|

*caturthyāṃ tu yugākhyāyāmāpanneṣu sureṣviha \|*  
*saṃbhūtaḥ sa samudrāttu hiraṇyakaśiporvadhe \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. During the fourth quartet of Yugas, when Suras became distressed, he issued forth from the ocean for killing Hiraṇyakaśipu.

## \|\| 1.19.96-97 \|\|

*dvitīyo narasiṃho'bhūdrudrastasya puraḥsaraḥ \|*  
*lokeṣu balisaṃstheṣu tretāyāṃ saptame yuge \|\| 96 \|\|*

*daityaistrailokya ākrāṃte tṛtīyo vāmanobhavat \|*  
*saṃkṣipyātmānamaṃgeṣu bṛhaspatipuraḥsaraḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

96-97. The second incarnation was Narasiṃha. Rudra was his priest.

In the seventh quartet of Yugas when all the worlds were under Bali, in the Tretāyuga when all the three worlds were overcome by Daityas. Viṣṇu became Vāmana reducing his limbs in size. Bṛhaspati was his priest.

## \|\| 1.19.98 \|\|

*tretāyuge tu daśame dattātreyo babhūva ha \|*  
*naṣṭe dharme caturthāṃśe mārkaṃḍeyapuraḥsaraḥ \|*  
*ete divyāvatārā vai mānuṣye kathitāḥ purā \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. In the tenth Tretā Yuga, Dattātreya was born when Dharma had disappeared in the fourth part. Mārkaṇḍeya was his priest. All these divine incarnations in the mortal world have been narrated earlier.

## Chapter 20 - Creation of the Moon

## \|\| 1.20.1-5 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*atha daityāvatārāṇāṃ kramo hi kathyate punaḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipū rājā varṣāṇāmarbudaṃ babhau \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tathā śata sahasrāṇi yāni kāni dvisaptatim \|*  
*aśītiṃ ca sahasrāṇi trailokyasyeśvaro'bhavat \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sautye'hanyatirātrasya kaśyapasyāśvamedhike \|\| 3 \|\|*

*upakṣiptā sanaṃ yattu hoturarthe hiraṇmayam \|*  
*niṣasāda sa garto 'tra hiraṇyakaśipustataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*śatavarṣasahasrāṇāṃ tapaścakre suduścaram \|*  
*daśavarṣasahasrāṇi dityā garbhe sthitaḥ purā \|\| 5 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-5. Henceforth, the order of the lineage of Daityas is being described again. Hiraṇyakaśipu shone as the king for one hundred seven million two hundred eighty thousand years. He was the emperor of the three worlds.

During the Aśvamedha of Kaśyapa, the Atirātra sacrifice was performed. On the Sautya day (day when Soma juice is extracted) thereof, a golden throne was assigned to the Hotṛ. A deep pit occurred there. Hiraṇyakaśipu sat there.

He performed a very severe penance for a hundred thousand years. Formerly he had stayed in the womb of Diti for ten thousand years.

## \|\| 1.20.6-9 \|\|

*hiṇayakaśipordaityaiḥ śloko gītaḥ purātanaḥ \|*  
*rājā hiraṇyakaśipuryāṃ yāmāśāṃ nirīkṣate \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tasyāṃ tasyāṃ diśi surā namaścakruḥ saharṣibhiḥ \|*  
*paryāye tasya rājābhūdbalirvarṣārbudaṃ punaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭiṃ caiva sahasrāṇi triṃśacca niyutāni ca \|*  
*bale rājyādhikārastu yāva tkālaṃ babhūva ha \|\| 8 \|\|*

*prahlādo nigṛhīto'bhūttāvatkālaṃ tathā suraiḥ \|*  
*iṃdrādayaste vikhyātā asurāñjaghnurojasā \|\| 9 \|\|*

6-9. An old verse has been sung about Hiraṇyakaśipu by Daityas: “The Suras along with the sages used to pay respect to that direction which Hiraṇyakaśipu, the king, looked at.”

After his term was over, Bali became the king for ten million three hundred sixty thousand years. While Bali continued to be the king, Prahlāda was held as hostage by the Suras. Indra and other famous (Suras) killed the Asuras with their valour,

## \|\| 1.20.10-12 \|\|

*daityasaṃsthamidaṃ sarvamā sīddaśayugaṃ kila \|*  
*asapatnaṃ tataḥ sarvamaṣṭādaśayugaṃ punaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*trailokyamidamavyagraṃ maheṃdreṇa tu pālitam \|*  
*tretāyuge tu daśame kārttavīryo mahābalaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*paṃcāśītisahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ vai narādhipaḥ \|*  
*sa saptaratnavānsamrāṭ cakravartī babhūva ha \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. The rule of the Daityas continued thus for ten Yugas without any enemy. Then for eighteen Yugas, the entire region of the three worlds was protected carefully by Mahendra. In the tenth Tretā Yuga, Kārtavīrya was the extremely powerful king for eighty-five thousand years. He was an emperor in possession of seven gems.

## \|\| 1.20.13 \|\|

*dvīpeṣu saptasu sa vai khaḍgī carmī śarāsanī \|*  
*rathī rājā sānucaro yogāccaurānapaśyata \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. During his reign that king used to go round in all the seven Dvīpas (continents) armed with a sword, shield and bow in his chariot, accompanied by his followers. By his Yogic power he used to detect thieves,

## \|\| 1.20.14-15 \|\|

*praṇaṣṭadravyatā yasya smaraṇānna bhavennṛṇām \|*  
*caturyuge tvatikrāṃte manau hyekādaśe prabhau \|\| 14 \|\|*

*arddhāvaśiṣṭe tasmiṃstu dvāpare saṃpravartite \|*  
*mānavasya nariṣyaṃto hyāsītputro madaḥ kila \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. If he is remembered, men will never lose their wealth. After the lapse of a quartet of Yugas (Caturyuga) the eleventh Manu became the Lord. Half the period of his reign elapsed and Dvāpara Yuga ensued. Mada was the son of Nariṣyanta, the son of Manu.

Ì6. His ninth successor was remembered as Tṛṇabindu. He became the king at the beginning of the third Tretāyuga.

## \|\| 1.20.17 \|\|

*tasya kanyā tvilavilā rūpe ṇāpratimā'bhavat \|*  
*pulastyāya sa rājarṣistāṃ kanyāṃ pratyapādayat \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. His daughter Ilavilā was unrivalled in beauty. The saintly king gave his daughter to Pulastya.

## \|\| 1.20.18-20 \|\|

*ṛṣirailavilo yasyāṃ viśravāḥ samapadyata \|*  
*tasya patnyaśca tisrastu paulastyakulamaṃḍanāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*bṛhaspateḥ śubhā kanyā nāmnā vai vedavarṇinī \|*  
*puṣpotkaṭā ca vīkā ca ubhe mālyavataḥ sute \|\| 19 \|\|*

*kekasī mālinaḥ kanyā tasyāṃ devi śṛṇu prajāḥ \|*  
*jyeṣṭhaṃ vaiśravaṇaṃ tasya suṣuve varavarṇinī \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. Sage Viśravas was born of her and he is known as Ailavila too. He had four wives and they were ornaments to the family of Pulastya: Bṛhaspati’s splendid daughter named Vedavarṇinī, the two daughters of Mālyavān named Puṣpotkaṭā and Bīkā and Kekasī, the daughter of Mālin. O goddess, listen to her progeny. The lady of excellent complexion gave birth to the eldest son of Viśravas.

## \|\| 1.20.21-22 \|\|

*aṣṭadaṃ haricchmaśruṃ śaṃkukarṇaṃ vilohitam \|*  
*śvapādaṃ hrasvabāhuṃ ca piṃgalaṃ śucibhūṣaṇam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tripādaṃ tu mahākāyaṃ sthūlaśīrṣaṃ mahāhanum \|*  
*evaṃvidhaṃ sutaṃ dṛṣṭvā virūpaṃ rūpatastadā \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. The boy had eight teeth and three feet like those of a dog. He had green moustache and pike-like ears. His hands were small. He was tawny in complexion but had pure ornaments. His body was huge and the head was large with a great chin. She saw the son so very ugly as this (and felt sad).

## \|\| 1.20.23-24 \|\|

*tadā dṛṣṭvābravīttaṃ tu kubero'yamiti svayam \|*  
*kutsāyāṃ kvitiśabdoyaṃ śarīraṃ veramucyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

*kuberaḥ kuśarīratvānnāmnā tena ca soṃkitaḥ \|*  
*tasya bhāryyā'bhavadvṛddhiḥ putrastu nalakūbaraḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. On seeing him, she said to herself: “This is Kubera”. The word Ku is used to denote contempt. Bera means the body. He was named Kubera because of his ugly body. His wife was Vṛddhi and son Nalakūbera.

## \|\| 1.20.25-26 \|\|

*kaikasyajanayatputraṃ rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasādhipam \|*  
*śaṃkukarṇaṃ daśagrīvaṃ pigalaṃ raktamūrddhajam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*vasupādaṃ viṃśadbhujaṃ mahākāyaṃ mahābalam \|*  
*kālāṃjananibhaṃ caiva daṃṣṭriṇaṃ raktalocanam \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Kaikasī (Kekasī is an alternate form) gave birth to Rāvaṇa who later became Lord of Rākṣasas. His ears were like pike. He was tawny in colour with red hairs. He had ten heads, eight feet and twenty arms. He was very powerful with a huge body. He had complexion resembling black collyrium. He had curved fangs and his eyes were red.

## \|\| 1.20.27 \|\|

*rākṣasenaujasā yuktaṃ rūpeṇa ca balena ca \|*  
*nisargāddāruṇaḥ krūro rāvaṇādrāvaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. He was endowed with the vigour of Rākṣasas. He was naturally terrible in features and strength. He was cruel. He was remembered as Rāvaṇa because his cry was shrill.

## \|\| 1.20.28 \|\|

*hiraṇyakaśipustvāsītsa rājā pūrvajanmani \|*  
*caturyugāni rājā tu tathā daśa sa rākṣasaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He was King Hiraṇyakaśipu in his previous birth. He was a king for fourteen Yugas as a Rākṣasa.

## \|\| 1.20.29-31 \|\|

*paṃca koṭīstu varṣāṇāṃ saṃkhyatāḥ saṃkhyāyā priye \|*  
*niyutānyekaṣaṣṭiṃ ca saṃkhyāvadbhirudāhṛtam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭiṃ caiva sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ sa hi rāvaṇaḥ \|*  
*devatānāmṛṣīṇāṃ ca ghoraṃ kṛtvā prajāgaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tretāyuge caturviṃśe rāvaṇastapasaḥ kṣayāt \|*  
*rāmaṃ dāśarathiṃ prāpya sagaṇaḥ kṣayameyivān \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. O my beloved, in terms of years, the time extended to five crore sixty-one lakh sixty thousand years. During this period, Rāvaṇa terrified Devas and the sages and made them sleepless. Rāvaṇa’s penance (i.e. power of penance) dwindled and in the twenty-fourth Tretā Yuga, he met with his death along with his followers at the hands of Rāma, the son of Daśaratha.

## \|\| 1.20.32-36 \|\|

*yo'sau devi daśagrīvaḥ saṃbabhūvārimarddanaḥ \|*  
*damaghoṣasya rājarṣeḥ putro vikhyātapauruṣaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*śrutaśravāyāṃ caidyastu śiśupālo babhūva ha \|*  
*rāvaṇaṃ kuṃbhakarṇaṃ ca kanyāṃ śūrpaṇakhāṃ tathā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*vibhīṣaṇaṃ caturthaṃ ca kaikasyajanayatsutān \|*  
*manoharaḥ prahastaśca mahāpārśvaḥ kharastathā \|\| 34 \|\|*

*puṣpotkaṭāyāste putrāḥ kanyā kumbhīnasī tathā \|*  
*triśirā dūṣaṇaścaiva vidyujjihvaśca rākṣasaḥ \|*  
*kanyaikā śyāmikā nāma vīkāyāḥ prasavaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*ityete krūrakarmāṇaḥ paulastyā rākṣasā nava \|*  
*vibhīṣaṇo viśuddhātmā daśamaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

32-36. O goddess, this same ten-heaḍed Rāvaṇa, a suppressor of enemies; was reborn as son of the saintly king Damaghoṣa. His manliness was well-known. He was born of Śrutaśravā as Śiśupāla and became king of Cedi (modern Bundelkhand, Madhya Pradesh). Kaikasī gave birth to four children, viz. Rāvaṇa, Kuṃbhakarṇa, Vibhīṣaṇa and Śūrpaṇakhā.

Puṣpotkaṭā’s children were Manohara, Prahasta, Mahāpārśva, Khara (four sons) and one daughter Kuṃbhīnasī. Triśiras, Dūṣaṇa, Rākṣasa Vidyujjihva and a daughter named Śyāmikā are remembered as the children of Bīkā. Thus in the family of Pulastya nine Rākṣasas were of ruthless activities. Vibhīṣaṇa, an extremely pure soul, is glorified as the tenth.

## \|\| 1.20.37 \|\|

*pulahasya mṛgāḥ putrāḥ sarve vyālāśca daṃṣṭriṇaḥ \|*  
*bhūtāḥ piśācāḥ sarpāśca śūkarā hastinastathā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The children of Pulaha were all the deer, all tigers with curved fangs, Bhūtas, Piśācas, serpents, boars and elephants.

## \|\| 1.20.38 \|\|

*anapatyaḥ kratustvasminsmṛto vaivasvateṃtare \|*  
*atreḥ patnyo daśaivāsansundaryaśca pativratāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. It is remembered that Kratu was issueless in this Vaivasvata Manvantara. Atri had ten wives. All of them were beautiful and chaste.

## \|\| 1.20.39 \|\|

*bhadrāśvasya ghṛtācyaṃtā jajñire daśa cāpsarāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The ten celestial damsels ending with Ghṛtācī were born of Bhadrāśva.

## \|\| 1.20.40-41 \|\|

*bhadrā śūdrā ca madrā ca naladā jaladā tathā \|*  
*urṇā pūrṇā ca deveśi yā ca gopucchalā smṛtā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*tathā tāmarasā nāma daśamī raktakoṭikā \|*  
*etāsāṃ ca mahādevi khyāto bharttā prabhākaraḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. O great goddess, Prabhākara is well-known as the husband of these ten: Bhadrā, Sūdrā, Madrā, Naladā, Jaladā, Uṛnā \[Ūrṇā?\], Pūrṇā, Gopucchalā, Tāmarasā and Raktakoṭikā the tenth.

## \|\| 1.20.42-44 \|\|

*svarbhānunā hate sūrye patitesmindivo mahīm \|*  
*tamo'bhibhūte lokesminprabhā yena pravarttitā \|\| \|\| 42 \|\|*

*svasti testviti caivoktaḥ patanniha divākaraḥ \|*  
*brahmarṣervacanāttasya na papāta yataḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tataḥ prabhākaretyuktaḥ prabhurevaṃ maharṣibhiḥ \|*  
*bhadrāyāṃ janayāmām somaṃ putraṃ yaśasvinam \|\| 44 \|\|*

42-44. When Sūrya was struck down by Svarbhānu (i.e. Rāhu) and the Lord fell to the ground from heaven, the whole world was assailed (enveloped) with darkness. At that time the Brāhmaṇical sage said: “Hail unto you”. Divākara (the Sun god) who was about to fall did not fall. Hence the sage was called Prabhākara because he caused light to function. The great sages called him so. Lord Prabhākara begot of Bhadrā the reputed son Soma.

## \|\| 1.20.45 \|\|

*tviṣimāndharmaputrastu somo devo varastu saḥ \|*  
*śītaraśmiḥ samutpannaḥ kṛttikāsu niśācaraḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The refulgent Lord Soma was a son unto Dharma. His rays are cool. He was born of Kṛttikās. He is cause of night (Niśākaraḥ \[Niśākara\]).

## \|\| 1.20.46 \|\|

*pitā somasya vai devi jajñe'trirbhagavānṛṣiḥ \|*  
*tatrātriḥ sarvalokeśaṃ bhṛtvā sve nayane sthitaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O goddess, Atri held the Lord of all the worlds in his eyes and stationed himself thus. In this way the holy sage Atri became the father of Soma.

## \|\| 1.20.47 \|\|

*karmaṇā manasā vācā śubhānyeva samā carat \|*  
*kāṣṭhakuḍyaśilābhūta ūrddhvabāhurmahādyutiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Mentally, verbally and physically, whatever he performed was only auspicious.

In the course of his penance the highly lustrous sage remained motionless like a wooden piece or a wall or a rock. He kept his arms raised up.

## \|\| 1.20.48 \|\|

*sudustaraṃ nāma tapastena taptaṃ mahatpurā \|*  
*trīṇi varṣasahasrāṇi divyāni surasuṃdari \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The penance performed by him formerly was very severe and great. O beautiful goddess, he performed that penance for three thousand years according to the reckoning of Devas.

## \|\| 1.20.49 \|\|

*tasyorddhvaretasastatra sthitasyānimiṣasya ha \|*  
*somatvaṃ vapurāpede mahābuddhestu vai śubhe \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O auspicious lady, the highly intelligent one remained winkless thus. He had sublimated his sexual energy. His body attained the state of Soma (Moon).

## \|\| 1.20.50 \|\|

*ūrddhvamācakrame tasya somasaṃbhāvitātmanaḥ \|*  
*netrābhyāṃ somaḥ susrāva daśadhā dyotayandiśaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. As his body attained the status of Soma, the Moon rose up and the Soma juice flowed out of his eyes illuminating the ten directions.

## \|\| 1.20.51 \|\|

*tadgarbhaṃ vidhinā dṛṣṭā diśodaśa dadhustadā \|*  
*sametya dhārayāmāsurna ca dhartumaśaknuvan \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The ten delighted directions duly conceived it in their wombs. They received it collectively but they could not hold it.

## \|\| 1.20.52 \|\|

*sa tābhyaḥ sahasaiveha digbhyo garbhaśca śāśvataḥ \|\| papāta bhāvayaṃllokāñchītāṃśuḥ sarvabhāvanaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. That eternal foetus, the cool-rayed Moon, the delighter of all, suddenly fell down from the directions and illuminated the worlds.

## \|\| 1.20.53 \|\|

*yadā na dhāraṇe śaktāstasya garbhasya tāḥ striyaḥ \|*  
*tatastābhyaḥ sa śītāṃśurnipapāta vasuṃdharām \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. When those ladies were unable to hold the foetus, Śītāṃśu (the cooI-rayed Moon) fellon to the ground from the directions.

## \|\| 1.20.54 \|\|

*patitaṃ somamālokya brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*rathamāropayāmāsa lokānāṃ hitakā myayā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, saw the fallen Soma. With a desire for the welfare of all the worlds, he placed him into a chariot.

## \|\| 1.20.55 \|\|

*sa tadaiva mayā devi dharmārthaṃ satyasaṃgaraḥ \|*  
*yukto vājisahasreṇa sitena surasuṃdari \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. O goddess, O beautiful lady of Suras, the chariot was fitted with a thousand white horses by me for the purpose of establishing piety. He was truthful in speech.

## \|\| 1.20.56 \|\|

*tasminnipatite devi putretreḥ paramātma ni \|*  
*tuṣṭuvurbrahmaṇaḥ putrā mānasāḥ sapta ye śrutāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. O goddess, when the great soul, the son of Atri, fell down, the well-known mental sons of Brahmā eulogized him.

## \|\| 1.20.57 \|\|

*tathaivāṃgirasaḥ sarve bhṛgoścaivātmajāstathā \|*  
*ṛgbhistu sāmabhiścaiva tathaivāṃgirasairapi \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. These as well as all the Aṅgirasas and sons of Bhṛgu eulogized him with the Mantras of Ṛg Veda, Sāmaveda and Atharva Veda.

## \|\| 1.20.58 \|\|

*tasya saṃstūyamānasya tejaḥ somasya bhāsvataḥ \|*  
*āpyāyamānaṃ lokāṃstrīnbhāsayāmāsa sarvaśaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. As he was being eulogized, the splendour of the refulgent Soma became well-nourished and enhanced. He illuminated all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.20.59 \|\|

*sa tena rathamukhyena sāgarāṃtāṃ vasuṃdharām \|*  
*triḥsaptakṛtvotiyaśāścakārābhipradakṣiṇam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The excessively renowned one circumambulated the ocean-girt earth twenty-one times (riding) in that excellent chariot.

## \|\| 1.20.60 \|\|

*tasya yaccāpi tattejaḥ pṛthivīmanvapadyata \|*  
*oṣadhyastāḥ samutpannāste jasā'jvalayanpunaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. From the part of (his) Tejas that reached the earth, arose (were born) medicinal herbs which shone with great lustre.

## \|\| 1.20.61 \|\|

*tābhirdhinotyayaṃ lokaṃ prajāścaiva caturvidhāḥ \|*  
*oṣadhyaḥ phalapākāṃtāḥ kaṇāḥ saptadaśa smṛtāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. With them, he (i.e. Moon) enlivens this world and the four types of subjects (creations). These Oṣadhīs (medicinal herbs) are of seventeen varieties (in the form of cereals and lentils). They mature and bear fruits.

## \|\| 1.20.62-64 \|\|

*vrīhayaśca yavāścaiva godhūmā aṇavastilāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*priyaṃguḥ kovidāraśca koradūṣāḥ satīnakāḥ \|*  
*māṣā mudgā masūrāśca niṣpāvāḥ sakulatthakāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*āḍhakyaścaṇakāścaiva kaṇāḥ saptadaśa smṛtāḥ \|*  
*ityetā oṣadhīnāṃ ca grāmyāṇāṃ jātayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

62-64. They are: Vrihi, Yava (barley), Godhūma (wheat), Aṇu, gingelly seeds, Priyaṅgu (the sixth), Kovidāra, Koradūṣa, Tinaka, Māṣa, Mudga, Masūra, Niṣpāva, Kulattha, Āḍhakī, and Caṇaka and Kaṇa. These are remembered as the rural varieties of Oṣadhīs.

## \|\| 1.20.65-68 \|\|

*oṣadhyo yajñiyāścaiva grāmyā raṇyāścaturddaśa \|*  
*vrīhayaśca yavāścaiva godhūmāstvaṇavastilāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*priyaṃguṣaṣṭhā ityete saptamāstu kulatthakāḥ \|*  
*śyāmākāstvatha nīvārā jartilāḥ sagavedhukāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*ūruvindā markaṭakāstathā veṇuyavāśca ye \|*  
*grāmyāraṇyāstathā hyetā oṣadhyastu caturdaśa \|\| 67 \|\|*

*tṛṇagulmalatā vīrudvallīgucchādi koṭiśaḥ \|*  
*eteṣāmadhipaścandro dhārayatyakhilaṃ jagat \|\| 68 \|\|*

65-68. Oṣadhīs pertaining to Yajñas are both Grāmya (rural) and Āraṇya (grown in forests). They are fourteen: Vrīhi, Yava, Godhūma, Aṇu, Tila (gingelly seeds), Priyaṅgu forming the sixth variety, Kulattha the seventh variety, Śyāmāka, Nīvāra, Jartila, Gavedhūka, Uruvinda, Markaṭaka, and Veṇuyava. These are the fourteen varieties grown in village fields and forests. There are crores and crores of varieties of grass and creepers etc. Candra is the Lord of all these. He sustains the entire universe.

## \|\| 1.20.69 \|\|

*jyotsnābhirbhagavānsomo jagato hitakāmyayā \|*  
*tatastasmai dadau rājyaṃ brahmā brahmavidāṃ varaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Lord Soma sustains the entire earth by means of Jyotsnā (Moonlight) with a desire for the welfare of the universe. Therefore, Brahmā the foremost among the knowers of Brahman, gave a kingdom unto him.

## \|\| 1.20.70 \|\|

*bījauṣadhīnāṃ viprāṇāṃ maṃtrāṇāṃ ca varānane \|*  
*so'bhiṣikto mahātejā rājā rājye niśākaraḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. O lady of excellent countenance, the highly resplendent Niśākara (Moon) was crowned in the kingdom of seeds and medicinal herbs, Brāhmaṇas and Mantras.

## \|\| 1.20.71-74 \|\|

*trīṃllokānbhāvayāmāsa svabhāsā bhāsvatāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*taṃ sinī ca kuhūścaiva dyutiḥpuṣṭiḥ prabhā vasuḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*kīrtirdhṛtiśca lakṣmīśca nava devyaḥ siṣevire \|*  
*saptaviṃśatiriṃdostu dākṣāyaṇyo mahāvratāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*dadau prācetaso dakṣo nakṣatrāṇīti yā viduḥ \|*  
*sa tatprāpya mahdrājyaṃ somaḥ somavatāṃ varaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*samājahre rājasūyaṃ sahasraśatadakṣiṇam \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbhaścodgātā brahmā brahmatvameyivān \|\| 74 \|\|*

71-74. The foremost among the refulgent luminaries sustained the three worlds with his lustre. Nine Devīs (goddesses) viz. Sinī, Kuhū, Dyuti, Puṣṭi, Prabhā, Vasu, Kīrti, Dhṛti and Lakṣmī served him. Dakṣa, the son of Pracetas, gave him his twenty-seven daughters of great holy rites, whom they (people) knew as constellations.

After attaining the great kingdom, Soma, the most excellent one among those endowed with Soma juice, performed a Rājasūya Yajña. The monetary gifts consisted of hundred thousand (gold coins). Hiraṇyagarbha was the Udgātṛ and Brahmā accepted the Brahmatva (the post of the presiding priest).

## \|\| 1.20.75 \|\|

*sadasyastasya bhagavānharirnārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*sanatkumārapramukhairādyairbrahmarṣibhirvṛtaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Lord Hari, Nārāyaṇa was his Sadasya (member of the sacrificial assembly). He was surrounded by the primordial sages, the chief of whom was Sanatkumāra.

## \|\| 1.20.76 \|\|

*dakṣiṇāmadadātsomastrīṃllokāṃstu varānane \|*  
*tebhyo brahmarṣimukhyebhyaḥ sadasyebhyaśca vai śubhe \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. O splendid lady of excellent countenance, Soma gave the three worlds as the Dakṣiṇā to those Sadasyas of whom the Brāhmaṇical sages were the chief ones.

## \|\| 1.20.77 \|\|

*prāpyāvabhṛthamavyagraḥ sarvadevarṣipūjitaḥ \|*  
*atirājati rājendro daśadhā bhāvayandiśaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. After the Avabhṛtha bath, unperturted and honoured by all the Devas and the sages, the leader of Rājās (kings) excelled all the kings illuminating the ten directions.

## \|\| 1.20.78 \|\|

*tena tatprāpa duṣprāpyamaiśvaryyamakṛtā tmabhiḥ \|*  
*sa evaṃ varttate candraścātreya iti viśrutaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Therefore, he attained that Aiśvarya (power and affluence) which persons lacking self-control find it impossible to obtain. Thus is Candra well-known as the son of Atri.

## Chapter 21 - Advice to Propitiate Śiva

## \|\| 1.21.1-5 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*śrutaṃ sarvamaśeṣeṇa candrasyotpatti kāraṇam \|*  
*cihnaṃ yathā'bhavattasya sāṃprataṃ tatprakīrttaya \|\| 1 \|\|*

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*brahmaṇastu purā devi dakṣo nāma suto'bhavat \|*  
*prajāḥ sṛjeti uddiṣṭaḥ pūrvaṃ dakṣaḥ svayaṃbhuvā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭiṃ dakṣo'sṛjatkanyā vairiṇyāṃ vai prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*dadau sa daśa dharmāya kaśyapāya trayodaśa \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sapta viśatiṃ somāya catasro'riṣṭanemine \|*  
*dve caiva bhṛguputrāya dve kṛśāśvāya dhīmate \|\| 4 \|\|*

*dve caivāṃgirase tadvattāsāṃ nāmāni vistarāt \|*  
*śṛṇu tvaṃ devi mātṝṇāṃ prajāvistaramāditaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

The Devī said:

1-5. The origin of Candra has been listened to entirely. Now do narrate how he acquired the stigma.

## \|\| 1.21.6-8 \|\|

*marutvatī vasurjāmī laṃbā bhānurarundhatī \|*  
*saṃkalpā ca muhūrtā ca sādhyā viśvā ca bhāmini \|\| 6 \|\|*

*dharma patnyaḥ samākhyātā dakṣaḥ prācetaso dadau \|*  
*aditirditirdanustadvadariṣṭā surasaiva ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

*surabhirvinatā caiva nāmnā krodhavaśā tvilā \|*  
*kadrūstviṣā vasustadvattāsāṃ putrānvadāmi vai \|\| 8 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

O goddess, formerly Brahmā had a son named Dakṣa. Earlier Dakṣa was instructed by the Self-born Lord (Brahmā): “Create the subjects”.

Dakṣa, the patriarch, begot of Vairiṇī sixty daughters. He gave ten of them to Dharma, thirteen to Kāśyapa, twenty-seven to Soma, four to Ariṣṭanemi, two to the son of Bhṛgu, two to the intelligent Kṛśāśva and two to Aṅgiras. O goddess, listen to their names. Listen to the expansion of progeny of the mothers from the beginning.

6-8. O beautiful lady, the following are mentioned as the wives of Dharma: Marutvatī, Vasu, Jāmī, Lambā, Bhānu, Arundhatī, Saṃkalpā, Muhūrtā, Sādhyā and Viśvā. Dakṣa, the son of Pracetas, gave them to him.

The wives of Kaśyapa are: Aditi, Diti, Danu, Ariṣṭā, Surasā, Surabhi, Vinatā, Krodhavaśā, Ilā, Kadrū, Tviṣā and Vasu. I shall enumerate their sons.

## \|\| 1.21.9 \|\|

*viśvedevāstu viśvāyāḥ sādhyā sādhyānajījanat \|*  
*marutvatyāṃ marutvaṃto vasostu vasavastathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Viśvedevas are the sons of Viśvā. Sādhyā gave birth to Sādhyas. Marutvantas were born of Marutvatī, Vasus were the sons of Vasu.

## \|\| 1.21.10 \|\|

*bhānostu bhānavastena muhūrttāyāṃ muhūrttakāḥ \|*  
*laṃbāyā ghoṣanāmāno nāgavīthistu jāmijā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Bhānus are the sons of Bhānu; Muhūrtakas are the sons of Muhūrtā; those named Ghoṣas were born of Laṃbā; Nāgavīthi was born of Jāmī.

## \|\| 1.21.11-12 \|\|

*saṃkalpāyāstu saṃkalpo dharmaputrā daśa smṛtāḥ \|*  
*āpo dhruvaśca somaśca dharaścaivānalo'nilaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*pratyūṣaśca prabhāsaśca vasavoṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*āpasya putrā vaidaṃḍyaḥ śramaḥ śānto dhvanistathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Saṃkalpa was the son of Saṃkalpā.

These ten are remembered as the ten sons of Dharma. The eight Vasus are: Āpa, Dhruva, Soma, Dhara, Anala, Anila, Pratyūṣa and Prabhāsa.

Vaidaṇḍya, Śrama, Śānta and Dhvani are the sons of Āpa.

## \|\| 1.21.13 \|\|

*dhruvasya putro bhagavānkālo lokaprakālanaḥ \|*  
*somasya bhagavāñcharvo dhruvaśca gṛhabodhanaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Lord Kāla, the reckoner of time, is the son of Dhruva. Soma’s sons are Bhagavān, Śarva, Dhruva and Gṛhabodhana.

## \|\| 1.21.14 \|\|

*hutahavyavahaścaiva dharasya draviṇa smṛtaḥ \|*  
*manojavo'nilasyāsīdavijñātagatistathā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Hutahavyavāha is also the son of Soma. Draviṇa is remembered as the son of Dhara. Manojava and Avijñātagati were born of Anila.

## \|\| 1.21.15 \|\|

*devalo bhagavānyogī pratyūṣasyābhavansutāḥ \|*  
*bṛhaspatestu bhaginī bhuvanā brahmavādinī \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Devala, Bhagavān and Yogi were the sons of Pratyūṣa. Bhuvanā, the sister of Bṛhaspati, was an expounder of Brahman.

## \|\| 1.21.16 \|\|

*prabhāsasya tu sā bhāryā vasūnāmaṣṭamasya ca \|*  
*viśvakarmā sutastasya śilpakarttā prajāpatiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. She became the wife of Prabhāsa, the eighth of the Vasus. Viśvakarmā was his son. He is the patriarch and the architect of Devas.

## \|\| 1.21.17-18 \|\|

*tuṣitānāṃ tu sādhyānāṃ nāmānyetāni vacmi te \|*  
*mano'numantā prāṇaśca naro'pānaśca vīryavān \|\| 17 \|\|*

*bhaktirbhayo'naghaścaiva haṃso nārāyaṇastathā \|*  
*vibhuścaiva prabhuścaiva sādhyā dvādaśa kīrtitāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. I shall mention the names of the Sādhyas called the Tuṣitas (the delighted ones). They are Mana, Anumantā, Prāṇa, Nara, the powerful Apāna, Bhakti, Bhaya, Anagha, Haṃsa, Nārāyaṇa, Vibhu and Prabhu. The twelve Sādhyas have been mentioned.

## \|\| 1.21.19-20 \|\|

*kaśyapasya pravakṣyāmi santatiṃ varavarṇini \|*  
*aṃśo dhātā bhagastvaṣṭā mitro'tha varuṇo ryamā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*vivasvānsavitā pūṣā hyaṃśumānviṣṇureva ca \|*  
*ete sahasrakiraṇā ādityā dvādaśa smṛtāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. O lady of excellent complexion, I shall enumerate the progeny of Kaśyapa. The following are remembered as the twelve Ādityas (sons of Aditi): Aṃśa, Dhātṛ, Bhaga, Tvaṣṭṛ, Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, Vivasvān, Savitṛ, Pūṣan, Aṃśumān and Viṣṇu. They are thousand-rayed ones.

## \|\| 1.21.21-22 \|\|

*ajaikapādahirbudhnyo virūpākṣo'tha raivataḥ \|*  
*haraśca bahurūpaśca tryaṃbakaśca sureśvaraḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*sāvitraśca jayantaśca pinākī cāparājitaḥ \|*  
*ete rudrāḥ samākhyātā ekādaśa gaṇeśvarāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. The following are called Rudras, the eleven leaders of Gaṇas: Ajaikapāt, Ahirbudhnya, Virūpākṣa, Raivata, Hara, Bahurūpa, Tryaṃbaka, Sureśvara, Sāvitra, Jayanta, Pinākī, Aparājita (unconquered).

## \|\| 1.21.23 \|\|

*ditiḥ putradvayaṃ lebhe kaśyapādbalagarvitam \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipuṃ śreṣṭhaṃ hiraṇyākṣaṃ tathānujam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. From Kaśyapa, Diti obtained two sons very arrogant of their power viz. Hiraṇyakaśipu, the elder and Hiraṇyākṣa, the younger one.

## \|\| 1.21.24-25 \|\|

*hiraṇyakaśipordaityaiḥ ślokogītaḥ purātanaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*rājā hiraṇyakaśipuryāṃyāmāśāṃ nirīkṣate \|*  
*tasyāṃ tasyāṃ diśi surā namaścakrurmaharṣibhiḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipoḥ putrāścatvāraḥ sumahābalāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. A verse has been sung about Hiraṇyakaśipu by the ancient Daityas: “The Suras together with the great sages paid respect to that direction which was looked at by Hiraṇyakaśipu.” Hiraṇyakaśipu had four very powerful sons.

## \|\| 1.21.26 \|\|

*prahlādaḥ pūrvajasteṣāmanuhrādastataḥ paraḥ \|*  
*hrādaścaiva hradaścaiva putrāścaite prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Prahrāda was the eldest among them. The next one was Anuhrāda. Then Hrāda and Hrada. Thus the sons have been enumerated.

## \|\| 1.21.27 \|\|

*ubhau sundopasundau tu hradaputrau babhūvatuḥ \|*  
*hrādasya putrastveko'bhūnmūka ityabhiviśrutaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Sunda and Upasunda were the two sons of Hrada. Hrāda had only one son well-known as Mūka.

## \|\| 1.21.28 \|\|

*mārīcaḥ suṃdaputrastu tāḍakāyāmajāyata \|*  
*daṇḍake nihataḥ so'yaṃ rāghaveṇa valīyasā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Mārīca, the son of Sunda, was born of Tāḍakā. He was killed in the Daṇḍaka forest by the powerful scion of the family of Raghu.

## \|\| 1.21.29-31 \|\|

*mūko vinihataścāpi kairāte sabyasācinā \|*  
*saṃhrādasya tu daityasya nivātakavacāḥ kule \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tisraḥ koṭyastu vikhyātā nihatāḥ savyasācinā \|*  
*gaveṣṭhī kālanemiśca jaṃbho valkala eva ca \|\| 30 \|\|*

*jṛṃbhaḥ ṣaṣṭhonujasteṣāṃ smṛtāḥ prahrādasūnavaḥ \|*  
*śuṃbhaścaiva niśuṃbhaśca gaveṣṭhinaḥ sutau smṛtau \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. Mūka was killed by Savyasācin (i.e. Arjuna) in the course of his encounter with the divine Kirāta (hunter) (i.e. Lord Śiva). There were three crores of Nivātakavacas of the family of Daitya Saṃhrāda. They were killed by Savyasācin (Arjuna). The following are remembered as the sons of Prahrāda: Gaveṣṭhī, Kālanemi, Jambha, Valkala, Jṛṃbha and a younger brother (the sixth) of them. Śuṃbha and Niśuṃbha are remembered as the two sons of Gaveṣṭhin.

## \|\| 1.21.32 \|\|

*dhanukaścāsilomā ca śuṃbhaputrau prakīrtitau \|*  
*virocanasya putrastu balirekaḥ pratāpavān \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Dhanuka and Asiloman are glorified as the two sons of Śuṃbha. Virocana had only one powerful son named Bali.

## \|\| 1.21.33-34 \|\|

*hiraṇyākṣasutāḥ paṃca vikrāṃtāḥ sumahābalāḥ \|*  
*andhakaḥ śakuniścaiva kālanābhastathaiva ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

*mahānābhaśca vikrāṃto bhūtasaṃtāpanastathā \|*  
*śataṃ śatasahasrāṇi nihatāstārakāmaye \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. (The following) five sons of Hiraṇyākṣa were very powerful and valorous: Andhaka, Śakuni, Kālanābha, Mahānābha the valorous and Bhūtasantāpana. Hundreds of hundred thousands of these Daityas were killed in the course of the hostilities pertaining to Tāraka.

## \|\| 1.21.35 \|\|

*iti saṃkṣapataḥ proktā kaśyapānvayasaṃtatiḥ \|*  
*yayā vyāptaṃ jagatsarvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Thus the lineage of Kaśyapa has been succinctly narrated. The entire universe consisting of Devas, Asuras and human beings is pervaded by these children.

## \|\| 1.21.56 \|\|

*anādṛtya tu te vākyaṃ rohiṇyāṃ nirato rahaḥ \|*  
*reme kāmaparītātmā asmākaṃ śokavarddhanaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. O great goddess, among the twenty-seven daughters given to Indu (Moon-god) Rohiṇī was his greatest favourite.

## \|\| 1.21.37 \|\|

*atha nakṣatranāthasya tāsāṃ madhyetivallabhā \|*  
*babhūva rohiṇī devī prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Among them, the fair lady Rohiṇī was the dearest darling of the Lord of Constellations, greater than his own vital airs.

## \|\| 1.21.38 \|\|

*sarvāstāḥ saṃparityajya rohiṇyā sahito rahaḥ \|*  
*reme kāmaparītātmā vaneṣūpavaneṣu ca \|*  
*ramaṇīyeṣu deśeṣu kandareṣu guhāsu ca \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. He forsook all the others and sported about secretly with her in forests and gardens. He was so passionately infatuated that he took her to beautiful lands, caves and crevices and sported about.

## \|\| 1.21.39 \|\|

*atha tā duḥkhasaṃpannāḥ patnyaḥ śeṣā yaśasvini \|*  
*jagmuśca śaraṇaṃ dakṣaṃ vacanaṃ cedamabruvan \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Thereupon, O renowned lady, the remaining miserable wives sought refuge in Dakṣa and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.21.40-43 \|\|

*somaḥ sarvā tikramya rohiṇyā saha modate \|*  
*saṃvatsarasahasraṃ tu krīḍamāno yathāsukham \|\| 40 \|\|*

*avaśiṣṭāstu ṣaḍviṃśanmalinā vigataśriyaḥ \|*  
*pāṇigrahaṇamārabhya rohiṇyā saha caṃdramāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*saṃvatsarasahasraṃ tu jānātyekāṃ sa śarvarīm \|*  
*parityaktā vayaṃ tāta śaśinā doṣavarjitāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*sa reme saha rohiṇyā asmākamasukhapradaḥ \|*  
*asmākaṃ duḥkhadagdhānāṃ śreyo'to maraṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 43 \|\|*

40-43. “Soma has eschewed all of us and is rejoicing with Rohiṇī alone. Ever since our marriage, for these thousand years he has been sporting about with her as he pleases. Ever since our marriage, all the twenty-six of us are devoid of glory and we have been rendered devoid of lustre and dirty, though we are faultless. He seems to consider this entire period of a thousand years a mere night. O dear father, though we are blameless, we have been abandoned. He diverts himself with that Rohiṇī alone. Hence our unhappiness. So, in view of this that we have already been burnt by misery, death itself would have been more welcome.”

## \|\| 1.21.44 \|\|

*tāsāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā duḥkhārtānāṃ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*brahmatejaḥ samāyuktaḥ putrīsnehena karṣitaḥ \|*  
*jagāma yatra ṛkṣeśo vacanaṃ cedamabravīt \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. On hearing these words of these distressed ones, the patriarch endowed with Brāhmaṇical splendour, urged by his affection for his daughters, went to the place where the Lord of Constellations was present and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.21.45 \|\|

*samaṃ varttasva kanyāsu māmakāsu niśākara \|*  
*anyathā doṣabhāgī tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. “O Niśākara (Moon), be have impartially in respect to all my daughters. If not, you will undoubtedly be incurring the fault.”

## \|\| 1.21.46 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā lajjayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*bāḍhamityeva ṛkṣeṃdro dakṣasya purato'bravīt \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. On hearing these words, the Lord of Constellations stood with his head bowing down due to shame and spoke thus to Dakṣa:

## \|\| 1.21.47 \|\|

*adyaprabhṛti viprarṣe samaṃ varttayitāsmyaham \|*  
*putrībhistava satyaṃ vai śape'haṃ śapathena te \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. “Of course, O Brāhmaṇical sage, from this day onwards I shall behave impartially with your daughters. It is the truth. I solemnly take this pledge.”

## \|\| 1.21.48 \|\|

*evaṃ pratijñāsaṃyukte niśānāthe tadāṃbike \|*  
*sarvā rūpeṇa saṃyuktāstasya kanyā niveditāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O Aṃbikā, when the Lord of Night took this oath, all the daughters endowed with beauty were duly informed.

## \|\| 1.21.49 \|\|

*dakṣaḥ svabhavanaṃ gatvā nirvṛtiṃ paramāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*candro'pi pūrvavaddevi rohiṇyāṃ nirato'bhavat \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Dakṣa went back to his abode, experiencing great relief and happiness. But, O goddess, Candra remained indulgent towards Rohiṇī as before.

## \|\| 1.21.50 \|\|

*saṃparityajya tāḥ sarvāḥ kāmopahatamānasaḥ \|*  
*atha bhūyastu tāḥ sarvā dakṣaṃ vacanamabruvan \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. With his mind deluded by infatuation he discarded all of them. So, once again, all of them complained to Dakṣa:

## \|\| 1.21.51 \|\|

*malināstāḥ kṛśāṃgyaśca dīnāḥ sarvā vicetasaḥ \|*  
*tato dṛṣṭvā tathārūpaṃ dakṣo mohamupāgataḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Even before it, on seeing them all emaciated and distressed, dusty and gloomy, Dakṣa fell into a swoon.

## \|\| 1.21.52-53 \|\|

*labdhasaṃjñaḥ punaḥ so'pi krodhodbhūtatanūruhaḥ \|*  
*uvāca sarvāḥ svāḥ putrīḥ kimitthaṃ malināṃbarāḥ \|*  
*kimidaṃ niṣprabhāḥ sarvāḥ kathayadhvaṃ mamānaghāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*asurānsānugāṃścaiva ye cānye surasattamāḥ \|*  
*adya śāpahatānputryaḥ kariṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. On regaining consciousness he spoke to all those daughters of his with the hair bristling due to anger: “Why are you in dirty garments? Why are you so pale in your faces? O my sinless dear ones, do tell me. O my daughters, whether they be the Asuras with their followers, or the other excellent Suras, I shall strike them all down by means of my curses.”

## \|\| 1.21.54 \|\|

*evamuktāstu dakṣeṇa sarvāstāḥ samudairayan \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. On being told thus by Dakṣa all of them uttered thus:

## \|\| 1.21.55-56 \|\|

*na cāsmākaṃ niśānātha ṛtumātramapi prabho \|*  
*prayacchati punastena yuṣmatpārśvaṃ samāgatāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*anādṛtya tu te vākyaṃ rohiṇyāṃ nirato rahaḥ \|*  
*reme kāmaparītātmā asmākaṃ śokavarddhanaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. “O Lord, the Lord of Night does not approach us

even after menstruation. Hence we have come to you. He has ignored your advice. Again he is addicted to Rohiṇī secretly. Causing us increased grief he diverts himself with her in his lasciviousness.”

## \|\| 1.21.57 \|\|

*tāsāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā dakṣaḥ kopamupāgataḥ \|*  
*gatvā caṃdraṃ mahādevi śaśāpa pramukhe sthitam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. On hearing their words, Dakṣa became furious. He went to Candra, O great goddess, and cursed him even as he stood face to face:

## \|\| 1.21.58 \|\|

*anādṛtya hi me vākyaṃ yasmāttvaṃ rohiṇīrataḥ \|*  
*saṃtyajya putrīścāsmākaṃ śeṣā doṣeṇa varjitāḥ \|*  
*tasmādyakṣmā śarīraṃ te grasiṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. “Since you ignored my advice and are going on in your exclusive indulgence with Rohiṇī by excluding the other faultless daughters of mine, the consumptive disease will assail you. There is no doubt about it.”

## \|\| 1.21.59 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu yakṣmā parvataputrike \|*  
*dakṣeṇa tu samādiṣṭastasya kāyaṃ samāviśat \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. In the meantime, O Daughter of the Mountain, the consumptive disease, at the behest of Dakṣa, penetrated the body of Candra.

## \|\| 1.21.60 \|\|

*yakṣmaṇā grastakāyo'sau kṣayaṃ yāti dinedine \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. With his body assailed by consumptive disease Candra waned day by day.

## \|\| 1.21.61 \|\|

*evaṃ somastu dakṣeṇa kṛtaśāpo gataprabhaḥ \|*  
*papāta vasudhāṃ devi niśceṣṭo rohiṇīyutaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O goddess, on being cursed thus by Dakṣa Soma became lustreless and motionless. He fell down on the ground along with Rohiṇī.

## \|\| 1.21.62 \|\|

*labdhvasaṃjño muhūrtena rohiṇīvākya mabravīt \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Regaining consciousness after a short while, he spoke to Rohiṇī:

## \|\| 1.21.63 \|\|

*devi kāryaṃ kimadhunā tvatpitrā śāpito hyaham \|*  
*kṣayakuṣṭhena saṃyuktaḥ kiṃ karomyadhunā priye \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. “O fair lady, what is to be done now? I have been cursed by your father. O my beloved, afflicted by consumption and leprosy what can I do now?”

## \|\| 1.21.64 \|\|

*evamuktā rohiṇī tu bāṣpavyākulalocanā \|*  
*dakṣaśāpahataṃ dṛṣṭvā somaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. On being told thus, Rohiṇī’s eyes became dimmed with tears. Glancing at Soma struck down by the curse of Dakṣa, she spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.21.65-66 \|\|

*yena śāpastu te dattastameva śaraṇaṃ vraja \|*  
*sa te śāpābhibhūtasya nūnaṃ śreyo vidhāsyati \|\| 65 \|\|*

*lapsyase tatprasādāttvaṃ prabhāṃ pūrvocitāṃ śubhām \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. “Seek refuge in him alone, by whom you have been cursed. Indeed, now that you have been afflicted by his curse, he will bring about your welfare by all means. With his favour, you will regain your lost splendour, the splendour with which you were formerly so pleasurable.”

## \|\| 1.21.67 \|\|

*rohiṇyā vacanaṃ śrutvā gato dakṣasamīpataḥ \|*  
*caṃdraḥ provāca vinayādvāṣpa vyākulalocanaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. On hearing the words of Rohiṇī, Candra went near Dakṣa and stood there humbly with tears rendering his eyes turbid.

## \|\| 1.21.68-70 \|\|

*kuruṣvānugrahaṃ dakṣa prasannenāṃtarātmanā \|*  
*kopaṃ tyaja maharṣe tvaṃ mamopari dayāṃ kuru \|\| 68 \|\|*

*tvayā krodhaparītena kāraṇe vāpyakāraṇe \|*  
*anukaṃpāṃ ca me kṛtvā kāryaṃ śāpasya mokṣaṇam \|\| 69 \|\|*

*viditaṃ tu mahābhāga śaptohaṃ yena karmaṇā \|*  
*kuruṣvānugrahaṃ dakṣa mama dīnasya yācataḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

68-70. “O great sage, Dakṣa, do bless me with a delighted heart. Cast off your anger and take pity on me. You had been extremely furious with or without reason. It behoves you to take pity on me and redeem me from the curse. O highly esteemed one, I am fully aware of the reason why I have been cursed. But I am distressed and I implore you, do bless me.”

## \|\| 1.21.71 \|\|

*evaṃ vilapamānasya somasya tu mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*anugrahe matiṃ kṛtvā idaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. When the noble-souled Soma lamented thus, Dakṣa felt inclined to bless him and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.21.72 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*mayā śāpahataḥ soma trātuṃ śakyo na daivataiḥ \|*  
*yadyadbravīmyahaṃ soma tattatheti na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:

72\. O Soma, no one who has been struck down by my curse can be saved by Devas. O Soma, whatever I say remains as it is (i.e. unchangeable). There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.21.73 \|\|

*āyuḥ karma ca vittaṃ ca vidyā nidhanameva ca \|*  
*pūrvasṛṣṭāni yānyeva saṃbhavaṃti hi tāni vai \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Span of life, Karma, wealth, learning and death—all these have been pre-destined and they remain so.

## \|\| 1.21.74 \|\|

*asurāśca surāścaiva ye cānye yakṣarākṣasāḥ \|*  
*sarvepi śaktā na trātuṃ varjayitvā maheśvaram \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Asuras, Suras, Yakṣas and Rākṣasas—none of these can save you, except Maheśvara.

## \|\| 1.21.75 \|\|

*eṣāṃ śāpo mayā datto'nugrahīṣya ti śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*nānyastrātuṃ bhavecchakto vinā paśupatiṃ bhavam \|*  
*tattvaṃ śīghrataraṃ gaccha samārādhaya śaṃkara \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Śaṅkara will bless even those whom I curse. No one except Bhava, Paśupati, is competent to grant succour. Hence, go quickly and propitiate Śaṅkara.

## \|\| 1.21.76 \|\|

*na śakto'nyaḥ punaścaṃdraḥ kartuṃ tvāṃ nirmalaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*varjayitvā mahādevaṃ śitikaṃṭhamumāpatim \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Excepting Mahādeva, the blue-throated consort of Umā, O Candra, none can free you from impurities.

## \|\| 1.21.77 \|\|

*dakṣasya ca vacaḥ śrutvā kṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca tadā somaḥ prahaṣṭenāṃtarātmanā \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. On hearing the words of Dakṣa, Soma stood there with palms joined in reverence. With an over-delighled mind he replied thus:

## \|\| 1.21.78-79 \|\|

*bhagavanyadi tuṣṭosi mama bhaktasya suvrata \|*  
*anugrahe kṛtā buddhistadācakṣva kutaḥ śivaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*kasminsthāne mayā dakṣa draṣṭavyo'sau maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tatsthānāni cariṣyāmi yāni tāni vadasva me \|\| 79 \|\|*

78-79. “O holy sage of excellent pious rites, if you are pleased with me, your devotee, and if you have decided to bless me, then tell me where is Śiva. O Dakṣa, where can I find Maheśvara? I shall go to those places. Tell me what those places are.”

## \|\| 1.21.80-81 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu soma prayatnena śrutvā caivāvadhāraya \|*  
*vāruṇīṃ diśamāśritya sāgarānūpasannidhau \|\| 80 \|\|*

*kṛtasmarasyāparato dhanvaṃtaraśatatraye \|*  
*liṃgaṃ mahāprabhāvaṃ ca svayaṃbhūtaṃ vyavasthitam \|\| 81 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:

80-81. O Soma, listen carefully. After hearing, understand it well. In the west, in the vicinity of the ocean and the marshy land nearby beyond Kṛtasmara, within a distance of three hundred Dhanus, there is a Liṅga of great power. It has come up by itself and has stationed itself there.

## \|\| 1.21.82 \|\|

*sūryyabiṃbasamaprakhyaṃ sarpa mekhalamaṃḍitam \|*  
*kukkuṭāṃḍakamānaṃ tadbhūmimadhye vyavasthitam \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. It’s lustre is like that of the solar disc. It is adorned by a girdle of serpents. Its magnitude is that of a hen’s egg. It is stationed within the ground.

## \|\| 1.21.83 \|\|

*sparśaliṃgaṃ hi tadviddhi tadbhaktyā jñāsyate bhavān \|*  
*tatra saṃnihito devaḥ śaṃkaraḥ parameśvaraḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Understand that it is a Sparśa Liṅga (a Liṅga to be known by touch). You will know it through devotion. Śaṅkara, Parameśvara is present therein.

## \|\| 1.21.84 \|\|

*gaccha tvaṃ tapasogreṇa ārādhaya sureśvaram \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Do go and propitiate the Lord of Suras by means of severe penance.

## \|\| 1.21.85 \|\|

*praśasya devadeveśamātmānaṃ nirmalaṃ kuru \|*  
*yasyāśu varadānena prāpsyase rūpamuttamam \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Make yourself free from impurities after eulogizing the Lord of the chiefs of Devas. He will grant you a boon and thus, you will regain your excellent form.

## Chapter 22 - Soma Gets a Boon

## \|\| 1.22.1-2 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*dakṣeṇaivamanujñātaḥ śocankarma svakaṃ tadā \|*  
*duḥkhaśokaparītātmā prabhāsaṃ kṣetramāgataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sa gatvā dakṣiṇaṃ tīraṃ sāgarasya samīpataḥ \|*  
*dadarśa parvataṃ tatra kṛtasmaramiti śrutam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-2. On being thus instructed by Dakṣa, Soma who bewailed his misdemeanour and was utterly grief-stricken, came to Prabhāsa. He went to the southern shore of the sea and saw nearby the mountain well-known as Kṛtasmara.

## \|\| 1.22.3-6 \|\|

*yakṣavidyādharākīrṇaṃ kinnarairupaśobhitam \|*  
*caṃdanāgurukarpūrairaśokaistilakaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kalhāraiḥ śatapatraiśca puṣpitaiḥ phalitaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*āmrajambūkapitthaiśca dāḍimaiḥ panasaistathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*niṃbujambīranāgaiśca kadalīkhaṃḍamaṃḍitaiḥ \|*  
*kramukairnāgavallyādyaiḥ śālaistālaistamālakaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*bījapūrakakharjūrairdrākṣāmadhurapāṭalaiḥ \|*  
*bilvacaṃpakatiṃdvādyaiḥ kadaṃbakakubhaistathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. The whole region was occupied by Yakṣas, Vidyādharas and Kinnaras. It was beautified by trees such as sandal, agallocham, camphor, Aśoka, splendid Tilaka, Kalhāra and Śatapatra in full bloom. It appeared beautiful with trees laden with fruits such as Āmra, Jaṃbū, Kapittha, Dāḍima, Panasa, Niṃba, Jaṃbīra, Nāga, banana, Kramuka, Nāgavallī etc., Śāla, Tamālaka, Bījapūra, date palm, grape-vines sweet and pinkish in colour. There were Bilva, Campaka, Tinḍu, Kadamba and Kakubha trees.

## \|\| 1.22.7 \|\|

*dhavāśokaśirīṣādyairnānāvṛkṣaiśca śobhitam \|*  
*kāmaṃ kāmaphalairvṛkṣaiḥ puṣpitaiḥ phalitaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The mountain shone with different kinds of trees—Dhava, Aśoka, Śirīṣa etc. The trees were splendid with pleasant fruits and flowers.

## \|\| 1.22.8 \|\|

*haṃsakāraṃḍavākīrṇaṃ cakravākopaśobhitam \|*  
*kokilābhiḥ śukaiścaiva nānāpakṣininādi tam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The place was resonant with the chirping sounds of various kinds of birds such as Haṃsa, Kāraṇḍava, Cakravāka, cuckoos, and parrots.

## \|\| 1.22.9-10 \|\|

*jātismarāḥ pakṣiṇaśca vyājahrurmānuṣīṃ giram \|*  
*gaṃdharvakiṃnarayugaiḥ siddhavidyādharoragaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*krīḍadbhirvividhairdivyaiḥ śobhitaṃ parvatottamam \|*  
*devagaṃdharvanṛtyaiśca veṇuvīṇānināditam \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Some birds having power to remember previous births spoke with human voice. The excellent mountain shone with couples of Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Siddhas, Vidyādharas, Serpents etc. who were playing different kinds of divine sports. Devas and Gandharvas were engaged in dances. The notes of flutes and lutes echoed all round.

## \|\| 1.22.11 \|\|

*vedadhvanitaghoṣeṇa yajñahomāgnihotrajaiḥ \|*  
*samāvṛtaṃ sarvamājyagaṃdhibhirucchritam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. It was resounded with the chanting of Vedas. It was enveloped with smoke which rose up from the fires of sacrifices and Homas emitting pleasant smell of clarified butter (oblated in them).

## \|\| 1.22.12-19 \|\|

*śobhitaṃ carṣibhirdivyaiścāturvidyairdvijottamaiḥ \|*  
*atriścaiva vasiṣṭhaśca pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*bhṛguścaiva marīciśca bharadvājo'tha kaśyapaḥ \|*  
*manuryamoṃ'girā viṣṇuḥ śātātapaparāśarau \|\| 13 \|\|*

*āpastaṃbo'tha saṃvartaḥ kātyaḥ kātyāyano muniḥ \|*  
*gautamaḥ śaṃkhalikhitau tathā vācaspatirmuniḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*jāmadagnyo yājñavalkya ṛṣyaśṛṃgo vibhāṃḍakaḥ \|*  
*gārgyaśaunakadālbhyāśca vyāsa uddālakaḥ śukaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*nāradaḥ parvataścaiva durvāsā ugratāpasaḥ \|*  
*śākalyo gālavaścaiva jābālirmudgalastathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*viśvāmitraḥ kauśikaśca jahnurviśvāvasustathā \|*  
*dhaumyaścaiva śatānando vaiśaṃpāyanajiṣṇavaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*śākaṭāyanavārddhikyāvagniko bādarāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*vālakhilyā mahātmāno ye ca bhūmaṇḍale sthitāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*te sarve tatra tiṣṭhaṃti parvate tu kṛtasmare \|*  
*tejasvino brahmaputrā ṛṣayo dhārmikāḥ priye \|\| 19 \|\|*

12-19. The mountain was graced by the divine sages and excellent Brāhmaṇas, experts in the four lores (or four Vedas). They were: Atri, Vasiṣṭha, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Bhṭgu, Marīci, Bharadvāja, Kaśyapa, Manu, Yama, Aṅgiras, Viṣṇu, Śātātapa, Parāśara, Āpastamba, Saṃvarta, Kātya (Kāvya? i.e, Śukra), Sage Kātyāyana, Gautama, Śaṅkha, Likhita, Sage Vācaspati, Jāmadagnya, Yājñavalkya, Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, Vibhāṇḍaka, Gārgya, Śaunaka, Dālbhya, Vyāsa, Uddālaka, Śuka, Nārada, Parvata, the fierce ascetic Durvāsas, Śākalya, Gālava, Jābāli, Mudgala, Viśvāmitra, Kauśika, Jahnu, Viśvāvasu, Dhaumya, Śatānanda, Vaiśaṃpāyana, Jiṣṇu, Śākaṭāyana, Vārdhikya, Agnika, Bādarāyaṇa and the noble-souled Vālakhilyas. In fact all the sages existing on the earth, reside there on Mountain Kṛtasmara. O my beloved, all the righteous sages and the refulgent sons of Brahmā (stayed there).

## \|\| 1.22.20 \|\|

*jvalaṃtastapasā sarve nirddhūmā iva pāvakāḥ \|*  
*māsopavāsinaḥ kecitkecitpakṣopavāsinaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. By their penance, all the ascetics were (refulgent like) blazing fire devoid of smoke. Some observed fasts for a month and some for a fortnight.

## \|\| 1.22.21 \|\|

*trairātrikāḥ sāṃtapanā nirāhārāstathā pare \|*  
*kecitpuṣpa phalāhārāḥ śīrṇaparṇāśinastathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Others took food once in three days. Yet others performed Sāntapana expiatory rite. Some abstained from food. Some had fruits and flowers for food. Some ate only dried and scattered leaves.

## \|\| 1.22.22 \|\|

*kecidgomayabhakṣāśca jalāhārāstathā pare \|*  
*sāgnihotrāḥ suvidvāṃso mokṣamārgārthacintakāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Some subsisted on cow-dung (Pañca-gavya?) and some on mere water. All were excellent scholars performing Agnihotra rites. They pondered over matters pertaining to salvation.

## \|\| 1.22.23 \|\|

*iti hāsapurāṇādiśrutismṛtiviśāradāḥ \|*  
*ete cānye ca bahavo mārkaṃḍeyapurogamāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. There were other sages with Mārkaṇḍeya as the leader. These and many others were experts in Śruti, Smṛti, Itihāsa, Purāṇa etc.

## \|\| 1.22.24 \|\|

*prabhāsaṃ kṣetramāsādya saṃsthitā kṛtaparvate \|*  
*evaṃ kṛtasmarastatra sarvadevaniṣevitaḥ \|*  
*manvaṃtaresminyo devi nirdagdho vaḍavāgninā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. All these sages, O goddess, came and stayed on the Kṛtasmara mountain in the holy spot of Prabhāsa. Thus Kṛtasmara is resorted to by all the Devas. Later in this Manvantara, it will be burnt completely by Vaḍavā fire, O fair lady.

## \|\| 1.22.25 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā parvataṃ ramyaṃ dṛṣṭvā caiva mahodadhim \|*  
*pradakṣiṇaṃ tataścakre saptakṛtvo niśākaraḥ \|*  
*gireḥ pradakṣiṇāṃ kṛtvā gato yatra maheśvaraḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On seeing the beautiful mountain and the great ocean, Niśākara (Moon) circumambulated it seven times. After circumambulating the mountain he went to the place where Maheśvara was present.

## \|\| 1.22.26 \|\|

*samīpe tu samudrasya sparśaliṃgasvarūpavān \|*  
*prasādayāmāsa vibhuṃ prasannenāṃtarātmanā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The deity was near the ocean, in the form of a Sparśa Liṅga (felt by touch?). He then propitiated the Lord with a delighted mind.

## \|\| 1.22.27-28 \|\|

*maraṇaṃ veti saṃdhyāya śaraṇaṃ vā maheśvaram \|*  
*varaṃ śāpābhighātārthaṃ mṛtyuṃ vā śaṃkarānmama \|\| 27 \|\|*

*iti somo matiṃ kṛtvā tapasā'rādhayañchivam \|*  
*yāvadvarṣasahasraṃ tu phalamūlāśano'bhavat \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. He resolved within himself: ‘I seek refuge in Maheśvara for the annihilation of the curse or I shall meet with death or it is better that I meet with death from Śaṅkara’. After resolving thus Soma began to propitiate Śiva by means of penance for a period of a thousand years. He took in only fruits and roots as food.

## \|\| 1.22.29 \|\|

*pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu caturthe varavarṇini \|*  
*tutoṣa bhagavānrudro vākyaṃ cedamuvāca ha \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O lady of excellent complexion, when the fourth round of a thousand years concluded Lord Rudra became pleased and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.22.30 \|\|

*parituṣṭo'smi te caṃdra varaṃ varaya suvrata \|*  
*kiṃ te kāmaṃ karomyadya brūhi yatsyātsudurllabham \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. “O Candra of good holy rites, I am pleased with you. Do choose your boon. Do tell me what wish of yours shall I fulfill even if it be very difficult to acquire.”

## \|\| 1.22.31 \|\|

*evaṃ pratyakṣamāpannaṃ dṛṣṭvā devaṃ vṛṣadhvajam \|*  
*praṇamya taṃ yathābhaktyā stutiṃ cakre niśākaraḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. On seeing that Bull-emblemed Lord has come within the ken of his vision, Niśākara (Candra) devoutly bowed down and eulogized.

## \|\| 1.22.32 \|\|

*caṃdra uvāca \|*  
*oṃ namo devadevāya śivāya paramātmane \|*  
*aprameyasvarūpāya byaktāvyaktasvarūpiṇe \|\| 32 \|\|*

Candra said:

32\. Om, obeisance to Śiva, the Lord of Devas, the supreme soul, the Lord whose form and features cannot be comprehended. Obeisance to the Lord whose form is both manifest and unmanifest.

## \|\| 1.22.33 \|\|

*tvaṃ patiryogināmīśa tvayi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*tvaṃ yajñastvaṃ vaṣaṭkārastvamoṃkāraḥ prajāpatiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Supreme God! You are the Lord of Yogins. Everything is well-established in you. You are Yajña. You are Vaṣaṭkāra. You are Oṃkāra and Prajāpati (patriarch).

## \|\| 1.22.34 \|\|

*caturviṃśatyadhikaṃ ca bhuvanānāṃ śatadvayam \|*  
*tasyopari paraṃ jyotirjāgarti tava kevalam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. There are two hundred twenty-four Bhuvanas (worlds). Above them the supreme refulgence of yours solely shines and keeps vigil.

## \|\| 1.22.35 \|\|

*kalpāṃta ādivārāhamuktabrahmāṃḍasaṃsthitau \|*  
*ādhārastaṃbhabhūtāya tejoliṃgāya te namaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Obeisance to thy refulgent Liṅga that became the pillar of support to the Cosmic Egg when, at the conclusion of the Kalpa, the primordial Varāha deserted it.

## \|\| 1.22.36 \|\|

*namo'nāmayanāmne te namaste kṛttivāsase \|*  
*namo bhairavanāthāya namaḥ someśvarāya te \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Obeisance to you having the name Anāmaya. Obeisance to Kṛttivāsas. Obeisance to Bhairavanātha. Obeisance to you, Someśvara.

## \|\| 1.22.37 \|\|

*iti saṃjñābhiretābhiḥ stutyābhiramṛteśvaraḥ \|*  
*bhūtairbhavyairbhaviṣyaiśca stūyase surasattamaiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. You Amṛteśvara are eulogized by excellent Suras of the past, present and future, through these names worthy of being eulogized.

## \|\| 1.22.38 \|\|

*ādyo viraṃcināmābhūdbrahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*mṛtyuñjayeti te nāma tadā'bhūtpārvatīpate \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. When there was the first Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds called by the name Virañci, O Consort of Pārvatī, your name was Mṛtyuñjaya.

## \|\| 1.22.39 \|\|

*dvitīyo'bhūdyadā brahmā padmabhūriti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*tadā kālāgnirudreti tava nāma prakīrtitam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. When the second Brahmā became well-known as Padmabhū, your name had been glorified as Kālāgnirudra.

## \|\| 1.22.40 \|\|

*tṛtīyo'bhūdyadā brahmā svayaṃbhūriti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*amṛteśeti te nāma kīrtitaṃ kīrtivarddhanam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. When the third Brahmā became well-known as Svayaṃbhū, your name was glorified as Amṛteśa, a name causing enhancement of glory.

## \|\| 1.22.41 \|\|

*caturtho'bhūdyadā brahmā parameṣṭhīti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*anāmayeti deveśa tava nāma smṛtaṃ tadā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. When the fourth Brahmā became well-known as Parameṣṭhin, O Lord of Devas, your name had been remembered as Anāmaya.

## \|\| 1.22.42 \|\|

*paṃcamo'bhūdyadā brahmā surajyeṣṭha iti śrutaḥ \|*  
*kṛttivāseti te nāma babhūva tripurāṃtaka \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. When the fifth Brahmā became known as Surajyeṣṭha, O destroyer of Tripura, your name was Kṛttivāsas.

## \|\| 1.22.43 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭhaścābhūdyadā brahmā hemagarbha iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tadā bhairavanātheti tava nāma prakīrtitam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. When the sixth Brahmā was remembered as Hemagarbha, your name was glorified as Bhairavanātha.

## \|\| 1.22.44-45 \|\|

*adhunā varttate yo'sau śatānaṃda iti śrutaḥ \|*  
*ādisomena yaścāsau vāmanetrodbhavena te \|\| 44 \|\|*

*pratiṣṭhārthaṃ tu liṃgasya ānītaścāṣṭavārṣikaḥ \|*  
*bālarūpī tadā tena somanātheti kīrtitam \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. Now the Brahmā who is present is known as Śatānanda. The Ādisoma (primordial Soma) who originated from your left eye brought that Brahmā when he was eight years old, in order to install your Liṅga. He was in the form of a boy. Hence your name is glorified as Somanātha.

## \|\| 1.22.46 \|\|

*tadāprabhṛti somānāṃ lakṣāṇāṃ dvitayaṃ gatam \|*  
*sahasradvitayaṃ caiva śataṃ caiva ṣaḍuttaram \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Since then two Lakh two thousand one hundred six Somas have come and gone.

## \|\| 1.22.47 \|\|

*saptamo'haṃ mahādeva ātreya iti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*prācetasena dakṣeṇa śaptastvāṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*rakṣa māṃ devadeveśa kṣayiṇaṃ pāparogiṇam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O Mahādeva, I am the seventh and am well-known as Ātreya. Being cursed by Dakṣa, the son of Pracetas, I seek refuge in you. O Lord of the chiefs of Devas, protect me suffering from the fell disease Phthysis.

## \|\| 1.22.48 \|\|

*iti saṃstuvatastasya caṃdrasya karuṇākaraḥ \|*  
*tutoṣa bhagavānrudro vākyaṃ cedamuvāca ha \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. As Candra eulogized thus, the compassionate Lord Rudra became pleased and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.22.49 \|\|

*parituṣṭo'smi te caṃdra varaṃ varaya suvrata \|*  
*ki te kāmaṃ karomyadya brūhi yatsyātsudurllabham \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. “O Candra of good holy rites, I am pleased with you. Choose you boon. What wish of yours shall I fulfill? Tell me, even if it be very difficult to acquire.

## \|\| 1.22.50 \|\|

*mama nāmāni guhyāni mama priyatarāṇi ca \|*  
*paṭhiṣyaṃti narā ye tu dāsye teṣāṃ manogatam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. These secret names of mine are dear to me. I will grant everything mentally cherished by those men who recite these.

## \|\| 1.22.51 \|\|

*atītā ye caṃdramaso bhaviṣyaṃti ca ye'dhunā \|*  
*teṣāṃ pūjyamidaṃ liṃgaṃ yāvadanyo'ṣṭavārṣikaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. In the 'case of Candras of the past and future, this Liṅga shall be worthy of being adored till another Brahmā of eight years arrives.

## \|\| 1.22.52 \|\|

*āḥ paraṃ caturvaktro brahmā yo bhavitā yadā \|*  
*prāṇanātheti devasya tadā nāma bhaviṣyati \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Henceforth, the four-faced Brahmā will be born; the name of the God will be Prāṇanātha then.

## \|\| 1.22.53 \|\|

*prāṇāstu vāyavaḥ proktāstadārādhananāma tat \|*  
*prāṇanātheti saṃproktaṃ me'dhunā tadbhaviṣyati \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Winds are called by the name Prāṇa. The name for the sake of propitiation is called Prāṇanātha. That will be my name now.

## \|\| 1.22.54-56 \|\|

*tasmādagnīśanāmeti kālarudretyanaṃtaram \|*  
*tāraketi tato nāma bhaviṣyatyeva kīrtitam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*mṛtyuñjayeti devasya bhavitā tadanaṃtaram \|*  
*tryaṃbakeśastvitīśeti bhuvaneśetyanantaram \|\| 55 \|\|*

*bhūtanātheti ghoreti brahmeśetyatha nāmakam \|*  
*bhaviṣyaṃ pṛthivīśeti ādināthetyanaṃtaram \|\| 56 \|\|*

54-56. Thereafter, these names will be used: Agnīśa, Kālarudra, Tāraka, Mṛtyuñjaya, Tryaṃbakeśa, Īśa, Bhuvaneśa, Bhūtanātha, Ghora, Brahmeśa, Pṛthvīśa and Ādinātha.

## \|\| 1.22.57 \|\|

*kalpeśvareti devasya caṃdranāthetyanantaram \|*  
*nāma devasya yadbhāvi sāṃprataṃ te prakāśitam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Then the Lord will have the names Kalpeśvara and Candranātha. The future names of the Lord have now been revealed.

## \|\| 1.22.58 \|\|

*ityevamādi nāmāni svasaṃkhyātāni ṣoḍaśa \|*  
*gatāni saṃbhaviṣyaṃti kālasyānaṃtabhāvataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. These and other names have been self-reckoned as sixteen. Those that have gone by will be revived, since infiniteness is the nature of Time.

## \|\| 1.22.59 \|\|

*ekaikaṃ vartate nāma brahmaṇaḥ pralayāvadhi \|*  
*tatonyajjāyate nāma yathā nāmānurūpataḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Each of the names continues to exist till the dissolution of Brahmā. Then another name crops up befittingly.

## \|\| 1.22.60 \|\|

*atha kiṃ bahunoktena rahasyaṃ te prakāśitam \|*  
*vatsa yatkāraṇeneha tapastaptaṃ tvayā'khilam \|*  
*tanme niḥśeṣato brūhi dāsye tuṣṭo'smi te varam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Of what avail is much talk? The secret has been revealed to you. O dear one, tell me entirely the purpose for which all this penance has been undertaken by you. I am pleased with you. I shall grant you the boon.”

## \|\| 1.22.61 \|\|

*candra uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ śaptastu dakṣeṇa kasmiṃścitkāraṇāṃtare \|*  
*yakṣmaṇā ca kṣayaṃ nītastasmāttvaṃ trātumarhasi \|\| 61 \|\|*

Candra said:

61\. I have been cursed by Dakṣa for some reason. I have been reduced in size through Phthysis. It behoves you to save me therefrom.

## \|\| 1.22.62 \|\|

*śaṃbhuruvāca \|*  
*adhunā bhoḥ samaṃ paśya sarvāstā dakṣakanyakāḥ \|*
