*kṣayaste bhavitā pakṣaṃ pakṣaṃ vṛddhirbhaviṣyati \|\| 62 \|\|*

Śaṃbhu said:

62\. Now, do look upon all the daughters of Dakṣa impartially. Reduction in your size is inevitable per fortnight. There will be waxing in the next fortnight.

## \|\| 1.22.63-64 \|\|

*pūrvocitāṃ prabhāṃ soma prāpsyase matprasādataḥ \|*  
*prācetasasya dakṣasya tapasā hatapāpmanaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tasyānyathā vacaḥ kartuṃ śakyaṃ nānyaiḥ surairapi \|*  
*brāhmaṇāḥ kupitā hanyurbhasmīkuryuḥ svatejasā \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. O Soma, with my favour, you will regain the lustre as it was previously. It is impossible to alter the utterance of Dakṣa, the son of Pracetas, the Brāhmaṇa whose sins have been destroyed by penance. No one else, not even Suras can alter his utterance. If infuriated Brāhmaṇas may kill, may reduce one to ashes by the power of their own refulgence.

## \|\| 1.22.65 \|\|

*devānkuryuradevāṃśca nāśayeyuridaṃ jagat \|*  
*brāhmaṇāścaiva devāśca teja ekaṃ dvidhā kṛtam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. They can reduce Devas to the position of non-Devas. They can destroy this universe. Brāhmaṇas and Devas constitute one mass of refulgence split into two.

## \|\| 1.22.66 \|\|

*pratyakṣaṃ brāhmaṇā devāḥ parokṣaṃ divi devatāḥ \|*  
*na vinā brāhmaṇā devairna devā brāhmaṇairvinā \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Brāhmaṇas are Devas, the perceptible (ones) in the world. Devas are invisible and are present in heaven. Without Devas Brāhmaṇas are non-entities; without Brāhmaṇas Devas are non-entities.

## \|\| 1.22.67 \|\|

*ekatra mantrā stiṣṭhanti teja ekatra tiṣṭhati \|*  
*brāhmaṇā devatā loke brāhmaṇā divi devatāḥ \|*  
*trailokye brāhmaṇāḥ śreṣṭhā brāhmaṇā eva kāraṇam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Mantras are present on one side. Refulgence is present on the other. Brāhmaṇas are deities in the world. Brāhmaṇas are Devatās in heaven. Brāhmaṇas are the most excellent ones in all the three worlds. Brāhmaṇas alone are the cause (of wefare \[welfare?\]).

## \|\| 1.22.68 \|\|

*piturniyuktāḥ pitaro bhavaṃti kriyāsu daivīṣu bhavaṃti devāḥ \|*  
*dvijottamā hastaniṣaktatoyāstenaiva dehena bhavaṃti devāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Excellent Brāhmaṇas employed in the holy rites of Pitṛs, become Pitṛs and if they are engaged in the rites of Devas, they become Devas. With the water sprinkled with their palms, the excellent Brāhmaṇas become Devas.

## \|\| 1.22.69 \|\|

*ṣaṭka rmatattvābhirateṣu nityaṃ vipreṣu vedārthakutūhaleṣu \|*  
*na teṣu bhaktyā praviśaṃti ghoraṃ mahābhayaṃ pretabhavaṃ kadācit \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The great fear and danger arising from Pretas (ghosts) do not assail Brāhmaṇas interested in the Vedic themes and engaged in the Ṣaṭkarmas (six duties of a Brāhmaṇa) due to their devotion to them.

## \|\| 1.22.70 \|\|

*yadbrāhmaṇāḥ stutyatamā vadanti taddevatā karmabhirācaraṃti \|*  
*tuṣṭeṣu tuṣṭāḥ satataṃ bhavanti pratyakṣadeveṣu parokṣadevāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Devas translate into real actions what highly praise worthy, Brāhmaṇas speak. When the perceptible (visible) Devas (Brāhmaṇas) are pleased the invisible Devas too always become pleased.

## \|\| 1.22.71 \|\|

*yathā rudrā yathā devā maruto vasavo'śvinau \|*  
*brahmā ca somasūryau ca tathā loke dvijottamāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The excellent Brāhmaṇas in the world are on a par with Rudras, Devas, Maruts, Vasus, Aśvins, Brahmā, Soma and Sūrya.

## \|\| 1.22.72 \|\|

*devādhīnāḥ prajāḥ sarvā yajñādhīnāśca devatāḥ \|*  
*te yajñā brāhmaṇādhīnāstasmāddevā dvijottamāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. All the subjects (people) are dependent on Devas; all the Devas are dependent on Yajñas. Those Yajñas are dependent on Brāhmaṇas. Hence the excellent Brāhmaṇas are Devas.

## \|\| 1.22.73 \|\|

*brāhmaṇānarcayennityaṃ brāhmaṇāṃstarpayetsadā \|*  
*brāhmaṇāstārakā loke brāhmaṇātsvargamaśnute \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. One should always adore Brāhmaṇas. One should propitiate Brāhmaṇas always. Brāhmaṇas are the redeemers in the world. One enjoys heavenly pleasures through Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.22.74 \|\|

*abhedyamacchedyamanādimakṣayaṃ vidhiṃ purāṇaṃ paripālayanti \|*  
*mahāmatistānabhipūjya vai dvijānbhavedajeyo divi devarāḍiva \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Brāhmaṇas guard and protect the ancient religious tradition that cannot be broken or cut off, that is beginningless and endless. A highly sensible man adores Brāhmaṇas and becomes invincible like the king of Devas in heaven.

## \|\| 1.22.75 \|\|

*śakyaṃ hi kavacaṃ bhettuṃ nārācena śareṇa vā \|*  
*api vajra sahasreṇa brāhmaṇāśīḥ sudurbhidā \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. An armour can be pierced through by a Nārāca (an iron dart or an arrow). But the Brāhmaṇical benediction cannot be split even by a thousand Vajras (thunderbolts).

## \|\| 1.22.76 \|\|

*hutena śāmyate pāpaṃ hutamannena śāmyati \|*  
*annaṃ hiraṇyadānena hiraṇyaṃ brāhmaṇāśiṣā \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. A sin is quelled by Homa. Food subdues Homa. Food is subdued by the gift of gold and gold is subdued by the blessings of Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.22.77 \|\|

*ya icchennarakaṃ gaṃtuṃ saputrapaśubāṃdhava \|*  
*deveṣvadhikṛtaṃ kuryādbrāhmaṇeṣu ca goṣu ca \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. If one wishes to go to hell along with his sons, cattle and kinsmen, one should assert undue authority over Devas, Brāhmaṇas and cows.

## \|\| 1.22.78 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāndveṣṭi yo mohāddevāngāśca makhānyadi \|*  
*naiva tasya paro loko nā'yaṃ loko durātmanaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. If due to delusion, a wicked-hearted person cherishes hatred for Brāhmaṇas, Devas, cows and Yajñas, he shall never attain the other worlds or even this world.

## \|\| 1.22.79 \|\|

*anindyā brāhmaṇā gāvaḥ kāṃcanaṃ salilaṃ striyaḥ \|*  
*pṛthivī tu ṣaḍetāni yo nindati sa pātakī \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Brāhmaṇas, cows, gold, water, women and the earth do not deserve to be censured. He who reviles these, is a sinner.

## \|\| 1.22.80 \|\|

*agraṃ dharmasya rājāno mūlaṃ dharmasya brāhmaṇāḥ \|*  
*tasmānmūlaṃ na hiṃsīta mūle hyagraṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Kings are the top of righteousness (Dharma) and Brāhmaṇas are the roots thereof. Hence one shall not injure the root. The top stands on the root.

## \|\| 1.22.81 \|\|

*phalaṃ dharmasya rājānaḥ puṣpaṃ dharmasya brāhmaṇāḥ \|*  
*tasmātpuṣpaṃ na hiṃsīta puṣpātsaṃjāyate phalam \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Kings are the fruit of Dharma and Brāhmaṇas are the flowers thereof. Hence one should not harm the flower. It is from flower that fruit grows.

## \|\| 1.22.82 \|\|

*rājā vṛkṣo brāhmaṇāstasya mūlaṃ paurāḥ parṇaṃ mantriṇastasya śākhāḥ \|*  
*tasmādrājñā brāhmaṇā rakṣaṇīyā mūle gupte nāsti vṛkṣasya nāśaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. King is a tree of which Brāhmaṇas are the roots. Citizens are the leaves. Ministers are its branches. Hence Brāhmaṇas should be protected by king. If root is protected tree is not destroyed.

## \|\| 1.22.83 \|\|

*āsanno hi dahatyagnirdūrāddahati brāhmaṇaḥ \|*  
*prarohatyagninā dagdhaṃ brahmadagdhaṃ na rohati \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Indeed fire bums when it is in close contact, but Brāhmaṇas burn from afar (by curse). What is burned by fire may grow again but what is burnt by Brāhmaṇas never grows.

## \|\| 1.22.84 \|\|

*brāhmaṇānāṃ ca śāpena sarvabhakṣo hutāśanaḥ \|*  
*samudraścāpyapeyastu viphalaśca puraṃdaraḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Hutāśana (Fire-god) became Sarvabhakṣa (omnivorous) due to the curse of Brāhmaṇas, so also the ocean became Apeya (water of which was not worthy of being drunk) and Purandara became Viphala (impotent).

## \|\| 1.22.85 \|\|

*tvaṃ candra rājayakṣmī ca pṛthivyāmūṣarāṇi ca \|*  
*sūryācandramasoḥ pātaḥ punaruddharaṇaṃ tayoḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. O Candra, you became afflicted with Phthysis. Unfertile arid lands abound on the earth. There occurred fall of sun and moon again and there is redemption (for them).

## \|\| 1.22.86-87 \|\|

*vanaspatīnāṃ niryāso dānavānāṃ parājayaḥ \|*  
*nāgānāṃ ca vaśīkāraḥ kṣatrasyotsādanaṃ tathā \|*  
*devotpatti viparyāso lokānāṃ ca viparyayaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*evamādīni tejāṃsi brāhmaṇānāṃ mahātmanām \|*  
*tasmādvipreṣu nṛpatiḥ praṇamennityameva ca \|\| 87 \|\|*

86-87 The exudation of juice (sap) from vegetation, defeat of Dānavas, subjugation of elephants, the extermination of Kṣattriyas, origin and death of Devas and upheavel of the world: These and other things constitute the refulgence of the noble-souled Brāhmaṇas. Hence a king should always bow down to Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.22.88 \|\|

*parā mapyāpadaṃ prāpto brāhmaṇānna prakopayet \|*  
*te hyenaṃ kupitā hanyuḥ sadyaḥ sabalavāhanam \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. (A king) may be in the greatest of adversities. Yet he should not infuriate Brāhmaṇas. If infuriated they may kill him along with his army and vehicles.

## \|\| 1.22.89 \|\|

*praṇītaścāpraṇītaśca yathāgnirdaivataṃ mahat \|*  
*evaṃ vidvānavidvānvā brāhmaṇo daivataṃ mahat \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Fire may or may not be consecrated with prayers. Yet it is a great deity. So also whether learned or not, a Brāhmaṇa is a great deity.

## \|\| 1.22.90 \|\|

*śmaśāneṣvapi tejasvī pāvako naiva duṣyati \|*  
*hūyamānaśca yajñeṣu bhūya evābhivarddhate \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Refulgent fire is not defiled even in cremation ground. Fire in which Homa is performed blazes all the more in the course of Yajñas.

## \|\| 1.22.91 \|\|

*evaṃ yadyapya niṣṭeṣu varttate sarvakarmasu \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ brāhmaṇaḥ pūjyo daivataṃ paramaṃ mahat \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. In the same manner, a Brāhmaṇa may be engaged in all undesirable activities. Yet he is worthy of being adored by all. He is a great deity.

## \|\| 1.22.92 \|\|

*kṣatrasyātipravṛddhasya brāhmaṇānāṃ prabhāvataḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṃ hi paramaṃ pūjyaṃ kṣatraṃ hi brahmasaṃbhavam \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. A Kṣatriya greatly flourishes through the power of Brāhmaṇas. The Brāhmaṇical power is extremely adorable. Indeed the Kṣatriya’s valour arises from that of Brāhmaṇa (power).

## \|\| 1.22.93 \|\|

*adbhyo'gnirbrahmataḥ kṣatramaśmano lohamutthitam \|*  
*teṣāṃ sarvatragaṃ tejaḥ svāsu yoniṣu śāmyati \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Fire originates from water; Kṣetra from Brahmā; steel from rock. The refulgence of these, which spreads everywhere gets dissolved in their respective sources.

## \|\| 1.22.94 \|\|

*yānsamāśritya tiṣṭhanti devalokāśca sarvadā \|*  
*brahmaiva vacanaṃ yeṣāṃ ko hiṃsyāttāñjijīviṣuḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. What person desirous of remaining alive can dare to assail (Brāhmaṇas) on whose support Devas and the worlds stand up and whose words are the Vedas?

## \|\| 1.22.95 \|\|

*mriyamāṇo'pyādadīta na rājā brāhmaṇātkaram \|*  
*na ca kṣudhā 'sya saṃsīdedbrāhmaṇo viṣaye vasan \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. A king shall not levy and exact tax from a Brāhmaṇa even when he is faced by death. A Brāhmaṇa residing in his realm should not (be allowed to) languish due to hunger.

## \|\| 1.22.96 \|\|

*yasya rājñaśca viṣaye brāhmaṇaḥ sīdati kṣudhā \|*  
*tasya tacchatadhā rāṣṭramacirādeva sīdati \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. If in the realm of any king, a Brāhmaṇa languishes due to hunger, ere long his entire kingdom splits into a hundred parts and faces annihilation.

## \|\| 1.22.97 \|\|

*yadrājā kurute pāpaṃ pramādādyacca vibhramāt \|*  
*vasanto brāhmaṇā rāṣṭre śrotriyāḥ śamayanti tat \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Brāhmaṇas well-versed in the Vedas staying in the realm of a king, suppress the sin a king commits due to inadvertence or delusion.

## \|\| 1.22.98 \|\|

*pūrvarātrāṃtarātreṣu dvijairyasya vidhīyate \|*  
*sa rājā saha rāṣṭreṇa vardhate brahmatejasā \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. If holy rites (of Agnihotra etc.) are duly performed by Brāhmaṇas in the beginning of a day or at the close thereof, that king flourishes along with the entire kingdom, as a result of the Brāhmaṇical splendour.

## \|\| 1.22.99 \|\|

*brāhmaṇānpūjayennityaṃ prātarutthāya bhūmipaḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇānāṃ prasādena dīvyanti divi devatāḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Everyday a king should get up early in the morning and adore Brāhmaṇas. It is by the favour of Brāhmaṇas that Devas shine in heaven.

## \|\| 1.22.100 \|\|

*atha kiṃ bahunoktena brāhmaṇā māmakī tanuḥ \|*  
*ye kecitsāgarāṃtāyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ kīrtitā dvijāḥ \|*  
*tadūpaṃ devadevasya śivasya paramātmanaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Of what avail is much talk? Brāhmaṇas constitute my person. The form of the Lord of Devas, Śiva the supreme soul, is glorified on the earth girdled by the ocean, as Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.22.101 \|\|

*etāndviṣaṃti ye mūḍhā brāhmaṇānsaṃśitavratān \|*  
*te māṃ dviṣaṃti vai nūnaṃ pūjanātpūjayanti mām \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. The foolish ones who hate these Brāhmaṇas of praiseworthy holy rites indeed hate me. Through worshipping them, they adore me.

## \|\| 1.22.102 \|\|

*na pradveṣastataḥ kāryo brāhmaṇeṣu vijānatā \|*  
*pradveṣeṇāśu naśyanti brahmaśāpahatā narāḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. Hence no sensible man should dare to hate Brāhmaṇas. Men struck down by the curse of Brāhmaṇas perish instantly by hating them.

## \|\| 1.22.103 \|\|

*ityevaṃ kathitaścandra brāhmaṇānāṃ guṇārṇavaḥ \|*  
*kuruṣvānantaraṃ kāryyaṃ yadbravīmyahameva te \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Thus, O Candra, the ocean-like expanse of the good qualities of Brāhmaṇas has been expounded to you. Carry out the subsequent work I am going to tell you.

## \|\| 1.22.104 \|\|

*śāpasyānugraho datto mayā tava niśākara \|*  
*na cānyathā vacaḥ karttuṃ śakyaṃ teṣāṃ drijanmanām \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. O Niśākara (creator of night), I give you protection from the curse. The utterance of those Brāhmaṇas cannot be altered.

## \|\| 1.22.105 \|\|

*śāpānugrahadaiḥ sarvai devairapi savāsavaiḥ \|*  
*tasmāccandra tvayā śoko naiva kāryo vijānatā \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. All Devas including Vāsava may be able to curse or bless but they cannot alter the words of Brāhmaṇas. Hence, O Candra, you are sensible enough not to grieve over this.

## \|\| 1.22.106 \|\|

*kṣayaste bhavitā pakṣaṃ pakṣaṃ vṛddhirbhaviṣyati \|*  
*athānyadvacanaṃ candra śṛṇu kāryaṃ yathā tvayā \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Your waning is inevitable during a fortnight but during the other fortnight you will wax. Listen, O Candra, to another task to be carried out by you.

## \|\| 1.22.107 \|\|

*idaṃ yatsāgaropāṃte tiṣṭhate liṃgamuttamam \|*  
*dharāmadhyagataṃ tacca devānāṃ dṛṣṭigocaram \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. This excellent Liṅga that is present near the ocean is in the centre of the earth. It is not in the range of the vision of Devas.

## \|\| 1.22.108 \|\|

*kukkuṭāṃḍasamaprakhyaṃ sarpamekhalamaṃḍitam \|*  
*mamādyaṃ paramaṃ tejo na cānyo veda kaścana \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. It has the size of a hen’s egg. It is adorned by serpentine girdle. It has the refulgence similar to that of hen’s egg. It is my primordial refulgence. No one else knows it.

## \|\| 1.22.109 \|\|

*itaḥ sāgaramadhye tu dhanuṣāṃ ca śatatraye \|*  
*tiṣṭhate tatra liṃgaṃ tu suguptaṃ lakṣaṇānvitam \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. But away from this side, in the centre of the ocean, within a distance of three hundred Dhanus, there stands (another) Liṅga endowed with all characteristics and well-guarded.

## \|\| 1.22.110 \|\|

*ādikalpe maharṣīṇāṃ śāpena patitaṃ mama \|*  
*liṃgaṃ sāgaramadhye tu tattvaṃ śīghraṃ samānaya \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. In the first Kalpa, due to the curse of the great sages, my Liṅga (Penis) fell into the ocean. Do bring it quickly.

## \|\| 1.22.111-112 \|\|

*sparśākhyaṃ yatra me liṃgaṃ tatra sthāne niveśaya \|*  
*niveśya tu prayatnena sahito viśvakarmaṇā \|\| 111 \|\|*

*tato brahmāṇamāhūya sametaṃ tu munīśvaraiḥ \|*  
*pratiṣṭhāṃ kāraya vibho iṣṭvā tatra mahāmakhaiḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

111-112. O Lord, summon Brahmā along with the leading sages. Make him perform great Makhas after placing it on my Liṅga called Sparśa (Touch) with effort in the company of Viśvakarman and cause the installation.

## \|\| 1.22.113 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa bhagavāṃstatraivāṃtaradhīyata \|*  
*tataḥ prabhāṃ punarlebhe rātrinātho varānane \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. After saying thus, the Lord vanished there itself. Then, O lady of excellent countenance, the Lord of night regained his refulgence.

## \|\| 1.22.114 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti tatkṣetraṃ prabhāsamiti viśrutam \|*  
*niṣprabhasya prabhā dattā prabhāsaṃ tena cocyate \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. Thereafter that holy spot became well- known as Prabhāsa. Refulgence was given to one (who was) without lustre. Hence it is called Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.22.115 \|\|

*dakṣasya tu vṛthā śāpo na kṛtastena lāṃchanam \|*  
*somaḥ prabhāsate lokānvaraṃ prāpya maheśvarāt \|*  
*vyaktībhūtaḥ sa deveśaḥ somasyaiva mahātmanaḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. Nor was the curse of Dakṣa in vain. There is the stigma. Soma illuminates the worlds after receiving the boon from Maheśvara. That Lord of Devas became manifest only to Soma, the noble-souled one.

## Chapter 23 - Installation of Someśvara (Soma-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.23.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tataḥ śāṃtamanā bhūtvā caṃdramā vismayānvitaḥ \|*  
*śaṃbhubhaktyā parītātmā prabhāsakṣetramāsthitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*pūrvoktaṃ yattu devena sa tathā kṛtavānvibhuḥ \|*  
*gatvā sāgaramadhye tu gṛhītvā liṃgamuttamam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*viśvakarmmāṇamāhūya sahitaṃ paricārakaiḥ \|*  
*ādideśa svayaṃ somastvaṣṭāraṃ devaśilpinam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Although surprised, Candramas retained his mental calmness. With devotion to Śaṃbhu filling his soul, he reached and stayed at Prabhāsa Kṣetra.

Vidhu (Moon-god) duly carried out what he had been told earlier by the Lord. He went to the interior of the ocean and picked up the excellent Liṅga. Summoning Viśvakarman along with his attendants, Soma ordered Tvaṣṭṛ, the divine architect.

## \|\| 1.23.4 \|\|

*caṃdra uvāca \|*  
*viśvakarmannidaṃ liṃgaṃ mama dattaṃ tu śaṃbhunā \|*  
*gṛhāṇa tvaṃ mahābāho yuktasthāne niveśaya \|\| 4 \|\|*

Candra said:

4\. O Viśvakarman, this Liṅga has been given to me by Śaṃbhu. Take this, O mighty one, and install it at a proper spot.

## \|\| 1.23.5 \|\|

*rakṣasva tāvadgantāsmi svakīyaṃ bhavanaṃ vibho \|*  
*yajñārthamānayiṣyāmi yajñopakaraṇāni ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Guard this, O Lord, I am going to my abode. I shall bring in the meanwhile all the requisites for the Yajña.

## \|\| 1.23.6-9 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā ca tadā caṃdraścaṃdra lokaṃ jagāma ha \|*  
*gatvā tatra mahādevi caṃdralokaṃmahāprabham \|\| 6 \|\|*

*koṭiyojanavistīrṇaṃ sadāmṛtamayaṃ śubham \|*  
*tatrāhūya mahādevi pratīhāraṃ sumedhasam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*maṃtriṇaṃ hemagarbhāṃgaṃ bṛhaspatisamaṃ dhiyā \|*  
*yajñopaskarasaṃbhāraṃ sarvamādāya satvarāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*prabhāsakṣetraṃ gacchaṃtu mamādeśaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*sāgnibhirbrāhmaṇaiḥ sārddhaṃ gacchaṃtu kṣetramuttamam \|\| 9 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

6-9. After saying this, Candra went to Candraloka. It is highly refulgent and extends to a crore of Yojanas. It is splendid and full of nectar always. O great goddess, he summoned the porter Sumedhas and the minister Hemagarbhāṅga who was on a par with Bṛhāspati in intellect, and ordered him: “Gather together everything necessary for a Yajña and hasten to Prabhāsa Kṣetra at my bidding. You should be accompanied by Brāhmaṇas with the sacred fires when you go to the excellent holy spot.

## \|\| 1.23.10-12 \|\|

*śīghraṃ saṃpādyatāṃ sarvaṃ yathā yajñaḥ pravartate \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva viprāṇāṃ caṃdralokanivāsinām \|\| 10 \|\|*

*pṛthakpṛthagvimānaṃ tu deyaṃ teṣāṃ mahādhanam \|*  
*gavāṃ ca daśalakṣāṇāṃ savatsānāṃ payomucām \|\| 11 \|\|*

*hemabhārairbhūṣitānāṃ kāmadhenūpamatviṣām \|*  
*aśvānāṃ śyāmakarṇānāṃ sapādaṃ lakṣameva ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. Gather everything together quickly so that the Yajña can be initiated duly. Send separate aerial chariots to everyone of the Brāhmaṇas residing in Candraloka. Ample wealth should be distributed among them. One million cows should be given along with their calves. Their lustre should be that of Kāmadhenu. They shall be bedecked with a Bhāra (weight) of gold. They must yield plenty of milk. Send one and one fourth million horses with black ears.

## \|\| 1.23.13 \|\|

*daṃtināmayutaṃ caiva ghaṃṭābharaṇaśobhitam \|*  
*sahasrāṇi ca catvāri rathānāṃ vātaraṃhasām \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. There should be ten thousand elephants fully resplendent with ornaments and bells. There should be four thousand chariots having the speed of wind.

## \|\| 1.23.14 \|\|

*lakṣaṃ tu karabhāṇāṃ ca maṇimāṇikyasaṃyutam \|*  
*sainyānāṃ koṭirekā tu caturaṃgabalānvitā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. There should be a hundred thousand camels laden with jewels and rubies. Ten million armies each consisting of four divisions should be sent.

## \|\| 1.23.15 \|\|

*agniśaucāni vastrāṇi brāhmaṇārthaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*vibhūṣaṇāni divyāni ṛtvigarthaṃ śubhāni ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. For the Brāhmaṇas, there should be garments as pure as the sacred fire. For the Ṛtviks, there should be splendid divine ornaments.

## \|\| 1.23.16 \|\|

*nānābhakṣyāṇi bhojyāni pānāni vividhāni ca \|*  
*lakṣaṃ karmakarāṇāṃ tu dāsīnāṃ lakṣameva ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Different kinds of articles of food and edibles and various kinds of beverages should be kept ready. There should be a hundred thousand servants and the same number of maid servants.

## \|\| 1.23.17 \|\|

*dāruvaṃśāvadhi proktaṃ yatkiṃcitsvaṃ madājñayā \|*  
*anyadyadbrāhmaṇā brūyustatsarvaṃ tatra nīyatām \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Whatever money is set apart for wooden pieces etc. as per my order and other things the Brāhmaṇas may ask for, should be brought there.

## \|\| 1.23.18-19 \|\|

*devānāṃ dānavānāṃ tu yakṣagaṃdharvarakṣa sām \|*  
*saptadvīpakṣitīśānāṃ saptapātālavāsinām \|\| 18 \|\|*

*nānānṛpasahasrāṇāṃ ghoṣaṇā kriyatāṃ muhuḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ ghoṣaṇā kāryā prabhāsāgamanaṃ prati \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Let there be a general proclamation inviting Devas, Dānavas, Yakṣas, Gandharvas, Rākṣasas staying in the seven Pātāla worlds, Kings of the seven continents, thousands of kings elsewhere. Let there be repeated announcements requesting the people to come to Prabhāsa.”

## \|\| 1.23.20 \|\|

*ityuktvā maṃtriṇaṃ tatra caṃdramāstvarayā'nvitaḥ \|*  
*brahmalokaṃ sa gatavānyajñārthaṃ brahmaṇoṃtikam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After saying thus to the minister, Candramas hurriedly went to Brahmaloka to the presence of Brahmā, for the purpose of Yajña.

## \|\| 1.23.21 \|\|

*so'pi caṃdramaso maṃtrī hemagarbho mahāprabhaḥ \|*  
*somājñāṃ śirasā kṛtvā yajñasaṃbhārasaṃbhṛtaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Hemagarbha, the highly refulgent minister of Candramas, took the command of Soma earnestly with his head bowed down and gathered the requisites for the Yajña.

## \|\| 1.23.22 \|\|

*prabhāsaṃ kṣetramāgatya yajñārthaṃ yatnavānabhūt \|*  
*tathaiva cāhvayāṃcakre bhūrbhuvaḥsvarnivāsinaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. He duly arrived at Prabhāsa and engaged himself in making provisions and arrangement for the Yajña. He invited all the residents of Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ and Svaḥ (Lokas).

## \|\| 1.23.23-24 \|\|

*śrutvā tu ghoṣaṇāṃ sarve śīghraṃ tatra samāyayuḥ \|*  
*raviyojanaparyaṃtaṃ kṣetramālokya tatra tat \|\| 23 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇāṃśca samāhūya somādhyakṣaṃ uvāca tān \|*  
*yajñāṃgaṃ sarvamānītaṃ mayā somājñayā dvijāḥ \|*  
*anaṃtaraṃ tu yatkṛtyaṃ bhavadbhistadvidhīyatām \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. On hearing the invitation, all of them hastened to that place. Surveying the entire holy spot extending to twelve Yojanas, the minister of Soma addressed the Brāhmaṇas: “O Brāhmaṇas, all the ancillaries of the Yajñas have been brought here at the behest of Soma. What should be done next may be carried out by you venerable ones.”

## \|\| 1.23.25 \|\|

*ityuktā brāhmaṇāḥ sarve taponirdhūtakalmaṣāḥ \|*  
*tatraiva dadṛśuḥ sarve tvaṣṭāraṃ devaśilpinam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On being told thus, all the Brāhmaṇas who had rid themselves of the sins through penance met Tvaṣṭṛ, the divine architect, there itself.

## \|\| 1.23.26 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā tu dvijāḥ sarve liṃgaṃ dṛṣṭvā samīpataḥ \|*  
*kathametaditi procurviśvakarmanbravīhi naḥ \|*  
*kasmādatra sthitastvaṃ vai śilpikoṭisamanvitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. On seeing him and the Liṅga too nearby, those Brāhmaṇas said: “How is this, O Viśvakarman, tell us. Why are you present here with a crores of other artisans?”

## \|\| 1.23.27 \|\|

*viśvakarmmovāca \|*  
*ahaṃ somaniyuktastu yukto'smi liṃgarakṣaṇe \|*  
*tadājñāpālane yatnaḥ kriyate'to mayā dvijāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

Viśvakarman said:

27\. I have been commanded by Soma and so am engaged in guarding this Liṅga. Due effort is being done by me to carry out his command, O Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.23.28 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ śrutvā yadā viprā jñātvā sarvaṃ tu kāraṇam \|*  
*caritā yajñakāryārthaṃ tataścakrurupa kramam \|\| 28 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

28\. On hearing this, the Brāhmaṇas understood the real purpose. Then they were glad and began the necessary preliminary rites of the Yajña.

## \|\| 1.23.29 \|\|

*tatra yojanaparyaṃtaṃ devānāṃ yajanaṃ śubham \|*  
*taddevayajanaṃ kṛtvā patnīśālāṃ ca cakrire \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The splendid place of sacrifice unto the Devas (Devayajana) extended to a Yojana. After making the Devayajana they made the Patnīśālā (chamber of the honoured wives of Yajamānas) ready.

## \|\| 1.23.30 \|\|

*havirddhānaṃ sadaścaiva uttarā vedireva ca \|*  
*brahmaṇaḥ sadanāgnīdhrītyevaṃ sthānāni cakrire \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. They made ready all the parts of the sacrificial chamber such as Havirdhāna, Sadas, Uttarā Vedī, the abode of Brahmā and Agnidhri.

## \|\| 1.23.31 \|\|

*tatra yojanaparyaṃtaṃ yajñayūpāṃśca maṃḍapān \|*  
*viśvakarmā cakārāśu kuṃḍāni vividhāni ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Viśvakarman erected Yūpas (sacrificial posts) in various places over a distance of a Yojana. Maṇḍapas (pavilions) and various kinds of Kuṇḍas were made.

## \|\| 1.23.32-35 \|\|

*sahasrasaṃkhyayā tatra kuṇḍānāṃ maṃḍapāvadhi \|*  
*tatra te brāhmaṇāḥ sarve pratiṣṭhāyajñakovidāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*nānābharaṇaratnaiśca brāhmaṇāḥ samalaṃkṛtāḥ \|*  
*cakruḥ sarve yathanyāyaṃ śāstraṃ dṛṣṭvā punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*vṛkṣāṃstathauṣadhīrdivyā samitpuṣpakuśādikān \|*  
*homadravyādikaṃ sarva mājyaṃ prājyaṃ navaṃ payaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tathānyadapi yatkiṃcidyajñopakaraṇaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*varddhanīkalaśādyaṃ ca sarvaṃ hemamayaṃ śubham \|\| 35 \|\|*

32-35. There were thousands of Kundas \[Kuṇḍas?\] to the end of the Maṇḍapas. All the Brāhmaṇas were experts in the rites of installation and Yajñas.

They were adorned with various kinds of ornaments. They referred to the scriptural texts frequently and performed the rites duly.

Trees, divine medicinal herbs, sacrificial twigs, flowers, Darbha grass, ingredients for Homa, plenty of ghee and fresh milk and all other requisite things for the purpose of Yajña were kept ready. Vardhanīkalaśa and other utensils were of gold and were auspicious.

## \|\| 1.23.36 \|\|

*cakruḥ sarvaṃ yathānyāyaṃ pratiṣṭhāmakhamādṛtāḥ \|*  
*tatra vipragaṇo hṛṣṭo bhakṣyabhojyāditarpitaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Groups of Brāhmaṇas performed the holy Yajña of the installation duly. They were duly fed and honoured. They were delighted by the various kinds of foodstuffs.

## \|\| 1.23.37 \|\|

*vedadhvanitanirghoṣairdivaṃ bhūmiṃ ca saṃspṛśan \|*  
*suśubhe maṃḍapastatra patākābhiralaṃkṛtaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The sounds of the chanting of the Vedic Mantras touched heaven and earth. The Maṇḍapa decorated with banners shone well.

## \|\| 1.23.38 \|\|

*divyasiṃhāsanopeto muktādāmapariṣkṛtaḥ \|*  
*divyacandanamālābhiḥ kalpapallavatoraṇaiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. There were divine thrones in the Maṇḍapa. Pearl strings, divine sandal garlands and festoons of the sprouts of Kalpa trees added to its beauty.

## \|\| 1.23.39 \|\|

*divyagandha sugandhādyaiḥ svargasthānamivābhavat \|*  
*caturdaśavidhastatra bhūtagrāmaḥ samāgataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Scents of celestial fragrance transformed it into a heavenly place. Fourteen kinds of Bhūtagrāma (living beings) had arrived there.

## \|\| 1.23.40-42 \|\|

*sthāvaraḥ sarpajātiśca pakṣijātistathaiva ca \|*  
*mṛgasaṃjñaścaturthaśca paśvākhyaḥ pañcamaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭhaśca mānuṣaḥ proktaḥ paiśācaḥ saptamaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭamo rākṣasaḥ prokto navamo yajña eva ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

*gāṃdharvaśākrasaumyāśca prājāpatyastathaiva ca \|*  
*brāhmaśceti samākhyātaścaturdaśavidho gaṇaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

40-42. Sthāvara (stationary beings), reptiles like those of serpent class, classes of birds, the fourth group of Mṛgas (deer etc.) the fifth one called Paśus (beasts), human beings constituting the sixth group, Paiśāca (ghosts) making up the seventh, the eighth one mentioned as Rākṣasas, the ninth group that of Yakṣas and the other groups in the fourteen referred to before, being Gandharvas, Gaṇas called Śākras, Saumyas, Prājāpatyas and the Brahma group (had arrived).

## \|\| 1.23.43 \|\|

*viśvedevāstathā sādhyā maruto vasavastathā \|*  
*lokapālāstathāṣṭau ca nakṣatrāṇi grahaiḥ saha \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. There were Viśvedevas, Sādhyas, Maruts, Vasus, the eight Guardians of the Quarters and the Constellations along with the Planets.

## \|\| 1.23.44 \|\|

*brahmāṇḍe devatā yāśca tāḥ sarvāstatra cāgatāḥ \|*  
*hṛṣṭāḥ prabhāsake kṣetre prārabdhe yajñakarmmaṇi \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. When the Yajña rite started at the Prabhāsaka Kṣetra all the Devas present in the whole Cosmic Egg had arrived there.

## \|\| 1.23.45 \|\|

*ghṛtakṣīravahā nadyo dadhipāyasakardamāḥ \|*  
*pakvānnānāṃ phalānāṃ ca rāśayaḥ parvatopamāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Rivers of ghee and milk flowed there. Curds and milk puddings constituted veritable quagmires there. Heaps of cooked food and fruits resembled mountains.

## \|\| 1.23.46 \|\|

*dṛśyante vividhākārāstasminyajñamahotsave \|*  
*jagu statraiva gandharvā nanṛtuścāpsarogaṇāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Various such heaps were seen in the place where the great festivity of the Yajña took place. The Gandharvas sang and the groups of celestial damsels danced.

## \|\| 1.23.47 \|\|

*bhakṣyabhojyaiśca vividhaiḥ kāmapānādibhistathā \|*  
*tṛptā devāśca munayo bhūtagrāmāścaturdaśa \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The Devas, the sages and the fourteen types of Bhūtas (Beings) were fully satisfied with the different kinds of edibles and foodstuffs and beverages etc. as desired by them.

## \|\| 1.23.48 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃbhārasahitaṃ yajñāṃgaṃ sarvameva hi \|*  
*praguṇīkṛtya sacivo muktvā tatraiva rakṣakān \|*  
*somasyāhvānanārthaṃ ca brahmalokaṃ jagāma ha \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. After having got together all the requisites for the Yajña, the minister (of Soma), appointing guards (for protecting) there itself, went to Brahmaloka to call Soma.

## \|\| 1.23.49-52 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*sa dṛṣṭvā brahmaṇaḥ pārśve sthitaṃ somamahāprabham \|*  
*praṇamya daṇḍavadbhūmau somaṃ brahmāṇameva ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

*kṛtāṃjalipuṭo bhūtvā uvāca natakaṃdharaḥ \|*  
*hemagarbha uvāca \|*  
*bhagavanbhavadādeśādyajñāṃgaṃ sarvameva hi \|\| 50 \|\|*

*tatra prābhāsike kṣetre mayā te praguṇīkṛtam \|*  
*tatra brahmarṣayaḥ sarve tathā rājarṣayo'pare \|\| 51 \|\|*

*tvanmārgaprekṣakāḥ sarve santiṣṭhante samākulāḥ \|*  
*anantaraṃ tu yatkṛtyaṃ tadbhavānkartumarhati \|\| 52 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

49-52. He saw the highly refulgent Soma standing by the side of Brahmā. He prostrated on the ground like a log of wood before Soma and Brahmā. With palms joined in reverence and bending down his neck (head) he spoke:

## \|\| 1.23.53 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*ityuktastu tadā candraḥ samudrasya sutena vai \|*  
*prahasyovāca brahmāṇaṃ candramā lokasākṣiṇam \|\| 53 \|\|*

Hemagarbha said:

O holy Sir, at your behest the entire requisites for the Yajña have been collected together at the Prābhāsika Kṣetra by me. All the Brāhmaṇa-sages and the saintly kings are awaiting your arrival with great eagerness. It behoves you to carry out what should be done henceforth.

Īśvara said:

53\. On being requested thus by the son of Samudra (i.e. Hemagarbha) Candra smiled and spoke to Brahmā, the witness unto all the worlds:

## \|\| 1.23.54 \|\|

*bhagavansarvadeveśa mamānugrahakāmyayā \|*  
*pratiṣṭhāyajñakāmasya mamātithyaṃ kuru prabho \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. “O Lord, O Lord of all the Devas, be pleased to accept my hospitality with a desire to bless me. I am desirous of performing the Yajña of installation (of the Liṅga).

## \|\| 1.23.55 \|\|

*adya me saphalaṃ janma saphalaṃ ca tapaḥ prabho \|*  
*devatvamadya me brahmaṃstvatprasādādbhaviṣyati \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Today my birth has become fruitful, O Lord, and my penance has borne fruit. O Brahmā, with your favour, I will attain Deva-hood today.

## \|\| 1.23.56 \|\|

*mayā ca tapasogreṇa prāptaṃ liṃgamumāpateḥ \|*  
*tatpratiṣṭhāvidhiṃ sarvaṃ tadbhavānkarttumarhati \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. With a very severe penance I have obtained this Liṅga of the Consort of Umā. It behoves you to perform the installation thereof.”

## \|\| 1.23.57 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*avaśyaṃ tava karttāsmi pratiṣṭhāṃ śaṃkarātmikām \|*  
*tvadārādhanaliṃge tu someśe'tiviśeṣataḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

57\. Certainly I will perform the installation ceremony of Śaṅkara in the Someśa Liṅga which you have to propitiate with special emphasis.

## \|\| 1.23.58 \|\|

*ye kecidbhavitāro vā atītā ye niśākarāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ somānvayānāṃ ca sarveṣāmādyadaivatam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. It is the primordial deity of all belonging to the family of Soma, of all Niśākaras (Moon-gods) whether they be bygones or are yet to be born.

## \|\| 1.23.59 \|\|

*yo'sau someśvaro deva ādau bhairavanāmabhṛt \|*  
*manvantarāntare'tīte pratiṣṭhe'haṃ punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. This Lord Someśvara bore the name Bhairava at the beginning, in the other Manvantara that has elapsed. I (shall) install it again and again (in every Manvantara).

## \|\| 1.23.60-61 \|\|

*yadā prābhāsikaṃ kṣetre gato'haṃ cāṣṭavārṣikaḥ \|*  
*āhūtaḥ pūrvamindreṇa bhairavasya pratiṣṭhite \|\| 60 \|\|*

*tatprabhṛtyeva me nāma bālarūpī nigadyate \|*  
*anyeṣu sarvatīrtheṣu vṛddharūpī vasāmyaham \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. When I went to the Prābhāsika Kṣetra, I was eight years old. I had been invited by Indra earlier for the purpose of the installation of Bhairava. My name is being mentioned as “Bālarūpin” since then. In all other Tīrthas I remain in the form of an elderly person.

## \|\| 1.23.62-63 \|\|

*prabhāse tu punaścaṃdra bālyāprabhṛti saṃvase \|*  
*brahmāṇḍe yāni tīrthāni brāhmaṇāsteṣu ye smṛtāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*teṣāmādyo niśānātha prabhāse'haṃ vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*kalpekalpe niśānātha mama nāmāṃtaraṃ bhavet \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. But, O Candra, I stay in Prabhāsa ever since my childhood. I am the first among all the Brāhmaṇas in the Tīrthas all over the Brahmāṇḍa. I am well established at Prabhāsa. In every Kalpa I get a new name.

## \|\| 1.23.64 \|\|

*svayaṃbhūḥ prathame nāma dvitīye padmabhūḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tṛtīye viśvakartteti bālarūpī turīyake \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The name in the first Kalpa was Svayaṃbhū. In the second I am remembered as Padmabhū. In the third I am remembered as Viśvakartṛ and in the fourth as Bālarūpī.

## \|\| 1.23.65 \|\|

*eṣāmeva parīvarto nāmnāṃ bhāvi punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*parārddhadvayaparyaṃtaṃ prabhāse saṃsthitasya me \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. There has been a repetition of these names again and again for two Parārdhas I settled in Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.23.66 \|\|

*ādisomena tatraiva śaṃbhornetrodbhavena vai \|*  
*prabhāse tu tapastaptvā pratyakṣīkṛtaīśvaraḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. It was there that the primordial Soma, arising from the eye of Śaṃbhu, performed penance in Prabhāsa and saw Īśvara directly.

## \|\| 1.23.67-69 \|\|

*tato dadau varaṃ tuṣṭaḥ pūrvacandrasya śūladhṛk \|*  
*yasmādārādhito'haṃ te soma bhaktyā cirantanam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*tasmātsomeśanāmaivamasmiṃlliṃge bhaviṣyati \|*  
*yāvadbrahmā śatānandaḥ prakṛtau na pralīyate \|\| 68 \|\|*

*ye kecidbhavitāro vai rātrināthā niśākarāḥ \|*  
*te madārādhanaṃ cātra kariṣyaṃti punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

67-69. Thereupon the delighted Trident-bearing Lord granted boon to the Full Moon: “O Soma, since I have been propitiated for a long time by you devoutly, so this Liṅga will be named Someśa. All the Moons who are yet to be born until Brahmā named Śatānanda is dissolved (dies) will repeatedly adore and propitiate me here.”

## \|\| 1.23.70 \|\|

*ityuktvā bhagavāñchaṃbhustatraivāṃtaradhīyata \|*  
*tasminkāle mayā soma ādyaṃ liṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. After saying this Lord Śaṃbhu vanished there itself. O Soma, the first Liṅga was installed by me then.

## \|\| 1.23.71 \|\|

*tadāprabhṛti somānāṃ lakṣāṇāṃ dvitayaṃ gatam \|*  
*sahasradvitayaṃ caiva śataṃ caikaṃ ṣaḍuttaram \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Ever since then two lakh two thousand one hundred six Somas have gone by.

## \|\| 1.23.72 \|\|

*saptamastvaṃ mahāvāho varttase soma sāṃpratam \|*  
*etāvantyeva liṃgāni pratiṣṭhāṃ prāpitāni me \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. You are the seventh (202107th), O mighty one, O Soma now. As many Liṅgas too have been installed by me.

## \|\| 1.23.73 \|\|

*eṣa evādhunā so'haṃ tadārādhanajaṃ phalam \|*  
*pratiṣṭhātāsmi bhadraṃ te soma kṛtya mamaiva tat \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. (I am enjoying) the benefit arising from his propitiation. Welfare unto you, O Soma. This is my duty. I shall install (the Liṅga).

## \|\| 1.23.74-78 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā bhagavānbrahmā vedavidyāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*sarvadevamayo devaiḥ sahitastīrthasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*sanatkumārapramukhai ryogīndrairṛṣibhiḥ saha \|*  
*bṛhaspatiṃ samāhūya puraskṛtya purodhasam \|\| 75 \|\|*

*haṃsayānaṃ samāruhya koṭibrahmarṣibhiḥ saha \|*  
*āgataḥ somarājena tadā brahmā jagatpatiḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*prābhāsike mahātīrthe yatra dāruvanaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*ṛṣitoyā nadī yatra mahāpātakanāśinī \|\| 77 \|\|*

*asmiṃstīrthe prabhāse tu brahmabhāgaḥ sa ucyate \|*  
*tridaivatamidaṃ kṣetraṃ mayā te kathitaṃ priye \|\| 78 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

74-78. After saying this, Lord Brahmā identical with all the Devas, equipped with all lores and accompanied by the Devas and Tīrthas summoned Bṛhaspati, the Purodhas. He was accompanied by the leading Yogins and sages, the chief of whom is Sanatkumāra, and also a crore of Brahmarṣis. He rode on his vehicle of Haṃsa (Swan). Thus Brahmā, the Lord of the Universe, came to the Prābhāsika Tīrtha along with Somarāja. In this Prābhāsika Tīrtha the region where there is Dāruvana grove as well as the river Ṛṣitoyā, the destroyer of great sins, is called Brahmabhāga. O my beloved, it has already been mentioned by me that this Kṣetra has three deities.

## \|\| 1.23.79 \|\|

*tatrāgatva caturvaktro brāhmabhāge'tinirmale \|*  
*munīnākārayāmāsa unnata sthānavāsinaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. The Four-faced One came to Brahmabhāga, the purest portion, and invited the sages residing in higher regions.

## \|\| 1.23.80 \|\|

*āyāṃtaṃ vedhasaṃ dṛṣṭvā devarṣigurusaṃyutam \|*  
*te sarve pūjayāmāsuḥ saṃstavairvedasaṃmitaiḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. On seeing Vedhas (Brahmā) coming in the company of celestial sages and the preceptor, all of them honoured and adored him through prayers on a par with the Vedic passages.

## \|\| 1.23.81-84 \|\|

*athovāca dvijānsarvānbrahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*ciramārādhya somena someśaṃ pāpanāśanam \|\| 81 \|\|*

*tasminprasanne somena labdhaṃ liṅgamanuttamam \|*  
*pratiṣṭhārthaṃ tu devasya āyātā dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*yathā mayā sadā kāryā pratiṣṭhā śaṃkarātmikā \|*  
*bhavadbhiḥ parikāryā sā mama bhāgasamāśrayaiḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*yataḥ kopena bhavatāṃ liṃgaṃ prapatitaṃ bhuvi \|*  
*pratiṣṭhā tasya kartavyā yuṣmābhirvai na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

81-84. Then Brahmā, the grandfather of all the worlds, spoke to all those Brāhmaṇas: “Someśa, the destroyer of sins, was propitiated by Soma for a long time. When he was pleased the excellent Liṅga was obtained by Soma. O excellent Brāhmaṇas we have come here for the sake of the installation of the Lord. Just as the installation ceremony of Śaṅkara should be performed always by me, the ancillary service should be performed by you all who have resorted to my Bhāga (portion of the Kṣetra). Since the Liṅga (Penis) fell on to the ground due to your anger, the installation also should be performed by you. There is no doubt about this.”

## \|\| 1.23.85-86 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*gṛhītvā'tha munīnsarvānbrahmā lokapitā mahaḥ \|*  
*ānītaḥ somarājena tadā brahmā jagatpatiḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*prābhāsike mahātīrthe sāvitryā sahitaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*kārayāmāsa kuṇḍānāṃ maṇḍapānāṃ śataṃśatam \|\| 86 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

85-86. Somarāja brought Brahmā, the Lord of the universe, to the great Prābhāsika Tīrtha along with Sāvitrī and all the sages. Lord Brahmā then erected a hundred Maṇḍapas and caused a hundred Kuṇḍas to be dug.

## \|\| 1.23.87 \|\|

*ekaike maṇḍape tatra cakre saptadaśartvijaḥ \|*  
*guruṇā prerito brahmā tatra devapurodhasā \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Directed by Guru (Bṛhaspati), the priest of Devas, Brahmā assigned seventeen Ṛtviks to each of the Maṇḍapas.

## \|\| 1.23.88 \|\|

*pārśve sthitastadā brahmā vidhānairveda bhāṣitaiḥ \|*  
*dīkṣayāmāsa somaṃ tu rohiṇyā sahitaṃ vibhum \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Standing by the side, Brahmā initiated Lord Soma accompanied by Rohiṇī, in accordance with the injunctions laid down in the Vedic passages.

## \|\| 1.23.89 \|\|

*patnīṃ ca rohiṇīṃ kṛtvā sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyutām \|*  
*mṛgacarmadharāṃ devīṃ kṣaumavastrāvaguṃṭhitā m \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Rohiṇī who had all the (auspicious) characteristic features was given the due place of Patnī (sacrificer’s wife). The fair lady wore deerskin and covered her face with a silken cloth.

## \|\| 1.23.90 \|\|

*patnīśālāṃ samānītā ṛtvigbhirvedapāragaiḥ \|*  
*caṃdramā dīkṣayā yukta ṛṣigaṃdharvasaṃstutaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. She was brought to the Patnīśālā (chamber of the sacrificer’s wife) by the Ṛtviks who were the masters of the Vedas. Candramas who had been duly initiated, was eulogized by the sages and Gandharvas.

## \|\| 1.23.91 \|\|

*auduṃbareṇa daṃḍena saṃvṛto mṛgacarmaṇā \|*  
*atīva tejasā yuktaḥ śuśubhe sadasi sthitaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. He was clad in deerskin and he held an Uduṃbara, staff. In the middle of the Assembly he shone with excessive refulgence.

## \|\| 1.23.92 \|\|

*tato brahmā mahādevi sarvalokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*ṛtvijāṃ varaṇaṃ cakre vedoktavidhinā tadā \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Then, O great goddess, Brahmā, the grandfather of all the worlds, performed the rite of Ṛtvigvaraṇa (formally selecting the Ṛtviks for starting their work) in the manner it has been enjoined in the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.23.93 \|\|

*gururhotā vṛtastatra vasiṣṭho'dhvaryureva ca \|*  
*tatrodgātā marīcistu brahmatve nāradaḥ kṛtaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Guru (Bṛhaspati) was selected as the Hotṛ there, Vasiṣṭha as Adhvaryu, Marīci as Udgātṛ and Nārada was placed in the position of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.23.94-95 \|\|

*sanatkumārasaṃyuktāḥ sadasyāstatra vai kṛtāḥ \|*  
*vastrairābharaṇairyuktā mukuṭairaṃgulīyakaiḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*bhūṣitā bhūṣaṇaughena tasminyajñe tadartvijaḥ \|*  
*caturṣu tajjñāścatvāra evaṃ te ṣoḍaśartvijaḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

94-95. Sanatkumāra and others connected with him were made the Sadasyas. They were bedecked in good garments and ornaments such as crowns, rings etc. The Ṛtviks were adorned with many ornaments in the course of that Yajña. In each of the four entrances there were four Ṛtviks. Thus there were sixteen Ṛtviks.

## \|\| 1.23.96 \|\|

*prastotā kaśyapastatra pratihartā tu gālavaḥ \|*  
*subrahmaṇyastathā gargaḥ sadasyaḥ pulahaḥ kṛtaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Kaśyapa was the Prastotṛ there and Gālava the Pratihartṛ. Garga was Subrahmaṇya and Pulaha was made Sadasya.

## \|\| 1.23.97 \|\|

*hotā śukraḥ samākhyāto neṣṭā kratha udāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*maitrāvaruṇo durvāsā brāhmaṇācchaṃsī kauśikaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Śukra was named Hotṛ. Kratha was cited as Neṣṭṛ. Durvāsas, Maitrāvaruṇa, and Kauśika were Brāhmaṇācchaṃsī.

## \|\| 1.23.98 \|\|

*acchāvākaśca śākalyo grāvasthaḥ kratureva ca \|*  
*prasthātā pratipūrvo yaḥ śālaṃkāyana eva ca \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Śākalya was Acchāvāka, Kratu was Grāvastha, Śālaṅkāyana was Pratiprasthātṛ.

## \|\| 1.23.99-100 \|\|

*agnīdhraśca manustatra unnetā tvaṃgirāḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*evamādyānmaṇḍapeṣu kṛtvā tānṛtvijaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

*anyeṣu maṇḍapeṣveva pratyekamṛtvijaḥ kṛtāḥ \|*  
*maṇḍapānāṃ śateṣveva kṛtvā kuṇḍānyakalpayat \|\| 100 \|\|*

99-100. Manu was Agnīdhra; Aṅgiras was made the Unnetṛ. The Lord thus made these the Ṛtviks in the Maṇḍapas. In the other Maṇḍapas too there were Ṛtviks similarly. After arranging thus in all the hundred Maṇḍapas, he caused the Kuṇḍas (to be prepared).

## \|\| 1.23.101 \|\|

*ekaiko maṇḍapastatra viṃśahastapramāṇataḥ \|*  
*astreṇāśodhya bhūmiṃ tu paṃcagavyena prokṣya ca \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Each one of the Maṇḍapas was twenty Hastas in dimension. The ground was sprinkled with Pañcagavya after duly cleansing it with Astra Mantra.

## \|\| 1.23.102 \|\|

*carmaṇā cāvaguṃṭhyaiva ālikhyāstreṇa pārvati \|*  
*ullikhya prokṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā khātaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. O Pārvatī, the ground was covered with the sacred Carman (leather), the rites of Ālekhana and Ullekhana (scratching and engraving) were performed with Astra Mantra. Then water was sprinkled and the digging was performed duly.

## \|\| 1.23.103 \|\|

*aṣṭau kuṃḍāni saṃkalpya tathaikamaṇḍape priye \|*  
*lepanaṃ maṇḍape kṛtvā vajrākaraṇameva ca \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. O my beloved, for each Maṇḍapa eight Kuṇḍas were assigned. The Maṇḍapa was duly plastered and Vajrākaraṇa (making the ground firm like thunderbolt) was performed.

## \|\| 1.23.104 \|\|

*caturasrakārmukaṃ ca vartulaṃ kamalākṛti \|*  
*pūrvāṃ diśaṃ samā rabhya kṛtvā tāni prayatnataḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. The shapes of the Kuṇḍas beginning with that in the east, were square, bow-like, circular and lotus-like.

## \|\| 1.23.105-107 \|\|

*catuḥkoṇasamāyuktaṃ pūrve kuṇḍaṃ niveśya tu \|*  
*bhagākṛti tathā'gneyyāṃ dakṣiṇe dhanurākṛti \|\| 105 \|\|*

*nairṛtye tu trikoṇaṃ vai vartulaṃ paścimena tu \|*  
*ṣaṭkoṇaṃ caiva vāyavye padmākāraṃ tathottare \|\| 106 \|\|*

*aiśānyāmaṣṭakoṇaṃ tu madhye caikaṃ vidhā nataḥ \|*  
*pratyekaṃ maṇḍapaṃ śubhraṃ stambhaiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiryutam \|\| 107 \|\|*

105-107. The square-shaped Kuṇḍa was in the east. That in the shape of Bhaga (vagina) was in the south-east, that in the shape of a bow was in the south, the triangular one in the south-west, the circular one was in the west, the hexagonal one in the north-west, the lotus-like one was in the north, the octagonal one was in the north-east. In the centre one was made in accordance with the injunction. Everyone of the Maṇḍapas was splendid with sixteen pillars.

## \|\| 1.23.108-110 \|\|

*dhvajaiḥ satoraṇairyuktaṃ cakre brahmā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*nyagrodhaṃ pūrvato nyasya dakṣe coduṃbaraṃ tathā \|\| 108 \|\|*

*aśvatthaṃ paścime caiva palāśaṃ cottare kramāt \|*  
*bāhudaṃḍapramāṇena dhvajāṃstatra niveśya vai \|\| 109 \|\|*

*aindryādau pītavarṇādi patākā parikalpitāḥ \|*  
*tato brahmā hyagnikuṃḍe cāgnisthāpanamārabhat \|\| 110 \|\|*

108-110. Banners and festoons were put up by Brahmā in accordance with the injunctions. The pillar of Nyagrodha tree was placed in the east, that of Uduṃbara in the south, Aśvattha in the west and Palāśa in the north. He fixed the banners in accordance with the length of the staff. A yellow-coloured banner was fixed in the east. (In the other quarters banners were of other colours.) Then Brahmā began the Agnisthāpana (installing or placing-sacred fires) rite in the Kuṇḍa.

## \|\| 1.23.111-115 \|\|

*svasthāne brāhmaṇāṃścaiva jāpye caiva nyayojayat \|*  
*śrīsūktaṃ pāvamānaṃ ca sadā caiva ca vājinam \|\| 111 \|\|*

*vṛṣākapiṃ tathaindraṃ ca bahvṛcaḥ pūrvato'japan \|*  
*rudrānpuruṣasūktaṃ ca krokādhyāyaṃ ca vaikriyam \|\| 112 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇaṃ paitryamaiṃdraṃ ca japeranyajuṣo yame \|*  
*devavrataṃ vāmadevyaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ sāma rathaṃtaram \|\| 113 \|\|*

*bheruṃḍāni ca sāmāni cchaṃdogaḥ paścime'japat \|*  
*atharvātharvaśirasaṃ skambhastaṃbhamatharvaṇam \|\| 114 \|\|*

*nīlarudramatharvāṇamatharvā cottare'japat \|*  
*garbhādhānādikaṃ sarvaṃ tato'gnerakarodvibhuḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

111-115. (Brāhmaṇas belonging to different Vedas were made to recite certain Sūktas of their respective Vedas as follows.) He made the Brāhmaṇas sit in their respective places and employed them in the utterance of Jāpya. In the east the Ṛgvedins recited Śrīsukta, Pāvamāna, Vājina, Vṛṣākapi and Aindra Sūktas. In the south the Yajuṣas (Yajurvedins) performed the Japa of Rudra Mantra, Puruṣasūkta, Krokādhyāya, Vaikriya, Brāhmaṇa, Paitrya and Aindra. The Chandogas (Sāmavedins) performed the Japa of the following in the west: Devavrata, Vāmadevya, Jyeṣṭha Sāman, Rathantara and Bheruṇḍa Sāmans. In the north the Atharvā (Brāhmaṇa of Atharva Śākhā) performed the Japa of Atharvaśiras, Skaṃbhastaṃbha, Nīlarudra etc. Then the Lord performed Garbhādhāna and other rites of Agni (Fire-god).

## \|\| 1.23.116-117 \|\|

*pūrṇāhutiṃ tato dattvā snānakarma tathā'rabhat \|*  
*paṃcapallavasaṃyuktaṃ mṛttikābhiḥ samanvitam \|\| 116 \|\|*

*kaṣāyaiḥ paṃcagavyaiśca paṃcāmṛtaphalaistathā \|*  
*tīrthodakaiḥ sametaṃ tu maṃtraiḥ snānamathārabhat \|\| 117 \|\|*

116-117. After the offering of the Pūrṇāhuti the rites for the holy ablution were begun. The waters from the Tīrthas were brought along with Pañcapallavas (sprouts of five specific trees), lumps of clay, Kaṣāyas, Pañcagavyas and the five Amṛtaphalas. With the utterance of the Mantras, the ablution started.

## \|\| 1.23.118-121 \|\|

*netrāṇyutpādya devasya kṛtvā ca tilakakriyām \|*  
*pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni pātāle ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

*svarga loke ca yānyeva tatra tānyāyayustadā \|*  
*etasminnantare brahmā devānāṃ paśyatāṃ tadā \|\| 119 \|\|*

*bhūmiṃ bhittvā viveśātha tatra liṃgamapaśyata \|*  
*sparśākhyaṃ taṃ tu saṃchādya madhunā darbhamūlakaiḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

*tatra brahmaśilāṃ nyasya tasyā ūrdhvaṃ mahāprabham \|*  
*liṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhayāmāsa kṛtvā niścalamā tmavān \|\| 121 \|\|*

118-121. Eyes were fixed to the deity and the sacred Tilaka mark was put. He caused all the Tīrthas on the earth, Pātāla and Svargaloka to be brought. In the meantime, even as the Devas were watching Brahmā pierced the ground and entered the bowels (of the earth). There he saw the Liṅga called Sparśa (i.e. Tactile? Liṅga) which he covered with roots of Darbha grass and poured honey over. Above it he placed the Brahmaśilā. Over that he installed highly refulgent Liṅga and made it firmly stable. The self-possessed Lord made it fixed.

## \|\| 1.23.122 \|\|

*sthitvā ca parame tattve maṃtranyāsamathākarot \|*  
*evaṃ liṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya tatra brahmā jagadguruḥ \|*  
*pūjayāmāsa vidhinā vedoktairmaṃtra vistaraiḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. Stationing (i.e. concentrating himself in the Supreme principle) he performed the Nyāsa rite with the Mantras. After installing the Liṅga thus, Brahmā, the preceptor of the universe, performed the adoration rite by means of elaborate Vedic Mantras.

## \|\| 1.23.123 \|\|

*mantranyāse kṛte tatra brahmaṇā lokakartṝṇā \|*  
*tatra vipragaṇo hṛṣṭo jayaśabdādimaṃgalaiḥ \|*  
*nirdhūmaścābhavadvahniḥ sūryakoṭisamaprabhaḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. When the Nyāsa rite with Mantras was performed by Brahmā, the creator of the worlds, the groups of Brāhmaṇas became delighted. They hailed with words “Be Victorious” and other auspicious sounds, The fire became smokeless and it had the refulgence of crore of Suns.

## \|\| 1.23.124 \|\|

*devadundubhayo neduḥ prasannāśca digīśvarāḥ \|*  
*puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ papātoccaistasminyajñamahotsave \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. In the great festivity of the sacrifice divine Dundubhi drums were beaten. The quarters and their Guardians became pleased. There was a shower of flowers.

## \|\| 1.23.125 \|\|

*pratiṣṭhāpya tato liṃgaṃ śrīsomeśaṃ pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*dāpayāmāsa viprebhyo bhūriśo yajñadakṣiṇām \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. After the installation ceremony of Śrīsomeśa the grandfather (Brahmā) caused plenty of Yajña Dakṣiṇā to be distributed among the Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.23.126 \|\|

*sanatkumārapramukhairādyairbrahmarṣibhirvṛtaḥ \|*  
*dakṣiṇāmadadātsomastrīṃllokānbrahmaṇe purā \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. Surrounded by the ancient Brahmarṣis, the chief of whom was Sanatkumāra, Soma gave the three worlds to Brahmā as Dakṣiṇā.

## \|\| 1.23.127 \|\|

*tebhyo brahmarṣimukhyebhyaḥ sadasyebhyastathaiva ca \|*  
*dadau hiraṇyaṃ ratnāni koṭiśo bhūridakṣiṇāḥ \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. Crores of gold pieces, jewels and plenty of cash presents were given to the Sadasyas (members of the sacrificial assembly) and principal Brahmarṣis.

## \|\| 1.23.128 \|\|

*sobhiṣikto mahātejāḥ sarvairbrahmarṣibhistataḥ \|*  
*trīṃllokānbhāvayāmāsa svabhāsā bhāsatāṃ varaḥ \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. After being crowned by all the Brahmarṣis, the most excellent one among the luminaries, illuminated the three worlds with his refulgence. He was endowed with excessive brilliance.

## \|\| 1.23.129 \|\|

*taṃ sinī ca kuhūścaiva dyutiḥ puṣṭiḥ prabhā vasuḥ \|*  
*kīrttirdhṛtiśca lakṣmīśca nava devyaḥ siṣevire \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. Nine goddesses viz Sinī, Kuhū, Dyuti, Puṣṭi, Prabhā, Vasu, Kīrti, Dhṛti and Lakṣmī served him.

## \|\| 1.23.130 \|\|

*prāpyāvabhṛthamavyagraḥ kṛtvā māheśvaraṃ makham \|*  
*kṛtārthaḥ paripūrṇaśca saṃbabhūva niśāpatiḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. The unperturbed Lord of the Night had his valedictory bath after the celebration of the Māheśvara Makha. He attained fullness and perfection and had his objects achieved.

## \|\| 1.23.131 \|\|

*tatastasmai dadau rājyaṃ prājyaṃ brahmā pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*bījauṣadhīnāṃ viprāṇāmavannānāṃ ca varānane \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. Thereafter, O lady of excellent countenance, Brahmā, the grandfather, gave him the flourishing kingdom of seeds (of plants), medicinal herbs, Brāhmaṇas and cooked food.

## \|\| 1.23.132 \|\|

*tasminyajñe samājagmurye kecitpṛthivīśvarāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ rājyaṃ dhanaṃ bhogāndadau svargaṃ tathā'kṣayam \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. To those kings who were present in that Yajña, he gave wealth, enjoyment of pleasures and everlasting Svarga,

## \|\| 1.23.133 \|\|

*brāhmaṇānbhojayāmāsa svayamevauṣadhīpatiḥ \|*  
*dadau sarvaṃ tadā teṣāṃ prabhāsakṣetravāsinām \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. The Lord of medicinal herbs himself fed the Brāhmaṇas and gave everything unto those who resided in Prabhāsa Kṣetra.

## \|\| 1.23.134 \|\|

*hiraṇyādīnyadāccaiva mahādānāni ṣoḍaśa \|*  
*yo yadarthayate tatra sāmānyaḥ prākṛto janaḥ \|*  
*nijakarmānusāreṇa sa lebhe ca tadeva hi \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. He made the great sixteen Dānas beginning with gold. Even an ordinary person, an uncultured rustic, got whatever he requested for according to his fate (past actions).

## \|\| 1.23.135 \|\|

*evaṃ samarthite yajñe sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ \|*  
*sthāpayitvā tu liṃgāni jagmuḥ sarve yathāgatam \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. After the accomplishment of the Yajña, Devas along with Indra installed their own Liṅgas and went the way they came.

## \|\| 1.23.136-137 \|\|

*candramāstu punardevi brahmaṇā sahito vibhuḥ \|*  
*liṃgamārādhayāmāsa prabhāse pāpanāśane \|\| 136 \|\|*

*trikālaṃ pūjayāmāsa dhūpamālyānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*taṃ praṇamya ca deveśi stauti nityaṃ niśāpatiḥ \|\| 137 \|\|*

136-137. O goddess, Lord Candramas in the company of Brahmā, once again propitiated the Liṅga in Prabhāsa which quells all sins. Thrice a day he adored it with incense, garlands and unguents. O goddess of Devas, the Lord of the night bowed down to and eulogized the Lord.

## Chapter 24 - Importance of Somavāra Vrata

## \|\| 1.24.1 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*kasminkāle jagannātha tatra liṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*kathamārādhanaṃ cakre kṛtārtho rohiṇīpatiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

The Devī said:

1\. O Lord of the universe, at what time was the Liṅga installed? How did the contented Consort of Rohiṇī continue the propitiation?

## \|\| 1.24.2-5 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tretāyuge ca daśame manorvaivasvatasya hi \|*  
*saṃjāto rohiṇīnātho yukto durvāsasā priye \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tasminkāle tadā tatra gate varṣasahasrake \|*  
*tataḥ kṛtvā tapaścāyaṃ pratyakṣīkṛtaśaṃkaraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*liṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhayāmāsa brahmaṇā lokakartṝṇā \|*  
*punarvarṣasahasraṃ tu pūjayāmāsa śaṃkaram \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tataḥ saṃpūjya vidhinā nijakāryārthasiddhaye \|*  
*stutiṃ cakre niśānāthaḥ pratyakṣīkṛtaśaṃkaraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

2-5. In the course of the Manvantara of Vaivasvata Manu in the tenth Tretā Yuga, O my beloved, the Lord of Rohiṇī was born along with Durvāsas.

During the period he performed penance and when a thousand years elapsed (in penance) he made Lord Śaṅkara manifest himself to him.

He caused the Liṅga to be installed by Brahmā, the creator of the worlds. Then he adored Śaṅkara for a thousand years.

After adoring the Lord in accordance with the injunctions for the purpose of realizing his own objectives, the Lord of the night who could perceive Śaṅkara directly eulogized (thus):

## \|\| 1.24.6 \|\|

*caṃdra uvāca \|*  
*nāsti śarvasamo devo nāsti śarvasamā gatiḥ \|*  
*nāsti śarvasamo devo nāsti śarvasamā gatiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

Candra said:

6\. There is no god on a par with Śaṅkara. There is no goal or destination like Śaṅkara. There is no Lord on a par with Śaṅkara. There is no goal like Śaṅkara.

## \|\| 1.24.7 \|\|

*yaṃ paṭhaṃti sadā sāṃkhyāścitayaṃti ca yoginaḥ \|*  
*paraṃ pradhānaṃ puruṣaṃ tasmai jñeyātmane namaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Obeisance to that Jñeyātman (the soul worthy of being realized) whom the Sāṃkhyas cite always and Yogins ponder over always as the supreme Pradhāna and Puruṣa.

## \|\| 1.24.8 \|\|

*utpattau ca vināśe ca kāraṇaṃ yaṃ vidurbudhāḥ \|*  
*devāsuramanuṣyāṇāṃ tasmai jñānātmane namaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Obeisance to that Jñānātman (the soul in the form of spiritual knowledge) whom learned men know as the cause of the origin and destruction of Devas, Asuras and human beings.

## \|\| 1.24.9 \|\|

*yamavyayamanādyaṃtaṃ yaṃ nityaṃ śāśvataṃ dhruvam \|*  
*niṣkalaṃ paramaṃ brahma tasmai yogātmane namaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Obeisance to that Yogātman whom the learned men know as the unchangeable, permanent and steady, eternal, supreme Brahman without beginning and end, and free from impurities.

## \|\| 1.24.10 \|\|

*yaḥ pavitraṃ pavitrāṇāmādidevo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*punāti darśanādeva tasmai tīrthātmane namaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Obeisance to that Tīrthātman (the soul of all holy places) who is the purest of all pure things; to the primordial Lord Maheśvara who sanctifies by his mere vision.

## \|\| 1.24.11 \|\|

*yataḥ pravarttate sarvaṃ yasminsarvaṃ vilīyate \|*  
*pālayedyo jagatsarvaṃ tasmai sarvātmane namaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Obeisance to that Sarvātman (the soul of all) from whom everything issues forth, who maintains the entire universe and into whom everything gets dissolved.

## \|\| 1.24.12 \|\|

*aniṣṭomādibhiryajñairyaṃ yajaṃti dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*saṃpūrṇadakṣiṇaireva tasmai yajñātmane namaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Obeisance to that Yajñātman (the soul of sacrifices) whom the twice-born adore by means of Agniṣṭoma and other Yajñas with the full complement of monetary gifts.

## \|\| 1.24.13 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ sa saṃstute yāvaddivārātrau niśākaraḥ \|*  
*abravīdbhagavānprītaḥ prahasanniva śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

13\. Thus Niśākara (Moon-god) continued to eulogize day and night when Lord Śaṅkara became pleased and said smilingly:

## \|\| 1.24.14 \|\|

*śaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*parituṣṭo'smi te vatsa stotreṇānena śītago \|*  
*varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te bhūyo yatte manogatam \|\| 14 \|\|*

Śaṅkara said:

14\. O Sītāṃśu (Cool-rayed One), O dear one, I am well-pleased with you due to this prayer. Welfare unto you! Choose your boon whatever may be in your mind.

## \|\| 1.24.15 \|\|

*caṃdra uvāca \|*  
*yadi deyo varo'smākaṃ yadi tuṣṭo'si me prabho \|*  
*sāṃnidhyaṃ kuru deveśa liṃge'sminsarvadā vibho \|\| 15 \|\|*

Candra said:

15\. O Lord, if a boon is to be granted to me, if you are pleased with me, O Lord of Devas, be present in this Liṅga for ever.

## \|\| 1.24.16 \|\|

*ye tvāṃ paśyaṃti cātrasthaṃ bhaktyā paramayā yutāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ tu paramā siddhistvatprasādātsureśvara \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O Lord of Suras, let those have the greatest Siddhi, who are endowed with the most ardent devotion and view you stationed here in the Liṅga. Let those have the Siddhi with your favour.

## \|\| 1.24.17 \|\|

*śaṃbhuruvāca \|*  
*agre tu mama sāṃnidhyamasmiṃlliṃge mahāprabho \|*  
*viśeṣato'dhunā caṃdra tava bhaktyā niraṃtaram \|\| 17 \|\|*

Śaṃbhu said:

17\. O great Lord, even earlier I had been present in this Liṅga! It is all the more so, O Candra, now due to your incessant devotion.

## \|\| 1.24.18 \|\|

*sthātavyamadyaprabhṛti kṣetre'sminnumayā saha \|*  
*yasmāttvayā prabhā labdhā kṣetre'sminmatprasādataḥ \|*  
*tasmātprabhāsamityevaṃ nāmāsya prabhaviṣyati \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. From this day onwards, I have to stay in this holy spot along with Umā. The name of this holy spot shall forever be Prabhāsa because with my favour illumination was acquired by you in this Kṣetra.

## \|\| 1.24.19 \|\|

*yasmātpratiṣṭhitaṃ liṃgaṃ tvayā soma śubhaṃ mama \|*  
*somanātheti me nāma tasmātkhyātiṃ gamiṣyati \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Since, O Soma, the splendid Liṅga of mine has been installed by you, my name shall be well-known as Somanātha.

## \|\| 1.24.20-21 \|\|

*yanmamāgretanaṃ nāmakhyātaṃ brahmāvasānikam \|*  
*somanātheti ca punastadeva pracariṣyati \|*  
*drakṣyaṃti hi narā ye māmatrasthaṃ bhaktitatparāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*śṛṇu teṣāṃ phalaṃ vatsa bhaviṣyati niśākara \|*  
*na teṣāṃ jāyate vyādhirna dāridryaṃ na durgatiḥ \|*  
*na ceṣṭena viyogaśca mama caṃdra prabhāvataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. This name Somanātha of mine has already been well-known earlier and will be so till the end of Brahmā. Again will this become popular. O dear one, O Niśākara, listen to the benefit of those persons who view me installed here with great devotion. By my power, they will have no ailment, no poverty, no wretchedness, nor any separation from their beloved ones.

## \|\| 1.24.22 \|\|

*yātrāṃ kurvaṃti ye bhaktyā mama darśanakāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*pade padeśvamedhasya teṣāṃ phalamudāhṛtam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. If they perform pilgrimage with a desire to view me stationed here with great devotion in their minds, their benefit is cited (as great) as that of a horse-sacrifice at every step.

## \|\| 1.24.23 \|\|

*kiṃ kṛtairbahubhiryajñairupavāsairniśākara \|*  
*sakṛtpaśyaṃti māṃ ye'tra te sarve lebhire phalam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O Niśākara, of what avail are the many Yajñas performed and fasts undertaken? Even those who view me only once, will attain the benefit thereof.

## \|\| 1.24.24-25 \|\|

*ekamāsopavāsaṃ tu kurute bhaktitatparaḥ \|*  
*yāvadvarṣasahasraṃ tu ekaḥ paśyaṃti māmiha \|\| 24 \|\|*

*dvābhyāmapi phalaṃ tulyaṃ nāsti kācidvicāraṇā \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. If one, imbued with devotion performs monthly fast (fast continuous for a period of one month during a year) for one thousand years and another (simply) views me, the benefit derived by both of them is the same. No hesitation need be entertained in this respect.

## \|\| 1.24.26 \|\|

*eko bhavedbrahmacārī yāvajjīvaṃ niśākara \|*  
*sakṛtpaśyati māmatra samaṃ tābhyāṃ phalaṃ smṛtam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. One may observe celibacy throughout his life, O Niśākara, and another may view me here, but once. Their benefit is remembered to be the same.

## \|\| 1.24.27 \|\|

*eko dānāni sarvāṇi prayacchati dvijātaye \|*  
*ekaḥ paśyati māmatra samaṃ tābhyāṃ phalaṃ smṛtam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. One makes all kinds of Dāna-offerings to the twice-born and another sees me here; their benefit is remembered as the same.

## \|\| 1.24.28 \|\|

*eko vratāni sarvāṇi kurute mṛgalāṃchana \|*  
*anyaḥ paśyati māmatra samaṃ tābhyāṃ phalaṃ smṛtam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O Mṛgalāñchana (The Moon, marked with the figure of a deer), one may perform all the Vratas while another sees me here; the benefits accrued to them is remembered as the same.

## \|\| 1.24.29 \|\|

*ekastīrthāni kurute japajāpyāni bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*anyaḥ paśyati māmatra phalaṃ tābhyāṃ samaṃ smṛtam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. One person undertakes pilgrimage to all the Tīrthas and performs plenty -of Japas; another views me here (in this Kṣetra); their benefit is remembered as the same.

## \|\| 1.24.30 \|\|

*eko jñānādiyogena mumukṣurjāyate dhruvam \|*  
*anyaḥ paśyati māmatra phalaṃ tābhyāṃ samaṃ smṛtam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. One may certainly be keen to get salvation through Jñānayoga etc. Another sees me here. Their benefit is remembered as equal.

## \|\| 1.24.31 \|\|

*ekastu bhṛgupātena yāti mṛtyuṃ niśākara \|*  
*anyaḥ paśyati māmatra samaṃ tābhyāṃ phalaṃ smṛtam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O Niśākara, one meets with death through the rite of Bhṛgupāta (falling from a precipice). Another views me here. The benefit of both is remembered as the same.

## \|\| 1.24.32 \|\|

*ekaḥ snāti sadā māghaṃ prayāge narasattamaḥ \|*  
*anyaḥ paśyati māmatra phalaṃ tābhyāṃ samaṃ smṛtam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. One excellent man takes holy bath always during the month of Māgha at Prayāga. Another views me here. The benefit of both is remembered as the same.

## \|\| 1.24.33 \|\|

*ekaḥ piṇḍapradānaṃ ca pitṛtīrthe samācaret \|*  
*anyaḥ paśyati māmatra phalaṃ tābhyāṃ samaṃ smṛtam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. One may offer rice-balls (to the manes) in the Pitṛtīrtha (like Gayā). Another views me here. The benefit of both is remembered as the same.

## \|\| 1.24.34 \|\|

*gosahasraprado hyeko brāhmaṇe vedapārage \|*  
*ekaḥ paśyati māmatra phalaṃ tābhyāṃ samaṃ smṛtam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. One makes the gift of a thousand cows to a Brāhmaṇa who has mastered the Vedas; (while) another sees me here. The benefit of both is remembered as equal.

## \|\| 1.24.35 \|\|

*pañcāgniṃ sādhayedeko grīṣmakāle sudāruṇe \|*  
*ekaḥ paśyati māmatra phalaṃ tābhyāṃ samaṃ smṛtam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. One may practise the penance amidst five fires during severe summer. Another views me here. The benefit of both is remembered as the same.

## \|\| 1.24.36 \|\|

*snātaḥ somagrahe candra somavāre ca bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*yo māṃ paśyati sarveṣāmeteṣāṃ labhate phalam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O Candra, if a person takes his holy bath devoutly at the time of lunar eclipse on a Monday and views me, he acquires the benefit of all these.

## \|\| 1.24.37 \|\|

*sarasvatī samudraśca somaḥ somagrahastathā \|*  
*darśanaṃ somanāthasya sakārāḥ pañca durllabhāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Five things beginning with the letter “sa” (S) are very rarely achieved viz Sarasvatī (the river), Samudra (the ocean), Soma (Moon, Soma juice), Soma-graha (lunar eclipse) and the opportunity to view Somanātha.

## \|\| 1.24.38 \|\|

*nairaṃtaryeṇa ṣaṇmāsānvidhinā yaḥ prapūjayet \|*  
*puṇyaṃ tadeva saphalaṃ labhate viṣuvārcanāt \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. If one offers worship duly and continuously for six months and another only on the Viṣuva (Equinox) day, both acquire the same meritorious benefit.

## \|\| 1.24.39 \|\|

*etadeva tu vijñeyaṃ grahaṇe cottarāyaṇe \|*  
*saṃkrāṃtidinacchidreṣu ṣaḍaśītimukheṣu ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The same should be understood in the case of eclipse, northern transit and the (group of) Saṃkrāntis (Solar transits) of Dhanus, Mithuna, Kanyā and Mīna called “Ṣaḍaśītimukhas”.

## \|\| 1.24.40 \|\|

*māsaiścaturbhiryatpuṇyaṃ vidhinā'pūjya śaṃkaram \|*  
*kārttikyāṃ sa labhetpuṇyaṃ caitryāṃ taddviguṇaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*puṇyametattu phālgunyāmāṣāḍhyāmevameva tu \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The benefit one gets by duly worshipping Śaṅkara for four months (of Cāturmāsa) is derived by Kārttikī (i.e. by viewing me present in the Someśvara Liṅga on the full-Moon day of Kārttika) alone and on the Caitrī it is remembered as twice. The benefit and merit on Phālgunī and Āṣāḍhī is also the same.

## \|\| 1.24.41 \|\|

*eko dadyādgavāṃ lakṣaṃ dogdhrīṇāṃ vedapārage \|*  
*eko mamārcayelliṃgaṃ tasya puṇyaṃ tato'dhikam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. If one adores my Liṅga, his merit is more than that of one who makes the gift of a hundred thousand milch-cows to one who has mastered the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.24.42 \|\|

*māsemāse ca yo'śnīyādyāvajjīvaṃ sureśvari \|*  
*yaścārccayetsakṛlliṃgaṃ samametanna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O goddess of Suras, one may take food only once in a month and continue thus throughout one’s life. Another may adore my Liṅga but once. These two are equal (in merit). There is no doubt.

## \|\| 1.24.43 \|\|

*tapaḥśīlaguṇopete pātre vedasya pārage \|*  
*suvarṇakoṭiṃ yaddattvā tatphalaṃ kusumena tu \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Through the offering of a flower, one gets the same benefit as is obtained by offering ten million pieces of gold to a deserving person who has mastered the Vedas and who is endowed with good qualities and is a regular practitioner of penance.

## \|\| 1.24.44 \|\|

*arkapuṣpe'pi caikasmiñchivāya vinivedite \|*  
*daśa dattvā suvarṇāni yatphalaṃ tadavāpnuyāt \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Even if a single Ārkapuṣpa is offered to Śiva, one gets the same benefit as one gets by offering ten pieces of gold.

## \|\| 1.24.45 \|\|

*arkapuṣpasahasrebhyaḥ karavīraṃ viśiṣyate \|*  
*karavīra sahasrebhyo droṇapuṣpaṃ viśiṣyate \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Karavīra (flower) excels thousands of Ārkapuṣpas. Droṇapuṣpa excels thousands of Karavīra.

## \|\| 1.24.46 \|\|

*droṇapuṣpasahasrebhyo hyapāmārgaṃ viśiṣyate \|*  
*apāmārgasahasrebhyaḥ kuśapuṣpaṃ viśiṣyate \|*  
*kuśapuṣpa sahasrebhyaḥ śamīpuṣpaṃ viśiṣyate \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Apāmārga excels thousands of Droṇapuṣpas. Kuśapuṣpa excels thousands of Apāmarga \[Apāmārga?\]. Śamīpuṣpa excels thousands of Kuśapuṣpas.

## \|\| 1.24.47 \|\|

*śamīpuṣpaṃ bṛhatyāśca kusumaṃ tulyamucyate \|*  
*karavīrasamā jñeyā jātīvijayapāṭalāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. A Śamīpuṣpa and a flower of Bṛhatī are mentioned as equal. The flower of Jāti, Vijaya and Pāṭalā should be known as equal to Karavīra.

## \|\| 1.24.48 \|\|

*śvetamaṃdāra kusumaṃ sitaṃpadmasamaṃ bhavet \|*  
*nāgacaṃpakapunnāgadhattūrakusumaṃ smṛtam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. A flower of white Mandāra and those of Nāga, Caṃpaka, Punnāga and Dhattūra are remembered on a par with white lotus.

## \|\| 1.24.49 \|\|

*ketakījātimuktaṃ ca kandayūthīmadantikāḥ \|*  
*śirīṣasarjajaṃbūkakusumāni vivarjjayet \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. One should avoid the following flowers: Ketakī, Atimukta, Kanda, Yūthī, Madantikā, Śirīṣa, Sarja, and Jaṃbūka flowers.

## \|\| 1.24.50 \|\|

*ākulīkusumaṃ patraṃ karaṃjendrasamudbhavam \|*  
*bibhītakāni puṣpāṇi kusumāni vivarjjayet \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. One should avoid Ākulī flower, leaf of Karañjendra, Vibhītaka flowers etc.

## \|\| 1.24.51 \|\|

*kanakāni kadaṃbāni rātrau deyāni śaṃkare \|*  
*devaśeṣāṇi puṣpāṇi divā rātrau ca mallikā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Kanaka and Kadambaka flowers are to be offered to Śaṅkara at night, all the remaining flowers of deities during the day and Mallikā during the night.

## \|\| 1.24.52-54 \|\|

*praharaṃ tiṣṭhate mallī karavīramaharniśam \|*  
*kīṭakeśāpaviddhāni rātrau paryuṣitāni ca \|\| 52 \|\|*

*svayaṃ patitapuṣpāṇi tyajedupahatāni ca \|*  
*tulasī śatapatraṃ ca gandhārī damanastathā \|\| 53 \|\|*

*sarvāsāṃ patrajātīnāṃ śreṣṭho marubakaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*etaiḥ puṣpaviśeṣaistu pūjyaḥ someśvaraḥ sadā \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. Malli stays (fresh) for a Prahara (three hours). Karavīra for a day and night.

The following flowers should be abandoned: Those eaten and defiled by insects and hairs; those that have been kept overnight and so are stale; flowers that have automatically dropped down and those that are broken (mutilated). Tulasī, Śatapatra, Gāndhārī, Damana and Marubaka are remembered as the most excellent ones among all leaves. Someśvara should always be adored by means of these flowers.

## \|\| 1.24.55 \|\|

*yātrāyāḥ phalamāpnoti svargaloke mahīyate \|*  
*etāvaduktvā vacanaṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The person attains the benefit of pilgrimage (or religious procession). He is honoured in the heavenly world.

After saying this much, he (Śaṃbhu) vanished there itself.

## \|\| 1.24.56 \|\|

*candramā yakṣmaṇā muktaḥ svasthānanirato'bhavat \|*  
*āhūya viśvakarmāṇaṃ prāsādaṃ paryakalpayat \|*  
*śuddhasphaṭikasaṃkāśaṃ gokṣīradhavalojjvalam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Candramas was rid of Phthysis and he settled himself in his own place. He summoned Viśvakarman and made him build a palace of crystal-like splendour and sparklingly white like cow’s milk.

## \|\| 1.24.57 \|\|

*prāsādaṃ merunāmānaṃ hemaprākāratoraṇam \|*  
*caturdaśānye paritaḥ prāsādāḥ parikalpitāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ nāmāni vakṣyāmi pratyekaṃ tāni me śṛṇu \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The palace was named after Meru. It has gold-ramparts and ornamental gates. All round it fourteen other palaces were also built. Their names I shall mention separately. Do listen.

\[Names of palaces of the Moon\]

## \|\| 1.24.58-60 \|\|

*kesarī sarvatobhadro nadano nandiśālakaḥ \|*  
*nandīśo mandaraścaiva śrīvṛkṣo hyamṛtodbhavaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*himavānhemakūṭaśca kailāsaḥ pṛthivījayaḥ \|*  
*indranīlo mahānīlo bhūdharo ratnakūṭakaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*vaiḍūryaḥ padmarāgaśca vajrako mukuṭojjvalaḥ \|*  
*airāvato rājahaṃso garuḍo vṛṣabhastathā \|\| 60 \|\|*

58-60. (The names exceed fourteen—See, Verse 64) Kesarī, Sarvatobhadra, Nadana, Nandīśālaka, Nandīśa, Mandara, Śrīvṛkṣa, Amṛtodbhava, Himavān, Hemakūṭa, Kailāsa, Pṛthivijaya, Indranīla, Mahānīla, Bhūdhara, Ratnakūṭaka, Vaiḍūrya, Padmarāga, Vajraka, Mukuṭojvala, Airāvata, Rājahaṃsa, Garuḍa and Vṛṣabha.

## \|\| 1.24.61 \|\|

*meruḥ prāsādarājā ca devānāmālayo hi saḥ \|*  
*ādau pañcāṇḍako jñeyaḥ kesarīnāmataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Meru is the king of the palaces. Indeed it is the abode of the Devas. At the outset the palace by the name Kesarī should be known as having five Aṇḍakas (domes).

## \|\| 1.24.62 \|\|

*caturthāṃśā ca tadvṛddhiryāvanmeruḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The height of the palaces goes on increasing to one fourth of the height of Meru.

## \|\| 1.24.63-64 \|\|

*evaṃ pṛthakkārayitvā prāsādāṃśca caturdaśa \|*  
*brahmādīnāṃ devatānāṃ samīpasthānavāsinām \|\| 63 \|\|*

*daśa cānyānbhūdharādīnvṛṣabhāntānvarānane \|*  
*ādau kaparddinaṃ kṛtvā prāsādānparyakalpayat \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. After building these fourteen palaces separately, O lady of excellent countenance, he caused ten more palaces to be built for the Devas beginning with Brahmā, who were the residents of the neighbourhood. These ten are palaces beginning with Bhūdhara and ending with Vṛṣabha. They were constructed with Kapardin in view as the first.

## \|\| 1.24.65 \|\|

*meruḥ prāsādarājo vai sa tu someśvare kṛtaḥ \|*  
*tretāyuge tu daśame manovairvasvatasya ca \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Meru is the king of the palaces. It was constructed at Someśvara, in the tenth Tretāyuga in the Vaivasvata Manvantara.

## \|\| 1.24.66 \|\|

*kārayitvā maṃḍapāṃśca pratiṣṭhāpya yathāvidhi \|*  
*nadānāṃ tu śataṃ kṛtvā vāpīkūpa sahasrakam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. After causing the Maṇḍapas to be made and having installed them duly, he caused a hundred Nadas (rivers, probably wide canals) and a thousand tanks and wells to be dug.

## \|\| 1.24.67 \|\|

*gṛhāṇāṃ tu sahasrāṇi dīnānāthāśrayāṇi ca \|*  
*kārayitvā vidhānena viprebhyaḥ pradadau pṛthak \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. After causing thousands of houses, hospitals and orphanages duly, he offered them to the Brāhmaṇas severally.

## \|\| 1.24.68 \|\|

*niveśya nagaraṃ somaḥ śrīsomeśvarasannidhau \|*  
*svakarmaṇāṃ pracārārthamathābhyarthayata dvijān \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Soma thus set up a city in the vicinity of Śrīsomeśvara and requested the Brāhmaṇas for an elaborate performance of their rites:

## \|\| 1.24.69 \|\|

*somo'smi bhavatāṃ rājā prasādātparameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*tathāpi vinayenaiva bhaktyāṃ vijñāpayāmi vaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. “With the favour of Parameṣṭhin, I am Soma your king. Yet I humbly and devoutly submit to you.

## \|\| 1.24.70-71 \|\|

*dhanaṃ hiraṇyaratnādi dhānyaṃ vrīhiyavādikam \|*  
*gomahiṣyādipaśavo vastrāṇi vividhāni ca \|\| 70 \|\|*

*kadalīnālikerāṇi tāṃbūlīpūgamālinaḥ \|*  
*mano'bhirāmacaramā ārāmāḥ paritaḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. I have placed at your disposal all these things: Wealth, cash, gold, jewels etc., food-grains, cereals, barley etc., cows, buffaloes and other animals, different kinds of garments, plantains, coconuts, betal leaves, areca palms and parks, all round with charming border strips.

## \|\| 1.24.72 \|\|

*jaṃbūdvīpādhipāḥ sarve bhavatāmatravāsi nām \|*  
*ādeśaṃ ca kariṣyaṃti śirasyādhāya śobhanam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. All the rulers of the Jaṃbūdvīpa will carry out your orders with heads bowed down. You who stay here can issue excellent orders which they will honour.

## \|\| 1.24.73 \|\|

*dvīpāṃtarādāgataiśca karpūrāgurucaṃdanaiḥ \|*  
*anyaiśca vividhairdravyaiḥ saṃpūrṇā bhavatāṃ gṛhāḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Your abodes are filled with camphor, agallocham, sandal and various other kinds of articles coming from other continents.

## \|\| 1.24.74 \|\|

*paṇyānāṃ śatasaṃkhyānāṃ vyavahāranidarśinaḥ \|*  
*brahmottarāṇi tanvaṃti vaṇijo lābhakāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The merchants who are engaged in trading activities in hundreds of commodities will set apart Brahmottaras (a percentage of their profit) for the sake of you, Brāhmaṇas, because they desire for more gain.

## \|\| 1.24.75 \|\|

*bhavatsu bhṛtyabhāvena varttamānā hitaiṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*te cānye ca tathā paurā nāvasīdaṃti karhicit \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Seeking their own welfare, they will be your well-wishers and behave like your servants. Thus they and the other citizens will never face failure and fatigue.

## \|\| 1.24.76 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃpūrṇavibhavairbhavadbhiḥ śreyase mama \|*  
*kratukriyā vitanyaṃtāṃ vidhivadbhūridakṣiṇāḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Thus equipped with full complements of the requisite materials, you should strive for my prosperity. Hence may the rites of Yajñas be performed duly with adequate monetary gifts.

## \|\| 1.24.77 \|\|

*brahmādīni ca sarvāṇi pravartaṃtāmaharniśam \|*  
*dīnāṃdhakṛpaṇādīnāṃ kriyatāmārtināśanam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. May all the rites pertaining to Brahman (Vedas) such as studies and recitation of the Vedas be performed day and night. May the distress of the blind, disabled and wretched ones be alleviated.

## \|\| 1.24.78 \|\|

*abhyāgatānāmaucityādātithyaṃ ca vidhīyatām \|*  
*tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena sametānāṃ mahātmanām \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Hospitality should be extended to the guests properly. Noble-souled ones who have assembled in the course of their pilgrimage should be honoured with due formalities.

## \|\| 1.24.79-84 \|\|

*brahmarṣīṇāmāśrameṣu dīyatāmāśrayāḥ sadā \|*  
*mayātra sthāpitaṃ liṃgaṃ sarvakālaṃ dṛḍhavratāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*pavitrairupacāraiśca pūjayaṃtu dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*aṣṭau pramāṇapuruṣāḥ paurāṇāṃ kāryadarśinaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*vyavahārānavekṣadhvaṃ smṛtyācāraviśāradāḥ \|*  
*vyavasthāṃ matkṛtāmetāṃ bhavaṃto'tra dvijottamāḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*dhārayaṃtu mahātmāno diggajā iva medinīm \|*  
*evaṃ prabhutvamāsthāya sthāne'smiñchivaśālini \|\| 82 \|\|*

*śrutismṛtipurāṇoktāndharmānācarata dvijāḥ \|*  
*niśamya somasya vaco vinītamiti te dvijāḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*uvāca kauśikasteṣu gotrāṇāṃ prathamo dvijaḥ \|*  
*sādhūpadiṣṭamasmākaṃ dvijarājena sarvathā \|\| 84 \|\|*

79-84. May shelter be always, given to Brāhmaṇas, sages in the hermitages. O learned Brāhmaṇas of steadfastness in the holy vows, may excellent Brāhmaṇas always worship with holy rites, the Liṅga installed by me here.

Eight persons of authority should look after the affairs of the citizens. They must be experts in the conventions laid down in the Smṛtis. You excellent Brāhmaṇas, the noble-souled ones, extend your support to the arrangement made by me here even as the Elephants of the Quarters do to the earth. Thus, O Brāhmaṇas, take up the leadership here, in this holy spot of Śiva and carry out the rites and activities mentioned in the Śrutis and the Smṛtis.”

## \|\| 1.24.85-86 \|\|

*sarvametatkariṣyāmaḥ kiṃtu kiṃcinniśāmaya \|*  
*niyogataḥ pūjayatāṃ śivanirmālyasevinām \|\| 85 \|\|*

*pātityaṃ jāyate'smākaṃ śrutismṛtivigarhitam \|*  
*śrutismṛtī hi rudrasya yasmādājñādvayaṃ mahat \|\| 86 \|\|*

On hearing these polite words of Soma, the Brāhmaṇas, Kauśika, the first among the families there said: “Dvijarāja (Soma) has given us excellent advices in every respect.

85-86. We shall carry out all this. But listen to (consider) one matter. Even while we adore in accordance with the direction, if we make use of Śivanirmālya (remnants of the adoration of Śiva) it will result in our downfall as it is censured in the Śrutis and Smṛtis. And the Śrutis and Smṛtis constitute the two great commands of Rudra.

## \|\| 1.24.87 \|\|

*kastadullaṃghayenmūḍhaḥ prāṇaiḥ kaṃṭhaga tairapi \|\| 87 \|\|*
