*saphalaiva pratijñā te nānṛtaṃ munibhāṣitam \|*  
*evaṃ kṛte'pi te sarvaṃ bhaviṣyati samīhitam \|\| 120 \|\|*

114-120. “O Lord of Suras, I have been sent to your very presence by the Devas who are afraid. Listen from me to the words wholesome unto the Cāraṇas (Devas) as well as unto you.

Your inconceivable and inordinate strength destructive of even self-possessed wise ones has become known certainly. This being the case, do as the Suras say. Everyday eat one of them.

There are thirty crores of leading powerful Suras. How will you eat them at the same time?

Hence, do eat them one-by-one. Then it is not impossible to eat them even if you are alone. (Read aśakyā for śakyā)

Further Hutabhuk (Fire-god) contracted the disease of jaundice. Overeating is not proper. So accept my suggestion.

Moreover if they are all eaten simultaneously, everyday hunger will prompt you to worry for the means of the next meal.

Thus, your vow can be successfully carried out. The statement of the sage will not be false even if you do like this. Further, your desire too will be fulfilled.”

## \|\| 1.32.121 \|\|

*tatkariṣyāyahaṃ sarvamāhaivaṃ sa janārdanaḥ \|*  
*ekaikaśaḥ sa vibudhānbhakṣayiṣyati vāḍavaḥ \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. So said Janārdana. The Vāḍava said: “I will do so.” The Vāḍava agreed to the suggestion that he should eat the Devas one by one.

## \|\| 1.32.122-123 \|\|

*tataḥ surāḥ sureśānaṃ taṃ viṣṇumamitaujasam \|*  
*praṇamyāhuryathāyuktaṃ śobhanaṃ bhavatā kṛtam \|\| 122 \|\|*

*bhūyo'dya punarevāsya doṣasyopaśamakriyām \|*  
*kartuṃ tvameva śakto'si nānyastrātā divauka sām \|\| 123 \|\|*

122-123. Then the Suras bowed down to Viṣṇu, the Lord of Suras, of unmeasured prowess. “What is befitting and splendid has been accomplished by you. Further, you alone are competent to avert this danger. No one else can be the saviour of the Heaven-dwellers.”

## \|\| 1.32.124 \|\|

*tataḥ pītāṃbaradharaḥ śaṃkhacakragadādharaḥ \|*  
*yuṣmadbhayaṃ hariṣyāmi tatsurānāha mādhavaḥ \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. Thereupon, Mādhava who wears yellow garments and holds the conch, the discus and the club told the Suras: “I will remove the cause of your fear.”

## \|\| 1.32.125 \|\|

*śrutvaitadvibudhāḥ sarve harṣeṇotphulla locanāḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. On hearing this, all the Devas became happy and their eyes beamed with delight.

## \|\| 1.32.126 \|\|

*tatastānvibudhāndṛṣṭvā provāca sa tu vāḍavaḥ \|*  
*kimidānīṃ mayā kāryaṃ bhavatāṃ kathyatāṃ hi tat \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. Looking at the Devas Vāḍava said: “What should be done by me to you? May that be mentioned.”

## \|\| 1.32.127 \|\|

*atrāntare viśva tanurmahaujā vimohayaṃstaṃ jvalanaṃ svabuddhyā \|*  
*provāca pūrvaṃ vihitā yadāpastā bhakṣayasveti mahānubhāvaḥ \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. In the meantime the dignified and illustrious Lord of great prowess having the cosmic body enchanted that Jvalana (fire) by means of his (greater) intellect and said, “Eat up the AP (waters) created at the outset.”

## \|\| 1.32.128 \|\|

*etadvyavasitaṃ viṣṇoryaḥ śṛṇoti samāhitaḥ \|*  
*so'ticārabhayānmukto jñānaṃ muktimavāpnuyāt \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. He who listens with concentration to this act of Viṣṇu shall be rid of the excessive fear of spies and attain salvation and perfect knowledge.

## Chapter 33 - The Story of Sarasvatī

## \|\| 1.33.1-2 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*piturvadhāmarṣasujāta manyunā yadyatkṛtaṃ karma purā maharṣiṇā \|*  
*dadhīciputreṇa suraprasādhinā sarvaṃ śrutaṃ taddhi mayā samādhinā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*punaḥpunarvai vibudhaiḥ samānaṃ yadvṛttamāsī tkimapi pradhānam \|*  
*kāryaṃ hi tatsarvamanukrameṇa vijñātumicchāmi kutūhalena \|\| 2 \|\|*

The Devī said:

1-2. Everything has been listened to by me with concentration. I have heard everything that was performed earlier by the great sage, whose anger was justifiably aroused by the killing of his father. What the son of Dadhīci, who wanted to take the revenge on Suras, did I have heard. It is now my curiosity to know similarly everything in due order that befell the Suras, which is of equal importance.

## \|\| 1.33.3-5 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*ukto yadāsau vibudhaiḥ samastairāpaḥ purā tvaṃ bhuvi bhakṣayasva \|*  
*yato'marāṇāṃ prathamaṃ hi jātā āpo'grajāḥ sarvasurāsurebhyaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tenaivamuktastu mahātmanā tadā pradarśayadhvaṃ mama tā yataḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*pītvā surāḥ sarvamahaṃ purastātkṛtyaṃ kariṣye surabhakṣaṇaṃ hi \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tatrāpi netuṃ yadi māṃ samarthā yatrāsate vāricayāḥ sametāḥ \|*  
*ato'nyathā nāhamalīkavādī prāṇe prayāte munivākyakārī \|\| 5 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

3-5. When he was thus addressed by that noble-souled one, “Swallow first of all Water because it was created in the world at first and so it is the eldest of all Suras and Asuras”, he said, “O Suras, show me where it is stationed. After drinking it entirely, I shall carry out the task of eating the Suras. If you are able to take me to the place where the water has collected together (do so). I will not be one uttering falsehood. Even if the vital airs depart, I will carry out the behest of the sage”.

## \|\| 1.33.6 \|\|

*āhokte puṃḍarīkākṣa aurvaṃ hi vāḍavaṃ tadā \|*  
*tvāṃ prāpayiṣye yatrāpaḥ kena yānena vāḍava \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. When this was said, Puṇḍarīkākṣa (Viṣṇu) said to the Vāḍava Aurva, “O Vāḍava, by what vehicle can I take you to the place where the water is present?”

## \|\| 1.33.7 \|\|

*vāḍava uvāca \|*  
*nāhaṃ hayādibhiryānairgaṃtuṃ tatra samutsahe \|*  
*kumārīkarasaṃparkamekaṃ muktvā mataṃ hi me \|\| 7 \|\|*

The Vādava said:

7\. I am not eager to go there by means of horses and other vehicles. Excepting the contact with the hand of a virgin (no other means of transport is desirable). This is what I think.

## \|\| 1.33.8 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*etatte sulabhaṃ yānaṃ tāṃ kanyāmānayāmyaham \|*  
*yā tvāṃ netuṃ samarthā syādapāṃ sthānaṃ suniścitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:

8\. This means of transport is easily available to you. I shall bring that girl who is certainly able to take you to the reservoir of water.

## \|\| 1.33.9 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*surabhīśāpasaṃtaptā prāgupāttadaśāphalā \|*  
*sarasvatī yānabhūtā tasya sā viṣṇunā kṛtā \|\| 9 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

9\. Sarasvatī who was distressed due to the curse of the (celestial) Surabhis and who suffered the result of the (false) step taken earlier, was turned into his (Vāḍava’s) vehicle by Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 1.33.10 \|\|

*tato'bravīdvibhurgaṃgāṃ pārśvataḥ samupasthitām \|*  
*enaṃ vahniṃ mahābhāge vegānnaya mahodadhim \|*  
*nānyā śaktā samānetuṃ tvāṃ vinā lokapāvani \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then the Lord spoke to Gaṅgā who was present by his side, “O highly esteemed lady, take this fire quickly to the great ocean. O sanctifier of the worlds, except you, no one is competent to take it.”

## \|\| 1.33.11 \|\|

*gaṅgovāca \|*  
*nāsti me bhagavañchakti raurvaṃ voḍhuṃ jagatpate \|*  
*raudrarūpī mahāneṣa dahatyevānalo bhṛśam \|\| 11 \|\|*

Gaṅgā said:

11\. O Lord, O master of the worlds, I do not have the strength to carry Aurva. He is huge and terrific in form. This Anala (Fire) burns excessively.

## \|\| 1.33.12 \|\|

*tatastu yamunāṃ prāha sindhuṃ tasyā hyanantaram \|*  
*anyā nadīśca vividhāḥ pṛthakpṛthagudāradhīḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thereupon the liberal-minded Lord spoke to Yamunā first, to Sindhu thereafter, and to various rivers severally.

## \|\| 1.33.13-15 \|\|

*aśaktāstāḥ samānetuṃ pṛṣṭāśca surasattamaiḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sarasvatīṃ prāha devadevo janārddanaḥ \|*  
*tvameva vaja kalyāṇi pratīcyāṃ lavaṇodadhau \|\| 13 \|\|*

*evaṃ kṛte surāḥ sarve bhaviṣyanti bhayojjhitāḥ \|*  
*anyathā vāḍavenaite dahyaṃte svena tejasā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tasmāttvaṃ rakṣa vibudhāne tasmāttumulādbhayāt \|*  
*māteva bhava suśroṇi surāṇāmabhayapradā \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. They were asked by the excellent one among Suras and they proved unable to take (Aurva). Then Janārdana, the Lord of Devas, spoke to Sarasvatī: “O auspicious one, you yourself go over to the west of the briny sea. If this is carried out, all the Suras will be rid of their fear. Otherwise they will be burned by the Vāḍava through its refulgence. So, save Vibudhas (Suras) from this terrible fear. O lady of excellent waist, like a mother ^ou alone can bestow freedom from fear on the Suras.”

## \|\| 1.33.16-18 \|\|

*evamuktā hi sā tena viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|*  
*āha nāhaṃ svatantrāsmi pitā me dhriyate cirāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tasyāhaṃ kāriṇī nityaṃ kumārī ca dhṛtavratā \|*  
*kālatrayepyasvatantrā śrūyate vibudhaiḥ sutā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*pitrādeśaṃ vinā nāhaṃ padamekamapi kvacit \|*  
*gacchāmi tasmātko'pyanya upāyaściṃtyatāṃ hare \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. On being told thus by Viṣṇu, the powerful one, she said: “I am not free. My father, the ancient one, is waiting. Being a daughter and having Vratas to be performed, I can only do what he orders. A daughter is never independent in the past, present and future. So learned men say. O Hari, without the specific command of my father, I will not move even a step,. So, may some other means be thought of.”

## \|\| 1.33.19-20 \|\|

*tatsvarūpaṃ viditvaivaṃ samabhyetya pitāmaham \|*  
*tamabravīdvāsudevo devakāryamidaṃ kuru \|\| 19 \|\|*

*nānyathā śakyate netuṃ vāḍavo'gnirmahābalaḥ \|*  
*adṛṣṭadoṣāṃ muktvemāṃ kumārīṃ tanayāṃ tava \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Having known her attitude, Vāsudeva approached Pitāmaha (Brahmā) and said: “This is the task of Devas. Carry it out. Excepting this virgin daughter of yours, without any apparent defect, no one else can carry the Vāḍava fire of great prowess.”

## \|\| 1.33.21 \|\|

*tacchrutvā viṣṇunā proktaṃ kumārīṃ tanayāṃ tadā \|*  
*śirasyādhāya sasnehamuvāca prapitāmahaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. On hearing the words uttered by Viṣṇu, the Great-grandfather sniffed the head of his virgin daughter and said lovingly:

## \|\| 1.33.22 \|\|

*yāhi devi surānsarvānrakṣa tvaṃ bhayamāgatān \|*  
*vinikṣipa tvaṃ nītvainaṃ vāḍavaṃ lavaṇāṃbhasi \|*  
*piturvākyaṃ hi sā śrutvā provāca śrutilakṣaṇā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. “O fair lady, do go. Save all the Devas caught in the midst of fearful danger. Take this Vāḍava with you and cast it into the salt sea.”

## \|\| 1.33.23 \|\|

*sarasvatyuvāca \|*  
*eṣāsmi prasthitā tāta tava vākyā dasaṃśayam \|*  
*raudro'yaṃ vāḍavo vahnistanuṃ me bhakṣayiṣyati \|\| 23 \|\|*

On hearing her father’s words she said:

Sarasvatī said:

23\. At your instance, O dear father, I am now setting out undoubtedly. This Vāḍava fire is very horrendous. He will consume my body.

## \|\| 1.33.24 \|\|

*prāptaṃ kaliyugaṃ raudraṃ sāṃprataṃ pṛthivītale \|*  
*lokaḥ pāpasamācāraḥ sparśayiṣyati māṃ prabho \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. It is the advent of the terrible Kali Age now on the earth. O Lord, folks of evil conduct will be coming into contact with me.

## \|\| 1.33.25 \|\|

*tato duḥkhataraṃ kiṃ syādyatpāpaiḥ saha saṃgamaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. What can be more painful than contact with sinners!

## \|\| 1.33.26 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*yadi pāpajanākīrṇaṃ na vāṃchasi dharātalam \|*  
*pātālatalasaṃsthā tvaṃ naya vahniṃ mahodadhau \|\| 26 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

26\. If you do not like the earth’s surface fully infested with sinful folks, do take the Vahni (Fire) to the great ocean confining yourself to the Pātālatala (nether worlds).

## \|\| 1.33.27 \|\|

*yadātiśramasaṃyuktā vahninā dahyase bhṛśam \|*  
*tadā vibhidya vasudhāṃ pratyakṣā bhava putrike \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. If you find yourself exceedingly over-burdened and weary and get scorched by the Vahni pierce through the ground, O dear daughter, and reveal yourself.

## \|\| 1.33.28 \|\|

*kṛtvā vaktraṃ viśālākṣi prācī bhava sumadhyame \|*  
*tato yāsyaṃti tīrthāni tvāṃ śrāṃtāṃ cāruhāsinīm \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O lady of wide eyes and excellent waistline, turn your face eastwards. Thereupon, the (other) Tīrthas will approach you in that weary state of yours, O lady of charming smiles.

## \|\| 1.33.29 \|\|

*tāni sarvāṇi cāgatya sāhāyyaṃ te varānane \|*  
*kariṣyaṃti trayastriṃśatkoṭyo vai mama śāsanāt \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O lady of excellent countenance, they will come to you for help. At my bidding thirty-three crores of them will render you help.

## \|\| 1.33.30 \|\|

*gaccha putri na saṃtāpastvayā kāryaḥ kathaṃcana \|*  
*ariṣṭaṃ vraja paṃthānaṃ mā santu paripaṃthinaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Do proceed ahead, dear daughter. Do not be worried at any cost. Let your path be free from misfortune and loss. May there be no antagonists.

## \|\| 1.33.31 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*evamuktā tadā tena brahmaṇātha sarasvatī \|*  
*tyaktvā bhayaṃ hṛṣṭamanāḥ prayātuṃ samupasthitā \|\| 31 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

31\. On being told thus by Brahmā, Sarasvatī got rid of her nervousness and trepidation. Delighted in her mind, she got ready to go ahead.

## \|\| 1.33.32 \|\|

*tasyāḥ prayāṇasamaye śaṃkhaduṃdubhiniḥsvanaiḥ \|*  
*maṃgalānāṃ ca nirghoṣairjagadāpūritaṃ śubhaiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. At the time of her departure, the whole world was filled with the sounds of conch-shells and Dundubhi drums as well as similar auspicious sounds.

## \|\| 1.33.33-36 \|\|

*sitāṃbaradharā devī sitacaṃdanaguṃṭhitā \|*  
*śāradāṃbudasaṃkāśā tārahāravibhūṣitā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*saṃpūrṇacaṃdravadanā padmapatrāyatekṣaṇā \|*  
*kīrtiryathā maheṃdrasya pūrayantī diśo daśa \|\| 34 \|\|*

*svatejasā dyotayaṃtī sarvamābhāsayajjagat \|*  
*anuvrajaṃtī gaṃgā vai tayoktā varavarṇini \|\| 35 \|\|*

*drakṣyāmi tvāṃ punarahaṃ kutra vai vasatīṃ sakhi \|*  
*evamuktā tayā gaṃgā provāca snigdhayā girā \|\| 36 \|\|*

33-36. The divine lady had white garments. She had smeared herself with white sandal-paste. She resembled the autumnal cloud; she was adorned with pearl necklaces. Her face was like the full moon. Her eyes were large like the petals of a lotus. Like the renown of Mahendra, she filled all the ten quarters. Shining with her own refulgence, she illuminated the entire universe. O lady of excellent complexion (Gaurī), Gaṅgā, following her was addressed by her: “Dear friend, where shall I see you staying again?” On being asked thus by her, Gaṅgā spoke in affectionate words:

## \|\| 1.33.37-43 \|\|

*yadaiva vīkṣase prācīdiśi prāpsyasi māṃ tadā \|*  
*suraiḥ parivṛtā sarvaistatrāhaṃ tava suvṛte \|\| 37 \|\|*

*darśanaṃ saṃpradāsyāmi tyaja śokaṃ śucismite \|*  
*tāmāpṛcchya tato gaṃgāṃ punardarśanamastu te \|\| 38 \|\|*

*gaccha svamālayaṃ bhadre smarttavyā'haṃ tvayā'naghe \|*  
*yamunāpi tathā caivaṃ gāyatrī sumanoramā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*sāvitrīsahitāḥ sarvāḥ sakhyaḥ saṃpreṣitāstadā \|*  
*tato visṛjya tāṃ devī nadī bhūtvā sarasvatī \|\| 40 \|\|*

*himavaṃtaṃ giriṃ prāpya plakṣāttatra vinirgatā \|*  
*avatīrṇā dharāpṛṣṭhe matsyakacchapasaṃkulā \|\| 41 \|\|*

*grāhaḍiṃḍimasaṃpūrṇā timinakragaṇairyutā \|*  
*hasaṃtī ca mahādevī phenaughaiḥ sarvato diśam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*puṇyato yavahā devīstūyamānā dvijātibhiḥ \|*  
*vāḍavaṃ vahnimādāya hayavegena niḥsṛtā \|\| 43 \|\|*

37-43. “As soon as you come to the east and espy me, O lady of excellent holy rites, I shall appear before you surrounded by all the Suras there. O lady of splendid smiles, cast off your grief.” She then took leave of Gaṅgā saying, “May there be a meeting later on, O fair lady, go to your abode. O sinless one, I should be remembered by you.”

Similarly Yamunā, the highly charming Gāyatrī and all friends including Sāvitrī were sent back by her.

After sending them away, the goddess became the river Sarasvatī and reached the mountain Himavān. There she came out of the Plakṣa tree and descended on the surface of the earth. There she (the river) abounded in fish, turtles, crocodiles, Ḍiṇḍīras (cuttlefish), whales and groups of alligators. The great goddess (river) appeared to smile as she flowed with foams all round.

The splendid divine river with sacred waters, was eulogized by twice-born ones. Holding the Vāḍava fire, she flowed on gallopping like a horse trotting swiftly.

## \|\| 1.33.44 \|\|

*bhittvā vegāddharāpṛṣṭhaṃ praviṣṭātha mahītalam \|*  
*yadāyadābhavacchrāṃtā dahyate vāḍavāgninā \|*  
*tadātadā martyaloke yāti pratyakṣatāṃ nadī \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. With the rapidity of her current, she pierced the ground and came to the surface of the Earth. Whenever she (the river) became weary and got scorched by the Vāḍava fire, the river became visible in the mortal world.

## \|\| 1.33.45-46 \|\|

*tatastu jāyate prācī saṃtaptā vāḍavena tu \|*  
*tato vai yāni tīrthāni kīrttitāni purātanaiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*divyāṃtarikṣabhaumāni sāṃnidhyaṃ yāṃti bhāmini \|*  
*tataścāśvāsitā taiḥ sā sarasvatī punarnadī \|*  
*pātālatalamā sādya jagāma makarālayam \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. Thereupon, Prācī (Eastern quarter) became scorched by the Vāḍava. Thereat all the Tīrthas glorified by the ancient seers, O beautiful woman, the Tīrthas of heaven, intermediate space and the earth asserted their presence there. On being consoled by them, the river Sarasvatī went over to the nether worlds and passed over to the ocean, the abode of sharks and crocodiles.

## \|\| 1.33.47 \|\|

*khadirāmodamāsādya tatra sā vīkṣya sāgaram \|*  
*gaṃtuṃ pravṛttā taṃ vahnimādāya surasuṃdari \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O beautiful woman among the Suras, she (river) reached Khadirāmoda and there saw the ocean. Afterwards she took up the Vahni and began to proceed onwards.

## \|\| 1.33.48 \|\|

*nirūḍhabhāramātmānaṃ devādeśādviciṃtya sā \|*  
*prahṛṣṭā sumanāstasmātpravṛttā dakṣiṇāmukhī \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. She thought of the fact that it was at the behest of the Lord that she had herself taken up the burden and was therefore delighted. With a clear conscience, she went ahead facing the South.

## \|\| 1.33.49 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu ṛṣayo vedapāragāḥ \|*  
*catvāraśca mahādevi prabhāsaṃ kṣetramāśritāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. In the meantime, O great goddess, four sages who had mastered the Vedas reached the holy spot Prabhāsa Kṣetra.

## \|\| 1.33.50 \|\|

*hariṇaścātha vajraśca nyaṃkuḥ kapila eva ca \|*  
*tapastapyaṃti tatrasthāḥ svādhyāyāsaktamānasāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. They were Hariṇa, Vajra, Nyaṅku and Kapila. After stationing themselves there, they began to perform penance, with their minds engrossed in the self-study (of the Vedas).

## \|\| 1.33.51 \|\|

*pṛthakpṛthaksamāhūtāḥ snānārthaṃ taiḥ sarasvatī \|*  
*sāgaraḥ sammukhastasyāḥ sahasā sammupasthitaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Sarasvatī was severally summoned by them for the sake of holy bath. Suddenly the Ocean appeared before her face-to-face.

## \|\| 1.33.52 \|\|

*tataḥ sā cintayāmāsa kathaṃ me sukṛtaṃ bhavet \|*  
*śāpabhītā ca sā sādhvī paṃcasrotāstadā'bhavat \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Thereupon, she began to reflect, ‘How can I attain some merit!’ Further the chaste lady (river) was afraid of the curse (of the sages). She then turned herself into one of five channels.

## \|\| 1.33.53 \|\|

*ekaikaṃ toṣayāmāsa tamṛṣiṃ varavarṇini \|*  
*tato'syāḥ paṃca nāmāni jātāni pṛthivītale \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O lady of excellent complexion (Gauri), she propitiated each of the sages. Then, she had five different names on the earth.

## \|\| 1.33.54-56 \|\|

*hariṇī vajriṇī nyaṃkuḥ kapilā ca sarasvatī \|*  
*pānāvagāhanānnṛṇāṃ paṃcasrotāḥ sarasvatī \|\| 54 \|\|*

*brahmahatyā surāpānaṃ steyaṃ gurvaṃganāgamaḥ \|*  
*eṣāṃ saṃyogajaṃ cānyannarāṇāṃ paṃcamaṃ hi yat \|\| 55 \|\|*

*etatpaṃcavidhaṃ puṃsāṃ paṃcadhā'vasthitā satī \|*  
*nāśayetpātakaṃ ghoraṃ sakhībhiḥ sahitā nadī \|\| 56 \|\|*

54-56. They are: Hariṇī, Vajriṇī, Nyaṅku, Kapilā, and Sarasvatī. The river Sarasvatī flowing in five channels shall dispel all the five sins of men if they plunge into it or drink the waters. The sins are those of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter, imbibing liquor, committing theft and ravishing the wife of the preceptor. The fifth sin accrues from contact with these sinners. Sarasvatī (flowing in five channels) accompanied by her friends dispels these sins.

## \|\| 1.33.57 \|\|

*brahmahatyāṃ mahāghorāṃ pratilomā sarasvatī \|*  
*pānāvagāhanānnṛṇāṃ nāśayatyakhilaṃ hi sā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Sarasvatī flowing backwards dispels the terrible sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter entirely, through drinking her water and bathing in it.

## \|\| 1.33.58 \|\|

*pramādānmadirāpānadoṣeṇopahatātmanām \|*  
*tadvyapohāya kapilā dvijānāṃ vahate nadī \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The river Kapilā flows dispelling the sin of imbibing liquor committed by the twice-born, if they had drunk it inadvertently.

## \|\| 1.33.59 \|\|

*upavāsājjapāddhomātsnānātpānāddvijanmanām \|*  
*saptāhānnāśayetpāpaṃ tattadbhāvena cetasā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. If the twice-born perform Japa and Homa, if they observe fast and if they take their holy bath in and drink her water, the river dispels the sin in seven days. Whatever they perform, shall be performed with fervour and devotion in the mind.

## \|\| 1.33.60 \|\|

*svayaṃ te'pi viśudhyaṃti yathoktavidhikāriṇaḥ \|*  
*nyaṃkuṃ nadīṃ samāsādya mahataḥ pātakātkṛtāt \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. By resorting to the river Nyaṅku, the devotees get rid of the great sin committed by them if they perform everything as mentioned.

## \|\| 1.33.61 \|\|

*snānopāsanapānena vajriṇī gurutalpagam \|*  
*nāśayatyakhilaṃ puṃsāṃ pāpaṃ bhūribhayaṃkaram \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. By observing fast, taking the holy bath and drinking the holy waters Vajriṇī redeems a sinner who has violated the sanctity of the preceptor’s bed. She annihilates the entire sin of men despite its massiveness and terrible nature.

## \|\| 1.33.62 \|\|

*saṃyogajasya pāpasya haraṇāddhariṇī smṛtā \|*  
*nadī puṇyajalopetā saptāhamavagāhanāt \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The river Hariṇī dispels the sin resulting from having contact with other sinners. The river has sacred and meritorious waters. By taking the holy plunge in her for seven days, the sin is removed. Hence the river is remembered as Hariṇī (the remover).

## \|\| 1.33.63 \|\|

*evametāni pāpāni sarvāṇi surasuṃdari \|*  
*nadī nāśayate tathyaṃ paṃcasrotā sarasvatī \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Thus, O beautiful goddess, the river Sarasvatī with five channels dispels all the sins. It is the truth.

## \|\| 1.33.64 \|\|

*tato'paśyatpunaścāru sā devī pathi saṃsthitam \|*  
*parvataṃ sāgarasyāṃte roddhuṃ mārgamiva sthitam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Then, further ahead, the fair lady (river) saw a beautiful mountain standing in her path near the ocean, as if to obstruct her way.

## \|\| 1.33.65 \|\|

*brahmāṇḍamānadaṇḍo'yaṃ purato girisattamaḥ \|*  
*vrajantyāḥ surakāryeṇa mama vighnakaraḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. ‘So, here is this excellent mountain. It is the measuring rod for the whole Cosmic Egg. It has now come as an obstacle before me even as I was going ahead on the errand of Suras.’ (Thought Sarasvatī.)

## \|\| 1.33.66 \|\|

*uccaistaraṃ mahāśailamavalokya sarasvatī \|*  
*atha vegena ruddhena giriṇā vismitā satī \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. The river Sarasvatī looked at the great lofty mountain. The chaste lady (river) became surprised, when the mountain held up the speed of her current.

## \|\| 1.33.67 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃcintayedyāvanmanasā tanma hādbhutam \|*  
*tāvanmaṃgalaśabdena pratibuddhaḥ kṛtasmaraḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Even as she was contemplating on this miracle in her mind, Kṛtasmara, the mountain, woke up (became aware of it) through the auspicious sound.

## \|\| 1.33.68-69 \|\|

*giriśṛṃgadvaṃdvacaraṃ dadarśa puruṣaṃ ca sā \|*  
*tāmāha devīṃ sa nago mārgo nāstīha suvrate \|\| 68 \|\|*

*anyatra kvāpi gaccha tvaṃ yatra te'bhimataṃ śubhe \|*  
*āhaivamukte sā devī naraṃ nagaśiraḥsthitam \|\| 69 \|\|*

68-69a. She (the river) saw a being walking over a pair of peaks of the mountain. The mountain said to her (the river), the divine lady: “O lady of excellent holy rites, there is no way here. O fair lady, go somewhere else where you please”.

69b. When this was said the divine lady (river) spoke to the being stationed on the top of the mountain:

## \|\| 1.33.70 \|\|

*devādeśātsamāyātā na nirodhyā gire tvayā \|*  
*evamukte giriḥ prāha tāṃ devīṃ sumanoramām \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. “O Mountain, I have come here at the behest of the Lord. I should not be hindered by you.” When this was spoken, the Mountain said to that charming divine lady (river):

## \|\| 1.33.71-72 \|\|

*parvato'haṃ tvayā bhadre kiṃ na jñātaḥ kṛtasmaraḥ \|*  
*tvatsparśanānna doṣosti kumārī tvaṃ yato'naghe \|\| 71 \|\|*

*atastvāṃ varaye devi bhāryā me bhava suvrate \|\| 72 \|\|*

71-72. “O fair one, haven’t you come to know that I am the Mountain Kṛtasmara. O sinless one, there is no fault in touching you because you are a virgin. So, O lady of excellent holy rites, I woo you. Become my wife.”

## \|\| 1.33.73 \|\|

*sarasvatyuvāca \|*  
*pitā me dhriyate yasmāttena nāhaṃ svayaṃvarā \|*  
*tava bhāryā bhaviṣyāmi mārgaṃ yaccha mamādhunā \|\| 73 \|\|*

Sarasvatī said:

73\. Since my father is alive and active I cannot be a Svayaṃvarā (a girl choosing her own groom) and become your wife. Leave the path free unto me now.

## \|\| 1.33.74 \|\|

*evamukto giriḥ prāha anicchaṃtīṃ mahābalāt \|*  
*udvāhayiṣye tvāṃ bhadre kastrātā sti tavādhunā \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. On being told thus the Mountain said: “O fair one, I will forcibly marry you, though you do not wish it. Who can come to help you now?”

## \|\| 1.33.75-76 \|\|

*sā taṃ manobhavākrāntaṃ matvā divyena cakṣuṣā \|*  
*āha nāsti mama trātā tvāmeva śaraṇaṃ gatā \|\| 75 \|\|*

*tvayodvāhyā yadya vaśyamahamevaṃ mahābala \|*  
*asnātāṃ nodvaha vibho snānaṃ karttuṃ ca dehi me \|\| 76 \|\|*

75-76. With her divine eyes, she came to consider him overwhelmed by Manobhava (Passion, Lord of love) and said: “There is no one to save me. I seek refuge in you. O highly powerful one, if I am to be certainly married thus, O Lord, do not marry me before I take my bath. Permit me to take my bath.”

## \|\| 1.33.77 \|\|

*tāmuvāca tataḥ śailaḥ svasaṃpadabhimānavān \|*  
*saukhyadaṃ paśya subhage mayi saṃpūrṇavaibhavam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Then, the Mountain in the fullness of his pride of his rich assets said: “O fortunate one, O beautiful lady (river), you can find all pleasing amenities in me.

## \|\| 1.33.78 \|\|

*dvaṃdvāni yatra gāyaṃti kiṃnarāṇāṃ manoramam \|*  
*śrūyate ca sunidhvānaṃ taṃtrīvādyamathāparam \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Yonder where pairs of Kinnaras sing in an enchanting manner, another highly pleasing note of the musical instrument, the lute, is heard.

## \|\| 1.33.79 \|\|

*tatra tālāstamālāśca pippalāḥ panasāstathā \|*  
*sadaiva phalapuṣpāścā dṛśyaṃte sumanoramāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. There the charming trees laden with fruits and flowers are seen—Tālas, Tamālas, Pippalas and Panasas.

## \|\| 1.33.80 \|\|

*kuṭajaiḥ kovidāraiśca kadaṃbaiḥ kurabaistathā \|*  
*mattālikulaghuṣṭaiśca bhūdharo bhāti sarvataḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. All round, the Mountain shines well with Kuṭajas, Kovidāras, Kadambas and Kurabas. All of them are reverberating with the humming sounds of the swarms of inebriated bees.

## \|\| 1.33.81 \|\|

*harāṃgarāgavadbhāti kvacitkuṭajakuḍmalaiḥ \|*  
*kvacittu karṇikāraiśca viṣṇorvāsaḥsamaprabhaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. In some places, with the buds of Kuṭaja it appears as though the unguent of Hara (i.e. the holy ash) has been smeared. In some places it appears to have the lustre resembling that of the robes of Viṣṇu, on account of the Karṇikāras.

## \|\| 1.33.82 \|\|

*tamāladalasaṃchannaḥ kvacidvaivasvatadyutiḥ \|*  
*kvaciddhātuviliptāṃgo gaṇādhyakṣavapurnagaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Covered with the Tamāla leaves in some places it has the lustre of Vaivasvata (Yama). In some places, its parts are smeared with minerals. So the mountain appears to have the body like that of Gaṇādhyakṣa (Vighneśvara).

## \|\| 1.33.83 \|\|

*caturmukha ivābhāti haritālavapuḥ kvacit \|*  
*kvacitsaptacchadairviṣṇorvapuṣā bhātyayaṃ giriḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. In some places, with Harìtāla (Yellow, Orpiment) over its body, it appears like the Four-faced Lord. In some places, with the Saptacchadas, the mountain appears to have the body of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 1.33.84 \|\|

*kvacitkātyāyanīprakhyaḥ priyaṃgususamākulaḥ \|*  
*kvacitkesarasaṃyuktairanalābho vibhātyasau \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. In some places abounding in Priyaṅgu, it resembles the refulgence of Kātyāyanī. In some places, with the trees having flower filaments it resembles Anala (Fire).

## \|\| 1.33.85 \|\|

*vṛttaiḥ sapulakaiḥ snigdhaiḥ strīṇāmiva payodharaiḥ \|*  
*duṣprāpyairalpapuṇyānāṃ kvacidābhāti bilvakaiḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. In some places is shine with Bilvaka fruits that look like the breasts of women, circular (globular), glossy and horripilant. They are inaccessible to those who are deficient in merit.

## \|\| 1.33.86-87 \|\|

*siṃhairvyāghrairmṛgairnāgairvarāhairvānaraistathā \|*  
*kvacitkvacidasau bhāti parasparamanuvrataiḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*śūlikodbhinnamākāśamiva kurvadbhiruccakaiḥ \|*  
*evamukte pratyuvāca śāradā taṃ nagottamam \|\| 87 \|\|*

86-87. In some places, it shines with lions, tigers, deer, elephants, boars and monkeys coming into contact with one another and rendering the sky pierced and covered with roasted meat sticking to pikes.”

When this was said, Śāradā (i.e. Sarasvatī) replied to the excellent Mountain:

## \|\| 1.33.88 \|\|

*yadi māṃ tvaṃ pariṇaye rudaṃtīmekikāṃ tathā \|*  
*gṛhāṇa vāḍavaṃ haste yāvatsnānaṃ karomyaham \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. “I am alone and isolated. I lament. Still if you are inclined to marry me, hold this Vāḍava in your hands while I take my holy bath.”

## \|\| 1.33.89 \|\|

*evamukte sa jagrāha ta nagedro'pavarjim \|*  
*kṛtasmarastatsaṃsparśātkṣaṇādbhasmatvamāgataḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. When this was said, Kṛtasmara, the excellent Mountain, seized the Vāḍava handed over by Sarasvatī. Due to its contact, Kṛtasmara was reduced to (a heap of) ash instantly.

## \|\| 1.33.90 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti te tasya pāṣāṇā mṛdutāṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*gṛhadevakulārthāya gṛhyaṃte śilpibhiḥ saha \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Ever since then all the rocks therein became soft. They are being taken by the artisans for use in (building) houses and temples.

## \|\| 1.33.91 \|\|

*dagdhvā kṛtasmaraṃ devī punarādāya vāḍavam \|*  
*samudrasya samīpe sā sthitā hṛṣṭatanūruhā \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. After burning Kṛtasmara and holding the Vāḍava once again, the divine lady (river) came near the sea and stood there with hairs standing on end due to delight.

## \|\| 1.33.92 \|\|

*tatrasthā sā mahādevī tamāha vaḍavānalam \|*  
*paśya vāḍava garjantaṃ sāgaraṃ purataḥ sthitam \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Stationed there, the great goddess (river) spoke to the Vāḍava fire: “O Vāḍava, see the roaring sea standing before you.”

## \|\| 1.33.93 \|\|

*garjaṃtaṃ so'pi taṃ dṛṣṭvā prasarpaṃtaṃ ca vīcibhiḥ \|*  
*tāmāha kimidaṃ bhadre bhīto me lavaṇodadhiḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. He saw the roaring sea lashing with its waves. He spoke to her, “What is this, O fair lady? The briny sea is afraid of me.”

## \|\| 1.33.94 \|\|

*prahasyovāca sā bālā ko na bhītastavānala \|*  
*bhakṣyaste vihito yasmāttava devairmahābala \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. The girl (river) laughed and said: “O Fire, who is not afraid of you? O highly powerful one, it has been assigned to you by the Devas as your food.”

## \|\| 1.33.95 \|\|

*sa tasyāstadvacaḥ śrutvā saṃprahṛṣṭastu pāvakaḥ \|*  
*dāsyāmi te varaṃ bhadre yatheṣṭaṃ prārthayasva naḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. On hearing her words the Fire was highly delighted. He said: “O fair one, I shall grant you a boon. Make a request as you please.”

## \|\| 1.33.96 \|\|

*tenaivamuktā sā devī vāḍavenāgninā tadā \|*  
*sasmāra kāraṇātmānaṃ viṣṇuṃ kamalalocanam \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. On being told thus by that Vāḍava fire, the divine lady (river) remembered the lotus-eyed Viṣṇu, the soul that is the cause (of all).

## \|\| 1.33.97 \|\|

*dṛṣṭosāvātmahṛtsaṃsthastayā devo janārddanaḥ \|*  
*smṛtamātraḥ sarasvatyā parastribhuvaneśvaraḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Immediately on being remembered by her, by Sarasvatī, Lord Janārdana, the great Lord of the three worlds, was seen by her as stationed in her own heart.

## \|\| 1.33.98 \|\|

*manodṛṣṭyā vilokyāha sā tamaṃtaḥsthamacyutam \|*  
*vāḍavo yacchati varamahaṃ taṃ prārthayāmi kim \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Looking at Acyuta stationed within, by means of her mind’s eye, she said, “The Vāḍava wishes to give a boon. What shall I ask him?”

## \|\| 1.33.99 \|\|

*tatastena hṛdisthena proktā devī sarasvatī \|*  
*prārthanīyo varo bhadre sūcīvaktratvamādarāt \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Sarasvatī, the goddess, was addressed by the Lord stationed in the heart, “O fair one, Sūcīvaktratva (state of having a mouth like a needle) should be respectfully requested for.”

## \|\| 1.33.100 \|\|

*tatastvabhihito devyā yadi me tvaṃ varapradaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sūcīmukho bhūtvā tvaṃ pibāpo mahābala \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Then (the Fire) was addressed by the goddess, “O highly powerful one, if you wish to grant a boon, then become Sūcīmukha (one with the mouth like a needle) and drink the waters.”

## \|\| 1.33.101-103 \|\|

*evamuktena tattena sūcīvedhasamaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*ghaṭikāpūraṇaṃ yadvatpapau tadvadanaṃ jalam \|\| 101 \|\|*

*evaṃ sa vāḍavo vahniḥ surāṇāṃ bhakṣaṇodyataḥ \|*  
*vaṃcito viṣṇunā yāti medhāmādhāya yatnataḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

*sargametaṃ naraḥ puṇyaṃ vācyamānaṃ śṛṇoti yaḥ \|*  
*sa viṣṇu lokamāsādya tenaiva saha modate \|\| 103 \|\|*

101-103. On being told thus, the mouth was rendered like a needle by him. It was like the minute hole in the Ghaṭikā. That mouth drank the water. Thus the Vāḍava fire that attempted to devour Suras was deceived by Viṣṇu. He then proceeded (to the holy spot) assiduously taking care of his intellect. He who listens to this holy Sarga (chapter) as it is being read attains Viṣṇuloka and rejoices with him.

## Chapter 34 - The Descent of Sarasvatī

## \|\| 1.34.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*sarasvatī varaṃ prāpya variṣṭhaṃ vaḍavānalāt \|*  
*punastaṃ sāgare kṣeptumudyatā sā manasvinī \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. The noble- minded Sarasvatī received the excellent boon from Vaḍavānala and thereafter she proceeded, ahead to hurl him into the ocean.

## \|\| 1.34.2 \|\|

*devādeśātprabhāsasya purataḥ saṃsthitā tadā \|*  
*samudramāhūya tadā vāḍavārpaṇakāṃkṣiṇī \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Desirous of handing over the Vāḍava at the behest of the Lord, she stationed herself before the holy place of Prabhāsa and invoked the ocean:

## \|\| 1.34.3 \|\|

*tvamādiḥ sarvadevānāṃ tvaṃ prāṇaḥ prāṇināṃ sadā \|*  
*devādeśādgṛhāṇa tvamāgatyārṇava vāḍavam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. “O Arṇava (Ocean), you are the primordial one among Devas. You are the vital air of all living beings always. Do come and accept the Vāḍava at the behest of the Lord.”

## \|\| 1.34.4 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃciṃtito devyā yadāsāvaṃbhasāṃpatiḥ \|*  
*tathā jalātsamuttīrya samāyāto mahādyutiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. When the Lord of waters was thus thought of by the divine lady (river), the ocean of great lustre, rose up from the water and came there.

## \|\| 1.34.5-7 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā vismitā devī divyaṃ viṣṇumivāparam \|*  
*śyāmaṃ kamalapatrākṣaṃ sāgaraṃ sumanoramam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*vicitramālyābharaṇaṃ citravastrānulepanam \|*  
*āpagābhiḥ sarūpābhiḥ strīrūpābhiḥ samāvṛtam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*evaṃvidhaṃ samālokya sā devī brahmaṇaḥ sutā \|*  
*sarasvatī jalanidhimuvācedaṃ śucismitā \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. On seeing the highly fascinating Ocean like another blue-complexioned, lotus-eyed, divine Viṣṇu the divine lady was surprised. He had ornaments and garlands of various kinds. He had garments of diverse colours and (was smeared with) unguents of various sorts. He was surrounded by the Āpagās (Rivers) in physical forms like ladies.

On seeing the Ocean of this description, the divine lady, the daughter of Brahmā, spoke to the Ocean with pure smiles:

## \|\| 1.34.8 \|\|

*tvamagrajaḥ sarvabhavodbhavānāṃ tvaṃ jīvitaṃ janmavatāṃ narāṇām \|*  
*tasmātsurāṇāṃ kuru kāryamiṣṭaṃ vahniṃ gṛhāṇa tvamihopanītam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. “You are the eldest of all beings born in the world. You are the vital life of all the men born. Hence carry out the task desired by Suras. Receive the (Vāḍava) Vahni brought here.”

## \|\| 1.34.9 \|\|

*atrāṃtare so'pi vimṛśya sarvaṃ kāryaṃ svabuddhyā kimihopapannam \|*  
*kṛtvā'nalasya grahaṇaṃ mayedaṃ kāryaṃ surāṇāṃ vihitaṃ bhavecca \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. In the meantime he too considered mentally everything to be carried out. ‘By accepting the Anala (fire) the task of the Suras will be carried out by me’.

## \|\| 1.34.10 \|\|

*evaṃ ciṃtayatastasya grahaṇaṃ rucitaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*vāḍavāgneḥ samudrasya surapīḍākṛte yadā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Contemplating thus Samudra (Sea-god) liked the acceptance of the Vaḍavāgni to stop the affliction caused to the Suras.

## \|\| 1.34.11 \|\|

*tadā tena puraḥsthena devī sābhihitā bhṛśam \|*  
*vāḍavaṃ saṃprayacchainaṃ suraśatruṃ sarasvati \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then the Devī was addressed by him as he stood in front, “O Sarasvatī, hand over this Vāḍava, the enemy of Suras.”

## \|\| 1.34.12-13 \|\|

*tatastayā praṇamyāśu pitāmahapuraḥsarān \|*  
*cāraṇāṃścārucitrāṃgyā sarasvatyā divi sthitān \|\| 12 \|\|*

*punaśca karasaṃstho'sau vāḍavo'bhihitastayā \|*  
*tvamapo bhakṣayasveti surairukta imā iti \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Then Sarasvatī of variegated limbs (beautiful) immediately bowed down to Cāraṇas standing in the firmament with Pitāmaha as the leader. Then she spoke to the Vāḍava held in her hands: “You have been asked to devour the ĀP (Waters) by Suras. These are they (the waters).”

## \|\| 1.34.14 \|\|

*evamuktvā samudrasya tadā devyā samarppitaḥ \|*  
*vāḍavo'gniḥ sarasvatyā surādeśānmahābalaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. After saying this the divine lady Sarasvatī handed over the highly powerful Vaḍavāgni to the Ocean at the behest of Suras.

## \|\| 1.34.15 \|\|

*taṃ samarpya tatastasmi nnadī bhūtvā sarasvatī \|*  
*praviṣṭā sāgaraṃ devī nāradeśvaramārgataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. After handing over the Fire to him, the divine lady Sarasvatī transformed herself into a river and entered the Sāgara (Sea) along the path of Nāradeśvara (the deity of that name installed there).

## \|\| 1.34.16 \|\|

*daityasūdanasāṃnidhye dattvārghyaṃ lavaṇāṃbhasi \|*  
*arghyeśvaraṃ pratiṣṭhāpya daityasūdana paścime \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. In the vicinity of Daityasūdana (Viṣṇu) she offered Arghya to the Salt Sea and installed Arghyeśvara to the west of Daityasūdana.

## \|\| 1.34.17 \|\|

*tato'bdhiṃ saṃpraviṣṭā sā paṃcasrotā mahānadī \|*  
*svarūpeṇaiva sā puṇyā punaḥ puṇyatamā'bhavat \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Then the great river of five channels entered the ocean. Already meritorious and holy in her own original form, she became now still more sacred.

## \|\| 1.34.18 \|\|

*prabhāsakṣetrasaṃparkātsamudrasya ca saṃgamāt \|*  
*sāgaro'pi samāsādya sarasvatyāstu vāḍavam \|*  
*nirdhano vai dhanaṃ prāpyācintayatkva kṣipāmyaham \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. She became holier due to the contact of the Prabhāsa Kṣetra and the confluence with the Ocean. After receiving the Vāḍava from Sarasvatī, Sāgara (Ocean) thought in the manner of a poor man who suddenly got much wealth: ‘Where shall I place this?’

## \|\| 1.34.19 \|\|

*sa tenaiva karasthena dīpya mānena sāgaraḥ \|*  
*vahninā śikharasthena bhāti merurivāparaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. With that fire held in the hand and blazing brightly the Sāgara appeared like another Meru with the fire held on the head.

## \|\| 1.34.20 \|\|

*taṃ tathāvidhamālokya tatra ye jalacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*yādogaṇāste mumucurdāhabhītā mahāsvanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On seeing him in that position, all the aquatic beings, the sea monsters etc. howled loudly as they were afraid of being scalded.

## \|\| 1.34.21-22 \|\|

*taṃ śrutvā bhairavaṃ śabdamāyāto daityasūdanaḥ \|*  
*āha yādogaṇānsarvānmā bhaiṣṭa sumahābalāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*yasmādanena prathamā āpo bhakṣyā na tatragāḥ \|*  
*prāṇinastanna bhetavyaṃ bhavadbhistu mamājñayā \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. On hearing that terrific sound, Daityasūdana (Viṣṇu) came there and told all the aquatic beings, “O highly powerful ones, do not be afraid, since, at the outset, only the waters are to be taken in by this (Vāḍava Fire) and not those beings living therein. At my bidding, do not get afraid.”

## \|\| 1.34.23 \|\|

*evamuktastu kṛṣṇena tūṣṇīṃbhūtā jalecarāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. On being told thus by Kṛṣṇa, the aquatic beings kept quiet.

## \|\| 1.34.24 \|\|

*tūṣṇīṃbhūteṣu sarveṣu jalajeṣu jaleśvaram \|*  
*prāhācyutaḥ prakṣipa tvamapāṃ madhye tu vāḍavam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. When all the aquatic beings became silent, Acyuta said to the Lord of Waters, “Do hurl the Vāḍava in the midst of the waters.”

## \|\| 1.34.25 \|\|

*agādhembhasi tenāsau nikṣipto vāḍavo'nalaḥ \|*  
*varuṇena pibannāste tajjalaṃ sumahābalaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The Vāḍava Anala was hurled into the deep waters. The highly powerful one remained drinking the water along with Varuṇa.

## \|\| 1.34.26 \|\|

*tasyocchvāsāniloddhūtaṃ tattoyaṃ sāgarādbahiḥ \|*  
*nirmaryādeva yuvatiritaścetaścadhāvati \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. That water shaken by the exhalation of the breath began to move about outside the ocean like a young woman who has set at nought all bounds and curbs of behaviour.

## \|\| 1.34.27-28 \|\|

*atha kāle gate devi śuṣyatyaṃbu śanaiḥśanaiḥ \|*  
*viditvā kṣīyamāṇāstā apo jalanidhistataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*āhaivaṃ puṃḍarīkākṣamapaḥ kuru tvamakṣayāḥ \|*  
*anyathā sarvanāśena jalānāṃ māmihāgrataḥ \|*  
*bhakṣayiṣyatyasau vahnirvāḍavo hi janārddana \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. As time passed on, O Goddess (Gaurī), the water began to dry up and evaporate slowly. The Storehouse of waters (the Sea) became aware of the fact that the (store of) waters are getting dwindled. He spoke to the Lotus-eyed Lord: “Do make the waters perennial. Otherwise, O Janārdana, if all the waters disappear, this Vāḍava fire will at the very outset swallow

## \|\| 1.34.29-30 \|\|

*etacchrutvā vacastasya samudrasya tu bhīṣaṇam \|*  
*kṛtaṃ tadakṣayaṃ toyamā tmano bhayanāśanam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*jñātvā surāḥ sarvamidaṃ viceṣṭitaṃ kṛtyānalasyāsya nibaṃdhanaṃ tathā \|*  
*pralobhanaṃ toyapuraḥsarā dviṣaḥ pupūjire keśavamatra cāriṇam \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. On hearing these awful, panicky words of the Ocean, the water was rendered perennial (by Acyuta). The Suras knew that the water thus rendered everlasting dispels their grief. They knew these activities (of Keśava) which bound the Kṛtyā Fire to a tempting promise. They worshipped Keśava who moved about there tempting their enemy (i.e. the Vāḍava Fire). In this they kept the waters as their leaders.

## \|\| 1.34.31 \|\|

*evaṃ sarasvatī prāptā prabhāsaṃ kṣetramuttamam \|*  
*brahmalokānmahādevi sarvapāpapraṇāśinī \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Thus, O great goddess (Gaurī), from the world of Brahmā, Sarasvatī, the destroyer of all sins, reached the excellent Prabhāsa Kṣetra.

## \|\| 1.34.32 \|\|

*someśāddakṣiṇāgneye sāgarasya samī pataḥ \|*  
*saṃsthitā tu mahādevī vaḍavānaladhāriṇī \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The great goddess holding the Vāḍava fire stationed herself to the south-east of Someśa near the ocean.

## \|\| 1.34.33-34 \|\|

*snātvā'gnitīrthe pūrvaṃ tāṃ pūjayedvidhinā naraḥ \|*  
*daṃpatyorbhojanaṃ tatra paridhānaṃ sakañcu kam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*dattvā tato mahādevaṃ pūjayecca kaparddinam \|*  
*iti vṛttaṃ purā devi cākṣuṣasyāṃtare'bhavat \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. At the outset, a pilgrim should take his bath in the Agnitīrtha and then worship her in accordance with the injunctions. He should feed a couple and give them garments along with bodice. Then he should worship the great Lord Kapardin. O goddess (Gaurī) this incident happened formerly in the Cākṣuṣa Manvantara.

## \|\| 1.34.35-37 \|\|

*dadhīcyanvayajātasya vāḍavasya mahā tmanaḥ \|*  
*asminpunarmahādevi prāpte vaivasvateṃ'tare \|*  
*aurvastu bhārgave vaṃśe samutpanno mahādvijaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*saṃkṣipto'sau sarasvatyā devamātrā mahāprabhaḥ \|*  
*tāvatsthāsyatyapāṃ garbhe yāvanmanvatarāvadhiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*iti te kathitaṃ devi sarasvatyāḥ samudbhavam \|*  
*śrutaṃ pāpaharaṃ nṛṇāṃ kīrttidaṃ puṇyavarddhanam \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. This incident refers to the Vāḍava born in the family of Dadhīci. O great goddess, when this Vaivasvata Manvantara began, Aurva, the great Brāhmaṇa, was born in the family of Bhārgava. The Aurva of great refulgence was controlled (within limits) by Sarasvatī, the mother of Devas. Till the end of this Manvantara he will stay within the womb of the waters.

Thus, O goddess, the origin of Sarasvatī has been narrated to you. If it is listened to, it dispels the sins of men. It gives reputation and increases merits.

## Chapter 35 - Greatness of Agni Tīrtha

## \|\| 1.35.1-4 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*bhagavanbhārgave vaṃśe yastvaurvaḥ kathitastvayā \|*  
*vaivasvateṃ'tare cāsmiṃstasyotpattiṃ vada prabho \|\| 1 \|\|*

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*brāhmaṇā nihatā ye tu kṣatriyairvittakāraṇāt \|*  
*kṣayaṃ nītāstu te sarve saputrāśca sagarbhataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*mriyamāṇeṣu sarveṣu ekā strī samatiṣṭhata \|*  
*tayā tu rakṣito garbha ūrvordeśe nidhāya ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

*anyāsāṃ caiva nārīṇāṃ sarvāsāmapi bhāmini \|*  
*garbhāni pātitāstaistu dravyārthaṃ kṣatriyādhamaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

The Devī said:

1-4. O holy Lord, an Aurva of the Bhārgava family was mentioned by you. O Lord, do narrate his nativity in this Vaivasvata Manvantara.

## \|\| 1.35.5 \|\|

*kālāṃtare tato bhittvā kurudeśaṃ mahāprabhaḥ \|*  
*nirgatottaṃbhitaśirā jvaladāsyotibhīṣaṇaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

Brāhmaṇas had been killed by Kṣatriyas for the sake of wealth. They were entirely exterminated along with sons and children in the womb.

Among the many who were killed, there was a woman who concealed the foetus within the region of the thighs and protected it.

O beautiful lady (Gaurī), the foetuses of all other women were aborted by the base Kṣatriyas for the sake of monetary gain.

5\. At a later time, the highly refulgent foetus pierced through the region of thighs and came out with the head propped up. He was extremely terrible and his face (mouth) blazed.

## \|\| 1.35.6 \|\|

*tadvairaṃ hṛdi cādhāya dadāha vasudhātalam \|*  
*utpādya vahniṃ tapasā raudramaurvaṃ jalāśanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. With the feelings of enmity cherished in his heart, he performed penance and created a terrible Aurva fire that could devour water. With this he scorched the surface of the earth.

## \|\| 1.35.7 \|\|

*tamindraḥ plāvayāmāsa vṛṣṭyaughairvaravarṇini \|*  
*na śaśāka yadā netuṃ tadā sa yatavāksthitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O lady of excellent complexion (Gaurī), Indra flooded him with incessant heavy downpour. When he was not successful in driving him away, Indra became quiet (ceased to shower).

## \|\| 1.35.8 \|\|

*tato devāḥ sagaṃdharvā brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*abhavanbhayasaṃtrastāḥ sarve prāṃjalayaḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then all the Devas and Gandharvas became excessively frightened. All of them sought refuge in Brahmā and stood with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 1.35.9 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhagavanbhārgave vaṃśe jātaḥ ko'pi mahādyutiḥ \|*  
*agnirūpeṇa sarvaṃ sa dadāha vasudhātalam \|\| 9 \|\|*

The Devas said:

9\. O holy Sir, a highly refulgent one is born of the family of Bhārgava. In the form of fire, he has burnt the surface of the earth.

## \|\| 1.35.10 \|\|

*kṛto yatnaḥ purā'smābhistadvināśāya sattama \|*  
*jalena vṛddhimāyāti tato no bhayamāgatam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O most excellent one, formerly attempt was made by us to destroy him. But his (destructive) power enhances with (shower) of water. Hence we are afraid.

## \|\| 1.35.11 \|\|

*vinaṣṭe bhūtale deva agniṣṭomādikāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*ucchidyate tato'smākaṃ nāśo nūnaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O Lord, if the terrestrial region is destroyed, Agniṣṭoma and other holy rites will be stopped altogether. Thereby our destruction is certain.

## \|\| 1.35.12 \|\|

*tasmādyatnaṃ kuru vibho trailokyahitakāmyayā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Hence, O Lord, do something urgently for the benefit of the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.35.13-14 \|\|

*tato brahmā suraiḥ sārddhaṃ bhārgavaiśca maha rṣibhiḥ \|*  
*āgatya cābravīdaurvaṃ kimarthaṃ dahasi kṣitim \|\| 13 \|\|*

*virāmaḥ kriyatāṃ sadyo mamārthaṃ ca dvijottama \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Thereafter, Brahmā arrived there along with the Suras and the sages, Bhārgava and others, and said: “O Aurva, O most excellent one among Brāhmaṇas, why do you burn the earth. May this be stopped immediately for my sake.”

## \|\| 1.35.15-16 \|\|

*aurva uvāca \|*  
*eṣa eva nivṛtto'haṃ tava vākyena sattama \|*  
*eṣa vahnirmayotsṛṣṭaḥ sa vibho tava śāsanāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yathā gacchetsamudrāṃtaṃ tathā nītirvidhīya tām \|\| 16 \|\|*

Aurva said:

15-16. O most excellent one, O Lord, at your instance I have desisted (from burning). Let some means be found out so that the fire discharged by me reaches the vicinity of the ocean at your behest.

## \|\| 1.35.17 \|\|

*samāhūya tato devīṃ svāṃ sutāṃ padmasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*uvāca putri gaccha tvaṃ gṛhītvāgniṃ mahodadhim \|*  
*madvākyaṃ nānyathā kāryaṃ gaccha śīghraṃ mahāprabhe \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The Lotus-born Lord summoned his daughter, the goddess, and said: “O my highly refulgent daughter, take this fire and go to the great ocean. My instruction should not be disobeyed. Go quickly.”

## \|\| 1.35.18 \|\|

*sarasvatyuvāca \|*  
*eṣāsmi prasthitā deva tava vākyādasaṃśayam \|*  
*ityukte sādhu sādhvīti brahmaṇā samudāhṛtā \|\| 18 \|\|*

Sarasvatī said:

18a. Here, O Lord, I am setting out undoubtedly at your instance.

18b. When this was said the words “Excellent! Excellent!” were uttered by Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.35.19 \|\|

*tatobhimaṃtritaṃ vahniṃ kṣiptvā kuṃbhe hiraṇmaye \|*  
*prāyacchata sarasvatyai svayaṃ brahmā pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*āśiṣo vividhā dattvā provācedaṃ punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Brahmā, the grandfather, himself deposited the fire inspired by Mantras in a gold pot and handed it over to Sarasvatī. After offering diverse kinds of benediction, he said thus again and again:

## \|\| 1.35.20 \|\|

*gaccha putri na saṃtāpastvayā kāryaḥ kathaṃcana \|*  
*ariṣṭaṃ vraja paṃthānaṃ mā saṃtu paripanthinaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. “Do go, dear daughter. You need not strain yourself on any account. May you traverse the path without obstacles. Let there be no antagonists.”

## \|\| 1.35.21-23 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*evamuktā tadā tena brahmaṇā ca sarasvatī \|*  
*himavaṃtaṃ giriṃ prāpya pippalādāśramāttadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*udbhūtā sā tadā devī adhastādvṛkṣamūlataḥ \|*  
*tatkoṭara kuṭīkoṭipraviṣṭānāṃ dvijanmanām \|\| 22 \|\|*

*śrūyante vedanirghoṣā sarasāraktacetasām \|*  
*viṣṇurāste tatra devo devānāṃ pravaro guruḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

21-23. On being told thus by Brahmā, Sarasvatī reached Himavān. From the hermitage of Pippalāda she proceeded ahead. The goddess (river) came out from beneath the (Plakṣa) tree.

There were Brāhmaṇas at the place near the hollow of the tree, in their numerous huts. Their chanting of the Vedas was heard and their minds were engrossed in chanting in good taste. Lord Viṣṇu, the excellent preceptor of Devas, was present there.

## \|\| 1.35.24 \|\|

*tasmātsthānāttato devī pratīcyabhimukhaṃ yayau \|*  
*antarddhānena sā prāptā kedāraṃ himamadhyagam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. From that spot, the goddess (river) proceeded westwards. After vanishing (for a while) she reached Kedāra in the midst of snow.

## \|\| 1.35.25-26 \|\|

*tatsaṃplāvya gireḥ śṛṃgaṃ kedārasya puraḥ sthitā \|*  
*tenāgninā karasthena dahyamānā sarasvatī \|\| 25 \|\|*

*bhūmiṃ vidārya tasyādhaḥ praviṣṭā gajagāminī \|*  
*tadaṃtarddhānamārgeṇa pravṛttā paścimāmukhī \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. After flooding the peak of the mountain Kedāra, she stood before it. Being burnt by that fire held in the hand, Sarasvatī pierced the ground and entered beneath. Along that hidden path, she proceeded with face towards the west with the gait of an elephant.

## \|\| 1.35.27 \|\|

*pāpabhūmimatikramya bhūmiṃ bhittvā vini gatā \|*  
*tatra kūpaḥ samabhavannāmnā gandharvasaṃjñitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. After crossing the sinful region, she pierced the ground and came out. It became a well (Kūpa) by name Gandharva there.

## \|\| 1.35.28-29 \|\|

*tasmātkūpātpunardṛśyā sā babhūva mahānadī \|*  
*matiḥ smṛtistathā prajñā medhā buddhirgirādharā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*upāsikāḥ sarasvatyāḥ ṣaḍetāḥ prasthitāstadā \|*  
*punaḥ pravṛttā sā tasmādudbhedātpaścimāmukhī \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. The great river became visible beyond that well. Six Upāsikās (servants, tributaries) of Sarasvatī started therefrom, viz. Mati, Smṛti, Prajñā, Medhā, Buddhi and Girādharā. Further, that river proceeded ahead from the pierced sector towards the West.

## \|\| 1.35.30 \|\|

*bhūtīśvaraṃ samāyātā siddho yatra mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*bhūtīśvare samīpasthaṃ tatra prāptā manoramam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. She (River) came to Bhūtīśvara where there was a great sage, a Siddha. There is a charming region near Bhūtīśvara.

## \|\| 1.35.31 \|\|

*tasya dakṣiṇadiksaṃsthaṃ rudrakoṭyupalakṣitam \|*  
*śrīkaṃṭha deśaṃ vikhyātaṃ gatā sarvauṣadhīyutam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. It is stationed in the southern quarter. It contains a crore of Rudras. Then she reached the famous Śrīkaṇṭha Deśa (Kurujāṅgala) abounding in all herbs.

## \|\| 1.35.32 \|\|

*tasmātpuṇyatamāddeśācchrīkaṇṭhātsā manasvinī \|*  
*saṃprāptā vahninā sārddhaṃ kurukṣetraṃ sarasvatī \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. From that highly meritorious region Śrīkaṇṭha, the noble-minded Sarasvatī came to Kurukṣetra along with the fire.

## \|\| 1.35.33 \|\|

*punastasmātkurukṣetrādvirāṭanagarasya sā \|*  
*samudbhūtā samīpasthā antarddhānānmanoramā \|*  
*gopāyano giriryatra tatra sā punarudgatā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Then the charming river proceeded from Kurukṣetra and vanished when nearing the city of Virāṭa She further came up at the place where the mountain Gopāyana is situated.

## \|\| 1.35.34 \|\|

*gopāyitā keśavena yatra te pāṇḍunandanāḥ \|*  
*kurvaṃtaḥ svāni karmāṇi na kaiścidupalakṣitā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. It was at this place that the sons of Pāṇḍu were concealed by Keśava, while they carried on their activities. They were not noticed (found out) by anyone.

## \|\| 1.35.35 \|\|

*tatra kuṃḍe sthitā devī mahāpātakanāśinī \|*  
*puna rgopāyanāddevī kṣetraṃ prāptātiśobhanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. There the goddess (river), the destroyer of great sins, stayed in a Kuṇḍa. Again from Gopāyana the goddess (river) reached a highly splendid holy spot.

## \|\| 1.35.36-37 \|\|

*kharjurīvanamāpannā nandānāmnīti tatra sā \|*  
*sarasvatī punastasmādvanātkharjūrasaṃjñitāt \|\| 36 \|\|*

*merupādaṃ samāsādya mārkaṃḍāśramamāgatā \|*  
*yatra mārkaṃḍakaṃ tīrthaṃ merupāde samāśritam \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. She (river) reached Kharjūrīvana where she became well-known by the name Nandā. Sarasvatī left Kharjūrīvana and came to Merupāda (foot of the mountain Meru) and reached Mārkaṇḍāśrama. At this place there is the Mārkaṇḍaka Tlrtha situated at Merupāda.

## \|\| 1.35.38 \|\|

*sarasvatī punastasmādarbudāraṇyamāśritā \|*  
*gatā vaṭavanaṃ ramyaṃ mārkaṃḍeyāśramācchubhāt \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. From the splendid hermitage of Mārkaṇḍeya Sarasvatī proceeded to Arbudāraṇya (Mt. Abu) and went to the charming Vaṭavana.

## \|\| 1.35.39 \|\|

*tapastaptaṃ purā yatra vasiṣṭhena samāśritāt \|*  
*tasmādvaṭavanātpuṇyādudumbaravanaṃ gatā \|*  
*merupāde ca tatraiva taṇḍiryatrā tapattapaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. It was here that Vasiṣṭha performed a penance. From that meritorious Vaṭavana that had been resorted to by Vasiṣṭha, she came to Uduṃbara Vana. It was there that Taṇḍi performed a penance on Merupāda.

## \|\| 1.35.40 \|\|

*ūduṃbaravanāttasmātpunardevī sarasvatī \|*  
*antarddhānena śikharamanyatprāptā mahānadī \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. From that Uduṃbara Vana, the great holy river Sarasvatī went ahead concealed and reached another peak.

## \|\| 1.35.41 \|\|

*merupādaṃ tu sumahatsurasiddhaniṣevitam \|*  
*bhinnāṃjanacayākāraṃ golāṃgūlamiti smṛtam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. This Merupāda too is very great and it is resorted to by Suras and Siddhas. It resembles split collyrium and it is remembered by the name Golāṅgūla \[Golāṅgūlam\] (cow’s tail).

## \|\| 1.35.42 \|\|

*sthānaṃ manoramaṃ tasmādudgatā sā sumadhyamā \|*  
*vaṃśastaṃbātsuvipulā pravṛttā dakṣiṇāmukhī \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. It is a very fascinating spot. The lady of excellent middle line (i.e. river) rose up from the Vaṃśastaṃba (Bamboo cluster), spread widely and proceeded to the South.

## \|\| 1.35.43 \|\|

*tatrodgamavaṭastasyāstatsamākhyo vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ prabhṛti sā devī suprabhaṃ prakaṭā sthitā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The Vaṭa (holy fig tree) from which it came up is well-known as Udgamavaṭa. Thenceforth, that goddess (the river) continues to be manifest with excellent lustre.

## \|\| 1.35.44 \|\|

*aṃtarddhānaṃ parityajya prāṇināmanukampayā \|*  
*tasyāstaṭeṣu ramyeṣu saṃti tīrthāni koṭiśaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. She has now abandoned the state of concealment, due to her compassion for all living beings. On her beautiful banks, there are crores of Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.35.45 \|\|

*teṣu tīrtheṣu sarveṣu dharmahetuḥ sarasvatī \|*  
*rudrāvatāra mārge'sminpravaraṃ prathamaṃ smṛtam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. In all those Tīrthas, the spiritual character is derived from Sarasvatī. On this path, Rudrāvatāra is remembered as the first and the foremost.

## \|\| 1.35.46 \|\|

*tarattaraṃganāmāḍhyaṃ kākatīrthaṃ mahāprabham \|*  
*tatra tīrthaṃ punastvanyattīrthaṃ dhāreśvaraṃ smṛtam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The Kāka Tīrtha of great refulgence designated as Tara Taraṅga is a great Tīrtha. There is a Tīrtha remembered as Dhāreśvara.

## \|\| 1.35.47 \|\|

*dhāreśvarātpunaścānyadgaṃgodbhedamiti smṛtam \|*  
*sārasvataṃ tathā gāṃgaṃ yatraikaṃ saṃsthitaṃ jalam \|*  
*tasmādanyatparaṃ tīrthaṃ puṃḍarīkaṃ tataḥ param \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Another Tīrtha beyond Dhāreśvara is remembered as Gaṅgodbheda. It is the place where the waters of Sarasvatī and Gaṅgā mingle together. There is another greater Tīrtha beyond it called Puṇḍarīka.

## \|\| 1.35.48-50 \|\|

*mātṛtīrthaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ sarvātaṃkaharaṃ param \|*  
*mātṛtīrthātpunastasmānnātidūre vyavasthitam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*tīrthaṃ tvanarakaṃnāma narakārti bhayāpaham \|*  
*tatastasmādanarakāttīrthamanyatpunaḥ sthitam \|\| 49 \|\|*

*saṃgameśvaranāmāḍhyaṃ prasiddhaṃ tanmahītale \|*  
*tatastasmātpunaścānyattīrthaṃ koṭīśvarāhvayam \|\| 50 \|\|*

48-50. The highly meritorious Mātṛtīrtha is fully destructive of all worries and fears. The Tīrtha by the name Anaraka is situated not very far from Mātṛtīrtha. It dispels the distress and fear caused by hell. Beyond that Anaraka Tīrtha, the other Tīrtha named Saṅgameśvara is situated. It is very well-known all over the earth. Beyond it is again another Tīrtha named Koṭīśvara.

## \|\| 1.35.51 \|\|

*tatastasmānmahādevi śaṃbhukuṇḍeśvaraṃ smṛtam \|*  
*tīrthe sarasvatītīre tasminsiddheśvaraṃ smṛtam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Beyond it, O great goddess, Śaṃbhukuṇḍeśvara is remembered among the Tīrthas on the banks of Sarasvatī. So also is Siddheśvara.

## \|\| 1.35.52 \|\|

*siddheśvarātpunastasmātpravṛttā paścimāmukhī \|*  
*paścimaṃ sāgaraṃ gaṃtuṃ sakhīṃ smṛtvā ruroda sā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. From Siddheśvara, the river (Sarasvatī) flows westwards in order to reach the Western ocean. There she remembered her companion and wept for her.

## \|\| 1.35.53 \|\|

*sthitvā pūrvamukhā devī hā gaṃgeti vinā tvayā \|*  
*ekākinī maṃdabhāgyā kva gamiṣyāmyabāṃdhavā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The goddess (river) stood facing the east and lamented, “Alas! Gaṅgā, I am lonely without you! Unlucky and bereft of kinsmen, how shall I go?”

## \|\| 1.35.54 \|\|

*tāṃ vijñāya tato gaṃgā rudatīṃ śokakarśitām \|*  
*śīghraṃ svargātsamāyātā tīrthānāṃ koṭibhiḥ saha \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Becoming aware that she was rendered lean due to grief and was lamenting, Gaṅgā hastened from heaven along with a crore of Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.35.55 \|\|

*tato duḥkhaṃ parityajya tatra prācī sarasvatī \|*  
*sarvadevaguṇaiyuktā evaṃ tatra sthitā'bhavat \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Thereupon, Prācī (Eastern) Sarasvatī gave up grieving. She stationed herself there accompanied by all the groups of Devas.

## \|\| 1.35.56 \|\|

*tatra siddhavaṭaṃnāma tīrthaṃ paitāmahaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*vaṭeśvarasya purataḥ sarvapāpakṣayaṃkaram \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. There, in front of Vaṭeśvara is the Tīrtha of Pitāmaha named Siddhavaṭa. It destroys all sins.

## \|\| 1.35.57 \|\|

*trikālaṃ yatra rudrastu samāgatya vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*tanmahālayamityuktaṃ sthānaṃ tasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Thrice every day, Rudra arrives there and stays. It is the holy spot of that great Soul and is called Mahālaya.

## \|\| 1.35.58 \|\|

*piṃḍatārakamityetatprācīnaṃ tīrthamuttamam \|*  
*kumbhakukṣigiristhaṃ tatpitrye karmaṇi siddhidam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. There is an excellent ancient Tīrtha named Piṇḍatāraka situated on the mountain Kuṃbhakukṣigiri. It accords great Siddhi in rites connected with the Manes.

## \|\| 1.35.59 \|\|

*prācīneśvaradevasya purobhūtaṃ prati ṣṭhitam \|*  
*prācī sarasvatī yatra tatra kiṃ mṛgyate param \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. It is well-settled in front of Lord Prācīneśvara. What other thing need be sought after in a place where Prācī Sarasvatī is present!

## \|\| 1.35.60 \|\|

*nivṛtte bhārate yuddhe tatra tīrthe kirīṭinā \|*  
*prāyaścittaṃ purā cīrṇaṃ viṣṇunā preritā tmanā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. When the Mahābhārata war was concluded Kirīṭin (Arjuna) performed expiatory rites in that Tīrtha on being directed by Viṣṇu earlier.

## \|\| 1.35.61 \|\|

*tena tasmādvinirmuktaḥ pātakātpūrvasaṃcitāt \|*  
*naratīrthaṃ tataḥ khyātaṃ tatra pāpabhayāpaham \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. By that rite he became rid of that sin incurre \[incurred?\] earlier. Therefore, it is well-known as Naratīrtha. It dispels all fears of sins.

## \|\| 1.35.62 \|\|

*naratīrthādanyatīrthaṃ puṃḍarīkamiti smṛtam \|*  
*arjunena sahāgatya yatra snāto hariḥ priye \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. O my beloved, there is another Tīrtha remembered as Puṇḍarīka different from Naratīrtha. Hari came there along with Arjuna and took his holy bath.

## \|\| 1.35.63 \|\|

*prācīneśātparaṃ tīrthaṃ vālakhilyeśvaraṃ mahat \|*  
*tatra tasmānmahātīrthāttīrthamanyanmaho dayam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Beyond Prācīneśa there is a great Tīrtha (named) Vālakhilyeśvara. Beyond that great Tīrtha there is another Tīrtha of great efficacy.

## \|\| 1.35.64-65 \|\|

*gaṃgāsamāgamaṃnāma tīrthamanyanmahodayam \|*  
*tatrālokya punardevīṃ dīnāsyāṃ dīnamānasām \|\| 64 \|\|*

*brahmāsṛjatsakhīṃ tasyāḥ kapilāṃ vipulekṣaṇām \|*  
*hariṇīṃ harirapyāśu vajriṇīmapi devarāṭ \|*  
*nyaṃkuṃ vinodanārthaṃ ca sarasvatyā dadau haraḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. There is another Tīrtha of great efficacy named Gaṅgāsaṃgama. On seeing the goddess (river) with a gloomy face and dejected in mind, Brahma created for her a companion of wide eyes named Kapilā. Hari hastily created Hariṇī and the Lord of Devas (Indra) Vajriṇī. Hara gave Nyaṅku to Sarasvatī in order to humour her.

## \|\| 1.35.66 \|\|

*tataḥ prahṛṣṭā sā devī devādeśātsarasvatī \|*  
*tasmādgantuṃ samārabdhā prācīnā pāpanāśinī \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Thereupon, the goddess (river) Prācīna Sarasvatī became happy. At the behest of the Lord, she, the destroyer of sins, proceeded to go.

## \|\| 1.35.67 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*dakṣiṇāṃ diśamāsthāya punaḥ paścānmukhī tadā \|*  
*sarasvatī mahādevī vaḍavānaladhāriṇī \|*  
*taduttare taṭe tīrthamekadvāramiti smṛtam \|\| 67 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

67\. At the outset, the river flowed towards south and then turned westwards. Sarasvatī, the great goddess continued to hold the Vaḍavānala. On her northern bank is the Tīrtha remembered as Ekadvāra.

## \|\| 1.35.68 \|\|

*ekadvāreṇa yatsenā svargaṃ prāptā tato varāt \|*  
*tasmāttīrthātpunaścānyattīrthaṃ yatra guheśvaraḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. It is so called because the army went to Svarga through Ekadvāra (single door) from that forest. There is another Tīrtha beyond, where the deity is Guheśvara.

## \|\| 1.35.69 \|\|

*guhena sthāpitaḥ pūrvaṃ yatra devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*guheśvarānnātidūre vaṭeśvaramiti smṛtam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Formerly it was installed by Guha, at the place where Lord Maheśvara is present. Not far from Guheśvara is the Tīrtha named Vaṭeśvara.

## \|\| 1.35.70-71 \|\|

*divyaṃ sarasvatītīre vyāsenārādhitaṃ purā \|*  
*āmarddakī nadī yatra sarasvatyā sahaikatām \|\| 70 \|\|*

*saṃprāptā tanmahātīrthaṃ phaladaṃ sarvadehinām \|*  
*āmardakī saṃgamaṃ taṃ nāpuṇyo veda kaścana \|*  
*saṃgameśvaranāmeti tatra liṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. It is a divine Tīrtha on the banks of Sarasvatī. Formerly it was propitiated by Vyāsa. The great Tīrtha where the river Āmardakī unites with Sarasvatī, accords benefit to all embodied beings. No one without merit can know the confluence of Āmardakī. A Liṅga named Saṅgameśvara has been installed there.

## \|\| 1.35.72-73 \|\|

*muṇḍīśvareti ca tathā prasiddhimagamatkṣitau \|*  
*muṃḍīśvarasamīpasthaṃ sarasvatyāṃ mahodayam \|\| 72 \|\|*

*nāmnā yatprāṅmukhaṃ tīrthaṃ sarasvatyāstaṭe sthitam \|*  
*māṃḍavyeśvaranāmnā vai yatreśaḥ saṃpratiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

72-73. It became famous over the earth by the name Muṇḍīśvara.

In the vicinity of Muṇḍīśvara there is an east-facing Tīrtha on Sarasvatī. It is situated on the banks of Sarasvatī. It is named Mahodaya. The Lord installed there is known by the name Māṇḍavyeśvara.

## \|\| 1.35.74 \|\|

*pīlukarṇikasaṃjñaṃ tu tīrthamanyatpunastataḥ \|*  
*sarasvatītīragatamṛṣiṇā sevitaṃ mahat \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. There is another Tīrtha named Pīlukarṇika on the banks of Sarasvatī. It is a great Tīrtha resorted to by sages.

## \|\| 1.35.75 \|\|

*tasmādanyatsarasvatyāṃ tīrthaṃ dvāravatī smṛtam \|*  
*tīrthānāṃ pravaraṃ devi yatra saṃnihito hariḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. There is another Tīrtha on the banks of the river. It is remembered as Dvāravatī. O goddess (Gaurī), it is the foremost of all Tīrthas and Hari is present there.

## \|\| 1.35.76 \|\|

*tatastasya samīpasthaṃ tīrthaṃ govatsasaṃjñitam \|*  
*yatrāvatīrya govatsasvarūpeṇāṃbikāpatiḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Further, situated nearby is the Tīrtha called Govatsa. It was here that the Consort of Aṃbikā (i.e. Śiva) descended in the form of a calf.

## \|\| 1.35.77 \|\|

*svayaṃ bhūliṃgarūpeṇa saṃsthitastejasāṃ nidhiḥ \|*  
*govatsānnairṛte bhāge dṛśyate lohayaṣṭikā \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. The storehouse of refulgence stayed there in the form of Bhūliṅga. On the south-west of Govatsa is seen a Lohayaṣṭikā (Iron Post).

## \|\| 1.35.78-80 \|\|

*svayaṃbhūliṃgarūpeṇa rudrastatra svayaṃ sthitaḥ \|*  
*ekaviṃśati vārasya bhaktyā piṃḍasya yatphalam \|\| 78 \|\|*

*gaṃgāyāṃ prāpyate puṃsāṃ śrāddhenaikena tatra tat \|*  
*tatastasmānmahātīrthādbālakrīḍanakī yathā \|\| 79 \|\|*

*sakhībhiḥ sahitā tatra krīḍatā'sau yathecchayā \|*  
*ānulomyavilomyena dakṣiṇenottareṇa ca \|\| 80 \|\|*

78-80. Rudra himself is stationed there in the form of Bhūliṅga.

By performing a single Śrāddha there men obtain the benefit that is usually derived by devoutly offering rice-balls twenty-one times in Gaṅgā.

Then from that great Tīrtha, the river proceeds ahead along with her friends like a child with its toys. Sometimes she flows southwards, sometimes northwards. Thus she flows backwards and forwards.

## \|\| 1.35.81-82 \|\|

*rullaṃ prāpya punardevī samudbhūtā manoramā \|*  
*rullaṃ nāma puraṃ yatra sṛṣṭaṃ devena śaṃbhunā \|\| 81 \|\|*

*saha devaistu pārvatyā dhārāyaṃtraprayogakaiḥ \|*  
*ekaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu śaṃbhunā tatra rullitam \|\| 82 \|\|*

81-82. After reaching Rulla, the goddess (river) becomes charming once again. It was here that the city Rulla was created by Lord Śaṃbhu. He played for a period of a thousand years with Pārvatī and the Devas jetting out water from the Dhārāyantra (a pump like instrument from which water is jetted out against other players).

## \|\| 1.35.83 \|\|

*rullaṃ tatra hradaṃ nāma sarasvatyāṃ mahodayam \|*  
*sākṣāttatra mahādeva ānaṃdeśvarasaṃjñitaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Rulla is a whirlpool of great efficacy in Sarasvatī. Mahādeva is directly present there by the name of Ānandeśvara.

## \|\| 1.35.84 \|\|

*paścimena sthitaṃ tatra śambhorāyatanasya tu \|*  
*sa merordakṣiṇe pāde nakhastu parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. To the west of the temple of Śaṃbhu, on the southern foot-hill of Meru, there is a nail-like mark. It is highly glorified.

## \|\| 1.35.85 \|\|

*paśyaṃti ye narāḥ samyakte'pi pāpavivarjitāḥ \|*  
*aśvamedhasahasrasya prāpnuvaṃti phalaṃ dhruvam \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Men who view this perfectly, become rid of sins. They certainly attain the benefit of a thousand horse-sacrifices.

## \|\| 1.35.86 \|\|

*paratastasya kūṣmāṃḍamunestatrāśramaṃ mahat \|*  
*kūṣmāṃḍeśvarasaṃjñaṃ tu tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Beyond it is the great hermitage of Sage Kūṣmāṇḍa. The Tīrtha called Kūṣmāṇḍeśvara is famous all over the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.35.87 \|\|

*kollādevī sthitā tatra sarvapāpabhayāpahā \|*  
*antarddhānena tāṃ kollāṃ saṃprāptā sā mahānadī \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. It is there that the goddess Kollā is stationed. She dispels all sins and fears. The great river reached the vicinity of Kollā, by proceeding under ground (in a concealed manner).

## \|\| 1.35.88 \|\|

*tato'pyaṃtarhitā bhūtvā saṃprāptā tu manoramam \|*  
*sānuṃ madanasaṃjñaṃ tu kṣetraṃ siddhaniṣevitam \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Again she became hidden (went underground) and reached a very charming tableland called Madana. It is a holy spot resorted to by Siddhas.

## \|\| 1.35.89 \|\|

*tato'pyaṃtarhitā bhūtvā punaḥ prāptā himācalam \|*  
*khādirāmodanāmānaṃ sarvartukusumojjvalam \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Going under cover once again, she (the river) reached a snow-clad mountain named Khādirāmoda. This place remarkably shines with the flowers of all the seasons.

## \|\| 1.35.90 \|\|

*tatrāruhya vilokyātha dadarśa sumanoramama \|*  
*kṣārodaṃ paścimāśāsthaṃ ghanavṛṃdamivonnatam \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Mounting it she espied the highly fascinating Kṣāroda (Sea) lofty like a clustre of clouds in the western quarter.

## \|\| 1.35.91 \|\|

*evaṃvidhaṃ ca taṃ tatra sā vilokya mahāprabhā \|*  
*harṣātpaṃcānanā bhūtvā devakāryārthamudyatā \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. On seeing this in this manner, the highly refulgent (river) became five-faced (five currents, mouths of the river) in her delight She then got ready to accomplish the task of Devas.

## \|\| 1.35.92 \|\|

*hariṇī vajriṇī nyaṃkuḥ kapilā ca sarasvatī \|*  
*paṃcasrotāḥ sthitā tatra muninoktā sarasvatī \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. The five channels are Hariṇī, Vajriṇī, Nyaṅku, Kapilā and Sarasvatī. On being told by the sage, Sarasvatī stood there with the five channels.

## \|\| 1.35.93 \|\|

*śramāpanodaṃ kurvāṇā munīnāṃ yatra saṃsthitā \|*  
*tattatpādakamityuktaṃ tīrthaṃ tīrthārthināṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ pātakānāṃ ca śodhanaṃ tadvarānane \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. The places where she stood dispelling the fatigue of sages, are each called after the name of the sage concerned (the Tīrtha of that sage). O lady of excellent countenance (Gaurī), these Tīrthas dispels all the sins of the men desirous of (undertaking pilgrimage) to them.

## \|\| 1.35.94 \|\|

*khādirāmodamāsādya tatrasthā vīkṣya sāgaram \|*  
*gantuṃ pravṛttā taṃ vahnimādāya surasundari \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Reaching Khādirāmoda and tarrying there she looked at the ocean. Then, O beautiful goddess, she took the fire and began to proceed ahead.

## \|\| 1.35.95 \|\|

*dagdhvā kṛtasmaraṃ devī punarādāya vāḍavam \|*  
*samudrasya samīpasthā sthitā hṛṣṭata nūruhā \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. After burning Kṛtasmara, the goddess (river) took up the Vāḍava once again and stood in the vicinity of the ocean. In her delight, her hairs stood on ends.

## \|\| 1.35.96 \|\|

*tataḥ praviṣṭā sā devī agādhe lavaṇāṃbhasi \|*  
*vāḍavaṃ vahnimādāya jalamadhye vyasarjayat \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Then goddess entered deep into the salt sea. She took the Vāḍava fire and cast (Vāḍava) off into the middle of the waters.

## \|\| 1.35.97 \|\|

*tatastasyāḥ punaḥ prītaḥ svaya meva hutāśanaḥ \|*  
*taddṛṣṭvā duṣkaraṃ karma vacanaṃ cedamabravīt \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Then Hutāśana (Fire-god) himself became pleased with her. On seeing that difficult task accomplished, he spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.35.98 \|\|

*parituṣṭo'smi te bhadre varaṃ varaya suvrate \|*  
*tatte dāsyāmyahaṃ prīto yadyapi syātsu durlabham \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. “O fair lady, I am pleased with you. O lady of excellent holy rites, choose your boon. That I shall gladly grant you even if it be very difficult to get.”

## \|\| 1.35.99 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*pragṛhya valayaṃ hastādidaṃ vacanamabravīt \|*  
*idaṃ me valayaṃ vahne vaktre dhāryaṃ sadā tvayā \|\| 99 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

99\. She took off a bangle from her forearm and spoke these words: “O Vahni, this bangle of mine should always be worn round your mouth.

## \|\| 1.35.100 \|\|

*anena śakyate yāvattāvattoyaṃ samāhara \|*  
*na tvayā śoṣaṇīyo'yaṃ samudaḥ saritāṃpatiḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Draw only that much water which can be drawn through this. Samudra, the Lord of rivers, should not be dried away by you.”

## \|\| 1.35.101 \|\|

*bāḍhamityeva coktvā sa praviṣṭo nidhimaṃbhasām \|*  
*evameṣā mahādevi prabhāse tu sarasvatī \|*  
*gṛhītvā vāḍavaṃ prāptā tuṣṭyarthaṃ ca manīṣiṇām \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. After saying “So it shall be”, he entered the storehouse of waters. It is thus, O great goddess, that Sarasvatī came to Prabhāsa taking the Vāḍava for the sake of the pleasure of noble-minded ones.

## \|\| 1.35.102 \|\|

*sā viśrāṃtā kurukṣetre bhadrāvarte ca bhāmini \|*  
*puṣkare śrīkalā devī prabhāse ca mahānadī \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. O beautiful lady, that great river halted and rested at Kurukṣetra, Bhadrāvarta and Śrīsthala.

## \|\| 1.35.103 \|\|

*devamāteti sā tatra saṃsthitā lavaṇodadhau \|*  
*asminmanvaṃtare devi ādau tretāyuge purā \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. In this Manvantara, O goddess, formerly in the first Tretāyuga she merged within the salty ocean in the form of Devamātā (Mother of the Devas).

## \|\| 1.35.104 \|\|

*iti vṛttaṃ sarasvatyā vāḍavāgnestathābhavat \|*  
*manvantare vyatīte'sminbhavitā'nyastu vāḍavaḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. This is what took place in the case of Sarasvatī and Vāḍava fire. When this Manvantara passes off another Vāḍava will be born.

## \|\| 1.35.105 \|\|

*jvālāmukheti nāmnā vai rudrakrodhādbhaviṣyati \|*  
*sarasvatyāstathā nāma khyātiṃ brāhmīti yāsyati \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. It will be born of the fury of Rudra under the name Jvālāmukha. Then the name of Sarasvatī will become well-known as Brāhmī.

## \|\| 1.35.106 \|\|

*sarasvatīti vai loke vartate nāma sāṃpratam \|*  
*atītaṃ nāma yattasyāḥ kamaṃḍalubhaveti ca \|*  
*ratnākareti sāmudraṃ satyaṃ nāmāṃtaraṃ purā \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Now in the world, the name current is Sarasvatī. Her name in the past was Kamaṇḍalubhavā (‘born of the water-pot’). It is true that another earlier name of Samudra (ocean) was Ratnākara (‘storehouse of jewels’).

## \|\| 1.35.107 \|\|

*asminmanvaṃtare devi sāgareti prakīrtitam \|*  
*kṣāṃrodeti bhaviṣyaṃ tu nāma devi prakīrti tam \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. O goddess, in this Manvantara it is glorified as Sāgara. It has been proclaimed, O goddess, that the future name is Kṣāroda.

## \|\| 1.35.108 \|\|

*evaṃ jānāti yaḥ kaścitsa tīrthaphalamaśnute \|*  
*svarganiḥśreṇisaṃbhūtā prabhāse tu sarasvatī \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Whoever knows it thus attains the benefit of the Tīrtha.

In the holy spot Prabhāsa Sarasvatī has become a ladder unto Svarga (heaven).

## \|\| 1.35.109 \|\|

*nāpuṇyavadbhiḥ saṃprāptuṃ puṃbhiḥ śakyā mahānadī \|*  
*prācī sarasvatī devi sarvatra ca sudurlabhā \|*  
*viśeṣeṇa kurukṣetre prabhāse puṣkare tathā \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. The great river cannot be attained (reached) by persons without merit. O goddess, Prācī Sarasvatī is everywhere very difficult of access, and especially so in Kurukṣetra, Prabhāsa and Puṣkara.

## \|\| 1.35.110 \|\|

*evaṃprabhāvā sā devī vaḍavānala dhāriṇī \|*  
*agnitīrthasamīpasthā sthitā devī sarasvatī \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. That goddess (river) holding the Vaḍavānala has such efficacy. The goddess Sarasvatī stood very near Agni Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.35.111 \|\|

*tāmādau pūjayedyastu sa tīrthaphalamaśnute \|*  
*sāgaraṃ yacca tattīrthaṃ pāpaghnaṃ puṇya varddhanam \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. One who worships her at the outset attains the benefit of the Tīrtha. That Sāgara Tīrtha is destructive of sins and it augments merit.

## \|\| 1.35.112-113 \|\|

*darśanādeva tasyaiva mahākratuphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*agnicitkapilā satrī rājā bhikṣurmahodadhiḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭamātrāḥ punaṃtyete tasmā tpaśyeddhi bhāvitaḥ \|*  
*agnitīrthe naraḥ snātvā pāvake prakṣipettataḥ \|*  
*guggulaṃ bhārasahitaṃ sogniloke mahīyate \|\| 113 \|\|*

112-113. By its mere sight, one attains the benefit of a great Kratu. An Agnicit (performer of Agnihotra), a Kapilā (the tawny-coloured cow), a Sattrī (one who performs a Sattra sacrifice), a king, a holy mendicant and the great ocean—these sanctify on being merely viewed. Hence one should view them with purity.

After taking the holy bath in Agnitīrtha a man should cast into the holy fire a Bhāra weight (twenty Tolas) of Guggula. He is honoured in Agniloka.

## \|\| 1.35.114 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃkṣepataḥ prokto hyagni tīrthamahodayaḥ \|*  
*sarasvatyāśca māhātmyaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. Thus has been briefly described the prosperity arising from Agnitīrtha and the greatness of Sarasvatī that is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.35.115 \|\|

*snātvāgnitīrthe vidhivatkaṃkaṇaṃ prakṣipetataḥ \|*  
*suvarṇasya mahādevi yathāvittānu sārataḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. After taking the holy bath duly in Agnitīrtha, O great goddess, one should cast into it a gold bangle as permitted by one’s funds.

## \|\| 1.35.116-119 \|\|

*tataḥ sarasvatīṃ pūjya kapardinamathārcayet \|\| 116 \|\|*

*tataḥ kedāranāmānaṃ bhīmeśvaramataḥparam \|*  
*bhairaveśvaranāmānaṃ caṇḍīśvaramataḥ param \|\| 117 \|\|*

*tataḥ someśvaraṃ devaṃ pūjayedvidhivannaraḥ \|*  
*navagraheśvarāniṣṭvā rudraikādaśakaṃ tathā \|\| 118 \|\|*

*tataḥ saṃpūjayeddevaṃ brahmāṇaṃ bālarūpiṇam \|*  
*evaṃ raudrī samākhyātā yātrā pātakanāśinī \|\| 119 \|\|*

116-119. Then after worshipping Sarasvatī, the devotee should adore Kapardin.

Then the deity named Keḍāra and Bhīmeśvara thereafter, then the deity named Bhairaveśvara and then Caṇḍīśvara, thereafter the man should duly adore Lord Someśvara. After worshipping Navagraheśvaras and the eleven Rudras, one should adore Lord Brahmā in the form of a boy. Thus the Yātrā (Pilgrimage) called Rādrī (Raudrī?) is accomplished. It is destructive of sins.

## \|\| 1.35.120-122 \|\|

*māhātmyamakhilaṃ tasyā yo jānāti narottamaḥ \|*  
*nivasankṣetramadhye tu sa tīrthaphalamaśnute \|\| 120 \|\|*

*evaṃ kṛtvā tato gacchenmahādevīṃ sarasvatīm \|\| 121 \|\|*

*sarasvatīvasasamā kuto guṇāḥ sarasvatīvāsasamā kuto ratiḥ \|*  
*sarasvatīṃ prāpya divaṃ gatā narāḥ punaḥ smariṣyaṃti nadīṃ sarasvatīm \|\| 122 \|\|*

120-122. An excellent man who resides within the Kṣetra and fully knows the greatness, obtains the benefit of the Tīrtha. After doing thus, the devotee goes to the great goddess Sarasvatī. Where else can the merit on a par with that of residence in Sarasvatī be obtained? Where else is pleasure on a par with that of residence in Sarasvatī? Men who went up to heaven after reaching Sarasvatī, will again remember the river.

## Chapter 36 - Greatness of Prācī Sarasvatī

## \|\| 1.36.1-2 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*yadetadbhavatā proktaṃ prācī sarvatra durllabhā \|*  
*viśeṣeṇa kurukṣetre prabhāse puṣkare tathā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kathaṃ prabhāsamāsādya saṃsthitā pāpanāśinī \|*  
*māhātmyamakhilaṃ tasyāḥ prācyāḥ pātakanāśanam \|*  
*kathayasva maheśāna yadyahaṃ te priyā vibho \|\| 2 \|\|*

The Devī said:

1-2. It has been said by you that Prācī Sarasvatī is difficult of access everywhere, especially in Kurukṣetra, Prabhāsa and Puṣkara. How did this river destructive of all sins reach Prabhāsa and halt there eventually? O Lord Maheśāna, describe fully the greatness that is destructive of sins, of that Prācī, if I am your beloved.

## \|\| 1.36.3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*sādhu proktaṃ tvayā bhadre prācī sarvatra durlabhā \|*  
*kurukṣetre puṣkare ca tasmātprābhāsike'dhikā \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

3\. O fair lady, you have said pertinently. Prācī is difficult of access everywhere, in Kurukṣetra, and Puṣkara and more so in the holy spot of Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.36.4 \|\|

*prabhāse tu mahādevī prācīṃ pāpapraṇāśinīm \|*  
*nāpuṇyo veda deveśi karmanirmūlanakṣamām \|\| 4 \|\|*
