4\. O great goddess, O goddess of Devas, no one devoid of merit obtains in Prabhāsa, Prācī the destroyer of sins and capable of rooting out (adverse) Karmas.

## \|\| 1.36.5 \|\|

*ye pibaṃti narāḥ puṇyāṃ prācīṃ devīṃ sarasvatīm \|*  
*na te manuṣyā vijñeyāḥ satyaṃsatyaṃ varānane \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. It is the truth, (I repeat) it is true that men who drink the water of Prācī Sarasvatī should never be thought of as mere men, O lady of excellent countenance.

## \|\| 1.36.6 \|\|

*dhanyāste munayaste ca puṇyāste ca tapasvinaḥ \|*  
*ye ca sārasvataṃ toyaṃ pibaṃtyaharahaḥ sadā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Blessed indeed are those sages and meritorious ascetics who drink the waters of the Sarasvatī everyday.

## \|\| 1.36.7 \|\|

*devāste na manuṣyāste nadīstisra pibaṃti ye \|*  
*caṃdrabhāgāṃ ca gaṃgāṃ ca tathā devīṃ sassvatīm \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. They are gods. They are not human beings, but gods who drink the waters of the three rivers, namely Gaṅgā, Candrabhāgā (Chinab) and the divine Sarasvatī.

## \|\| 1.36.8 \|\|

*bhuktvā vā yadi vā'bhuktvā divā vā yadi vā niśi \|*  
*na kālaniyamastatra yatra prācī sarasvatī \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. This can be after taking food or while abstaining from food. It may be by day or at night; In Prācī Sarasvatī there is no time restriction (for drinking water).

## \|\| 1.36.9 \|\|

*prācīṃ sarasvatīṃ ye tu pibaṃti satataṃ mṛgāḥ \|*  
*te'pi svargaṃ gamiṣyaṃti yajñairdvijavarā yathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Even those animals that drink Prācī Sarasvatī always will go to Svarga as in the case of excellent Brāhmaṇas (who do so) through Yajñas.

## \|\| 1.36.10 \|\|

*sarvakāmaprapūrtyarthaṃ nṛṇāṃ tatkṣetramuttamam \|*  
*ciṃtāmaṇisamā devī yatra prācī sarasvatī \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. In the case of laymen, that excellent holy place serves the purpose of fulfilling all desires. There, Prācī Sarasvatī is on a par with Cintāmaṇi (the fabulous philosopher’s stone yielding everything wished for).

## \|\| 1.36.11 \|\|

*yathā kāmadughā gāvaḥ sarvakāmaphalapradāḥ \|*  
*tathā svargāpavargābhyāṃ prācī devī sarasvatī \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Just as the Kāmadhuk (wish-yielding) cows accord the benefit of achieving all desires, so also the divine Prācī Sarasvatī through heavenly pleasures and absolute salvation.

## \|\| 1.36.12 \|\|

*aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi munīnāmūrdhvaretasām \|*  
*yatra sthitāni saṃnyāsaṃ tasmātkimadhikaṃ smṛtam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. What else can. be regarded as superior to this (holy spot) where eighty-eight thousand sages of sublimated sexuality have stayed on, renouncing the idea of leaving for other holy spots?

IB. It is the place where Maṅkaṇaka attained Siddhi. He observed restrictions and self-control in Prācīna (a holy spot on the Prācī river). O lady of excellent countenance, I performed the expiatory rite for (the sin of) Brāhmaṇa-slaughter in that place.

## \|\| 1.36.14 \|\|

*vṛṣatīrthe mahāpuṇye prācīkūlasamāśrite \|*  
*nivṛtte bhārate yuddhe tasmiṃstīrthe kirīṭinā \|*  
*prāyaścittaṃ purā cīrṇaṃ viṣṇunā preritātmanā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. When the Mahābhārata war concluded, Kirīṭin (Arjuna) performed expiatory rite on being directed by Viṣṇu (Kṛṣṇa). He performed the rite in that Tīrtha, the highly meritorious Tīrtha situated on the banks of Prācī.

## \|\| 1.36.15 \|\|

*trailokye sarvatīrthānāṃ tattīrthaṃ pravaraṃ smṛtam \|*  
*pāpaghnaṃ puṇyajananaṃ prāṇināṃ puṇyakīrttida \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Among all the Tīrthas of the three worlds, that Tīrtha is remembered as the most excellent. It destroys the sins of living beings. It generates (confers) merits and it accords meritorious renown.

## \|\| 1.36.16 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*āhaivamukte sā devī śaṃkaraṃ loka śaṃkaram \|*  
*prāyaścittaṃ kathaṃ prāptaḥ pārthaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ \|*  
*jñātikṣayodbhavaṃ pāpaṃ kathaṃ nāśamagātprabho \|\| 16 \|\|*

Sūta said:

16\. On this being told thus, the goddess spoke to Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds: “O Lord, how did Pārtha (Arjuna), the conqueror of the cities of the enemies, undergo the expiation? How did the sin caused by the killing of the kinsmen get dissolved?”

## \|\| 1.36.17 \|\|

*evamuktaḥ punaḥ prāha viśveśo nīlalohitaḥ \|*  
*prāyaścittasya saṃprāptaḥ kāraṇaṃ tadyathā sthitam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On being asked thus, Nīlalohita, the Lord of the universe, spoke of the manner in which he realized the expiation as obtaining there.

## \|\| 1.36.18 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇuṣvāvahitā bhadre kathāṃ pātakanāśinīm \|*  
*yāṃ śrutvā mānavo bhaktyā pavitrātmā prajāyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

18\. O fair lady, listen with attention to the story that ḍestroys sins. By listening to this devoutly, a man becomes one of purified soul.

## \|\| 1.36.19 \|\|

*yo'sau devi samākhyātaḥ kirīṭī śvetavāhanaḥ \|*  
*sa jitvā kauravānsarvānsaṃhṛtya hayakuñjarān \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O goddess, he who is called Kirīṭin and Śvetavāhana (i.e. Arjuna) conquered all the Kauravas and slaughtered horses and elephants.

## \|\| 1.36.20 \|\|

*paścātsuyodhanaṃ hatvā bhīmena prayayau gṛhān \|*  
*nārāyaṇena sahito naro'sau prasthito raṇāt \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thereafter, with the help of Bhīma he got Suyodhana (killed). This Nara along with Nārāyaṇa set off homewards from the battlefield and reached the abode.

## \|\| 1.36.21-23 \|\|

*draṣṭuṃ dharmasutaṃ dṛṣṭaḥ praṇataḥ prāṃjaliḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*sa vijñāya tadā'yāntau naranārāyaṇāvubhau \|\| 21 \|\|*

*rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ prāha dvārasthāndvārapālakān \|*  
*bhavadbhiretāvāyāṃtau niṣedhyau dvārasaṃsthitau \|\| 22 \|\|*

*nara nārāyaṇau krūrau pāpapaṃkānulepinau \|*  
*evametaditi proktau tau tadā dvāramāgatau \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23a. With a desire to meet the son of Dharma, the delighted Arjuna bowed down to him and stood ready with palms joined in reverence. On coming to know that both of them, Nara and Nārāyaṇa were coming, King Yudhiṣṭhira spoke to the sentries at the entrance gate: “You who are at the gate should prevent these two from entering. Nara and Nārāyaṇa are cruel. They are smeared with the mire of sins”.

23b. They said, “It will be so”. When the two came near the gate, they were told thus:

## \|\| 1.36.24 \|\|

*bhavantau necchati draṣṭuṃ rājā durnayakāriṇau \|*  
*tatrasthaḥ pṛṣṭavānbhūyaḥ pratīhāraṃ naraḥ svayam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. “The king does not wish to see both of you because you are guilty of misconduct.” Nara himself who was standing there asked the sentry:

## \|\| 1.36.25 \|\|

*āvāṃ kiṃ kāraṇaṃ rājā nekṣate vaśavartinau \|*  
*provāca praṇato rājā tato dvāḥsthaṃ puraḥsthitam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. “What is the reason? Why does our king not wish to see both of us (who are) completely under his control?” Then the King who was bowed to, said to the sentry standing before:

## \|\| 1.36.26 \|\|

*nārāyaṇena sahitaṃ naraṃ narakanirbhayam \|*  
*duryodhanena sahitā bāṃdhavāste yato hatāḥ \|*  
*pitṛtulyāśca rājānastena vai pāpabhājanam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He also spoke to Nara who was dauntless of even hell and who was accompanied by Nārāyaṇa: “Since all the kinsmen including Duryodhana and all the kings on a par with the parents were killed by you, you have incurred sins.”

## \|\| 1.36.27 \|\|

*evamukte tu tenātha mukhamālokitaṃ hareḥ \|*  
*tena proktamidaṃ tathyaṃ yatte rājñā prabhāṣitam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. When this was spoken, he (Nara) looked at the face of Hari. Hari said, “What has been uttered by the king is the truth.”

## \|\| 1.36.28-29 \|\|

*evamukte naraḥ prāha punareva janārddanam \|*  
*kathayasva kathaṃ pāpātkṛṣṇa śuddhyāmahe vayam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tīrthasnānena me śuddhiryathā syāttadvada sphuṭam \|*  
*tacca gaṃgādikaṃ kṛṣṇa yathā'syāghasya nāśanam \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. When this was uttered, Nara spoke to Janārdana once again: “O Kṛṣṇa, say, how are we going to get free from the sin? O Kṛṣṇa, tell me clearly how I will get purified through the holy bath in a Tīrtha viz. Gaṅgā etc. which is destructive of sins.”

## \|\| 1.36.30 \|\|

*kṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*mā gayāṃ gaccha kauṃteya mā gaṃgāṃ mā ca puṣkaram \|*  
*tatra gaccha kuruśreṣṭha yatra prācī sarasvatī \|\| 30 \|\|*

Kṛṣṇa said:

30\. O Kaunteya, do not go to Gayā. Do not go to Puṣkara. O most excellent one among the scions of the family of Kuru, go to that place where Prācī Sarasvatī flows.

## \|\| 1.36.31 \|\|

*brahmaghnāśca surā pāśca ye cānye pāpakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*tatra snātvā vimucyaṃte yatra prācī sarasvatī \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Brāhmaṇa-slayers, those who imbibe liquor as well as other sinners, become rid of the sins by taking the holy bath at the place where Prācī Sarasvatī flows.

## \|\| 1.36.32 \|\|

*nārāyaṇena prokto'sau narastadvacanāddrutam \|*  
*sahitastena saṃprāptaḥ prācīnaṃ tīrthamuttamam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On being told thus by Nārāyaṇa, Nara, immediately in compliance of his words, reached the excellent Prācīna Tīrtha accompanied by him.

## \|\| 1.36.33 \|\|

*trirātropoṣitaḥ snātastrikālaṃ niyatātmavān \|*  
*tena tasmādvinirmuktaḥ pātakātpūrvasaṃcitāt \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. He observed fast for three nights and took his holy ablution thrice a day with full self-control. Thereby he got rid of the sins accumulated earlier.

## \|\| 1.36.34 \|\|

*vijñāya śuddhamenaṃ tu rājā dharmasuto drutam \|*  
*bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitaḥ prāptastaṃ draṣṭuṃ narapuṃgavam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. On realizing that he had become pure, King Dharmaputra, accompanied by his brothers came there to see the leading Nara.

## \|\| 1.36.35 \|\|

*tatastaṃ praṇataṃ dṛṣṭvā dharmaputraḥ puraḥsthitam \|*  
*āliliṃga prahṛṣṭātmā pṛṣṭavāṃścāpyanāmayam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then Dharmaputra saw him in front bowing down. With a delighted soul, he embraced him and enquired after his health.

## \|\| 1.36.36 \|\|

*bhīmādibhirbhrātṛbhiśca tadā gurugaṇairvṛtaḥ \|*  
*āliṃgitaḥ prahṛṣṭaistu naro guṇagaṇairvṛtaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Nara endowed with many good qualities, was surrounded by the group of elders. He was embraced by his delighted brothers Bhīma and others.

## \|\| 1.36.37 \|\|

*etaddhi tanmahātīrthaṃ prācīneti ca śabditam \|*  
*snānakrameṇa marttyānāmanyeṣāmapi pāvakam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Such is that great Tīrtha called Prācīna. It is the purifier of men and others through regular holy ablution.

## \|\| 1.36.38 \|\|

*trirātropoṣitaḥ snātastīrthe'sminbrahmahā'pi yaḥ \|*  
*vimuktaḥ pātakāttasmānmodate divi rudravat \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Even one who is a slayer of a Brāhmaṇa, but takes his bath in this Tīrtha and observes fast for three nights, becomes rid of that sin. He rejoices in heaven like Rudra.

## \|\| 1.36.39 \|\|

*prācīne devyahaṃ nityaṃ vasāmi sahitastvayā \|*  
*prabhāse tu mahākṣetre viśeṣāttatra bhāmini \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O goddess, O beautiful woman, I reside along with you in this great ancient holy spot Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.36.40 \|\|

*sarasvatyuttare tīre yastyajedātmanastanum \|*  
*prācīne tu varārohe na cehāgacchate punaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. He who casts off his body, O beautiful lady, in the holy spot Prācīna on the northern bank of Sarasvatī, does not come here again.

## \|\| 1.36.41 \|\|

*āpluto vājimedhasya phalaṃ prāpsyati puṣkalam \|*  
*niyamaiścopavāsaiśca śoṣayeddehamātmanaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. If he takes his plunge he will get the full benefit of a horse-sacrifice. He should get his body dried up by means of restraints and fasts.

## \|\| 1.36.42-43 \|\|

*jalāhārā vāyubhakṣāḥ parṇāhārāśca tāpasāḥ \|*  
*yathā sthaṃḍilagā nityaṃ ye cānyaniyamāḥ pṛthak \|\| 42 \|\|*

*evaṃ maṃkyāśrame yeṣāṃ vasatāṃ mṛtyurāgataḥ \|*  
*na te manuṣyā devāste satyametadbravīmi te \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. There are ascetics of various kinds: some take in only water; some take in only air; others have leaves for diet. They observe many restraints such as always lying down on the dry bare ground. If the people who reside in the hermitage of Maṅki, meet with death, they are no longer men. They are Devas. I speak the truth.

## \|\| 1.36.44 \|\|

*asmiṃstīrthe tu yo dadyāttruṭimātraṃ tu kāṃcanam \|*  
*śraddhayā dvijamukhyāya merutulyaṃ phalaṃ labhet \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. In this Tīrtha, if anyone offers a bit of gold with great faith to a leading Brāhmaṇa, he will obtain the benefit thereof on a par with Meru.

## \|\| 1.36.45 \|\|

*asmiṃstīrthe tu ye śrāddhaṃ kariṣyaṃti ca mānavāḥ \|*  
*ekaviṃśatkulopetāḥ svargaṃ yāsyaṃti te dhruvam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Men who perform Śrāddha in this Tīrtha will certainly go to heaven in the company of twenty-one generations.

## \|\| 1.36.46 \|\|

*pitṝṇāṃ vallabhe tīrthe piṇḍenaikena tarppitāḥ \|*  
*brahmalokaṃ gamiṣyaṃti gayāśrāddhakṛto yathā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Those propitiated with a single rice-ball in this Tīrtha that is a favourite of the Pitṛs, will go to Brahmaloka like those who perform Gayāśrāddha.

## \|\| 1.36.47 \|\|

*kṛṣṇapakṣe caturddaśyāṃ snānaṃ ca vihitaṃ sadā \|*  
*piṇyākaiṃgudakenāpi piṃḍaṃ tatra dadāti yaḥ \|*  
*pitṝṇāmakṣayā tṛptiḥ pitṛlokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Holy bath on the fourteenth day in the dark half is always laid down. If a devotee offers balls of Piṇyāka or Iṅgudaka, the Pitṛs are eternally satisfied. The devotee goes to Pitṛloka.

## \|\| 1.36.48 \|\|

*bhūyaścānnaṃ prayacchaṃti mokṣamārgaṃ vrajaṃti te \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. If they offer much rice (food), they go along the path to salvation.

## \|\| 1.36.49 \|\|

*dadhi dadyādyo'pi tatra brāhmaṇāya manoramam \|*  
*so'gnilokaṃ samāsādya bhuṃkte bhogānsuśobhanān \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. He who offers excellent curds there to a Brāhmaṇa, reaches Agniloka and enjoys splendid pleasures.

## \|\| 1.36.50 \|\|

*ūrṇāṃ prāvaraṇaṃ yo'pi bhaktyā dadyāddvijottame \|*  
*so'pi yāti parāṃ siddhiṃ martyairanyaiḥ sudurllabhām \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. He who devoutly offers a woollen blanket to an excellent Brāhmaṇa attains great Siddhi very difficult for others to acquire.

## \|\| 1.36.51 \|\|

*ye cātra malanāśāya viśeyurmānavā jalam \|*  
*gopradānasamaṃ teṣāṃ sukhena phalamādiśet \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. If men enter the waters here for getting rid of dirt, one can easily predict the benefit acquired on a par with the gift of cows.

## \|\| 1.36.52 \|\|

*bhāvena yo narastatra kaścitsnānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. A man who takes the holy bath with ardent fervour, shall be rid of all sins and will be honoured in Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 1.36.53 \|\|

*tarpaṇātpiṃḍadānācca narakeṣvapi saṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*svargaṃ prayāṃti pitaraḥ suputreṇa hi tāritāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The Pitṛs detained in Narakas can be redeemed by an excellent son by means of libations and offerings of rice-balls. They go to Svarga.

## \|\| 1.36.54 \|\|

*prācīṃ sarasvatīṃ prāpya yāti tīrthaṃ himālayam \|*  
*sa karasthaṃ samutsṛjya kūrpareṇa samālihet \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. If anyone who has gone to Prācī Sarasvatī turns to Himālaya, he forsakes what he has in his hand and begins to lick with the elbow (obscure).

## \|\| 1.36.55 \|\|

*yaṃyaṃ kāmamabhidhyāya tasminprāṇānparityajet \|*  
*taṃtaṃ sakalamāpnoti tīrthamāhātmyayogataḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. He who casts away his life thinking of anything whatever before death, obtains it entirely, thanks to the greatness of the Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.36.56-58 \|\|

*anyaddevi purā gītaṃ gāṃgeyena yudhiṣṭhire \|*  
*satyameva hi gaṃgāyāṃ vayaṃ jātā yudhiṣṭhira \|\| 56 \|\|*

*yāḥ kāścitsarito loke tāsāṃ puṇyā sarasvatī \|\| 57 \|\|*

*sarasvatī sarvanadīṣu puṇyā sarasvatī lokasukhāvahā sadā \|*  
*sarasvatīṃ prāpya suduḥkhitā narāḥ sadā na śocanti paratra ceha ca \|\| 58 \|\|*

56-58. Another thing, O goddess. This has been said by Gāṅgeya (Bhīṣma) to Yudhiṣṭhira: “It is true that we are born of Gaṅgā, O Yudhiṣṭhira, but out of all the rivers in the world, Sarasvatī is the greatest and the most meritorious of all of them. Sarasvatī is the most meritorious of all the rivers. Sarasvatī always accords happiness to all the people. After reaching Sarasvatī, even a most miserable man never grieves here or hereafter.

## Chapter 37 - Importance of Offering a Bracelet (kaṅkaṇa)

## \|\| 1.37.1-2 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*kimarthaṃ kaṃkaṇaṃ deva kṣipyate lavaṇāṃbhasi \|*  
*tasyā puṇyaṃ na pūrvoktaṃ yathāvadvaktumarhasi \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ke maṃtrāḥ kiṃ vidhānaṃ tatkasminkāle mahatphalam \|*  
*kiṃ purābhūcca tadvṛttaṃ bhagavankaṃkaṇāśritam \|\| 2 \|\|*

The Devī said:

1-2. O Lord, what for is a gold bracelet \[kaṅkaṇa\] thrown into the Salt Sea? The merit acquired thereby has not been mentioned before. It behoves you to tell it exactly. What are the Mantras? What is the injunction? At what time is it highly efficacious? What is the episode associated with the gold bracelet \[kaṅkaṇa\], O holy Lord?

## \|\| 1.37.3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*āsītpurā mahīpālo bṛhadratha iti śrutaḥ \|*  
*tasya bhāryā'bhavatsādhvī nāmnā ceṃdumatī priyā \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

3\. Formerly there was a king well-known as Bṛhadratha. He had a beloved wife, a chaste lady named Indumatī.

## \|\| 1.37.4 \|\|

*na devī na ca gandharvī nāsurī na ca kiṃnarī \|*  
*tādṛgrūpā mahādevi yādṛśī sā sumadhyamā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O great goddess, neither among the Deva women nor in Gandharvīs nor in Asurīs nor in Kinnarīs is (was) there a slenḍer-waisted lady like her (in beauty.).

## \|\| 1.37.5 \|\|

*śīlarūpaguṇopetā nityaṃ sā tu pativatā \|*  
*sarvayoṣidguṇairyuktā yathā sādhvī hyarundhatī \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. She was endowed with good manners, beauty, and other qualities. She was always chaste. Like the chaste lady Arundhatī, she possessed all the womanly good qualities.

## \|\| 1.37.6 \|\|

*pradhāna hasrasya saubhāgyamadagarvitā \|*  
*na vinā sa tayā reme muhūrttamapi pārthivaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. She was the most important one among a thousand inmates. Naturally she was proud of her conjugal felicity. Without her, the king did not divert himself even for a moment.

## \|\| 1.37.7 \|\|

*ekadā tasyarājarṣerarddhāsanagatā satī \|*  
*yāvattiṣṭhati rājeṃdramṛṣistāvadupāgataḥ \|*  
*kaṇvo nāma mahātejāstapasvī vedapāragaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Once, she was occupying half the throne of the saintly king, when a sage named Kaṇva came near the saintly king. He was an ascetic of great refulgence and was a master of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.37.8-9 \|\|

*tamāgatamatho dṛṣṭvā sahasotthāya pārthivaḥ \|*  
*pūjāṃ kṛtvā yathānyāyaṃ dattvā cārghyamanuttamam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sukhāsīnaṃ tato matvā viśrāṃtaṃ munipuṃgavam \|*  
*āpṛcchatkuśalaṃ rājā sa sarvaṃ cānvamodayat \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Seeing him coming, the king promptly got up. He duly adored him and offered excellent Arghya. Assured that the leading sage was comfortably seated and relaxed, the king enquired after his health and well-being and the sage congratulated him.

## \|\| 1.37.10 \|\|

*tato dharmakathāṃ cakre sa ṛṣirnṛpasannidhau \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then the sage held discourse on piety in the audience with the king.

## \|\| 1.37.11 \|\|

*tataḥ kathāvasāne sā bhāryā tasya mahīpateḥ \|*  
*abravīdamṛtaṃ vākyaṃ kṛtāṃjalipuṭā satī \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. At the end of the discourse, the wife of the king stood there with palms joined in reverence and spoke these nectarine words:

## \|\| 1.37.12 \|\|

*indumatyuvāca \|*  
*tvaṃ vetsi bhagavansarvamatītānāgataṃ vibho \|*  
*pṛcche tvāṃ kautukāviṣṭā tasmāttvaṃ kṣaṃtumarhasi \|\| 12 \|\|*

Indumatī said:

12\. O holy Sir, O Lord, you know everything past and future. Urged by curiosity I am asking you. So it behoves you to excuse me.

## \|\| 1.37.13 \|\|

*anyadehodbhavaṃ karma mama sarvaṃ prakīrttaya \|*  
*īdṛśaṃ mama saubhāgyaṃ patirdevasutopamaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Do narrate to me all my Karmas done in the earlier bodies. Mine is such a great conjugal felicity. My husband is comparable to a son of Devas.

## \|\| 1.37.14 \|\|

*saubhāgyaṃ patidevatvaṃ śīlaṃ trailokyaviśrutam \|*  
*kiṃ prabhāvo vratasyaiṣa utāhopoṣitasya vā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Due to my good fortune, I am having a husband as a Lord unto me whose good conduct is well-known all over the three worlds. Is this the result of any Vrata or that of a religious fast?

## \|\| 1.37.15 \|\|

*dānasya vā muniśreṣṭha yanme saubhāgyamuttamam \|*  
*vaśo rājā mahābāhurmama vākyānugaḥ sadā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O leading sage, is this the efficacy of a Dana that I possess excellent conjugal felicity? The mighty king is under my control. He always acts according to what I say.

## \|\| 1.37.16 \|\|

*etanme sarvamācakṣva paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Do explain this to me entirely. My curiousity is excessive.

## \|\| 1.37.17 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā dhyātvā ca suciraṃ muniḥ \|*  
*abravītprahasanvākyaṃ kaṇvo vedavidāṃ varaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

Sūta said:

17\. On hearing her words, the sage meditated for a long time. Ultimately Kaṇva, the most excellent one among knowers of the Vedas, laughingly spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.37.18 \|\|

*kaṇva uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu rājñi pravakṣyāmi anyadehodbhavaṃ tava \|*  
*na roṣaśca tvayā kāryo lajjā vāpi sumadhyame \|\| 18 \|\|*

Kaṇva said:

18\. Listen, O queen. 1 shall tell the details of your previous birth. O lady of slender waist-line, you must not be angry. Nor is there any need to feel ashamed.

## \|\| 1.37.19 \|\|

*tvamāsīdanyadehe tu ābhīrī paṃcabhartṛkā \|*  
*saurāṣṭraviṣaye hīnā devaṃ someśvaraṃ gatā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. In the previous birth you were a cowherdess with five husbands in the land of Saurāṣṭra. When you became Hīnā (a widow devoid of husbands) you went to the deity Someśvara.

## \|\| 1.37.20 \|\|

*tataḥ snātuṃ praviṣṭā ca sāgare lavaṇāṃbhasi \|*  
*hatā kallolamālābhirvihvalatvamupāgatā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then, for your holy bath, you entered the salty sea. On being struck by a series of waves, you became agitated.

## \|\| 1.37.21 \|\|

*tava hastāccyutaṃ tatra haimaṃ kaṃkaṇameva ca \|*  
*naṣṭaṃ samudrasalile paścāttāpastu te sthitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. From your forearm the gold bracelet \[kaṅkaṇa\] slipped down and got lost in the waters of the ocean. You began to regret it.

## \|\| 1.37.22 \|\|

*atha kālena mahatā paṃcatvaṃ tvamupāgatā \|*  
*daśārṇādhipatergehe tato jātāsi sundari \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. After a long time, you met with your death. Then, O beautiful woman, you were born in the abode of the king of Daśārṇa.

## \|\| 1.37.23-24 \|\|

*bṛhadrathena coḍhāsi kaṃkaṇasya prabhā vataḥ \|*  
*na vrataṃ na tapo dānaṃ tvayā cīrṇaṃ purā śubhe \|\| 23 \|\|*

*etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ yanmāṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi \|*  
*tacchrutvā sā viśālākṣī trapayā'dho mukhī tathā \|*  
*āsīttūṣṇīṃ tadā devī śrutvā vākyaṃ ca tādṛśam \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24a. Thanks to the power of the gold bracelet (lost in the sea), you were married to Bṛhadratha. O splendid lady, no Vrata, penance or Dāna was undertaken by you before. Here everything has been mentioned to you, all which you had asked me.

24b. On hearing those words the large-eyed lady stood with face down due to bashfulness. On hearing those words, the fair lady remained silent.

## \|\| 1.37.25 \|\|

*evaṃ nivedya sa munī rājapatnīṃ varānane \|*  
*jagāma bhavanaṃ svaṃ ca āmaṃtrya vasudhādhipam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. After intimating this to the wife of the king, O lady of excellent countenance (i.e. Gaurī), the sage took leave of the king and went to his abode.

## \|\| 1.37.26 \|\|

*jñātvā phalaṃ kaṃkaṇasya munestasya prabhāvataḥ \|*  
*gatvā someśvaraṃ devaṃ snātvā ca lavaṇāṃbhasi \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Having understood that the benefit was a result of (offer of) gold bracelet \[kaṅkaṇa\] by the power of the sage, she went to Lord Someśvara and took her holy bath in the salty ocean.

## \|\| 1.37.27 \|\|

*prākṣipatkaṃkaṇaṃ tatra prativarṣaṃ mahāprabhe \|*  
*tato devatvamāpannā prabhāvāttasya bhāmini \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O lady of great refulgence, every year she used to throw down a gold bracelet \[kaṅkaṇa\]. Then she attained the state of Deva, thanks to its power, O lady of great beauty.

## \|\| 1.37.28 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*eṣa prabhāvaḥ sumahānkaṃkaṇasya prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*sarvakāmaprado devi sarvapāpapraṇāśanaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

28\. This great power of (offering to sea) a gold bracelet \[kaṅkaṇa\] has been described. O goddess, it accords all desires. It is destructive of all sins.

## Chapter 38 - Kapardi-Vināyaka

## \|\| 1.38.1-2 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*yadetadbhavatā proktaṃ paśyetpūrvaṃ kaparddinam \|*  
*bhagavansaṃśayaṃ hyenaṃ yathāvadvaktumarhasi \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sa bhṛtyaḥ kila deveśa tava śambho mahāprabhaḥ \|*  
*prabhoranantaraṃ bhṛtya eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

The Devī said:

1-2. In regard to your earlier statement that one should visit Kapardin at the outset, I have a doubt. It behoves you to clarify it. O Lord of Devas, O Śaṃbhu, is he not your attendant though highly lustrous? According to a convention the honouring of a servant should take place only after that of the master.

## \|\| 1.38.3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi yathā pūjyatamo hi saḥ \|*  
*kaparddī sarvadevānāmādyo vighneśvaraḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

3\. Listen, O goddess, I shall explain how Kapardin is the most adorable. He is the foremost of all the Devas. He is Lord Vighneśvara.

## \|\| 1.38.4 \|\|

*yo'sāvatīṃdriyagrāhyaḥ prabhāsakṣetrasaṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*someśvaro mahādevi liṃgarūpī sadāśivaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O great goddess, Someśvara, Sadāśiva who is stationed in Prabhāsa Kṣetra in the form of a Liṅga is beyond the ken of sense-organs.

## \|\| 1.38.5 \|\|

*tasya vāme sthito viṣṇurvarāha iti yaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasya dakṣiṇabhāge tu sthito brahmā prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*kaparddirūpamāsthāya sāvitryāḥ kopakāraṇāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On his left is stationed Viṣṇu who is remembered as Varāha (the Boar). Brahmā, the Prajāpati (Lord of the subjects), is stationed on his right. Since he is angry with Sāvitrī he has adopted the form of Kapardin.

## \|\| 1.38.6 \|\|

*kṛte heraṃbanāmā tu tretāyāṃ vighnamarddanaḥ \|*  
*laṃbodaro dvāpare tu kaparddī tu kalau smṛtaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. In Kṛta Yuga, his name was Heraṃba; in Tretā he was Vighnamardana. In Dvāpara he was Laṃbodara and he is remembered as Kapardin in Kali Age.

## \|\| 1.38.7 \|\|

*evaṃ yugeyuge tasya avatāraḥ pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*yathākāryānurūpeṇa jāyate ca punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thus his incarnation is distinct in every Yuga. He is born again and again in accordance with the task on hand.

## \|\| 1.38.8 \|\|

*aṣṭāviṃśatime tatra devi prāpte caturyuge \|*  
*kāraṇātmā yathotpannaḥ kaparddī tatra me śṛṇu \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. At the advent of the twenty-eighth Caturyuga Kapardin was born there as Kāraṇātman (in the form of the original cause). Listen how he was born so.

## \|\| 1.38.9 \|\|

*purā dvāparasaṃdhau tu saṃprāpte ca kalau yuge \|*  
*striyo mlecchāśca śūdrāśca ye cānye pāpakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*prayāṃti svargamevāśu dṛṣṭvā someśvaraṃ prabhum \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Formerly at the junction of Dvāpara when Kaliyuga began, women, barbarians, Śūdras and those who were sinners used to go to Svarga quickly after viewing Lord Someśvara.

## \|\| 1.38.10 \|\|

*na yajñā na tapo dānaṃ na svādhpāyo vrataṃ na ca \|*  
*kurvatopi narā devi sarve yāṃti śivālayam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. There were no Yajñas, no austerity, no Dāna, no study of the Vedas and no Vrata. Men who never performed any of these things, O goddess, used to go to the abode of Śiva.

## \|\| 1.38.11 \|\|

*taṃ prabhāvaṃ viditvaivaṃ someśvarasamudbhavam \|*  
*agniṣṭomādikāḥ sarvāḥ kriyā naṣṭāḥ sureśvari \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. As a result of this power of Someśvara, O goddess of Suras, all holy rites beginning with Agniṣṭoma (sacrifice) became extinct.

## \|\| 1.38.12 \|\|

*tato bālāśca vṛddhāśca ṛṣayo vedapāragāḥ \|*  
*śūdrāḥ striyo'pi taṃ dṛṣṭvā prayāṃti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thereupon boys, old men, sages who had mastered the Vedas, Śūdras and even women used to attain the highest state.

## \|\| 1.38.13 \|\|

*naṣṭayajñotsave kāle śūnye ca vasudhātale \|*  
*ūrddhvabāhubhirākrāṃtaṃ paripūrṇaṃ triviṣṭapam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. At a time when the festivities of Yajña were extinct, the whole of the earth became vacant and heaven became filled with persons of raised arms (Since there was no living space left in the crowded heaven, all could stand only with raised arms).

## \|\| 1.38.14 \|\|

*tato devā maheṃdrādyā duḥkhenaiva samanvitāḥ \|*  
*paribhūtā manuṣyaiste śaṃkaraṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thereupon, the Devas beginning with Mahendra, became miserable on being attacked and defeated by human beings as it were. They sought refuge in Śaṅkara.

## \|\| 1.38.15-18 \|\|

*ūcuḥ prāṃjalayaḥ sarva indrādyāḥ surasattamāḥ \|*  
*vyāptoyaṃ mānuṣaiḥ svargaḥ prasādāttava śaṃkara \|\| 15 \|\|*

*nivāsāya prabho'smākaṃ sthānaṃ kiṃcitsamādiśa \|*  
*ahaṃ śreṣṭho hyahaṃ śreṣṭha ityevaṃ te parasparam \|*  
*jalpaṃtaḥ sarvato deva paryaṭaṃti yathecchayā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*dharmarājaḥ sudharmātmā teṣāṃ karma śubhāśubham \|*  
*svayaṃ likhitamālokya tūṣṇīmāste suvismitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*yeṣāmatha kṛtaṃ sajjaṃ kumbhīpākaṃ sudāruṇam \|*  
*rauravaḥ śālmalirdeva dṛṣṭvā tāndivi saṃsthitān \|*  
*vailakṣyaṃ paramaṃ gatvā vyāpāraṃ tyaktavānasau \|\| 18 \|\|*

15-18. With palms joined in reverence all the excellent Suras beginning with Indra said: “O Śaṅkara, due to your favour this Svarga has become over-crowded with human beings.

They are boasting to one another, “I am the most excellent one, I am the most superior one” and move about everywhere as they please. O Lord, suggest some place for us to stay.

Dharmarāja, the highly virtuous one, is reviewing their auspicious and inauspicious Karmas recorded by himself. He keeps quiet with extreme surprise.

The extremely terrible Kuṃbhīpāka, Raurava and Śālmali hells had been kept ready by him for these sinners. But on seeing those very persons well-settled in heaven he felt embarrassed. So he has abandoned his work.

## \|\| 1.38.19 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*pratijñātaṃ mayā sarvaṃ bhaktyā tuṣṭena vai surāḥ \|*  
*somāya mama sāṃnidhyamasminkṣetre bhaviṣyati \|\| 19 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

19\. When I was pleased with the devotion of Soma I had promised him everything. My presence (proximity to Soma) in this holy spot was promised.

## \|\| 1.38.20 \|\|

*na śakyamanyathākartumātmano yadudīritam \|*  
*evaṃ yāsyaṃti te svargaṃ ye māṃ drakṣyaṃti tatra vai \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. What has been promised by me cannot be altered. Those who visit me there will thus go to Svarga.

## \|\| 1.38.21 \|\|

*bhayodvignāstato devāḥ pārvatīṃ prekṣya viśvataḥ \|*  
*ūcuḥ prāṃjalayaḥ sarve tvamasmākaṃ gatirbhava \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Agitated by fear, the Devas looked at Pārvatī present everywhere and spoke to her with palms joined in reverence, “Do be our refuge”.

## \|\| 1.38.22 \|\|

*evamuktvā'stuvandevāḥ stotreṇānena sattama \|*  
*jānubhyāṃ dharaṇīṃ gatvā śirasyādhāya cāṃjalim \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. After saying so, they knelt on the ground. With joined palms kept over the head all those Devas eulogized her by means of this prayer.

The Devas prayed:

## \|\| 1.38.23 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*namaste devadeveśi namaste viśvadhātrike \|*  
*namaste padmapatrākṣi namaste kāṃcanadyute \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Obeisance to you, O goddess of the chiefs of Devas. Obeisance to you, O mother of the Universe. Obeisance to you with eyes like lotus-petals. Obeisance to you, O goddess with golden lustre.

## \|\| 1.38.24 \|\|

*namaste saṃhartri kartri namaste śaṃkarapriye \|*  
*kālarātri namastubhyaṃ namaste giriputrike \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Obeisance to you, O great annihilatrix and creatrix. Obeisance to you, O beloved of Śaṅkara. Obeisance to you, O Kālarātri (Durgā identified as the goddess of the night of annihilation) Obeisance to you, O daughter of the Mountain.

## \|\| 1.38.25 \|\|

*ārye bhadre viśālākṣi namaste lokasundari \|*  
*tvaṃ ratistvaṃ dhṛtistvaṃ śrīstvaṃ svāhā tvaṃ sudhā satī \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O fair lady, O noble lady, O Viśālākṣī (large-eyed one)! Obeisance to you, to the most beautiful lady of the world. You are Rati (pleasure). You are Dhṛti (fortitude). You are Śrī (fortune). You are Svāhā. You are Svadhā and Satī.

## \|\| 1.38.26 \|\|

*tvaṃ durgā tvaṃ manirmedhā tvaṃ sarvaṃ tvaṃ vasundharā \|*  
*tvayā sarvamidaṃ vyāptaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. You are Durgā, you are Mati (intellect) you are Medhā (retentive power of memory). You are everything. You are the earth, the repository of rich wealth. This entire range of the three worlds consisting of mobile and immobile beings has been pervaded by you.

## \|\| 1.38.27-28 \|\|

*nadīṣu parvatāgreṣu sāgareṣu guhāsu ca \|*  
*araṇyeṣu ca caityeṣu saṃgrāmeṣvāśrameṣu ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

*trailokye tatra paśyāmo yatra tvaṃ devi na sthitā \|*  
*etajjñātvā viśālākṣi trāhi no mahato bhayāt \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. We have been looking for you in rivers, tops of mountains, oceans, caves, forests, altars and sanctuaries, battlefields, hermitages—all those places in the three worlds where, O goddess, you were not present. In view of all this, O Viśālākṣī, save us from the great danger.

## \|\| 1.38.29 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*evamuktā tu sā devī devairiṃdrapurogamaiḥ \|*  
*kāruṇyānnijadehaṃ tvaṃ tadā mardditavatyasi \|\| 29 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

29\. That goddess was prayed to thus by the Devas with Indra as their leader. Out of mercy you caused your own body to be massaged and pressed by those Devas.

## \|\| 1.38.30 \|\|

*mardayaṃtyāstava tadā saṃjātaṃ ca mahanmalam \|*  
*tatra jajñe gajeṃdrāsyaścaturbāhurmanoharaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. A great deal of dirt issued forth as you were being pressed and massaged. It was there that the four- armed charming Gajendrāsya (one with the face of a leading tusker) appeared.

## \|\| 1.38.31-33 \|\|

*tatobravītsurānsarvānbhavatī karuṇātmikā \|*  
*eṣa eva mayā sṛṣṭo yuṣmākaṃ hitakāmyayā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*eṣa vighnāni sarvāṇi prāṇināṃ saṃvidhāsyati \|\| 32 \|\|*

*mohena mahatā'viṣṭāḥ kāmopahatabuddhayaḥ \|*  
*somanāthamapaśyaṃto yāsyaṃti narakaṃ narāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. You mercifully spoke to all the Suras: “This is the being created by me with a desire for your benefit. He will cause all obstacles to the living beings. Men overwhelmed with great delusion, with intellect overpowered by lust, will never see Somanātha. Hence they will fall into hell.”

## \|\| 1.38.34 \|\|

*evaṃ te vacanaṃ śrutvā sarve te hṛṣṭamānasāḥ \|*  
*svasthānaṃ bhejire devāstyaktvā mānuṣajaṃ bhayam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. All the Devas were delighted in their minds on hearing these words of yours. They went back to their respective abodes shedding off all fear arising from human beings.

## \|\| 1.38.35 \|\|

*athe bhavadanaḥ prāha tvāṃ devi vinayānvitaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ karomi viśālākṣi ādeśo dīyatāṃ mama \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then, O goddess, the Elephant-faced One spoke to you humbly: “O large-eyed one, what shall I do? May some command be given to me.”

## \|\| 1.38.36-38 \|\|

*śrībhagavatyuvāca \|*  
*gaccha prābhāsikaṃ kṣetraṃ yatra saṃnihito haraḥ \|*  
*tadrakṣa mānuṣāṇāṃ ca yathā nāyāti gocaram \|\| 36 \|\|*

*liṃgaṃ tu devadevasya sthāpitaṃ śaśinā svayam \|*  
*bhavatyā'deśito nityaṃ nṛṇāṃ vighnaṃ karoti yaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*prasthitaṃ puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā somanāthaṃ prati prabhum \|*  
*sa karoti mahāvighnaṃ kapardī lokapūjitaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavatī said:

36-38. Go to the holy place of Prabhāsa where Hara is present and protect it. See that the Liṅga of the Lord of Devas which is installed by the Moon himself does not fall within the range of vision of human beings.

On being commanded by you thus, he causes obstacles to men always. Kapardin begins to cause great obstacles to everyone on seeing him proceeding to Somanātha, the Lord. Hence Kapardin is highly adored by people.

## \|\| 1.38.39 \|\|

*putradāragṛhakṣetra dhanadhānyasamudbhavam \|*  
*janayetsa mahāmohaṃ tataḥ paśyati no haram \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. He creates unto him the great infatuation of sons, wives, houses, fields, wealth and food-grain. As a result the man does no see Hara.

## \|\| 1.38.40 \|\|

*athavā gaḍugaṃḍādi vyādhiṃ caiva samutsṛjet \|*  
*tairgrastaḥ puruṣo mohānna paśyati tato haram \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Or he may generate some illness like goitre, swelling in the neck etc. and the man afflicted with those illnesses becomes deluded and never sees Hara.

## \|\| 1.38.41 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena someśvaraparīpsayā \|*  
*sa nityaṃ pūjanīyastu smartavyastu divāniśam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Hence with a desire to (attain) Someśvara one should assiduously worship him (Kapardin) always and remember him day and night.

## \|\| 1.38.42 \|\|

*stotreṇānena deveśi sarvavighnāṃtakena vai \|*  
*samārādhya gaṇādhyakṣaḥ prabhāsakṣetrarakṣakaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Gaṇādhyakṣa, the protector of Prabhāsa Kṣetra, should be propitiated, O goddess of Devas, by means of this prayer that destroys all obstacles.

## \|\| 1.38.43 \|\|

*tatte'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi stotraṃ tadvighramardanam \|*  
*kapardino mahādevi sāvadhānāvadhāraya \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O great goddess, I shall proclaim to you that prayer which suppresses obstacles, the prayer to Kapardin. Listen with attention.

Prayer (44-51): (Prayer to Kapardin)

## \|\| 1.38.44 \|\|

*oṃ namo vighnarājāya namaste'stu kapardine \|*  
*namo mahogradaṃṣṭrāya prabhāsakṣetravāsine \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Oṃ, obeisance to the Lord of obstacles. O Kapardin, obeisance to you. Obeisance to the Lord of great and fierce fang-like teeth, to the resident of the holy spot of Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.38.45 \|\|

*kapardinaṃ namaskṛtya yātrānirvighrahetave \|*  
*stoṣye'haṃ vighnarājānaṃ siddhibuddhipriyaṃ śubham \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. After bowing down to Kapardin for the sake of freedom from obstacles in the course of the pilgrimage, I shall eulogize Vighnarāja, the splendid lover of Siddhi and Buddhi.

## \|\| 1.38.46 \|\|

*mahāgaṇapatiṃ śūramajitaṃ jayavarddhanam \|*  
*ekadaṃtaṃ ca dvidaṃtaṃ caturdaṃtaṃ caturbhujam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. (I adore) Mahāgaṇapati, heroic one, unconquered one, one who enhances victory, single-toothed one, double-toothed one, four-toothed one, four-armed one.

## \|\| 1.38.47 \|\|

*tryakṣaṃ ca śūlahastaṃ ca rakta netraṃ varapradam \|*  
*ajeyaṃ śaṃkukarṇaṃ ca pracaṇḍaṃ daṃḍanāyakam \|*  
*āyaskadaṃḍinaṃ caiva hutavaktraṃ hutapriyam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. (I adore) the three-eyed one, the trident-armed one, the red-eyed one, the bestower of boons, the invincible one, the pike-eared one, the fierce one, the leader of the army, one with iron staff held up, Hutavaktra (one in whose mouth the sacrificial articles are consigned), and Hutapriya (one fond of the performance of Homa).

## \|\| 1.38.48 \|\|

*anarcito vighnakaraḥ sarvakāryeṣu yo nṛṇām \|*  
*taṃ namāmi gaṇādhyakṣaṃ bhīmamugramumāsutam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. I bow down to that Gaṇādhyakṣa, the terrifying and fierce son of Umā, who, if not worshipped, causes obstacles in all the activities of men.

## \|\| 1.38.49 \|\|

*madavataṃ virūpākṣamibhavaktrasamaprabham \|*  
*dhruvaṃ ca niścalaṃ śāṃtaṃ taṃ namāmi vināyakam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. I bow down to that Vināyaka who is full of inebriation, who has uneven (three) eyes, whose lustre is befitting the elephant-faced deity, who is firm and motionless, and who is quiescent.

## \|\| 1.38.50 \|\|

*tvayā pūrveṇa vapuṣā devānāṃ kāryasiddhaye \|*  
*gajarūpaṃ samāsthāya trāsitāḥ sarvadānavāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. With a previous physical form you adopted the guise of an elephant for the fulfilment of the tasks of Devas. You then terrified all the Dānavas.

## \|\| 1.38.51 \|\|

*ṛṣīṇāṃ devatānāṃ ca nāyakatvaṃ prakāśitam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. You have revealed your leadership of the sages and the Devas.

## \|\| 1.38.52-55 \|\|

*iti stutaḥ surairagre pūjyase tvaṃ bhavātmaja \|*  
*tvāmārādhya gaṇādhyakṣamibhavaktrasamaprabham \|\| 52 \|\|*

*dhruvaṃ ca niścalaṃ śāṃtaṃ parītaṃ vi jayaśriyā \|*  
*kāryārthaṃ raktakusumai raktacaṃdanavāribhiḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*raktāṃbaradharo bhūtvā caturthyāmarcayettu yaḥ \|*  
*ekakālaṃ dvikālaṃ vā niyato niyatāśanaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*rājānaṃ rājaputraṃ vā rājamaṃtriṇameva ca \|*  
*rājyaṃ vā sarvavighneśo vaśīkuryātsarāṣṭrakam \|\| 55 \|\|*

52-55. O son of Bhava, you are adored at the outset by the Suras after being eulogized thus.

A devotee shall propitiate you, O Gaṇādhyakṣa, having the lustre befitting the elephant-faced Lord. The devotee should eulogize the steady, motionless, quiescent Lord surrounded by the glory of victory. For the realization of any task the devotee should wear red garments and worship with red flowers and the waters (rendered fragrant) with red sandal-paste. He should restrain himself and restrict his food intake. He can worship once a day or twice a day. The Lord of all obstacles shall control everyone, be it a king, king’s son, king’s minister or the kingdom.

## \|\| 1.38.56 \|\|

*yatphalaṃ sarvatīrtheṣu sarvayajñeṣu yatphalam \|*  
*sa tatphalamavāpnoti smṛtvā devaṃ vināyakam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. By remembering Lord Vināyaka, one obtains that benefit which results from visiting all the Tīrthas and performing all the Yajñas.

## \|\| 1.38.57 \|\|

*viṣamaṃ na bhavettasya na sa gacchetparābhavam \|*  
*na ca vighnaṃ bhavettasya jano jātismaro bhavet \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. He will never meet with difficulty. He will face no defeat or discomfiture, nor will he have any obstacle. The man shall become competent to remember the previous birth.

## \|\| 1.38.58 \|\|

*ya idaṃ paṭhati stotraṃ ṣaḍbhirmāsairvaraṃ labhet \|*  
*saṃvatsareṇa siddhiṃ ca labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. He who recites this hymn shall be granted boons within six months. He will obtain Siddhi within a year. There is no doubt about this.

## \|\| 1.38.59 \|\|

*prasādāddarśanaṃ yāti tasya someśvaraḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*kapardākāramudaraṃ yato'sya samudāhṛtam \|*  
*tato'sya nāma jānīhi kaparddīti mahātmanaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Lord Someśvara favours him and comes within the view of that devotee. Since his belly has the shape of a Kaparda (a courrie used as a coin, a shell) the noble-souled one has come to be named Kapardin.

## Chapter 39 - Kedāreśvara Liṅga (Kedāra-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.39.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*atha saṃpūjya vidhinā devadevaṃ kaparddinam \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi ligaṃ kedārasaṃsthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tasyaivāgneyabhāgasthaṃ bhīmeśvarasamīpagam \|*  
*svayaṃbhūtaṃ mahādevi kalpaliṃgaṃ mama priyam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*mayā saṃpūjitaṃ devi vṛddhiliṃga mahāprabham \|*  
*nirāhārastu yastatra karotyekaṃ prajāgaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

*caturdaśyāṃ viśeṣeṇa tasya lokāḥ sanātanāḥ \|*  
*rudreśvareti devasya tvāsīnnāma purā yuge \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. After duly adoring Kapardin, the Lord of Devas, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the Liṅga situated in Kedāra and set up in its south-east sector. It is near Bhīmeśvara. It is self-born Kalpaliṅga, O great goddess, and is my favourite. This Vṛddhiliṅga of great lustre was worshipped by me, O goddess. If any devotee abstains from food and keeps vigil on the night of the fourteenth lunar day, his worlds shall be eternal. But the name of this Lord in the earlier Yuga was Rudreśvara.

## \|\| 1.39.5 \|\|

*tiṣyesmiṃstu punaḥ prāpte mlecchasparśabhayāturaḥ \|*  
*asmiṃlliṃge layaṃ yātaḥ kedāraścābdhisaṃnidhau \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. When at the advent of this Tiṣya (Kali Yuga) the Lord became afraid and agitated about contact with barbarians, he, Lord Kedāra, got merged into this Liṅga in the vicinity of the sea.

## \|\| 1.39.6-8 \|\|

*tena kedāranāmeti tasya khyātaṃ dharātale \|*  
*māghe māsi yatāhāraḥ snātvā tu lavaṇodadhau \|\| 6 \|\|*

*padmake tu mahākuṃḍe madhyesya lavaṇāṃbhasaḥ \|*  
*rudreśāddakṣiṇe bhāge dhanuṣāṃ daśake sthite \|\| 7 \|\|*

*snātvā vidhānato devi rudreśaṃ cārcayiṣyati \|*  
*samyakkedārayā trāyāḥ phalaṃ tasya bhaviṣyati \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. Hence, the name of the Lord became well-known as Kedāra.

In the month of Māgha, the pilgrim should restrict his diet and take his holy bath in the great Padmaka Kuṇḍa within the salty sea. It is situated at a distance of ten Dhanus to the south of Rudreśa.

O goddess, after taking the holy bath in accordance with the injunctions he should adore Rudreśa. Thereby he shall derive the benefits of the perfect performance of the pilgrimage to Kedāra.

## \|\| 1.39.9-10 \|\|

*brahmahatyādipāpānāṃ pūjanānnāśanaṃ mahat \|*  
*atha tasyaiva devasya itihāsaṃ purātanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*sarvakāmapradaṃ nṛṇāṃ kathyate te surapriye \|*  
*āsīdrājā purā devi śaśabiṃduriti śrutaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. By adoring the Lord, the sins of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter etc. shall be dispelled.

Now, O beloved of Suras, the ancient legend of the same Lord is being told. It yields the fulfilment of all the cherished desires unto men.

Formerly, O goddess, there was a king well-known as Śaśabindu.

## \|\| 1.39.11 \|\|

*sārvabhaumo mahīpālo vipakṣagaṇasūdanaḥ \|*  
*kalidvāparayoḥ saṃdhau sabhūtaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He was born during the junction of Kali and Dvāpara. He was an emperor and Lord of all kings. He was competent to slay all antagonists and their hosts.

## \|\| 1.39.12-14 \|\|

*tasya bhāryā'bhavatsādhvī prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī \|*  
*na devī na ca gandharvī nāsurī na ca pannagī \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tādṛgrūpā varārohe yathā'sya śubhalocanā \|*  
*tasya hemamayaṃ padmaṃ śatapatraṃ manoramam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*khecaraṃ vegi nityaṃ ca tasya rājño mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*sa tena paryaṭaṃllokānsarvāndevi svakāmataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. He had a chaste wife dear to him more than his own life. O beautiful lady (Gaurī), neither a Deva lady nor a Gandharvī, neither an Asurī lady nor a Pannagī was as beautiful as this lady of splendid eyes, the queen of the king. He had a hundred-petalled charming lotus moving through the sky. It was a fast vehicle of that noble-souled king. O goddess, he wandered over all the worlds as he pleased by means of that (lotus-vehicle).

## \|\| 1.39.15 \|\|

*ekadā phālgune māsi śuklapakṣe varānane \|*  
*caturddaśyāṃ tu saṃprāptaḥ prabhāsakṣetramuttamam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Once, O lady of excellent countenance, on the fourteenth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Phālguna, he arrived at the excellent Prabhāsa Kṣetra.

## \|\| 1.39.16 \|\|

*athāpaśyadṛṣīnsarvāñchrīsomeśapuraḥsthitān \|*  
*rātrau jāgaraṇārthāya japahomaparāyaṇān \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He saw all the sages gathered before Śrīsomeśa. They were engaged in Japa and Homa at night for the purpose of keeping awake.

## \|\| 1.39.17 \|\|

*sa dṛṣṭvā somanāthaṃ tu praṇipatya vidhānataḥ \|*  
*pūjayāmāsa sarvāṃ stānyathārhaṃ bhaktisaṃyutaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. After viewing Somanātha and making the bow of veneration in accordance with the injunctions, he adored all of them in a fitting manner with devotion.

## \|\| 1.39.18-19 \|\|

*tataḥ kedāramāsādya saṃsnāpya vidhivatpriye \|*  
*pūjayitvā vicitrābhiḥ puṣpamālābhirīśvaram \|\| 18 \|\|*

*naivedyairvividhairvastrairbhūṣaṇaiśca manoharaiḥ \|*  
*tato'tra kārayāmāsa jāgaraṃ susamāhitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Then, O my beloved, he proceeded to Kedāra and bathed (the deity) duly. He worshipped Īśvara with flower garlands of various kinds, Various kinds of food-offerings were made. Charming robes and ornaments were dedicated to the deity. Thereafter, with great concentration he made arrangements for Jāgara (keeping awake at night).

## \|\| 1.39.20-21 \|\|

*tataste munayaḥ sarve kutūhalasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*cyavano yājñavalkyaśca śāṃḍilyaḥ śākaṭāyanaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*raibhyo'tha jaiminiḥ krauṃco nāradaḥ parvataḥ śilaḥ \|*  
*mārkaṃḍaṃ purataḥ kṛtvā jagmustasya samīpataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Sages Cyavana, Yājñavalkya, Śāṇḍilya, Śākaṭāyana, Raibhya, Jaimini, Krauñca, Nārada, Parvata and Śīla were filled with eager curiosity. Keeping Mārkaṇḍa at their head, they approved him.

## \|\| 1.39.22 \|\|

*cakruḥ kathāḥ suvicitrā itihāsāni bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*kīrttayaṃtaḥ sthitāstatra papracchū rājasattamam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. They conducted diverse kinds of discourses mostly in mythology and old legends. After remaining thus for some time, they asked the excellent king:

## \|\| 1.39.23 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kasmātsomeśvaraṃ devaṃ parityajya narādhipa \|*  
*kedārasya puro'kārṣīrjāgaraṃ tadbravīhi naḥ \|*  
*nūnaṃ vetsi phalaṃ cāsya liṃgasya tvaṃ mahodayam \|\| 23 \|\|*

The sages said:

23\. O king, why did you ignore Lord Someśvara and perform the rite of keeping awake before Lord Kedāra? Do tell us this. Certainly you know the efficacy of this Liṅga, in conferring prosperity.

## \|\| 1.39.24 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*śṛṇvaṃtu brāhmaṇāḥ sarve anyadehodbhavaṃ mama \|*  
*purā'haṃ śūdrajātīya āsaṃ brāhmaṇapūjakaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

The King said:

24\. May all the Brāhmaṇas listen to the details of mine in the other body (i.e. earlier birth). Formerly I was a man of Śūdra caste, venerating Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.39.25 \|\|

*saurāṣṭraviṣaye śubhre dhanadhānyasamākule \|*  
*atha kālāṃtare tatra anāvṛṣṭirabhūddvijāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. It was in the splendid land of Saurāṣṭra in a family possessing much wealth and food-grains. Then, O Brāhmaṇas, on another occassion a state of drought overran it.

## \|\| 1.39.26 \|\|

*tato'haṃ kṣudhayāviṣṭaḥ prabhāsaṃ kṣetramāsthitaḥ \|*  
*athāpaśyaṃ saraḥ śubhraṃ hariṇīmūlasaṃsthitam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Then I came to the Prabhāsa Kṣetra. I was afflicted with hunger. Then I espied a splendid lake situated near the Hariṇī river.

## \|\| 1.39.27 \|\|

*tacca rāmasaronāma padminīṣaṇḍamaṃḍitam \|*  
*kṣīrodāṃbudhisaṃkāśaṃ dṛṣṭvā snātaḥ klamānvitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The name of that lake was Rāmasaras. It was adorned with clusters of lotuses. It resembled the Ocean of Milk. As I was tired, on seeing it, I took my bath there.

## \|\| 1.39.28-29 \|\|

*saṃtarpya ca pitṝndevānpītvā svacchamathodakam \|*  
*tato'haṃ bhāryayā prokto gṛhāṇemānsaroruhān \|\| 28 \|\|*

*etatsamīpato ramyaṃ dṛśyate sthānamuttamam \|*  
*vikrīṇīmo'tra gatvā tu yena syādbhojanaṃ vibho \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. After offering libations to the Pitṛs and Devas, I drank the clear water. Then my wife told me thus: “Take these lotuses. Here, nearby an excellent charming holy spot is seen. We can sell these after going there so that, O dear Lord, we shall get our food.”

## \|\| 1.39.30 \|\|

*athāvatīrya salilaṃ gṛhītāni mayā dvijāḥ \|*  
*kamalāni subhū rīṇi prasthitaśca puraṃ prati \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thereupon, I got down into the water, O Brāhmaṇas, and plucked plenty of lotus flowers. Then I started towards the city.

## \|\| 1.39.31-32 \|\|

*tatra gatvā ca rathyāsu catvareṣu trikeṣu ca \|*  
*praphullakamalānyeva kretuṃ vai munisattamāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*na kaścitprati gṛhṇāti astaṃ prāpto divākaraḥ \|*  
*prāsādaṃ kaṃcidāsādya suptohaṃ saha bhāryayā \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. O excellent sages, in order to sell the lotuses in full bloom, I went along the roads and places where three roads and four roads met. No one came forward to take (the flower). By that time, the sun also set. Accompanied by my wife, I went to a big building and slept there.

## \|\| 1.39.33-34 \|\|

*tatra suptasya me buddhiḥ śrutvā gītadhvaniṃ tadā \|*  
*samutpannā sabhā ryasya kṣudhārtasya viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*nūnaṃ jāgaraṇaṃ hyetatkasmiṃścidvibudhālaye \|\| 33 \|\|*

*saroruhāṇi cādāya vrajāmyatra surālaye \|*  
*yadi kaścitpragṛhṇāti prāṇayātrā tato bhavet \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. While sleeping I heard the sound of music. My wife and I were very hungry. It occurred to me that certainly the ritual of keeping awake was on, in a certain temple and that I shall go there to the temple with the lotus flowers. If anyone buys them, we can have our means of sustenance (food).

## \|\| 1.39.35 \|\|

*athotthāya samāyāto hyatrāhaṃ munipuṃgavāḥ \|*  
*apaśyaṃ liṃgametattu pūjitaṃ kusumaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O leading sages, I got up and came to this place and saw this Liṅga adored with splendid flowers.

## \|\| 1.39.36-42 \|\|

*rudreśvarābhidhamidaṃ vṛddhaliṃgaṃ svayaṃbhuvam \|*  
*veśyānaṃgavatīnāmnī śivarātriparāyaṇā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*jāgartti puratastasya gītanṛtyotsavādinā \|*  
*tataḥ kaścinmayā dṛṣṭaḥ kimetadrātrijāgaram \|\| 37 \|\|*

*keyaṃ strī dṛśyate'tyarthaṃ gītanṛtyotsave ratā \|*  
*so'bravīcchivadharmoktā śivarātriḥ sudharmadā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tāṃ cānaṃgavatīnāmnī veśyeyaṃ dharmasaṃyutā \|*  
*jāgartti paramaṃ śreyaḥ śivarātrivrataṃ śubham \|\| 39 \|\|*

*śivarātrivrataṃ hyetadyaḥ samyakkurute naraḥ \|*  
*na sa duḥkhamavāpnoti na dāri dryaṃ na baṃdhanam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*duṣṭaṃ cāriṣṭayogaṃ vā na rogaṃ na bhayaṃ kvacit \|*  
*sukhasaubhāgyasaṃpanno jāyate satkule naraḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*tejasvī ca yaśasvī ca sarvakalyāṇabhājanam \|*  
*bhavedasya prasādena evamāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

36-38a. This Vṛddha Liṅga is a self-born one and is named Rudreśvara.

A harlot named Anaṅgavatī was celebrating Śivarātri. With songs, dances and other festivities she kept awake before the deity.

I saw someone (and asked him): “Is this the ritual of keeping awake? Who is this lady seen here very ardently engaged in songs, dances and festivities?”

38b-42. He replied: “This is the ritual of Śivarātri mentioned in the scripture as Sivadharma. It yields great merit.

This is the harlot named Anaṅgavatī. She is very pious. She keeps awake at night after performing the splendid Śivarātri Vrata.

A man who perfectly celebrates this Śivarātri Vrata never meets with misery or poverty. Nor does he get into bondage.

He does not suffer due to malefic position of Planets, illness or anything fearsome. The man becomes richly endowed with good luck and happiness and is born in a good family.

He becomes refulgent, famous and recipient of everything by way of welfare. With the favour (of this deity) all this happens, so say learned men.

## \|\| 1.39.43 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*atha me buddhirutpannā tadvrataṃ prati niścalā \|*  
*ciṃtitaṃ manasā hyetanmayābrāhmaṇasattamāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

The King said:

43\. Then I became finally inclined to perforin that Vrata, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. I thought thus in my mind.

## \|\| 1.39.44 \|\|

*annābhāvānmamotpanna upavāso balādyataḥ \|*  
*tadahaṃ padmake tīrthesnātvā ca lavaṇāṃbhasi \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. As there was no food I was compelled to observe fast. Then I took my holy bath in the Padmaka Tīrtha in the salty ocean.

## \|\| 1.39.45 \|\|

*etaiḥ saroruhairdevaṃ pūjayāmi maheśvaram \|*  
*tato mayā sabhāryeṇa rudreśaḥ saṃprapūjitaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. I thought, I shall worship Lord Maheśvara by means of these lotuses. Then Rudreśa was duly adored by me along with my wife.

## \|\| 1.39.46 \|\|

*padmaiśca bhaktiyuktena sabhāryeṇa viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*jāgratsthitastu devāgre tāṃ rātriṃ saha bhāryayā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The Lord was worshipped devoutly by means of the lotuses. Further, my wife had accompanied me in the adoration. Throughout that night, I had kept awake along with my wife.

## \|\| 1.39.47-48 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhātasamaya udite sūryamaṇḍale \|*  
*sā veśyā māmuvācedaṃ kaladhautapalatrayam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*gṛhāṇamūlyaṃ padmānāṃ na gṛhītaṃ mayā hi tat \|*  
*sāttvikaṃ bhāvamāsthāya sabhāryeṇa dvijottamāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. After the day had dawned and the disc of the sun had risen, that harlot told me: “Take the three palas of silver as the price of the lotuses.” But I did not accept it, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. A Sāttvika feeling arose in me and in my wife.

## \|\| 1.39.49 \|\|

*tato bhikṣāṃ samāhṛtya prāṇayātrā mayā kṛtā \|*  
*kālena mahatā prāptaḥ kāladharmaṃ munīśvarāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Then I began to beg for alms and thus I sustained my life. Then after a great deal of time, O leading sages, I met with my death.

## \|\| 1.39.50 \|\|

*iyaṃ me dayitā sādhvī prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī \|*  
*mama dehaṃ samādāya praviṣṭā havyavāhanam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. This chaste wife of mine who is dearer to me more than my own life, entered fire along with my dead body.

## \|\| 1.39.51 \|\|

*tatprabhāvādahaṃ jātaḥ sarvabhaumo mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*jātismaraḥ sabhāryastu satyametaddvijottamāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Thanks to its power, I was born as an emperor. Along with my wife I could remember the earlier birth. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, this is the truth.

## \|\| 1.39.52 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇādasya bhaktirliṃgasya copari \|*  
*mama nityaṃ sabhāryasya satyametadbravīmi vaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. It is for this reason that my devotion is concentrated on this Liṅga permanently along with my wife too. I am speaking the truth to you.

## \|\| 1.39.53 \|\|

*mayā kriyāvihīnena bhaktibāhyena sattamāḥ \|*  
*vratametatsamācīrṇaṃ tasyedaṃ sumahatpha lam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O excellent ones, this Vrata was performed by me who (as a Śūdra) had been excluded from all holy rites and devotional fervour. This is the great benefit yielded by it.

## \|\| 1.39.54 \|\|

*adhunā bhaktiyuktasya yathopakaraṇānmama \|*  
*bhaviṣye yatphalaṃ kiṃcinno vedmi ca munīśvarāḥ \|*  
*yena someśamutsṛjya atrāhaṃ bhakti tatparaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Now I am fully endowed with devotion and I have all essential requisites. What benefit is in store for me in the future, I do not know, O leading sages. Therefore, I have ignored Someśvara and became devouted \[devoted?\] to this deity (Kedāreśvara).

## \|\| 1.39.55 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ śrutvā tu te viprā vismayotphullalocanāḥ \|*  
*sādhusādhviti jalpaṃto rājānaṃ saṃpraśaṃsire \|\| 55 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

55\. On hearing this, those Brāhmaṇas wondered much. With their eyes beaming, they said: “Excellent! Excellent!” They praised the king.

## \|\| 1.39.56 \|\|

*pūjayāmāsuraniśaṃ liṃgaṃ tatra svayaṃbhuvam \|*  
*tato'sau pārthivaśreṣṭho liṃgasyāsyaprasādataḥ \|*  
*saṃsiddhiṃ paramāṃ prāpto durllabhāṃ tridaśairapi \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. They always worshipped that self-born Liṅga. Thanks to the favour of this Liṅga, the most excellent king attained great Siddhi inaccessible even to Devas.

## \|\| 1.39.57 \|\|

*sā ca veśyā bhagavatī śivarātriprabhāvataḥ \|*  
*tasya liṃgasya māhātmyādraṃbhānāmāpsarā'bhavat \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Thanks to the favour of the holy Śivarātri and the greatness of that Liṅga, the harlot became the celestial lady Raṃbhā.

## \|\| 1.39.58 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena talliṃgaṃ pūjayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*dharmakāmārthamokṣaṃ ca yo vāṃchatyakhilapradam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Hence a sensible man should adore that Liṅga with all means and efforts, if he desires Puruṣārthas viz. virtue, love, wealth and salvation. The deity bestows everything.

## Chapter 40 - Bhīmeśvara (Bhīma-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.40.1-2 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi śvetaketupratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*liṃgaṃ mahāprabhāvaṃ tu bhīmenārādhitaṃ purā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kedāreśvarasāṃnidhye nātidūre vyavasthitam \|*  
*pūjayate ttadvidhānena kṣīrasnānādibhiḥ kramāt \|*  
*yātrāphalamabhiprepsuḥ pretya svargaphalāya vai \|\| 2 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-2. Then, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the Liṅga of great power installed by Śvetaketu. It was propitiated earlier by Bhīma.

It is in the vicinity of Kedāreśvara and is installed not very far therefrom.

One should worship it in accordance with the injunctions in due order, by means of bathing with milk etc. The pilgrim desirous of getting the benefit of the pilgrimage (here) and the benefit of heavenly pleasures after death, should do so.

## \|\| 1.40.3 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*śvetaketostu yaddeva liṃgaṃ proktaṃ tvayā mama \|*  
*tasya jātaṃ kathaṃ deva nāma bhīmeśvareti ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

The Devī said:

3\. O Lord, you have mentioned about the Liṅga of Śvetaketu. How did it come to be named Bhīmeśvara also?

## \|\| 1.40.4 \|\|

*kathaṃ vinirmitaṃ pūrvaṃ tasmindṛṣṭe tu kiṃ phalam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. How was it evolved before? What is the benefit of viewing it?

## \|\| 1.40.5 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*āsīttretāyuge pūrvaṃ rājā svāyaṃbhuveṃtare \|*  
*śvetaketuriti khyāto rājarṣiḥ sumahātapāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

5\. Formerly, in the course of the Svāyaṃbhuva Manvantara, in Tretā Yuga there was a king well-known as Śvetaketu. The saintly king had performed a very severe penance.

## \|\| 1.40.6 \|\|

*sa prabhāsaṃ samāgatya pratiṣṭhāpya mahe śvaram \|*  
*tapastepe suvipulaṃ sāgarasya taṭe śubhe \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He came to Prabhāsa, installed Maheśvara and performed a very severe penance on the splendid shore of the ocean.

## \|\| 1.40.7 \|\|

*paṃcāgnisādhako grīṣme varṣāsvākāśagastathā \|*  
*hemaṃte jalamadhyastho nava varṣāṇi paṃca ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. This continued for fourteen years. During the summer he practised the Pañcāgni (i.e. four fires were kindled on all sides and the sun blazed above when he performed the penance). During rainy season he remained under the open sky. During winter, he remained in water.

## \|\| 1.40.8 \|\|

*tataścaturddaśe devi tapasā niyamena ca \|*  
*tuṣṭenokto mayā devi varaṃ varaya suvrata \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In the fourteenth year, I became highly pleased with his penance and observance of restraints. O goddess, I told him, “O sage of good holy rites, choose your boon.”

## \|\| 1.40.9 \|\|

*śvetaketurathovāca bhaktiṃ dehi suniścalām \|*  
*sthāne'sminsthīyatāṃ deva yadi tuṣṭo'si me prabho \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then Śvetaketu said: “O Lord, grant me a steady devotion. If the Lord is pleased, do stay behind in this holy spot.”

## \|\| 1.40.10-11 \|\|

*evamastvityathoktvā'haṃ tasyāṃtarddhānamāgataḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kālāṃtare'tīte śvetaketurmahāprabhaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*samārādhya tvidaṃ liṃgaṃ prāptaḥ sthānaṃ mahodayam \|*  
*tato jātaṃ nāma tasya śvetaketvīśvaraṃ śrutam \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. After saying “So be it”, I vanished there. Later on Śvetaketu of great refulgence propitiated this Liṅga and attained highly prosperous state. Thereupon, It became well-known by the name Śvetaketvīśvara.

## \|\| 1.40.12-14 \|\|

*agnitīrthe mahāpuṇye sarvapātakanāśane \|*  
*tataḥ kaliyuge prāpte bhrātṛbhiśca samanvitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena yadā prabhāsamāgataḥ \|*  
*bhīmaseno mahābāhurvāyuputro mamāṃśajaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*talliṃgaṃ pūjayāmāsa kṛtvā jāgeśvaraṃ nijam \|*  
*matvā tīrthaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ sāgarasya samīpataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. It was in the highly meritorious Agnitīrtha that is destructive of all sins. Thereafter, when Kali Yuga (?) arrived, in the course of his pilgrimage the mighty Bhīmasena, the son of Vāyu, born of a part of mine came to Prabhāsa. Realizing that the Tīrtha is highly meritorious, he installed his own deity Jāgeśvara near the sea, but adored that Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.40.15-16 \|\|

*tadā prabhṛti bhīmeśaṃ punarnāmā'bhavacchubham \|*  
*dṛṣṭamātreṇa tenaiva sakṛlliṃgena bhāmini \|\| 15 \|\|*

*anyajanmakṛtānyeva pāpāni subahūnyapi \|*  
*nāśamāyāṃti sarvāṇi tathaivāmuṣmikāṇi tu \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Ever since then the splendid name of the Liṅga was Bhīmeśa. O beautiful lady, if that Liṅga is viewed even once, all the sins committed in earlier births perish. So also those (committed) hereafter.

## Chapter 41 - Bhairaveśvara (Bhairava-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.41.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tasyaiva pūrvadigbhāge sarasvatyā pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*liṃgaṃ mahāprabhāvaṃ tu someśādagnigocare \|\| 1 \|\|*

*bhairaveśvararūpastu vāḍavaḥ kumbhasaṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*yatra devyā samānītaḥ sāgarasya samīpataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*viśrāmārthaṃ kṣaṇaṃ muktvā devyā liṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*samabhyarcya vidhānena gṛhītvā vaḍavānalam \|*  
*samudramadhye cikṣepa devānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. To the east thereof and to the south-east of Someśa, there is a Liṅga of great power, installed by Sarasvatī.

The Vāḍava fire kept in a pot in the form of Bhairaveśvara, was brought by the goddess near the sea.

She left it for a moment to take rest and then the Liṅga was installed. After worshipping it in accordance with the injunctions, she took the Vāḍava fire and cast it into the Sea with a desire for the welfare of the Devas.

## \|\| 1.41.4 \|\|

*tato hṛṣṭatarā devāḥ śaṃkhadundubhiniḥsvanaiḥ \|*  
*pūrayantoṃ'baraṃ devīmīḍire puṣpavṛṣṭibhiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Thereupon, the Devas became extremely pleased. They adored the goddess with showers of flowers and filled the sky with the sounds of Śaṅkha and Dundubhi drums.

## \|\| 1.41.5-6 \|\|

*devamāteti te nāma kṛtvocustāṃ tadā surāḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā tu bhairavaṃ kāryamasādhyaṃ devadānavaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*pratiṣṭhitavatī cātra yasmālliṃgaṃ mahodayam \|*  
*tvaṃ sarvasaritāṃ śreṣṭhā sarvapātakanāśinī \|*  
*tasmādbhairavanāmeti liṃgaṃ khyātiṃ gamiṣyati \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. The Suras named her Devamātā (Mother of the Devas) and said to her: “You have accomplished a terrific task that could not be accomplished by Devas and Dānavas and installed here the Liṅga of great power. You are the most excellent of all rivers and the destroyer of all sins. Hence this Liṅga will become famous by the name Bhairava.”

## \|\| 1.41.7-9 \|\|

*ityuktā tu tadā devī bhairaveśvaranairṛte \|*  
*sāgarasya sthitā ramye tatra mūrttimatī satī \|\| 7 \|\|*

*pūjayettāṃ vidhānena taṃ tathā bhairaveśvaram \|*  
*mahānavamyāṃ yatnena kṛtvā snānaṃ vidhānataḥ \|*  
*sarasvatīṃ pūjayitvā vāgdoṣānmucyate'khilāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tasyā liṃgaṃ tu saṃpūjya saṃsnāpya payasā pṛthak \|*  
*aghoreṇaiva vidhivatsamyagyātrāphalaṃ labhet \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. On being told thus, the goddess stationed herself in the form of an image to the south-east of Bhairaveśvara on the charming shore of the ocean.

A pilgrim should worship her as well as Bhairaveśvara in accordance with the injunction on the Mahānavamī day with great effort. After duly bathing and worshipping Sarasvatī, one becomes rid of all defects of speech.

If the Liṅga is adored after bathing it with milk, uttering the Aghora Mantra duly, one will get the benefit of the pilgrimage.

## Chapter 42 - Caṇḍīśa

## \|\| 1.42.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi caṇḍīśaṃ devamuttamam \|*  
*someśādīśadigbhāge dhanuṣāṃ saptake sthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Then a pilgrim should go over to the excellent Lord Caṇḍīśa, O great goddess. It is situated within a distance of seven Dhanus to the north-east of Someśa.

## \|\| 1.42.2 \|\|

*daṇḍapāṇestu bhavanāddakṣiṇe nātidūragam \|*  
*caṃḍyā pratiṣṭhitaṃ pūrvaṃ caṇḍenārādhitaṃ tataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. It was installed by Caṇḍī formerly not far from the abode of Daṇḍapāṇi. It was then adored by Caṇḍa.

## \|\| 1.42.3 \|\|

*gaṇena mama deveśi tatkṛtvā duṣkaraṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*tena caṇḍeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ prakhyātaṃ dharaṇītale \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. After performing a very difficult penance, O goddess of Devas, Caṇḍa, a Gaṇa of mine, propitiated it. Therefore, the Liṅga became well-known all over the earth as Caṇḍeśvara.

## \|\| 1.42.4 \|\|

*snāpayetpayasā pūrvaṃ dadhnā ghṛtayutena ca \|*  
*madhunekṣurasenaiva kuṃkumena vilepayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The pilgrim should at the outset bathe the Liṅga with Payas (milk, water), then with curds mixed with ghee, then with honey and sugarcane juice. He should smear it with Kuṃkuma (saffron).

## \|\| 1.42.5 \|\|

*karpūrośīramiśreṇa mṛganābhirasena ca \|*  
*candanena sugandhena puṣpaiḥ saṃpūjayettataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then he should apply the liquefied musk mixed with camphor and Uśīra (Khus). Sweet-scented sandal-paste is then applied. The pilgrim should then adore it with flowers.

## \|\| 1.42.6 \|\|

*dagdhvā dhūpaṃ puro devi tato devasya cāgurum \|*  
*vastraiḥ saṃpūjayetpaścādātmavittānusārataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O goddess, incense and agallocham should be fumigated before the Lord. Thereafter, garments are offered during the worship in accordance with one’s wealth.

## \|\| 1.42.7 \|\|

*naivedyaṃ paramānnaṃ ca dattvā dīpasama nvitam \|*  
*tato dadyāddvijātibhyo yathāśaktyā tu dakṣiṇām \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The “best cooked rice” (sweet rice pudding) is offered as Naivedya along with a lamp. Thereafter, the pilgrim should give monetary gifts to Brāhmaṇas within his capacity.

## \|\| 1.42.8 \|\|

*dakṣiṇāṃ diśamāsthāya yatkiṃcittatra dīyate \|*  
*caṇḍīśasya varārohe tatsarvaṃ cākṣayaṃ bhavet \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O beautiful lady, the pilgrim should face the southern quarter. Whatever is offered then to Caṇḍīśa, shall become everlasting in its benefit.

## \|\| 1.42.9 \|\|

*yaḥ śrāddhaṃ kurute tatra caṇḍīśasya tu dakṣiṇe \|*  
*ākalpaṃ tṛptimāyāṃti pitarastasya bhāmini \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. If the pilgrim performs Śrāddha on the right side of Caṇḍīśa, O beautiful lady, the Pitṛs become satisfied for the period of a Kalpa.

## \|\| 1.42.10 \|\|

*ayane cottare prāpte yaḥ kuryādghṛta kambalam \|*  
*na sa bhūyo'tra saṃsāre janma prāpnoti dāruṇam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. In the course of the Uttarāyaṇa (northern transit of the Sun) the pilgrim should perform the rite of Ghṛtakaṃbala (woollike thick application of ghee over the idol or Liṅga). He will never again take up the terrible worldly birth.

## \|\| 1.42.11 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛtvā naro bhaktyā yātrāṃ devasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*nirmālyātikramodbhūtairajñānādbhakṣaṇodbhavaiḥ \|*  
*pāpaiḥ pramucyate jaṃtustathā'nyaiḥ karmasaṃbhavaiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thus, the pilgrim performs the Yātrā (pilgrimage) of the Trident-bearing Lord. Thereby the creature becomes rid of various sins such as those caused by overstepping the remnants of the adoration of Śiva, eating unwittingly the prohibited food etc. All the entanglaments due to earlier Karmas perish (get dissolved).

## Chapter 43 - Ādityeśvara (Āditya-īśvara) or Ādityeśa (Āditya-īśa)

## \|\| 1.43.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchedvarārohe liṃgaṃ sūryapratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*someśātpaścime bhāge dhanuṣāṃ saptake sthitam \|*  
*ādityeśvaranāmānaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Then, O beautiful lady, a pilgrim should go to the shrine named Ādityeśvara, destructive of all sins. The Liṅga was installed by Sūrya (the Sun god) himself. It is situated within a distance of seven Dhanus to the west of Someśa.

## \|\| 1.43.2 \|\|

*tretāyuge mahādevi samudreṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*ratnaiḥ saṃpūjitaṃ liṃgaṃ varṣāṇāmayutaṃ priye \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O beautiful woman, O my beloved, O great goddess, the Liṅga was worshipped by the noble-souled Ocean in Tretāyuga for a period of ten thousand years.

## \|\| 1.43.3 \|\|

*tena ratneśvaraṃnāma sāṃprataṃ prathitaṃ kṣitau \|*  
*paṃcāmṛtena saṃsnāpya paṃcaratnaiḥ prapūjayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Therefore, now it is well-known over the earth by the name Ratneśvara. The deity should be bathed with Pañcāmṛta and worshipped with five jewels.

## \|\| 1.43.4 \|\|

*tato rājopacāreṇa pūjayedvidhivannaraḥ \|*  
*evaṃ kṛte mahādevi merudānaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Then the man should duly worship it with all royal offerings of services. If it is done so, O great goddess, one shall obtain the benefit of Merudāna (gifting the great mountain Meru).

## \|\| 1.43.5 \|\|

*sarveṣāṃ caiva yajñānāṃ dānānāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. There is no doubt in this that he will get the merit of performing all Yajñas and Dānas.

## \|\| 1.43.6 \|\|

*tīrthānāṃ cāpi sarveṣāṃ yaccānyatsukṛtaṃ bhuvi \|*  
*uddharetpitṛvargaṃ ca mātṛvargaṃ ca mānavaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He shall get the fruit of (pilgrimage to) all Tīrthas and he will derive every merit on the earth. The man will redeem all the generations on his father’s side as well as on the mother’s side.

## \|\| 1.43.7 \|\|

*bālye vayasi yatpāpaṃ vārddhake yauvane'pi vā \|*  
*kṣālayeccaiva tatsarvaṃ dṛṣṭvā ratneśvaraṃ naraḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. By viewing Ratneśvara, a man shall wash off all the sins committed during childhood, youth and old age.

## \|\| 1.43.8 \|\|

*dhenudānaṃ praśaṃsaṃti tasminsthāne maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*dhenudastārayennūnaṃ daśa pūrvāndaśāparān \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Great sages praise Dhenu Dāna (gift of cows) at that holy spot. The donor of cows redeems ten preceding and ten succeeding generations certainly.

## \|\| 1.43.9 \|\|

*devasya dakṣiṇe bhāge yo japecchatarudriyam \|*  
*saṃpūjya vidhivalliṃgaṃ na sa bhūyaḥ prajāyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He who worships the Liṅga duly and performs the Japa of the Śatarudriya on the right side of the deity is never born again.

## \|\| 1.43.10 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃkṣepataḥ proktamādityeśamahodayam \|*  
*śrutvā'vadhārya yatnena mucyate karmabaṃdhanaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thus, the great prosperity arising from Ādityeśa has been succinctly spoken. It should be listened to attentively and retained carefully. The pilgrim is rid of the bondage due to his Karmas,

## Chapter 44 - Someśvara (Soma-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.44.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*ādityeśaṃ samabhyarcya punaḥ someśvaraṃ vrajet \|*  
*taṃ saṃpūjya vidhānena paṃcāṃgena viśeṣataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. After adoring Ādityeśa, a pilgrim should once again go to Someśvara and worship the deity duly with all five ancillary features.

## \|\| 1.44.2 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā someśvaraṃ caiva sāṣṭāṃgaṃ praṇipatya ca \|*  
*pradakṣiṇādikaṃ kuryātsaṃpaśyecca punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. After viewing Someśvara, the pilgrim prostrates (before the deity) and then circumambulates (it). Again he should view the Lord repeatedly. A pilgrim who, with purity circumambulates the Liṅga of (installed by) the Sun and the Moon gets the same benefit as when Agniṣṭoma rite has been performed by him.

## \|\| 1.44.3-4 \|\|

*sūryācandramasorliṃgaṃ triḥkṛtvā prayataḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*agnīṣomātmakaṃ karma tena sarvaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavet \|\| 3 \|\|*

*umādevīṃ tato gacchetsomeśvarasamīpataḥ \|*  
*dvitīyāṃ tu tato gaccheddaityasūdanasannidhau \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Then the pilgrim proceeds to goddess Umā in the vicinity of Someśvara. He should also proceed to a second image of the goddess in the vicinity of Daityasūdana (Viṣṇu).

## Chapter 45 - Aṅgāreśvara (Aṅgāra-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.45.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi aṃgāreśvaramuttamam \|*  
*sthāpitaṃ bhūmiputreṇa someśādīśa gocare \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tripuraṃ dagdhukāmasya purā mama varānane \|*  
*krodhādaśru viniṣkrāṃtaṃ locanatritayena tu \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tacca bhūmau nipatitaṃ tato bhūbhisuto'bhavat \|*  
*sa prabhāsaṃ tato gatvā bālyātprabhṛti śaṃkaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tapasā'rādhayāmāsa bahūnvarṣagaṇānpriye \|*  
*tasya tuṣṭo mahādevaḥ suprītātmā varaṃ dadau \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Then, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the excellent Aṅgāreśvara established by the Son of the Earth (or Maṅgala) on the north-east of Someśa.

Formerly, O lady of excellent countenance, I was desirous of burning down the Tripuras. Due to anger, tears came out of all the three eyes. They fell down and therefrom arose Bhūmiputra (Mars).

He went to Prabhāsa and ever since his childhood, he propitiated Śaṅkara for many years, by means of his penance.

O my beloved, Mahādeva was pleased with him. With his soul extremely delighted he granted him a boon.

## \|\| 1.45.5 \|\|

*so'bravīdyadi me deva tuṣṭosi vṛṣabhadhvaja \|*  
*grahatvaṃ dehi sarveśa na cānyaṃ varamutsahe \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He said: “O Lord, O Bull-emblemed One, if you are pleased, grant me the state of being a planet. O Lord of all, I am not eager to have any other boon.”

## \|\| 1.45.6-9 \|\|

*sa tatheti pratijñāya punastaṃ vākyamabravīt \|*  
*ihāgatya naro yo māṃ pūjayiṣyati bhaktitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*na bhaviṣyati vai pīḍā tāvakī tasya kutracit \|*  
*puṣpāṇi raktavarṇāni madhvājyāktāni bhūriśaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*homayiṣyati yo bhaktyā lakṣamekaṃ tadagrataḥ \|*  
*paṃcopacāravidhinā tvāṃ tu saṃpūjya yatnataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tasya janmāvadhirnaiva tava pīḍā bhaviṣyati \|\| \|*  
*tathā vidrumadānena lapsyate phalamīpsitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

6-9. He (the Lord) promised: “So it shall be” and again spoke to him these words: “A man who comes here and devoutly adores me will never get afflicted by you at all. The devotee should perform Homa with many red flowers soaked in honey and ghee with great devotion before the deity. With the mode of offering the five types of services, he should strenuously worship you. For the whole of that life, he will never get troubled by you. Further, through the gift of a piece of coral, he will get the desired benefit.”

## \|\| 1.45.10 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa bhagavānatraivāṃtaradhīyana \|*  
*bhaumo'pi grahamadhyastho vimānena virājate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After saying thus the Lord vanished here itself. Bhauma (Mars) shines amongst the Planets by means of the aerial chariot.

## \|\| 1.45.11 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ bhaumamāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*śrutaṃ harati pāpāni tathārogyaṃ prayacchati \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thus, the excellent greatness of Bhauma has been succinctly spoken. On being listened to it dispels sins and yields freedom from illness.

## Chapter 46 - Budheśvara (Budha-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.46.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi tasyaivottarataḥ sthitam \|*  
*liṃgaṃ mahāprabhāvaṃ tu budheśvaramiti śrutam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*dhanuṣāṃ dvitaye caiva nātidūre vyavasthitam \|*  
*sarvapāpa haraṃ liṃgaṃ darśanādeva bhāmini \|\| 2 \|\|*

*budhena caiva deveśi tatra taptaṃ mahātapaḥ \|*  
*sthāpitaṃ vimalaṃ liṃgaṃ samārādhya sadāśivam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Then, O great goddess, a pilgrim should proceed towards the Liṅga of great efficacy well-known as Budheśvara.

It is situated to the north of it (Aṅgāreśvara) not very far, say within a couple of Dhanus in distance, O beautiful lady.

This Liṅga dispels all sins by its mere vision. O goddess of Devas, Budha (Mercury) performed a great penance there and this pure Liṅga was installed. He then propitiated Sadāśiva.

## \|\| 1.46.4 \|\|

*varṣāyutāni catvāri saṃpūjya tu vidhānataḥ \|*  
*ananyacetāḥ śāṃtātmā pratyakṣīkṛtavānbhavam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Worshipping the Lord for forty thousand years in accordance with the injunctions, he kept his mind quiescent without straying into anything else. He had the direct vision of Bhava (Śiva).

## \|\| 1.46.5 \|\|

*tatastuṣṭamanā devo grahatvaṃ tasya taddadau \|*  
*taṃ saṃpūjya vidhānena somaputrapratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*saumyāṣṭamyāṃ viśeṣeṇa rājasūyaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Pleased with him, the Lord granted him the status of being a Planet. The devotee who worships the deity installed by the son of Soma (i.e. Budha) especially on a Wednesday coinciding with the eighth lunar day derives the fruit of (performing) Rājasūya sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.46.6 \|\|

*na daurbhāgyaṃ kule tasya na caiveṣṭaviyojanam \|*  
*śatruto na bhayaṃ tasya bhavettasyaprasādataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Due to the favour of the deity, no one in the family of the devotee becomes wretched or separated from near and dear ones. He will never have any cause to fear from enemies.

## \|\| 1.46.7 \|\|

*iti saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ māhātmyaṃ budhadaivatam \|*  
*śrutvā'bhinaṃdya prayataḥ prāpnoti paramaṃ padam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thus, the greatness of the deity installed by Budha has been succinctly spoken. One who listens to it, delights in it and remains pure attains the greatest region.

## Chapter 47 - Bṛhaspatīśvara (Bṛhaspati-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.47.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi devaṃ guruniṣevitam \|*  
*umāyāḥ pūrvadigbhāge siddheśāgneyagocare \|\| 1 \|\|*

*saṃsthitaṃ tu mahalliṃgaṃ devācārya pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*ārādhya parayā bhaktyā liṃgaṃ varṣasahasrakam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*toṣayāmāsa deveśaṃ bhavaṃ śarvamumāpatim \|*  
*prāptavānakhilānkāmānaprāpyānakṛtātmabhiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Then, O great goddess, a devotee should go over to the Lord resorted to by Guru (Jupiter). It is situated to the east of Umā and south-east of Siddheśa.

This great Liṅga was installed by the Preceptor of Devas. With great devotion, he propitiated the Liṅga for a thousand years and pleased Śarva, the consort of Umā, the Lord of the Devas. He attained all the cherished desires inaccessible to those who have no self-control.

## \|\| 1.47.4 \|\|

*devānāṃ caiva pūjyatvaṃ prāpya jñānamathaiśvaram \|*  
*grahatvaṃ ca tathā prāpya modate divi sāṃpratam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Now he has the knowledge pertaining to Īśvara and the state of being adorable by Devas. He has attained the status of a planet. He rejoices in heaven only.

## \|\| 1.47.5-7 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā mānavo bhaktyā na durgati mavāpnuyāt \|*  
*bṛhaspatikṛtaṃ liṃgaṃ ye paśyaṃti narottamāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*bṛhaspatikṛtā pīḍā naiva teṣāṃ hi jāyate \|*  
*tatra śuklacaturdaśyāṃ guruvāre tathā priye \|\| 6 \|\|*

*saṃpūjya vidhivalliṃgaṃ samyagrājopacārataḥ \|*  
*athavā bhaktibhāvena prāpnuyātparamaṃ padam \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. A man who views that Lord, never meets with a distressed condition. The affliction brought about by an adverse Bṛhaspati will never torment those excellent men who view the Liṅga installed by Bṛhaspati.
