O my beloved, one who duly worships the Liṅga with royal attendance and service, or with devotional fervour, on the fourteenth lunar day in the bright half coinciding with a Thursday attains the greatest region.

## \|\| 1.47.8 \|\|

*snānaṃ palasahasreṇa paṃcāmṛtarasena yaḥ \|*  
*karoti bhaktyā martyo vai mucyate sa ṛṇatrayāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The man who ritualistically bathes the deity with a thousand Palas of Pañcāmṛta devoutly, is rid of the three types of indebtedness.

## \|\| 1.47.9 \|\|

*mātṛkātpaitṛkāddevi tathā gurusamudbhavāt \|*  
*sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā nirdvaṃdvo muktimāpnuyāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O goddess, he becomes purified of all sins inherited from or pertaining to his mother, father or preceptor. He is rid of all Dvandvas (mutually opposed pairs such as pleasure-pain) and he attains salvation.

## \|\| 1.47.10 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ māhātmyaṃ gurudaivatam \|*  
*śṛṇuyādyastu bhāvena tasya prīto gururbhavet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thus, the greatness of the deity pertaining to (i.e. resorted to by) Guru has been succinctly described. He who listens to this with devotional fervour, Guru will become pleased with him.

## Chapter 48 - Śukreśvara (Śukra-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.48.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi liṃgaṃ śukrapratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*sarvapāpaharaṃ devi vibhūtīśvarapaścime \|\| 1 \|\|*

*nātidūre sthitaṃ tatra svayaṃ śukreṇa nirmitam \|*  
*yatra saṃjīvanīṃ prāpto vidyāṃ rudraprabhāvataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*saṃtapya tu mahāghoraṃ tapovarṣasahasrakam \|*  
*saṃprasādya virūpākṣaṃ yo'vāpa grahatāṃ sudhīḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said.:

1-3. Then, O Great Goddess, a pilgrim should go towards the Liṅga installed by Śukra, to the west of Vibhūtīśvara.

It dispels all sins. It is not far off and it has been created by Śukra himself. At this holy spot, thanks to the power of Rudra, he obtained the Vidyā (secret formula) called Sañjīvanī. The wise one performed a very severe penance for a thousand years and propitiated the Odd (three)-eyed Lord. He then attained the status of a Planet.

## \|\| 1.48.4 \|\|

*grastena śaṃbhunā yena devakāryārthasiddhaye \|*  
*tatrodaragatenaiva tapastaptaṃ suduṣkaram \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He was swallowed by Śaṃbhu for the sake of accomplishing some task of the Devas. Even as Śukra was held inside the belly, he performed a very severe penance.

## \|\| 1.48.5 \|\|

*varṣāṇāmayutaṃ sāgraṃ tuṣṭiṃ nīto maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*niṣkāsitastataḥ śīghraṃ śukra mārgeṇa śaṃbhunā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. When more than ten thousand years elapsed Maheśvara was pleased. Thereafter, he was discharged quickly by Śaṃbhu through the seminal path (tube).

## \|\| 1.48.6-7 \|\|

*tataḥ śukreti nāmābhūdbhārgavasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*tadārādhayate liṃgaṃ yaḥ kṛtvā niścalaṃ manaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*mṛtyuṃjayaṃ japellakṣaṃ sa samīhitamāpnuyāt \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Thereupon, the noble-souled Bhārgava got the name Śukra. The devotee shall keep his mind steady and propitiate the Liṅga. He shall repeat the Mṛtyuñjaya Mantra (death-defying formula) one hundred thousand times. He shall (thereby) obtain what is desired.

## \|\| 1.48.8 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā tvathavā spṛṣṭvā janmādimaraṇāntakāt \|*  
*mucyate pātakānmṛtyoḥ prasādāttasya bhāmini \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. By viewing him and touching him, O beautiful woman, a man becomes rid of all sins committed from birth till death.

## \|\| 1.48.9-11 \|\|

*mṛtasaṃjīvanārthaṃ yadaiśvaryamaṇimādikam \|*  
*prāpnuyānnātra saṃdeho yasya bhaktiḥ suniścalā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*paṃcāmṛtena saṃsnāpya devaṃ śukapratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*sugandhapuṣpaiḥ saṃpūjya śaukrīṃ pīḍāṃ sa nāpnuyāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

*iti sarvaṃ samāsena māhātmyaṃ śukradaivatam \|*  
*kathitaṃ tava suśroṇi śrutaṃ pāpabhayāpaham \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. A person whose devotion is highly steady shall undoubtedly obtain the power of Mṛtasañjīvana (resuscitating the dead) and Aṇimā (becoming as small as an atom) and other supernatural powers (Siddhis).

A devotee who bathes the deity installed by Śukra with Pañcāmṛta and worships with sweet-smelling flowers, will never have seminal affliction.

Thus the greatness of the deity installed by Śukra has been fully described to you, O lady of excellent buttocks. On being heard, it dispels the fear resulting from sins.

## Chapter 49 - Śanaiścareśvara (Śanaiścara-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.49.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tasmācchukreśvarādgaccheddevi liṃgaṃ mahāprabham \|*  
*śanaiścaraiśvaraṃnāma mahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*budheśvarātpaścimato hyajādevyagnigocare \|*  
*tasyā dhanuḥ paṃcakena nātidūre vyavasthitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kalpaliṃgaṃ mahādevi pūjitaṃ devadānavaiḥ \|*  
*chāyāputreṇa saṃtaptaṃ tapaḥ paramaduṣkaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said,:

1-3. From that Śukreśvara shrine, O Goddess, a pilgrim should go to the highly lustrous Liṅga named Śanaiścareśvara. It is destructive of all great sins.

It is to the west of Budheśvara and to the south-east of Ajādevī from which it is not very far. It is situated only five Dhanus away.

It is a Kalpa Liṅga (i.e. existing ever since the beginning of the Kalpa), O Great Goddess, worshipped by Devas and Dānavas. A very severe and most difficult penance was performed by the Son of Chāyā (i.e. Saturn or Śani).

## \|\| 1.49.4 \|\|

*anādi nidhano devo yena liṃge'vatāritaḥ \|*  
*prāptavānyo graheśatvaṃ bhaktyā śaṃbhoḥ prasādataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The Lord without beginning or death was brought down to the Liṅga by him. Due to his devotion to Śaṃbhu, he gained his favour and the status of a Planet.

## \|\| 1.49.5-7 \|\|

*yasya dṛṣṭyā bibheti sma devāsuragaṇo mahān \|*  
*na sa ko'pyasti vai prāṇī brahmāṃḍe sacarācare \|\| 5 \|\|*

*devo vā dānavo vāpi sauriṇā pīḍito na yaḥ \|*  
*śanivāreṇa saṃpūjya bhaktyā saurīśvaraṃ śivam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*śamīpatrairmahādevi tilamāṣaguḍaudanaiḥ \|*  
*saṃtarpya tu vidhānena dadyātkṛṣṇaṃ vṛṣaṃ dvije \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. The great community of Devas and Asuras is afraid of his (adverse) look. In the whole of the Cosmos consisting of mobile and immobile beings, there is no living being, Deva or Dānava who is not afflicted by Sauri (i.e. Saturn).

The devotee should worship Saurīśvara Śiva devoutly on Saturdays with Śamī leaves and rice cooked with gingelly seeds, black gram and jaggery. After offering libations in accordance with the injunctions, he should offer a black bull to a Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.49.8 \|\|

*stutvā stotraiśca vividhaiḥ purāṇaśrutisaṃbhavaiḥ \|*  
*atha vaikena deveśaḥ stotreṇa paritoṣitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The deity may be eulogized with hymns of diverse kinds taken from the Purāṇas and Śrutis. Or it is possible to propitiate the Lord of Devas with a single hymn.

## \|\| 1.49.9 \|\|

*rājñā daśarathenaiva kṛtena tu balīyasā \|*  
*stutyaḥ saurīśvaro devaḥ sarvapīḍopaśāṃtaye \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Lord Saurīśvara should be eulogized with a single Stotra composed by the powerful King Daśaratha. The Lord should be eulogized for the sake of subduing all afflictions.

## \|\| 1.49.10 \|\|

*devyu vāca \|*  
*kathaṃ daśaratho rājā cakre śānaiścarīṃ stutim \|*  
*kathaṃ saṃtuṣṭimagamattasya devaḥ śanaiścaraḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

The Devī said:

10\. How did King Daśaratha compose the hymn of Śanaiścara? How did Lord Śanaiścara become pleased with him?

## \|\| 1.49.11 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*raghuvaṃśe'ti vikhyāto rājā daśaratho balī \|*  
*cakravartī sa vijñeyaḥ saptadvīpādhipaḥ purā \|\| 11 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

11\. There was a very powerful king named Daśaratha in the dynasty of Raghu. He was a very well-known emperor, a former overlord of the seven continents.

## \|\| 1.49.12-13 \|\|

*kṛttikāṃte śaniṃ kṛtvā daivajñairjñāpito hi saḥ \|*  
*rohiṇīṃ bheda yitvā tu śaniryāsyati sāṃpratam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*uktaṃ śakaṭabhedaṃ tu surāsurabhayaṃkaram \|*  
*dvādaśābdaṃ tu durbhikṣaṃ bhaviṣyati sudāruṇam \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. When Śani was at the extremity of Kṛttikā the king was informed by astrologers: “Now Śani will pierce through Rohiṇī and go beyond. This is what is called Śakaṭabheda which causes fright even to Suras and Asuras. There will be an extremely disastrous famine lasting for twelve years.”

## \|\| 1.49.14-15 \|\|

*etacchrutvā munervākyaṃ maṃtribhiḥ sahito nṛpaḥ \|*  
*ākulaṃ tu jagaddṛṣṭvā paurajānapadādikam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*vadaṃti satataṃ lokā niyamena samāgatāḥ \|*  
*deśāśca nagara grāmā bhayākrāṃtāḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*munīnvasiṣṭhapramukhānpapraccha ca svayaṃ nṛpaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. On hearing the words of the astrologer-sage he in the company of his ministers saw the entire world including the citizens and rural folk got agitated. People said: “This always occurs regularly. The lands, cities, and villages become terrified all round”. The king asked the sages beginning with Vasiṣṭha:

## \|\| 1.49.16 \|\|

*daśaratha uvāca \|*  
*samādhānaṃ kimatrāste brūhi me dvija sattama \|\| 16 \|\|*

Daśaratha said:

16\. O most excellent-one among Brāhmaṇas, what is the solution of this problem?

## \|\| 1.49.17 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*prājāpatye ca nakṣatre tasminbhinne kutaḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*ayaṃ yogo hyasādhyastu brahmādīṃdrādibhiḥ suraiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

17\. When the constellation pertaining to Prajāpati (i.e. Rohiṇī) is pierced, how can the subjects (survive)? This combination (of planets etc.) has no remedy to be devised by Brahmā, Indra and others too among the Suras.

## \|\| 1.49.18-19 \|\|

*tadā saṃciṃtya manasā sāhasaṃ paramaṃ mahat \|*  
*samādāya dhanurdivyaṃ divyairastraiḥ samanvitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*rathamāruhya vegena gato nakṣatramaṃḍalam \|\| \|*  
*rathaṃ tu kāṃcanaṃ divyaṃ maṇiratnavibhūṣitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. The king pondered over it and decided to take a great risk. He took up his divine bow fitted with divine missiles. He got into his divine golden chariot and hurried towards the stellar zone.

## \|\| 1.49.20 \|\|

*dhvajaiśca cāmaraiśchatraiḥ kiṃkiṇairatha śobhitam \|*  
*haṃsavarṇahayairyuktaṃ mahāketusamanvitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. His chariot was adorned with jewels. It was decorated with banners, Cāmaras, umbrellas and tinkling bells. There was a lofty flagstaff there. It was fitted with swan-coloured horses.

## \|\| 1.49.21 \|\|

*dīpyamāno mahāratnaiḥ kirīṭamukuṭojjvalaḥ \|*  
*babhrāja sa tadākāśe dvitīya iva bhāskaraḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Dazzling with great jewels and refulgent with coronets, he shone in the sky like another Sun.

## \|\| 1.49.22-23 \|\|

*ākarṇaṃ cāpamāpūrya saṃhārāstraṃ niyojya ca \|*  
*kṛttikāṃte śaniṃ jñātvā praviśya kila rohiṇīm \|\| 22 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā daśaratho'syāgre tasthau sabhrukuṭīmukhaḥ \|*  
*saṃhārāstraṃ śanirdṛṣṭvā surāsuravimarddanam \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. He bent the bow as far as his ears after fitting it with a Saṃhārāstra (destructive missile). He saw that Śani had already come to the extremity of Kṛttikā and was about to enter Rohiṇī. Daśaratha stood before him with knitted eyebrows. Śani looked at the Saṃhārāstra that could suppress Suras and Asuras.

## \|\| 1.49.24-26 \|\|

*hasitvā tadrayātsauriridaṃ vacanamabravīt \|*  
*pauruṣaṃ tava rājeṃdra paraṃ ripubhayaṃkaram \|\| 24 \|\|*

*devāsuramanuṣyāśca siddhavidyādharoragāḥ \|*  
*mayā vilokitāḥ sarve bhayaṃ cāśu vrajaṃti te \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tuṣṭohaṃ tava rājeṃdra tapasā pauruṣeṇa ca \|*  
*varaṃ brūhi pradāsyāmi manasā yadabhīpsitam \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. After laughing (to himself), Saturn spoke these words (as though) out of fear for it: “O great king, your manliness is terrifying to your foes. I looked at the Devas, Asuras, human beings, Siddhas, Vidyādharas, Uragas etc. and found all of them terrified. I am now pleased with your bravery and the power of penance, O great king. Tell me what boon you will like to have. I shall grant you whatever you desire.”

## \|\| 1.49.27-28 \|\|

*daśaratha uvāca \|*  
*rohiṇīṃ bhedayitvā tu na gaṃtavyaṃ tvayā śane \|*  
*saritaḥ sāgarā yāvadyāvaccadrārkamedinī \|\| 27 \|\|*

*yācitaṃ te mayā saure nānya micchāmi te varam \|*  
*evamuktaḥ śaniḥ prādādvaraṃ tasmai tu śāśvatam \|\| 28 \|\|*

Daśaratha said:

27-28. O Śani, as long as the rivers and oceans are in existence, as long as the moon, sun and earth are present, you must not pierce through Rohiṇī and go beyond.

O Sauri, no other boon is desired from you by me.

On being told thus, Śani granted him a boon of permanent benefit.

## \|\| 1.49.29 \|\|

*prāpyaivaṃ tu varaṃ rājā kṛtakṛtyo'bhavattadā \|*  
*punarevābravītsaurirvaraṃ varaya suvrata \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. After receiving this boon, the king became gratified. Sauri once again told him, “O king of excellent holy rites, choose your boon.”

## \|\| 1.49.30-31 \|\|

*prārthayāmāsa hṛṣṭātmā varamevaṃ śanestadā \|*  
*na bhettavyaṃ ca śakaṭaṃ tvayā bhāskaranaṃdana \|\| 30 \|\|*

*dvādaśābdaṃ tu durbhikṣaṃ na kartavyaṃ kadācana \|*  
*kīrtireṣā madīyā ca trailokye vicariṣyati \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. (The king) delighted in his mind requested for this boon from Śani: “O son of Bhāskara, the Śakaṭa (Cart-shaped constellation, Rohiṇī) should not be pierced through by you. Never should the famine lasting for twelve years be caused. This fame of mine shall spread all over the three worlds.”

## \|\| 1.49.32-33 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*varadvayaṃ tataḥ prāpya hṛṣṭaromā sa pārthivaḥ \|*  
*rathopari dhanurmuktvā bhūtvā caiva kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*dhyātvā sarasvatīṃ devīṃ gaṇanāthaṃ vināyakam \|*  
*rājā daśarathaḥ stotraṃ saureridamathākarot \|\| 33 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

32-33. The king experienced horripilation on receiving the two boons. He put the bow in the chariot and stood with palms joined in reverence. Meditating on Goddess Sarasvatī and Vināyaka, the leader of Gaṇas, King Daśaratha composed this prayer of Sauri (Śani).

## \|\| 1.49.34 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*namo nīlamayūkhāya nīlotpalanibhāya ca \|*  
*namo nirmāṃsadehāya dīrghaśmaśrujaṭāya ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

The king said:

(King Daśaratha’s prayer to Saturn)

34\. Obeisance to the blue-rayed one, to the one resembling a blue lotus. Obeisance to one with the body bereft of flesh, to one with long beard and matted hairs.

## \|\| 1.49.35 \|\|

*namo viśālanetrāya śuṣkodarabhayāna ka \|*  
*namaḥ paruṣagātrāya sthūlaromāya vai namaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O dry (lean)-bellied one, O terrible one, obeisance to the one with large eyes. Obeisance to the rough-limbed one. Obeisance to the thick-haired one.

## \|\| 1.49.36 \|\|

*namo nityaṃ kṣudhārttāya nityataptāya vai namaḥ \|*  
*namaḥ kālāgnirūpāya kṛtāṃtaka namostu te \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Obeisance to one, always distressed with hunger. Obeisance to one who is satisfied always. Obeisance to one in the form of Kālāgni (Black fire i.e. Fire at the end of the world).

## \|\| 1.49.37 \|\|

*namo dīrghāya śuṣkāya kāladṛṣṭe namo'stu te \|*  
*namaste koṭarākṣāya durnirīkṣyāya vai namaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Obeisance to the long one, to the dry one. O black-eyed one, (I offer) obeisance to you. Obeisance to the hollow-eyed one. Obeisance to one very difficult to look at.

## \|\| 1.49.38 \|\|

*namo ghorāya raudrāya bhīṣaṇāya karā line \|*  
*namaste sarvabhakṣāya valīmukha namo'stu te \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Obeisance to the frightening one, to the terrible one, to the awe-inspiring one, to the appalling one. Obeisance to you the all-consuming one. Obeisance to you, O wrinkle-faced one.

## \|\| 1.49.39 \|\|

*sūryaputra namaste'stu bhāskare bhayadāyaka \|*  
*adhodṛṣṭe namastubhyaṃ vapuḥśyāma namo'stu te \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Obeisance to you, O son of the Sun-god. O Bhāskari, the frightening one. O one with downcast eyes, obeisance to you, O one black in body, obeisance to you.

## \|\| 1.49.40 \|\|

*namo mandagate tubhyaṃ nistriṃśāya namonamaḥ \|*  
*namasta ugrarūpāya caṇḍatejāya te namaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Obeisance to you, O slow-gaited one. Obeisance! Obeisance to the pitiless one. Obeisance to you, the fierce-formed one. Obeisance to you fierce in refulgence.

## \|\| 1.49.41 \|\|

*tapasā dagdhadehāya nityaṃ yogaratāya ca \|*  
*namaste jñānanetrāya kaśyapātmajasūnave \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Obeisance to the one always burnt with penance. Obeisance to one always sitting in Yogic posture. Obeisance to you with vision of knowledge, the offspring of the son of Kaśyapa (Sun-god).

## \|\| 1.49.42-45 \|\|

*tuṣṭo dadāsi vai rājyaṃ ruṣṭo harasi tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*devāsuramanuṣyāśca paśupakṣisarīsṛpāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tvayā vilokitāḥ saure dainyamāśu vrajaṃti ca \|*  
*brahmā śakro yamaścaiva ṛṣayaḥ saptatārakāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*rājyabhraṣṭāśca te sarve tava dṛṣṭyā vilokitāḥ \|*  
*deśāśca nagaragrāmā dvīpāścaivādrayastathā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*raudradṛṣṭyā tu ye dṛṣṭāḥ kṣayaṃ gacchaṃti tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 45 \|\|*

42-45. When pleased, you grant a kingdom; when angry you deprive one of it in and instant.

Devas, Asuras, and human beings, beasts, birds and reptiles looked at (adversely) by you, O Sauri, immediately become wretched.

Brahmā, Śakra, Yama, the seven redeeming sages—all these become ousted from their kingdoms on being glared at by your eyes.

The lands, cities, villages, continents, and mountains—when looked at with horrible eyes perish in an instant.

## \|\| 1.49.46 \|\|

*prasādaṃ kuru me saure varārthe'haṃ tavāśritaḥ \|*  
*saure kṣamasvāparādhaṃ sarvabhūtahitāya ca \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Be favourable to me, O Sauri, I have resorted to you for the sake of boons. O Sauri, forgive my fault for the sake of the welfare of all living beings.

## \|\| 1.49.47 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ stutastadā saurī rājñā daśarathena ca \|*  
*maharājaḥ śanirvākyaṃ hṛṣṭaro mā'bravīdidam \|\| 47 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

47\. On being eulogized thus by King Daśaratha, Śani, the son of Sun, the king of Planets, spoke these words with hairs standing on ends:

## \|\| 1.49.48 \|\|

*śaniruvāca \|*  
*tuṣṭo'haṃ tava rājendra stavenānena suvrata \|*  
*varaṃ brūhi pradāsyāmi svecchayā raghunaṃdana \|\| 48 \|\|*

Śani said:

48\. O great king of good holy rites, O scion of the family of Raghu, I am pleased with this prayer of thine. Tell me what boon you will like to have; I shall grant that voluntarily.

## \|\| 1.49.49 \|\|

*daśaratha uvāca \|*  
*adyaprabhṛti piṃgākṣa pīḍā kāryā na kasyacit \|*  
*devāsuramanuṣyāṇāṃ paśupakṣisarīsṛpām \|\| 49 \|\|*

Daśaratha said:

49\. O tawny-eyed one, from now onwards no one should be afflicted, none among the Devas, Asuras and human beings, among beasts, birds and reptiles.

## \|\| 1.49.50 \|\|

*śaniruvāca \|*  
*grahāṇāṃ durgraho jñeyo grahapīḍāṃ karomyaham \|*  
*adeyaṃ prārthitaṃ rājankiṃcidyuktaṃ dadāmyaham \|\| 50 \|\|*

Śani said:

50\. I should be known as an evil Planet among all the Planets. I cause affliction as a Planet. O king, something that should not be given has been requested for. I am ready to grant something which is appropriate.

## \|\| 1.49.51-53 \|\|

*tvayā proktaṃ mama stotraṃ ye paṭhi ṣyaṃti mānavāḥ \|*  
*puruṣāśca striyo vāpi madbhayenopapīḍitāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*devāsuramanuṣyāstu siddhavidyādharoragāḥ \|*  
*mṛtyusthāne sthito vāpi janmaprāṃtagatastathā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*ekakālaṃ dvikālaṃ vā teṣāṃ śreyo dadāmyaham \|*  
*pūjayitvā japetstotraṃ bhūtvā caiva kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

51-53. To men or women who recite the hymn composed by you on me after being afflicted with fear of mine, to Devas, Asuras and human beings, to Siddhas, Vidyādharas and Uragas I shall grant permanent welfare. I may be staying in the House of Death or I may be in the House of Nativity (in their horoscopes), they should recite the hymn once or twice a day, the devotee should worship me and repeat the Stotra in all reverence with palms joined together.

## \|\| 1.49.54 \|\|

*tasya pīḍāṃ na caivāhamiha kuryāṃ kadācana \|*  
*janmasthāne sthito vāpi mṛtyusthāne sthito'pi ca \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. I will not cause affliction to him at any time whether I am present in the House of Nativity or in the House of Death (in his horoscope).

## \|\| 1.49.55 \|\|

*janmaṛkṣe ca lagne ca daśāsvaṃtardaśāsu ca \|*  
*rakṣāmi satataṃ tasya pīḍāṃ cānyagrahasya ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. I shall always grant him protection from other Planets too and their affliction in the Constellation of Nativity or Lagna or in the Daśās (aspects of Planets) or sub-Daśās.

## \|\| 1.49.56 \|\|

*anenaiva prakāreṇa rpāḍāmuktastvasau bhavet \|*  
*etatproktaṃ mayā dattaṃ varaṃ ca raghunaṃdana \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. In this manner he shall be rid of afflictions. Thus the boon asked for by you has been granted by me, O scion of Raghu’s family.

## \|\| 1.49.57 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*varadvayaṃ ca saṃprāpya rājā daśarathaḥ purā \|*  
*mene kṛtārthamātmānaṃ namaskṛtya śanaiścaram \|\| 57 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

57\. After acquiring the pair of boons formerly, King Daśaratha considered himself blessed. He bowed to Śanaiścara with reverence.

## \|\| 1.49.58 \|\|

*śaniṃ stutvā'bhyanujñāto rathamāruhya vīryavān \|*  
*svasthānaṃ gatavānrājā pūjyamāno divaukasaiḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. After eulogizing Śani and on being permitted by him, the powerful king got into his chariot and went back to bis abode. He was duly honoured by the Heaven-dwellers.

## \|\| 1.49.59 \|\|

*ya idaṃ prātarutthāya saurivāre paṭhennaraḥ \|*  
*sarvagrahodbhavā pīḍā na bhavedbhuvi tasya tu \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. If any man gets up early in the morning on a Saturday and recites this Stotra he will never suffer from affliction caused by any Planet.

## \|\| 1.49.60 \|\|

*śanaiścaraṃ smareddevaṃ nityaṃ bhaktisamanvitaḥ \|*  
*pūjayitvā paṭhetstotraṃ tasya tuṣyati bhāskariḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. One should always remember Lord Śanaiścara with great devotion. One should recite the Stotra after adoration. The Son of Bhāskara (Śani) becomes pleased with him.

## \|\| 1.49.61 \|\|

*iti te kathitaṃ devi māhātmyaṃ śanidaivatam \|*  
*sarvapāpopaśamanaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Thus, O goddess, the greatness pertaining to the deity Śani (or deity installed by Śani) has been told to you. It suppresses all sins. It yields all the desired benefits.

## Chapter 50 - Greatness of Rāhvīśvara (Rāhu-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.50.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi liṃgaṃ rāhupratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*śanaiścareśvarāddevi vāyavye saṃpratiṣṭhitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ajādevyāścottarato dhanuṣāṃ saptake sthitam \|*  
*maṃgalāyāḥ samīpasthaṃ nātidūre vyavasthitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*liṃgaṃ mahāprabhāvaṃ tu saiṃhikeyapratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*tatra varṣasahasraṃ tu vaipracittistapo'karot \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, O great goddess, the pilgrim should proceed to the Liṅga well installed by Rāhu to the north-west of Śanaiścara.

It is situated within a distance of seven Dhanus to the north of Ajādevī. It is also in the vicinity of Maṅgalā, not very far off.

The Liṅga installed by Saiṃhikeya (Rāhu) is of great efficacy. Vaipracitti (Rāhu) performed a penance there for a thousand years.

## \|\| 1.50.4-5 \|\|

*svarbhānuḥ sa mahāvīryo vaktrayodhī mahāsurāḥ \|*  
*samārādhya mahādevaṃ divyena tapasā prabhum \|\| 4 \|\|*

*liṃge'vatārayāmāsa jagaddīpaṃ maheśvaram \|*  
*yaścainaṃ pūjayedbhaktyā naraḥ samyakca paśyati \|*  
*tasya pāpaṃ kṣayaṃ yāti api brahmavadhodbhavam \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. That mighty and great Asura, Svarbhānu, adept in crooked fighting propitiated the great Lord by means of his wonderful penance and caused Maheśvara, the light of the Universe, to come down in the Liṅga.

He who worships it with devotion and views it clearly shall get his sin reduced to nothing, even if it be the result of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter.

## \|\| 1.50.6 \|\|

*nāṃdho na badhiro mūko na rogī na ca nirddhanaḥ \|*  
*kadācijjāyate martyastena dṛṣṭena bhūtale \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. If he is viewed, the devotee, the man, never becomes blind, deaf, dumb, sick or poor.

## \|\| 1.50.7 \|\|

*sukhasaubhāgyasaṃpannastadā bhavati rūpavān \|*  
*sarvakāmasamṛddhātmā modate divi devavat \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He becomes handsome and richly endowed with happiness and conjugal felicity. With all his desires richly realized, he rejoices like a Deva in heaven.

## \|\| 1.50.8 \|\|

*iti te kathitaṃ devi māhātmyaṃ rāhudaivatam \|*  
*śrutvā tu mohaniryāto naro niṣkalmaṣo bhavet \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thus, O goddess, the greatness of the deity installed by Rāhu has been spoken to you. One listening to this, comes out of delusion and becomes free from sins.

## Chapter 51 - Greatness of Ketvīśvra (Ketu-īśvra)

## \|\| 1.51.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi ketuliṃgaṃ mahāprabham \|*  
*rāhvīśānāduttare ca maṃgalāyāśca dakṣiṇe \|\| 1 \|\|*

*dhanuṣoṃtaramānena nātidūre vyavasthitam \|*  
*liṃgaṃ mahāprabhāvaṃ hi sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*keturnāma grahotyugraḥ śivasadbhāvabhāvitaḥ \|*  
*vartulo'tīva vistīrṇo locanābhyāṃ subhīṣaṇaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Then, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to Ketuliṅga of great lustre. It is on the north of Rāhvīśāna and the south of Maṅgalā.

It is situated not very far off, say, within a few Dhanus. This Liṅga is of great efficacy and is destructive of all sins.

The Planet named Ketu is extremely ferocious but sanctified by means of Śivasadbhāva (good feelings towards Lord Śiva). He is extremely terrible with round large eyes.

## \|\| 1.51.4 \|\|

*palāladhūmasaṃkāśo grahapīḍāpahārakaḥ \|*  
*tatrākarottapaścograṃ divyābdānāṃ śataṃ priye \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He resembles in colour smoke emitted by burning straws, dispels the afflictions caused by evil Planets, and O my beloved, he performed a severe penance there for a hundred years according to divine reckoning.

## \|\| 1.51.5 \|\|

*tasya tuṣṭo mahādevo graha tvaṃ pradadau priye \|*  
*ekādaśaśatānāṃ ca grahāṇāmādhipatyatām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Mahādeva was pleased with him and granted him the status of a Planet and also the overlordship of eleven hundred Grahas (Planets).

## \|\| 1.51.6-7 \|\|

*tatrasthaṃ pūjayedbhaktyā ketuliṃgaṃ mahāprabham \|*  
*ketūdaye mahāghore tasmindṛṣṭe viśeṣataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*grahapīḍāsu cogrāsu pūjayettaṃ vidhānataḥ \|*  
*puṣpairgaṃdhaistathā dhūpairnaivedyairvividhaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. At the time of the terrible rise of Ketu, especially when he is seen, and also during the horrible afflictions caused by evil Planets, one should worship the deity in accordance with the injunctions.

The devotee should adore the deity with flowers, sweet scents, incense and splendid Naivedyas of various kinds.

## \|\| 1.51.8 \|\|

*toṣayedvidhivaddevaṃ ketuṃ kalmaṣanāśanam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He should duly propitiate Lord Ketu, the destroyer of sins.

## \|\| 1.51.9 \|\|

*iti saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ ketuliṃgaṃ mahodayam \|*  
*grahapīḍopaśamanaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thus Ketuliṅga granting great prosperity has been succinctly mentioned. It suppresses the afflictions caused by the Planets and destroys all sins.

## \|\| 1.51.10 \|\|

*etāni nava liṃgāni grahāṇāṃ kathitāni te \|*  
*yaḥ paśyati naro nityaṃ tasya pīḍābhayaṃ kutaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thus the nine Liṅgas of the Planets have been spoken to you. If a man views them all everyday, whence can he have the fear of afflictions?

## \|\| 1.51.11 \|\|

*na daurbhāgyaṃ kule tasya na rogī naiva duḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*jāyate putravaddevi taṃ rakṣaṃti mahāgrahāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O goddess, wretchedness never occurs in his family. No sick or miserable one is born in his family. The great Planets protect him like a son.

## \|\| 1.51.12 \|\|

*iti te kathitaṃ samyakcaturdaśāyatanaṃ priye \|*  
*vighneśvaraṃ samārabhya yāvatketupratiṣṭhitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thus, O my beloved, the fourteen shrines beginning with Vighneśvara and ending with the shrine installed by Ketu, have been described to you.

## \|\| 1.51.13 \|\|

*navagraheśvarāṇāṃ tu māhātmyaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*tathaiva paṃcaliṃgānāṃ śrutvā pāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The greatness of the deities of the nine Planets is destructive of sins. So also is that of the five Liṅgas. By listening to it, one is rid of all sins.

## \|\| 1.51.14 \|\|

*kaparddinaṃ samārabhya caṃḍanāthāṃtakāni ca \|*  
*paṃcaiva mudrāliṃgāni nāpuṇyo veda mānavaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. A man devoid of merits never knows the five Mudrā Liṅgas beginning with Kapardin and ending with Caṇḍanātha.

## \|\| 1.51.15 \|\|

*sūryeśvaraṃ samārabhya ketuliṃgāṃtakāni vai \|*  
*navagrahāṇāṃ liṃgāni nānyo jānāti kaścana \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. No one else knows the Liṅgas of the nine Planets beginning with Sūryeśvara and ending with Ketuliṅga.

## \|\| 1.51.16 \|\|

*caturdaśavidhā tvevaṃ proktā'yatanasaṃgatiḥ \|*  
*yaścaināṃ veda bhāvena sa kṣetraphalamaśnute \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thus the fourteen types of shrine setting have been described. He who attentively knows this, attains the benefit of (visiting) the holy spots.

## Chapter 52 - Greatness of Siddheśvara (Siddha-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.52.1-2 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*paṃcātha siddhaliṃgāni kathayāmi yaśasvini \|*  
*yeṣāṃ darśanato devi siddhā yātrā bhavennṛṇām \|\| 1 \|\|*

*someśādīśadigbhāge varāroheti yā smṛtā \|*  
*tasyāśca pūrvadigbhāge devaṃ siddheśvaraṃ param \|*  
*abhigamya naro bhaktyā aṇimādikamāpnuyāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-2. O glorious lady, I shall describe to you the five Siddha Liṅgas, which on being seen make the pilgrimage of men fruitful or perfectly accomplished.

Lord Siddheśvara is stationed to the east of the deity remembered as Varārohā situated to the north-east of Someśa. A man who visits with devotion this great Siddheśvara shall acquire supernatural powers like Aṇimā etc.

## \|\| 1.52.3 \|\|

*siddhaiḥ pratiṣṭhitaṃ liṃgaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhaktyā tu mānavaḥ \|*  
*mucyate pātakaiḥ sarvaiḥ siddhalokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. By devoutly viewing the Liṅga installed by Siddhas, a man is rid of all sins. He goes to the Siddhaloka.

## \|\| 1.52.4-6 \|\|

*vighnāni nāśamāyāṃti tatra kṣetranivāsinām \|*  
*kāmaḥ krodho bhaya lobho rāgo matsara eva ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

*īrṣyā daṃbhastathā'lasyaṃ nidrā mohastvahaṃkṛtiḥ \|*  
*etāni vighnarūpāṇi siddhervighnakarāṇi tu \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tāni nāśaṃ samāyāṃti tatra siddhe śvarārcanāt \|*  
*evaṃ jñātvā tu yatnena tatra yātrāṃ samācaret \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. All obstacles of the residents of those holy spots are destroyed. The obstacles are lust, anger, fear, covetousness, passion, rivalry, jealousy, hypocrisy, lethargy, drowsiness, delusion and egotism. These are obstacles to the achievement of (spiritual) perfection.

By worshipping the Siddheśvaras there all these obstacles disappear. One should undertake the pilgrimage strenuously after knowing this very well.

## \|\| 1.52.7 \|\|

*ityevaṃ kathitaṃ devi siddheśvaramahodayam \|*  
*sarvakāmapradaṃ nṛṇāṃ śrutaṃ pātakanāśanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thus, O goddess, the great rise and prosperity of Siddheśvara has been spoken. It yields all cherished desires unto men. If listened to (attentively), it is destructive of sins.

## Chapter 53 - Greatness of Kapileśvara (Kapila-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.53.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi kapileśvaramuttamam \|*  
*tasyaiva pūrvadigbhāge nātidūre vyava sthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*liṃgaṃ mahāprabhāvaṃ tu darśanātpāpanāśanam \|*  
*kapilonāma rājarṣiryatra taptvā mahātapaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*saṃprāptaḥ paramāṃ siddhiṃ pratiṣṭhāpya maheśvaram \|*  
*devasāṃnidhyamīśānaṃ tasmiṃlliṃge sadā hariḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śuklapakṣe caturdaśyāṃ sarvalokahitārthataḥ \|*  
*saptakṛtvo mahādevaṃ someśaṃ kapileśvaram \|*  
*yaḥ paśyetprayato bhūtvā sa godānaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Then, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the excellent shrine of Kapileśvara. It is stationed not far from it (i.e. Siddheśvara) in the eastern quarter.

This Liṅga is of very great power. It destroys sins by its very sight. A saintly king named Kapila performed a great penance there after installing Maheśvara. He attained great Siddhi (spiritual achievement). Hari always worships Īśāna in the presence of the Devas in that Liṅga.

Especially on the fourteenth lunar day in the bright half of a month, he worships, Mahādeva seven times, for the sake of the welfare of all the worlds.

One who remains pure and clean and visits Someśa named Kapileśvara shall attain the merit of gifting cows.

## \|\| 1.53.5 \|\|

*tiladhenuṃ ca yo dadyāttasmiṃstīrthe samāhitaḥ \|*  
*tilasaṃkhyāyugānyeva sa svarge vasati priye \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O my beloved, one who is mentally pure and offers Tiladhenu (cow made of gingelly seeds) in that holy spot, remains in heaven for as many Yugas as there are gingelly seeds.

## Chapter 54 - Greatness of Gandharveśvara (Gandharva-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.54.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi gaṃdharveśvaramuttamam \|*  
*daṇḍapāṇestu bhavanāduttare nikaṭe sthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yatra gaṃdharvarājo vai ghanavāheti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*tasya gaṃdharvaseneti khyātā putrī mahāprabhā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*śikhaṃḍinā gaṇenaiva sā śaptā rūpagarvitā \|*  
*tato gośṛṃgaṛṣiṇā dattastasyā anugrahaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Then, O great goddess, one should go to the excellent Gandharveśvara. It is situated very near, to the north of the abode of Daṇḍapāṇi.

It was here that the king of Gandharvas well-known as Ghanavāha (ruled). His daughter well-known as Gandharvasenā was highly lustrous.

She was arrogant due to her beauty and so was cursed by a Gaṇa named Śikhaṇḍin. Thereupon, blessings were given to her by Sage Gośṛṅga.

## \|\| 1.54.4-5 \|\|

*somavāravratenaiva someśārādhanaṃ prati \|*  
*tataḥ kṣetraṃ samāgatya tapaḥ kṛtvā suduścaram \|\| 4 \|\|*

*liṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhayāmāsa tatra gaṃdharvarāṭ svayam \|*  
*tathaiva putryā tasyaiva tatra liṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. He directed her to propitiate Someśa by means of the Somavāra Vrata. Thereafter, the king of Gandharvas himself came to the holy spot and performed very difficult penance and installed a Liṅga. Another Liṅga was installed by his own daughter.

## \|\| 1.54.6-7 \|\|

*atha tatraiva deveśi daṃḍapāṇeḥ samīpataḥ \|*  
*ghanavāheśvaraṃ nāma yo liṃgaṃ yatnato'rcayet \|\| 6 \|\|*

*gaṃdharvalokamāpnoti dṛṣṭvā sa prayataḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*iti te kathitaṃ devi gāṃdharvaṃ liṃgamuttamam \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. O goddess of Devas, one who scrupulously worships the Liṅga named Ghanavāheśvara there itself in the vicinity of Daṇḍapāṇi and/or visits the deity, himself being clean and pure, attains Gandharva world. Thus, O goddess, the excellent Gandharva Liṅga has been spoken to you.

## \|\| 1.54.8-9 \|\|

*tṛtīyaṃ sarvapāpānāṃ nāśanaṃ puṇyavarddhanam \|*  
*agnitīrthe naraḥ snātvā pūjya gaṃdharvapūjitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*ayane cottare prāpte nirvāṇamadhigacchati \|*  
*śrutvā 'bhinaṃdya māhātmyaṃ mucyate mahato bhayāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. It is the third Liṅga (in this context). It is destructive of all sins and it increases merit. A man who bathes in the Agnitīrtha and worships the Liṅga adored by Gandharvas at the time of the northern transit of the Sun, attains salvation. By listening to and approving the greatness of it, one is rid of great danger.

## Chapter 55 - Greatness of Vimaleśvara (Vimala-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.55.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi tatpūrve vimaleśvaram \|*  
*gauryāḥ pūrvaṃ samīpasthaṃ nātidūre vyavasthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*gurornairṛtyadigbhāge sthitaṃ pāpapraṇāśanam \|*  
*api kṛtvā mahāpāpaṃ nārī vā puruṣo'pi vā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kṣayābhibhūtadeho vā taṃ samabhyarcya bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*sarvaduḥkhāntago bhūtvā nirmalaṃ padamāpnuyāt \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Then, O great goddess, one should go to Vimaleśvara (stationed) to the east thereof. It is very near, not far from Gaurī’s shrine.

It is situated on the south-west of Guru (Jupiter). It is destructive of sins. Even after committing a great sin, a devotee, be it a woman or a man, becomes pure.

Even one who is afflicted with pulmonary consumption, attains the destruction of all miseries by adoring the deity with devotion. He shall attain the region devoid of impurities.

## \|\| 1.55.4 \|\|

*gaṃdharvasenā yatraiva vimalā'bhūtkṣayā nvitā \|*  
*vimaleśvaranāmnā vai talliṃgaṃ prathitaṃ kṣitau \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. It was there that Gandharvasenā who was afflicted with phthysis got rid of impurities. That Liṅga has become famous all the world over by the name Vimaleśvara.

## \|\| 1.55.5 \|\|

*iti te kathitaṃ sarvaṃ vimaleśvarasūcakam \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ sarvapāpaghnaṃ turīyaṃ bhavasundari \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Thus the greatness of Vimaleśvara has been entirely spoken to you, O beautiful lady of Bhava. It is the fourth (Liṅga) destructive of all sins.

## Chapter 56 - Greatness of Dhanadeśvara (Dhanada-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.56.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*atha te paṃcamaṃ vacmi siddhaligaṃ mahāprabham \|*  
*brahmaṇo nairṛte bhāge dhanuṣāṃ ṣoḍaśe sthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*rāhuliṃgasya cābhyāśe liṃgaṃ dhanadanirmitam \|*  
*dhanadatvaṃ ca saṃprāpto yatra taptvā mahattapaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*saṃsthāpya vidhivatpūjya liṃgaṃ varṣasahasrakam \|*  
*alakādhipatirjātastatra śaṃbhoḥ prasādataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Henceforth I shall describe the fifth Siddha Liṅga of great lustre. It is situated on the south-western side of Brahmā at a distance of about sixteen bows.

The Liṅga installed by Dhanada (i.e. Kubera, the bestower of wealth) is near Rāhuliṅga. Here he performed great penance and attained the status of Dhanada (Giver of wealth).

He installed the Liṅga and duly worshipped it for a thousand years. With the favour of Śaṃbhu, he became the Lord of Alakā.

## \|\| 1.56.4-7 \|\|

*jātiṃ smṛtvā pūrvikāṃ tu jñātvā dīpadaśāphalam \|*  
*śivarātre prabhāvaṃ tu prabhāsaṃ punarāgataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*prabhāvātiśayaṃ jñātvā sthāpayāmāsa śaṃkaram \|*  
*tatra pratyakṣatāṃ nītastapasā yena śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*mahābhaktyā mahādevi tasmiṃlliṃge'vatāritaḥ \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā mānavo bhaktyā pūjayitvā yathāvidhi \|\| 6 \|\|*

*pañcopacāraiḥ sadbhaktyā gandhadhūpānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*tasyānvaye daridraśca kadāpi na bhaviṣyati \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-7. He remembered his previous birth and knowing the merit of supplying a wick for lamp and the power of Śivarātri, came to Prabhāsa.

Knowing the great power of it he installed Śaṅkara. By means of penance, he made Śaṅkara manifest. O great goddess, by means of his great devotion he caused Śaṅkara to come down in that Liṅga. A man of devotion should visit it and perform worship duly observing the five Upacāras (varieties of service) and offering scents, incense and unguents with great devotion. Never will a destitute person be born in his family.

## \|\| 1.56.8-9 \|\|

*ye caitatpūjayiṣyaṃti liṃgaṃ bhaktiyutā narāḥ \|*  
*ajeyāste bhaviṣyaṃti śatrūṇāṃ darpanāśanāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*iti te kathitaṃ sarvaṃ dhanadeśamahodayam \|*  
*śrutvānumodya yatnena daridro naiva jāyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Those men who with devotion worship the Liṅga become invincible to enemies whose arrogance they will destroy.

Thus the greatness of Dhandeśa has been fully spoken to you. By listening to this and approving of it, one shall avert poverty.

## Chapter 57 - Greatness of Varārohā

## \|\| 1.57.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*paṃcaivaṃ siddhaliṃgāni kathitāni tava priye \|*  
*yaścainaṃ veda saṃketaṃ kṣetravāsī sa ucyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

*atha śaktitrayāṇāṃ te raudrīṇāṃ vacmi vistaram \|*  
*icchā kriyājñānaśaktyastisrastāḥ parikīrttitāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*punastāsāṃ pūjanāyānukramaṃ kramataḥ śṛṇu \|*  
*caturdaśa tathā paṃca pūrvamuktāni yāni tu \|\| 3 \|\|*

*catvāri trīṇi caikaṃ vā yathāśaktyābhipūjya ca \|*  
*liṃgāni tāni saṃpūjya śaktīstisrastato'rcayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Thus, O my beloved, five Siddhaliṅgas have been spoken to you. He who understands this convention is called Kṣetravāsin (a resident of holy spot).

Henceforth, I shall describe in detail the three Śaktis of Rudra to you. They are: Icchā (Volition), Jñāna (Knowledge) and Kriyā (Action) of the Liṅgas mentioned to you previously. Listen to the sequence of their worship. A devotee duly worships fourteen, five, four, three or one in accordance with his capacity and thereafter adores the three Śaktis.

## \|\| 1.57.5 \|\|

*someśādīśadigbhāge varāroheti yā smṛtā \|*  
*amā kalā sā somasya umā paścātprakīrttitā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The deity stationed on the north-east of Someśa and remembered as Varārohā is the digit Amā of Soma (Moon). It is later glorified as Umā.

## \|\| 1.57.6 \|\|

*icchāśaktistu sā jñeyāprabhāsakṣetrasaṃsthitā \|*  
*tatra devi hitārthāya sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ bhuvi \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The deity is to be known as Icchā Śakti. She is stationed in Prabhāsa Kṣetra, O goddess, for the welfare of all the living beings on the earth.

## \|\| 1.57.7-9 \|\|

*tasyā māhātmyamakhilaṃ kathayāmi tavādhunā \|*  
*purā somena tyaktābhirbhāryābhistu varānane \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ṣaḍviṃśadbhistapastaptaṃ kṣetre prābhāsike śubhe \|*  
*gaurī sā'rādhyamānātha divyavarṣagaṇānbahūn \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tāsāṃ pratyakṣatāṃ prāptā pārvatī parameśvarī \|*  
*uvāca varadā brūta yadvo manasi saṃsthitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. Now I shall fully narrate the greatness of that deity to you. O lady of excellent countenance, a penance was performed by the twenty-six wives ignored and abandoned by Soma. For many years according to the divine reckoning, Gaurī was propitiated in the splendid holy spot of Prabhāsa. Pārvatī, the great goddess, became manifest to them and said: “I am the bestower of boons. Do tell me what has been thought of in your minds.”

## \|\| 1.57.10-11 \|\|

*atha tāścābruvandevi yadi tuṣṭāsi pārvati \|*  
*saubhāgyaṃ dehi no bhūri lāvaṇyaṃ paramaṃ tathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tyaktāḥ sarvā vayaṃ devi nirdoṣāḥ svāminā śubhe \|*  
*daurbhāgyadoṣasaṃdagdhā daurbhāgyeṇa tu pīḍitāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Then they said: “O goddess Pārvatī, if you are pleased, grant unto us the utmost conjugal felicity and excellent loveliness. O splendid goddess, though guiltless, all of us have been deserted by our Lord and master. We have been scorched by the fault of unluckiness and afflicted by adverse fate.”

## \|\| 1.57.12 \|\|

*gauryuvāca \|*  
*adyaprabhṛti sarvā vaḥ samaṃ drakṣyati rātripaḥ \|*  
*prasādānmama cārvaṃgyo naitanmithyā bhaviṣyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

Gaurī said:

12\. From now onwards the Lord of the Night (Soma) will treat all of you alike, with my favour. O ladies of exquisitely beautiful limbs, this will never be false.

## \|\| 1.57.13-16 \|\|

*varadā ceti mannāma varadānādbhaviṣyati \|*  
*ihāgatya tu yā nārī pūjayiṣyati māṃ śubhām \|\| 13 \|\|*

*na daurbhāgyaṃ kule tasyāḥ kvacitprāpsyaṃti yoṣitaḥ \|*  
*māghamāse tṛtīyāyāmupavāsaparāyaṇā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yā māṃ drakṣyati suśroṇī mattulyā sā bhavi ṣyati \|*  
*dampatī ṣoḍaśaivātra paridhāpya prayatnataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*phalāni bhakṣyabhojyaṃ ca pakvānnāni ca ṣoḍaśa \|*  
*yā pradāsyati vai nārī sā tūmaiva bhaviṣyati \|\| 16 \|\|*

13-16. On account of this granting of the boon, my name will be Varadā. If any woman comes here and adores me, the splendid one, the women in her family will never meet with bad luck.

A woman of excellent hips who observes fast on the third lunar day in the month of Māgha and views me, will be on a par with me.

A woman who scrupulously offers garments to sixteen couples and feeds them with fruits and various foodstuffs as well as sixteen types of sweetmeats will definitely become Umā.

## \|\| 1.57.17 \|\|

*etadgaurīvrataṃnāma tṛtīyāyāṃ tu kārayet \|*  
*aprasūtā ca yā nārī yā nārī durbhagā bhavet \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. A woman of ill-luck and one who has not yet given birth to any child, should perform this holy rite named Gaurīvrata on the third lunar day.

## \|\| 1.57.18 \|\|

*pumānasakṛdapyaivaṃ kṛtvā prāpsyatyabhīpsitam \|*  
*evamuktvā sthitā tatra sā devī cārulocanā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. A man who performs this Vrata frequently shall obtain the desired things.

After saying this, that goddess of beautiful eyes stood by.

## \|\| 1.57.19-21 \|\|

*paśyate rātrināthaśca sarvāstā rohiṇīṃ yathā \|*  
*anyāpi duḥkhasaṃdagdhā daurbhāgyeṇa tu pīḍitā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*apūjayadumāṃ devīṃ subhagā sā'bhavattataḥ \|*  
*iti saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ māhātmyaṃ śaktisaṃbhavam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*someśvare varārohā nāmeti kathitaṃ tava \|*  
*sarvapāpakṣayakaraṃ sarvadāridryanāśanam \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. The Lord of the Night began to treat all of them as he treated Rohiṇī. Another woman scorched by misery and blighted by misfortune worshipped Goddess Umā and she became happy and lucky thereafter.

Thus the greatness of Śakti has been succinctly described. The name Varārohā of thine, has been mentioned in the holy spot of Someśvara. It causes the destruction of all sins and of poverty of all sorts.

## Chapter 58 - Greatness of Ajāpāleśvarī (Ajāpāla-īśvarī)

## \|\| 1.58.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*atha dvitīyāṃ te vacmi śaktiṃ devi kriyātmikām \|*  
*prabhāsasthāṃ mahādevīṃ devānāṃ prītidāyinīm \|\| 1 \|\|*

*someśādvāyave bhāge ṣaṣṭidhanvatare sthitā \|*  
*tatra pīṭhaṃ mahādevi yoginīgaṇavanditam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tasminsthāne sthitaṃ devi pātālavivaraṃ mahat \|*  
*tasminmahāprabhe sthāne rakṣārūpeṇa saṃsthitām \|\| 3 \|\|*

*pātālanidhi nikṣepadivyauṣadhirasāyanam \|*  
*kṣetramadhye sthitaṃ sarvaṃ tadarcanarato labhet \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Henceforth, O goddess, I shall describe unto you the Śakti of the nature of Kriyā (Action). It is stationed in Prabhāsa as the great goddess bestowing pleasure on Devas.

The deity is situated within a distance of sixty Dhanus in the north-west direction of Someśvara. O great goddess, the pedestal there is honoured by groups of Yoginīs.

At that spot, O goddess, there is a great Pātāla Vivara (the great crevice leading to the nether worlds). In that highly lustrous spot, she is stationed for protection and security.

One engaged in adoring that deity shall obtain excellent medicines and valuable treasures of Pātāla, present in the centre of the holy spot.

## \|\| 1.58.5 \|\|

*bhairavīti ca taddevyāḥ pūrvaṃ nāma prakīrttitam \|*  
*asminpunaścāṃtare tu aṣṭāviṃśe caturyuge \|*  
*tretāyugamukhe rājā ajāpālo babhūva ha \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The earlier name of that goddess was Bhairavī.

There was a king named Ajāpāla in the beginning of the Tretā Yuga of the twenty-eighth set of four Yugas (Caturyuga) in this Manvantara.

## \|\| 1.58.6 \|\|

*tena cāgatya kṣetresminpaṃcavarṣaśatāni ca \|*  
*bhairavī pūjitā devī vyādhigrastena bhāmini \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O beautiful woman, he was afflicted by diseases. So he came to this holy spot. Goddess Bhairavī was adored by him in this Kṣetra for five hundred years.

## \|\| 1.58.7 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca taṃ devī saṃtuṣṭā rājasattamam \|*  
*alaṃ kleśena rājarṣe tuṣṭāhaṃ tava bhaktitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The goddess who was pleased said to that excellent king: “Do not strain yourself, O saintly king, I am pleased with your devotion.”

## \|\| 1.58.8 \|\|

*ityuktaḥ sa tadā rājā kṛtāñjalipuṭaḥ sudhīḥ \|*  
*praṇamyovāca tāṃ devīmānaṃdāsrāvilekṣaṇaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On being told thus, the wise king joined his palms together. With his eyes dimmed with tears of joy, he bowed down and said to the goddess:

## \|\| 1.58.9 \|\|

*yadi tuṣṭāsi me devi varārho yadi vāpyaham \|*  
*sarve rogāḥ śarīrānme nāśaṃ yāṃtu bahiḥ kṛtāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. “O goddess, if you are pleased with me and if I deserve boons, may all the ailments in my body be destroyed and expelled.”

## \|\| 1.58.10 \|\|

*evamuktā tu sā devī punaḥ provāca taṃ nṛpam \|*  
*sarvameva mahārāja yathoktaṃ te bhaviṣyati \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On being told thus the goddess said to the king again: “O great king, all will happen as mentioned now.”

## \|\| 1.58.11 \|\|

*ityukte tu tadā devyā tasya rājñaḥ kalevarāt \|*  
*nirgatā vyādhayastatra ajārūpeṇa vai pṛthak \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. As soon as it was uttered by the goddess, all the ailments came out severally from the body of the king in the form of goats.

## \|\| 1.58.12 \|\|

*sahasrāṇāṃ tu pañcaiva niyataṃ sārddhameva ca \|*  
*iti vṛtte mahādevyā punaḥ prokto narādhipaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. These were definitely five thousand fifty of them. When this happened, the king was again addressed by the goddess:

## \|\| 1.58.13 \|\|

*rājannetānajārūpānvyādhīnpālaya kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*kiṃkurvāṇā bhaviṣyaṃti tavaivādeśakāriṇaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. “O king, take full care of these ailments in the forms of goats. They will be your servants carrying out your behests.

## \|\| 1.58.14 \|\|

*ajāpāleti te nāma khyātaṃ loke bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tava nāmnā mama nāma ajāpāleśvarīti ca \|*  
*bhaviṣyati dharāpṛṣṭhe tacca yāvaccaturyugam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Your name will become well-known in the world as Ajāpāla and after your name, my name Ajāpāleśvarī shall spread over the earth till the Caturyuga is complete.

## \|\| 1.58.15 \|\|

*aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturddaśyāṃ yo'tra māṃ pūjayiṣyati \|*  
*tasyāṣṭaguṇamaiśvaryaṃ dāsye tuṣṭā na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. When pleased, I shall undoubtedly grant eightfold Aiśvarya (prosperity and power) to the person who adores me here on the eighth and fourteenth lunar days.

## \|\| 1.58.16 \|\|

*aśvayukchuklāṣṭamyāṃ ca triḥ kṛtvā tu pradakṣiṇām \|*  
*someśaṃ madhyataḥ kṛtvā saṃsnāpyābhyarcya māṃ pṛthak \|*  
*tasya varṣatrayaṃ rājanna bhīḥ śoko bhaviṣyati \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On the eighth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Aśvayuj, the devotee should circumambulate Someśa three times. He should keep me in the centre, bathe me and adore me separately. No fear or sorrow shall befall him, O king, for three years.

## \|\| 1.58.17 \|\|

*yā tu vaṃdhyā bhavennārī rogiṇī durbhagā tathā \|*  
*tayoktā navamī kāryā mamāgre tuṣṭivarddhinī \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. A barren woman, a sick one and an unlucky one should perform worship in front of me on the ninth lunar day of the half and month mentioned before. It shall enhance her pleasure.

## \|\| 1.58.18-19 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā tu tadā devī tatraivāṃtarhitā'bhavat \|*  
*prabhāsakṣetramadhyasthaḥ sa rājātulavikramaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*pālayāmāsa dharmātmā tānajānvyādhirūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*auṣadhīrvividhākārāsteṣāṃ yāḥ puṣṭihetavaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

18-19. After saying this, the goddess vanished there itself. Staying in the middle of the holy spot of Prabhāsa Kṣetra, that king of unequalled valour righteously reared those transformations of ailments into goats. He fed them with various kinds of medicinal herbs causing their nourishment.

## \|\| 1.58.20 \|\|

*tatra varṣaśataṃ sāgraṃ puṣṭiṃ nītā ajāḥ pṛthak \|*  
*mahānidhānasaṃsthānamajāpālena nirmiṃtam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The goats were nourished thus for more than a hundred years. A big place for storage was built by Ajāpāla.

## \|\| 1.58.21 \|\|

*atha tasyāḥ prasādena sa rājā pṛthuvikramaḥ \|*  
*saptadvīpādhipo jātaḥ sūryavaṃśavibhūṣaṇaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then due to her (the deity’s) favour the king became extremely valorous. An ornament unto the solar race, he became the Lord of all the seven continents.

## \|\| 1.58.22-23 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*atyāścaryamidaṃ deva ajā devyāḥ samudbhavam \|*  
*punaśca śrotumicchāmi tasya rājñodbhutaṃ mahat \|\| 22 \|\|*

*kathaṃ rājā sa deveśa saptadvīpāṃ vasundharām \|*  
*śaśāsa eka evāsau kathaṃ te vyādhayaḥ kṛtāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

The Devī said:

22-23. O Lord, this origin of the goddess Ajā is wonderful. I wish to know further the great, miraculous story of that king. O Lord of Devas, how did that king rule the earth consisting of seven continents by himself alone? How were those Ailments kept?

## \|\| 1.58.24 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*purā babhūva rājarṣirdilīpa iti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*dīrgho nāma sutastasya raghustasmādajāyata \|\| 24 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

24\. Formerly there was a saintly king well-known as Dilīpa. His son was Dīrgha (?) and Raghu was born of him.

## \|\| 1.58.25 \|\|

*ajaḥputro raghoścāpi tasmādyaścātivīryavān \|*  
*sa bhairavīṃ samārādhya kṛtvā vyādhīnajāgaṇān \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Aja was the son of Raghu. He excelled him in valour. By propitiating Bhairavī, he transformed the ailments into groups of goats.

## \|\| 1.58.26 \|\|

*pālayāmāsa saṃhṛṣṭo hyajāpālastato'bhavat \|*  
*tasminkāle babhūvātha rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. With great delight he reared them. Therefore, he became Ajāpāla. Rāvaṇa was the king of Rākṣasas at that time.

## \|\| 1.58.27 \|\|

*laṃkāsthitaḥ suragaṇānniyuyoja svakarmasu \|*  
*akhaṃḍamaṃḍalaṃ candramātapatraṃ cakāra ha \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Residing in Laṅkā, he employed groups of Suras in his own service. He made the Moon of complete disc, his own umbrella.

## \|\| 1.58.28 \|\|

*indraṃ senāpatiṃ cakre vāyuṃ pāṃsupramārjakam \|*  
*varuṇaṃ dūtakarmasthaṃ dhanadaṃ dhanarakṣakam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He made Indra the chief of his army, Vāyu, the sweeper of dust particles, Varuṇa, one engaged in carrying messages, and Dhanada cashier in-charge of monetary affairs.

## \|\| 1.58.29 \|\|

*yamaṃ saṃyamane'rīṇāṃ yuyuje mantraṇe manum \|*  
*meghāśchardaṃti liṃpaṃti drumāḥ puṣpāṇi cikṣipuḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. He employed Yama for curbing and controlling his enemies, and Manu as counsellor. Clouds vomited (showered) and smeared (?). The trees scattered flowers.

## \|\| 1.58.30 \|\|

*saptarṣayaḥ śāṃtiparā brāhmaṇāḥ śaṃsinaḥ priyaḥ \|*  
*nāgā yāmakakakṣāyāṃ gandharvā gītatatparāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The Saptarṣis (seven sages) of quiescent disposition were appointed as the Brāhmaṇas, speaking pleasing things. Nāgas (Serpents) were put in the guardroom and Gandharvas were made to attend musical performance.

## \|\| 1.58.31 \|\|

*prekṣaṇīye'psarovṛṃdaṃ vādye vidyādharā vṛtāḥ \|*  
*gaṃgādyāḥ saritaḥ pāne gārhapatye hutāśanaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The group of celestial damsels was engaged in dramatic performance. Vidyādharas were assigned musical instruments. Gaṅgā and other rivers were made in-charge of preparation of beverages. Hutāśana (Fire-god) was given the charge of Gārhapatya (culinary duties).

## \|\| 1.58.32 \|\|

*viśvakarmāṃgasaṃskāre tena śilpī niyojitaḥ \|*  
*tiṣṭhaṃti pārthivāḥ sarve puraḥ sevāvidhāyinaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The divine architect Viśvakarman was engaged by him in Aṅgasaṃskāra (the duties of a barber for massage etc.). All the kings stood before him ready to serve him.

## \|\| 1.58.33-34 \|\|

*dṛśyaṃte bhāsvarai ratnaiḥ praskhalaṃto vibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*tāndṛṣṭvā rāvaṇaḥ prāha prahastaṃ pratihārakam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sevāṃ karttuṃ mama sthāne brūhi ke'tra samāgatāḥ \|*  
*uvāca sa praṇamyāgre daṇḍapāṇirniśācaraḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. They faltered in their steps due to their dazzling jewels. On seeing them, Rāvaṇa said to Prahasta, his doorkeeper: “Tell me, who have all come to my place in order to render service?”.

## \|\| 1.58.35-36 \|\|

*eṣa kākutstho māṃdhātā dhundhumāro nalo'rjunaḥ \|*  
*yayātirnahuṣo bhīmo rāghavo'yaṃ vidūrathaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*ete cānye ca bahavo rājāna iha cāgatāḥ \|*  
*sevākarāstava sthāne nājāpāla iho gataḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

The demon-attendant armed with his staff bowed before him and said:

35-36. “This is Kākutstha, this is Māndhātā, this Dhundhumāra, this Nala, this Arjuna, Yayāti, Nahuṣa, Bhīma, Vidūratha the scion of the family of Raghu—these and many other kings have come here to your place for rendering services. But Ajāpāla has not come here.”

## \|\| 1.58.37 \|\|

*rāvaṇaḥ kupitaḥ prāha śīghraṃ dūta visarjaya \|*  
*ityuktvā prahito dūto dhūmrākṣo nāma rākṣasaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The furious Rāvaṇa said: “Send a messenger quickly.”

After being told thus, the Rākṣasa named Dhūmrākṣa was sent as messenger:

## \|\| 1.58.38-40 \|\|

*dhūmrākṣa gaccha brūhi tvamajāpālaṃ mamā jñayā \|*  
*sevāṃ karttuṃ mamāgaccha karaṃ vā yaccha pārthiva \|\| 38 \|\|*

*athavā candrahāsena tvāṃ kariṣye vikaṃdharam \|*  
*rāvaṇenaivamuktastu dhūmrākṣo garuḍo yathā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*saṃprāptastāṃ purīṃ ramyāṃ tava rājakulaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*dadarśāyāṃtamekaṃ sa ajāpālamajāvṛtam \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. “O Dhūmrākṣa, go. Tell Ajāpāla at my behest: O king, either come to render service or pay tribute. If not I will make you headless by means of my sword Candrahāsa.”

On being told thus by Rāvaṇa, Dhūmrākṣa flew like Garuḍa, reached that beautiful city and entered the royal abode. There he saw Ajāpāla coming alone but surrounded by his goats.

## \|\| 1.58.41 \|\|

*muktakeśaṃ muktakacchaṃ svarṇakaṃbaladhāriṇam \|*  
*yaṣṭiskaṃdhaṃ reṇuvṛtaṃ vyādhibhiḥ parivāritam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. His hairs were dishevelled. His robes were loose. He was having a golden blanket round his body. There was a staff on his shoulder. He was dust-covered and surrounded by the ailments.

## \|\| 1.58.42 \|\|

*nighnaṃtamiva śārdūlaṃ sarvopadravanāśanam \|*  
*mahyāmālikhya nāmāni vinighnaṃtaṃ dviṣāṃ gaṇam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. He was like a murderous (ferocious) tiger ready to destroy and resist all onslaughts. He was killing the groups of enemies simply by writing down their names on the earth.

## \|\| 1.58.43 \|\|

*snātaṃ bhuktaṃ nijasthāne kṛtakṛtyaṃ manuṃ yathā \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭamanāḥ prāha dhūmrākṣo rāvaṇoditam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. He appeared to have had his bath and food. He was seated in his place blessed and contented like Manu. On seeing him, Dhūmrākṣa was delighted in his mind. He spoke out what was spoken by Rāvaṇa.

## \|\| 1.58.44 \|\|

*ajāpālo'pi sākṣepaṃ pratyu ktvā kāraṇottaram \|*  
*preṣayāmāsa dhūmrākṣaṃ tataḥ kṛtyaṃ samādadhe \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. After a defiant reproach and a suitable reply Ajāpāla dismissed Dḥūmrākṣa back and attended to his duties.

## \|\| 1.58.45 \|\|

*jvaramākārayitvā tu provācedaṃ mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*gaccha laṃkādhipasthānamācara tvaṃ yathoditam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The king summoned Jvara (fever) and spoke thus, “Go to the abode of the king of Laṅkā and do as you are ordered.”

## \|\| 1.58.46 \|\|

*niyuktastvajapālena jvaro divi jagāma ha \|*  
*gatvā ca kaṃpayāmāsa rāvaṇaṃ rākṣaseśvaram \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Directed by Ajāpāla, Jvara went through space. After going (to Laṅkā) he made the Rākṣasa king Rāvaṇa tremble.

## \|\| 1.58.47 \|\|

*rāvaṇastaṃ viditvā tu jvaraṃ paramadāruṇam \|*  
*provāca tiṣṭhatu nṛpastena me na prayojanam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Rāvaṇa realized that it was the highly terrible Jvara and said: “Let the king stay away. I don’t have anything to do with him.”

## \|\| 1.58.48 \|\|

*tataḥ sa vijvaro rājā babhūva dhanadānujaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ tasya caritrāṇi saṃti cānyāni koṭiśaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Then the younger brother of Dhanada, the king (Rāvaṇa), became free from fever. Thus there are millions of his other activities.

## \|\| 1.58.49 \|\|

*ajāpālasya deveśi sūryavattviṭkirīṭinaḥ \|*  
*tenaiṣā'rādhitā devī ajāpālena dhīmatā \|*  
*sarvarogapraśamanī sarvo padravanāśinī \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O goddess of Devas, there are innumerable such acts of Ajāpāla having a crown resplendent like the sun. This goddess was propitiated by such an intelligent king Ajāpāla. The deity suppresses all ailments. She destroys all torments.

## \|\| 1.58.50 \|\|

*pūjayettāṃ vidhānena bhogepsuryadi mānavaḥ \|*  
*gaṃdhairdhūpairalaṃkārairvastrairanyaiśca bhaktitaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. If a man is desirous of enjoyment of pleasure, he should worship her in accordance with the injunctions, devoutly offering scents, incense, ornaments, garments and other things.

## \|\| 1.58.51 \|\|

*iti te kathitaṃ sarvamajādevyāḥ samudbhavam \|*  
*sarvaduḥkhopaśamanaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Thus the origin of Ajādevī has been fully narrated to you. It suppresses all miseries and destroys all sins.

## Chapter 59 - Greatness of Ajādevī

## \|\| 1.59.1-2 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*atha vacmi tṛtīyāṃ te jñānaśaktiṃ śivātmikām \|*  
*prabhāsakṣetramadhyasthāṃ dāridryaughavināśinīm \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ajeti nāmnīṃ tāṃ devīṃ rāhvīśāddakṣiṇe sthitām \|*  
*mama vaktrādviniṣkrāṃtā ṣaṣṭhādvai viṣṇupūjitāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-2. Henceforth, I shall describe unto you the third deity Jñānaśakti (power of knowledge), identical with Śiva. She resides in the holy Prabhāsa Kṣetra and is destructive of poverty in abundance.

The goddess is named Ajā. She is stationed to the south of Rāhvīśa. She has issued forth from my sixth mouth/face adored by Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 1.59.3 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*paṃcavaktrāṇi deveśa prasiddhāni tava prabhau \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhaṃ yadvadanaṃ deva tasya kiṃ nāma saṃsmṛtam \|*  
*samutpannā kathaṃ tasmādajādevīti yā śrutā \|\| 3 \|\|*

The Devī said:

3\. O my Lord, O Lord of Devas! Five faces of yours are well-known. What may be the name of the sixth face, O Lord? How did the deity well-known as Ajādevī issue forth therefrom?

## \|\| 1.59.4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā devi yadgopyaṃ svasuteṣvapi \|*  
*tatte'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi aprasiddhāgamoditam \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

4\. O goddess, what has been asked by you is pertinent. I shall describe unto you what should be kept as a secret even from one’s own sons. It was (originally) narrated in an Āgama (scriptural text) which is not (so) well-known.

## \|\| 1.59.5 \|\|

*vaktrāṇi mama deveśi saptāsanpūrvameva hi \|*  
*sadyojātādipaṃcaiva ṣaṣṭhaṃ smṛtamajeti ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Earlier, even at the outset, O goddess of Devas, I had seven faces. Five are Sadyojāta etc. The sixth one is remembered as Aja (Unborn).

## \|\| 1.59.6 \|\|

*saptamaṃ picunāmeti saptaivaṃ vadanāni me \|*  
*tebhyo'jaṃ brahmaṇe dattaṃ picuvaktraṃ tu viṣṇave \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The seventh one was named Picu. Thus I had seven faces. Of them Aja was given to Brahmā and Picu to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 1.59.7 \|\|

*tasmādahaṃ mahādevi paṃcavaktro'dhunā'bhavam \|*  
*ajastu brahmā sañjajñe picurviṣṇurajāyata \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Hence, O great goddess, I now become five-faced. Aja became Brahmā and Picu became Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 1.59.8 \|\|

*ajavaktrānmahādevi ajā jātā mahāprabhā \|*  
*andhāsuraraṇe ghore mama krodhena bhāmini \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. From the face Aja, O great goddess, (the Deity) Ajā of great lustre was born. O beautiful lady, it was at the time of the terrible fight with Andhāsura and that too due to my anger.

## \|\| 1.59.9 \|\|

*khaḍgacarmadharādevī surūpā siṃhavāhinī \|*  
*marddayantī mahādaityāndevīkoṭisamanvitā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The goddess held a sword and a shield. Riding on a lion, she had a splendid form. She was accompanied by crores of other goddesses. She crushed the great Daityas.

## \|\| 1.59.10 \|\|

*tasyā bhayena ye daityā vidrutā dakṣiṇārṇavam \|*  
*pṛṣṭhato'nuyayau tānvai sā devī siṃhavāhinī \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A few Daityas fled to the southern sea out of fear of her. The lion-riding goddess chased them closely behind.

## \|\| 1.59.11 \|\|

*itastataste dhāvanto māryamāṇāśca tadgaṇaiḥ \|*  
*prabhāsa kṣetrasaṃprāptā naśyamānā mahārṇavam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Running here and there, they were slain by her Gaṇas. In the course of their destruction, they proceeded towards the great sea and reached Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.59.12-13 \|\|

*kecittatra hatā daityāḥ kecitpātālamāyayuḥ \|*  
*niḥśeṣānnihatāndṛṣṭvā sā devī siṃhavāhinī \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kṣetraṃ pavitramājñāya tatra sthāne sthitā śubhā \|*  
*someśādīśakoṇasthā saurīśāduttare sthitā \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Some of the Daityas were slain there. Some went to Pātāla (nether worlds). On seeing that they were all killed, the goddess riding a lion realized the sanctity of the place. The splendid deity haltred at that place, stationing herself to the north-east of Someśa and to the north of Saurīśa.

## \|\| 1.59.14 \|\|

*yastāṃ tatra sthitāṃ paśyedyoṣidvātha naro'pi vā \|*  
*sa bhūyātsattvasaubhāgyaiḥ saptajanmāni saṃyutaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Whoever, whether a man or a woman, views her stationed there, shall become endowed with Sattva quality and conjugal felicity for the duration of seven births.

## \|\| 1.59.15 \|\|

*gītavādyādikaṃ nṛtyaṃ yastatra kurute naraḥ \|*  
*tasyānvaye na daurbhāgyaṃ bhūyāttasyāḥ prasādataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. If a man arranges for vocal music, instrumental music and dance there, there shall be no wretchedness in his family, due to her favour.

## \|\| 1.59.16 \|\|

*ghṛtena dīpakaṃ tatra yā nārī saṃprayacchati \|*  
*raktavartyā mahādevi yāvaṃtastatra taṃtavaḥ \|*  
*tāvajjanmāṃtarāṇyeva sā saubhāgyamavāpnuyāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O great goddess, if any woman offers a lamp with ghee (clarified butter) with a red wick there, she will attain conjugal felicity in the course of as many births as there are threads there in the wick.

## \|\| 1.59.17 \|\|

*yaścaitattu paṭhennityaṃ tṛtīyāyāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*śṛṇuyādvā'pi yo bhaktyā sa kāmānakhilāllaṃbhet \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He who reads this daily, especially on the third lunar day, or listens to this devoutly, shall obtain all cherished desires.

## \|\| 1.59.18-19 \|\|

*iti saṃkṣepataḥ prokto rudraśaktitrayakramaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*etāḥ śaktīḥ pūjayitvā someśaṃ pūjayettataḥ \|*  
*samyagyātrāphalāpekṣī ekāṃ vā varadāmatha \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Thus it has been described succinctly how, in what order, the three Śaktis of Rudra are to be worshipped.

After adoring these Śaktis the devotee should worship Someśa, if he is desirous of the full benefit of the pilgrimage. Or he may worship one Śakti who is the bestower of boons.

## Chapter 60 - Greatness of Maṅgalā

## \|\| 1.60.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*prabhāsakṣetradūtīnāṃ tritayaṃ varavarṇini \|*  
*atha te saṃpravakṣyāmi śṛṇu hyekamanāḥ priye \|\| 1 \|\|*

*prathamā maṃgalā devī viśālākṣī dvitīyikā \|*  
*tathā catvaradevī tu tṛtīyā parikīrtitā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yathānukramataḥ pūjyāḥ śaktayastā varānane \|*  
*prabhāsakṣetrayātrāyāḥ phalaprepsurnaro yadi \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. O my beloved, one of excellent complexion, I shall describe the three Dūtīs (lady-messengers) of the holy spot of Prabhāsa. Listen with an attentive mind.

The first one is goddess Maṅgalā. The second one is Viśālākṣī and goddess Catvaradevī is glorified as the third one.

O lady of excellent countenance, those Śaktis are to be worshipped in this order, if a man is desirous of attaining the benefit of the pilgrimage to Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.60.4 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*kasminsthāne sthitā deva dūtyastāḥ kṣetrarakṣikāḥ \|*  
*kasya tāḥ kathamārādhyāḥ kathaṃ pūjyā jagatpate \|\| 4 \|\|*

The Devī said:

4\. O Lord, at what spot did those Dūtīs, the guardians of the holy spot, halt and stationed themselves. Of whom are they the Śaktis? How are they to be propitiated? O Lord of the universe, how are they to be adored?

## \|\| 1.60.5 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*brāhmī tu maṃgalā proktā viśālākṣī tu vaiṣṇavī \|*  
*raudrīśaktiḥ samākhyātā devī sā catvarapriyā \|\| 5 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

5\. Maṅgalā is said to be of Brahmā; Viśālākṣī is of Viṣṇu. The deity Catvarapriyā is the Śakti of Rudra.

## \|\| 1.60.6 \|\|

*maṃgalā prathamaṃ pūjyā ajādevyuttare sthitā \|*  
*rāhvīśāddakṣiṇebhāge nātidūre varānane \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O lady of excellent countenance, Maṅgalā who is stationed to the north of Ajādevī and to the south of Rāhvīśa, not very far, should be worshipped first.

## \|\| 1.60.7 \|\|

*someśvarapratiṣṭhāpya prārabdhe yajñakarmaṇi \|*  
*somena tatra devānāmāgatā sā didṛkṣayā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. When Someśvara was installed and the rite of Yajña was started, she had come there along with Soma (the Moon) with a desire to see the Devas.

## \|\| 1.60.8 \|\|

*brahmādīnāṃ ca sā yasmānmāṃgalyaṃ kṛtavatyume \|*  
*tasmātsā maṃgalā proktā sarvamāṃgalyadāyinī \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O Umā, since she gave auspiciousness unto Brahmā and others, she is called Maṅgalā. She is the bestower of all auspiciousness.

## \|\| 1.60.9 \|\|

*tṛtīyāyāṃ tu yā nārī naro vā pūjayiṣyati \|*  
*tasyā'maṃgalyaduḥkhāni nāśaṃ yāsyaṃti kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Inauspiciousness and miseries due to it, shall entirely perish in regard to that person, be it a man or a woman, who adores her on the third lunar day.

## \|\| 1.60.10 \|\|

*dampatībhojanaṃ tatra phaladānaṃ sakañcukam \|*  
*praśastaṃ pṛṣadājyasya prāśanaṃ pāpanāśanam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Feeding a couple and offering them fruits along with a bodice at that site is laudable. Feeding of Pṛṣadājya (ghee mixed with curds) is destructive of sins.

## \|\| 1.60.11 \|\|

*iti saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ mahābhāgyaṃ mahodayam \|*  
*maṃgalāyāśca māhātmyaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thus the greatness of Maṅgalā has been succinctly spoken. It is conducive to great fortune and great benefit as a result and it is destructive of all sins.

## Chapter 61 - Greatness of Lalitomāviśālākṣī (Lalitomā-viśālākṣī)

## \|\| 1.61.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevīṃ kṣetradūtīṃ tu vaiṣṇavīm \|*  
*śrīdaityasūdanāddevi pūrvabhāge vyavasthitām \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yogeśvaryāstathaiśānyāṃ dhanuṣāṃ saptake sthitām \|*  
*mahādaurbhāgyadagdhānāṃ sthitāṃ bheṣajarūpiṇīm \|\| 2 \|\|*

*cākṣuṣasyāṃtare devi yadā daityā balotkaṭāḥ \|*  
*hanyamānā viṣṇunā'tha dakṣiṇāṃ diśamāviśan \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tatra varṣaśataṃ sāgraṃ daityāścakrurmahāhavam \|*  
*viṣṇunā saha deveśi divyāstraiśca pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Then a pilgrim should go to the great goddess Kṣetradevī of Viṣṇu, O goddess. She is stationed to the east of Śrīdaityasūdana and within a distance of seven bows (Dhanus) to the north-east of Yogeśvarī.

She has established herself as the medicine (balm) unto those who are burned (by the fire) of great wretchedness.

Iṅ the Cākṣuṣa Manvantara, O goddess, when the excessively powerful Daityas proceeded towards the southern quarter on being slain by Viṣṇu, they fought for more than a hundred years in a great battle there with Viṣṇu. O goddess of Devas, they fought with wonderful missiles of various kinds.

## \|\| 1.61.5 \|\|

*duḥkhavadhyāṃstato jñātvā viṣṇuḥ kamalalocanaḥ \|*  
*sasmāra bhairavīṃ śaktiṃ mahāmāyāṃ mahāprabhām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Knowing that they could not be killed easily, the lotus-eyed Viṣṇu remembered Bhairavī Śakti, the Mahāmāyā of great lustre.

## \|\| 1.61.6 \|\|

*sā smṛtā kṣaṇamātreṇa viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|*  
*tatrāgatā mahādevī ānaṃdasphuritekṣaṇā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On being remembered by Viṣṇu, the all-powerful one, the great goddess came there within a moment with her eyes shining with great delight.

## \|\| 1.61.7 \|\|

*viśāle tu kṛte devyā locane viṣṇudarśanāt \|*  
*viśālākṣī tato jātā tatrasthā daityanāśinī \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. At the sight of Viṣṇu, the eyes became large and wide (Viśāla). Hence the goddess stationed there who is the destroyer of Daityas, became (known as) Viśālākṣī.

## \|\| 1.61.8 \|\|

*asminkalpesamākhyātā lalitomā varānane \|*  
*umādvayaṃ samākhyātaṃ someśe daityasūdane \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In this Kalpa, O lady of excellent countenance, she is called Lalitomā. Thus there are two Umās mentioned, one in Someśa and the other in Daityasūdana (Viṣṇu).

## \|\| 1.61.9 \|\|

*pūrvaṃ someśvare paśyetpaścācchrīdaityasūdane \|*  
*umā dvayaṃ pūjayitvā tīrthayātrāphalaṃ labhet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The pilgrim should view (Umā) at the outset in Someśvara and then in Daityasūdana thereafter. By worshipping the two Umās, one will derive the full benefit of the pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.61.10 \|\|

*māghe māsi tṛtīyāyāṃ vidhinā yo'rcayettu tām \|*  
*na saṃtativihīnaḥ syāttasyakoṭyanvaye naraḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. If a devotee duly worships her on the third lunar day in the month of Māgha, he shall never be devoid of progeny. His line will extend to ten millions.

## \|\| 1.61.11 \|\|

*yo nityamīkṣate tatra bhaktyā paramayā yutaḥ \|*  
*ārogyasukhasaubhāgyasaṃyukto'sau bhavecciram \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He who is endowed with great devotion and visits her everyday, shall be always blessed with health, happiness and conjugal felicity for a long time.

## \|\| 1.61.12 \|\|

*iti saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ māhātmyaṃ lalitodbhavam \|*  
*śrutaṃ yatpāpanāśāya jāyate dharmavṛddhaye \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thus the greatness of Lalitā has been succinctly spoken. If listened to, it becomes conducive to the destruction of sins and increase of piety.

## Chapter 62 - Greatness of Catvarādevī

## \|\| 1.62.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi tṛtīyāṃ catvarapriyām \|*  
*lalitāpūrvadigbhāge daśadhanvaṃtare sthitām \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kṣetradūtīṃ mahāraudrīṃ rudraśaktiṃ mahāprabhām \|*  
*kṣetrarakṣāvidhau tatra mayā muktāṃ tu madhyataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*koṭibhūtasamāyuktā mahākāyā mahāprabhā \|*  
*jīrṇe gṛhe tathodyāne prāsādāṭṭālake pathi \|\| 3 \|\|*

*catvareṣu ca sarveṣu kṣetra madhyasthitā satī \|*  
*rātrau paryaṭate devī bhūtānāṃ koṭibhirvṛtā \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Thereafter, a pilgrim should go to the third goddess Catvarapriyā. O great goddess, she is stationed on the eastern side of Lalitā within a distance of ten Dhanus.

She is the great and terrible Kṣetradūtī, the Śakti of Rudra possessing great lustre. She was left there in the centre for the job of guarding the holy spot by me.

She is accompanied by a crore of Bhūtas (goblins). She is huge-bodied and highly lustrous. Surrounded by crores of Bhūtas, the goddess wanders at night in dilapidated houses, gardens, palaces, attics, paths, courtyards—everywhere within the holy spot.

## \|\| 1.62.5-6 \|\|

*mahānavamyāṃ yastatra nārī vātha naropi vā \|*  
*nānāpūjopacāraiśca pūjayedvidhivacchubhām \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tasya tuṣṭā'khilānkāmānsādevī saṃpradāsyati \|*  
*daṃpatyorbhojanaṃ tatra deyaṃ yātrāphalepsubhiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. If a man or a woman duly adores her on the great Navamī day, with all types of service-offerings, the splendid goddess becomes pleased with him or her and grants all cherished desires. Feeding of couples must be performed by those who wish for the benefit of the pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.62.7 \|\|

*iti saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ māhā tmyaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*kṣetradūtyāstṛtīyāyāḥ śrutamaiśvaryakārakam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thus the greatness of the third Kṣetradūtī has been succinctly spoken. On being listened to it she bestows prosperity and destroys sins.

## Chapter 63 - Greatness of Bhairaveśvara (Bhairava-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.63.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi bhairaveśvaramuttamam \|*  
*yogeśvaryā dakṣiṇato nātidūre vyavasthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ dibyaiśvaryapradāyakam \|*  
*purā daityavināśārthaṃ yadā devī kṛtodyamā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tadā bhairavamāhūya dūtatve niyuyoja ha \|*  
*śivadūtī tadā khyātā paścādyogeśvarīti ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the excellent Bhairaveśvara. It is stationed not very far from Yogeśvarī to the south.

It is destructive of sins. It bestows supernatural prosperity and glory. Formerly when the goddess made effort for the destruction of Daityas, she summoned Bhairava and employed him as a messenger. Then she became well-known as Śivadūtī and thereafter as Yogeśvarī.

## \|\| 1.63.4-5 \|\|

*bhairavo yatra vai devyā dūtatve viniyojitaḥ \|*  
*tena liṃgaṃ samākhyātaṃ bhairaveśvaranāmakam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*pūjitaṃ devadaityaiśca bhairaveṇa pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*yastatpūjayate bhaktyā kārtikyāṃ vidhinā naraḥ \|*  
*niraṃtaraṃ vā ṣaṇmāsaṃ so'bhīṣṭaṃ labhate phalam \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. The place where Bhairava was employed as a messenger by the goddess, has the Liṅga called by the name Bhairaveśvara.

It is installed by Bhairava and is adored by Devas and Daityas. A man who devoutly adores it duly on the Kārttikī day or continuously for six months, obtains the desired benefit.

## Chapter 64 - Greatness of Laksmīśvara

## \|\| 1.64.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tasyaiva pūrvadigbhāge dhanuṣāṃ paṃcake sthitam \|*  
*lakṣmīśvareti vikhyātaṃ dāridryaughavināśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yatra devyā samānītā lakṣmīrdetyānnihatya ca \|*  
*tena lakṣmīśvaraṃ nāma svayaṃ devyā pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yastaṃ pūjayate bhaktyā śrīpaṃcamyāṃ vidhānataḥ \|*  
*na vimukto bhavellakṣmyā yāvanmanvataraṃ priye \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. To the eastern side of the same is the shrine well-known as Laksmīśvara stationed within a distance of ten Dhanus. It is destructive of series of impoverished states.

At the place where Lakṣmī was brought by the Supreme Devī after killing the Daityas, is the idol named Laksmīśvara installed by the supreme goddess herself.

He who devoutly worships that Lord in accordance with the injunctions on Śrīpañcamī day (i.e. the fifth lunar day in the bright half of Māgha) is never separated from Lakṣmī (fortune) till the end of the Manvantara, O my beloved!

## Chapter 65 - Greatness of Vāḍaveśvara (Vāḍava-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.65.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi liṃgaṃ vai vāḍaveśvaram \|*  
*lakṣmīśāduttare bhāge viśālākṣyāśca dakṣiṇe \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sthitaṃ mahāprabhāvaṃ hi vāḍavena pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*kṛtasmaro yadā dagdhaḥ parvato vāḍavāgninā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*samīkṛtyākhilaṃ sthānaṃ tena liṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*pūjayettaṃ vidhānena daśa saṃsnāpya śaṃkaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dadhi dadyācca vai tatra brāhmaṇe vedapārage \|*  
*so'gnilokamavāpnoti samyagyātrāphalaṃ labhet \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Thereafter, a pilgrim should go to the shrine of Vāḍaveśvara Liṅga to the northern side of Lakṣmīśa and to south of Viśālākṣī.

It is stationed there. It has great efficacy. It was installed by Vāḍava at the time when the mountain Kṛtasmara was burnt by the Vāḍava fire.

The Liṅga was installed by him after levelling the entire spot. After bathing Lord Śaṅkara with curds, the pilgrim should worship him in accordance with the injunctions.

The pilgrim should offer curds there to a Brāhmaṇa who has mastered the Vedas. Thereby he attains the Agniloka and obtains the full benefit of a perfect pilgrimage.

## Chapter 66 - Greatness of Arghyeśvara (Arghya-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.66.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahāliṃgamarghyeśvaramiti śrutam \|*  
*uttare tu viśālākṣyā nātidūre vyavasthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*liṃgaṃ mahāprabhāvaṃ hi suragandharvapūjitam \|*  
*yadā devī samāyātā vaḍavānaladhāriṇī \|\| 2 \|\|*

*prabhāsakṣetramāsādya dṛṣṭvā tatra mahodadhim \|*  
*arghyaṃ dattavatī tatra vidhinā tanmahodadheḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*pratiṣṭhāpya mahalliṃgaṃ saṃpūjya vidhinā tataḥ \|*  
*praviveśātha deveśi snānārthaṃ ca mahodadhau \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Thereafter, a pilgrim should go to the great Liṅga welḥ known as Arghyeśvara. It is situated to the north of Viśālākṣī not very far from there.

Worshipped by Suras and Gandharvas, this Liṅga is highly powerful. The goddess (river) reached Prabhāsa Kṣetra holding the Vāḍava fire and when she saw the great ocean there, she offered Arghya in accordance with the injunctions to the great ocean.

After installing the great Liṅga and worshipping it in accordance with the injunctions, O goddess of Devas, she entered the great ocean for the sake of holy ablution.

## \|\| 1.66.5-6 \|\|

*yasmādarghyaṃ purā dattvā paścā dīśaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*tenārghyeśeti vikhyātaṃ liṃgaṃ pāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*paṃcāmṛtena saṃsnāpya vidhinā yastamarcayet \|*  
*saptajanmāni deveśi sa vidyāmadhigacchati \|*  
*samyakchāstrapravaktā ca sarvasaṃdehavittamaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Since the Arghya was offered earlier and the Lord is installed later, the Liṅga is well-known as Arghyeśa.

It is destructive of sins. O goddess of Devas, one who bathes the Lord with Pañcāmṛta in accordance with the injunctions and worships him, acquires learning in seven births. He will be a perfect expounder of the scriptures. He will have perfect knowledge, enabling him to clarify all doubts.

## Chapter 67 - Greatness of Kāmeśvara (Kāma-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.67.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gachenmahāliṃgaṃ kāmeśvaramiti śrutam \|*  
*kāmenārādhitaṃ pūrvaṃ daityasūdanapaścime \|\| 1 \|\|*

*dhanuṣāṃ saptake tatra sthitaṃ devi mahāprabham \|*  
*nirdagdhastu yadā kāma stṛtīyenāgninā mama \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tadā varṣasahasraṃ tu samārādhya maheśvaram \|*  
*prapede kāmanāsargaṃ yatrānaṃgaḥ purā kila \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tena kāmeśvaraṃnāma khyātaṃ liṃgaṃ dharātale \|*  
*sarvapāpaharaṃ devi sarvakāmaphalapradam \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Thereafter, a pilgrim should go to the shrine of the great Liṅga well-known as Kāmeśvara. It is to the west of Daityasūdana and was worshipped by Kāma. O goddess, it is stationed within a distance of seven Dhanus and is highly refulgent.

When Kāma was reduced to ashes by my third (eye) of fire, he propitiated Maheśvara. The disembodied one propitiated Maheśvara for a thousand years and attained a creative form as he desired.

Therefore, the Liṅga became well-known all over the earth by the name Kāmeśvara. O goddess, it is destructive of all sins and it bestows all the desired benefits.

## \|\| 1.67.5 \|\|

*trayodaśyāṃ vidhānena śuklāyāṃ māsi mādhave \|*
