*so'gniḥ so'rko mahātejā viṣaṃ bhavati kopitaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. He who destroys all this world may destroy Brāhmaṇa also in the same manner. If infuriated a Brāhmaṇa becomes like fire, the highly blazing Arka (Sun) and poison.

## \|\| 1.106.42 \|\|

*bhūtānāmagrabhugvipro varṇaśreṣṭhaḥ pitā guruḥ \|*  
*na skandate na vyathate na vinaśyati karhicit \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. A Brāhmaṇa has precedence in the matter of taking food, among all living beings. He is the most excellent among all castes. He is the father, the preceptor. He does not perish. He does not incur pain or loss. He is not afflicted at all.

## \|\| 1.106.43 \|\|

*variṣṭhamagnihotrāddhi brāhmaṇasya mukhe hutam \|*  
*viprāṇāṃ vapurāśritya sarvāstiṣṭhaṃti devatāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. What is consigned to the mouth of a Brāhmaṇa is more excellent than (oblation in fire) even in Agnihotra. All Devas stay resorting to the bodies of Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.106.44 \|\|

*ataḥ pūjyāstu te viprā alābhe pratimādayaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Hence Brāhmaṇas are worthy of being worshipped. If they be not available, idols and images are to be adored.

## \|\| 1.106.45 \|\|

*avidyo vā savidyo vā brāhmaṇo mama daivatam \|*  
*praṇītaścāpraṇītaśca yathāgnirdaivataṃ mahat \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Whether he is equipped with learning or not, a Brāhmaṇa is my deity, just as the Fire is a great divinity whether consecrated with prayers or not.

## \|\| 1.106.46 \|\|

*smaśāneṣvapi tejasvī pāvako naiva duṣyati \|*  
*havyakavyavyapeto'pi brāhmaṇo naiva duṣyati \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. A fire does not become impure even in cremation grounds. A Brāhmaṇa even bereft of Havya and Kavya does not become impure.

## \|\| 1.106.47 \|\|

*mahāpātakavarjyaṃ hi pūjyo vipro varānane \|*  
*sarvathā brāhmaṇāḥ pūjyāḥ sarvathā daivataṃ mahat \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena rakṣedāpadgataṃ dvijam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Barring the case where a Mahāpātaka (great sin) is involved, O lady of excellent countenance, a Brāhmaṇa is worthy of veneration. By all means Brāhmaṇas are to be worshipped. He is a great divinity by all means. Hence, by all efforts, a Brāhmaṇa in danger should be protected.

## \|\| 1.106.48 \|\|

*evaṃ viprā mahādevi pūjyāḥ sarvatra mānavaiḥ \|*  
*kiṃ punaḥ saṃjitātmāno viśeṣātkṣetravāsinaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Thus, O great goddess, Brāhmaṇas are to be worshipped everywhere by men. Those who have subdued their selves and especially those who reside in a Kṣetra (holy place) are still more venerable.

## \|\| 1.106.49 \|\|

*atha kṣetrasthitānāṃ ca caturāśramavāsinām \|*  
*viprāṇāṃ vṛttito bhedaṃ pravakṣyāmyānupūrvyaśaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Henceforth I shall describe the difference among the Brāhmaṇa residents of a holy spot of all the four stages in life in due order as based on their avocation.

## \|\| 1.106.50 \|\|

*kṣetrasya saṃnyāsavidhiṃ ye jānaṃti dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*vṛttibhedaṃ kramāccaiva te kṣetraphalabhāginaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Those Brāhmaṇas who know the procedure of Sannyāsa (perfect placement) of the Kṣetra and also the difference in avocation in due order are the partakers of the benefit of the holy spot.

## \|\| 1.106.51 \|\|

*yathā kṣetre nivasatā vartitavyaṃ dvijātinā \|*  
*prājāpatyādibhedena tacchṛṇu tvaṃ varānane \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O lady of excellent countenance, listen to the details of how a Brāhmaṇa-resident of a Kṣetra is to conduct himself in the different avocations of Prājāpatya etc.

## \|\| 1.106.52-54 \|\|

*prājāpatyā mahīpālāḥ kapotā graṃthikāstathā \|*  
*kuṭikāścātha vaitālāḥ padmahaṃsā varānane \|\| 52 \|\|*

*dhṛtarāṣṭrā bakāḥ kaṃkā gopālāścaiva bhāmini \|*  
*truṭikā maṭharāścaiva guṭikā daṃḍikāḥ pare \|\| 53 \|\|*

*kṣetrasthānāmime bhedā vṛttiṃ teṣāṃ śṛṇuṣva ca \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. O lady of excellent countenance, the following are the pursuits of the residents under the different names (titles) such as Prājāpatyas, Mahīpālas, Kapotas, Granthikas, Kuṭikas, Vaitalas, Padmahaṃsas, Dhṛtarāṣṭras, Bakas, Kaṅkas, Gopālas, Truṭikas, Maṭharas and Guṭikas. O beautiful woman, the others are Daṇḍikas. Listen to their special activities for maintaining themselves.

## \|\| 1.106.55 \|\|

*ahiṃsā guruśuśrūṣā svādhyāyaḥ śaucasaṃyamaḥ \|*  
*satyamasteyametaddhi prājāpatyaṃ vrataṃ smṛtam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. These are remembered as constituting the Vrata called prājāpatya: non-violence, service to preceptors and elders, self-study of the Vedas, cleanliness of the body, restraint of the sense-organs, truthfulness and abstention from theft.

## \|\| 1.106.56 \|\|

*kṣayapuṣṭyarthavidveṣakarmabhiḥ śāṃtikādibhiḥ \|*  
*pālayaṃti mahīṃ yasmānmahīpālāstataḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The second category of people is remembered as Mahīpāla because they sustain the earth by means of the rites such as Śāntika (conducive to tranquality) etc. with destruction, nourishment and enmity as the objective.

## \|\| 1.106.57 \|\|

*patitā ye kaṇā bhūmau saṃharaṃti kapotavat \|*  
*uddhṛtyājīvanaṃ yeṣāṃ kapotāste tu sādhakāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Those Sādhakas (persons in pursuit of perfection in spirituality) whose sustenance is affected by means of gleaning grains that are scattered on the ground as in the case of pigeons (Kapotas) are also called Kapotas.

## \|\| 1.106.58 \|\|

*gṛhaṃ kṛtvā tu sadgraṃthāḥ sahasaiva tyajaṃti ye \|*  
*kuṭikā sādhakāste vai śivārādhanatatparāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Those who get houses built and stay in them are called Sadgranthas (or Granthikas).

Those Sādhakas who suddenly forsake houses after building them are called Kuṭikas (dwellers of huts). They are devoted to the propitiation of Śiva.

## \|\| 1.106.59 \|\|

*tīrthāsaktāḥ sapatnīkā yathālabdhopajīvinaḥ \|*  
*mahāsāhasayuktāste vaitālākhyāstu sādhakāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The Sādhakas called Vaitālas are attached to Tīrthas. With great daring, they live there with their wives and sustain themselves with what they casually get.

## \|\| 1.106.60 \|\|

*saṃyatāḥ kāmanāsaktā rājyakāmārthasādhakāḥ \|*  
*padmāste sādhakāḥ khyātā bhikṣācaryāratāḥ sadā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Those who have self-restraint though they are attracted by desires, and who pursue the desire for kingdom and wealth are known as Padmas. They are always engaged in seeking alms.

## \|\| 1.106.61 \|\|

*jñānayogasamāyuktā dvaitācāraratāśca ye \|*  
*haṃsāste sādhakāḥ khyātāḥ svayamutpannasaṃvidaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Those Sādhakas who adopt Jñānayoga (pursuit of the path of Jñāna—spiritual knowledge) and are engaged in the practice of dualism are well-known as Haṃsas. Knowledge dawns on them automatically.

## \|\| 1.106.62 \|\|

*brahmacaryeṇa sattvena tathā'lubdhatayāpi vā \|*  
*jitaṃ jagaddhārayanto dhṛtarāṣṭrā matāstu ye \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Those who sustain the universe won over by means of celibacy, Sattva quality and absence of greed, are known as Dhṛtarāṣṭras.

## \|\| 1.106.63 \|\|

*gūḍhāścaraṃti ye jñānaṃ vrataṃ dharmamathāpi vā \|*  
*svārthaikāgataniṣṭhāstu bakāste sādhakā matāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Those Sādhakas are known as Bakas who secretly pursue knowledge (Jñāna), Vrata and Dharma but whose Niṣṭhā (established faith) is in their own selfish interest.

## \|\| 1.106.64 \|\|

*jalāśrayaṃ samāśritya sthitā utkṛṣṭasiddhaye \|*  
*bisaśṛṃgāṭakāhārāste kaṃkāḥ sādhakāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Those who for the purpose of achieving the noblest objectives resort to ponds and water reservoirs and subsist on lotus stalks and Śṛṅgāṭaka plants, are remembered as the Sādhakas of the Kaṅka type.

## \|\| 1.106.65 \|\|

*gobhiḥ sārddhaṃ vrajaṃtyatra goṣṭhe ca nivasaṃti ye \|*  
*paṃcagavyarasā ye vai gopālāste tu sādhakāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Those Sādhakas who wander along with cows and stay in cow-pen, and subsist on Pañcagavya (five cow products) are (known as) Gopālas.

## \|\| 1.106.66 \|\|

*kṛcchracāṃdrāyaṇaiścaiva kṣapayaṃti svakaṃ vapuḥ \|*  
*truṭimātrāśanāste tu truṭikāḥ sādhakā matāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Those who let their bodies become emaciated by the practice of Kṛcchra and Cāndrāyaṇa vows and eat only very small quantity (Cardamom size) (Truṭi) of food are known as the Sādhakas of the Truṭika type.

## \|\| 1.106.67 \|\|

*kṛtvā kuśamayīṃ patnīṃ maṭhe ye gṛhamedhinaḥ \|*  
*bhaikṣavṛttiratāḥ śuddhā maṭharāste tu sādhakāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The Sādhakas called Maṭharas consider themselves householders in a Maṭha (monastery) with the replica of a woman made of Kuśa Grass representing their wives. They are very pure and simple. They sustain themselves by seeking alms.

## \|\| 1.106.68 \|\|

*grāsamātrasamānābhirguṭikābhirathāṣṭabhiḥ \|*  
*kandamūlaphalotthābhirguṭikāste dvijātayaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Those Brāhmaṇas who regularly eat eight morsel like pills made of bulbous roots, roots and fruits are called Guṭikas.

## \|\| 1.106.69 \|\|

*svadehadaṇḍanairyuktā rātrau vīrāsane sthitāḥ \|*  
*daṃḍinaste samākhyātāḥ sarvametattavoditam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. They keep their bodies well-disciplined and subjected to restraints. During nights they remain in Vīrāsana (hero-like posture). They are called Daṇḍins (Daṇḍikas). Now everything has been explained to you.

## \|\| 1.106.70 \|\|

*sāmānyo'pi viśeṣaśca vṛttino gṛhiṇo'pi vā \|*  
*teṣāṃ bhedo mayā khyātāḥ samyakkṣetranivāsinām \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. The general and particular avocations of the householders and others among the residents of holy spots along with their diverse varieties have been fully narrated to you.

## \|\| 1.106.71 \|\|

*evamādidharmayuktāḥ prabhāsakṣetravāsinaḥ \|*  
*taiḥ pūjyo bhagavāndevo bālarūpī pitāmahaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The residents of the Prabhāsa Kṣetra have the Dharmas (rites and customs) in this manner and Lord Pitāmaha in the form of a boy is worthy of their adoration.

## \|\| 1.106.72 \|\|

*mahāpātakino ye tu ye tu viprairbahiṣkṛtāḥ \|*  
*na ca te saṃspṛśeyurvai brahmāṇaṃ bālarūpiṇam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Those who are guilty of Mahāpātakas, those who have been excommunicated by Brāhmaṇas, should never touch Brahmā in the form of a boy.

## \|\| 1.106.73 \|\|

*brahmacārī sadā dāṃto jitakrodho jiteṃdriyaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ te brāhmaṇāḥ khyātāḥ kṣetramadhyanivāsinaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. They are always celibate. They are self-controlled. They subdue their anger. They control all the sense-organs. Thus the Brāhmaṇas residing in a Kṣetra are known.

## \|\| 1.106.74 \|\|

*taiḥ pūjyo bhagavāndevo bālarūpī pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*ye vedādhyayane yuktāstaiḥ prapūjyaḥ pitāmahaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The holy Lord Pitāmaha in the form of a boy is worthy of their veneration. Pitāmaha is to be perfectly worshipped by those who regularly study (and recite) the Vedas.

## Chapter 107 - Procedure of the Worship of Brahmā

## \|\| 1.107.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*atha pūjāvidhānaṃ te kathayāmi samāsataḥ \|*  
*bhaktibhedānpṛthaktasya brahmaṇo bālarūpiṇaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Henceforth I shall succinctly describe to you the procedure for the worship of Brahmā as a boy. I shall mention different types of adoration.

## \|\| 1.107.2 \|\|

*rathayātrāvidhānaṃ tu stotramaṃtravidhikramam \|*  
*vividhā bhaktiruddiṣṭā manovākkāyasaṃbhavā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. I shall tell you the procedure of chariot procession, the (serial) order of eulogies, Mantras as well as different types of devotion, viz. physical, oral and mental.

## \|\| 1.107.3 \|\|

*laukikī vaidikī cāpi bhavedādhyātmikī tathā \|*  
*dhyānadhāraṇayā yā tu vedānāṃ smaraṇena ca \|*  
*brahmaprītikarī caiṣā mānasī bhaktirucyate \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Further, it may be Laukikī (Mundane), Vaidikī (Vedic) and Ādhyātmikī (spiritual).

That which causes delight to Brahmā by means of Dhyāna (meditation) and Dhāraṇā (steady absorption of the mind) as well as recollecting Vedic Mantras is called Mānasī (mental) Bhakti.

## \|\| 1.107.4 \|\|

*maṃtravedanamaskārairagniśrāddhavidhānakaiḥ \|*  
*jāpyaiścāraṇyakaiścaiva vācikī bhaktirucyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Recitation of Vedic Mantras, prostrating oneself while bowing, performance of rites in the sacred fire, Śrāddha ceremonies, Japa and repetition of Āraṇyaka passages—This is called Vācikī (verbal) Bhakti.

## \|\| 1.107.5-6 \|\|

*vratopavāsaniyamaiściteṃdriyanirodhibhiḥ \|*  
*kṛcchra sāṃtapanaiścānyaistathā cāṃdrāyaṇādibhiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*brahmoktaiścopavāsaiśca tathānyaiśca śubhavrataiḥ \|*  
*kāyikī bhaktirākhyātā trividhā tu dvijanmanām \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. The Kāyikī (physical) Bhakti includes the following: Restraints of the mind and the sense-organs through the regulations of Vratas, fasts etc., observance of Kṛcchra, Sāntapana, Cāndrāyaṇa and other expiatory rites, and of auspicious Vratas as explained in the Scriptural Texts and similar fasts. Thus Bhakti in the case of Brāhmaṇas is of three kinds.

## \|\| 1.107.7-10 \|\|

*goghṛtakṣīradadhibhirmadhvikṣusukuśodakaiḥ \|*  
*gaṃdhamālyaiśca vividhairvastubhiścopapādibhiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ghṛtagugguladhūpaiśca kṛṣṇāgurusugaṃdhibhiḥ \|*  
*bhūṣaṇai haimaratnādyaiścitrābhiḥ sragbhireva ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*nyāsaiḥ parisaraiḥ stotraiḥ patākābhistathotsavaiḥ \|*  
*nṛtyavāditragītaiśca sarvavastūpahārakaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*bhakṣyabhojyānna pānaiśca yā pūjā kriyate naraiḥ \|*  
*pitāmahaṃ samuddiśya sā bhaktirlaukikī matā \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-10. The worship of Brahmā of the worldly kind is called Laukikī Bhakti. The following articles are made use of therein: cow’s ghee, milk, curds, honey, sugarcane juice, water from excellent Kuśa grass, sweet scents, garlands, various subsidiary articles of worship, incense from Guggala and ghee, black Aguru of sweet scent, gold ornaments, jewels, wreaths of various sorts, Nyāsa (ritualistic touching of the limbs), Parisara (circumambulation), flags, banners, prayers in chorus, dances, songs, musical instruments, offerings of all kinds of articles, foodstuffs, cooked rice, beverages etc.

## \|\| 1.107.11 \|\|

*vedamaṃtrahavirbhāgaiḥ kriyā yā vaidikī smṛtā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The sacred rite performed with Vedic Mantras, Havis etc. is remembered as Vaidikī (Vedic type) Bhakti.

## \|\| 1.107.12-13 \|\|

*darśe ca paurṇamāsyāṃ ca karttavyaṃ cāgnihotrajam \|*  
*prāśanaṃ dakṣiṇādānaṃ puroḍāśa iti kriyā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*iṣṭirdhṛtiḥ somapānaṃ yājñiyaṃ karma sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*ṛgyajuḥ sāmajāpyāni saṃhitādhyayanāni ca \|*  
*kriyate brahmāṇamuddiśya sā bhaktirvedikocyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Various sacred rites are performed with Brahmā in view. Those rites constitute what is called Vaidikā Bhakti: Agnihotra rite is performed on New-Moon day and Full-Moon day. The holy Havis is consumed. Monetary gifts are offered. Puroḍāśa is offered in sacrificial rites such as Iṣṭi and Dhṛti. Soma juice is drunk as a sacrificial rite. Ṛk., Yajus and Sāma Mantras are used in Japa. The Saṃhitā texts are studied and recited.

## \|\| 1.107.14-16 \|\|

*prāṇāyāmaparo nityaṃ dhyānavānvijiteṃdriyaḥ \|*  
*bhaikṣyabhakṣī vratī cāpi sarvapratyāhṛteṃdriyaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*dhāraṇaṃ hṛdaye kṛtvā dhyāyamānaḥ prajeśvaram \|*  
*hṛtpadmakarṇikāsīnaṃ raktavarṇaṃ sulocanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*paśyannuddyotitamukhaṃ brahmāṇaṃ sukaṭītaṭam \|*  
*raktavarṇaṃ caturbāhuṃ varadābhayahastakam \|*  
*evaṃ yaściṃtayeddevaṃ brahmabhaktaḥ sa ucyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. A person who is called Brahmabhakta (devotee of Brahmā) is like this: He is always engaged in Prāṇāyāma (restraint of breath). He meditates with full control over the sense-organs. He eats what is obtained by way of alms. He observes Vratas. He withdraws his sense-organs from everything (with the aim of sublimating his desires). Prajeśvara (i.e. Lord of the Subjects, Brahmā) is retained by him in his heart. Brahmā is meditated upon as seated in the pericarp of the lotus of the heart, red in colour and having excellent eyes. The devotee visualizes Brahmā with excellent waist and seat and beaming face. The Lord has four arms granting boons and fearlessness (freedom from fear). Such is the devotee of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.107.17 \|\|

*vidhiṃ ca śṛṇu me devi yaḥ smṛtaḥ kṣetravāsinām \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O goddess, listen to the procedure and injunction regarding the residents of the holy spot.

## \|\| 1.107.18 \|\|

*nirmamā nirahaṃkārā niḥsaṃgā niṣparigrahāḥ \|*  
*caturvargepi niḥsnehāḥ samaloṣṭāśmakāṃcanāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. They are free from the sense of Mamatva (my-ness, possession). They are not egoistic. They have no close attachments (with anything). They do not accept gifts. They have no love for the usual four aims of life (Puruṣārthas). They view (regard) equally a lump of clay, a stone and a piece of gold.

## \|\| 1.107.19 \|\|

*bhūtānāṃ karmabhirnityaṃ trividhairabhayapradāḥ \|*  
*prāṇāyāmaparā nityaṃ paradhyānaparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. By means of their three-fold activity (verbal, mental and physical) they grant freedom from fear to all living beings. They perform Prāṇāyāma always. They are devoted to the meditation of the Supreme Absolute.

## \|\| 1.107.20 \|\|

*jāpinaḥ śucayo nityaṃ yatidharmakriyāparāḥ \|*  
*sāṃkhyayogavidhijñā ye dharmavicchinnasaṃśayāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. They are engaged in the performance of Japa always. They remain always pure. They are engaged in the pious activities of ascetics. They are conversant with the procedures of Sāṃkhya and Yoga. They get all their doubts cleared by persons well-versed in the Dharma Śāstras.

## \|\| 1.107.21-22 \|\|

*brahmapūjāratā nityaṃ te viprāḥ kṣetravāsinaḥ \|*  
*tairyathā pūjanīyo vai bālarūpī pitāmahaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tathāhaṃ kīrttayiṣyāmi śṛṇuṣvaikamanāḥ priye \|*  
*snātvā tu vimale tīrthe śuklāṃbaradharaḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*pūjopahārasaṃyuktastato brahmāṇamarcayet \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Those Brāhmaṇas residing in holy spots are always engaged in the worship of Brahmā. I shall explain how Pitāmaha in the form of a boy, should be worshipped by them. O my beloved, listen attentively. After taking holy bath in the Tīrtha free from impurities, he should wear white clothes and remain pure and clean. Fully equipping himself with the requisites for adoration and offerings he should worship Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.107.23 \|\|

*pūrvaṃ saṃsnāpya vidhinā paṃcāmṛtarasodakaiḥ \|*  
*gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. At the outset, he has to bathe the deity in accordance with the injunctions, by means of Pañcāmṛtarasa (may be Pañca Gavya) and water. He has to take cow’s urine, dung, milk, curds and ghee. Then water with Kuśa blades.

## \|\| 1.107.24 \|\|

*gāyatryā gṛhya gomūtraṃ gaṃdhadvāreti gomayam \|*  
*āpyāyasveti ca kṣīraṃ dadhikrāvṇeti vai dadhi \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He takes Gomūtra (cow’s urine) uttering the Gāyatrī Mantra. He takes cow-dung uttering the Vedic text beginning with gandhadvārā. He takes cow’s milk uttering the Mantra beginning with apyāvasva. He takes up curds with the Mantra beginning with dadhikrāvṇa.

## \|\| 1.107.25 \|\|

*tejo'si śukramityājyaṃ devasya tvā kuśodakam \|*  
*āpohiṣṭheti maṃtreṇa paṃcagavyena snāpayet \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. He takes Ājya (ghee) uttering the Mantra beginning with tejośi śukram He takes the Kuśa water uttering the Mantra beginning with devasya tvā. He should then bathe the deity uttering the Mantra beginning with āpo hiṣṭhā.

## \|\| 1.107.26 \|\|

*kapilāpaṃcagavyena kuśavāriyutena ca \|*  
*snāpayenmaṃtrapūtena brahmasnānaṃ hi tatsmṛtam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The devotee thus bathes the deity with the five milk products from a Kapilā (tawny-coloured) cow further sanctified by the Mantras. This is remembered as Brahmasnāna.

## \|\| 1.107.27 \|\|

*varṣakoṭisahasraistu yatpāpaṃ samupārjitam \|*  
*surajyeṣṭhaṃ tu saṃsnāpya dahetsarvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. By bathing Surajyeṣṭha (the senior-most god i.e. Brahmā) one undoubtedly reduces to ash all the sins incurred in the course of thousands of crores of years.

## \|\| 1.107.28 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃsnāpya vidhinā brahmāṇaṃ bālarūpiṇam \|*  
*karpūrāgarutoyena tataḥ saṃsnāpayeddvijaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. After duly bathing thus, the deity Brahmā in the form of a boy, the Brāhmaṇa then bathes the deity further with water mixed with camphor and agallochum.

## \|\| 1.107.29 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛtvārccayeddevaṃ gāyatrīnyāsayogataḥ \|*  
*mūrdhnaḥ pādatalaṃ yāvatpraṇavaṃ vinyasedbudhaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. After doing this the devotee should worship the Lord through the Gāyatrī Nyāsa (ritualistic touching of the limbs while uttering the syllables of the Gāyatrī Mantra). A wise man should perform the Nyāsa with Praṇava (all over the body) beginning with the head and ending with the sole of the foot.

## \|\| 1.107.30 \|\|

*takāraṃ vinyasenmūrdhni sakāraṃ mukhamaṇḍale \|*  
*vikāraṃ kaṃṭhadeśe tu tukāraṃ cāṃgasaṃdhiṣu \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The Nyāsa of Takāra (the syllable tat) is on the head, that of ‘sa’ syllable is in the region of the face, that of ‘vi’ is in the region of the throat and that of ‘tu’ (that is tur) is in the joints of the limbs.

## \|\| 1.107.31 \|\|

*vakāraṃ hṛdi madhye tu rekāraṃ pārśvayordvayoḥ \|*  
*ṇikāraṃ dakṣiṇe kukṣau yakāraṃ vāmasaṃjñite \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The Nyāsa of syllable ‘va’ is in the centre of the heart and of the syllable ‘re’ at the two sides. The Nyāsa of syllable ‘ni’ is in the right side of belly and that of ‘ya’ in the left one (‘nya’ split into ‘ni’ and ‘ya’).

## \|\| 1.107.32 \|\|

*bhakāraṃ kaṭinābhisthaṃ gokāraṃ pārśvayordvayoḥ \|*  
*dekāraṃ jānunornyasya vakāraṃ pādapadmayoḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The Nyāsa of syllable ‘bha’ (i.e. bhar) should be in the navel of the waist and of ‘go’ in the two sides (in the Jaṅghā—calf muscles). After the Nyāsa of ‘de’ on the two knees that of the syllable ‘va’ is to be on the lotus-like feet.

## \|\| 1.107.33 \|\|

*syakāramaṃguṣṭhayornyasya dhīkāramurasi nyaset \|*  
*makāraṃ jānumūle tu hi kāraṃ guhyamāśritam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. After the ritualistic touch of the two thumbs with the syllable ‘sye’ that of the chest shall be made with syllable ‘dhi’. The Nyāsa of syllable ‘ma’ is at the root of the knee and of the syllable ‘hi’ is on the private parts.

## \|\| 1.107.34 \|\|

*dhikāraṃ hṛdaye nyasya yokāraṃ cādharoṣṭhake \|*  
*yokāraṃ ca tathaivānyamuttaroṣṭhe nyasetsudhīḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The Nyāsa of syllable ‘dhi’ is on the heart and that of ‘yo’ is in the lower lips. A wise devotee should perform the Nyāsa of the other syllable ‘yo’ on the upper lip.

## \|\| 1.107.35 \|\|

*nakāraṃ nāsikāgre tu prakāraṃ netramāśritam \|*  
*cokāraṃ ca bhruvormadhye dakāraṃ prāṇamāśritam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The Nyāsa of the syllable ‘na’ (i.e. naḥ) is at the tip of the nose and that of ‘pra’ is on the eye. The Nyāsa of syllable ‘co’ is in the middle of the eyebrows and of the syllable ‘da’ is on Prāṇa (life breath).

## \|\| 1.107.36 \|\|

*yātkāraṃ ca lalāṭāṃte vinyasedvai sureśvari \|*  
*nyāsaṃ kṛtvā'tmano dehe deve kuryāttathā priye \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O goddess of Suras, the Nyāsa of the syllable ‘ya’ is on the forehead. O beloved, after the Nyāsa on his own body, the devotee shall make the Nyāsa on the deity too.

## \|\| 1.107.37-38 \|\|

*sarvopahārasaṃpannaṃ kṛtvā samyaṅnirīkṣayet \|*  
*kuṃkumāgarukarpūracaṃdanena vimiśritam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*gaṃdhatoyairupaskṛtya gāyatryā praṇavena ca \|*  
*prokṣayetsarvadravyāṇi paścādarcanamārabhet \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. After making the deity full with all the offerings, the devotee reviews it completely. After supplementing the holy articles mixed with saffron, Agaru, camphor and sandal by means of scented water, the devotee sprinkles all those articles uttering Gāyatrī (beginning with Oṃ) and Praṇava. Thereafter he should begin the adoration.

## \|\| 1.107.39 \|\|

*divyai puṣpaiḥ sugaṃdhaiśca mālatīkamalādibhiḥ \|*  
*aśokaiḥ śatapatraiśca bakulaiḥ pūjayetkramāt \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. He should worship in due order with divine flowers of sweet scents such as Mālatī, Kamala, Aśoka, Śatapatra and Bakula.

## \|\| 1.107.40 \|\|

*kṛṣṇāgarusudhūpena ghṛtadīpaistathottamaiḥ \|*  
*tataḥ pradāpayettatra naivedyaṃ vividhaṃ kramāt \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Fumigation should be done with excellent incense of black Agaru as well as excellent lamps with ghee. Thereafter the devotee should offer the Naivedya of different kinds in due order.

## \|\| 1.107.41 \|\|

*khaṇḍalaḍḍukaśrīveṣṭakāṃsārāśokapallavaiḥ \|*  
*svastikollipikādugdhā tilaveṣṭakilāṭikām \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The Naivedya should consist of Khaṇḍa, Laḍḍuka, Śrīveṣṭa, Kāṃsāra, Aśoka Pallava (sprouts and shoots of Aśoka), Svastika (Marathi—Saṅkarapāli), Ullipikā, Dugdhā, Tila-veṣṭa as well as Kilāṭikā.

## \|\| 1.107.42 \|\|

*phalāni caiva pakvāni mūlamaṃtreṇa dāpayet \|*  
*ṛgvedaṃ ca yajurvedaṃ sāmavedaṃ ca pūjayet \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Ripe fruits should be offered uttering the Mūla Mantra. The devotee should worship Ṛgveda, Yajurveda and Sāmaveda.

## \|\| 1.107.43 \|\|

*jñānaṃ vairāgyamaiśvaryaṃ dharmaṃ saṃpūjayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*īśānādikramāddevi diśāsu vidiśāsu ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. A wise man should worship Jñāna (knowledge), Vairāgya (disinterestedness), Aiśvarya (or authority) and Dharma (piety), O goddess, in the quarters and the intervening spaces between them beginning with north-east and proceeding in due order.

## \|\| 1.107.44 \|\|

*caturddaśavidyāsthānāni brahmaṇo'gre prapūjayet \|*  
*hṛdayāni tato nyasya devasya purataḥ kramāt \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The devotee should worship the places of the fourteen Vidyā (Lores) before Brahmā. Then Nyāsa on Hṛdaya (heart) etc. should be performed in front of the Lord in the proper order.

## \|\| 1.107.45-46 \|\|

*āpohiṣṭheti ṛgiyaṃ hṛdayaṃ parikīrttitam \|*  
*ṛtaṃ satyaṃ śikhā proktā udutyaṃ netramādiśet \|\| 45 \|\|*

*citraṃ devānāmityevaṃ sarvalokeṣu viśrutam \|*  
*brahmaṃste chādayāmīti kavacaṃ samudāhṛtam \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. The Mantra for the Nyāsa on the heart is the Ṛk beginning with āpo hi ṣṭhā. The Mantra beginning with ṛtam satyam is said to be the Mantra for the Nyāsa of Śikhā (tuft of hair). The Mantra for the Nyāsa on the eyes is that beginning with udutyam. The Mantra beginning with citram devānām is well-known in all the worlds. It is pointed out that the Kavaca (protective Mantra) is uttering the Mantra brahmaṃs te chādayāmi.

## \|\| 1.107.47 \|\|

*bhūrbhuvaḥ svaritīreśa pūjanaṃ parikīrtitam \|*  
*gāyatryā pūjayeddevamoṃkāreṇābhimaṃtritam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The worship of Īśa is proclaimed with the utterance of bhūḥ bhuvaḥ svaḥ After consecrating with Oṃkāra the devotee should worship the Lord by means of Gāyatrī Mantra.

## \|\| 1.107.48 \|\|

*praṇavenāparānsarvānṛgvedādīnprapūjayet \|*  
*gāyatrī paramo maṃtro vedamātā vibhāvarī \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The devotee should worship all the others beginning with Ṛgveda by means of Praṇava. Gāyatrī is the greatest Mantra, it is the mother of the Vedas. It is Vibhāvarī (excellent due to its splendour).

## \|\| 1.107.49 \|\|

*gāyatryakṣaratattvaistu brahmāṇaṃ yastu pūjayet \|*  
*upoṣya paṃcadaśyāṃ tu sa yāti paramaṃ padam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. He who observes fast on the Pañcadaśī (fifteenth day, Full-Moon or New-Moon day) and worships Brahmā by means of the principles underlying the syllables of the Gāyatrī attains the greatest position (Mokṣa).

## \|\| 1.107.50 \|\|

*saṃsārasāgaraṃ ghoramuttitīrṣurdvijo yadi \|*  
*prabhāse kārttike māsi brahmāṇaṃ pūjayetsadā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. If a Brāhmaṇa is desirous of crossing the terrible ocean of mundane existence, he should always worship Brahmā in the Prabhāsa Kṣetra in the month of Kārttika.

## \|\| 1.107.51 \|\|

*yasya darśanamātreṇa aśvamedha phalaṃ labhet \|*  
*kastaṃ na pūjayedvidvānprabhāse bālarūpiṇam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. As a mere sight of Brahmā in the form of a boy gives the fruit of a horse-sacrifice, a sensible learned man will not worship him.

## \|\| 1.107.52 \|\|

*yasyaikadivasaprāṃte sadevāsuramānavāḥ \|*  
*vilayaṃ yāṃti deveśi kastaṃ na pratipūjayet \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O goddess of Devas, who will not eagerly worship Brahmā within whose unit of time reckoned as one day, all the Devas, Asuras and human beings become annihilated?

## \|\| 1.107.53 \|\|

*pitā yaḥ sarvadevānāṃ bhūtānāṃ ca pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*yasmādeṣa sa taiḥ pūjyo brāhmaṇaiḥ kṣetravāsibhiḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. It is he who is the father of all the Devas. He is the grandfather of all the living beings. Hence he should be worshipped by all the Brāhmaṇas residing in the holy spot.

## \|\| 1.107.54 \|\|

*rudrarūpī viśvarūpī sa eva bhuvaneśvaraḥ \|*  
*paurṇamāsyāmupoṣitvā brahmāṇaṃ jagatāṃ patim \|*  
*arcayedyo vidhānena so'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. He alone is the Lord of the Bhuvana (universe). He is in the form of Rudra. He is multi-formed. He who observes fast on the Full-Moon day and duly worships Brahmā, the Lord of the worlds, shall get the fruit of a horse sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.107.55 \|\|

*kārttike māsi devasya rathayātrā prakīrttitā \|*  
*yāṃ kṛtvā mānavo bhaktyā yāti brahmasalokatām \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The Rathayātrā (religious procession or a Car festival) of the Lord in the month of Kārttika is glorified. A man who devoutly performs it, attains Sālokya Mukti i.e. residence in the same world as that of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.107.56-57 \|\|

*kārttike māsi deveśi paurṇamāsyāṃ caturmukham \|*  
*mārgeṇa carmaṇā sārddhaṃ sāvitryā ca paraṃtapaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*bhrāmayennagaraṃ sarvaṃ nānāvādyaiḥ samanvitam \|*  
*sthāpayedbhrāmayitvā tu sakalaṃ nagaraṃ nṛpaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. O goddess of Devas, a king who wishes to be a Parantapa (destroyer of enemies) should take the Four-faced Lord clad in deer-hide and accompanied by Sāvitrī all through the city. It shall be on the Full-Moon day. Many kinds of musical instruments should be played. After taking the deity round the entire city, he shall be installed.

## \|\| 1.107.58 \|\|

*brāhmaṇānbhojayitvāgre śāṃḍileyaṃ prapūjya ca \|*  
*āropayedrathe devaṃ puṇyavāditraniḥsvanaiḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. At the outset a Brāhmaṇa belonging to the Śāṇḍilya Gotra should be honoured. Then the Brāhmaṇas should be fed. Then the Lord is to be placed on a chariot (car) to the accompaniment of music played on different musical instruments.

## \|\| 1.107.59 \|\|

*rathāgre śāṃḍilīputraṃ pūjayitvā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇānvācayitvā ca kṛtvā puṇyāhamaṃgalam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. In front of the Ratha (chariot) the son of Śāṇḍilī should be worshipped in accordance with the injunctions. The Brāhmaṇas should be made to recite the Mantras and the auspicious ceremony of Puṇyāha (-vācana) is to be performed.

## \|\| 1.107.60 \|\|

*devamāropayitvā tu rathe kuryātprajāgaram \|*  
*nānāvidhaiḥ prekṣaṇakairbrahmaśeṣaiśca puṣkalaiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The Lord (deity) is to be placed on the chariot. The devotees then keep awake by seeing various kinds of visual scenes of dramatic performance and listening to profound sounds of the Vedic chant.

## \|\| 1.107.61 \|\|

*nāroḍhavyaṃ rathe devi śūdreṇa śubhamicchatā \|*  
*nādharmeṇa viśeṣeṇa muktvaikaṃ bhojakaṃ priye \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. A Śūdra who wishes for welfare should not ride the chariot. O my beloved wife and goddess, particularly a man of no pious nature abstains from riding it. In fact excepting a Bhojaka (Brāhmaṇa of Bhoja clan—MW) no one gets into the chariot.

## \|\| 1.107.62 \|\|

*brahmaṇo dakṣiṇe pārśve sāvitrīṃ sthāpayetpriye \|*  
*bhojakaṃ vāmapārśve tu purataḥ paṃkajaṃ nyaset \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. O my beloved, the devotee should place Sāvitrī on the right side of Brahmā. The Bhojaka should be seated on the left side. A lotus is to be placed in front.

## \|\| 1.107.63 \|\|

*evaṃ tūryaninādaiśca śaṃkhaśabdaiśca puṣkalaiḥ \|*  
*bhrāmayitvā rathaṃ devi puraṃ sarvaṃ ca dakṣiṇam \|*  
*svasthāne sthāpayedbhūyaḥ kṛtvā nīrājanaṃ budhaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Thus, a wise devotee makes the chariot go round the city to the accompaniment of sounds of conchs and musical instruments, O goddess. After performing the Nīrājana rite (waving lights before an idol) the deity is placed on its own original place.

## \|\| 1.107.64 \|\|

*ya evaṃ kurute yātrāṃ bhaktyā yaścāpi paśyati \|*  
*rathaṃ vā'karṣayedyastu sa gacchedbrahmaṇaḥ padam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. He who devoutly conducts this religious procession, he who views it and he who pulls the car, shall go to the region of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.107.65 \|\|

*yo dīpaṃ dhārayettatra brahmaṇo rathapṛṣṭhagaḥ \|*  
*padepade'śvamedhasya sa phalaṃ viṃdate mahat \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. He who holds a lamp there at the back of the car of Brahmā, obtains the great fruit of a horse-sacrifice at every step.

## \|\| 1.107.66 \|\|

*yo na kārayate rājā rathayātrāṃ tu brahmaṇaḥ \|*  
*sa pacyate mahādevi raurave kālamakṣayam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. O great goddess, a king who does not make arrangements for the car festival of Brahmā is cooked in Raurava hell for an endless period of time.

## \|\| 1.107.67 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena rāṣṭrasya kṣemamicchatā \|*  
*rathayātrāṃ viśeṣeṇa svayaṃ rājā pravarttayet \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Hence by all means, with a keen desire for the welfare of the nation, a king himself should make special arrangements for the chariot festival.

## \|\| 1.107.68 \|\|

*pratipadbrāhmaṇāṃścāpi bhojayedvi dhivatsudhīḥ \|*  
*vāsobhirahataiścāpi gandhamālyānulepanaiḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. A wise king should duly feed Brāhmaṇas on the first lunar day and honour them with unwashed clothes (fresh from the loom), sweet scents, garlands and unguents.

## \|\| 1.107.69 \|\|

*kārttike māsyamāvāsyāṃ yastu dīpapradīpanam \|*  
*śālāyāṃ brahmaṇaḥ kuryātsa gacchetparamaṃ padam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. He who lights lamps in the sacred chamber of Brahmā on the New-Moon day in the month of Kārttika, shall go to the highest region.

## \|\| 1.107.70 \|\|

*utsaveṣu ca sarveṣu sarvakāle viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*pūjayeyurimaṃ viprā brahmāṇaṃ jagatāṃ gurum \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. During all festivals, especially on all occasions, Brāhmaṇas should worship Brahmā, the preceptor of all the worlds.

## \|\| 1.107.71 \|\|

*yathākṛtyaprayogeṇa samyakchraddhā samanvitāḥ \|*  
*pūjyo divyopacāreṇa yathāvittānusārataḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Those Brāhmaṇas should possess perfect faith and celebrations should be befitting their duties. The deity should be honoured with divine offerings and services according to one’s means and affluence.

## \|\| 1.107.72 \|\|

*evaṃ te kathitaṃ devi pūjāmāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*prabhāsakṣetramāhātmyaṃ brahmaṇaḥ bālarūpiṇaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Thus, O goddess, the excellent greatness of the worship of Brahmā in the form of a boy, along with the greatness of Prabhāsa Kṣetra has been narrated to you.

## \|\| 1.107.73 \|\|

*tasyāhaṃ kathayiṣyāmi nāmnāmaṣṭottaraṃ śatam \|*  
*pradattvā ca paṭhitvā ca yajñāyutaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. I shall now mention his (Brahmā’s) one hundred eight names by reciting and handing over of which to others, one will derive the fruit of ten thousand Yajñas.

## \|\| 1.107.74 \|\|

*gāyatryā lakṣajāpyena samyagjaptena yatphalam \|*  
*tatphalaṃ samavāpnoti stotrasyāsya udīraṇāt \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. By reciting this prayer, one obtains that fruit which accrues by perfect articulation of a hundred thousand Gāyatrī Japas.

## \|\| 1.107.75 \|\|

*idaṃ stotravaraṃ divyaṃ rahasyaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*na deyaṃ duṣṭabuddhīnāṃ nindakānāṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. This is the most excellent of all eulogies. It has divine esoteric significance. It is destructive of all sins. It should not be imparted to evil-minded persons indulging in censuring others.

## \|\| 1.107.76 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāya pradātavyaṃ śrotriyāya mahātmane \|*  
*viṣṇunā hi purā pṛṣṭaṃ brahmaṇaḥ stotramuttmam \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. It should be given to a noble-souled Brāhmaṇa having perfect acquaintance with the Vedic texts.

Formerly this excellent eulogy of Brahmā was enquired about by Viṣṇu:

## \|\| 1.107.77 \|\|

*keṣukeṣu ca sthāneṣu devadeva pitāmaha \|*  
*saṃcintyastanmamācakṣva tvaṃ hi sarvaviduttama \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. “O Pitāmaha, O Lord of Devas, how are you to be meditated upon and in which holy spot? Do tell this to me. You are indeed the most excellent one of the omniscient ones.”

## \|\| 1.107.78 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*puṣkare'haṃ suraśreṣṭho gayāyāṃ prapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*kānyakubje vedagarbho bhṛgukṣetre caturmukhaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

78\. I am Suraśreṣṭha in Puṣkara. Prapitāmaha (Great-grandfather) in Gayā, Vedagarbha in Kānyakubja and Caturmukha (Fourfaced) in Bhṛgu Kṣetra.

## \|\| 1.107.79 \|\|

*kauberyāṃ sṛṣṭikartā ca nandipuryāṃ bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*prabhāse bālarūpī ca vārāṇasyāṃ surapriyaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. I am: Sṛṣṭikartā (Creator) in Kauberī (northern region), Bṛhaspati in Nandipurī. (I am one) in the form of a boy at Prabhāsa and Surapriya in Vārāṇasī.

## \|\| 1.107.80 \|\|

*dvārāvatyāṃ cakradevo vaidiśe bhuvanādhipaḥ \|*  
*pauṃḍrake puṇḍarīkākṣaḥ pītākṣo hastināpure \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. (I am) Cakradeva in Dvārāvatī. Bhuvanādhipa in Vaidiśa (Vidiśa), Puṇḍarīkākṣa (Lotus-eyed) in Pauṇḍraka (N. Bengal?) and Pītākṣa in Hastināpura.

## \|\| 1.107.81 \|\|

*jayaṃtyāṃ vijayaścāsau jayantaḥ puruṣottame \|*  
*vāḍeṣu padmahasto'haṃ tamolipte tamonudaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. I am Vijaya in Jayantī (Jyntia in Assam). Jayanta in Puruṣottama (Jagannāthapurī), Padmahasta in Vāḍa, and Tamonuda in Tamolipta (Tāmralipti—mod. Tamluk).

## \|\| 1.107.82 \|\|

*āhicchatryāṃ janānaṃdaḥ kāñcīpuryāṃ janapriyaḥ \|*  
*karṇāṭasya pure brahmā ṛṣikuṇḍe munistathā \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. (I am) Janānanda in Āhicchatrī\[4\], Janapriya (favourite of the people) in Kāñcīpurī, Brahmā in Karṇāṭa’s city and Muni in Ṛṣikuṇḍa.

## \|\| 1.107.83 \|\|

*śrīkaṇṭhe śrīnivāsaśca kāmarūpe śubhaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*ucchriyāṇe devakarttā sraṣṭā jālaṃdhare tathā \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. (I am called) Śrīnivāsa in Śrīkaṇṭha; Śubhaṃkara in Kāmarūpa (Assam), Devakartā in Ucchriyāṇa (Orissa) and Sraṣṭā (Creator) in Jālandhara (Punjab);

## \|\| 1.107.84 \|\|

*mallikākhye tathā viṣṇurmahendre bhārgavastathā \|*  
*gonardaḥ sthavirākāre hyujjayinyāṃ pitāmahaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Viṣṇu in the holy spot named Mallika; Bhārgava in Mahendra; Gonarda in Sthavirākāra and Pitāmaha in Ujjayinī;

## \|\| 1.107.85 \|\|

*kauśāṃbyāṃ tu mahādevo hyayodhyāyāṃ tu rāghavaḥ \|*  
*viraṃciścitrakūṭe tu vārāho vindhyaparvate \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Mahādeva in Kauśāmbi; Rāghava in Ayodhyā; Virañci in Citrakūṭa and Vārāha in Vindhyaparvata;

## \|\| 1.107.86 \|\|

*gaṃgādvāre suraśreṣṭho himavante tu śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*dehikāyāṃ srucāhastaḥ padmahastastathā'rbude \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Suraśreṣṭha in Gaṅgādvāra; Śaṅkara in Himavanta; Srucāhasta in Dehikā; Padmahasta in Arbuda (Mt. Abu);

## \|\| 1.107.87 \|\|

*vṛndāvane padmanetraḥ kuśa hastaśca naimiṣe \|*  
*gopakṣetre ca govindaḥ surendro yamunātaṭe \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Padmanetra in Vṛndāvana, Kuśahasta in Naimiṣa; Govinda in Gopakṣetra and Surendra in Yamunātaṭa (the banks of Yamunā);

## \|\| 1.107.88 \|\|

*bhāgīrathyāṃ padmatanurjanānando janasthale \|*  
*kauṃkaṇe ca sa madhvakṣaḥ kāmpilye kanakaprabhaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Padmatanu in Bhāgīrathi and Janānanda in Janasthala. Madhvakṣa in Kauṅkaṇa and Kanakaprabha in Kāmpilya (Farrukhabad in U.P.);

## \|\| 1.107.89 \|\|

*kheṭake cānnadātā ca śaṃbhuścaiva kratusthale \|*  
*laṃkāyāṃ caiva paulastyaḥ kāśmīre haṃsavāhanaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Ānnadātā (one who provides with food) in Kheṭaka (Kaira-Gujarat); Śaṃbhu in Kratusthala; Paulastya in Laṅkā and Haṃsavāhana, (Swan-vehicled) in Kaśmīra;

## \|\| 1.107.90 \|\|

*vasiṣṭhaścārbude caiva nāradaścotpalāvane \|*  
*medhake śrutidātā ca prayāge yajuṣāṃ patiḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Vasiṣṭha too in Arbuda (See 86); Nārada in Utpalavana; Śrutidātā in Medhaka; and Yajuṣāmpati (Lord of Yajus Mantras) in Prayāga.

## \|\| 1.107.91 \|\|

*śivaliṃge sāmavedo markaṭe ca madhupriyaḥ \|*  
*nārāyaṇaśca gomante vidarbhāyāṃ dvija priyaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Sāmaveda in Śivaliṅga; Madhupriya in Markaṭa; Nārāyaṇa in Gomanta (Goa) and Dvijapriya (favourite of Brāhmaṇas) in Vidarbha (Maharashtra);

## \|\| 1.107.92 \|\|

*aṃkulake brahmagarbho brahmavāhe sutapriyaḥ \|*  
*indraprasthe durādharṣaścaṃpāyāṃ suramardanaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Brahmagarbha in Aṅkulaka (Aṅkola in Gujarat); Sutapriya in Brahmavāha; Durādharṣa in Indraprastha (Delhi); and Suramardana in Campā (Bhagalpur) (Orissa, around Jaypur on the river Vaitaraṇī);

## \|\| 1.107.93 \|\|

*virajāyāṃ mahārūpaḥ surūpo rāṣṭravardhane \|*  
*kadaṃbake janādhyakṣo devādhyakṣaḥ samasthale \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Mahārūpa in Virajā; Surūpa in Rāṣṭravardhana; Janādhyakṣa in Kadambaka; and Devādhyakṣa in Samasthala;

## \|\| 1.107.94 \|\|

*gaṃgādharo rudrapīṭhe supīṭhe jaladaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tryaṃbake tripurāriśca śrīśaile ca trilocanaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Gaṅgādhara in Rudrapīṭha; remembered as Jalada in Supīṭha; Tripurāri in Tryaṃbaka (Nasik, Maharashtra); and Trilocana in Śriśaila (Karnul, Andhra);

## \|\| 1.107.95 \|\|

*mahādevaḥ plakṣapure kapāle vedhanāśanaḥ \|*  
*śṛṅgaverapure śaurirnimiṣe cakradhārakaḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Mahādeva in Plakṣapura; Vedhanāśana in Kapāla; Śauri in Śṛṅgaverapura (Singraur on Gaṅgā; Allahabad Dist.), and Cakradharaka in Nimiṣa;

## \|\| 1.107.96 \|\|

*nandipuryāṃ virūpākṣo gautamaḥ plakṣapādape \|*  
*mālyavānhastināthe tu dvijendro vācike tathā \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Virūpākṣa in Nandipurī (See 79); Gautama in Plakṣapādapa, Mālyavān in Hastinātha and Dvijendra in Vācika (Vaṭika?);

## \|\| 1.107.97 \|\|

*indrapuryāṃ divānātho bhūtikāyāṃ puraṃdaraḥ \|*  
*haṃsabāhuśca candrāyāṃ caṃpāyāṃ garuḍapriyaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Divānātha in Indrapurī; and Purandara in Bhūtikā; Haṃsabāhu in Candrā and Garuḍapriya in Caṃpā (see v 92);

## \|\| 1.107.98 \|\|

*mahodaye mahāyakṣaḥ suyajñaḥ pūtake vane \|*  
*siddheśvare śuklavarṇo vibhāyāṃ padmabodhakaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Mahāyakṣa in Mahodaya (Kanoj); Suyajña in Pūtakavana; Śuklavarṇa in Siddheśvara and Padmabodhaka in Vibhā;

## \|\| 1.107.99 \|\|

*devadāruvane liṃgī udaketha umāpatiḥ \|*  
*vināyako mātṛsthāne alakāyāṃ dhanādhipaḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Liṅgin in Devadāruvana, Umāpati in Udaka; Vināyaka in Mātṛsthāna and Dhanādhipa in Alakā;

## \|\| 1.107.100 \|\|

*trikūṭe caiva goviṃdaḥ pātāle vāsukistathā \|*  
*kovidāre yugādhyakṣaḥ strīrājye ca surapriyaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Govinda in Trikūṭa (a mountain in Laṅkā), Vāsuki in Pātāla, Yugādhyakṣa in Kovidāra and Surapriya in Strīrājya (kingdom of women—Kāmarūpa, Assam);

## \|\| 1.107.101 \|\|

*pūrṇagiryāṃ subhogaśca śālmalyāṃ takṣakastathā \|*  
*amare pāpahā caiva aṃbikāyāṃ sudarśanaḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Subhoga in Pūrṇagiri; Takṣaka in Śālmalī; Pāpahā in Amara; and Sudarśana in Aṃbikā;

## \|\| 1.107.102 \|\|

*naravāpyāṃ mahāvīraḥ kāntāre durganāśanaḥ \|*  
*padmavatyāṃ padmagṛho gagane mṛgalāñchanaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. Mahāvīra in Naravāpī; Durganāśana in Kāntāra; Padmagṛha in Padmāvatī and Mṛgalāñchana in Gagana (Sky).

## \|\| 1.107.103 \|\|

*aṣṭottaraṃ nāmaśataṃ yatraitatparipaṭhyate \|*  
*tatraiva mama sāṃnidhyaṃ trisaṃdhyaṃ madhusūdana \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. O Madhusūdana, my presence all through the three twilights is only in that place where these one hundred eight names are recited.

## \|\| 1.107.104 \|\|

*teṣāmapi yastvekaṃ paśyedvai bālarūpiṇam \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ labhate puṇyaṃ pūrvoktānāṃ ca vedhasām \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. He who views anyone of these in the form of the boy-Brahmā, obtains the merit of all the Vedhas (gods—Brahmās) mentioned before.

## \|\| 1.107.105 \|\|

*etairyo nāmabhiḥ kṛṣṇa prabhāse stauti māṃ sadā \|*  
*sthānaṃ me vijayaṃ labdhvā modate śāśvatīḥ samāḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. O Kṛṣṇa, he who always eulogizes me at Prabhāsa by means of these names, goes to my region called Vijaya and rejoices there for endless years.

## \|\| 1.107.106 \|\|

*mānasaṃ vācikaṃ caiva kāyikaṃ caiva duṣkṛtam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ nāśamāyāti mama stotrā'nu kīrtanāt \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. By reciting my prayer, all the sins, mental, verbal and physical, get destroyed.

## \|\| 1.107.107 \|\|

*puṣpopahaurardhūpaiśca brāhmaṇānāṃ ca tarpaṇaiḥ \|*  
*dhyānena ca sthireṇāśu prāpyate yatphalaṃ naraiḥ \|*  
*tatphalaṃ samavāpnoti mama stotrānu kīrtanāt \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. By reciting my prayer one obtains that fruit which is attained by men through offerings of flowers and incense, propitiation of Brāhmaṇas and by steady meditation.

## \|\| 1.107.108 \|\|

*brahmahatyādipāpāni iha loke kṛtānyapi \|*  
*akāmataḥ kāmato vā tāni naśyaṃti tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. The sins of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter etc. committed in this world knowingly or unknowingly, do perish in a moment.

## \|\| 1.107.109 \|\|

*idaṃ stotraṃ mamābhīṣṭaṃ śṛṇuyādvā paṭhecca vā \|*  
*sa muktaḥ pātakaiḥ sarvaiḥ prāpnuyānmahadīpsitam \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. This eulogy of mine is liked by me. He who listens to it or recites it shall be rid of all sins. He will obtain intensely desired things.

## \|\| 1.107.110 \|\|

*anyadrahasyaṃ te vacmi śṛṇu kṛṣṇa yathārthataḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. O Kṛṣṇa, I shall tell you another secret thing. Listen to it with attention.

## \|\| 1.107.111 \|\|

*āgneyaṃ tu yadā ṛkṣaṃ kārtikyāṃ bhavati kvacit \|*  
*mahatī sā tithirjñeyā prabhāse mama vallabhā \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. In the month of Kārttika, if the constellation Kṛttikā coincides with the Kārttikī day, that lunar day is to be considered very great. It is my favourite in Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.107.112 \|\|

*prājāpatyaṃ yadā ṛkṣaṃ tithau tasyāṃ bhavedyadi \|*  
*sā mahākārtikī puṇyā devānāmapi durlabhā \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. If the constellation Rohiṇī coincides with that lunar day, that is the meritorious Mahākārttika day inaccessible even to Devas.

## \|\| 1.107.113 \|\|

*maṃde vārke gurau vā'pi kārtikī kṛttikāyutā \|*  
*tatrāśvamedhikaṃ puṇyaṃ dṛṣṭvā vai bālarūpiṇam \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. If the constellation Kṛttikā coincides with the Kārttikī lunar day or Saturday, Sunday or Thursday and the devotee views Brahmā in the form of a boy, he attains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.107.114 \|\|

*viśākhāsu yadā sūryaḥ kṛttikāsu ca candramāḥ \|*  
*sa yogaḥ padmako nāma prabhāse durlabho hare \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. When the Sun is in the constellation Viśākhā and the Moon in Kṛttikā, that Yoga is called Padmāka. O Hari, it is very rare in Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.107.115 \|\|

*tasminyoge naro dṛṣṭvā prabhāse bālarūpiṇam \|*  
*pāpakoṭiyuto vā'pi yamalokaṃ na paśyati \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. During that Yoga a man must view Brahmā in the form of a boy at Prabhāsa. Even if he is defiled by crores of sins he does not see the world of Yama.

## \|\| 1.107.116 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*ityevaṃ kathitaṃ stotraṃ brahmaṇā haraye punaḥ \|*  
*mayā tava samākhyātaṃ māhātmyaṃ brahmadaivatam \|\| 116 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

116\. In this manner, the prayer was recounted to Hari by Brahmā. The greatness of Brahmā as a deity has been explained by me to you.

## \|\| 1.107.117 \|\|

*sarvapāpaharaṃ nṛṇāṃ śrutaṃ sarvārthasādhakam \|*  
*bhūmidānaṃ ca dātavyaṃ tatra yātrāphalepsubhiḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. If it is listened to, it destroys all sins of men. It facilitates the acquisition of all objectives. Gift of a plot of land should be made there by those who desire the fruit of the (complete) pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.107.118 \|\|

*kamaṃḍaluḥ śvetavastraṃ mahādānāni ṣoḍaśa \|*  
*tatraiva devi deyāni brahmaṇe bālarūpiṇe \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. O goddess, there itself a water-pot, a white cloth and sixteen great gifts should be made to Brahmā in the form of a boy.

## \|\| 1.107.119 \|\|

*mahāparvaṇi saṃprāpte kuryuḥ pārāyaṇaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*sarve te brāhmaṇā devi kṣetramadhyanivāsinaḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. When great Parvan days (festival days) come all the Brāhmaṇas residing in the holy place should perform Pārāyaṇa (reading and reciting the scriptures), O goddess.

## Chapter 108 - Greatness of Pratyūṣeśvara (Pratyūṣa-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.108.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi vasūnāṃ liṃgamuttamam \|*  
*someśādīśadigbhāge pañcāśaddhanuṣāntare \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sthitaṃ liṃgaṃ mahādevi caturvaktraṃ surapriyam \|*  
*pratyūṣeśvaranāmānaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*darśanāttasya devasya saptajanmāntarodbhavam \|*  
*pāpaṃ praṇāśamāyāti satyaṃsatyaṃ varānane \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, O great goddess, a devotee should go to the excellent Liṅga of Vasus. It is within a distance of fifty Dhanus from Someśa, in the north-eastern direction.

The Liṅga installed there, O great goddess, has four faces and iṣ a favourite of Suras. Its name is Pratyūṣeśvara and it destroys great sins.

By visiting that deity, sins incurred in the course of seven births get destroyed, O lady of excellent countenance. It is truth, it is the truth.

## \|\| 1.108.4 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*ko'sau pratyūṣanāmeti kathaṃ liṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*kasya putraḥ sa vikhyāta etanme vada śaṃkara \|\| 4 \|\|*

The Devī said:

4\. Who is this person named Pratyūṣa? Whose son was he? How was the Liṅga installed? How is he famous? O Śaṅkara do tell me all this.

## \|\| 1.108.5 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*dakṣo brahmasuto devi prajāpatiriti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasya kanyāḥ purā ṣaṣṭirdadau dharmāya vai daśa \|\| 5 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

5\. O goddess, Dakṣa, a son of Brahmā, is remembered as Prajāpati. He had sixty daughters. He gave ten of them to Dharma.

## \|\| 1.108.6 \|\|

*tāsāṃ madhye mahādevi ekā viśveti viśrutā \|*  
*sā dharmācca mahādevi aṣṭāvajanayatsutān \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Among them, O great goddess, one was well-known as Viśvā. She begot of Dharma eight sons.

## \|\| 1.108.7 \|\|

*āpo dhruvaśca somaśca dharaścaivā'nalo'nilaḥ \|*  
*pratyūṣaśca prabhāsaśca vasavo'ṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. They are glorified as the eight Vasus. They are Apa, Dhruva, Soma, Dhara, Anala, Anila, Pratyūṣa and Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.108.8 \|\|

*teṣāṃ madhye saptamo'sau pratyūṣa iti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*sa putrakāmo deveśi prabhāsaṃ kṣetramāgataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The seventh among them (the Vasus) is well-known as Pratyūṣa. O goddess of Devas, desirous of begetting a son, he came to the holy spot of Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.108.9 \|\|

*sa jñātvā kāmikaṃ kṣetraṃ pratiṣṭhāpya maheśvaram \|*  
*tapaścacāra vipulaṃ divyaṃ varṣaśataṃ priye \|*  
*dhyāyandevaṃ mahādevaṃ śāntastadgatamānasaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He came to know that the holy spot is Kāmika (wish-yielding) and installed Maheśvara. O my beloved, he performed an elaborate penance for a hundred years according to divine reckoning. Tranquil and concentrating his mind within himself, he meditated on Mahādeva.

## \|\| 1.108.10 \|\|

*tatastuṣṭo mahādevastasya bhaktyā nirañjanaḥ \|*  
*dadau tasya sutaṃ devi devalaṃ yogināṃ varam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O goddess, the unsullied great Lord became pleased with his devotion and granted him a son Devala, a most excellent one among Yogins.

## \|\| 1.108.11 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti deveśi talliṃgasya prabhāvataḥ \|*  
*devalo bhagavānyogī pratyūṣasyā'bhavatsutaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Ever since then, by the power of that Liṅga, Devala, the son of Pratyūṣa, became a divine Yogin.

## \|\| 1.108.12 \|\|

*anena kāraṇenāsau pratyūṣeśvarasaṃjñitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. For this same reason, the deity is designated Pratyūṣeśvara.

## \|\| 1.108.13 \|\|

*yaścānapatyaḥ puruṣastaṃ samārādhayiṣyati \|*  
*tasyānvavāye deveśi saṃtatirna vinaśyati \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. If any person without a child propitiates that Lord, O goddess of Devas, the line of progeny in his race never gets broken.

## \|\| 1.108.14 \|\|

*yaḥ pratyūṣe mahādevi pratyūṣeśvaramuttamam \|*  
*pūjayiṣyati sadbhaktyā satataṃ niyatātmavān \|*  
*tasyaiṣyati kṣayaṃ pāpamapi brahmavadhodbhavama \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O great goddess, if anyone worships the excellent deity Pratyūṣeśvara, early at dawn with excellent devotion and perpetual restraint of himself, his sin gets destroyed even if it is incurred by the slaughter of a Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.108.15 \|\|

*vṛṣastatraiva dātavyaḥ samyagyātrāphalepsubhiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. A bull should be given away there by those who wish to get the perfect fruit of the pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.108.16 \|\|

*māghe kṛṣṇacaturddaśyāṃ jāgṛyāttatra vai niśi \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ dānayajñānāṃ phalaṃ jāgaraṇāllabhet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The devotee should keep awake at night on the fourteenth lunar day in the dark half of the month of Māgha. By keeping awake one shall attain the fruit of all Dānas and Yajñas.

## Chapter 109 - Greatness of Anileśvara (Anila-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.109.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi anileśvaramuttamam \|*  
*tasyottareśānadiksthaṃ dhanuṣāṃ tritaye priye \|\| 1 \|\|*

*liṃgaṃ mahāprabhāvaṃ hi darśanātpāpanāśanam \|*  
*vasūnāṃ pañcamo yo'sāvanilaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sa cā'rādhya mahādevaṃ pratyakṣīkṛtavānbhavam \|*  
*liṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhayāmāsa samyakchraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the excellent shrine of Anileśvara. O my beloved, it is situated within a distance of three Dhanus to the north-east thereof (i.e. of Pratyūṣeśvara).

The Liṅga is highly powerful. By merely viewing, it destroys sins. The fifth among Vasus who is known as Anila (Wind god) propitiated Mahādeva and made him manifest to him. Equipped with perfect faith, he installed the Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.109.4 \|\|

*evamīśaprabhāvena sutastasyā'pyabhūdbalī \|*  
*manojaveti vikhyāto hyavijñātagatistathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Thus, by the power of Īśa, his son became very strong. He became well-known as Manojava (having speed of the mind) and his movement could not be comprehended fully.

## \|\| 1.109.5 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā vyādhinā martyo pīḍyate na kadācana \|*  
*nāndho na badhiro mūko na rogī na ca nirdhanaḥ \|*  
*kadācijjāyate martyastena dṛṣṭena bhūtale \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. By visiting him, a man ceases to be afflicted with sickness. He will never again be sick. If he is viewed, neither a blind one, nor a deaf one, neither a dumb person nor a sickly and impoverished one is born in the family.

## \|\| 1.109.6 \|\|

*puṣpamekaṃ tu yo dadyāttasya liṃgasya copari \|*  
*sukhasaubhāgyasaṃpannaḥ sa sadā rūpavānbhavet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He who offers a single flower on the Liṅga becomes richly endowed with happiness and good fortune. He will always be handsome.

## \|\| 1.109.7 \|\|

*ityevaṃ kathitaṃ devi māhātmyaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*śrutvā'numodya bhāvena sarvakāmaiḥ samṛddhyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thus, O goddess, the greatness that destroys sins, has been narrated. By listening to this and approving this with emotional fervour, one becomes rich by realizing all his desires.

## Chapter 110 - Greatness of Prabhāseśvara (Prabhāsa-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.110.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchedvarārohe prabhāseśvaramuttamam \|*  
*gaurītapovanāddevi paścime samudāhṛtam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*dhanuṣāṃ saptake devi nātidūre vyavasthitam \|*  
*sthāpitaṃ tanmahāliṃgaṃ vasūnāmaṣṭamena hi \|\| 2 \|\|*

*prabhāsa iti nāmnā hi śivapūjāratena vai \|*  
*sa putrakāmo deveśi prabhāsakṣetramāgataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, O beautiful woman, a pilgrim should go to the excellent shrine of Prabhāseśvara. O goddess, it is stated to be situated within a distance of seven Dhanus to the west of Gaurītapovana (penance grove of Gaurī). It is not very far away. That great Liṅga was installed by the eighth of the Vasus named Prabhāsa, who was engaged in the adoration of Śiva. O goddess of Devas, he had come to the holy spot of Prabhāsa with a keen desire for a son.

## \|\| 1.110.4 \|\|

*pratiṣṭhāpya mahāliṅgaṃ cacāra vipulaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*āgneyamiti vikhyātaṃ divyābdānāṃ śataṃ priye \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. After installing the great Liṅga well-known as Āgneya (fiery), he performed an elaborate penance for a hundred years according to divine reckoning, O my beloved.

## \|\| 1.110.5 \|\|

*tatastasya mahādevi samyakchraddhānvi tasya vai \|*  
*tutoṣa bhagavānrudro dadau yanmanasīpsitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Thereafter, O great goddess, Lord Rudra became pleased with him as he had great faith. The Lord granted him what he had desired in his mind.

## \|\| 1.110.6 \|\|

*bṛhaspatestu bhaginī bhuvanā brahmavādinī \|*  
*prabhāsasya tu sā bhāryā vasūnāmaṣṭamasya ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Bhuvanā, the sister of Bṛhaspati, was an expounder of Brahman. She was the wife of Prabhāsa, the eighth one among Vasus.

## \|\| 1.110.7 \|\|

*viśvakarmā sutastasyāḥ sṛṣṭikartā prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ takṣako vidvānmanormātāmahaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Her son was Viśvakarman, creator of the universe and a patriarch. He is remembered as the maternal grandfather of Manu. He was an expert architect.

## \|\| 1.110.8 \|\|

*takṣakaḥ sūryabiṃbasya tejasaḥ śātano mahān \|*  
*evaṃ tasyā'bhavatputro vasūnāmaṣṭamasya vai \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He became the fashioner of the Solar disc, the great hewer of the refulgence. The son of the eighth one among the Vasus was like this.

## \|\| 1.110.9 \|\|

*prabhāsanāmno deveśi talliṃgārādhanodyataḥ \|*  
*iti te kathitaṃ devi prabhāseśvarasūcakam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O goddess of Devas, the son of the Vasu named Prabhāsa was also engaged in the propitiation of that Liṅga. Thus, O goddess, the greatness pertaining to Prabhāseśvara has been spoken to you.

## \|\| 1.110.10 \|\|

*māhātmyaṃ sarvapāpaghnaṃ sarvakāmapradaṃ śubham \|*  
*yastaṃ pūjayate bhaktyā samyakchraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The greatness is destroyer of all sins. It is splendid and it fulfills all desires. A devotee should worship him with devotion and should possess perfect faith.

## \|\| 1.110.11 \|\|

*bhūmiśāyī nirāhāro japanvai śatarudriyam \|*  
*māghe māsi caturdaśyāṃ snātvā sāgarasaṃgame \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He should observe fast and recite the Śatarudriya Mantra. He should lie down on the bare ground. On the fourteenth lunar day in the month of Māgha, he should take a holy dip at the confluence with the ocean (of a river).

## \|\| 1.110.12 \|\|

*paṃcāmṛtena saṃsnāpya pūjayitvā vidhānataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He should bathe the deity with Pañcāmṛta and worship it in accordance with the injunctions.

## \|\| 1.110.13 \|\|

*ya evaṃ kurute devi samyagyātrāmahotsavam \|*  
*sa muktaḥ pātakaiḥ sarvaiḥ sarvakāmaiḥ samṛddhyate \|*  
*vṛṣastatraiva dātavyaḥ samyagyātrāphalepsubhiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O goddess, he who performs the great festival of the chariot and concludes the pilgrimage shall be rid of all sins. He becomes prosperous with the realization of all desires. A bull should be offered as a gift there by those who wish to get the fruit of a perfect pilgrimage.

## Chapter 111 - Greatness of Rāmeśvara Kṣetra (Rāma-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.111.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi puṣkarāraṇyamuttamam \|*  
*tasmādīśānakoṇasthaṃ dhanuṣāṃ ṣaṣṭibhiḥ sthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tatra kuṇḍaṃ mahādevi hyaṣṭapuṣkarasaṃjñitam \|*  
*sarva pāpaharaṃ devi duṣprāpyamakṛtātmabhiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tatra kuṇḍasamīpe tu purā rāmeśadhīmatā \|*  
*sthāpitaṃ tanmahāliṅgaṃ rāmeśvara iti smṛtam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tasya pūjanamātreṇa mucyate brahmahatyayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Thereafter, a pilgrim should go to the excellent Puṣkarāraṇya, O great goddess, situated within sixty Dhanus in the north-eastern corner thereof.

O great goddess, there is a Kuṇḍa there named Aṣṭapuṣkara. It is a destroyer of all sins. O goddess, it is inaccessible to those who have not controlled their selves.

Near the Kuṇḍa is the great Liṅga named Rāmeśvara installed by the intelligent Rāmeśa (Rama). Merely through its worship, one is rid of the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter.

## \|\| 1.111.5 \|\|

*śrīdevyuvāca \|*  
*bhagavanvistarādbrūhi rāmeśvarasamudbhavam \|*  
*kathaṃ tatrāgamadrāmaḥ sasītaśca salakṣmaṇaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Śrī Devī said:

5\. O great Lord, do tell me in detail everything pertaining to Rāmeśvara. How did Rāma come there accompanied by Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa?

## \|\| 1.111.6 \|\|

*kathaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ liṅgaṃ puṣkare pāpataskare \|*  
*etadvistarato brūhi phalaṃ māhātmyasaṃyutam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. How was the Liṅga installed in Puṣkara that removes all sins? Describe this in detail as well as the benefit along with its greatness.

## \|\| 1.111.7 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*caturviṃśayuge rāmo vasiṣṭhena purodhasā \|*  
*purā rāvaṇanāśārthaṃ jajñe daśarathātmajaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

7\. In the twenty-fourth Yuga, formerly Rāma was born as the son of Daśaratha with Vasiṣṭha as his family priest. He was born for the purpose of slaying Rāvaṇa.

## \|\| 1.111.8 \|\|

*tataḥ kālāntare devi ṛṣiśāpānmahātapāḥ \|*  
*yayau dāśarathī rāmaḥ sasītaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then, O goddess, due to the curse of a sage (?) Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, went (to the forest) after some time along with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa and performed a great penance.

## \|\| 1.111.9 \|\|

*vanavāsāya niṣkrāṃto divyairbrahmarṣibhirvṛtaḥ \|*  
*tato yātrāprasaṃgena prabhāsaṃ kṣetramāgataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He set out surrounded by divine Brāhmaṇa-sages, for a stay in the forest. In the course of his wanderings he came to Prabhāsa Kṣetra.

## \|\| 1.111.10 \|\|

*taṃ deśaṃ tu samāsādya suśrāṃto niṣasāda ha \|*  
*astaṃ gate tataḥ sūrye parṇānyāstīrya bhūtale \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After reaching that spot, he sat there because he was extremely tired. When the Sun set he prepared a bed of leaves on the ground.

## \|\| 1.111.11 \|\|

*suṣvāpātha niśāśeṣe dadṛśe pitaraṃ svakam \|*  
*svapne daśarathaṃ devi saumyarūpaṃ mahāprabham \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He went to sleep. O goddess, at the close of the night, he saw his father Daśaratha in a dream. He was highly brilliant yet gentle in appearance.

## \|\| 1.111.12 \|\|

*prātarutthāya tatsarvaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo nyavedayat \|*  
*yathā daśarathaḥ svapne dṛṣṭastena mahātmanā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. After getting up in the morning, he related to the Brāhmaṇas how Daśaratha was seen in dream by that noble-souled one.

## \|\| 1.111.13 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*vṛddhikāmāśca pitaro varadāstava rāghava \|*  
*darśanaṃ hi prayacchaṃti svapnānte hi svavaṃśaje \|\| 13 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

13\. Pitṛs desirous of the prosperity of the persons born in their family appear before them in dreams. O Rāghava, your ancestors do bestow boons on you.

## \|\| 1.111.14 \|\|

*etattīrthaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ suguptaṃ śārṅgadhanvanaḥ \|*  
*puṣkareti samākhyātaṃ śrāddhamatra pradīyatām \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. This Tīrtha of Śārṅgadhanvan (Viṣṇu, the bearer of Śārṅga bow) is highly meritorious and well-guarded. It is called Puṣkara. May the Śrāddha be offered here.

## \|\| 1.111.15 \|\|

*nūnaṃ daśaratho rājā tīrthe cāsminsamīhate \|*  
*tvayā dattaṃ śubhaṃ piṇḍaṃ tataḥ sa darśanaṃ gataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Indeed King Daśaratha desires that an auspicious ball of rice should be offered by you in this Tīrtha. Therefore, he has appeared to you.

## \|\| 1.111.16 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ \|*  
*nimaṃtrayāmāsa tadā śrāddhārhānbrāhmaṇāñchubhān \|\| 16 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

16\. On hearing their words, the lotus-eyed Rāma invited splendid Brāhmaṇas worthy of the invitation to Śrāddha.

## \|\| 1.111.17 \|\|

*abravīllakṣmaṇaṃ pārśve sthitaṃ vinatakaṃdharam \|*  
*phalārthaṃ vraja saumitre śrāddhārthaṃ tvarayā'nvitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He told Lakṣmaṇa who was standing humbly at his side: “O son of Sumitrā, go to fetch fruits for the Śrāddha. Do go quickly.”

## \|\| 1.111.18-20 \|\|

*sa tatheti pratijñāya jagāma raghunaṃdanaḥ \|*  
*ānayāmāsa śīghraṃ sa phalāni vividhāni ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

*bilvāni ca kapitthāni tindukāni ca bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*badarāṇi karīrāṇi karamardāni ca priye \|\| 19 \|\|*

*cirbhaṭāni parūṣāṇi mātuliṃgāni vai tathā \|*  
*nālikerāṇi śubhrāṇi iṃgudīsaṃbhavāni ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. After saying “So it shall be”, the scion of the family of Raghu went out and quickly brought different kinds of fruits like Bilva, Kapittha, plenty of Tinduka, Badara, Karīra and Karamarda, O my beloved. There were also Cirbhaṭa, Parūṣa, Mātuliṅga (citron), Nālikera (coconut) and white Iṅgudi fruits.

## \|\| 1.111.21-24 \|\|

*athaitāni papācāśu sītā janakanaṃdinī \|*  
*tatastu kutape kāle snātvā valkalabhṛcchuciḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇānānayāmāsa śrāddhārhāndvijasattamān \|*  
*gālavo devalo raibhyo yavakrīto'tha parvataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*bharadvājo vasiṣṭhaśca jāvālirgautamo bhṛguḥ \|*  
*ete cānye ca bahavo brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*śrāddhārthaṃ tasya saṃprāptā rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*etasminneva kāle tu rāmaḥ sītāmabhāṣata \|\| 24 \|\|*

21-24. Sītā, the daughter of Janaka, cooked them immediately. Then at the auspicious hour of Kutapa Rāma had his bath and wore a clean bark garment and invited excellent Brāhmaṇas worthy of the Śrāddha honour. They were: Gālava, Devala, Raibhya, Yavakrīta, Parvata, Bharadvāja, Vasiṣṭha, Jābāli, Gautama, Bhṛgu etc. These and many other Brāhmaṇas who had mastered the Vedas (came there). They came there for the Śrāddha to be performed by Rāma of energetic actions. At that time Rāma spoke to Sītā:

## \|\| 1.111.25 \|\|

*ehi vaidehi viprāṇāṃ dehi pādāvanejanam \|*  
*etacchrutvā'tha sā sītā praviṣṭā vṛkṣamadhyataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. “Do come, O Vaidehī, for the holy rite of washing the feet of the Brāhmaṇas.” On hearing this, Sītā entered a place in the midst of the trees,

## \|\| 1.111.26 \|\|

*gulmairācchādya cātmānaṃ rāmasyādarśane sthitā \|*  
*muhurmuhuryadā rāmaḥ sītāsītāmabhāṣata \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. She got hidden among the bushes. She was out of Rāmā’s sight, despite the fact that Rāma repeatedly called “Sītā! Sītā!”

## \|\| 1.111.27 \|\|

*jñātvā tāṃ lakṣmaṇo naṣṭāṃ kopāviṣṭaṃ ca rāghavam \|*  
*svayameva tadā cakre brāhmaṇārha pratikriyām \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Seeing Rāma very angry and Sītā out of view, Lakṣmaṇa himself performed the duty of honouring the Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.111.28 \|\|

*atha bhukteṣu vipreṣu kṛta piṃḍapradānake \|*  
*āgatā jānakī sītā yatra rāmo vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. After the Brāhmaṇas had taken their food and the ball of rice was also offered, Sītā, the daughter of Janaka, came to the place where Rāma was present.

## \|\| 1.111.29 \|\|

*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā paruṣairvākyairbhartsayāmāsa rāghavaḥ \|*  
*dhigdhikpāpe dvijāṃstyaktvā pitṛkṛtyamahodayam \|*  
*kva gatā'si ca māṃ hitvā śrāddhakāle hyupasthite \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. On seeing her, Rāghava rebuked her with harsh words: “Fie upon you, O sinful woman! Where had you been leaving me as well as the Brāhmaṇas when the time for Śrāddha had arrived? This was the holy rite of Pitṛs which brings about great prosperity.”

## \|\| 1.111.30 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā bhayabhītā ca jānakī \|\| 30 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

30\. On hearing his words Jānakī became extremely frightened.

## \|\| 1.111.31-36 \|\|

*kṛtāñjalipuṭā bhūtvā vepamānā hyabhāṣata \|*  
*mā kopaṃ kuru kalyāṇa mā māṃ nirbhartsaya prabho \|\| 31 \|\|*

*śṛṇu yasmādvibho'nyatra gatā tyaktvā tavāntikam \|*  
*dṛṣṭastatra pitā me'dya tathā caiva pitāmahaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tasya pūrvataraścāpi tathā mātāmahādayaḥ \|*  
*aṃgeṣu brāhmaṇendrāṇāmākrāntāste pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tato lajjā samabhavattatra me raghunandana \|*  
*pitrā tatra mahābāho manojñāni śubhāni ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

*bhakṣyāṇi bhakṣitānyeva yāni vai guṇavanti ca \|*  
*sa kathaṃ sukaṣāyāṇi kṣārāṇi kaṭukāni ca \|*  
*bhakṣayiṣyati rājendra tato me duḥkhamāviśat \|\| 35 \|\|*

*etasmātkāraṇānnaṣṭā lajjayā'haṃ raghūdvaha \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā śvaśuravargaṃ svaṃ tasmātkopaṃ parityaja \|\| 36 \|\|*

31-36. With palms joined in Veneration and trembling much she spoke: “O noble one, do not be angry. O Lord, do not rebuke me. Listen, O my Lord, why I went elsewhere leaving your side. Your father was seen by me. So also your grandfather. The one earlier than he and the maternal grandfather and others were seen separately in the bodies of the leading Brāhmaṇas. They had separately occupied those bodies. So, O scion of the family of Raghu, bashfulness overwhelmed me. O mighty one, your father was accustomed to eat charmingly delicious fooḍ-stuffs of good qualities. O great king, how will he eat this saltish, astringent and bitter stuff? So I became miserable. O leader of the descendants of Raghu, for this reason, on seeing the kinsmen of the father-in-law I disappeared through bashfulness. Hence eschew your anger.”

## \|\| 1.111.37 \|\|

*tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā vismito rāghavo'bhavat \|*  
*viśeṣeṇa dadau tasmiñchrāddhaṃ tīrthe tu puṣkare \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. On hearing her words Rāghava became surprised. He offered a special Śrāddha in the holy Puṣkara Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.111.38 \|\|

*tatra puṣkarasānnidhye dakṣiṇe dhanuṣāṃ traye \|*  
*liṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhayāmāsa rāmeśvaramiti śrutam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. There in the vicinity of Puṣkara itself, within a distance of three Dhanus to the south, he installed the Liṅga well-known as Rāmeśvara.

## \|\| 1.111.39 \|\|

*yastaṃ pūjayate bhaktyā gandhapuṣpādibhiḥ kramāt \|*  
*sa prāpnoti paraṃ sthānaṃ yratra devo janārdanaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. He who devoutly worships him with sweet scents, flowers etc. in due order, attains the great region where Lord Janārdana is present.

## \|\| 1.111.40 \|\|

*kimatra bahunoktena dvādaśyāṃ yatpradāpayet \|*  
*na tatra parisaṃkhyānaṃ triṣu lokeṣu vidyate \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Of what avail is profuse talk? If the Śrāddha is offered on Dvādaśī (twelfth lunar day) the merit thereof cannot be properly estimated in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.111.41 \|\|

*śukrāṃgārakasaṃyuktā caturthī yā bhavetkvacit \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhī vātra varārohe tatra śrāddhe mahatphalam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O beautiful lady, there is great merit in offering Śrāddha on any day when Ṣaṣṭhī (6th lunar day) or Caturthī (4th lunar day) coincides with Friday or Tuesday.

## \|\| 1.111.42 \|\|

*yāvaddvādaśavarṣāṇi pitaraśca pitāmahāḥ \|*  
*tarpitā nānyamicchanti puṣkare svakulodbhave \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. If propitiated in Puṣkara by one of their own family, the fathers and grandfathers become delighted for a period of twelve years. They never wish for anything else.

## \|\| 1.111.43 \|\|

*tatra yo vājinaṃ dadyātsamyagbhaktisamanvitaḥ \|*  
*aśvamedhasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. A man who offers the gift of a horse there with perfect devotion, attains the fruit of an Aśvamedha Yajña (horse-sac-rīfice).

## \|\| 1.111.44 \|\|

*iti te kathitaṃ samyaṅmāhātmyaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*rāmeśvarasya devasya puṣkarasya ca bhāmini \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Thus the sin-destroying greatness of Lord Rāmeśvara and Puṣkara has been perfectly spoken to you, O beautiful woman.

## Chapter 112 - Greatness of Lakṣmaṇeśvara (Lakṣmaṇa-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.112.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi lakṣmaṇeśvaramuttamam \|*  
*rāmeśātpūrvadigbhāge dhanustriṃśakasaṃsthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sthāpitaṃ lakṣmaṇenaiva tatra yātrāgatena vai \|*  
*mahāpāpaharaṃ devi talliṃgaṃ surapūjitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yastaṃ pūjayate bhaktyā nṛtyagītādivādanaiḥ \|*  
*homajāpyaiḥ samādhisthaḥ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, a pilgrim should go to the excellent Lakṣmaṇeśvara, O great goddess. It is situated within a distance of thirty Dhanus to the east of Rāmeśa.

It was installed by Lakṣmaṇa who had come there in the course of his pilgrimage. O goddess, that Liṅga is a destroyer of great sins. It is adored by Suras.

He who worships it devouḍy and remains absorbed in meditation and also offers dance, instrumental music and songs along with Homa and Japa attains the greatest goal.

## \|\| 1.112.4 \|\|

*annodakaṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca tatra deyaṃ dvijātaye \|*  
*saṃpūjya devadeveśaṃ gaṃdhapuṣpādibhiḥ kramāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Cooked food, water and gold should be gifted there to a Brāhmaṇa after worshipping the Lord of the chiefs of Devas with sweet scents, flowers etc, in due order.

## \|\| 1.112.5 \|\|

*māghe kṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ viśeṣastatra pūjane \|*  
*snānaṃ dānaṃ japastatra bhavedakṣayakārakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5, Worshipping there on the fourteenth day in the dark half of Māgha is particularly recommended. Holy ablution, donation and Japa there shall be of everlasting benefit.

## Chapter 113 - Greatness of Jānakīśvara (Jānakī-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.113.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi jānakīśvaramuttamam \|*  
*rāmeśānnaiṛte bhāge dhanustriṃśakasaṃsthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*pāpaghnaṃ sarvajaṃtūnāṃ jānakyā'rādhitaṃ purā \|*  
*pratiṣṭhitaṃ viśeṣeṇa samyagārādhyaśaṃkaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

*pūrvaṃ tasyaiva liṃgasya vasiṣṭheśeti nāma vai \|*  
*tatpaścājjānakīśeti tretāyāṃ prathitaṃ kṣitau \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the excellent shrine of Jānakīśvara situated within a distance of thirty Dhanus to the south-west of Rāmeśa.

Formerly it was worshipped by Jānakī. It destroys sins of all creatures. It was installed after propitiating Śaṅkara perfectly.

Earlier, the very same Liṅga was called Vasiṣṭheśa. Thereafter, it became famous on the earth in Tretā as Jānakīśa.

## \|\| 1.113.4 \|\|

*tataḥ ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi vālakhilyā maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*tatra siddhimanuprāptāstena siddheśvareti ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Thereafter, sixty thousand great sages named Vālakhilyas attained Siddhi there. So it is known as Siddheśvara also.

## \|\| 1.113.5 \|\|

*khyātaṃ kalau mahādevi yugaliṃgaṃ mahāprabham \|*  
*taddṛṣṭvā mucyate pāpairduḥkhadaurbhāgyasaṃbhavaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O great goddess, that Yugaliṅga of great refulgence became well-known as Siddheśvara in Kali Age. On seeing it one is rid of sins arising from misery and bad luck.

## \|\| 1.113.6 \|\|

*yastaṃ pūjayate bhaktyā nārī vā puruṣo'pi vā \|*  
*saṃsnāpya vidhivadbhaktyā sa muktaḥ pātakairbhavet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. A pilgrim who worships it devoutly after bathing it duly, shall be rid of sins whether one is a man or a woman.

## \|\| 1.113.7-8 \|\|

*snātvā ca puṣkare tīrthe yastalligaṃ prapūjayet \|*  
*niyato niyatāhāro māsamekaṃ nirantaram \|\| 7 \|\|*

*dinedine bhavettasya vājimedhādhikaṃ phalam \|*  
*māghe māsi tṛtīyāyāṃ yā nārī taṃ prapūjayet \|*  
*tadanvaye'pi daurbhāgyaṃ duḥkhaṃ śokaśca no bhavet \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. A pilgrim should bathe in the Puṣkara Tīrtha and worship the Liṅga regularly for a month continuously with restriction in his diet. Each day he will get more fruit than that of a horse-sacrifice. If a woman worships it on the third lunar day in the month of Māgha, there shall be no ill-luck, misery or grief in that family.

## \|\| 1.113.9 \|\|

*iti te kathitaṃ devi māhātmyaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*śrutaṃ harati pāpāni saubhāgyaṃ saṃprayacchati \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thus, O goddess, the sin-destroying greatness has been related to you. If listened to, it eradicates sins and accords conjugal felicity.

## Chapter 114 - Greatness of Vāmanasvāmī (Vāmanasvāmin)

## \|\| 1.114.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi viṣṇuṃ pāpapraṇāśanam \|*  
*vāmanasvāmināmānaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*puṣkarānnairṛte bhāge dhanurviśatibhiḥ smṛtam \|*  
*yadā baddho balirdevi viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tadā tatra padaṃ nyastaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ viśvarūpiṇā \|*  
*dvitīyaṃ meruśṛṃge tu tṛtīyaṃ gagane priye \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the shrine of sin-destroying Viṣṇu named Vāmanasvāmin. He is the destroyer of all sins.

It is remembered that the deity is stationed within a distance of twenty Dhanus on the south-western side of Puṣkara.

When, O goddess, Bali was bound by the powerful Viṣṇu, the right foot was placed there by the Viśvarūpin (Omni-formed One). O beloved, the second step was placed on the peak of Meru and the third in the firmament.

## \|\| 1.114.4 \|\|

*yāvadūrdhvaṃ cotkṣipati tāvadbhinnaṃ sudūrataḥ \|*  
*pādāgreṇa tu brahmāṇḍaṃ niṣkrāntaṃ salilaṃ tataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. When he lifted up the foot the Cosmic Egg received a long crack by the tip of the foot (of Viṣṇu) and water gushed forth therefrom.

## \|\| 1.114.5 \|\|

*tataḥ svajānumātreṇa saṃprāptaṃ pṛthivītale \|*  
*tato viṣṇupadī gaṃgā prasiddhimagamatkṣitau \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. It came up to his knees on the earth. Therefore, it became famous on the earth as Viṣṇupadī Gaṅgā (the Gaṅgā arising from Viṣṇu’s foot).

## \|\| 1.114.6 \|\|

*pūrvaṃ sā puṣkare prāptā puṣkarātsā mahānadī \|*  
*puṣkaraṃ kathyate vyoma puṣkaraṃ kathyate jalam \|*  
*tena tatpuṣkaraṃ khyātaṃ saṃnidhānaṃ prajāpateḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. At the outset that great river reached Puṣkara from the sky. The sky is called by the name Puṣkara. Water is also called Puṣkara. Hence the place of the presence of Prajāpati is famous as Puṣkara.

## \|\| 1.114.7 \|\|

*tatra snānaṃ naraḥ kṛtvā yaḥ paśyati hareḥ padam \|*  
*sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yatra devo hariḥ svayam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. After taking holy bath there, the man who views the foot of Hari, attains the greatest region where Hari himself is present.

## \|\| 1.114.8 \|\|

*tatra piṃḍapradānena tṛptiḥ syātkoṭivārṣikī \|*  
*pitṝṇāṃ ca varārohe hyetadāha hariḥ svayam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O beautiful lady, by offering balls of rice there to the Pitṛs, they become satisfied for a crore of years. Hari himself has said this.

## \|\| 1.114.9 \|\|

*atra gāthā purā gītā vasiṣṭhena maharṣiṇā \|*  
*vāmanasvāminaṃ dṛṣṭvā tāṃ śṛṇuṣva samāhitā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. In this context a couplet has been sung by the great sage Vasiṣṭha after viewing Vāmanasvāmin. Listen to it attentively.

## \|\| 1.114.10 \|\|

*snātvā tu puṣkare tīrthe dṛṣṭvā viṣṇupadaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*api kṛtvā mahatpāpaṃ kimataḥ paritapyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. “After bathing in Puṣkara and viewing Viṣṇu’s foot thereafter, why should there be worry even after committing great sins?”

## \|\| 1.114.11 \|\|

*yastatropānahau dadyādbrāhmaṇāya yatavrataḥ \|*  
*sa yānavaramārūḍho viṣṇuloke mahīyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He who makes a gift of a pair of shoes to a Brāhmaṇa and observes Vratas, proceeds to Viṣṇu’s world riding on a vehicle and is also honoured in Viṣṇuloka.

## Chapter 115 - Greatness of Puskareśvara (Puskara-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.115.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi puṣkareśvaramuttamam \|*  
*tasyaiva dakṣiṇe bhāge jānakīśvaramuttamam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*liṃgaṃ mahāprabhāvaṃ tu brahmaputreṇa pūjitam \|*  
*sanatkumāramuninā śraddhayā hema puṣkaraiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*pūjitaṃ tadvidhānena tena tatpuṣkareśvaram \|*  
*khyātaṃ tatra varārohe sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yastaṃ pūjayate bhaktyā gaṃṣapuṣpādibhiḥ kramāt \|*  
*yātrā kṛtā bhavettena pauṣkarī nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the excellent shrine of Puskareśvara to the south of the excellent Jānakīśvara.

The Liṅga is of great power and has been worshipped by sage Sanatkumāra, a son of Brahmā. It has been worshipped with faith by means of golden lotuses in accordance with the injunctions. Hence it is well-known as Puṣkareśvara. O beautiful lady, it is a destroyer of all sins.

If anyone devoutly worships him with sweet scents, flowers etc, it is as good as a pilgrimage to Puṣkara performed by him. There is no doubt about it.

## Chapter 116 - Greatness of Śaṅkhodakakuṇḍeśvarī Gaurī (Śaṅkhodaka-kuṇḍeśvarī)

## \|\| 1.116.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi devīṃ saubhāgyakāriṇīm \|*  
*kuṇḍeśvarīti vikhyātāṃ puṣkarādvāyugocare \|\| 1 \|\|*

*dhanuṣāṃ triṃśatā devi bhūtanāthācca nairṛte \|*  
*saṃsthitā pāpadamanī dāridryaughavināśinī \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tasyā nairṛtadigbhāge dhanuḥpañcadaśe sthitam \|*  
*śaṃkhodakaṃnāma kuṇḍaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, a pilgrim should go to the shrine of the goddess well-known as Kuṇḍeśvari, O great goddess. She confers conjugal felicity. The shrine is situated within a distance of thirty Dhanus to the north-west of Puṣkara and south-west of Bhūtanātha. The goddess that supresses sins and destroys a series of impoverished states is stationed there. There is a Kuṇḍa (holy pit) named Śaṅkhodaka situated within a distance of fifteen Dhanus to the south-west of the shrine of the goddess. This holy pit destroys all sins.

## \|\| 1.116.4 \|\|

*tatra snātvā tu ye martyā nārī vā śubhavāriṇi \|*  
*pūjayettāṃ mahādevi śaṃkhāvarteti viśrutām \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Whether a man or a woman, the pilgrim should take the holy bath in the auspicious water, O great goddess and worship that goddess well-known as Śaṅkhāvartā.

## \|\| 1.116.5-6 \|\|

*kalau kuṇḍeśvarīnāma sarvasaukhyapradāyinī \|*  
*śaṃkho nāma purā devi viṣṇunā nihataḥ priye \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tasya dehaṃ samādāya mahāntaṃ śaṃkharūpiṇam \|*
