It is said that great sins like those of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter, imbibing liquor, theft, defiling the wife of preceptor etc., perish by viewing that deity.

In the auspicious month of Bhādrapadā on the occasion of Ṛṣipañcamī (fifth day in the bright half of Bhādrapada) one who worships Akṣamāleśvara, is rid of the fear of hell.

## \|\| 1.129.52-53 \|\|

*gopradānaṃ praśaṃsaṃti tatrānnamudakaṃ tathā \|*  
*sarvapāpavināśāya pretyānaṃtasukhāya ca \|\| 52 \|\|*

*iti te kathitaṃ devi hyakṣamāleśvarodbhavam \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ pāpaśamanaṃ śrutaṃ duḥkhanibarhaṇam \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. For the purpose of the destruction of all sins and for attaining infinite happiness after death, they recommend the gift of cows, food and water there.

Thus, O goddess, the greatness pertaining to Akṣamāleśvara has been narrated to you. It suppresses sins. On being listened to it dispels misery.

## Chapter 130 - Greatness of Pāśupateśvara (Pāśupata-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.130.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi devaṃ pāśupateśvaram \|*  
*ugraseneśvarāddevi pūrvabhāge vyavasthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*gopādityāttathāgneyyāṃ dhruveśāddakṣiṇāṃ śritam \|*  
*sarvapāpaharaṃ devi pūrvabhāge vyavasthitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*gopādityāttathā liṃgaṃ darśanātsarvakāmadam \|*  
*asminyuge samākhyātaṃ saṃtoṣeśvarasaṃjñitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the shrine of the deity Pāśupateśvara situated on the eastern side of Ugraseneśvara, to the south-east of Gopāditya and to the south of Dhruveśa. It is destroyer of all sins. The Liṅga is situated to the east of Gopāditya (also). It fulfills all desires when one visits it. In this Yuga it is called by the name Santoṣeśvara.

## \|\| 1.130.4 \|\|

*saṃtuṣṭo bhagavānyasmātteṣāṃ tatra tapasvinām \|*  
*tena saṃtoṣanāmnā tu prakhyātaṃ dharaṇītale \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Since the Lord is pleased with the ascetics there, the Liṅga is well-known all over the earth by the name Santoṣa.

## \|\| 1.130.5 \|\|

*yugaliṃgaṃ mahādevi siddhisthānaṃ mahāprabham \|*  
*sthānaṃ pāśupatānāṃ ca bheṣajaṃ pāparogiṇām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O great goddess, this is a Yugaliṅga and the abode of Siddhis. It is highly lustrous. It is the place of Pāśupata devotees and is a panacea for persons who are afflicted with disease in the form of sins.

## \|\| 1.130.6 \|\|

*catvāro munayaḥ siddhāstasmiṃlliṃge yaśasvini \|*  
*vāmadevastu sāvarṇiraghoraḥ kapilastathā \|*  
*tasmiṃlliṃge tu saṃsiddhā anādīśe niraṃjane \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O renowned lady, four sages, Vāmadeva, Sāvarṇi, Aghora and Kapila have achieved their Siddhi in that Liṅga. They have attained Siddhi in the unsullied primordial Lord through that Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.130.7 \|\|

*tasya devasya sāmīpye vane śrīmukhasaṃjñitam \|*  
*lakṣmīsthānaṃ mahādevi siddhayogaistu sevitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In the forest, in the vicinity of that Lord, there is the spot of Lakṣmī called Śrīmukha. O great goddess, it is resorted to by persons of perfect mastery in Yoga.

## \|\| 1.130.8 \|\|

*tatra pāśupatāḥ śreṣṭhā mama liṃgārcane ratāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ caiva nivāsārthaṃ taddevyā nirmitaṃ vanam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Excellent Pāśupatas are engaged in the adoration of my Liṅga there. It is as a place of their habitation that the forest has been created by the goddess.

## \|\| 1.130.9 \|\|

*tasya madhye tu suśroṇi liṃgaṃ pūrvamukhaṃ sthitam \|*  
*tasminpāśupatāḥ siddhā aghorādyā maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*anenaiva śarīreṇa gatāste śivamandiram \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. In the centre thereof, O lady of excellent hips, is situated a Liṅga facing east. The great sages, the devotees of Paśupati, beginning with Aghora have become Siddhas therein. They went to Śiva’s place with the present physical body itself.

## \|\| 1.130.10 \|\|

*tatra prābhāsike kṣetre surasiddhaniṣevite \|*  
*rocate me sadā vāsastasminnāyatane śubhe \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva sthānānāmatiramyamatipriyam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Residence for ever in that auspicious shrine in the holy place of Prabhāsa, the abode of Suras and Siddhas, appeals to me very much. It is the most beautiful and most lovable of all holy spots.

## \|\| 1.130.11 \|\|

*tatra pāśupatā devi mama dhyānaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*mama putrāstu te sarve brahmacaryeṇa saṃyutāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O goddess, Pāśupatas are engaged in meditation on me there. All of them are my sons. They observe celibacy.

## \|\| 1.130.12 \|\|

*dāntāḥ śāṃtā jitakrodhā brāhmaṇāste tapasvinaḥ \|*  
*talliṃgasya prabhāvena siddhiṃ te paramāṃ gatāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. They have subdued their sense-organs. They are quiescent. They have conquered anger. Those Brāhmaṇas are performers of penance. By the power of that Liṅga, they have attained great Siddhis.

## \|\| 1.130.13 \|\|

*tasmāttaṃ pūjayennityaṃ kṣetravāsī dvijottamaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Hence, an excellent Brāhmaṇa resident of that holy spot, should always adore that deity.

## \|\| 1.130.14-17 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*bhagavandevadeveśa saṃsārārṇavatāraka \|*  
*prabhāse tu mahākṣetre tvadīyavratacāriṇām \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sthānaṃ teṣāṃ mahatpuṇyaṃ yogaṃ pāśupataṃ tathā \|*  
*kathayasva prasādena liṃgamāhātmyamuttamam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*kimādināma devasya kathaṃ pūjyo narottamaiḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ pāśupatāstatra sadehāḥ svargamāgatāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*etatkathaya deveśa dayāṃ kṛtvā mama prabho \|\| 17 \|\|*

The Devī said:

14-17. O Lord, O Lord of the chiefs of Devas, O redeemer from the ocean of worldly existence, have mercy on me and narrate to me details of the observers of holy vows in that highly meritorious shrine pertaining to you, the Pāśupata Yoga, the excellent greatness of the Liṅga, the ancient name of the deity and how it is to be worshipped by excellent men and how Pāśupatas attained heaven along with their physical bodies.

## \|\| 1.130.18-20 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*yastvayā pṛchyate bhadre yogaḥ pāśupato mahān \|*  
*teṣāṃ caiva prabhāvo yastathā liṃgasya suvrate \|\| 18 \|\|*

*anādīśasya devasya ādināma mahāprabhe \|*  
*tasmiṃlliṃge tu ye devi madīyavratamāśritāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ciraṃ niyogaṃ suśroṇi vrataṃ pāśupataṃ mahat \|*  
*dhārayaṃti yathoktaṃ tu mama vismayakārakam \|*  
*teṣāmanugrahārthāya mama cittaṃ pradhāvati \|\| 20 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

18-20. O fair lady, the great Yoga of Pāśupata is being enquired by you, so also, O lady of excellent vows, the power of the Liṅga as well as that of those who have adopted my Vrata in that Liṅga, O goddess. O lady of great refulgence, the primordial name of the Lord having no beginning is also being asked by you. O lady of excellent buttocks, the Pāśupata Vrata is great and its duration is very long. These devotees who observe this Vrata in the manner as has been mentioned, cause wonder unto me as well. My mind yearns (and is very eager) to bless them.

## \|\| 1.130.21 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*harasya vacanaṃ śrutvā devī vismayamāgatā \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ viprāḥ sarvalokapatiṃ patim \|\| 21 \|\|*

Sūta said:

21\. O Brāhmaṇas, the goddess became highly surprised on hearing the words of Hara. She spoke these words to her husband, the Lord of all the worlds.

## \|\| 1.130.22 \|\|

*mamāpi kautukaṃ deva kimakārṣīttato bhavān \|*  
*tadbrūhi me mahādeva yadyahaṃ tava vallabhā \|\| 22 \|\|*

The Devī said:

22\. O Lord, I too have earnestness and curiosity (to know) what your holiness did then? O great god, if I am your beloved, do tell it to me.

## \|\| 1.130.23 \|\|

*tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā mahādevo jagāda tām \|*  
*śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi mama bhaktaviceṣṭitam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. On hearing her words, Mahādeva spoke to her: “Listen, O goddess, I shall explain the activities of my devotees.”

## \|\| 1.130.24 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā caiva taponiṣṭhāṃ teṣāmādyaḥ sureśvaraḥ \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ devaḥ praṇatānpārśvataḥ sthitān \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. On seeing their steadfast adherence to penance, the first Lord of Suras spoke these words to the devotees (who were) standing at the sides with bowed heads.

## \|\| 1.130.25 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*gaccha śīghraṃ nandikeśa yatra te mama putrakāḥ \|*  
*caraṃti ca vrataṃ ghoraṃ madīyaṃ cātiduṣkaram \|\| 25 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

25\. O Nandikeśa, do hurry to that place where my sons (devotees) perform my severe and elaborate Vrata which is very difficult to be performed (by ordinary persons).

## \|\| 1.130.26 \|\|

*tatkṣetrasya prabhāvena bhaktyā ca mama nityaśaḥ \|*  
*tena te munayaḥ siddhāḥ svaśarīreṇa suvratāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. By the power of that holy spot as well as of their constant devotion to me, those sages of excellent holy vows have achieved supernatural powers in their own physical forms.

## \|\| 1.130.27 \|\|

*tasmānmadvacanānnandingaccha prābhāsikaṃ śubham \|*  
*āmantraya tvaṃ tānsarvānkailāsaṃ śīghramānaya \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Hence, O Nandin, do go to that splendid holy spot of Prabhāsa at my behest and invite them all on my behalf. Do bring them to Kailāsa quickly.

## \|\| 1.130.28 \|\|

*idaṃ padmaṃ gṛhāṇa tvaṃ sanālaṃ kalikojjvalam \|*  
*liṃgasya mūrdhni dattvedaṃ padmanālamihānaya \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Take this refulgent lotus bud along with its stalk. Offer this bud (flower) on the top of the Liṅga and bring only this stalk here.

## \|\| 1.130.29 \|\|

*muktastadā sa vai nandī devadevena śaṃbhunā \|*  
*kailāsanilayāttasmātprabhāsaṃ kṣetramāgataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Dispatched thus by Śaṃbhu, the Lord of Devas, Nandin went to the Prabhāsa Kṣetra from the Kailāsa resort.

## \|\| 1.130.30 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā caiva punarliṅgaṃ devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā tāṃścaiva yogīndrānparaṃ vismayamāgataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. On seeing the Liṅga of the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas as well as those leading Yogins, he became overwhelmed with great surprise.

## \|\| 1.130.31 \|\|

*keciddhyānaratāstatra kecidyogaṃ samāśritāḥ \|*  
*kecidvyākhyāṃ prakurvanti vicāramapi cāpare \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. There some of them were engaged in meditation. Some had resorted to the practice of Yoga. Some explained the texts and others were pondering or conducting discourses.

## \|\| 1.130.32 \|\|

*kurvantyanye liṃgapūjāṃ praṇāmaṃ ca tathā'pare \|*  
*pradakṣiṇaṃ prakurvanti sāṣṭāṃgaṃ praṇamanti ca \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Others were adoring the Liṅga. Still others were paying obeisance to it. Some were circumambulating and prostrating before the Liṅga with the eight limbs (touching the ground).

## \|\| 1.130.33 \|\|

*kecitstutiṃ prakurvanti bhāvayajñaistathā pare \|*  
*kecitpūjāṃ ca kurvanti ahiṃsākusumaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Some were eulogizing with Bhāvayajña (Yajña offered mentally), Some were worshipping by means of splendid flowers in the form of non-injury.

## \|\| 1.130.34 \|\|

*bhasmasnānaṃ prakurvaṃti gaṇḍukaiḥ snāpayanti ca \|*  
*evaṃ vyākulatāṃ yātaṃ tapasvigaṇamaṇḍalam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Some had Bhasma Snāna (bath by means of holy ash smeared over the body). Others were having bath with Gaṇḍukas (?) In this manner the assemblage of the sages was engaged in feverish activity.

## \|\| 1.130.35 \|\|

*tattādṛśamathālokya nandī vismayamāgataḥ \|*  
*cintayāmāsa manasā sarvaṃ teṣāṃ nirīkṣya ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On seeing them in such a state and minutely observing everything pertaining to them, Nandin reflected thus mentally.

## \|\| 1.130.36-37 \|\|

*āgato'hamimaṃ deśaṃ na kaścinmāṃ nirīkṣate \|*  
*na kenacidahaṃ pṛṣṭo'bhyāgataḥ kutra kasya ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

*ahaṃkārāvṛtāḥ sarve na vadanti ca māṃ kvacit \|*  
*evaṃ manasi saṃdhāya liṃgapārśvamupāgataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. ‘I have come to this region. None takes cognisance of me. I have not been asked by anyone. ‘Where have you come from’? Whose guest are you? All of these are full of haughtiness. They never care to talk to me.’ After thinking thus he approached the Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.130.38 \|\|

*dattaṃ liṃgasya tatpadmanālaṃ chittvā tu nandinā \|*  
*arcayitvā tu tannandī liṃgaṃ pāśupateśvaram \|*  
*nālaṃ gṛhītvā yatnena ṛṣīnvacanamabravīt \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The flower was separated by cutting away the stalk and offered to the Liṅga by Nandin. After adoring the Liṅga of Paśupati, Lord Nandin carefully took up the stalk and spoke to the sages.

## \|\| 1.130.39 \|\|

*nandikeśvara uvāca \|*  
*śāsanāddevadevasya bhavatāṃ pārśvamāgataḥ \|*  
*ājñāpayati deveśastapasvigaṇamaṇḍalam \|\| 39 \|\|*

Nandikeśvara said:

39\. I have come to the vicinity of your honours at the bidding of the Lord of Devas. The Lord of Devas commands the assembly of the groups of sages.

## \|\| 1.130.40 \|\|

*yuṣmābhistatra gantavyaṃ yatra devaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*yuṣmānsarvānsamādāya gamiṣyāmi bhavālayam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. “All of you should go to that place where the eternal Lord is present. I shall go to the abode of Lord Bhava taking you all with me. Get up quickly. We shall go to Kailāsa, the most excellent one among mountains.”

## \|\| 1.130.41 \|\|

*uttiṣṭhatāśu gacchāmaḥ kailāsaṃ parvatottamam \|*  
*tūṣṇīṃbhūtāstataḥ sarve procuste saṃjñayā dvijāḥ \|*  
*gamyatāmagrato nandinpaścādeṣyāmahe vayam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. All those Brāhmaṇas remained silent. They made gestures indicating “Nandin, you may go ahead. We shall come afterwards”.

## \|\| 1.130.42 \|\|

*evamuktastu munibhirnandī śīghrataraṃ gataḥ \|*  
*kathayāmāsa tatsarvaṃ kupitenāntarātmanā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. On being intimated thus, Nandin hastened back. With his inner soul burning with rage, he reported everything (to the Lord).

## \|\| 1.130.43 \|\|

*nandikeśvara uvāca \|*  
*deva tatra gato'haṃ vai yatra te yoginaḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*santoṣito na caivāhaṃ kenacittatra saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

Nandikeśvara said:

43\. O Lord, I had been to that place where those Yogins stayed. Though I waited there, I was not welcomed by anyone.

## \|\| 1.130.44 \|\|

*na māṃ deva nirīkṣante nālapaṃti kathaṃcana \|*  
*padmaṃ tatra mayā deva sthāpitaṃ liṃga mūrdhani \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. O Lord, none of them even looked at me nor they spoke to me. O Lord, the lotus flower was placed by me on the top of the Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.130.45 \|\|

*uktaṃ deva mayā teṣāṃ yogīndrāṇāṃ maheśvara \|*  
*ājñaptā devadevena ihāgacchata mā ciram \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O Lord Maheśvara, I informed the leading Yogins: “You have been commanded by the Lord of Devas: ‘Come here. Do not delay’.”

## \|\| 1.130.46 \|\|

*etacchrutvā vacaḥ svāminsarve tatra maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*āgamiṣyāma iti vai pṛṣṭhato gaccha mā ciram \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. On hearing this, O Lord, those great sages said (intimated by gestures): “You go, ḍo not delay. We shall come close behind.”

## \|\| 1.130.47 \|\|

*ityukte taistathā deva ahaṃ śīghramihāgataḥ \|*  
*śṛṇu cemaṃ gṛhāṇa tvaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ kuru me prabho \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O Lord, when this was intimated I came here quickly. Do take this stalk, O my Lord, be pleased to do (as you deem fit).

## \|\| 1.130.48 \|\|

*ekaṃ me saṃśayaṃ deva cchettumarhasi sāṃpratam \|*  
*mayā vinā mahādeva āgamiṣyaṃti te katham \|*  
*saṃśayo me mahādeva kathayasva maheśvara \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Here is a doubt of mine. It behoves you to dispel it now. O Mahādeva, how can they come without me. O Mahādeva, O Maheśvara, this is my doubt. Do tell me.

## \|\| 1.130.49 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu naṃdinyathāścaryaṃ teṣāṃ vai bhāvitātmanām \|*  
*na dṛśyanta ime siddhā māṃ muktvā'nyaiḥ surairapi \|\| 49 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

49\. Listen, O Nandin, this is the mystery regarding those sages of purified souls. These Siddhas cannot be seen by others, even by Suras, barring me.

## \|\| 1.130.50 \|\|

*madbhāvabhāvitāste vai yogaṃ viṃdaṃti śāṃkaram \|*  
*paśyaitatkautukaṃ naṃdindarśayāmi tavādhunā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. They have been sanctified by their devotion to me. They know the Yoga pertaining to Śaṅkara. Note this wonderful thing, O Nandin. I shall show it to you now.

## \|\| 1.130.51 \|\|

*ānītaṃ yattvayā nālaṃ tasminnāle tu sūkṣmavat \|*  
*praviśya cāgatāḥ sarve yogaiśvaryabalena ca \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. You see the stalk brought by you here. They have penetrated it in a subtle form by means of the power of their Yogic achievement.

## \|\| 1.130.52 \|\|

*evamuktastadā naṃdī vismayotphullalocanaḥ \|*  
*apaśyannālamadhyasthānmaharṣīnparamāṇuvat \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. On being told thus then, Nandin was wonder-struck and his eyes beamed. He saw the great sages stationed in the centre of the stalk like atoms.

## \|\| 1.130.53 \|\|

*yathārkaraśmimadhyasthā dṛśyante paramāṇavaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ tannālamadhyasthā dṛśyaṃta ṛṣayaḥ pṛthak \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Just as minute dust particles are seen in the rays of the sun, so also the sages were severally seen in the centre of the stalk.

## \|\| 1.130.54 \|\|

*evaṃ dṛṣṭvā tadā naṃdī vismayotphullalocanaḥ \|*  
*āścaryaṃ paramaṃ gatvā kiñcinnevābravītpunaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. On seeing thus, the eyes of Nandin sparkled with wonder. In such a great state of wonderment he did not utter anything.

## \|\| 1.130.55 \|\|

*evaṃ tatkautukaṃ dṛṣṭvā devī vacanamabravīt \|*  
*kiṃ dṛśyate mahādeva hṛṣṭaḥ kasmānmaheśvara \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. On noticing this curious thing the goddess spoke these words: “O great Lord, what is seen? O Maheśvara, why are you so elated with joy?”

## \|\| 1.130.56 \|\|

*ityukte vacane devyā provācedaṃ maheśvaraḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. As these words were uttered by the goddess Maheśvara spoke thus:

## \|\| 1.130.57 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*yogayuktā mahātmāno yoge pāśupate sthitāḥ \|*  
*ete māṃ ca samārādhya prabhāsakṣetravāsinam \|*  
*īdṛśīṃ siddhimāpannāḥ svacchaṃdagaticāriṇaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

57\. These noble souls are fully endowed with Yogic power. They are engaged in the Yoga pertaining to Paśupati. They have propitiated me stationed in the Prabhāsa Kṣetra and so have attained such spiritual powers. They have the power to go anywhere as they please.

## \|\| 1.130.58 \|\|

*ityuktavati deveśa ṛṣayaste mahāprabhāḥ \|*  
*padmanālādviniḥsṛtya sarve vai yogamāyayā \|*  
*pradakṣiṇāṃ prakurvaṃti devaṃ devyā bahiṣkṛtam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. When the Lord of Devas said thus, those sages of great splendour came out of the lotus stalk by means of Yogic Māyā. They circumambulated the Lord who stood away from the goddess.

## \|\| 1.130.59 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*kimarthaṃ māṃ na paśyaṃti durācārā ime dvijāḥ \|*  
*vismayo'yaṃ mahādeva kathayasva prasādataḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

The goddess said:

59\. Why don’t these Brāhmaṇas of evil conduct look at me? This is surprising O Mahādeva, kindly do explain.

## \|\| 1.130.60-63 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*prakṛtitvānna paśyaṃti siddhā hyete mahātapāḥ \|*  
*evamuktā tu girijā devedevena śūlinā \|\| 60 \|\|*

*cukopa teṣāṃ suśroṇī śaśāpa krodhitānanā \|*  
*strīlaulyena durācārā nāśameṣyatha garviṇaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*rājapratigrahāsaktā vṛttyā devārcane ratāḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyatha kalau prāpte liṃgadravyopajīvinaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*veśyāsaktāśca saṃbhrāṃtā sarvalokabahiṣkṛtāḥ \|*  
*devadravyavināśāya bhaviṣyatha kalau yuge \|\| 63 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

60-6la. These sages of great penance have great spiritual powers. They do not look at you because you are the Prakṛti.

On being told thus by the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas, the Daughter of the Mountain became furious. The lady of excellent buttocks with her anger expressed on the face, imprecated them:

61b-63. “O haughty men of evil conduct, you will face destruction due to infatuation for women. At the advent of Kali Age, you will become covetous of gifts from kings. You will be engaged in worshipping the Lord as means of living. You will be maintaining yourself by the money belonging to the Liṅga. In Kali Yuga, you will become fondly attached to prostitutes. You will become confused and boycotted by all the people as a result of the destruction of the property of the Lord (temple).”

## \|\| 1.130.64 \|\|

*iti datte tadā śāpa ṛṣīṇāṃ ca mahātmanām \|*  
*gaurīṃ prasādayāmāsuste ca sarve sureśvarāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. When this curse was pronounced upon the noble-souled sages, all the chiefs of Suras propitiated Gaurī.

## \|\| 1.130.65 \|\|

*devadevasya vacanātprasannā sā'bhavatpunaḥ \|*  
*nālaṃ devo'pi saṃgṛhya dakṣiṇāśāṃ samākṣipat \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. At the instance of the Lord of Devas, she became pleased once again. The Lord took up the stalk and threw it to the southern quarter.

## \|\| 1.130.66 \|\|

*patitaṃ tacca vai nālaṃ prabhāsakṣetramadhyataḥ \|*  
*tadeva liṃgaṃ saṃjātaṃ mahānāleti viśrutam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. That stalk fell in the middle of the Prabhāsa Kṣetra. That itself became a Liṅga well known as Mahānala.

## \|\| 1.130.67 \|\|

*kalau yuge ca saṃprāpte taddhruveśvarasaṃjñitam \|*  
*saṃsthitaṃ cottareśāne tasmātpāśupateśvarāt \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. At the advent of Kali Age, it came to be called Dhruveśvara. It is stationed to the north-east of Pāśupateśvara.

## \|\| 1.130.68 \|\|

*purā'nādīśanāmeti paścātpāśupateśvaraḥ \|*  
*prabhāse tu mahākṣetre sthitaḥ pātakanāśanaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Earlier it was known by the name Anādīśa and afterwards as Pāśupateśvara. It thus stationed itself as the destroyer of sins in the great holy spot of Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.130.69 \|\|

*idaṃ sthānaṃ paraṃ śreṣṭhaṃ mama vrataniṣevaṇam \|*  
*idaṃ liṃgaṃ paraṃ brahma anādīśeti saṃjñitam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. This holy spot of mine is excellent for the purpose of observing my Vrata. This Liṅga termed Anādīśa is the great Brahman.

## \|\| 1.130.70 \|\|

*atra siddhiśca muktiśca brāhmaṇānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*anenaiva śarīreṇa ṣaḍbhirmāsastu siddhyati \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. There is no doubt about it that Brāhmaṇas will attain Siddhi and Mukti (liberation) here. They will attain salvation in six months with the same body.

## \|\| 1.130.71 \|\|

*saṃsārasya vimokṣārthamidaṃ liṃgaṃ tu dṛśyatām \|*  
*durlabhaṃ sarvalokānāmidaṃ mokṣapradaṃ param \|*  
*idaṃ pāśupataṃ jñānamasmiṃlliṃge pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. May this Liṅga be visited for effecting liberation from the worldly existence. It is of difficult access unto ordinary people. It grants salvation. The mystic knowledge of Pāśupata is well established in this Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.130.72 \|\|

*yaścainaṃ pūjayedbhaktyā māghe māsi niraṃtaram \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ vai kratūnāṃ ca dānānāṃ labhate phalam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. He who devoutly worships this throughout the month of Māgha, attains the merit of performing all Kratus (sacrifices) and offering holy gifts.

## \|\| 1.130.73 \|\|

*hiraṇyaṃ tatra dātavyaṃ samyagyātrāphalepsubhiḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Gold should be offered there by those who are desirous of getting the full benefit of a perfect pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.130.74 \|\|

*ityetatkathitaṃ devi māhātmyaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*paśupāśavimokṣārthaṃ samyakpāśupateśvaram \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Thus, O goddess, the sin-destroying greatness of Pāśupateśvara has been described duly for the sake of the liberation from the bondage of being a Paśu.

## \|\| 1.130.75 \|\|

*caturṇāmapi varṇānāṃ pūjyo brāhmaṇa ucyate \|*  
*tasya caivādhikāro'sti cāsminpāśupateśvare \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. It is said that Brāhmaṇa is the most worthy of adoration among all the castes. Only he is authorised in the worship of Pāśupateśvara.

## \|\| 1.130.76 \|\|

*yaddevatānāṃ prathamaṃ pavitraṃ viśvavrataṃ pāśupataṃ babhūva \|*  
*ayaṃ panthā naiṣṭhiko vai mayokto yena devā yāṃti bhuvanāni viśvā \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. This Pāśupata Vrata that has become the first and foremost universal Vrata of all the deities, has been explained by me as the. well established pathway whereby the Devas proceed to all the Bhuvanas (worlds).

## \|\| 1.130.77 \|\|

*surāṃ pītvā gurudārāṃśca gatvā steyaṃ kṛtvā brāhmaṇaṃ cāpi hatvā \|*  
*bhasmacchanno bhasmaśayyāśayāno rudrādhyāyī mucyate pātakebhyaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. A Rudrādhyāyī (one who recites the Vedic Rudra Mantras) covered with holy ash and lying on the bed of holy ash becomes rid of all sins incurred by imbibing liquor, ravishing preceptor’s wife, stealing (gold) and slaying a Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 1.130.78 \|\|

*agnirityādinā bhasma gṛhītvāṃgāni saṃspṛśet \|*  
*gṛhṇīyātsaṃyate cāgnau bhasma tadgṛhavāsinām \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. One should take up the holy ash uttering the Mantra beginning with the word Agni and smear his limbs therewith. Ash should be collected when the fire has cooled down in the abodes of the residents (of the holy spot).

## \|\| 1.130.79 \|\|

*agniriti bhasma vāyuriti bhasma jalamiti bhasma sthalamiti bhasma sarvaṃ ha vā idaṃ bhasmābhavat \|*  
*etāni cakṣūṃṣi nādīkṣitaḥ saṃspṛśet \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Agni became Bhasma (holy ash), Vāyu became Bhasma. Jala (Water) became Bhasma, Sthala (the earth) became Bhasma. Everything became Bhasma. One who is not initiated should not touch these i.e. not smear it over the eyes.

## \|\| 1.130.80-81 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaiśca samādeyaṃ na tu śūdraiḥ kadācana \|*  
*nādhikāro'sti śūdrasya vrate pāśupate sadā \|\| 80 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇeṣvadhikāro'sti vrate pāśupate śubhe \|*  
*brāhmaṇīṃ tanumāsthāya saṃbhavāmi yugeyuge \|\| 81 \|\|*

80-81. It should be collected by Brāhmaṇas and never by Śūdras; a Śūdra is never eligible for the Pāśupata Vrata which is auspicious. I am born in every Yuga adopting the body of a Brāhmaṇa (only Brāhmaṇas are authorized in the auspicious Pāśupata Vrata).

## \|\| 1.130.82 \|\|

*caṇḍālaveśmanyatha vā smaśāne rājñaśca mārgeśvatha vartmamadhye \|*  
*karīṣamadhye niḥsṛtā narādhamāḥ śaivaṃ padaṃ yāṃti na saṃśayo'tra \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. There is no doubt about this that even base men placed in Karīṣa (holy ash) attain the region of Śiva whether it is in the house of a Cāṇḍāla or in a cremation ground, or in royal pathways or in the middle of highway.

## Chapter 131 - Greatness of Dhruveśvara (Dhruva-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.131.1 \|\|

*śrīdevyuvāca \|*  
*yadetadbhavatā proktaṃ nāleśvaramiti śrutam \|*  
*dhruveśvareti talliṃgaṃ kathaṃ vai saṃbabhūva ha \|\| 1 \|\|*

Śrī Devī said:

1\. How did that shrine and Liṅga mentioned by your worship as well-known by the name Nāleśvara become Liṅga Dhruveśvara?

## \|\| 1.131.2 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi dhruveśvaramahodayam \|*  
*yacchrutvā mānavo devi mucyate bhavabaṃdhanāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

2\. Listen, O goddess, I shall explain the greatness of Dhruveśvara, on listening to which a man is released from the bondage of the worldly existence.

## \|\| 1.131.3 \|\|

*uttānapādanṛpateḥ putro'bhūddhruvasaṃjñitaḥ \|*  
*mahātmā jñānasaṃpannaḥ sarvajñaḥ priyadarśanaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. There was a son of a king named Uttānapāda. He was called Dhruva. He was a noble soul richly endowed with perfect knowledge. He was omniscient and had a pleasant appearance.

## \|\| 1.131.4 \|\|

*sa kadācitsamāsādya prabhāsaṃ kṣetramuttamam \|*  
*tatāpa vipulaṃ devi tapaḥ paramadāruṇam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O goddess, once he came to Prabhāsa, the excellent holy spot. O fair lady, he performed an elaborate and extremely terrible penance.

## \|\| 1.131.5 \|\|

*divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu pratiṣṭhāpya maheśvaram \|*  
*saṃpūjayati sadbhaktyā stauti stotraiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. After installing Maheśvara, he devoutly worshipped him for a period of a thousand years according to the divine reckoning and eulogized with various kinds of hymns and prayers.

## \|\| 1.131.6 \|\|

*tatstotraṃ te pravakṣyāmi yenāhaṃ tuṣṭimāgataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. I shall recite to you that prayer whereby I became delighted.

## \|\| 1.131.7 \|\|

*dhruva uvāca \|*  
*kailāsatuṃgaśikharaṃ pravikampyamānaṃ kailāsaśṛṃgasadṛśena daśānanena \|*  
*yaḥ pādapadmaparipīḍanayā dadhāra taṃ śaṃkaraṃ śaraṇadaṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi \|\| 7 \|\|*

Dhruva said:

\[Dhruva’s Prayer:\]

7\. I seek refuge in Śaṅkara who bestows succour and who, by pressing with his lotus-like feet, steadied the lofty-peaked Kailāsa that was being shaken by the ten-headed Rāvaṇa resembling the peak of Kailāsa.

## \|\| 1.131.8 \|\|

*yenāsurāścāpi danośca putrā vidyādharoragagaṇaiśca vṛtāḥ samagrāḥ \|*  
*saṃyojitā na tu phalaṃ phalamūlamuktāstaṃ śaṃkaraṃ śaraṇadaṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. I seek refuge in Śaṅkara who bestows succour and by whom all Asuras and Dānavas surrounded by the Vidyādharas and groups of Uragas (serpents) were denied the fruit further but rendered free from attachment to the results of their actions, by making them Jīvanmukta (souls free from Saṃsāra while alive).

## \|\| 1.131.9 \|\|

*yasyākhilaṃ jagadidaṃ vaśavarti nityaṃ yo'ṣṭābhireva tanubhirbhuvanāni bhuṃkte \|*  
*yatkāraṇaṃ paramakāraṇakāraṇānāṃ taṃ śaṃkaraṃ śaraṇadaṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. I seek refuge in that Śaṅkara who bestows succour, under whose control the entire visible universe remains forever, who enjoys (makes use of) all the worlds by means of his eight cosmic bodies, and who is the cause of the great causes of all causes.

## \|\| 1.131.10 \|\|

*yaḥ savyapāṇikamalāgranakhena devastatpaṃcamaṃ ca sahasaiva purātiruṣṭaḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṃ śirastaruṇapadmanibhaṃ cakarta taṃ śaṃkaraṃ śaraṇadaṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. I seek refuge in that Śaṅkara who bestows succour and who formerly became extremely angry and cut off the tender lotus-like fifth head of Brahmā by means of the tip of the nail of the lotus-like left hand.

## \|\| 1.131.11 \|\|

*yasya praṇamya caraṇau varadasya bhaktyā śrutvā ca vāgbhiramalābhirataṃdritābhiḥ \|*  
*dīptastamāṃsi nudati svakarairvivasvāṃstaṃ śaṃkaraṃ śaraṇadaṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. I seek refuge in that Śaṅkara who bestows succour. Lord Śaṅkara is the bestower of boons. The blazing Vivasvān (Sun-god) devoutly bows down to his feet and eulogizes with words without impurities and free from lethargy and weariness. Thereby he can dispels darkness by means of his rays.

## \|\| 1.131.12 \|\|

*yaḥ paṭhetstavamidaṃ rucirārthaṃ mānavo dhruvakṛtaṃ niyatātmā \|*  
*viprasaṃsadi sadā śucisiddhaḥ sa prayāti śivalokamanādim \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. A man who restrains himself and always remains pure and perfect, recites, in the assembly of Brāhmaṇas this prayer of sweet import, composed by Dhruva, goes to the beginningless Śivaloka.

## \|\| 1.131.13 \|\|

*tasyaivaṃ stuvato devi tuṣṭo'haṃ bhāvitātmanaḥ \|*  
*pūrṇe varṣasahasrāṃte dhruvasyāha mahātmanaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O goddess, I became pleased with the noble-souled Dhruva of sanctified heart, even as he eulogized thus. When the thousand years were concluded, I spoke to Dhruva:

## \|\| 1.131.14-16 \|\|

*putra tuṣṭo'smi bhadraṃ te jātastvaṃ nirmalo'dhunā \|*  
*divyaṃ dadāmi te cakṣuḥ paśya māṃ vigatajvaraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yacca te manasā kiñcitkāṃkṣitaṃ phalamuttamam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ te pradāsyāmi brūhi śīghraṃ mamāgrataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*brāhmyaṃ vā vaiṣṇavaṃ śākraṃ padamanyatsudurlabham \|*  
*dadāmi nātra saṃdeho bhaktyā saṃprīṇitastava \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. “Dear son, welfare unto you. I am pleased with you. Now you have become free from impurities. I shall give you divine vision. Look at me freed from all ailments.

Whatever excellent benefit has been all along cherished by you mentally, I shall grant unto you. Do tell me quickly.

I have been devoutly propitiated by you. There is no doubt about it. I shall grant you even that inaccessible region whether of Brahmā or Viṣṇu or Śakra or another.”

## \|\| 1.131.17 \|\|

*dhruva uvāca \|*  
*brāhmyaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ māhendraṃ padamāvṛttilakṣaṇam \|*  
*viditaṃ mama tatsarvaṃ manasā'pi na kāmaye \|\| 17 \|\|*

Dhruva said:

17\. It is known to me that the region of Brahmā, of Viṣṇu and of Mahendra is characterized by a return (unto this world therefrom). I do not even mentally covet all these.

## \|\| 1.131.18 \|\|

*yadi tuṣṭo'si me deva bhaktiṃ dehi sunirmalām \|*  
*asmiṃlliṃge sadā vāsaṃ kuru deva vṛṣadhvaja \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. If you are pleased with me, O Lord, do grant me devotion fully free from impurities. O Bull-emblemed One, do stay in this Liṅga always.

## \|\| 1.131.19 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*iti yatprārthitaṃ sarvaṃ taddattaṃ sarvameva hi \|*  
*sthānaṃ ca tasya taddhrauvyaṃ tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam \|\| 19 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

19\. Everything requested thus was granted indeed. His abode was rendered steady and permanent. That is the great region of Viṣṇu (too).

## \|\| 1.131.20 \|\|

*śrāvaṇasya tvamāvāsyāṃ yastalliṃgaṃ prapūjayet \|*  
*āśvayukpaurṇamāsyāṃ vā so'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He who worships that Liṅga on the New-Moon day of the month of Śrāvaṇa or on the Full-Moon day in the month of Aśvayuk, obtains the merit of a horse-sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.131.21 \|\|

*aputro labhate putraṃ dhanārthī labhate dhanam \|*  
*rūpavānsubhago bhogī sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ \|*  
*haṃsayuktavimānena rudraloke mahīyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. A man without a son gets a son. One who seeks wealth obtains wealth. He becomes handsome and fortunate and enjoys all pleasures. He becomes an expert in all scriptural texts. He goes to Rudraloka by means of an aerial chariot yoked with swans. He is honoured there.

## \|\| 1.131.22 \|\|

*asurasuragaṇānāṃ pūjitasya dhruvasya kathayati kamanīyāṃ kīrtimetāṃ śṛṇoti \|*  
*sakalasukhanidhānarudralokaṃ suśāṃtaḥ suragaṇadanunāthairarcitaṃ yātyanaṃtam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. He who expounds or listens to this beautiful glory of Dhruva honoured by groups of both Asuras and Suras, becomes quiescent and goes to Rudraloka, the eternal abode of all happiness. He is honoured by the leaders of the groups of Suras and Dānavas.

## Chapter 132 - Greatness of Siddhalakṣmī

## \|\| 1.132.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi vaiṣṇavīṃ śaktimuttamām \|*  
*someśādīśadigbhāge nātidūre vyavasthitām \|\| 1 \|\|*

*siddhalakṣmīti vikhyātā hyatra pīṭhādhidevatā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*brahmāṇḍe prathamaṃ pīṭhaṃ yatprabhāsaṃ vyavasthitam \|*  
*tatra devi mahāpīṭhe yoginyo bhūcarāḥ khagāḥ \|*  
*bhairaveṇa same tāstu krīḍante svecchayā priye \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should visit the shrine of the excellent Vaiṣṇavī Śakti. It is situated not very far from Someśa in the north-eastern direction.

Here the presiding deity of the shrine is well-known as Siddhalakṣmī. The first Pīṭha (seat or shrine) in the Cosmic Egg is what is well-established in Prabhāsa; There, O my beloved goddess, in the great Pīṭha, Yoginīs, both Earth-stalkers and Sky-stalkers, sport about as they please, accompanied by Bhairava.

## \|\| 1.132.4 \|\|

*jālaṃdharaṃ mahāpīṭhaṃ kāmarūpaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*śrīmadrudranṛsiṃhaṃ ca caturthaṃ pīṭhamuttamam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Jālandhara (the second great Mahāpīṭha) and Kāmarūpa (are also Pīṭhas). The glorious Rudranṛsiṃha is the fourth excellent Pīṭha.

## \|\| 1.132.5 \|\|

*ratnavīryaṃ mahāpīṭhaṃ kāśmīraṃ pīṭhameva ca \|*  
*etāni devi pīṭhāni yo vetti sa ca mantravit \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. There are also Pīṭhas such as the great Pīṭha Ratnavīrya and Kāśmīra Pīṭha. O goddess, he who is familiar with these Pīṭhas is a Mantravit (one conversant with Mantras).

## \|\| 1.132.6 \|\|

*sarveṣāṃ caiva pīṭhānāmādhāraṃ pīṭhamuttamam \|*  
*saurāṣṭre tu mahādevi nāmnā khyātaṃ mahodayam \|*  
*kāmarūpadharaṃ jñānaṃ yatrādyāpi pravartate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O great goddess, the excellent Pīṭha in Saurāṣṭra, which is the basic support of all the Pīṭhas, is well known by the name Mahodaya. It is the place where the knowledge facilitating the assumption of a form as one pleases, is effective even today.

## \|\| 1.132.7 \|\|

*tatra pīṭhe sthitā devī mahālakṣmīti viśrutā \|*  
*sarvapāpapraśamanī sarvakāryaśubhapradā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In the Pīṭha there, the goddess well-known as Mahālakṣmī is stationed. She suppresses all sins and lends auspiciousness to all activities.

## \|\| 1.132.8 \|\|

*śrīpañcamyāṃ naro yastu pūjayettāṃ vidhānataḥ \|*  
*gandhapuṣpādibhirbhaktyā tasyālakṣmībhayaṃ kutaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Where is the fear due to Alakṣmī (inglorious poverty) unto that man who devoutly worships her on Śrīpañcamī day (the fifth lunar day in the bright half of Māgha) strictly in accordance with the injunctions, with sweet scent, flowers etc.?

## \|\| 1.132.9-11 \|\|

*uttarāṃ diśamāsthāya mahāla kṣmyāstu sannidhau \|*  
*yo japenmantrarājñīṃ tāṃ siddhalakṣmīti viśrutām \|\| 9 \|\|*

*lakṣajāpyavidhānena dīkṣāsnānādipūrvakam \|*  
*daśāṃśahomasaṃyuktaṃ trimadhuśrīphalesubhiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*evaṃ pratyakṣatāṃ yāti tasya lakṣmīrna saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*dadāti vāṃchitāṃ siddhimiha loke paratra ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. A devotee should seat himself in the vicinity of Mahālakṣmī on the northern side (for facing north) and perform the Japa of the queen of Mantras well-known as Siddhalakṣmī. With due observance of initiation, holy ablution etc., the Mantra is to be repeated a hundred thousand times duly. Homas are to be performed by repeating the Mantra ten thousand times with Trimadhu (sugar, honey and ghee), coconuts etc. If it is performed thus there is no doubt about this that Lakṣmī becomes manifest. She will grant desired Siddhis in this world as well as in the other.

## \|\| 1.132.1-2 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi vaiṣṇavīṃ śaktimuttamām \|*  
*someśādīśadigbhāge nātidūre vyavasthitām \|\| 1 \|\|*

*siddhalakṣmīti vikhyātā hyatra pīṭhādhidevatā \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Siddhi (perfect achievement of spiritual power) is within the grasp of that person who devoutly worships her duly on the third, eighth and fourteenth lunar days.

## Chapter 133 - Greatness of Mahākālī

## \|\| 1.133.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tatraiva saṃsthitā devi mahākālīti viśrutā \|*  
*adhaḥ sthite mahāpīṭhe pātālavivarānvite \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sarvaduḥkhapraśamanī sarvaśatrukṣayaṃkarī \|*  
*pūjanīyā vidhānena kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ mahāniśi \|*  
*gandhaiḥ puṣpaistathā dhūpaiḥ kravyairbalibhireva ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*phalatṛtīyāṃ nārī ca kuryādvai tatra bhāvitā \|*  
*varṣamekaṃ site pakṣe devīṃ pūjya vidhānataḥ \|*  
*phalāni brāhmaṇe deyānyeva nūnaṃ vidhānataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. O goddess, the deity well-known as Mahākālī is stationed there itself in the crevasse of the nether worlds on the great Pīṭha situated beneath.

She subdues all miseries. She destroys all enemies. She should be adored duly at midnight on the eighth day of dark half, with sweet scents, flowers, incense, Kravya (raw meat) and oblations.

A woman devotee should perform the worship with Phalatraya (three types of fruits), remaining pure in person. For a year during bright halves of the months, she should worship the goddess in accordance with the injunctions. The fruits should, of course, be given away to a Brāhmaṇa duly.

## \|\| 1.133.4-5 \|\|

*etāni varjayennakte hyannāni surasundari \|*  
*niṣpāvā āḍhakī mudgā māṣāścaiva kulitthakāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*masūrā rājamāṣāśca godhūmāstripuṭāstathā \|*  
*caṇakā vartalā vāpi makuṣṭhāścaivamādayaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. O beautiful lady of Suras, the following grains and lentils should be avoided at night: Niṣpāva, Āḍhakī, Mudga, Māṣa, Kulitthaka, Masūra, Rājamāṣa, Godhūma, Tripuṭa, Caṇaka, Vartala, Makuṣṭha and others.

## \|\| 1.133.6 \|\|

*na bhakṣyāstāvatte devi yāvadgaurīvrataṃ caret \|*  
*tasyāḥ puṇyaphalaṃ vakṣye kathyamānaṃ śṛṇuṣva me \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O goddess, these should not be eaten as long as Gaurīvrata is being performed. I shall mention the meritorious fruit thereof. Listen to it even as it is being narrated.

## \|\| 1.133.7 \|\|

*dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ gṛhe tasyā na kadācitkṣayaṃ vrajet \|*  
*duḥkhitā durbhagā dīnā sapta janmāni no bhavet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Neither wealth nor grains shall become exhausted in her house. For seven successive births that woman shall never be miserable, unlucky or distressed.

## \|\| 1.133.8 \|\|

*mahākālīvrataṃ proktaṃ devyā māhātmyasaṃyutam \|*  
*kṛtaṃ pātakanāśāya sarvakāmasamṛddhaye \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The Vrata pertaining to Goddess Mahākālī has been described along with its greatness. If it is performed, it is conducive to the destruction of sins and the fulfilment of all desires.

## \|\| 1.133.9 \|\|

*evaṃ devi samākhyātaṃ mahākālīmahodayam \|*  
*kṣetrapīṭhaṃ mahādevi mantrasiddhipradāyakam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thus, O goddess, the greatness of Mahākālī has been extolled. O great goddess, the Pīṭha of the holy spot gives success in the employment of Mantras.

## \|\| 1.133.10 \|\|

*āśvayukchuklapakṣe tu navamyāṃ tatra jāgṛyāt \|*  
*pīṭhe pūjābaliṃ dattvā mantraṃ kāmaṃ japanniśi \|*  
*saumyacittaḥ samāpnoti vāṃchitāṃ siddhimuttamām \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On the ninth day in the bright half of Aśvayuj, a devotee should keep vigil at night. A devotee who offers oblations in the form of adoration, should recite the Mantra at night at will. He should be gentle in mind. He shall obtain the excellent Siddhi as desired.

## Chapter 134 - Greatness of Puṣkarāvartakā (Puṣkara-āvartakā)

## \|\| 1.134.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi puṣkarāvartakāṃ nadīm \|*  
*brahmakuṃḍāduttarato nātidūre vyavasthitām \|\| 1 \|\|*

*purā yajñe vartamāne somasya tu mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*brahmā suragaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ prabhāsaṃ kṣetramāgataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*somanāthapratiṣṭhārthamṛkṣarājanimaṃtritaḥ \|*  
*pratijñātaṃ purā tena brahmaṇā lokakāriṇā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yāvatsthāsyāmyahaṃ martye kasmiṃścitkāraṇāṃtare \|*  
*tāvatsaṃdhyātrayaṃ vaṃdyaṃ nityameva tripuṣkare \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to River Puṣkarāvartakā situated not far from Brahmakuṇḍa, on the northern side.

Formerly, as the Yajña of the noble-souled Soma was going on, Brahmā had come to Prabhāsa Kṣetra along with groups of Suras.

He had been invited by Ṛkṣarāja (the Moon, Soma) for the purpose of installing Somanātha as promised earlier by Brahmā, the creator of the worlds: “As long as I continue to stay in the mortal world for any reason, obeisance should be offered thrice a day (during the periods of junction) in Tripuṣkara.”

## \|\| 1.134.5 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu lagnakāla upasthite \|*  
*ādiṣṭaṃ śobhanaṃ kālaṃ brāhmaṇairdaivacintakaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In the meantime, the auspicious hour had come. The period was recommended as the auspicious hour by the Brāhmaṇas thinking about deities.

## \|\| 1.134.6 \|\|

*tatastaṃ prasthitaṃ jñātvā puṣkare tu pitāmaham \|*  
*saṃdhyārthaṃ rātrinātho vai vākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On coming to know that Pitāmaha was about to proceed ahead towards Puṣkara for the purpose of Sandhyā (prayer at the prescribed hours of junction) Rātrinātha (the Lord of night namely Soma, Moon) said these words:

## \|\| 1.134.7 \|\|

*daivajñaiḥ kalitaḥ kāla eṣa eva śubhodayaḥ \|*  
*yathā kālātyayo na syāttathā nītirvidhīyatām \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. “This period alone is reckoned as the auspicious hour by persons conversant with astrology. May the arrangement be so made as to avoid lapse of the auspicious time.”

## \|\| 1.134.8 \|\|

*taṃ jñātvā sāṃprataṃ kālaṃ brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*manasā cintayāmāsa puṣkarāṇi samāhitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Having come to know that the time was propitious, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, concentrated his mind and thought of the Puṣkaras mentally.

## \|\| 1.134.9 \|\|

*tāni vai smṛtamātrāṇi brahmaṇā varavarṇini \|*  
*prādurbhūtāni tatraiva nadyāstīre suśobhane \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O auspicious and splendid lady of excellent complexion, on being remembered by Brahmā, those (Puṣkaras) manifested themselves immediately on the refulgent banks of the river.

## \|\| 1.134.10 \|\|

*āvartāstatra sañjātā jyeṣṭhamadhyakanīyasaḥ \|*  
*atha nāmākarottasyā brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. There arose whirlpools (in the river) \[i.e., āvarta, also āvartaka\] of three sizes, large, medium and small. Then, Brahmā the grandfather of the worlds, gave her (the river) a name.

## \|\| 1.134.11-13 \|\|

*puṣkarāvartakā nāmnā adyaprabhṛti śobhanā \|*  
*nadī prayāsyate loke khyātiṃ mama prasādataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*atra snātvā naro bhaktyā tarpayiṣyati yaḥ pitṝn \|*  
*tripuṣkarasamaṃ puṇyaṃ lapsyate sa tathepsitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*śrāvaṇe śuklapakṣasya tṛtīyāyāṃ narottamaḥ \|*  
*yaḥ pitṝṃstarpayettatra tṛptiḥ kalpāyutaṃ bhavet \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. “With my favour, the splendid river will become well-known from today by the name Puṣkarāvartakā. A man who takes his holy bath here and offers libation to the Pitṛs with devotion, will attain what is desired and the merit befitting the Tripuṣkara. If an excellent man offers libation there on the third lunar day in the bright half of the month of Śrāvaṇa, the satisfaction (of the Pitṛs) shall last for ten thousand Kalpas.”

## Chapter 135 - Greatness of Śītalāgaurī (Śītalā-gaurī)

## \|\| 1.135.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tatraiva saṃsthitāṃ paśyeddevīṃ duḥkhāṃtakāriṇīm \|*  
*śītaleti purā khyātā yuge dvāparasaṃjñite \|*  
*kalau punaḥ samākhyātāṃ kaliduḥkhāntakāriṇīm \|\| 1 \|\|*

*śītalaṃ kurute dehaṃ bālānāṃ rogavarjitam \|*  
*pūjitā bhaktibhāvena tena sā śītalā smṛtā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*visphoṭānāṃ praśāṃtyarthaṃ bālānāṃ caiva kāraṇāt \|*  
*mānena māpitānkṛtvā masūrāṃstatra kuṭṭayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. A pilgrim should visit the misery-quelling goddess stationed there itself. Earlier she was well-known as Śītalā in Dvāpara Yuga. But in Kali Age she is famous as Kali-duḥkhāntakāriṇī (she who quells miseries of Kali Age).

If adored with ardent devotion, she will make the bodies of children cool (Śītala) and free from ailments. Hence she is remembered as Śītalā.

In order to dispel swellings (boils) in the case of children, Masūras should be properly measured and pounded.

## \|\| 1.135.4 \|\|

*śītalāpurato dattvā bālāḥ santu nirāmayāḥ \|*  
*visphoṭacarcikādīnāṃ vātādīnāṃ śamo bhavet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The same is placed before Śītalā uttering, “May the children be free from ailments”. Thereby there shall be suppression of Visphoṭa (swelling, boils), Carcikā (small boils) etc. as well as Vāta (rheumatic complaints) etc.

## \|\| 1.135.5 \|\|

*śrāddhaṃ tatraiva kurvīta brāhmaṇāṃstatra bhojayet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Śrāddha should be performed there and Brāhmaṇas should be fed.

## \|\| 1.135.6 \|\|

*karpūraṃ kusumaṃ caiva mṛganābhiṃ sucandanam \|*  
*puṣpāṇi ca sugandhāni naivedyaṃ ghṛtapāyasam \|*  
*nivedya devyai tatsarvaṃ daṃpatyoḥ paridhāpayet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Camphor, flowers, musk, excellent sandal-paste, saffron and sweet scents should be offered. The food offering shall be pudding made with ghee. After dedicating it to the goddess, everything should be given to a couple.

## \|\| 1.135.7 \|\|

*navamyāṃ śuklapakṣe tu mālāṃ vilvamayīṃ śubhām \|*  
*bhaktyā nivedya tāṃ devyai sarvasiddhimavāpnuyāt \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On the ninth day in the bright half a splendid garland of Bilva should be offered to the goddess. Thereby the devotee shall attain all Siddhis.

## Chapter 136 - Greatness of Lomaśeśvara (Lomaśa-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.136.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi lomaśeśvaramuttamam \|*  
*duḥkhāntakāriṇīpūrve dhanuṣāṃ saptake sthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sthāpitaṃ tatra deveśi lomaśena maharṣiṇā \|*  
*guhāmadhye mahāliṃgaṃ tapaḥ kṛtvā suduścaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

*koṭīnāṃ tritayaṃ sārdhamiṃdrādyāḥ svarbhujaḥ priye \|*  
*yadā nāśaṃ gamiṣyaṃti tadā tasya kṣayo dhruvam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the excellent shrine of Lomaśeśvara. It is situated within a distance of seven Dhanus to the east of Duḥkhāntakāriṇī.

O goddess of Devas, a great Liṅga was installed by the great sage Lomaśa in the middle of the cave, after performing a great penance very difficult to be performed.

O my beloved, when the three and a half crores of Heaven-dwellers beginning with Indra perish he too shall perish.

## \|\| 1.136.4 \|\|

*yāvaṃti deharomāṇi indrāstāvanta eva ca \|*  
*kramādindre vinaṣṭe tu tallomapatanaṃ bhavet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Indras are as many as there are hairs on the body. When Indra perishes duly, a hair (of the sage) may fall down.

## \|\| 1.136.5 \|\|

*evamīśaprasādena cirāyurlomaśo'bhavat \|*  
*brahmāṇaḥ ṣaḍvinaśyanti samagrāyuṣi lomaśe \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Thus, with the favour of Īśa, Lomaśa became long-lived. By the time Lomaśa completes his life-span, six Brahmās would have perished.

## \|\| 1.136.6 \|\|

*ya evaṃ pūjayedbhaktyā talliṃgaṃ lomaśārcitam \|*  
*so'pi dīrghāyurāpnoti nirvyādhirnīrujaḥ sukhī \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He who devoutly worships that Liṅga adored by Lomaśa shall also attain long life, happiness and freedom from sickness and sorrow.

## Chapter 137 - Greatness of Kaṅkāla-bhairava

## \|\| 1.137.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tatraiva saṃsthitaṃ paśyetkṣetrapālamanuttamam \|*  
*kaṃkālabhairavaṃnāma bhairaveṇa niyojitam \|*  
*tasya kṣetrasya rakṣārthaṃ prāṇināṃ duṣṭacetasām \|\| 1 \|\|*

*śrāvaṇe śuklapañcamyāmaṣṭamyāmāśvinasya ca \|*  
*yastaṃ pūjayate bhaktyā balipuṣpādibhiḥ kramāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tasya kṣetre nivasataḥ puṣkarasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*nirvighnakārī bhavati tathā rakṣati putravat \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. A pilgrim should visit the excellent Kṣetrapāla stationed there itself, named Kaṅkālabhairava. He was employed by Bhairava for the protection of that holy spot from evil-minded living beings.

If the devotee of noble soul residing in Puṣkara Kṣetra worships that deity devoutly on the fifth lunar day in the bright half of Śrāvaṇa, and on the eighth lunar day of the month of Āśvina, by means of oblations, flowers etc. duly, the deity protects him like his own son and removes all the obstacles.

## Chapter 138 - Greatness of Tṛṇabindvīśvara (Tṛṇabindu-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.138.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tasyaiva paścime bhāge dhanupāṃ pañcake sthitam \|*  
*tṛṇabindvīśvaraṃnāma tīvrabhaktyā pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kṛtvā mahattapo devi tṛṇabiṃdumu nīśvaraḥ \|*  
*māsimāsi kuśāgreṇa jalabiṃduṃ nipīya vai \|\| 2 \|\|*

*saṃvatsarāṇyanekāni evamārādhya ceśvaram \|*  
*saṃprāptaṃ paramāṃ siddhiṃ kṣetre prābhāsike śubhe \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. The deity named Tṛṇabindvīśvara is stationed within a distance of five Dhanus to the west thereof (i. e. of Kaṅkālabhairava). It was installed with perfect devotion, O goddess, after the leading sage Tṛṇabindu had performed an elaborate penance, drinking only a drop of water from the tip of a blade of Darbha every month. Thus he propitiated Īśvara for many years and attained the greatest Siddhi in the Prābhāsika Kṣetra of great refulgence.

## Chapter 139 - Greatness of Citrāditya (Citra-āditya)

## \|\| 1.139.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi citrādityamanuttamam \|*  
*tasyaiva dakṣiṇe bhāge vrahmakuṇḍasamīpataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*mahāprabhāvo deveśi sarvadāridryanāśanaḥ \|*  
*mitro nāma purā devi dharmātmā'bhūddharātale \|*  
*kāyasthaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ nityaṃ bhūtahite rataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tasyāpatyadvayaṃ jajña ṛtukālābhigāminaḥ \|*  
*putraḥ paramatejasvī citronāma varānane \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tathā citrā'bhavatkanyā rūpāḍhyā śīlamaṃḍanā \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the excellent shrine of Citrāditya to the south thereof (i.e. of Tṛṇabindvīśvara) in the vicinity of Brahmakuṇḍa. O goddess of Devas, he has great power. He is the destroyer of all types of poverty.

O goddess, formerly there was a righteous soul named Mitra on the earth He was a Kāyastha, always engaged in the welfare of all living beings.

He used to have close physical intimacy with his wife only during the prescribed days after menstruation. He had two children. O lady of excellent countenance, one was a boy of great refulgence named Citra. He had a daughter called Citrā who was a girl of great beauty and good habits that embellished her.

## \|\| 1.139.5 \|\|

*ābhyāṃ tu jātamātrābhyāṃ mitraḥ pañcatvameyivān \|*  
*atha tasya varā bhāryā saha tenāgnimāviśat \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Immediately after the birth of these two, Mitra met with his death. His excellent wife entered the funeral pyre along with him.

## \|\| 1.139.6 \|\|

*atha tau bālakau dīnāvṛṣibhiḥ paripālitau \|*  
*vṛddhiṃ gatau mahāraṇye bālāveva sthitau vrate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Those two wretched children were brought up by the sages. They grew up in the great forest engaging themselves in Vratas even while they were yet children.

## \|\| 1.139.7 \|\|

*prabhāsaṃ kṣetramāsādya tapaḥ paramamāsthitau \|*  
*pratiṣṭhāpya mahā devaṃ bhāskaraṃ vāritaskaram \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. They came to Prabhāsa Kṣetra, installed the great deity Bhāskara, the water-thief (evaporator), and performed an elaborate penance.

## \|\| 1.139.8 \|\|

*pūjayāmāsa dharmātmā dhūpamālyānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*vasiṣṭhakathitaiścaiva hyaṣṭaṣaṣṭisamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*nāmabhiḥ sūryadeveśaṃ tuṣṭāva prāñjaliḥ prabhum \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The righteous-souled (Citra) worshipped the deity with incense, garlands and unguent. He joined his palms in veneration and eulogized Lord Sūryadeva by means of the sixty-eight names enumerated by Vasiṣṭha.

## \|\| 1.139.9 \|\|

*citra uvāca \|*  
*praṇamya śirasā devaṃ bhāskaraṃ gaganādhipam \|*  
*ādidevaṃ jagannāthaṃ pāpaghnaṃ roganāśanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

Citra said:

9\. I bow down to Lord Bhāskara, the master of the firmament. He is the primordial Lord, the Lord of the universe, the destroyer of sins and ailments.

## \|\| 1.139.10 \|\|

*sahasrākṣaṃ sahasrāṃśuṃ sahasrakiraṇadyutim \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. (I bow down) to the thousand-rayed, thousand-eyed god with thousand lustrous rays.

Epithets of the Sun-god and his sacred places:

## \|\| 1.139.11 \|\|

*tamahaṃ saṃstaviṣyāmi saṃpṛktaṃ guhyanāmabhiḥ \|*  
*muṃḍīrasvāminaṃ prātargaṃgāsāgarasaṃgame \|*  
*kālapriyaṃ tu madhyāhne yamunātīramāśritam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. I shall eulogize that Lord endowed with secret epithets. At daybreak, he is Muṇḍīra-Svāmin at the confluence of Gaṅgā and the ocean. At midday he is Kālapriya resorting to the banks of Yamunā.

## \|\| 1.139.12 \|\|

*mūlasthānaṃ cāstamane candrabhāgātaṭe sthitam \|*  
*yatra sāṃbaḥ svayaṃ siddha upavāsaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. At dusk he is at Mūlasthāna (modern Multan) on the banks of Candrabhāgā (modern Chinab) where Sāṃba (Kṛṣṇa’s son) engaged himself in holy fast and achieved Siddhi.

## \|\| 1.139.13 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāṃ lohitākṣaṃ gobhilākṣe bṛhanmukham \|*  
*prayāgeṣu pratiṣṭhānaṃ vṛddhādityaṃ mahādyutim \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. (I eulogize) Lohitākṣa at Vārāṇasī, Bṛhanmukha in Gobhilākṣa and the highly lustrous Vṛddhāditya in Pratiṣṭhāna in Prayāga.

## \|\| 1.139.14 \|\|

*koṭyakṣe dvādaśādityaṃ gaṃgādityaṃ caturghaṭe \|*  
*naimiṣe caiva goghne ca bhadraṃ bhadrapuṭe sthitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. (I praise) Dvādaśāditya in Koṭyakṣa, Gaṅgāditya in Caturghaṭa and Naimiṣa and Goghna and Bhadra stationed in Bhadrapuṭa.

## \|\| 1.139.15 \|\|

*jayāyāṃ vijayādityaṃ prabhāse svarṇavetasam \|*  
*kurukṣetre ca sāmaṃtaṃ trimaṃtraṃ ca ilāvṛte \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. (I eulogize) Vijayāditya in Jaya, Svarṇavetasa in Prabhāsa, Sāmanta in Kurukṣetra and Trimantra in Ilāvṛta.

## \|\| 1.139.16 \|\|

*mahendre kramaṇādityamṛṇe siddheśvaraṃ viduḥ \|*  
*kauśāṃbyāṃ padmabodhaṃ ca brahmabāhau divākaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. They know as stationed, Kramaṇāditya in Mahendra, Siddheśvara in Ṛṇa, Padmabodha in Kauśāmbī (Kosam near Allahabad) and Divākara in Brahmabāhu

## \|\| 1.139.17 \|\|

*kedāre caṇḍakāṃtiṃ ca nitye ca timirāpaham \|*  
*gaṃgāmārge śivadvāramādityaṃ bhūpradī pane \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. (I bow to) Caṇḍakānti in Kedāra, Timirāpaha in Nitya, Śivadvāra in Gaṅgā-Mārga and Āditya in Bhūpradīpana.

## \|\| 1.139.18 \|\|

*haṃsaṃ sarasvatītīre viśvāmitraṃ pṛthūdake \|*  
*ujjayinyāṃ naradvīpaṃ siddhāyāmamaladyutim \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. (I bow to) Haṃsa on Sarasvatītīra (the banks of Sarasvatī), Viśvamitra in Pṛthūdaka (Pehoa in Karnal District, Punjab), Naradvīpa in Ujjayinī and Amaladyuti in Siddha.

## \|\| 1.139.19 \|\|

*sūryaṃ kuntīkumāre ca pañcanadyāṃ vibhāvasum \|\| \|*  
*mathurāyāṃ vimalādityaṃ saṃjñādityaṃ tu saṃjñike \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. (I bow to) Sūrya in Kuntīkumāra, Vibhāvasu in Pañcanadī, (Punjab), Vimalāditya in Mathurā and Saṃjñāditya in Saṃjñika.

## \|\| 1.139.20 \|\|

*śrīkaṇṭhe caiva mārtaṇḍaṃ daśārṇe daśakaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*godhane gopatiṃ devaṃ karṇaṃ caiva marusthale \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. (I eulogize) Mārtaṇḍa stationed in Śrīkaṇṭha, Daṃśaka in Daśārṇa (Eastern Malwa), Lord Gopāti in Godhana and Karṇa in Marusthala (Marwar in Rajasthan).

## \|\| 1.139.21 \|\|

*puṣpaṃ devapure caiva keśavārkaṃ tu lohite \|*  
*vaidiśe caiva śārdūlaṃ śoṇe vāruṇavāsinam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. (I eulogize) Puṣpa in Devapura, Keśavārka in Lohita, Śārdūla in Vaidiśa (Vidiśā) and Vāruṇavāsin in Śoṇa.

## \|\| 1.139.22 \|\|

*vardhamāne ca sāṃbākhyaṃ kāmarūpe śubhaṃkaram \|*  
*mihiraṃ kānyakubje ca maṃdāraṃ puṇyavardhane \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. (I eulogize) Sāṃbākhya in Vardhamāna, Śubhaṃkara in Kāmarūpa, Mihira in Kānyakubja and Mandāra in Puṇyavardhana.

## \|\| 1.139.23 \|\|

*gandhāre kṣobhaṇādityaṃ laṃkāyāmamaradyutim \|*  
*karṇādityaṃ ca caṃpāyāṃ prabodhe śubhadarśinam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. (I bow to) Kṣobhaṇāditya in Gandhāra (Kandhar, Afghanistan), Amaradyuti in Laṅkā, Karṇāditya in Campā (Bhagalpur, Bihar) and Śubhadarśin in Prabodha.

## \|\| 1.139.24 \|\|

*dvārā vatyāṃ tu pārvatyaṃ himavante himāpaham \|*  
*mahātejaṃ tu lauhitye amalāṃge ca dhūjaṭim \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. (I bow to) Pārvatya in Dvārāvatī (Dvārkā, Gujarat), Himāpaha in Himavanta, Mahāteja in Lauhitya (Assam) and Dhūrjaṭi in Amalāṅga.

## \|\| 1.139.25 \|\|

*rohike tu kumārākhyaṃ padmāyāṃ padmasaṃbhavam \|*  
*dharmādityaṃ tu lāṭāyāṃ marddake sthaviraṃ viduḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. (I bow to) Kumārākhya (one named Kumāra) in Rohika, Padmasaṃbhava in Padma, Dharmāditya in Lāṭa (South Gujarat) and Sthavira in Mardaka.)

## \|\| 1.139.26 \|\|

*sukhapradaṃ tu kauberyāṃ kosale gopatiṃ tathā \|*  
*kauṃkaṇe tu padmadevaṃ tāpanaṃ vindhyaparvate \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. (I bow to) Sukhaprada in Kauberī, Gopati in Kosala (Oudh), Padmadeva in Koṅkaṇa and Tāpana in Vindhya mountain.

## \|\| 1.139.27 \|\|

*tvaṣṭāraṃ caiva kāśmīre caritre ratnasaṃbhavam \|*  
*puṣkare hemagarbhasthaṃ vidyātsūryaṃ gabhastike \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. (I bow to) Tvaṣṭṛ in Kāśmīra, Ratnasaṃbhava in Caritra, Hemagarbhastha in Puṣkara and Sūrya in Gabhastika.

## \|\| 1.139.28 \|\|

*prakāśāyāṃ tu mujjhālaṃ tīrthagrāme prabhākaram \|*  
*kāṃpilye rillakādityaṃ dhanake dhanavāsinam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. (I bow to) Mujjhāla in Prakāśā, Prabhākara in Tīrthagrāma, Rillakāditya in Kāmpilya (modern Kampil, Farrukhabad District, U.P.) and Dhanavāsin in Dhanaka.

## \|\| 1.139.29 \|\|

*analaṃ narmadātīre sarvatra gamanādhikam \|*  
*aṣṭaṣaṣṭiṃ tu devasya bhāskarasyāmitadyuteḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. (I bow to) Anala on the banks of Narmadā and Gamanādhika everywhere. (Thus the devotee shall repeat) the sixty-eight (shrines) of Lord Bhāskara of unlimited lustre.

## \|\| 1.139.30 \|\|

*prātarutthāya vai nityaṃ śaktimāñchucimānnaraḥ \|*  
*yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. A man who is pure and powerful and gets up early in the morning and recites these or listens to these (names of the Sun-god) is rid of all sins.

## \|\| 1.139.31 \|\|

*rājyārthī labhate rājyaṃ dhanārthī labhate dhanam \|*  
*putrārthī labhate putrānsaukhyārthī labhate sukham \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. One who seeks a kingdom gets a kingdom; one who seeks wealth gets wealth, one who seeks sons gets sons, and one who seeks happiness gets happiness.

## \|\| 1.139.32 \|\|

*rogārto mucyate rogādbaddho mucyeta bandhanāt \|*  
*yānyānprārthayate kāmāṃstāṃstānprāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. One who is distressed due to ailments is rid of ailments; one who is in bondage is released from bondage. Yes, the man attains whatever other things he may desire.

## \|\| 1.139.33 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ ca stuvatastasya citrasya vimalātmanaḥ \|*  
*tatastuṣṭaḥ sahasrāṃśuḥ kālena mahatā vibhuḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

33\. Even as Citra of a soul free from impurities eulogized thus, the Thousand-rayed Lord Sun became pleased with him after a long time.

## \|\| 1.139.34 \|\|

*abravīdvatsa bhadraṃ te varaṃ varaya suvrata \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. He said, “Dear son, welfare unto you, O devotee of excellent holy vows, choose your boon.”

## \|\| 1.139.35 \|\|

*so'bravīdyadi me tuṣṭo bhagavaṃstīkṣṇadīdhiteḥ \|*  
*prauḍhatvaṃ sarvakāryeṣu naya māṃ jñānitāṃ tathā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He said “O Lord of hot, severe, blazing rays, if you are pleased with me give me perfection in all activities and knowership as well”

## \|\| 1.139.36 \|\|

*tattatheti prati jñātaṃ sūryeṇa varavarṇini \|*  
*tataḥ sarvajñatāṃ prāptaścitro mitrakulodbhavaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O lady of excellent complexion, that was duly assented to by the Sun-god. Thereupon, Citra the scion of the family of Mitra, attained omniscience.

## \|\| 1.139.37-39 \|\|

*taṃ jñātvā dharmarājastu buddhyā paramayā yutam \|*  
*ciṃtayāmāsa medhāvī lekha ko'yaṃ bhavedyadi \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tato me sarvasiddhiḥ syānnirvṛtiśca parā bhavet \|*  
*evaṃ ciṃtayatastasya dharmarājasya bhāmini \|\| 38 \|\|*

*agnitīrthe gate citre snā nārthaṃ lavaṇāmbhasi \|*  
*sa tatra praviśanneva nītastu yamakiṃkaraiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. The God of Death, Dharmarāja, came to know that he had been endowed with extremely remarkable intellect. He thought, ‘If this highly intelligent one becomes my writer (Clerk), I will be able to achieve everything and be extremely carefree.’ O beautiful lady, while Dharmarāja was thinking thus, Citra went to Agnitīrtha in the salt ocean for the sake of his daily ablution. Even as he entered it, he was carried off by the servants of Yama.

## \|\| 1.139.40 \|\|

*saśarīro mahādevi yamādeśaparāyaṇaiḥ \|*  
*sa citraguptanāmā'bhūdviśvacāritralekhakaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O great goddess, he was carried off bodily by the servants carrying out the behests of Yama. This Citra came to be known by the name Citragupta. He became the scribe recording the conduct of all mortal beings.

## \|\| 1.139.41 \|\|

*citrādityetināmā'bhūttato loke varānane \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Thereupon, O lady of excellent countenance, the deity came to be known by the name of Citrāditya in the world.

## \|\| 1.139.42 \|\|

*saptamyāṃ niyatāhāro yastaṃ pūjayate naraḥ \|*  
*sapta janmāni dāridryaṃ na duḥkhaṃ tasya jāyate \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. If a man regulates his diet and worships the deity on the seventh lunar day, he will never meet with poverty and misery in the course of seven succeeding births.

## \|\| 1.139.43 \|\|

*tatraiva cāśvo dātavyaḥ sakoṣaṃ khaḍgameva ca \|*  
*hiraṇyaṃ caiva viprāya evaṃ yātrāphalaṃ labhet \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. There itself, the pilgrim should make the gift of a horse along with a sword in a sheath as well as gold to a Brāhmaṇa. Thus the benefit of the pilgrimage will be realized.

## Chapter 140 - Greatness of Citrapathā River

## \|\| 1.140.1-5 \|\|

*tato gacchenmahādevi nadīṃ citrapathāṃ tataḥ \|*  
*brahmakuṇḍasamīpasthāṃ citrādityasya madhyataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yadā ca citraḥ saṃnīto yamadūtaiḥ surapriye \|*  
*saśarīro mahāprājño yamādeśaparāyaṇaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*evaṃ jñātvā tu tatrasthā bhaginī tasya duḥkhitā \|*  
*citrā nadī tato bhūtvā svasā tasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*praviṣṭā sāgare devi anveṣantī ca bāṃdhavam \|*  
*tataścitrapathānāma tasyāścakrurdvijātayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*evaṃ tatra samutpannā sā nadī varavarṇini \|\| 5 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-5. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the river Citrapathā situated in the vicinity of Brahmakuṇḍa in the centre of the shrine Citrāditya.

O beloved goddess of Suras, when the highly intelligent Citra was bodily carried off by the messengers of Yama carrying out his behests, his sister who was there came to know of it. She became extremely miserable. O goddess, the sister of that noble-souled one became the river Citrā and entered the great ocean in search of her kinsman (brother). Brāhmaṇas assigned her the name Citrapathā. It was in this manner, O lady of excellent complexion, that the river came to flow there.

## \|\| 1.140.6 \|\|

*tasyāṃ snātvā naro yastu citrādityaṃ prapaśyati \|*  
*sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yatra devo divākaraḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. A man who takes his holy bath there and visits Citrāditya goes to that great region where Lord Divākara (Sun) is present.

## \|\| 1.140.7 \|\|

*asminkaliyuge devi aṃtardhānaṃ gatā nadī \|*  
*prāvṛṭkāle ca dṛśyeta durlabhaṃ tatra darśanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O goddess, that river has vanished in this Kali Age. She may rarely be seen in rainy season. It is very difficult to see her.

## \|\| 1.140.8 \|\|

*snānaṃ dānaṃ viśeṣeṇa sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Holy ablution and pious gifts offered (there) are specially destructive of sins.

## \|\| 1.140.9-10 \|\|

*bhukto vāpyathavā'bhukto rātrau vā yadi vā divā \|*  
*parvakāle'thavā'kāle pavitro'pyathavā'śuciḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*yadaiva dṛśyate tatra nadī citrapathā priye \|*  
*pramāṇaṃ darśanaṃ tasyā na kālastatra kāraṇam \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. After taking food or before taking food, at night or by day, on festive occasions or at odd hours, whether one is personally clean or not, O beloved, whenever the river is visible she should be viewed. The viewing is authorized. There is no restriction of time.

## \|\| 1.140.11 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā nadīṃ mahādevi pitaraḥ svargasaṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*gāyaṃti tatra sāmāni nṛtyanti ca hasaṃti ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On seeing the river, O great goddess, the Pitṛs stationed in heaven sing Sāman Mantras, dance and laugh.

## \|\| 1.140.12 \|\|

*asmākaṃ vaṃśajaḥ kaścicchrāddhamatra kariṣyati \|*  
*yāvatkalpaṃ tathā'smākaṃ prītimutpādayiṣyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. (They say) ‘If anyone born of our family performs Śrāddha here, he will be causing delight to us as long as the Kalpa lasts.’

## \|\| 1.140.13 \|\|

*evaṃ jñātvā narastatra snānaṃ śrāddhaṃ ca kārayet \|*  
*sarvapāpavināśārthaṃ pitṝṇāṃ prītaye tathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. By realizing this, a man should get a Śrāddha performed there and have his holy bath there for the sake of destroying all sins, and also for the delight of the Pitṛs.

## \|\| 1.140.14 \|\|

*ityetatkathitaṃ devi yathā citrapathā nadī \|*  
*prabhāsakṣetramāsādya saṃsthitā pāpanāśinī \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thus, O goddess, it has been narrated as to how the river Citrapathā reached Prabhāsa and settled here as destroyer of sins.

## Chapter 141 - Greatness of Kapardicintāmaṇi (Kapardi-cintāmaṇi)

## \|\| 1.141.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi kapardī yatra saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*tasyaiva uttare bhāge nātidūre vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*ciṃtitārthaprado devi cintāmaṇirivāparaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to that shrine where Kṛpardin is stationed. It is situated not far therefrom (i.e. Citrapathā river) on the northern side. Like another Cintāmaṇi (wish-yielding philosopher’s stone). O goddess, it bestows the object thought of.

## \|\| 1.141.2 \|\|

*caturthyāṃ taṃ tu deveśi aṃgārakadine punaḥ \|*  
*snāpayitvā tu saṃpūjya naivedyairvividhaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*santarpya vighnarājeśaṃ sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O goddess of Devas, on the fourth lunar day coinciding with a Tuesday, the deity should be bathed, adored with various kinds of excellent food offerings and propitiated. By propitiating Vighnarāja, one shall attain all desires.

## Chapter 142 - Greatness of Citreśvara (Citra-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.142.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi citreśvara manuttamam \|*  
*dhanuṣāṃ saptake tasya sthitamāgneyadakṣiṇe \|\| 1 \|\|*

*liṃgaṃ mahāprabhāvaṃ hi sarvapātakanāśanam \|*  
*tatra citreśvaraṃ pūjya narakānna bhavedbhayam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*paṭasthitaṃ tasya pāpaṃ citro mārjayati priye \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena citreśaṃ pūjayetsadā \|*  
*yaḥ syātpāpayuto vāpi narakaṃ naiva paśyati \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the excellent shrine of Citreśvara situated within a distance of seven Dhanus to the south-south-east thereof (i.e. Kapardicintāmaṇi)

The Liṅga is of great power and is destructive of all sins. To one who regularly adores Citreśvara there, there is no fear of hell.

His sin though committed to writing in Citragupta records, O my beloved, is wiped off by him. Hence one should always adore Citreśa with all efforts. Even he who is defiled by sins does not see the hell.

## Chapter 143 - Greatness of Vicitreśvara (Vicitra-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.143.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi vicitreśvaramuttamam \|*  
*tasyaiva pūrvadigbhāge kiñcidāgneyagocare \|*  
*dhanuṣāṃ daśake tatra sthitaṃ pāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*vicitreṇa mahādevi lekha kena yamasya ca \|*  
*sthāpitaṃ tanmahāliṃgaṃ tapaḥ kṛtvā suduścaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā pūjitaṃ caiva muktaḥ syātsarvapātakaiḥ \|*  
*saṃpūjya ca vidhānena na duḥkhī jāyate naraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the excellent shrine of Vicitreśvara situated within a distance of ten Dhanus to the east thereof (i. e. Citreśvara) or rather a little to the south-east. It is destructive of sins.

O great goddess, that great Liṅga was installed by Vicitra, the scribe (clerk) of Yama after performing a very difficult penance.

One who adores after visiting the deity shall be rid of all sins. A man who worships in accordance with the injunctions shall never become miserable.

## Chapter 144 - Greatness of Puṣkara-Kuṇḍa

## \|\| 1.144.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi tṛtīyaṃ puṣkaraṃ mahat \|*  
*tasyaiva pūrvadigbhāge kiñcidīśānagocare \|*  
*kanīyaḥ saṃsmṛtaṃ kuṃḍaṃ puṣkaraṃnāma nāmataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yatra madhyāhnasamaye brahmaṇā samupāsitā \|*  
*sandhyā trailokyajananī pratiṣṭhārthaṃ gatena ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tatra yaḥ kurute snānaṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*samyakkṛtaṃ bhavettena snānaṃ tatrādipuṣkare \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the third great Puṣkara to the east thereof (i. e. Vicitreśvara), slightly deviating to the north-east. This Kuṇḍa is remembered as the smallest one and named Puṣkara.

When Brahmā went there at midday for the installation, the midday prayer, Sandhyā, the mother of the three worlds, was adored by him.

If the pilgrim takes his ablution there with concentration and mental purity on the Full-Moon day, it is as good as the ablution is perfectly taken by him in the Ādi-Puṣkara.

## \|\| 1.144.4 \|\|

*hiraṇyaṃ tatra dātavyaṃ sarvapāpāpanuttaye \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. For the sake of the eradication of all sins, gold should be gifted there.

## \|\| 1.144.5 \|\|

*iti saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ māhātmyaṃ tava pauṣkaram \|*  
*śrutaṃ pāpaharaṃ nṝṇāṃ sarvakāmapradaṃ tathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Thus the greatness pertaining to Puṣkara has been spoken to you. On being listened to, it removes the sins of men and fulfills all desires.

## Chapter 145 - Greatness of Gajakuṃbhodara (Gaja-kuṃbhodara)

## \|\| 1.145.1-2 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tatraiva saṃsthitaṃ paśyedvighneśaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*gajakuṃbhodaraṃ nāma sarvasiddhipradāyakam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tatra kuṃḍe naraḥ snātvā caturthyāṃ prayatātmavān \|*  
*pūjayedyastu taṃ bhaktyā vighneśastasya tuṣyati \|\| 2 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-2. A pilgrim should visit the sin-destroying Vighneśa stationed there itself. He is named Gajakuṃbhodara and he is the bestower of all Siddhis. Being a great devotee he should remain pure in mind and take his holy bath in the Kuṇḍa (holy pit) there on the fourth lunar day and devoutly adore him. Vighneśa becomes pleased with him.

## Chapter 146 - Greatness of Yameśvara (Yama-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.146.1-4 \|\|

*\|īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi dharmarājapratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*yameśvaraṃ mahādevaṃ tasyai vottarataḥ sthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yadā śapto dharmarājaśchāyayā varavarṇini \|*  
*tadā tasyāpatatpādaḥ sa ca duḥkhānvito'bhavat \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tataḥ prābhāsike kṣetre tapastepe mahātapāḥ \|*  
*sthāpayāmāsa liṃgaṃ tu tatra devasya śūlinaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tasya tuṣṭo mahādevastataḥ pratyakṣatāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*abravīddharma bhadraṃ te varaṃ varaya cepsitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the shrine of the great Lord Yameśvara installed by Dharmarāja (the Lord of Death). It is situated to the north thereof (i. e. Gajakuṃbhodara).

O lady of excellent complexion, when Dharmarāja was cursed by Chāyā, his foot fell down and he became miserable.

Then the Lord (Dharma) of great penance performed great penance in the holy place of Prābhāsika. There he installed the Liṅga of the Trident-bearing Lord.

Mahādeva was pleased with him and became manifest to him and said, “O Dharma, welfare unto you. Choose a boon desired by you.”

## \|\| 1.146.5-7 \|\|

*tadā'bravīddharmarājaḥ pādaḥ prapatito mama \|*  
*prasādāttava deveśa jāyatāṃ punareva hi \|\| 5 \|\|*

*etalliṃgaṃ suraśreṣṭha yanmayā nirmitaṃ tava \|*  
*etadye bhaktisaṃyuktāḥ paśyaṃti prāṇino bhuvi \|\| 6 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ tava prasādena bhūyātpāpavimokṣaṇam \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. Then Dharmarāja said, “Thanks to your favour, O Lord of Devas, may the foot of mine that has fallen down, grow again. O most excellent one among Suras, this Liṅga of yours has been installed by me. If the creatures on the earth visit this with great devotion, let them have freedom from sins with your favour.”

## \|\| 1.146.8 \|\|

*evaṃ bhaviṣyatītyuktā hyantardhānaṃ gato haraḥ \|*  
*yamo'pi labdhapādastu punareva divaṃ yayau \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. “It will happen thus.” Saying this Hara vanished. Yama regained his foot and went back to heaven.

## \|\| 1.146.9 \|\|

*tasmindṛṣṭe suraśreṣṭha yamalokasamudbhavam \|*  
*na bhayaṃ vidyate nṛṇāmapi duṣkṛtakāriṇām \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. If that most excellent one among Suras is visited, even men who perpetrate evil actions need not be afraid of the danger arising from Yama’s world.

## \|\| 1.146.10 \|\|

*bhrātṛdvitīyāsaṃyoge snātvā puṣkariṇījale \|*  
*yameśvarasamīpastho yameśamavalokayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On the day of Bhrātṛdvitīyā (the second lunar day after Dīpāvalī) a devotee should take his holy bath in the waters of Puṣkariṇī, approach Yameśvara and view Yameśa.

## \|\| 1.146.11 \|\|

*tilapātraṃ pradātavyaṃ dīpaṃ gāḥ kāṃcanā dikam \|*  
*yamadevaṃ samuddiśya mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. With Yamadeva in view, the devotee should gift a vessel of gingelly seeds, a lamp, cows, gold, and the like. He is redeemed from all sins.

## Chapter 147 - Greatness of Brahmakuṇḍa

## \|\| 1.147.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi brahmakuṇḍamanuttamam \|*  
*tasyaiva nairṛte bhāge brahmaṇā nirmitaṃ purā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yadā tu ṛkṣarājena somanāthaḥ prati ṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*tadā brahmādayo devāḥ sarve tatra samāgatāḥ \|*  
*pratiṣṭhārthaṃ hi devasya śaśāṃkena nimantritāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*athā'bravīnniśānātho brahmāṇaṃ vinayānvitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kṛtaṃ bhavadbhirjānāti sthāpanaṃ vai yathā janaḥ \|*  
*tathā kuru suraśreṣṭha cihnamātmasamudbhavam \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the excellent Brahmakuṇḍa, formerly created by Brahmā to the south-west thereof (i.e. Yameśvara)

When Somanātha was installed by Ṛkṣarāja (Lord of stars, the Moon-god), Brahmā and all other Devas had arrived there on being invited by Śaśāṅka (Moon-god) for the installation of the Lord.

Then Niśānātha (Lord of the night, Moon-god) humbly spoke to Brahmā, “O most excellent one among Suras, leave a mark by which people will know that the installation was performed by you.”

## \|\| 1.147.5 \|\|

*evaṃ śrutvā tadā brahmā dhyānaṃ kṛtvā tu niścalam \|*  
*āhvayatsarvatīrthāni puṣkarādīni sarvaśaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On hearing this, Brahmā meditated motionlessly and invoked (summoned) Puṣkara and all other Tīrthas from everywhere.

## \|\| 1.147.6 \|\|

*svarge vai yāni tīrthāni tathaiva ca rasātale \|*  
*tapaḥsāmarthyayogena brahmaṇā'karṣitāni ca \|*  
*atastasyaiva nāmnā tu brahmakuṇḍaṃ tu gīyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. All the Tīrthas present in heaven as well as in the nether worlds were drawn to him by Brahmā as a result of the efficacy of his penance. Hence it is being sung about as Brahmakuṇḍa in his name.

## \|\| 1.147.7 \|\|

*gaṇānāṃ ca sahasraistu caturdaśabhirīkṣyate \|*  
*ataścābhaktiyuktānāṃ duṣprāpyaṃ tīrthamuttamam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. It is being watched by fourteen thousand Gaṇas. Hence this excellent Tīrtha is inaccessible to those not endowed with devotion.

## \|\| 1.147.8 \|\|

*athābravītsarvadevānbrahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then Brahmā, the grandfather of all the worlds, spoke to all the Devas:

## \|\| 1.147.9-10 \|\|

*atra kuṇḍe naraḥ snātvā yaḥ pitṝṃstarpayiṣyati \|*  
*agniṣṭomaphalaṃ sava lapsyate sa ca mānavaḥ \|*  
*tatprasādātsvargaloke vimānena cariṣyati \|\| 9 \|\|*

*godānaṃ cāśvadānaṃ ca tathā svarṇakamaṇḍalum \|*  
*dadyādviprāya viduṣe sarvapāpāpanuttaye \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. “A man who takes his holy bath in the Kuṇḍa here and offers libation to the Pitṛs, shall attain all the benefit of Agniṣṭoma. With the favour thereof, he will roam about in the heavenly world by means of an aerial chariot.

For the eradication of all the sins, a pilgrim should make gifts of horses and golden water-pitchers to a learned Brāhmaṇa.”

## \|\| 1.147.11 \|\|

*paurṇamāsyāṃ mahādevi tathā ca pratipaddine \|*  
*sarvapāpavināśārthaṃ tatra snāti sarasvatī \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O great goddess, Sarasvatī (river) takes her bath on the Full-Moon day and the first lunar day there for eliminating all sins.

## \|\| 1.147.12 \|\|

*siddhaṃ rasāyanaṃ devi tatra vai hyudakaṃ priye \|*  
*nānāvarṇasamāyuktamupadeśena siddhyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O my beloved, O goddess, the water there is the very Siddha Rasāyana (holy elixir and a panacea). By taking regular instruction (from a preceptor) it can be rendered full of various colours.

## \|\| 1.147.13 \|\|

*dāridryaduḥkharukchokānmānavaḥ sevate katham \|*  
*brahmakuṇḍamanuprāpya kalpavṛkṣamivāparam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. How can a man be assailed by poverty, misery, ailment and sorrows after approaching Brahmakuṇḍa which is another wish-yielding celestial tree!

## \|\| 1.147.14 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*bhagavanvistarādbrūhi brahmakuṇḍamahodayam \|*  
*sarvaprāṇihitārthāya vistarādvada me prabho \|\| 14 \|\|*

The Devī said:

14\. O Lord, O venerable one, do expound fully the greatness of Brahmakuṇḍa. For the welfare of all living beings, explain it in detail.

## \|\| 1.147.15 \|\|

*brahmakuṃḍasya māhātmyaṃ śrotuṃ me kautukaṃ mahat \|*  
*lokānāṃ duḥkhanāśāya dāridyakṣayahetave \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. I have great eagerness to hear the greatness of Brahmakuṇḍa (as one leading) to the destruction of the misery of the worlds and to the elimination of poverty.

## \|\| 1.147.16 \|\|

*bhagavanmānuṣāḥ sarve duḥkhaśokanipīḍitāḥ \|*  
*bhramaṃti sakalaṃ janma rasāyanavimohitāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O venerable Sir, all human beings are afflicted with miseries and sorrow. They roam about throughout their life in their delusive search for Rasāyanas.

## \|\| 1.147.17 \|\|

*teṣāṃ hitāya me brūhi nirvāṇaṃ rasamuttamam \|*  
*ādāviha śarīraṃ tu akṣayyaṃ tu yathā bhavet \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. For their benefit tell me about the excellent Rasa that gives ultimate liberation (Nirvāṇa). At first it may make the body everlasting.

## \|\| 1.147.18 \|\|

*aṣṭasiddhisamā yuktaṃ sarvavidyāsamanvitam \|*  
*kāmarūpaṃ kriyāyuktaṃ sarvavyādhivivarjitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. It shall be equipped with the eight Siddhis and all lores. It must possess the power to assume any desired form and do any intended work. It shall be free from all ailments.

## \|\| 1.147.19 \|\|

*tatastu paramaṃ deva nirvāṇaṃ yena vai labhet \|*  
*mānavaḥ kṛtakṛtyaśca jāyate ca yathā prabho \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Thereafter one shall attain the greatest Nirvāṇa (salvation) thereby. O Lord, the man shall eventually feel contented and blessed.

## \|\| 1.147.20 \|\|

*tathā kathaya me deva dayāṃ kṛtvā jagatprabho \|*  
*nirvāṇaparamaṃ kalpaṃ sarvabhrāṃtivivarjitam \|*  
*prasiddhaṃ sukhadaṃ divyaṃ samā cakṣva maheśvara \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Do take pity on me, O Lord of the worlds. Narrate to me the means to such an accomplishment. Let the undertaking culminate in Nirvāṇa after avoiding all errors and delusions. O Maheśvara, expound such a divine means of achieving happiness.

## \|\| 1.147.21-22 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*sādhusādhu mahādevi lokānāṃ hitakāriṇi \|*  
*martyaloke mahādevi tīrthaṃ tīrthavaraṃ śubham \|\| 21 \|\|*

*prabhāsaṃ paramaṃ khyātaṃ tacca dvādaśayojanam \|*  
*tatra someśvaro devastriṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

Īśvara said:
