21-22. Excellent! O great goddess, O benefactress of all the worlds! O great goddess, this splendid and excellent Tīrtha in the mortal world well-known as Prabhāsa extends to twelve Yojanas. Lord Someśvara there is well-known in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.147.23 \|\|

*tasya pūrve samākhyātaḥ śrīkṛṣṇo daityasūdanaḥ \|*  
*caṇḍikā yoginī tatra sakhībhiḥ parivāritā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. To the east thereof is the well-known shrine of Śrīkṛṣṇa, the slayer of Daityas. Caṇḍikā, the Yoginī, there, is surrounded by female companions.

## \|\| 1.147.24 \|\|

*tataḥ pūrve diśāṃ bhāge caturvaktreṇa nirmitam \|*  
*tīrthāttīrthaṃ varaṃ divyaṃ sarvāścaryamayaṃ śubham \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. To the east thereof, is the divine and excellent Tīrtha created by the Four-faced Lord, splendid and full of all wonders.

## \|\| 1.147.25 \|\|

*sevitaṃ sarvadevaistu siddhaiḥ sādhyairgrahaistathā \|*  
*apsaromunibhirdivyairyakṣaiśca pannagaiḥ sadā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. It is always resorted to by all the Devas, Siddhas, Sādhyas, Grahas (planets), celestial damsels, divine sages, Yakṣas and serpents.

## \|\| 1.147.26 \|\|

*siddhyarthaṃ sarvakāmārthaṃ divyabhogāvahaṃ śubham \|*  
*brahmakuṇḍamiti khyātaṃ brahmaṇā nirmitaṃ yataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. This is the splendid Kuṇḍa conducive to divine enjoyment. It serves all desires and is conducive to Siddhi. It is well-known as Brahmakuṇḍa because it was created by Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.147.27-28 \|\|

*tasya vāyavyakoṇe tu hira ṇyeśaḥ svayaṃ sthitaḥ \|*  
*tamārādhya mahādevaṃ hiraṇyeśvaramuttamam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*mahāmantraṃ japetkṣipraṃ daśāṃśaṃ homayetsudhīḥ \|*  
*homena siddhyate mantraḥ satyaṃ satyaṃ varānane \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Lord Hiraṇyeśa is stationed in the north-western corner thereof. That great Lord, the excellent Hiraṇyeśvara is to be propitiated. A devotee should perform the Japa of the great Mantra. A wise man should perform Homas one-tenth in number thereof. Through Homa the Mantra is stabilised and mastered. O lady of excellent countenance, this is the truth. (I repeat it is) the truth.

## \|\| 1.147.29 \|\|

*tasyottare tu digbhāge kiñcidīśānamāśritaḥ \|*  
*caturvaktro mahādevi kṣetrapo liṃgarūpadhṛk \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. To the northern quarter thereof, slightly deviating to the north-east, O great goddess, is the Four-faced Lord Kṣetrapa (Protector of the holy spot) assuming the form of a Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.147.30 \|\|

*tatsthānaṃ rakṣate devi liṃgarūpeṇa śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*tamārādhya prayatnena tataḥ kuṇḍaṃ samāśrayet \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O goddess, Śaṅkara in the form of Liṅga guards that holy spot. After propitiating him with effort, a devotee should resort to the Kuṇḍa.

## \|\| 1.147.31 \|\|

*sarvaiśvaryamayaṃ devi nānāvarṇavicitritam \|*  
*kuṇḍasyāsyeśadigbhāge bhairaveśvaramuttamam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O goddess, to the north-eastern quarter of the Kuṇḍa is the excellent shrine Bhairaveśvara, full of all wonders. It is full of different colours.

## \|\| 1.147.32-33 \|\|

*durgandhā bhāsurā devi vahate rasarūpiṇī \|*  
*tasyā rasena saṃyuktaṃ pṛthagvarṇaṃ hi karburam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*meghavarṇaṃ mahādivyaṃ rājataṃ ca punaḥ śubham \|*  
*kapilaṃ dugdhavarṇaṃ ca karpūrābhaṃ suśobhanam \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. O goddess, the foul-odoured Bhāsurā (channel) flows in the form of liquid. Liquids of different colours, get mingled with its Rasa (current of juice). The most divine one has the colour of cloud. Then it is silvery and splendid. Again it is tawny-coloureḍ. Then the highly splendid one resembling camphor has the colour of milk.

## \|\| 1.147.34 \|\|

*kadā kastūrikābhāsaṃ kuṃkumacchavikāvaham \|*  
*saugandhaṃ caṃdanopetaṃ kadācidraudhi rodakam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Sometimes it shines like musk. Then it flows with a saffron lustre. Sometimes it has the sweet odour of sandal. Sometimes the water is bloody (red in colour).

## \|\| 1.147.35 \|\|

*ete rasāśca vividhā dṛśyaṃte tatra sarvadā \|*  
*yasya tuṣṭo mahādevaḥ siddhyate tasya tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. These Rasas of different kinds are seen there always. If Mahādeva is pleased with one, he gets them instantly.

## \|\| 1.147.36 \|\|

*rajataṃ kṣipyate tatra suvarṇa miva jāyate \|*  
*pratyakṣameva tatraiva rasāyanamanuttamam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. If silver is thrown there, it becomes like gold. There the excellent Rasāyana is visible.

## \|\| 1.147.37 \|\|

*paśyaṃti mānavā devi kautukaṃ tatkṣaṇādbhṛśam \|*  
*rasaṃ hi paramaṃ divyaṃ tatrasthaṃ ca kalau yuge \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O goddess, men see this fanciful thing at the same time. The Rasa present there is highly divine in Kali Yuga.

## \|\| 1.147.38 \|\|

*siddhaṃ siddharasaṃ puṃsāṃ vyādhīnāṃ kṣayakārakam \|*  
*hemabījamayaṃ divyaṃ brahmakuṇḍodbhavaṃ mahat \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. This divine Rasa arising from Brahmakuṇḍa is full of Hemabīja (seeds of gold). It causes the eradication of all ailments of men. It is Siddha (perfect) Rasa.

## \|\| 1.147.39 \|\|

*idānīṃ te pravakṣyāmi manuṣyāṇāṃ hitāya vai \|*  
*dāridryaṃ kṣayamāpnoti tatkṣaṇācca yaśasvini \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Now I am narrating this to you for the benefit of human beings. O renowned one, poverty is instantly removed.

## \|\| 1.147.40 \|\|

*ādāveva prakurvanti tāmrakumbhaṃ dṛḍhaṃ śubham \|*  
*tīrthodakaṃ kṣipettatra patraistāmrastathā yutam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. At the outset, people make an excellent pot with sheets of copper. Water from the Tīrtha should be poured therein.

## \|\| 1.147.41 \|\|

*nikṣipya bhūmau tatkumbhaṃ jvālayedanalaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*cuhlīrūpeṇa ṣaṇmāsaṃ pācayettaṃ śanaiḥśanaiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The pot should be put under the ground and burnt in fire. For six months the process of heating should be carried out slowly in an oven under ground.

## \|\| 1.147.42 \|\|

*paścāduddhṛtya taṃ kumbhaṃ punareva jalaṃ kṣipet \|*  
*māsamekaṃ punaḥ kuryānmāsamekaṃ punarbhṛśam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Afterwards the pot is taken out and Filled with water. This should be repeated for a month and once again for another month.

## \|\| 1.147.43 \|\|

*tataḥ sarvāṇi khaṇḍāni ekīkṛtya prayatnataḥ \|*  
*punarevodakenaiva plāvya cāvartayetpunaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Then all the pieces should be gathered together with effort. Again it should be washed with water. This is repeated once more.

## \|\| 1.147.44 \|\|

*kāṃcanaṃ jāyate tatra yadi tuṣṭo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. If Maheśvara is pleased, it becomes gold.

## \|\| 1.147.45-46 \|\|

*siddhiṃ śarīrajāṃ devi yadīcchenmānavottamaḥ \|*  
*sa snānamāditaḥ kṛtvā saṃvatsaratrayaṃ punaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*maunena niyamenaiva mahāmaṃtrajapānvitaḥ \|*  
*pūjayecca hiraṇyeśaṃ kṣetrapālaṃ prayatnataḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. If an excellent man desires the Siddhi (perfection) of the body, he should at the outset take the holy bath regularly for three years. Regularly observing the vow of silence, he should repeat the Mahāmantra. Then he should worship Hiraṇyeśa, the Kṣetrapāla, assiduously.

## \|\| 1.147.47 \|\|

*paṃcopacārasaṃyuktaṃ dhyānadhāraṇasaṃyutam \|*  
*tīrthodakena pākaṃ vai peyaṃ tadvadudumbare \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Five Upacāras are included in the adoration. Then he should perform Dhyāna and Dhāraṇā. Cooking and boiling should be in the waters of the Tīrtha in Uduṃbara (i.e. Copper, according to the commentator) vessel.

## \|\| 1.147.48 \|\|

*evaṃ varṣatrayeṇaiva divyadehaḥ prajāyate \|*  
*tejasvī valavānprājñaḥ sarvavyādhivivarjitaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. In this manner, within three years he acquires a divine body. He shall be refulgent, strong, intelligent and bereft of all ailments.

## \|\| 1.147.49 \|\|

*jīvedvarṣeśatānyeva trīṇi duḥkhavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*varṣatrayamavicchinnaṃ yastatra snānamācaret \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. He who bathes there for three years without a break, shall live for three hundred years free from misery.

## \|\| 1.147.50 \|\|

*vāgīśvarīṃ japennityaṃ pūjāhomasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*tasya pravartate vāṇī siddhiḥ sārasvatī bhavet \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The devotee should repeat Vāgīśvarī Mantra every day along with adoration and Homa. He will attain eloquency of speech. He will attain Sarasvatī Siddhi.

## \|\| 1.147.51 \|\|

*saṃskṛtaṃ prākṛtaṃ caivāpabhraṃśaṃ bhūtabhāṣitam \|*  
*gāṃgasrotaḥpravāheṇa udgiredgiramātmavān \|*  
*aśrāntāṃ ca varārohe hyavicchinnāṃ ca saṃtatam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. He will become a perfect master of Saṃskṛta, Prākṛta, Apabhraṃśa and Paiśācī (the speech of Bhūtas). He will be able to utter words fluently like the current of Gaṅgā. O beautiful lady, he will be able to speak without being tired and without any break.

## \|\| 1.147.52-53 \|\|

*vadedvādisahasraistu na śramastasya jāyate \|*  
*tīrthasyāsya prabhāveṇa sarvaśāstraviśāradāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*paṃḍitā garvitāḥ sarve tarkaśāstraviśāradāḥ \|*  
*āgacchanti samaṃ tāta vidyayoddhatakandharāḥ \|*  
*na śaknuvaṃti te vaktuṃ draṣṭuṃ vaktramapi priye \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. He will be capable of arguing with thousands of disputants. He will never become tired due to the power of this Tīrtha.

All scholars, proud and proficient in the science of logic come with their necks (heads) held up in pride. They may approach him simultaneously. But, O my beloved, they will not be able to speak anything; they dare not even look at his face.

## \|\| 1.147.54 \|\|

*vādināṃ ca sahasrāṇi bhanaktyevaṃ nirīkṣaṇāt \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Merely by looking at them, he will be able to break thousands of disputants.

## \|\| 1.147.55-56 \|\|

*udvāhayati śāstrāṇi vibuddhārthāni satvaram \|*  
*vimalaṃ pāñcarātraṃ ca vaiṣṇavaṃ śaivameva ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

*itihāsapurāṇaṃ ca bhūtataṃtraṃ ca gāruḍam \|*  
*bhairavaṃ ca mahātaṃtraṃ kulamārgaṃ dvidhā priye \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. He will make people understand all scriptural texts with clear expositions of their meanings. The pure Pañcarātra texts both Vaiṣṇava and Śaiva, Itihāsas, Purāṇas, Bhūta Tantras, Gāruḍa Tantra, the great Bhairava Tantra and the twofold Kulamārga shall be expounded by him. O my beloved.

## \|\| 1.147.57 \|\|

*rathapravaravegena vāṇī cāskhalitā bhavet \|*  
*naśyaṃti vādinaḥ sarve garuḍasyeva pannagāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The flow of his speech will be with the speed of an excellent chariot and will not falter even a bit. Like serpents before Garuḍa, all disputants will be defeated and destroyed.

## \|\| 1.147.58 \|\|

*na dāridryaṃ na rogaśca na duḥkhaṃ mānasaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*rājamānyo mahāmānī bhavedbrahmaprasādataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Due to the favour of Brahmā, he will be honoured by kings and one of great prestige. He will have no mental worries, neither poverty nor ailments.

## \|\| 1.147.59 \|\|

*utsāhabalasaṃyukto devavajjīvate sudhīḥ \|*  
*dātā bhoktā ca vāggmī ca tīrthasyāsya prasādataḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. With the favour of this holy Tīrtha, he will become one endowed with energy, enthusiasm and strength. He will be intelligent and will live like a Deva. He will be a donor, an enjoyer of pleasures and very eloquent.

## \|\| 1.147.60 \|\|

*tailābhyaktasya yattejo jāyate manujeṣu ca \|*  
*snātamātre tathā tejastīrthasyaiva prasādataḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Due to the efficacy of this Tīrtha, the moment a devotee takes his bath herein, he will get the same refulgence and splendour as a person regularly annointing his body with oil gets.

## \|\| 1.147.61 \|\|

*yatpāpaṃ kurute jaṃtuḥ paiśunyaṃ ca kṛtaghnatām \|*  
*mitradrohe ca yatpāpaṃ yatpāpaṃ pāradārikam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ vilayaṃ yāti kuṃḍasnānaratasya ca \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. All sins that creatures (men) are prone to commit (such as) calumny, ingratitude and treachery to friends, the sin resulting from violation of the chastity of another man’s wife, perish if one takes bath in the Kuṇḍa.

## \|\| 1.147.62 \|\|

*muśalaṃ laṅghayed yastu yo gāstyajati vai dvijaḥ \|*  
*tatpāpaṃ kṣayamāpnoti brahmakuṇḍasya darśanāt \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. By the sight of Brahmakuṇḍa, sin resulting from crossing a Muśala (pestle), sin of a Brāhmaṇa who abandons cows are destroyed.

## \|\| 1.147.63 \|\|

*pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni daivatāni tathā punaḥ \|*  
*pūjitāni ca sarvāṇi kuṇḍasnānaprabhāvataḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. By the power of ablution in this Kuṇḍa, one gets the benefit of taking bath in all the Tīrthas on the earth and the benefit of worshipping all the deities.

## \|\| 1.147.64 \|\|

*saptajanmārjitaṃ pāpaṃ darśanātkṣayamāvrajet \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. By seeing it, the sins accrued in the course of seven births, perish.

## \|\| 1.147.65 \|\|

*yatpāpaṃ gurugoghne ca parasvaharaṇeṣu ca \|*  
*tatpāpaṃ kṣayamāpnoti brahmakuṇḍaniṣevaṇāt \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. By resorting to Brahmakuṇḍa, the sin of a slayer of preceptor or a cow and robbing other men’s wealth perishes.

## \|\| 1.147.66 \|\|

*pradakṣiṇaṃ ca yaḥ kuryātsnātvā kuṇḍasya nāmataḥ \|*  
*saṃkhyayā paṃcadaśa vai śṛṇu tasyāpi yatphalam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Listen to the benefit that one gets by fifteen circumambulations of the Kuṇḍa after taking bath therein.

## \|\| 1.147.67 \|\|

*pradakṣiṇīkṛtā tena saptadvīpā vasundharā \|*  
*saptapātālasahitā tīrthakoṭibhirāvṛtā \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. It is as good as circumambulating the whole earth consisting of seven continents, together with the seven nether worlds and surrounded by crores of Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.147.68 \|\|

*āhāramātraṃ yo dadyāttatra vedavidāṃ vare \|*  
*lakṣabhojyaṃ kṛtaṃ tena tīrthasyāsya prabhāvataḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. A pilgrim who feeds one well-versed in the Vedas with simple food at this holy spot, gets the benefit of feeding a hundred thousand persons (elsewhere) by the power of this holy spot.

## \|\| 1.147.69 \|\|

*brahmeśvaraṃ ca saṃpūjya hiraṇyeśvaramuttamam \|*  
*kṣetrapālaṃ caturvaktraṃ pūjayeccintitaṃ labhet \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. After worshipping Brahmeśvara, the excellent Hiraṇyeśvara, the devotee should worship the four-faced Kṣetrapāla. He will get whatever is thought of by him.

## \|\| 1.147.70 \|\|

*ekaviṃśatkulai ryuktaḥ sarvapāpavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*brahmalokaṃ sa vai yāti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. No doubt need be entertained about the fact that such a person goes to the world of Brahmā along with twenty-one members of his family and is freed from all sins.

## \|\| 1.147.71 \|\|

*viraṃcikuṇḍe snātvā vā yo japedvedamātaram \|*  
*lakṣajāpyavidhānena sa muktaḥ pātakairbhavet \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. After taking the holy bath in Virañci (Brahma) kuṇḍa i.e., the pilgrim should repeat the Gāyatrī Mantra a hundred thousand times duly. He shall be rid of all sins.

## \|\| 1.147.72 \|\|

*sa eva puṇyakarttā ca sa eva puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*yātrā tatra kṛtā yena brahmakuṇḍe varānane \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. O lady of excellent countenance, if a pilgrim undertakes the pilgrimage to Brahmakuṇḍa, he becomes a performer of meritorious deeds. He is the most excellent one among men.

## \|\| 1.147.73 \|\|

*aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi ṛṣīṇāmūrdhvaretasām \|*  
*brahmakuṇḍaṃ samāśritya brahmadevamupāsate \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Eighty-eight thousand sages of perfect control of their sense-organs resort to Brahmakuṇḍa and adore Lord Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.147.74 \|\|

*tāvadgarjaṃti tīrthāni trailokye sacarācare \|*  
*yāvadbrahmeśvaraṃ tīrthaṃ na paśyanti narāḥ priye \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. All the other Tīrthas in the three worlds consisting of mobile and immobile beings, roar only as long as men do not view Brahmeśvara Tīrthas, O my beloved.

## \|\| 1.147.75 \|\|

*brahmakuṇḍe ca pānīyaṃ ye pibanti narāḥ sakṛt \|*  
*na teṣāṃ saṃkrametpāpaṃ vācikaṃ mānasaṃ tanau \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. If men drink the holy water of Brahmakuṇḍa but once, they will incur no sin mental, physical or verbal.

## \|\| 1.147.76 \|\|

*brahmāṃḍottaramadhye tu yāni tīrthāni saṃti vai \|*  
*teṣāṃ puṇyamavāpnoti brahmakuṇḍe pradakṣiṇāt \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. By circumambulating Brahmakuṇḍa, one acquires the merit of all the Tīrthas in Brahmāṇḍa (Cosmic Egg) and beyond.

## \|\| 1.147.77 \|\|

*yājñavalkyo mahātmā ca parabrahmasvarūpavān \|*  
*so'pi kuṃḍaṃ na muṃceta nikuṃ bhastu gaṇastathā \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. The noble-souled Yājñavalkya who has attained the form of the supreme Brahman, never leaves this Kuṇḍa. So also the Gaṇa Nikuṃbha.

## \|\| 1.147.78 \|\|

*iti saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ māhātmyaṃ brahmakuṇḍajam \|*  
*tava snehena deveśi kimanyatparipṛcchasi \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Thus the greatness of Brahmakuṇḍa has been succinctly narrated due to my love for you, O goddess of Devas. What else do you wish to ask?

## \|\| 1.147.79 \|\|

*ya idaṃ śṛṇuyānmartyaḥ samyakchraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*sa muktaḥ pātakaiḥ sarvairbrahmalokaṃ ca gacchati \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. A man who is thoroughly equipped with faith and who listens to this, shall be rid of all sins. He shall go to the world of Brahmā.

## Chapter 148 - Greatness of Kuṇḍalakūpa (Kuṇḍala-kūpa)

## \|\| 1.148.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi kūpaṃ kuṃḍalasaṃbhavam \|*  
*tasyaiva cottare bhāge brahmakuṇḍasamīpataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yatra siddho mahādevi rūpakuṃḍalahārakaḥ \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro devi mucyetsteyakṛtādaghāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sapta janmāni deveśi na tasyānvayasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*cauraḥ kaścidbhavetkrūrastatra snānaprabhāvataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śivarātryāṃ viśeṣeṇa piṃḍadānādikāṃ kriyām \|*  
*kuryācchastrahatānāṃ ca pāpināṃ tatra muktaye \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the Kūpa (well) pertaining to Kuṇḍala. It is near Brahmakuṇḍa on the northern side thereof.

It was there, O great goddess, that a thief Rūpakuṇḍalahāraka (‘who removed the beautiful earrings’) became a Siddha.

O goddess, a man who takes his holy bath there becomes free from the sin incurred from stealing as a result of the power of bathing therein. O goddess of Devas, no one belonging to his family shall ever be a thief or a ruthless one, for seven generations.

For the redemption of sinners killed by weapons, the pilgrim should perform rites like offering balls of rice etc., particularly on the Śivarātri day.

## \|\| 1.148.5 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ kuṇḍalarūpaṃ tu pṛthivyāṃ khyātimāgatam \|*  
*etatkathaya me deva vistarādvadatāṃ vara \|\| 5 \|\|*

The Devī said:

5\. O Lord, O most excellent one among speakers, tell me in detail how (the Kūpa) associated with earrings became famous on the earth.

## \|\| 1.148.6 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi mahāpuṇyāṃ kathāṃ pāpapraṇāśanīm \|*  
*yāṃ śrutvā mucyate pāpānnaro janmaśatārjitāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

6\. Listen, O goddess, to the sin-destroying, highly meritorious story, on hearing which a man becomes rid of sins acquired in the course of a hundred births.

## \|\| 1.148.7 \|\|

*prabhāsakṣetramāhātmyācchivarātryāmupoṣitaḥ \|*  
*āsītsudarśano rājā pṛthivyāmekarāṭ sudhīḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. There was a king named Sudarśana who was very intelligent and the sole emperor of the earth. That was because he had observed fast on Śivarātri day and also a result of the greatness of Prabhāsakṣetra.

## \|\| 1.148.8 \|\|

*dhanyo hi sa dhanāḍhyaśca prajāṃ yatnairapālayat \|*  
*rājyaṃ tasya susaṃpannaṃ brāhmaṇairupaśobhitam \|*  
*samṛddhamṛddhisaṃyuktaṃ viṭataskaravarjitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He was very rich and blessed. He ruled over the subjects assiduously. His kingdom was very prosperous and rendered brilliant by (residing) Brāhmaṇas. It was flourishing and was devoid of lecherous persons and thieves.

## \|\| 1.148.9 \|\|

*tasmiñjanapade ramye purī bhagavatī śubhā \|*  
*cāturvarṇyasamāyuktā puraprākāramaṃḍitā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. In that beautiful region, his city was splendid and divinely blessed, adorned with ramparts and consisted of persons of all the four castes.

## \|\| 1.148.10 \|\|

*tasminpuravare ramye rājyaṃ nihatakaṇṭakam \|*  
*karoti bāndhavaiḥ sārddhamṛddhiyuktaḥ sudarśanaḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyadattasya suto jāto gāṃdhārakanyayā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. In that beautiful and excellent city, King Sudarśana ruled the kingdom free from all thorns (enemies and traitors) along with his kinsmen. This prosperous king was the son of Hiraṇyadatta born of a Gāndhāra princess.

## \|\| 1.148.11 \|\|

*tasya bhāryā priyā sādhvī bhartṛvrataparāyaṇā \|*  
*sunaṃdā nāmavikhyātā kāśirājasutā śubhā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. His chaste and beloved queen was well-known by the name Sunandā. She was a splendid princess, daughter of the king of Kāśī. She was earnestly devoted to her husband and observed Vratas.

## \|\| 1.148.12 \|\|

*tayā sārdhaṃ hi rājendro bhogānsa bubhuje sadā \|*  
*bhuṃjamānasya bhogānvai cirakālo gatastadā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The eminent king enjoyed all pleasures along with her. A great deal of time passed thus while he enjoyed diverse pleasures.

## \|\| 1.148.13 \|\|

*akarotsa mahāyajñāndadau dānāni bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ kālo gatastasya bhāryayā saha suvrate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He performed great Yajñas and made many religious gifts. O lady of excellent holy vows, (thus) he passed his days in the company of his wife.

## \|\| 1.148.14 \|\|

*kadācinmāghamāse tu śivarātryāṃ varānane \|*  
*sasmāra pūrvajātiṃ sa bhāryāmāhūya cābravīt \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Once, O lady of excellent countenance, during the Śivarātri (festival) in the month of Māgha, he happened to recollect his previous birth. He called his wife and said:

## \|\| 1.148.15 \|\|

*sudarśana uvāca \|*  
*śivarātrivrataṃ devi mayā kāryaṃ varānane \|*  
*vratasyāsya prabhāvena prāptaṃ rājyaṃ mayā kila \|\| 15 \|\|*

Sudarśana said:

15\. O fair lady of excellent countenance, I have to observe the Śivarātri Vrata. Indeed it was due to the efficacy of this Vrata that this kingdom has been gained by me.

## \|\| 1.148.16 \|\|

*rājñyuvāca \|*  
*mahānprabhāvo rājendra evamuktaṃ tvayā mama \|*  
*etanme kāraṇaṃ brūhi āścaryaṃ hṛdi vartate \|\| 16 \|\|*

The queen said:

16\. O great king, what you have told me amounts to this that the power (of this Vrata) is very great. My heart (mind) is surprised. Tell the reason hereof to me.

## \|\| 1.148.17-19 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu tīrthasya māhātmyaṃ śivarātrimupoṣaṇāt \|*  
*tasmiñchivapure ramye svargadvāre suśobhane \|\| 17 \|\|*

*āditīrthe prabhāse tu kāmike tīrtha uttame \|\| 18 \|\|*

*ṛddhiyukte pure tasminnityaṃ dharmānusevite \|*  
*śivarātryāṃ gato rājñi tithīnāmuttamā tithiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

The king said:

17-19. Listen to the greatness of that Tīrtha, especially of fasting on Śivarātri day. O my queen, on the Śivarātri day, I had gone to that primordial Tīrtha named Prabhāsa. It is highly splendid. It is the veritable entrance to the heavenly world. It is a beautiful and charming city of Śiva. It is the most excellent Tīrtha causing the fulfilment of onés desires. It is a flourishing city, always resorted to by pious people. This Tithi (i.e. fourteenth lunar day) is the most excellent one of all Tithis.

## \|\| 1.148.20 \|\|

*mānavāstatra ye kecitpurarāṣṭrani vāsinaḥ \|*  
*tatrāgatā varārohe śivarātryāmupoṣitum \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Men of all cities and countries came there, O beautiful lady, in order to observe the holy fast on the Śivarātri day.

## \|\| 1.148.21 \|\|

*dhananāmā vaṇikkaścittatraiva vasate sadā \|*  
*dhanāḍhyaḥ sa tu dharmātmā sadā dharmaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. A merchant named Dhana used to stay there always. He was wealthy and a pious soul devoted to righteous practices.

## \|\| 1.148.22 \|\|

*sa bhāryāsahitastatra śivarātrimupoṣitaḥ \|*  
*tasya bhāryā'bhavatsādhvī rūpayauvanasaṃvṛtā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. He observed fast in the company of his wife. This wife was highly chaste and endowed with beauty and youth.

## \|\| 1.148.23-24 \|\|

*pracalanmekhalāhārā sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā \|*  
*sa tayā bhāryayā sārdhaṃ kāmakrodhavivarjitaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*prabhāsasyāgrato bhūtvā snātaḥ śuklāṃbaraḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*yathoktena vidhānena bhaktyā nidrāvivarjitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. She was bedecked with all ornaments including oscillating necklaces and girdles. The merchant and his wife eschewed lust and anger. They headed towards the holy spot. He had his bath and wore white garments and remained pure. They performed every rite devoutly in accordance with the injunctions. They observed vigil at night too.

## \|\| 1.148.25 \|\|

*tatrāhaṃ caurarūpeṇa pāpaḥ stainyaṃ samāśritaḥ \|*  
*sacchūdrāṇāṃ kule jāto devabrāhmaṇapūjakaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. I was (then) born in a good Śūdra family. I was a regular worshipper of deities and Brāhmaṇas. But there I was present as a thief and sinner resorting to thievery.

## \|\| 1.148.26 \|\|

*pūrvakarmānusaṃyogādvikarmaṇi rataḥ sadā \|*  
*tasyāṃ rātryāmahaṃ tatra janamadhye tu saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. There again it was still my Karma of the previous birth that made me engrossed in misdeeds always. Well, on that night I stayed amongst common people.

## \|\| 1.148.27 \|\|

*kuṇḍalīnaḥ sthitastatra raṃdhrāpekṣī varānane \|*  
*vaṇijastasya bhāryāyāśchidrānveṣaṇatatparaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O lady of excellent countenance, I was lying hidden near the Kuṇḍa waiting for an opportunity to find a fault on the part of the wife of the merchant.

## \|\| 1.148.28-30 \|\|

*sā rātrirjāgratastasya gatā me vijane tathā \|*  
*gītanṛtyādinirghoṣairvedamaṃgalapāṭakaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tālaśabdaistathā bandhaiḥ pustakānāṃ ca vācakaiḥ \|*  
*evaṃ rātryāṃ tu śeṣāyāṃ yāvattiṣṭhati tatra vai \|\| 29 \|\|*

*nirodhena samāyuktā pīḍyamānā śucismitā \|*  
*dhanibhāryā nirodhārtā devāgārādbahirgatā \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. The whole of that night was spent by me keeping awake in the isolated place. But I also listened to the sounds of songs and auspicious chantings of the Vedic passages and witnessed the dances.

There were sounds of clapping of hands and holy books were being read. The night was about to come to a close and I was waiting there when the ever smiling wife of the rich merchant had some painful experience of suppressed evacuation of bowels. Distressed due to that, she came out of the temple.

## \|\| 1.148.31 \|\|

*tasyāḥ karṇau troṭayitvā pupluve'haṃ jale sthitaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kolāhalastatra kṛtastatpuravāsibhiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. I tore away her ears and leapt into the water where I stayed. A great hue and cry was raised by the residents of the city.

## \|\| 1.148.32 \|\|

*śrutvā kolāhalaṃ śabdaṃ karṇatroṭanajaṃ tadā \|*  
*dhāvitā rakṣakāstatra rājaśāsanakārakāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On hearing the tumult and the lament due to the slitting of the ears, the police and the servants of the royal administration ran here and there.

## \|\| 1.148.33 \|\|

*tairahaṃ śastrahastaiśca ulkāhastaiḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*nirīkṣito'tha na prāptaṃ suvarṇaṃ manmukhe sthitam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. With torches and weapons in their hands, I was thoroughly searched by those people. But the gold was not found by them as it lay hidden in my mouth.

## \|\| 1.148.34 \|\|

*khaḍgena tīkṣṇadhāreṇa chittvā śīrṣaṃ tadā mama \|*  
*ulkāhastā nirīkṣanto nāpaśyansvarṇamaṇvapi \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. With a keen-edged sword they cut off my head and searched everywhere with torches in their hands. They did not see even a bit of gold.

## \|\| 1.148.35 \|\|

*hitvā māṃ te gatāḥ sarve gatvā rājñe nyavedayan \|*  
*na kiñcittatra saṃprāptaṃ hato'smābhiśca tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Leaving me there all of them went to the king and reported to him, “The fellow has been killed by us instantly but nothing was found out.”

## \|\| 1.148.36-38 \|\|

*kathayitvā tu te sarve yathādeśaṃ gatāḥ punaḥ \|*  
*tato vai bandhunā tatra bhayabhītena cetasā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*nikhātaṃ mama tatraiva śiraḥ kāyena saṃyutam \|*  
*khātaṃ kṛtvā priye tatra brahmatīrthasya cottare \|\| 37 \|\|*

*pihito'haṃ tu tatraiva prabhāse tīrtha uttame \|*  
*śivarātriprabhāvena tajjātismaratāṃ gataḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

36-38. Having told thus, they went to their respective places. My kinsmen who became very afraid, dug a pit on the northern side of Brahmatīrtha, O my beloved, and put my head and body together. Thus I was kept covered in the excellent Tīrtha named Prabhāsa. I became a Jātismara (one capable of remembering previous births) by the power of Śivarātri (rite and vow).

## \|\| 1.148.39 \|\|

*rājyaṃ niṣkaṇṭakaṃ prāptaṃ samṛddhaṃ varavarṇini \|*  
*etatprabhāsamāhātmyaṃ śivarātrerupoṣaṇāt \|*  
*etatphalaṃ mayā labdhaṃ gatvā tasmādupoṣaye \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O lady of excellent complexion, this flourishing kingdom free from thorns (i.e. enemies and traitors) has been acquired by me. This is the efficacy of Prabhāsa due to the fasting on Śivarātri day. This is the benefit that has been received by me. Hence I shall once again go there and observe fast.

## \|\| 1.148.40 \|\|

*rājñyuvāca \|*  
*gacchāvastatra yatraiva kapālaṃ patitaṃ tava \|*  
*sphoṭite ca kapāle ca hiraṇyaṃ dṛśyate yadi \|*  
*pratyayo me bhavetpaścāttava vākyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

The queen said:

40\. We shall go there where your skull had fallen. If, on breaking the skull gold is seen I shall become convinced of your story. There is no doubt.

## \|\| 1.148.41 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*kalpaṃ hi tiṣṭhate cāsthi yāvadbhūmiviparyayaḥ \|*  
*uttiṣṭha vraja bhadraṃ te prabhāsaṃ kṣetramuttamam \|\| 41 \|\|*

The king said:

41\. Bones last (unaffected) for a Kalpa till the earth is annihilated. Get up. Welfare unto you. Go to the excellent Kṣetra named Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.148.42 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā yadrājñā samudīritam \|*  
*gamanāya matiṃ cakre śivarātryā upoṣaṇe \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. On hearing the words uttered by the king she also decided to go there for the observance of fast on Śivarātri day.

## \|\| 1.148.43 \|\|

*tato'śvairjavanaiyurktaṃ rathaṃ hemavibhūṣitam \|*  
*āsthāya saha patnyā ca prabhāsaṃ kṣetrameyivān \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Along with his wife, he got into a chariot bedecked with gold and yoked with fast running horses and went to Prabhāsa Kṣetra.

## \|\| 1.148.44-45 \|\|

*vrataṃ kṛtvā prabhāse tu yathoktaṃ varavarṇini \|*  
*brahmatīrthe samāgatya uddhṛtya sakalaṃ tataḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*hiraṇyaṃ darśayāmāsa sphoṭayitvā śavaṃ svayam \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. O lady of excellent complexion, they observed the Vrata in the Prabhāsa Kṣetra and came to Brahma Tīrtha. They then dug up everything, slit the corpse and took up the gold. (The king showed it to the queen.)

## \|\| 1.148.46-47 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*jātasaṃpratyayā bhāryā tasya rājño babhūva ha \|*  
*jagāma paramaṃ sthānaṃ yatra kalyāṇamuttamam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*jano'pi vismitaḥ sarvo dṛṣṭvā citraṃ tadadbhutam \|\| 47 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

46-47. The king’s wife was convinced. She went to the greatest spot where they had the excellent benefit. On seeing that miraculous event all the people were surprised.

## \|\| 1.148.48 \|\|

*nadī citrapathānāma tatrotpannā varānane \|*  
*citrādityasya pūrveṇa brahmatīrthasya cottare \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O lady of excellent countenance, a river named Citrapathā sprang up there to the east of Citrāditya and to the north of Brahma Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.148.49 \|\|

*tasyāṃ tattiṣṭhate tatra sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. That holy Kuṇḍalakūpa Tīrtha that destroys all sins is situated there.

## \|\| 1.148.50-51 \|\|

*śrāvaṇe māsi saṃprāpte tasminkūpe vidhānataḥ \|*  
*yaḥ snānaṃ kurute devi śrāddhaṃ tatra viśeṣataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*citrādityaṃ tu saṃpūjya śivaloke mahīyate \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. In the month of Śrāvaṇa a devotee should take his holy ablution in the Kūpa in accordance with the injunctions. O goddess, he should perform a special Śrāddha too. Then he should adore Citrāditya. He is thereby honoured in the world of Śiva.

## \|\| 1.148.52 \|\|

*etatte kathitaṃ sarvaṃ śivarātryā mahatphalam \|*  
*bhuktimuktipradaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Thus everything regarding the benefit of Śivarātri has been mentioned to you. It grants worldly pleasures and salvation. It is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.148.53 \|\|

*ya idaṃ paṭhate nityaṃ śṛṇuyādvāpi mānavaḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto rudraloke mahīyate \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. A man who reads this everyday or listens to this shall be rid of all sins. He is honoured in Rudra-Loka.

## Chapter 149 - Greatness of Bhairaveśvara (Bhairava-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.149.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi bhairaveśvaramuttamam \|*  
*brahmakuṇḍasya īśāne sthitaṃ pāpapraṇāśanam \|*  
*caturvaktraṃ mahādevaṃ saṃsthitaṃ tīrtharakṣaṇe \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the excellent shrine of Bhairaveśvara situated to the north-east of Brahmakuṇḍa. It is destructive of sins. The great Four-faced Lord is ready stationed there for guarding the Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.149.2-3 \|\|

*tatra snātvā mahākuṇḍe yastaṃ pūjayate naraḥ \|*  
*paṃcopacāravidhinā bhaktiyukto yatendriyaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kulāni yānyatītāni bhaviṣyāṇi ca yāni vai \|*  
*tārayetsa naro devi nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. If the pilgrim takes his holy bath in the great Kuṇḍa and worships the deity in accordance with the injuctions regarding the five Upacāras devoutly and with perfect control of the sense-organs, the man redeems all the earlier members of his family as well as all the future generations. No doubt need be entertained in this respect.

## \|\| 1.149.4 \|\|

*na cātra saṃbhavastasya vināśo naiva jāyate \|*  
*vimānaiścarate nityaṃ divākarasamaprabhaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He is not reborn here in this world. He will never meet with destruction. He will roam about always by means of aerial chariots shining like the sun.

## \|\| 1.149.5 \|\|

*strīsahasrairvṛto nityaṃ krīḍate devava ddivi \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Surrounded by thousands of women, he will sport about like Devas in heaven.

## \|\| 1.149.6 \|\|

*etalliṃgaṃ mahādevi caturvaktraṃ mahāprabham \|*  
*dṛṣṭvāpi tadvimucyeta sarvapāpaistu mānavaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O great goddess, this Four-faced Deity is highly refulgent. By viewing this Liṅga, a man is rid of all sins.

## Chapter 150 - Greatness of Brahmeśvara (Brahma-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.150.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato brahmeśvaraṃ gacchettasya dakṣiṇataḥ sthitam \|*  
*brahmaṇā sthāpitaṃ pūrvaṃ brahmakuṇḍasamīpataḥ \|*  
*triṣu lokeṣu vikhyātaṃ rakṣyamāṇaṃ gaṇairmama \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Thereafter, a pilgrim should go to the shrine of Brahmeśvara stationed towards the south thereof (i.e. Bhairaveśvara). It is near Brahmakuṇḍa and was installed by Brahmā formerly. It is being guarded by my Gaṇas and is well-known in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.150.2 \|\|

*tatra snātvā caturdaśyāmamāvāsyāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ ca vidhivatkṛtvā brahmeśaṃ pūjayettataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The pilgrim should take his holy bath there on the fourteenth lunar day and more particularly on the New-Moon day. He should then perform the Śrāddha duly. Then he should worship Brahmeśa.

## \|\| 1.150.3 \|\|

*viprebhyaḥ kāṃcanaṃ dadyātprītaye śaṃkarasya ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. For propitiating Śaṅkara, he should give gold to the Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.150.4 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛtvā naro devi labhate janmanaḥ phalam \|*  
*vipulāṃ kīrtimāyāti modate brahmaṇā priye \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O goddess, by doing thus the man attains the benefit of his birth. He gains extensive renown, O my beloved, and rejoices along with Brahmā.

## Chapter 151 - Greatness of Sāvitrīśvara Bhairava

## \|\| 1.151.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tasyaiva dakṣiṇe bhāge tṛtīyo bhairavaḥ sthita \|*  
*brahmakuṇḍasamīpe tu sāvitryā saṃpratiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. On the southern side thereof is stationed the third Bhairava. It was installed by Sāvitrī near Brahmakuṇḍa.

## \|\| 1.151.2 \|\|

*ārādhya tatra deveśaṃ devānāṃ prapitāmaham \|*  
*vāyubhakṣā nirāhārā toṣayāmāsa śaṃkaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. After propitiating the Lord of Devas, the great-grandfather of Devas, there, she propitiated Śaṅkara by her penance wherein she accepted no food except the intake of air.

## \|\| 1.151.3-6 \|\|

*tuṣṭaḥ prāheśvaro devi śaṃkarastāṃ varānanām \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yo'sminkuṃḍe naraḥ snātvā malliṃgaṃ pūjayiṣyati \|*  
*paurṇamāsyāṃ vidhānena gandhapuṣpādibhiḥ kramāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

*dāsyaṃ tasya varā niṣṭānmanasā'bhīsitāñchubhān \|\| 5 \|\|*

*mahāpātakayukto'pi mukto bhavati pātakaiḥ \|*  
*sarvakāmasamṛddhātmā sa bhūyādvṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. On being pleased, O goddess, Lord Śaṅkara said to that lady of excellent countenance: “I will grant all the splendid boons mentally wished for to that man who, on a Full-Moon day, takes the holy bath in this Kuṇḍa and worships my Liṅga with sweet scents, flowers etc. duly and in accordance with the injunctions. Even one afflicted with great sins shall be rid of those sins. Richly endowed with everything desired, he will become the Bull-emblemed Lord himself.”

## \|\| 1.151.7 \|\|

*ityevamuktvā deveśi tato'ntardhānamāgataḥ \|*  
*sāvitrī brahmaloke tu gatā saṃsthāpya śaṃkaram \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. After saying this, O goddess of Devas, he vanished. After installing Śaṅkara, Sāvitrī went to the world of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.151.8 \|\|

*iti saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ sāvitrīśamahodayam \|*  
*śṛṇuyādyastu matimānsa muktaḥ pātakairbhavet \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thus the greatness of Sāvitrīśa has been briefly described. An intelligent one who listens to this becomes rid of sins.

## Chapter 152 - Greatness of Nāradeśvara Bhairava

## \|\| 1.152.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tṛtīyo bhairavaḥ proktaścaturthaṃ bhairavaṃ śṛṇu \|*  
*brahmeśātpaścime bhāge dhanuṣāṃ tritaye sthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. The third Bhairava has been extolled. Now listen to the efficacy of the fourth Bhairava stationed within a distance of three Dhanus on the western side of Brahmeśa.

## \|\| 1.152.2 \|\|

*sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ sarva kāmapradaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*nāradeśvaranāmānaṃ sthāpitaṃ nāradena vai \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The deity subdues all sins. He bestows all desired things on men. He is named Nāradeśvara because the idol was installed by Nārada.

## \|\| 1.152.3-4 \|\|

*brahmaloke sthitaḥ pūrvaṃ nārado bhagavānṛṣiḥ \|*  
*tatra dṛṣṭvā mahāvīṇāṃ divyāṃ taṃtryayutai ryutām \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sarasvatyā vinirmuktāṃ brahmaloke mahāprabhām \|*  
*tenāsau kautukāviṣṭo vādayāmāsa tāṃ tadā \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. The great exalted sage Nārada was staying in the world of Brahmā. He saw the great divine Vīṇā (Lute) with ten thousand strings. It was left there by Sarasvatī. It was highly refulgent. On seeing it, Nārada became curious and played on it.

## \|\| 1.152.5 \|\|

*taṃtrībhyo vādyamānābhyo brāhmaṇāḥ patitā bhuvi \|*  
*sapta svarāste vikhyātā mūrcchitāḥ ṣaḍjakādayaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. While the strings were being played seven Brāhmaṇas fell down from there. They were well-known as Svaras (notes), Saḍja etc.

## \|\| 1.152.6-7 \|\|

*tāndṛṣṭvā vismayāviṣṭo muktvā vīṇāṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*papraccha devaṃ brahmāṇaṃ kimidaṃ kautukaṃ vibho \|\| 6 \|\|*

*vādyamānāsu tantrīṣu patitā brāhmaṇā bhuvi \|*  
*ka ete brāhmaṇā deva kiṃ mṛtā iva śerate \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. On seeing them Nārada was dismayed and he let off the lute. He then asked Brahmā: “O Lord, what is this miracle? While the strings were being played these Brāhmaṇas have fallen on the ground. O Lord, who are these Brāhmaṇas? Why do they lie down as though they are dead?”

## \|\| 1.152.8 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ete svarā mahābhāga mūrcchitāḥ patitā bhuvi \|*  
*ajñānavādanenaiva pāpaṃ jātaṃ tavādhunā \|\| 8 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

8\. O highly esteemed one, these are the seven Svaras who have fallen down unconscious. Because of your ignorance of playing properly, you have committed a great sin.

## \|\| 1.152.9 \|\|

*saptabrāhmaṇavidhvaṃsapātakaṃ te samā gatam \|*  
*tasmācchīghraṃ vraja mune prabhāsaṃ kṣetramuttamam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. You have committed the sin of the slaughter of seven Brāhmaṇas. Hence, O sage, hasten to the excellent holy spot of Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.152.10-12 \|\|

*samārādhaya deveśaṃ sarvapāpaviśuddhaye \|*  
*ityukto nāradastatra saṃtapya ca muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kṛtvā viṣādaṃ bahuśaḥ prabhāsaṃ kṣetramāgataḥ \|*  
*tatraiva brahmakuṇḍaṃ tu samāsādya prayatnataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*bhairavaṃ pūjayāmāsa divyābdānāṃ śataṃ priye \|*  
*tato niṣkalmaṣo bhūtvā gītajñaścābhavattathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. For the riddance of all the sins, ḍo propitiate the Lord of Devas.

On being told thus, Nārada expressed his regret frequently and grieved over this. He came to the holy spot of Prabhāsa. After reaching Brahmakuṇḍa, he assiduously adored Bhairava for a hundred years in accordance with the reckoning of Devas.

O my beloved, he became free from sins and became fully conversant with the art of singing.

## \|\| 1.152.13 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti talliṃgaṃ nāradeśvarabhairavam \|*  
*khyātaṃ loke mahādevi sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Ever since then, O goddess, the Liṅga became well-known as Nārādeśvara Bhairava in the world. O great goddess, it is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.152.14 \|\|

*ajñānādvādayedyastu vīṇāṃ caiva tathā svarān \|*  
*sa tatpātakaśuddhyarthaṃ tatra gacchenmaheśvari \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. One who, out of ignorance, wrongly plays on the Vīṇā and the notes, O Maheśvari (Maheśvarī?), shall go there for redemption from the sin thereof.

## \|\| 1.152.15 \|\|

*māghe māsi jitāhārastrikālaṃ yo'rcayettataḥ \|*  
*nāradeśaṃ bhairavaṃ sa svargarāmāmanoharaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He who observes fast in the month of Māgha and worships Nāradeśa Bhairava thrice a day, becomes charming unto beautiful damsels of heaven.

## Chapter 153 - Greatness of Hiraṇyeśvara (Hiraṇya-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.153.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi hiraṇyeśvaramuttamam \|*  
*brahmakuṇḍasya vāyavye dhanuṣāṃ dvitaye sthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ dāridryaughavināśanam \|*  
*kṛtasmarācca parato hyagnitīrthācca pūrvataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yameśvarācca nairṛtye samudrasyottare tathā \|*  
*tasya liṃgasya prāgbhāge brahmā tepe mahattapaḥ \|*  
*ārādhayāmāsa tadā devadevaṃ trilocanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tatastuṣṭo mahādevo brahmanbrūhi varo mama \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the excellent shrine of Hiraṇyeśvara situated within a distance of two Dhanus to the north-west of Brahmakunda \[Brahmakuṇḍa?\].

It is destructive of all sins and dispels all sorts of impoverished states. It is on the west of Kṛtasmara and on the east of Agnitīrtha.

It is on the south-west of Yameśvara and on the north of the ocean. Brahmā performed a great penance on the eastern side of the Liṅga. Then he propitiated the Three-eyed Lord of Devas.

## \|\| 1.153.5 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭo'si me deva yāja yāmīti me matiḥ \|*  
*sthānaṃ ca yanmahāpuṇyaṃ tanmamākhyātumarhasi \|\| 5 \|\|*

Then the great Lord who was pleased said: “O Brahmā, tell me what boon you want.”

Brahmā said:

5\. O Lord, if you are pleased with me, it is my intention that I should perform a Yajña. It behoves you to recommend to me a highly meritorious spot for the purpose.

## \|\| 1.153.6 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*kṛtasmarādbrahmakuṃḍaṃ yameśātsāgarāvadhi \|*  
*etadaṃtaramāsādya pāpī cāpi vimucyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

6\. Even a great sinner becomes relieved of sins if he be staying in the intervening space between Kṛtasmara and Brahmakuṇḍa and between Yameśa and the ocean.

## \|\| 1.153.7 \|\|

*vahedviṣuvatī tatra sadā puṇyātmanāṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*yatra tatra kuru vibho manasā te yathepsitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O great Lord, You should do whatever is desired by you and delights your mind at the place where the river Viṣuvatī always flows for the benefit of the meritorious men.

## \|\| 1.153.8 \|\|

*ityuktaḥ sa tadā brahmā prārebhe yajñamuttamam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On being told thus Brahmā started his excellent Yajña.

## \|\| 1.153.9 \|\|

*tato bhāgārthino devā indrādyāstatra cāgatāḥ \|*  
*ṛṣayo bhāgakāmāstu sarve tatra samāgatāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thereupon, Indra and other Devas seeking their shares came there. All the sages who too desired their shares came there.

## \|\| 1.153.10 \|\|

*tato yajñāgatebhyaḥ sa dakṣiṇāmadadātpunaḥ \|*  
*tato'tha dakṣiṇā kṣīṇā dīyamānā yaśasvini \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thereupon, he (Brahmā) gave Dakṣiṇā to those who came to the Yajña. Then, O lady of renown, on being distributed thus, the Dakṣiṇā dwindled.

## \|\| 1.153.11 \|\|

*tatobrahmā bahūdvigno dadhyau vai manasā tadā \|*  
*baddhāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā idaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then Brahmā became extremely distressed. He began to meditate mentally. With palms joined in reverence he spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.153.12-13 \|\|

*bhagavanvai virūpākṣa kraturnaiva samāpyate \|*  
*dakṣiṇāhai nyato deva na yāti paripūrṇatām \|\| 12 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇāsahitāḥ sarve yathā yāṃti tathā kuru \|*  
*pitāmahavacaḥ śrutvā kṛtvā dhyānaṃ tadā mayā \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13a. “O Lord Virūpākṣa, the Yajña cannot be concluded. Due to shortage of Dakṣiṇā the Yajña will not be complete and perfect. Kindly do see to this that all go back receiving adequate Dakṣiṇā.”

13b. On hearing the words of Pitāmaha, I began to meditate.

## \|\| 1.153.14 \|\|

*smṛtā sarasvatī devī devānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|*  
*āgatā sā mahāpuṇyā uktā devī mayā tadā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Goddess Sarasvatī was remembered with a desire for the welfare of Devas. That highly meritorious goddess came and the Devī was told by me then:

## \|\| 1.153.15 \|\|

*padmayonerdhanaṃ kṣīṇaṃ kraturvai na samāpyate \|*  
*tasmānmama prasādena bhava kāñcanavāhinī \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. “The monetary position of the Lotus-born One is weak. The Kratu could not be concluded. Hence with my favour, be one flowing with gold.”

## \|\| 1.153.16 \|\|

*sarasvatyāstataḥ srota utthitaṃ paścimāmukham \|*  
*kāñcanānāṃ tu padmāni ucchritāni sahasraśaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thereupon the flow of Sarasvatī deflected towards the west. Thousands of flowers of gold sprouted up.

## \|\| 1.153.17 \|\|

*kāñcanena pravāheṇa toyaṃ sārasvataṃ śubham \|*  
*daityasūdanamāsādya agnitīrthāvadhi priye \|*  
*pūrayāmāsa padmaiśca koṭiśaśca samaṃtataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. By the flow of gold, the splendid waters of Sarasvatī, O my beloved, filled with millions of lotuses the area between the Daityasūḍana shrine and Agnitīrtha.

## \|\| 1.153.18 \|\|

*kāñcanāni tu tānyeva dattvā vipreṣu dakṣiṇām \|*  
*yajñaṃ nirvartayāmāsa hṛṣṭo brahmā dvijaiḥ saha \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Brahmā concluded the Yajña by gifting those golden lotuses to the Brāhmaṇas (as Dakṣinā). Brahmā was delighted along with the Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.153.19 \|\|

*śeṣāṇi yāni padmāni tāni niḥkṣipya bhūtale \|*  
*tadūrdhvaṃ sthāpayāmāsa ligaṃ tu kanake śvaram \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. With the remaining lotuses, he filled the ground and installed the Kanakeśvara Liṅga above it.

## \|\| 1.153.20 \|\|

*tatra liṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya sarvadevanamaskṛtam \|*  
*ṛṣibhyo dakṣiṇāṃ prādādekaikasya yathākramam \|*  
*kāñcanānāṃ ca padmānāṃ pratyekamayutaṃ dadau \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After installing the Liṅga of the Lord bowed to by all the Devas, he gave each of the sages ten thousand golden lotuses as monetary gift.

## \|\| 1.153.21 \|\|

*tataḥ śeṣāṇi padmāni nihitāni dharātale \|*  
*brahmakuṇḍasya madhye tu nāpuṇyo labhate naraḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The remaining lotuses were placed under the ground in the middle of Brahmakuṇḍa. A man of no merits does not get them.

## \|\| 1.153.22 \|\|

*tatkuṇḍatoyamadyāpi nānāvarṇaṃ pradṛśyate \|*  
*tatrādhaḥ padmasaṃyogānnīraṃ svarṇāyate kṣaṇāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Even today the water of that Kuṇḍa appears of variegated colour. There, due to the contact of the lotuses beneath, the water turns into gold in a moment.

## \|\| 1.153.23 \|\|

*hiraṇmayāni padmāni adhaḥ kṛtvā prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*liṃgamūrdhvaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya svayaṃ pūjitavāṃstadā \|*  
*hiraṇyakamalairdivyairhiraṇyeśastato'bhavat \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. After keeping the golden lotuses and installing the Liṅga above, Prajāpati (Brahmā) himself worshipped it. Due to the golden lotuses the deity became Hiraṇyeśa.

## \|\| 1.153.24 \|\|

*sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ tathā dāridryanāśanam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā hiraṇmayeśānaṃ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The deity suppresses all sins and destroys poverty. By viewing Lord Hiraṇyeśa, one is relieved of all sins.

## \|\| 1.153.25 \|\|

*māgha māse caturdaśyāṃ yastalliṃgaṃ prapūjayet \|*  
*pūjitaṃ tena sakalaṃ brahmāṇḍaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. If a devotee worships that Liṅga on the fourteenth lunar day in the month of Māgha, it is as good as the entire Brahmāṇḍa including all mobile and immobile beings, has been worshipped by him.

## \|\| 1.153.26 \|\|

*sarvadānāni dattāni sarve devāśca toṣitāḥ \|*  
*brahmāṇḍaṃ tena dattaṃ syādyena talliṃgamarcitam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. A person by whom that Liṅga has been adored is considered as one who has gifted everything and as one who has propitiated all the Devas, as one who has gifted the whole Cosmos.

## \|\| 1.153.27 \|\|

*etanmayā te kathitaṃ snehena varavarṇini \|*  
*na kasyacinmayā'khyātaṃ mahāgopyaṃ varānane \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O lady of excellent complexion, this has been narrated to you out of love. This has never been narrated to anyone else by me. O lady of excellent countenance, it is a great secret.

## \|\| 1.153.28 \|\|

*ya idaṃ śṛyuyādbhaktyā paṭhedvā bhaktisaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*sa gaccheddevalokaṃ tu muktaḥ sarvaistu pātakaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. One who devoutly listens to this, who reads this with devotion, shall be rid of all sins and shall go to the world of Devas.

## \|\| 1.153.29 \|\|

*iti te cātivikhyātāḥ pavitrāḥ pañca bhairavāḥ \|*  
*brahmakuṇḍasamīpasthāḥ kathitāstava sundari \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Thus, O beautiful lady, the highly famous five Sacred Bhairavas stationed in the vicinity of Brahmakuṇḍa have been narrated to you.

## Chapter 154 - Greatness of Gāyatrīśvara (Gāyatrī-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.154.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi liṃgaṃ pāpavimocanam \|*  
*hiraṇyeśvaravāyavye dhanuṣāṃ tritaye sthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*pāpaghnaṃ sarvajaṃtūnāṃ darśanātsparśanādapi \|*  
*ādyaṃ liṃgaṃ mahādevi gāyatryā saṃpratiṣṭhitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*talliṃgaṃ samanuprāpya gāyatrīṃ japate tu yaḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇastu śucirbhūtvā mucyate duṣpratigrahāt \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to a shrine to the north-west of Hiraṇyeśvara where the sin-relieving Liṅga is present within a distance of three Dhanus.

It dispels the sins of all creatures who view or touch it. It is the first Liṅga, O great goddess, installed by Gāyatrī.

A Brāhmaṇa who goes to that Liṅga and repeats the Gāyatrī Mantra after purifying himself adequately, becomes relieved from the sin of Duṣpratigraha (acceptance of gifts from a defiled person).

## \|\| 1.154.4 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhasya pūrṇimāyāṃ tu daṃpatī yastu bhojayet \|*  
*paridhāpya yathāśaktyā daurbhāgyairmucyate naraḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. A man who feeds a couple of Brāhmaṇas after presenting them with garments in accordance with his capacity on the Full-Moon day in the month of Jyeṣṭha, becomes rid of misfortunes.

## \|\| 1.154.5 \|\|

*gaṃdhapuṣpopahāraiśca paurṇamāsyāṃ tu yo'rcayet \|*  
*brāhmaṇyaṃ jāyate tasya sapta janmāni suṃdari \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. If a devotee adores with scents, flowers and other offerings on the Full-Moon day, O beautiful lady, he retains his Brāhmaṇa-hood in seven successive births.

## \|\| 1.154.6 \|\|

*ityevaṃ kathitaṃ devi māhātmyaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*brahmakuṇḍaprasādena sārātsārataraṃ priye \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Thus, O goddess, the sin-destroying greatness has been narrated. O my beloved, it is the most essential of all.

## Chapter 155 - Greatness of Ratneśvara (Ratna-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.155.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi ratneśvaramanuttamam \|*  
*tatra taptvā tapo devi viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|*  
*sthāpitaṃ tatra talliṃgaṃ sarvakāmapradaṃ priye \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ratnakuṃḍe naraḥ snātvā yastaṃ pūjayate sadā \|*  
*sarvopacārairbhaktyā sa prāpnuyādīpsitaṃ phalam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*atra kṛtvā tapo ghoraṃ kṛṣṇenāmitatejasā \|*  
*prāptaṃ sudarśanaṃ cakraṃ sarvadaityāntakārakam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the excellent shrine of Ratneśvara. O my beloved goddess, after performing penance there, the powerful Viṣṇu installed that Liṅga that grants all desires.

A man who always takes his bath in Ratnakuṇḍa and devoutly worship with all formalities, shall attain the desired benefit.

It was by performing a very severe penance here that the Sudarśana discus that causes the destruction of all Daityas, was acquired by Kṛṣṇa (Viṣṇu) of unmeasured radiance.

## \|\| 1.155.4 \|\|

*etatsthānaṃ mahādevi sadā priyataraṃ mama \|*  
*vasāmi tatra deveśi pralaye'pi na saṃtyaje \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O great goddess, this spot is always very dear to me. O goddess of Devas, I stay there even during the time of Pralaya. I do not desert it.

## \|\| 1.155.5 \|\|

*smṛtaṃ tadvaiṣṇavaṃ kṣetraṃ nāmnā devi sudarśanam \|*  
*dhanvaṃtarāṇi ṣaṭtriṃśatsamaṃtātparimaṇḍalam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O goddess, that holy spot pertaining to Viṣṇu is known by the name Sudarśana. The area all around extends to thirty-six Dhanus.

## \|\| 1.155.6 \|\|

*etadantaramāsādya ye kecitprāṇino'dhamāḥ \|*  
*mṛtāḥ kālavaśāddevi te yāsyaṃti paraṃ padam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Any living being, even of the lowest category, that dies within this area when death becomes due, O goddess, shall attain the greatest region (liberation).

## \|\| 1.155.7 \|\|

*kāṃcanaṃ tatra garuḍaṃ pītāni vasanāni ca \|*  
*viṣṇumuddiśya yo dadyātsa tu yātrāphalaṃ labhet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. A pilgrim who makes the gift of gold replica of Garuḍa and yellow garments with Viṣṇu in view shall attain the benefit of the pilgrimage.

## Chapter 156 - Greatness of Garuḍeśvara (Garuḍa-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.156.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi vainateyapratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*ratneśvarāduttarato dhanuṣāṃ tritaye sthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*vainateyaśca deveśi jñātvā kṣetraṃ tu vaiṣṇavam \|*  
*liṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhayāmāsa sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yastaṃ pūjayate bhaktyā paṃcamyāṃ tu vidhānataḥ \|*  
*na viṣaṃ kramate tasya sapta janmāni sarpajam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*paṃcāmṛtena saṃsnāpya pūjayitvā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*prāpnuyātsakalaṃ puṇyaṃ modate divi devavat \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the shrine installed by Garuḍa, the son of Vinatā. It is situated within a distance of three Dhanus to the north of Ratneśvara. After realizing that the holy place is associated with Viṣṇu, O goddess of Devas, Vainateya installed the Liṅga that destroys all sins.

If a pilgrim duly worships it on the fifth lunar day in accordance with the injunctions, no serpent poison becomes effective in his case for a period of seven births.

If a devotee bathes the Liṅga with Pañcāmṛta and worships it in accordance with the injunctions, he shaīl attain the entire merit, O goddess. He rejoices in heaven like Devas.

## Chapter 157 - Greatness of Satyabhāmeśvara (Satyabhāmā-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.157.1-5 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi satyabhāmeśvaraṃ śubham \|*  
*ratneśvarāddakṣiṇe tu dhanuṣāṃtaramāsthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ sthāpitaṃ satyabhāmayā \|*  
*kṛṣṇasya kāntayā devi rūpaudāryasametayā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*snātvā tadvaiṣṇavaṃ sthānaṃ nṛṇāṃ pātakanāśanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*māghe māsi tṛtīyāyāṃ nārī vā puruṣo'pi vā \|*  
*yastaṃ pūjayate bhaktyā sa muktaḥ pātakairbhavet \|\| 4 \|\|*

*daurbhāgyaduḥkhaśokebhyastathā vighnaiśca duḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*mucyate nātra saṃdehaḥ satyabhāmānvito bhavet \|\| 5 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-5. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the splendid shrine of Satyabhāmeśvara situated within a distance of a Dhanus to the south of Ratneśvara.

It suppresses all sins. It was installed by Satyabhāmā, the beloved wife of Śrīkṛṣṇa, endowed with excellent beauty and munificence.

The holy spot associated with Viṣṇu is destructive of sins of men who, after going there, take holy ablution.

A man or a woman who devoutly worships the deity on the third lunar day in the month of Māgha shall surely be rid of sins.

One who is miserable through misfortunes, grief and distress as well as obstacles shall also be relieved. There is no doubt that he shall be endowed with Satya (Truth), Bhā (Refulgence), Mā (Lakṣmī, glory).

## Chapter 158 - Glory of Anaṅgeśvara (Anaṅga-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.158.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi anaṃgeśvaramuttamam \|*  
*ratneśvarādagrataḥsthaṃ dhanuṣāntaramāsthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sthāpitaṃ kāmadevena talliṃgaṃ viṣṇusūnunā \|*  
*jñātvā tadvaiṣṇavaṃ sthānaṃ kalau pātakanāśanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā pūjayitvā tu kāmadevasamo bhavet \|*  
*svargavidyādharīṇāṃ ca jāyate cittamohakaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the excellent shrine of Anaṅgeśvara stationed within a distance of a Dhanus in front of Ratneśvara.

After realizing that the place is a great holy spot dispelling sins in Kali Age, Kāmadeva, the son of Viṣṇu, installed that Liṅga.

One who views the deity and worships it, shall be equal to Kāmadeva, one who enchants the minds of heavenly damsels and Vidyādharīs.

## \|\| 1.158.4-6 \|\|

*tasyānvaye'pi na bhavetkurūpo durbhago'pi vā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tatrānaṃgatrayodaśyāṃ vratena varavarṇini \|*  
*viśeṣārādhanaṃ tatra janmasāphalyakāraṇam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*śayyādānaṃ tu dātavyaṃ tatra viprāya śīline \|*  
*viśeṣādviṣṇubhaktāya samyagyātrāphalaṃ labhet \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. No one in his family shall ever be ugly and unfortunate.

O lady of excellent complexion, if the holy vow is observed on the thirteenth lunar day associated with Anaṅga with special propitiation, it makes the birth fruitful. The devotee should make the gift of a bed to a Brāhmaṇa of good conduct, especially a devotee of Viṣṇu. He shall obtain the benefit of the pilgrimage.

## Chapter 159 - Greatness of Ratneśvara (Ratna-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.159.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi ratnakuṇḍamanuttamam \|*  
*ratneśāddakṣiṇe bhāge dhanuṣāṃ saptake sthitam \|*  
*mahāpāpopaśamanaṃ viṣṇunā nirmitaṃ svayam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*aṣṭakoṭīstu tīrthāni bhūdyo'ntarikṣagāṇi tu \|*  
*samānīya tu kṛṣṇena tatra kṣiptāni bhūriśaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*gaṇānāṃ koṭirekā tu tatkuṇḍaṃ rakṣati priye \|*  
*kalau yuge tu saṃprāpte duṣprāpyamakṛtātmabhiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, a pilgrim should go to the excellent Ratnakuṇḍa, O great goddess. It is situated within a distance of seven Dhanus to the south of Ratneśa. It is destructive of great sins and was created by Viṣṇu himself.

Eight crores of Tīrthas existing on the earth, heaven and intermediate space were brought by Kṛṣṇa and caused to flow there.

O my beloved, a crore of Gaṇas guard that Kuṇḍa (holy pit). After the advent of Kali Age, it becomes inaccessible to those who have no control over themselves.

## \|\| 1.159.4 \|\|

*tatra snātvā mahādevi vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā \|*  
*prāpnuyādaśvamedhasya phalaṃ śataguṇottaram \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. By taking bath therein, O great goddess, and by performing rites laid down by injunctions, one will acquire the benefit of a horse-sacrifice more than a hundred times thereof.

## \|\| 1.159.5 \|\|

*ekādaśyāṃ viśeṣeṇa piṃḍaṃ tatra pradāpayet \|*  
*akṣayyāṃ tṛptimāyāṃti pitarastasya bhāmini \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O beautiful lady, the devotee should offer balls of rice especially on the Ekādaśī (eleventh lunar day) day. The Pitṛs will have unending satisfaction.

## \|\| 1.159.6 \|\|

*kuryājjāgaraṇaṃ tatra ekādaśyāṃ vidhānataḥ \|*  
*vāñchitaṃ labhate devi yadi śraddhā dṛḍhā bhavet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O goddess, the devotee should keep awake on the Ekādaśī day in accordance with the injunctions. If he be of steady, unwavering faith, he will get what is desired.

## \|\| 1.159.7 \|\|

*deyāni pītavastrāṇi tathā dhenuḥ payasvinī \|*  
*tatra viṣṇuṃ samuddiśya samyagyātrāphalāptaye \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In order to get the full benefit of proper performance of the pilgrimage, the devotee should make the gift of a milch cow and yellow garments with Viṣṇu in view.

## \|\| 1.159.8 \|\|

*hemakuṇḍaṃ kṛte proktaṃ tretāyāṃ raupyanāmakam \|*  
*dvāpare cakrakuṃḍaṃ tu ratnakuṃḍaṃ kalau smṛtam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. It is called Hemakuṇḍa in Kṛta age. It is named Raupya (Kuṇḍa) in Tretā Age; Cakra-kuṇḍa in Dvāpara Age; and it is remembered as Ratna-kuṇḍa in Kali Age.

## \|\| 1.159.9 \|\|

*pātālavāhinīgaṃgā srotāṃsi tatra bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*samānītāni hariṇā tatra tiṣṭhaṃti bhāmini \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O beautiful lady, many of the currents of the Pātālavāhinī Gaṅgā, flowing through Pātāla were brought there by Hari and they exist therein now.

## \|\| 1.159.10 \|\|

*tatra snānena deveśi sarvatīrthābhiṣecanam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A bath there is akin to the holy ablution in all the Tīrthas, O goddess of Devas.

## Chapter 160 - Greatness Of Raivantakarāja Bhaṭṭāraka (Raivantaka-Rāja)

## \|\| 1.160.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi rājabhaṭṭārakaṃ param \|*  
*raivantakaṃ sūryaputramaśvārūḍhaṃ mahābalam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*saṃsthitaṃ kṣetramadhye tu sāvitryā nairṛte priye \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā mānavo devi sarvāpadbhyo vimucyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ravivāreṇa saptamyāṃ yastaṃ pūjayate naraḥ \|*  
*tasyā'nvaye'pi no devi daridrī jāyate naraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena tamevārādhayenmanāk \|*  
*nirvighnaṃ kṣetravāsārthaṃ rājā vā'śvavivṛddhaye \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the great shrine of the great son of the Sun-god, Rājabhaṭṭāraka Raivantaka. He is highly powerful and is represented as seated on a horse. (The icon is equestrian.)

O my beloved, he is stationed in the middle of the holy spot to the south-west of Sāvitrī. By viewing him, O fair lady, a man is rid of all disasters.

If a man worships him on the seventh lunar day coinciding with a Sunday, O goddess, no one in his family becomes destitute.

Hence, one should endeavour to propitiate him in every respect for an obstacle-free residence in the holy spot (in the case of an ordinary man) or for the increase of cavalry forces in the case of a king.

## Chapter 161 - Greatness of Ananteśvara (Ananta-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.161.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi tasya dakṣiṇataḥ sthitam \|*  
*īśāne lakṣmaṇeśācca dhanuṣāṃ ṣoḍaśe priye \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ananteśvaranāmānamanantena pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*nāgarājena deveśi jñātvā kṣetraṃ tu pāvanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yastu taṃ pūjayeddevi paṃcamyāṃ phālgune site \|*  
*pañcopacāravidhinā jitāhāro jitendriyaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*na taṃ daśaṃti phaṇino daśa varṣāṇi paṃca ca \|*  
*viṣaṃ na kramate devi dehe tvacarameva vā \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the shrine named Ananteśvara situated to the south of (Rājabhaṭṭāraka) and within a distance of sixteen Dhanus to the north-east of Lakṣmaṇeśa. O my beloved, after realizing that the holy spot is very sacred, it was installed by Ananta (Śeṣa), the king of serpents. O goddess of Devas, a devotee should worship the deity on the fifth lunar day in the bright half of the month of Phālguna. He should control his diet and sense-organs and worship by means of the five Upacāras (Means of Service). For the next fifteen years, serpents will not bite him. (Even if they bite) the poison will not spread in the body.

## \|\| 1.161.5-6 \|\|

*tasmāttaṃ pūjayedyatnātpaṃcamyāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tatrānaṃtavrataṃ kāryaṃ madhupāyasasaṃyutam \|*  
*pāyasaṃ madhusaṃyuktaṃ deyaṃ viprāya bhojanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Hence, one should assiduously worship the deity especially on the fifth lunar day. On that day the rite of Ananta Vrata should be performed along with the preparation of milk pudding with honey. Food consisting of milk pudding and honey should be given to Brāhmaṇas.

## Chapter 162 - Greatness of Aṣṭakuleśvara (Aṣṭakula-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.162.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi tasmāddakṣiṇataḥ sthitam \|*  
*lakṣmaṇeśācca pūrvasmiṃlliṃgamaṣṭakuleśvaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ mahāviṣapraṇāśanam \|*  
*pūjitaṃ siddhagandharvairvāñchitārthapradāyakam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yastaṃ pūjayate martyaḥ kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ vidhānataḥ \|*  
*sa muktaḥ pātakairghorairnāgaloke mahīyate \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the shrine of Aṣṭakuleśvara stationed to the south thereof (i.e. of Ananteśvara) and to the east of Lakṣmaṇeśa.

This Liṅga suppresses all sins and eliminates great poison. It is adored by Siddhas and Gandharvas and it grants desired objects.

A man who worships this deity on the eighth lunar day in a dark half in accordance with the injunctions, shall be rid of all terrible sins. He is honoured in the region of Nāgas.

## Chapter 163 - Greatness of Nāsatyeśvara (Nāsatya-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.163.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi tasmātpūrveṇa saṃsthitam \|*  
*nāsatyeśvaranāmānaṃ mahā kalmaṣanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the shrine named Nāsatyeśvara stationed on the east of it. It is destructive of great sins.

## Chapter 164 - Greatness of Aśvineśvara (Aśvina-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.164.1-5 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi tasmātpūrveṇa saṃsthitam \|*  
*mahāpāpaughaśamanaṃ pūjitaṃ sarvakāmadam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*aśvineśvaranāmānaṃ dhanuṣāṃ paṃcake sthitam \|*  
*sarvarogapraśamanaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ sarvārthasādhakam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ye kecidrogiṇo loke teṣāṃ tadbheṣajaṃ mahat \|*  
*māghamāse dvitīyāyāṃ darśanaṃ tasya durlabham \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tasmātpaśyecca tadbhaktyā yadi śreyo'bhikāṃkṣitam \|*  
*mahāpāpaughaśamanaṃ pūjitaṃ sarvakāmadam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*iti liṅgadvayaṃ devi sūryaputrapratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*tasminneva dine paśyetsaṃyatātmā narottamaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-5. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the shrine named Aśvineśvara stationed within a distance of five Dhanus to the east thereof. It suppresses a series of great sins. On being adored, it fulfills all desires. On being viewed, it suppresses all ailments and facilitates the acquisition of all objects.

It is a great antidote to all who suffer from ailment in the world.

Viewing it on the second lunar day in the month of Māgha is very rare. Hence if welfare is desired, one should devoutly view it. On being adored, it suppresses all great sins and fulfills all desires.

Thus, O goddess, these are two Liṅgas installed by the sons of the Sun. An excellent man with full control over himself should view them on the same day.

## Chapter 165 - Greatness of Sāvitrī

## \|\| 1.165.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi sāvitrīṃ lokamātaram \|*  
*mahā pāpapraśamanīṃ someśādīśadiksthitām \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the shrine of Sāvitrī, the mother of the worlds, who suppresses great sins. She is installed on the north-eastern side of Someśa.

## \|\| 1.165.2 \|\|

*saṃyatātmā naraḥ paśyettatra tāṃ niyatātmavān \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. A man who has controlled himself and restrained his senses shall be able to view her.

## \|\| 1.165.3 \|\|

*brahmaṇā yaṣṭukāmena sāvitrī sahadharmiṇī \|*  
*kṛtā tāṃ balato jñātvā gāyatrīṃ kopamāviśat \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On coming to know that Brahmā, desirous of performing a sacrifice, has married perforce another woman as co-wife, Sāvitrī got angry with Gāyatrī.

## \|\| 1.165.4 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃtyajya sā devī brahmāṇaṃ kamalodbhavam \|*  
*sapatnīroṣasantaptā prabhāsaṃ kṣetramāśritā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Then that goddess (Sāvitrī) abandoned Brahmā born of the lotus and resorted to the holy place of Prabhāsa. She continued to be distressed on account of the anger of her cowife.

## \|\| 1.165.5 \|\|

*tapaḥ karoti vipulaṃ devairapi suduḥsaham \|*  
*tatra sthale sthitā devī sā'dyāpi priyadarśanā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The fair lady of pleasing appearance stays in that spot even today and performs an elaborate penance unbearable even to Devas.

## \|\| 1.165.6 \|\|

*śrīdevyuvāca \|*  
*kimarthaṃ sā parityaktā sāvitrī brahmaṇā purā \|*  
*gāyatrī ca kathaṃ prāptā kena cāsya niveditā \|\| 6 \|\|*

Śrī Devī said:

6\. Why was that Sāvitrī abandoned by Brahmā earlier? How was Gāyatrī obtained (by him)? By whom was she offered?

## \|\| 1.165.7 \|\|

*kīdṛśīṃ tāṃ ca gāyatrīṃ labdhavānpadmasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*yastāṃ patnīṃ samutsṛjya tasyāmeva mano dadhau \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Of what sort was Gāyatrī whom the Lotus-born One obtained (and how was it) that he abandoned his (first) wife and became interested in her?

## \|\| 1.165.8 \|\|

*kasya sā duhitā deva kimarthaṃ ca vivāhitā \|*  
*etanme kautukaṃ sarvaṃ yathāvadvaktumarhasi \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Whose daughter was she, O Lord? For what purpose the marriage was celebrated? This is my curiosity. It behoves you to clarify it.

## \|\| 1.165.9 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi sāvitryāścaritaṃ mahat \|*  
*yathā sā brahmaṇā tyaktā gāyatrī ca vivāhitā \|\| 9 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

9\. Listen, O goddess. I shall explain to you the great story of Sāvitrī as to how she was abandoned by Brahmā and how Gāyatrī was wedded.

## \|\| 1.165.10-13 \|\|

*purā buddhiḥ samutpannā brahmaṇo'vyaktajanmanaḥ \|*  
*iti vedā mayā proktā yajñārthaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*yajñaiḥ saṃtarpitā devā vṛṣṭiṃ dāsyaṃti bhūtale \|*  
*tataścauṣadhayaḥ sarvā bhaviṣyaṃti dharātale \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tasmātsaṃjāyate śukraṃ śukrātsṛṣṭiḥ pravartate \|*  
*sṛṣṭyarthaṃ sarvalokānāṃ tato yajñaṃ karomyaham \|\| 12 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā māṃ yajña āsaktaṃ ye ca viprā dharātale \|*  
*te yajñānpracariṣyaṃti śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

10-13. Formerly, this idea occurred to Brahmā, born of the Unmanifest One. ‘Undoubtedly these Vedas were enunciated by me thus, for the sake of the Yajñas. On being propitiated by means of Yajñas, Devas will shower rain on the earth. Thereupon, all herbs and vegetation will crop up on the earth. Therefrom Śukra (semen) will be generated and the process of creation will get initiated through Śukra. Therefore, I shall perform Yajña for the creation of all the worlds. On seeing me ardently interested in Yajñas, Brāhmaṇas who are on the earth shall perform hundreds and thousands of Yajñas.’

## \|\| 1.165.14 \|\|

*evaṃ sa niścayaṃ kṛtvā yajñārthaṃ surasuṃdari \|*  
*tīrthaṃ niveśayāmāsa puṣkaraṃ nāma nāmataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thus, O beautiful lady among Suras, he resolved to perform Yajñas. For that purpose he established the holy place named Puṣkara.

## \|\| 1.165.15-16 \|\|

*yajñavāṭo mahāṃstatra āsīttasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*tatra devarṣayaḥ sarve devāḥ sendrapurogamāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*samāyātā mahādevi yajñe paitāmahe tadā \|*  
*puṇyāste'pi dvijaśreṣṭhāstatrartvijaḥ prajajñire \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. O great goddess, a great sacrificial pandal was raised on behalf of that noble-souled one. All the celestial sages and Devas along with Indra as their leader arrived there for the Yajña of Pitāmaha. Holy and excellent Brāhmaṇas became the Ṛtviks (sacrificial priests).

## \|\| 1.165.17 \|\|

*sāvitrī lokajananī patnī tasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*gṛhakārye samāsaktā dīkṣā kālavyatikramāt \|*  
*adhvaryuṇā samāhūtā sāvitrī vākyamabravīt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Sāvitrī, the wife of that noble-souled one and the mother of the worlds, was engaged in domestic tasks. As the time for initiation elapsed, she was summoned by the Adhvaryu. Thereupon Sāvitrī spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.165.18 \|\|

*sāvitryuvāca \|*  
*adyāpi na kṛto veṣo na gṛhe gṛhamaṇḍanam \|*  
*lakṣmīrnādyāpi saṃprāptā na bhavānī na jāhnavī \|\| 18 \|\|*

Sāvitrī said:

18\. As yet I have not completed the make-up and embellishment in the house. Lakṣmī has not come till now, nor Bhavānī nor Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 1.165.19 \|\|

*na svāhā na svadhā caiva tathā caivāpyaruṃdhatī \|*  
*indrāṇī devapatnyo'nyāḥ kathamekākinī vraje \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Neither Svāhā, nor Svadhā, nor Arundhatī, nor Indrāṇī nor the other wives of Devas. How can I go (come) alone?

## \|\| 1.165.20-22 \|\|

*uktaḥ pitāmaho gatvā pulastyena mahātmanā \|*  
*sāvitrī deva nāyāti prasaktā gṛhakarmaṇi \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tvatpatnī kimidaṃ karma phalena saṃpravartate \|*  
*tacchrutvā dīkṣito vācaṃ śikhī muṃḍī mṛgājinī \|\| 21 \|\|*

*patnīkopena saṃtaptaḥ prāha devaṃ puraṃdaram \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-21a. Pulastya, the noble-souled sage, went and told Brahmā: “O Lord, Sāvitrī is engaged in domestic tasks. She has not come. This is your wife. What sort of rite is this? Can it bear any fruit?”

21b-22. God Brahmā, the initiated one, with a head with a tuft of hair behind and clad in the hide of a deer, became angry with his wife and spoke to Indra:

## \|\| 1.165.23 \|\|

*gaccha madvacanācchakra patnīmanyāṃ kutaścana \|*  
*gṛhītvā śīghramāgaccha na syātkālātyayo yathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. “O Śakra, this is my directive. Fetch another wife from somewhere and return quickly so that there will be no transgression of the (specific) time (for this Yajña).”

## \|\| 1.165.24-26 \|\|

*jagāma balahā tūrṇaṃ vacanātparameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*apaśyamānaḥ kāṃcitstrīṃ yā yogyā haṃsavāhane \|\| 24 \|\|*

*atha śāpādbibhītena sahasrākṣeṇa dhīmatā \|*  
*dṛṣṭā gopālakanyaikā rūpayauvanaśālinī \|\| 25 \|\|*

*bibhratī tatra pūrṇaṃ sā kumbhaṃ kanyetyacodayat \|*  
*tāṃ gṛhītvā tataḥ śakraḥ samāyādyatra dīkṣitaḥ \|*  
*devadevaścaturvaktro viṣṇurudrasamanvitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. At the behest of Parameṣṭhin (i.e. Brahmā) the Slayer of Bala (i. e. Indra) hurried out but could not see any woman fit to be the wife of the Swan-vehicled One (i.e. Brahmā).

The intelligent Thousand-eyed One became afraid of being cursed by Brahmā. A beautiful and youthful cowherd lass was seen by him. She was carrying a full pitcher. Inferring that she was a virgin, he requested her. Taking her with him, Śakra came to the place where the Four-faced Lord of Devas was seated as the initiated one accompanied by Viṣṇu and Rudra.

## \|\| 1.165.27 \|\|

*saṃpradānaṃ tu kṛtavānkanyāyā madhusūdanaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The Slayer of Madhu (i.e. Viṣṇu) gave the virgin in marriage (to Brahmā.)

## \|\| 1.165.28 \|\|

*preritaḥ śaṃkareṇaiva brahmā devarṣibhistathā \|*  
*pariṇīyatāṃ tato dīkṣāṃ tasyāścakre yathātmanaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Urged by Śaṅkara himself as well as by the celestial sages, Brahmā married her and performed the rites of initiation in her case as in his own case.

## \|\| 1.165.29 \|\|

*tataḥ pravartito yajñaḥ sarvakāmasamanvitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Thereupon the Yajña equipped with everything desirable was begun.

## \|\| 1.165.30 \|\|

*atrirhotārcikastatra pulastyo'dhvaryureva ca \|*  
*udgātā'tho marīciśca brahmāhaṃ surapuṃgavaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. There Atri was made the Hotṛ, reciter of Ṛgvedic hymns, Pulastya became the Adhvaryu, Marīci the Udgātṛ, and I, the leading Sura, became the Brahmā (presiding priest).

## \|\| 1.165.31-33 \|\|

*sanatkumārapramukhāḥ sadasyāstasya nirmitāḥ \|*  
*vastrairābharaṇairyuktā mukuṭairaṃgulīyakaiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*bhūṣitā bhūṣaṇopetā ekaikasya pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*trayastrayaḥ pṛṣṭhato'nye te caivaṃ ṣoḍaśartvijaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*proktā bhavadbhi ryajñe'sminnanugṛhyo'smi sarvadā \|*  
*patnī mameyaṃ gāyatrī yajñe'sminnanugṛhyatām \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. Those with Sanatkumāra as the chief one, were made the Sadasyas (members of sacrificial assembly). They had put on befitting garments and ornaments. They were adorned with crowns and rings and other ornaments. Behind everyone of these, there were three other Ṛtviks (priests). Thus there were sixteen Ṛtviks altogether. They were asked (by Brahmā): “I should be blessed by you throughout this Yajña. Let my wife Gāyatrī too be blessed in this Yajña.”

## \|\| 1.165.34-35 \|\|

*mṛduvastradharāṃ sākṣātkṣaumavastrāvaguṇṭhitām \|*  
*niṣkramya patnīśālāta ṛtvigbhirvedapāragaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*audumbareṇa daṇḍena saṃvṛto mṛgacarmaṇā \|*  
*tayā sārdhaṃ praviṣṭaśca brahmā taṃ yajñamaṇḍapam \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. Gāyatri was clad in fine fabrics. She had a covering veil of silken cloth. With a staff made of Uduṃbara, Brahmā came out of the Patnīśālā (wife’s chamber) accompanied by the Ṛtviks well-versed in the Vedas. He was covered with a deer skin. Brahmā thus entered the Yajña-pavilion along with her (i.e. Gāyatri).

## \|\| 1.165.36 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*etasminneva kāle tu saṃprāptā devayoṣitaḥ \|*  
*saṃprāptā yatra sāvitrī yajñe tasminnimaṃtritāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

36\. In the meantime, the celestial ladies who had been invited for the Yajña arrived at the place where Sāvitrī was present.

## \|\| 1.165.37 \|\|

*bhṛgoḥ khyātyāṃ samutpannā viṣṇupatnī yaśasvinī \|*  
*āmantritā sā lakṣmīśca tatrāyātā tvarānvitā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The renowned Lakṣmī who was born to Khyāti and Bhṛgu and who was the wife of Viṣṇu and was invited there, arrived in a hurry.

## \|\| 1.165.58 \|\|

*kathaṃ sā bhavitā yajñaḥ samāptiṃ vā kathaṃ vrajet \|*  
*evaṃ cintayatāṃ teṣāṃ praviṣṭā kamalālayā \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. There, the highly esteemed goddess was embellished by Yoganidrā and others. There was the fair lady Kānti and Śraddhā, Dyuti and Tuṣṭi too.

## \|\| 1.165.39 \|\|

*satī yā dakṣatanayā umā yā pārvatī śubhā \|*  
*trailokyasundarī devī strīṇāṃ saubhāgyadāyakā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. There was Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa and also Umā, the splendid daughter of Mountain. The goddess who bestows conjugal felicity on women was the most beautiful lady in the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.165.40 \|\|

*jayā ca vijayā caiva gaurī caiva mahādhanā \|*  
*manojavā vāyupatnī ṛddhiśca dhanadapriyā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. There were Jayā, Vijayā, Gaurī and Mahādhanā (one having enormous wealth). There was Manojavā, the wife of Wind-god and also Ṛddhi, the beloved of Kubera.

## \|\| 1.165.41 \|\|

*devakanyāstathā'yātā dānavyo danuvaṃśajāḥ \|*  
*saptarṣīṇāṃ tathā patnya ṛṣīṇāṃ ca tathaiva ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Daughters of Devas, Dānavīs and those born of Danu’s \[???\] had also come. There were the wives of the seven sages \[???f\] the other saints as well.

## \|\| 1.165.42 \|\|

*plavā mitrā duhitaro vidyādharagaṇāstathā \|*  
*pitaro rakṣasāṃ kanyāstathā'nyā lokamātaraḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. There were Plavā, Mitrā and the daughters (of other sages). There were the groups of Vidyādharas. There were the Pitṛs and the daughters of Rākṣasas. There were the other Lokamātṛs (Mothers of the world).

## \|\| 1.165.43-44 \|\|

*vadhūbhiścaiva mukhyābhiḥ sāvitrī gantumicchati \|*  
*adityādyāstathā devyo dakṣakanyāḥ samāgatāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tābhiḥ parivṛtā sārdhaṃ brahmāṇī kamalālayā \|*  
*kāścinmodakamādāya kāścitpūpaṃ varānane \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. There were the Devīs beginning with Aditi. The daughters of Dakṣa came. Accompanied by them Sāvitrī, the wife of Brahmā, residing in the lotus, desired to proceed ahead.

O lady of excellent countenance, some of them carried Modaka (sweetmeat) and some carried Apūpa (bread, pie).

## \|\| 1.165.45 \|\|

*phalāni tu samādāya prayātā brahmaṇo'ntikam \|*  
*āḍhakīścaiva niṣpāvānrājamāṣāṃstathā'parāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Others carried fruits and proceeded towards Brahmā.

Still others carried Āḍhakī (pulse), Niṣpāva (legume) and Rājamāṣa (beans).

## \|\| 1.165.46-51 \|\|

*dāḍimāni vicitrāṇi mātuliṃgāni śobhane \|*  
*karīrāṇi tathā cānyā gṛhītvā karamardakān \|\| 46 \|\|*

*kausuṃbhaṃ jīrakaṃ caiva kharjūraṃ cāparāstathā \|*  
*utatīścāparā gṛhya nālikerāṇi cāparāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*drākṣayā pūritaṃ cāmraṃ śṛṅgārāya yathā purā \|*  
*karburāṇi vicitrāṇi jaṃbūkāni śubhāni ca \|\| 48 \|\|*

*akṣoḍāmalakāngṛhya jaṃbīrāṇi tathā parāḥ \|*  
*bilvāni paripakvāni cirbhaṭāni varānane \|\| 49 \|\|*

*annapānādhikārāṇi bahūni vividhāni ca \|*  
*śarkarāputtalīṃ cānyā vastre kausumbhake tathā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*evamādīni cānyāni gṛhya pūrve varānane \|*  
*sāvitryā sahitāḥ sarvāḥ saṃprāptāstu tadā śubhāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

46-51. Others carried various kinds of Dāḍima (pomegranate) and Mātuliṅga (citron). O splendid lady, yet others carried Karīra and Karamardaka. A few carried Kausumbha, Jīraka and Kharjūra; others carried Utatī and coconuts. Others carried mangoes along with grapes for the purpose of embellishment as before. A few carried various kinds of excellent Jambūka, Akṣoḍa, Āmalaka and Jaṃbīra. O lady of excellent countenance, some carried ripe Bilva fruits and Cirbhaṭa. Others carried many vessels of food and beverages of various kinds. Others carried lumps of sugar and Kausuṃbha garments (or in Kausumbha cloth).
