*chandyamānā varaiste tu śaṃkareṇa mahātmanā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*liṃgasya darśanaṃ muktvā na te'nyaṃ vavrire varam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ tu niścayaṃ jñātvā sarveṣāṃ vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*anukampāparo bhūtvā svaliṃgaṃ tānadarśayat \|\| 14 \|\|*

*etasminneva kāle tu bhittvā caiva vasundharām \|*  
*utthitaṃ sahasā liṃgaṃ tadeva varavarṇini \|\| 15 \|\|*

12-15. O lady of excellent complexion, when they attained old age, the noble-souled Śaṅkara lured them with offering boons. Excepting the vision of the Liṅga, they did not accept any other boon.

## \|\| 1.195.14 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tu niścayaṃ jñātvā sarveṣāṃ vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*anukampāparo bhūtvā svaliṃgaṃ tānadarśayat \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Realizing their determination, the Bull-emblemed Lord became sympathetic and revealed his own Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.195.15 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu bhittvā caiva vasundharām \|*  
*utthitaṃ sahasā liṃgaṃ tadeva varavarṇini \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O lady of excellent complexion, at that very time, the Liṅga suddenly rose up, piercing through the ground.

## \|\| 1.195.16 \|\|

*ṛṣayaste ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve ca tridivaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*atha teṣu prayāteṣu śakrastaptamanā hyabhūt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. All those sages viewed it and went to heaven. When they thus proceeded (to heaven) Śakra was distressed in mind.

## \|\| 1.195.17 \|\|

*tamapi cchādayāmāsa vajreṇa śataparvaṇā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He concealed that too by means of his Vajra of hundred knots.

## \|\| 1.195.18 \|\|

*vṛddhabhāve yatasteṣāmṛṣīṇāṃ darśanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*ato vṛddhaprabhāsaṃ tatkīrtyate vasudhātale \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Since the Liṅga appeared before them (the sages), in their old age, it is glorified as Vṛddhaprabhāsa on the earth.

## \|\| 1.195.19 \|\|

*tasmindṛṣṭe varārohe adyāpi labhate phalam \|*  
*rājasūyāśvamedhānāṃ naro bhaktisamanvitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O beautiful lady, when it is viewed the benefit is obtained even to-day. A man equipped with devout feelings, gets the benefit of Rājasūyas and Aśvamedhas.

## \|\| 1.195.20 \|\|

*evaṃ tatra samutpannaṃ prabhāsaṃ vṛddhasaṃjñakam \|*  
*tatrokṣā brāhmaṇe deyaḥ samyagyātrāphalepsubhiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. It was thus that the sacred shrine Vṛddhaprabhāsa originated there. A bull is to be offered there to a Brāhmaṇa by those who wish to get the benefit of a perfect pilgrimage.

## Chapter 196 - Glory of Jalaprabhāsa (Jala-prabhāsa)

## \|\| 1.196.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi prabhāsaṃ jalasaṃsthitam \|*  
*vṛddhaprabhāsāddakṣiṇato nātidūre vyavasthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tasyaiva devi devasya śṛṇu māhātmyamuttamam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*jāmadagnyena rāmeṇa yadā kṣattravadhaḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*tadā'sya paramā jātā ghṛṇā manasi bhāmini \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the shrine of Prabhāsa stationed in water \[i.e., jala-saṃsthita\]. It is situated not far from Vṛddhaprabhās \[Vṛddhaprabhāsa?\] to the south.

O goddess, listen to the excellent greatness of that deity. When the genocide of Kṣatriyas was carried out by Rāma, the son of Jamadagni, O fair lady, he was overcome with a great deal of contemptuous disgust in his mind.

## \|\| 1.196.4 \|\|

*tatastvārādhayāmāsa mahādevaṃ sureśvaram \|*  
*ugraṃ tapaḥ samāsthāya bahūnvarṣa gaṇānpriye \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Thereupon, O my beloved, he performed a very fierce penance for many years and propitiated Mahādeva, the Lord of Suras.

## \|\| 1.196.5 \|\|

*tatastuṣṭo mahādevastasya pratyakṣatāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*abravīdvaradaste'haṃ varaṃ varaya suvrata \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then Mahādeva became pleased and appeared before him directly and said, “O sage of excellent Vratas, I wish to grant you boons; choose the boons that you wish to have.”

## \|\| 1.196.6 \|\|

*rāma uvāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭo'si me deva yadi deyo varo mama \|*  
*darśayasva svakaṃ liṃgaṃ yajñe vajreṇa chāditam \|\| 6 \|\|*

Rāma said:

6\. O Lord, if you are pleased with me, if a boon is to be granted to me, do reveal your Liṅga that has been concealed by Vajra.

## \|\| 1.196.7-8 \|\|

*ghṛṇā me mahatī jātā hatvemānkṣatriyānbahūn \|*  
*darśanāttava liṃgasya yena me naśyate ghṛṇā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tathā me pātakaṃ sarvaṃ prasādāttava śaṃkara \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. After having massacred many Kṣatriyas, I felt a great revulsion and contemptuous disgust. By viewing your Liṅga, perhaps, this feeling may perish. With your favour, O Śaṅkara, may my sin be destroyed entirely.”

## \|\| 1.196.9-10 \|\|

*śaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*mama liṃgaṃ sahasrākṣa utthitaṃ tu punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*vajreṇācchādayatyeva bhayena mahatā vṛtaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*na te'haṃ darśanaṃ yāsye liṃgarūpī kadācana \|\| 10 \|\|*

Śaṅkara said:

9-10. The thousand-eyed Indra conceals by means of Vajra again and again my Liṅga that rises up frequently because he gets frightened much. I shall never come within your view in the form of a Liṅga.

## \|\| 1.196.11 \|\|

*yanmāṃ vadasi ghṛṇayā vṛto'haṃ pātakena tu \|*  
*tatte'haṃ nāśayiṣyāmi sparśanāttu dvijottama \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. That is because you say that you have been overwhelmed by revulsion, disgust and sin. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, by means of physical touch, I shall eradicate it!

## \|\| 1.196.12-13 \|\|

*asmiñjalāśraye puṇye jalamadhye mahāmate \|*  
*utthāsyati mahāliṃgaṃ tasya tvaṃ darśanaṃ kuru \|\| 12 \|\|*

*gamiṣyati ghṛṇā sarvā niṣpāpastvaṃ bhaviṣyasi \|*  
*uktvaivamudatiṣṭhacca jalamadhyādvarānane \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13a. O highly intelligent one, a great Liṅga will come up in the middle of this meritorious expanse of water. Do view it. The entire revulsive feelings will vanish and you will be free from sins.

13b. After this was spoken (the Liṅga) came up from the centre of the watery expanse, O lady of excellent countenance.

## \|\| 1.196.14 \|\|

*jalaprabhāsanāmāsya tato jātaṃ dharātale \|*  
*tasyālaṃ sparśanāddevi śivalokaṃ vrajennaraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Therefore, its name Jalaprabhāsa spread over the earth. O goddess, by touching it, a man will be able to go to Śivaloka.

## \|\| 1.196.15 \|\|

*ekaṃ bhojayate yo'tra brāhmaṇaṃ śaṃsitavratam \|*  
*bhojito'haṃ bhavettena sapatnīko na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. If the devotee feeds a Brāhmaṇa of praiseworthy holy vows here, I shall undoubtedly be considered to have been fed in the company of my wife.

## \|\| 1.196.16 \|\|

*eṣā jalaprabhāsasya saṃbhūtiste mayoditā \|*  
*śrutā pāpopaśamanī sarvakāmaphalapradā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. This origin of Jalaprabhāsa has been narrated to you by me. When listened to, it suppresses sins and bestows all desired benefits.

## Chapter 197 - Greatness of Jamadagnīśvara (Jamadagni-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.197.1-5 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi jamadagnīśvaraṃ śivam \|*  
*vṛddhaprabhāsasāmīpye nātidūre vyavasthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sarvapāpopaśamanaṃ sthāpitaṃ jamadagninā \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā mānavo devi mucyate ca ṛṇatrayāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

*snātvā nidhānavāpyāṃ ca saṃpūjya prāpnuyāddhanam \|*  
*nidhānaṃ pāṃḍavairlabdhaṃ tatra sthāne purā priye \|\| 3 \|\|*

*nidhānenaiva sā khyātā vāpī trailokyavaṃditā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tasyāṃ snātvā mahādevi durbhagā subhagā bhavet \|*  
*labhate vāñchitānkāmāniti proktaṃ mayā tava \|\| 5 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-5. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the shrine of Śiva called Jamadagnīśvara. It is situated not far but very near Vṛddhaprabhāsa.

It is destructive of all sins. It was installed by Jamadagni. On viewing it, O goddess, a man becomes released from the three types of indebtedness.

By taking the holy bath in the tank Nidhāna Vāpī and worshipping the deity, the devotee will acquire wealth,

O my beloved, a treasure-trove was acquired by the Pāṇḍavas earlier at that spot.

It is through the treasure-trove that the tank became adorable to all the three worlds and well-known.

By taking the holy bath there, O great goddess, the unlucky one (lady) will become blessed with conjugal felicity and will attain all desired objects. Thus everything has been told by me to you.

## Chapter 198 - Greatness of Pañcamaprabhāsa Kṣetra

## \|\| 1.198.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi mahāprabhāsamuttamam \|*  
*jalaprabhāsato yāmye yamamārgavighātakam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*śṛṇu tasyaiva māhātmyaṃ yathā jātaṃ dharātale \|\| 2 \|\|*

*pūrvaṃ tretāyuge devi sparśaliṃgaṃ tu tatsmṛtam \|*  
*divyaṃ tejomayaṃ nṛṇāṃ sparśanānmuktidāyakam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*atha kāle ca kasmiṃścidvajriṇācchāditaṃ priye \|*  
*indreṇāgatya vasudhāṃ bhayākrāṃtena sundari \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. Thereafter, O great goddess, a devotee should go to the excellent shrine of Mahāprabhāsa. It is situated to the south of Jalaprabhāsa. It causes obstacle in the path of Yama. Listen to its greatness and how it originated on the surface of the earth.

O goddess, formerly in the Tretā Yuga it was remembered as Sparśa-Liṅga. It was divine and radiant, capable of bestowing salvation on men merely on being touched. O my beloved and beautiful lady, once Indra who was overcome by fear came to the earth and covered it with his thunderbolt.

## \|\| 1.198.5-7 \|\|

*uṣmā tadudbhavo devi nirgacchannavarodhitaḥ \|*  
*daśakoṭipravistīrṇaṃ jvālāgraṃ liṃgarūpadhṛk \|\| 5 \|\|*

*prabhāsakṣetramāsthāya bhittvā'virbhāvamāsthitam \|*  
*vajreṇa ruṃdhite devi bhittvā caiva vasuṃdharām \|\| 6 \|\|*

*dhūmasaṃghaiḥ sametaṃ tu vyāpayāmāsa tajjagat \|*  
*tatastrailokyamakhilaṃ jvālābhirvyākulīkṛtam \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. The heat issuing therefrom, O goddess, was restrained. A mass of flames extending to ten crores assumed the form of a Liṅga. It pierced through the ground at Prabhāsa Kṣetra and manifested itself. O goddess, when it was restrained by the thunderbolt it broke through the earth and extended all over the universe along with masses of smoke. Thereupon, all the three worlds became confounded with the flames.

## \|\| 1.198.8 \|\|

*tataḥ suragaṇāḥ sarva ṛṣayo vedapāragāḥ \|*  
*astuvanvividhaiḥ sūktairvedoktaiḥ śaśiśekharam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thereupon, all the groups of Suras and sages who had mastered the Vedas eulogized the Moon-crested Lord by means of different types of Vedic hymns.

## \|\| 1.198.9 \|\|

*saṃharasva suraśreṣṭha tejaḥ svadahanātmakam \|\| trai \|*  
*lokyaṃ vyākulībhūtamevaṃ sarvaṃ carācaram \|*  
*na yāvatpralayaṃ yāti tāvadrakṣa sureśvara \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. “O most excellent one among Suras, withdraw your own burning refulgence. All the three worlds as well as the mobile and immobile beings are confused and disturbed. Oh! Restrain it before the utter annihilation (of the worlds).”

## \|\| 1.198.10-11 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*evamābhāṣamāṇeṣu tridiveṣu sureśvari \|*  
*tattejaḥ pañcadhāviṣṭaṃ vyāpyāśeṣaṃ jagattrayam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*pañcaprabhāsarūpeṇa bhittvā tatra vasundharām \|*  
*yena mārgeṇa niṣkrāntaṃ tanmārge ca mahanmahaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

10-11. O goddess of Suras, when the Devas were speaking thus, that splendour split into five and pervaded the three worlds. It broke through the earth in the form of Pañcaprabhāsa. The path through which the great splendour issued forth there was a great light.

## \|\| 1.198.12 \|\|

*tatra taiḥ sthāpitaṃ dvāraṃ supradeśe'śmajaṃ priye \|*  
*pihite'tha ca raṃdhre'smindhūmo nāśamupeyivān \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O my beloved, rocks were placed at the entrance in a proper place. When the hole was thus closed the smoke vanished.

## \|\| 1.198.13 \|\|

*svasthāścaivābhavaṃllokāstejastatraiva saṃsthitam \|*  
*evaṃ mayā preritāste liṃgaṃ tatra samādadhuḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. All the worlds became normal. The splendour settled there. On being urged by me thus, they placed the Liṅga in a proper set-up.

## \|\| 1.198.14 \|\|

*tanmahastatra deveśi viśrāmamakarottadā \|*  
*tato mahāprabhāseti kīrtyate devadānavaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. That splendour settled down there, O goddess of Devas. Therefore, it is being glorified as Mahāprabhāsa by Devas and Dānavas.

## \|\| 1.198.15 \|\|

*yastaṃ pūjayate bhaktyā liṃgaṃ puṣpaiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|*  
*sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He who devoutly worships the Liṅga with different kinds of flowers, attains the great region devoid of death and old age.

## \|\| 1.198.16 \|\|

*dṛṣṭena tena deveśi mucyate pātakairnaraḥ \|*  
*labhate vāñchitānkāmānmanasā cepsitānpriye \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O goddess of Devas, if it is viewed, the man becomes rid of all sins. He attains desired benefits. O my beloved, whatever is mentally desired is acquired.

## \|\| 1.198.17 \|\|

*hiraṇyaṃ tatra dātavyaṃ brāhmaṇe śaṃsitavrate \|*  
*godānaṃ vidhivattatra deyaṃ caiva dvijanmane \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Gold is to be offered as gift to a Brāhmaṇa of praiseworthy holy vows. A gift of cows is to be duly offered there to twice-borns.

## \|\| 1.198.18 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛtvā mahādevi labhate janmanaḥ phalam \|*  
*rājasūyāśvamedhānāṃ prāpnuyātphalamūrjitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. By doing like this, O great goddess, a man obtains cherished objectives of his birth. He shall get the powerful benefit of Rājasūyas and Aśvamedhas.

## Chapter 199 - Destruction of Dakṣa’s Sacrifice

## \|\| 1.199.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi tasya dakṣiṇataḥ sthitam \|*  
*sarasvatyāstaṭe ramye devaṃ tatra kṛtasmaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

*svayaṃbhūtaṃ mahādevi sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|*  
*tasyotpattiṃ pravakṣyāmi yathā jātaṃ mahītale \|\| 2 \|\|*

*purā kāmo mayā dagdho yadā tatra varānane \|*  
*tadā ratiḥ samāgamya vilalāpa suduḥkhitā \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the shrine of Lord Kṛtasmara situated to the south thereof on the charming banks of Sarasvatī.

O great goddess, it has manifested itself and is destructive of all sins. I shall narrate how it originated on the earth.

Formerly when Kāma was burnt by me there, O lady of excellent countenance, Rati came there in great misery and lamented much.

## \|\| 1.199.4 \|\|

*tāṃ tu śokāturāṃ dṛṣṭvā tatrāhaṃ karuṇānvitaḥ \|*  
*avocaṃ mā rudiṣveti tava bhartā punaḥ śubhe \|*  
*samutthāsyati kālena matprasādānna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On seeing her extremely grief-stricken I was moved with pity and so I told her: “O splendid lady, do not weep. Your husband will come to life again with my favour. There is no doubt about it.”

## \|\| 1.199.5 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*kimarthaṃ sa purā dagdhaḥ kāmadevastvayā vibho \|*  
*kathamāpa punarjanma vistarātkathayasva me \|\| 5 \|\|*

Devī said:

5\. O lord, why was he burnt earlier by you? How will Lord Kāma regain his life. Do tell me this in detail.

## \|\| 1.199.6 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*dakṣaḥ prajāpatiḥ pūrvaṃ babhūva tvatpitā priye \|*  
*śataṃ sutānāṃ jajñe'sya gaurīṇāṃ dīrghacakṣuṣām \|\| 6 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

6\. O my beloved, formerly your father was Dakṣa. He begot a hundred young, fair-complexioned daughters of longish eyes.

## \|\| 1.199.7-8 \|\|

*dadau tvāṃ prathamaṃ mahyaṃ satīnāmeti kīrtitām \|*  
*dadau daśa ca dharmāya śraddhā medhā dhṛtiḥ kṣamā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*anasūyā śucirlajjā smṛtiḥ śaktiḥ śrutistathā \|*  
*dve bhārye kāmadevāya ratiḥ prītistathaiva ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. At the outset he gave you who was well-known by the name Satī to me. Then he gave ten daughters to Dharma, viz. Śraddhā, Medhā, Dhṛti, Kṣamā, Anasūyā, Śuci, Lajjā, Smṛti, Śakti and Śruti. Then he gave two daughters as wives unto Kāmadeva. Their names were Rati and Prīti.

## \|\| 1.199.9-10 \|\|

*ekāṃ svāhāṃ dadau vahneḥ pitṝṇāṃ ca tataḥ svadhām \|*  
*saptaviṃśacchaśāṅkāya aśvinyādyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tavāpi viditā devi revatyantāstathā jane \|*  
*kaśyapāya dadau devi sa tu kanyāstrayodaśa \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. One daughter he gave to Vahni. She was Svāhā. Then he gave Svadhā to the Pitrṛṣ \[Pitṛs?\]. He gave twenty-seven daughters to the Moon-god. They are well-known as those beginning with Aśvinī. The last of them was Revatī and all of them are known to you and even to the people. O goddess, he gave thirteen daughters to Kaśyapa.

## \|\| 1.199.11-12 \|\|

*aditiśca ditiścaiva vinatā kadrureva ca \|*  
*siṃhikā suprabhā caiva ulūkī yā varānane \|\| 11 \|\|*

*anuviddhā sitā caiva īrṣyā hiṃsā tathā parā \|*  
*māyā niṣkṛtisaṃyuktā dakṣaḥ pūrvaṃ mahāmatiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Formerly, Dakṣa, the highly intelligent one, gave these (to Kaśyapa): Aditi, Diti, Vinatā, Kadru, Siṃhikā, Suprabhā, Ulūkī, Anuviddhā, Sītā, Īrṣyā, Hiṃsā, Māyā and Niṣkrti \[Niṣkṛti?\], O lady of excellent countenance.

## \|\| 1.199.13 \|\|

*gaurī ca suprabhā caiva vārttā sādhvī sumālikā \|*  
*varuṇāya dadau pañca tadā'sau parvatātmaje \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O daughter of the Mountain, then he gave five daughters to Varuṇa: Gaurī, Suprabhā, Vārttā, Sādhvī and Sumālikā.

## \|\| 1.199.14 \|\|

*bhadrā ca madirā caiva vidyā dhanyā dhanā śubhā \|*  
*dadau pañca kuberāya patnyarthaṃ parvatātmaje \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O daughter of the Mountain, he gave five daughters to Kubera as wives viz. Bhadrā, Madirā, Vidyā, Dhanyā, and the splendid Dhanā.

## \|\| 1.199.15-18 \|\|

*jayā ca vijayā caiva madhuspandā irāvatī \|*  
*supriyā janakā kāntā subhadrā dhārmikā śubhā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*rudrāṇāṃ pradadau kanyā daśānāṃ dharmavittadā \|*  
*prabhāvatī subhadrā ca vimalā nirmalā'nṛtā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tīvrā dakṣāruṇā vidyā dhārapālā ca varcasā \|*  
*ādityānāṃ dadau dakṣaḥ kanyādvādaśakaṃ priye \|\| 17 \|\|*

*yoganidrābhibhūtasya saṃsarpā saramā guhā \|*  
*mālā caṃpā tathā jyotsnā sa viśvebhyaśca eva ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

15-18. Dakṣa, conversant with Dharma, gave ten daughters to ten Rudras: Jayā, Vijayā, Madhuṣpandā \[Madhuspandā?\], Irāvatī, Supriyā, Janakā, Kāntā, Subhadrā, Dharmikā and Śubhā. O my beloved wife, Dakṣa gave twelve daughters to Ādityas. They are: Prabhāvatī, Subhadrā, Vimalā, Nirmalā, Aṅṛtā \[Anṛtā?\], Tīvrā, Dakṣā, Aruṇā, Vidyā, Dhārapālā, Varcasā and (probably) Yoganidrā (mentioned in verse 18 in a curious phrase).

He gave to Viśvedevas the following daughters: Saṃsarpā, Saramā, Guhā, Mālā, Caṃpā and Jyotsnā.

## \|\| 1.199.19 \|\|

*aśvibhyāṃ dve tathā kanye suveṣā bhūṣaṇā śubhā \|*  
*ekā kanyā tathā vāyordattā etāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He gave two daughters to Aśvins: Suveṣā and the splendid Bhūṣaṇā. One daughter was given to Vāyu. All these are well enumerated.

## \|\| 1.199.20-21 \|\|

*sāvitrīṃ brahmaṇe prādāllakṣmīṃ viṣṇormahātmanaḥ \|*  
*kasyacittvatha kālasya sa īje dakṣiṇāvatā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*yajñena parvatasute himavante mahāgirau \|*  
*yajñavāṭo hyabhūttasya sarvakāmasamṛddhimān \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. He gave Sāvitrī to Brahmā and Lakṣmī to the noble-souled Viṣṇu. After some time, O daughter of the Mountain, he performed a Yajña including monetary gifts on the great mountain Himavān. His sacrificial hall was richly equipped with all desirable items.

## \|\| 1.199.22-26 \|\|

*tasminyajñe samāyātā ādityā vasava stathā \|*  
*viśvedevāśca maruto lokapālāśca sarvaśaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*brahmā viṣṇuḥ sahasrākṣo vāruṇo yama eva ca \|*  
*dhanadaśca kumāraśca tathā nadyaśca sāgarāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*vāpyaḥ kūpāstathā caiva taḍāgāḥ palvalāni ca \|*  
*suparṇaścātha ye nāgāḥ sarve mūrtā vyavasthitāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*dānavāpsarasaścaiva yakṣāḥ kinnaraguhyakāḥ \|*  
*sānugāste sabhāryāśca vedavedāṃgapāragāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*maharṣayo mahābhāgāstathā devarṣayaśca ye \|*  
*te bhāryāsahitāstatra vasaṃti ca varānane \|\| 26 \|\|*

22-26. O lady of excellent countenance, all these assembled on that Yajña: the Ādityas, Vasus, Viśvedevas, Maruts, all the Lokapālas, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, the thousand-eyed Indra, Varuṇa, Yama, Dhanada, Kumāra, the Nadīs (rivers personified) along with the oceans, tanks, wells, lakes, puddles, Suparṇa, all the Nāgas, (serpants \[serpents?\]) in personified forms, Dānavas, Apsarās, Yakṣas, Kinnaras, Guhyakas. All these came with their wives and attendants and followers. The highly esteemed great sages and celestial sages who had mastered the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas were present there with their wives.

## \|\| 1.199.27 \|\|

*kapālamālābharaṇaścitābhasma bibharti yaḥ \|*  
*apavitratayā śaṃbhurnāhūtastu tathāvidhaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Śaṃbhu who had a garland of skulls as his ornament, who applied ash from cremation ground (all over his body) and who was not considered pure on that account was not invited.

## \|\| 1.199.28 \|\|

*yatastataḥ samāyātāḥ kailāse parvatottame \|*  
*aśvinyādyā bhaginyastāstvāṃ pratīdaṃ vaco'buvan \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Aśvinī and other sisters of yours who had arrived from here and there at Kailāsa, the most excellent one among mountains, spoke to you these words:

## \|\| 1.199.29-30 \|\|

*kiṃ tuṣṭeva ca kalyāṇi tiṣṭhasi tvaṃ sumadhyame \|*  
*vayaṃ ca prasthitāḥ sarvāḥ pituryajñe sabhartṛkāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*vayamākāritāstena sutāḥ sarvā yaśasvini \|*  
*na tvāmāhūtavāndakṣastrapate śaṃkarādyataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. “O fair lady of excellent waistline, why do you stay back here complacently? All of us have set off for the Yajña of our father, along with our husbands. O lady of renown, all of us, the daughters, have been invited by him, but Dakṣa has not invited you because he is ashamed of Śaṅkara.”

## \|\| 1.199.31-32 \|\|

*tāsāṃ vacanamākarṇya satī prāha krudhānvitā \|*  
*hā dhigdakṣa durācāra kiṃ vadiṣye maheśvaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

*kathaṃ saṃdarśaye vaktramityuktvā'tmānamātmanā \|*  
*visasarja tapoyogātsasmārānyanna kiñcana \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32a. On hearing the words of those ladies, the infuriated Satī said: Fie upon you! O Dakṣa of evil conduct, what will I say to Maheśvara? How can I show my face?”

32b. After saying this, she gave up her own soul by herself by means of her power of penance and Yoga. She did not remember anything else.

## \|\| 1.199.33-34 \|\|

*atha dṛṣṭvā mahādevaḥ satīṃ prāṇairvinā sthitām \|*  
*avamānāttathā'tmānaṃ tyaktvā matvā kapālinam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*gaṇānsaṃpreṣayāmāsa yajñavidhvaṃsanāya ca \|*  
*te gatāśca gaṇā raudrāḥ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. Mahādeva observed that Satī became lifeless because she had to abandon him in view of the fact that he was a Kapālin (One having skulls round the neck). It was due to her Sense of shame that she had forsaken him. In order to destroy the Yajña, he despatched his Gaṇas. Hundreds and thousands of those terrible Gaṇas proceeded there.

## \|\| 1.199.35-59 \|\|

*vikṛtā vikṛtākārā asaṃkhyātā mahābalāḥ \|*  
*rudreṇa preritāndṛṣṭvā vīrabhadrapurogamān \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tato devagaṇāḥ sarve vasavaḥ saha bhāskaraiḥ \|*  
*viśvedevāśca sādhyāśca dhanurhastā mahābalāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*yuddhāya ca viniṣkrāntā muñcantaḥ sāyakāñchitān \|*  
*te sametya tato'nyonyaṃ pramathā vibudhaiḥ saha \|\| 37 \|\|*

*mumucuḥ śaravarṣāṇi vāridhārāṃ yathā ghanāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ hastī gaṇenātha śūlena hṛdi bheditaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*sa tu tena prahāreṇa visaṃjño niṣasāda ha \|*  
*atha muṣṭyā hataḥ kumbhe nāga airāvaṇastadā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*sahasā sa hatastena vāraṇo bhairavānravān \|*  
*vinadañjavamāsthāya yajñavāṭamupādravat \|\| 40 \|\|*

*viśvedevā nirucchvāsāḥ kṛtā raudrairmahāśaraiḥ \|*  
*cakarṣa sa dhanuṣyeṇa vasumānbalavataraḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*nistejasastadādityāḥ kṛtāstena raṇājire \|*  
*etasminnantare devāḥ kṛtāstena parāṅmukhāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tataste śaraṇaṃ jagmurviṣṇuṃ tatra ca saṃsthitam \|*  
*tataḥ kopasamāviṣṭo viṣṇurdevānsavāsavān \|\| 43 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā vidrāvitānsarvānmumocāśu sudarśanam \|*  
*tamāpatantaṃ vegena viṣṇoścakraṃ sudarśanam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*prasārya vaktraṃ sahasā udarasthaṃ cakāra ha \|*  
*tasmiṃścakre tadā graste amoghe parvatātmaje \|\| 45 \|\|*

*cukopa bhagavānviṣṇuḥ śārṅgahasto 'bhyadhāvata \|*  
*sa hatvā daśabhistīkṣṇairnaṃdiṃ bhṛṅgiṃ śatena ca \|\| 46 \|\|*

*mahākālaṃ sahasreṇa hyayutena gaṇādhipam \|*  
*bāṇānāmayutairbhittvā vīrabhadramupādravat \|\| 47 \|\|*

*taṃ hatvā gadayā viṣṇurvihvalaṃ rudhirokṣitam \|*  
*gṛhītvā pādayorbhūmau nijaghānātiroṣitaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*hanyamānasya tasyātha bhūmau cakraṃ sudarśanam \|*  
*rudhirodgārasaṃyuktaṃ prahāramakaronna tu \|\| 49 \|\|*

*rudralabdhavaro devi vīrabhadro gaṇeśvaraḥ \|*  
*yanna pañcatvamāpanno gadayā pīḍito'pi saḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*patitaṃ vīkṣya taṃ sarve viṣṇutejobalārditāḥ \|*  
*vidrutāḥ sarvato yātā yatra devo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*tasmai sarvaṃ tathā vṛttaṃ samācakhyuḥ parābhavam \|*  
*vikramaṃ vīrabhadrasya tataḥ kruddho maheśvaraḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*pragṛhya sahasā śūlaṃ prasthitaḥ svagaṇaiḥ saha \|*  
*yajñavāṭaṃ tu dakṣasya parābhavabhavaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*vikramanvīrabhadreṇa yatra viṣṇuḥ svayaṃ sthitaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*tamāyāntaṃ samālokya kopayuktaṃ maheśvaram \|*  
*saṃgrāme so'jayaṃ matvā tatraivāntaradhīyata \|\| 54 \|\|*

*marudbhiḥ sārdhamindro'pi vasubhiḥ saha kinnaraiḥ \|*  
*śivaḥ krodhaparītātmā tataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*kevalaṃ brāhmaṇāstatra sthitāḥ sadasi bhāmini \|*  
*te dṛṣṭvā śaṃkaraṃ prāptaṃ kopasaṃraktalocanam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*homaṃ cakrustato bhītā rudramaṃtraiḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*anye trāsasamāyuktāḥ palāyaṃte diśo daśa \|\| 57 \|\|*

*athāgatya mahādevo dṛṣṭvā tānbrāhmaṇottamān \|*  
*apaśyamāno vibudhāṃstatra yajñaṃ jaghāna saḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*sa ca mṛgavapurbhūtvā praṇaṣṭaḥ śivabhītitaḥ \|*  
*pṛṣṭhatastu dhanuṣpāṇirjagāma bhagavāñchivaḥ \|*  
*adyāpi dṛśyate vyomni tārārūpo maheśvari \|\| 59 \|\|*

35-59. They were deformed and had ugly features. Those mighty ones were innumerable. On observing that these Gaṇas with Vīrabhadra as their leader had been urged by Rudra, all the groups of the Devas along with Bhāskaras (i.e. Ādityas), Viśvedevas and Sādhyas set out for the battle. They were highly powerful with bows in their hands. They began to discharge sharp arrows. They met with one another. Pramathas clashed with Devas. Like the clouds pouring showers of water, they discharged volleys of arrows. Their elephant was pierced through the chest with their lance by the Gaṇas. Losing consciousness due to that attack, the elephant sat down. Then the elephant Airāvaṇa was hit on its forehead with fist.

## \|\| 1.199.40 \|\|

*sahasā sa hatastena vāraṇo bhairavānravān \|*  
*vinadañjavamāsthāya yajñavāṭamupādravat \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Attacked forcefully thus, the elephant trumpeted terrible sounds and hurried to the Yajñavāṭa with great speed.

## \|\| 1.199.41-42 \|\|

*viśvedevā nirucchvāsāḥ kṛtā raudrairmahāśaraiḥ \|*  
*cakarṣa sa dhanuṣyeṇa vasumānbalavataraḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*nistejasastadādityāḥ kṛtāstena raṇājire \|*  
*etasminnantare devāḥ kṛtāstena parāṅmukhāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. Viśvedevas were rendered breathless by him (Vīrabhadra) through huge, terrible arrows. The powerful Vasumān was dragged along with his bow. Ādityas were deprived of their brilliance by him in the battlefield. In the meantime, the Devas were thus routed by him.

## \|\| 1.199.43-47 \|\|

*tataste śaraṇaṃ jagmurviṣṇuṃ tatra ca saṃsthitam \|*  
*tataḥ kopasamāviṣṭo viṣṇurdevānsavāsavān \|\| 43 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā vidrāvitānsarvānmumocāśu sudarśanam \|*  
*tamāpatantaṃ vegena viṣṇoścakraṃ sudarśanam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*prasārya vaktraṃ sahasā udarasthaṃ cakāra ha \|*  
*tasmiṃścakre tadā graste amoghe parvatātmaje \|\| 45 \|\|*

*cukopa bhagavānviṣṇuḥ śārṅgahasto 'bhyadhāvata \|*  
*sa hatvā daśabhistīkṣṇairnaṃdiṃ bhṛṅgiṃ śatena ca \|\| 46 \|\|*

*mahākālaṃ sahasreṇa hyayutena gaṇādhipam \|*  
*bāṇānāmayutairbhittvā vīrabhadramupādravat \|\| 47 \|\|*

43-47. Thereupon they sought refuge in Viṣṇu who was present there. On seeing all the Devas along with Vāsava routed, Viṣṇu became furious. He hurriedly discharged his Sudarśana. On seeing Viṣṇu’s discus Sudarśana rushing hurriedly, Vīrabhadra opened his mouth wide and gulped the discus into his belly.

O daughter of the Mountain, when the never failing discus was thus swallowed, Lord Viṣṇu became angry. He rushed at him seizing Śārṅga bow with his hand. He hit Nandin with ten sharp arrows and Bhṛṅgī with a hundred, Mahākāla with a thousand and Gaṇādhipa with ten thousand arrows. He pierced Vīrabhadra with ten thousand arrows and rushed at him.

## \|\| 1.199.48 \|\|

*taṃ hatvā gadayā viṣṇurvihvalaṃ rudhirokṣitam \|*  
*gṛhītvā pādayorbhūmau nijaghānātiroṣitaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The infuriated Viṣṇu hit him with his Gadā (i.e. mace). When he became distressed and covered with blood, he seized him by the feet and dashed him against the ground with great ferocity.

## \|\| 1.199.49 \|\|

*hanyamānasya tasyātha bhūmau cakraṃ sudarśanam \|*  
*rudhirodgārasaṃyuktaṃ prahāramakaronna tu \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. When he was struck on the ground, the discus came out with a lot of blood vomited but did not hit him.

## \|\| 1.199.50 \|\|

*rudralabdhavaro devi vīrabhadro gaṇeśvaraḥ \|*  
*yanna pañcatvamāpanno gadayā pīḍito'pi saḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. O goddess, Vīrabhadra, the Lord of Gaṇas, had received a boon from Rudra. That was why he did not die even when afflicted, struck with the mace.

## \|\| 1.199.51 \|\|

*patitaṃ vīkṣya taṃ sarve viṣṇutejobalārditāḥ \|*  
*vidrutāḥ sarvato yātā yatra devo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. On seeing him fallen, all the Gaṇas got tormented by Viṣṇu’s valour and might, fled in every direction and proceeded to the place where Lord Maheśvara was present.

## \|\| 1.199.52 \|\|

*tasmai sarvaṃ tathā vṛttaṃ samācakhyuḥ parābhavam \|*  
*vikramaṃ vīrabhadrasya tataḥ kruddho maheśvaraḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. They recounted to him all the discomfiture they met with and also the exploit of Vīrabhadra. Thereupon, Maheśvara became infuriated.

## \|\| 1.199.53-55 \|\|

*pragṛhya sahasā śūlaṃ prasthitaḥ svagaṇaiḥ saha \|*  
*yajñavāṭaṃ tu dakṣasya parābhavabhavaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*vikramanvīrabhadreṇa yatra viṣṇuḥ svayaṃ sthitaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*tamāyāntaṃ samālokya kopayuktaṃ maheśvaram \|*  
*saṃgrāme so'jayaṃ matvā tatraivāntaradhīyata \|\| 54 \|\|*

*marudbhiḥ sārdhamindro'pi vasubhiḥ saha kinnaraiḥ \|*  
*śivaḥ krodhaparītātmā tataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

53-55. Seizing his trident, he set off with his Gaṇas to Yajñavāṭa, the cause of all defeat. Viṣṇu was standing fighting with Vīrabhadra.

On seeing the angry Maheśvara coining, Viṣṇu considered that he (Śiva) was invincible or he would not be victorious. Hence he vanished. Śiva stood there furious. Along with Maruts, Vasus and Kinnaras, Indra too vanished from the scene.

## \|\| 1.199.56-57 \|\|

*kevalaṃ brāhmaṇāstatra sthitāḥ sadasi bhāmini \|*  
*te dṛṣṭvā śaṃkaraṃ prāptaṃ kopasaṃraktalocanam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*homaṃ cakrustato bhītā rudramaṃtraiḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*anye trāsasamāyuktāḥ palāyaṃte diśo daśa \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. O fair lady, only those Brāhmaṇas remained there in the sacrificial hall. On observing that Śaṅkara had arrived there furiously rolling his red eyes the terrified Brāhmaṇas performed Homa by means of Rudra Mantras. All those who remained around fled in all ten directions.

## \|\| 1.199.58-59 \|\|

*athāgatya mahādevo dṛṣṭvā tānbrāhmaṇottamān \|*  
*apaśyamāno vibudhāṃstatra yajñaṃ jaghāna saḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*sa ca mṛgavapurbhūtvā praṇaṣṭaḥ śivabhītitaḥ \|*  
*pṛṣṭhatastu dhanuṣpāṇirjagāma bhagavāñchivaḥ \|*  
*adyāpi dṛśyate vyomni tārārūpo maheśvari \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. Mahādeva arrived there but could not see the Devas. He saw only the Brāhmaṇas. So he destroyed the Yajña there. Frightened of Śiva the Yajña assumed the form of a deer and fled with the bow in his hand, Lord Śiva closely pursued him. O great goddess, even today he is seen in the sky in the form of a constellation, (i.e. Mṛgaśīrṣa).

## Chapter 200 - Greatness of Kāmakuṇḍa

## \|\| 1.200.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ vidhvaṃsite yajñe gatāste brāhmaṇā gṛham \|*  
*aprāptakāmanā devi ye cānye tatra vai gatāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*haro'pi vigatāmarṣaḥ kailāsaṃ parvataṃ gataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*etasminneva kāle tu tārakonāma dānavaḥ \|*  
*utpannaḥ sa mahābāhurdevānāṃ baladarpahā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tena indrādikānsarvānsurāñjitvā mahāhave \|*  
*svargaḥ svairvyāpito devi brahmalokaṃ tato gatāḥ \|*  
*ūcuḥ surā duḥkhayuktā brahmāṇaṃ parvatātmaje \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-4. When the Yajña was thus destroyed, those Brāhmaṇas and others who had gone there went home with their desires frustrated. Hara too ceased to be angry and returned to the Kailāsa Mountain.

At this very time a mighty Dānava named Tāraka was born. He was destined to be one who would destroy the power and arrogance of Devas.

He conquered Indra and all other Suras in a great battle. O goddess, the whole of heaven was filled by him with his own people. The miserable Suras went to Brahmaloka, O daughter of the Mountain, and appealed to Brahmā:

## \|\| 1.200.5-6 \|\|

*tārakeṇa suraśreṣṭha svargānnirvāsitā vayam \|*  
*svayamindraḥ samabhavadvasavo'nye tathā kṛtāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*rudrāḥ sādhyāstathā viśve aśvinau marutastathā \|*  
*ādityāśca vadhopāyaṃ tasmādvada pitāmaha \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. “O most excellent one among Suras, we have been driven out of Svarga by Tāraka. He has become Indra himself. Viṣṇu and others, Rudras. Sādhyas, the Viśvedevas, Aśvins, Maruts and Ādityas too have been similarly (substituted). O Pitāmaha, do suggest a means to kill him.”

## \|\| 1.200.7-8 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*avadhyaḥ sa tu sarveṣāṃ devānāmiti me matiḥ \|*  
*ṛte tu śāṃkaraṃ tejo nānyena vinipātyate \|*  
*tasmādgacchata bhadraṃ vo devadevaṃ maheśvaram \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tasya bhāryā mṛtā pūrvaṃ jātā himavato gṛhe \|*  
*tasyāṃ ca jāyate putraḥ sa haniṣyati tārakam \|*  
*tasmātprasādayadhvaṃ vai tadarthaṃ śūlapāṇinam \|\| 8 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

7-8. It is my considered opinion that he cannot be slain by any of Devas. He cannot be brought down by anyone except the radiance of Śaṅkara. Hence, welfare unto you all, do go to Maheśvara, the Lord of Devas. His earlier wife passed away and is reborn in the abode of Himavān. A son will be born to her. He will kill Tāraka. Hence for that purpose propitiate the Trident-bearing Lord.

## \|\| 1.200.9-10 \|\|

*tato devaiḥ samādiṣṭaḥ kāmadevo varānane \|*  
*mṛtabhāryaṃ haraṃ gatvā tataḥ pīḍaya sāyakaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*yenāsau kāmasaṃtapto bhāryārthaṃ yatnavānbhavet \|*  
*ayaṃ gacchatu te bhrātā vasaṃtaśca manoharaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Then, O lady of excellent countenance, Kāmadeva was directed by Devas to go to the widower Hara, to assail him with his arrows so that due to the distress of love he (Hara) might endeavour to get a wife for himself. They said, “Let this charming Vasanta, your brother, also go.”

## \|\| 1.200.11 \|\|

*sa tatheti pratijñāya kailāsaṃ parvataṃ gataḥ \|*  
*tato dṛṣṭvā mahādevaḥ kāmadevaṃ dhṛtāyudham \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Promising “That shall be done”, he proceeded towards Kailāsa mountain. Mahādeva saw Kāmadeva fully armed.

## \|\| 1.200.12 \|\|

*vasantasahitaṃ devi rudro'ndhakaniṣūdanaḥ \|*  
*gaṃgādvāramanuprāpya apaśyadyāvadagrataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O goddess, Rudra, the slayer of Andhaka, realized that Kāma was accompanied by Vasanta. He proceeded to Gaṅgādvāra and saw (found) Kāma before him.

## \|\| 1.200.13-15 \|\|

*dattāyudhaṃ kāmadevaṃ dudruve sa bhayātpunaḥ \|*  
*tato vārāṇasīṃ gatvā naimiṣaṃ puṣkaraṃ tathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*śrīkaṃṭhaṃ rudrakoṭiṃ ca kurukṣetraṃ gayāṃ tathā \|*  
*jvālāmārgaṃ prayāgaṃ ca viśālāmarbudaṃ śubham \|\| 14 \|\|*

*bahūnvarṣagaṇānevaṃ bhramansa dharaṇītale \|*  
*kāmadevabhayāddevi devadevo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. On seeing Kāmadeva equipped with his weapon Rudra fled out of fear. He fled to Vārāṇasī, Naimiṣa, Puṣkara, Śrīkaṇṭha, Rudrakoṭi, Kurukṣetra, Gayā, Jvālāmārga, Prayāga, Viśālā, and the splendid Arbuda (Mt. Abu). Thus, O goddess, Maheśvara, the Lord of Devas, wandered over the earth for many years due to the fear of Kāmadeva.

## \|\| 1.200.16 \|\|

*avaikṣata tadā kāmaṃ visphārya nayanaṃ tadā \|*  
*tṛtīyaṃ devadeveśi devadevastrilocanaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thereupon, O goddess of the chiefs of Devas, the Three-eyed Lord of Devas widely opened the third eye and stared at Kāma.

## \|\| 1.200.17 \|\|

*tasya taṃ vīkṣamāṇasya saṃjātāḥ pāvakārciṣaḥ \|*  
*tābhiḥ sa dhanuṣā yukto bhasmasātsamapadyata \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Even as he looked at (that Kāma) sparks of fire rose up and he was reduced to ash along with his bow.

## \|\| 1.200.18 \|\|

*taṃ dagdhvā bhagavāñchaṃbhurgatvā roṣasya nirṇayam \|*  
*nivāsamakarottatra kṣetre prābhāsike śubhe \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After burning him, Lord Śaṃbhu’s fury got pacified. He took up his residence in the auspicious Prābhāsika Kṣetra.

## \|\| 1.200.19 \|\|

*tasmindagdhe tadā kāme ratiḥ śokaparāyaṇā \|*  
*vilalāpa suduḥkhārtā patibhaktiparāyaṇā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. After the burning of Kama, Rati became grief-stricken. Very loyal to her husband, the miserable woman lamented loudly.

Rati lamented:

## \|\| 1.200.20 \|\|

*hā nāthanātha bhoḥ svāminkiṃ jahāsi pativratām \|*  
*pativratāṃ patiprāṇāṃ kasmānmāṃ tyajasi prabho \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O Lord, O Lord, O my master, why do you leave off your chaste wife. O Lord, why do you abandon me, a chaste wife to whom the husband is the very vital breath?

## \|\| 1.200.21-22 \|\|

*evaṃ vilapatīṃ tāṃ tu vāguvācāśarīriṇī \|*  
*mā tvaṃ ruda viśālākṣi punareva patistava \|\| 21 \|\|*

*prasādāddevadevasya ucchvāsyati śivasya tu \|*  
*etāṃ vācaṃ ratiḥ śrutvā tataḥ svasthā babhūva ha \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Even as she was lamenting thus, an unembodied aerial voice spoke to her: “O lady of large eyes, do not cry. With the favour of Śiva, the Lord of the Devas, your husband will breathe once again.” On hearing these words, Rati became composed and normal.

## \|\| 1.200.23-24 \|\|

*tato devāḥ śivaṃ natvā prārthayāmāsurīśvari \|*  
*kalatrasaṃgrahaṃ deva kuru kāryārthasaṃgrahe \|\| 23 \|\|*

*eṣa kāmastvayā dagdhaḥ krodhena mahatā svayam \|*  
*vinā tena vibho naṣṭā sṛṣṭirvai dharaṇītale \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Thereafter, Devas bowed down to Śiva, O goddess of Suras, and prayed to him: “O Lord, in our interest do take up a wife unto you. In your limitless fury, this Kāma has been burnt down by you. O Lord, bereft of him the entire created beings of the surface of the world are no better than dead.”

## \|\| 1.200.25 \|\|

*bhagavānuvāca \|*  
*eṣa kāmo mayā dagdhaḥ krodhena surasattamāḥ \|*  
*tasmādanaṃga evaiṣa prajāsu pracariṣyati \|*  
*tadvīryastatprabhāvaśca vinā dehaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 25 \|\|*

The Lord said:

25\. O excellent Suras, this Kāma has been burnt down by me out of anger. Hence he will move about among the subjects in his incorporeal state itself. He will have the same power and vigour even without a physical body.

## \|\| 1.200.26 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhagavankuru pūrvaṃ tvaṃ saṃsmarasva ratīśvaram \|*  
*hitāya sarva lokānāṃ yathā naḥ pratyayo bhavet \|\| 26 \|\|*

The Devas said:

26\. O Lord, do this at the outset. Remember the Lord of Rati for the sake of the welfare of the worlds, so that we can have assurance.

## \|\| 1.200.27 \|\|

*tataḥ sa smṛtavānkāmaṃ svayaṃ devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tatastacchāśvataṃ liṃgaṃ samuttasthau mahītale \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thereupon, Lord Maheśvara himself remembered Kama. Then the eternal Liṅga rose up from the surface of the earth.

## \|\| 1.200.28 \|\|

*kṛtasmaraḥ punastatra anaṃgo balavāṃstathā \|*  
*tenoḍhā śailajā tena śaṃkareṇa mahātmanā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Though unembodied, Kāma who was recollected (Kṛtasmara) became powerful yet. Thanks to (the power of) Kama, the Daughter of the Mountain was married by the noble-souled Śaṅkara.

## \|\| 1.200.29 \|\|

*jātaḥ skandaḥ suraśreṣṭhastārako yena sūditaḥ \|*  
*patitenaiva liṃgena yasmāccaiva kṛtasmaraḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Skanda, the foremost one among Suras, was born. Tāraka was slain by him even though the Liṅga (Kāma) was fallen because it was Kṛtasmara (was recollected).

## \|\| 1.200.30 \|\|

*tasmātkṛtasmaro loke kīrtyate sa mahītale \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā na jaḍo nāṃdho nāsukhī na ca durbhagaḥ \|*  
*jāyate tu kadā martyo na daridro na rogavān \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. He is therefore glorified as Kṛtasmara in the world. A man who views the deity will never become dull, blind, devoid of happiness and unfortunate. The man will never be poor or sickly.

## \|\| 1.200.31 \|\|

*evaṃ te sarvamākhyātaṃ yanmāṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi \|*  
*dagdho yathā smaraḥ pūrvaṃ punarvīryānvitaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Thus everything has been narrated to you, whatever you have asked viz. how Smara was burnt at the outset and how he became inspired with power, virility once again.

## \|\| 1.200.32 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tatraiva saṃsthitaṃ kuṇḍaṃ dakṣiṇena kṛtasmarāt \|*  
*kāmakuṃḍeti vai nāma yatrodbhūtaḥ punaḥ smaraḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

32\. There itself to the south of Kṛtasmara is situated a sacred Kuṇḍa. Its name is Kāmakuṇḍa where Smara was born again.

## \|\| 1.200.33 \|\|

*anaṃgarūpī devyatra snānādvai rūpavānbhavet \|*  
*ikṣavastatra vai deyāḥ suvarṇaṃ gāstathaiva ca \|*  
*vastrāṇi caiva vidhivadbrāhmaṇe vedapārage \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O goddess, Smara was born there again but without a body. A devotee who takes his holy bath here shall become handsome. Sugarcane should be gifted there to a Brāhmaṇa who has mastered the Vedas. Similarly gold, cows and garments also should be given.

## Chapter 201 - Greatness of Kālabhairava Śmaśāna

## \|\| 1.201.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tasminsthāne mahādevi smaśānaṃ kālabhairavam \|*  
*brahmakuṇḍaṃ varārohe yāvaddevaḥ kṛtasmaraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tatra ye prāṇino dagdhā mṛtāḥ kālaviparyayāt \|*  
*te sarve muktimāyāṃti mahāpātakino'pi vā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kṛtasmarānmahādevi yāvanmaṃkīśvaraḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*mahāsmaśānaṃ taddevi apunarbhavadāyakam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. At that spot, O great goddess, is the cremation ground (of) Kālabhairava. From Brahmakuṇḍa, O beautiful lady, up to Lord Kṛtasmara (is the extent).

Living beings who die due to the lapse of time and get cremated there, attain salvation even if they are great sinners.

O great goddess, the spot extends from Kṛtasmara up to the deity Maṅkīśvara. That portion (of) the great cremation ground bestows stopping of recurrent birth.

## \|\| 1.201.4-5 \|\|

*tasminsthāne vahedyatra viṣuvaṃ prāṇināṃ priye \|*  
*tatroṣaraṃ smṛtaṃ kṣetraṃ tanme priyataraṃ sadā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kalpāṃte'pi na muṃcāmi avimuktātpriyaṃ mama \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. At that place (Cremation ground) where there is the flow of Viṣuva (Suṣumṇā Nāḍī) of all living beings, is the holy spot of Uṣara (Arid land—no rebirth-growing). It is a favourite of mine always. I do not leave it even at the end of a Kalpa. I like it more than Avimukta” (i.e. Banaras).

## Chapter 202 - Greatness of Rāmeśvara Ksetra

## \|\| 1.202.1-2 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi rāmeśvaramanuttamam \|*  
*maṃkīśāddakṣiṇe bhāge āgneye tu kṛtasmarāt \|*  
*pūrvatastu sarasvatyā balabhadrapratiṣṭhitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yatra mukto'bhavaddevi rāmo brahmavadhātkila \|*  
*pātakātpratilomāṃ tāmagāhata sarasvatīm \|\| 2 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-2. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the excellent shrine of Rāmeśvara. It was installed by Balabhadra to the south of Maṅkīśa, south-east of Kṛtasmara and east of Sarasvatī.

It is the place where, it is said, Rāma (i.e. Balarāma) was rid of the killing of Brahmā (a Sūta who sat in the place of Brahmā in a sacrifice: vide verse 33), and dived into Sarasvatī flowing backwards.

## \|\| 1.202.3 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ sa pātakānmuktaḥ kathaṃ pāpamabhūtpurā \|*  
*kathaṃ tatsthāpitaṃ liṃgaṃ kiṃprabhāvaṃ vadasva me \|\| 3 \|\|*

The Devī said:

3\. Then how did he get rid of the sin? How was that Liṅga installed? What is its efficacy? Do tell me how at the outset he incurred the sin.

## \|\| 1.202.4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi kathāṃ pāpapraṇāśinīm \|*  
*yāṃ śrutvā mānavo devi muktaḥ saṃsārasāgarāt \|*  
*sarvānkāmānsa labhate satataṃ manasi priyān \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

4\. Listen, O goddess, I shall narrate the sin-destroying story, listening to which, O goddess, a man becomes released from the ocean of worldly existence. He shall obtain all the desired items lovingly cherished always in the mind.

## \|\| 1.202.5-8 \|\|

*rāmaḥ pūrvaṃ parāṃ prītiṃ kṛtvā kṛṣṇasya lāṃgalī \|*  
*cintayāmāsa bahudhā kiṃ kṛtaṃ sukṛtaṃ bhavet \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇena hi vinā nāhaṃ yāsye duryodhanāntikam \|*  
*pāṇḍavānvā samāśritya kathaṃ duryodhanaṃ nṛpam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*jāmātaraṃ tathā śiṣyaṃ ghātayiṣye nareśvaram \|*  
*tasmānna pārthaṃ yāsyāmi nāpi duryodhanaṃ nṛpam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tīrtheṣvāplāvayiṣyāmi tāvadātmānamātmanā \|*  
*kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca yāvadaṃtāya kalpate \|\| 8 \|\|*

5-8. Rāma, armed with the plough, delighted Kṛṣṇa very much and thought thus: ‘What should I do which will be a meritorious act’. Without Kṛṣṇa, I will not go to (the side of) Duryodhana. How can I resort to the Pāṇḍavas and kill Duryodhana, the king, my disciple and son-in-law? Therefore, I will not go to the son of Kuntī (i.e. Yudhiṣṭhira) nor to King Duryodhana. I shall immerse myself in holy Tīrthas till this war ends with the end of dispute among Kurus and Pāṇḍavas.

## \|\| 1.202.9 \|\|

*ityādiśya hṛṣīkeśaṃ pārthaduryodhanāvapi \|*  
*jagāma dvārakāṃ śauriḥ svasainyaiśca parīvṛtaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Having told this to Hṛṣīkeśa, Pārtha and Duryodhana, Śauri (i.e. Rāma) went to Dvārakā surrounded by his armies.

## \|\| 1.202.10 \|\|

*gatvā dvārāvatīṃ rāmo hṛṣṭatuṣṭajanākulām \|*  
*svairantaḥpuragaiḥ sārdhaṃ papau pānaṃ halāyudhaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Rāma with the plough as his weapon, went to the city of Dvārāvatī teeming with delighted and contented people. There he indulged in a drunken bout with the persons (ladies) of his Antaḥpura.

## \|\| 1.202.11 \|\|

*pītapāno jagāmātha raivatodyānamṛddhimat \|*  
*haste gṛhītvā sa gadāṃ revatyādibhiranvitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. After imbibing wine, he seized a mace with his hand and went to the splendid garden of Raivatodyāna accompanied by Revatī and others.

## \|\| 1.202.12 \|\|

*strīkadaṃbakamadhyastho yayau mattavadāskhalan \|*  
*dadarśa ca vanaṃ vīro ramaṇīyamanuttamam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Moving in the midst of groups of women, he went along with faltering steps like an inebriated person. The valorous Rāma surveyed an excellent and fascinating park.

## \|\| 1.202.13 \|\|

*sarvatra tarupuṣpāḍhyaṃ śākhāmṛgagaṇākulam \|*  
*puṣpa padmavanopetaṃ sapalvalamahāvanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Everywhere there were flowering trees abounding in monkeys. There were extensive forests with puddles and lakes full of clusters of lotuses.

## \|\| 1.202.14 \|\|

*sa śṛṇvanprītijanakānvanyānmadakalāñchubhān \|*  
*śrotraramyānsumadhurāñchabdānkhagasukheritān \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He listened to the delightful notes of music issuing forth from the beaks of birds charming to the ears. The diverse sounds indicated that the forest birds were inebriated too.

## \|\| 1.202.15 \|\|

*sarvataḥ phalaratnāḍhyānsarvataḥ kusumojjvalān \|*  
*apaśyatpādapāṃścaiva vihagairanumoditān \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He saw many trees all round laden with gem-like fruits, and glittering with flowers. The chirping birds appeared to be cheering them.

## \|\| 1.202.16-21 \|\|

*āmrānāgrātakānbhavyānnālikerānsatiṃdukān \|*  
*ābalvanāṃsthā pītāndāḍimānbījapūrakān \|\| 16 \|\|*

*panasāṃllakucānmocāṃstāpāṃścāpi manoharān \|*  
*pālevatānkusaṃkullānnalinānatha vetasān \|\| 17 \|\|*

*bhallātakānāmalakīṃstindukāṃśca mahāphalān \|*  
*iṃgudānkaramardāṃśca harītakabibhītakān \|\| 18 \|\|*

*etānanyāṃśca sa tarūndadarśa yadunandanaḥ \|*  
*tathaivāśokapunnāgaketakībakulāṃstathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*caṃpakānsaptaparṇāṃśca karṇikārānsumālatīḥ \|*  
*pārijātānkovidārā nmandārendīvarāṃstathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*pāṭalānpuṣpitānrambhāndevadārudrumāṃstathā \|*  
*śālāṃstālāṃśca stamālāṃniculānvañjulāṃstathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

16-21. There were Āmras (mango trees), excellent Āmrātakas, Nālikeras (coconuts), Tindukas, Balvalas, yellow Dāḍimas (pomegranates), Bījapūrakas, Panasas (Jackfruit trees), Lakucas, Mocas, charming Tāpas, Pālevatas, Kusaṃkullas, Nalinas, Vetasas (canes), Bhallātakas, Āmalakīs, Tindukas with big fruits, Iṅgudas, Karamardas, Harītakas and Bibhītakas. The scion of the family of Yadus saw these and other trees. So also he saw Aśokas, Punnāgas, Ketakīs, Bakulas, Campakas, Saptaparṇas, Karṇikāras, excellent Mālatīs, Pārijatas, Kovidāras, Mandāras, Indīvaras, Pāṭalas in full bloom, Raṃbhās (bananas), Devadāru trees, Śālas, Tālas, Tamālas, Niculas and Vañjulas.

## \|\| 1.202.22-23 \|\|

*cakoraiḥ śatapatraiśca bhṛṃgarājaiḥ samāvṛtān \|*  
*kokilaiḥ kalaviṃkaiśca hārītairjīvajīvakaiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*priyaputraiścātakaiśca śukairanyairvihaṃgamaiḥ \|*  
*śrotraramyaṃ sumadhuraṃ kūja dbhiścāpyadhiṣṭhitaiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. These trees abounded in birds perching on them, such as Cakoras, Śatapatras(?), lotuses full of Bhṛṅgarājas (bees), Kokilas (cuckoos), Kalaviṅkas, Hārītas, Jīvajīvakas, Cātakas fond of their young ones, parrots and other birds. They were perched on the trees and chirping very sweetly.

## \|\| 1.202.24-26 \|\|

*sarāṃsi ca sapadmāni manojñasalilāni ca \|*  
*kumudaiḥ puṇḍarīkaiśca tathā rocanakotpalaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kahlāraiḥ kamalaiścāpi carcitāni samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*kadaṃbaiścakravākaiśca tathaiva jalakukkuṭaiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*kāraṇḍavaiḥ plavairhaṃsaiḥ kūrmairmaṃḍubhireva ca \|*  
*etairanyaiśca kīrṇāni tathānyairjalavā sibhiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. There were lakes with fascinating waters and lotuses in full bloom. There were lilies, Puṇḍarīkas (white lotuses), glistening Utpalas, Kalhāras, Kamalas spread everywhere. The place was full of aquatic birds such as Kadaṃbakas, Cakravākas, Jalakukkuṭas, Kāraṇḍavas, floating (swimming) Haṃsas (swans), and tortoises and Maṇḍus (frogs). These and other aquatic animals filled the lakes.

## \|\| 1.202.27 \|\|

*krameṇa saṃcaranrāmaḥ prekṣamāṇo manoramam \|*  
*jagāmānugataḥ strībhirlatāgṛhamanuttamam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Proceeding ahead slowly and followed by the women, Rāma surveyed the charming scene and reached a grotto of excellent features.

## \|\| 1.202.28-29 \|\|

*sa dadarśa dvijāṃstatra vedavedāṃgapāra gān \|*  
*kauśikānbhārgavāṃścaiva bhāradvājāṃśca gautamān \|\| 28 \|\|*

*vividheṣu ca saṃbhūtānvaṃśeṣu dvijasattamān \|*  
*kathāśravaṇasotkaṇṭhānupaviṣṭānmahā tmanaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. He saw Brāhmaṇas who had mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas hailing from different families such as Kauśikas, Bhārgavas, Bhāradvājas and Gautamas. These excellent Brāhmaṇas of noble souls were seated there and were eager to listen to the stories (from Sūta).

## \|\| 1.202.30 \|\|

*kṛṣṇājinottarīyeṣu kūrceṣu ca vṛsīṣu ca \|*  
*sūte ca teṣāṃ madhyasthaṃ kathayānaṃ kathāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. They were seated on Darbha grass covered with antelope-skins as well as Bṛsīs (special mats) Sūta was seated in their midst narrating excellent tales and legends.

## \|\| 1.202.31-32 \|\|

*paurāṇikāḥ surarṣīṇāmā dyānāṃ caritakriyāḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ dvijāḥ sarve madhupānāruṇekṣaṇam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*matto'yamiti manvānāḥ samuttasthustvarānvitāḥ \|*  
*pūjayanto haladharaṃ tamṛte sūtavaṃśajam \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. The Brāhmaṇas assembled there, were well-versed in the Purāṇas and were glad to listen to the stories and conducts of the primordial celestial sages. On seeing Rāma with eyes reddened due to drinking wine they thought, ‘He is thorougly drunk’, and hurriedly got up and began to honour and adore Halāyudha excepting Sūta who continued to sit.

## \|\| 1.202.33-34 \|\|

*tataḥ krodhasamāviṣṭo halī sūtaṃ mahābalaḥ \|*  
*nijaghāna vivṛttākṣaḥ kṣobhitāśeṣadānavaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*anvāsite padaṃ brāhmyaṃ tasminsūte nipātite \|*  
*niṣkrāntāste dvijāḥ sarve vanātkṛṣṇājināṃbarāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. The powerful Halin became angry. With eyes staring wide open, the mighty Rāma who could make all Dānavas agitated, killed Sūta. When Sūta who had occupied the seat of Brahmā was slain all those Brāhmaṇas clad in black-antelope skins dispersed.

## \|\| 1.202.35 \|\|

*avadhūtaṃ tathātmānaṃ manyamāno halāyudhaḥ \|*  
*cintayāmāsa sumahanmayā pāpamidaṃ kṛtam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Considering himself insulted, Halāyudha thought thus: ‘A great sin has been committed by me.

## \|\| 1.202.36 \|\|

*brahmāsanagato hyeṣa yaḥ sūto vinipātitaḥ \|*  
*tathā hyete dvijāḥ sarve māmavekṣya vinirgatāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. This person, Sūta who was seated in the Brahmāsana has been slain. That is why all these Brāhmaṇas went away on seeing me.

## \|\| 1.202.37 \|\|

*śarīrasya ca me gandho lohasyevāsukhāvahaḥ \|*  
*ātmānaṃ cāvagacchāmi brahmaghnamiti kutsitam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The odour from my body is displeasing and despicable like that of iron that causes unhappiness. I know that I am a despicable Brahmaghna (Brāhmaṇa-slayer).

## \|\| 1.202.38 \|\|

*dhiṅmamārthaṃ tathā madyaṃ mahimānamakīrtidam \|*  
*yenā viṣṭena sumahanmayā pāpamidaṃ kṛtam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Fie upon my wealth, greatness and this ignominous wine overwhelmed by which this great sin has been committed by me!

## \|\| 1.202.39 \|\|

*smṛtyuktaṃ te kariṣyāmi prāyaścittaṃ yathāvidhi \|*  
*uktamastyeva manunā prāyaścittādikaṃ kramāt \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. I shall perform the expiatory rites mentioned in the Smṛtis. Indeed expiatory and other rites have been duly laid down by Manu.

## \|\| 1.202.40 \|\|

*japaḥ pracchannapāpānāṃ manastāpa eva ca \|*  
*bhūtātmanastapovidye buddherjñānaṃ viśodhanam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. In the case of Pracchannapāpas (those who unknowingly or unwittingly commit a sin), Japa and repentance of the mind are the expiatory rites. Tapas (Kṛcchra, Cāndrāyaṇa etc.) and Vidyā (repetition of Mantras) are the expiatory rites for the physical form. The expiatory rite for the intellect is perfect knowledge.

## \|\| 1.202.41 \|\|

*kṣetreśvarasya vijñānādviśuddhiḥ paramā matā \|*  
*śarīrasya viśuddhistu prāyaścittaiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The cleansing of the Kṣetreśvara (individual soul) through Vijñāna (perfect spiritual knowledge) is considered great. The purification of the body is by means of the different kinds of expiatory rites.

## \|\| 1.202.42 \|\|

*tato'dyataḥ kariṣyāmi vrataṃ dvādaśavārṣikam \|*  
*svakarmakhyāpanaṃ kurvanprāyaścittamanuttamam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Therefore, from today, I shall perform an excellent Vrata lasting for twelve years. This expiatory rite I shall perform is proclaiming my misdemeanour.

## \|\| 1.202.43 \|\|

*iyaṃ viśuddhirajñānāddhatvā cākāmato dvijam \|*  
*kāmato brāhmaṇavadhe niṣkṛtirna vidhīyate \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. This purificatory rite is for the murder of a Brāhmaṇa unwittingly done or committed without any ulterior selfish motive. If a Brāhmaṇa is slain intentionally for self-interest, there is no expiatory rite.

## \|\| 1.202.44 \|\|

*yaḥ kāmato mahāpāpaṃ naraḥ kurynātkathaṃcana \|*  
*na tasya niṣkṛtirdṛṣṭā bhṛgvagnipatanādṛte \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. If a man commits a great sin with self-interest or personal grudge, there is no expiatory rite for him except leaping down to death from a precipice or entering into a blazing fire.

## \|\| 1.202.45 \|\|

*akāmataḥ kṛte pāpe prāyaścittaṃ vidurbudhāḥ \|*  
*kāmakārakṛte'pyāhureke śrutinidarśanāt \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Learned men know that expiatory rites are recommended when the sin is committed without self-interest. Some say that even when it is committed with personal motive there is expiatory rite as indicated in the Śruti.

## \|\| 1.202.46 \|\|

*vidhiḥ prāthamikastasmāddvitīye dviguṇaṃ caret \|*  
*tṛtīye triguṇaṃ proktaṃ caturthe nāsti niṣkṛtiḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. This rule is applicable when the sin is committed for the first time. If it is repeated a second time, the expiatory rite is to be doubled; for a third time it is trebled. If it is repeated further for the fourth time there is no expiatory rite at all.

## \|\| 1.202.47 \|\|

*auṣadhaṃ snehamāhāraṃ dadadgobrāhmaṇādiṣu \|*  
*dīyamāne vipattiḥ syānna sa pāpena lipyate \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. If a medicinal oil or ghee or food is given to a Brāhmaṇa or others and if there is a disaster (death) in the course thereof, he is not defiled by the sin.

## \|\| 1.202.48 \|\|

*akāraṇaṃ tu yaḥ kaściddvijaḥ prāṇānparityajet \|*  
*tasyaiva tatra doṣaḥ syānna tu yo'smai dadāti tat \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. If for no apparent reason, a Brāhmaṇa forsakes life, the fault is that of his alone and not of the man who gives it (medicine etc.).

## \|\| 1.202.49-50 \|\|

*pariṣkṛto yadā vipro hatvā'tmānaṃ mṛto yadi \|*  
*nirguṇaḥ sahasā krodhādgṛhakṣetrādikāraṇāt \|\| 49 \|\|*

*trivārṣikaṃ vrataṃ kuryā tpratilomāṃ sarasvatīm \|*  
*gacchedvāpi viśuddhyarthaṃ tatpāpasyeti niścitam \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. If a consecrated Brāhmaṇa who is one without any good quality, gets furious over domestic matters or those of agricultural lands etc., and suddenly kills himself and dies (the witness thereof) shall perform Vrata for three years and visit Sarasvatī river flowing backwards for wiping off that sin. This is the fixed rule.

## \|\| 1.202.51 \|\|

*uddiśya kupito hatvā toṣitaṃ vāsayetpunaḥ \|*  
*tasminmṛte na doṣo'sti dvayorucchrāvaṇe kṛte \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. When someone gets furious and strikes but is pacified and made to stay there, but if he dies, there is no crime if the same is proclaimed loudly twice (or in the presence of two).

## \|\| 1.202.52-54 \|\|

*ṣaṇḍhaṃ tu brāhmaṇaṃ hatvā śūdrahatyāvrataṃ caret \|*  
*bahūnāmekakāryāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ śastradhāriṇām \|\| 52 \|\|*

*yadyeko ghātayettatra sarve te ghātakāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*prāyaścitte vyavasite yadi kartā vipadyate \|\| 53 \|\|*

*enastatprāpnuyādenamiha loke paratra ca \|*  
*tadahaṃ kiṃ karomyeṣa kva gacchāmi durātmavān \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. After killing an impotent Brāhmaṇa, one should perform the expiatory rite as in the case of the murder of a Śūdra.

When many are engaged in a single task and all of them bear weapons and if one of them murders someone, all the others too are considered murderers.

When expiatory rite is undertaken and the performer meets with danger, sin will affect him in this world as well as in the other.

Therefore, now that I have committed an evil deed, what shall I do? Where shall I go?

## \|\| 1.202.55 \|\|

*dhiṅmāṃ ca pāpacaritaṃ mahāduṣkṛtakarmiṇam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Fie upon me of sinful conduct, the perpetrator of a great evil deed!’

## \|\| 1.202.56 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*ityevaṃ vilapanyāvacchokā kulitamānasaḥ \|*  
*tāvadākāśasaṃbhūtā vāguvācāśarīriṇī \|\| 56 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

56\. While he was lamenting thus with the mind extremely agitated, an aerial unembodied voice spoke thus:

## \|\| 1.202.57 \|\|

*bhobho rāma na saṃtāpastvayā kāryaḥ kathaṃcana \|*  
*gaccha prābhāsikaṃ kṣetraṃ yatra devī sarasvatī \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. “O Rāma, you need not at all feel distressed. Go to the Prābhāsika Kṣetra where the divine Sarasvatī flows.

## \|\| 1.202.58 \|\|

*pañcasrotāḥ sthitā tatra pañcapātakanāśanī \|*  
*nadīnāṃ pravarā sā tu brahmabhūtā sarasvatī \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The most excellent of rivers, Sarasvatī, identical with Brahman, quells the five sins through her Fivefold currents.

## \|\| 1.202.59 \|\|

*ekataḥ sarvatīrthāni brahmāṇḍe sacarācare \|*  
*gaṃgādīni naraśreṣṭha teṣāṃ puṇyā sarasvatī \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Let there be all the Tīrthas in the whole of the Cosmic Egg, beginning with Gaṅgā, O most excellent one among men, on one side. The meritorious Sarasvatī far excels them.

## \|\| 1.202.60 \|\|

*tāvadgarjaṃti pāpāni brahmahatyādikāni ca \|*  
*yāvanna dṛśyate devī prabhāsasthā sara svatī \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. All the sins beginning with that of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter roar only as long as the divine Sarasvatī situated in Prabhāsa is not seen.

## \|\| 1.202.61 \|\|

*tasmāttatraiva gaccha tvaṃ yatra devī sarasvatī \|*  
*nānyaistīrthaiḥ sahasraistvaṃ kartuṃ śakyo vikalmaṣaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Hence go there itself where the divine Sarasvatī is present. You cannot be rid of the sins by other Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.202.62 \|\|

*tanmā kārṣīrvilaṃbaṃ tvaṃ gaccha tīraṃ mahodadheḥ \|*  
*prābhāsike mahādevīṃ pratilomāṃ vigāhaya \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Hence do not delay. Go to the shore of the ocean. In the holy Kṣetra of Prābhāsika, dive into the divine Sarasvatī which flows backwards.

## \|\| 1.202.63 \|\|

*tatraivārādhaya vibhuṃ liṃgarūpiṇamīśvaram \|*  
*pratiṣṭhāpya mahāpāpācchārī rāttvaṃ vimokṣyasi \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. There itself install the Lord Īśvara in the form of a Liṅga and propitiate him. You will be rid of the great physical

## \|\| 1.202.64 \|\|

*iti śrutvā vaco rāmaḥ paramānaṃdapūritaḥ \|*  
*prabhāsakṣetragamane matiṃ cakre mahāmanāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. On hearing these words, Rāma was filled with excess of delight. The noble-minded one resolved to go to Prabhāsa-Kṣetra.

G5. Then accompanied by his army and equipped with all requisite articles, he came to the great Kṣetra well-known as Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 1.202.66 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā manorama tīrthaṃ sarasvatyabdhisaṃgame \|*  
*cakāra hṛdi saṃkalpaṃ prati lomāvagāhane \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. On seeing the charming Tīrtha at the confluence of Sarasvatī and the ocean, he resolved to take bath where the river flows backwards (pratilomāvagāhana).

## \|\| 1.202.67 \|\|

*āhūya brāhmaṇāṃstatra prabhāsakṣetravāsinaḥ \|*  
*samyagyātrāvidhānena yātrāṃ tatrākarodvibhuḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The Lord summoned the Brāhmaṇas residing in Prabhāsa Kṣetra. He performed the pilgrimage in accordance with the regulations regarding perfect pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.202.68 \|\|

*yāni prābhāsike kṣetre tīrthāni vividhāni tu \|*  
*raviyojanasaṃsthāni teṣu yātrāṃ cakāra saḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. He performed the pilgrimage to all the different kinds of Tīrthas situated within the area of twelve Yojanas thereof.

## \|\| 1.202.69-70 \|\|

*pratyekaṃ ca dadau teṣu dānāni vividhāni tu \|*  
*tathā'dhaḥ sthāpa yāmāsa sarasvatyabdhisaṃgame \|\| 69 \|\|*

*pūrvabhāge mahāliṃgaṃ kṛtvā yajñavidhikriyām \|*  
*evaṃ kṛte mahādevi vimuktaḥ pātakairabhūt \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. To each one of them he gave different kinds of gifts. At the confluence of Sarasvatī and the sea, lower down to the east, he installed the great Liṅga after performing a Yajña. When this was performed, O great goddess, he became rid of sins.

## \|\| 1.202.71 \|\|

*nirmarlāṃgastato devi dināni daśa saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*tatastāṃ caiva sa snātvā pratilomāṃ kramādyayau \|*  
*plakṣāvaharaṇaṃ yāvatsamudrācca himāhvayam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Then, O goddess, he stayed there for ten days in the state of pure limbs (body). After taking the holy bath he gradually went in the opposite direction from the ocean upto the Himālaya named Plakṣāvaharaṇa.

## \|\| 1.202.72 \|\|

*evaṃ muktaḥ sa pāpaughai rāmo'bhūtprathitaḥ priye \|*  
*tasya liṃgasya māhātmyātsarasvatyāḥ prasādataḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Thus, O my beloved, thanks to the greatness of that Liṅga and the favour of Sarasvatī, he became rid of the series of sins.

## \|\| 1.202.73 \|\|

*yastatpūjayate devi liṃgaṃ pāpabhayāpaham \|*  
*rāmeśvareti kathitaṃ so'pi mucyeta pātakāt \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. O goddess, he who worships that Liṅga called Rāmeśvara that quells the fear of sins, shall be rid of sins.

## \|\| 1.202.74 \|\|

*aṣṭamyāṃ ca viśeṣeṇa brahmakūrcavidhānataḥ \|*  
*yastatra kurute devi so'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. O goddess, on the eighth lunar day, he who performs the rite in accordance with the regulations governing Brahma Kūrca there, shall get the benefit of an Aśvamedha.

## \|\| 1.202.75 \|\|

*snātvā tatra varārohe sarasvatyabdhisaṃgame \|*  
*rāmeśvaretināmānaṃ tataḥ saṃpūjya śaṃkaram \|*  
*godānaṃ tatra deyaṃ tu samyagyātrāphalepsubhiḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. O beautiful lady, after taking the holy bath at the confluence of Sarasvatī and the ocean and after worshipping the deity Śaṅkara named Rāmeśvara, the gift of cows should be made by those who wish to get the benefit of perfect pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.202.76 \|\|

*ityevaṃ kathitaṃ devi rāmeśvaramahodayam \|*  
*yacchrutvā mānavaḥ samyakchraddhāvānprāpnuyāddivam \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Thus, O goddess, the greatness of Rāmeśvara has been narrated to you. On listening to it, a man with faith shall attain heaven.

## Chapter 203 - Greatness of Maṅkīśvara (Maṅkī-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.203.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi maṃkīśvara mahālayam \|*  
*rāmeśāduttare bhāge devamātuḥ samīpagam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*arkasthalāttato yāmye pūrvataśca kṛtasmarāt \|*  
*liṃgaṃ mahāprabhāvaṃ tu maṃkinā sthāpitaṃ purā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā mānavaḥ samyagaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 3 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-3. Thereafter, O great goddess, a pilgrim should go to the great shrine of Maṅkīśvara to the north of Rāmeśa and in the vicinity of Devamātṛ.

It is to the south of Arkasthala and to the east of Kṛtasmara. This Liṅga of great efficacy was formerly installed by Maṅki. By viewing it properly a man will get the benefit of a perfect horse sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.203.4 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*ko'sau maṃkirmahādeva kathaṃ liṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*kiṃ prabhāvaṃ ca talliṃgametanme vada vistarāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

The Devī said:

4\. O great god, who is this Maṅki? How was the Liṅga installed? Of what efficacy is that Liṅga? Do mention this to me in detail.

## \|\| 1.203.5 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*maṃkirnāmābhavatpūrvaṃ kubjakāyo dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*prabhāsaṃ kṣetramāsādyatapastepe mahattamam \|\| 5 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

5\. Once there was an excellent Brāhmaṇa with a hunchbacked body named Maṅki. He came to Prabhāsa Kṣetra and performed a very great penance.

## \|\| 1.203.6 \|\|

*pratiṣṭhāpya mahādevaṃ śivabhaktiparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*na tutoṣa harastasya vahuvarṣagaṇārcitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Engrossed in devotion to Śiva, he installed a Liṅga of Mahādeva. But Hara was not pleased with him though he was adored by him for many many years.

## \|\| 1.203.7 \|\|

*tasyaivaṃ tapyamānasya siddhiṃ prāptā hyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*tatrārādhya mahādevaṃ svargalokamito gatāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Even as he was performing the penance many attained Siddhi. After propitiating Mahādeva they went to the heavenly world from here.

## \|\| 1.203.8 \|\|

*tato duḥkhaṃ samabhavanmaṃkestatra varānane \|*  
*kasmānme bhagavāṃstuṣṭiṃ na gacchati maheśvaraḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thereupon, O lady of excellent countenance, Maṅki felt deep sorrow. ‘Why is not Lord Maheśvara pleased with me?’

## \|\| 1.203.9 \|\|

*tatastīvraratiṃ cakre kṛtvā tīvranivartanam \|*  
*evaṃ vṛddhatvamāpanno japadhyānaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then he became intensely interested in his penance vowing not to desist (from penance) unless the Lord becomes pleased. Engaged in Japa and meditation, he grew very old.

## \|\| 1.203.10 \|\|

*tasya tuṣṭo mahādevo vayaso'nte varaṃ dadau \|*  
*parituṣṭo'smi te maṃke brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi te \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Mahādeva became pleased with him towards the closing period of his years and granted him a boon: “O Maṅki, I am pleased with you. Tell me what shall I do for you?”

## \|\| 1.203.11 \|\|

*maṃkiruvāca \|*  
*kiṃ vareṇa suraśreṣṭha mama vṛddhasya sāṃpratam \|*  
*kiñcinme paramaṃ duḥkhaṃ sthitasyātra paraṃ prabho \|\| 11 \|\|*

Maṅki said:

11\. O most excellent one among Suras, what interest have I got in a boon now that I have grown too old having stayed here too long, I have a great grievance, O Lord.

## \|\| 1.203.12 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu yatkāraṇaṃ tatra teṣāṃ tava tapasvinām \|*  
*vratacaryāptaye viprāḥ pūjayantyadhikaṃ hi te \|\| 12 \|\|*

Śiva said:

12\. Listen to the reason thereof. (There is a Siddhi) in the case of those sages (and not) in your case. Indeed those Brāhmaṇas worship more than you in getting the daily rites accomplished.

## \|\| 1.203.13 \|\|

*te puṣpāṇi samānīya nānāvarṇāni sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*vṛkṣāṇāmatigaṃdhīni na teṣāṃ harṣakāraṇam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Don’t they collect flowers of different colours and of superior fragrance from trees everywhere? That is the cause of their delight.

## \|\| 1.203.14 \|\|

*tvaṃ punaḥ kubjarūpaśca yajñapūjāparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*na ca prāpnoṣi vṛkṣāṇāṃ śākhāgrāṇyatiyatnavān \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. As for you, you are hunch-backed. Though you are engaged in Yajña and Pūjā and though you exert yourself much, you do not reach the tops of trees.

## \|\| 1.203.15 \|\|

*ekenāpi pradattena puṣpeṇa dvijasattama \|*  
*bhaktyā śirasi liṃgasya labhyate yājñikaṃ phalam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, if even a single flower is offered with devotion on the top of the Liṅga, the benefit of a Yajña is obtained.

## \|\| 1.203.16 \|\|

*liṃgasya dakṣiṇe brahmā svayameva vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*vāme ca bhagavānviṣṇurmadhyehaṃ vai pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. To the right of the Liṅga, Brahmā has established himself. To the left is Lord Viṣṇu and I have been installed in the centre.

## \|\| 1.203.17 \|\|

*trayo'pi pūjitāstena yena liṃgaṃ prapūjitam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. If the Liṅga is worshipped, all the three deities become worshipped by him.

## \|\| 1.203.18 \|\|

*bilvapatraṃ śamīpatraṃ karavīraṃ ca mālatīm \|*  
*unmattakaṃ campakaṃ ca sadyaḥ prītikaraṃ bhavet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Leaves of Bilva and Śamī trees, Karavīra, Mālatī, Unmattaka and Caṃpaka are those that please (the Lord) immediately.

## \|\| 1.203.19 \|\|

*caṃpakāśoka kahlāraiḥ karavīraistathā mama \|*  
*pūjeṣṭā dvijaśārdūla ye cānye vahugaṃdhinaḥ \|*  
*etairhi pūjito nityaṃ śīghraṃ tuṣṭiṃ prayāmyaham \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O tiger among the twice-born, Caṃpaka, Kalhāra and Karavīra and other flowers of great fragrance, are desirable for worship. I like it. Worshipped by these everyday, I become pleased immediately.

## \|\| 1.203.20-21 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭo'si me deva yadi deyo varo mama \|*  
*ihāgatya naraḥ snātvā yo jalenāpi siñcati \|\| 20 \|\|*

*liṃgametaddhi sarvāsāṃ pūjānāṃ phalamāpnuyāt \|*  
*adyaprabhṛti ye vṛkṣā daivikāḥ pārthivāśca ye \|*  
*teṣāṃ sānnidhyamatrāstu prasādāttava śaṃkara \|\| 21 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇa said:

20-21. O Lord, if you are pleased with me, if a boon is to be granted to me, then let this be granted: If a man comes here, takes his holy bath and sprinkles this Liṅga even with water, let him obtain the benefit of all the worships. O Śaṅkara, with your favour, let there be the presence of all types of trees, divine and worldly here.

## \|\| 1.203.22-26 \|\|

*bhagavānuvāca \|*  
*salilenāpi yaḥ pūjāmasmiṃlliṃge vidhāsyati \|*  
*tasya pūjāphalaṃ sarvaṃ bhaviṣyati dvijottama \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vṛkṣāṇāmatrasānnidhyaṃ sarveṣāṃ ca bhaviṣyati \|*  
*adyaprabhṛti nāmnaitannāgasthānaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 23 \|\|*

*yatastu sarvanāgānāṃ sāṃnidhya matra saṃsthitam \|*  
*tvamapi dvijaśārdūla prayāsyasi mamāntikam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*evamuktvā tu bhagavāṃstatraivāntaradhīyata \|*  
*maṃkistu dehamutsajya śivalokaṃ tato gataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ityevaṃ kathitaṃ devi maṃkīśodbhavamuttamam \|*  
*śrutaṃ harati pāpāni samyakchraddhāsamanvitaiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

The Lord said:

22-26. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, if anyone worships this Liṅga even with water, he will get the benefit of all worships. All types of trees will be present here. From today, this spot will be named Nāgasthāna since all Nāgas (serpents) are present here. O tiger among the twice-borns, you will come to my presence.

After saying this the Lord vanished there itself. Maṅki gave up his body and went to the world of Śiva.

Thus, O goddess, the excellent origin of Maṅkīśa has been narrated. If it is listened to by persons of perfect faith it dispels all sins.

## Chapter 204 - Greatness of Sarasvatī-Saṅgama

## \|\| 1.204.1-4 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*bhagavandevadeveśa saṃsārārṇavatāraka \|*  
*sarasvatyāśca māhātmyaṃ vistarātkathayasva me \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yātrāgatānāṃ deveśi puruṣāṇāṃ jitātmanām \|*  
*mukhadvāre tu kiṃ puṇyaṃ snānadāne ca śaṃkara \|\| 2 \|\|*

*avagāhanena cānyatra phalaṃ kiṃsvitprajāyate \|*  
*śrāddhasya kiṃ vidhānaṃ tu ke maṃtrāstatra ke dvijāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kiṃ grāhyaṃ kiñca bhoktavyaṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ śrāddhakarmaṇi \|*  
*kāni dānāni deyāni nṛbhiryātrā phalepsubhiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

The Devī said:

1-4. O Lord of the Chiefs of Devas, O redeemer of people from the ocean of worldly existence, do tell me in detail the greatness of Sarasvatī. O Lord Śaṅkara, O Lord of Devas, what is the merit gained by the pilgrims, the persons of controlled selves, through holy baths and gifts at her month?

Does one get the merit, if one plunges into her elsewhere? What is the procedure in the case of Śrāddha? What are the Mantras and who are the Brāhmaṇas? What should be accepted and what should be eaten by the Brāhmaṇas at the rites of Śrāddha? What gifts should be made by the men who wish to get the benefit of the pilgrimage.

## \|\| 1.204.5 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devipravakṣyāmi dānaśrāddhavidhikramam \|*  
*sarasvatyāśca māhātmyaṃ kīrtyamānaṃ nibodha me \|\| 5 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

5\. Listen, O goddess. I shall explain the procedure in the case of Dāna and Śrāddha. Know from me the greatness of Sarasvatī as it is being glorified by me.

## \|\| 1.204.6 \|\|

*puṇyaṃ sārasvataṃ toyaṃ yatra tatrāvagāhyate \|*  
*sāgareṇa tu saṃmiśraṃ devānāmapi durlabham \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The waters of Sarasvatī are sacred and meritorious wherever one takes the holy plunge, but that at conjunction with the ocean, is rare even unto Devas.

## \|\| 1.204.7 \|\|

*sarasvatī sarvanadīṣu puṇyā sarasvatī lokasukhāvagāhā \|*  
*sarasvatīṃ prāpya na duḥkhitā narāḥ sadā na śocaṃti paratra ceha vā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Sarasvatī is the most meritorious of all rivers. Sarasvatī gives happiness unto all who take plunge therein. Men cease to be miserable after reaching Sarasvatī. They never bewail here or hereafter.

## \|\| 1.204.8 \|\|

*puṇyaṃ sārasvataṃ tīrthaṃ puṇyakṛllabhate naraḥ \|*  
*durlabhaṃ triṣu lokeṣu vaiśākhyā somaparvaṇi \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Only a meritorious man gets the meritorious waters of Sarasvatī. It is rare in the three worlds on the Vaiśakhī day and in the Parva day coinciding with Monday.

## \|\| 1.204.9 \|\|

*amā somena saṃyuktā yadi tatraiva labhyate \|*  
*tatra kiṃ kriyate devi parvakoṭiśatairapi \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. If the New Moon coinciding with a Monday is obtained there, O goddess, what can one do with hundreds and crores of Parvas.

## \|\| 1.204.10 \|\|

*cāndrāyaṇāni kṛcchrāṇi mahāsāṃ tapanāni ca \|*  
*prāyaścittāni dīyante yatra nāsti sarasvatī \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The expiations like Cāndrāyaṇa, Kṛcchra, and Mahāsāntapana are prescribed where there is no Sarasvatī.

## \|\| 1.204.11-13 \|\|

*yāvadasthi śarīrasya tiṣṭhetsārasvate jale \|*  
*tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi viṣṇuloke vase nnaraḥ \|*  
*jātyandhaiste samā jñeyā mṛtaiḥ paṃgubhireva ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

*samarthā ye na paśyanti prabhāsasthāṃ sarasvatīm \|*  
*te deśāstāni tīrthāni āśramāste ca parvatāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*yeṣāṃ sarasvatī devī madhye yāti saridvarā \|*  
*trailokyapāvanīṃ puṇyāṃ saṃśritā ye sarasvatīm \|*  
*saṃsārakardamāmodamājighranti na te punaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. A man shall reside in Viṣṇuloka as many thousand years as the bones of the body lie in the waters of Sarasvatī.

If despite being hale and hearty people do not see Sarasvatī present in Prabhāsa, they should be known as on a par with congenitally blind, dead and lame.

Those are the real Deśas (countries), Tīrthas, Āśramas and Parvatas (Mountains), if the divine excellent river flows through them.

Those who resort to the sacred, meritorious Sarasvatī that sanctifies all the three worlds, will never smell the nasty odour of the slough of worldly existence.

## \|\| 1.204.14 \|\|

*śabdavidyeva vistīrṇā mataiva jagataḥ priyā \|*  
*satāṃ matiriva svacchā ramaṇīyā sarasvatī \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The charming Sarasvatī is as extensive as the science of Words (i.e. Grammar), as favourite unto the whole world as one’s mother and as clear and pure as the intellect of the good.

## \|\| 1.204.15 \|\|

*trailokyaśobhitāṃ devīṃ divya toyāṃ sunirmalām \|*  
*sa nīco yaḥ pumānetāṃ na vandeta sarasvatīm \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. That man is utterly base and mean who does not pay respects to Sarasvatī, the divine river that renders all the three worlds splendid and that has divine and clear waters.

## \|\| 1.204.16 \|\|

*svarganiśreṇisaṃbhūtā prabhāse tu sarasvatī \|*  
*nāpuṇyavadbhiḥ saṃprāptuṃ puṃbhiḥ śakyā mahānadī \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The great river Sarasvatī in Prabhāsa has become a staircase unto heaven. It cannot be attained by non-meritorious men.

## \|\| 1.204.17 \|\|

*candrabhāgā ca gaṃgā ca tathā yatra sarasvatī \|*  
*devāste na manuṣyāste tisro nadyaḥ pibanti ye \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Candrabhāgā (modern Chinab), Gaṅgā and Sarasvatī are the holiest of rivers. They are not ordinary men who drink the waters of these three rivers. They are veritable Devas.

## \|\| 1.204.18 \|\|

*satyameva mayā devi jāhnavī śirasā dhṛtā \|*  
*yāḥ kāścitsarito loke tāsāṃ puṇyā sarasvatī \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. It is but true, O goddess, that Jāhnavī was held by me on the head but Sarasvatī is the most meritorious of all the rivers in the world.

## \|\| 1.204.19 \|\|

*darśanena sarasvatyā rājasūyo na rājate \|*  
*gaṃḍūṣaścāśvamedhādvai sarva kratuvaraṃ payaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Rājasūya sacrifice pales into insignificance against the vision of Sarasvatī. A mouthful of her waters is the most excellent of all Kratus (holy sacrifices).

## \|\| 1.204.20-21 \|\|

*bhasmāsthicarmatoyāni nakhakeśādikāni ca \|*  
*vātairapi dhutānyeva tathā sārasvate jale \|\| 20 \|\|*

*vahanti yeṣāṃ kālena te na kāla vaśā narāḥ \|*  
*devi kiṃ bahunoktena varṇitena punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*sarasvatyāḥ paraṃ tīrthaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. ‘īṭ the ashes, bones, skins, nails, hairs etc. of a man are carried off by the wind, which float in the waters of Sarasvatī in due course, that person is not under the control of Kāla (God of death).

O goddess, why should I say much? Why should I describe repeatedly? There never was a Tīrtha greater than Sarasvatī nor will there ever be.

## \|\| 1.204.22 \|\|

*tatraiva durlabhaṃ snānaṃ yatra sāgarasaṃgamaḥ \|*  
*tatra snānena dānena koṭiyajñaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. In that spot where the ocean joins her holy bath is very rare. By taking the holy bath there and offering gifts there one gets the benefit of a crore of Yajñas.

## \|\| 1.204.23 \|\|

*yatra sārasvataṃ toyaṃ sāgarormisamākulam \|*  
*tatra snāsyaṃti ye martyā bhāgyavanto yugeyuge \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Men who have their holy bath in the waters of Sarasvatī mingled and agitated by the billows of the ocean, are the most fortunate men in every Yuga.

## \|\| 1.204.24 \|\|

*te dhanyāste namaskāryāsteṣāṃ sphītataraṃ yaśaḥ \|*  
*yeṣāṃ kalevaraṃ nṝṇāṃ siktaṃ sārasvatairjalaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Those men whose bodies are sprinkled with the waters of Sarasvatī are blessed ones. They deserve to be bowed to. Their fame is wide.

## Chapter 205 - Brāhmaṇas Unfit for Śrāddha

## \|\| 1.205.1-3 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*bhagandevadeveśa saṃsārārṇavatāraka \|*  
*brūhi śrāddhavidhiṃ puṇyaṃ vistarājjagatāṃpate \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kasminvāsarabhāge tu śrāddhakṛcchrāddhamācaret \|*  
*asminsarasvatī tīrthe prabhāsakṣetra uttame \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kasmiṃstīrthe kṛtaṃ śrāddhaṃ bahupuṇyaphalaṃ bhavet \|*  
*etatsarvaṃ mahādeva yathāvadvaktumarhasi \|\| 3 \|\|*

The Devī said:

1-3. O holy Lord, O Lord of the Chiefs of Devas, O redeamer from the ocean of worldly existence, O Lord of the worlds, do tell me the highly meritorious procedure of Śrāddha in detail.

At which part of the day should a performer of Śrāddha perform the rite in this Sarasvatī Tīrtha in the excellent Prabhāsa Kṣetra?

At which Tīrtha should a Śrāddha be performed so that it may yield abundant merit? O Mahādeva, it behoves you to expound all this truthfully.

## \|\| 1.205.4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*prātaḥkāle muhūtāṃstrīnsaṃgavastāvadeva tu \|*  
*madhyāhnastrimuhūrtaḥ syādaparāhṇastataḥ param \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

4\. Three Muhūrtas in the morning constitute Prātaḥkāla, the second unit of three Muhūrtas constitutes Saṅgava. The unit of next three Muhūrtas constitutes Madhyāhna (midday). Then (next) three Muhūrtas constitute Aparāhna.

## \|\| 1.205.5 \|\|

*sāyāhnastrimuhūrtaḥ syācchrāddhaṃ tatra na kārayet \|*  
*rākṣasīnāma sā velā garhitā sarvakarmasu \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The last three Muhūrtas of a day constitute Sāyāhna. Śrāddha should not be performed at this time. This period is called Rākṣasī Velā. It is despised in the case of all holy rites.

## \|\| 1.205.6 \|\|

*ahno muhūrtā vikhyātā daśapaṃca ca sarvadā \|*  
*tatrāṣṭamo muhūrto yaḥ sa kālaḥ kutapaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*
