7\. He who, on the Ekādaśī (eleventh lunar) day observes complete fast and visits that God, sees (attains) after death the eternal, limitless region of Hari.

## \|\| 1.337.8 \|\|

*tena pītāni vastrāṇi deyāni dvijapuṃgave \|*  
*snānaṃ śrāddhaṃ ca kartavyaṃ samyagyātrāphalepsubhiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. By persons desirous of the complete benefit of the performance of Yātrā (pilgrimage), yellow garments should be given to an excellent Brāhmaṇa. Proper ablutions and Śrāddha should also be performed.

## \|\| 1.337.9 \|\|

*iti te kathitaṃ mahāprabhāvaṃ harisaṃketaniketanodbhavam \|*  
*śṛṇute vā prayatastu yaḥ sudhīḥ paṭhate vā labhate sa sadgatim \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thus is related to you the great efficacy of the house named after Hari. An intelligent person who assiduously listens to or reads it, attains the greatest goal.

## Chapter 338 - Greatness of Jāleśvara (Jāla-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.338.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi devikātaṭasaṃsthitam \|*  
*jāleśvareti vikhyātaṃ surāsuranamaskṛtam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. O great goddess, thereafter one should go to (the shrine) known as Jāleśvara situated on the bank of Devikā. It (Jāleśvara) is bowed to by Suras and Asuras.

## \|\| 1.338.2-3 \|\|

*manvantare cākṣuṣe ca samprāpte dvāpare yuge \|*  
*nāmnā jāleśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ devikātaṭasaṃsthitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*pūjyate nāgakanyābhirna tatpaśyaṃti mānavāḥ \|*  
*mahā tejomaṇimayaṃ caṃdrabiṃbasamaprabham \|*  
*smaraṇāttasya devasya brahmahatyā praṇaśyati \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. In Cākṣuṣa Manvantara, when there was the advent of Dvāpara Yuga, the Liṅga called Jāleśvara, situated on the banks of Devikā (river), was worshipped by Nāga girls. Human beings could not see it.

It comprised precious stones of very great refulgence. It has brilliance like the disc of the Moon. By its very remembrance, the (sin of) Brāhmaṇa-killing perishes.

## \|\| 1.338.4 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ jāleśvaraṃ nāma kasminkāle babhūva tat \|\| 4 \|\|*

Devī said:

4\. Why is it (the Liṅga) named Jāleśvara? In what period did it come into existence?

## \|\| 1.338.5 \|\|

*sādhubhiḥ saha saṃvāsātke guṇāḥ parikīrttitāḥ \|*  
*ke lokāḥ kāni puṇyāni tatsarvaṃ śaṃsa me prabho \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. What good qualities resulting from association with the good and saintly are glorified? Which regions and what merits are gained? O Lord, tell me everything.

## \|\| 1.338.6 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*atraivodāharaṃtīmamitihāsaṃ purātanam \|*  
*nābhāgasya ca saṃvādamāpastaṃbataponidheḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

6\. In this context, they relate this ancient episode: a dialogue between (king) Nābhāga and (sage) Āpastaṃba, the treasure of penance.

## \|\| 1.338.7 \|\|

*maharṣirātmavānpūrvamāpastaṃbo dvijāgraṇīḥ \|*  
*upāvasansadā rambho babhūva bhagavāṃstadā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Formerly there lived the great sage Āpastaṃba of self-dependent will power, the leader of the twice-born ones (Brāhmaṇas). The holy Lord was engaged in good deeds.

## \|\| 1.338.8 \|\|

*nityaṃ krodhaṃ ca lobhaṃ ca mohaṃ drohaṃ visṛjya saḥ \|*  
*devikāsarito madhye viveśa salilāśaye \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He always eschewed anger, avarice, delusion and hostility. He entered the waters of the river Devikā.

## \|\| 1.338.9 \|\|

*kṣetre prābhāsike ramye samyagjñātvā śivapriye \|*  
*tatrāsya vasataḥ kālaḥ samatīto mahāṃstadā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O beloved of Śiva, knowing that the holy place Prabhāsa was pleasant, he lived there for a big period of time.

## \|\| 1.338.10 \|\|

*pareṇa dhyānayogena sthāṇubhūtasya tiṣṭhataḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kadācidāgatya taṃ deśaṃ matsyajīvinaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. While he stayed therein in a pillar-like stable posture practising the supreme Yoga of meditation, one day fishermen came to that place.

## \|\| 1.338.11 \|\|

*prasārya sumahajjālaṃ sarve cākarṣayanbalāt \|*  
*atha taṃ ca mahāmatsyaṃ niṣādā baladarpitāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Spreading out their extremely wide net, the Niṣādas (fishermen), proud of their strength, powerfully dragged out that great fish (the sage).

## \|\| 1.338.12 \|\|

*tasmāduttārayāmāsuḥ salilādbrahmanaṃdanam \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā tapasā dīptaṃ kaivarttā bhayavihvalāḥ \|*  
*śirobhiḥ praṇipatyoccairidaṃ vacanamabruvan \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Out of the water, they pulled the son of Brahmā. Seeing him blazing with penance, the fishermen were overwhelmed with fear. Bowing down their heads in obeisance, they spoke these words loudly:

## \|\| 1.338.13 \|\|

*niṣādā ūcuḥ \|*  
*ajñānātkṛtapāpānāmasmākaṃ kṣantumarhasi \|*  
*kiṃ vā kāryaṃ priyaṃ te'dya tadājñāpaya suvrata \|\| 13 \|\|*

Niṣādas said:

13\. It behoves you to forgive us who have committed a sin unknowingly, O sage of good vows. Order us what pleasant task should be done for you.

## \|\| 1.338.14 \|\|

*sa munistanmahaddṛṣṭvā matsyānāṃ kadanaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*kṛpayā parayāviṣṭo dāśānprovāca duḥkhitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The sage saw the great slaughter of fishes. Deeply grieved and overcome with great pity, he spoke to the fishermen:

## \|\| 1.338.15 \|\|

*kena me syādupāyo hi sarve svārthe bata sthitāḥ \|*  
*jñānināmapi yaccetaḥ kevalātmahite ratam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. “What remedy can I have? Alas! All are deeply engaged in their self-interest. Even the mind of those knowers is busy only in the interest of the self.

## \|\| 1.338.16 \|\|

*jñāninopi yadā svārthamāśritya dhyānamāsthitāḥ \|*  
*duḥkhārttānīha sattvāni kva yāsyaṃti sukhaṃ tataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. When persons endowed with (spiritual) knowledge are engaged in meditation depending on (i.e. for the sake of) their own objectives, where can grief-stricken miserable beings go for happiness?

## \|\| 1.338.17-19 \|\|

*yo'bhivāṃchati bhoktuṃ vai duḥkhānyekāṃtato janaḥ \|*  
*pāpātpāpataraṃ taṃ hi pravadaṃti mumukṣavaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ko nu me syādupāyo hi yenāhaṃ duḥkhitātmavān \|*  
*aṃtaḥ praviṣṭaḥ sattvānāṃ bhaveyaṃ sarvaduḥkhabhuk \|\| 18 \|\|*

*yanmamāsti śubhaṃ kicittadenānupagacchatu \|*  
*yatkṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ taiśca tadaśeṣamupetu mām \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. Persons desirous of liberation praise a person who desires to experience griefs and miseries only—one worse than the previous one. Persons desirous of Mokṣa say: ‘What means can I have, whereby I, entering into all beings, can get an experience of miseries of all and become one possessing a miserable self? Whatever is auspicious merit of mine should go to them. Whatever evil deeds be perpetrated by them may entirely come to me.’

## \|\| 1.338.20 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvāṃdhānkṛpaṇānvyaṃgānanāthānrogiṇastathā \|*  
*dayā na jāyate yasya sa rakṣa iti me matiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. It is my opinion that he is a demon in whom mercy does not arise on seeing the blind, the miserable, the disabled, the helpless and the diseased.

## \|\| 1.338.21 \|\|

*prāṇasaṃśayamāpannānprāṇino bhayavihvalān \|*  
*yo na rakṣati śaktopi sa tatpāpaṃ samaśnute \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Though capable of doing so, if one does not save beings in the danger of death and the beings overwhelmed with fear, he eats the fruit of (suffers the consequences of) sin.

## \|\| 1.338.22 \|\|

*āhurjanānāmārttānāṃ sukhaṃ yadupajāyate \|*  
*tasya svargo'pavargo vā kalāṃ nārhati ṣoḍaśīm \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. They say that (the happiness in) heaven and liberation (from Saṃsāra) does not deserve to be even one-sixteenth fraction of the happiness that comes to distressed persons (when relieved).

## \|\| 1.338.23 \|\|

*tasmānnaitānahaṃ dīnāṃstyaktvā mīnānsuduḥkhitān \|*  
*padamātraṃ tu yāsyāmi kiṃ punastridaśālayam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. I shall not go a single step abandoning these poor, extremely distressed fishes. What to say of going to the region of Devas!”

## \|\| 1.338.24 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*niśamyaitadṛṣervākyaṃ dāśāste jātasaṃbhramāḥ \|*  
*yathāvṛttaṃ tu tatsarvaṃ nābhāgāya nyavedayan \|\| 24 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

24\. On hearing the statement of that sage, those fishermen got confused. They reported to King Nābhāga everything as it took place.

## \|\| 1.338.25 \|\|

*nābhāgo'pi tataḥ śrutvā taṃ draṣṭuṃ brahmanandanam \|*  
*tvaritaḥ prayayau tatra sāmātyaḥ sapurohitaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On hearing it, even Nābhāga accompanied by his ministers and family priest quickly hastened to see the son of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.338.26 \|\|

*sa samyakpūjayitvā taṃ devakalpamuniṃ nṛpaḥ \|*  
*provāca bhagavanbrūhi kiṃ karomi tavājñayā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. After worshipping properly the Deva-like sage, the king requested, “O Lord, tell me what should be done at your bidding?”

## \|\| 1.338.27 \|\|

*āpastaṃba uvāca \|*  
*śrameṇa mahatāviṣṭāḥ kaivarttā duḥkhajīvinaḥ \|*  
*mama mūlyaṃ prayaccheti yadyogyaṃ manyase nṛpa \|\| 27 \|\|*

Āpastaṃba said:

27\. These fishermen lead a miserable life and are greatly overwhelmed with fatigue. Pay them whatever you think proper as the price of mine.

## \|\| 1.338.28 \|\|

*nābhāga uvāca \|*  
*sahasrāṇāṃ śataṃ mūlyaṃ niṣādebhyo dadāmyaham \|*  
*nigrahākhyasya bhagavanyathāha brahmanaṃdanaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

Nābhāga said:

28\. As you, the son of god Brahmā say, I shall pay one hundred thousand (coins) as the remuneration for drawing you out.

## \|\| 1.338.29 \|\|

*āpastaṃba uvāca \|*  
*nāhaṃ śatasahasraiśca niyamyaḥ pārthiva tvayā \|*  
*sadṛśaṃ dīyatāṃ mūlyamamātyaiḥ saha ciṃtaya \|\| 29 \|\|*

Āpastaṃba said:

29\. O king, I should not be fixed with a hundred thousand as my worth. Adequate price should be given. Consult your ministers.

## \|\| 1.338.30 \|\|

*nābhāga uvāca \|*  
*koṭiḥ pradīyatāṃ mūlyaṃ niṣādebhyo dvijottama \|*  
*yadyetadapi te mūlyaṃ tato bhūyaḥ pradīyate \|\| 30 \|\|*

Nābhāga said:

30\. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, ten million (coins) be given to the fishermen if this be your price. If it be more, it will be given.

## \|\| 1.338.31 \|\|

*āpastaṃba uvāca \|*  
*nārhaṃ mūlyaṃ ca me koṭiradhikaṃ vāpi pārthiva \|*  
*sadṛśaṃ dīyatāṃ mūlyaṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ saha ciṃtaya \|\| 31 \|\|*

Āpastarhba said:

31\. O king, my price is not merely hundred thousand or more. Deserving price be paid after consulting Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.338.32 \|\|

*nābhāga uvāca \|*  
*arddharājyaṃ samastaṃ vā niṣādebhyaḥ pradīyatām \|*  
*etanmūlyamahaṃ manye kiṃ vā'nyanmanyase dvija \|\| 32 \|\|*

Nābhāga said:

32\. Half of the kingdom or the whole of the kingdom be given to the Fishermen. I regard this as the (proper) price. What else do you think, O Brāhmaṇa?

## \|\| 1.338.33 \|\|

*āpastaṃba uvāca \|*  
*ardharājyasamastaṃ vā nāhamarhāmi pārthiva \|*  
*sadṛśaṃ dīyatāṃ mūlyamṛṣibhiḥ saha ciṃtaya \|\| 33 \|\|*

Āpastaṃba said:

33\. O king, I am not to be valued by half of the kingdom or the entire kingdom. Consult with some sages and a suitable value should be given.

## \|\| 1.338.34 \|\|

*maharṣestadvacaḥ śrutvā nābhāgaḥ sa viṣādavān \|*  
*cintayāmāsa duḥkhārtaḥ sāmātyaḥ sapurohitaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. On hearing the words of the great sage, Nābhāga, along with his ministers and family, felt dejected.

## \|\| 1.338.35 \|\|

*tataḥ kaścidṛṣistatra lomaśastu mahātapāḥ \|*  
*nābhāgamabravīnmā bhaistoṣayiṣyāmi taṃ munim \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then a certain sage Lomaśa of great penance assured Nābhāga: “Do not be afraid, I shall satisfy the sage.”

## \|\| 1.338.36 \|\|

*nābhāga uvāca \|*  
*brūhi mūlyaṃ mahābhāga munerasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*paritrāyasva māmasmātsajñātikulabāṃdhavam \|\| 36 \|\|*

Nābhāga said:

36\. Tell me the value of the great sage, O highly fortunate one. Protect me along with my clan, and family relatives from this (sage).

## \|\| 1.338.37 \|\|

*nirdahedbhagavānrudrastrailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*kiṃ punarmānuṣaṃ hīnamatyaṃtavi ṣayātmakam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Lord Rudra will burn down the three worlds along with the mobiles and immobiles. What then of the weakling of a man extremely indulging in sensual pleasures?

## \|\| 1.338.38 \|\|

*lomaśa uvāca \|*  
*tvamīḍyo hi mahārāja jagatpūjyo dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*gāvaśca divyāstasmādgaurmūlyamamyai pradīyatām \|\| 38 \|\|*

Lomaśa said:

38\. O great king, the excellent Brāhmaṇa worthy of being worshipped by the world, should be eulogized by you. Cows are divine. Hence, cows being his proper price, should be given to him.

## \|\| 1.338.39 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ rājā sāmātyaḥ sapurohitaḥ \|*  
*harṣeṇa mahatāviṣṭaḥ provācedaṃ vacomunim \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. On hearing that statement the king along with his ministers and family priest was overwhelmed with excessive joy. He spoke to the sage:

## \|\| 1.338.40 \|\|

*uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhagavankrīta eva na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*etadyogyatamaṃ mūlyaṃ bhavato munisattama \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. “Get up, get up, O holy Sir, (you are) purchased undoubtedly. This is the most deserving price for your honourable self, O excellent sage.”

## \|\| 1.338.41 \|\|

*āpastaṃba uvāca \|*  
*uttiṣṭhāmyeṣa suprītaḥ samyakkrīto'smi pārthiva \|*  
*gobhyo mūlyaṃ na paśyāmi pavitraṃ paramaṃ bhuvi \|\| 41 \|\|*

Āpastaṃba said:

41\. Being highly pleased I stand here as I am bought at the proper price, O king. I do not see any excellent, pure value higher than cows in this world, O king.

## \|\| 1.338.42 \|\|

*gāvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkāryāḥ pūjanīyāśca nityaśaḥ \|*  
*maṃgalāyatanaṃ devyaḥ sṛṣṭā hyetāḥ svayaṃbhuvā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Cows are always to be worshipped and circumambulated. These goddesses (cows) are the receptacle of auspiciousness. These have been created by the self-born god (Brahmā).

## \|\| 1.338.43 \|\|

*agnyagārāṇi viprāṇāṃ devatāyatanāni ca \|*  
*yadgomayena śuddhyaṃti kiṃbhūtamadhikaṃ tataḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The hall of fire-worship and the temples of gods become purified with cow-dung. What purer thing could have been created?

## \|\| 1.338.44 \|\|

*gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpistathaiva ca \|*  
*gavāṃ paṃca pavitrāṇi punaṃti sakalaṃ jagat \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Urine of a cow, cowḍung, (cow’s) milk, curds and ghee (prepared from cow’s milk)—all these five (pure) products from cow purify the whole world.

## \|\| 1.338.45 \|\|

*gāvo mamāgrato nityaṃ gāvaḥ pṛṣṭhata eva ca \|*  
*gāvo me hradaye caiva gavāṃ madhye vasāmyahama \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. “Cows be always in front of me and cows be at my rear. Cows are in my heart. I always stay among cows.”

## \|\| 1.338.46 \|\|

*evaṃ japannaro maṃtraṃ trisaṃdhyaṃ niyataḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*mucyate sarvapāpebhyaḥ svargalokaṃ ca gacchati \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. If a self-controlled pure person mutters this Mantra three times (morning, noon and evening) a day, he is absolved of all sins and goes to heaven.

## \|\| 1.338.47 \|\|

*tṛṇāhāraparā gāvaḥ karttavyā bhaktito'nvaham \|*  
*akṛtvā svayamāhāraṃ kurvanprāpnoti durgatim \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Everyday with devotion cows must mainly be fed on grass. A person taking his meal without feeding cows, incurs misfortune.

## \|\| 1.338.48 \|\|

*tenāgnayo hutāḥ samyakpitaraścāpi tarpitāḥ \|*  
*devāśca pūjitāstena yo dadāti gavāhnikam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. He who gives daily fodder (and other services) to cows, has offered oblations into fire, has properly satisfied the Pitṛs and performed worship of Devas.

## \|\| 1.338.49 \|\|

*mantraḥ \|*  
*saurabheyī jagatpūjyā devī viṣṇupade sthitā \|*  
*sarvameva mayā dattaṃ pratīcchatu sutoṣitā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Mantra: “The daughter of (the divine cow) Surabhī (i.e. a cow) deserves to be worshipped by the world. The goddess dwells in Viṣṇu’s region. May she accept all that has been given by me and be fully satisfied.”

## \|\| 1.338.50 \|\|

*rakṣaṇādbālaputrāṇāṃ gavāṃ kaṇḍūyanāttathā \|*  
*kṣīṇārtarakṣaṇāccaiva naraḥ svarge mahīyate \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. By protecting the male calves of cows and by easing the itching of cows and by protecting the weak and suffering cows, a man is praised in heaven.

## \|\| 1.338.51 \|\|

*ādirgāvo hi martyasya madhye cāṃte prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*rakṣaṃti tāstu devānāṃ kṣīrājyamamṛtaṃ sadā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Cows are proclaimed to be the beginning, middle and end of mortal beings. They protect (sustain) milk, ghee and nectar of all Devas.

## \|\| 1.338.52 \|\|

*tasmādgāvaḥ pradātavyāḥ pūjanīyāśca nityaśaḥ \|*  
*svargasya saṃgamā hyetāḥ sopānamiva nirmitāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Hence, cows always deserve to be worshipped and gifted. They are created like a staircase for easy passage to heaven.

## \|\| 1.338.53 \|\|

*etacchrutvā niṣādāste gavāṃ māhātmyamutta mam \|*  
*praṇipatya mahātmānamāpastaṃbamathābruvan \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Hearing the excellent greatness of cows, the Niṣādas (fishermen) prostrated themselves before the noble-souled Āpastaṃba and spoke:

## \|\| 1.338.54 \|\|

*niṣādā ūcuḥ \|*  
*saṃbhāṣo darśanaṃ sparśaḥ kīrtanaṃ smaraṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*pāvanāni kilaitāni sādhūnāmiti ca śrutam \|\| 54 \|\|*

Niṣādas said:

54\. It is heard (by us) that conversation, viewing, touch, glorification, remembrance of saintly persons are sanctifying.

## \|\| 1.338.55 \|\|

*saṃbhāṣo darśanaṃ caiva sahāsmābhiḥ kṛtaṃ tvayā \|*  
*kuruṣvānugrahaṃ tasmādgaureṣā pratigṛhyatām \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Viewing us and conversation with us has been done by you. Render a favour unto us and accept this cow.

## \|\| 1.338.56 \|\|

*āpastaṃba uvāca \|*  
*etā vaḥ pratigṛhṇāmi gāṃ yūyaṃ muktakilviṣāḥ \|*  
*niṣādā gacchata svargaṃ saha matsyairjaloddhṛtaiḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

Āpastaṃba said:

56\. I accept this cow. You are now absolved of your sins. O fishermen, go to heaven along with the fish taken out of water by you.

## \|\| 1.338.57 \|\|

*prāṇināṃ prītimutpādya nindite nāpi karmaṇā \|*  
*narakaṃ yadi paśyāmi vatsyāmi svarga eva tat \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. If I see hell by creating affinity with living beings even by censurable means, I shall stay therein as if it is veritable heaven.

## \|\| 1.338.58 \|\|

*yanmayā sukṛtaṃ kiñcinmanovākkāyakarmabhiḥ \|*  
*kṛtaṃ syāttena duḥkhārtāḥ sarve yāṃtu śubhāṃ gatim \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. If I have done some slight merit by my mind, speech and actions, may all miserable beings go to auspicious goal (heaven).

## \|\| 1.338.59 \|\|

*tatastasya prasādena maharṣerbhāvitātmanaḥ \|*  
*niṣādāstena vākyena saha matsyairdivaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Then by the grace of the great sage of sanctified soul, the fishermen along with the fish went to heaven at his words.

## \|\| 1.338.60 \|\|

*tāndṛṣṭvā vrajataḥ svargaṃ samatsyānmatsyajīvinaḥ \|*  
*sāmātyabhṛtyo nṛpatirvismayādidamabravīt \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Looking at the fishermen going to heaven along with the fish, the king along with the ministers and servants was struck with wonder and he spoke:

## \|\| 1.338.61 \|\|

*sevyāḥ śreyo'rthibhiḥ santaḥ puṇyatīrthe jalopamāḥ \|*  
*kṣaṇo pāsanamapyatra na yeṣāṃ niṣphalaṃ bhavet \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. “Saintly persons are like water in (a sacred) Tīrtha. They should be served by persons intent on securing welfare. Rendering services to them even for a moment does not become fruitless.

## \|\| 1.338.62 \|\|

*sadbhiḥ saha sadāsīta sadbhiḥ kurvīta satkathām \|*  
*satāṃ vratena varteta nāsadbhiḥ kiñcidācaret \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. One should always sit with good people. Pious stories or conversation should be carried on with good people. One should behave as per vows of the good. One should not do anything with evil persons.

## \|\| 1.338.63 \|\|

*satāṃ samāgamādete samatsyā matsyajīvinaḥ \|*  
*triviṣṭapamanuprāptā narāḥ puṇyakṛto yathā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. These fishermen along with the fish went to heaven due to their association with the good. I like persons who practice virtuous deeds.”

## \|\| 1.338.64 \|\|

*āpastaṃbo munistatra lomaśaśca mahāmanāḥ \|*  
*varaistaṃ vividhairiṣṭaiśchaṃdayāmāsaturnṛpam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Then sage Āpastaṃba and the noble-hearted Lomaśa blessed the king with various desired boons.

## \|\| 1.338.65 \|\|

*tataḥ sa varayāmāsa dharmabuddhiṃ sudurlabhām \|*  
*tatheti coktvā tau prītyā taṃ nṛpaṃ vai śaśaṃsatuḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Then he (the king) selected the boon of having a virtuous mind which is so very difficult to get. Saying "So be it” with great affection, both of them praised the king.

## \|\| 1.338.66 \|\|

*aho dhanyo'si rājendra yatte dharmaparā matiḥ \|*  
*dharmaḥ sudurlabhaḥ puṃsāṃ viśeṣeṇa mahīkṣitām \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. “O chief of kings, how blessed you are that your mind is attached to virtue! Dharma (Piety) is very difficult to obtain, especially so in the case of kings.”

## \|\| 1.338.67 \|\|

*yadi rājā madāviṣṭaḥ svadharmaṃ na pari tyajet \|*  
*tato jagati kastasmātpumānabhyadhiko bhavet \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. What man in the world can be more powerful than a king who puffed up with pride, does not abandon his own duties!

## \|\| 1.338.68 \|\|

*dhruvaṃ janma sadā rājñāṃ mohaścāpi sadā dhruvaḥ \|*  
*mohāddhruvaśca narako rājyaṃ nindantyato budhāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Always the birth (life) of a king is certainly prone to delusion. From delusion hell is a certainty. Hence wise men censure kingship.

## \|\| 1.338.69 \|\|

*rājyaṃ hi bahu manyaṃte narā viṣayalolupāḥ \|*  
*manīṣiṇastu paśyanti tadeva narakopamam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Persons addicted to sensual pleasure think highly of a kingdom. Wise men, however, look upon it as comparable to hell.

## \|\| 1.338.70 \|\|

*tasmāllokadvayadhvaṃsī na karttavyo madastvayā \|*  
*yadīcchasi mahārāja śāśvatīṃ gatimātmanaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Hence, O great king, do you desire to secure eternal position (Mokṣa) to yourself? Pride, the destroyer of both the worlds should not be entertained by you.”

## \|\| 1.338.71 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā tau mahātmānau jagmatuḥ svaṃ svamāśramam \|*  
*nābhāgo'pi varaṃ labdhvā prahṛṣṭaḥ prāviśatpuram \|\| 71 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

71\. After speaking thus, those two noble-souled ones went to their respective hermitages. Having got the boon, Nābhāga who was highly delighted, entered his capital.

## \|\| 1.338.72 \|\|

*etatte kathitaṃ devi prabhāvaṃ devikodbhavam \|*  
*ṛṣiṇā sthāpitaścāpi bhavo jāle śvarastadā \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. As the most excellent sage was caught in the net of fishermen, it became well-known in the world as Jāleśvara.

## \|\| 1.338.73-76 \|\|

*jāle nipatito yasmāddāśānāmṛṣisattamaḥ \|*  
*jāleśvareti nāmāsau vikhyātaḥ pṛthivītale \|\| 73 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā mahādevi jāleśvarasamarcanāt \|*  
*āpastaṃbaśca nābhāgo niṣādā matsyajīvinaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*matsyaiḥ saha gatāḥ svargaṃ devikāyāḥ prabhāvataḥ \|*  
*caitrasyaiva tu māsasya śuklapakṣe trayodaśīm \|\| 75 \|\|*

*dadyātpiṇḍaṃ pitṛbhyo yastasyāṃto naiva vidyate \|*  
*godānaṃ tatra deyaṃ tu brāhmaṇe vedapārage \|*  
*śrotavyaṃ caiva māhātmyaṃ draṣṭavyo jālakeśvaraḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

73-76. O great goddess, after bathing there and worshipping Jāleśvara, Āpastaṃba, Nābhāga and the Niṣādas who live by fish (catching) went to heaven along with the fish due to the efficacy of Devikā. Piṇḍa should be offered to Pītṛs on the thirteenth day in the bright half of Caitra. There is no end to his merits.

Therein (in that Tīrtha) the religious gift of a cow to a Brāhmaṇa expert in the Vedas should be performed. The greatness (of Jāleśvara) should be heard and Jāleśvara should be visited.

## Chapter 339 - Greatness of Huṃkāra Kūpa

## \|\| 1.339.1-4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi kūpaṃ trailokyaviśrutam \|*  
*devikāyāstaṭe ramye huṃkāreṇaiva pūryate \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tato'dhastātpunaryāti salilaṃ tatra bhāmini \|*  
*taṇḍīnāma purā prokto devikātaṭamāsthitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tapastepe mahādevi śivabhaktiparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*tasyaivaṃ tapyamānasya tasmindeśe varānane \|\| 3 \|\|*

*ājagāma mṛgo vṛddhastaṃ deśamandha dṛkpriye \|*  
*sa papāta mahāgarte agādhe jalavarjite \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-2a. Thereafter, O great goddess, one should go to the well, renowned in all the three worlds, on the beautiful bank of Devikā. It is filled with the sound ‘Hum’. Then, O beautiful woman, the water again goes down there.

2b-4. O great goddess, it is reported that formerly there was (a sage) called Taṇḍi who resided on the bank of Devikā. He was a great devotee of Śiva, who performed penance.

O lady of excellent countenance, while he was thus performing penance in that part of country, there came an old deer blind in eyes. He fell in a fathomless deep ditch devoid of water.

## \|\| 1.339.5 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛpayāviṣṭaḥ sa munirmaunamāsthitaḥ \|*  
*huṃkāraṃ kurute tatra bhūyobhūyaśca bhāmini \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Seeing him the sage was moved with compassion. But having adopted (the vow of) silence, he repeatedly uttered the Huṃ sound, O beautiful lady.

## \|\| 1.339.6 \|\|

*atha huṃkāraśabdena tasya gartaḥ prapūritaḥ \|*  
*tato mṛgo viniṣkrāṃtaḥ kṛcchreṇa salilātpriye \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then by the sound ‘Hum’ of the sage, the ditch was overfilled (with water) and the deer came out with difficulty from the water.

## \|\| 1.339.7-10 \|\|

*mānuṣaṃ rūpamāśritya tamṛṣiṃ paryapṛcchata \|*  
*vismayaṃ paramaṃ gatvā kāmyadaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*mṛgatve patitaścātra naro bhūtvā vinirgataḥ \|*  
*so'bravīttasya māhātmyaṃ salilasya dvijottamaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*ato'haṃ naratāṃ prāpto nānyadastīha kāraṇam \|*  
*tatastatsalilaṃ bhūyaḥ praviṣṭaṃ dharaṇītale \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tato huṃkṛtavānbhūyaḥ sa ṛṣiḥ kautukānvitaḥ \|*  
*āpūritaḥ punaḥ kūpaḥ salilena purā yathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-9a. Assuming human form, he (the deer) who was extremely surprised, asked the sage about the attainment of the desired fruit from the act of falling (in the ditch) in the form of deer and emergence by becoming transformed into a man.

The excellent Brāhmaṇa told him that (it was) the efficacy of that water. “It is thereby that I attained the status of man. There is no other reason.”

9b-10. Then the water again entered underground. Urged by curiosity, the sage uttered the sound ‘Hum’. The well was filled again with water as before.

## \|\| 1.339.11 \|\|

*tataḥ sa kṛtavānsnānaṃ tathā ca pitṛtarpaṇam \|*  
*matvā tīrthavaraṃ tatra tataḥ prāptaḥ parāṃ gatim \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Considering it (the well) to be a prominent Tīrtha, he took his bath and gave oblations to satisfy Pitṛs. Thence he attained the highest goal.

## \|\| 1.339.12-14 \|\|

*adyāpi huṃkṛte tasminsalilaughaḥ pravartate \|*  
*tatra gatvā naro bhaktyā api pāparato'pi yaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*na mānuṣyaṃ punarjanma prāpnoti jagatītale \|*  
*tatra snātvā śucirbhūtvā yaḥ śrāddhaṃ kurute naraḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*mucyate sarvapāpebhyaḥ pitṛloke mahīyate \|*  
*kulāni tārayetsapta atītā'nāgatāni ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-13a. Even today, if the sound Huṃ is uttered it is flooded with water.

Even if a man be a confirmed sinner, if he goes there with devotion, he does not get the birth of a man on the surface of the earth.

13b-14. If a person sanctifies himself by taking a bath there and performs Śrāddha, he is absolved of all sins and is prai\[???\] \[praised?\] in the world of Pitṛs. He redeems seven generations preceding him and seven following him.

## Chapter 340 - Greatness of Caṇḍīśvara

## \|\| 1.340.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi tatra sthāne tu saṃsthitam \|*  
*caṇḍīśvaraṃ mahāliṃgaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Thereafter, O great goddess, one should go to the great Liṅga Caṇḍīśvara which destroys all sins. It is situated at that very place.

## \|\| 1.340.2 \|\|

*tatra śuklacaturddaśyāṃ kārtike māsi bhāmini \|*  
*upavāsaparo bhūtvā yaḥ karoti prajāgaram \|*  
*sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yatra devo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O beautiful lady, there, on the fourteenth day of the bright half of the month of Kārttika, if one observes fast and remains awake at night, he goes to the highest place where dwells god Maheśvara.

## Chapter 341 - Greatness of God Vighnarāja of Āśāpūra

## \|\| 1.341.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*āśāpūraṃ tato gacchedvighnarājamakalmaṣam \|*  
*śaśibhūṣaṇa vāyavye saṃsthitaṃ vighnanāśanam \|*  
*āśāṃ pūrayate yasmāttenāśāpūrakaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. One should then go to the blemishless (sacred) Āśāpūra (granter of desires) Gaṇeśa (Vighnarāja—the Lord, controller of obstacles), the Moon-crested Lord. He is situated on the north-west. He fulfills hopes and desires and hence is remembered as Āśāpūraka.

## \|\| 1.341.2 \|\|

*yatra rāmeṇa deveśi sītayā lakṣmaṇena ca \|*  
*samārādhya ca vighneśaṃ prāptaṃ kāmamabhīpsitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O goddess, cherished desires were obtained by Rāma, Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa after propitiating the controller of obstacles (Gaṇeśa) there.

## \|\| 1.341.3 \|\|

*yatra caṃdramasā devi samārādhya gaṇādhipam \|*  
*labdhaṃ tadvāṃchitaṃ pūrvaṃ sarvakuṣṭhavināśanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. There, by propitiating the Lord of Gaṇas, complete healing of leprosy as desired by him, formerly, was attained by the Moon-god.

## \|\| 1.341.4-6 \|\|

*caturthyāṃ śuklapakṣe ca māsi bhādrapade tathā \|*  
*tatra saṃpūjya deveśaṃ modakairbhojayeddvijān \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vāñchitāṃ labhate siddhiṃ vighnarājaprasādataḥ \|*  
*kṣetrasyāsya mahādevi rakṣārthaṃ tu mayā purā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tato niyukto deveśi yāyināṃ vighnanāśanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. On the fourth day in the bright half of the month of Bhādrapada, one should properly worship the Lord of Devas (Gaṇeśa) and feed Brāhmaṇas with Modakas (a special sweet dish). The person obtains his cherished accomplishment.

For the protection of this Kṣetra, O great goddess, the Destroyer of Obstacles was appointed by me, for the pilgrims.

## Chapter 342 - Greatness of Candreśvara-Kalā Kuṇḍa

## \|\| 1.342.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tasya dakṣiṇanairṛtye nātidūre vyavasthitam \|*  
*liṃgaṃ pāpaharaṃ devi svayaṃ somapratiṣṭhitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Not far from it, to the south-southeast direction, is situated a sin-destroying Liṅga installed by Soma himself.

## \|\| 1.342.2-4 \|\|

*tatraivāmṛtakuṇḍaṃ tu kalākuṇḍaṃ tu tatsmṛtam \|*  
*tatra snātvā tu caṃdreśaṃ yo naraḥ pūjayiṣyati \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sa tu varṣasahasrasya tapaḥphalamavāpsyati \|*  
*tatraiva saṃsthitaṃ devi taḍāgaṃ caṃdranirmitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dhanuḥṣoḍaśavistāraṃ caṃdreśātpūrvapaścime \|*  
*tatpūrvaṃ te samākhyātaṃ muktidānādipūrvakam \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. There is a Kuṇḍa of nectar remembered as Kalā Kuṇḍa. A man who, after taking his bath therein, worships Candreśa, attains the fruit of practising penance for one thousand years. There is a lake created there by the Moon-god, O goddess. It is sixteen Dhanus in extent (east-west) from Candreśa. It has been described to you formerly along with Mukti-dāna (granting of liberation etc.).

## Chapter 343 - Importance of (Observing the Vow of) Kapilā-Ṣaṣṭhī

## \|\| 1.343.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi kapileśvaramuttamam \|*  
*śīrābhūṣaṇapūrveṇa koṭitīrthācca paścime \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Then, O great goddess, one should go to the excellent (Liṅga) Kapileśvara. It is to the east of Śaśibhūṣaṇa and to the west of Koṭi Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.343.2 \|\|

*jaradgaveśāddakṣiṇe samudrottaratastathā \|*  
*etadvai kāpilaṃ kṣetraṃ nāpuṇyaiḥ prāpyate naraiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The Kṣetra pertaining to Kapila extends to the south of Jaradgaveśa and to the north of the sea. It is not (reached) by men devoid of merit.

## \|\| 1.343.3 \|\|

*kapilena purā devi yatra taptaṃ tapo mahat \|*  
*varṣāṇāmayutaṃ sāgraṃ pratiṣṭhāpya maheśvaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Installing Maheśvara in front of him, an intense penance was performed there by Kapila for ten thousand years.

## \|\| 1.343.4 \|\|

*samāhūtā tatra devī kapiladhārā mahānadī \|*  
*samudramadhye sā'dyāpi puṇyavadbhiḥ pradṛśyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. There, the great river, goddess Kapiladhārā, was invoked there. She is dearly seen today in the middle of the sea by meritorious people.

## \|\| 1.343.5-6 \|\|

*tatra snātvā mahādevi kapilāṣaṣṭhyāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*kapilāṃ dāpayettatra gokoṭiphalabhāgbhavet \|\| 5 \|\|*

*sarveṣāṃ caiva pāpānāṃ prāyaścittamidaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*kapileśvaraṃ tu saṃpūjya kanyākoṭiphalaṃ labhet \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. O great goddess, taking bath there especially on the Kapilā Ṣaṣṭhī day, one should gift away a tawny-coloured cow, which is equal to gifting ten million cows. This is remembered as the expiation of all sins.

After properly worshipping Kapileśvara, one gets the benefit of (giving in marriage) ten million girls.

## \|\| 1.343.7 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*āścaryaṃ mama deveśa kapilaṣaṣṭhyā maheśvara \|*  
*vidhānaṃ śrotumicchāmi dānamantrādi pūrvakam \|\| 7 \|\|*

Devī said:

7\. O Lord of Devas, it appears miraculous to me. I desire to listen to the procedure beginning with Dāna (religious gifts), Mantras etc. pertaining to Kapilā Ṣaṣṭhī.

## \|\| 1.343.8 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*janmajīvitamadhye tu yadyekā labhyate naraiḥ \|*  
*saṃyogayuktā sā ṣaṣṭhī tatkiṃ devi bravīmyaham \|\| 8 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

8\. Even if one (Kapilā) Ṣaṣṭhī along with all its astrological associations, is obtained within the span of one’s life by men, what more (propitious) can I say?

## \|\| 1.343.9 \|\|

*prauṣṭhapadyasite pakṣe ṣaṣṭhyāmaṃgārako yadi \|*  
*vyatīpātaśca rohiṇyāṃ sā ṣaṣṭhī kapilā smṛtā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The sixth lunar day in the dark half of Bhādrapada occurring on Tuesday and coinciding with Rohiṇī as the asterism and also with Vyatīpāta as Yoga is remembered as Kapilā Ṣaṣṭhī.

## \|\| 1.343.10-11 \|\|

*tatra kṣetre naraḥ snātvā athavārkasthale śubhe \|*  
*mṛdā śukla tilaiścaiva kapilāsaṃgame śubhe \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kṛtasnānajapaḥ paścātsūryāyārghyaṃ nivedayet \|*  
*raktacaṃdanatoyena karavīrayutena ca \|*  
*kṛtvārghapātraṃ śirasi maṃtreṇānena dāpayet \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Then a man should take his bath in a Kṣetra or an auspicious place pertaining to the Sun-god. After performing ablution with mud, white gingelly seeds on the auspicious confluence of Kapilā, he should perform Japa. Then he should offer Arghya to the Sun-god with water mixed with red sandal-paste with Karavīra (flowers) added to it. Taking upon his head a pot containing the Arghya, he should gift it uttering this Mantra:

## \|\| 1.343.12 \|\|

*namastrailokyanāthāya udbhāsitajagattraya \|*  
*vedaraśme namastubhyaṃ gṛhāṇārghyaṃ namo'stu te \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. “Obeisance to you, the Lord of the three worlds, who have illuminated the three worlds. O Veda-rayed one, accept the Arghya. My obeisance to you.”

## \|\| 1.343.13-16 \|\|

*sūryaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya saṃpūjya kapileśvaram \|*  
*upalipte śubhe deśe puṣpākṣatavibhūṣite \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sthāpayedavraṇaṃ kumbhaṃ candanodakapūritam \|*  
*paṃcaratnasamāyuktaṃ dūrvāpuṣpākṣatānvitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*raktavastrayugacchannaṃ tāmrapātreṇa saṃyutam \|*  
*ratho rukmaphalasyaiva ekacitravicitritaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sauvarṇapalasaṃyuktāṃ mūrtiṃ sūryasya kārayet \|*  
*kuṃbhasyopari saṃsthāpya gaṃdhapuṣpaiḥ samarcayet \|\| 16 \|\|*

13-16. Circumasmbulating the Sun-god and having worshipped Kapileśvara, he should place an uncracked earthen pot on an auspicious place besmeared (with cow-dung) and decorated with flowers and raw rice-grains.

The pot should be filled with water mixed with sandal-paste, with five jewels placed in it. It should have in it Dūrvā grass, flowers and raw rice-grains. It should be covered with a pair of red cloths and with a copper pot placed on the chariot of gold should be drawn (obscure!).

Picture of the icon of the Sun-god should be made of a Pala of gold. The idol (of the Sun-god) should be placed on the (earthen) pot and one should worship it with fragrant flowers.

## \|\| 1.343.17 \|\|

*kapileśvarasānnidhye maṇḍape homasaṃskṛte \|*  
*ādityaṃ pūjayeddevaṃ nāmabhiḥ svairyathoditaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. In the vicinity of Kapileśvara, in a panḍal sanctified by (performance of) Homa, the Sun-god should be worshipped by (reciting) his epithers \[epithets?\] as stated (below):

## \|\| 1.343.18 \|\|

*ādityabhāskara rave bhāno svayaṃ divākara \|*  
*prabhākara namastubhyaṃ sasārānmāṃ samuddhara \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. “O Āditya, Bhāskara, Ravi, Bhānu, Prabhākara, O maker of the day, I bow down to you; uplift me from Saṃsāra.

## \|\| 1.343.19 \|\|

*bhuktimuktiprado yasmāttasmācchāṃtiṃ prayaccha naḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. As you are the donor of enjoyment of pleasures here and liberation hereafter, give unto us peace and tranquility.

## \|\| 1.343.20 \|\|

*prārthanāmantraḥ \|*  
*namonamaste varada ṛksāmayajuṣāṃpate \|*  
*namo'stuviśvarūpāya viśvadhāmne namo'stu te \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Obeisance, Obeisance to you, O bestower of boons, O Lord of the Ṛk, Sāman and Yajurveda. Obeisance to you, O one having the universe as your form, O receptacle of the universe.

## \|\| 1.343.21 \|\|

*amṛtaṃ devi te kṣīraṃ pavitramiha puṣṭidam \|*  
*tvatprasādātpramucyaṃte manujāḥ sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O goddess (Kapilā), your milk is sanctifying, nutritious nectar here. It is through your grace that men get absolved from all sins.

## \|\| 1.343.22 \|\|

*brahmaṇotpādite devi vahnikuṇḍānmahāprabhe \|*  
*namaste kapile puṇye sarvadevanamaskṛte \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O goddess, created by god Brahmā from sacrificial pit, O Kapilā of great refulgence, salute to you, O meritorious (goddess) bowed to by all Devas.

## \|\| 1.343.23 \|\|

*sarvadevamaye devi sarvatīrthamaye śubhe \|*  
*dātāraṃ pūjayānaṃ māṃ brahmalokaṃ naya svayam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O goddess, comprising all Devas and all Tīrthas, O auspicious one, take me, yourself, your donor who worships you, to Brahma-Loka.”

## \|\| 1.343.24 \|\|

*pūjāmaṃtraḥ \|*  
*evaṃ saṃpūjya kapilāṃ kumbhasthaṃ ca divākaram \|*  
*brāhmaṇe vedaviduṣa ubhayaṃ pratipādayet \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. After properly adoring the Kapilā (tawny-coloured) cow, the divine one and Sun-god who is installed on the pot, both of them should be gifted to a Brāhmaṇa, a knower of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.343.25-26 \|\|

*vyāsāya sūryabhaktāya maṃtreṇānena dāpayet \|\| 25 \|\|*

*divyamūrttirjagaccakṣu rdvādaśātmā divākaraḥ \|*  
*kapilāsahito devo mama muktiṃ prayacchatu \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. They should be given to Vyāsa, the devotee of the Sun-god with (i.e. uttering) this Mantra: “O God of refulgent form, O eye of the world, O soul of the twelve, O maker of the day, accompanied with the Kapilā cow give unto me liberation (from Saṃsra).

## \|\| 1.343.27 \|\|

*yasmāttvaṃ kapile puṇyā sarvalokasya pāvanī \|*  
*pradattā saha sūryeṇa mama muktipradā bhava \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O Kapilā, inasmuch as you, the meritorious one, the sanctifier of the whole world, have been gifted along with the Sun-god, be a conferor unto me of liberation.”

## \|\| 1.343.28 \|\|

*palena dakṣiṇā kāryā tadardhārdhena vā punaḥ \|*  
*śaktito dakṣiṇāyuktāṃ tāṃ dhenuṃ pratipādayet \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Dakṣiṇā should be offered in the form of a Pala or half or one-fourth (of a Pala gold). The cow should be gifted with some Dakṣiṇā within one’s capacity.

## \|\| 1.343.29 \|\|

*yo'nena vidhinā kuryā tṣaṣṭhīṃ kapilasaṃjñitām \|*  
*so'śvamedhasahasrasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. A man who follows this procedure of the Ṣaṣṭhī (the sixth lunar day) designated as Kapilā (i.e. the Yoga called Kapilā-Ṣaṣṭhī) gets the benefit of performing one thousand horse-sacrifices.

## \|\| 1.343.30 \|\|

*yatphalaṃ sarvatīrtheṣu sarvadāneṣu yatphalam \|*  
*tatphalaṃ sarvamāpnoti yaḥ ṣaṣṭhīṃ kapilāṃ caret \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. He who observes Kapilā Ṣaṣṭhī (by this procedure) gets entirely all the benefits that accrue from (pilgrimage to) all Tīrthas and (offering) all (kinds of) religious gifts.

## \|\| 1.343.31 \|\|

*kapilākoṭisahasrāṇi kapilākoṭiśatāni ca \|*  
*sūryaparvaṇi yaddattvā tatphalaṃ koṭiśo bhavet \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Thousands of crores of Kapilās, hundreds of crores of Kapilās, whatever is given on this specific day of the Sun-god, the benefit of it becomes ten-million-fold.

## \|\| 1.343.32 \|\|

*koṭigoroma saṃkhyāni varṣāṇi varavarṇini \|*  
*tāvatsa vasate svarge yaḥ ṣaṣṭhīṃ kapilāṃ caret \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O lady of excellent complexion, he who performs the Kapilā Ṣaṣṭhī observance resides in heaven for as many years as there are hairs on the body of one crore cows.

## \|\| 1.343.33 \|\|

*jñānato'jñānato vāpi yatpāpaṃ pūrvasaṃcitam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ nāśamāyāti ityāha kapilo muniḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Sage Kapilā said that all the sins committed previously knowingly or unknowingly get annihilated (by the observance of Kapilā Ṣaṣṭhī).

## Chapter 344 - Greatness of Jaradgaveśvara (Jaradgava-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.344.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi liṃgaṃ pāpapraṇāśanam \|*  
*kapileśvarasyaiśānyāmuttareṇa vyavasthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Thereafter, O great goddess, one should go to the great sin-destroying Liṅga situated to the north of northeastern direction.

## \|\| 1.344.2 \|\|

*jaradgaveśvaraṃnāma jaradgavapratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*brahmahatyādi pāpānāṃ nāśanaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. It is called Jaradgaveśvara as it is installed by sage Jaradgava. There is no doubt that it is the destroyer of sins like killing of a Brāhmaṇa etc.

## \|\| 1.344.3 \|\|

*tatraiva saṃsthitā devi devī aṃśumatī nadī \|*  
*tatra snātvā vidhānena piḍadānaṃ tu dāpayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O goddess, there is the divine river Aṃśumatī. After taking a bath therein, one should offer Piṇḍas as per procedure.

## \|\| 1.344.4 \|\|

*varṣakoṭiśataṃ sāgraṃ pitṝṇāṃ tṛptimāvahet \|*  
*vṛṣabhastatra dātavyo brāhmaṇe vedapārage \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. It brings satisfaction unto the Pitṛs for a period of more than ten million years. A bull should be given to a Brāhmaṇa expert in the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.344.5-6 \|\|

*tatastu pūjayeddevaṃ gandhapuṣpairjaradgavam \|*  
*pañcāmṛtarasenaiva tathā guggu ludhūpanaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*stutidaṇḍanamaskāraiḥ pradakṣiṇairaharniśam \|*  
*brāhmaṇānbhojayettatra bhakṣyabhojyaiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|*  
*ekena bhojitenaiva koṭirbhavati bhojitā \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Thereafter, one should worship god Jaraḍgava with Pañcāmṛta (mixture of milk, sour milk, butter, honey and sugar), flowers as well as guggula-fumigation, with eulogy, prostrations and circumambulations day and night.

One should feed Brāhmaṇas there, with various eatables and delicacies. By feeding one, (the merit) becomes ten-million-fold.

## \|\| 1.344.7 \|\|

*kṛte siddhodakaṃnāma tattīrthaṃ parikīrttitam \|*  
*jaradgaveśvaraṃ tīrthaṃ kalau tu parikīrtyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. That Tīrtha was known as Siddhodaka in Kṛta Age. In Kali Age it is glorified as Jaradgaveśvara.

## Chapter 345 - Greatness of Naleśvara (Nala-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.345.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi liṃgaṃ vai hāṭakeśvaram \|*  
*jaradgavātpūrvabhāge dhanuṣāṃ ṣaṣṭibhistribhiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Thereafter, O great goddess, one should go to the Liṅga Hāṭakeśvara situated at a distance of one hundred eighty Dhanus to the east of Jaradgaveśvara.

## \|\| 1.345.2 \|\|

*nāmnā naleśvaraṃ devi sthāpitaṃ tu nalena vai \|*  
*damayantīyutenaiva jñātvā kṣetraṃ taduttamam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Knowing that it is an excellent Kṣetra, a Liṅga called Naleśvara was installed by Nala along with Damayantī.

## \|\| 1.345.3 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā mānavo devi pūjayitvā vidhānataḥ \|\| kalibhirmucyate jaṃturdyūte ca vijayī bhavet \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Visiting it and by worshipping it as per procedure, O goddess, a being (man) is freed from Kali and becomes victorious in gambling.

## Chapter 346 - Greatness of Karkotārka

## \|\| 1.346.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tasmādāgneyadigbhāge sthitaḥ karkoṭako raviḥ \|*  
*pūrvakalpe mahādevi smṛtaḥ karkoṭakānvitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. In the south-east region thereof, is situated the Sun-god called Karkoṭaka, O great goddess. In the previous Kalpa, it was remembered as associated with Karkoṭaka.

## \|\| 1.346.2 \|\|

*tasya darśanamātreṇa prītāḥ syuḥ sarvadevatāḥ \|*  
*saptamyāṃ ravivāreṇa dhūpa gaṃdhānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*pūjayedyo vidhānena mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. By merely visiting it, all deities become pleased. He who worships it with proper procedure by smearing it with fragrant substances and fumigate it with incense, is absolved of all sins.

## Chapter 347 - Greatness of Hāṭakeśvara (Hāṭaka-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.347.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi liṃgaṃ vai hāṭakeśvaram \|*  
*naleśvarātpūrvabhāge śatadhanvaṃtaradvaye \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Thenafter \[Thereafter?\], O great goddess, one should go to the Liṅga called Hāṭakeśvara at a distance of two hundred Dhanus to the east of Naleśvara.

## \|\| 1.347.2 \|\|

*agastyāmravanaṃnāma tatra sthāne tu saṃsthitam \|*  
*ciṃtāmaṇestu pūrveṇa īśāne triśataṃdhanuḥ \|*  
*tatra pūrvaṃ tapastaptamagastyena mahātmanā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. There, on the north-east, to the east of Cintāmaṇi, at a distance of three hundred Dhanus, there is situated a mango-park called Agastya. There formerly penance was performed by the great noble-souled Agastya.

## \|\| 1.347.3 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*kasminkāle mahādeva sarvaṃ vistarato vada \|\| 3 \|\|*

Devī said:

3\. O great god, tell me in detail in what period (he did so).

## \|\| 1.347.4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*purā daityagaṇā raudrā babhūvurvaravarṇini \|*  
*kālakeyā iti khyātāstrailokyocchedakārakāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

4\. O lady of excellent complexion, formerly terrible groups of Daityas known as Kālakeya came into existence. They were the exterminators of the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.347.5 \|\|

*atha te nihatāḥ sarve viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|*  
*daityasūdananāmnā tu prabhāsakṣetravāsinā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. All of them were killed by powerful Viṣṇu called Daityasūdana who was a resident of Prabhāsa Kṣetra.

## \|\| 1.347.6 \|\|

*kṛtvā vyāghrasya rūpaṃ tu nāmnā cakramukhīti ca \|*  
*hatā vai tena rūpeṇa tato'bhūddaityasūdanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He assumed the form of a tiger named Cakramukhin. They were killed by that form. Thereby he became known as Daityasūdana.

## \|\| 1.347.7 \|\|

*hataśeṣāḥ samudrāṃte praviṣṭā bhayavihvalāḥ \|*  
*tataste maṃtrayāmāsuḥ pīḍyaṃte devatāḥ katham \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The remaining (demons) overwhelmed with fear entered the sea. Then they held consultations as to how Devas could be harassed:

## \|\| 1.347.8 \|\|

*hanyaṃtāṃ dharmiṇo ye'tra vidyaṃte dhara ṇītale \|*  
*tapaḥsvādhyāyaniratā yajñadānaratāśca ye \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. “Those religious people who exist on the earth and are engaged in penance and Vedic studies and in performing sacrifices and making charitable gifts should be killed.”

## \|\| 1.347.9 \|\|

*atha te samayaṃ kṛtvā rātrau niṣkramya sāgarāt \|*  
*nirjaghnustāpasāṃstatra yajñadānaratānpriye \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O dear one, after taking such a decision they used to come out of the sea at night and kill the ascetics who were engaged in performance of sacrifice and charity.

## \|\| 1.347.10-11 \|\|

*prabhāse tu mahādevi tatra dvādaśayojane \|*  
*vasiṣṭhasyāśrame tatra maharṣīṇāṃ mahātmanām \|\| 10 \|\|*

*bhakṣitāni sahasrāṇi paṃca sapta ca tāpasān \|*  
*śatāni paṃca raibhyasya viśvāmitrasya ṣoḍaśa \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. O great goddess, in the Prabhāsa Kṣetra of twelve Yojanas (in extent) in the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha, they ate up seventy-five thousand noble-souled sages. (They devoured) five hundred sages in the hermitage of Raibhya and sixteen hundred in that of Viśvāmitra.

## \|\| 1.347.12 \|\|

*cyavanasya ca saptaiva jābālerdviśataṃ muneḥ \|*  
*vālakhilyāśrame puṇye ṣaṭchatāni durātmabhiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. By those wicked-souled ones, seven hundred sages in the hermitage of Cyavana, two hundred sages in the hermitage of Jābāli, and six hundred in the holy hermitage of Vālakhilyas (were killed).

## \|\| 1.347.13 \|\|

*yatra kvacidbhavedyajñastatra gatvā niśāgame \|*  
*yajñadānasamāyuktānṛtvijo bhakṣayaṃti ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. If any sacrifice perchance was performed at a place, after nightfall, they devoured the sacrificial priests employed for (performance of) the sacrifice and religious gifts.

## \|\| 1.347.14 \|\|

*tato bhayākulāḥ sarve babhūvurjagatī tale \|*  
*na ca kaścidvijānāti daityānāṃ tu viceṣṭitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then all over the world, all were distressed with terror. Nobody knew these deeds of the Daityas.

## \|\| 1.347.15 \|\|

*rātrau svapaṃti munayaḥ sukhaśayyāgatāśca te \|*  
*prabhāte tvadhvare teṣāmasthisaṃghāśca kevalam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Sages occupied cosy beds and slept at night. At dawn only their heaps of bones were found in the places of sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.347.16 \|\|

*tato dharmakriyāstyaktā bhūtale sarvamānavaiḥ \|*  
*niḥsvādhyāyavaṣaṭkāraṃ bhūtalaṃ samapadyata \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thereafter, on the surface of the earth, all religious acts were abandoned by all men. The whole world became devoid of Svādhyāya and the utterance of Vaṣaṭ.

## \|\| 1.347.17-21 \|\|

*athānye tāpasā rātrau saṃyutāśca ca dhṛtāyudhāḥ \|*  
*athocchedaṃ gate dharme pīḍitāstridivaukasaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kimetaditi jalpaṃto brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*bhagavaṃstāpasāḥ sarve tathā ye jñānaśīlinaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*bhakṣyante kenacidrātrau mṛtyumeva prayānti ca \|*  
*naṣṭadharmakriyāḥ sarve bhūtale prapitāmaha \|\| 19 \|\|*

*yo dharmamācaredahni sa rātrau mṛtyumeti ca \|*  
*na svādhyāyavaṣaṭkāraṃ samaste bhūtale vibho \|\| 20 \|\|*

*dharmābhāvādvayaṃ sarve saṃdehaṃ paramaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā dhyātvā devaḥ pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*abravīttridaśānsarvānsandehaṃ paramaṃ gatān \|\| 21 \|\|*

17-21. Then some other ascetics equipped with weapons stood united at night. Thus when religious acts stopped, the residents of Svarga (Devas) became harassed. They sought refuge in god Brahmā, asking: “What is it (going on)? O Lord, all the ascetics as well as those possessing knowledge are devoured by someone at night and they meet death. O Greatgrandfather, all religious acts have become extinct on the earth. He who abides by religious duties during the day meets death at night. In the entire world there is no Svādhyāya or utterence of Vaṣaṭ. Due to the stoppage of religious acts, all of us have found ourselves in doubtful (precarious) position.” After hearing their speech, the Grandfather (Brahmā) meditated (for a while) and spoke to all the Devas who were enmeshed in deep uncertainty:

## \|\| 1.347.22-26 \|\|

*kāleyā iti vikhyātā dānavā raudrakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*te samudraṃ samāsādya tāpasānbhakṣayaṃti ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

*yuṣmākaṃ ca vināśāya te na śakyā niṣūditum \|*  
*yatadhvameṣāṃ nāśāya no cennāśo bhaviṣyati \|\| 23 \|\|*

*vrajadhvaṃ bhūtale śīghramagastyo yatra tiṣṭhati \|*  
*vratacaryārato nityaṃ prabhāse kṣetra uttame \|\| 24 \|\|*

*sa śaktaḥ sāgaraṃ pātuṃ mitrāvaruṇasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*prasādyaśca sa yuṣmābhiḥ samudraṃ piba sattama \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tatastathā kṛte tena te sarve dānavādhamāḥ \|*  
*vadhyā yuṣmākaṃ bhaviṣyaṃti evaṃ ca tridiveśvarāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

22-26. “Dānavas known as Kāleyas are terrible in action. They resort to the sea (by day) and eat up the sages (at night). For you, they cannot be killed by you. Try to destroy them, otherwise there will be annihilation. Quickly go down to the earth where, in the excellent Prabhāsa Kṣetra, Agastya always resides engaged in observance of vows. Born of gods Mitra and Varuṇa, he is capable of drinking up the ocean. He should be persuaded by you: ‘O excellent one, drink up the sea.’ When he has accomplished that, all the Dānavas will thus be killed by you, O Devas.”

## \|\| 1.347.27 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*evamuktāḥ surāḥ sarve brahmaṇā lokakāriṇā \|*  
*prabhāsaṃ kṣetramāsādya agastyaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. When addressed thus by god Brahmā, the creator of the world, all the Devas came to the holy place of Prabhāsa and sought refuge in him (Agastya).

## \|\| 1.347.28 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*rakṣarakṣa dvijaśreṣṭha trailokyaṃ saṃśayaṃ gatam \|*  
*kālakeyaiḥ pratidhvastaṃ samudraṃ samupāśritaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

Devas said:

28\. O, greatest one among Brāhmaṇas, please do protect us. The group of the three worlds is in an embarrasssing position. It has been devastated by Kālakeyas who take refuge in the sea.

## \|\| 1.347.29 \|\|

*taṃ śoṣaya dvijaśreṣṭha hitārthaṃ tridivaukasām \|*  
*nānyaḥ śaktaḥ pumānkaścitkartumīdṛkkriyā vibho \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O great Brāhmaṇa, dry it (the sea) up for the welfare of the Devas. O mighty one, no other man is capable of achieving such a feat.

## \|\| 1.347.30 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*evamuktaḥ suragaṇairagastyo munipuṅgavaḥ \|*  
*jagāma tridaśaiḥ sārdhaṃ samudraṃ prati harṣitaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

30\. When addressed thus by groups of Suras, Agastya, the eminent sage, became elated (with joy) and went to the sea along with Devas.

## \|\| 1.347.31 \|\|

*gīyamānastu gaṃdharvaiḥ stūyamānastu kinnaraiḥ \|*  
*ślāghyamānastu vibudhairvākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. While being sung by Gandharvas, eulogized by Kinnaras and praised by Vibudhas (Devas), he spoke the (following) words:

## \|\| 1.347.32 \|\|

*eṣa trailokyarakṣārthaṃ śoṣayāmi mahārṇavam \|*  
*drakṣyadhvaṃ kautukaṃ devāḥ samīnamakarairmahat \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. “O Devas, do behold the miraculous act. For the protection of the three world, here I dry up the vast ocean along with its fishes and crocodiles.”

## \|\| 1.347.33 \|\|

*evamuktvā dvijaśreṣṭho hyagastyo bhagavānmuniḥ \|*  
*gaṃḍūṣamakarotsarvaṃ sāgaraṃ saritāṃpatim \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. After saying this, the venerable sage Agastya, the greatest of Brāhmaṇas, gulped the entire Ocean, the Lord of rivers (holding him up in his hollow palms of hands.).

## \|\| 1.347.34 \|\|

*pīte tatra mahāsindhāvagatsye na mahātmanā \|*  
*dānavā bhayasaṃtrastā itaścetaśca babhramuḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. When the great Ocean was drunk up by the noble-souled Agastya, Dānavas became panick-stricken and ran helter-skelter.

## \|\| 1.347.35 \|\|

*vadhyamānāḥ suraistatra śastraiḥ suniśitaistathā \|*  
*kāṃtāramanye gacchaṃtaḥ palāyanaparāyaṇā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. While they were being killed by Suras with sharp weapons, some others took to flight into a jungle.

## \|\| 1.347.36 \|\|

*hatabhūyeṣu daityeṣu vidārya dharaṇītalam \|*  
*pātālaṃ viviśustūrṇaṃ rudhireṇa pariplutāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. When most of the Daityas were killed some quickly split up the earth and entered the nether world, smeared with blood.

## \|\| 1.347.37 \|\|

*athocustridaśā hṛṣṭā agastyaṃ munisattamam \|*  
*siddhaṃ no vāṃchitaṃ sarvaṃ pūryatāṃ sāgaraḥ punaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Then the Devas who were delighted spoke to the most excellent sage Agastya: “Our desired objective has been completely achieved. Now fill up the sea again.”

## \|\| 1.347.38-40 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*jīrṇaṃ toyaṃ mayā devāstathaivāmedhyatāṃ gatam \|*  
*utpatsyati raghūṇāṃ hi kule nṛpatisattamaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*bhagīratheti vikhyātaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*sa jñātikāraṇādeva gaṃgāṃ tatrānayiṣyati \|\| 39 \|\|*

*brahmalokātsaricchreṣṭhāṃ tayā pūrṇo bhaviṣyati \|*  
*evamuktvā suraiḥ sārddhaṃ svasthānaṃ cāgamanmuniḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

Agastya said:

38-40. O Devas, the water that is consumed by me has been reduced to an impure condition.

In the family of Raghu a most excellent king well-known as Bhagīratha will be born. That eminent one among the bearers of arms will bring Gaṅgā, the greatest river, from the region of Brahmā, for the sake of his clan. It will be then filled up by her.”

After saying thus, the sage went to his abode along with Suras.

## \|\| 1.347.41-42 \|\|

*tataḥ svamāśramaṃ prāptaṃ devā vākyamathābuvan \|*  
*anena karmaṇā brahmanparituṣṭā vayaṃ mune \|\| 41 \|\|*

*kiṃ kurmo brūhi te'bhīṣṭaṃ yadyapi syātsudurlabham \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. When he reached his hermitage, Devas spoke to him: “O sage, we are completely satisfied, O Brāhmaṇa. Speak out what desired object of yours we should do (grant) even if it be very difficult to obtain.”

## \|\| 1.347.43 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*yāvadbrahmasahasrāṇi paṃcaviṃśatikoṭayaḥ \|*  
*vaimāniko bhaviṣyāmi dakṣiṇāṃbaramūrddhani \|\| 43 \|\|*

Agastya said:

43\. Let me be a celestial being (a star) in the southern (region of the) firmament for the duration of twenty-five hundred crores of Brahmās.

## \|\| 1.347.44-49 \|\|

*atrāgatya naro yastu mamāśramapade śubhe \|*  
*hāṭakeśvarasāṃnidhye prabhāsakṣetra uttame \|\| 44 \|\|*

*snānamācarate samyaksa yātu paramāṃ gatim \|*  
*pātālādavatīrṇaṃ taṃ liṃgarūpaṃ maheśvaram \|\| 45 \|\|*

*mayā tapaḥ prabhāvena sthāpitaṃ yaḥ prapūjayet \|*  
*dinedine bhavettasya gośatasya phalaṃ dhruvam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*lopāmudrāsahāyaṃ māṃ yo martyaḥ saṃprapūjayet \|*  
*arghyaṃ dadyādvidhānena kāśa puṣpaiḥ samāhitaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*prāpte śaradi kāle ca sa yātu paramāṃ gatim \|*  
*lopāmudrāsahāyaṃ māṃ hāṭakeśvarasaṃyutam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*ayane cottare pūjya golakṣa phalamāpnuyāt \|*  
*yaḥ śrāddhaṃ kurute cātra ayane cottare dvijaḥ \|*  
*bhūyāttasya phalaṃ kṛtsnaṃ gayāśrāddhasya sattamāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

44-49. A man who comes here to the auspicious region of my hermitage near Hāṭakeśvara in this excellent holy place of Prabhāsa and takes an ablution properly, will go to the excellent region.

He who elaborately worships Maheśvara in the form of a Liṅga which has emerged from the nether worlds and has been installed by me by the prowess of my penance shall definitely derive everyday the fruit of having gifted a hundred cows. May a man who duly worships me in the company of Lopāmudrā and offers me Arghya as per procedure with Kāśa flowers when the autumnal season arrives, reach the excellent goal (Heaven).

May he who worships me in the company of Lopāmudrā and along with Hāṭakeśvara in the summer solstice, get the benefit of (the gift of) a hundred thousand cows. O excellent one, may the entire fruit of Gayā-Śrāddha accrue to the Brāhmaṇa who performs a Śrāddha here during the northern transit of the Sun.”

## \|\| 1.347.50 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*bāḍhamitye va te coktvā sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ \|*  
*svasthānaṃ tu gatāḥ sarve saṃhṛṣṭamanasastadā \|\| 50 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

50\. Saying “Definitely so (it will happen),” all Devas along with Vāsava (Indra) with their minds highly delighted went to their own abodes.

## \|\| 1.347.51 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena prāpte śaradi mānavaḥ \|*  
*agastyasyāśramaṃ gatvā hāṭakeśaṃ prapūjayet \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Therefore, putting in all efforts a man should go to the hermitage of Agastya when the autumnal season arrives and should elaborately adore Hāṭakeśa.

## \|\| 1.347.52 \|\|

*agastyeśvaranāmānaṃ kalpaliṃgaṃ surapriyam \|*  
*yaścaitacchuṇuyādbhaktyā ṛṣestasya viceṣṭitam \|*  
*ahorātrakṛtātpāpāttatkṣaṇā deva mucyate \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. He who listens to the action of the sage and to the Kalpa-Liṅga called Agastyeśvara so dear to Devas, is instantly absolved of the sin committed during that day and night.

## Chapter 348 - Greatness of Nāradeśvarī (Nārada-īśvarī)

## \|\| 1.348.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi paścime nāradeśvarīm \|*  
*nāradeśvarasāṃnidhye sarvadaurbhāgyanāśanīm \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Then, O great goddess, one should go to the west to Nāradeśvarī in the vicinity of Nāraḍeśvara. She destroys all (effects of) ill luck (especially widowhood).

## \|\| 1.348.2 \|\|

*yā nārī pūjayeddevīṃ tṛtīyāyāṃ samāhitā \|*  
*tadanvaye na daurbhāgyayuktā nārī bhaviṣyati \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. If a woman, with concentration, worships the goddess on the third lunar day, no woman in her family shall be affected by ill luck (widowhood).

## Chapter 349 - Greatness of Mantra-vibhūṣaṇā Gaurī

## \|\| 1.349.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi devīṃ maṃtravibhūṣaṇām \|*  
*bhīmeśvarasya sānnidhye somenārādhitāṃ purā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Then, O great goddess, one should go to the goddess Mantra-vibhūṣaṇā (Gaurī) in the vicinity of Bhīmeśvara. She was formerly propitiated by Soma.

## \|\| 1.349.2 \|\|

*śrāvaṇe māsi vidhinā yā nārī tāṃ prapūjayet \|*  
*tṛtīyāyāṃ śuklapakṣe sā duḥkhairmucyate'khilaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. A woman who duly worships her on the third lunar day in the bright half of the month of Śrāvaṇa is relieved of all miseries.

## Chapter 350 - Greatness of Durga-Kūṭa Gaṇapati

## \|\| 1.350.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi viśveśaṃ durgakūṭakam \|*  
*bhallatīrthasya pūrveṇa yoginīcakradakṣiṇe \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. O great goddess, one should thereafter go to Gaṇeśa (Vighneāsa \[Vighneśa?\] master-controller of obstacles) called Durgakūṭa. (He is) to the east of Bhalla Tīrtha and to the south of Yoginīcakra.

## \|\| 1.350.2-3 \|\|

*ārādhito'sau bhīmena sarvakāmaprado'bhavat \|*  
*phālgunasya caturthyāṃ tu śuklapakṣe vidhānataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yastaṃ pūjayate devaṃ gandhapuṣpaiḥ samodakaiḥ \|*  
*nirvighnaṃ jāyate tasya varṣamekaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. He was worshipped by Bhīmasena and became the granter of all desires. On the fourth day in the bright half of Phālguna, he who worships him (the god) as per proper procedure, with fragrant paste and flowers along with (the Naivedya of) Modakas (a sweet dish) gets one year undoubtedly free from all obstacles.

## Chapter 351 - Greatness of Kauraveśvarī (Kaurava-īśvarī)

## \|\| 1.351.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi tasmādvai kauraveśvarīm \|*  
*yasya nāmnā kurukṣetraṃ tena sārādhitā purā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Thereafter, O great goddess, from thence one should go to Kauraveśvarī who was propitiated by Kuru himself, after whom Kurukṣetra is named.

## \|\| 1.351.2 \|\|

*ārādhitā'sau bhīmena kṛtvā kṣetrasya rakṣaṇam \|*  
*mahānavamyāṃ yatnena yastāṃ pūjayate naraḥ \|*  
*taṃ putramiva kalyāṇī rakṣate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. She was propitiated by Bhīma after protecting the holy place (Kṣetra). A man who assiduously worships her on Mahānavamī (ninth day in the bright half of Āśvina), the auspicious deity protects him like her son. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.351.3 \|\|

*bhojanaṃ tatra dātavyaṃ daṃpatīnāṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*divyairbhakṣyaiḥ sumiṣṭānnaiḥ sā tuṣyati tataḥ stutā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Meals should be served to couples there with heavenly eatables and excellent delicious food. There is no doubt that when eulogized she gets pleased.

## Chapter 352 - Greatness of Suparṇelā

## \|\| 1.352.2 \|\|

*suparṇena purā devi pātālādamṛtaṃ hṛtam \|*  
*gṛhītvā tatra muktaṃ tu nāgānāṃ paśyatāṃ kila \|\| 2 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

Thereafter, O great goddess, one should go to the Bhairavī called Suparṇelā, to the south of Durga-Kūṭa (Gaṇapati) at a distance of five hundred Dhanus.

2\. Formerly, while the Nāgas (serpents) were watching, Nectar (Amṛta) was taken away by Suparṇa and was kept there (at a spot in Prabhāsa).

## \|\| 1.352.3 \|\|

*tato devyā tadā dṛṣṭvā rakṣitaṃ nāgapārśvataḥ \|*  
*tataḥ suparṇeletyevaṃ khyātā sā vasudhātale \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Seeing that Amṛta was protected by her by the side of Nāgas, she therefore became famous in the world as Suparṇelā.

## \|\| 1.352.4 \|\|

*ilā tu kathyate bhūmiḥ suparṇena pratiṣṭhitā \|*  
*tataḥ suparṇeletyeva nāmnā pātakanāśinī \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The earth is called ‘Ilā’. That spot was established by Suparṇa. Hence that sin-destroying spot came to be known by the name ‘Suparṇelā.’

## \|\| 1.352.5 \|\|

*suparṇakuṇḍe tatraiva snātvā tāṃ pūjayennaraḥ \|*  
*viprebhyo bhojanaṃ dadyānnāpadbhirmriyate naraḥ \|*  
*jīvavatsā bhavennārī ātmajaiścāpyalaṃkṛtā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. A man should worship her after taking a bath in Suparṇa Kuṇḍa. He should feed Brāhmaṇas. He does not die in miseries. The woman has all her children alive. She is (as if) decorated by her children.

## Chapter 353 - Greatness of Bhalla Tīrtha

## \|\| 1.353.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi bhallatīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*tasyāśca paścime bhāge yatra viṣṇuścaturbhujaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Thereafter, O great goddess, one should go to the excellent Bhalla Tīrtha on the western side of Suparṇelā where stands the four-armed Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 1.353.2-3 \|\|

*yatra tyaktaṃ śarīraṃ tu viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|*  
*tasminmitravane ramye yojanārddhārddhavistṛte \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yugeyuge mahādevi kalpamanvatarādiṣu \|*  
*tatraiva saṃsthitirviṣṇornānyatra ca ratirbhavet \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. His own body was abandoned by the powerful Viṣṇu (Kṛṣṇa). There in the beautiful Mitra-vana extending to one-fourth of a Yojana, the death of Viṣṇu takes place in every Yuga in (all the) Kalpas and Manvantaras, O great goddess. He has no liking for any other (place).

## \|\| 1.353.4-7 \|\|

*kṣetrāṇāmādikṣetraṃ tu vaiṣṇavaṃ tadvidurbudhāḥ \|*  
*tisraḥ koṭyarddhakoṭiśca tīrthānāṃ pravarāṇi ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

*divi bhuvyaṃtarikṣe ca tāni tatraiva bhāmini \|*  
*tatra mūrtimatī gaṃgā svayameva vyavasthitā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*viṣṇoḥ saṃplavanārthāya prāṇināṃ ca hitāya vai \|*  
*gaṃgā gayā kurukṣetraṃ naimiṣaṃ puṣkarāṇi ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

*purī dvāravatīṃ tyaktvā atraiva vasate hariḥ \|*  
*tasyaurdhvadaihikaṃ devi prakaromi yugeyuge \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-5a. Learned people know it to be the first Vaiṣṇava Kṣetra (sacred place pertaining to Viṣṇu) in all the Kṣetras.

Three and half crores of prominent Tīrthas which exist in heaven, earth and the intermediate space, abide therein only.

5b-6a. There Gaṅgā herself in her personal form stays for the ablution of Viṣṇu and for the welfare of beings.

6b-7. Abandoning sacred places like Gaṅgā, Gayā, Naimiṣa forest, Puṣkara lake and the city of Dvārāvatī, Hari stays (dies) at this very place. O goddess, I perform his obsequies in every Yuga.

## \|\| 1.353.8-11 \|\|

*nabhasye dvādaśīyoge tatra gatvā svayaṃ priye \|*  
*karomi tadvidhānena tatra brāhmaṇapuṃgavaiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tatra dattvā tu dānāni vidhivadvedapārage \|*  
*tatraiva dvādaśīyoge snātvā caiva vidhānataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*santarpya ca pitṝnbhaktyā mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|*  
*tatra viṣṇuṃ tu saṃpūjya kṛtvā jāgaraṇaṃ niśi \|\| 10 \|\|*

*dīpādidānaṃ kṛtvā tu kṛtakṛtyo'bhijāyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

8-9a. In the month of Bhādrapada on the twelfth day, I personally go there. I perform those (obsequies) as per procedure with prominent Brāhmaṇas and offer Dāna as per procedure to the knowers of the Vedas.

9b-10a. At that very place, on the twelfth lunar day, one should take bath as per procedure, and by devoutly gratifying the Pitṛs one is absolved of all sins, O dear.

10b-11. By worshipping Viṣṇu there and keeping awake at night (in the service of god Viṣṇu) and making gifts like those of lamps etc. one becomes one who has performed every (prescribed) act worth doing.

## \|\| 1.353.12-14 \|\|

*atha tasya pravakṣyāmi purāvṛtta mahaṃ priye \|*  
*saṃhṛtya yādavānsarvānvāsudevaḥ pratāpavān \|\| 12 \|\|*

*durvāsasā'nuliptena pāyasena padastale \|*  
*vajrāṃgabhūtadehastu sarvavyāpī janārddanaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*gatvā tīre samudrasya samādhistho babhūva ha \|*  
*sarvasrotāṃsi saṃyamya niveśyātmānamātmani \|\| 14 \|\|*

12a-14. O my dear, now I relate what happened there formerly. After eliminating all Yādavas, powerful Vāsudeva whose body had become as impregnable as Vajra by the Pāyasa wherewith he was smeared by Durvāsas that all-prevading \[pervading?\] Janārdana went to the shore of the sea. He controlled all the sense-organs, concentrated his individual self on the higher self and became absorbed in Samādhi.

## \|\| 1.353.15 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare prāpto bāṇahasto jarābhidhaḥ \|*  
*dāśaputro'tikṛṣṇāṃgo matsyaghātī ca pāpakṛt \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In the meanwhile there came an extremely dark-complexioned, sinful fisherman named Jara, son of a Dāsa, with an arrow in his hand.

## \|\| 1.353.16 \|\|

*tena dṛṣṭastato dūrānniṣādātmasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇoḥ padaṃ mṛgaṃ matvā śaraṃ tasya mumoca ha \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then from a distance that son of Niṣāda saw the foot (sole) of Viṣṇu. Thinking it to be a deer, he shot his arrow (at it).

## \|\| 1.353.17-19 \|\|

*tato'sau paśyate yāvadgatvā tasya ca saṃnidhau \|*  
*caturbāhuṃ mahākāyaṃ śaṃkhacakragadādharam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*puruṣaṃ nīlameghābhaṃ puḍarīkanibhe kṣaṇam \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhayabhītastu vepamānaḥ kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*abravīnna mayā jñātastvaṃ vibho divyarūpadhṛk \|\| 18 \|\|*

*ajñānāttvaṃ mayā viddhastvatpadāgre surottama \|*  
*kṣantumarhasi me nātha na tvaṃ kroddhumihārhasi \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. Thereafter, when he approached him (Kṛṣṇa) he saw a huge-bodied person with four arms holding a conch, discus and mace. His complexion was like a blue cloud and eyes like lotuses.

Seeing him, he got terrified. Trembling (with fear) and with folded hands, he spoke: “I did not know, O Lord, that it was you, the divine-bodied one. O excellent Sura, (it was) out of ignorance that you were hit in the sole of your foot. It behoves you, O Lord, to pardon me and not to be angry with me.”

## \|\| 1.353.20 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*śāpasyāṃtodya me bhadra śarapātātkṛtastvayā \|*  
*tasmāttvaṃ matprasādena svargaṃ gaccha mahādyute \|\| 20 \|\|*

Viṣṇu (Kṛṣṇa) said:

20\. By hitting me with an arrow, you have put an end to my curse. Therefore, through my grace, go to heaven, O highly refulgent one.

## \|\| 1.353.21 \|\|

*ye cānye māmihāgatya drakṣyaṃti hi narottamāḥ \|*  
*te yāsyaṃti paraṃ sthānaṃ yatrāhaṃ nityasaṃsthitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Those other excellent men who come here and view me will go to the great region where I permanently reside.

## \|\| 1.353.22 \|\|

*bhallenāhaṃ yato viddhastvayā pādatale śubhe \|*  
*bhallatīrthamiti khyātaṃ tato hyetadbhaviṣyati \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Inasmuch as I have been hit by you with a Bhalla (a kind of arrow), this place will become famous as ‘Bhalla Tīrtha’.

## \|\| 1.353.23 \|\|

*harikṣetramiti proktaṃ pūrvaṃ svāyaṃbhuve'ntare \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Formerly in Svāyaṃbhuva Manvantara it was spoken of as Harikṣetra.

## \|\| 1.353.24 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvāṃtardadhe viṣṇurlubdhako'pi divaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*ye'tra snānaṃ kariṣyaṃti bhaktyā paramayā yutāḥ \|*  
*viṣṇulokaṃ gamiṣyaṃti prītyā te matprasādataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

24\. After saying this, Viṣṇu (Kṛṣṇa) disappeared. The hunter too went to heaven. Those who perform ablution here endowed with deep devotion, will go to Viṣṇuloka out of love, through my grace.

## \|\| 1.353.25 \|\|

*ye'tra śrāddhaṃ kariṣyaṃti pitṛbhaktiparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*tṛptiṃ teṣāṃ gamiṣyaṃti pitaraścaiva tarpitāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Those who are intent in their devotion to Pitṛs and perform Śrāddha here, their Pitṛs so gratified, attain satisfaction.

## \|\| 1.353.26 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena prāpya tatkṣetramuttamam \|*  
*dṛśyo devaścaturbāhuḥ snātvā tīrthe tu bhallake \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Hence, putting in all efforts, one should go to that excellent Kṣetra. After taking bath in the Bhallaka, the Fourarmed God should be visited.

## \|\| 1.353.27 \|\|

*madbhaktibaladarpiṣṭhā matpriyaṃ na namaṃti ye \|*  
*vāsudevaṃ na te jñeyā madbhaktāḥ pāpino hi te \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. People who, being extremely proud of the power of their devotion to me, do not pay obeisance to Vāsudeva so dear to me, should not be regarded as my devotees. They are sinners.

## \|\| 1.353.28 \|\|

*madbhakto'pi hi yo bhūtvā bhuṃkta ekādaśīdine \|*  
*malliṃgasyārcanaṃ kāryaṃ na tena pāpabuddhinā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Worship of my Liṅga should not be performed by that man of evil intellect who even being my devotee, takes meals on the eleventh lunar day.

## \|\| 1.353.29 \|\|

*yā tithirdayitā viṣṇoḥ sā tithirmama vallabhā \|*  
*na tāṃ copoṣayedyastu sa pāpiṣṭhatarādhikaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The lunar day which is dear to Viṣṇu is also dear to me. He who does not observe fast on that day is the greatest sinner.

## \|\| 1.353.30 \|\|

*tadvatsa dvādaśīyoge bhallatīrthasya saṃnidhau \|*  
*yastu māṃ pūjayedbhaktyā nārī vā'pi naro'pi vā \|*  
*tasya janmasahasrāṇi gṛhabhaṃgo na jāyate \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Similarly one who, on the twelfth lunar day, devoutly worships me in the vicinity of Bhalla Tīrtha, whether one be a man or a woman, has no break (bereavement) at home in thousands of births.

## \|\| 1.353.31 \|\|

*ityetatkathitaṃ devi māhātmyaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*bhallatīrthasya viṣṇostu sarva pātakanāśanam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Thus has been narrated, O goddess, the greatness of Bhalla Tīrtha of Viṣṇu which is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.353.32 \|\|

*tatra viṣṇostu sāṃnidhye vāyavye kumbhamuttamam \|*  
*bhallatīrthaṃ tu vikhyātaṃ yatra bhallahato hariḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. There, in the vicinity of Viṣṇu, in the north-west, is an excellent Kumbha (this word should be Kuṇḍa as there is no pitcher but a pool of water there). It is famous as Bhalla Tīrtha as Hari was killed with a Bhalla type of arrow.

## \|\| 1.353.33 \|\|

*tatra deyāni vāsāṃsi padaṃ gāvo vidhānataḥ \|*  
*deyāni vipramukhyebhyaḥ samyagyātrāphalepsubhiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. There cloths and cows should be given as per procedure to prominent Brāhmaṇas by persons desirous of securing the fruit of (proper performance of) the Yātrā.

## Chapter 354 - Greatness of Kardamāla

## \|\| 1.354.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi kardamālamanuttamam \|*  
*tīrthaṃ trailokyavikhyātaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Thereafter, O great goddess, one should go to the excellent Tīrtha Kardamāla famous in all the three worlds as destroyer of all sins.

## \|\| 1.354.2-3 \|\|

*tasminnekārṇave ghore naṣṭe sthāvarajaṃgame \|*  
*candrārkatapane naṣṭe jyotiṣi pralayaṃ gate \|\| 2 \|\|*

*rasātalagatāmurvīṃ dṛṣṭvā devo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*vārāhaṃ rūpamāsthāya daṃṣṭrāgreṇa varānane \|*  
*utkṣipya dharaṇīṃ mūrdhnā svasthāne saṃnyaveśayat \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. In that terrible expanse of one ocean everywhere, the mobiles and immobiles got destroyed. The Moon, the Sun and fire disappeared and all heavenly luminaries became extinct. God Janārdana saw that the Earth has submerged in Rasātala. He assumed the form of a (divine) Boar and lifted up the Earth with the tip of his tusk and with his head he placed the Earth in her original position.

## \|\| 1.354.4 \|\|

*uddhṛtya bhagavānviṣṇurvākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. After lifting her up, Lord Viṣṇu spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.354.5 \|\|

*atra sthāne sthitenaiva mayā tvaṃ devi coddhṛtā \|*  
*mamātra niyataṃ vāsaḥ sadaivāyaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. “O goddess, by staying at this very place you were lifted up by me. Hence, my permanent residence shall be here forever.

## \|\| 1.354.6 \|\|

*ye pitṝṃstarpayiṣyaṃti kardamāle varānane \|*  
*ākalpaṃ tarpitāstena bhaviṣyaṃti na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Those who propitiate their Pitṛs in Kardamālaya, O lady of excellent face, their Pitṛs get satisfied for a period of a Kalpa. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.354.7 \|\|

*tatra śrāddhaṃ kariṣyaṃti śākairmūlaphalena vā \|*  
*bhaviṣyati kṛtaṃ śrāddhaṃ sarvatīrtheṣu vai śubhe \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Performing Śrāddha with greens, roots and fruits here is as good as the Śrāddha performed in all the Tīrthas, O auspicious lady.

## \|\| 1.354.8 \|\|

*atra tīrthe naraḥ snātvā yo māṃ paśyati mānavaḥ \|*  
*api kīṭapataṃgā ye nidhanaṃ yāṃti mānavāḥ \|*  
*te mṛtāstri divaṃ yānti sukṛtena yathā dvijāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. A man who after taking bath in this Tīrtha, views me and even insects, birds and men who die here, go to heaven with this merit like Brāhmaṇas (with their meritorious acts.)

## \|\| 1.354.9-10 \|\|

*tato dvīpeṣu jāyante dhanāḍhyāścottame kule \|*  
*daṃṣṭrābhedena yattoyaṃ nirgataṃ te śarīrataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā naro devi tiryagyonau na jāyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Then they are born in (different) continents in excellent, affluent families. A man who takes his bath in the water that comes out of your body pierced by the tusk, will never be born in non-human species, O goddess!”

## \|\| 1.354.11 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi yathāvṛttamāścaryaṃ tatra vai purā \|*  
*mṛgayūthaṃ susantrastaṃ lubdhakaiḥ paripīḍitam \|*  
*praviṣṭaṃ kardamāle tu sadyo mānuṣatāṃ gatam \|\| 11 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

11\. Listen, O goddess, to the factual account of the miracles that happened there formerly. A group of deer extremely harrassed by hunters entered the Kardamāla Tīrtha and was transformed into human beings.

## \|\| 1.354.12 \|\|

*atha te lubdhakā dṛṣṭvā vismayotphullalocanāḥ \|*  
*apṛcchaṃta ca saṃbhrātāstānmartyānvaravarṇini \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The hunters witnessed this with their eyes blooming with wonder and became embarrassed. They asked those mortal beings, O excellent lady:

## \|\| 1.354.13-14 \|\|

*mṛgayūthamanuprāptaṃ kena mārgeṇa nirgatam \|*  
*athocuste vayaṃ prāptā mānuṣaṃ mṛgarūpiṇaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*etattīrthaprabhāvo'yaṃ na vidmo hyātma kāraṇam \|*  
*tataste lubdhakāstyaktvā dhanūṃṣi saśarāṇi ca \|*  
*tatra snātvā mahābhāge muktāśca sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. “Which way has the group of deer which arrived here escaped?” They replied: “We who had the form of deer have obtained human form. We did not know the efficacy of this Tīrtha for ourselves.”

Then the hunters abandoned their bows and arrows, took bath therein and became absolved of all sins, O highly fortunate lady.

## \|\| 1.354.15 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*bhagavanvistaraṃ brūhi kardamālamahodayam \|*  
*utpattiṃ ca vidhānaṃ ca kṣetrasīmādikaṃ kramāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:

15\. O Lord, tell me in detail the extent, greatness, its creation, the boundaries of the Kṣetra Kardamāla and the procedures to be followed.

## \|\| 1.354.16 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi rahasyaṃ tu karda mālasamudbhavam \|*  
*gūḍhaṃ brahmarṣisarvasvaṃ na deyaṃ kasyacittvayā \|\| 16 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

16\. O goddess, listen to the esoteric importance of the creation of Kardamāla. It is mysterious, and in exclusive possession of Brāhmaṇa-sages. It should not be given to anybody by you.

## \|\| 1.354.17-18 \|\|

*pūrvamekārṇave ghore naṣṭe sthāvarajaṃgame \|*  
*candrārkapavane naṣṭe jyotiṣi pralayaṃ gate \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ekārṇavaṃ jagadidaṃ brahmāpaśyadaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tasminvasumatī magnā pātālatalamāgatā \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Formerly it was a terrible (one) expanse of water (sea) only, where mobiles and immobiles were destroyed. Then the Moon, Sun and Wind disappeared and heavenly luminaries merged (became destroyed). God Brahma saw that the whole world had become one expanse of water and the Earth sank down and reached the bottom of Pātāla.

(The Boar form of Viṣṇu is identified with sacrifice. The sacrifice in the form of a Boar extricated the Earth out of Pātāla.)

## \|\| 1.354.19 \|\|

*tato yajñavarāho'sau kṛtvā yajñamayaṃ vapuḥ \|*  
*uddadhāra mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ daṃṣṭrāgreṇa varānane \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Then that Boar transformed his body as sacrifice and lifted up the entire Earth with the tip of his (protruding) tusk, O lady of excellent countenance.

(Sacrifice-Boar Identification)

## \|\| 1.354.20 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*vedapādo yūpadaṃṣṭraḥ kratudaṃtaḥsrucīmukhaḥ \|*  
*agnijihvo darbharomā brahmaśīrṣā mahātapāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He had the (four) Vedas as the feet; the sacrificial post was the (protruding) tusk; the Kratu was his teeth, the mouth was the ladle (for offering oblations); the fire was his tongue and the Darbha grass the hair (on its body); his head was Brahmā of great penance.

## \|\| 1.354.21 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*ahorātrekṣaṇaparo vedāṃgaśrutibhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*ājyanāsaḥ sruvatuḍaḥ sāmaghoṣasvano mahān \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Day and night were the vigilant eyes (of the Boar); Vedāṅgas were ear-ornaments; clarified butter for oblations was his nose; Sruva (a kind of spoon in sacrifice) was his mouth; his voice was the loud chanting of Sāmaveda.

## \|\| 1.354.22 \|\|

*prāgvaṃśakāyo dyutimānmātrādīkṣābhirāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*dakṣiṇā hṛdayo yogī mahāsatramaho mahān \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Prāg-vaṃśa was his body. The lustrous one was covered with Mātrā-dīkṣā. Dakṣiṇā (sacrificial fee) was his heart. The great Yogī has the refulgence of a great sacrifice (extending over a long duration).

## \|\| 1.354.23 \|\|

*upākarmoṣṭharucakaḥ pravargyāvartabhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*nānācchandogatipatho brahmoktakramavikramaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Upākarma (commencement of sacrifice by reading the Vedas) was the golden ornament and Pravargya (a ceremony introductory to a Soma sacrifice) was an ornament of jewels. His path of going consisted of various Chandas (Vedic metres) and his course (of going) was as spoken (laid down by Brahmā).

## \|\| 1.354.24 \|\|

*bhūtvā yajñavarāho'sāvuddadhāra mahīṃ tataḥ \|*  
*tasyoddhṛtavataḥ pṛthvīṃ daṃṣṭrāgraṃ nirgataṃ bahiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. After becoming Yajña-Varāha (sacrifice in the form of a boar) he lifted the Earth. While he was extricating the Earth upwards a tip of his teeth fell out.
