## \|\| 1.354.25 \|\|

*tasminprābhāsike kṣetre karddamena vilepitam \|*  
*taddaṃṣṭrāgraṃ yato devi karddamālaṃ tataḥ smṛtam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. That tip of the tooth smeared with mud fell in the Prābhāsika Kṣetra. Hence, O Devī, it is remembered as Kardamāla.

## \|\| 1.354.26 \|\|

*daṇḍodbhedaṃ mahākuṇḍaṃ yatra daṃṣṭrā susaṃsthitā \|*  
*taddaṃṣṭrayoddhṛtaṃ toyaṃ koṭigaṃgābhiṣekavat \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Daṇḍodbheda is a great Kuṇḍa where the fangs are securely deposited. The water that is brought upwards by that fang is like ten million Gaṅgā rivers (for ablutions).

## \|\| 1.354.27 \|\|

*tatra gavyūti mātraṃ tu viṣṇukṣetraṃ sanātanam \|*  
*deśāṃtaraṃ gatā ye ca daṇḍodbhede mriyaṃti vai \|*  
*yāvatkalpasahasrāṇi viṣṇulokaṃ vrajaṃti te \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. There the ancient Viṣṇu Kṣetra is of the extent of a Gavyūti. Those who have gone to another country but die in Daṇḍodbheda go to the region of Viṣṇu for a period of a thousand Kalpas.

## \|\| 1.354.28 \|\|

*yastu paśyenmahādevi kardamāle tu sūkaram \|*  
*koṭihiṃsāyuto vāpi sa prāpsyati parāṃ gatim \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O great goddess, he who sees the Boar (Viṣṇu) in Kardamāla attains the supreme region although he may be burdened with ten million Hiṃsās (injury to living beings).

## \|\| 1.354.29-31 \|\|

*daśajanmakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ naśyettaddarśanātpriye \|*  
*janmāntarasahasreṣu yatkṛtaṃ pāpasaṃcayam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*kardamāle tu vārāhaṃ dṛṣṭvā tannāśameṣyati \|*  
*hemakoṭisahasrāṇi gavāṃ koṭiśatāni ca \|\| 30 \|\|*

*dattvā yallabhate puṇyaṃ sakṛdvārāhadarśanāt \|*  
*kalau yuge mahāraudre prāṇināṃ ca bhayāvahe \|*  
*nānyatra jāyate muktirmuktvā kṣetraṃ tu saukaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

29a. O dear one, by his very sight, sins committed during ten births perish.

29b-30a. Whatever sins have been perpetrated during a thousand previous births get instantly perished as soon as the Boar (Viṣṇu) is viewed.

30b-31a. The merit that accrues by gifting thousands of crores of gold (coins) and by gifting away hundred of crores of cows, is obtained by viewing the Boar but once only.

31bc. No salvation can be obtained in this very terrible Kali Age anywhere except at this Kṣetra of Varāha.

## \|\| 1.354.32 \|\|

*etatsārataraṃ devi proktamuddeśatastava \|*  
*karddamālasya māhātmyaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O goddess, this brief statement (of the greatness of the Kṣetra) which destroys all sins is made for your sake.

## Chapter 355 - Greatness of Gupteśvara (Gupta-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.355.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi devagupteśvaraṃ priye \|*  
*tatra paścimavāyavye yatra somo'karottapaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. O great goddess, thereafter, one should go to Lord Gupteśvara to the west of the north-west (of Kardamāla) where Soma performed a great penance.

## \|\| 1.355.2 \|\|

*gupto bhūtvā kuṣṭharogāllajjayādhomukhaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu prabhāsakṣetra uttame \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. He became invisible. He stayed hanging his head down out of shame for the disease of leprosy (afflicting him). In the excellent holy place of Prabhāsa (he performed penance) for one thousand years of Devas.

## \|\| 1.355.3 \|\|

*tataḥ pratyakṣatāṃ yātaḥ sarvadevapatiḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭo babhūva caṃdrasya kṣayanāśaṃ tathā'karot \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Then Śiva, the Lord of all Devas, appeared to him. He became satisfied and healed pulmonary consumption of the Moon-god.

## \|\| 1.355.4 \|\|

*kṣayarogavinirmuktastato'bhūnmṛgalāṃchanaḥ \|*  
*pratiṣṭhāpya mahāliṃgaṃ surāsuranamaskṛtam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Then the Deer-marked One (the Moon-god) became completely free from the disease of pulmonary consumption. He installed a great Liṅga bowed to by Suras and Asuras.

## \|\| 1.355.5 \|\|

*guptastepe tapo yasmāttasmādgupteśvaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*sarvakuṣṭhaharo devo darśanātsparśanādapi \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He is remembered as Gupteśvara as he performed the penance in concealment. The god removes leprosy of all sorts when viewed and touched (by a devotee).

## \|\| 1.355.6 \|\|

*somavāre viśeṣeṇa yastalliṃgaṃ prapūjayet \|*  
*tasyānvaye'pi deveśi kuṣṭhī kaścinna jāyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He who worships that Liṅga especially on Mondays, no leper is born in his family at any time.

## Chapter 356 - Greatness of Bahusuvarṇakeśvara (Bahusuvarṇaka-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.356.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi devaṃ bahusuvarṇakam \|*  
*hiraṇyāpūrvadigbhāge sthāne bahusuvarṇake \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Thereafter, O great goddess, one should go to god Bahusuvarṇaka in the place called Bahusuvarṇaka to the east of Hiraṇī.

## \|\| 1.356.2 \|\|

*dharmaputreṇa yatraiva kṛto yajñaḥ suduṣkaraḥ \|*  
*nāmnā bahusuvarṇeti sthāpya liṃgaṃ mahāprabham \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. There a very difficult sacrifice was performed by Dharmaputra after installing a very refulgent Liṅga called Bahusuvarṇa.

## \|\| 1.356.3 \|\|

*sarvakratūnāṃ phaladaṃ nāmnā sarveśvaraṃ viduḥ \|*  
*tatraiva saṃsthitaṃ liṃgaṃ pūrṇaṃ sārasvatairjalaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. It grants the benefits of all Kratus. It is known by the name Sarveśvara. There itself is situated a Liṅga filled (bathed) with the waters of Sarasvatī.

## \|\| 1.356.4 \|\|

*snātvā tatra varārohe piṇḍadānaṃ dadāti yaḥ \|*  
*kulakoṭiṃ samuddhṛtya rudraloke mahīyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O beautiful lady, he who takes his bath and offers rice-balls there, redeems ten million members of his family and is praised in the region of Rudra.

## \|\| 1.356.5 \|\|

*yastaṃ pūja yate bhaktyā gandhapuṣpairvidhānataḥ \|*  
*koṭipūjāphalaṃ tasya tathetyāha sadāśivaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Sadāśiva has declared that he who devoutly worships it (the Liṅga) with fragrant paste and flowers as per procedure, gets the benefit of (performance of) ten million worships.

## Chapter 357 - Greatness of Śṛṅgeśvara (Śṛṅga-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.357.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi śṛṃgeśvaramanuttamam \|*  
*śukasthānasya sānnidhye sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Thereafter, O great goddess, one should go to the excellent Śṛṅgeśvara in the vicinity of Śukra-Sthāna. It is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.357.2 \|\|

*snātvā tatraiva vidhivacchṛṃgeśaṃ pūjayennaraḥ \|*  
*muktaḥ syātpātakaiḥ sarvairṛṣyaśṛṃgo yathā purā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. After taking bath there, a man should worship Śṛṅgeśa as per procedure. He becomes absolved of all sins as in the case of Ṛṣyaśṛṅga formerly.

## Chapter 358 - Greatness of Koṭīśvara (Koṭi-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.358.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tasmādīśānadigbhāge tatkoṭinagaraṃ smṛtam \|*  
*tasya dakṣiṇadigbhāge sthitaṃ yojanamātrakam \|*  
*koṭīśvaraṃ mahāliṃgaṃ koṭiyajñaphalapradam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. In the north-eastern region (a place called) Koṭinagara is remembered to be on the southern side thereof. At a distance of a Yojana is situated a great Liṅga called Koṭīśvara which grants the benefit of ten million sacrifices.

## \|\| 1.358.2 \|\|

*snātvā tatra vidhānena yastalliṃgaṃ prapūjayet \|*  
*sa muktaḥ pātakaiḥ sarvaiḥ koṭiyajñaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. He who, after taking his bath there, worships the Liṅga with due elaborate procedures becomes absolved of all sins and gets the benefit of one crore sacrifices.

## Chapter 359 - Greatness of Nārāyaṇa Tīrtha

## \|\| 1.359.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi tīrthaṃ nārāyaṇābhidham \|*  
*tasyaiveśānadigbhāge vāpī śāṃḍilyakīrtitā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Then, O great goddess, one should go to the Tīrtha called Nārāyaṇa. In the north-eastern region is a well well-known as Śāṇḍilya (Tīrtha).

## \|\| 1.359.2 \|\|

*snātvā tatraiva vidhivacchāṃḍilyaṃ yaḥ prapūjayet \|*  
*ṛṣipaṃcamyāṃ vidhinā nārī caiva pativratā \|*  
*spṛṣṭvāspṛṣṭvā vimucyeta rajodoṣabhayāddhruvam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. After taking bath therein, one should worship as per procedure Śāṇḍilya on the Ṛṣipañcamī day. Also a chaste woman who worships it (on that day) is definitely absolved of the sin resulting from the violation of restrictions pertaining to menstruation, whether touching it or not.

## Chapter 360 - Greatness of Śṛṅgāreśvara (Śṛṅgāra-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.360.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi sthānaṃ śṛṃgasaro'bhidham \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Then, O great goddess, one should go to the place called Śṛṅgasaras.

## \|\| 1.360.2 \|\|

*śṛṃgāreśvaranāmā ca tatra devaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*śṛṅgāraṃ vidhivaccakre yatra gopīyuto hariḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. A god called Śṛṅgāreśvara is installed there. There Hari along with a Gopī (a cowherd lass) performed Śṛṅgāra as per procedure.

## \|\| 1.360.3 \|\|

*śṛṅgāreśvaranāmā ca tena pāpaughanāśanaḥ \|*  
*pūjayedyo vidhānena tatra sthāne sthitaṃ bhavam \|*  
*dāridryaduḥkhasaṃyukto na sa bhūyādbhave kvacit \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He is thereby (known as) Śṛṅgāreśvara. He destroys floods of sins. He who worships with due procedure, Bhava (Śiva) who is situated at that place, shall never be affected by miseries and poverty in Saṃsāra.

## Chapter 361 - Greatness of Mārkaṇḍeśvara (Mārkaṇḍa-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.361.1-2 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi hiraṇyātaṭasaṃsthitam \|*  
*ghaṭikāsthānamiti ca yatra siddhaḥ purā ṛṣiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*nāḍyaikayā mṛkaṇḍastu dhyānayogādvarānane \|*  
*tatraiva sthāpitaṃ liṃgaṃ mārkaṃḍeśvaranāmataḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpopaśamanaṃ darśanātpūjanādapi \|\| 2 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1-2. Thereafter, O goddess, one should go to Ghaṭikā-sthāna situated on the bank of Hiraṇyā. There formerly a sage (Mṛkaṇḍa) became Siddha within one Ghaṭi (24 minutes) by his Yoga of concentration.

He installed the Liṅga. It is Mārkaṇḍeśvara by name. By viewing and worshipping it quells all sins.

## Chapter 362 - Koṭihrada-Maṇḍūkeśvara

## \|\| 1.362.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi maṇḍūkeśvaramityapi \|*  
*māṃḍūkyāyananāmnā vai liṃgaṃ tatra pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Then, O great goddess, one should go to Maṇḍūkeśvara. A Liṅga called Māṇḍukyāyana was installed there.

## \|\| 1.362.2 \|\|

*tatra koṭihrado devi tathā koṭīśvaraḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*tatra mātṛgaṇaścaiva sthitaḥ kāmaphalapradaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. There is a pool called Koṭihrada, O goddess; there Śiva is Koṭīśvara. There the group of Mātṛs who grant desired objects is settled.

## \|\| 1.362.3 \|\|

*snātvā koṭi hrade tīrthe talliṃgaṃ yaḥ prapūjayet \|*  
*mātṝstatraiva saṃpūjya duḥkhaśokādvimucyate \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He who, after taking bath in Koṭi Tīrtha, elaborately worships the Liṅga and adores the Mātṛs there, becomes relieved of misery and affliction.

## \|\| 1.362.4 \|\|

*tasmātpūrveṇa deveśi yojanaikena nirmalam \|*  
*tritakūpeti vikhyātaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ devi tīrthānāṃ yattatraiva vyavasthitiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O Deveśī, to the east of it, at a distance of a Yojana, there is a well of translucent waters known as Trita. It destroys all sins. There is the residence of all Tīrthas therein.

## Chapter 363 - Greatness of Ekādaśa-Rudra-Liṅga

## \|\| 1.363.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi goṣpadasyottare sthitam \|*  
*gavyūtidvitayenaiva valāya iti viśrutam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Thereafter, O great goddess, one should go to what is known as Valāya situated to the north of Goṣpada at a distance of two Gavyūtis.

## \|\| 1.363.2 \|\|

*tatraikādaśarudrāṇāṃ sthānaliṃgānyapi priye \|*  
*ajaikapādahirbudhnyaḥ saṃtītyādīni nāmataḥ \|*  
*pūjayettāni vidhivanmucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. There are the Sthāna-liṅgas of eleven Rudras. They are named Ajaikapāda, Ahirbudhnya etc. Those should be worshipped as per procedure. Thereby one is absolved of all sins.

## Chapter 364 - Greatness of Gharghara-Hrada and Kandeśvara

## \|\| 1.364.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi hiraṇyātaṭasaṃsthitam \|*  
*sthānaṃ tuṇḍapuraṃnāma yatrāsau ghargharo hradaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Thereafter, O great goddess, one should go to the place called Tuṇḍapura situated on the banks of Hiraṇyā. There is the pool (Hrada) called Gharghara.

## \|\| 1.364.2 \|\|

*tatra kandeśvaro devo yatra baddhā jaṭā mayā \|*  
*tatra snātvā naraḥ samyaktṃ devaṃ yaḥ prapūjayet \|*  
*sa muktaḥ pātakairghoraiḥ prāpnuyācchāsanaṃ śubham \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. There is god Kandeśvara, where I tied up my matted hair.

He, who, taking his bath properly, worships that god becomes absolved of terrible sins and attains the auspicious order (protection) of Śiva.

## Chapter 365 - Greatness of Saṃvarteśvara (Saṃvarta-īśvara)

## \|\| 1.365.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi saṃvarteśvaramuttamam \|*  
*indreśvarātpaścimataḥ pūrvataścārkabhāskarāta \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Then, O great goddess, one should go to Saṃvarteśvara to the west of Indreśvara and to the east of Arka-Bhāskara.

## \|\| 1.365.2 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā tu mahādevaṃ snātvā puṣkariṇījale \|*  
*daśānāmaśvamedhānāṃ phalamāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. After taking bath in the waters of the well and viewing Mahādeva, a man gets the benefit of (performing) ten horse-sacrifices.

## Chapter 366 - Greatness of Miscellaneous Sthāna-Liṅgas

## \|\| 1.366.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi hiraṇyāyāśca uttare \|*  
*siddhisthānāni divyāni yatra siddhā maharṣayaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. Thereafter, O great goddess, one should go to the north of Hiraṇyā to the celestial place granting Siddhis (miraculous powers) where Siddhas are great sages.

## \|\| 1.366.2 \|\|

*tatra liṃgānyanekāni śakyaṃte kathituṃ na hi \|*  
*sāgraṃ śataṃ punastatra liṃgānāṃ pravaraṃ smṛtam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. There are innumerable Liṅgas which are impossible to describe (or count). Out of them there are some more than hundred Liṅgas which are remembered as very excellent.

## \|\| 1.366.3 \|\|

*vajriṇyāstu taṭe devi liṃgānyekonaviṃśatiḥ \|*  
*nyaṃkumatyāstaṭe devi sahasraṃ dviśatādhikam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On the bank of Vajriṇī there are nineteen Liṅgas. On the bank of Nyaṅkumatī there are one thousand two hundred Liṅgas.

## \|\| 1.366.4 \|\|

*prādhānyena varārohe pūrve svāyaṃbhuveṃ'tare \|*  
*kapilāyāstaṭedevi liṃgānāṃ ṣaṣṭiruttamā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O beautiful lady, in the Svāyaṃbhuva Manvantara there were mainly sixty excellent Liṅgas on the bank of Kapilā.

## \|\| 1.366.5 \|\|

*sarasvatyāṃ punastatra liṃgasaṃkhyā na vidyate \|*  
*evaṃ paṃcamukhā devi liṃgamālā vibhūṣitā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The number of Liṅgas on the bank of Sarasvatī cannot be told (counted). Thus the garland of Liṅgas of five faces has been adorned.

## \|\| 1.366.6 \|\|

*prabhāse kathitā devi paṃcasrotāḥ sarasvatī \|*  
*yasyāḥ pravāhaiḥ saṃbhinnaṃ kṣetraṃ dvādaśayojanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. It is stated that river Sarasvatī is of five channels in the Prabhāsa Kṣetra. By her, the Kṣetra extending to twelve Yojanas is divided.

## \|\| 1.366.7 \|\|

*tatra vāpīṣu kūpeṣu yatra tatrodbhavaṃ jalam \|*  
*sārasvataṃ tu tajjñeyaṃ te dhanyā ye pibaṃti tat \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The water that comes up in the wells (big and small) there is the water of Sarasvatī. Blessed are those who drink it.

## \|\| 1.366.8 \|\|

*yatratatra naraḥ snātvā samyakchraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*sārasvatasnānaphalaṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Wherever one takes bath devoutly (in that region) one gets the benefit of having ablutions in Sarasvatī. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.366.9 \|\|

*yatproktaṃ sparśaliṃgaṃ tu śrīsomeśeti viśrutam \|*  
*prabhāsakṣetraliṃgānāṃ kalā tasyaiva śāṃkarī \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. What is called Sparśa-Liṅga (a Liṅga to be touched by hand) is well-known as Someśa. The digit of the Liṅgas in the Prabhāsa Kṣetra pertains to Śaṅkara.

## \|\| 1.366.10 \|\|

*yadvā tadvā pūjayitvā liṃgaṃ kṣetrasya madhyagam \|*  
*śrīsomeśamiti jñātvā someśaḥ pūjito bhavet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. If at any place a Liṅga at the centre of the Kṣetra is worshipped knowing (or in the belief) that it is Someśa, Lord Someśa becomes worshipped.

:: End of Prabhāsa Kṣetra Māhātmya ::

## Section 2 - Vastrāpatha-kṣetra-māhātmya

## Chapter 1 - The Greatness of Dāmodara

## \|\| 2.1.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*atha te saṃpravakṣyāmi kṣetragarbhaṃ mahodayam \|*  
*tadvastrāpathamāhātmyaṃ yatra raivatako giriḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Obeisance to Śrī Gaṇeśa! Obeisance to Śrī Sarasvatī! Now begins Section II named The Greatness of the Vastrāpathakṣetra of Book Seven entitled Prabhāsa Khaṇḍa of the Skanda Purāṇa.

The Lord said:

1\. I shall now narrate to you the great prosperity due to a sacred place viz. the greatness of the (holy place) called Vastrāpatha where stands the mountain Raivataka.

## \|\| 2.1.2 \|\|

*dāmodaraṃ raivatake bhavaṃ vastrāpathe tathā \|*  
*etadraivatakaṃ kṣetraṃ vastrāpathamiti smṛtam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. (They worship) Dāmodara on the Raivataka (mountain) and Bhava (i.e. Śiva) at Vastrāpatha. This holy place on the Raivataka (mountain) is known as Vastrāpatha.

## \|\| 2.1.3 \|\|

*suvarṇarevā yatrasthā nadī pātakanāśanī \|*  
*yatra sākṣātsthitaḥ kṛṣṇo dāmodara iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The river there is Suvarṇarekhā, the destroyer of sins. There Kṛṣṇa Dāmodara actually stays.

## \|\| 2.1.4 \|\|

*yatra sthitaṃ mṛgīkuṇḍaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|*  
*sakṛcchrāddhe kṛte yatra kalpakoṭisahasrakam \|*  
*pitṝṇāṃ jāyate tṛptirapunarbhavakāṃkṣiṇī \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. There is a lake called Mṛgīkuṇḍa, which destroys great sins, and where, if a Śrāddha is performed (even) once, such a satisfaction is caused in the (minds of) the dead ancestors, that in them there remains no desire for rebirth.

## \|\| 2.1.5 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*bhagavanvistarādbrūhi dāmodaramahodayam \|*  
*kṣetragarbhasya māhātmyaṃ karṇikārūpasaṃsthitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

The Goddess said:

5\. O Lord, tell me in detail the great prosperity of Dāmodara (and) the greatness in the holy place remaining in the form of Karṇikā.

## \|\| 2.1.6 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi dāmodarahariṃ prati \|*  
*itihāsaṃ purākhyātamṛṣibhiḥ kalpavāsibhiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

The Lord said:

6\. O Goddess, listen. I shall tell (you) the history of Dāmodara Han, formerly narrated by the sages, living in the Kalpa.

## \|\| 2.1.7-8 \|\|

*gaṃgātīre śubhe ramye puṇye janapadākule \|*  
*ṛṣibhiḥ sevite nityaṃ svargamārgaprade dhruvam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tatra jñānavido viprā yajaṃti vividhairmakhaiḥ \|*  
*ṛṣayaḥ sāṃkhyayogena dānenaivetare janāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. On the auspicious, charming, meritorious bank of Gaṅgā, full of people, always inhabited by sages, and certainly leading in the path of heaven, the learned Brāhmaṇas perform various kinds of sacrifices. The sages worship in ways laid down in Sāṃkhya and yoga and other people with gifts only.

## \|\| 2.1.9 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrā svargamabhīpsavaḥ \|*  
*sevaṃte tajjalaṃ divyaṃ devānāmapi durlabham \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras, desiring (a place in) Heaven everyday resort to her water, difficult (to be obtained) even by gods.

## \|\| 2.1.10 \|\|

*tatra rājā gajonāma balī sarvajanādhipaḥ \|*  
*gaṃgājalābhiṣekārthaṃ tyakvā rājyaṃ jagāma ha \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A powerful king, lord of all people and Gaja by name, abandoned his kingdom, and came there for a bath in Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 2.1.11 \|\|

*bhāryā tasya satī sādhvī putriṇī rūpasaṃyutā \|*  
*sā'pyayātsaha tenaiva bhartrā vai bhartṛvatsalā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. His wife, a chaste, beautiful, virtuous wife, having sons, and fondly loving her husband, came there with her husband himself.

## \|\| 2.1.12 \|\|

*saṃgatā nāma nāmnā ca dakṣā dākṣāyaṇī yathā \|*  
*evaṃ nivasatostatra varṣāṇāmayutaṃ gatam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Her name was Saṃgatā and was like Dākṣāyaṇī to Dakṣa. Living (there) like that they passed a myriad of years.

## \|\| 2.1.13-14 \|\|

*ājagāma ṛṣistatra bhadronāma mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*sahito bahubhirviprairjapahomaparāyaṇaiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tyaktvā saṃsāramārgaṃ tu svargamārgajigīṣavaḥ \|*  
*gaṃgāniṣevaṇaṃ kṛtvā sphoṭayitvā'tmajaṃ malam \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. A renowned sage named Bhadra, with many Brāhmaṇas, engaged in sacrifice. They had renounced the way of the world, and desired to conquer the path to Heaven after bathing in Gaṅgā and getting rid of their impurity.

## \|\| 2.1.15 \|\|

*jalaṃ dattvā tu bhūtebhyaḥ pūjayitvā janārddanam \|*  
*yāvadyāṃti nadītīra ṛṣayo bhadrakādayaḥ \|*  
*tāvatpaśyaṃti rājānaṃ gajaṃ varagajopamam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Just when, after having offered water to the spirits and having worshipped Janārdana, Bhadraka and others went to the river bank, they saw King Gaja, resembling an excellent elephant.

## \|\| 2.1.16 \|\|

*tenaiva dṛṣṭā munayo rājñā nihatakalmaṣāḥ \|*  
*saptarṣayo yathā svarge surarājena dhīmatā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The King (too) himself saw the sages with their sins destroyed as the intelligent King of gods would see the Seven Sages.

## \|\| 2.1.17-18 \|\|

*tamṛṣiṃ sa ca saṃprekṣya padāni daśa paṃca ca \|*  
*āgacchantvatra pūjārhā bhavato mama mandiram \|\| 17 \|\|*

*paśyaṃtu saṃgatāṃ sarve mama bhāryāṃ yaśasvinīm \|*  
*tasyāḥ pūjāṃ samādāya yo mārgo manasi sthitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Seeing the sage as having taken fifteen steps towards him he spoke to him: “O you deserving worship, (please) come to my abode. (Please) all of you together meet my glorious wife. After having accepted homage from her, O magnanimous and holy ones, desiring merits, you may go along the path you have in your mind.”

## \|\| 2.1.19 \|\|

*taṃ gacchadhvaṃ mahābhāgāḥ puṇyāḥ puṇyamabhīpsavaḥ \|*  
*evamuktāstu te rājñā ṛṣayaḥ kautukānvitāḥ \|*  
*ājagmurmaṃdiraṃ śubhraṃ puraṃdarapuropamam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Thus addressed by the King, the sages, full of delight, went to the King’s shining mansion, resembling the city of Indra.

## \|\| 2.1.20 \|\|

*āsanāni vicitrāṇi dattvā teṣāṃ manasvinī \|*  
*saṃgatā rājarājena sārddhamagre vyavasthitā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The wise lady, after offering them seats, accompanied by King Gaja, stood beside them.

## \|\| 2.1.21 \|\|

*kṛtvā karapuṭaṃ rājā ṛṣīṇāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām \|*  
*babhāṣe vacanaṃ rājā bhadro bhadraṃ susaṃgatam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Having folded his hands before the sages of meritorious deeds, the noble King (Gaja) spoke relevant words to Bhadra:

## \|\| 2.1.22-25 \|\|

*vasudhā vasusaṃpūrṇā maṃḍitā nagarī purī \|*  
*parvataiśca samudraiśca saridbhiśca sarovaraiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*grāmaiścatuṣpathairghorairgokulairākulīkṛtā \|*  
*nararatnairaśvaratnairgajaratnaistu saṃkulā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*dustyajā bhogabhoktṛṇāṃ paraṃ jñānamajānatām \|*  
*saṃsāre'tra mahāghore punarāvṛttikāriṇi \|\| 24 \|\|*

*pataṃti puruṣā bhadra patrāṇīva punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*kṛtena yena vipreṃdra svargaṃ prāpnoti nirmalam \|*  
*dānena tapasā caiva tattvamā cakṣva suvrata \|\| 25 \|\|*

22-25. “The earth is full of wealth, towns, cities that are decorated, full of mountains, seas, rivers and lakes, so also with villages, crossways, fearful herds of cows, jewels of men, and elephants. It is difficult to be abandoned by those who indulge in enjoyments and are ignorant of the highest knowledge. O Bhadra, into this very fearful worldly existence, causing rebirth, men fall repeatedly like leaves. O you best Brāhmaṇa of a good vow, please tell me about the spotless act of charity and austerities by doing which Heaven is obtained.”

## \|\| 2.1.26-27 \|\|

*bhadra uvāca \|*  
*tīrthāni toyapūrṇāni devāḥ pāṣāṇamṛnmayāḥ \|*  
*ātmasthaṃ ye na paśyaṃti te na paśyaṃti tatparam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*saṃti tīrthānyanekāni puṇyānyāyatanāni ca \|*  
*puṇyatoyā pavitraśca saritaḥ sāgarāstathā \|*  
*bahupuṇyapradā pṛthvī sthānesthāne padepade \|\| 27 \|\|*

Bhadra said:

26-27. Holy places are full of water; (idols of) deities are made of stone and clay. Rivers have holy water and are sacred. Seas' also are like that. At every place, at every step the earth is the giver of great merit.

## \|\| 2.1.28 \|\|

*yadyasti tava rājeṃdra jñānaṃ jñānavatāṃ vara \|*  
*viṣṇuṃ jiṣṇuṃ hṛṣīkeśaṃ śaṃkhinaṃ gadinaṃ tathā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. If O best King, O best one among the wise, if you have knowledge (you should worship the One, that is all-pervading (Viṣṇu), the conquerer, Hṛṣīkeśa, the Conch-holder, the Mace-holder;

## \|\| 2.1.29 \|\|

*caturbhujaṃ mahābāhuṃ prabhāse daityasūdanam \|*  
*vārāhaṃ vāmanaṃ caiva nārasiṃhaṃ balārjunam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. the One having four arms, the mighty-armed One, the Killer of the demon at Prabhāsa, Vārāha, Vāmana, Narasiṃha, Balārjuna;

## \|\| 2.1.30 \|\|

*rāmaṃ rāmaṃ ca rāmaṃ ca puruṣottamameva ca \|*  
*puṃḍarīkekṣaṇaṃ caiva gadāpāṇiṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. and Rāma, Rāma, (none else but) Rāma, the best among men, the lotus-eyed One, the One having a mace in His hand;

## \|\| 2.1.31 \|\|

*rāghavaṃ śakradamanaṃ goviṃdaṃ bahupuṇyadam \|*  
*jayaṃ ca bhūdharaṃ caiva devadevaṃ janārddanam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. so also Rāghava who subdued Śakra, Govinda, the Giver of much religious merit, Jaya, Bhūdhara (One that supports the Earth) and Janārdana, the God of gods;

## \|\| 2.1.32 \|\|

*surottamaṃ śrīdharaṃ ca hariṃ yogīśvaraṃ tathā \|*  
*kapileśaṃ bhūtanāthaṃ śvetadvīpapatiṃ harim \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. the best among gods, Śrīdhara and also Hari, the Lord of Yogins, Lord of Kapila, Lord of beings, the Lord of the Śveta Dvīpa, Hari.

## \|\| 2.1.33 \|\|

*badaryāśramavāsau ca naranārāyaṇau tathā \|*  
*padmanābhaṃ sunābhaṃ ca hayagrīvaṃ viśāṃ pate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. So also (pay homage to) Nara and Nārāyaṇa, living in the hermitage at Badari, (so also) Padmanābha, so also Sunābha, Hayagrīva, O King.

## \|\| 2.1.34 \|\|

*dvijanāthaṃ dharānāthaṃ khaḍgapāṇiṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*dāmodaraṃ jalāvāsaṃ sarvapāpaharaṃ harim \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. So also (pay homage to) Dvijanātha, Dharānātha, Khaḍgapāṇi (i.e. one having a sword in his hand), Dāmodara living in water, (i.e.) Hari, remover of all sins.

## \|\| 2.1.35 \|\|

*etānyeva hi sthānāni devadevasya cakriṇaḥ \|*  
*gacchate yatra tatraiva mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. These are just the places of (i.e. sacred to) the Lord of gods, the Holder of the Disc. One is freed from all his sins there only wherever one goes.

## \|\| 2.1.36 \|\|

*gaṃgā ca yamunā caiva tathā devī sarasvatī \|*  
*dṛṣadvatī gomatī ca tāpī kāveriṇī tathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Gaṅgā, Yamunā, so also the divine Sarasvatī, (and) Dṛṣadvatī, Gomatī, and Tāpī, so also Kāveriṇī,

## \|\| 2.1.37 \|\|

*narmadā śarmadā caiva nadī godāvarī tathā \|*  
*śatadruśca tathā viṃdhyā payoṣṇī varadā tathā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Narmadā, the giver of happiness; so also the river Godāvarī; similarly Śatadru, Vindhyā, and the boon-giving Payoṣṇī;

## \|\| 2.1.38 \|\|

*carmaṇvatī ca sarayūrgaṃḍakī caṃḍapāpahā \|*  
*caṃdrabhāgā vipāśā ca śoṇaścaiva punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. and Carmaṇvatī, Sarayū, Guṇḍakī, destroyer of great sins, Candrabhāgā, Vipāśā, and repeatedly Śoṇa:

## \|\| 2.1.39 \|\|

*etāścānyāśca bahavo himavatprabhavāḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*tāsu snāto naraḥ svargaṃ yāti pātakavarjitaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. These and others are many auspicious rivers rising from Himālaya. A man bathing in (any one of) them, becoming free from sins, goes to Heaven

## \|\| 2.1.40 \|\|

*vanāni naṃdanādīni parvatā maṃdarādayaḥ \|*  
*nāmoccāreṇa yeṣāṃ hi pāpaṃ yāti rasātale \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. There are forests like Nandana and mountains like Mandara, by uttering the names of which (ones’) sin goes down to hell.

## \|\| 2.1.41 \|\|

*gaja uvāca \|*  
*bhadraṃ hi bhāṣitaṃ bhadra ākhyānamamṛtopamam \|*  
*pṛcchāmi sarvadharmajña tvāmahaṃ kiṃcideva hi \|\| 41 \|\|*

Gaja said:

41\. You have well told the nectar-like tale. O you, who know the duties of all, I am going to ask you something.

## \|\| 2.1.42 \|\|

*yasminmāse dine yasmiṃstīrthe yasminkramānnaraiḥ \|*  
*akṣayaṃ sevyate svargastanmamācakṣva suvrata \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O you of a good vow, tell me serially in which month, on which day and at which holy place Heaven is eternally resorted to.

## \|\| 2.1.43 \|\|

*snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ svādhyāyo devatārcanam \|*  
*akṣayo yena vai svargastanme gaditumarhasi \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Please tell me (about) the bath, gifts, prayers to be muttered, sacrifice, self-recitation, worship of deities, by means of which I can get eternal (abode in) Heaven.

## \|\| 2.1.44 \|\|

*bhadra uvāca \|*  
*śrūyatāṃ rājaśārdūla kathāṃ kathayato mama \|*  
*yāṃ śrutvā mucyate pāpānnaro naravarottama \|\| 44 \|\|*

Bhadra said:

44\. O foremost one among kings, listen to the story I am telling, by hearing which a man is freed from sin, O best one among excellent men.

## \|\| 2.1.45 \|\|

*ṛṣīṇāṃ kathitaṃ pūrvaṃ nāradena mahātmanā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. This was formerly told by magnanimous Nārada.

## \|\| 2.1.46 \|\|

*evaṃ pṛṣṭaśca taiḥ sarvairnārado munisattamaḥ \|*  
*kathayāmāsa saṃhṛṣṭo meghadudubhinisvanaiḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. That best sage Nārada when asked like this by all (the sages), told it (as he was) delighted by (their) sounds like thunderings of clouds.

## \|\| 2.1.47 \|\|

*ramye himavataḥ pṛṣṭhe samavāye mayā śrutam \|*  
*tadahaṃ tava vakṣyāmi śrotukāmaṃ nararṣabha \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. I heard (what Nārada told) in the gatherings on the top of Himālaya. O best king, desirous of hearing that, I shall narrate it to you.

## \|\| 2.1.48 \|\|

*tīrthānyeva hi sarvāṇi punarāvarttakāni tu \|*  
*akṣayāṃllabhate lokāṃstattīrthaṃ kathayāmi te \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. All holy places just cause return to Saṃsāra. I shall tell you about that holy place by (visiting) which inexhaustible worlds are obtained.

## \|\| 2.1.49 \|\|

*mārgaśīrṣe kānyakubja uṣitvā rājasattama \|*  
*na śocati naro nārī svargaṃ yāti parāvaram \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O best king, a man or woman, having lived at Kānyakubja in (the month of) Mārgaśīrṣa, does not come to grief, and goes to the far end near Heaven.

## \|\| 2.1.50 \|\|

*pauṣasya paurṇamāsī yā yadi sā kriyate'rbude \|*  
*varṣāṇāmarbudaṃ svarge modate pitṛbhiḥ saha \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. If the (vow of the) Full-Moon night is observed on the Arbuda mountain (by a man), he enjoys in Heaven for a hundred million years along with his ancestors.

## \|\| 2.1.51 \|\|

*māghyāṃ yadi gayāśrāddhaṃ pitṝṇāṃ yacchate naraḥ \|*  
*trayāṇāmapi devānāṃ caturthaḥ sa prajāyate \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. If, on the Full-Moon day of Māgha a man offers Śrāddha at Gayā, He is born as fourth to even the three gods.

## \|\| 2.1.52 \|\|

*phālgunyāṃ himavatpṛṣṭhe vasannekāṃ niśāṃ naraḥ \|*  
*sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yatra devo janārddanaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. If a man lives for one night on the upper part of Himālaya on the Full-Moon night of Phālguna, he goes to the highest place where resides Janārdana.

## \|\| 2.1.53 \|\|

*caitryāṃ śrāddhaṃ prabhāse tu ye kurvaṃti manīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*na te marttyā bhavantīha kulajaiḥ saha sattamāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Those wise ones, who perform Śrāddha at (the holy place called) Prabhāsa, do not become mortals (i.e. are not subject to death) along with members of their families.

## \|\| 2.1.54 \|\|

*caturbhuje tu vaiśākhyāṃ ye kurvaṃti jalapriye \|*  
*tathāvaṃtyāṃ naraḥ kaścitsa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. O Dākṣāyaṇī, those who perform a Śrāddha at Caturbhuja or at Avanti on the Full-Moon night of Vaiśākha get the highest state.

## \|\| 2.1.55 \|\|

*jyaiṣṭhyāṃ jyeṣṭharkṣayuktāyāṃ śrāddhaṃ ca tritakūpake \|*  
*kuryuryugāni te trīṇi vasaṃti nākasadmani \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Those who perform a Śrāddha on the Full-Moon day of Jyeṣṭha connected with the Jyeṣṭha constellation, will live in health for three Yugas.

## \|\| 2.1.56 \|\|

*yo vrajeśavane nadyāṃ dināni nava paṃca ca \|*  
*tiṣṭhate ca naraḥ svargaṃ vaikuṇṭhamabhigacchati \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. A man who stays in the river in the Vrajeśa forest for fourteen days, resides in Heaven and goes to Vaikuṇṭha.

## \|\| 2.1.57 \|\|

*śrāvaṇasya tu māsasya pūrṇāyāṃ pūrvasāgare \|*  
*snānaṃ dānaṃ japaṃ śrāddhaṃ naraḥ kurvanna śocati \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. That man who bathes, gives gifts, mutters (names of deities), performs Śrāddha, on the (shore of) Eastern Ocean on the Full-Moon day of Śrāvaṇa;

## \|\| 2.1.58 \|\|

*tathā bhādrapade kṣetre prabhāse śaśibhūṣaṇam \|*  
*pūjayitvā naro liṃgaṃ devaliṃgī bhavettataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. similarly a man, on worshipping Śiva, his Liṅga, would become the devotee of that god.

## \|\| 2.1.59 \|\|

*āśvine caṃdrabhāgāyāṃ śrāddhaṃ snānaṃ karoti yaḥ \|*  
*sthānaṃ yugasahasrāṇāṃ kṛtaṃ tena triviṣṭape \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. He who performs Śrāddha and bathes in Candrabhāgā in Āśvina, has secured a seat in Heaven for thousands of Yugas.

## \|\| 2.1.60 \|\|

*aṣṭākṣaraiścaturbāhuṃ dhyāyaṃti munisattamāḥ \|*  
*bahunā'tra kimuktena gajāhaṃ pravadāmi te \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The best sages maditate \[meditate?\] upon (Brahmā) the four-armed one; what is the use of speaking more? O Gaja, I shall tell it to you.

## \|\| 2.1.61 \|\|

*dāmodarasamaṃ tīrthaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati \|*  
*māsānāṃ kārttikaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ kārttike bhīṣmapaṃcakam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. There is no, nor will there be, a holy place like Dāmodara. Among months Kārttika is the best, and in Kārttika the Bhīṣmapañcaka (the five days from the eleventh to the fifteenth day of the bright half of Kārttika, sacred to Bhīṣma).

## \|\| 2.1.62 \|\|

*tatrāpi dvādaśī śreṣṭhā rājandāmodare jale \|*  
*kimanyairbahubhistīrtheḥ ki kṣetraiḥ ki mahāvanaiḥ \|*  
*dāmodare naraḥ snātvā sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. There also Dvādaśī is the best in the water of Dāmodara, O King. What is the use of other many holy places, places of pilgrimage and great forests? By bathing in the Dāmodara lake, a man is freed from all sins.

## \|\| 2.1.63 \|\|

*gaja uvāca \|*  
*bhadra bhadraṃ tvayā proktaṃ rasāyanamivāparam \|*  
*bhūyo'haṃ śrotumicchāmi tīrthasyāsya mahāphalam \|\| 63 \|\|*

Gaja said:

63\. O good one, you have spoken well, as if it were another elixir. I again desire to hear the great fruit of this holy place.

## \|\| 2.1.64 \|\|

*ke deśāḥ kiṃ pramāṇaṃ tu kā nadī keḥ ca parvatāḥ \|*  
*janā vasaṃti ke tatra ṛṣayaḥ ke tapasvinaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Which countries, and of what size, are there? Which is the river? Which are the mountains? Which people, which sages and which ascetics reside there?

## \|\| 2.1.65 \|\|

*bhadra uvāca \|*  
*pṛthivī vasusaṃpūrṇā sāgareṇa tu veṣṭitā \|*  
*maṃḍitā nagarairgrāmaiḥ suraiḥ parapuraṃjaya \|\| 65 \|\|*

Bhadra said:

65\. The earth is full of wealth; but is surrounded by the ocean. O you who conquer the cities of your enemies, it is adorned with cities, towns and villages,

## \|\| 2.1.66 \|\|

*vārāṇasī prabhāsaṃ ca saṃgamaṃ sitakṛṣṇayoḥ \|*  
*evaṃ sārāṇi tīrthāni yasmānmṛtyuharāṇi ca \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Vārāṇasī, and Prabhāsa, the confluence of the white and black (rivers). Thus the holy places are excellent since they avert death.

## \|\| 2.1.67 \|\|

*dāmodareti ye nūnaṃ smaraṃto yatra tatra hi \|*  
*te vasaṃti harergehaṃ na saraṃti kadācana \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Those, who indeed recollect (the name of) Dāmodara, and live anywhere, live in Hari’s house, and never move (from it).

## \|\| 2.1.68 \|\|

*somanāthasya sānnidhya udayanto girirmahān \|*  
*tasya paścimabhāge tu raivataka iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. In the vicinity of Somanātha appears the great mountain. In its western part is (the mountain) known as Raivataka.

## \|\| 2.1.69 \|\|

*vāhinī vahate tatra nadī kāṃcanaśekharāt \|*  
*dhātavastatra te raktāḥ śvetā nīlāstathā'sitāḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The river Vāhinī flows there from “the peak” of Kāñcana. There are red, white, blue and black minerals.

## \|\| 2.1.70 \|\|

*pāṣāṇāḥ kuñjarākārāścānye sairibhasannibhāḥ \|*  
*caṇakākṛtayaścānye anye gokṣurakaprabhāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. There are (some) stones of the size of elephants, and others resemble buffalos. Others have shape like grams; still others have the splendour of the hoofs of cows.

## \|\| 2.1.71 \|\|

*vṛkṣā vallyaśca gulmāśca saṃtānāḥ saṃtyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ tatkāṃcanamayaṃ mūlaṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ dalam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. There are in large numbers, trees, bushes, creepers and Santāna trees (as in paradise). Everything there—root, flower, fruit, petal—is golden.

## \|\| 2.1.72 \|\|

*na hi paśyati pāpātmā muktaḥ pāpena paśyati \|*  
*sevyate sa girirnityaṃ dhātuvādaparairnaraiḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. A sinner does not (i.e. is not able to) see it. One freed from sin sees it. The mountain is everyday resorted to by men intent on (looking for) minerals;

## \|\| 2.1.73 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaiḥ kṣatriyairvaiśyaiḥ śūdraiḥ śūdrānugairbahiḥ \|*  
*pakṣiṇastatra bahavaḥ śivāśivagirastadā \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. (so also) by Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras and followers of Śūdras, externally. There are also many birds of auspicious and inauspicious notes.

## \|\| 2.1.74 \|\|

*haṃsasārasacakrāhvāḥ śukakokilabarhiṇaḥ \|*  
*mṛgāśca vānarendrāśca haṃsā vyāghrāstathaiva ca \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. There are birds like swans, cranes, ruddy geese, parrots, cuckoos and peacocks, deer, mighty monkeys; so also swans and tigers.

## \|\| 2.1.75 \|\|

*tattīrthasya prabhāvena na duṣṭānyācaraṃti te \|*  
*kālena mṛtyumāyāṃti paśupakṣisarīsṛpāḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Due to the power of that holy place they do not act in an evil manner. The beasts, birds and serpents meet with death at the (proper) time.

## \|\| 2.1.76 \|\|

*sarve vimānamārūḍhā gacchanti harimandiram \|*  
*vāyunā pātitaṃ yatra patrapuṣpaphalādikam \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. All, getting into an aeroplane, go to Viṣṇu’s abode. There a leaf, a flower, a fruit etc. are caused to fall by the wind (only).

## \|\| 2.1.77 \|\|

*tasyā nadyā jalaṃ spṛṣṭvā sarvaṃ vai muktimāpnute \|*  
*sā nadī pṛthivīṃ bhittvā pātālādāgatā nṛpa \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Every (object) gets liberated by touching the water of that river. O King, that river has come up cleaving the earth from the last of the seven regions under the earth.

## \|\| 2.1.78 \|\|

*pūrvaṃ pannagarājastu tena mārgeṇa cāgataḥ \|*  
*snātuṃ dāmodare tīrthe yamamṛtyupraghātini \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Formerly the King of serpents arrived along that path to bathe in the holy place Dāmodara which destroys birth and death.

## \|\| 2.1.79 \|\|

*svargādāgatya candro'pi yaṣṭuṃ yajñaṃ supuṣkalam \|*  
*yakṣmarogādvinirmukto gataḥ svargaṃ nirāmayaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Even the Moon had come from Heaven to perform a very rich sacrifice; he became free from the disease of consumption and (thus) being free from the disease went to Heaven.

## \|\| 2.1.80 \|\|

*balinā caiva dānāni dattānyāgatya kārtike \|*  
*hariścandreṇa vidhinā nalena nahuṣeṇa ca \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Having come (to this holy place) in Kārttika Bali also gave gifts; so also Hariścandra, Vidhi, Nala and Nahuṣa.

## \|\| 2.1.81 \|\|

*nābhāgenāṃbarīṣādyaiḥ kṛtaṃ karma suduṣkaram \|*  
*dattvā dānānyanekāni gajā gāvo hayā rathāḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Nābhāga, Ambarīṣa and others performed a very difficult task by giving away many gifts like elephants, cows, horses and chariots.

## \|\| 2.1.82 \|\|

*anaḍutkāṃcanā bhūmiṃ ratnāni vividhāni ca \|*  
*chatrāṇi vipramukhyebhyo yānāni caiva vāsasī \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. (They gave) bulls, gold, land, and gems of various kinds. (They gave) umbrellas, vehicles and pair(s) of garments.

## \|\| 2.1.83 \|\|

*annāni rasamiśrāṇi dattvā dāmodarāgrataḥ \|*  
*gatāste viṣṇu bhuvanaṃ nāgacchaṃti mahītale \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Having given foods mixed with jui\[?\]es \[juices?\] in front of Dāmodara, they have gone to Viṣṇu’s world, and will not return to the surface of the earth.

## \|\| 2.1.84 \|\|

*patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ toyaṃ tasmiṃstīrthe dadāti yaḥ \|*  
*dvijānāṃ bhaktisaṃyuktaḥ sa yāti jalaśāyinam \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. He who devotedly gives a leaf, a flower, a fruit, water to Brāhmaṇas in that sacred place, goes to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.1.85 \|\|

*prakṛtiṃ cāpi yo dadyānmuṣṭiṃ vātha kṣudhārthine \|*  
*vimānavaramārūḍhaḥ sa somaṃ prati gacchati \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. He who gives a handful or fistful (of corn) to one begging through hunger, gets into the best aeroplane and goes to Soma.

## \|\| 2.1.86 \|\|

*dāmodarāgrataḥ kṛtvā parvatānannasaṃbhavān \|*  
*pūjitānphalapuṣpaiśca dīpaṃ dadyātsavarttikam \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. One should prepare mountains of food and present them with fruits and flowers and lamps along with the wick.

## \|\| 2.1.87-88 \|\|

*avāpya duṣkaraṃ sthānaṃ kulānāṃ tārayecchatam \|*  
*caturaṃgulamātrepi datte dāmodarāgrataḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

*dāne yugasahasrāṇi svargaloke mahīyate \|*  
*mā gaccha himavatpṛṣṭhaṃ malayaṃ mā ca mandaram \|\| 88 \|\|*

87-88a. Having secured a place difficult to be obtained, he would emancipate a hundred families (i.e. generations of his family). If a gift of the measure of four fingers is given in front of Dāmodara, the giver rejoices for a thousand Yugas in Heaven.

88b. Do not go to the side of Himālaya, or do not go to Malaya or Mandara.

## \|\| 2.1.89-90 \|\|

*gaccha raivatakaṃ śailaṃ yatra dāmodaraḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā māsopavāsaṃ tu dvijo dāmodarāgrataḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

*na nivartati kālena dāmodarapuraṃ vrajet \|*  
*karotyanaśanaṃ yaśca naro nāryathavā punaḥ \|*  
*sarva lokānatikramya sa harergehamāpnuyāt \|\| 90 \|\|*

89-90. Go to the Raivataka mountain where Dāmodara dwells. A Brāhmaṇa who fasts for one month in front of Dāmodara, does not die, (but) would go to the city of Dāmodara. A man or a woman who observes a fast, would secure Hari’s (i.e. Viṣṇu’s) abode after going beyond all worlds.

## \|\| 2.1.91 \|\|

*vighnāni tatra tiṣṭhanti nityaṃ pañcaśatāni ca \|*  
*dharmavidhvaṃsakartṝṇi narastatra na gacchati \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Everyday there occur five hundred perils, which destroy piety. A man does not go there.

## \|\| 2.1.92 \|\|

*pradyumnabalaśaineyagadācakrādibhiḥ sadā \|*  
*śatalakṣapramāṇaistu sevyate sa girirmahān \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. That great mountain is always resorted to in the measure of hundreds of lakhs by Pradyumna, Bala, Śaineya, rṇaces, discs etc.

## \|\| 2.1.93-94 \|\|

*krīḍaṃti nāryasteṣāṃ hi nityaṃ dāmodarāgrataḥ \|*  
*sucandravadanā gauryaḥ śyāmāścaiva sumadhyamāḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

*nitaṃbinyaḥ sukeśāśca śubhrāḥ svāyatalocanāḥ \|*  
*sugaṃḍā lalitāścaiva sukakṣāḥ supayodharāḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

93-94. Their wives, of beautiful faces like the moon, fair and dark, of a beautiful waist and hips, of beautiful hair, fair and having broad eyes, of fine cheeks, and charming, having fine girdles, and beautiful breasts, everyday dance in front of Dāmodara.

## \|\| 2.1.95 \|\|

*śobhamānāḥ sujaṃghāśca supādāḥ sundarāṃgulīḥ \|*  
*rājaputryo girau tasminhasaṃti ca ramaṃti ca \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Princesses, looking charming, of beautiful shanks and feet, and fingers laugh and enjoy on that mountain.

## \|\| 2.1.96 \|\|

*kausuṃbhaṃ pādayugale kuṃkumaṃ pītakaṃcukam \|*  
*brāhmaṇībhyo dadantīha sparddhamānāḥ pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Competing (with one another), they separately give to (married) Brāhmaṇa ladies wild safflower (applying it) to their pairs of feet saffron and yellow cloth.

## \|\| 2.1.97 \|\|

*bhakṣyaṃ bhojyaṃ ca peyaṃ ca lehyaṃ coṣyaṃ ca picchilam \|*  
*tāṃbūlaṃ puṣpasaṃyuktaṃ kārtike harivāsare \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Eatables, food, drinks, things to be eaten by licking and by sucking, sauce mixed with rice-gruel, betel-leaf with flower are given on Viṣṇu’s day (i.e. the eleventh day of a lunar fortnight).

## \|\| 2.1.98 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tu revatīkuṃḍaṃ pradadyātphalamuttamam \|*  
*putriṇī ṛddhisaṃpannā subhagā jāyate satī \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. On seeing the pool of Revatī (a lady) should give excellent fruit. (Such) a chaste lady gets a son, prospers, and is fortunate.

## \|\| 2.1.99-100 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛtvā tu sā rātri nīyate nidrayā vinā \|*  
*vedaghoṣaiḥ supuṇyaistu bhāratākhyānavācanaiḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

*huṃkṛtaistalaśabdaiśca tālaśabdaiḥ punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*deśabhāṣāvibhāṣiṇyo rāmāmaṇḍalamadhyataḥ \|*  
*hāsyanṛtyasamāyuktā rājandāmodarāgrataḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

99-100. Having done so the night is passed without sleep (and) with very holy recitations of Vedas, and readings of the story of (Mahā-) Bhārata \[=Mahābhārata\] with hum-sounds, sounds made with palms, and clappings repeatedly. The ladies participating from the group of ladies speaking well the local tongue, laugh and dance in front of Dāmodara, O King.

## \|\| 2.1.101 \|\|

*pañcapāṣāṇakaṃ harmyaṃ yaḥ karoti śivālayam \|*  
*paṃcavarṣasahasrāṇi svarga loke mahīyate \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. He who fashions a palatial building of five stones as a temple of Śiva enjoys in Heaven for five thousand years.

## \|\| 2.1.102 \|\|

*daśapāṣāṇasaṃyuktaṃ kṛtvā dāmodarāgrataḥ \|*  
*daśavarṣasahasrāṇi svarge hallati mallati \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. Having fashioned (a palatial building) with ten stones in front of Dāmodara, one enjoys in Heaven for ten thousand years.

## \|\| 2.1.103 \|\|

*śatapāṣāṇakaṃ harmyaṃ yaḥ karoti mahannṛpa \|*  
*mandiraṃ sundaraṃ śubhraṃ sa yāti harimandiram \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. O King, he who fashions a big, beautiful, white building of a hundred stories, goes to Viṣṇu’s abode.

## \|\| 2.1.104 \|\|

*kṛtvā sāhasrikaṃ caityaṃ bahurūpasamanvitam \|*  
*sarvāṃllokānatikramya paraṃ brahmādhigacchati \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. One, having made a temple with a thousand stories having many graces, goes, after crossing all worlds, to the highest Brahman.

## \|\| 2.1.105 \|\|

*paṃcavarṇadhvajaṃ dadyāddāmodaragṛhopari \|*  
*taṃ tu pramāṇavarṣāṇi divyāni sa divaṃ vrajet \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. On the temple of Viṣṇu he should hoist a flag of five colours. He would go to (and live in) Heaven for as many divine years as the number of fibres (in the flag).

## \|\| 2.1.106 \|\|

*tasya gavyūtimātreṇa kṣetraṃ vastrāpathaṃ śubham \|*  
*yaddṛṣṭvā sarvapāpāni vilīyante bahūni ca \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. The Vastrāpatha holy place is a krośa in size. Seeing it all (or) many sins perish.

## \|\| 2.1.107-108 \|\|

*rājaṃstatpadamāyāti yadgatvā na nivarttate \|*  
*pūjayitvā bhavaṃ devaṃ bhavasaṃbhavanāśanam \|\| 107 \|\|*

*naro nārī nṛpaśreṣṭha śivaloke mahīyate \|*  
*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya bhadrasya ca subhāṣitam \|\| 108 \|\|*

107-108. O King, he reaches that position, going to which he never returns. O best king, a man or a woman, having worshipped god Bhava, destroyer of birth in the worldly existence, enjoys in the world of Śiva.

## \|\| 2.1.109-110 \|\|

*āgataḥ kārtikīṃ karttuṃ deve dāmodare tataḥ \|*  
*ṛgyajuḥsāmasaṃyuktairbrāhmaṇairbrahmavittamaiḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

*kṣatriyaiḥ kṣatradharmajñairvaiśyairdānaparāyaṇaiḥ \|*  
*saha śūdraiḥ samāyātastasmiṃstīrthe gajo nṛpaḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

109a. Having heard those good words of Bhadra, he then came to (the temple) of god Dāmodara for observing (the vow of) Kārttikī.

109b-110. Along with best Brāhmaṇas, (followers of) Ṛg, Yajus, Sāman (Vedas), Kṣatriyas knowing the duties of Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas intent on giving gifts, and Śūdras King Gaja came to that holy place.

## \|\| 2.1.111 \|\|

*dattvā dānānyanekāni hutvā havirhutāśane \|*  
*agniṣṭomādikānyajñānhayamedhādikānbahūn \|*  
*cakāra vidhivadrājā gajastatra samāhitaḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. Having given many gifts and having offered (oblations) into fire, King Gaja performed many sacrifices like Agniṣṭoma and many horse-sacrifices, according to the rules and with concentration.

## \|\| 2.1.112 \|\|

*tataśca nyavasattatra tapaḥ kartuṃ saharṣibhiḥ \|*  
*ūrddhvapādāḥ sthitā viprāḥ pītvā dhūmamadhomukhāḥ \|*  
*śuṣkapatrāśanāścānye anye vai phalabhojanāḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. Then to practise penance he remained there with sages. The Brāhmaṇas, with their faces downwards and inhaling smoke remained with their feet above. Some ate dry leaves; others ate fruits.

## \|\| 2.1.113 \|\|

*mūlāni cānye bhakṣaṃti anye vāryaṃśanā dvijāḥ \|*  
*ālokaṃti svamanye ca tathānye jalaśāyinaḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Some Brāhmaṇas ate roots (of trees); others ate (i.e. drank) water. Some looked at themselves; others lay in water.

## \|\| 2.1.114 \|\|

*pañcāgnisādhakāścānye śilācūrṇasya bhakṣakāḥ \|*  
*japaṃti cānye saṃśuddhā gāyatrīṃ vedamātaram \|*  
*sāvitrīṃ manasā cānye devīmanye sarasvatīm \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. Some resorted to (the vow of) ‘Pañcāgnisādhana’, others eat stone-powder. Others, having purified themselves mutter the Gāyatrī (hymn), the mother of the Vedas. Others mentally mutter the Sāvitrī (hymn); others (meditate upon) Sarasvatī.

## \|\| 2.1.115 \|\|

*sūktāni hi pavitrāṇi brahmaṇā nirmitāni ca \|*  
*anye'vasaṃstadā tatra dvādaśākṣaracintakāḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. The hymns produced by Brahmā are sacred. Others remained meditating upon (the hymn of) twelve letters.

## \|\| 2.1.116 \|\|

*ālokya sarvaśāstrāṇi vicārya ca punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*idameva suniṣpannaṃ dhyeyo nārāyaṇaḥ sadā \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. After viewing all scriptures and having thought repeatedly this (conclusion) has been arrived at: Nārāyaṇa should always be meditated upon.

## \|\| 2.1.117 \|\|

*ārādhitaḥ suduṣpāre bhave bhagavato vinā \|*  
*tathā nānyo mahādevātpatantaṃ yo'bhirakṣati \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. In the worldly existence, very difficult to cross, there is none else except the Lord, that can be propitiated. In the same way (there is none else) but Mahādeva, who protects one that is falling.

## \|\| 2.1.118 \|\|

*gatāgatāni vartaṃte caṃdrasūryādayo grahāḥ \|*  
*adyāpi na nivartaṃte dvādaśākṣaraciṃtakāḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. Planets like Moon and Sun come and go and relive. Even now those who meditate upon the (hymn of) twelve letters do not retire.

## \|\| 2.1.119 \|\|

*ye'kṣarā ṛṣayaścānye devalokajigīṣavaḥ \|*  
*prāpnuvaṃti tataḥ sthānaṃ dagdhabījaṃ ca tattathā \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. The unmoving sages and others desiring to go to the world of gods, reach that place with seed (of sins) burnt like that.

## \|\| 2.1.120 \|\|

*sakṛduccaritaṃ yena harirityakṣaradvayam \|*  
*baddhaḥ parikarastena mokṣāya gamanaṃ prati \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. One who has (even) once uttered the couple of letters ‘Hari’ has girt up ones’ loins for salvation.

## \|\| 2.1.121 \|\|

*ekabhaktaṃ tathā naktamayācyamuṣitaṃ tathā \|*  
*evamādīni cānyāni kṛtvā dāmodarāgrataḥ \|*  
*kṛtakṛtyā bhavaṃtīha yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. Having done (such deeds as) eating once (a day), eating at night only, or living without imploring others in front of Dāmodara they become blessed here till the universal destruction.

## \|\| 2.1.122 \|\|

*sa rājā ṛṣibhiḥ sārddhaṃ yāvattiṣṭhati tatra vai \|*  
*vimānāni sahasrāṇi tāvattatrāgatāni ca \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. Just when the king remained there with the sages, thousands of aeroplanes came there.

## \|\| 2.1.123 \|\|

*gaṃdharvāpsarastatra siddhacāraṇakinnarāḥ \|*  
*sarve vimānamārūḍhāḥ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. Hundreds and thousands Gandharvas, celestial nymphs, Siddhas, divine bards, Kinnaras—all boarded the plane.

## \|\| 2.1.124 \|\|

*sarvairjanapadaiḥ sārddha sa rājā bhāryayā saha \|*  
*gato vimānamārūḍho yattatpadamanāmayam \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. With all the people and his wife the king got into the plane and reached that sound place.

## \|\| 2.1.125 \|\|

*ya idaṃ paṭhate nityaṃ śṛṇuyādvā'pi mānavaḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ paraṃ brahmādhigacchati \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. One who recites or listens to this, being free from all sins, reaches the Highest Brahman.

## Chapter 2 - The Greatness of Bhava

## \|\| 2.2.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi kṣetraṃ vastrāpathaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*yatprabhāsasya sarvasvaṃ kṣetraṃ nābhiḥ priyaṃ mama \|\| 1 \|\|*

The Lord said:

1\. O great Goddess, thence one should again go to the holy place Vastrāpatha, which is the central holy place of Prabhāsa, dear to me.

## \|\| 2.2.2 \|\|

*yatra sākṣādbhavo devaḥ sṛṣṭisaṃhārakārakaḥ \|*  
*pṛthivyāṃ sa tvadhiṣṭhātā tattvānāmādimaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. There actually God Bhava, causing the destruction to the world (dwells). He, the first Lord, is the guardian, the first Lord of the (five) elements.

## \|\| 2.2.3 \|\|

*sa svayaṃbhūḥ sthitastatra prabhāse bhūtido bhavaḥ \|*  
*bhavatīdaṃ jagadyasmāttasmādbhava iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He, the self-existent One, Bhava, the giver of prosperity remains there at Prabhāsa. He is known as Bhava since the world comes from Him.

## \|\| 2.2.4 \|\|

*yaḥ sakṛtkurute yātrāṃ kṣetre vastrāpathe punaḥ \|*  
*vigāhya tatra tīrthāni kṛtakṛtyaḥ sa jāyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He, who goes on a pilgrimage (but) once, and that too of the holy place Vastrāpatha, and bathes at the holy spots there, is blessed.

## \|\| 2.2.5 \|\|

*atha dṛṣṭvā bhavaṃ devaṃ sakṛtpūjyavidhānataḥ \|*  
*kedārayātrāphalabhāksa bhavenmanujottamaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Having seen God Bhava, and worshipped Him according to rules and having once worshipped Him properly, that best man would be the sharer of the pilgrimage to Kedāra.

## \|\| 2.2.6 \|\|

*caitre māsi bhavaṃ dṛṣṭvā na punarjāyate bhuvi \|*  
*vaiśākhyāmathavā samyagbhavaṃ dṛṣṭvā vimucyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On seeing Bhava in the month of Caitra, one is not reborn on the earth; on seeing Bhava on the Full-Moon night of Vaiśākha one is liberated.

## \|\| 2.2.7 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāṃ kurukṣetre narmadāyāṃ tu yatphalam \|*  
*tatphalaṃ nimiṣārddhena bhavaṃ dṛṣṭvā dinedine \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. That fruit which is obtained in Vārāṇasī, Kurukṣetra or (a bath) in Narmadā (is secured) in the twinkling of an eye on seeing Bhava everyday.

## \|\| 2.2.8 \|\|

*durllabhastatra vāsastu durllabhaṃ bhavadarśanam \|*  
*pretatvaṃ naiva tasyāsti na yāmyā nārakī vyathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Residence there (at Vastrāpatha) is difficult to have; seeing Bhava is difficult. (For a person who resides there, and sees Bhava) does not undergo the condition of being dead, nor does he suffer the pain due to Yama or hell.

## \|\| 2.2.9 \|\|

*yeṣāṃ bhavālaye prāṇā gatā vai varavarṇini \|*  
*dhanyānāmapi dhanyāste devānāmapi devatāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O You of excellent complexion, those, who die in the abode of Bhava, are (more) blessed of the blessed, and deities of the deities.

## \|\| 2.2.10 \|\|

*vastrāpathe matiryeṣāṃ bhave yeṣāṃ matiḥ sthirā \|*  
*godānaṃ tatra śaṃsaṃti brāhmaṇānāṃ ca bhojanam \|*  
*piṃḍadānaṃ ca tatraiva kalpāṃtaṃ tṛptimā vahet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Those whose mind is fixed on Vastrāpatha and Bhava (are blessed). They recommend the gift of a cow there, so also meals to Brāhmaṇas. The offering of a lump of rice to the Manes at Śrāddhas would gratify them till the end of a kalpa.

## \|\| 2.2.11 \|\|

*iti saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ māhātmyaṃ te bhavodbhavam \|*  
*śrutaṃ pāpopaśamanaṃ yajñāyutaphalapradam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thus in brief is narrated to you, the greatness of Bhava. When heard it puts an end to sins and gives the fruit of myriads of sacrifices.

## Chapter 3 - Principal Holy Places in Vastrāpatha

## \|\| 2.3.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*atha vastrāpathe kṣetre saṃti tīrthāni koṭiśaḥ \|*  
*tathāpi sāraṃ te vacmi sarvatīrthamahodayam \|\| 1 \|\|*

The Lord said:

1\. In Vastrāpatha area there are crores of holy places. Yet I shall tell you the essence, of great glory.

## \|\| 2.3.2 \|\|

*dāmodare nadī proktā svarṇareṣeti yā smṛtā \|*  
*brahmakuṇḍaṃ ca tatraiva tathā brahmeśvaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. At Dāmodara is said to be the river known as Svarṇareṣā. There also is the Brahmakuṇḍa and also Brahmeśvara.

## \|\| 2.3.3 \|\|

*kālameghaśca saṃprokto bhavo dāmodaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*gavyūtidvitayenaiva kālikā tatra kīrtitā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Bhava is called Kālamegha and is also remembered as Dāmodara. Kālikā is said to be at a distance of four miles.

## \|\| 2.3.4 \|\|

*indreśvaraśca tatraiva raivataḥ parvatastathā \|*  
*ujjayaṃtaśca tatraiva devaḥ kumbhīśvaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Indreśvara is just there, so also the mountain Raivata. God Vījayanta Kumbhīśvara is also said to be there only.

## \|\| 2.3.5 \|\|

*bhīmeśvaraśca tatraiva tataḥ kṣetraṃ mahāprabham \|*  
*tailasāraṇikaṃnāma tretāyāṃ haimamārakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Bhīmeśvara is just there; then there is the very bright holy place called Tailasāraṇikta, (called) Haimamāraka in the Tretā (yuga).

## \|\| 2.3.6 \|\|

*paṃcagavyūtimātraṃ tu tatkṣetraṃ saṃprakīrtitam \|*  
*mṛgīkuṇḍaṃ ca tatraiva sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The holy place is said to be spread over ten miles. Mṛgīkuṇḍa, destroyer of all sins, is just there only.

## \|\| 2.3.7 \|\|

*etadvastrāpathaṃ kṣetraṃ ratnadhātvostathā'karam \|*  
*kathitaṃ tava deveśi punaḥ saṃkṣepato mayā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. This is the holy place Vastrāpatha, the mine of jewels and minerals. O Goddess, I have told (this) to you again in brief.

## Chapter 4 - The Greatness of Dunnāvillahṛdgiri (Dunnāvilla-hṛdgiri)

## \|\| 2.4.1-2 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi dunnāvilleti viśrutam \|*  
*yojanasyāṃtare devi paścime maṃgalasthiteḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*dunnako yatra bhīmena bhuktvā tyaktaḥ purā priye \|*  
*tatraiva vivaraṃ divyaṃ mahā pātālamārgadam \|\| 2 \|\|*

The Lord said:

1-2. Then, O great Goddess, one should go to (the holy place) known as Dunnāvilla, at a distance of a Yojana, to the west of the place of Maṅgala, where, O dear one, formerly Bhīma overpowered Dunnaka and threw him. There only is a divine fissure, leading the way to the great lower region.

## \|\| 2.4.3 \|\|

*tasya kalpaḥ purā proktaḥ pātālottarasaṃgrahe \|*  
*tatra liṃgānyanekāni siddhasthānāni ṣoḍaśa \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The sacred precept about it is formerly told in the Pātālottarasaṅgraha. There are many places of (the worship of) the Phallus, and sixteen sanctified places.

## \|\| 2.4.4 \|\|

*suvarṇasyākaraḥ pūrvaṃ tatsthānamabhavatpriye \|*  
*tasminsthāne narairdevi gantavyaṃ bhūtilipsayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O dear one, formerly it was a mine of gold. O goddess, people, with a desire for prosperity, should go there.

## Chapter 5 - The Greatness of Gaṅgeśvara (Gaṅga-īśvara)

## \|\| 2.5.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchenmahādevi maṃgalātpaścime sthitam \|*  
*gaṃgāsrotastathā liṃgaṃ surārkaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

The God said:

1\. O great Goddess, from there one should go to the holy place Gaṅgāsrotas (the stream of Gaṅgā) lying to the west of Maṅgala, and then to the Phallus, and especially to Surārka.

## \|\| 2.5.2 \|\|

*tāngacchedvidhivaddevi yadi yātrāphalepsutā \|*  
*snātvā piṇḍapradānaṃ ca kuryāttatra yathārthataḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇebhyastathā deyamannaṃ bhūri sadakṣiṇam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. If there is a desire for the fruits of the pilgrimage one should visit these places, according to the rules. Having bathed one should properly offer the piṇḍas (balls of rice offered to the manes while performing Śrāddha). Then ample food, along with Dakṣiṇā should be given to Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 2.5.3 \|\|

*iti te kathitaṃ mayā priye kalipāpaughavināśanaṃ śubham \|*  
*nikhilaṃ tīrthamahodayodayaṃ paṭhitaṃ sadvinihaṃti pāpasaṃhatim \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O dear one, I have thus narrated to you the entire account of the greatness of the holy place; it is auspicious and destroys the mass of sins of Kali. If it is recited it destroys the mass of sins.

## \|\| 2.5.4 \|\|

*idaṃ na deyaṃ durbuddheḥ sutarāṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*śrotavyaṃ vidhinā tadvadbhaviṣyoktavidhānataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. This should not be told to a wicked-minded person. It completely destroys sins. It should be listened to according to the rules spoken in the Bhaviṣya (Purāṇa).”

## Chapter 6 - Seven Previous Births of the Deer-faced Lady and King Bhoja

## \|\| 2.6.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*adhunā saṃpravakṣyāmi maṃgalātpaścime vrajet \|*  
*tatra siddheśvaraṃ paśyetsarvasiddhipradāyakam \|\| 1 \|\|*

The Lord said:

1\. Now I shall speak (again). One should go to the West of (the holy place) Maṅgala. There one should see Siddheśvara, the giver of all prosperity.

## \|\| 2.6.2 \|\|

*tatraiva cakratīrthaṃ tu tīrthakoṭiphalapradam \|*  
*lokeśvaraṃ svayaṃbhūtaṃ pūrvamiṃdreśvareti ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Just there is Cakratīrtha giving a crore of fruits. (One should go to) Lokeśvara, self-originated and formerly (called) Indreśvara.

## \|\| 2.6.3 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā taṃ vidhivaddevi tato yakṣavanaṃ vrajet \|*  
*maṃgalātpaścime bhāge yatra devī svayaṃ sthitā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O Goddess, seeing it properly (one should) then go to Yakṣavana, in the Western region of Maṅgala where the Goddess herself dwells.

## \|\| 2.6.4 \|\|

*yakṣeśvarī mahābhāgā vāṃchitārthapradāyinī \|*  
*tāṃ saṃpūjya vidhānena tato vastrāpathaṃ punaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. (She is) the illustrious Yajñeśvarī, giver of the desired object. Having worshipped her according to proper rules, one should again come to Vastrāpatha.

## \|\| 2.6.5 \|\|

*giriṃ raivatakaṃ gatvā kuryādyātrāvidhānataḥ \|*  
*mṛgīkuṃḍāditīrthāni saṃti tatraiva koṭiśaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Having gone to Raivataka mountain one should do the pilgrimage properly. Just there are crores of holy places like Mṛgīkuṇḍa.

## \|\| 2.6.6 \|\|

*yadbhuktiśikhare devi sīmāliṃgaṃ hi tatsmṛtam \|*  
*daśakoṭistu tīrthāni tatra saṃti varāna ne \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O Goddess, on the top of its limit is remembered to be Sīmāliṅga, O you of an excellent face, there are ten crores of holy places there.

## \|\| 2.6.7 \|\|

*yatra vai yādavāḥ siddhāḥ kalau ye buddhirūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*śatasahasrārbudaṃ ca liṃgaṃ tatraiva tiṣṭhati \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. There stay the illustrious Yādavas, who are of the form of intellect in the Kaliyuga. The Liṅga called Śata, Sahasrārbuda remains just there.

## \|\| 2.6.8 \|\|

*gajeṃdrasya padaṃ tatra tatraiva rasakūpikāḥ \|*  
*sapta kuṇḍāni tatraiva raivate parvatottame \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. There is the foot (-print) of Gajendra. Just there are seven

water-wells. On that excellent Raivata mountain there are seven ponds.

## \|\| 2.6.9 \|\|

*aṃbikā ca sthitā devī pradyumnaḥ sāṃba eva ca \|*  
*liṃgākāre parvate tu tatra tīrthāni koṭiśaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Goddess Ambikā resides there; so also Pradyumna and Sāmba. On the mountain Liṅgākāra there are crores of holy places.

## \|\| 2.6.10 \|\|

*mṛgīkuṃḍaṃ ca tatraiva kālameghastathaiva ca \|*  
*kṣetrapālasvarūpeṇa mahodadhi svayaṃ sthitaḥ \|*  
*dāmodaraśca tatraiva bhavo brahmāḍanāyakaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Mṛgīkuṇḍa is just there; so also Kālamegha. The great ocean remains there in the form of the guardian of the holy place. Dāmodara is just there; so also Bhava, the Lord of the universe.

Pārvatī spoke:

## \|\| 2.6.11-12 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*śrutāni tava tīrthāni deveśa vadatastava \|*  
*gaṃgā sarasvatī puṇyā yamunā ca mahānadī \|\| 11 \|\|*

*godāvarī gomatī ca nadī tāpī ca narmadā \|*  
*sarayūḥ svarṇarekhā ca tamasā pāpanāśinī \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. O Lord of gods, I heard about the holy places when you were describing them. I heard about (the holy rivers) like Gaṅgā, holy Sarasvatī, the great river Yamunā, Godāvarī and Gomatī, Tāpī and Narmadā, (so also) Sarayū, Svarṇarekhā, and Tamasā, the destroyer of sins.

## \|\| 2.6.13 \|\|

*nadyaḥ samudrasaṃyogāḥ sarvāḥ puṇyāḥ śrutā mayā \|*  
*mokṣāraṇyāni divyāni \|divyakṣetrāṇi yāni ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. I have heard about all sacred rivers joining the sea. (I have also heard about) forests (giving) salvation; so also divine, wonderful holy places whichever are there.

## \|\| 2.6.14 \|\|

*nagaryo muktidāyinyastāḥ śrutāstvatprasādataḥ \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇuśivādīnāṃ sūryeṃduvaruṇasya ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Through your favour I have learnt about cities giving liberation. There are many places of (i.e. sacred to) Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva and others; so also of the Sun, the Moon, and Varuṇa.

## \|\| 2.6.15 \|\|

*devatānā mṛṣīṇāṃ ca saṃti sthānānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*paraṃ deva tvayā puṇyaṃ prabhāsaṃ kathitaṃ mama \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. There are many places of (i.e. sacred to) deities and sages. O Lord, you described to me the holy (place) Prabhāsa.

## \|\| 2.6.16 \|\|

*tasmādyaccādhikaṃ proktaṃ kṣetraṃ vastrāpathaṃ tvayā \|*  
*śṛṇvaṃtyā ca mayā pūrvaṃ na pṛṣṭaṃ kāraṇaṃ tadā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. You (also) described to me the holy place, Vastrāpatha, superior to that (i.e. Prabhāsa). Formerly while listening to the account, I did not ask you about the cause (of the greatness of these holy places).

## \|\| 2.6.17 \|\|

*idānīṃ ca śrutaṃ sarvaṃ svasthāhaṃ kāraṇaṃ vada \|*  
*prabhāvaṃ prathamaṃ brūhi kṣetrasya ca bhavasya ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Now I have heard everything. I am composed. Tell me the cause. First tell me about the efficacy of the place and of Bhava also.

## \|\| 2.6.18 \|\|

*kasmindeśe ca tattīrthaṃ śivaḥ kenātra saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*svayaṃbhūrbhagavānrudraḥ kathaṃ tatra sthitaḥ svayam \|*  
*prabho me mahadāścaryaṃ vartate tadvadādhunā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In which region is that holy place? For what reason did Śiva stay there? How (is it that) the Self-born Rudra himself stays there? O Lord, I have great curiosity. So (please) now tell it (to me).

## \|\| 2.6.19 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*vastrāpathasya kṣetrasya prabhāvaṃ prathamaṃ śṛṇu \|*  
*paścādbhavasya māhātmyaṃ śṛṇu tvaṃ ca varānane \|\| 19 \|\|*

The Lord said:

19\. O you of charming face, first listen to the greatness of the holy place Vastrāpatha. Then listen to the greatness of Bhava.

## \|\| 2.6.20 \|\|

*kānyakubje mahākṣetre rājā bhojeti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*purā puṇyayuge dharmyaḥ prajā dharmeṇa śāsati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. In the great holy place Kānyakubja a well known religious king justly ruled his subjects formerly in the puṇya yuga (righteous age).

## \|\| 2.6.21 \|\|

*viśālākṣo dīrghabāhurvidvānvāggmī priyaṃvadaḥ \|*  
*sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpūrṇo bahvāścaryavilokakaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. His eyes were broad, arms long; he was learned, was an orator, and spoke sweetly. He was full of all (auspicious) signs, and noticed many wonders.

## \|\| 2.6.22 \|\|

*vanātkadācidabhyetya vanapālobravīdidam \|*  
*āścaryaṃ bhramatā deva vane dṛṣṭaṃ mayādhunā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Once the keeper of forests, approaching him said: “O Lord, while roaming in the forest now I saw a wonder.

## \|\| 2.6.23 \|\|

*girau viṣamabhūbhāge vahuvṛkṣasamākule \|*  
*mṛgayūthagatā nārī mayā dṛṣṭā mṛgānanā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. “On the mountain, on an uneven part of land, crowded with great many trees I saw a damsel having a deer’s face in the herd of deer.

## \|\| 2.6.24 \|\|

*mṛgavatplavate bālā sadā tatraiva dṛśyate \|*  
*iti śrutvā vaco rājā tuṣṭastasmai dhanaṃ dadau \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. “That young girl jumps like a deer and is always seen at the same place.” Hearing these words the king was pleased, and gave him much wealth,

## \|\| 2.6.25 \|\|

*caturaṃ turagaṃ divyaṃ vāsasī svarṇabhūṣaṇam \|*  
*idānīmeva yāsyāmi senādhyakṣa tvayā saha \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. a swift, divine horse, two garments and a golden ornament, (and said to him:) “O chief of the army, now only I shall go with you.

## \|\| 2.6.26 \|\|

*aśvānāṃ daśasāhasraṃ vāgurāṇāṃ tvanekadhā \|*  
*pattayo yāṃtu sarvatra veṣṭayaṃtu giriṃvaram \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. “Let ten thousand horses, snares of various kinds, foot-soldiers go everywhere and surround the excellent mountain.

## \|\| 2.6.27 \|\|

*na haṃtavyo mṛgaḥ kaścidrakṣaṇīyā hi sā mṛgī \|*  
*strīveṣadhāriṇī nārī mṛgī bhavati bhūtale \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. “No deer should be killed, and that female deer should be protected. A lady in a female’s garb, bceomes a female deer on the surface of the earth.

## \|\| 2.6.28-29 \|\|

*kva yāsyati varākī sā madbalaiḥ paripīḍitā \|*  
*śastrāstravarjitaṃ sainyaṃ vanapālapadānugam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*ahorātreṇa saṃprāptaṃ bahuvyādhajanāgrataḥ \|*  
*aśvādhirūḍho balavānbhojarājo yayau svayam \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29a. “Harassed by my armies where will that poor one go?” In front of many hunters an army without arms, following the foot (steps) of the forest-keeper night and day reached the many men and hunters.

29b. Mounted on a horse, mighty king Bhoja, himself went (with the army).

## \|\| 2.6.30 \|\|

*niḥśabdapadasañcāraḥ saṃjñāsaṃketabhāṣakaḥ \|*  
*giriṃ saṃveṣṭayāmāsa vāgurābhiḥ svayaṃ nṛpaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The king moving without making the sound of his footsteps, and speaking in the language of signs, himself surrounded the mountain with snares.

## \|\| 2.6.31 \|\|

*vanapālena sahito mṛgayūthaṃ dadarśa saḥ \|*  
*sā mṛgī mṛgamadhyasthā nārīdehā mukhe mṛgī \|*  
*mṛgavacceṣṭate bālā dhāvate ca mṛgaiḥ saha \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. With the protector of the forest he saw the herd. The female deer was among the male deer. She had a woman’s body and a female deer’s face. She acted like a girl and ran with male deer.

## \|\| 2.6.32 \|\|

*aśvagaṃdhānsamāghrāya santrastā mṛgayūthapāḥ \|*  
*kṣubdhā bhrāntāḥ kṣaṇe tasminsarve yāṃti diśo daśa \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. All the heads of the herds, being distressed on smelling the odour of the horses, being agitated and confused, that moment only, ran in (all) the ten directions.

## \|\| 2.6.33 \|\|

*mṛgavaktrā tu yā nārī mṛgaiḥ katipayaiḥ saha \|*  
*plavamānā nipatitā vāgurāyāṃ vicetanā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. That damsel, with the face of a female deer, jumping along with a few deer, fell into a trap (and became) unconscious.

## \|\| 2.6.34 \|\|

*balādhyakṣeṇa vidhṛtā mṛgaiḥ saha śanairnṛpaḥ \|*  
*dadarśa mahadāścaryaṃ bhojarājo janairvṛtaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. She was gently caught along with the deer by the chief of the army. King Bhoja, surrounded by people, saw (that) great wonder.

## \|\| 2.6.35 \|\|

*tataḥ kolāhalo jātaḥ paramānaṃdinisvanaḥ \|*  
*mṛgaiḥ saha samāninye kānyakubjaṃ mṛgīṃ nṛpaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then a tumult, with a sound indicating great joy, was produced. The king brought the female deer along with the male deer to Kānyakubja.

## \|\| 2.6.36 \|\|

*divyavastrasamācchannā divyābharaṇabhūṣitā \|*  
*narayānasthitā nārī praviveśa mṛgairvṛtā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The damsel, clad in divine garments, and adorned with celestial ornaments, seated in a vehicle drawn by men, and surrounded by male deer, entered (the city).

## \|\| 2.6.37-38 \|\|

*vāditrairbrahmaghoṣaiśca nīyate nṛpamaṃdiram \|*  
*janairjānapadairmārge dṛśyate nṛpamandire \|\| 37 \|\|*

*nīyamānā nāgaraiśca mahadāścaryabhāṣakaiḥ \|*  
*puṇye muhūrtte saṃprāpte sā mṛgī nṛpamandiram \|\| 38 \|\|*

37a. With (the sound of) musical instruments and shouts of Brāhmaṇas, she was taken to the residence of the king.

37b-38. She, being taken at an auspicious time, to the king’s residence, was seen on the way by rustics and citizens, talking and wonderstruck.

## \|\| 2.6.39 \|\|

*pratīhāreṇa rājendra vacasā vārito janaḥ \|*  
*gataḥ senāpatiḥ sainyaṃ gṛhītvā svaniketanam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The door-keeper warded off the people with words. The chief of the army, taking the army with him, went home.

## \|\| 2.6.40 \|\|

*rājāpi svagṛhaṃ prāpya snātvā saṃpūjya devatāḥ \|*  
*tāṃ mṛgīṃ snāpayāmāsa divyagandhānulepanām \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The king too, going home, bathing and worshipping deities, got that female deer bathed, after applying celestial perfumes and anointing her with ointments.

## \|\| 2.6.41 \|\|

*kuṅkumena viliptāṃgīṃ divyavastrāvaguṃṭhitām \|*  
*yathocitaṃ yathāsthānaṃ divyābharaṇabhūṣitām \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The king, in private, spoke to her whose body was anointed with saffron, who was covered with divine garments, who was properly decorated at proper places with divine ornaments.

## \|\| 2.6.42 \|\|

*ekāṃte nirjane rājā babhāṣe cārulocanām \|*  
*kā tvaṃ kasya sutā kena kāraṇena mṛgaiḥ saha \|\| 42 \|\|*

42a. In a lonely, unfrequented place the king spoke to the lady with charming eyes:

42b. “Who are you? Whose daughter are you? For what reason do you (roam with) the male deer?

## \|\| 2.6.43 \|\|

*strīṇāṃ śarīraṃ te kasmānmṛgīṇāṃ vadanaṃ kutaḥ \|*  
*iti sarvaṃ samācakṣva paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. “Why do you have the body like that of a woman and face like that of female deer? (Please) tell me all this; I have a great curiosity.”

## \|\| 2.6.44 \|\|

*evaṃ sā procyamānāpi na babhāṣe kathaṃcana \|*  
*mūkavanna vijānāti na ca bhuṃkte sulocanā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Though spoken to like this, she said nothing. Like a dumb person, she did not know (anything); and the charming-eyed lady did not eat (anything).

## \|\| 2.6.45 \|\|

*na bhuṃkte pṛthivīpālo na rājyaṃ bahu manyate \|*  
*na dārairvidyate kāryaṃ nāśvairna ca gajai rathaiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The King (too) did not eat (anything), nor did he care much for his kingdom. He had nothing to do with his wife, nor did he have anything to do with horses, elephants and chariots.

## \|\| 2.6.46 \|\|

*tadeva rājyaṃ te dārāste gajāstaddhanaṃ bahu \|*  
*pramadāmadasaṃraktaṃ yatra saṃkrīḍate manaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. That alone is the kingdom, that is the wife, those are the elephants, that alone is profuse wealth, when the mind is tinged with passion for women.

## \|\| 2.6.47-48 \|\|

*āhūyāha pratīhāraṃ tayā saṃmohito nṛpaḥ \|*  
*purodhasaṃ guruṃ viprānācāryāñchīghramānaya \|\| 47 \|\|*

*daivajñānatha mantrajñānbhiṣajastāṃtrikāṃstathā \|*  
*iti sannodito rājñā pratīhāro yayau svayam \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. The king fascinated by her, calling the door-keeper, said to him: “Quickly call the chief priest, the preceptor, Brāhmaṇas, preceptors, so also astrologers, those skilled in spells, physicians and those who are well-versed in Tantra doctrines.” Thus ordered by the king, the door-keeper himself went (to execute the king’s order).

## \|\| 2.6.49 \|\|

*ājagāma sa vegena samānīya dvijottamān \|*  
*rājñe vijñāpayāmāsa deva viprāḥ samāgatāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Speedily he came (back), bringing with him best Brāhmaṇas. He informed the king: “O Lord, the Brāhmaṇas have arrived.”

## \|\| 2.6.50 \|\|

*praveśaya guruṃ dvāḥsthaṃ saṃprāptānmaddhite ratān \|*  
*iti sannodito rājñā tathā cakre sa buddhimān \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. “Bring in the preceptor waiting at the door, and (the Brāhmaṇas) interested in my welfare.” Thus ordered by the king, the intelligent one (the door-keeper) did like that.

## \|\| 2.6.51 \|\|

*abhyutthāya nṛpaḥ pūrvaṃ namaskṛtya prapūjya ca \|*  
*āsaneṣūpaviṣṭāṃstānbabhāṣe kāryatatparaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The king having got up (before them), having saluted and honoured them, the dieligent \[diligent?\] one in duty spoke to them, seated on the seats:

## \|\| 2.6.52 \|\|

*idamāścaryamevaikaṃ kathaṃ śakyaṃ niveditum \|*  
*jānīta hi svayaṃ sarve lokataḥ śāstrato'pi vā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. “This is just a wonder. How is it possible to communicate it? You yourselves (should) know it from (the ways of) the world or even from science.

## \|\| 2.6.53 \|\|

*kathameṣā samutpannā kasyedaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam \|*  
*asyāṃ kena prakāreṇa vacanaṃ mānuṣaṃ bhavet \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. “How is she born? Of which act is that (i.e. her birth) the fruit? In what way will her speech be human?

## \|\| 2.6.54 \|\|

*svayaṃ manuṣyavadanā kathameṣā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*sāvadhānairdvijairbhūyaḥ sarvaṃ saṃcintya cocyatām \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. “How will she herself have human face? All the Brāhmaṇas should again be attentive and having thought over (the phenomenon) fully, should tell (me).”

## \|\| 2.6.55 \|\|

*viprā ūcuḥ \|*  
*deva sārasvato nāma kurukṣetre dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*ūrddhvaretāḥ sarasvatyāṃ tapastepe jitendriyaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇas said:

55\. O Lord, at Kurukṣetra there was the best Brāhmaṇa Sārasvata by name. He, living in perpetual celibacy, and with his senses controlled, practised penance.

## \|\| 2.6.56-57 \|\|

*kathayiṣyati sarvaṃ te tenādiṣṭā mṛgī svayam \|*  
*iti śrutvā vaco rājā yayau sārasvataṃ dvijam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*sarasvatījale snātaṃ prabhāse dhyānatatparam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā pradakṣiṇīkṛtya sāṣṭāṃgaṃ taṃ praṇamya ca \|*  
*upaviṣṭo nṛpo bhūmau prāṃjaliḥ sañjitendriyaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. He will tell you everything. He himself had ordered the female deer.

Hearing these words the king went to the Brāhmaṇa Sārasvata, who had, in the morning, bathed in the water of Sarasvatī, and was engaged in meditation. Seeing him, the king went round him, and sat on the ground with folded hands, and senses controlled.

## \|\| 2.6.58 \|\|

*manuṣyapadasaṃcāraṃ śrutvā jñātvā ca kāraṇam \|*  
*sārasvato babhāṣe'tha taṃ nṛpaṃ bhaktitatparam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Hearing (the sound of) the movement of human steps, and knowing its cause, Sārasvata spoke to the king who was exclusively devoted to him.

## \|\| 2.6.59 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*bhojarāja śubhaṃ testu jñātaṃ tatkāraṇaṃ mayā \|*  
*mṛgānanā tvayā nārī samānītā vanātkila \|\| 59 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

59\. Welfare to you, O king Bhoja. I have come to know the cause. You have brought that woman with a deer’s face from the forest.

## \|\| 2.6.60 \|\|

*mahadāścaryamevaitattava cetasi varttate \|*  
*ādiṣṭā tu mayā bālā sarvaṃ te kathayiṣyati \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. It is a great wonder that is in your mind. The young damsel commanded by me will tell you everything.

## \|\| 2.6.61 \|\|

*jānāmyahaṃ mahārāja caritraṃ janma yādṛśam \|*  
*āścaryaṃ saṃbhavelloke kathyamānaṃ tayā svayam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O great King, I know her life and (about) what kind of birth she has. It would be a great wonder in the world when it is narrated by herself.

## \|\| 2.6.62 \|\|

*ityādiśya gato vegādrathenādityavarcasā \|*  
*ahorātradvayenaiva saṃprāpto nṛpa mandiram \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Directing like this, he went in a chariot bright like the sun. Just after two days and nights he reached the king’s abode.

## \|\| 2.6.63 \|\|

*praviśya ca mṛgīṃ dṛṣṭvā yatrāste mṛgalocanā \|*  
*tayā sārasvato jñāto dharmajñaḥ sarvaviddvijaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Entering he saw the female deeṇ when the lotus-eyed woman stood. She recognized Sārasvata, a Brāhmaṇa, who knew piety and was omniscient.

## \|\| 2.6.64 \|\|

*mṛgyuvāca \|*  
*eṣa sarvaṃ hi jānāti kāraṇaṃ yacca yādṛśam \|*  
*varttamānaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ ca bhūtaṃ yadbhuvanatraye \|\| 64 \|\|*

The Female Deer said:

64\. This one knows everything - the cause and of what type it is. (He also knows) the present, the future and the past in the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.6.65 \|\|

*etena maraṇaṃ jñātaṃ madīyaṃ pūrvajanmani \|*  
*vastrāpathe mahākṣetre tapastaptaṃ bhavālaye \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. He knew my death in the former birth. He practised penance in the abode (temple) of Bhava in the great holy place Vastrāpatha.

## \|\| 2.6.66 \|\|

*vidhūya kaluṣaṃ sarvaṃ jñānamutpādya yatnataḥ \|*  
*jarāmaraṇanirmuktaḥ pratyakṣaṃ dṛṣṭavānbhavam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Destroying all sins and producing knowledge carefully, he, freed from old age and death, acutally \[actually?\] saw Bhava.

## \|\| 2.6.67 \|\|

*asya tuṣṭo bhavo devo jñātaṃ tīrthasya kāraṇam \|*  
*ādiṣṭayā mayā vācyaṃ bhavejjanmani kāraṇam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. God Bhava was pleased with him and the reason (for the visit to) the holy place was known. The cause of birth (as female deer) will have to be told by me when directed.

## \|\| 2.6.68 \|\|

*iti cintāparā yāvattāvadvipraḥ samāgataḥ \|*  
*tasmai praṇāmaparamā mūrcchitā nipapāta sā \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. When she was thinking like this, the Brāhmaṇa came there. She intent on saluting him, fell down in swoon.

## \|\| 2.6.69-70 \|\|

*atha sārasvato jñānājjñātavānkāraṇaṃ ca tat \|*  
*ānayantu dvijā vegātkalaśaṃ toyasaṃbhṛtam \|\| 69 \|\|*

*savauṃṣadhīḥ pallavāṃśca dūrvāḥ puṣpāṇi cākṣatān \|*  
*dhūpaṃ ca caṃdanaṃ caiva gomayaṃ madhusarpiṣī \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. Due to his (superior) knowledge, he knew the reason. (He said:) “Brāhmaṇas should quickly bring a pitcher full of water, (and) all herbs, sprouts, dūrvā (grass), flowers and akṣatas (entire unhusked rice washed with water and used as an article for worship), incense, sandal, cow-dung, honey and clarified butter.”

## \|\| 2.6.71-72 \|\|

*ityādiṣṭairdvijairvegātsamānītaṃ nṛpājñayā \|*  
*upalipya ca bhūbhāgaṃ svastikaṃ saṃniveśya ca \|\| 71 \|\|*

*tatrāgnikāryaṃ kṛtvā'tha vedānkuṃbhe nidhāya saḥ \|*  
*indraṃ tasmiṃśca vinyasya dikpālāṃśca yathākramam \|*  
*hutvāgniṃ sa caruṃ kṛtvā grahapūjāmakārayat \|\| 72 \|\|*

71-72. The Brāhmaṇas thus ordered quickly brought (all the articles) by royal order. Having smeared with cow-dung a part of the ground, and having placed (i.e. drawn) a Svastika on it having offered oblations to fire, and placing the Vedas in a pitcher, having placed (image of) Indra in that, so also the (images of the) Guardians of the quarters in due order, and having offered (oblations) into the fire, he worshipped the Planets after making an oblation of boiled rice etc. to gods and manes.

## \|\| 2.6.73 \|\|
