*toyaṃ suvarṇapātrasthaṃ kṛtvā kuṃbhānsvayaṃ guruḥ \|*  
*abhiṣekaṃ tataścakre muhūrte sārvakāmike \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Pouring water into golden pots, the preceptor himself put the pitchers. Then he bathed (her) at a time, desired by all.

## \|\| 2.6.74 \|\|

*abhiṣiktā tu sā tena pūtā snānārthavāriṇā \|*  
*jātā sacetanā bālā sarvaṃ paśyati cakṣuṣā \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. She was bathed by him, was purified by the water (used) for bath. The young lady became conscious, and saw everything with her own eyes.

## \|\| 2.6.75 \|\|

*śṛṇoti sarvaṃ jānāti caritraṃ pūrvajanmanaḥ \|*  
*badarīphalamātraṃ tu puroḍāśaṃ dadau guruḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. She heard (and understood) everything, and knew the acts of her former birth. The preceptor gave her the oblation of the size of a jujube fruit.

## \|\| 2.6.76 \|\|

*tayopabhuktaṃ yatnena tataścakre sa mārjjanam \|*  
*mānuṣe vacane karṇe dadau jñānaṃ gurustataḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. She ate it with effort. Then she cleansed herself. Then the preceptor himself gave her ears and understanding of human speech.

## \|\| 2.6.77-78 \|\|

*gurave dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā tataḥ sā ca mṛgānanā \|*  
*bhojarājāya sarva ca caritraṃ pūrvajanmanaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*vaktuṃ pracakrame bālyādyadvṛttaṃ pūrvajanmani \|*  
*namaskṛtya guruṃ pūrvaṃ brāhmaṇānkṣatriyāṃstathā \|\| 78 \|\|*

77-78a. Then that lady having a deer’s face, having given Dakṣiṇā to the preceptor, commenced to narrate whatever had happened from her childhood in the former birth.

78b. Having first saluted the preceptor, and then the Brāhmaṇas and Kṣatriyas, the female deer said:

## \|\| 2.6.79 \|\|

*mṛgyuvāca \|*  
*na viṣādastvayā kāryo rājañcchrutvā mayoditam \|*  
*itastvaṃ saptame sthāne kaliṃgādhipateḥ sutaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

The female deer said:

79\. O King, do not be dejected on hearing my account. You were the son of King Kaliṅga who existed in the seventh previous generation.

## \|\| 2.6.80 \|\|

*mṛte pitari bālastvaṃ svabhiṣiktaḥ svamaṃtribhiḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ hi vaṃgarājasya saṃjātā duhitā kila \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. When your father died, your ministers consecrated you. (even though) you were a child. It is said, I was born as the daughter of the king of Vaṅga.

## \|\| 2.6.81 \|\|

*pariṇītā tvayā deva pitrā dattā svayaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*tvayā'haṃ paṭṭamahiṣī kṛtā yoṣidvarā yataḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. I was married to you. My father himself gave me (to you in marriage). O King, Since I was most beautiful among ladies you made me the principal queen.

## \|\| 2.6.82 \|\|

*yuvā jātaḥ krameṇaiva hiṃsraḥ krūro babhūva ha \|*  
*na vedaśāstrakuśalo dayādharmavivarjitaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Gradually you became a youth and hurtful and cruel. You were not proficient in the Vedas, and were pitiless.

## \|\| 2.6.83 \|\|

*lubdho mānī mahākrodhī satyācāra bahiṣkṛtaḥ \|*  
*na devaṃ na guruṃ viprānno jānāti durāśayaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. You were greedy, proud, very wrathful, and bereft of good behaviour. Being of a wicked heart you knew not (i.e. did not care for) god, preceptor, Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 2.6.84 \|\|

*viraktā hi prajāstasya brāhmaṇocchedakārakaḥ \|*  
*samāsannairnṛpaistasya deśaḥ sarvo viluṃpitaḥ \|*  
*sainyaṃ sarvaṃ samādāya yuddhāyopajagāma saḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Your subjects were indifferent to you (as) you killed Brāhmaṇas. Your entire country was seized by neighbourhood kings. Taking your entire army (with you) you went to fight.

## \|\| 2.6.85 \|\|

*sahaivāhaṃ gatā deva yuddhaṃ jātaṃ nṛpaiḥ saha \|*  
*hāritaṃ sainikaistasya gatā naṣṭā diśo daśa \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. I too accompanied you. A battle took place with (those) kings. Your soldiers lost the battle. They went into the ten directions or perished.

## \|\| 2.6.86 \|\|

*tyaktvā dharmaṃ nijaṃ rājā palāyanaparo'bhavat \|*  
*gacchamānastu nṛpatiḥ śatrubhiḥ paripīḍitaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. You, the king, giving up your duty took to heals. You while (thus) going (away) were harassed by (your) enemies.

## \|\| 2.6.87 \|\|

*tavāsmivādī duṣṭātmā hato lokavirodhakaḥ \|*  
*dehaṃ tasya gṛhītvāgnau praviṣṭāhaṃ nṛpottama \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. He, saying, ‘I am yours’, of a wicked nature, opposing the people, was killed. O best king, taking (with me) your (dead) body, I entered fire.

## \|\| 2.6.88-89 \|\|

*mṛtasyaivaṃ gatirnāsti narake sa vipacyate \|*  
*mṛtaṃ kāṃtaṃ samādāya bhāryāgnau praviśedyadi \|\| 88 \|\|*

*sā tārayati pāpiṣṭhaṃ yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|*  
*iha pāpakṣayaṃ kṛtvā paścātsvarge mahīyate \|\| 89 \|\|*

88-89. One that dies like this has no (other) course, (but) is roasted in hell. If his wife, taking (the dead body of) her husband, enters fire, she rescues him, the worst sinner, till the universal destruction. Having destroyed the sins here (i.e. in this world), he prospers in Heaven.

## \|\| 2.6.90 \|\|

*atastvaṃ brāhmaṇo jāto deśe mālavake nṛpa \|*  
*tasyaiva tatra bhāryāhaṃ saṃbhūtā brāhmaṇī nṛpa \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Therefore you were born as a Brāhmaṇa in Mālavaka country; O King, I was born just as his wife, a Brāhmaṇa lady.

## \|\| 2.6.91 \|\|

*dhanadhānyasamṛddho'bhūttathā jīvadhanādhikaḥ \|*  
*mṛtaḥ pitā mṛtā mātā sa ca bhrātṛvivarjitaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. He was rich with wealth and com, and had more wealth than required for living. His father died. His mother died. He was brotherless.

## \|\| 2.6.92 \|\|

*dhanadhānyasamṛddho'pi lubdho bhramati bhūtale \|*  
*atīva kopano vipro vedapāṭhavivarjitaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Though rich with wealth and com, he moved greedily on the earth. The Brāhmaṇa (i.e. you) was very irascible, and was without Vedic studies.

## \|\| 2.6.93 \|\|

*snānasaṃdhyādihīnaśca māyāvī yācate janam \|*  
*bhaktiṃ karomi paramāṃ sa ca krudhyati māṃ prati \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. The deceitful one, without bath and prayers, solicits people. I was given to great devotion, and (so) he used to get angry with me.

## \|\| 2.6.94 \|\|

*saṃtānaṃ tasya vai nāsti dhanarakṣāparo hi saḥ \|*  
*na dadāti na cāśnāti na juhoti sa rakṣati \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. He had no child. He was given to preserving wealth. He did not give (in charity); did not eat; did not offer an oblation to a deity; he (only) protected (money).

## \|\| 2.6.95 \|\|

*na tarpaṇaṃ tilairvipro vidadhātyatilo bhataḥ \|*  
*kārttike'pi ca saṃprāpte viṣṇupūjāvivarjitaḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Due to extreme greed, that Brāhmaṇa did not make offering with sesamum seeds. Even when the month of Kārttika arrived he was without (i.e. did not perform) the worship of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.6.96 \|\|

*dīpaṃ dadāti no vipro māsamekaṃ nirantaram \|*  
*na bhuṃkte śākapatraṃ sa ekāhāro niraṃtaram \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. The Brāhmaṇa did not regularly offer for one month a lamp to a deity. He did not eat vegetable leaf, and stuck continously to one (kind of) meal.

## \|\| 2.6.97 \|\|

*māse nabhasye saṃprāpte prāpte kṛṣṇe nṛpottama \|*  
*na karoti gṛhe śrāddhaṃ snānatarpaṇavarjitaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. When the month of Bhādrapada arrived, and when it was the dark half (of the month), O best king, he did not perform a Śrāddha at his residence, and remained without a bath or making offerings to the manes.

## \|\| 2.6.98 \|\|

*na jānāti dinaṃ pitryaṃ pakṣamekaṃ nirantaram \|*  
*anyatra bhuṃkte vipro'sau kṣayāhe'pi samāgate \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. He never thought the day or the fortnight sacred to the head ancestors. This Brāhmaṇa ate at other place (than his house) even when the loss of a lunar day (Kṣayāha) came.

## \|\| 2.6.99 \|\|

*makarasthe'pi saṃkrāṃtau kṛśarānnaṃ dadāti na \|*  
*tilānsuvarṇaṃ tāraṃ vā vastraṃ vā phalameva ca \|*  
*śākapatraṃ sa puṣpaṃ vā na dadāti tatheṃdhanam \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. When, on a Saṃkrānti day the Sun is in the Capricomus sign he does not offer rice and peas boiled together with a few spices. Nor does he offer sesamum seeds or an excellent garment or a fruit, or a vegetable leaf, a flower, so also fuel.

## \|\| 2.6.100 \|\|

*gavāṃ gavāhnikaṃ naiva kathaṃ muktirbhaviṣyati \|*  
*na yāti viṣṇuśaraṇaṃ saṃprāpte dakṣiṇāyane \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Also he does not at all give the (prescribed) daily measures of food to a cow. (Then) how will he be liberated? He does not seek Viṣṇu’s shelter when the winter solstice has come.

## \|\| 2.6.101 \|\|

*dhenuṃ dadāti no vipro grahaṇe caṃdrasūryayoḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. On the lunar or solar eclipse the Brāhmaṇa does not offer a cow (to a Brāhmaṇa).

## \|\| 2.6.102 \|\|

*ekāpi dattā supayasvinī sā savastraghaṃṭābharaṇopapannā \|*  
*vatsena yuktā hi dadāti dātre muktiṃ kulasyāsya karoti vṛddhim \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. One good milch cow, along with a garment, a bell, an ornament, is given along with her calf, gives final emancipation to the giver, and makes his family prosper.

## \|\| 2.6.103 \|\|

*yāvaṃti romāṇi bhavaṃti tasyāstāvaṃti varṣāṇi mahīyate saḥ \|*  
*brahmālaye siddha gaṇairvṛto'sau saṃtiṣṭhate sūryasamānatejāḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. He prospers for me, many years as the number of hair on her body. He, as lustrous as the sun, and surrounded by groups of Siddhas dwells in Brahmā’s abode.

## \|\| 2.6.104 \|\|

*devālayaṃ no vidadhāti vāpīṃ kūpaṃ taḍāgaṃ na karoti kuṇḍam \|*  
*puṇyaṃ vivāhaṃ sujanopakāraṃ nāsau satāṃ vā dvijamaṃdiraṃ ca \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. He did not put up a temple, or dug a big or small well or (constructed) a lake or a pool. He does not arrange a just marriage, does not oblige a good person, nor does he construct a house for the good or for a Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 2.6.105 \|\|

*dhanaṃ sadā bhūmigataṃ karoti dharmaṃ na jānāti kulasya cāsau \|*  
*ahaṃ hi tasyānugatā bhavāmi kathaṃ hi kāṃtaṃ parivaṃ cayāmi \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. He always buries his wealth, and does not know the duties to his family. I followed him. How can I deceive my husband?

## \|\| 2.6.106 \|\|

*evaṃ hi varttamānaḥ sa kāladharmamupeyivān \|*  
*dhanalobhānmayā deva maraṇaṃ parivarjitam \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Being like this, he died. Due to greed for wealth, I avoided dying (after him), O Lord.

## \|\| 2.6.107 \|\|

*paśyantyā gotribhiḥ sarvaṃ gṛhītaṃ dhanasaṃcayam \|*  
*kālena mahatā deva mṛtā'haṃ dvijamaṃdire \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. (My) relatives took all my stock of wealth while I was watching (i.e. under my very nose). O Lord, after a long time, I died in the house of the Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 2.6.108 \|\|

*śvetasarpaḥ samabhavaddeśe tasminnarottama \|*  
*tatraivāhaṃ brāhmaṇasya saṃjātā tanayā nṛpa \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. O best king, my husband was born as a white serpent in that country. O king, I was born as a Brāhmaṇa’s daughter there only.

## \|\| 2.6.109 \|\|

*varṣeṣṭame tu saṃprāpte pariṇītā dvijanmanā \|*  
*tasminneva gṛhe sarpo madīye vasate nṛpa \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. When the eighth year approached (i.e. when I entered the eighth year) I was married to a Brāhmaṇa. O king, the serpent lived in just that house, i.e. my house.

## \|\| 2.6.110 \|\|

*bhāryā mameti saṃdaṣṭo rātrau bharttā mahā hinā \|*  
*mṛto'pi brāhmaṇaiḥ sarpo laguḍairvinipātitaḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. Thinking ‘This is my wife’, my husband, the great serpent, bit me at night. Though dead the serpent was struck with clubs by the Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 2.6.111 \|\|

*vaidhavyaṃ mama dattvā tu dvijasarpau mṛtāvubhau \|*  
*pitrā mātrā mahāśokaṃ kṛtvā me muṇḍitaṃ śiraḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. Giving me widowhood both the Brāhmaṇa and the serpent died. My mother and father grieved much and shaved my head.

## \|\| 2.6.112 \|\|

*vasānā śvetavastraṃ ca viṣṇubhaktiparāyaṇā \|*  
*māsopavāsaniratā yāni tīrthānyanekaśaḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. Putting on a white garment and solely devoted to Viṣṇu, and engaged in a monthly fast (I visited) many times whatever holy places I could visit.

## \|\| 2.6.113 \|\|

*sarpastu makaro jāto godāvaryāṃ śivālaye \|*  
*devaṃ bhīmeśvaraṃ draṣṭuṃ gatā'haṃ svajanaiḥ saha \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. In Godāvarī, in the Śiva temple, the serpent was born as a crocodile. With my relatives I went to visit Lord Bhīṣmeśvara.

## \|\| 2.6.114 \|\|

*yāvatsnātuṃ praviṣṭā'haṃ vṛtā sarvajanairnṛpa \|*  
*makareṇa tadā dṛṣṭā bhāryeyaṃ mama vallabhā \|*  
*gṛhītā makareṇāhaṃ netumaṃtarjale nṛpa \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. When, I, surrounded by all people, entered (the water), the crocodile saw me and recognized: ‘This is my dear wife.’ O king, the crocodile seized me to take me into (the water).

## \|\| 2.6.115 \|\|

*hāhākāraḥ samabhavajjanaḥ kṣubdhaḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*kuṃtāghātena kenāsau makarastu nipātitaḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. A loud cry of lamentation came up; on all sides people were agitated. Someone struck down the crocodile with the stroke of a lance.

## \|\| 2.6.116 \|\|

*jhaṣavaktraḥ sthitā cāhaṃ mṛtā kṛṣṭā janairbahiḥ \|*  
*agniṃ dattvā jale kṣiptvā bhasma lokā gṛhāngatāḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. I who remained in the mouth of the large fish, died, and was dragged out by people. Burning (my body), throwing the ash into water, the people went home.

## \|\| 2.6.117 \|\|

*strīvadhāllubdhvako jāto jhaṣastīrthaprabhāvataḥ \|*  
*mānuṣīṃ yonimāpannastasminneva mahāvane \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. Due to his murdering a woman he became a hunter, and a fish due to the prowess of the holy place. He secured birth as a human being in the same forest.

## \|\| 2.6.118 \|\|

*agnerjalācca sarpācca gajātsiṃhādavṛṣādapi \|*  
*jhaṣādvisphoṭakānmṛtyuryeṣāṃ te narake gatāḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. Those who get death due to fire, water, a serpent, an elephant, a lion, and even a bull, (so also) a big fish, or a tumour go to hell.

## \|\| 2.6.119 \|\|

*ātmahā bhrūṇahā strīhā brahmaghnaḥ kūṭasākṣyadaḥ \|*  
*kanyāvikrayakartā ca mithyā bratadharastu yaḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. All those—who commit suicide, destroy an embryo, kill a woman or a Brāhmaṇa, give false testimony, so also those who sell their daughters, who take up a vow falsely,

## \|\| 2.6.120 \|\|

*vikrīṇāti kratuṃ yastu madyapaḥ syāddvijastu yaḥ \|*  
*rājadrohī svarṇacauro brahmavṛttivilopakaḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. (similarly) he who sells a sacrifice, a Brāhmaṇa who is a drunkard, one who deceives a king, one who steals gold, who gives up the profession of a Brāhmaṇa,

## \|\| 2.6.121 \|\|

*goghnastu nikṣepaharo grāmasīmāharastu yaḥ \|*  
*sarve te narakaṃ yāṃti yā ca strī pativaṃcakā \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. he who kills a cow, who deprived one of one’s deposit, who violates the boundary of the village (-land)—all these go to hell; so also a woman who deceives her husband.

## \|\| 2.6.122 \|\|

*jhaṣamṛtyuprabhāvena jātā krauṃcī vane nṛpa \|*  
*godāvarīvane vyādho bhramate mṛgamārgakaḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. O king, due to the effect of the fish’s death I was born as a female Krauñca bird. In the Godāvarī-forest a hunter wanders chasing the deer.

## \|\| 2.6.123-124 \|\|

*vane krauṃcaḥ sakāmo māṃ mudā kāmayitumudyataḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭāhaṃ bhramatā tena vyādhenākṛṣya kārmukam \|\| 123 \|\|*

*hataḥ krauṃco mṛto rāja nnaṣṭā sthānādahaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*godāvarīvane tasminnevaṃrūpaṃ dadarśa tam \|\| 124 \|\|*

123-124. A Krauñca bird, that was passionate, was gladly eager to rouse passion in me. The wandering hunter saw me and drawing his bow, struck the Krauñca bird, that (afterwards) died; O king, I then fled from that spot. In that Godāvān-forest, I saw him of such a form.

## \|\| 2.6.125 \|\|

*ṛṣirvyādhaṃ śaśāpātha dṛṣṭvā karma vigarhitam \|*  
*kāmadharmamakurvāṇaṃ priyā saṃbhāṣatatparam \|*  
*krauṃcaṃ tvamavadhīryasmāttasmātsiṃho bhaviṣyasi \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. Seeing the shameful deed a sage cursed the hunter: “Since you killed the Krauñca that had not executed the act due to passion, and that was eager to converse with his beloved, you will, therefore, be (born as) a lion.”

## \|\| 2.6.126 \|\|

*ṛṣistena vinītena sthitvā santoṣito nṛpa \|*  
*ṛṣirvadati tasyāgre na me mithyā vaco bhavet \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. Due to his being modest, the sage became glad. In front of (i.e. to) him the sage said, “My words shall not be false.”

## \|\| 2.6.127 \|\|

*siṃhasthasya prasādaṃ te kariṣye muktihetave \|*  
*surāṣṭradeśe bhavitā siṃho raivatake girau \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. “For your liberation I shall do favour to you when Jupiter is in the Leo Constellation. On the Raivataka mountain in Surāṣṭra you will be (born as) a lion.”

## \|\| 2.6.128 \|\|

*vastrāpathe mahā kṣetre muktiste vihitā dhruvā \|*  
*ityuktvā sa ṛṣirdeva gato bhīmeśvaraṃ prati \|*  
*durvacaḥśravaṇādvyādhaḥ kramātpaṃcatvamāyayau \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. “Your liberation is certainly decreed in the great holy place Vastrāpatha.” Speaking like this, the sage went to the deity Bhīmeśvara. Hearing the bad words (i.e. the curse) the hunter in due course died,

## \|\| 2.6.129 \|\|

*krauṃcī krauṃcaviyogena gatā sā ca vanāṃtare \|*  
*mṛtā daivavaśājjātā mṛgī raivatake girau \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. and the female Krauñca bird, due to her separation from the male Krauñca, went to another forest. She died, and due to (the power of) destiny was born as a female deer on the Raivataka mountain.

## \|\| 2.6.130 \|\|

*mṛgayūthagatā nityaṃ modate madavihvalā \|*  
*vyādhaḥ siṃhaḥ samabhavadgirestasya mahāvane \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. She, after having gone to the herd of deer was always agitated by ardent passion. The hunter was born as a lion in the great forest of that mountain.

## \|\| 2.6.131 \|\|

*kāmārtā bhramatā dṛṣṭā mṛgī siṃhena yatnataḥ \|*  
*tatra saṃbhramate nityaṃ siṃhaścāpi mṛgī vane \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. The lion carefully saw the passionate female deer wandering (in the forest). Everyday the lion, so also the female deer, wandered there regularly.

## \|\| 2.6.132 \|\|

*siṃho'pi daivayogena mameyamiti manyate \|*  
*paraṃ hiṃsrasvabhāvena tāmādātuṃ pracakrame \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. The lion also, as destiny would have it, looked upon her as his (possession). But due to his cruel nature the lion set out to seize her.

## \|\| 2.6.133 \|\|

*calatvaṃ mṛgajātīnāṃ vihitaṃ vedhasā svayam \|*  
*punargatā mṛgī yūthaṃ krīḍate cārulocanā \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. Brahmā Himself has laid down the fickleness of the species of deer. She, of charming eyes, again went to the herd of deer, and sported.

## \|\| 2.6.134 \|\|

*bhavasya paścime bhāge tatra raivatake girau \|*  
*anuyātaḥ śanaiḥ so'tha mṛgendro mṛgayūthapaḥ \|*  
*utpapāta tataḥ siṃho saṃghasya mūrddhani \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. On the western part (of the holy place) of Bhava, on the Raivataka mountain, the chief of the herd of deer, the lion, slowly followed (her). Then the lion jumped upon the top of the herd of deer.

## \|\| 2.6.135 \|\|

*siṃhasya na mṛgaiḥ kāryaṃ hariṇīṃ prati paśyataḥ \|*  
*yatra sā hariṇī yāti yayau siṃhastathaiva tām \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. The lion, looking at the female deer had nothing to do with the deer. The lion just went to the female deer wherever she went.

J36. In the forest when the female took up (greater) speed the lion was angry. The lion too caught (greater) speed and became speedier than the speed of the female deer.

## \|\| 2.6.137 \|\|

*yadā siṃhena saṃkrāṃtā dadau jhampāṃ mṛgī tu sā \|*  
*bhavasyāgre nadītoye patitā jalamūrddhani \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. When the lion reached the female deer, she took a leap, and fell into the water of the river in front of Bhava.

## \|\| 2.6.138 \|\|

*laṃbate tu śarīraṃ me veṇau protaṃ śiro mama \|*  
*siṃhaḥ sahaiva patito mṛtaḥ payasi madhyataḥ \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. (The female deer speaks:) My body hung; my head was fastened to my braid. The lion fell with (me) and died in the water.

## \|\| 2.6.139 \|\|

*svarṇareṣājale deva viśīrṇaṃ mama tadvapuḥ \|*  
*na tu vaktraṃ nipatitaṃ tvaksāraśirasi sthitam \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. O Lord, that my body was shattered in the water of Svarṇarekhā; my face (however) did not fall (into the river) and remained on the top of tvaksāra (? bamboo?).

## \|\| 2.6.140 \|\|

*etaccaritraṃ yatsarvaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ sārasvatena vai \|*  
*tattīrthasya prabhāvena siṃhastvaṃ samajāyathāḥ \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. This is the account of what Sārasvata saw. Due to the power of the holy place you were born as a lion.

## \|\| 2.6.141 \|\|

*idaṃ hi saptamaṃ janma sarvapāpakṣayodayam \|*  
*kānyakubje mahādeśe rājā bhojetiviśrutaḥ \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. This is the seventh birth, the cause of the end of all sins. You were born as a very famous king in the great country Kānyakubja.

## \|\| 2.6.142 \|\|

*ahaṃ hi hariṇīgarbhe jātā mānuṣarūpiṇī \|*  
*jātaṃ vaktraṃ mṛgīṇāṃ me yasmānna patitaṃ jale \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. I was conceived in the womb of a female deer and was bora in a human form, (but) my face became like that of the female deer, since it did not fall into the water.

## Chapter 7 - The Greatness of Svarṇarekhā

## \|\| 2.7.1 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*kathaṃ tvaṃ hariṇīrūpe jātā mānuṣarūpiṇī \|*  
*kena saṃvardhitā bālye kathaṃ te rūpamīdṛśam \|\| 1 \|\|*

The king said:

1\. How did you, of a human form, turn into the form of a female deer? Who brought you up in your childhood? (How did you get) such a form?

## \|\| 2.7.2-3 \|\|

*mṛgyuvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu deva pravakṣyāmi yadvṛttaṃ kanyake vane \|*  
*ṛṣiruddālakonāma gaṃgākūle mahātapāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*prabhāte mūtramutsṛṣṭuṃ gato deva vanāṃtare \|*  
*mūtrāṃte patito bhūmau vīryabiṃdurdvijanmanaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

The female deer said:

2-3. O Lord, listen. I shall tell you what happened in the Kanyaka forest. O Lord, the sage, Uddālaka by name, having great penance, went, in the morning, into a forest, to pass urine. At the end of his urination a drop of the semen of that Brāhmaṇa fell on the ground.

## \|\| 2.7.4 \|\|

*yāvatsa calito vipraḥ śaucaṃ kṛtvā prayatnataḥ \|*  
*tāvanmṛgī samāyātā dṛṣṭvā puṣpavanāṃtarāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. While after having purified himself with care, the sage moved, a female deer came there from a flower-garden on seeing (the drop).

## \|\| 2.7.5 \|\|

*cāpalyādbhakṣitaṃ vīryaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ brahmarṣiṇā svayam \|*  
*yasmādaśnāti me vīryaṃ tasmādgarbho bhaviṣyati \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. She quickly swallowed the semen, (and) the Brāhmaṇa sage himself saw this (phenomenon). (He thought to himself:) ‘Since she has swallowed my semen, she will conceive.’

## \|\| 2.7.6 \|\|

*mamarūpā tavavaktrā nārī garbhe bhaviṣyati \|*  
*varddhayiṣyati devyastāṃ rasairdivyaiḥ sutāṃ tava \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. (He said to her:) ‘In the embryo there will be (conceived) a female of my form and face like you. Goddesses will bring up your daughter with divine liquids.

## \|\| 2.7.7 \|\|

*kenāpi daivayogena jñānaṃ tasyā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*evamuddālakādeva saṃjātāhaṃ mṛgānanā \|*  
*praviśyāgnau mṛtā pūrvaṃ tvayā sārddhaṃ narādhipa \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. ‘Due to some chance she will have knowledge’ Thus from Uddālaka only I was born as a deer-faced one, O king, after formerly entering into fire with you.

## \|\| 2.7.8-9 \|\|

*tasmājjātaṃ satītvaṃ me saptajanmani vai prabho \|*  
*yattvayā kurvatā rājyaṃ pāpaṃ vai samupārjitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*kṣattradharmaṃ parityajya palāyanaparo mṛtaḥ \|*  
*tadeno hi mayā dagdhaṃ citāgnau nṛpasattama \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Due to that was my chastity in the seventh birth. O best king, I burnt into the funeral fire, that sin, which you, while ruling, committed- (viz.) you died while running away abandoning your duty as a Kṣatriya.

## \|\| 2.7.10 \|\|

*patiṃ gṛhītvā yā nārī mṛtamagnau viśedyadi \|*  
*sā tārayati bhartāramātmānaṃ ca kuladvayam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. If a lady enters fire along with her dead husband, she emancipates her husband, herself and both the families (of herself and of her husband).

## \|\| 2.7.11 \|\|

*gograhe deśabhaṃge ca saṃgrāme sammukhe mṛtaḥ \|*  
*sa sūryamaṇḍalaṃ bhittvā brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He who dies while capturing cows, or at the time of the downfall of his country, prospers in the world of Brahmā, after piercing the orb of the Sun.

## \|\| 2.7.12 \|\|

*anāśakaṃ yo vidadhāti marttyo dinedine yajñasahasrapuṇyam \|*  
*sa yāti yānena gaṇānvitena vidhūya pāpāni suraiḥ sa pūjyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. That mortal who observes a fast (for many days), causing religious merit of a thousand sacrifices, goes in a vehicle (to Heaven), accompanied by (Śiva’s) attendants, after having shaken off his sins, and is adored by gods.

## \|\| 2.7.13 \|\|

*gaṃgājale prayāge vā kedāre puṣkare ca ye \|*  
*vastrāpathe prabhāse ca mṛtāste svargagāminaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Those who die in the water of Gaṅgā, at Prayāga or Kedāra, at Vastrāpatha or Prabhāsa go to Heaven.

## \|\| 2.7.14 \|\|

*dvārāvatyāṃ kurukṣetre yogābhyāsena ye mṛtāḥ \|*  
*harirityakṣaraṃ mṛtyau yeṣāṃ te svargagāminaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Those who die at Dvārāvatī or Kurukṣetra after practising yoga, and utter the letters ‘Hari’ at the time of death, go to Heaven.

## \|\| 2.7.15-17 \|\|

*pūjayitvā hariṃ ye tu bhūmau darbhatilaiḥ saha \|*  
*tilāṃśca pañcalohaṃ ca dattvā ye tu payasvinīm \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ye mṛtā rājaśārdūla te narāḥ svarga gāminaḥ \|*  
*utpādya putrānsaṃsthāpya pitṛpaitāmahe pade \|\| 16 \|\|*

*nirmalā niṣkalaṃkā ye te mṛtāḥ svargagāminaḥ \|*  
*vratopavāsaniratāḥ satyācāraparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*ahiṃsāniratāḥ śāṃtāste narāḥ svargagāminaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-16a. Those, O lion among kings, who die after having worshipped Hari on the earth with darbhas and sesamum seeds, and having gifted sesamum seeds and five metals (viz. gold, silver, copper, tin and lead) and a milch-cow go to Heaven.

16b-17a. Having produced sons and having established them in the position of (i.e. the position occupied by) the father or grandfather, those who are clean and spotless go to Heaven after death.

17b. (So also) those who are engaged in vows and fasts, whose behaviour is truthful, who are engaged in non-violence, who are calm, go to Heaven.

## \|\| 2.7.18 \|\|

*sāpavādo raṇaṃ tyaktvā mṛto yasmānnarādhipa \|*  
*saptayoniṣu te janma tasmājjātaṃ mayā saha \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O king, since you left the battlefield and died reproachfully, you had birth in the seven generations with me.

## \|\| 2.7.19 \|\|

*tvāṃ vinā me patirmā bhūnmaraṇe yācitaṃ mayā \|*  
*tadāṃtarikṣe rājendra vāguvācāśarīriṇī \|*  
*ādau pāpaphalaṃ bhuktvā paścā tsvargaṃ gamiṣyasi \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. At the time of my death I had implored that I should not have a husband other than you. O Lord of kings, at that time an incorporeal speech said from the sky: First you will suffer the fruit of your sins, and then you will go to Heaven.

## \|\| 2.7.20 \|\|

*yadi vastrāpathe gatvā śiraḥ kaścidvimuṃcati \|*  
*svarṇarekhājale rājanmānuṣaṃ syānmukhaṃ mama \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O king, if someone, after going to Vastrāpatha leaves my head into the water of Svarṇarekhā, my face will be human again.

## \|\| 2.7.21 \|\|

*ahaṃ mānuṣavaktrā'smi pāpacchāyā'vṛtaṃ mukham \|*  
*dṛśyate mṛgavaktrābhaṃ tasmācchīghraṃ vimuṃcaya \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. I am (really) human-faced; (but) my face is covered with the shadow of sin; (so) it appears like the face of a deer. Therefore, quickly leave it (into the river).

## \|\| 2.7.22 \|\|

*iti śrutvā vaco rājā sārasvatamudaikṣata \|*  
*jano vihasya sānandaṃ sarvaṃ satyaṃ mṛgīvacaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Hearing these words, the king looked up at Sārasvata. The people laughed with joy: “Every word of the female deer is true”

## \|\| 2.7.23-26 \|\|

*ityuktvā'ha dvijendraḥ sa evaṃ kuru nṛpottama \|*  
*evaṃ rājñā samādiṣṭaḥ pratīhāro yayau vanam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*vastrāpathe mahātīrthe bhavaṃ draṣṭuṃ tvarānvitaḥ \|*  
*tvaksārajālirmahatī svarṇarekhājalopari \|\| 24 \|\|*

*varttate tacchiro yatra vaṃśaprotaṃ mahāvane \|*  
*sārasvatasya śiṣyeṇa kuśalena niveditam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tīrthaṃ vastrāpathaṃ gatvā bhavasyāgre mahānadī \|*  
*jāle tatra śiro dṛṣṭaṃ tacca toye vimocitam \|\| 26 \|\|*

23-25a. Speaking like this the best Brāhmaṇa (Sārasvata) said: “O best king, do like this.” (Then) ordered like this by the king, the door-keeper went to the forest, making haste to see Bhava at the great holy place Vastrāpatha. (He went to) that place where there was a great mass of marrow on the surface of the water of Svarṇarekhā, transfixed with bamboos in the great forest.

25b-26. Kuśala, Sārasvata’s (clever) disciple reported: “Having gone to the holy place Vastrāpatha, I saw a great river in front of Bhava. There (I saw) a head in the mass (of marrow), released into the water.”

## \|\| 2.7.27 \|\|

*snātvā saṃpūjya tīrtheśaṃ pratīhāraḥ samabhyagāt \|*  
*śiṣyeṇa sahito vegādrathenādityavarcasā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Having bathed and having worshipped well the Lord of the holy place, the door-keeper returned speedily in a chariot bright like the sun, along with the disciple.

## \|\| 2.7.28 \|\|

*yadāgataḥ pratīhārastadā sārasvatena sā \|*  
*vṛtā cāndrāyaṇenaiva māsamekaṃ nirantaram \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. When the door-keeper came (back), Sārasvata asked her for (i.e. to observe) the Cāndrāyaṇa vow (the vow regulated by the Moon’s waxing and waning) only continuously for one month.

## \|\| 2.7.29-30 \|\|

*saṃpūrṇe tu vrate tasyā divyaṃ vaktraṃ sulocanam \|*  
*suśobhanaṃ dīrghakeśaṃ dīrghakarṇaṃ śubhadvijam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*kambugrīvaṃ padmagaṃdhaṃ sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyutam \|*  
*vratāṃte mūrcchitā bālā gatajñānā vabhūva sā \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. When the vow was over, her face was divine, had fine eyes, looked charming, had long hair, long ears and fine teeth, had conch-like neck, smelt like lotus and had all (auspicious) signs. At the end of the vow the young lady swooned and lost her (faculty of) knowledge.

## \|\| 2.7.31 \|\|

*na devī na ca gaṃdharvī nāsurī na ca kiṃnarī \|*  
*yādṛśī sā tadā jātā tīrthabhāvena sundarī \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The beautiful lady was not a goddess, not a Gandharva-lady, not a demoness, nor a Kinnara, as she became (none of these) due to the superhuman power of the holy place.

## \|\| 2.7.32 \|\|

*pariṇītā tu sā tena bhojarājena sundarī \|*  
*mṛgīmukhīti vikhyātā devī sā bhuvaneśvarī \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. That king Bhoja married that beautiful lady. That queen

became known as ‘Mṛgīmukhā’.

## \|\| 2.7.33 \|\|

*na jānāti punaḥ kiṃcidyadvṛttaṃ rājamandire \|*  
*kṛtā sā paṭṭamahiṣī bhojarājena dhīmatā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. She did not also know what happened in the palace. The wise king Bhoja made her the chief queen.

## \|\| 2.7.34 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*deśānāṃ pravaro deśo girīṇāṃ pravaro giriḥ \|*  
*kṣetrāṇāmuttamaṃ kṣetraṃ vanānāmuttamaṃ vanam \|\| 34 \|\|*

The Lord said:

34\. (In that holy place was) the best of countries, the best of mountains, the best of the holy places, the best of forests.

## \|\| 2.7.35-37 \|\|

*gaṃgā sarasvatī tāpī svarṇarekhājale sthitā \|*  
*brahmā viṣṇuśca sūryaśca sarva indrādayaḥ surāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*nāgā yakṣāśca gandharvā asminkṣetre vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*brahmāṃḍaṃ nirmitaṃ yena trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 36 \|\|*

*devā brahmādayo jātāḥ sa bhavo'tra vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*śivo bhaveti vikhyātaḥ svayaṃ devastrilocanaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-36a. (The rivers) Gaṅgā, Sarasvatī, Tāpī remained in the water of Svarṇarekhā. All gods Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Sun, Indra and others, Nāgas, Yakṣas, Gandharvas, have settled in this holy place.

36b-37. He, that Bhava, who created the universe - the three worlds with the moveable and the immoveable, and from whom gods like Brahmā came up, dwells here. The three-eyed god is very well known as Bhava, Śiva.

## \|\| 2.7.38 \|\|

*veveti skandaracanādbhavānī cātra saṃsthitā \|*  
*ato yannādhikaṃ proktaṃ tīrthaṃ devi mayā tava \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Due to Kārttikeya’s creation it shines. Bhavānī too dwells here. Therefore, O Goddess, I have not said much about this holy place.

## \|\| 2.7.39 \|\|

*tasmiñjale snānaparo naro yadi saṃdhyāṃ vidhāyānu karoti tarpaṇam \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca dadāti dakṣiṇāṃ bhavodbhavaṃ paśyati mucyate bhavāt \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. If after bathing in its water, a man, after performing Sandhyā (-prayer) gratifying (deities), offers a Śrāddha to the dead ancestors, gives dakṣiṇā (to Brāhmaṇas), sees the (place of) rise of Bhava, is liberated from the worldly (existence).

## \|\| 2.7.40 \|\|

*atha yadi bhavapūjāṃ divyapuṣpaiḥ karoti tadanu śivaśiveti stotrapāṭhaṃ ca gītam \|*  
*suravara gaṇavṛndaiḥ stūyamāno vimānaiḥ suravaraśivarūpo mānavo yāti nākam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. If a man worships Bhava with divine flowers, then sings the text of the hymn ‘Śiva, Śiva’, he, being praised by the groups of Śiva’s attendants, goes, being of the form of Śiva, the excellent god, to Heaven, (being carried by) aeroplanes.

## Chapter 8 - Propitiation of Rudra by Brahmā

## \|\| 2.8.1-2 \|\|

*bhojarāja uvāca \|*  
*prabho sārasvata mayā śrutaṃ māhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*vastrāpathasya kṣetrasya gire raivatakasya ca \|\| 1 \|\|*

*viśeṣeṇa svarṇarekhābhavasya ca jalasya ca \|*  
*idānīṃ śrotumicchāmi tīrthotpattiṃ vadasva me \|\| 2 \|\|*

King Bhoja said:

1-2. O Lord Sārasvata, I have listened to the excellent (description of the) greatness of the holy place Vastrāpatha and also of the Raivataka mountain, especially of the water of Svarṇarekhā. Now I desire to listen to the creation of the holy place. Please tell it to me.

## \|\| 2.8.3 \|\|

*brahmaviṣṇuśivādīnāṃ madhye ko'yaṃ vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*keyaṃ nadī svarṇarekhā sarvapātakanāśinī \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Who is the one that is placed in the midst of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva? What is this river Svarṇarekhā, destroying all sins?

## \|\| 2.8.4 \|\|

*kasmādbrahmādayā devā asmiṃstīrthe samāgatāḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ nārāyaṇo devaḥ svayameva samāgataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Why have Gods like Brahma come to this holy place? How is it that God Nārāyaṇa (i.e. Viṣṇu) has himself come here?

## \|\| 2.8.5 \|\|

*hemālayaṃ parityajya bhavānī girimūrddhani \|*  
*saṃsthitā skandamādāya devairindrādibhiḥ saha \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. (How is it that) abandoning her golden abode, Bhavānī, bringing Kārttikeya with her, stays here along with gods like Indra?

## \|\| 2.8.6 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu sarvaṃ mahārāja kathayiṣye savistaram \|*  
*yena vai kathyamānena sarvapāpakṣayo bhavet \|\| 6 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

6\. O great king, listen to the full (account). I shall tell you, in detail; by telling it all the sins will end.

## \|\| 2.8.7 \|\|

*purā brahmadinasyāṃte jagadetaccarācaram \|*  
*saṃhṛtya bhagavānrudro brahmaviṣṇupuraskṛtaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Formerly at the end of Brahmā’s Day, Rudra withdrew this world with the movable and immovable objects. He was honoured by Brahmā and Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.8.8 \|\|

*tāṃ ca te sakalāṃ rātrimekamūrttibhavāstrayaḥ \|*  
*tiṣṭhanti rātri paryante punarbhinnā bhavaṃti te \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. All that night the three had become one figure; they remained like that till the end of the Night, and again became separate.

## \|\| 2.8.9 \|\|

*brahmaviṣṇuśivā devā rajaḥsattvatamomayāḥ \|*  
*sṛṣṭiṃ karoti bhagavānbrahmā pālayate hariḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The (three) gods, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva, were full of Rajas (passion), Sattva (goodness) and Tamas (ignorance). Venerable Brahmā brought about the creation; Hari protected it.

## \|\| 2.8.10 \|\|

*sarvaṃ saṃharate rudro jagatkālapramāṇataḥ \|*  
*tenādau bhagavānsṛṣṭo dakṣo nāma prajāpatiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Rudra withdraws the entire (creation) according to the measure of the period of the world. He first created the revered Dakṣa, the lord of created beings.

## \|\| 2.8.11 \|\|

*sarve saṃkṣepataḥ kṛtvā brahmāṇḍaṃ sacarā caram \|*  
*bhinnā devāstrayo jātāḥ satyalokavyavasthitāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. They all, having made the universe together with the movable and the immovable, the three gods, became separate, and remained in Satyaloka.

## \|\| 2.8.12 \|\|

*trayo bhuvaṃ samāsādya kautukāviṣṭacetasaḥ \|*  
*kailāsaṃ te girivaraṃ samārūḍhāḥ surervṛtāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. With their minds full of curiosity, the three having reached the earth, surrounded by gods, climbed the excellent mountain Kailāśa.

## \|\| 2.8.13 \|\|

*ahaṃ jyeṣṭho ahaṃ jyeṣṭho vādo'bhūdbrahmarudrayoḥ \|*  
*tadā kruddho mahādevo brahmāṇaṃ hantumudyataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A dispute arose between Brahmā and Rudra, (both saying:) ‘I am the most senior’. Then Mahādeva, (getting) angry, was eager to kill Brahmā.

## \|\| 2.8.14 \|\|

*viṣṇunā vārito brahmā na te vādastu yujyate \|*  
*tattvaṃ nāhaṃ yadā nedaṃ brahmāṃḍaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Brahmā was warded off by Viṣṇu, saying, “Dispute is not proper for you. Neither you nor I was there, when this universe with the movable and immovable objects, was not there.

## \|\| 2.8.15 \|\|

*eka eva tadā devo jale śete maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*jāgarti ca yadā devaḥ svecchayā kautukāttataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. “Lord Maheśvara alone lay in the water. When the God was awake willingly, he through curiosity first created you and then me.

## \|\| 2.8.16 \|\|

*anena tvaṃ kṛtaḥ pūrvamahaṃ paścāttvayā kṛtaḥ \|*  
*brahmāṃḍaṃ kūrmarūpeṇa dhṛtamasya prasādataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. “Due to his favour the universe was held (by me) in the form of tortoise.

## \|\| 2.8.17 \|\|

*anupraviṣṭā brahmāṃḍaṃ prasādācchaṃ karasya ca \|*  
*sṛṣṭistvayā kṛtā sarvā mayi rakṣā vyavasthitā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. “Entry was made into the universe due to Śaṅkara’s favour also. The entire creation was fashioned by you and its protection was entrusted to me.

## \|\| 2.8.18 \|\|

*udāsīnavadāsīnaḥ saṃsārātsāramīkṣate \|*  
*eka eva śivo devaḥ sarvavyāpī maheśvaraḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. “God Śiva is one only, the omnipresent Great Lord.

## \|\| 2.8.19 \|\|

*pitāmahatvaṃ saṃjātaṃ prasādācchaṃkarasya te \|*  
*prasādayāmāsa haraṃ śrutvā brahmā vaco hareḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. “One seated like one that is indifferent, sees the best from the worldly existence. The status of the grandsire is made in your case due to “Śaṅkara’s grace.” Hearing the words of Viṣṇu Brahmā propitiated Hara.

## \|\| 2.8.20 \|\|

*anādinidhano devo bahuśīrṣo mahābhujaḥ \|*  
*ityādivedavacanaistatastuṣṭo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*prāha brahmanvaraṃ yatte vṛṇīṣva manasi sthitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Maheśvara was then pleased by such Vedic words as ‘One without a beginning or an end’, ‘the God with many heads’, ‘the one with great arms.’ He said: “O Brahman, ask for the boon that is in your mind.”

## Chapter 9 - The Rise of Bhava

## \|\| 2.9.1-2 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*yadi sṛṣṭaṃ mayā sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*tadā mūrtimimāṃ tyaktvā bhavaḥ sṛṣṭo mayā'dhunā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*pitāmahamahattvaṃ syāttathā śīghraṃ vidhīyatām \|*  
*brahmaṇo vacanaṃ śrutvā viṣṇunā sa pramoditaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

1-2. When I created the entire group of the three worlds with the movable and the immovable, I gave up this form and now created Bhava so quickly that by it there would be the greatness of the Grandsire.

Hearing the words of Brahma Viṣṇu pleased him.

## \|\| 2.9.3 \|\|

*mahadāścaryajanake saṃprāpto girimūrddhani \|*  
*na vicārastvayākāryaḥ karttavyaṃ brahmabhāṣitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He reached the top of the mountain that gave rise to great wonders. (He said to Śiva): “You should not entertain any thought. Do as is told by Brahmā.”

## \|\| 2.9.4 \|\|

*tathetyuktvā śivo devastatraivāṃtaradhīyata \|*  
*brahmā yayau meruśṛṃgaṃ manasaḥ śirasi sthitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Saying “All right”, God Śiva disappeared there only. Brahmā went to the peak of the mountain situated at the top of the mind (manalaḥ śirasi sthitām)?

## \|\| 2.9.5-6 \|\|

*tapastepe prajānātho vedoccāraṇatatparaḥ \|*  
*atharvavedoccaraṇaṃ yāvaccakre pitāmahaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*mukhādrudraḥ samabhavadraudrarūpo bhavāpahaḥ \|*  
*arddhanārīnaravapurduṣprekṣyo'tibhayaṃkaraḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. The Lord of the created beings, engaged in the recitation of the Veda, performed penance. When the Grandsire uttered (the words of) the Atharva Veda, from his mouth was created Rudra, of a fearful form and the destroyer of the worldly existence. He had the form of half woman and half man and was of a terrible appearance causing extreme fright.

## \|\| 2.9.7 \|\|

*vibhajātmānamityuktvā brahmā cāṃtardadhe bhayāt \|*  
*tathoktosau dvidhā strītvaṃ puruṣatvaṃ tathā'karot \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. “Divide yourself”, saying so, Brahmā vanished through fear. Told like this, He divided himself into two, woman and man.

## \|\| 2.9.8 \|\|

*bibheda puruṣatvaṃ ca daśadhā caikadhā punaḥ \|*  
*ekādaśaite kathitā rudrāstribhuvaneśvarāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He divided the man-form (first) into ten forms, and again one. These are called the eleven Rudras, the lords of the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.9.9-10 \|\|

*kṛtvā nāmāni sarveṣāṃ devakārye niyojitāḥ \|*  
*vibhajya punarīśānī svātmānaṃ śaṃkarādvibhoḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*mahādevaniyogena pitāmahamupasthitā \|*  
*tāmāha bhagavānbrahmā dakṣasya duhitā bhava \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Giving names to all (of them) they were appointed to do God’s work. Again Īśānī, separating herself from Lord Śaṅkara, attended upon the Grandsire by the order of Mahādeva. Revered Brahmā said to her: “Be the daughter of Dakṣa.”

## \|\| 2.9.11 \|\|

*sāpi tasya niyogena prādurāsītprajāpateḥ \|*  
*niyogādbrahmaṇo dakṣo dadau rudrāya tāṃ satīm \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. She too, by his command appeared from Prajāpati. By Brahmā’s command Dakṣa gave that Satī (virtuous girl) to Rudra.

## \|\| 2.9.12 \|\|

*dākṣīṃ rudro'pi jagrāha svakīyāmeva śūlabhṛt \|*  
*atha brahmā babhāṣe taṃ sṛṣṭiṃ kuru satīpate \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Rudra, the holder of the trident, accepted her as his own. Then Brahmā said to him: “O Lord of Satī, bring forth the creation.”

## \|\| 2.9.13 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*sṛṣṭirmayā na karttavyā karttavyā bhavatā svayam \|*  
*pālanaṃ viṣṇunā kāryaṃ saṃhartā'haṃ vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

Rudra said:

13\. I shall not bring forth the creation. You yourself bring it forth. I am fixed as the destroyer.

## \|\| 2.9.14 \|\|

*sthāṇuvatsaṃsthito yasmā ttasmātsthāṇurbhavāmyaham \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Since I remain as a branchless trunk (of a tree), therefore I am Sthāṇu.

## \|\| 2.9.15 \|\|

*rajorūpāḥ sattvarūpāstamorūpāśca ye narāḥ \|*  
*sarve te bhavatā kāryā guṇatrayavibhāgataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. You have to fashion, according to the division based on their qualities, all men that are passionate, good or ignorant.

## \|\| 2.9.16 \|\|

*yadā te tāmasaiḥ kāryaṃ tadā raudro bhava svayam \|*  
*yadā te rājasaiḥ kāryaṃ tadā tvaṃ rājaso bhava \|*  
*sāttvikaiste yadā kāryaṃ tadā tvaṃ sāttviko bhava \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. When you have to deal with the ignorant (tāmasaiḥ) you become fearful yourself. When you have to deal with the passionate (rājasaiḥ) you become passionate. When you have to deal with the good (sāttvikaiḥ) you become good.

## \|\| 2.9.17-18 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*ityājñāpya ca brahmāṇaṃ svayaṃ sṛṣṭyādikarmasu \|*  
*gṛhītvā tāṃ satīṃ rudraḥ kailāsamadhitiṣṭhati \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dakṣaḥ kālena mahatā harasyālayamāyayau \|\| 18 \|\|*

The Lord (Īśvara) said:

17-18. Thus himself ordering Brahmā in acts like creation, Rudra, taking with him that Satī remained on Kailāśa. After a long time Dakṣa went to Hara’s abode.

## \|\| 2.9.19 \|\|

*atha rudraḥ samutthāya kṛtavāngauravaṃ bahu \|*  
*tato yathocitāṃ pūjāṃ na dakṣo bahu manyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Rudra got up and gave him great respect. Dakṣa did not give much value to that hospitality.

## \|\| 2.9.20 \|\|

*tadā vai tamasāviṣṭaḥ so'dhikaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ śubhaḥ \|*  
*pūjāmanarghyāmanvicchañjagāma kupito gṛham \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then that bright Brāhmaṇa was very much full of grief; and expecting a highly respectable hospitality, went home angry.

## \|\| 2.9.21 \|\|

*kadācittāṃ gṛhaṃ prāptāṃ satīṃ dakṣaḥ sudurmanāḥ \|*  
*bhartrā saha viniṃdyaināṃ bhartsayāmāsa vai ruṣā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Once that very dispirited Dakṣa, angrily censured Satī who had come to his house with her husband and reproached her:

## \|\| 2.9.22 \|\|

*paṃcavaktro daśabhujo mukhe netratrayānvitaḥ \|*  
*kaparddī khaṃḍacaṃdrosau tathāsau nīlalohitaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. “(Your husband) has five faces, ten arms and three eyes. He wears braided and matted hair; has a broken moon (on his head); so also he is dark-blue.

## \|\| 2.9.23 \|\|

*kapālī śūlahasto'sau gajacarmāvaguṃṭhitaḥ \|*  
*nāsya mātā na ca pitā na bhrātā na ca bāndhavaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. “He wears skulls, has a spear in his hand, is covered with elephant’s hide. He has no mother, no father, no brother, no relative.

## \|\| 2.9.24 \|\|

*sarpāsthimaṃḍitagrīvastyaktvā hemavibhūṣaṇam \|*  
*bhikṣayā bhojanaṃ yasya kathamannaṃ pradāsyati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. “Giving up golden ornaments, he has adorned his neck with serpents’ bones. (Who) will give food to him, who lives on alms?

## \|\| 2.9.25 \|\|

*kadācitpūrvato yāti gacchanyāti sa paścime \|*  
*dakṣiṇasyāṃ vṛṣo yāti svayaṃ yāti sa cottare \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. “While moving he sometimes walks in the eastern direction, sometimes in the western one; (His) bull goes in the southern direction,(but) he himself goes in the northern direction.

## \|\| 2.9.26 \|\|

*tiryagūrdhvamadho yāti naiva yāti na tiṣṭhati \|*  
*iti citraṃ caritraṃ te bhartturnānyasya dṛśyate \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. “He moves in a slanting manner, or above or, below. (Sometimes) he does not go at all (but) remains (at one place). Thus strange is your husband’s behaviour, as is not at all noticed in any other (individual).

## \|\| 2.9.27 \|\|

*nirguṇaḥ sa guṇātīto niḥsneho mūkavatsthitaḥ \|*  
*sarvajñaḥ sarvagaḥ sarvaḥ paṭhyate bhuvanatraye \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. “He is devoid of all (good) qualities, beyond all qualities. He has no affection; he remains like one that is dumb. In the three worlds he is mentioned as omniscient, omnipresent and all together.

## \|\| 2.9.28 \|\|

*kadācinnaiva jānāti na śṛṇoti na paśyati \|*  
*daityānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca rākṣasānāṃ dadāti yaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. “Perhaps, he who gives (desired objects) to demons (to Daityas, Dānavas and Rākṣasas), does not know (anything) at all, or does not listen to or see (anything) at all.

## \|\| 2.9.29 \|\|

*na cāsya ca pitā kaścinna ca bhrātāsti kaścana \|*  
*eka eva vṛṣārūḍho nagno bhramati bhūtale \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. “He has no father; he has no brother; He, the naked one, mounted on his bull; all alone roams on the surface of the earth.

## \|\| 2.9.30 \|\|

*na gṛhaṃ na dhanaṃ gotramanādinidhanovyayaḥ \|*  
*sthirabuddhirna caivāsau krīḍate bhuvanatraye \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. “He has no abode, no wealth, no family. He is without birth and death; he is immutable. He is not at all of a firm mind; and sports in the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.9.31 \|\|

*kadācitsatyaloke sau pātālamadhitiṣṭhati \|*  
*girisānuṣu śete'sāvaśivopi śivaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. “At times he is in Satyaloka; at times he resides in the nether world; he sleeps on mountain-peaks. Though inauspicious, he is said to be Lord Śiva (i.e. auspicious).

## \|\| 2.9.32 \|\|

*śrīkhaṃḍādīni saṃtyajya sadā bhasmāvaguṃṭhitaḥ \|*  
*sarvadeti vacaḥ satyaṃ kimanyatsa pradāsyati \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. “Giving up sandalwood etc. he is always smeared with ashes. (Only) his designation ‘Sarvadā’ (giver of everything) is true. What else will he give?

## \|\| 2.9.33 \|\|

*dhiktvāṃ jāmātaraṃ dhiktaṃ yayoḥ snehaḥ parasparam \|*  
*tasya tvaṃ vallabhā bhāryā sa ca prāṇādhikastava \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. “Fie upon you! Fie upon that son-in-law (and you) who love each other! You are his dear wife. You value him more than your own life.

## \|\| 2.9.34 \|\|

*na ca pitrāsti te kāryaṃ na mātrā na sakhīṣu ca \|*  
*kevalaṃ bhartṛbhaktā tvaṃ tasmādgaccha gṛhānmama \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. “You have nothing to do with your father, your mother, or your friends! You are only devoted to your husband. Therefore go (away) from my house.

## \|\| 2.9.35 \|\|

*anye jāmātaraḥ sarve bhartustava pinākinaḥ \|*  
*tvamadyaivāśu cāsmākaṃ gṛhādgaccha varaṃ prati \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. “There are other sons-in- law ṃan your husband. You today only go out of my house to your husband.”

## \|\| 2.9.36 \|\|

*tasya tadvākyamākarṇya sā devī śaṃkarapriyā \|*  
*viniṃdya pitaraṃ dakṣaṃ dhyātvā devaṃ maheśvaram \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Having heard these words of him, that goddess, dear to Śiva, condemning her father, Dakṣa, meditating on her Lord Maheśvara,

## \|\| 2.9.37 \|\|

*śvetavastrā jale snātvā dadāhātmānamātmanā \|*  
*yācitastu śivo bharttā punarjanmāṃtare tayā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. (put on) white garments, bathed in the water and burnt herself. She sought Śiva as her husband in the next birth:

## \|\| 2.9.38 \|\|

*pitā me himavānastu menāgarbhe bhavāmyaham \|*  
*atrāṃtare himavatā tapasā toṣito haraḥ \|*  
*pratyakṣaṃ darśanaṃ dattvā himavaṃtaṃ vaco'bravīt \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. “May my father be Himavat; I shall be in the womb of Menā.” In the meanwhile Himavat pleased Hara with penance. Actually presenting Himself before Himavat, he spoke (these) words:

## \|\| 2.9.39 \|\|

*eṣā dattā sutā tubhyaṃ pariṇeṣyāmi tāmaham \|*  
*devānāṃ kāryyasiddhyarthaṃ girirājo bhaviṣyasi \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. “I have presented this one as your daughter. I shall marry her. To accomplish the mission of gods you will be the Lord of mountains.”

## \|\| 2.9.40 \|\|

*ātmamūrttau praviṣṭāṃ tāṃ jñātvā devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*śaśāpa dakṣaṃ kupitaḥ samāgatyātha tadgṛham \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. God Maheśvara, knowing her to have entered His form, being angry, cursed Dakṣa, after coming to his house:

## \|\| 2.9.41 \|\|

*tyaktvā dehamimaṃ brāhmyaṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ kule bhava \|*  
*svāyaṃbhuvatvaṃ saṃtyajya dakṣa prācetaso bhava \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. “Giving up this body of a Brāhmaṇa, be (bom) in the family of Kṣatriyas. Giving up your status as Svayambhū (self-born), be Prācetas Dakṣa.

## \|\| 2.9.42 \|\|

*svasyāṃ sutāyāmūḍhāyāṃ putramutpādayiṣyasi \|*  
*evaṃ śaptvā mahādevo yayau kailāsaparvatam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. “You will produce a son on your married daughter.” Having cursed (Dakṣa) like this, Mahādeva went to the mountain, Kailāsa.

## \|\| 2.9.43 \|\|

*svāyabhuvo'pi kālena dakṣaḥ prācetaso'bhavat \|*  
*bhavānīṃ sa sutāṃ labdhvā giristuṣṭo himā layaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Svayambhuva also became Prācetas Dakṣa after (due) time. Mountain Himalaya, getting Bhavānī as his daughter, was pleased.

## \|\| 2.9.44 \|\|

*menāpi tāṃ sutāṃ labdhvā dhanyaṃ mene gṛhāśramam \|*  
*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā jāyamānāṃ ca svecchayaiva varānanām \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Menā too, obtaining her as her daughter, looked upon the order of a householder as blessed. Seeing that beautifulfaced one born of her own will,

## \|\| 2.9.45-48 \|\|

*menā himavataḥ patnī prāhedaṃ parvateśvaram \|*  
*paśya bālāmimāṃ rājanrājīvasadṛśānanām \|\| 45 \|\|*

*hitāya sarvabhūtānāṃ jātāṃ ca tapasā śubhām \|*  
*so'pi dṛṣṭvā mahādevīṃ taruṇādityasannibhām \|\| 46 \|\|*

*kapardinīṃ caturvaktrāṃ trinetrāmatilālasām \|*  
*aṣṭahastāṃ viśālākṣīṃ caṃdrāvayavabhūṣaṇām \|\| 47 \|\|*

*praṇamya śirasā bhūmau tejasā tu suvihvalaḥ \|*  
*bhītaḥ kṛtāṃjaliḥ stabdhaḥ provāca parameśvarīm \|\| 48 \|\|*

45-48. Menā, wife of Himavat, said these words to the Lord of Mountains: “O Lord, see this child, with a lotus-like face born for the good of all and auspicious due to penance.” He too, seeing the great goddess resembling a young swan, having braided and matted hair, having four faces, three eyes and very strong desire, having eight hands, broad eyes, having parts of her body like the moon, being very much beyond himself due to her lustre, was afraid. Being motionless, he said to the goddess.

## \|\| 2.9.49 \|\|

*himavānuvāca \|*  
*kā tvaṃ devi viśālākṣi śaṃsa me saṃśayo mahān \|\| 49 \|\|*

Himavān said:

49\. O you goddess of broad eyes, who are you? Tell me. I have a strong doubt.

## \|\| 2.9.50 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*māṃ viddhi paramāṃ śaktiṃ maheśvarasamāśrayām \|*  
*ananyāmavyayāmekāṃ yāṃ paśyaṃti mumukṣavaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

The goddess said:

50\. Know me to be the greatest power resorting to Maheśvara, whom those desirous of liberation look upon as unique, immutable and one (only).

## \|\| 2.9.51 \|\|

*divyaṃ dadāmi te cakṣuḥ paśya me rūpamaiśvaram \|*  
*etāvaduktvā vijñānaṃ dattvā himavate svayam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. I shall give you divine sight. See my divine form. Speaking this much the Goddess herself gave special power to Himavat.

## \|\| 2.9.52-57 \|\|

*sūryakoṭipratīkāśaṃ tejobiṃbaṃ nirākulam \|*  
*jvālā mālāsahasrāḍhyaṃ kālānalaśatopamam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*daṃṣṭrākarālamuddharṣaṃ jaṭāmaṃḍalamaṃḍitam \|*  
*praśāṃtaṃ saumyavadanamanaṃtāścaryasaṃyutam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*caṃdrāvayavalakṣmāṇaṃ caṃdrakoṭisamaprabham \|*  
*kirīṭinaṃ gadāhastaṃ nupurairupaśobhitam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*divyamālyāṃbaradharaṃ divyagaṃdhānulepanam \|*  
*śaṃkhacakradharaṃ kāmyaṃ trinetraṃ kṛttivāsasam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*aṃḍasthaṃ cāṃḍabāhyasthaṃ bāhyamabhyaṃtaraṃ param \|*  
*sarvaśaktimayaṃ śubhraṃ sarvālaṃkārasaṃyutam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*brahmendropendrayogīndrairvandyamāna padāṃbujam \|*  
*sarvataḥ pāṇipādāṃtaṃ sarvato'kṣiśiromukham \|\| 57 \|\|*

52-57. (Himavat) saw the Highest Lord, resembling crores of suns, an orb of light, clear, encompassed with the row of thousand flames, resembling hundreds of destructive fires at the end of the world, fearful due to the fangs, exciting, adorned with a mass of matted hair, very calm, of a mild face, full of endless wonders, having signs like the lunar digits, having lustre like that of crores of moons, having a crown, with a mace in his hand, adorned with anklets, having put on a divine chaplet and garments, having smeared the body with divine fragrant substances, holding a conch and a disc, desirable, having three eyes, clad in hide, residing in the Egg (of the universe) and out of it, being external, internal and the highest, full of all power, bright, (and adorned) with all ornaments, whose lotus-like feet were saluted by Brahmā, Indra, Upendra and best yogins, who reached everything with His hands and feet, and eyes, head and face, and who remained after having occupied everything.

## \|\| 2.9.58-62 \|\|

*sarvamāvṛtya tiṣṭhaṃtaṃ dadarśa parameśvaram \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā nandīśvaraṃ devaṃ devyā maheśvaraṃ param \|\| 58 \|\|*

*bhayena ca samāviṣṭaḥ sa rājā hṛṣṭamānasaḥ \|*  
*ātmanyādhāya cātmānamoṃkāraṃ samanusmaran \|\| 59 \|\|*

*nāmnāmaṣṭasahasreṇa stutvā'sau hima vāngiriḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*bhūyaḥ praṇamya bhūtātmā provācedaṃ kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*yadetadaiśvaraṃ rūpaṃ jātaṃ te parameśvari \|\| 61 \|\|*

*bhīto'smi sāṃprataṃ dṛṣṭvā tattvamanyatpradarśaya \|*  
*evamuktā ca sā devī tena śailena pārvatī \|\| 62 \|\|*

58-62. Seeing the Lord of Nandī, the highest one, i.e. Maheśvara, along with the Goddess, the king, Himālaya Mountain, full of fear and (at the same time) delighted in mind, concentrating himself, remembering Oṃkāra, praising Him with eight thousand epithets, again saluted him, and spoke with folded hands: “O highest goddess, I am now afraid of your divine form that has come up. So (please) show another (form).” That goddess Pārvatī, thus addressed by that Mountain,

## \|\| 2.9.63 \|\|

*saṃhṛtya darśayāmāsa svarūpamaparaṃ param \|*  
*nīlotpaladalaprakhyaṃ nīlotpalasugaṃdhikam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. having withdrawn that form, showed him another highest form. (It was) like the petal of a blue lotus; it had fragrance like blue lotus.

## \|\| 2.9.64 \|\|

*dvinetraṃ dvibhujaṃ saumyaṃ nīlālakavibhūṣitam \|*  
*raktapādāṃbujatalaṃ suraktakarapallavam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. It had two eyes (and) two arms; it was adorned with black hair. The soles of her lotus-like feet were red. Her tender hands were red.

## \|\| 2.9.65 \|\|

*śrīmadviśālasadvṛttaṃ lalāṭatilakojjvalam \|*  
*bhūṣitaṃ cārusarvāṃgaṃ bhūṣaṇairatikomalam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. It was graceful, large and well-covered. It was bright with a mark on the forehead. It was decorated; all its limbs were charming; it was very pleasing due to ornaments.

## \|\| 2.9.66 \|\|

*dadhānaṃ corasā mālāṃ viśālāṃ hemanirmitām \|*  
*īṣatsmitaṃ subiṃboṣṭhaṃ nūpurārāvaśobhitam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. On its bosom it had a big golden necklace. It had a gentle smile; its beautiful lips were like the bimba (a plant bearing bright red gourd—MW) fruit. It was graceful with the sound of the anklets.

## \|\| 2.9.67 \|\|

*prasannavadanaṃ divyaṃ cārubhrūmahimāspadam \|*  
*tadīdṛśaṃ samālokya svarūpaṃ śailasattamaḥ \|*  
*bhayaṃ saṃtyajya hṛṣṭātmā babhāṣe parameśvarīm \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Its face was pleasing; it was wonderful; it was the abode of glory due to charming eyebrows. Seeing such a form the best Mountain (Himavat), gave up his fear, and with a pleased mind said to the goddess.

## \|\| 2.9.68 \|\|

*himavānuvāca \|*  
*adya me saphalaṃ janma adya me saphalāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*yanme sākṣāttvamavyaktā prasannā dṛṣṭigocarā \|*  
*idānīṃ kiṃ mayā kāryaṃ tanme brūhi maheśvari \|\| 68 \|\|*

Himavān said:

68\. Today my life is fruitful. So also my acts are fruitful, since you, the invisible one, (being) pleased have become visible to me. O great goddess, tell me what should be done by me now.

Maheśvarī spoke:

## \|\| 2.9.69 \|\|

*maheśvaryuvāca \|*  
*śivapūjā tvayā kāryā dhyānena tapasā sadā \|*  
*ahaṃ tasmai pradātavyā kenacitkāraṇena vai \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. By means of meditation and penance you should always worship Śiva. And for some reason or other, I should be given to him (in marriage).

## \|\| 2.9.70 \|\|

*yādṛśastu tvayā dṛṣṭo dhyeyo vai tādṛśastvayā \|*  
*eka eva śivo devaḥ sarvādhāro dharādharaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Meditate upon him as you have seen him. Śiva is the one God that is the prop of all and that sustains the earth.

## \|\| 2.9.71 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*tapaśca kṛtavānrudraḥ samāgamya himācalam \|*  
*tasyomā paramāṃ bhaktiṃ cakāra śivasaṃnidhau \|\| 71 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

71\. Having come to Himālaya, Rudra practised penance. In the vicinity of Śiva, Umā remained greatly devoted to him.

## \|\| 2.9.72 \|\|

*devakāryeṇa kenāpi devo vai jñāpitaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*upayeme haro devīmumāṃ tribhuvaneśvarīm \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. The Lord was informed that some mission of God, was to be carried out. Hara married Goddess Umā, the ruler of the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.9.73 \|\|

*sa śaptaḥ śaṃbhunā pūrvaṃ dakṣaḥ prācetaso nṛpaḥ \|*  
*viniṃdya pūrvavaireṇa gaṃgādvāre'yajaddharim \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. King Prācetas Dakṣa was formerly cursed by Śaṃbhu. Having condemned Him due to former enmity Dakṣa worshipped Hari at Gaṅgādvāra (i.e. Haridvāra).

## \|\| 2.9.74 \|\|

*devāśca yajñabhāgārthamāhūtā viṣṇunā svayam \|*  
*sahaiva munibhiḥ sarvairāgatā munipuṃgavāḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Viṣṇu himself invited all gods for a share in the sacrifice. Prominent sages arrived (there) just with all sages.

## \|\| 2.9.75 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā devakulaṃ kṛtsnaṃ śaṃkareṇa vinā'gatam \|*  
*dadhīco nāma viprarṣiḥ prācetasamathābravīt \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Seeing the entire group of gods that had come there without Śaṅkara, the Brāhmaṇa sage named Dadhīci said to Prācetas.

## \|\| 2.9.76 \|\|

*dadhīciruvāca \|*  
*brahmādyāstu piśācāṃtā yasyājñānuvidhāyinaḥ \|*  
*sa hi vaḥ sāṃprataṃ rudro vidhinā kiṃ na pūjyate \|\| 76 \|\|*

Dadhīci said:

76\. (All) beginning with Brahmā and ending with goblins obey Rudra’s orders. Why do you not now worship Him in the (proper) manner?

## \|\| 2.9.77 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*sarveṣveva hi yajñeṣu na bhāgaḥ parikalpitaḥ \|*  
*na maṃtrā bhāryayā sārddhaṃ śaṃkarasyeti neṣyate \|\| 77 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:

77\. A share is not assigned to Him in all sacrifices (for Śaṅkara). Hymns are not offered to Śaṅkara with his wife. This is not desired (i.e. not desirable).

## \|\| 2.9.78 \|\|

*vihasya dakṣaṃ kupito vacaḥ prāha mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*śṛṇvatāṃ sarvadevānāṃ sarvajñānamayaḥ svayam \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Laughing at Dakṣa, the great sage (Dadhīci) possessing all (kinds of) knowledge himself said, where all the gods were listening:

## \|\| 2.9.79 \|\|

*yataḥ pravṛttirviśvātmā yaścāsau bhuvaneśvaraḥ \|*  
*na tvaṃ pūjayase rudraṃ devaiḥ saṃpūjyate haraḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. “You are not worshipping that Rudra, from whom is the origin (of the world) and who is the Lord of the world. He (i.e. Hara) is worshipped (even) by gods.”

## \|\| 2.9.80 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*asthimālādharo nagnaḥ saṃhartā tāmaso haraḥ \|*  
*viṣakaṃṭhaḥ śūlahastaḥ kapālī nāgaveṣṭitaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:

80\. Hara puts on a string of bones. He is naked. He is the destroyer. He is vicious. He has poison in his throat; has a trident in his hand. He wears skulls. He is encircled by serpents.

## \|\| 2.9.81 \|\|

*īśvaro hi jagatsraṣṭā prabhuryo'sau sanātanaḥ \|*  
*sattvātmako'sau bhagavānijyate sarvakarmasu \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. The Lord, who is the eternal master, is the Creator of the world. He is of a good nature. He, the venerable one, is worshipped in all religious rites.

## \|\| 2.9.82 \|\|

*dadhīciruvāca \|*  
*kiṃ tvayā bhagavāneṣa sahasrāṃśurna dṛśyate \|*  
*sarvalokaikasaṃhartā kālātmā parameśvaraḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

Dadhīci said:

82\. Do you not see this venerable one, the highest lord, of a thousand rays, the only destroyer of all worlds, the Supreme Spirit?

## \|\| 2.9.83 \|\|

*eṣa rudro mahādevaḥ kaparddī cāgraṇīrharaḥ \|*  
*ādityo bhagavānsūryo nīlagrīvo vilohitaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. This Rudra is Mahādeva (the great god). He wears braided and matted hair. He is the leader. (This) Hara is Āditya, the revered Sun; has a dark-blue throat, and is of a purple colour.

## \|\| 2.9.84 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*ya ete dvādaśādityā āgatā yajñabhāginaḥ \|*  
*sarve sūryā iti jñeyā na hyanyo vidyate raviḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:

84\. These twelve Ādityas, having a share in the sacrifice, that have come should all be known as the Suns. There is no other Sun.

## \|\| 2.9.85 \|\|

*evamukte tu munayaḥ samāyātā didṛkṣavaḥ \|*  
*bāḍhamityabruvandakṣaṃ tasya sāhāyyakāriṇaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. When it was spoken like thus, the sages came with a desire to see (the sacrifice). Saying ‘Very well’ to Dakṣa they helped him.

## \|\| 2.9.86 \|\|

*tapasāviṣṭamanaso na paśyaṃti vṛṣadhvajam \|*  
*sahasraśo'tha śataśo bahuśo'tha ya eva hi \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. With their minds engrossed in penance, they were there in thousands, hundreds, and in great numbers.

## \|\| 2.9.87 \|\|

*devāṃśca sarve bhāgārthamāgatā vāsavādayaḥ \|*  
*nāpaśyandevamīśānamṛte nārāyaṇaṃ harim \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. All gods like Indra and others, came there for their (sacrificial) portion. They did not see Lord Śiva, except Nārāyaṇa Han.

## \|\| 2.9.88-89 \|\|

*rudraṃ krodhaparaṃ dṛṣṭvā brahmā brahmāsanādyayau \|*  
*antarhite bhagavati dakṣo nārāyaṇaṃ harim \|\| 88 \|\|*

*rakṣakaṃ jagatāṃ devaṃ jagāma śaraṇaṃ svayam \|*  
*pravartayāmāsa ca taṃ yajñaṃ dakṣo'tha nirbhayaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

88-89. Seeing Rudra to be angry, Brahma went (away) from His seat. When the Lord had disappeared, Dakṣa surrendered himself to Nārāyaṇa, Hari (i.e. Viṣṇu), the protector of the world; and Dakṣa, being fearless, proceeded wiith the sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.9.90 \|\|

*rakṣako bhagavānviṣṇuḥ śaraṇāgatarakṣakaḥ \|*  
*punaḥ prāhādhvare dakṣaṃ dadhīco bhagavannṛpa \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Fearless Viṣṇu, the protector of those who submit to him, protected (the sacrifice). Revered, fearless, Dadhīca again said to Dakṣa in the sacrifice:

## \|\| 2.9.91-92 \|\|

*nirbhayaḥ śṛṇu dakṣa tvaṃ yajñabhaṃgo bhavi ṣyati \|*  
*apūjyapūjanāddakṣa pūjyasya ca vivarjanāt \|\| 91 \|\|*

*naraḥ pāpamavāpnoti mahadvai nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*asatāṃ pragraho yatra satāṃ caiva vimānatā \|\| 92 \|\|*

91-92. “Listen, O Dakṣa, there will be the destruction of the sacrifice. O Dakṣa, by worshipping those who do not deserve to be worshipped, and by avoiding (to worship) the deserving, a man acquires great sin. There is no doubt about this. A fearful punishment is inflicted by God when the bad are accepted and the good are insulted.

## \|\| 2.9.93 \|\|

*daṇḍo devakṛtastatra sadyaḥ patati dāruṇaḥ \|*  
*evamuktvā sa viprarṣiḥ śaśāpeśvaravidviṣaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. “Severe divine punishment will suddenly fall (on you).” Speaking like this, the Brāhmaṇa-sage cursed the haters of the Lord:

## \|\| 2.9.94 \|\|

*yasmādbahiṣkṛto devo bhavadbhiḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyadhvaṃ trayībāhyāḥ sarve'pīśvaravidviṣaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. “Since you excluded the Highest Lord, all of you, haters of the Lord, will be excluded from the (fold of) three Vedas.

## \|\| 2.9.95-96 \|\|

*mithyārītisamācārā mithyājñānaprabhāṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*prāpte kaliyuge ghore kalijaiḥ kila pīḍitāḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

*kṛtvā tapobalaṃ ghoraṃ gacchadhvaṃ narakaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati hṛṣīkeśaḥ svāmī vo'pi parāṅmukhaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

95-96. “Having wrong customs and behaviour, talking through ignorance, you, when the Kali age has arrived, being certainly tormented by those born in Kali (age), having had a severe power of penance, go again to hell. Your Lord Hṛṣīkeśa also will be averse to you.”

## \|\| 2.9.97 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā sa brahmarṣirvirarāma taponidhiḥ \|*  
*jagāma manasā rudramaśeṣādhvaranāśanam \|\| 97 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

97\. Speaking like this, that Brāhmaṇa-sage, store of penance, ceased (speaking). He mentally went to Rudra, the destroyer of the entire sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.9.98 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare devī mahādevaṃ maheśvaram \|*  
*gatvā vijñāpayāmāsa jñātvā dakṣamakhaṃ śivā \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. In the meanwhile, Goddess Śiva, going to the great God, Maheśvara, and knowing about Dakṣa’s sacrifice, respectfully said to him:

## \|\| 2.9.99 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*dakṣo yajñena yajate pitā me pūrvajanmani \|*  
*tena tvaṃ dūṣitaḥ pūrvamahaṃ cātīva duḥkhitā \|*  
*vināśayasva taṃ yajñaṃ varamenaṃ vṛṇomyaham \|\| 99 \|\|*

The Goddess said:

99\. Dakṣa, my father in the former existence, is performing a sacrifice. Formerly he had blamed you; and I am very much pained. (Please) destroy that sacrifice. I ask for this boon.

## \|\| 2.9.100 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ vijñāpito devyā devadevo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*sasarja sahasā rudraṃ dakṣayajñajighāṃsayā \|\| 100 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

100\. Maheśvara, the Lord of Gods, thus entreated by the Goddess, at once produced Rudra, with a desire to destroy Dakṣa’s sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.9.101 \|\|

*sahasraśirasaṃ krūraṃ sahasrākṣaṃ mahābhujam \|*  
*sahasrapāṇiṃ durddharṣaṃ yugāṃtānalasannibham \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. He had a thousand heads; he was cruel; he had a thousand eyes and large arms. He had a thousand hands. He was difficult to restrain. He resembled the fire at the end of the age of the world.

## \|\| 2.9.102 \|\|

*daṃṣṭrākarālaṃ duṣprekṣyaṃ śaṃkhacakradharaṃ prabhum \|*  
*daṇḍahastaṃ mahānādaṃ śārṅgiṇaṃ bhūtibhūṣaṇam \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. He had terrible tusks; he was difficult to look at. He, the mighty one, held a conch and a disc. He had a staff in his hand. He made a large sound. He was an archer, having ashes as his decoration.

## \|\| 2.9.103 \|\|

*vīrabhadra iti khyātaṃ devadevasamanvitam \|*  
*sa jātamātro deveśamupatasthe kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. He was known as ‘Vīrabhadra’, and was accompanied by the god of gods. The moment he was born, he, with folded hands, stood by the Lord of gods.

## \|\| 2.9.104 \|\|

*tamāha dakṣasya makhaṃ vināśaya śamastu taṃ \|*  
*vinindya māṃ sa yajate gaṃgādvāre gaṇeśvara \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. He (Maheśvara) said to him (Vīrabhadra): “Destroy Dakṣa’s sacrifice. May you have peace, O Lord of the Gaṇas, condemning me, he is performing a sacrifice at Gaṅgādvāra.”

## \|\| 2.9.105 \|\|

*tato baṃdhapramuktena siṃheneva ca līlayā \|*  
*vīrabhadreṇa dakṣasya nāśārthaṃ roma coddhutam \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Then, like a lion freed from bondage, Vīrabhadra easily uprooted a hair (from his body) to destroy Dakṣa.

## \|\| 2.9.106 \|\|

*romṇā sahasraśo rudrā nisṛṣṭāstena dhīmatā \|*  
*romajā iti vikhyātāstatra sāhāyyakāriṇaḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. The intelligent one produced thousands of Gaṇas with that hair. They, who helped him, are well-known as ‘Romaja’.

## \|\| 2.9.107-108 \|\|

*śūlaśaktigadāhastā daṇḍopalakarāstathā \|*  
*kālāgnirudrasaṃkāśā nādayanto diśo daśa \|\| 107 \|\|*

*sarve vṛṣasamārūḍhāḥ sabhā ryāścātibhīṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*samāśritya gaṇaśreṣṭhaṃ yayurdakṣamakhaṃ prati \|\| 108 \|\|*

107-108. They had spears, swords, maces in their hands; so also they had staffs and stones in their hands. They, resembling the destructive fire at the end of the world, Rudra, and filling with noise the ten quarters, mounted, along with their wives, bulls. They, very fearful, resorting to the greatest Gaṇa, went to Dakṣa’s sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.9.109-110 \|\|

*devāṃganāsahasrāḍhyamapsarogītināditam \|*  
*vīṇāveṇuninādāḍhyaṃ vedavādābhi nāditam \|\| 109 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā dakṣaṃ samāsīnaṃ devaibrahmarṣibhiḥ saha \|*  
*uvāca sa vṛṣārūḍho dakṣaṃ vīraḥ smayanniva \|\| 110 \|\|*

109-110. Seeing Dakṣa, surrounded by a thousand divine ladies, (engaged in listening to) the sound of songs sung by divine damsels, and of the sound of lutes and flutes, so also the sound of Vedic discussions, seated with gods and Brāhmaṇa sages, the brave hero, mounted on a bull, smilingly sad to Dakṣa:

## \|\| 2.9.111 \|\|

*vayaṃ hyacaturāḥ sarve śarvasyāmitate jasaḥ \|*  
*bhāgārthalipsayā prāptā bhāgānyaccha tvamīpsitān \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. “We all are not skilled like Śarva of unlimited lustre. We have come here with a desire for (our) shares. Give us the desired (shares).

## \|\| 2.9.112 \|\|

*bhāgo bhavadbhyo deyastu nāsmabhyamiti kathyatām \|*  
*tato vayaṃ viniścitya kariṣyāmo yathocitam \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. “The share is not to be given to you, but to us’—Say (this); then we, having decided (among ourselves) shall do what is proper.”

## \|\| 2.9.113 \|\|

*evamuktā gaṇeśena prajāpatipuraḥsarāḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Thus addressed by the Lord of the Gaṇas, gods, led by Prajāpati, said:

## \|\| 2.9.114 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*pramāṇaṃ no vijānītha bhāgaṃ maṃtrā iti dhuvam \|\| 114 \|\|*

Gods said:

114\. O Incantations, you do not certainly know the measure of share.

## \|\| 2.9.115 \|\|

*maṃtrā ūcuḥ \|*  
*surā yūyaṃ tamobhūtāstamopahatacetasaḥ \|*  
*ye nādhvarasya rājānaṃ pūjayeyurmaheśvaram \|\| 115 \|\|*

The Incantations said:

115\. O gods, you, who would not worship Maheśvara, the king of the sacrifice, are ignorant; your minds are struck with Tamas (ignorance).

## \|\| 2.9.116 \|\|

*īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ sarvadevatanurharaḥ \|*  
*gaṇa uvāca \|*  
*pūjyate sarvayajñeṣu kathaṃ dakṣo na pūjayet \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. Hara is the Lord of all beings, the body of all gods. He is worshipped in all sacrifices. How is it that Dakṣa would not worship him?

## \|\| 2.9.117 \|\|

*maṃtrāḥ pramāṇaṃ na kṛtā yuṣmābhirbalagarvitaiḥ \|*  
*yasmādasahyaṃ tasmānno nāśayāmyadya garvitam \|\| 117 \|\|*

Gaṇa said:

117\. You, proud of your power, have not regarded the Incantations as the authority. Since this is unbearable, I shall today destroy your pride.

## \|\| 2.9.118 \|\|

*ityuktvā yajñaśālāṃ tāṃ devo'hangaṇapuṃgavaḥ \|*  
*gaṇeśvarāśca saṃkruddhā yūpānutpāṭya cikṣipuḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. Speaking like this that best Gaṇa struck down the sacrificial hall. The lordly Gaṇas too, who were very angry uprooted the sacrificial posts and threw them.

## \|\| 2.9.119 \|\|

*prastotāraṃ sahotāramadhvaryuṃ ca gaṇeśvaraḥ \|*  
*gṛhītvā bhīṣaṇāḥ sarve gaṃgāsrotasi cikṣipuḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. The chief Gaṇa (and other Gaṇas) all being fearful, seized the sacrificial priest assisting the Udgātṛ, and the sacrificial priest reciting the hymns of the Ṛgveda, and threw them into the stream of Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 2.9.120-121 \|\|

*vīrabhadro'pi dīptātmā vajrayuktaṃ karaṃ hareḥ \|*  
*vyaṣṭaṃbhayadadīnātmā tathānyeṣāṃ divaukasām \|\| 120 \|\|*

*bhaganetre tathotpāṭya karāgreṇaiva līlayā \|*  
*nihatya muṣṭinā daṃḍaiḥ saptāśvaṃ ca nyapātayat \|\| 121 \|\|*

120-121. Vīrabhadra with his mind ablaze struck down the hand of Indra holding the Vajra. He, the giver of fearlessness to the wretched souls, and to others, the residents of Heaven, easily uprooted the eyes of Bhaga and struck down Saptāśva (Sun) with a stroke of his fist.

## \|\| 2.9.122 \|\|

*tathā caṃdramasaṃ devaṃ pādāṃguṣṭhena līlayā \|*  
*dharṣayāmāsa valavānsmayamāno gaṇeśvaraḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. The strong, smiling Lord of the Gaṇas easily assailed, with his toe, god Candra.

## \|\| 2.9.123 \|\|

*vahnerhastadvayaṃ chittvā jihvāmutpāṭya līlayā \|*  
*jaghāna mūrdhni pādena munīnapi munīśvarān \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. Cutting off the pair of hands of Vahni (Fire-god), and uprooting his tongue, he also struck the heads of sages and even lords of sages with his foot.

## \|\| 2.9.124 \|\|

*tathā viṣṇuṃ sagaruḍaṃ samāyātaṃ mahābalaḥ \|*  
*vivyādha niśitairbāṇaiḥ staṃbhayitvā sudarśanam \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. So also stopping handsome Viṣṇu who had come there with Garuḍa the strong one, stopped him and pierced him.

## \|\| 2.9.125 \|\|

*tataḥ sahasraśo bhadraḥ sasarja garuḍānbahūn \|*  
*vainateyādabhyadhikāngaruḍaṃ te pradudruvuḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. Then Bhadra produced many Garuḍas, stronger than Vainateya (the eagle that was Viṣṇu’s vehicle). They fled away.

## \|\| 2.9.126 \|\|

*tāndṛṣṭvā garuḍo dhīmānpalāyanaparo'bhavat \|*  
*tatsthito mādhavo vegādyathā gauḥ siṃhapīḍitā \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. Seeing them the intelligent Garuḍa became intent on fleeing, so also Viṣṇu seated on him, as a cow (flees) on being harassed by a lion.

## \|\| 2.9.127 \|\|

*aṃtarhite vainateye viṣṇau ca padmasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*āgatya vārayāmāsa vīrabhadraṃ śivapriyam \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. When Garuḍa and Viṣṇu disappeared, the Lotus-born (Brahmā) came there and warded off Vīrabhadra, dear to Śiva.

## \|\| 2.9.128 \|\|

*prasādayāmāsa sa taṃ gauravātparameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*te'dṛśyaṃ naiva jānaṃti rudraṃ tatrāgataṃ surāḥ \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. He (i.e. Vīrabhadra) propitiated Him, due to the greatness of the Highest Lord. The gods did not at all notice the invisible Rudra that had come there.

## \|\| 2.9.129 \|\|

*sa devo viṣṇunā jñāto brahmaṇā ca dadhīcinā \|*  
*tuṣṭāva bhagavānbrahmā dakṣo viṣṇudivaukasaḥ \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. The God (Rudra) was recognised by Viṣṇu, Brahmā, and Dadhīci. Brahmā, Dakṣa, and Viṣṇu and other gods praised Him.

## \|\| 2.9.130 \|\|

*viśeṣātpārvatīṃ devīmīśvarārddhaśarīriṇīm \|*  
*stotrairnānāvidhairdakṣaḥ praṇamya ca kṛtāñjaliḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. Especially they praised Goddess Pārvatī, occupying half the body of the Lord (Śiva). Dakṣa, (propitiating) Pārvatī with hymns of praise, saluted her with folded hands.

## \|\| 2.9.131 \|\|

*tato bhagavatī prāha prahasaṃtī maheśvaram \|*  
*tvameva jagataḥ sraṣṭā saṃhartā caiva rakṣakaḥ \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. Then the Goddess (Pārvatī), laughing, said to Maheśvara: “You alone are the creator, destroyer and protector of the world.

## \|\| 2.9.132 \|\|

*anugrāhyo bhagavatā dakṣaścāpi divau kasaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ prahasya bhagavānkarpaddī nīlalohitaḥ \|*  
*uvāca praṇatāndevāndakṣaṃ prācetasaṃ haraḥ \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. “The revered one should favour Dakṣa and the gods.” Then Lord Hara, wearing braided and matted hair, dark in complexion, said to the gods and Prācetas Dakṣa, who had bent before Him:

## \|\| 2.9.133 \|\|

*gacchadhvaṃ devatāḥ sarvāḥ prasanno bhavatāmaham \|*  
*saṃpūjyaḥ sarvayajñeṣu prathamaṃ devakarmaṇi \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. “O all deities, (You may) go. I am pleased with you. In all sacrifices and rites about deities, I should be worshipped first.

## \|\| 2.9.134 \|\|

*tvaṃ cāpi śṛṇu me dakṣa vacanaṃ sarvarakṣaṇam \|*  
*tyaktvā lokeṣaṇāmenāṃ madbhakto bhava yatnataḥ \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. “O Dakṣa, you too listen to my words. Giving up this worldly desire, be my devotee with efforts.

## \|\| 2.9.135 \|\|

*bhaviṣyasi gaṇeśānaḥ kalpāṃte'nugrahānmama \|*  
*tāvattiṣṭha mamādeśātsvādhikāreṣu nirvṛtaḥ \|*  
*ityuktvā'darśanaṃ prāpto dakṣasyāmitatejasaḥ \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. “With my favour you will be Gaṇeśāna at the end of the Kalpa. Till that time, being contented with your duty remain doing it by my order.” Saying this he disappeared from Dakṣa, of an unlimited lustre.

## \|\| 2.9.136 \|\|

*dadhīcinā śivo dṛṣṭo vijñaptaḥ śāpamocane \|*  
*kathaṃ śāpaṃ mayā dattaṃ tariṣyaṃti tavājñayā \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. Dadhīci saw Śiva and entreated him for freedom from the curse. “How will those be freed from the curse given by your order?”

## \|\| 2.9.137 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*bhaviṣyaṃti trayī bāhyāḥ saṃprāpte tu kalau yuge \|*  
*paṭhiṣyaṃti ca ye vedāste viprāḥ svargagāminaḥ \|\| 137 \|\|*

Śiva said:

137\. They will be out of the fold of the three Vedas. Those who, on the arrival of Kali age, will recite the Vedas, will go to Heaven.

## \|\| 2.9.138 \|\|

*āgamā viṣṇuracitāḥ paṭhyante ye dvijātibhiḥ \|*  
*tepi svargaṃ prayāsyaṃti matprasādānna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. When the Sacred writings composed by Viṣṇu are recited by Brāhmaṇas, they also will go to Heaven with my favour. There is no doubt about this.

## \|\| 2.9.139 \|\|

*kalikālaprabhāvena yeṣāṃ pāṭho na vidyate \|*  
*gṛhasthadharmācaraṇaṃ kartavyaṃ mama pūjanam \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. Those, who cannot recite (the Sacred Texts) due to the effect of the Kali age, should perform the duties of a householder and should worship me.

## \|\| 2.9.140 \|\|

*avaśyaṃ ca mayā kāryaṃ teṣāṃ pāpavimocanam \|*  
*bhikṣāṃ bhramāmi madhyāhne atīte bhasmaguṃṭhitaḥ \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. I shall certainly free them from their sins. When the midday is over, I besmeared with ashes, wander for alms.

## \|\| 2.9.141 \|\|

*jaṭājūṭadharaḥ śāṃto bhikṣāpātrakaro dvijaḥ \|*  
*yo dadāti ca me bhikṣāṃ svargaṃ yāti sa mānavaḥ \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. I am a Brāhmaṇa having twisted hair, appearing calm, and with a begging bowl in my hand. That man who gives me alms, goes to Heaven.

## \|\| 2.9.142 \|\|

*upānahau vā cchatraṃ vā kaupīnaṃ vā kamaṃḍalum \|*  
*yo dadāti tapasvibhyo naro muktaḥ sa pātakaiḥ \|*  
*dadhīceḥ sa varāndattvā vabhāṣe saha viṣṇunā \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. A man who gives a pair of sandals, an umbrella, a small piece of cloth for covering the privities, or a water-pot to ascetics, is freed from sins. Having granted boons to Dadhīci, he talked with Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.9.143 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*yaste mitraṃ sa me mitraṃ yaste ripuḥ sa me ripuḥ \|*  
*yastvāṃ pūjayate viṣṇo sa māṃ pūjayate dhruvam \|\| 143 \|\|*

Rudra said:

143\. He, who is your friend, is my friend. He, who is your enemy, is my enemy. O Viṣṇu, he who worships you, certainly worships me.

## \|\| 2.9.144 \|\|

*yaḥ stauti tvāṃ sa māṃ stauti priyo yaste sa me priyaḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ yatra ca tatra tvaṃ nāsti bhedaḥ parasparam \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. He, who extols you, extols me. He who is dear to you, is dear to me. You are there where I am. There is no difference between us.

## \|\| 2.9.145-148 \|\|

*kṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*evametatparaṃ deva vaktavyaṃ yattathaiva tat \|*  
*arddhanārīnaravapuryadā dṛṣṭo mayā purā \|\| 145 \|\|*

*neyaṃ nārī mayā dṛṣṭā dṛṣṭaṃ rūpaṃ kilātmanaḥ \|*  
*śaṃkhacakragadāhastaṃ vanamālāvibhūṣitam \|\| 146 \|\|*

*śrīvatsāṃkaṃ pītavastraṃ kaustubhena virāji tam \|*  
*dvitīyārddhaṃ mayā dṛṣṭaṃ śūlahastaṃ trilocanam \|\| 147 \|\|*

*caṃdrāvayavasaṃyuktaṃ jaṭājūṭakapālinam \|*  
*ekībhāvaṃ prapannohaṃ yathā pūrvaṃ tathā'dhunā \|*  
*na māṃ gaurī prapaśyeta prapaśyāmi tathaiva ca \|\| 148 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:

145-148. O God, this statement is thus final. It is as it should be. When, formerly, I saw you having half the body of a woman (i.e. Pārvatī), and half of Naṭeśvara, I did not see the lady (i.e. Pārvatī), but saw my own form, having in my hands, the conch, disc and mace, adorned with a garland of wood-flowers, having a mark on my chest, clad in a yellow garment, and adorned with Kaustubha gem. The other half I saw having a trident in his hand, three eyes, having lunar digits, mass of twisted hair and a skull. I have now reached union as before. I am not seeing this as Gaurī, but am seeing (your form) as before.

## \|\| 2.9.149 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*āvayoraṃtaraṃ nāsti caikarūpāvubhāvapi \|*  
*yo jānāti sa jānāti satyalokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 149 \|\|*

The Lord (i.e. Śiva) said:

149\. There is no difference between us. We both are of one form. He who knows (this) knows (the truth). He goes to Satyaloka.

## \|\| 2.9.150 \|\|

*ityuktvā sa yayau tatra kailāsaṃ parvatottamam \|*  
*kṛṣṇopi maṃdaraṃ prāpto devakāryeṇa kenacit \|\| 150 \|\|*

150\. Saying so he went there (i.e.) to the best Mountain, Kailāsa. To carry out some mission of the gods, Kṛṣṇa (i.e. Viṣṇu) too reached Mandāra.

## \|\| 2.9.151 \|\|

*atrāṃtare daityarājo mahādevaprasādataḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyanetratanayo bādhatesau jagattrayam \|\| 151 \|\|*
