151\. In the meanwhile, the demon-king, Hiraṇyanetra’s son, harassed the three worlds, through Mahādeva’s favour.

## \|\| 2.9.152-154 \|\|

*amaratvaṃ harāllabdhvā kāmāṃdho naiva paśyati \|*  
*harāṃgadhāriṇīṃ devīṃ divyarūpāṃ sulocanām \|\| 152 \|\|*

*mameti sa ca jānāti yācate ca haraṃ prati \|*  
*haro'pi kāryavyasanastyaktvā kailāsaparvatam \|\| 153 \|\|*

*maṃdaraṃ samanuprāpto devaṃ draṣṭuṃ janārddanam \|*  
*parasparaṃ samālocyāmuṃcaddevīṃ sa maṃdare \|\| 154 \|\|*

152-154. He, having secured immortality from Hara (i.e. Śiva) and being blinded by passion did not perceive (things properly). He looks upon the Goddess (Pārvatī) occupying half the body of Hara, possessing a divine form, having beautiful eyes, as his (possession) and solicits Hara for her. Hara too, engaged in some mission, left the mountain Kailāsa, reached Mandara (mountain) to see God Janārdana. Having reflected with each other He left the Goddess at the Mandara mountain.

## \|\| 2.9.155 \|\|

*nārāyaṇagṛhe devī sthitā devīgaṇairvṛtā \|*  
*atrāṃtare gautamastu govadhānmalinīkṛtaḥ \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. The Goddess surrounded by her attendants stayed in Nārāyaṇa’s house. In the meanwhile Gautama was stained by a cow’s murder.

## \|\| 2.9.156 \|\|

*pavitrīkaraṇāyāsya bhikṣurūpadharo haraḥ \|*  
*gautamasya gṛhaṃ prāpto maṃdaraṃ cāṃdhako gataḥ \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. To purify him, Hara, who had taken up the form of a mendicant reached Gautama’s house, and Andhaka (a demon, son of Kaśyapa and Diti, and killed by Śiva) went to Mandara.

## \|\| 2.9.157 \|\|

*yayāce pārvatīṃ duṣṭo yuddhaṃ cakre sa viṣṇunā \|*  
*hāritaṃ tu gaṇaiḥ sarvairdevīṃ daityo na paśyati \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. He, the wicked one, solicited Pārvatī; he fought with Viṣṇu. Being defeated by all the attendants he did not see the Goddess.

## \|\| 2.9.158 \|\|

*strīrūpadhārī kṛṣṇo'sau gaurīṃ rakṣati maṃdire \|*  
*gaurīṇāṃ tu śataṃ cakre haristatra sa māyayā \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. Kṛṣṇa in the garb of a woman protected Gaun in the house. Han, through trickery, produced there a hundred Gaurīs.

## \|\| 2.9.159 \|\|

*viṣṇordehasamudbhūtā divyarūpā varastriyaḥ \|*  
*andhako naiva jānāti kaiṣā gaurī nu pārvatī \|\| 159 \|\|*

159\. Excellent ladies of a divine form came up from Viṣṇu’s body. Andhaka did not know who was Gaurī (Pārvatī).

## \|\| 2.9.160 \|\|

*vilaṃbastatra sañjāto mohito viṣṇumāyayā \|*  
*tāvacchivaḥ samāyātaḥ kṛtvā gautamapāvanam \|\| 160 \|\|*

160\. There was delay. He was deluded by Viṣṇu’s trickery. Just then Śiva, after having purified Gautama, arrived there.

## \|\| 2.9.161 \|\|

*bhikṣāmātreṇa cānnena gautamo nirmalīkṛtaḥ \|*  
*soṃdhakena tadā yuddhaṃ cakre rudro'pi kopitaḥ \|\| 161 \|\|*

161\. Gautama was purified just with food (collected as) alms. Rudra, who was angry, then fought with Andhaka.

## \|\| 2.9.162 \|\|

*amaro'sau harājjātaḥ śūle protaḥ sudāruṇe \|*  
*śūlasthastu stutiṃ cakre tasya tuṣṭo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 162 \|\|*

162\. Due to Hara (i.e. Śiva) he had become immortal. He was fastened to a very fearful trident. While (fastened) to the trident, he extolled Śiva. Maheśvara (i.e. Śiva) was pleased with him.

## \|\| 2.9.163 \|\|

*gaṇeśatvaṃ dadau tasmai yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|*  
*svasarūpāmumādevīṃ kṛṣṇastasmai dadau svayam \|\| 163 \|\|*

163\. He gave him the position of the chief of his attendants till universal destruction. Kṛṣṇa himself gave him Goddess Umā of His own form.

## \|\| 2.9.164-165 \|\|

*gaurīrūpāḥ striyaścānyā dharitryāṃ tāstu preṣitāḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā nāmāni sarvāsāṃ loke pūjyā bhaviṣyatha \|\| 164 \|\|*

*etā ye pūjayiṣyaṃti pūjayiṣyanti te śivām \|*  
*śivāṃ ye pūjayiṣyaṃti te'rcayante haraṃ harim \|\| 165 \|\|*

164-165. Other ladies, of the form of Umā that were on the earth, were also sent. He named them all (and said,: “You will be venerable in the world. Those who will worship these, will worship Śivā (i.e. Pārvatī). Those who will worship Śiva, will worship Hara (i.e. Śiva) and Hari (i.e. Viṣṇu).”

## \|\| 2.9.166 \|\|

*umāṃ samādāya yayau haro giriṃ vṛṣaṃ samāruhya surāsurārcitaḥ \|*  
*haristu reme ramayā sahāṃdhake hate ca devāḥ surarājamāyayuḥ \|\| 166 \|\|*

166\. Taking Umā, Hara, mounted on the bull (Nandī) and worshipped by gods and demons, went to the mountain (Kailāśa). Hari amused himself with Lakṣmī, and when Andhaka was killed gods went to the Lord of gods.

## \|\| 2.9.167 \|\|

*brahmeśanārāyaṇapuṇyacetasāṃ śṛṇvanti citraṃ caritaṃ mahātmanām \|*  
*mucyaṃti pāpaiḥ kalikālasaṃbhavairyāsyaṃti nākaṃ gaṇavṛndavaṃditāḥ \|\| 167 \|\|*

167\. Those who listen to the wonderful account of the magnanimous, of holy minds like Brahmā, Īśa (i.e. Śiva) and Nārāyaṇa (i.e. Viṣṇu) are freed from the sins due to the Kali age and saluted by multitudes of the Gaṇas, will go to Heaven.

## \|\| 2.9.168 \|\|

*evaṃ kāle varttamāne haraḥ kailāsaparvate \|*  
*rakṣodānavadaityaistu gṛhyate'sau varānbahūn \|\| 168 \|\|*

168\. Thus, in the present time, from Hara (residing) on the Kailāsa mountain many boons are received by the demons, evil spirits and goblins.

## \|\| 2.9.169 \|\|

*brahmadattavaro raudrastārakākhyo mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*tena sarvaṃ jagadvyāptaṃ tasya naṣṭā surā raṇe \|\| 169 \|\|*

169\. A great fearful demon Tāraka, who was given a boon by Brahmā, had overpowered the entire world. In war, the gods had fled from him.

## \|\| 2.9.170 \|\|

*mahādevasutenājau haṃtavyo'sau sasarja tam \|*  
*kārtikeyamumāputraṃ rudravīryasamudbhavam \|\| 170 \|\|*

170\. He was to be killed by Mahādeva’s (i.e. Śiva’s) son, Kārttikeya, Umā’s son, born from Rudra’s semen.

## \|\| 2.9.171 \|\|

*devairindrādibhiḥ sarvaiḥ senādhyakṣyebhiṣecitaḥ \|*  
*tenāpi daivayogena tārakākhyo nipātitaḥ \|\| 171 \|\|*

171\. He was consecrated as the General of the army by all gods like Indra. He too, luckily, struck down (the demon) named Tāraka.

## \|\| 2.9.172-173 \|\|

*kailāsaśikharāsīno devadevo jagadguruḥ \|*  
*umayā saha saṃtuṣṭo nandibhadrādibhirvṛtaḥ \|\| 172 \|\|*

*skandena gajavaktreṇa dhanādhyakṣeṇa saṃyutaḥ \|*  
*atha hāsaparaṃ devaṃ śanaiḥ provāca taṃ śivā \|\| 173 \|\|*

172-173a. The God of gods, the preceptor of the world, seated on the peak of Kailāsa, surrounded by Nandī and others, and accompanied by Skanda, Gaṇapati and Kubera.

173b. Śivā (i.e. Pārvatī) gently spoke to God (Śiva), intent on laughing:

## \|\| 2.9.174 \|\|

*kena deva prakāreṇa toṣaṃ yāsyasi śaṃkara \|*  
*martyānāṃ kena dānena tapasā niyamena vā \|\| 174 \|\|*

174\. “By what mode, O Śaṅkara, will you be pleased? By means of which gift of (i.e. made by) the mortals, or by which austerities or vow (will you be pleased)?

## \|\| 2.9.175 \|\|

*kena vā karmaṇā deva kena mantreṇa vā punaḥ \|*  
*snānena kena deveśa kena dhūpena tuṣyasi \|\| 175 \|\|*

175\. “O God, by which deed or incantation, by which (kind of) bath, or, O Lord of gods, by which incense will you be pleased?

## \|\| 2.9.176 \|\|

*puṣpeṇa kena me nātha kena patreṇa śaṃkara \|*  
*kayā saṃtuṣyase stutyā sāhasena ca kena vai \|\| 176 \|\|*

176\. “O my Lord, by which flower, or, O Śaṅkara, by which leaf, by which eulogy, by which act of daring (will you be pleased)?

## \|\| 2.9.177 \|\|

*naivedyena ca kena tvaṃ kena homena tuṣyasi \|*  
*kena kaṣṭena vā deva kenārgheṇa mama prabho \|\| 177 \|\|*

177\. “By which act of offering of eatables presented to a deity, (or) by which sacrifice will you be pleased? By which hard work or respectful offering will you be pleased?

## \|\| 2.9.178 \|\|

*ṣoḍaśaite mayā praśnāḥ pṛṣṭā me nirṇayaṃ vada \|\| 178 \|\|*

178\. “These sixteen questions I have put to you. Speak (out) your verdict.”

## \|\| 2.9.179 \|\|

*śaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā devi kathayiṣye mama priyam \|*  
*śivapūjāprakāro'yaṃ kriyate vacasā guroḥ \|\| 179 \|\|*

Śaṅkara said:

179\. O Goddess, you have asked well. I shall tell what is dear to me. This kind of Śiva’s worship is done at the advice of the preceptor.

## \|\| 2.9.180 \|\|

*abhayaṃ sarvajaṃtūnāṃ dānaṃ devi mama priyam \|*  
*satyaṃ tapaḥ samākhyātaṃ paradāravivarjanam \|\| 180 \|\|*

180\. O Goddess, granting fearlessness to all beings is dear to me. Avoiding (contact with) other’s wife is said to be real penance.

## \|\| 2.9.181 \|\|

*priyo me niyamo devi karma tallokarañjanam \|*  
*mayoṃ namaḥ śivāyeti mantro'yamurarīkṛtaḥ \|\| 181 \|\|*

181\. Regulation is dear to me, O Goddess; act (liked by me) is amusing people. I have accepted this formula ‘Om, salutation to Śiva’.

## \|\| 2.9.182 \|\|

*sarvapāpavinirmukto mama devi sa vallabhaḥ \|*  
*pāpatyāgo bhavetsnānaṃ dhūpo me gauggulaḥ priyaḥ \|\| 182 \|\|*

182\. O Goddess, he, who is free from all sins, is dear to me. Bath would be the giving up of (all) sins. The incense of guggula is dear to me.

## \|\| 2.9.183 \|\|

*dhattūrakasya puṣpaṃ me bilvapatraṃ mama priyam \|*  
*stutiḥ śivaśivāyeti sāhasaṃ raṇakarmaṇi \|\| 183 \|\|*

183\. The flower of Dhatturaka is dear to me; so also the Bilva-leaf (is dear to me). (I like) the eulogy ‘Śiva, Śivāya’ (is dear to me). (I like) daring in fighting.

## \|\| 2.9.184 \|\|

*na bibheti naro yastu tasyāgre saṃbhavāmyaham \|*  
*haṃtakāro gavāṃ yastu naivedyaṃ mama vallabham \|\| 184 \|\|*

184\. I present myself before him who is not afraid. The ‘hum’ sound produced by cows is a dear offering to me.

## \|\| 2.9.185 \|\|

*pūrṇāhutyā parā prītirjāyate mama sundari \|*  
*śuśrūṣā vallabhaṃ kaṣṭaṃ yatīnāṃ ca tapasvinām \|\| 185 \|\|*

185\. O Goddess, by an offering made with a full ladle I am highly pleased. Attendance upon ascetics and those who practise penance is the hard work dear to me.

## \|\| 2.9.186 \|\|

*sūryodaye mahādevi madhyāhne'stamane tathā \|*  
*argho yo dīyate sūrye vallabho'sau mama priye \|\| 186 \|\|*

186\. O dear great Goddess, a respectful offering made to the Sun in the morning, noon and evening also, is dear to me.

## \|\| 2.9.187 \|\|

*kiṃ dānaiḥ kiṃ tapobhirvā kiṃ yajñairbhāvavarjitaiḥ \|*  
*dayā satyaṃ ghṛṇā'steyaṃ daṃbhapaiśunyavarjitam \|*  
*bhaktyā yaddīyate stokaṃ devi tadvallabhaṃ mama \|\| 187 \|\|*

187\. What is the use of (giving) gifts, austerities or sacrifices without devotion? Compassion, truth, tenderness, non-stealing, absence of hypocrisy and of wickedness (are most important). O Goddess, whatever little is given with devotion is dear to me.

## \|\| 2.9.188 \|\|

*evaṃ yāvatkathayati praśnānsūkṣmānyathoditān \|*  
*tāvadbrahmādibhirdevairviṣṇustatra yayau svayam \|\| 188 \|\|*

188\. While (Śaṅkara) was thus telling (the answers) to subtle questions as they came up, Viṣṇu himself, along with the gods Brahmā and others, came there.

## \|\| 2.9.189 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*nāhaṃ pālayituṃ śaktastvaṃ dadāsi varānbahūn \|*  
*daityānāṃ dānavādīnāṃ rākṣasānāṃ maheśvara \|\| 189 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:

189\. I cannot fulfil (the boons). You give many boons to demons, evil spirits etc., O great God.

## \|\| 2.9.190 \|\|

*vikṛtiṃ yāṃti paścātte kaṣṭaṃ vadhyā bhavaṃti me \|*  
*patreṇa puṣpamātreṇa oṃkāreṇa śivena ca \|*  
*muktiṃ yāti naro deva bhavabhaktiṃ karotu kaḥ \|\| 190 \|\|*

190\. They later change, and with difficulty are killed by me, O God, with a leaf, just with a leaf. By (uttering the syllable) Om, or by reciting the hymn Śivena (ca. Śivāya ca... etc), a man is liberated. Who (then) would be devoted to Śiva?

## \|\| 2.9.191 \|\|

*indrādayo'pi ye devā yajñairāpyāyayaṃti te \|*  
*na yajaṃti dvijā yajñānbhikṣādānena tuṣyasi \|\| 191 \|\|*

191\. Gods like Indra and others are satisfied with sacrifices Brāhmaṇas do not perform sacrifices (since) you are pleased (even) with giving alms.

## \|\| 2.9.192 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*indrādibhirna me kāryaṃ brahmā me kiṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*yena kena prakāreṇa prajāḥ pālyāstvayā 'dhunā \|\| 192 \|\|*

Rudra said:

192\. I have nothing to do with Indra and others. What will Brahmā do to me? Now you have somehow to protect the subjects.

## \|\| 2.9.193 \|\|

*madīyā prakṛtistveṣā tāṃ kathaṃ tyaktumutsahe \|*  
*tvayāhaṃ brahmaṇā devairvarakarmaṇi yojitaḥ \|\| 193 \|\|*

193\. It is my nature? How would I be able to give it up? You, Brahmā have appointed me to do the work of (giving) boons.

## \|\| 2.9.194 \|\|

*idānīmeva kiṃ naṣṭaṃ muktvā devīṃ tavāgrataḥ \|*  
*bhūtvā mūrtiṃ parityajya ekākī vicarāmyaham \|\| 194 \|\|*

194\. What is lost in leaving the Goddess before you? Giving up the image and being all alone, I shall wander.

## \|\| 2.9.195 \|\|

*ityuktvā sa śivo devastatraivāṃtaradhīyata \|*  
*gate tasmiñchive tatra saṃkṣobhaḥ sumahānabhūt \|\| 195 \|\|*

195\. Speaking like this that Śiva vanished just there. When that Śiva had gone, there was a great agitation.

## \|\| 2.9.196 \|\|

*umā provāca cendrādīnbrahmaviṣṇugaṇāṃstathā \|*  
*idānīṃ kiṃ mayā kāryaṃ bhavadbhiḥ śivavarjitaiḥ \|\| 196 \|\|*

196\. Umā said to Moon and others, so also to the attendants of Viṣṇu: “Now what am I to do with you who are without Śiva?”

## \|\| 2.9.197 \|\|

*atrāntare ca ye cānye devāstatra samāgatāḥ \|*  
*ṛṣayaścaiva siddhāśca tathā nāradaparvatau \|\| 197 \|\|*

197\. In the meanwhile other gods also came there; so also sages, Siddhas and Nārada and Parvata.

## \|\| 2.9.198 \|\|

*gaṃgāsarasvatīnadyo nāgā yakṣāḥ samāgatāḥ \|*  
*brahmādibhiḥ samālocya kathametadbhaviṣyati \|\| 198 \|\|*

198\. Rivers Gaṅgā, Sarasvatī, (so also) Nāgas, Yakṣas came there. Brahmā and others after having thought (said): “How will this take place?”

## \|\| 2.9.199 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*sahaiva gamyatāṃ tatra yatra devo gataḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*svalpā yāsena te yāntu narāḥ svargaṃ śivājñayā \|\| 199 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:

199\. Let us together go where God Śiva has gone. By Śiva’s command, let the people go to Heaven with a little effort (only).

## \|\| 2.9.200 \|\|

*satyaloke narā yāntu devā yāntu dharātalam \|*  
*rakṣodānavadaityānāṃ varānyacchatu śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 200 \|\|*

200\. Let men go to Satyaloka; let gods go to the earth. May Śiva grant boons to the evil spirits, goblins, demons.

## \|\| 2.9.201 \|\|

*teṣāṃ bādhā mayā kāryā yai ca syurdharmalopakāḥ \|*  
*hṛṣṭe śive mayā kāryā vyavasthā svargagāminām \|\| 201 \|\|*

201\. I should torment those who violate their duties. When Śiva is pleased, I would make arrangement for who go to Heaven.

## \|\| 2.9.202 \|\|

*trayīdharmaṃ parityajya ye'nyaṃ dharmamupāsate \|*  
*te narā narakaṃ yāṃtu yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 202 \|\|*

202\. Let those men who perform duties other than those enjoined by the three Vedas, go to hell till universal destruction.

## \|\| 2.9.203-204 \|\|

*yadā'dṛśyaḥ śivo jātaḥ pravi veśa girervanam \|*  
*girīṇāṃ madhyamāsthāya tyaktvā divye sa vāsasī \|\| 203 \|\|*

*gajājinaṃ parityajya tyaktvā mūrttiṃ maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*bhittvā bhūmitalaṃ devaḥ sthāṇurūpo babhūva saḥ \|\| 204 \|\|*

203-204. When Śiva became invisible, he entered a mountain-forest; resorting to the centre of the mountains; giving up the elephant-hide, and His form, Maheśvara (i.e. Śiva) and piercing the earth, he became (one) of the form of a post.

## \|\| 2.9.205 \|\|

*yasmātsvaṃyabhūrbhavati bhavaṃstasmātsvayaṃ haraḥ \|*  
*atrāṃtare surāḥ sarve na paśyaṃti maheśvaram \|*  
*jñānātītaṃ kalātītaṃ divyadhyānabahiḥ sthitam \|\| 205 \|\|*

205\. Since Hara is self-bom, he is Hara himself (alone). In the meanwhile all the gods did not see Maheśvara, remaining beyond knowledge and ingenuity, and remaining beyond divine thought.

## \|\| 2.9.206 \|\|

*yadā devā vyākulāḥ saṃpataṃti ravirvāyuraṃbaraṃ toyamurvī \|*  
*nije sthāne varttamānā umāyāḥ śaśaṃsurvai devadevaṃ surāṇām \|\| 206 \|\|*

206\. When gods being perplexed fell, (when) the sun, the wind, the sky, the water and the earth remained in their own places, they praised the great Lord of Umā and of the gods:

## \|\| 2.9.207 \|\|

*svarge dharitryāṃ caritaṃ taleṣu deveṣu martyeṣu sarīsṛpeṣu \|*  
*sthūleṣu sūkṣmeṣu yathā tathaiva satyaṃ hi vācyaṃ padamasmadīyam \|\| 207 \|\|*

207\. “Our position should be said to be as genuine as the behaviour (of beings) in Heaven, on the earth,in the lower parts, among gods, mortals, reptiles, the gross and the subtle.”

## \|\| 2.9.208 \|\|

*tato devāḥ pracalitāḥ kṛtvā gaurīṃ purassaram \|*  
*naṃdi bhadrādayaḥ sarve devā iṃdrādayastathā \|\| 208 \|\|*

208\. Then the gods, making Gaurī their leader, moved on. So also Nandin, Bhadra and all gods like Indra (moved on).

## \|\| 2.9.209 \|\|

*skandena sahitā devī siṃhārūḍhā yayau svayam \|*  
*adhiruhya garutmaṃtaṃ yayau viṣṇuḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 209 \|\|*

209\. The Goddess (Umā) herself, along with Skanda, mounted upon a lion and moved on. Viṣṇu, the eternal One, mounted on Garuḍa and went.

## \|\| 2.9.210 \|\|

*haṃsādhirūḍho bhagavānbrahmā yāti sa pṛṣṭhataḥ \|*  
*airāvataṃ samāruhya devarājo'gamatsvayam \|\| 210 \|\|*

210\. Brahmā, mounted on the Swan, followed them. The Lord of gods (Indra) himself, mounting upon Airāvata, went (with them).

## \|\| 2.9.211 \|\|

*gaṃgā sarasvatī devī yamunā ca mahānadī \|*  
*devatāśca gatāḥ sarve nāgā yakṣāḥ sakiṃnarāḥ \|\| 211 \|\|*

211\. (The rivers) Gaṅgā, divine Sarasvatī, the great river Yamunā, so also all the deities, moved on. All Nāgas, Yakṣas with Kinnaras also (went on).

## \|\| 2.9.212 \|\|

*gatāḥ saṃkṣepataḥ sarve yatra devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*adhiruhya gireḥ śṛṃgamaṃbā devī vyavasthitā \|\| 212 \|\|*

212\. In short, all went there where stood Mahādeva (i.e. Śiva). Goddess Ambā, going up the peak of a mountain, settled (there).

## \|\| 2.9.213 \|\|

*viṣṇurmuktvā garutmaṃtaṃ sthito raivatake girau \|*  
*stutiṃ cakre tadā devī jagurgītaṃ susaṃyatāḥ \|\| 213 \|\|*

213\. Leaving Garuḍa, Viṣṇu remained on the Raivataka mountain. The Goddess then extolled (Śiva); (gods) well-restrained sang a song (in praise of Śiva).

## \|\| 2.9.214 \|\|

*airāvatapadākrāṃto na cacāla sa parvataḥ \|*  
*bhittvā bhūmitalaṃ tatra nāgarājaḥ samāgataḥ \|\| 214 \|\|*

214\. That mountain trampled by the feet of Airāvata, did not move. Piercing the surface of the earth, the King of Nāgas came there.

## \|\| 2.9.215-216 \|\|

*gaṃgādyāḥ saritaḥ sarvāstena raṃdhreṇa cāgatāḥ \|*  
*brahmā viṣṇuryadā devāḥ stutiṃ cakruḥ samaṃtataḥ \|\| 215 \|\|*

*dadarśa rūpaṃ bhagavānbhavo devastadā haraḥ \|\| 216 \|\|*

215-216. All rivers like Gaṅgā, came through the same hole. When Brahmā, Viṣṇu (and other) gods praised (Śiva) on all sides, the venerable God Hara (i.e. Śiva) manifested this form.

## \|\| 2.9.217 \|\|

*tato hṛṣṭāḥ surāḥ sarve aṃbā hṛṣṭā gaṇāśca te \|*  
*gamyatāṃ deva kailāsaṃ devyeti saṃpramoditaḥ \|\| 217 \|\|*

217\. Then all gods were delighted. Ambā was delighted, and the Gaṇas also (were delighted), delighted by the words of the Goddess, “O Lord, let us go to Kailāsa”.

## \|\| 2.9.218 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*yadi hṛṣṭāḥ surāḥ sarve gaṃgādyāḥ saritastathā \|*  
*girau raivatake viṣṇuraṃbā cātraiva tiṣṭhatu \|\| 218 \|\|*

The Lord said:

218\. If all gods, so also rivers like Gaṅgā are pleased, let Viṣṇu reside on the Raivataka mountain and Ambā here only.

## \|\| 2.9.219 \|\|

*sarasvatī ca yamunā revā cāsminvyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*svarṇarūpaṃ jalaṃ yasmātsvarṇarekheti sā nadī \|\| 219 \|\|*

219\. (The rivers) Sarasvatī, Yamunā, Revā are settled in this (region). The river Svarṇarekhā is so called (because her water) looks like gold.

## \|\| 2.9.220 \|\|

*vastrāpathamidaṃ kṣetraṃ bhavo devo'tra tiṣṭhatu \|*  
*tīrthametanmayā proktaṃ bhuktimuktipradāyakam \|*  
*atra snāto naro nārī mucyate sarva pātakaiḥ \|\| 220 \|\|*

220\. Let this holy place be called Vastrāpatha, and let God Bhava stay here. I have declared this holy place giving enjoyment and (final) liberation. A man or a woman who bathes here is freed from all sins.

## \|\| 2.9.221 \|\|

*iti procya śivo devaḥ kalāṃ nyasya bhave tadā \|*  
*paśyatāṃ sarvadevānāṃ yayau kailāsaparvatam \|\| 221 \|\|*

221\. Speaking like this, God Śiva, relinquishing a small part on Bhava went to mountain Kailāsa when all gods were looking on.

## \|\| 2.9.222 \|\|

*aṃbeti skandavadanātkalāṃ nyasya girau tadā \|*  
*devena sahitā devī vṛṣārūḍhā yayau svayam \|\| 222 \|\|*

222\. Hearing the word ‘Ambā’ from Skanda’s mouth, the Goddess herself, leaving a small part on the mountain, mounted the bull (Nandī) and went with the God (Śiva).

## \|\| 2.9.223 \|\|

*nārāyaṇo raivatake girau ramye sthitaḥ svayam \|*  
*kalpādau ca yugādau ca sthito viṣṇuḥ sadā girau \|\| 223 \|\|*

223\. Nārāyaṇa (i.e. Viṣṇu) himself stayed on the charming Raivataka mountain. Viṣṇu has always stayed on the mountain at the beginning of a Kalpa or a Yuga.

## \|\| 2.9.224 \|\|

*bahurātrasthito devaḥ kṛtvā daityanibarhaṇam \|*  
*reme raivatake devo yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 224 \|\|*

224\. The God (Viṣṇu), having lived there for many yugas and having destroyed the demons, rejoiced on the Raivataka mountain till universal deluge.

## \|\| 2.9.225 \|\|

*nārasiṃhena rūpeṇa hiraṇyakaśipurhataḥ \|*  
*hatvā tadā gatastatra nārasiṃhaṃ mumoca ha \|\| 225 \|\|*

225\. In the form of Narasiṃha he killed Hiraṇyakaśipu. Having killed him he left and on that occasion liberated Narasiṃha.

## \|\| 2.9.226 \|\|

*mahāvarāharūpeṇa hiraṇyākṣo nipātitaḥ \|*  
*tadeva muktvā deveśaḥ sthito raivatake girau \|\| 226 \|\|*

226\. In the form of the great Boar, he struck down Hiraṇyākṣa. Just leaving it (there) only, the Lord of gods remained on the Raivataka mountain.

## \|\| 2.9.227 \|\|

*sa pṛthuṃ pārthivaṃ kṛtvā devakāryeṇa vai nṛpa \|*  
*girau raivatake deva uvāsa surapūjitaḥ \|\| 227 \|\|*

227\. He, making Pṛthu the king, to carry out the mission of gods, remained, being worshipped by gods, on the Raivataka mountain.

## \|\| 2.9.228 \|\|

*atrāgatya pṛthuḥ pūrvaṃ cakre devaprapūjanam \|*  
*japamālā tadā kaṇṭhe pṛthunā saṃniveśitā \|*  
*dāmodareti deveśanāma cakre pṛthuḥ svayam \|\| 228 \|\|*

228\. Having come here, Pṛthu first put round his neck the rosary of beads. Pṛthu, on his own, fixed the name of the Lord of gods as ‘Dāmodara’.

## \|\| 2.9.229 \|\|

*vastrāpathe devavaro bhavaḥ sthito dāmodaro raivatake vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*aṃbetidevī girimūrdhni saṃsthitā devāśca sarve paritaḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ \|\| 229 \|\|*

229\. The excellent God Bhava (i.e. Śiva) remained in (the holy place) Vastrāpatha, and Dāmodara got well-settled on Raivataka. Goddess Ambā remained on the top of the mountain; and all other gods settled around (them).

## \|\| 2.9.230 \|\|

*kṣetrādhipāstīrthavarasya rakṣakā devena muktā bhavasaṃnidhānataḥ \|*  
*paśyaṃti ye devavaraṃ bhavābhidhaṃ mucyaṃti te yāṃti divaṃ narā bhuvaḥ \|\| 230 \|\|*

230\. The Lords of the best holy place, the protectors (of the holy place) were left by the God near Bhava. Those men, who see the best God called Bhava, are liberated; they go to Heaven from the earth.

## \|\| 2.9.231 \|\|

*vastrāpathasya kṣetrasya bhavasya ca mayā tava \|*  
*utpattiḥ kathitā rājankimanyacchrotumicchasi \|\| 231 \|\|*

231\. O King, I have told you about the origin of the holy place Vastrāpatha and of Bhava. What else do you want to hear?

## \|\| 2.9.232 \|\|

*śṛṇoti paṭhate yaśca kathāṃ cemāṃ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ svargaloke mahīyate \|\| 232 \|\|*

232\. He who listens to and recites fully the tale, being free from all sins, prospers in Heaven.

## \|\| 2.9.233 \|\|

*brahmaghnaśca surāpaśca bhrūṇahā gurutalpagaḥ \|*  
*svarṇarekhājale snāto mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 233 \|\|*

233\. One who kills a Brāhmaṇa, who is a drunkard, who is a killer of an embryo, who has violated his teacher’s wife, is freed from all sins when he has bathed in the water of Svarṇarekhā.

## \|\| 2.9.234 \|\|

*ye ca kīṭapataṃgādyāḥ svarṇarekhā jale mṛtāḥ \|*  
*sarvapātakanirmuktāste prayāṃti surālayam \|\| 234 \|\|*

234\. The worms, moths etc. that die in the water of Svarṇarekhā, being free from all sins, go to (Heaven) the abode of gods.

## \|\| 2.9.235 \|\|

*svarṇarekhājale snātvā saṃdhyāṃ śrāddhaṃ karoti yaḥ \|*  
*vastrāpathe bhavaṃ pūjya brahmalokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 235 \|\|*

235\. He who, bathing in the Svarṇarekhā (river), performs a Śrāddha and worships, Bhava at Vastrāpatha, goes to Brahmaloka.

## Chapter 10 - Sārasvata’s Advice to King Bhoja

## \|\| 2.10.2 \|\|

*gaṃgā sarasvatī caiva gomatī narmadā nadī \|*  
*svarṇarekhājale sarvāstathā brahmā savāsavaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:

I. Oh! The glory of the holy place, and of the mountain Raìvataka, of Bhava, the God of gods and so also of Vastrāpatha!

2\. The (rivers) Gaṅgā, Sarasvatī, so also Gomatī, and the river Narmadā—all exist in the water of Svarṇarekhā; so also Brahmā with Indra (resides there).

## \|\| 2.10.3-4 \|\|

*brahmendra viṣṇumukhyānāṃ devānāṃ śaṃkarasya ca \|*  
*vāso viracitastatra yāvadbrahmadinaṃ bhavet \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kṣetratīrthaprabhāvaṃ ca prasādāttava śaṃkara \|*  
*śrutaṃ savistaraṃ sarvamidaṃ tvaduditaṃ mayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. The residence of the chief gods like Brahmā, Indra, Viṣṇu and also of Śaṅkara is there till the end of the Day of Brahmā.

## \|\| 2.10.5 \|\|

*maheśvara prabho brūhi kiṃ cakāra janeśvaraḥ \|*  
*bhojarājo mṛgīṃ prāpya sa ca sārasvato muniḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O Maheśvara, O Lord, tell (me) what King Bhojarāja did on getting the female deer and what Sage Sārasvata did.

## \|\| 2.10.6 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tāsu sarvāsu nārīṣu rūpaudāryaguṇādhikā \|*  
*nityaṃ pramuditā śāṃtā nityaṃ maṃgalakārikā \|\| 6 \|\|*

The Lord said:

6\. She was the best of all women in respect of qualities like beauty, generosity. She was always delighted, calm and always did auspicious things.

## \|\| 2.10.7 \|\|

*mātā svasā sakhī putrī strīṣu saṃbandhavardhanī \|*  
*pitā bhrātā guruḥ putraḥ puruṣeṣu tathā kṛtaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. She enhanced her relation among women as mother, sister, friend, daughter, and among men she established her relation as father, brother, preceptor, son.

## \|\| 2.10.8 \|\|

*evaṃ guṇavatīṃ bhāryāṃ prāpya hṛṣṭo janeśvaraḥ \|*  
*sārasvataṃ muniṃ stutvā rājā vacanamabravīt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Having got such a virtuous wife, the king was delighted. Praising Sage Sārasvata, the king spoke (these) words.

## \|\| 2.10.9 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*brahmā viṣṇurharaḥ sūrya indro'gnirmarutāṃ gaṇaḥ \|*  
*brahmacaryeṇa tapasā tvayā santoṣitāḥ prabho \|\| 9 \|\|*

The King said:

9\. O Lord, by your celibacy and penance you have pleased Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Hara, Sūrya, Indra, Agni and the group of Maruts.

## \|\| 2.10.10 \|\|

*daivataṃ paramaṃ me tvaṃ pitā mātā guruḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*yena janmāṃtaraṃ sarvaṃ pratyakṣaṃ kathitaṃ mama \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. You are my highest deity. You are my father, mother, preceptor and master. You have actually narrated may other (i.e. previous) birth.

## \|\| 2.10.11 \|\|

*surāṣṭradeśo vikhyāto girī raivatako mahān \|*  
*bhavaḥ svayaṃbhūrbhagavānkṣetre vastrāpathe śrutaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The great Raivataka mountain is well known in Surāṣṭra country. Bhava is known as self-born in the holy place Vastrāpatha.

## \|\| 2.10.12 \|\|

*ujjayaṃtagirermūrdhni gaurīskandagaṇeśvarāḥ \|*  
*bhāvayaṃto bhavaṃ sarve saṃsthitā brahmavāsaram \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On the top of the mountain Ujjayanta Gaurī, Skanda, and the chiefs of the (attendants) Gaṇas, have all, cherishing Bhava, stayed till the Day of Brahmā.

## \|\| 2.10.13 \|\|

*vāmano nagaraṃ sthāpya śivaṃ siddheśvaraṃ prati \|*  
*jitvā daityaṃ baliṃ baddhvā svayaṃ raivatake sthitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Vāmana, having founded a city for (i.e. in honour of) Śiva, Siddheśvara, having conquered and bound Bali himself remains at Raivataka.

## \|\| 2.10.14 \|\|

*ityetatsarvamāścaryaṃ jīvadbhiryadi dṛśyate \|*  
*tīrthayātrāvidhānena bhavo vastrāpathe hariḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Perhaps all this wonder is seen by the living by undertaking pilgrimage to the sacred place. Hari is at Vastrāpatha.

## \|\| 2.10.15 \|\|

*tyaktvā rājyaṃ priyānputrānpattyaśvarathakuñjarān \|*  
*putraṃ rājye pratiṣṭhāpya gantavyaṃ niścitaṃ mayā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Abandoning my kingdom, dear sons, foot-soldiers, horses, chariots, elephants, putting the son on the throne I should cerainly \[certainly?\] go.

## \|\| 2.10.16 \|\|

*tvatprasādācchrutaṃ sarvaṃ gamyate yadi dṛśyate \|*  
*tīrthayātrāvidhānena bhavo vastrāpathe hariḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Through your favour I have heard everything. If I go on the piltrimage \[pilgrimage?\] I shall see Bhava, Hari at Vastrāpatha.

## \|\| 2.10.17 \|\|

*sūryalokaṃ somalokamiṃdralokaṃ hareḥ puram \|*  
*brahmalokamatikramya yāsye'haṃ śivamaṃdiram \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Having gone beyond the world of the Sun, of Soma (i.e. the Moon), of Indra, Viṣṇu’s city, the world of Brahmā, I shall go to the abode of Śiva.

## \|\| 2.10.18 \|\|

*śrutvā hi vākyaṃ vividhaṃ narendrātprahṛṣṭaromā sa munirbabhūva \|*  
*jijñāsamāno hi nṛpasya sarvaṃ nivārayāmāsa munirnarendram \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The sage, hearing the various words of the king, was horripilated. Desiring to know everything about the king, the sage warded off the king.

## \|\| 2.10.19 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*gṛhe'pi devā haraviṣṇumukhyā jalāni darbhā nṛpate tilāśca \|*  
*anekadeśāṃtaradarśanārthaṃ mano nivāryaṃ nṛpate tvayeti \|\| 19 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

19\. O king, even in the house there are chief gods like Śiva, Viṣṇu, water, Darbhas, sesamum seeds. O King, you should restrain your mind from seeing the interior of many countries.

## Chapter 11 - Pilgrimage to Vastrāpatha

## \|\| 2.11.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*sārasvatasya viprasya śrutvā bhojanṛpo vacaḥ \|*  
*vivarṇavadano bhūtvā pragṛhyāṃghrī vaco'bravīt \|\| 1 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

1\. King Bhoja, hearing the words of Brāhmaṇa Sārasvata, and with his face turned pale, grasping (the Brāhmaṇa’s) feet said (these) words:

## \|\| 2.11.2 \|\|

*mune naivaṃ tvayā vācyaṃ gaṃtavyaṃ niścitaṃ mayā \|*  
*narāṇāṃ puṇyadā yātrā kathayasva kathaṃ bhavet \|\| 2 \|\|*

The King said:

2\. O sage, do not speak like this. I shall certainly go. Tell me how the pilgrimage, giving religious merit to men, would be undertaken.

## \|\| 2.11.3 \|\|

*kiṃ grāhyaṃ kiṃ ca moktavyaṃ kiṃ deyaṃ kiṃ na dīyate \|*  
*tīrthopavāsaḥ snānaṃ ca saṃdhyāsnānavidhikramaḥ \|*  
*pūjā nidrā japo rātrau sarvaṃ saṃkṣepato vada \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Tell me in brief: What should be taken; what should be left; what should be given; what is not given. (So also tell me about) the fast at the holy place; bath; the order of the rites like Sandhyā (the morning, noon, evening prayers); the worship; sleep; the muttering of prayers at night.

## \|\| 2.11.4 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*surāṣṭradeśe gantavyaṃ girau raivatake yadi \|*  
*nṛpa yātrāvidhiṃ vakṣye tvamekāgramanāḥ śṛṇu \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

4\. O King, if you are going to the Raivataka mountain in the Suraṣṭra \[Surāṣṭra?\] country, I shall tell you the procedure of the pilgrimage. Listen with a concentrated mind.

## \|\| 2.11.5-6 \|\|

*bṛhaspatibalaṃ gṛhya sūryaṃ saṃtarpya cottamam \|*  
*vāmataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ sarvaṃ vṛtvā saṃśodhya vāsaram \|\| 5 \|\|*

*caṃdralagnaṃ grahājjñātvā baliṣṭhājjanmarāśitaḥ \|*  
*śakunaṃ ca śubhaṃ labdhvā prasthātavyaṃ nṛpairnṛpa \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Taking the strength of Bṛhaspati, having very well gratified Sūrya, having screened everything on the left and at the back, having properly examined the day, having known the rising of the Moon from a powerful sign of the Zodiac under which one is born, finding an auspicious omen, kings should start (for the pilgrimage).

## \|\| 2.11.7 \|\|

*tīrthe sadaiva gaṃtavyaṃ sarve māsāśca śobhanāḥ \|*  
*tithayaścottamāḥ sarvāḥ snānadānārcanādiṣu \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. One should always go to a holy place. All months are auspicious. All lunar days are excellent for a bath, for charity or worship (of the deity).

## \|\| 2.11.8 \|\|

*aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ māsāṃte pūrṇimādine \|*  
*saṃkrāṃtau grahaṇe kālā ete proktā bhavārcane \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The times on the eighth, fourteenth, end of the month, Full-Moon day, on a Saṃkrānti day (i.e. the day of the passage of the Sun or any planetary body from one Zodiacal sign into another), or a day of eclipse are good for Bhava’s worship.

## \|\| 2.11.9 \|\|

*kailāsaṃ parvataṃ tyaktvā devīṃ devāṃśca saṃgatān \|*  
*vaiśākhe paṃcadaśyāṃ tu bhūmiṃ bhittvā bhavo'bhavat \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Leaving the Kailāśa mountain and accompanied by the Goddess (Pārvatī) and (other) gods, Bhava presented Himself after piercing the earth on the fifteenth of Vaiśākha.

## \|\| 2.11.10 \|\|

*tasminneva dine devī svarṇarekhā nadī talāt \|*  
*paṃthānaṃ vāsukiṃ prāpya sarvapāpapraṇāśanī \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On the same day the Goddess, the river Svarṇarekhā, the destroyer of all sins, resorting to the path of (i.e. made by) Vāsuki came up from the bottom.

## \|\| 2.11.11 \|\|

*airāvatapadākrāṃta ujjayanto mahāgiriḥ \|*  
*susrāva toyaṃ bahudhā gajapādodbhavaṃ śuci \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The great mountain Ujjayanta, trampled over by the feet of Airāvata, exuded variously pure water, rising from the elephants’ feet.

## \|\| 2.11.12 \|\|

*devā brahmādayaḥ sarve gaṃgādyāḥ saritastathā \|*  
*vastrāpathe mahākṣetre bhavabhāvena saṃgatāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. All gods led by Brahmā, rivers led by Gaṅgā, came together due to their devotion to Bhava at the great holy place Vastrāpatha.

## \|\| 2.11.13-15 \|\|

*vastrāpathasya kṣetrasya pramāṇaṃ śṛṇu bhūpate \|*  
*harasya tyajato bhūmau patitaṃ vastrabhūṣaṇam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tāvanmātraṃ smṛtaṃ kṣetraṃ devairvastrāpathaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*uttareṇa nadī bhadrā pūrvasyāṃ yojanadvayam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇena baleḥ sthānamujjayanto nadīmanu \|*  
*aparasyāṃ paraṃ nadyo saṃgamaṃ vāmanātpurāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. O King, listen to the measure of (the holy place) Vastrāpatha. The excellent garment of Hara, when he was leaving (the place) fell on the earth. The holy place, just recollected by gods, was made (i.e. named) Vastrāpatha by gods. River Bhadrā (Gaṅgā) in the north (flows) for two yojanas in the east. In south is Bali’s place, (the mountain) Ujjayanta near the river. In the west, there is the confluence of two rivers, (not far) from the city of Vāmana.

## \|\| 2.11.16 \|\|

*etadvastrāpathaṃ kṣetraṃ bhuktimuktipradāyakam \|*  
*kṣetrasya vistaro jñeyo yojanānāṃ catuṣṭayam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. This is the holy place (called) Vastrāpatha, which gives enjoyment and liberation. The expanse of the holy place should be known to be four yojanas.

## \|\| 2.11.17 \|\|

*vaiśākhapaṃcadaśyāṃ tu bhavo bhāvena bhūpate \|*  
*pūjyate śivaloke tu sthīyate brahmavāsaram \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. (If) on the fifteenth (i.e. the Full-Moon) day of Vaiśākha Bhava is worshipped with devotion (by a person), he dwells in the world of Śiva for Brahmā’s Day.

## \|\| 2.11.18-19 \|\|

*ato vasaṃte saṃprāpte prayāṇaṃ kuru bhūpate \|*  
*nigṛhya niyamānbhūtvā śuciḥ snāto jitendriyaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*gajavājirathāṃstyaktā padābhyāṃ yāti yo naraḥ \|*  
*puṣpakeṇa vimānena sa yāti śivamaṃdiram \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Therefore, O King, when spring comes, go (to Vastrāpatha). Observing restrictions, being pure, having bathed, having controlled the senses, giving up elephants, horses and chariots, a man who goes (to Vastrāpatha), goes to Śiva’s abode in an aeroplane.

## \|\| 2.11.20-21 \|\|

*ekabhaktena naktena tathaivāyācitena ca \|*  
*bhikṣāhāreṇa toyena phalāhāreṇa vā yadi \|\| 20 \|\|*

*upavāsena kṛcchreṇa śākāhāreṇa yāti yaḥ \|*  
*sa yāti sundarīvṛndairvījyamāno gaṇairdivi \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. He, who, eating once (only) at night, so also without requesting (anyone for food), by eating food obtained as alms, (or subsisting) on water, or eating fruits, observing fast, (performing) religious penance, eating vegetarian food goes (to Śiva-temple), goes, being fanned by groups of beautiful ladies, along with attendants, to Heaven.

## \|\| 2.11.22-23 \|\|

*malasnānaṃ vinā mārge pādābhyaṃgavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*maladhārī kṣīṇatanuryaṣṭihasto jitendriyaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*śītātapajalakliṣṭaḥ śivasmaraṇatatparaḥ \|*  
*yadi yāti naro yāti sa bhittvā sūryamaṃḍalam \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. On the way, if he goes without being soiled by dust, (so also) without smearing the feet with perfumes, observing silence, with his body emaciated, with a stick in his hand, having conquered his senses, tormented by cold, heat (of the sun), water, engrossed in the recollection of Śiva, (on a pilgrimage) he goes (to the highest position) by breaking the orb of the Sun.

## \|\| 2.11.24 \|\|

*narakasthānapi pitṝnmātṛtaḥ pitṛto nṛpa \|*  
*akṣayaṃ sapta saptaiva nayedevaṃ śivālaye \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In this way he takes to the Śiva abode, permanently, his (dead) ancestors, seven on the father’s side and seven on the mother’s side, even though they are in Hell.

## \|\| 2.11.25-29 \|\|

*luṇṭhanbhūmau yadā yāti mṛgacarmāvaguṃṭhitaḥ \|*  
*daṇḍapramāṇabhūmervā saṃkhyāṃ kurvannaro yadi \|\| 25 \|\|*

*araṇye nirjale sthāne jalāṃtaḥparipīḍitaḥ \|*  
*śaraṇyaṃ śaṃkaraṃ kṛtvā mano niścalamātmanaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*saptadvīpavatīṃ pṛthvīṃ samudravasanāṃ nṛpa \|*  
*sa labdhvā bahubhiryajñairyajñe dattvā ca medinīm \|\| 27 \|\|*

*saptabhaumavimānastho divyadeho harākṛtiḥ \|*  
*nirīkṣya medinīṃ maṃdaṃ kṛta maṃgalamaṇḍanam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*mṛganetrābhujasparśalagnapīnapayodharaḥ \|*  
*gītavādyavinodena satyalokaṃ vrajennaraḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

25-29. When a man, covered with a dear-hide, goes rolling, measuring the number of divisions of land with a staff, in a forest or in an uninhabited land, tormented by thirst within, making Śaṅkara his refuge, making his mind steady, he obtains the earth with seven islands and clad with the oceans; (and) giving it away in many sacrifices, he, of a divine body, having Hara’s form, seated in an aeroplane with seven stories, gradually observing the earth (below), in a manner in whch \[which?\] auspicious ornaments are put on (the body), receiving the touch of the arms and stout breasts of fawn-eyed ladies would go to Satyaloka with his mind diverted by songs and music.

## \|\| 2.11.30-31 \|\|

*vidhāya bhujavegaṃ vā pādau baddhvā śanaiḥ śanaiḥ \|*  
*maunena mānuṣo māyāṃ tyaktvā yāti śivālaye \|\| 30 \|\|*

*brahmaghno vā surāpo vā steyī vā gurutalpagaḥ \|*  
*kṛtaghno mucyate pāpairmṛto muktimavāpnuyāt \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. A man who, resorting to the strength of his arms or tying his feet, abandoning illusion, silently and slowly goes to the temple of Śiva, is delivered (from this mortal world), though he is a killer of Brāhmaṇa, or a drunkard or a thief, or one who has violated his preceptor’s wife, or an ungrateful person; and on death he would obtain final beatitude.

## \|\| 2.11.32-35 \|\|

*mātaraṃ pitaraṃ deśaṃ bhrātaraṃ svajanabāṃdhavān \|*  
*grāmaṃ bhūmiṃ gṛhaṃ tyaktvā kṛtvā ceṃdriyasaṃyamam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*gṛhītvā śivasaṃskāraṃ naro bhrāmyati bhūtale \|*  
*draṣṭuṃ tīrthānyanekāni puṇyānyāyatanāni ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

*kasmiṃstīrthe śubhe sthāne chittvā saṃsārabandhanam \|*  
*abhayāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā śivaśiveti bhāṣakaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*ekāṃte nirjane sthāne śivasmaraṇatatparaḥ \|*  
*yadi tiṣṭhati taṃ yānti namaskartuṃ narādhipa \|\| 35 \|\|*

32-35. Obtaining auspicious sanctification, a man wanders on the surface of the earth to see many holy places and sanctuaries. If, at a holy place, on an auspicious spot, a man stays, cutting off the bond of the worldly existence, giving the gift of fearlessness, muttering ‘Śiva, Śiva’, engrossed in remembering Śiva at a lonely, deserted place, (then), O King, people go to him to pay him respectful obeisance.

## \|\| 2.11.36 \|\|

*āyāṃti devatāḥ sarve cihnaṃ tasya nirīkṣitum \|*  
*vimānavṛndairnetavyaḥ kadāsau puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. All deities come (to him) to observe his mark, (and discuss among themselves): When should this best man be taken (to Heaven) by a fleet of aeroplanes?

## \|\| 2.11.37 \|\|

*yadā tu pañcatvamupaiti kāle kalevaraṃ skandhakṛtaṃ naraiśca \|*  
*nirīkṣyamāṇaḥ surasundarībhiḥ sa nīyamāno madavihvalābhiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. When at the (due) time (of death), he dies, and his dead body is carried by men on their shoulders, he (being thus) carried, is observed by divine ladies maddened with lust.

## \|\| 2.11.38 \|\|

*surendrasūryāgnidhaneśarudraiḥ saṃpūjyamānaḥ śivarūpadhārī \|*  
*surādilokānpravimucya vegācchivālaye tiṣṭhati rudrabhaktaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. He, Śiva’s devotee, having the form of Śiva, and being worshipped by the Lord of gods, Sūrya, Agni, Kubera, Rudra, quickly leaving the worlds of gods etc. resides in Śiva’s abode.

## Chapter 12 - Yātrā (Pilgrimage): How It Is to Be Done

## \|\| 2.12.1-3 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*gaṃgodakaṃ madhughṛte kuṃkumāgurucaṃda nam \|*  
*guggulaṃ bilvapatrāṇi bakapuṣpaṃ ca yo vahet \|\| 1 \|\|*

*padacārī śucitanurbhāraṃ skandhe nidhāya ca \|*  
*tīrthe snātvā śivaṃ viṣṇuṃ brahmāṇaṃ śaṃkaraṃ priyam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā nivedayedyastu sa muktaḥ sarvabandhanaiḥ \|*  
*sa naro gaṇatāṃ yāti yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

1-3. He, who carries water of Gaṅgā, honey and clarified butter, saffron, fragrant aloe-wood, sandal, guggula, bilva-leaves, baka-flower, who goes on foot, who has purified his body, who, having put the burden on his shoulders, who, having bathed at the holy place, who, after seeing the dear Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Śaṅkara, would make offerings (to the deities) is freed from all bonds of (i.e. due to) acts. That man becomes a (divine) attendant (Gaṇa) till the universal deluge.

## \|\| 2.12.4-8 \|\|

*kalatramitraputrairvā bhrātṛbhiḥ svajanairnaraiḥ \|*  
*sahito vā narairyāti tīrthe devaṃ viciṃtya ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

*devamūrtiṃ śubhāṃ kṛtvā rathasthāṃ supratiṣṭhitām \|*  
*candanāgurukarpūrairarcitāṃ kuṃkumena ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

*pūjayanvividhaiḥ puṣpairdhūpadīpādikairnṛpa \|*  
*gītanṛtyaiḥ savāditrairhāsyalāsyairanekadhā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*dharitrīṃ kāṃcanaṃ gāśca jalānnavasanāni ca \|*  
*tṛṇendhane priyāṃ vāṇīṃ yacchanyāti naro yadi \|\| 7 \|\|*

*devāṃganākaragrāhagṛhīto nandanaṃ vanam \|*  
*prāpya bhuṃkte śubhānbhogānyāvadācandratārakam \|\| 8 \|\|*

4-8. If a man, along with his wife, friends, sons, brothers or with his relatives goes to a holy place and having thought about the deity, having fashioned an auspicious image of the deity, places it properly in a chariot, and having worshipped it with sandal, aloe-wood, camphor, and saffron, with various flowers, incense, lamp etc., goes, accompanied variously by songs, dances, musical instruments, laughters, dancing, and, O King, giving land, gold, cows, water, food, garments, grass, fuel, agreeable words, he, with his hands held by divine ladies, enjoys, after reaching paradise, beautiful pleasures, as long as the moon and stars (shine in the sky).

## \|\| 2.12.9 \|\|

*tīrthe saṃcaritaḥ puruṣo rogaiḥ prāṇānvimuñcati \|*  
*adṛṣṭvā daivataṃ tīrthe dṛṣṭatīrthaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. If a man, moving in a holy place, dies of diseases, without seeing the deity, he would obtain the fruit of having seen the deity.

## \|\| 2.12.10-11 \|\|

*saṃsāradoṣānvividhānvicintya strīputramitreṣvapi baṃdhamuktaḥ \|*  
*vijñāya baddhaṃ puruṣaṃ pradhānaiḥ sa sarvatīrthāni karoti deham \|\| 10 \|\|*

*ājanmajanmāṃntarasaṃcitāni dagdhvā sa pāpāni naro narendra \|*  
*tejomayaṃ sarvagataṃ purāṇaṃ bhavodbhavaṃ paśyati mucyate saḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Having thought over the various defects of the worldly existence, having been free from the bonds of his wife, sons, friends, having realised that the body is bound by main (vices) if he visits all holy places, O King, he, having burnt all sins (committed) from his birth and in other (i.e. previous) births, sees the bright, omnipresent, ancient source of Bhava, and is liberated.

## \|\| 2.12.12 \|\|

*tīrthe vipravaco grāhyaṃ snātvā saṃdhyārcanādikam \|*  
*darbhāstilā haviṣyānnaṃ prayogāḥ śraddhayā kṛtāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. At the holy place the words of a Brāhmaṇa should be accepted as authority. A man (visiting a holy place) should offer the (morning, noon and evening) prayer and worship etc. He should offer sesamum-seeds, food fit for an oblation; (such) acts done with faith (are the giver of religious merit).

## \|\| 2.12.13 \|\|

*agastyaṃ bhṛṅgarājaṃ ca puṣpaṃ śatadalaṃ śubham \|*  
*karpūrāguruśrīkhaṃḍaṃ kuṃkumaṃ tulasīdalam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. (He should offer) auspicious leaves of Agastya, Bhṛṅgarāja, a flower with a hundred petals, camphor, aloewood, sandal, saffron, Tulasi-leaf.

## \|\| 2.12.14 \|\|

*bilvapramāṇapiṃḍeṣu dīpoddyotitabhūmiṣu \|*  
*tāṃbūla phalanaivedyaṃ tiladarbhodakena ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. (He should offer) fruits with sesamum and Darbhas with water, on grounds shining with lamps, balls of the size of Bilva-fruits.

## \|\| 2.12.15-17 \|\|

*tīrthe saṃkalpitaṃ martyaistadanaṃtaṃ prajāyate \|*  
*ayane viṣuve caiva saṃkrāṃtau grahaṇeṣu ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

*māsāṃte'para pakṣe tu kṣayāhe pitṛmātṛke \|*  
*gajacchāyāṃ trayodaśyāṃ dravye prāptau dvijottamaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*gṛhe śrāddhaṃ prakurvīta pitṝṇāmṛṇamuktaye \|*  
*gṛhācchataguṇaṃ nadyāṃ yā nadī yāti sāgaram \|\| 17 \|\|*

15a. (All this) offered at a holy place by the mortals, multiplies indefinitely.

15b-17a. At the time of the Sun’s passage from one solstice to another, at an equinoctial point, on Saṃkrānti (i.e. on the day of the Sun’s passage from one Zodiacal sign into another), on eclipse-days, at the end of a month, in the second half of a month, on the day of the death of father or mother, at the time of the solar eclipse, on the thirteenth day of a month, when wealth is obtained, the best Brāhmaṇa should perform a Śrāddha at his house for paying off the debt of his dead ancestors.

17b. Śrāddha performed in (i.e. on the bank of) a river meeting the ocean is hundred times more effective.

## \|\| 2.12.18-19 \|\|

*prabhāse puṣkare rājangaṃgāyāṃ piṃḍatārake \|*  
*prayāge nṛpagomatyāṃ bhavadāmodarāgrataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*narmadādiṣu tīrtheṣu kuryācchrāddhaṃ naro yadi \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ pitaro yāṃti sadgatim \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. O King, if a man performs Śrāddha at Prabhāsa, Puṣkara, in (i.e. on the bank of) Gaṅgā, at Piṇḍatāraka in Prayāga, in (i.e. on the bank of the river) Gomatī facing Bhava and Dāmodara, or at a holy place like (the bank of rivers like) Narmadā, being free from all sins, attains beatitude.

## \|\| 2.12.20 \|\|

*saṃtānamuttamaṃ labdhvā bhuktvā bhogānanuttamān \|*  
*divyaṃ vimānamāruhya prānte yāti surālayam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Getting good progeny, enjoying excellent pleasures, he, getting into a divine aeroplane, ultimately goes to Heaven.

## \|\| 2.12.21 \|\|

*jātakarmādiyajñeṣu vivāhe yajñakarmaṇi \|*  
*devapratiṣṭhāprāraṃbhe vṛddhiśrāddhaṃ prakalpayet \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. One should perform Vṛddhiśrāddha (i.e. an offering made to the Manes on prosperous occasions like the birth of a son), at the sacrifices performed at the birth of a child, at the time of a marriage, performing a sacrifice, at the time of the installation of (the image of) a deity.

## \|\| 2.12.22 \|\|

*tṛpyanti devatāḥ sarvā stṛpyaṃti pitaro nṛṇām \|*  
*vṛddhiśrāddhakṛto gehe jāyate sarvamaṃgalam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. All deities are gratified, all dead ancestors are satisfied, everything auspicious takes place in the house of him who performs Vṛddhiśrāddha.

## \|\| 2.12.23-26 \|\|

*kāmaḥ krodhaśca lobhaśca moho madyamadādayaḥ \|*  
*māyā mātsaryapaiśunyamaviveko vicāraṇā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*ahaṃkāro yadṛcchā ca cāpalyaṃ laulyatā nṛpa \|*  
*atyāyāsopyanāyāsaḥ pramādo drohasāhasam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*ālasyaṃ dīrghasūtratvaṃ paradāropasevanam \|*  
*alpāhāro nirāhāraḥ śokaścauryaṃ nṛpottama \|\| 25 \|\|*

*etāndoṣāngṛhe nityaṃ varjayanyadi vartate \|*  
*sa naro maṇḍanaṃ bhūmerdeśasya nagarasya ca \|\| 26 \|\|*

23-26. O best king, if a man lives in his house avoiding such faults as desire of sensual enjoyments, anger, greed, infatuation, drinking liquor, intoxication, deceit, jealousy, calumny, imprudence, doubt, ego, randam \[random?\] act, fickleness, unsteadiness, too much exertion, want of exertion, error, deceit, rash act, laziness, procrastination, enjoying another’s wife, eating less, fasting, lamentation, theft, he is the ornament of that land, the country and the city.

## \|\| 2.12.27 \|\|

*śrīmānvidvānkulīno'sau sa eva puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*sarvatīrthābhiṣekaśca nityaṃ tasya prajāyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. He is rich, learned and well-born. He alone is the best man. To him accrues (the religious merit of) bathing at all holy places.

## \|\| 2.12.28 \|\|

*tadā tīrthaphalaṃ samyaktyaktadoṣasya jāyate \|*  
*snānaṃ sandhyā japo homaḥ pitṛdevarṣitarpaṇam \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ devasya pūjā ca tyaktadoṣasya jāyate \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Then the fruit of (staying at) a holy place is well produced in the case of him who has given up (i.e. who is free from) defects. A bath, prayer (at three times in a day), muttering of prayers, a sacrifice, pleasing manes, gods and sages, a Śrāddha, worship of the deities becomes (fruitful) in his case.

## \|\| 2.12.29-32 \|\|

*prayāge vā kurukṣetre sarasvatyāṃ ca sāgare \|*  
*gayāyāṃ vā rudrapade naranārāyaṇāśrame \|\| 29 \|\|*

*prabhāse puṣkare kṛṣṇe gomatyāṃ piṃḍatārake \|*  
*vastrāpathe girau puṇye tathā dāmodare nṛpa \|\| 30 \|\|*

*bhīmeśvare narmadāyāṃ skāṃde rāmeśvarādiṣu \|*  
*ujjayinyāṃ mahākāle vārāṇasyāṃ ca bhūrbhuvaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*kāliṃdyāṃ mathurāyāṃ ca sakṛdyāti naro yadi \|*  
*sadoṣo mucyate doṣairbrahmahatyādibhiḥ kṛtaiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

29-32. If a man (even) once visits any of the holy places on the earth like Prayāga, Kurukṣetra, (the bank of) Sarasvatī, (the coast of) an ocean, Gaṅgā, abode of Rudra, hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa, Prabhāsa, Puṣkara, Kṛṣṇa, (the bank of) Gomatī, Piṇḍatāraka, Vastrāpatha, the holy mountain, Dāmodara, Bhīmeśvara, on the bank of Narmadā, place of Skanda, and Rāmeśvara and Mahākāla at Ujjayinī, (Śiva) at Vārāṇasī, any holy place on the earth, (bank of) Kālindī, Mathurā, he, (even) guilty of sins like the murder of a Brāhmaṇa, is freed.

## \|\| 2.12.33-35 \|\|

*api kīṭaḥ pataṃgo vā pakṣī vā sūkaro'pi vā \|*  
*kharoṣṭrakuṃjarā vājimṛgasiṃhasarīsṛpāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*jñānato'jñānato rājaṃsteṣu sthā neṣu ye mṛtāḥ \|*  
*sarve te puṇyakarmāṇaḥ svargaṃ bhuktvā sukhaṃ bahu \|\| 34 \|\|*

*caturvarṇeṣu sarve te jāyaṃte karmabaṃdhanāt \|*  
*karmabaṃdhaṃ vihāyāśu muktiṃ yāṃti narāḥ punaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. O King, those—even a worm, a moth, a bird, or even a pig, a donkey, a camel, an elephant, a horse, a deer, a lion, or reptiles - who, knowingly or unknowingly die at (any one of) those places, all those, meritorious ones, having enjoyed great happiness in Heaven, are born among human beings of the four castes due to the bondage of their acts; and quickly casting off the bondage of acts, they are finally delivered.

## \|\| 2.12.36-37 \|\|

*modaṃte tīrthamaraṇātsvargabhogāvasānataḥ \|*  
*saṃprāpya bhārate khaṃḍe karmabhūmiṃ mahodayam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*anekāścaryasaṃyuktaṃ bahuparvatamaṃḍitam \|*  
*gaṃgāyāḥ saritaḥ sarvāḥ samudraiḥ saha saṃgatāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. After enjoying pleasures in Heaven due to death at a holy place, they having come to Bhārata Khaṇḍa, the land of their acts and very prosperous, full of many wonders, and adorned with many mountains, are delighted. (In Bharata) all rivers like Gaṅgā have met the oceans.

## \|\| 2.12.38 \|\|

*padepade nidhānāni saṃti tīrthānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*yeṣāṃ smaraṇamātreṇa sarvapāpakṣayo bhavet \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. (In it) there are many holy places, by remembering which all the sins are destroyed.

## \|\| 2.12.39 \|\|

*pātālamārgā bahavaḥ svargamārgaśca dṛśyate \|*  
*gagane dṛśyate sūryo hṛdaye dṛśyate haraḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Many roads leading to the Nether world (are seen). So also is seen the path to Heaven. The Sun is seen in the sky. Hara is seen in the heart.

## \|\| 2.12.40 \|\|

*dhyānena jñānayogena tapasā vacasā guroḥ \|*  
*satyena sāhasenaiva dṛśyate bhuvanatrayam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The triad of the worlds is seen by means of meditation, contemplation, penance, speech, and by means of the words of the preceptors. The triad of the worlds is seen by means of truth and boldness only.

## \|\| 2.12.41 \|\|

*vedasmṛtipurāṇaiśca ye na paśyaṃti bhūtalam \|*  
*pātālaṃ svargalokaṃ ca vaṃcitāste narā iha \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Those men, who do not see the world by means of the Vedas, Smṛtis and Purāṇas, so also the Nether world and the Heaven, are duped here.

## \|\| 2.12.42 \|\|

*ye virajyaṃti na strīṣu kāmāsaktā vicetasaḥ \|*  
*dehonyathā varastrīṇāmanyathā taiśca ciṃtitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. So also are duped those who are lustful and stupid. The body of excellent ladies is of another kind; and they think it to be different.

## \|\| 2.12.43 \|\|

*janmabhūmiṣu te raktā janyaṃte jaṃtavaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*muktimārgātpunarbhraṣṭā jāyaṃte paśuyoniṣu \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Attached to their birth places the creatures are reborn. Again falling off from the path of deliverance they are born in the species of beasts.

## \|\| 2.12.44 \|\|

*dhanāni saṃprāpya varāṭikāṃ ye dvijātimukhyāya vidhāya pūjām \|*  
*yacchaṃti no nirmalacetanā ye narādhamā daivahatā mṛtāste \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. They (not) of pure conscience, who having received (ample) wealth do not worship and offer (even) a cowrie to the chief Brāhmaṇa are mean men, ill-fated, and are (as good as) dead.

## \|\| 2.12.45-46 \|\|

*dehaṃ supuṣṭaṃ vijaraṃ ca yauvanaṃ labdhvā na gaṃgādiṣu yāṃti ye narāḥ \|*  
*mātā pitā no na suto na bāṃdhavo bhāryā svasā no duhitā na vidyate \|\| 45 \|\|*

*ekastu yo yāti kathaṃ na kliśyate mūrkho na jānāti bhavaṃ maheśvaram \|*  
*snātvā na paśyaṃti haraṃ maheśvaraṃ daivena te vai muṣitā narādhamāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

45a. Similar are persons, who in spite of getting a strong, unaging body, and youth, do not go to Gaṅgā etc.

46\. How is the man who does not have (with him, his) mother, father, son, relative, wife, sister, daughter, and goes (all) alone (on a pilgrimage \[i.e., yātrā\]) not pained! The fool does not know Maheśvara. Those mean men who after bathing do not see Hara, the great Lord, are carried off by fate.

## Chapter 13 - The Importance of Śrāddha Dāna

## \|\| 2.13.1-2 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*chittvā śubhāśubhaṃ karma muktimicchecchivāṃ tataḥ \|*  
*idaṃ na śakyate karttuṃ śubhaṃ kāryaṃ tadā naraiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*utthāyotthāya snātavyaṃ pūjyau hariharau svayam \|*  
*satyaṃ vācyaṃ hitaṃ kāryaṃ dānaṃ deyaṃ svaśaktitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

1-2. Having cut off (the effects of) auspicious or inauspicious acts, one should then desire happy deliverance. If it is not possible to do this good act, one should bathe after waking up and worship Viṣṇu and Śiva; one should speak the truth, do whatever is beneficial, give in charity according to one’s capacity.

## \|\| 2.13.3 \|\|

*parāpavādabhīrutvaṃ paradārānvivarjayet \|*  
*suvarṇabhūmiharaṇabrahmadevasvavarjanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. One should avoid scandal and timidity; so also other’s wife; one should avoid taking away (others’) gold, land, wealth of a Brāhmaṇa, of a deity.

## \|\| 2.13.4 \|\|

*brāhmaṇastrīnareṃdrāṇāṃ bālavṛddhatapasvinām \|*  
*pitṛmātṛgurūṇāṃ ca nāpriyaṃ manasā vadet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. One should not mentally talk (i.e. think) unpleasant things about a Brāhmaṇa, a woman, a king, a child, an old person, an ascetic; so also about one’s father, mother and teacher.

## \|\| 2.13.5-8 \|\|

*deśakālaparijñānaṃ pātrāpātravivecanam \|*  
*chāyā nṛṇāṃ na vaktavyā takrāgnīṃdhanakāṃjikam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*auṣadhaṃ śākamarthibhyo dātavyaṃ gṛha medhibhiḥ \|*  
*ekādaśīpaṃcadaśīcaturdaśyaṣṭamīṣu ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

*amāvāsyāvyatīpātasaṃkrāṃtigrahaṇeṣu ca \|*  
*vaidhṛte pitṛmātrośca kṣayāhadivaseṣu ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

*yugādimanvādidine gṛhe kāryo mahotsavaḥ \|*  
*tīrthe vā gamanaṃ kāryaṃ gṛhācchataguṇaṃ yataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

5-8. (One should have) the knowledge of place and time and should discriminate between the worthy and the unworthy; one should not talk about (other) mens’ darkness (i.e. defect); householders should give butter-milk, fire, wealth, sour gruel, medicine, vegetables to the suppliants. On the eleventh day, the fifteenth day, the fourteenth day, the eighth day (of a fortnight), on the New-Moon day, on the day of any great calamity, on a Śaṃkrānti \[Saṃkrānti?\] day, so also on the day of an eclipse, on the day of a particular position of the Sun and the Moon considered to be inauspicious and malignant, on the day of the death of one’s father or mother, so also on a day when the Yuga had started, on a day when the age of Manu set in, a great festival should be observed in the house, or one should go to a holy place, as this is hundredfold more effective (than staying at one’s residence).

## \|\| 2.13.9 \|\|

*idriyāṇāṃ jayaḥ kāryo madyaṃ dyūtaṃ vivarjayet \|*  
*vivādaṃ gamanaṃ yuddhaṃ gṛhī yatnena varjayet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The sense-organs should be controlled, one should avoid liquor, gambling. A householder should carefully avoid dispute, march, war.

## \|\| 2.13.10 \|\|

*snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homo devapūjā dvijārcanam \|*  
*akṣayaṃ jāyate sarvaṃ vidhivaccedbhavetkṛtam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. If a bath, giving (gifts), muttering of prayers, sacrifice, worship of deities and of Brāhmaṇa are properly done, all of them become inexhaustible.

## \|\| 2.13.11 \|\|

*ekāpi gauḥ pradātavyā vastrālaṃkārabhūṣaṇā \|*  
*dogdhrī savatsā taruṇī dvijamukhyāya kalpitā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. At least one cow, adorned with garments and ornaments, yielding milk, having a calf, young, designed for the chief of Brāhmaṇas, should be given (to a Brāhmaṇa).

## \|\| 2.13.12 \|\|

*saṃprāpya bhārataṃ khaṃḍaṃ mānuṣaṃ janma cottamam \|*  
*dhanyo dadāti yo dhenuṃ sa naraḥ sūryamaṇḍalam \|*  
*bhittvā yāti vimānena gamyamāno gavādibhiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. After reaching Bhārata Khaṇḍa, securing the best (i.e. human) birth, a man who gives a cow is blessed. Piercing the sun’s orb, accompanied by cows etc. he goes in an aeroplane (to Heaven).

## \|\| 2.13.13 \|\|

*sapta janmāni pāpāni kṛtvā pāpīha cādhamaḥ \|*  
*eko dadāti yo dhenuṃ mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A mean sinner, who, having committed sins in seven births, gives a cow, is freed from all sins.

## \|\| 2.13.14 \|\|

*yadā sa nīyate baddho yamamārgeṇa kiṃkaraiḥ \|*  
*tadā naṃdā samāgatya svaṃ putramiva paśyati \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. When, he, being bound by (Yama’s) servants is taken along Yama’s path, Nandā (the divine cow) comes there and looks upon him as her own son.

## \|\| 2.13.15 \|\|

*vijitya huṃkṛtenaiva tāndūtāndūrataḥ sthitān \|*  
*gopradaṃ taṃ samādāya prayāti śivamandiram \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Overpowering them, standing away, just by her ‘hum’ sound, and taking (with her) the giver of the cow she goes to Śiva’s abode.

## \|\| 2.13.16-18 \|\|

*vṛṣo dharma hati prokto yena muktaḥ sa mucyate \|*  
*goṣu madhye pitṝnsarvānharamuddiśya vā harim \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sūryabrahmapure vāso jāyate brahmavāsare \|*  
*dṛḍhaṃ kakudminaṃ saṃtaṃ yuvānaṃ bhārasādhanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*halakṣamaṃ balīvardaṃ dattvā viprāya parvasu \|*  
*tamāruhya naro yāti golokaṃ śivasaṃnidhau \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. Dharma (moral merit) is said to be a bull. One who is liberated by it is really liberated. (If) among the cows a man makes offerings to all his dead ancestors, or to Hara or Han, he gets residence in the city of the Sun or Brahmā on the Day of Brahmā. By giving a bull capable of drawing a plough to a Brāhmaṇa on the days of the four changes of the moon (viz. 2nd, 8th, 14th tithis & Full Moon), he, mounted on that bull, goes to the world of cows, viz., the proximity of Śiva.

## \|\| 2.13.19 \|\|

*aśvaṃ sāstaraṇaṃ dattvā khalīnena ca saṃyutam \|*  
*aśvarājabalātsvarge modate brāhmavāsaram \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. By giving a horse with a covering or a bit of a bridle, he enjoys, due to the power of the lordly horse, for a Day of Brahmā.

## \|\| 2.13.20 \|\|

*gajadānādgajeṃdreṇa nīyate naṃdanaṃ vanam \|*  
*pṛthivyāṃ sāgarāṃtāyāmeṣa rājā bhaviṣyati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Due to the gift of a lordly elephant, he is taken to Indra’s garden by that elephant. He becomes the king of the earth.

## \|\| 2.13.21 \|\|

*gṛhaṃ sopaskaraṃ dattvā viprāya gṛhamedhine \|*  
*labhate naṃdane divyaṃ vimānaṃ sārvakāmikam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. By giving a house with furniture to a Brāhmaṇa householder, he gets a divine aeroplane fulfilling all desires in Indra’s garden.

## \|\| 2.13.22 \|\|

*dravyaṃ pṛthivyāṃ paramaṃ suvarṇaṃ hṛṣyaṃti devā yadi dīyate tataḥ \|*  
*sūryopi tasmai ruciraṃ vimānaṃ dadāti tāvadbhramate'tra yāvat \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Gold is great wealth on the earth; Gods are delighted if it is given. As long as he roams here the Sun also gives him a shining aeroplane.

## \|\| 2.13.23 \|\|

*raupyaṃ pitṝṇāmativallabhaṃ taddattvā naro nirmalatāmupaiti \|*  
*somasya lokaṃ labhate sa tāvadbhuve nivaddhā ṛṣayo hi yāvat \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Silver is very dear to the dead ancestors. By giving it a man becomes pure. As long as the (Seven) Sages are fixed on Dhruva (the Polar Star) he resides in the world of Soma.

## \|\| 2.13.24 \|\|

*śrīkhaṃḍakarpūrasamākulāni tāṃbūlaratnādiphalāni dattvā \|*  
*puṣpāṇi vastrāṇi sukhena yāti sākaṃ śaśāṃkaṃ divi devavṛṃdaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. If he gives betel-leaf, jewels with sandalwood, camphor, (so also) flowers and garments, he happily goes to the Moon with groups of gods.

## \|\| 2.13.25-26 \|\|

*takrodakatailaghṛtadugdhekṣurasamadhūni yo dadyāt \|*  
*kharjūrakhaṃḍadrākṣāvātāmāṃjīrakaiḥ sākam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*darbhākṣatamṛdgomayadūrvāyajñopavītāni \|*  
*tilacarmasūryapiṭakaṃ dattvā khyātaściraṃ svarge \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. He, who would, give buttermilk, water, oil, clarified butter, milk, sugarcane juice, with candy, dates, bunches of grapes and figs, Darbhas, grains (whole used as article of worship), clay, cow-dung, Dūrvā grass, sacred threads, sesamum seeds, hide, Arka plant, is known for a long time in Heaven.

## \|\| 2.13.27 \|\|

*ātmāhārāccaturbhāgaṃ siddhānnādyadi dīyate \|*  
*hantakāraḥ sa taṃ dattvā dhruvaṃ yāti dhruvālaye \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. If from one’s food that is ready, one-fourth is given as an offering, the giver, one giving it certainly goes to Dhruva’s place.

## \|\| 2.13.28 \|\|

*ātmāhārapramāṇena pratyahaṃ goṣu dīyate \|*  
*gavāhnikaṃ tāsu dattvā naro yāti surālayam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. If, according to the measure of one’s food, daily measure of food is everyday given to cows, a man (who gives it) goes to the abode of gods.

## \|\| 2.13.29 \|\|

*kaṃḍanīpeṣaṇīcullīmārjanībhiśca yatkṛtam \|*  
*pāpaṃ gṛhī kṣālayati dadadbhikṣāṃ dinaṃ prati \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. By giving alms everyday, a householder washes off the sins committed with (the use of) a wooden mortar, a muller, a fire-place, a broom.

## \|\| 2.13.30 \|\|

*grāsamātrā bhavedbhikṣā sā nityaṃ yatra dīyate \|*  
*tadgṛhaṃ gṛhamanyacca smaśānamiva dṛśyate \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The alms may be of the size of a morsel; (but) if it is given everyday, (then) that is (indeed) a home; any other house appears like a cremation ground.

## \|\| 2.13.31 \|\|

*kumbhānsodakasiddhānnāṃśchatropānatkamaṃḍalum \|*  
*aṃgulīyakavāsāṃsi dattvā yāti naro divi \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. By giving pitchers with water, ready (cooked) food, an umbrella, shoes, a water-pot used by ascetics, a ring, garments a man goes to the abode of gods.

## \|\| 2.13.32 \|\|

*śrāṃtasya yānaṃ tṛṣitasya pānamannaṃ kṣudhārttasya naro narendra \|*  
*dattvā vimānena surāṃganābhiḥ saṃstūyamānastridivaṃ sa yāti \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O King, by giving a vehicle to one who is tired, water to a thirsty man, food to a hungry man, one goes, being praised by divine ladies, to Heaven in an aeroplane.

## \|\| 2.13.33 \|\|

*bhojanaṃ satataṃ deyaṃ yathāśaktyā ghṛta plutam \|*  
*tanmayā hi yataḥ prāṇā ataḥ puṣyaṃti prāṇinaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. A meal covered with ghee should always be given according to one’s capacity. Since the (five) vital airs are made of it, therefore beings are nourished (by it).

## \|\| 2.13.34 \|\|

*kṣutpīḍā mahatī loke hyannaṃ tadbheṣajaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*tena sā śāṃtimāyāti tatonnaṃ deyamuttamam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. In the world the suffering due to hunger is great. Food is supposed to be the medicine against it. By that he gets peace. Therefore excellent food should be given.

## \|\| 2.13.35-37 \|\|

*annaṃ vastraṃ phalaṃ toyaṃ takraṃ śākaṃ ghṛtaṃ madhu \|*  
*patraṃ puṣpaṃ tathopānatkaṃthāṃ yaṣṭiṃ kamaṃḍalum \|\| 35 \|\|*

*chatrapātre vrataṃ vidyā akṣamālā surārcanam \|*  
*kanyā kuśopavītāni bījauṣadhagṛhāṇi ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

*sasyaṃ kṣetraṃ yajñapātraṃ yogapaṭṭaṃ ca pāduke \|*  
*kṛṣṇājinaṃ buddhidānaṃ dharmādeśakathānakam \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. A man should always give food, garments, fruits, water, butter milk, vegetables, clarified butter, honey, leaves, flowers; so also shoes, a patched garment, a stick, a water-pot used by ascetics, an umbrella, a pot, a vow, learning, a rosary worship of deities, his daughter, sacred threads worn by the first three classes of Hindus, seeds, medicines, houses, crop, field, sacrificial utensils, a cloth thrown over the back and knees used by ascetics during abstract meditation, wooden shoes, hide of black antelope, knowledge, (tell) a tale for religious instruction.

## \|\| 2.13.38 \|\|

*athaitatsaṃtataṃ deyaṃ tena śreyo mahadbhavet \|*  
*sarvapāpakṣayaṃ kṛtvā dātā yāti śivālayam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. And this should be given regularly. Due to that great credit would be (accomplished). Having destroyed all (his) sins the giver goes to Śiva’s abode.

## \|\| 2.13.39 \|\|

*śrāddhe gṛhasthā bhoktavyāḥ kulīnā vedapāragāḥ \|*  
*akrodhanāḥ snānaśīlāḥ svadeśācāratatparāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. At a śrāddha (a funeral rite performed in honour of the departed spirits of dead relatives) having invited Brāhmaṇas who belong to a good family, who have mastered the Vedas, who do not get angry, who are habituated to taking bath everyday, who are exclusively devoted to the practices of their country, who are free from desires, who are not greedy, who are free from any disease, who are not village-priests, should be invited on the previous day, and the presentation of the obsequial rice-balls should be done in front of them.

## \|\| 2.13.40 \|\|

*āmaṃtrya pūrvadivase nirīhā api ye dvijāḥ \|*  
*alolupā vyādhihīnā na tu ye grāmayājinaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Śrāddha offered by one who has no faith, is as good as not performed, even though it is performed.

## \|\| 2.13.41 \|\|

*teṣāṃ puraḥ pradātavyaṃ piṃḍadānaṃ vidhānataḥ \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ śraddhāvihīnena kṛtamapyakṛtaṃ bhavet \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Therefore Śrāddha should be performed by those, free from anger, who have faith.

## \|\| 2.13.42-43 \|\|

*tasmācchraddhānvitaiḥ śrāddhaṃ karttavyaṃ krodhavarjitaiḥ \|*  
*vānaprastho brahmacārī pathikastīrthasevakaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*atithirvaiśvadevāṃte sa pūjyaḥ śrāddhakarmaṇi \|*  
*sarvadā yatayaḥ pūjyāḥ svaśaktyā gṛhamedhibhiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. One living in the forest, a celebate, a traveller, one visiting holy places, should be honoured at a Śrāddha with the thought ‘A guest is all gods’.

## \|\| 2.13.44 \|\|

*yātrāvidhimatho vakṣye setihāsaṃ nṛpottama \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Householders should always honour ascetics according to their capacity.

## \|\| 2.13.45 \|\|

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O best king, now I shall tell the mode of pilgrimage.

## Chapter 14 - The Birth of Someśvara (Soma-īśvara)

## \|\| 2.14.1-3 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*vastrāpathe mahākṣetre nagare vāmane purā \|*  
*putraśokābhisaṃtapto vasiṣṭho bhagavānṛṣiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ājagāma tapastaptuṃ svarṇarekhānadītaṭe \|*  
*īśānakoṇe nagarātsvarṇarekhānadījale \|\| 2 \|\|*

*snātvā dhyātvā śivaṃ devaṃ manasā'cintayadyadā \|*  
*tadā rudraḥ samāyātastrinetro vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*maharṣe tava tuṣṭo'haṃ kiṃ karomi vadasva tat \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

1-2a. Formerly revered sage Vasiṣṭha tormented by the grief (of the loss) of his son came to a small city in the great holy place Vastrāpatha on the bank of the river Svarṇarekhā to practise penance.

2b-3. Having bathed in the river in the north-east comer and having meditated upon God Śiva, when he thought with his mind, Rudra, having three eyes, came there and said: “O great sage, I am pleased with you. Tell me what I should do”.

## \|\| 2.14.4 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭo mahādeva varo deyo mamādhunā \|*  
*tadā'tra bhavatā stheyaṃ yāvadācaṃdratārakam \|\| 4 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

4\. If, O Mahādeva, you are pleased (with me) then I should be given a boon now. You should stay here as long as the Moon and the Stars exist (in the sky).

## \|\| 2.14.5 \|\|

*atra snānaṃ kariṣyaṃti ye narāḥ pāpakarmiṇaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ pāpakṣayo deva kartavyo bhavatā sadā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O God, you should always destroy the sin of those sinners who bathe here.

## \|\| 2.14.6 \|\|

*narā ye pāpakarmāṇaḥ pūjayaṃti trilocanam \|*  
*tānnarānnaya deveśa vimānaiḥ śivamaṃdiram \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O Lord of Gods, take those people, who have committed sins (but) worship Śiva, to Śiva’s abode in aeroplanes.

## \|\| 2.14.7 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*tathetyuktā haro devastatraivāṃtara dhīyata \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipuṃ hatvā narasiṃho mahābalaḥ \|*  
*trailokyamiṃdrāya dadau kālarudraṃ svayaṃ yayau \|\| 7 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

7\. Saying “Let it be so” God Śiva, vanished. The very powerful Narasiṃha, having killed Hiraṇyakaśipu, gave the three worlds to Indra and himself went to Kālarudra.

## \|\| 2.14.8 \|\|

*tadanvaye balirjātaḥ sa cātīva balā dhikaḥ \|*  
*ekātapatrāṃ pṛthivīṃ baliścakre balādhikaḥ \|*  
*akṛṣṭapacyā sujalā dharitrī sasyaśālinī \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Bali was born in his family, and he was very powerful. The very strong Bali brought the world under one umbrella. The earth had crops growing exuberantly, was well-watered, and had (ample) crops.

## \|\| 2.14.9 \|\|

*gandhavaṃti ca puṣpāṇi rasavaṃti phalāni ca \|*  
*āskandhaphalino vṛkṣāḥ puṭake puṭake madhu \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The flowers were fragrant; the fruits were juicy; trees bore fruits (even) from the trunks; honey (was found) in every food.

## \|\| 2.14.10 \|\|

*caturvedā dvijāḥ sarve kṣatriyā yuddhakovidāḥ \|*  
*goṣu sevāparā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāḥ śuśrūṣaṇe ratāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. All Brāhmaṇas had mastered (all) the four Vedas; Kṣatriyas were proficient in fighting; Vaiśyas were intent on serving the cows; Śūdras were engaged in serving (other castes).

## \|\| 2.14.11 \|\|

*sadācārā janapadā ītivyādhivivarjitāḥ \|*  
*hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanāḥ sarve sadānaṃdāḥ sadodyatāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Nations were free from calamities of the season (and other) diseases; all people in them were delighted and nourished, always joyful, and always busy.

## \|\| 2.14.12 \|\|

*kuṃkumāguruliptāṃgāḥ suveṣāḥ sādhumaṃḍitāḥ \|*  
*dāridryaduḥkhamaraṇairvimuktāścirajīvinaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. People had their bodies besmeared with saffron and aloe-wood (paste) and well-decorated; they were free from poverty, misery and death, and lived long.

## \|\| 2.14.13 \|\|

*dīpoddyotitabhūbhāgā rātrāvapi yathā dine \|*  
*vicaraṃti tathā martyā devā devālaye yathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Regions were lighted by lamps (and were bright) at night as by day. Men wandered as gods in the abode of gods.

## \|\| 2.14.14 \|\|

*pṛthivyāṃ svargarūpāyāṃ rājyaṃ cakre'suro baliḥ \|*  
*nityaṃ vivāhavāditrairnāditaṃ bhūpamaṃdiram \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The demon Bali ruled over the earth of the form of (i.e. resembling) Heaven. The palace everyday resounded with musical instruments.

## \|\| 2.14.15 \|\|

*dharitrīṃ bubhuje daityo devarājo yathā divi \|*  
*devendro balinā nityaṃ yajñaiḥ saṃtoṣitastadā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The demon enjoyed the earth as the King of gods in Heaven. The Lord of gods was always pleased by Bali with sacrifices at that time.

## \|\| 2.14.16 \|\|

*devānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca nāsti yuddhaṃ parasparam \|*  
*eka eva mahīpālo yuddhaṃ nāsti dharātale \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. There was no war between gods and demons. There was only one king; there was no war on the surface of the earth.

## \|\| 2.14.17 \|\|

*sapatnakakalirnāma nāsti yuddhaṃ harergajaiḥ \|*  
*na sarppanakulairnityaṃ na biḍālaiśca mūṣakaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Kali may be hostile; (but) a lion does not fight with elephants; a fight does not always take place between serpents and mongooses, nor between cats and mice.

## \|\| 2.14.18-19 \|\|

*maitrībhāvaṃ gataṃ sarvaṃ jagatsthāvara jaṃgamam \|*  
*trailokyabhramaṇaṃ kṛtvā nārado naṃdane vane \|\| 18 \|\|*

*gato na paśyate yuddhaṃ trailokye sacarācare \|*  
*tāvattasyodare pīḍā mahatī samajāyata \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. The entire world- immobile and mobile—had become friendly. Having roamed in the three worlds Nārada went to Indra’s garden. He did not see war in the three mobile and immobile worlds. Then great ache was produced iin his belly.

## \|\| 2.14.20 \|\|

*na me snānādinā kāryaṃ tarppaṇaiḥ kiṃ prayojanam \|*  
*japahomādinā sarvamanyathā mama ceṣṭitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. “I have nothing to do with a bath etc. What is the use of libation of water to the Manes of the deceased ancestors or with muttering prayers or sacrifices? All my behaviour is different.

## \|\| 2.14.21 \|\|

*tatsnānaṃ yatra yudhyante gajā daṃtavighaṭṭanaiḥ \|*  
*sā saṃdhyā yatra nihataiḥ kabandhairbhūrvibhūṣitā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. “That is a bath where the elephants fight by striking with their tusks. That is twilight which is adorned with headless trunks that are struck down.

## \|\| 2.14.22 \|\|

*kuṃtaghātavinirbhinnagajakumbhodbhavāsṛjā \|*  
*tṛpyaṃti yatra kravyādāstarpaṇaṃ tanmama priyam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. “That is libation of water in which goblins are satisfied with the blood coming up from the temples of elephants pierced by the strokes of lances.

## \|\| 2.14.23 \|\|

*gajaśīrṣairagamyāste nihatāḥ kṣatriyā raṇe \|*  
*sa homo yatra hūyaṃte gajāśca narapuṃgavāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. “Kṣatriyas unreachable by elephants’ heads are killed in the battle. That is a sacrifice where elephants and best men are killed.

## \|\| 2.14.24-28 \|\|

*śabdāgnau nāradasyāyaṃ homastrai lokyaviśrutaḥ \|*  
*chinnapādaśirohastairaṃtarāṃtravilabitaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*yadarcyate bhūmitalaṃ tanme nityaṃ surārcanam \|*  
*kiṃ devairdivi me kāryaṃ kiṃ manuṣyairdharātale \|\| 25 \|\|*

*pannagaiḥ kiṃ tu pātāle na yudhyante parasparam \|*  
*tathā kariṣye devendrādupendrācca dharātale \|\| 26 \|\|*

*rasātalaṃ baliryātu satyamastu vaco mama \|*  
*jīvitenāpi rājyena yadā dāmodaraṃ harim \|\| 27 \|\|*

*toṣayiṣyati yatnena tadendro'sau bhaviṣyati \|*  
*devendro vṛtrahā bhūtvā bhraṣṭarājyo bhaviṣyati \|\| 28 \|\|*

24-25a. “This sacrifice performed by Nārada into the fire of words is known in the three worlds. That is my daily worship of the gods where the ground is worshipped with the bodies with feet, heads, hands cut off, and entrails hanging.

25b-27a. “O Goddess, what have I to do with gods, or men on the earth, or with serpents in the nether world? I shall act in such a way that they do not fight with one another. From the Lord of gods and Upendra let Bali go to the Nether worlds; let my words come true.

27b-28. “When even by (sacrificing) his life or kingdom, he will please Dāmodara Hari, he will be Indra. The Lord of gods, being the killer of Vṛtra, will be deprived of his kingdom.

## \|\| 2.14.29 \|\|

*yadā vastrāpathe gatvā bhavaṃ bhāvena pūjayet \|*  
*surādhipastadā bhūyo brahmahatyāvivarjitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. “When he will, after going to Vastrāpatha, worship Bhava with devotion, he will, being free from the (sin of) killing a Brāhmaṇa, again be the Lord of gods.

## \|\| 2.14.30 \|\|

*anena mantrajāpyena sa śāṃtodarave danaḥ \|*  
*nārado devarājasya samīpaṃ sahasā yayau \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. With the muttering (i.e. repeated thoughts) of this sort (i.e. anxiety shout the outcome of the war), Nārada, with the pain in his belly (i.e. mind) ceased, suddenly went into the vicinity of the Lord of gods.

## \|\| 2.14.31-32 \|\|

*siṃhāsanaṃ samāruhya nandane saṃsthito hariḥ \|*  
*āste parivṛto deverdevarājo mahābalaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*nirīkṣamāṇo nṛtyantīṃ raṃbhāṃ tāṃ surasundarīm \|*  
*āyāṃtaṃ dadṛśe devo nāradaṃ vismayānvitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Indra, mounted on a throne, remained in Nandana (garden). The very powerful king of gods, watching Raṃbhā, the beautiful divine lady, saw with astonishment, Nārada arriving there.

## \|\| 2.14.33-34 \|\|

*aho viruddho bhagavānnārado mayi dṛśyate \|*  
*nṛtyate kiṃ na vā nṛtye gīyate kiṃ na gīyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

*vādyatāṃ tālamānaiḥ kiṃ yāvacciṃtāparo hariḥ \|*  
*ṛṣiḥ samāgatastāvajjalābhyukṣaṇata tparaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. “Oh! (the behaviour of) Nārada seems hostile to me. Why does he not dance in a dance (party)? Why does he not sing when musical instruments are played upon?”

When Hari was (thus) thinking the sage got inclined to bathing with water.

## \|\| 2.14.35 \|\|

*siṃhāsanaṃ parityajya samutthāyāgrataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*svāgatenābhivādyātha babhāṣe nāradaṃ hariḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Hari leaving the throne and getting up stood before (Nārada). Saluting him with a welcome, Hari said to Nārada:

## \|\| 2.14.36 \|\|

*maharṣe svāgataṃ te'dya kuto vā'ga myate tvayā \|*  
*snāne saṃdhyārcane home kuśalaṃ tava vidyate \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. “O great sage, today what brings you here? Is (everything) well with regard to your bath, prayers (offered in the morning, noon and evening) and sacrifices?”

## \|\| 2.14.37-38 \|\|

*iti prokto vihasyātha babhāṣe nārado harim \|*  
*yadyetajjāyate mahyaṃ kimanyena prayojanam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*prekṣaṇīkasya te sthānaṃ nāhaṃ paśyāmi svarpate \|*  
*yāvadrājyaṃ balestāvattvayā me na prayojanam \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Thus addressed, Nārada, laughed and said: “If this happens in my case, what have I to do with other (things)? O Lord of Heaven, I do not see you, who are lovely to the sight. As long as there is Bali’s rule, I have nothing to do with you.

## \|\| 2.14.39 \|\|

*ādityādyā grahāḥ sarve kāla mānena yojitāḥ \|*  
*āhutyā plāvitā meghā varṣaṃti hṛṣitā bhuvi \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. “All Planets like the Sun are fixed in view of the measure of time. Clouds overflowed with offerings, being delighted, shower (water) on the earth.

## \|\| 2.14.40 \|\|

*rogādimaraṇaṃ nāsti yamo dharmeṇa pīḍitaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. “There was no death due to a disease etc. Yama was harassed by Dharma.

## \|\| 2.14.41 \|\|

*ekātapatrāṃ pṛthivīṃ bubhuje sa narādhipaḥ \|*  
*trailokyanātheti mahānṛpeti saṃgrāmavidyākuśaleti nityam \|*  
*trailokyalakṣmīkucakāmuketi saṃstūyate cāraṇabaṃdivṛndaiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. “That Lord of men (i.e. King Bali) enjoyed the earth under one umbrella. He was everyday praised by the groups of wandering singers and bands as ‘the Lord of the three worlds’, as ‘a great king’, as ‘proficient in the knowledge of fighting’, as ‘desirous of the breasts of the Glory (Lakṣmī) of the three worlds’.

## \|\| 2.14.42 \|\|

*brahmeti kṛṣṇeti hareti bhūmāviṃdreti sūryeti dhanādhipeti \|*  
*devārinātheti surādhipeti jegīyate cāraṇabaṃdivṛndaiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. “He is praised by the groups of the wandering singers and bands as ‘Brahmā, Kṛṣṇa, Hara, Indra on the earth, Sun, the Lord of wealth (i.e. Kubera)’.

## \|\| 2.14.43 \|\|

*yuddhaṃ vinā daityagaṇā hasaṃti mattāḥ pramattāḥ kariṇo nadaṃti \|*  
*rathādhirūḍhāḥ puruṣā bhramaṃti senādhipā strīṣu gṛhe ramaṃti \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. “Without a war the hosts of demons are laughing; elephants in rut trumpetting; men, seated in chariots are wandering; Generals of army are amusing themselves among women.

## \|\| 2.14.44 \|\|

*yajñāgnidhūmena nabho virājate suvarṇarūpā pṛthivī virājate \|*  
*śūnyaṃ tu vedairbhuvanaṃ ca śobhate dhiṣṇyaṃ balerdairtyaigaṇaiśca śobhate \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. “The sky shines with the smoke of sacrificial fire. The golden earth shines. The house void of the Vedas looks gay. The place for the sacrificial fire looks splendid with the hosts of the demons of Bali.

## \|\| 2.14.45 \|\|

*balirna jānāti surādhipaṃ tvāṃ surāśca sarve baliyajñabhojinaḥ \|*  
*tvameva te'riṃ hṛdi ciṃtaya svayaṃ yuktaṃ tavedaṃ kathitaṃ mayeti \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. “Bali does not know (i.e. care for) you, the Lord of gods. All gods take their meals at Bali’s sacrifice. You yourself think of your enemy. I have told you this that is proper.

## \|\| 2.14.46 \|\|
