*raṃbhā na rājate raṃge menakā tvāṃ na manyate \|*  
*tilottamāpi manute balirājaṃ sureśvaram \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. “Raṃbhā does not appear beautiful on the stage. Menakā does not care for you. Even Tilottamā regards King Bali as the Lord of gods.

## \|\| 2.14.47 \|\|

*urvaśī caiva taṃ yāti sukeśā saha bhāṣate \|*  
*mañjughoṣā mukhaṃ vaktraṃ kṛtvā tvāṃ na nirīkṣate \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. “Urvaśī, of excellent hair, goes to him and talks with him. Mañjughoṣā, turning (away) her face, does not look at you.

## \|\| 2.14.48 \|\|

*pulomā pulakodbhedaṃ na karoti baliṃ vinā \|*  
*paulomī purato gatvā baliṃ stauti ca maṃtharā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. “Pulomā does not have horripilation without Bali. Mantharā goes in front of Paulomī (Indra’s wife) and praises Bali.

## \|\| 2.14.49 \|\|

*nāradaḥ parvataścaiva hāhā hūhūśca tuṃburuḥ \|*  
*balirājyaṃ praśaṃsaṃti rudrasyāgre mayā śrutam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. “Nārada, Parvata, Hāhā, Hūhū and Tumburu praise Bali’s kingdom in the presence of Rudra. I have heard this.

## \|\| 2.14.50-51 \|\|

*ājyāhutībhiḥ santuṣṭā ṛṣayo brahmasadmani \|*  
*brahmaṇo'gre praśaṃsaṃti tadevaṃ kathitaṃ mayā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*bṛhaspatiryadācaṣṭe na tadvācyaṃ mayā tava \|*  
*iṃdrāṇī balinaṃ matvā baliṃ citreṣu paśyati \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. “The sages are satisfied with the offerings of clarified butter in Brahmā’s house; they praise (Bali) in the presence of Brahmā. Thus I have told (you). “Whatever Bṛhaspati said, is not to be told.”

## \|\| 2.14.52-53 \|\|

*anena vākyena surādhipastu cacāla kopāvaritastadānīm \|*  
*gajeti vajreti jagāda sūtaṃ samānayāsiṃ kavacaṃ rathaṃ ca \|\| 52 \|\|*

*rathena sūryo maruto gajena vṛṣeṇa rudro mahiṣeṇa sauriḥ \|*  
*vādyaṃtu vādyāni raṇāya me'dya caṇḍī gaṇeśāstvaritāḥ prayātu \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. The Lord of gods, then, filled with anger, trembled. He said to the charioteer. “O Gaya, go; bring (my) sword, armour, and chariot. Let the Sun with the chariot, Maruta (Wind) with the elephant, Rudra with the bull, Yama with the buffalo play upon musical instruments for my fight today. Let Caṇḍī and Gaṇeśa go quickly.”

## \|\| 2.14.54 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā surendraṃ saṃkruddhaṃ bṛhaspatirudāradhīḥ \|*  
*ṛṣimadhye gato vidvānbabhāṣe samayocitam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Seeing the Lord of gods (Indra) angry, the highly intelligent Bṛhaspati went among the sages and spoke what was proper for the occasion:

## \|\| 2.14.55-57 \|\|

*sāmādyā nītayaḥ proktāścatasro manunā purā \|*  
*sāmasādhyeṣu kāryeṣu daṇḍastena na pātyatām \|\| 55 \|\|*

*ato hyupendrmāhūya maṃtrayantu surottamāḥ \|*  
*tadadhīnaṃ jagatsarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 56 \|\|*

*vinaṣṭeṣu ca kāryeṣu tasya vācyaṃ śubhāśubham \|*  
*sa eva prathamaṃ gacchetpṛthivyāṃ svārthasiddhaye \|\| 57 \|\|*

55-57. “Formerly Manu has advised four expedients to be used by a king against his enemy like conciliation. He should not inflict punishment for a matter that can be settled through conciliation. Therefore, let the best gods, calling Upendra, hold consultation. The entire world, the three worlds including the movable and the immovable, are under his control. When moves have failed, whatever there is good or bad should be reported to him. He alone would first go to the earth for our own interest.”

## \|\| 2.14.58 \|\|

*tatheti devairvijñaptastathā cakre sureśvaraḥ \|*  
*mandare'tha girau viṣṇuḥ satyalokātsamāgataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Respectfully told by the gods ‘All right’, the Lord of gods did likewise. From Satyaloka Viṣṇu came (down) to Mandāra mountain.

## \|\| 2.14.59 \|\|

*ṛṣayastatra te yāṃtu samānetuṃ janārddanam \|*  
*ityukto nāradaḥ svargātsnātuṃ prāptaḥ sa mandare \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. “Let the sages go there to fetch Janārdana.” Thus told Nārada came down from Heaven to bathe at Mandāra.

## \|\| 2.14.60 \|\|

*gautamo'trirbharadvājo viśvāmitro'tha kaśyapaḥ \|*  
*jamadagnirvasiṣṭhaśca saṃprāptā harimandire \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Gautama, Atri, Bharadvāja, Viśvāmitra and Kaśyapa, (so also) Jamadagni, Vasiṣṭha came to Hari’s abode.

## \|\| 2.14.61 \|\|

*girau gaṃgā jale snānaṃ saṃdhyāṃ cakre sa nāradaḥ \|*  
*yāvadāste tadā hṛṣṭā vālakhilyā maharṣayaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. In the mountain that Nārada bathed in the water and offered his prayer. When he sat there, he saw the great sages Vālakhilyas.

## \|\| 2.14.62 \|\|

*vinayenābhivādyātha kathayāmāsa nāradaḥ \|*  
*ṛṣayo mandare prāptā viṣṇuṃ netuṃ surālaye \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Having politely saluted, Nārada said: “To take Viṣṇu to Heaven the sages have reached Mandara.

## \|\| 2.14.63 \|\|

*ṛṣayo darśanaṃ karttuṃ bhavatāmapi yujyate \|*  
*tadetadvacanaṃ śrutvā harṣitāste maharṣayaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. “It is proper if the sages see you.” Hearing these words the great sages were delighted.

## \|\| 2.14.64-66 \|\|

*aṃguṣṭhaparvamātrāṃstānvāmanānharimandire \|*  
*gatāngaṃgājale snātuṃ vālakhilyānpuro hariḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*jahāsa vāmanānsarvānbhāvikāryabalāttataḥ \|*  
*brahmaputrā vālakhilyāḥ sarve te śaṃsitavratāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*lajjānvitāḥ krodhaparā uccairūcuḥ parasparam \|*  
*kenāpi devakāryeṇa vāmano'yaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 66 \|\|*

64-66. Seeing them (i.e. the Vālakhilyas) of the size of a portion of thumb, who had gone to Hari’s abode, and who had gone to bathe in the water of Gaṅgā, Harī \[Hari?\] laughed before all of them. Then due to the importance of the future undertaking all of them, the sons of Brahmā, and (they) whose vows were praised, being full of shame and very angry spoke to one another: “Due to some mission of gods, this (Hari) will be a dwarf’.

## \|\| 2.14.67 \|\|

*ṛṣibhirvi ṣṇunā sarve pratibodhya prasāditāḥ \|*  
*bhāgyamokṣaḥ kadā viṣṇorbhaviṣyati taducyatām \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. All of them, advised by the sages, (and) Viṣṇu were propitiated. “Say when there will be the lucky release of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.14.68 \|\|

*prabhāsādadhikaṃ kṣetraṃ yadā vastrāpathaṃ bhavet \|*  
*bhaviṣyati tadā vṛddhirdhruvamaṇḍalavyāpinī \|*  
*tathā vastrāpathaṃ kṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati yavādhikam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. “When the holy place Vastrāpatha will be superior to Prabhāsa, there will be prosperity pervading the orb of Dhruva. So also the holy place Vastrāpatha will be (known as) ‘Yavādhika’.

## \|\| 2.14.69 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā someśvaraṃ devaṃ doṣamukto bhaviṣyati \|*  
*asādhyasādhanī śaktirbhaviṣyati sthirā tava \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. “Seeing god Someśvara he will be free from censure. You will have a firm power capable of accomplishing what is impossible to accomplish.

## \|\| 2.14.70 \|\|

*vastrāpathe somanāthaṃ yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati \|*  
*indropendrau samāliṃgyāthāsīnau tau varāsane \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. “He who sees Somanātha at Vastrāpatha, sees (everything). Indra and Upendra embracing (each other) sat on excellent seat.”

## \|\| 2.14.71 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*kiṃ te kāryaṃ devarāja tadavaśyaṃ karomyaham \|\| 71 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:

71\. What is your mission, O King of gods? I shall certainly do it.

## \|\| 2.14.72 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśiporvaṃśe balirdaityo mahā balaḥ \|*  
*tenedaṃ sakalaṃ vyāptaṃ devā yajñabhujaḥ kṛtāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

Indra said:

72\. Bali is a very powerful demon in the family of Hiraṇyakaśipu. He has occupied all this. He has made gods enjoy it.

## \|\| 2.14.73 \|\|

*devaloke bhūmiloko gataḥ sarvo'pi keśava \|*  
*yāvanno vikṛtiṃ yāti pūrvavairamanusmaran \|*  
*bhraṣṭarājyo balistāvatpātālamadhitiṣṭhatu \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. O Keśava, the entire world has gone to Heaven. As long as Bali, recollecting the former enmity, is not disturbed, let him, deprived of his kingdom, resort to the last of the seven regions under the earth.

## \|\| 2.14.74 \|\|

*sūryasomānvaye kaścidrājā bhavatu bhūtale \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Let there be some king on the earth in the solar or lunar family.

## \|\| 2.14.75-76 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*ityetadvacanaṃ śrutvā svayaṃ saṃcintya cetasā \|*  
*tathā kariṣye taṃ procya munīnprāha janārdanaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*ṛṣayastatra gacchaṃtu kārayantu mahāmakham \|*  
*ahaṃ tatrāgamiṣyāmi sādhayiṣyāmi taṃ balim \|\| 76 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

75-76. Hearing these words, and thinking to himself, Janārdana, speaking to him, “I shall do like that”, said to the sages: “Let the sages go there and perform a great sacrifice. I shall come there and subdue that Bali.”

## \|\| 2.14.77 \|\|

*ityuktā munayaḥ sarve gatāste yajñamaṇḍape \|*  
*dvādaśāho mahāyajñaḥ prārabdhaḥ sarvadakṣiṇaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Thus addressed, all the sages went to the hall of the sacrifice. A sacrifice in which everything was given as present to the Brāhmaṇas, was begun.

## \|\| 2.14.78 \|\|

*surāṣṭradeśaṃ vikhyātaṃ kṣetraṃ vastrāpathaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*tasya dakṣiṇadigbhāge baleḥ siddhaṃ mahāpuram \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. O King, in the Surāṣṭra country the holy place Vastrāpatha is well known. In its southern part is established the great city of Bali.

## \|\| 2.14.79 \|\|

*kṣetrādbahiḥ samārabdho yajñaḥ sarvasvadakṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*śukreṇāmantritāḥ sarve munayo yajñakarmaṇi \|*  
*atihṛṣṭo baliryajñe dadau dānānyanekadhā \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Outside the holy place a sacrifice in which everything was given as present to the Brāhmaṇas, Śukra invited all sages in the performance of the sacrifice. Bali, who was very much delighted, gave away various kinds of gifts.

## \|\| 2.14.80 \|\|

*svarṇapātreṣu sarveṣu dīyate bhojanaṃ bahu \|*  
*atithirbrāhmaṇo vidvānsarvasvenāpi pūjyate \|*  
*dānādyajño bhavetpūrṇo dānahīno vṛthā bhavet \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Sumptuous meals were given in golden plates. A guest, a learned Brāhmaṇa is propitiated even with all the wealth. A sacrifice will be complete with gifts, (but) without gifts it will be futile.

## \|\| 2.14.81 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu viṣṇurvāmanatāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*madhyadeśe caturvedo brāhmaṇastīrthayātrikaḥ \|*  
*mahodaro hrasvabhujaḥ khañjapādo mahāśirāḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. During this time only Viṣṇu became a dwarf in the Madhyadeśa. He became a Brāhmaṇa, who had mastered the four Vedas, who undertook a pilgrimage. His belly was large; his hands were short; he was lame; he had a large head.

## \|\| 2.14.82 \|\|

*mahāhanuḥ sthūlajaṃghaḥ sthūlagrīvo'tilaṃpaṭaḥ \|*  
*śvetavastro baddhaśikhaśchatropānatkamaṇḍalūn \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. His chin was big; his shanks were fat; his neck was bulky; he was very greedy. He had put on white garments; he had tied the lock of hair on the crown of the head. He carried an umbrella, sandals, and a water-pot used by ascetics.

## \|\| 2.14.83 \|\|

*draṣṭuṃ tīrthānyanekāni babhrāma sa mahītale \|*  
*surāṣṭradeśe saṃprāptaḥ kṣetre vastrāpathe dvijaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. To see many holy places, he wandered over the earth. The Brāhmaṇa reached the holy place Vastrāpatha in the Surāṣṭra country.

## \|\| 2.14.84 \|\|

*svarṇarekhā nadītīre ciṃtayāmāsa vāmanaḥ \|*  
*prathamaṃ kiṃ bhavaṃ dṛṣṭvā yāmi someśvaraṃ śivam \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Vāmana pondered at the bank of Svarṇarekhā river: ‘Shall I go to Someśvara Śiva after first seeing Bhava?

## \|\| 2.14.85-91 \|\|

*atha someśvaraṃ pūjya paścādyāsyāmi mandaram \|*  
*iti cintāparo bhūtvā kṛtyaṃ sañcintya cetasā \|*  
*atra sthitaḥ somanāthaṃ pūjayiṣyāmi niścitam \|\| 85 \|\|*

*vastrāpathe mahākṣetre bhavaṃ someśvaraṃ vṛthā \|*  
*pūjayaṃti janā nityaṃ tathā kāryaṃ mayā dhuvam \|\| 86 \|\|*

*deśānāmuttamo deśo girīṇāmuttamo giriḥ \|*  
*kṣetrāṇāmuttamaṃ kṣetraṃ nadīnāmuttamā sarit \|\| 87 \|\|*

*divyaṃ vanaṃ vanānāṃ tu devānāmuttamo bhavaḥ \|*  
*yadā someśvaro devo bhūmiṃ bhittvā bhaviṣyati \|\| 88 \|\|*

*tadāmramaṇḍale divyaṃ kṣetrametadyavādhikam \|*  
*caitra śuklacaturdaśyāmagnisādhanatatparaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

*ūrdhvabāhuḥ sūryakāle bhavaṃ tāvatsa paśyati \|*  
*madhyaṃdinaṃ paraṃ yāte dinanāthe vilaṃbite \|\| 90 \|\|*

*agni tāpāṃgasaṃtaptastāvatpaśyati śaṃkaram \|*  
*somanāthaṃ śivaṃ śāṃtaṃ sarvadevanamaskṛtam \|*  
*arghyeṇa puṣpamiśreṇa jalamiśreṇa bhāmini \|\| 91 \|\|*

85-89a. ‘Having worshipped Someśvara I shall then go to Mandāra.’ Thus given to thinking Vāmana thought about the act: ‘Remaining here I shall certainly do as people always do. They worship Someśvara Bhava at the great holy place Vastrāpatha. The country is the best among countries; the mountain is the best of mountains; the holy place is the best among holy places; the river is the best among rivers. The forest is divine among forests; Bhava is the best of gods. When God Someśvara will become (visible) after piercing the land, then in the sky a divine holy place larger by a yava (a very small measure will appear).

89b-90a. He, engaged in propitiating Agni on the fourteenth of the bright half of Caitra, and with his hands raised up, would see Bhava at the time of (the appearance of) the Sun (i.e. in the morning).

90b-91. When the forenoon has passed, and the Sun is hanging down (i.e. setting), he with his entire body heated by the heat of fire, and, O beautiful lady, with a respectful offering with flowers, sees Śaṅkara, Somanātha, Śiva (i.e. propitious), calm, and saluted by all gods’

## \|\| 2.14.92 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*bhūmiṃ bhittvātha deveśaḥ svayaṃ someśvaraḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*liṃgarūpo mahādevo yāvadābrahmavāsaram \|\| 92 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

92\. Piercing the land, the Lord of gods, Someśvara, Mahādeva, of the form of phallus remained (there) till Brahmā’s day.

## \|\| 2.14.93 \|\|

*someśvara uvāca \|*  
*siddhastvaṃ matprasādena kāryaṃ siddhaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*ityukto vāmano devaṃ pratyuvāca maheśvaram \|\| 93 \|\|*

Someśvara said:

93\. You are equipped through my favour. Your mission will succeed.

Thus addressed, Vāmana spoke back to God Maheśvara.

## \|\| 2.14.94 \|\|

*vāmana uvāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭo mahādeva yadi deyo varo mama \|*  
*tadā'tra liṃge sthātavyamastu divyaṃ puro mama \|\| 94 \|\|*

Vāmana said:

94\. If, O Mahādeva, you are pleased, if a boon is to be given to me, then you should remain here in (this) phallus. Let the divine (phallus) remain before me.

## \|\| 2.14.95-97 \|\|

*yastu svāyaṃbhuvaṃ liṃgaṃ vāmane nagare mama \|*  
*pūjayiṣyati brahmaghno goghno vā bālaghātakaḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

*gurudrohī svarṇacoro mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|*  
*nirdoṣaḥ pūjayedyastu sakṛtsomeśvaraṃ haram \|\| 96 \|\|*

*mṛto vimānamāruhya divyastrīpariveṣṭitaḥ \|*  
*saṃstūyamāno dikpālairyātu svarge śivālaye \|\| 97 \|\|*

95-96a. He, (even) a murderer of a Brāhmaṇa, a killer of a cow, or of a child, one committing perfidy against one’s teacher, stealing gold, who will worship this self-existent phallus in this city of Vāmana, is freed from all sins.

96b-97. That faultless man who (even) once worships Someśvara Hara, will go, after death, getting into an aeroplane, surrounded by divine ladies, praised by the Regents of Quarters, to the abode of Śiva in Heaven.

## \|\| 2.14.98 \|\|

*brahmalokamatikramya rudraloke sa gacchatu \|*  
*tathetyuktvā somanāthastatraivāntaradhīyata \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Crossing Brahmaloka, he will go to the world of Rudra. Saying (‘Let it be so’), Somanātha vanished there only.

## \|\| 2.14.99 \|\|

*prakāśya vāmano ligaṃ somanāthaṃ svayaṃbhuvam \|*  
*prāptajñāno labdhavṛddhiryayau draṣṭuṃ bhavaṃ haram \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Vāmana, having manifested the self-existent phallus of Somanātha, receiving knowledge and prosperity went to see Bhava Hara.

## \|\| 2.14.100 \|\|

*gaṃgādyāḥ saritaḥ sarvāḥ svarṇarekhājale sthitāḥ \|*  
*etāṃ someśvarotpattiṃ ye śṛṇvaṃti narāḥ striyaḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpakṣayasteṣāṃ jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. All rivers like Gaṅgā have remained in the water of Svarṇarekhā. There is no doubt that all the sins of those men or women, who listen to this origin of Bhava, are destroyed.

## Chapter 15 - The Greatness of Dāmodara

## \|\| 2.15.1-3 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*athāsau vāmano vipro labdhajñāno bhavārcane \|*  
*jagāma tadvanaṃ ramyaṃ gire raivatakasya yat \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yatra vṛkṣā bahuvidhā dīrghaśākhāḥ phalānvitāḥ \|*  
*vaṭodumbarabilvāśca sarjārjunakadaṃbakāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*palāśāśvatthaniṃbāśca dhavāṭīvāruṇīdrumāḥ \|*  
*śamīkaṃkolaliṃbāṃśca bījapūrī ca dāḍimaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

1-2a. Then that Brāhmaṇa Vāmana, who had obtained knowledge about the worship of Bhava, went to that charming forest which is on the Raivataka mountain, where there are various kinds of trees having long branches and fruits.

2b-3. (The trees were:) Vaṭa, udumbara, bilva, sarja, arjuna, kadambaka, palāśa, aśvattha, nimba, dhavāṭi, vāruṇī, śamī, kaṅkola, limba, bījapūrī, dāḍima,

## \|\| 2.15.4 \|\|

*badarī niṃbakaḥ pūgaḥ kadalī śallakī śivā \|*  
*tālahiṃtālaśirasā bījakāvaṃśakhādirāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. badara, nimbaka, pūga, kadalī, śallakī, śivā, tāla, hintāla, śirasa, bījaka, vaṃśa, khadira,

## \|\| 2.15.5 \|\|

*ajagāsanagāgucchā iṃgudīkoraveṃgudāḥ \|*  
*brahmavṛkṣāḥ kurubakāḥ karaṃjāḥ putrajīvinaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. ajaga, āsanaga, aguceha \[aguccha?\], iṅgudī, kora, veṅguda, brahmavṛkṣa, kurubaka, karañja, putrajīvin,

## \|\| 2.15.6 \|\|

*aṃkollāḥ pāribhadrāśca kalaṃbāḥ panasāstathā \|*  
*ujjvalāśca haridrāśca gaṃgaḍīvāyavā drumāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. aṅkolla, paribhadra, kalamba, paṅasa \[panasa?\], ujjvala, haridrā, gaṅgaḍī vāyava,

## \|\| 2.15.7 \|\|

*tesuṇḍakāḥ śirīṣāśca kharjūrīkaravaṃdikāḥ \|*  
*sevālī śālmalī śālā madhūkāśca vibhītakāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. tesuṇḍaka, sirīṣa, kharjūrī, karavandika, sevālī, śālmalī, śālā, madhūka, vibhītaka,

## \|\| 2.15.8 \|\|

*harītakyaḥ kaṭāhāśca karyaṣṭā āṭarūṣakāḥ \|*  
*vikacchavaḥ kapitthāśca rohiṇīvetrakadrumāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. harītakī, kaṭāha, karyaṣṭa, āṭarūpaka, vikacchu, kapittha, rohiṇī, vetraka,

## \|\| 2.15.9 \|\|

*madanaphalānirguṇḍīpāṭalānaṃdipādapāḥ \|*  
*lavaṃgailālavalyaśca santānā agarudrumāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. madanaphala, nirguṇḍī, pāṭala, nandi, creepers of lavaṅga, elāla-creepers, and tree like santāna, agaru,

## \|\| 2.15.10 \|\|

*śrīkhaṇḍakarpūranagāḥ kalpavṛkṣā nagotamāḥ \|*  
*vāmanena tadā dṛṣṭāśchāyāvṛkṣāḥ surārcitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. trees like śrīkhaṇḍa, karpūra, best trees like the resin-yielding trees. Vāmana saw shady trees worshipped by gods.

## \|\| 2.15.11 \|\|

*udayāstamane yeṣāṃ chāyā na pratihanyate \|*  
*teṣāṃ darśanamātreṇa sarvapāpakṣayo bhavet \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Their shadow was never lost at sunrise or sunset. Merely by seeing them all sins would be destroyed.

## \|\| 2.15.12 \|\|

*ye janāḥ puṇyakarmāṇasteṣāṃ te dṛṣṭigocarāḥ \|*  
*etānpaśyanyayau vṛkṣāṃstato raivatakaṃ girim \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. They are visible to those who have done pious acts. Seeing those trees he then went to Raivataka mountain.

## \|\| 2.15.13 \|\|

*yāvannirīkṣate tuṃgaṃ śikharaṃ tasya mūrddhani \|*  
*āścaryaṃ dadṛśe vipro mahallokabhayaṃkaram \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. When he saw the high peak (of the mountain) he saw on its top a great wonder, terrible in the world.

## \|\| 2.15.14 \|\|

*dhūmajvalanamadhyasthānpuruṣānpaṃca paśyati \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃgānkhecarānraudrānkṛṣṇāguruvibhūṣitān \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He saw five men in the midst of smoke and fire. Their bodies were dark; they moved in the sky; they were fearful; they were decorated with (the powder of) black aloe wood.

## \|\| 2.15.15 \|\|

*sārameya samārūḍhānkarihastānsamekhalān \|*  
*khaṅgakheṭakahastāṃśca ḍamaruḍḍāmarasvanān \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. They were mounted on dogs, having trunks like elephants and girdles. They had swords and clubs in their hands. They had a shrieking sound like that of a small drum.

## \|\| 2.15.16 \|\|

*saghargharīkacaraṇanyāsanāditaparvatān \|*  
*phetkārabhāsurākārānkāśakuñcitamūrddhajān \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. They had resounded the mountain by planting their feet that had bells. They had shapes fearful due to the cries. They had their hair curled wth \[with?\] kāśa grass.

## \|\| 2.15.17 \|\|

*naramāṃsavasāsārakavalavyagratālukān \|*  
*janagaṃdhasamājñānabhavatīvravilocanān \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Their palates were full with the essence of the marrow of human flesh. They had sharp eyes like Bhava cognizing the odour of the people.

## \|\| 2.15.18 \|\|

*pañcāgnisādhanāvyāptadivyacakṣuḥ prabhāvataḥ \|*  
*devānpaśyati viprendro jñātakāryaparaṃparaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The best Brāhmaṇa, who knew the series of errands, and who had obtained divine sight resulting from the practice of Pañcāgni (i.e. the austerity in which four fires are around the ascetic, and the fifth is the sun above), saw the gods.

## \|\| 2.15.19 \|\|

*ete kṣetrādhipāḥ pañca mahādevena nirmitāḥ \|*  
*mahābalā raivatake nivasaṃti girau sadā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. These five lords of the holy place were created by Mahādeva. They were very powerful. They always lived on the Raivataka mountain.

## \|\| 2.15.20 \|\|

*svecchācārānnarānmarttyānvārayati nage tathā \|*  
*hariṃ haraṃ nadīṃ devīṃ na paśyaṃti giriṃ yathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On the mountain they also ward off mortals acting according to their own will; so also those who do not see (with respect) Hari, Hara, a river, or a goddess, or the mountain.

## \|\| 2.15.21 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā jñātvā stutiṃ cakre dhyātvā devaṃ maheśvaram \|*  
*jayaṃti duṣṭadaityeṃdrayuddhadhyānāṃkitaṃ vapuḥ \|*  
*bibhrati bhrātaro ye te paṃceṃdrasamavikramāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Seeing, knowing and meditating upon God Maheśvara, they are spiteful. The five brothers, having prowess like five Indras, have a body marked with the thought about the war with the wicked lord of demons.

## \|\| 2.15.22 \|\|

*rudravaktrodbhavā dakṣā dakṣādhvaravināśakāḥ \|*  
*svāvalīḍhāhutīnaṣṭabhītavāḍavanaṃditāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The gods have sprung from the mouth of Rudra, are spiteful, and destroyers of Dakṣa’s sacrifice. They are delighted with the submarine fire extinguished and afraid due to having licked the offerings.

## \|\| 2.15.23 \|\|

*kuṅkumāgarukarpūraliptāṃgāḥ suvibhūṣitāḥ \|*  
*madirāmodamattāṃganṛtyagītakarāḥ surāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Their bodies were besmeared with saffron, sandal and camphor; they were well-decorated. They were singing and dancing with their bodies intoxicated with liquor.

## \|\| 2.15.24 \|\|

*brahmāṃḍabhramaṇaśrāṃta svagaṃdhatrastasaṃcarāḥ \|*  
*manojavāḥ kāmagamā kṣetrapālā jayaṃti te \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The Guardians of the holy place, who were tired due to moving in the universe and the odour of their own bodies, who had mind-like speed, who moved as they liked, were victorious.

## \|\| 2.15.25-26 \|\|

*ityādivacanāttuṣṭā dvijasyāgre svayaṃ sthitāḥ \|*  
*ekapādo'smyahaṃ caiko dvitīyo giridāruṇaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tṛtīyo meghanādastu siṃhanādaścaturthakaḥ \|*  
*paṃcamaḥ kālamegho'haṃ kurmaḥ kiṃ te vadasva tat \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Pleased with such and other words, they themselves remained before the Brāhmaṇa. (One of them said to the Brāhmaṇa:) “I am Ekapāda; the second one is Giridāruṇa. The third is Meghanāda; the fourth is Siṃhanāda; the fifth Kālamegha. What should we do? Tell us that.”

## \|\| 2.15.27 \|\|

*dvija uvāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭā bhavaṃto me yadi deyo varo dhuvam \|*  
*aho āpralayaṃ yāvatsthātavyaṃ matpratiṣṭhitaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇa said:

27\. If you are pleased with me, if you are certainly giving me a boon, (then) Oh! set up by me you should stay here till the final deluge.

## \|\| 2.15.28-29 \|\|

*ekapādo giri taṭe praharṣātprathamaṃ sthitaḥ \|*  
*vasatau vasatā tena girau ca giridāruṇaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*pratiṣṭhitaḥ prasādyātha varado'sau svayaṃ sthitaḥ \|*  
*ujjayaṃtagirermūrdhni meghanādaḥ svayaṃ yayau \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29a. Ekapāda, due to great joy, first remained on the slope of the mountain. Remaining in the dwelling on the mountain, he, having pleased Giridāruṇa, also set him up; and he, the giver of the boon, himself stayed there.

29b. Meghanāda himself went to the top of the mountain.

## \|\| 2.15.30 \|\|

*bhavānīśaṃkaraṃ ramyaṃ siṃhanādastathāviśat \|*  
*svayaṃ vastrāpathenaiva bhavasyāgre nirūpitaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Like that Simhanāda also entered the charming (holy place) Bhavānīśaṅkara and was settled before Bhava by Vastrāpatha himself.

## \|\| 2.15.31 \|\|

*svaṇarekhānadītīre kālamegho mahābalaḥ \|*  
*sarvalokopakārārthaṃ tīrthaṃ saṃsthāpitaṃ purā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The very mighty Kālamegha (was settled) on the bank of the river Svarṇarekhā. A holy place was established for obliging all people.

## \|\| 2.15.32-33 \|\|

*vāmanena svayaṃ gatvā kṣetrapālāstu pūjitāḥ \|*  
*purā yugādau rājeṃdra sarve devāḥ samāgatāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*surāṣṭradeśe saṃprāptāḥ puṇye raivatake girau \|*  
*rakṣārthaṃ sarvalokānāṃ vadhārthaṃ devavairiṇām \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. Vāmana himself went and worshipped the Guardians of the holy place. O Lord of Kings, formerly, at the beginning of the (Kali) age, all gods came, reached the holy Raivataka mountain for the protection of all worlds and killing the enemies of gods.

## \|\| 2.15.34 \|\|

*viṣṇoḥ kaṇṭhe tadā muktā jayamālā surottamaiḥ \|*  
*dāmodareti vikhyātaṃ dattaṃ nāmottamaṃ hareḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Then the best gods put the garland of victory round Viṣṇu’s neck. The holy place was given the well-known, best name of Hari viz. Dāmodara.

## \|\| 2.15.35 \|\|

*tatrādau kārtike śukle vāsare viṣṇuvallabhe \|*  
*upoṣya sahite devaistattīrthaṃ viṣṇunā kṛtam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. There in the beginning in the bright half of Kārttika, dear to Viṣṇu, fasting along with (other) gods, fashioned that holy place.

## \|\| 2.15.36-38 \|\|

*sarvatīrthamayī puṇyā svarṇarekhā nadī sthitā \|*  
*bhuktimuktipradaṃ puṇyaṃ viṣṇulokapradāyakam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*kṣālanaṃ sarvapāpānāṃ rogadāridryanāśanam \|*  
*dāmodaraṃ raivatake paramānaṃdadāyakam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*ye paśyaṃti vimānaiste nīyaṃte viṣṇumaṃdire \|*  
*na gṛhe kārtikaḥ kāryo viśeṣādbhīṣmapaṃcakam \|\| 38 \|\|*

36-38a. The river Svarṇarekhā, full of all holy places and sacred, remains (here). Those who see the holy place Dāmodara giving enjoyments and salvation, which washes off all sins, and destroys diseases and poverty, which gives great joy, are taken in aeroplanes to Viṣṇu’s abode.

38b. Kārttika should not be observed in the house especially Bhīṣmapañcaka (i.e. the five days from the eleventh to the fifteenth of the bright half of Kārttika).

## \|\| 2.15.39 \|\|

*paṃcakāddvādaśī śreṣṭhā kāryā dāmodare jale \|*  
*prātaḥsnānaṃ prakarttavyaṃ saṃprāpte kārtike janaiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39a. Dvādaśī is better than Pañcaka. It should be observed in the water of Dāmodara.

39b. When Kārttika has arrived people should bathe in the morning.

## \|\| 2.15.40 \|\|

*māsopavāsaḥ karttavyo yatibhirbrahmacāribhiḥ \|*  
*satībhirvidhavābhiśca muktisthānamabhīpsubhiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Ascetics and celebates should observe fast for a month, so also chaste women and widows and those who desire salvation.

## \|\| 2.15.41-43 \|\|

*ekabhaktena naktena tathaivāyācitena ca \|*  
*upavāsevana kṛcchreṇa śākāhāreṇa vā punaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*saṃsevyaḥ kārttike viṣṇurdīpadānaparairnaraiḥ \|*  
*brahmacaryaparairmāso nīyate yadi mānavaiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tadā viṣṇupure vāsaḥ kriyate viṣṇunā saha \|*  
*pañcopavāsāḥ karttavyāḥ saṃprāpte bhīṣmapaṃcake \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-42a. In Kārttika Viṣṇu should be worshipped by men intent on giving a gift of lamp, by eating once a day, or at night or eating unsolicited food or by fasting, or kṛchra (bodily mortification), or eating vegetables.

42b-43a. If men, intent on celibacy, pass the month (of Kārttika) then they live with Viṣṇu in Viṣṇupura.

43b. On the arrival of Bhīṣmapañcaka five fasts should be observed.

## \|\| 2.15.44 \|\|

*ekādaśīṃ samārabhya paṃcamī pūrṇimādinam \|*  
*tadetatpaṃcakaṃ proktaṃ sarvapāpaharaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The pañcaka (group of five days) is said to last for five days beginning with Ekādaśī and ending on the Full-Moon day, and it destroys all sins of men.

## \|\| 2.15.45 \|\|

*sarveṣāmapi māsānāṃ pañcakātkārtikādapi \|*  
*ekādaśī kārtikasya puṇyā dāmodare kṛtā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Of all months, and the group of five days in Kārttika, Ekādaśī, observed in Kārttika is meritorious, when observed at the holy place Dāmodara.

## \|\| 2.15.46 \|\|

*miṣṭānnaṃ kārtike deyaṃ haviṣyaṃ saghṛtaplutam \|*  
*suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ vastraṃ toyamannaṃ phalāni ca \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. In Kārttika sweet food, oblation covered with ghee should be given (to a Brāhmaṇa); so also gold, silver, a garment, water, food and fruits.

## \|\| 2.15.47-48 \|\|

*māsāṃte vividhaṃ deyaṃ gaustilāḥ kusumāni ca \|*  
*sarvadāneṣu yatpuṇyaṃ sarva tīrtheṣu yatphalam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*aśvamedhādibhiryajñairgayāyāṃ piṃḍadasya yat \|*  
*tatphalaṃ jāyate nṝṇāṃ dṛṣṭe dāmodare nṛpa \|\| 48 \|\|*

47a. At the end of the month various (objects), a cow, sesamum seeds and flowers should be given.

47b-48. O King, that fruit which is most holy of all gifts, which is secured by visits to all sacred places, or by sacrifices like horse-sacrifice, by one offering the funeral rice balls at Gayā is produced for men on seeing Dāmodara.

## \|\| 2.15.49-50 \|\|

*ekādaśyāṃ kṛtasnāno deva pūjāparo bhavet \|*  
*snāpya pañcāmṛtenaiva tatastīrthodakena ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

*kuṃkumāgaruśrīkhaṃḍakarpūrodakamiśritaiḥ \|*  
*pūjayitvā tataḥ puṣpaiḥ śatapatraiḥ sugaṃ dhibhiḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

49a. On the Ekādaśī day one should, after having bathed, be engaged in worshipping (a deity).

49b-50. Having (first) bathed (the deity) with the collection of five (sweet things like milk, sugar, clarified butter, curds and honey) one should then worship (the deity) with fragrant flowers and lotuses.

## \|\| 2.15.51 \|\|

*mālatīkusumaiḥ śubhrairbahubhistulasīdalaiḥ \|*  
*vastrayajñopavītaṃ ca dattvā dhūpaṃ pradhūpayet \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. with white jasmine flowers and many tulasī-leaves. Having given a garment and a sacred thread he should bum incense.

## \|\| 2.15.52 \|\|

*dīpaṃ dadyāddhṛtenaiva tailenāpi ghṛtaṃ vinā \|*  
*naivedyaṃ vividhaṃ deyaṃ phalaṃ tāṃbūlameva ca \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. He should offer to the deity a lamp full with ghee or with oil in the absence of ghee. An offering of a variety of foods, so also fruit or tāmbūla should be given.

## \|\| 2.15.53 \|\|

*prāsādapūjā karttavyā dhvajadānādinā nṛpa \|*  
*gauḥ savatsā tato deyā saṃsārārṇavatāriṇī \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O King, the palace should be worshipped with the gift of a flag etc. Then a cow, helping one to cross the ocean of the human existence, should be given along with her calf.

## \|\| 2.15.54 \|\|

*tataḥ pradakṣiṇāṃ kṛtvā gītavāditranisvanaiḥ \|*  
*vedapāṭhapurāṇaiśca vyākhyādivyakathādibhiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Then he should go round (the deity) with the accompaniment of songs and the sounds of musical instruments, recitations of Vedic texts, Purāṇas, expositions and divine tales etc.

## \|\| 2.15.55-56 \|\|

*devāgre jāgaraḥ kāryo dīpo deyoṃ'tibhūmiṣu \|*  
*saptadhānyamayāḥ sapta parvatā dīpasaṃyutāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*phalatāṃbūlapakvānnapūritāḥ parikalpitāḥ \|*  
*vidvadbhiḥ śrotriyaiḥ śrāṃtairbrāhmaṇairgṛhamedhibhiḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. He should keep awake before a deity, and a lamp should be offered in the neighbourhood of the house. Seven mountains (i.e. heaps) of seven (kinds of) com, with a lamp, so also full of fruits, tāmbūlas, cooked food prepared by learned Brāhmaṇa householders,

## \|\| 2.15.57 \|\|

*strībhiśca naraśārdūla śrotavyā vaiṣṇavī kathā \|*  
*evaṃ jāgaraṇaṃ kāryaṃ rāgakrodhavivarjitaiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. and women also, O greatest king, and story about Viṣṇu should be listened to. Thus being free from attachment or anger, they should keep awake.

## \|\| 2.15.58 \|\|

*kṛtvā jāgaraṇaṃ rātrāvudite sūryamaḍale \|*  
*pūrvāṃ saṃdhyāṃ tataḥ snātvā kṛtvā madhyāhnamācaret \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Having kept awake at night, he, when the sun has risen, should, having offered the morning prayer, observe (the rite at) the noon.

## \|\| 2.15.59 \|\|

*devānpitṝnmanuṣyāṃśca saṃtarpya vidhipūrvakam \|*  
*kṛtvā śrāddhaṃ pitṝṇāṃ tu dadyāddānaṃ svaśaktitaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Having satiated deities and dead ancestors according to rule, he should perform a funeral rite in honour of dead ancestors or should give gifts according to his capacity.

## \|\| 2.15.60 \|\|

*devaṃ dāmodaraṃ pūjya puṣpadhūpādinā punaḥ \|*  
*narasiṃhaṃ suraṃ pūjya vainateyaṃ ca pūjayet \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Having once again worshipped God Dāmodara with flowers, incense etc. he should, having worshipped Narasiṃha, worship Vainateya.

## \|\| 2.15.61 \|\|

*kṛtvā jāgaraṇaṃ rātrāvutthāpya madhusūdanam \|*  
*dvādaśībhuktimāsādya kāryaṃ pāraṇakaṃ naraiḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Having kept awake at night, and having awakened Madhusūdana, and having had the meal of Dvādaśī, men should break their fast.

## \|\| 2.15.62 \|\|

*brāhmaṇānbhojayitvā ca sahitaḥ putrabāṃdhavaiḥ \|*  
*vikalāṃdhakṛpaṇānāṃ deyamannaṃ svaśaktitaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Having fed the Brāhmaṇas along with sons and relatives, they should give food, according to their capacity, to those with defective limbs, to the blind, and to the helpless at the holy place Dāmodara or Raivataka or in the water of the river Svarṇarekhā.

## \|\| 2.15.63 \|\|

*dāmodare raivatake svarṇarekhānadījale \|*  
*evaṃ yaḥ kurute yātrāṃ tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Listen to the fruit, the religious merit, of him who does the pilgrimage in this way.

## \|\| 2.15.64 \|\|

*brahmaghnaśca surāpaśca grāmasīmāvilopakaḥ \|*  
*rājadrohī gurudrohī mithyāvratadharaśca yaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. One who kills a Brāhmaṇa, one who drinks liquor, who usurps the boundary of the village, one who plots against the king, the preceptor, and who deceitfully observes a vow,

## \|\| 2.15.65 \|\|

*kūṭasākṣyaprado yaśca yaśca nyāsāpahārakaḥ \|*  
*bālastrīghātako vipraḥ saṃdhyāsnānavivarjitaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. who is a false witness, who takes off a deposit, who kills a child or a lady, a Brāhmaṇa who does not take bath or who does not offer the morning, noon and evening prayers,

## \|\| 2.15.66 \|\|

*devabrahma svaharttā ca vedavikrayakārakaḥ \|*  
*kanyāvikrayakarttā ca devabrāhmaṇaniṃdakaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. so also one who usurps (others’) wealth, who sells (the knowledge in) the Vedas, one who sells his daughter, who censures gods and Brāhmaṇaas,

## \|\| 2.15.67 \|\|

*viśvāsaghātako vipraḥ śūdrānnādo'tha lubdhakaḥ \|*  
*nāyakaḥ paradārāṇāṃ svayaṃdattāpahārakaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. a Brāhmaṇa who is a traitor, who eats the food of a Śūdra, who is a hunter, who is the lover of others’ wife, who snatches away what is given by himself,

## \|\| 2.15.68 \|\|

*parvamaithunasevī ca tathā vai setubhedakaḥ \|*  
*pariṇītāmṛtusnātāṃ svayaṃ yo nābhigacchati \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. one who cohabits on the day of the lunar or solar eclipse, one who breaks down barriers, one who does not copulate with (his wife) that is married to him and is fit for intercourse;

## \|\| 2.15.69 \|\|

*brāhmaṇī vidhavā bālā na bhavecchrutadhāriṇī \|*  
*mahāpātakinaścaite tathānye bahavo nṛpa \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. so a Brāhmaṇa lady who is a widow or young but does not remember the scriptures-(all) these and many others are great sinners, O King.

## \|\| 2.15.70 \|\|

*svarṇarekhājale snātvā dṛṣṭvā dāmodaraṃ harim \|*  
*rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtvā mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Having bathed in the water of Svarṇarekhā, having (then) seen (the idol of) Dāmodara Hari, and having kept awake at night, he is freed from all sins.

## \|\| 2.15.71 \|\|

*na tu ye pāpakarmāṇaḥ samāyātāḥ prajāgare \|*  
*saṃsārasāgare tīrthe gacchaṃti na hareḥ puram \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Those sinners who do not come for sitting up at night as a part of a religious ceremony, remain in the ocean of the worldly existence, but do not go to Hari’s city.

## \|\| 2.15.72 \|\|

*yathā yathā yāti naraḥ prajāgare tathātathā viṣṇupure viciṃtyate \|*  
*vāsaḥ surairvaiṣṇavalokahetave mṛdaṃgagītadhvaninādite gṛhe \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. As a man goes for sitting up at night as required in a religious ceremony, he is considered by gods for residence in a house, resounding with the sounds of tabors and songs, in Viṣṇu’s city.

## \|\| 2.15.73 \|\|

*gadāsi śaṃkhāridharāścaturbhujā daiteyadarpāpaharūpadhāriṇaḥ \|*  
*pragīyamānāḥ surasuṃdarībhiste yāṃti khaṃ khecaragātrasaṃgāḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. They, holding a mace, a sword, a conch, a wheel, having four hands, having forms (of gods) that remove the pride of the demons, being sung by the heavenly beauties, go (possessing) limbs of those who move in the sky.

## \|\| 2.15.74 \|\|

*vārāhakalpe prathamaṃ yugādau dāmodaro raivatake prasiddhaḥ \|*  
*saiṣā nadī yā saritāṃ variṣṭhā so'yaṃ hariryo bhuvanasya kartā \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. In the Varāha Kalpa at the beginning of the yuga, Dāmodara was well-known at Raivataka. This is the river that was greatest among rivers. This is that Hari, the creator of the universe.

## \|\| 2.15.75 \|\|

*idaṃ purāṇaṃ paṭhate śṛṇoti naro vimānairmadhusūda nālaye \|*  
*devāṃganādattabhujaścaturbhujaḥ sa nīyate devagaṇairabhiṣṭutaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. The man who recites or listens to it (being recited), with a supporting hand given by divine ladies, and having four arms, so also praised by groups of gods, is taken to Madhusūdana’s abode by aeroplanes.

## Chapter 16 - The Great Efficacy of Śivarātri

## \|\| 2.16.1 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*athāsau vāmano vipraḥ praviṣṭo gahane vane \|*  
*ekākī kiṃ cakārātha kautukaṃ tadvadasva me \|\| 1 \|\|*

The King said:

1\. That Brāhmaṇa, Vāmana, who was alone, entered that dense forest. I have curiosity (to know) what he did there. (Please) tell it to me.

## \|\| 2.16.2-3 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*athāsau vāmano vipro gatvā raivatake girau \|*  
*svarṇarekhānadītoye snātvātha vidhipūrvakam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sugaṃdhapuṣpadhūpādyairdevaṃ saṃpūjya bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*tasthau tadagrato rājannekākī nirjane vane \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

2-3. Then that Brāhmaṇa Vāmana, having gone to the Raivataka mountain, and having bathed in the water of the river Svarṇarekhā according to rule, having devotedly worshipped the deity with fragrant flowers, incense etc., remained all alone, in front of him, in the lonely forest,

## \|\| 2.16.4 \|\|

*sarvasattvasamāyukte sarīsṛpasamākule \|*  
*anekasvarasaṃghuṣṭe mayūradhvaninādite \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. which was full of all animals, crowded with reptiles, resounding with many voices, filled with the sounds of peacocks,

## \|\| 2.16.5 \|\|

*kokilārāvaramye ca vanakukkuṭaghoṣite \|*  
*khadyotadyotite tasminvalīmukhavidhūnite \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. charming with the cooings of cuckoos, had sounds of wild cocks, was illuminated fire-flies, and tossed about by monkeys,

## \|\| 2.16.6 \|\|

*kvacidvaṃśāgninā śāṃte kvacitpuṣpitapādape \|*  
*gaganāsaktaviṭape sūryatāpavivarjite \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. which was calm at places with the fire of bamboos, having at places trees with flowers, trees which had touched the sky, was without the sun’s heat,

## \|\| 2.16.7 \|\|

*lubdhakāghāta saṃtrastabhrāṃtasūkaraśaṃbare \|*  
*saṃhṛṣṭakṣatriyavātasthānadānavicakṣaṇe \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. in which pigs and deer, being frightened by the hunters were confused, which was able to give room to the groups of delighted Kṣatriyas,

## \|\| 2.16.8-9 \|\|

*anekāścaryasaṃpannaṃ sasmāra manasā harim \|*  
*taṃ bhītamiva vijñāya narasiṃhaḥ samāyayau \|\| 8 \|\|*

*rakṣārthaṃ tasya viprasya babhāṣe purataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*na bhetavyaṃ tvayā vipra vada te kiṃ karomyaham \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. He mentally remembered Han, full of many wonders. Knowing him to be just afraid, Narasiṃha came (there), and remaining in front of the Brāhmaṇa, for his protection said: “O Brāhmaṇa, do not be afraid; tell me what I should do for you.”

## \|\| 2.16.10-11 \|\|

*vipra uvāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭo varo deyo narasiṃha tvayā mama \|*  
*sadātra rakṣā karttavyā sarveṣāṃ tīrthavāsinām \|\| 10 \|\|*

*devasyāgre sadā stheyaṃ yāvadiṃdrāścaturddaśa \|*  
*evamastviti taṃ procya tathā cakre haristadā \|\| 11 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇa said:

10-11. If, O Narasiṃha, if you are pleased, then grant me a boon. You should always give protection to all those who live in this holy place. You should always remain before the god, as long as the fourteen Indras exist. Saying “let it be so”, Hari then did like that.

## \|\| 2.16.12 \|\|

*ato dāmodarasyāgre narasiṃhaḥ sa pūjyate \|*  
*vanaṃ saumyaṃ kṛtaṃ tena tīrtharakṣāṃ karoti saḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Therefore Narasiṃha is worshipped in front of Dāmodara. He has made the forest pleasing; he protects the holy place.

## \|\| 2.16.13 \|\|

*bhūtapretādisaṃvāso vane tasminna jāyate \|*  
*narasiṃhaprabhāvena naṣṭaṃ siṃhādijaṃ bhayam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Ghosts and departed ones do not stay in the forest. Due to the prowess of Narasiṃha the fear from lions etc. has gone.

## \|\| 2.16.14 \|\|

*kārttike vāsare viṣṇordvādaśyāṃ pāraṇe kṛte \|*  
*dāmodaraṃ namaskṛtya bhavaṃ draṣṭuṃ tato yayau \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On the twelfth day in Kārttika, the fast was broken, and he then went to see Bhava.

## \|\| 2.16.15 \|\|

*caturdaśyāṃ kṛtasnāno bhavaṃ saṃpūjya bhāvataḥ \|*  
*bhavabhāvabhavaṃ pāpaṃ bhasmībhūtaṃ bhavārcanāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Having bathed, and having worshipped Bhava with devotion, the sin due to the existence in the world was burnt to ashes by the worship of Bhava.

## \|\| 2.16.16 \|\|

*sa kṣīṇapāpanicayo jāto devasya darśanāt \|*  
*bhavasyāgre sthitaṃ śāṃtaṃ tathā vastrāpathasya ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. By seeing the God, the stock of his sins diminished. He remained calm in front of Bhava and so also Vastrāpatha.

## \|\| 2.16.17-18 \|\|

*taṃ kālameghaṃ samabhyarcya tato vastrāpathaṃ yayau \|*  
*devaṃ saṃpūjya maṃtraiḥ sa vedoktairvidhipūrvakam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dhūpadīpādinaivedyaiḥ sarvaṃ cakre sa vāmanaḥ \|*  
*pradakṣiṇāśataṃ kṛtvā bhavasyāgre vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Having well worshipped Kālamegha, he went to Vastrāpatha from there. That Vāmana, having duly worshipped the God with Vedic hymns, he did everything with incense, lamp and offerings. Having gone round (the deity) he remained in front of Bhava.

## \|\| 2.16.19-20 \|\|

*yāvannirīkṣate sarvaṃ tāvatpaśyati parvatam \|*  
*ujjayaṃtaṃ girivaraṃ mainākasya sahodaram \|\| 19 \|\|*

*surāṣṭradeśe vikhyātaṃ yugādau prathamaṃ sthitam \|*  
*bhūdharaṃ bhūdharairyuktaṃ śilāpādapamaṃḍitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. When he saw everything, he saw the mountain, the excellent mountain, Ujjayanta, the brother of (i.e. come up with) Maināka, that was well-known in Surāṣṭra country, and that stood first in the beginning of the age. It was accompanied by other mountains and was decorated with stones and trees.

## \|\| 2.16.21 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā ciṃtayāmāsa sūkṣmāndharmānsa vāmanaḥ \|*  
*alpāyāsānsubahulānputralakṣmīpradāyakān \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Seeing it Vāmana thought about subtle rules, which required little trouble to follow, were very many, and the givers of sons and wealth.

## \|\| 2.16.22 \|\|

*avaśyaṃ kriya māṇeṣu svadharma upajāyate \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā nadīṃ sāgaragāṃ snātvā pāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. When the rules are definitely followed, righteousness is produced in one. On seeing the river flowing to the ocean, and having bathed in it, one is freed from sins.

## \|\| 2.16.23-24 \|\|

*gāṃ spṛṣṭvā brāhmaṇaṃ natvā saṃpūjya gurudevatāḥ \|*  
*tapasvinaṃ yatiṃ śāṃtaṃ śrotriyaṃ brahmacāriṇam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*pitaraṃ mātaraṃ bhaginīṃ tatpatiṃ duhitāṃ patim \|*  
*bhāgineyamatha dauhitraṃ mitrasaṃbadhibāṃdhavān \|*  
*saṃbhojya pātakaiḥ sarvairmucyaṃte gṛhamedhinaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Householders are freed from all sins (after bathing in the river), touching a cow, saluting a Brāhmaṇa, properly worshipping deity-like preceptors, one who has practised penance, an ascetic, a calm, learned celibate Brāhmaṇa,(so also) his father, mother, sister, her husband, his daughter and her husband, his sister’s son, his daughter’s son, friends, kinsmen and relatives. Having fed them householders are freed from all sins.

## \|\| 2.16.25 \|\|

*rājā gajāśvanakulaṃ satīvṛṣamahīdharāḥ \|*  
*ādarśakṣīravṛkṣāśca satatānnapradāstu te \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. A king, an elephant, a horse, a mongoose, a chaste lady, a bull, a mountain, ādarśa (common name of four trees viz. nyagrodha, udumbara, aśvattha and madhūka) trees are always givers of food.

## \|\| 2.16.26-28 \|\|

*dṛṣṭamātrāḥ punantyete ye nityaṃ satyavādinaḥ \|*  
*vedadharmakathāṃ śrutvā bhuktimuktipradā narān \|\| 26 \|\|*

*smṛtvā hariharau gaṃgāṃ kṛtvā tīreṇa mārjanam \|*  
*gatvā jāgaraṇe viṣṇordattvā dānaṃ ca śaktitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tāṃbūlaṃ kusumaṃ dīpaṃ naivedyaṃ tulasīdalam \|*  
*gītaṃ nṛtyaṃ ca vādyaṃ ca vidhāya suramaṃdire \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. These, just seen purify those who are always truth-speaking. By listening to a Vedic, religious story giving enjoyment and salvation to men, remembering Han, Hara and Gaṅgā, bathing at her bank, going for keeping awake (in honour) of Viṣṇu, giving gifts according to one’s capacity, so also a tāmbūla, a flower, a lamp, a leaf tulasī, doing singing, dancing and instrumental music in the temple of god (one is freed from the worldly existence).

## \|\| 2.16.29 \|\|

*ete sūkṣmāḥ smṛtā dharmāḥ kriyamāṇā mahodayāḥ \|*  
*ato girīndraṃ paśyāmi sarvadevālayaṃ śubham \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. These are said to be subtle practices. When practised they cause great prosperity. Therefore, I shall see the mountain, the auspicious abode of all gods.

## \|\| 2.16.30 \|\|

*teṣāṃ karatale svargaḥ śikharaṃ yāṃti ye narāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Heaven is on the palm of (i.e. easy to attain) for those who go to the peak (of the mountain).

## \|\| 2.16.31 \|\|

*iti jñātvā samā rūḍho vāmano girimūrddhani \|*  
*airāvatapadākrāṃtyā yatra toyaṃ viniḥsṛtam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Realising this, Vāmana climbed on the top of the mountain, where water had come out due to the planting of the foot of Airāvata.

## \|\| 2.16.32 \|\|

*tataḥ śikharamārūḍhāṃ bhavānīṃ skandamātaram \|*  
*draṣṭuṃ sa vāmano yāti śikhare gaganāśrite \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Then Vāmana went up to the summit (of the mountain) touching the sky to see Bhavānī, Skanda’s mother, who had ascended the peak.

## \|\| 2.16.33 \|\|

*yathāyathā girivare samārohaṃti mānavāḥ \|*  
*tathātathā vimucyaṃte pātakaiḥ sarvadehinaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. As human beings climb the excellent mountain, they all are freed from sins.

## \|\| 2.16.34 \|\|

*iti kṛtvā matiṃ vipro jagāma girimūrddhani \|*  
*bhavabhakto bhavānīṃ sa dadarśa skandamātaram \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Thinking like this, the Brāhmaṇa went up to the top of the mountain. He, the devotee of Bhava, saw Bhavānī, the mother of Skanda.

## \|\| 2.16.35-36 \|\|

*aṃbeti bhāṣate skaṃdastato'nye sarvadevatāḥ \|*  
*pṛthivyāṃ mānavāḥ sarve pātāle sarvapannagāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*ato hyaṃbeti vikhyātā pūjyate girimūrddhani \|*  
*saṃpūjya vividhairmukhyaiḥ phalairnānāvidhairdvijaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. Skanda addresses her as ‘Ambā’. Therefore all other deities, all human beings on the earth, all serpents in the nether world (address her like that). So she is well-known as Ambā, and is worshipped on the top of the mountain. The Brāhmaṇa, having worshipped (her) with various important kinds of fruits, got full of curiosity, and remained on the peak touching the sky. He, all alone, with his hands folded remained on the peak.

## \|\| 2.16.37-41 \|\|

*gaganāsaktaśikhare saṃsthitaḥ kautukānvitaḥ \|*  
*ekākī śikhare tasminnūrddhvabāhurvyavasthitaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*nirīkṣya medinīṃ sarvāṃ saparvatasasāgarām \|*  
*ādyaṃ sanātanaṃ devaṃ bhāskaraṃ triguṇātmakam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*sarvatejomayaṃ sarvadevaṃ devairnamaskṛtam \|*  
*bhramamāṇaṃ nirādhāraṃ kālamānaprayojakam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*yāvatpaśyati taṃ viprastāvatpaśyati śaṃkaram \|*  
*digaṃbaraṃ bhavaṃ devaṃ samaṃtādaśmaguṃṭhitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*buddharūpākṛtiṃ devaṃ sarvajñaṃ guṇabhūṣitam \|*  
*kṛśāṃgaṃ jaṭilaṃ saumyaṃ vyomamārge svayaṃ sthitam \|\| 41 \|\|*

37-41. When, having observed the whole earth along with mountains and oceans, the Brāhmaṇa saw the first ancient god Bhāskara (i.e. the Sun) having three qualities (viz. Sattva, Rajas and Tamas), full of all lustre, the god of all, saluted by gods, wandering without, a prop, causing the measure of time, just saw Śaṅkara, God Bhava, naked, encircled by clouds, having figure like that of Buddha, omniscient, endowed with virtues, of a thin body, having matted hair, mild and himself remaining in the sky path.

## \|\| 2.16.42 \|\|

*śrīśiva uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu vāmana tuṣṭo'haṃ dāsye te vividhānvarān \|*  
*trailokyavyāpinī vṛddhirbhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

Śrī Śiva said:

42\. Listen, O Vāmana, I am pleased with you. I shall give you various boons. Your enlargement will pervade the three worlds. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 2.16.43 \|\|

*pratibhāsyaṃti te vedā gītanṛtyādikaṃ ca yat \|*  
*asādhyasādhanī śakti bhaviṣyati tava sthirā \|*  
*paraṃ vastrāpathe gatvā kuru tīrthāvalokanam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The Vedas will manifest themselves to you; so also whatever dancing and singing there is (in the world) You will have a stable power securing what cannot be secured. Go to Vastrāpatha and see the sacred place.

## \|\| 2.16.44 \|\|

*vāmana uvāca \|*  
*vastrāpathe mahādeva yāni tīrthāni tāni me \|*  
*vada deva viśeṣeṇa yadyasti karuṇā mayi \|\| 44 \|\|*

Vāmana said:

44\. O great god, please tell me especially about the holy places at Vastrāpatha, if you have pity on me.

## \|\| 2.16.45-46 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*vastrāpathasya vāyavye koṇe divyaṃ sarovaram \|*  
*tasya paścimadigbhāge jālirgahanapallavā \|\| 45 \|\|*

*bilvavṛkṣamayī madhye liṃgaṃ tatrāsti mṛnmayam \|*  
*yatrāsau lubdhakaḥ siddho gato mama pure purā \|\| 46 \|\|*

Rudra said:

45-46. In the north-west corner of Vastrāpatha, there is a divine lake. To the west of it, there is a thicket thick with leaves (and full of Bilva trees). In the midst of it there is an image of the phallus, made of clay, where formerly the pious hunter, went to my city.

## \|\| 2.16.47 \|\|

*tasya darśanamātreṇa brahmahatyā vinaśyati \|*  
*iṃdro vai vṛtrahā yasminvimukto brahmahatyayā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Merely by seeing him, (the sin of) the murder of a Brāhmaṇa perishes. Indra, the killer of Vṛtra got freed from (the sin of) the killing of a Brāhmaṇa there.

## \|\| 2.16.48 \|\|

*tasmādruttaradigbhāge dhanadena pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*liṃgaṃ trailokyavikhyātaṃ tatra devī triśūlinī \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. To the northern direction of that there is an image of the phallus established by Kubera, and well known in the three worlds. The Goddess having a Triśūla (trident) stays there.

## \|\| 2.16.49 \|\|

*yasyā darśanamātreṇa putro'sya nalakūbara \|*  
*pāśānuṣaktahasto'bhūddevaṃ cakre triśūlinam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. By merely seeing her, his son, Nalakūbera, became one whose hands were clung to nooses. He fashioned God Śiva.

## \|\| 2.16.50 \|\|

*bhavasya nairṛte koṇe gaṇo heraṃbasaṃjñitaḥ \|*  
*yamena kurvatā liṃgaṃ prathamaṃ ca pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. In the south-west comer of Bhava there is (the image of) the attendant of Śiva known as Heramba. Yama first established him while fashioning the image of the Phallus.

## \|\| 2.16.51 \|\|

*vicitraṃ tasya māhātmyaṃ citragupto'ti vismitaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā samāgato draṣṭuṃ devaṃ taṃ mṛnmayaṃ purā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Its greatness is wonderful. Citragupta was very much wonder-struck. Formerly he came to see (that image of) the god made of clay.

## \|\| 2.16.52 \|\|

*tenāpi nirmitaṃ liṃgaṃ tasminkṣetre dvijottama \|*  
*citragupteśvaraṃnāma vikhyātaṃ bhuvana traye \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O best Brāhmaṇa, he too fashioned an image of the Phallus, known as Citragupteśvara and well known in the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.16.53 \|\|

*paścimena cakāroccaiḥ prajāpatirudāradhīḥ \|*  
*kedārākhyaṃ tadā liṃgaṃ girau raivatake sthitam \|*  
*prajāpatiḥ svayaṃ tasthau tatra parvatasānuni \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. In the west Brahmā, of a noble mind fashioned an image of the Phallus, high up, remaining on the Raivataka mountain. On the peak of the mountain Brahmā himself stayed.

## \|\| 2.16.54 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*iṃdreśvarasya māhātmyaṃ kathayiṣye śṛṇuṣva tat \|*  
*īśānakoṇe vikhyātaṃ bhavasya viditaṃ mama \|\| 54 \|\|*

Rudra said:

54\. I shall (now) tell you (about) the greatness of god Indreśvara. Listen to it. I know that it is situated in the northeast comer of Bhava.

## \|\| 2.16.55 \|\|

*vāmana uvāca \|*  
*kasmādiṃdraḥ samāyātaḥ kathaṃ cakre haraṃ hariḥ \|*  
*kathāṃ savistarāmetāṃ kathayasva mama prabho \|\| 55 \|\|*

Vāmana said:

55\. For what purpose did Indra come there? How did Hari (Indra) fashion the image of Hara? O Lord, tell this story to me in detail.

## \|\| 2.16.56 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*lubdhakastu purā siddhaḥ śivarātriprajāgarāt \|*  
*śivaloke tadā prāptaṃ vimānaṃ gaṇasaṃyutam \|\| 56 \|\|*

Rudra said:

56\. Formerly, the hunter, due to keeping awake on the Śivarātri, became a semi-divine being. At that time an aeroplane, along with the attendants, reached Śiva’s world.

## \|\| 2.16.57 \|\|

*sarvatragaṃ suruciraṃ divyastrīgītanāditam \|\| tadāruhya samāyāto draṣṭuṃ tāṃ nagarīṃ hareḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. It moved everywhere; it was very charming and resounded with the songs of divine ladies. Getting into it, he went to see that city of Hara.

## \|\| 2.16.58 \|\|

*yasyāṃ yuddhaṃ samabhavadgaṇānāṃ yamakiṃkaraiḥ \|*  
*āgacchamānaṃ taṃ jñātvā devarājena ciṃtitam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58a. In it there took place a battle of the attendants of Śiva with Yama’s servants.

58b. Seeing him coming the King of gods thought:

## \|\| 2.16.59-60 \|\|

*pūjyo'yaṃ haravatsarvaiścitraguptayamādibhiḥ \|*  
*iṃdro gajaṃ samāruhya mahiṣeṇa yamo yataḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*vidhāya lekhanīṃ karṇe citragupto yamājñayā \|*  
*tato hūtā gaṇāḥ sarve ye nītā dharaṇītalāt \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. ‘He is venerable like Hara to all like Citragupta, Yama and others.’ Indra mounting the elephant, and Yama, mounting the he-buffalo, (went to him). Citragupta, keeping the pen on his ear, (also went there) by Yama’s order. Then all attendants were invited. They were taken from the surface of the earth.

## \|\| 2.16.61-62 \|\|

*nijāparādhasaṃtaptā gatāste dakṣiṇāmukham \|\| āthityapū \|*  
*jā kartavyā lubdhake gṛhamāgate \|\| 61 \|\|*

*apūjite gate hyasminharo māṃ śapayiṣyati \|*  
*tasmātpūjāṃ kariṣyāmi yathā tuṣyati śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. Afflicted by their own offence, they went towards the south. ‘The worship of the guest must be done when the hunter comes to my house. If he goes unhonoured Hara will curse me. So I shall worship him in such a way that Śaṅkara will be pleased.’

## \|\| 2.16.63 \|\|

*devaṃ draṣṭuṃ samāyātaṃ dadarśādūrataḥ sthitam \|*  
*vimānasthaṃ harākāraṃ sūryakoṭisamaprabham \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. He saw him who had come to see the God, and who remained not far, who remained in the aeroplane, who had the figure of Hara, who had the lustre of a crore of suns.

## \|\| 2.16.64-65 \|\|

*saṃstūyamānaṃ caritaiḥ śivarātreḥ śivasya ca \|*  
*māghe māse caturddaśyāṃ kṛṣṇāyāṃ jāgare kṛte \|\| 64 \|\|*

*tadevaṃ jāyate sarvaṃ sureśvara dharātale \|*  
*evaṃ devāṃganā kācidācakṣaṃtī puraṃdaram \|*  
*nivārya hastamudyamya gajeṃdraṃ cārulocanā \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. He was being extolled with acts of the Śivarātri and of Śiva, in the month of Māgha on the fourteenth of the dark fortnight. O Lord of gods, like this everything took place on the earth. Thus some divine lady, of charming eyes, setting aside the Lord of elephants (Airāvata), was telling Indra:

## \|\| 2.16.66 \|\|

*kiṃ dānairbahubhirdattairvrataiḥ kiṃ kiṃ surārcanaiḥ \|*  
*kiṃ yogaiḥ kiṃ tapobhiśca brahmacaryyaiḥ sureśvara \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. “What is the use of giving many gifts? What is the use of vows? What is the use of worship of gods? What is the use of deep and abstract meditation? What is the use of penances? What is the use of celibacy, O Lord of gods?

## \|\| 2.16.67 \|\|

*gayāyāṃ piṃḍadānena prayāgamaraṇena kim \|*  
*someśvare sarasvatyāṃ somaparvaṇi kiṃ gataiḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. “What is the use of the presentation of the obsequial rice-balls at Gayā? What is the use of dying at Prayāga? What is the use of visits to Sarasvatī at Someśvara on the Full-Moon or the New-Moon day?

## \|\| 2.16.68 \|\|

*kurukṣetragataiḥ kiṃ syādrāhugraste divākare \|*  
*tulāsuvarṇadānena vedapāṭhena kiṃ bhavet \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. “What is the use of visits to Kurukṣetra when the Sun is eclipsed by Rāhu? What would happen by the gift of gold equal to one’s weight? What is the use of recitaton of Vedic texts?

## \|\| 2.16.69 \|\|

*sarvapāpakṣayo yena vṛṣotsargeṇa tena kim \|*  
*godānaṃ kiṃ karotyevaṃ jaladānaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. “What is the use of presenting a bull by means of which all sins are washed off? What does the gift of a cow do? So also (what does) giving of water (do)?

## \|\| 2.16.70 \|\|

*ayane viṣuve caiva saṃkrāṃtau kīdṛśaṃ phalam \|*  
*māghamāse caturdaśyāṃ yādṛśaṃ jāgare kṛte \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. “What kind of fruit would be obtained by making a present during the time from one solstice to another, on the equinoctial point, or during the time of the passage of the Sun from one Zodiacal sign to another or by keeping awake on the fourteenth day of the month of Māgha?”

## \|\| 2.16.71 \|\|

*yamaḥ saṃbhāṣate vāṇyā mahiṣopari saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*paśya rudrasya māhātmyaṃ citragupta vicāraya \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Yama, seated on a he-buffalo, speaks aloud: “See the greatness of Rudra, O Citragupta, and remember.

## \|\| 2.16.72-73 \|\|

*ayaṃ sa lubdhako yena haraḥ saṃpūjitaḥ purā \|*  
*surāṣṭradeśe vikhyātaṃ tīrthaṃ vastrāpathaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 72 \|\|*

*ujjayaṃto giristatra tathā raivatako giriḥ \|*  
*mahatī varttate jālistayormadhye mayā śrutam \|\| 73 \|\|*

72-73. “This is that hunter who formerly worshipped Hara. Listen: There is a well-known holy place Vastrāpatha in the Surāṣṭra country. There is the mountain Ujjayanta; so also (there is) the mountain Raivataka. I have heard that there is a great thicket between them.

## \|\| 2.16.74 \|\|

*mṛnmayaṃ vartate ligaṃ rātrau cānena pūjitaḥ \|*  
*rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ karttuṃ yena kāryeṇa cāgataḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. “There is an image of the Phallus made of clay. He worshipped it at night. For that reason he had come to keep awake.

## \|\| 2.16.75 \|\|

*tadasmābhiḥ kathaṃ vācyaṃ svayaṃ jānaṃti te surāḥ \|*  
*varāṃganā varaṃ draṣṭuṃ varayaṃti parasparam \|*  
*iṃdrāvāsātsamāyātā naṃdane vegavattarāḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. “How should it be disclosed by people like us? The gods themselves know it. The excellent ladies solicit one another to see the choice. They have come from Indra’s abode very speedily and are in Indra’s garden.

## \|\| 2.16.76 \|\|

*viraṃcinā rāyaṇaśaṃkaratviṣā dehena cāgacchati ko'pi pūruṣaḥ \|*  
*purīṃ sureśādhipaternirīkṣituṃ bharttā mamāyaṃ tava cāsti kiṃ patiḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. “Some man, with a body having the lustre of Brahmā, Viṣṇu or Śaṅkara comes to see the city of the Lord of gods. Is he my husband or yours?

## \|\| 2.16.77 \|\|

*mṛdaṃgavīṇā paṭahasvarastutaiḥ pravodhitābhiḥ surarājamandire \|*  
*devo haro'yaṃ na naro harākṛtirdṛṣṭoṃganābhistava kiṃ kimāvayoḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. “In the dwelling of the King of gods, the ladies awakened by the eulogies made by the sounds of tabors, lutes, drums, saw god Hara and said: ‘He is not a man having Hara’s figure. Is he your lord or of both of us?’

## \|\| 2.16.78 \|\|

*gāyaṃti kāścidvihasaṃti kāścinnṛtyaṃti kāścitprapaṭhaṃti kāścit \|*  
*vadanti kāścijjayaśabdasaṃyutairvākyairanekairgurusannidhāne \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. “Some sing (songs), some speak in many sentences containing words of victory in the presence of the preceptor.

## \|\| 2.16.79 \|\|

*kācicchivaṃ stauti śivāṃ tathānyā pṛcchatyathānyā kimu bilvapatrāt \|*  
*kiṃ vopavāsena phalaṃ tavedaṃ nidrākṣayeṇātha phalaṃ tavaitat \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. “Someone eulogizes ‘Śiva’, and someone else asks (another lady): ‘Is it the fruit of (observing) a fast? Or is this your fruit due to the loss of sleep?’

## \|\| 2.16.80-81 \|\|

*tāsāṃ nānāvidhā vācaḥ śrūyante nandane vane \|*  
*brahmalokādikā vārttāḥ kṛtvā ca tadanantaram \|\| 80 \|\|*

*devendro lubdhakaṃ bhūyo babhāṣe kautukānvitaḥ \|*  
*kasmindeśe girau jālirliṃgaṃ yatrāsti darśaya \|\| 81 \|\|*

80-81. “Various kinds of words of (i.e. uttered by) them were heard in Indra’s garden. Having talked about Brahmā’s world etc., the Lord of gods, full of curiosity, again said to the hunter: ‘Show in which place on the mountain the image of Phallus in the thicket exists.’

## \|\| 2.16.82 \|\|

*lubdhaka uvāca \|*  
*surāṣṭradeśe vikhyāto yasmindeśe sarasvatī \|*  
*vāḍavaṃ śirasā dhṛtvā praviṣṭā lavaṇodadhau \|\| 82 \|\|*

The hunter said:

82\. The country Surāṣṭra is well known. In it Sarasvatī, holding the subamarine fire on her head, has entered the Salt Ocean.

## \|\| 2.16.83 \|\|

*yatra sā gomatī yāti yatrāste gandhamādanaḥ \|*  
*ujjayaṃto girivaro yatra raivatako giriḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. There flows the river Gomatī; there is the Gandhamādana (mountain) there is the best mountain Ujjayanta; there is the Raivataka mountain.

## \|\| 2.16.84 \|\|

*tatra vastrāpathaṃ kṣetraṃ bhavastatra vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*tatrāste mṛnmayaṃ liṃgaṃ jālimadhye surottama \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. There in the holy place Vastrāpatha Bhava is well-settled. O best god, there in the thicket of trees is the clay image of the Phallus (of Śiva).

## \|\| 2.16.85 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*sahitaistatra gaṃtavyaṃ pūjayiṣye bhavaṃ svayam \|*  
*jālimadhye tathā liṃgaṃ darśayasva ca lubdhaka \|\| 85 \|\|*

Indra said:

85\. Together we shall go there. I shall myself worship Bhava, and, O hunter, show me the image of the Phallus in the thicket.

## \|\| 2.16.86 \|\|

*paradārādikaṃ pāpaṃ daityānāṃ tu vikṛṃtane \|*  
*vadhe vṛtrasya saṃjātaṃ tatsarvaṃ kṣālayāmyaham \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Sin like molesting someone else’s wife, the sin committed due to Vṛtra’s murder while destroying the demons—I shall wipe out all that.

## \|\| 2.16.87 \|\|

*ityuktvā sahitāḥ sarve saṃprāptā girimūrddhani \|*  
*vāhanāni ca te tyaktvā prasthitāḥ pādacāriṇaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Saying so all together reached the top of the mountain. Abandoning their vehicles, they started (going there) on foot.

## \|\| 2.16.88-89 \|\|

*ujjayantagirermūrdhni gajarājaḥ samāgataḥ \|*  
*tadāgracaraṇaṃ tasya dadau mūrdhani kāraṇāt \|\| 88 \|\|*

*tenākrānto girivarastoyaṃ susrāva nirmalam \|*  
*gajapādodbhavaṃ vāri bhaviṣyati sadā sthiram \|\| 89 \|\|*

88-89. The Lord of elephants (Airāvata) arrived on the top of the mountain. Then for (some) reason he put his forefoot on the top (of the mountain). The best mountain trampled by that (forefoot) let flow pure water. “The water rising from the foot of the mountain would always be stable.”

## \|\| 2.16.90 \|\|

*iti proktaṃ surendreṇa lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|*  
*sarve samāgatāstatra yatra jālirvyavasthitā \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Indra thus addressed (them) with a desire for the wellbeing of the people. All came there where the thicket remained.

## \|\| 2.16.91 \|\|

*saṃpūjya vividhaiḥ puṣpairmāghamāse caturdaśī \|*  
*tasyāṃ jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtvā sañjāto nirmalo hariḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. On the fourteenth day of Māgha having worshipped the deity with various flowers, and having kept awake on that night Hari (Indra) became pure.

## \|\| 2.16.92 \|\|

*vastrāpathe bhavaṃ pūjya hariṃ raivatake girau \|*  
*indreśvaraṃ pratiṣṭhāpya saṃprāptaḥ svanikatanam \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Having worshipped Bhava at Vastrāpatha and Hari (Viṣṇu) on the Raivataka mountain and having established Lord Indreśvara, he returned home.

## \|\| 2.16.93 \|\|

*lubdhako'pi vimānena saṃprāpto harimandire \|*  
*ityuktvā sa bhavo devastatraivāṃtaradhīyata \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. The hunter too reached Hari’s abode by an aeroplane. Thus speaking that god Bhava vanished there only.

## \|\| 2.16.94-95 \|\|

*vāmanopi tataścakre tatra tīrthāvagāhanam \|*  
*yādṛgrūpaḥ śivo dṛṣṭaḥ sūryabiṃbe digaṃbaraḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*padmāsanasthitaḥ saumyastathā taṃ tatra saṃsmaran \|*  
*pratiṣṭhāpya mahāmūrttiṃ pūjayāmāsa vāsaram \|\| 95 \|\|*

94-95. Then Vāmana too remembering Śiva in his naked form seated in Padmāsana position and benign in appearance, plunged in the holy place. Having installed the great figure he worshipped it by that day.

## \|\| 2.16.96 \|\|

*mano'bhīṣṭārthasiddhyarthaṃ tataḥ siddhimavāptavān \|*  
*nemināthaśivetyevaṃ nāma cakre sa vāmanaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Then, he secured a divine power for securing what was desired by his mind. Vāmana, named that figure Neminātha-Śiva.

## \|\| 2.16.97 \|\|

*bhavasya paścime bhāge pratyāsanne dharātale \|*  
*vāmano vasatiṃ cakre tīrthe vastrāpathe tadā \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. On the ground in the vicinity of the western side of Bhava, in the holy place Vastrāpatha, Vāmana then took his abode.

## \|\| 2.16.98-99 \|\|

*ato yavādhikaṃ proktaṃ tīrthaṃ devaiḥ savāsavaiḥ \|*  
*iṃdreṇa kurvatā devaṃ samāgatya bhavāgrataḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

*yavādhikaṃ prabhāsāttu tīrthametadbhavājñayā \|*  
*anyeṣāṃ ṣaḍguṇaṃ tīrthaṃ bhaviṣyati śivājñayā \|\| 99 \|\|*

98a. Therefore the sacred place is called Yavādhika by gods along with Indra.

98b-99. Having arrived in front of Bhava, Indra fashioned his image. This holy place is superior by a yava (a very small measure) to Prabhāsa due to Bhava’s order and due to Śiva’s order it will be six times superior to other holy places.

## \|\| 2.16.100 \|\|

*ityetatkathitaṃ sarvaṃ kimanyatparipṛcchasi \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Thus I have told you everything. What else do you ask?

## \|\| 2.16.101 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*śivarātriprabhāvoyamatulaḥ parikīrttitaḥ \|*  
*ajānatā kṛtā tena lubdhakena purā śrutam \|\| 101 \|\|*

The King said:

101\. This efficacy of the (vow of) Śivarātri is said to be incomparable. It is heard that formerly the hunter ignorant (of its efficacy) observed it.

## \|\| 2.16.102 \|\|

*idānīṃ vada karttavyā kathamanyairjanairvibho \|*  
*kiṃ grāhyaṃ kiṃ nu moktavyaṃ śivarātryāṃ vadasva me \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. O Lord, now say how other people should observe it. Tell me what should be accepted and what should be rejected on the Śivarātri (day).

## \|\| 2.16.103 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*saṃprāpya mānuṣaṃ janma jñātvā devaṃ maheśvaram \|*  
*śivarātriḥ sadā kāryā bhuktimuktipradāyinī \|\| 103 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

103\. Having obtained human birth, and having known god Maheśvara, the (vow of) Śivarātrī, giving enjoyments and salvation, should always be observed.

## \|\| 2.16.104 \|\|

*īdṛśaṃ jāyate puṇyamekayā kṛtayā nṛpa \|*  
*ye kurvaṃti sadā marttyāsteṣāṃ puṇyamanaṃtakam \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. O King, such religious merit is produced by observing this vow alone. The religious merit of those who always observe this vow is unending.

## \|\| 2.16.105-106 \|\|

*dvādaśābdaṃ vratamidaṃ karttavyaṃ prativatsaram \|*  
*jīvitaṃ caṃcalaṃ nṛṇāṃ yadi kartuṃ na śakyate \|\| 105 \|\|*

*tadā dvādaśabhirmāsairvrata metatsamāpyate \|*  
*māghamāse caturdaśyāṃ prārambhaḥ kriyate nṛpa \|\| 106 \|\|*

105-106. This is a twelve-year vow. It should be observed every year. Life of men is fickle. (So) if it cannot be observed (for twelve years) then this vow can be completed within twelve months. O King, its commencement is done on the fourteenth day in the month of Māgha.

## \|\| 2.16.107-108 \|\|

*pratimāsaṃ tataḥ kāryaṃ pauṣāṃte tu samāpyate \|*  
*vighnaścejjāyate madhye kathaṃ ciddaivayogataḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

*na bhavedvratabhaṃgastu punaḥ kāryamanantaram \|*  
*dvādaśaiva prakartavyāḥ kṛtvā saṃkhyā viśeṣataḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

107-108. Thereafter, it should be observed every month. It should be completed at the end of Pauṣa. If accidentally some difficulty comes up, there would be no breach of the vow; it should be observed without any pause. Twelve (such vows) should be observed, especially counting the number.

## \|\| 2.16.109-110 \|\|

*kṛtaṃ na naśyate loke śubhaṃ vā yadi vā'śubham \|*  
*kṛṣṇāyāṃ tu caturdaśyāṃ kṛtapūrvāhnikakriyaḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

*upavāsaniyamo grāhyo nadyāṃ snānaṃ vidhīyate \|*  
*tadabhāve taḍāgādau kāryaṃ snānaṃ svaśaktitaḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

109-110. In the world, nothing auspicious or inauspicious (ever) perishes. On the fourteenth day of the dark half, having performed the duties of the earlier part of the day, the observance of a fast should be taken up. Bathing in a river is enjoined. In its absence one should, according to one’s capacity, bathe in a lake etc.

## \|\| 2.16.111 \|\|

*tailābhyaṃgo na karttavyo na kāryaṃ gamanaṃ kvacit \|*  
*tīrthasevā prakarttavyā tasmiṃścāgamanaṃ śubham \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. The body should not be anointed with oil. (So also) one should not go anywhere. One should resort to a sacred place. Arrival into a holy place is auspicious.

## \|\| 2.16.112 \|\|

*śivarātriḥ sadā kāryā liṃge svāyaṃbhuve naraiḥ \|*  
*tadabhāve mahāpuṇye liṃge varṣaśatādhike \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. Men should always observe the Śivarātri-vow (in the vicinity of) a self-existent image of (Śiva’s) Phallus. In its absence (in the vicinity) of a very meritorious image of the Phallus more than a hundred years old.

## \|\| 2.16.113 \|\|

*girau vane samudrāṃte nadyāṃ yacca śivālaye \|*  
*tadvai svāyaṃbhuvaṃ liṃgaṃ svayaṃ tatraiva saṃsthitam \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. That which has just remained of its own accord, there only—on a mountain, in a forest, near an ocean, or a river is the self-existing image of the Phallus.

## \|\| 2.16.114-115 \|\|

*vāluliṃgādikaṃ liṃgaṃ pūjitaṃ phaladaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*divā saṃpūjya yatnena puṣpadhūpādinā naraḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

*varjayenmadirāṃ dyūtaṃ nārīṃ nakhanikṛntanam \|*  
*brahmacaryaparaiḥ śāṃtaiḥ karttavyaṃ samupoṣaṇam \|\| 115 \|\|*

114-115. The image of the Phallus made with sand etc., if worshipped, is said to be fruitful. A man having worshipped it carefully by day with flowers, incense etc., should avoid liquor, gambling, (the company of) a woman, and cutting off nails. Intent on celibacy, and being calm a fast should be observed.

## \|\| 2.16.116 \|\|

*rātrau devāgrato gatvā karttavyāḥ sapta parvatāḥ \|*  
*pakvānnaphalatāṃbūlapuṣpadhūpādicarcitāḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. Having, at night, gone in front of a deity, seven mountains should be fashioned. They should be smeared with cooked food, tāmbūla, flowers, incense etc.

## \|\| 2.16.117 \|\|

*ghṛtena dīpaḥ karttavyaḥ pāpanāśanahetave \|*  
*yato dīpasya māhātmyaṃ vijñeyaṃ muktidāyakam \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. The lamp should have clarified butter in it for destroying sins, since the greatness of a lamp should be known to give liberation.

## \|\| 2.16.118 \|\|

*dīpaḥ sadaiva karttavyo gṛhe devālaye naraiḥ \|*  
*divā niśi ca saṃdhyāyāṃ dīpaḥ kāryaḥ svaśaktitaḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. Men should always light a lamp in the house, in a temple. A lamp should be kept by day or during night according to one’s capacity

## \|\| 2.16.119 \|\|

*kiñciduddyotamātreṇa devāstuṣyaṃti bhūtale \|*  
*pitṝṇāṃ prathamaṃ dīpaḥ karttavyaḥ śrāddhakarmaṇi \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. With (even) a little light gods are pleased on the earth. In a śrāddha ceremony a lamp should be first kindled in honour of the dead ancestors.

## \|\| 2.16.120 \|\|

*rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kāryaṃ yathā nidrā na jā yate \|*  
*śivarātriprabhāvo'yaṃ śrotavyaḥ śivasaṃnidhau \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. At night men should keep awake in such a way that sleep does not overcome them. This glory of the Śivarātri should be listened to in the presence of listeners.

## \|\| 2.16.121 \|\|

*śivasya caritaṃ rātrau śrotavyaṃ bahuvistaram \|*  
*gītaṃ nṛtyaṃ tathā vādyaṃ kartavyaṃ śivasaṃnidhau \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. The story of Śiva fully detailed should be listened to at night. Singing, dancing, playing on musical instruments should be done in the vicinity of Śiva.

## \|\| 2.16.122 \|\|

*evaṃ sā nīyate rātrirmukhyaṃ jāgaraṇaṃ yataḥ \|*  
*rātrau deyāni dānāni śaktyā vai tatra jāgare \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. The night is passed like this since keeping awake is the main (object). While keeping awake at night gifts should be given according to one’s capacity.

## \|\| 2.16.123 \|\|

*punaḥ snātvā prabhāte tu karttavyaṃ śivapūjanam \|*  
*pūjanīyāśca yatayo bhojanācchādanādibhiḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. Again, taking a bath in the morning worship of Śiva should be done. Ascetics also should be honoured by giving them food, covering etc.

## \|\| 2.16.124 \|\|

*tapasvināṃ pradātavyaṃ bhojanaṃ gṛhamedhibhiḥ \|*  
*dvādaśāṣṭau ca catvāro bhoktavyā eka eva vā \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. Householders should give a meal to ascetics. Twelve, or eight or four, or even one should be fed.

## \|\| 2.16.125 \|\|

*eko'pi brahmacārī yo brahmavicchivapūjakaḥ \|*  
*sahasrāṇāṃ samo bhaktyā gṛhe saṃbhojito bhavet \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. Even one celibate, who is devotee of Śiva, is equal to a thousand ones when given a good meal in one’s house.

## \|\| 2.16.126 \|\|

*akṣārālavaṇaṃ patre bhoktavyaṃ vāgyataiḥ svayam \|*  
*putramitrakalatrāṇāṃ dātavyaṃ bhojanaṃ puraḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. They (i.e. the householders), controlling speech, should eat (food) which is not juicy or saltish, from a plate. He should first give food to his son, friends, wife.

## \|\| 2.16.127-128 \|\|

*anena vidhinā kāryā śivarātriḥ śivavrataiḥ \|*  
*dvādaśaitā yadā pūrṇāstilapātrāṇi vai tadā \|\| 127 \|\|*

*dvādaśaiva pradeyānigurubrāhmaṇajñātiṣu \|*  
*vratāṃte gauḥ pradātavyā kṛṣṇā vatsayutā dṛḍhā \|\| 128 \|\|*

127-128. In this way Śivarātri should always be observed by men. When these pots are filled with sesamum seeds, then only twelve (pots) should be given to the preceptor, a Brāhmaṇa, or members of his caste. At the end of the vow, a strong cow, with her calf, should be given.

## \|\| 2.16.129-130 \|\|

*savastrābharaṇā deyā ghaṃṭābharaṇabhūṣitā \|*  
*aṃgulīyakavāsāṃsi cchatropānatkamaṇḍalu \|\| 129 \|\|*

*gurave dakṣiṇā deyābrāhmaṇebhyaḥ svaśaktitaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ kṛtvā tato deyaṃ tapasvibhyo'tha bhojanam \|*  
*miṣṭānnaṃ vividhaṃ dattvā kṣamāpya ca visarjayet \|\| 130 \|\|*

129-130. She should be given along with garments and ornaments, and decorated with a decorative bell A ring, clothes, an umbrella, shoes, water-pot, should be given.Gifts should be given to one’s preceptor and Brāhmaṇas according to one’s capacity. Doing like this, meal should be given to ascetics. Having given sweet food of various kinds, he should give them leave after begging their pardon.

## \|\| 2.16.131-132 \|\|

*evaṃ yaḥ kurute satyaṃ tasya pāpaṃ na vidyate \|*  
*saṃtānamuttamaṃ labdhvā bhuktvā bhogānanuttamān \|\| 131 \|\|*

*divyavimānamārūḍho divyastrīpariveṣṭitaḥ \|*  
*gativāditranirghoṣairnīyate śivamandire \|\| 132 \|\|*

131-132. Truly there is no sin of him who does like this. Obtaining excellent progeny, enjoying excellent pleasures, he is taken to Śiva’s abode, after he gets into a divine aeroplane and is surrounded by divine ladies, accompanied by the sounds of songs, musical instruments.

## \|\| 2.16.133 \|\|

*tadetatkathitaṃ puṇyaṃ śivarātrivrataṃ mayā \|*  
*kṛtena yena lokānāṃ sarvapāpakṣayo bhavet \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. (Thus) I have narrated the holy vow of Śivarātri, having done which all the sins of men are exhausted.

## Chapter 17 - The Efficacy of Bali’s Sacrifice

## \|\| 2.17.1-2 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*vicitramidamākhyānaṃ tvatprasādācchrutaṃ mayā \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā nārāyaṇaṃ śakraṃ nārado maṃdare girau \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kiṃ cakāra munīṃdro'tha tanme vistarato mune \|*  
*vada saṃsārasaraṇodbhūtamāyāprapīḍitam \|*  
*kathāmṛtajalaughena vitṛṣaṃ kuru māṃ prabho \|\| 2 \|\|*

The King said:

1-2a. Through your favour I have heard this lovely narration. Having seen Nārāyaṇa, Śakra in the temple on the mountain, what did the best of sages do? Tell it to me in detail.

2bc. Tell me about the trouble caused by illusion arising from the unsteady worldly existence. O Lord, remove my thirst by the flow of the nectar-like water of tales.

## \|\| 2.17.3-4 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*athāsau nārado devaṃ jñātvā śaptaṃ dvijanmanā \|*  
*bhṛguṇā ca tathā pūrvaṃ nānyathaitadbhaviṣyati \|\| 3 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyaṃ yadbhavaṃ deva vartamānaṃ viciṃtyatām \|*  
*ayaṃ ca vāmano bhūtvā viṣṇuryāsyati tāṃ purīm \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

3-4. Then this Nārada knew that the god was cursed by the Brāhmaṇa, Bhṛgu, formerly. “This will not change. Think of the future, O god, of the present (also). This Viṣṇu, becoming Vāmana, will go to that city.

## \|\| 2.17.5 \|\|

*nigrahaṃ sa baleḥ paścātkariṣyati mama priyam \|*  
*yuddhaṃ vinā kathaṃ stheyaṃ vartamānaṃ maholbaṇam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. “Then he will chastise Bali. This is dear to me. How can this great (danger) stop without war?

## \|\| 2.17.6 \|\|

*devadānavayuddhāni daityagandharva rakṣasām \|*  
*nivāritāni sarvāṇi sarīsṛpapatatriṇām \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. “Wars among gods and demons, among demons, Gandharvas, goblins, so also among reptiles and birds—all have been kept off.

## \|\| 2.17.7 \|\|

*sāpatnajaḥ kalirnāsti mama bhāgyaparikṣaye \|*  
*devendro guruṇā pūrvaṃ vāritaḥ kiṃ karomyaham \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. “To harm my destiny there is no dissension due to belonging to a rival wife. The Lord of gods was formerly warded off by Guru (our preceptor). What should I do (now)?

## \|\| 2.17.8 \|\|

*mānanīyo gururme'yamatastaṃ na śapāmyaham \|*  
*yuddhārthaṃ tu tato yatno na sidhyati karomi kim \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. “This Guru is venerable to me. Therefore I do not curse hiim. Then an attempt at war will not succeed. What shall I do?

## \|\| 2.17.9 \|\|

*kenāpi daivayogena puruṣārtho na sidhyati \|*  
*tathāpi yatnaḥ kartavyaḥ puruṣārthe vipaścitā \|*  
*daivaṃ puruṣakāreṇa vināpi phalati kvacit \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. “Due to some coincidence a human effort does not succeed. Yet a wise man should try to secure the object of human exertion. At times fate succeeds even without manly effort.’

## \|\| 2.17.10 \|\|

*yaduktaṃ tadvaco vyarthaṃ yataḥ siddhiḥ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*baliṃ gatvā bhaṇiṣyāmi yathā yuddhaṃ kariṣyati \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. “These words that are uttered, are in vain, since success is due to effort. I shall go and speak to Bali so that he will wage a war.

## \|\| 2.17.11-12 \|\|

*na śroṣyati sa cedvākyaṃ niścitaṃ taṃ śapāmyaham \|*  
*ityuktvā sa yayau vegānnārado balimaṃdire \|*  
*nimeṣāṃtaramātreṇa śiṣyābhyāṃ gagane sthitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*prāsāde śailasaṃkāśe saptabhaume mahojjvale \|*  
*tasyopari sabhā divyā nirmitā viśvakarmaṇā \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12a. “If he does not listen to (my) words, I shall certainly curse him.” Speaking like this that Nārada speedily went to Bali’s residence. In a moment he reached a palace resembling a mountain, with seven stories and very bright, in the sky, with his disciples.

12b. Above it Viśvakarman constructed a divine hall.

## \|\| 2.17.13 \|\|

*tasyāṃ siṃhāsanaṃ divyaṃ tatrāsīno balirnṛpa \|*  
*daityaiḥ parivṛtaḥ sarvaiḥ prauḍhihāsyakathāparaiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. In it there was a divine throne, and Bali was seated on it, O King. He was surrounded by all demons, engaged in discussions, jokes.

## \|\| 2.17.14 \|\|

*ṛṣibhirbrāhmaṇaiḥ śāṃtaista thaivośanasā svayam \|*  
*putramitrakalatraiśca saṃvṛto divyamandire \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. (He was surrounded by) calm sages, Brāhmaṇas, so also by Uśanas himself; he was surrounded by sons, friends, wife in the divine hall.

## \|\| 2.17.15-16 \|\|

*devāṃganākaragrāhagṛhītairdivyacāmaraiḥ \|*  
*saṃvījyamāno daityendraḥ stūyamānaḥ sa cāraṇaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yāvadāste madonmattā mantrayaṃti parasparam \|*  
*daityadānavamukhyā ye te sarve yuddhakāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. That Lord of the demons was fanned with chowries held in the hands of celestial ladies, he was extolled by bards. (At this time) the chiefs of demons and fiends, all desiring war, arrogant with pride consulted one another.

## \|\| 2.17.17 \|\|

*utthāyotthāya bhāṣaṃte pragalbhaṃte suraiḥ saha \|*  
*asmadīyamidaṃ sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sāṃprataṃ gatam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Getting up again and again they were bold with the gods. “The three worlds, belonging to us, have now gone.

## \|\| 2.17.18-19 \|\|

*śukrabuddhyā vinā yuddhaṃ prāpsyate kiṃ mahodayaḥ \|*  
*daityendro devarājena snehaṃ ca kuruto yadi \|\| 18 \|\|*

*airāvaṇaṃ sadā mattaṃ kathaṃ no yācate baliḥ \|*  
*caturaṃ turagaṃ kasmānnārpayati divākaraḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*
