18-19. “Will a lucky person accept war without the intellect (i.e. wise guidance) of Śukra? If the king of the Daityas forms friendship with the Lord of gods, why does Bali not ask for the ever-intoxicated Airāvata? Why does Divākara (the Sun) not give the smart horse?

## \|\| 2.17.20 \|\|

*yāvannākramyate lubdho dhanādhyakṣo raṇājire \|*  
*tāvannārpayate vittaṃ yadā tatsaṃcitaṃ suraiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. “As long as the greedy Lord of wealth (Kubera) is not overpowered on the battlefield, he will not give the wealth which is collected by the gods.

## \|\| 2.17.21 \|\|

*na darśayati ratnāni jalarāśī rasātalāt \|*  
*yāvanna mandaraṃ kṣiptvā vimathnīmo vayaṃ ca tam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. “The ocean will not show the heap of wealth from the bottom of the earth, as long as it is not churned by us by throwing Mandāra (into it).

## \|\| 2.17.22 \|\|

*yathāmṛtakalāścandrādbhujyante kramaśaḥ suraiḥ \|*  
*evaṃ bhāgaṃ baleḥ kasmānna dadāti jalātmakaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. “As the drops of nectar are serially enjoyed by the gods, why, in the same way, the Moon does not give them (to the gods)?

## \|\| 2.17.23 \|\|

*svardhunī śītalo vātaḥ padmarkijalkavāsitaḥ \|*  
*svarge vāti śanairyadvattathā na balimaṃdire \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. “As the wind, cold due to the heavenly flow, and fragrant with lotus-filaments, slowly blows in Heaven, why does it not blow in Bali’s residence?

## \|\| 2.17.24 \|\|

*indracāpodyatā meghā jalaṃ muṃcaṃti bhūtale \|*  
*balikhaṅgoddhutāḥ svargaṃ punaste yāṃti bhūtalāt \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. “Clouds, raised by Indra’s bow, release water on the earth; and again, raised up by Bali’s sword, go to Heaven from the earth.

## \|\| 2.17.25 \|\|

*asmadīye dharāpṛṣṭhe yamo mārayate janam \|*  
*naivaṃ svarge na pātāle paśyāho kāryakāraṇam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. “On the surface of our earth, Yama kills people. This is not the case (either) in Heaven (or) in the Nether world. See the (relation between) the effect and the cause.

## \|\| 2.17.26 \|\|

*āyurvṛttiṃ sutānsaukhyamasmākaṃ likhati svayam \|*  
*lalāṭe citragupto'sau na devānāṃ tu tatsamam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. “Citragupta himself writes on our foreheads (the span of) life, means of living, number of sons, and happiness. Similar is not the case with the gods.

## \|\| 2.17.27 \|\|

*varṣāśītātapāḥ kālā vartaṃte bhuvi sāṃpratam \|*  
*na svarge naiva pātāle bhītā bhūmau bhramaṃti hi \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. “Now the seasons, the rainy season, the cold season, the hot season, exist on the earth. They do not exist either in the Heaven, or in the Nether world. Getting frightened they move (only) on the earth.

## \|\| 2.17.28 \|\|

*ekavīryodbhavā yūyaṃ svasrīyā devadānavāḥ \|*  
*bhūmau sthitā vayaṃ kasmāddevāḥ kenoparikṛtāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. “You, the gods and demons, have risen from the same energy, and are sisters’ sons. We remain on the earth. Who has, and why has he, made the gods above (i.e. superior to) us?

## \|\| 2.17.29 \|\|

*samudre mathyamāne tu daityendro vaṃcitaḥ suraiḥ \|*  
*ekataḥ sarvadevāśca baliścaivaikataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. “When the ocean was churned, the Lord of demons was cheated by gods. On one side were all gods, and on the other was Bali.

## \|\| 2.17.30-31 \|\|

*utpanneṣu ca ratneṣu bhāgyaṃ vai yasya yādṛśam \|*  
*gajāśvakalpavṛkṣādyāścaṃdragogaṇadaṃtinaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*gṛhītvā hyamṛtaṃ devairvayaṃ pāne niyojitāḥ \|*  
*etayā cūrṇitā yūyaṃ na jānīthātigarvitāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. “When the gems were produced they were distributed according as the destiny of one (was fixed). Taking elephants, horse, desiring-yielding tree etc., so also the Moon, herd of cows and elephants, nectar, we were instigated to drink (wine) (by gods). By this you reeled, (but) being too much proud, did not notice it.

## \|\| 2.17.32 \|\|

*pītāvaśeṣaṃ pīyūṣaṃ satyaloke dhṛtaṃ suraiḥ \|*  
*ahotikuṭilā devāḥ kasmāccheṣaṃ na dīyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. “The nectar that remained after (a part of it) was drunk, was held in the Satyaloka (the uppermost of the seven worlds) by the gods. Oh! the gods are extremely crooked. Why was not the remnant given (to us)?

## \|\| 2.17.33 \|\|

*surāmṛtamiti jñātvā pīyūṣādvaṃcitā vayam \|*  
*tilatailamevamiṣṭaṃ yairna dṛṣṭaṃ ghṛtaṃ kvacit \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. “We, looking upon wine as nectar, were deprived of nectar. Sesamum oil was looked upon as sweet dish; ghee was rarely (enjoyed).

## \|\| 2.17.34 \|\|

*viṣṇorvakracaritrāṇāṃ saṃkhyā kartu na śakyate \|*  
*tathāpi kathyate tuṣṭairhṛṣṭaistairyadanuṣṭhitam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. “It is not possible to count the vicious acts of Viṣṇu. Yet I shall tell what they, delighted and satisfied, did.

## \|\| 2.17.35-37 \|\|

*gaurāṃgī sundarī subhrūḥ pīnonnatapayodharā \|*  
*sukeśā caṃdravadanā karṇāsaktavilocanā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*valitrayāṃkitā madhye bālā muṣṭyāpi gṛhyate \|*  
*sthalāraviṃdacaraṇā lateva bhujabhūṣitā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*sā sarvābharaṇopetā sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyutā \|*  
*trailokyamohinī devī saṃjātā'mṛtamanthane \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. “They created, at (the time of) the churning of nectar, the goddess enchanting the three worlds. She was fair-skinned; she was beautiful, had beautiful eyebrows, had stout and raised breasts; she had beautiful hair; her face was (beautiful) like the Moon; her eyes were wide up to the ears; on the middle part of her body (i.e. on her belly) the young lady had three folds; (she was so thin that) she could be held even by the fist. Her feet were like white lotuses growing on the ground. Like a creeper with branches she was adorned with arms. She had all ornaments; she had all (good) signs.

## \|\| 2.17.38 \|\|

*amṛtādutthitā pūrvaṃ yasya sā tasya taddhruvam \|*  
*trailokyaṃ vaśagaṃ tasya yasya sā cārulocanā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. “She had formerly come up before nectar, and belonged certainly to him who had (got) her. The one, to whom the lady of charming eyes belonged, had the three words in his possession.

## \|\| 2.17.39 \|\|

*tayā saṃmohitāḥ sarve devadānavarākṣasāḥ \|*  
*vimucya manthanaṃ sarve tāṃ grahītuṃ samudyatāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. “She lured all gods, demons, fiends. Giving up the churning (of the ocean), all exerted to hold her.

## \|\| 2.17.40 \|\|

*ekā strī bahavo devā dānavādaityarākṣasāḥ \|*  
*vivādaḥ sumahāñjātaḥ kathamatra bhaviṣyati \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. “There was (just) one woman, (but) there were many gods, demons and fiends. A great dispute broke up as to what would happen in this case.

## \|\| 2.17.41-42 \|\|

*āgatya viṣṇunā sarve bhuje dhṛtvā nivāritāḥ \|*  
*asyārthe kimaho vādaḥ kriyate bhoḥ parasparam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*amṛtārthe samārambho mahilārthe vinaśyati \|*  
*saṃketaṃ prathamaṃ kṛtvā viṣṇunā cuṃbitā punaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. “Viṣṇu, having come there, warded off all (by) holding their arms. ‘Oh! Why do you quarrel for the sake of this (gem of a lady)? (Our) effort for obtaining nectar will perish (if we quarel \[quarrel?\]) for the sake of a lady.’ Having made a sign again thought of her.

## \|\| 2.17.43-44 \|\|

*divyarūpadharaḥ sragvī vanamālāvibhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*kaustubhoddyotitatanuḥ śaṃkhacakragadādharaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tasyā haste śubhāṃ mālāṃ dattvā viṣṇuḥ puraḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*uddhṛtya bāhuṃ sarveṣāṃ babhāṣe vacanaṃ hariḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. “Viṣṇu, taking up a divine form, having put on a garland, decorated with a sylvan garland, with his body brightened with Kaustubha, holding a conch, a disc, a mace, and giving an auspicious garland in her hand, stood before her, and raising his hand, he, Han, said (these) words to all:

## \|\| 2.17.45 \|\|

*kurvaṃtu kuṇḍalaṃ sarve tiṣṭhantu svayamāsane \|*  
*vilokya svecchayā lakṣmīrvaramālāṃ prayacchatu \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. “Let all form a circle; let all remain in their seats. Let Lakṣmī, having observed (all) according to her desire, offer the marriage-garland.

## \|\| 2.17.46 \|\|

*svayaṃvaravibhedaṃ yaḥ kariṣyatyatilaṃpaṭaḥ \|*  
*sa vadhyaḥ sahitaiḥ sarvaiḥ parastrīlubdhako yathā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. “He, who, being very lustful, disturbs the self-choice marriage, should be killed by all coming together, as one who covets another’s wife.

## \|\| 2.17.47 \|\|

*paradārakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ strīvadhyā tasya jāyatām \|*  
*anyo'pi yaḥ karotyevamevamastu taducyatām \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. “Let the offence of the murder of a woman be said to be committed by him who has committed the sin of molesting another’s wife. Anyone else who does likewise will have the same sin. Let it be said.’

## \|\| 2.17.48 \|\|

*sādhāraṇaṃ hariṃ jñātvā tathetyuktvā tathā kṛtam \|*  
*devadānavadaityānāṃ gaṃdharvoragarakṣasām \|*  
*madhye yo'bhimato bhartā sa te satyaṃ bhavediti \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. “Knowing Hari to be ordinary, and saying, ‘all right’ it was done like that. You will really have him as your husband who is dear to you from among gods, demons, fiends, Gandharvas, serpents, and goblins.

## \|\| 2.17.49 \|\|

*tenāsau mohitā pūrvaṃ dṛṣṭidānena karṣitā \|*  
*ādyaṃ saṃmohanaṃ strīṇāṃ cakre dṛṣṭinirīkṣaṇam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. “He formerly attracted her; she was first attracted by him by casting a glance (at her). He made an observation by his eyes - that is the first allurement for women.

## \|\| 2.17.50-52 \|\|

*evameveti tatkarṇe hastaṃ dattvā yaducyate \|*  
*dadhāti hṛdi yaṃ nārī kāmabāṇaprapīḍitā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*tameva varayedatra kaścinnāstyeva saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*saṃjāte kalahe pūrvaṃ hariṇā taṃ nivartitum \|\| 51 \|\|*

*yadā gṛhītā sarvaiḥ sā hariṃ naiva vimuṃcati \|*  
*tvameva bhartā sā'caṣṭe muṃca māṃ vraja dūrataḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

50a. “It is exactly so’—this is said by one by putting one’s hand on one’s ear.

50b-51a. “A woman troubled by the arrows of Cupid chooses him only, whom she holds in her heart. There is no doubt about this.

51b-52a. “When, formerly, in a quarrel that had come up, all (the demons) had seized her to keep Hari away from her, she did not leave him at all.

52b. “You alone are my husband. Leave me, go away’.

## \|\| 2.17.53 \|\|

*muktvā dūraṃ tato viṣṇuḥ praviṣṭaḥ suramaṇḍale \|*  
*tadā sarve ca māmuktvā yathāsthānaṃ svayaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. “Leaving her away, Viṣṇu then entered the circle of gods. Then all, leaving me (i.e. Lakṣmī) went to their respective places.

## \|\| 2.17.54 \|\|

*ācaṣṭa vijayā pūrvaṃ sarvāndevānyathākramam \|*  
*sā ca nirīkṣate paścāttaṃ vicārya vimuñcati \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. “Vijayā first told all gods in due order. She reflected and having thought left him.

## \|\| 2.17.55 \|\|

*udāsīnaḥ śivaḥ śāṃto gaurīkāṃtastrilocanaḥ \|*  
*nānyāṃ nirīkṣate nityaṃ dhyānāsaktastrilocanaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. “Śiva, the three-eyed God, neutral, calm, the husband of Gaurī, dd \[did?\] not see any other (woman, but) was always engaged in meditation.

## \|\| 2.17.56 \|\|

*pitāmahoyamityuktaṃ yadā sakhyā tadā tayā \|*  
*namaskṛtya gataṃ dūre kṛtvā maunaṃ na paśyati \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. “When her friend said to her, ‘This is the Grandsire’, she saluted him and went away. Observing silence, she did not look (at him).

## \|\| 2.17.57 \|\|

*ādityaṃ padmakaṃ muñca dahanaṃ dahanātmakam \|*  
*vāti vāto gatā dūre varuṇo me pitā yataḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. “Leave Āditya, an army, arranged in the form of a lotus-flower; (so also leave) Fire, of the nature of burning. The Wind bīows (i.e. is not steady). She went away since, (she said): ‘Varuṇa is my father’.

## \|\| 2.17.58 \|\|

*paulomīvadanāsakto devendro me na rocate \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. “I do not like Devendra as he is attracted to Paulomī’s face.

## \|\| 2.17.59 \|\|

*vadhabaṃdhakṛtacchedabhedadaṇḍavikarṣa ṇam \|*  
*kurvanna kurute saumyaṃ rūpaṃ vaivasvato yamaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. “Yama, the son of Vivasvān, who commits murders, binds (beings), cuts (them) off, creates cleaving, punishes, drags, does not have a mild form.

## \|\| 2.17.60-63 \|\|

*devadānavagaṃdharvadaityapannagarākṣasān \|\| 60 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvātyugrāṃstato yāti dṛṣṭo'sau puruṣo ttamaḥ \|*  
*karṇāṃtalocanabhrāṃtavaktraṃ dṛṣṭyāvalokya tam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*saubhāgyātiśayākrāṃtaṃ ramyaṃ kāmamanoharam \|*  
*saṃjātapulakodbhedasvedavārikaṇāṃkitam \|\| 62 \|\|*

*devadānavadaityendrakrodhadṛṣṭinirīkṣitam \|*  
*ramyaṃ rāmā varaṃ cakre dadau mālāṃ tataḥ svayam \|\| 63 \|\|*

60-63. “Seeing the very fierce gods, demons, Gandharvas, fiends, serpents, goblins, she moves from that place. She saw Puruṣottama (i.e. Viṣṇu). By turning her face, the eyes of which were drawn upto the ears (i.e. in a staring manner), she looked at him who was having excessive charm, delightful, attractive as desired, marked with sweat caused by horripilation, who was looked at angrily by the best gods, demons, fiends, the lady (Lakṣmī) chose the charming bridegroom, and herself offered the (marriage-) garland to him.

## \|\| 2.17.64 \|\|

*daityāḥ parasparaṃ procuḥ prekṣya tatsuraceṣṭitam \|*  
*vibhāgaṃ paśya devānāṃ svarge sarve svayaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. “Seeing that divine movement, the demons said to one another: ‘See the division of (made by) gods. All of them have gone to Heaven.

## \|\| 2.17.65 \|\|

*pātālasya tale yūyaṃ mānavā dharaṇītale \|*  
*devāstribhuvane yāṃtu na vayaṃ svargagāminaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. “We are at (i.e. driven to the bottom of) the Nether world. Human beings are (left) on the surface of the earth. Gods can go to (i.e. move in) the three worlds, (but) we cannot go to Heaven.

## \|\| 2.17.66-67 \|\|

*mānavāḥ kṣatriyā rājyaṃ kurvaṃtu pṛthivītale \|*  
*pātālaṃ tu parityajya dhātrī yadi tu rakṣyate \|\| 66 \|\|*

*daityadānavajaiḥ kaiścidrākṣasaistanna śobhanam \|*  
*atha kiṃ bahunoktena rājā tribhuvane baliḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. “Let the men viz. Kṣatriyas rule over the earth, leaving the Nether world, if the earth is to be protected by those born of the demons and goblins, it is not fair. What is the use of prolixity? Bali is the king in (i.e. of) the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.17.68-72 \|\|

*saṃvibhajyātha ratnāni samaṃ rājyaṃ vidhīyatām \|*  
*yāvadevaṃ pragalbhaṃte tāvatpaśyaṃti nāradam \|\| 68 \|\|*

*gaganātsamupāyāṃtaṃ dvitīyamiva bhāskaram \|*  
*brahmadaṃḍakarāsaktayuddhapustakadhāriṇam \|\| 69 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇājinadharaṃ śāṃtaṃ chatravīṇākamaṇḍalūn \|*  
*mauṃjīguṇatrayāsaktagraṃthipravaramekhalam \|\| 70 \|\|*

*brahmarūpadharaṃ śāṃtaṃ divyarudrākṣabhūṣitam \|*  
*gata kalpakṛtagraṃthisūtramālāvalaṃbitam \|\| 71 \|\|*

*viraṃciharasaṃvādo janmāhaṃkāragarvitaḥ \|*  
*saṃkruddhaiḥ kriyate ko'dya ciṃtātatparamānasam \|\| 72 \|\|*

68-72. “Having divided the gems, let the kingdom be (divided) equally.’ When they were talking confidently like this, they saw Nārada who was coming from the sky, who was as it were another Sun, who had held a book that was about a war in his hand, holding the divine staff, had put on the skin of black antelope, was calm, held an umbrella, a lute, a water-pot, an excellent girdle with three knots, tied with muñja grass, who had the form of a Brāhmaṇa, was calm, was adorned with divine Rudrākṣas, had put on a garland with a thread and knots of the former Kalpa (age), whose mind was anxious to know as to what talk full of the pride due to the ego of birth, was today going on between Brahmā and Śiva, who were angry.

## \|\| 2.17.73-75 \|\|

*āyātaṃ nāradaṃ dṛṣṭvā vismitāḥ samupasthitāḥ \|*  
*prabho prasādaḥ kriyatāmāgaṃtavyaṃ gṛhe mama \|\| 73 \|\|*

*dhanyo'haṃ kṛtapuṇyo'haṃ yasya me tvaṃ gṛhāgataḥ \|*  
*ityukto balinā vipro viveśāsuramaṃdire \|*  
*āsanaṃ pādyamarghyaṃ ca dattvā saṃpūjito dvijaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*praviśya sahitāḥ sarve saṃviṣṭā daityadānavāḥ \|*  
*śukreṇa sahito daityo babhāṣe nāradaṃ baliḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

73-74a. “Seeing Nārada coming, all stood amazed. ‘O Lord, favour me; come to my house, to whose house you have come. I am blessed; I have secured religious merit.’

74b-75. “Thus addressed by Bali, the Brāhmaṇa (Nārada) entered the dwelling of the demon (Bali). The Brāhmaṇa was worshipped by offering him a seat, water to wash feet with, and a respectful offering.

## \|\| 2.17.76 \|\|

*idaṃ rājyamime dārā ime putrā ahaṃ baliḥ \|*  
*brūhi yenātra te kāryaṃ dānaṃ me prathamaṃ vratam \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. “All gods and demons, together entered (Bali’s residence). Bali was accompanied by Śukra. Bali said to Nārada: ‘This is my kingdom; this is my wife; these are my sons. I am Bali. Say with whom you have business. Charity is my first vow’.

## \|\| 2.17.77 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*bhaktyā tuṣyaṃti ye viprāste viprā bhūmidevatāḥ \|*  
*na tu ye pūjitāḥ śaktyā punaryācaṃti te'dhamāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

Nārada said:

77\. Those Brāhmaṇas who are pleased by devotion are deities on the earth. Those who are worshipped (according to the capacity of the worshipper), and yet ask (for more), are mean.

## \|\| 2.17.78 \|\|

*tvayā'haṃ pūjito hṛṣṭo na vittairme prayojanam \|*  
*hṛṣṭo'haṃ tava rājyena yajñairdānairvrataistathā \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. I, who was worshipped by you, am glad. I have nothing to do with riches. So also I am pleased with your kingdom, sacrifices, gifts and vows.

## \|\| 2.17.79 \|\|

*devaiḥ kṛtaṃ vipriyaṃ te kiṃcitpaśyāmyahaṃ bale \|*  
*tvayā saṃpūjyamāno'pi devarājo na tuṣyati \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. O Bali, I see that the gods have done some wrong to you. The King of gods (Indra), though being worshipped by us is not pleased.

## \|\| 2.17.80 \|\|

*na kṣamaṃti surāḥ sarve tava rājyaṃ dharātale \|*  
*svarge me tāpako jāto devānāṃ tava vigrahe \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. All the gods do not tolerate your kingdom on the earth. He (Indra) became troublesome to me in your war with the gods.

## \|\| 2.17.81 \|\|

*saṃnahya prathamaṃ yāti yaḥ sainyaṃ śatrubhūmiṣu \|*  
*sa kṣatriyo vijayate tasya rājyaṃ ca vardhate \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. He, the Kṣatriya, who, clad in armour, takes his army to the lands of the enemy, is victorious, and his kingdom gains strength.

## \|\| 2.17.82 \|\|

*ucchedastava rājyasya bhaviṣyati śrutaṃ mayā \|*  
*evaṃ jñātvā yathāyuktaṃ tacchīghraṃ tu vidhīyatām \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. I have learnt that his kingdom is destroyed. Realising this, do quickly what is proper.

## \|\| 2.17.83 \|\|

*baliruvāca \|*  
*yairguṇaiḥ kurute rājyaṃ rājā tānvada me vibho \|*  
*dānaṃ pātre pradātavyaṃ mayā tvamapi taṃ vada \|\| 83 \|\|*

Bali said:

83\. O eminent one, tell me the virtues due to which a king rules over his kingdom. Tell me also about him who is worthy, as a gift is to be given to a worthy recipient.

## \|\| 2.17.84 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*ṣaḍviṃśadguṇasaṃpanno rājā rājyaṃ karoti ca \|*  
*sa rājyaphalamāpnoti śṛṇu tatkathayāmyaham \|\| 84 \|\|*

Nārada said:

84\. A king endowed with thirty-six merits rules over the kingdom. He obtains the fmit of the kingdom. Listen. I shall (tell) about it (i.e. how he obtains it).

## \|\| 2.17.85 \|\|

*careddharmānakaṭuko muṃcetsnehamanāstike \|*  
*anṛśaṃsaścaredarthaṃ caretkāmamanuddhataḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Not being harsh he should do his duties; he should give up friendship with an athiest \[atheist?\]. Without being wicked he should try to attain riches; he should, without being arrogant indulge in sexual enjoyments.

## \|\| 2.17.86 \|\|

*priyaṃ brūyādakṛpaṇaḥ śūraḥ syādavikatthanaḥ \|*  
*dātā cā'yāmavarjaḥ syātpragalbhaḥ syādaniṣṭhuraḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Without being mean, he should speak (what is) pleasing. Being brave, he should not brag. He should be an unrestrained giver; he should be bold; he should not be cruel.

## \|\| 2.17.87 \|\|

*saṃdadhīta na cānāryānvigṛhṇīyānna baṃdhubhiḥ \|*  
*nānāptaiścārayeccārānkuryātkāryamapīḍayan \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. He should not join the vulgar; he should not fight with his kinsmen. He should not employ spies against the faithful; he should do acts without harassment.

## \|\| 2.17.88 \|\|

*arthānbrūyānna cāpatsu guṇānbrūyānna cātmanaḥ \|*  
*ādadyānna ca sādhubhyo nāsatpuruṣamāśrayet \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. In calamities he should not talk about wealth. He should tell his own virtues (to others). He should not take (anything) from the noble. He should not take shelter with a bad man.

## \|\| 2.17.89 \|\|

*nāparīkṣya nayeddaṇḍaṃ na ca maṃtraṃ prakāśayet \|*  
*visṛjenna ca lubdhebhyo viśvasennāpakāriṣu \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. He should not inflict punishment without (proper) scrutiny. He should not disclose counsel. He should not give to the greedy; he should trust the wrong-doers.

## \|\| 2.17.90 \|\|

*āptaiḥ suguptadāraḥ syādrakṣyaścānyo ghṛṇī nṛpaḥ \|*  
*striyaṃ seveta nātyarthaṃ mṛṣṭaṃ bhuṃjīta nā'hitam \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. With his relatives he should well protect his wife. He should also protect another kind King. He should not indulge in sex with women too much; he should eat pure (food), and not harmful.

## \|\| 2.17.91 \|\|

*asteyaḥ pūjayenmānyānguruṃ sevedamāyayā \|*  
*arcyo devo na dambhena śriyamicchedakutsitām \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Keeping nothing secret, he should respect the respectable. He should serve his preceptor without deceit. He should not worship a deity deceitfully. He should desire glory that is not mean.

## \|\| 2.17.92 \|\|

*seveta praṇayaṃ kṛtvā dakṣaḥ syādatha kālavit \|*  
*sāṃtvavākyaṃ sadā vācyamanugṛhṇanna cākṣipet \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. He should serve his master lovingly. He should be diligent, and know the (importance of) time. He should always speak mild words; favouring a person, he should not spurn him.

## \|\| 2.17.93 \|\|

*praharenna ca viprāya hatvā śatrūnna śeṣayet \|*  
*krodhaṃ kuryānna cākasmānmṛduḥ syānnāpakāriṣu \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. He should not strike a Brāhmaṇa; while striking his enemies he should not spare them. He should not be suddenly angry. He should not be soft to the harmful.

## \|\| 2.17.94-95 \|\|

*evaṃ rājye ciraṃ stheyaṃ yadi śreya ihecchasi \|*  
*tapaḥsvādhyāyadānāni tīrthayātrā'śramāṇi ca \|\| 94 \|\|*

*yogenātmaprabodhasya kalāṃ nārhaṃti ṣoḍaśīm \|*  
*tvayā saṃsāravairāgyaṃ karttavyaṃ viprapūjanam \|\| 95 \|\|*

94-95. In this way you should rule the kingdom for a long time if you desire welfare in this world. Penance, self-study, charity, visits to holy places, and (residence in) hermitages do not deserve even the sixteenth fraction of self-realisation by means of deep and abstract meditation. Being dejected with the worldly existence you should honour a Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 2.17.96 \|\|

*yaṣṭavyaṃ vividhairyajñairdhyeyo nārāyaṇo hariḥ \|*  
*prasaṃgena samāyāto yāsye raivatake girau \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. You should perform various sacrifices; you should meditate upon Nārāyaṇa Hari. I, who have incidentally come here, will go to the Raivataka mountain.

## \|\| 2.17.97 \|\|

*tatrāste bhagavānviṣṇurnadī trailokyapāvanī \|*  
*tatrāste ca śivāvṛkṣo bahupuṣpaphalānvitaḥ \|*  
*tatra gatvā kariṣyāmi vrataṃ tadviṣṇuvallabham \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. There is Lord Viṣṇu; so also (there is) the river purifying the three worlds. There is also the Śiva tree, having many flowers and fruits. Going there I shall observe the vow dear to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.17.98 \|\|

*baliruvāca \|*  
*ko'yaṃ raivatakonāma vrataṃ kiṃ viṣṇuvallabham \|*  
*śivāvṛkṣāstu ke proktāstatkathaṃ kathayasva me \|\| 98 \|\|*

Bali said:

98\. What is this Raivataka? What is the vow dear to Viṣṇu? What trees are called Śivā? How is it (i.e. How is the vow observed)? Tell me that.

## \|\| 2.17.99 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*purā yugādau daityendra sapakṣāḥ parvatāḥ kṛtāḥ \|*  
*saṃciṃtya brahmaṇā paścādacalāste kṛtāḥ punaḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

Nārada said:

99\. O Lord of demons, formerly, at the beginning of the Yuga (age of the world), the mountains were made to have wings. Thinking over (this phenomenon), Brahmā again made them steady.

## \|\| 2.17.100 \|\|

*utpataṃti mahākāyā nipataṃti yadṛcchayā \|*  
*merumaṃdarakailāsā vacasā saṃsthitāḥ sthirāḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. (The mountains) Meru, Mandāra, Kailāśa, that used to fly and fall accidentally, were (made) steady by (just) a command.

## \|\| 2.17.101-102 \|\|

*vāritā na sthitā ye tu ta iṃdreṇa sthirīkṛtāḥ \|*  
*merordakṣiṇa śṛṃge tu kumudeti sa parvataḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

*divyaḥ sapakṣaḥ sauvarṇo divyavṛkṣaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasyopari purī divyā vaiṣṇavī viṣṇunā kṛtā \|\| 102 \|\|*

101-102. Those (mountains) that did not stop though so warded off were made steady by Indra. On the south peak of Meru there is that mountain Kumuda. It is divine, has wings, is golden and covered with divine trees. On it is Vaiṣṇavī city made by Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.17.103 \|\|

*tasyā madhye gṛhaṃ divyaṃ yasmillaṃkṣmīḥ sadā sthitā \|*  
*meroḥ śṛṃge purī ramyā gṛhaṃ tatra manoramam \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. In its midst there is a divine dwelling in which Lakṣmī always stays. On the peak of Mem is a beautiful city in which there is a charming house.

## \|\| 2.17.104 \|\|

*tatrāste sa bhavo devo bhavānī yatra saṃsthitā \|*  
*sabhā māheśvarī ramyā sauvarṇī ratnamaṃḍitā \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. In it dwells God Bhava, where Bhavānī also stays. Maheśvara’s hall is charming, golden and decorated with jewels.

## \|\| 2.17.105 \|\|

*tatrāste bhagavānviṣṇurdevairbrahmādibhirvṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasyāṃ viṣṇuḥ sadā yāti devaṃ draṣṭuṃ maheśvaram \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. There is Lord Viṣṇu, surrounded by gods like Brahmā. Viṣṇu always goes into it (i.e. the hall) to see God Maheśvara.

## \|\| 2.17.106 \|\|

*sauvarṇaiḥ kumudairyasmādasau sarvatra maṃḍitaḥ \|*  
*kumudeti kṛtaṃ nāma devaistatra samāgataiḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Since it is all over decorated with golden lotuses, gods that had come there named it Kumuda.

## \|\| 2.17.107 \|\|

*ekadā bhagavānrudro girau tasminsamāgataḥ \|*  
*draṣṭuṃ tacchikhare ramye tāṃ purīṃ viṣṇupālitām \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. Once Lord Rudra came īo that mountain to see on that peak the city protected by Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.17.108 \|\|

*gṛhāgataṃ haraṃ dṛṣṭvā hariṇā sa tu pūjitaḥ \|*  
*lakṣmyā saṃpūjitā gaurī harṣitā tatra saṃsthitā \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Seeing Hara to have come to (his) house, he was honoured by Hari. Gaurī was honoured by Lakṣmī. She, being delighted, remained there.

## \|\| 2.17.109 \|\|

*ekāsanopaviṣṭau tau maṃtrayaṃtau parasparam \|*  
*hareṇa kāraṇaṃ jñātvā tatsarvaṃ kathitaṃ hareḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. Seated on the same seat, the two (Hara and Hari) consulted each other. Hara, knowing the cause, told all that to Hari.

## \|\| 2.17.110 \|\|

*tvayeyaṃ nagarī kāryā maṃdare parvatottame \|*  
*praṣṭavyaḥ kāraṇaṃ nāhamavaśyaṃ tadbhaviṣyati \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. “You should situate this city on Mandāra, the excellent mountain. You should not ask me the reason (for doing so). There certainly will be (some reason).

## \|\| 2.17.111-112 \|\|

*hara eva vijānāti kāraṇaṃ katamo'pi na \|*  
*evaṃ tatheti tau proktvā saṃsthitau parvato'pi saḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃgataṃ rudraṃ kumudaḥ svayamāyayau \|*  
*dhanyo'haṃ kṛtapuṇyo'haṃ yasya me gṛhamāgatau \|\| 112 \|\|*

111-112. “Hara alone knows it, and (none) else. ‘Thus’, ‘Like that’—speaking like this, they remained (there). That Mountain, Kumuda, also, seeing Rudra accompanied by (Hari), himself came there. ‘Oh! I am blessed; I must have done (acts of) religious merit, for to my house you have come.’

## \|\| 2.17.113 \|\|

*dvābhyāmukto girivaro dadāva kiṃ varaṃ tava \|*  
*ityuktaḥ parvatastābhyāṃ varaṃ vavre sa mūḍhadhīḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. The best Mountain was addressed by the two: ‘What boon should we give to you?’ Thus addressed, the stupid Mountain asked for a boon from the two.

## \|\| 2.17.114 \|\|

*bhaviṣyatkāryahetutvādbhaviṣyati na tadvṛthā \|*  
*yatrāhaṃ tatra vastavyaṃ bhavadbhyāmastu me varaḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. “It will not be futile for it will produce a result in future. You two should stay there where I stay.

## \|\| 2.17.115 \|\|

*matsannidhau samāgatya sthātavyaṃ brahmavāsaram \|*  
*tathetyuktvā sapatnīkau gatau hariharāvubhau \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. “Coming near me, you should stay (near me) for a day of Brahmā.” Saying “All right” both Hari and Hara, went (back) along with their wives.

## \|\| 2.17.116 \|\|

*pañcamo yo manuḥ pūrvaṃ raivato nāma viśrutaḥ \|*  
*tasyotpattau tu yadvṛttaṃ kumudāgre śṛṇuṣva tat \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. O Kumuda, listen to what happened at the creation of the fifth Manu who was formerly known as Raivata.

## \|\| 2.17.117 \|\|

*ṛṣirāsīnmahābhāga ṛtavāgiti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*tasyāputrasya putro'bhūdrevatyante mahātmanaḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. O illustrious one, there was a well-known sage Ṛtavāk. A son was born to the magnanimous one, who was sonless, from Revatī.

## \|\| 2.17.118 \|\|

*sa tasya vidhivaccakre jātakarmādikāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*tathopanayanādyāśca sa cāśīlo'bhavannṛpa \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. He performed all his rites like the ceremony performed at the birth of a child; so also rites like the thread ceremony, (but) O King, he turned to be characterless.

## \|\| 2.17.119 \|\|

*yataḥ prabhṛti jāto'sau tataḥ prabhṛtyasāvṛṣiḥ \|*  
*dīrgharogaparāmarśamavāpātīva durddharam \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. From the time he was born, the sage suffered from a chronic disease, difficult to be cured.

## \|\| 2.17.120 \|\|

*mātā cāsya parāmārtiṃ kuṣṭharogābhipīḍitā \|*  
*jagāma cintāṃ sa ṛṣiḥ kimetaditi duḥkhitaḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. His mother too, affected by leprosy, suffered from great pain. The sage became anxious, and was worried (thinking) “What is this (that has befallen me)?”

## \|\| 2.17.121 \|\|

*mūrkhastu maṃdadhīḥ putro duḥkhaṃ janayate pituḥ \|*  
*amārgago viśeṣeṇa duḥkhādduḥkhataraṃ hi tat \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. A foolish, dull son, especially one that goes astray, causes agony to the father. It is more painful than (any other) pain.

## \|\| 2.17.122 \|\|

*aputratā manuṣyāṇāṃ śreyase na kuputratā \|*  
*suhṛdāṃ nopakārāya pitṝṇāṃ nāpi tṛptaye \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. To be sonless is preferable to having a bad son, for human beings. (A bad) son does not oblige the kind-hearted (relatives). Nor does he satisfy his forefathers.

## \|\| 2.17.123 \|\|

*suputro hṛdaye'bhyeti mātāpitrordinedine \|*  
*pitrorduḥkhāya dhigjanma tasya duṣkṛtakarmaṇaḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. A good son everyday enters the hearts of his parents. (But) fie upon the life of that (bad son) doing bad deeds, since they cause pain to the parents!

## \|\| 2.17.124 \|\|

*dhanyāste tanayā ye syuḥ savarlokābhisaṃmatāḥ \|*  
*paropakāriṇaḥ śāṃtāḥ sādhukarmaṇyanuvratāḥ \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. Blessed are those sons who would be liked by all people. They oblige others, are calm and engaged in good deeds.

## \|\| 2.17.125 \|\|

*anirvṛtaṃ nirānaṃdaṃ duḥkhaśokapariplutam \|*  
*narakāya na svargāya kuputratvaṃ hi janminaḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. The state of a bad son of one who is born, is never contented, is always joyless, and full of grief and lamentation. It begets miserable state for the friendly ones, and joy for the hostile! Having a bad son of a being, neither leads to Hell nor to Heaven.

## \|\| 2.17.126 \|\|

*karoti suhṛdāṃ dainyamahitānāṃ tathā mudam \|*  
*akāle tu jarāṃ pitroḥ kuputraḥ kurute kila \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. It produces miserable state among the kind-hearted (relatives) and joy among the enemies. A bad son indeed produces untimely old age in the parents.

## \|\| 2.17.127 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ so'tyantaduṣṭasya putrasya caritairmuniḥ \|*  
*dahyamānamanovṛttirvṛddhagargamapṛcchata \|\| 127 \|\|*

Nārada said:

127\. Then the sage whose mental condition was thus being perturbed by acts of the extremely wicked son, asked the old Garga.

## \|\| 2.17.128 \|\|

*ṛtavāguvāca \|*  
*suvratena purā vedā adhītā vidhinā mayā \|*  
*samāpya vidyā vidhavatkṛto dāraparigrahaḥ \|\| 128 \|\|*

Ṛtavāk said:

128\. Formerly, I, of a good vow, studied the Vedas properly. Having finished the studies I married with proper rites.

## \|\| 2.17.129 \|\|

*sadāreṇa hi yāḥ kāryāḥ śrautasmārttādikāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*tāḥ kṛtāśca vidhānena kāmaṃ samanurudhya ca \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. Those rites—performed according to the scriptures and Smṛtis—along wih the wife, were performed properly after having restrained desire of sensual enjoyments.

## \|\| 2.17.130 \|\|

*putrārthaṃ janitaścāyaṃ puṃnāmno vicyutau mune \|*  
*so'yaṃ kimātmadoṣeṇa māturdoṣeṇa kiṃ mama \|*  
*asmadduḥkhāvaho jāto dauḥśīlyādvada kovida \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. He was given birth for having a son in the absence of a son. O you learned one, tell me whether due to his own sin or that of his mother or me he has become a pain.

## \|\| 2.17.131 \|\|

*garga uvāca \|*  
*revatyante muniśreṣṭha jāto'yaṃ tanayastava \|*  
*tena duḥkhāya te duṣṭe kāle yasmādajāyata \|\| 131 \|\|*

Garga said:

131\. O best sage, this your son is born at the end of Revatī (constellation). So he is causing pain to you since he was born in your bad period.

## \|\| 2.17.132 \|\|

*tavāpacāro naivāsya māturnāpi kulasya ca \|*  
*anyaddauḥśīlyahetutvaṃ revatyaṃta upāgatam \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. This is not your fault, nor of his mother or the family. There is another cause of the bad character which has occurred at the end of the Revatī (constellation).

## \|\| 2.17.133 \|\|

*revatī aśvinormadhyamāśleṣāmaghayostathā \|*  
*jyeṣṭhāmūlarkṣayoḥ proktaṃ gaṃḍāṃtaṃ tu bhayāvaham \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. A fearful impediment is said (to take place) between Revatī and Aśvinī, between Aśleṣā and Maghā, and Jyeṣṭha and Mūla.

## \|\| 2.17.134 \|\|

*gaṃḍatraye tu ye jātā naranārīturaṃgamāḥ \|*  
*tiṣṭhaṃti na ciraṃ gehe tiṣṭhanto'pi bhayaṃkarāḥ \|*  
*evamukto'tha gargeṇa cukrodhātīva kopanaḥ \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. Those who are born in the impediments, whether, a man, a woman or a horse, do not remain in the house for a long time, or if they stay they are fearful.

Thus addressed by Garga, the wrathful sage became very much angry.

## \|\| 2.17.135-136 \|\|

*ṛtavāguvāca \|*  
*yasmānmamaika putrasya revatyante samudbhavaḥ \|\| 135 \|\|*

*revatī kiṃ na jānāti māṃ vipraḥ śāpayiṣyati \|*  
*jājvalyamānā gaganāttasmātpatatu revatī \|\| 136 \|\|*

Ṛtavāk said:

135-136. Since my only son is born at the end of Revatī, does Revatī not know—“The Brāhmaṇa (i.e. Ṛtavāk) will curse me?” Let, therefore, the bright Revatī fall from the sky.

## \|\| 2.17.137 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*tenaivaṃ vyāhṛte vākye revatyṛkṣaṃ papāta ha \|\|*  
*paśyataḥ sarvalokasya vismayāviṣṭacetasaḥ \|\| 137 \|\|*

Nārada said:

137\. When he uttered words like this, the constellation Revatī fell down, in the presence of all people with their minds full of wonder.

## \|\| 2.17.138 \|\|

*īśvarecchāprabhāvena patitā girimūrddhani \|*  
*revatyṛkṣaṃ nipatitaṃ kumudādrau samantataḥ \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. Due to the prowess of the will of the Lord, Revatī fell on the top of the mountain, - the Revatī constellation fell all around on the mountain Kumuda.

## \|\| 2.17.139-140 \|\|

*surāṣṭradeśe sa prāptaḥ patito bhūtale śubhe \|*  
*himācalasya putro ya ujjayaṃto girirmahān \|\| 139 \|\|*

*kumudena samaṃ maitrī kṛtā pūrvaṃ parasparam \|*  
*yatra tvaṃ sthāsyase sthātā tatrāhamapi niścitam \|\| 140 \|\|*

139-140. The mountain reached the Surāṣṭra country, and fell on an auspicious ground. The great mountain Ujjayanta, the son of Himālaya, formed friendship mutually with Kumuda. “I shall certainly stay wherever you will stay.”

## \|\| 2.17.141 \|\|

*iti kṛtvā gṛhītvātha gaṃgāvāri sayāmunam \|*  
*sārasvataṃ tathā puṇyaṃ siṃcituṃ taṃ samāgataḥ \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. Thinking so, and taking the water of Gaṅgā along with that of Yamunā, and the auspicious Sarasvatī, he came there to sprinkle him.

## \|\| 2.17.142 \|\|

*āhūtasaṃplavaṃ yāvatsaṃsthitau tau parasparam \|*  
*kumudādriśca tatpātātkhyāto raivatako'bhavat \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. They stayed with each other till the time of universal destruction. Due to that fall the mountain Kumuda was known as Raivataka.

## \|\| 2.17.143-144 \|\|

*atīva ramyaḥ sarvasyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ pṛthivīpate \|*  
*kumudādriśca sauvarṇo revatīcyavanātpunaḥ \|\| 143 \|\|*

*paṃkajābhaḥ sa bāhyena jāto varṇena bhūpate \|*  
*meruvarṇaḥ sa madhye tu sauvarṇaḥ parvatottamaḥ \|\| 144 \|\|*

143-144. O Lord of the earth, the mountain Kumuda is charming in the entire world. The mountain Kumuda is golden, and again after the fall of Revatī, it has turned similar to a lotus in the outer complexion. O King, in the middle it is of Meru’s colour; the best mountain is golden.

## \|\| 2.17.145 \|\|

*tataḥ sañjanayāmāsa kanyāṃ raivatako giriḥ \|*  
*revatīkāṃti saṃbhūtāṃ revatīsadṛśānanām \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. Then Raivataka Mountain produced a daughter, with the complexion of Revatī, and having face like Revatī.

## \|\| 2.17.146 \|\|

*pramuco nāma rājarṣistena dṛṣṭā varāṃganā \|*  
*pitṛvadrevatīnāma kṛtaṃ tasyā nṛpottama \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. A royal sage Pramuñca saw that excellent lady following his father. He named her Revatī.

## \|\| 2.17.147 \|\|

*revatīti ca vikhyātā sā sarvatra varāṃganā \|*  
*sarvatejomayaṃ sthānaṃ sarvatīrthajalāśrayam \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. That excellent lady was known everywhere as Revatī. The place was full of all lustre, and was the resort of the water of all holy places.

## \|\| 2.17.148 \|\|

*gaṃgājalapravāhaiśca saṃyuktaṃ yāmunaistathā \|*  
*sthitaṃ sārasvataṃ toyaṃ tatra garteṣu tattrayam \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. It was joined with streams of Gaṅgā; so also of Yamunā. In the ditches there remained the Sārasvata water.

## \|\| 2.17.149 \|\|

*vikhyātaṃ revatīkuṃḍaṃ yatra jātā ca revatī \|*  
*smaraṇāddarśanātsnānātsarvapāpakṣayo bhavet \|\| 149 \|\|*

149\. (There is) the well known Revatī-kuṇḍa, where Revatī was born. By remembering it, seeing it, bathing there, all the sins perish.

## \|\| 2.17.150 \|\|

*sā bālā varddhitā tena pramuṃcena mahātmanā \|*  
*yauvanaṃ tu tayā prāptaṃ tasminraivatake girau \|\| 150 \|\|*

150\. The girl was brought up by that magnanimous Pramuñca. On that Raivataka mountain she attained puberty.

## \|\| 2.17.151 \|\|

*tāṃ tu yauvanasaṃpannāṃ dṛṣṭvā'tha pramuco muni \|*  
*ekāṃte cintayāmāsa ko'syā bhartā bhaviṣyati \|\| 151 \|\|*

151\. Seeing her endowed with youth the sage Pramuñca thought in loneliness: “Who will be her husband?”

## \|\| 2.17.152 \|\|

*hūtvāhūtvā sa papraccha guruṃ vahniṃ dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*prasādaṃ kuru me brūhi ko'syā bhartā bhaviṣyati \|\| 152 \|\|*

152\. Repeatedly invoking Fire, the preceptor, the best Brāhmaṇa asked him: “Favour me, tell me who her husband will be.”

## \|\| 2.17.153 \|\|

*anyo'syāḥ sadṛśaḥ ko'pi vaṃśe nāsti karomi kim \|*  
*vahnikuṇḍātsamutthāya proktavānhavyavāhanaḥ \|\| 153 \|\|*

153\. “There is none other in the family who is worthy of her; what shall I do?” Fire, rising from the pool of fire, said:

## \|\| 2.17.154-155 \|\|

*śṛṇu me vacanaṃ vipra yo'syā bhartā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*priyavratānvayabhavo mahābalaparākramaḥ \|\| 154 \|\|*

*putro vikramaśīlasya kāliṃdījaṭharodbhavaḥ \|*  
*durdamo nāma bhavitā bhartā hyasyā mahīpatiḥ \|\| 155 \|\|*

154-155. “O Brāhmaṇa, listen to my words as to who will be her husband. Born in the family of Priyavrata (‘one to whom vows are dear’), very strong and brave, the son of Vikrama, born from the womb of Kālindī, King Durdama will be her husband.”

## \|\| 2.17.156 \|\|

*atrāṃtare samāyāto durdamaḥ sa mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*girau mṛgavadhākāṃkṣī muniṃ gehe na paśyati \|*  
*priye'yi tātaḥ kva gata ehi satyaṃ bravīhi me \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. In the meantime arrived that great King Durdama, on the mountain; he desired to kill a deer, he did not see the sage in the house. “O beloved, where has my father gone? Come on, tell me the truth.”

## \|\| 2.17.157 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*agniśālāsthitenaiva tacchrutaṃ vacanaṃ priyam \|*  
*priyetyāmantraṇaṃ ko'yaṃ karoti mama veśmani \|\| 157 \|\|*

Nārada said:

157\. He remaining in the fire-chamber only heard the dear words. ‘In my house who is addressing as ‘dear one’?’

## \|\| 2.17.158-160 \|\|

*sa dadarśa mahātmānaṃ rājānaṃ durdamaṃ muniḥ \|*  
*jaharṣa durdamaṃ dṛṣṭvā muniḥ prāha sa gautamam \|\| 158 \|\|*

*śiṣyaṃ vinayasampannamarghyaṃ pādyaṃ samānaya \|*  
*ekaṃ tāvadayaṃ bhūpaścirakālādupāgataḥ \|\| 159 \|\|*

*jāmātā sāṃprataṃ rājā yogyāsya ca sutā mama \|*  
*tataḥ sa ciṃtayāmāsa rājā jāmātṛ kāraṇam \|\| 160 \|\|*

158-160. The sage saw the magnanimous King Durdama. The sage was delighted to see Durdama, and said to Gautama, his modest disciple, to bring water to wash the feet with. ‘(First thing) is: this King, this my son-in-law, has come after a long time. My daughter is worthy of him.’ Then the King thought about (the arrival of) the son-in-law.

## \|\| 2.17.161-162 \|\|

*maunena vidhinā rājā jagṛhe'rghyaṃ dvijājñayā \|*  
*tamāsanagataṃ vipro gṛhītārghyaṃ mahāmuniḥ \|\| 161 \|\|*

*prastutaṃ prāha rājendraṃ nṛpate kuśalaṃ pure \|*  
*kośe bale ca mitre ca bhṛtyāmātya prajāsu ca \|*  
*tathātmani mahābāho yatra sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 162 \|\|*

161-162. By the order of the Brāhmaṇa, the King silently accepted the respectful offering. The Brāhmaṇa, the great sage, spoke to the best King, who was praised: “O King, is there happiness in the city, treasure, army, friend, servants, ministers and subjects; so also are you, in whom everything is settled, happy?

## \|\| 2.17.163 \|\|

*patnī ca te kuśalinī yā'tra sthāne hi tiṣṭhati \|*  
*anyāsāṃ kuśalaṃ brūhi yāḥ saṃti tava maṃdire \|\| 163 \|\|*

163\. “Is your wife, who stays at this place, all right? Tell me also about the happiness of others who stay in your residence.”

## \|\| 2.17.164 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*tvatprasādādakuśalaṃ nāsti rājye kvacinmama \|*  
*jātakautūhalo'smyasmi mama bhāryā'tra kā mune \|\| 164 \|\|*

The King said:

164\. Through your favour there is absolutely no unhappiness in my kingdom. O sage, I have a curiosity: Who is my wife here?

## \|\| 2.17.165 \|\|

*pramuca uvāca \|*  
*revatī te varā bhāryā kiṃ na vetsi nṛpottama \|*  
*trailokyasundarī yā tu kathaṃ sā vismṛtā tava \|\| 165 \|\|*

Pramuñca said:

165\. Your excellent wife is Revatī. Do you not recognize her? How have you forgotten her who is the most beautiful in the three worlds?

## \|\| 2.17.166-167 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*subhadrāṃ śāṃtapāpāṃ ca kāverītanayāṃ tathā \|*  
*sūrātmajānujātāṃ ca kadaṃbāṃ ca varaprajām \|\| 166 \|\|*

*vipāṭhāṃ naṃdinīṃ caiva vedmi bhāryāṃ gṛhe mama \|*  
*tiṣṭhanti naiva jānāmi bhāryā me revatī kutaḥ \|\| 167 \|\|*

The King said:

166-167. I recognize Subhadrā, Śāntapāpā, so also Kāverī’s daughter, Kadambā the younger sister of Sūra’s son, who (i.e. Kadamabā) has excellent progeny. (But) I do not at all know where my wife Revatī is.

## \|\| 2.17.168 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca \|*  
*priyeti sāṃprataṃ proktā revatī sā priyā tava \|*  
*tadanyathā na bhavitā vacanaṃ nṛpasattama \|\| 168 \|\|*

The sage said:

168\. The one referred to as ‘dear one’ now, is Revatī, your beloved. O best King, therefore the statement will not be otherwise (i.e. untrue)”.

## \|\| 2.17.169 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*nāsti bhāvakṛto doṣaḥ kṣamyatāṃ tadvaco mama \|*  
*vinirgataṃ vacovaktrānnāhaṃ jāne dvijottama \|\| 169 \|\|*

The King said:

169\. There is no fault in the purpose. Pardon me for my words. They went (slipped) out of my mouth. I do not know (how), O best Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 2.17.170 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca \|*  
*nāsti bhāvakṛto doṣaḥ parivedmi kuruṣva tat \|*  
*vahninā kathitastvaṃ me jāmātādya bhaviṣyasi \|\| 170 \|\|*

The sage said:

170\. I know that there is no fault in the purpose. Do that. Fire told (me) that today you will be my son-in-law.

## \|\| 2.17.171 \|\|

*ityādivacanai rājā bhāryā mene sa revatīm \|*  
*ṛṣistathodyataḥ kartuṃ vivāhaṃ vidhi pūrvakam \|*  
*uvāca kanyā pitaraṃ kiñcinme śrūyatāṃ pitaḥ \|\| 171 \|\|*

171\. Hearing these words the king looked upon Revatī as his wife. The sage also became ready to celebrate the marriage according to the rites. The daughter said to the father: “O father, listen to what I say.

## \|\| 2.17.172 \|\|

*yadi me patinā tāta vivāhaṃ kartumicchasi \|*  
*revatyṛkṣaṃ vivāhaṃ me tatkarotu prasādataḥ \|\| 172 \|\|*

172\. “If, O father, you desire to marry me to (the future) husband of mine, then let the Revatī constellation do me favour and bring about that marriage.”

## \|\| 2.17.173 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca \|*  
*revatyṛkṣaśca na vai bhadre candrayoge divi sthitam \|*  
*ṛkṣāṇyanyānyapi saṃti subhrūrvaivāhakāni ca \|\| 173 \|\|*

The sage said:

173\. When there occurs the auspicious conjunction of the Moon, O good one, the Revatī constellations does not remain in the sky. There are also other constellations, O you of fine eyebrows, that are favourable for marriage.

## \|\| 2.17.174 \|\|

*kanyovāca \|*  
*tāta tena vinā kālo vikalaḥ pratibhāti me \|*  
*vivāho vikale tāta madvidhāyāḥ kathaṃ bhavet \|\| 174 \|\|*

The daughter said:

174\. I think without him the time is defective. How would the marriage of someone like me take place at a defective time?

## \|\| 2.17.175-176 \|\|

*pramuñca uvāca \|*  
*ṛtavāgiti vikhyātastapasvī revatīṃ prati \|*  
*cakāra kopaṃ kruddhena tenarkṣaṃ tannipātitam \|\| 175 \|\|*

*mayā cāsmai pratijñātā bhāryeti viditaṃ tava \|*  
*na cecchasi vivāhaṃ tvaṃ saṃkaṭaṃ naḥ samāgatam \|\| 176 \|\|*

Pramuñca said:

175-176. A well-known ascetic Ṛtavāk became angry with Revatī. The angry one felled down the constellation. I have promised him a wife - you know it. If you do not desire the marriage, then calamity has approached us.

## \|\| 2.17.177 \|\|

*kanyovāca \|*  
*ṛtavāgeva sa muniḥ kimetattaptavānsvayam \|*  
*na tvayā mama tātena brahmabandhoḥ sutā'smi kim \|\| 177 \|\|*

The daughter said:

177\. Why did that sage Ṛtavāk himself heat this (constellation)? I have nothing to do as my father. Am I the daughter of a nominal Brāhmaṇa?

## \|\| 2.17.178 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca \|*  
*brahmabandhoḥ sutā na tvaṃ tapasvī nāsti me'dhikaḥ \|*  
*sutā tvaṃ ca mayā deyā nānyatkartuṃ samutsahe \|\| 178 \|\|*

The sage said:

178\. You are not the daughter of a nominal Brāhmaṇa. There is no greater ascetic than I. You are my daughter; you are to be given (in marriage). I do not dare to do anything else.

## \|\| 2.17.179 \|\|

*kanyovāca \|*  
*tapasvī yadi me tātastatkimṛkṣamidaṃ divi \|*  
*samāropya vivāho me kasmānna kriyate punaḥ \|\| 179 \|\|*

The daughter said:

179\. If my father is an ascetic, then why by planting the constellation again in the sky my marriage is not celebrated?

## \|\| 2.17.180 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca \|\|*  
*evaṃ bhavatu bhadraṃ te bhadre prītimatī bhava \|*  
*āropayāmīndumārge revatyṛkṣaṃ kṛte tava \|\| 180 \|\|*

The sage said:

180\. Let it be so. Welfare to you, O good one, be affectionate. For you I shall plant the Revatī constellation on the lunar track.

## \|\| 2.17.181 \|\|

*tatastapaḥprabhāvena revatyṛkṣaṃ mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*yathā pūrvaṃ tathā cakre somayogi dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*vivāhaṃ duhituḥ kṛtvā jāmātaramuvāca ha \|\| 181 \|\|*

181\. Then, by the power of his penance the great sage, the best Brāhmaṇa, put the Revatī constellation, as it was before, with the Moon. Having accomplished the marriage of his daughter he said to his son-in-law:

## \|\| 2.17.182 \|\|

*audvāhikaṃ te bhūpāla kathyatāṃ kiṃ dadāmyaham \|*  
*duṣprāpamapi dāsyāmi vidyate me mahattapaḥ \|\| 182 \|\|*

182\. “O King, tell me what I should give as dowry. I shall give it even though difficult to obtain (since) I have great penance (to my credit).”

## \|\| 2.17.183 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*manoḥ svāyaṃbhuvasyāhamutpannaḥ saṃtatau mune \|*  
*manvaṃtarādhipaṃ putraṃ tvatprasādādvṛṇomyaham \|\| 183 \|\|*

The King said:

183\. O sage, I am born in the family of Svāyambhuya Manu. Through your grace I solicit a son who is the chief of the Age of Manu.

## \|\| 2.17.184 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca \|*  
*bhaviṣyati mahīpālo mahābalaparākramaḥ \|*  
*revatī revatīkuṇḍe snātvā putraṃ janiṣyati \|\| 184 \|\|*

The sage said:

184\. There will be a king of great strength and valour. Revatī, bathing in the pool Revatī, will give birth to a son.

## \|\| 2.17.185 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛtvā gato rājā sā ca putramajījanat \|*  
*raivateti kṛtaṃ nāma babhūva sa manurnṛpaḥ \|\| 185 \|\|*

185\. Having done so, the king left, and she gave birth to a son. He was named Raivata; he became a king, Manu.

## \|\| 2.17.186 \|\|

*amunā ca tadā proktamasminraivatake girau \|*  
*striyaḥ snānaṃ kariṣyaṃti tāsāṃ putrā mahābalāḥ \|*  
*dīrghāyuṣo bhaviṣyaṃti duḥkhadāridryavarjitāḥ \|\| 186 \|\|*

186\. At that time he proclaimed on the Raivataka mountain: “The sons of those women who bathe on this Raivataka mountain, will be very powerful, will live long and will be free from grief and poverty.”

## \|\| 2.17.187 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*ityukte parvato rājandīrgho bhūtvā papāta saḥ \|*  
*etau tau saṃsmṛtau devau sabhāryau hariśaṃkarau \|\| 187 \|\|*

Nārada said:

187\. When this was said, the mountain became long and fell down. The two gods Hari and Śaṅkara were remembered along with their wives.

## \|\| 2.17.188 \|\|

*smṛtamātrau tadā'yātau tena baddhau purā yataḥ \|*  
*yatrāhaṃ tatra sthātavyaṃ bhavadbhyāmiti niścitam \|\| 188 \|\|*

188\. The moment they were remembered, they arrived, since they were formerly tied by him. ‘It is decided that you will stay where I am’

## \|\| 2.17.189 \|\|

*ato viṣṇuharau devau sthitau tau parvatottame \|*  
*girau raivatake ramye svarṇarekhānadījale \|*  
*ārādhayaddhariṃ devaṃ revatī tāṃ ca sobravīt \|\| 189 \|\|*

189\. Therefore the (two) gods Viṣṇu and Hara stayed on that best mountain - charming mountain Raivataka, in the water of the river Svarṇarekhā. Revatī propitiated God Hari. He said to her.

## \|\| 2.17.190 \|\|

*bhavatāccaṃdrayogaste gagane brāhmaṇājñayā \|*  
*anyadvṛṇīṣva tuṣṭo'haṃ varaṃ manasi yatsthitam \|\| 190 \|\|*

190\. “By the order of the Brāhmaṇa, you will have conjunction with the Moon in the sky. I am pleased. Ask for something else - a boon cherished in your mind.”

## \|\| 2.17.191-192 \|\|

*revatyuvāca \|*  
*girau raivatake deva sthātavyaṃ bhavatā sadā \|*  
*mayā snānaṃ kṛtaṃ yatra tatra snāsyaṃti ye janāḥ \|\| 191 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ viṣṇupure vāso bhavatviti vṛtaṃ mayā \|*  
*evamastu tadā procya girau raivatake sthitaḥ \|*  
*dāmodaraścaturbāhuḥ svayaṃ rudropi saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 192 \|\|*

Revatī said:

191-192. O God, you should always stay on the Raivataka mountain. The people who bathe where I bathed, would dwell in Viṣṇu’s city.

The four-armed Dāmodara, saying “Let it be so”, remained on the Raivataka mountain. Rudra himself also stayed there.

## \|\| 2.17.193-194 \|\|

*gaṃgādyāḥ saritaḥ sarvāḥ saṃsthitā viṣṇunā saha \|*  
*kṣīrode mathyamāne tu yadā vṛkṣaḥ samutthitaḥ \|\| 193 \|\|*

*āmardde devadaityānāṃ tena sāmardakī smṛtā \|*  
*asminvṛkṣe sthitā lakṣmīḥ sadā pitṛgṛhe nṛpa \|\| 194 \|\|*

193-194. All rivers like Gaṅgā remained with Viṣṇu. When the tree came up when the Milky Ocean was being churned, it was called Āmardakī since it came up at the time of conflict between the gods and demons. O King, on this tree, Lakṣmī always stayed in her father’s house.

## \|\| 2.17.195 \|\|

*śivālakṣmīḥ smṛto vṛkṣaḥ sevyate surasattamaiḥ \|*  
*devairbrahmādibhiḥ sarvairvṛkṣo'sau vaiṣṇavaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 195 \|\|*

195\. The tree is called ‘Śivalakṣmī’ and is resorted to by best gods; by gods like Brahmā and others, it is said to belong to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.17.196-197 \|\|

*sarvaiḥ saṃciṃtya mukto'sau girau raivatake purā \|*  
*asya vṛkṣasya yātrāṃ ye kariṣyaṃti harerdine \|\| 196 \|\|*

*phālgune ca site pakṣa ekādaśyāṃ nṛpottama \|*  
*teṣāṃ putrāśca pautrāśca bhaviṣyaṃti guṇādhikāḥ \|*  
*prāṃte viṣṇupure vāso jāyatenātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 197 \|\|*

196-197. All, thinking together, formerly left this tree on the Raivataka (mountain). The sons and grandsons of those who go on a pilgrimage of this tree, on Viṣṇu’s day, so also in the bright half of Phālguna on the Ekādaśī day, O best king, become very meritorious. Abode in Viṣṇu’s city is secured by them (i.e. the pilgrims).

## \|\| 2.17.198 \|\|

*baliruvāca \|*  
*kathametadvrataṃ kāryaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ viṣṇuvallabham \|*  
*rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kāryaṃ vidhinā kena tadvada \|\| 198 \|\|*

Bali said:

198\. How is this vow of Viṣṇu, dear to him, to be observed? Tell me in what way keeping awake at night it is to be carried out?

## \|\| 2.17.199-200 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*phālgunasya site pakṣa ekādaśyāmupoṣitaḥ \|*  
*snātvā nadyāṃ taḍāge vā vāpyāṃ kūpe gṛhe'pi vā \|\| 199 \|\|*

*gatvā girau vane vā'pi yatra sā prāpyate śivā \|*  
*pūjyā puṣpaiḥ śubhai rātrau kāryaṃ jāgaraṇaṃ naraiḥ \|\| 200 \|\|*

Nārada said:

199-200. In the bright half of Phālguna, on the eleventh day, having observed a fast, one should bathe in a river, in a lake or a well or even at home, and then having gone up a mountain or in a forest, or where Śiva can be reached, one should worship her with auspicious flowers; men should keep awake at night.

## \|\| 2.17.201 \|\|

*aṣṭādhikaśataiḥ kāryā phalaistasyāḥ pradakṣiṇā \|*  
*pradakṣiṇīkṛtya nagaṃ bhoktavyaṃ tu phalaṃ naraiḥ \|\| 201 \|\|*

201\. One should go round (the deity) a hundred and eight times. Men should go round the mountain, and (then) eat a fruit.

## \|\| 2.17.202 \|\|

*karakaṃ jalapūrṇaṃ tu karttavyaṃ pātrasaṃyutam \|*  
*haviṣyānnaṃ tu karttavyaṃ dīpaḥ kāryo vidhānataḥ \|\| 202 \|\|*

202\. They should fill a water-pot with water, and keep it along with a plate. They should prepare food to be eaten during days of fast, and should light a lamp according to the rule.

## \|\| 2.17.203 \|\|

*evaṃ jāgaraṇaṃ kāryaṃ kathāśravaṇatatparaiḥ \|*  
*mucyaṃte dehinaḥ pāpaiḥ kalijaiḥ kāyasaṃbhavaiḥ \|\| 203 \|\|*

203\. They should thus keep awake while taking delight in listening to a tale. They are freed from the sins of body incurred in the Kali (age).

## \|\| 2.17.204 \|\|

*dehāṃte te narāḥ sarve pūjyaṃte harimaṃdire \|\| 204 \|\|*

204\. All those (i.e. such) men are respected in Hari’s abode at the fall of their bodies.

## \|\| 2.17.205 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā nārado daityaṃ yayau raivatakaṃ girim \|*  
*daityendro maṃtrayāmāsa kiṃkāryaṃ sāṃprataṃ mayā \|\| 205 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

205\. Speaking like this to the demon, Nārada went to the Raivataka mountain. The King of demons pondered over: “What should be done by me now? O best gods, I do not like a war with the gods.”

## \|\| 2.17.206-207 \|\|

*na rocate suraiḥ sārddhaṃ vigraho me surottamāḥ \|\| 206 \|\|*

*maṃtriṇa ūcuḥ \|*  
*nāsti kṣamā bhṛśaṃ teṣāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ gṛhe satām \|*  
*aśaktamapi maṃsyaṃte svayamāyāṃti te yataḥ \|*  
*tasmātsvayaṃ prayāsyāmo devendraṃ sahitā vayam \|\| 207 \|\|*

The ministers said:

206-207. The Kṣatriyas, who remain at home do not much deserve pardon. They (the enemies) will look upon them as weak, since they will themselves come (to fight). Therefore, along with the Lord of gods, we ourselves, getting together, shall proceed.

## \|\| 2.17.208-209 \|\|

*iti śrutvā dadau ḍhakkāṃ prathamaṃ suravigrahe \|*  
*gṛhītvā vāhinīṃ daityāḥ prasthitā meru parvate \|\| 208 \|\|*

*yatra sā nagarī ramyā devarājasya pūrvataḥ \|*  
*āgacchamānāṃ tāṃ jñātvā vāhinīṃ meruparvate \|\| 209 \|\|*

208-209a. Hearing ths \[this?\], he first beat a large drum for fighting the war of gods. Taking an army the demons proceeded to the Meru mountain, where the city of the Lord of gods was from old times.

209b. Knowing the army (of the demons) coming up the Meru mountain

## \|\| 2.17.210 \|\|

*devarājasamādeśāccalitā deva vāhinī \|*  
*sumeroḥ pūrvadigbhāge yuddhamāsītparasparam \|\| 210 \|\|*

210\. the army of gods started by the order of the King of gods. On the eastern side of the mountain Meru the war between the two (armies) took place.

## \|\| 2.17.211 \|\|

*devasainyaṃ yadā sarvaṃ daityasainyenasaṃyutam \|*  
*mahāpralayasādṛśyaṃ yuddhaṃ vṛttaṃ tadā tayoḥ \|\| 211 \|\|*

211\. When the entire army of gods got mixed with that of the demons, a war between the two appeared like the final deluge.

## \|\| 2.17.212 \|\|

*airāvaṇaṃ samāruhya devarājaḥ samāgataḥ \|*  
*rathamāruhya daityendro yuddhāyānye samāgatāḥ \|\| 212 \|\|*

212\. The Lord of gods arrived after mounting upon Airāvata. The Lord of the demons (arrived) after getting into a chariot. Others also came there to fight.

## \|\| 2.17.213 \|\|

*devā yajñabhujo yasmāttasmānna yuddha kāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*airāvaṇo baliṃ dṛṣṭvā na cacālāgrato mṛdhe \|\| 213 \|\|*

213\. Since gods enjoyed sacrifices, therefore they did not desire war. Seeing Bali, Airāvata did not move on.

## \|\| 2.17.214-215 \|\|

*saṃgrāme vimukho yāti diggajaiḥ pariveṣṭitaḥ \|*  
*adhvare bāhunā yena saṃkalpaṃ kṛtavānbaliḥ \|\| 214 \|\|*

*tena vai sa surānsarvānvārayāmāsa saṃyuge \|*  
*vāritā vimukhā yāṃti devarājaḥ karotu kim \|\| 215 \|\|*

214-215. In the war he, being surrounded by the quarter-elephants, turned away. With that arm, with which he expressed a desire, he warded off all gods. Being (thus) warded off they went turning away their faces. What would the Lord of gods do?

## \|\| 2.17.216 \|\|

*kuliśaṃ na kurute karma bhujamuktaṃ na gacchati \|\| 216 \|\|*

216\. The thunderbolt did not work. Though released from the arm it did not go (to the target).

## \|\| 2.17.217 \|\|

*evaṃ bahūni yuddhāni nivṛttāni tadā tayoḥ \|*  
*na haṃtuṃ śakyaṃte yuddhe devairdaityā mahābalāḥ \|\| 217 \|\|*

217\. Thus many wars took place among them. The very powerful demons could not be killed by the gods, in the war.

## \|\| 2.17.218-219 \|\|

*balākāṃkṣāḥ sthitā devā guruṇā te prabodhitāḥ \|*  
*amarā devatāḥ sarva iti śukreṇa vāritāḥ \|\| 218 \|\|*

*avatāraṃ harerjñātvā pañcamaṃ vāmanaṃ sthitam \|*  
*atihṛṣṭo'marāvatyāṃ rājyaṃ cakre sureśvaraḥ \|\| 219 \|\|*

218-219. The gods desired to be powerful. They were enlightened by Guru. (The demons) were warded off by Śukra, saying, “All gods are immortal.” Knowing that the fifth incarnation of Hari (i.e. Viṣṇu) is Vāmana, the Lord of gods (i.e. Indra) being very much glad, ruled in Amarāvatī.

## \|\| 2.17.220 \|\|

*nanartta yuddhe daityendraḥ svagṛhe yajate surān \|*  
*pātālābhisṛtā daityā rājyaṃ kurvaṃti mānavāḥ \|\| 220 \|\|*

220\. The Lord of demons danced in the war; he reveled them at home. The demons moved to the Nether world; men ruled.

## \|\| 2.17.221 \|\|

*tadā devagaṇāḥ sarve mantrayanti suraiḥ saha \|*  
*daityo lokadvayaṃ śāsti svargaṃ śāsti sureśvaraḥ \|\| 221 \|\|*

221\. Then all groups of gods held consultations with (other) gods. The demon rules the two worlds. The Lord of gods governs the Heaven.

## \|\| 2.17.222 \|\|

*kṣaṃtavyaṃ tāvadevāsya vāmano raivataṃ girim \|*  
*yāvadyāti suraiḥ kāryaṃ maunaṃ daityajitairapi \|\| 222 \|\|*

222\. Let him be pardoned. Till Vāmana goes to the Raivata mountain, the gods, though conquered by demons, should observe silence.

## \|\| 2.17.223 \|\|

*yadāprabhṛti sañjāto vāmano dharaṇītale \|*  
*tadāprabhṛti daityānāṃ dunirmittāni jajñire \|\| 223 \|\|*

223\. Since the time Vāmana was born on the surface of the earth, ill omens for the demons have come up.

## \|\| 2.17.224 \|\|

*śivā praviśya nagare rauti sā visvaraṃ niśi \|*  
*bhramanti nagare kākā divārātraṃ virāviṇaḥ \|\| 224 \|\|*

224\. A female jackal enters the city at night and cries discordantly. Crows, crying aloud, move in the city day and night.

## \|\| 2.17.225 \|\|

*sarppāḥ sarppaṃti geheṣu kṛṣṇā raudrā viṣolbaṇāḥ \|*  
*kaṃkā gṛdhrā bakā bhrāṃtā bhramanti nagaropari \|\| 225 \|\|*

225\. Black, fearful serpents powerful with poison creep in the houses. Over the city fly herons, vultures, cranes, that are confused.

## \|\| 2.17.226 \|\|

*jāyante vimukhā garbhāḥ strīṣu goṣu mṛgīṣu vā \|*  
*ghṛtaṃ dugdhaṃ ca naivāsti tile tailaṃ na vidyate \|\| 226 \|\|*

226\. Foetuses are born with their faces turned away among women, cows or female deer. Neither ghee nor milk exists; there is no oil in the sesamum seed(s).

## \|\| 2.17.227-228 \|\|

*jane jānapado nityaṃ yudhyate ca parasparam \|*  
*kālī karālavadanā dīrghakeśī vilocanā \|\| 227 \|\|*

*ajñātā rudatī yāti nagare sā gṛhaṃ prati \|*  
*ko'yaṃ na jñāyate kasmāttapasvī bhasmaguṃṭhitaḥ \|\| 228 \|\|*

227-228. In the tribe the rustics always fight among themselves. Kālī, of a fearful face, with long hair, of deformed eyes, unknown, and weeping goes to (every) house in the city. It is not known who this ascetic, is, and why she is besmeared with ashes.

## \|\| 2.17.229 \|\|

*yatirmaunavratī nagna puro yāti gṛhegṛhe \|*  
*ḍamarūḍḍāmaruṃ paścāddhuṃkāraṃ vidadhāti ca \|\| 229 \|\|*

229\. In front of, a naked ascetic, observing the vow of silence goes from house to house, and gives out the ‘hum’ sound, formidable like that of a drum.

## \|\| 2.17.230 \|\|

*akāle kupitā meghā jalaṃ muñcaṃti puṣkalam \|*  
*karakaiḥ pūritā garbhā garjaṃti girayo bahu \|\| 230 \|\|*

230\. Clouds, untimely furious, release profuse water. Foetuses appear full of wounds; mountains thunder profusely.

## \|\| 2.17.231-232 \|\|

*samajāyata bhūkaṃpo digdāhaścāpyajāyata \|*  
*militvā śvagaṇaḥ sarvo mukhamuccairvidhāya ca \|\| 231 \|\|*

*rauti rātrau pure nityaṃ ghūkaḥ śabdaṃ viśabdate \|*  
*balirājyakṣayo jāto divi ketūdayo niśi \|\| 232 \|\|*

231-232. Earthquakes came about, and the quarters also burnt. The entire group of dogs gathered, and raising their faces, always barked at night. An owl cried, “The end of Bali’s kingdom has come about” and in the sky Ketu had risen at night.

## \|\| 2.17.233 \|\|

*ādityamaṇḍale vedhaḥ kīlakairdṛśyate kṛtaḥ \|*  
*kabandhasaṃkule vyomni candramā na prakāśate \|\| 233 \|\|*

233\. Piercing into the orb of the sun seemed to be made by wedges. The moon did not shine in the sky full of headless trunks.

## \|\| 2.17.234 \|\|

*sa jāto rohiṇīvedho yo jāto yugavyatyaye \|*  
*nakṣatrāṇi divā lokairgaṇyante guṇavattaraiḥ \|\| 234 \|\|*

234\. That (type of) piercing of Rohiṇī took place which had taken place at the time of the passing over of the Age. Good people counted the constellations by day.

## \|\| 2.17.235 \|\|

*bījānāṃ vyatyayo jajñe bhūmistrīgomṛgīṣu ca \|*  
*aśvā hreṣaṃti sahasā madaṃ kurvaṃti no gajāḥ \|\| 235 \|\|*

235\. Obstacle was produced in case of land, women, cows, female deer. The horses neighed all of a sudden; the elephants were not intoxicated.

## \|\| 2.17.236 \|\|

*mantriṇāṃ maṃtrito mantro bhidyate rājyasaṃkṣaye \|*  
*ghṛtāhutyā huto vahnirjvalati na tadā dvijaiḥ \|\| 236 \|\|*

236\. On the destruction of the kingdom, the policy pondered over by the ministers was violated. The fire to which an offering of ghee was made by Brāhmaṇas, did not bum.

## \|\| 2.17.237 \|\|

*pracaṇḍaḥ pāvano vāti vātyayā ghūrṇitadrumaḥ \|*  
*dhvajā jvalanti caityeṣu nabho bhavati dhūsaram \|\| 237 \|\|*

237\. Powerful wind, that had shaken the trees with storm, blew. Flags burnt at sanctuaries; the sky became greyish.

## \|\| 2.17.238 \|\|

*ete cānye ca bahava utpātā balino gṛhe \|*  
*saṃjātā vāmane jāte nāradāgamanādanu \|\| 238 \|\|*

238\. These and many other portents took place in Bali’s house when Vāmana was born after Nārada’s arrival.

## \|\| 2.17.239-240 \|\|

*anyacca jāyate raudraṃ yaddivā svapnadarśanam \|*  
*saṃnahyaṃte yadā daityāḥ patitā nipataṃti ca \|\| 239 \|\|*

*nimittāni sa sainyasya dṛṣṭvaivaṃ na pravarttate \|*  
*sadā saṃtiṣṭhate gehe rājyaṃ ca kurute baliḥ \|\| 240 \|\|*

239-240. At other place terrific happening like seeing a dream by day took place. When the demons are bound they are fallen and are reduced to misery. Seeing the omens of the army he did not proceed like this Bali always remained at home and reigned.

## \|\| 2.17.241 \|\|

*śarīre na sukhaṃ tasya gātrabhaṃgaḥ śirovyathā \|*  
*jvarito na sukhaṃ śete na bhuṃkte na pibatyasau \|*  
*na bhuktaṃ jīryate lokaḥ sarvopi vyākulīkṛtaḥ \|\| 241 \|\|*

241\. In his body there was no pleasure; there was a breaking of a limb or headache. He was attacked with fever; he did not sleep happily; he did not drink (drinks). People did not digest what was eaten by them. All were troubled.

## \|\| 2.17.242 \|\|

*viparītaṃ jagaddṛṣṭvā balirvyākulamānasaḥ \|*  
*mantrayāmāsa kimidaṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ saha duḥkhitaḥ \|\| 242 \|\|*

242\. Seeing the world inverted, Bali, with his mind perplexed, and being grieved, consulted Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 2.17.243 \|\|

*śukraṃ guruṃ samānīya sabhāyāṃ saṃniveśya ca \|*  
*papraccha kuśalaṃ daityo bhaktyā paramayā yutaḥ \|*  
*viparītamidaṃ sarvaṃ varttate tadvadasva me \|\| 243 \|\|*

243\. The demon (i.e. Bali) having brought Śukra, his preceptor, and having made him sit in the court, and full of great devotion asked him about his well-being: “All this is topsy turvy; so tell me (what should be done).

## \|\| 2.17.244 \|\|

*nāradena yaduktaṃ me guro satyaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*utpātaśāṃtikaṃ brūhi brāhmaṇaiḥ sahito mama \|\| 244 \|\|*

244\. “O Preceptor, all this appears topsy turvy, as told by Nārada. So please tell me if what Nārada told me will come true. Along with the Brāhmaṇas tell me about the observances to remove the effects of a portent.”

## \|\| 2.17.245 \|\|

*śukra uvāca \|*  
*utpātaśāṃtaye kāryo yajñaḥ sarvasvadakṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇaiḥ kṣatriyaiḥ sārddhaṃ dvādaśābdo vidhīyatām \|\| 245 \|\|*

Śukra said:

245\. For cessation of (the evil effects of) the portent perform a sacrifice where the whole of your possession is to be given as a present to a Brāhmaṇa. Perform a sacrifice lasting for twelve years along with the Brāhmaṇas and Kṣatriyas.

## \|\| 2.17.246 \|\|

*ṛṣayo brāhmaṇā ye ca munayo brahmacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*āgacchantu mahāyajñe ye ca dūre'pi saṃsthitāḥ \|\| 246 \|\|*

246\. Brāhmaṇas, so also the sages, the celibates, so also those who stay far away should come for the great sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.17.247 \|\|

*nagarātpūrvadigbhāge karttavyo yajñamaṇḍapaḥ \|*  
*yasya yasyābhirucitaṃ deyaṃ dānaṃ tvayā nṛpa \|*  
*tathā kariṣya ityuktvā yajñārthaṃ tatparobhavat \|\| 247 \|\|*

247\. A pavilion for the sacrifice should be put up in the eastern direction of the city. O King, give gifts according to the liking of those (who ask for them). Saying, “I shall do so”, he became ready for the sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.17.248 \|\|

*ānāyya brāhmaṇānsarvānkuśalānyajñakarmaṇi \|*  
*gṛhītā yajñadīkṣā tairyajñe vai sarva dakṣiṇe \|\| 248 \|\|*

248\. He brought all Brāhmaṇas skilled in performing a sacrifice; he made them to get initiated into the sacrifice where everything was given as a gift.

## \|\| 2.17.249 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāya mayā deyaṃ sarvasvamiha yācite \|*  
*śarīraputramitrāṇi dārāndāsyāmi yācitaḥ \|\| 249 \|\|*

249\. “Here (i.e. in this sacrifice), I, when solicited, shall give everything to a Brāhmaṇa. When solicited, I shall give my body, sons, friends, wife.

## \|\| 2.17.250 \|\|

*dātavyaṃ satataṃ dānaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo mayādhvare \|*  
*vāritenāpi na stheyaṃ dātavyaṃ niścitaṃ mayā \|*  
*yācitaścenna dāsyāmi tadā vyartho mamā'dhvaraḥ \|\| 250 \|\|*

250\. “I have decided that in the sacrifice I should constantly give gifts to Brāhmaṇas; I would not cease (giving gifts) even though warded off. If I shall not give (gifts) even though I am solicited, then my sacrifice is futile.

## \|\| 2.17.251 \|\|

*vidhāya maṇḍapaṃ divyaṃ bahuyojanavistaram \|*  
*tatra dānāni dīyante bhojanācchādanāni ca \|\| 251 \|\|*

251\. “Putting up a divine pavilion, extending over many yojanas, gifts, meals and coverings will be given away.”

## \|\| 2.17.252 \|\|

*saptarṣayaḥ samāyātā gaganāddharaṇītale \|*  
*digbhyaḥ samāgatāḥ sarve brāhmaṇāḥ saṃti ye bhuvi \|\| 252 \|\|*

252\. From the sky the Seven Sages came (down) to the surface of the earth. All the Brāhmaṇas that live on the earth have come from (various) directions.

## \|\| 2.17.253 \|\|

*kṣatriyāśca samāyātā vigṛhya vividhaṃ vasu \|*  
*nivedayanti te rājñe prārabdhe yajñakarmaṇi \|\| 253 \|\|*

253\. Taking with them various kinds of wealth Kṣatriyas have arrived; they announced themselves when the sacrifice was begun.

## \|\| 2.17.254-255 \|\|

*āsamudrātsamāyātā naṭanarttakayācakāḥ \|*  
*gītavāditranirghoṣo vedadhvanivimiśritaḥ \|\| 254 \|\|*

*trailokyaṃ badhirīcakre dehidehīti yācitam \|*  
*mā dehīti vaco nāsti stokaṃ dehīti caiva na \|\| 255 \|\|*

254-255. Actors, dancers and suppliants have come (even) from the sea. The loud noise of songs and musical instruments, mixed with the sound of (the recitation of) the Vedas, deafened the three worlds. There were no words like “Do not give”, or “Give a little”.

## \|\| 2.17.256 \|\|

*yadyadyo yācate vastu tattasmai tatra dīyate \|*  
*brāhmaṇo hi na so'pyasti yo hi taṃ bahu yācate \|\| 256 \|\|*

256\. He, who asked for whatever object, was given that. There was also no Brāhmaṇa who asked for much.

## \|\| 2.17.257-258 \|\|

*bhojanācchādanārthaṃ ca na gṛhṇaṃti dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*suvarṇaratnaraupyāṇi tathāśvarathakuṃjarān \|\| 257 \|\|*

*gṛhagobhūmigrāmāṃśca na gṛhṇaṃti dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*balirājyena saṃtuṣṭāḥ kiṃ kurvati dhanena te \|\| 258 \|\|*

257-258. Brāhmaṇas did not ask for food and coverings, gold, jewels or silver (objects), so also horses and elephants. They did not accept houses, cows, land, villages. Satisfied with Bali’s kingdom what would they do with wealth?

## \|\| 2.17.259 \|\|

*evaṃ pravartate yajño mahānsarvasvadakṣiṇaḥ \|\| 259 \|\|*

259\. Thus proceeded the great sacrifice where everything was given as a gift.

## \|\| 2.17.260 \|\|

*nṛtyaṃti gāyaṃti paṭhaṃti cānye stuvaṃti yajñaṃ bahudānayuktam \|*  
*brahmendra rudragrahasūryacaṃdrāḥ prasāditā āhutibhiśca mantraiḥ \|\| 260 \|\|*

260\. They danced, sang, recited (hymns); others praised the sacrifice in which large gifts were given. Brahmā, Indra, Rudra, the Planets, the Sun, the Moon, were propitiated with offerings and sacred hymns.

## \|\| 2.17.261 \|\|

*baliṃ praśaṃsaṃti guruṃ tathānye hotārameke parivārameke \|*  
*prajāpaternāpi surādhipasya samāpyate cedatha yāsyati dhuvam \|*  
*pradāya rājyaṃ dvijapuṃgavebhyaḥ saputramitraiḥ sahito rasātalam \|\| 261 \|\|*

261\. Some glorified Bali; some the preceptor; some the sacrificial priest reciting the hymns from the Ṛgveda at the sacrifice; some praised the attendants. Not only of Brahmā or of Indra (?obscure) if such a sacrifice is performed he will go to Dhruva. Having given his kingdom to best Brāhmaṇas he will certainly go to the Nether world.

## \|\| 2.17.262 \|\|

*itīti vācaḥ pravadaṃti vāḍavāḥ śṛṇvaṃti daityāḥ kimidaṃ vadaṃti \|*  
*baleḥ puraḥsthāḥ kathayaṃti saṃgatā baliḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ pradadāti yācitam \|\| 262 \|\|*

262\. The submarine fires uttered such words, the demons heard them, and said: “What is this?” Together they, getting in front of Bali, tell it (to him). Bali, being pleased, gave them what they asked for.

## Chapter 18 - Subjugation of Bali

## \|\| 2.18.1 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*vastrāpathe mahākṣetre samprāpto vāmano yadā \|*  
*tadāprabhṛti kiṃ cakre tanme vistarato vada \|\| 1 \|\|*

The King said:

1\. Tell me in detail what Vāmana did after he reached the great holy place Vastrāpatha.

## \|\| 2.18.2 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*vāmano vasatiṃ cakre bhavasyāgre nṛpottama \|*  
*svarṇarekhājale snātvā bhavaṃ sampūjya bhāvataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

2\. O best King, having bathed in the water of Svarṇarekhā, and having devoutly and properly worshipped Bhava, Vāmana took his abode in front of Bhava.

## \|\| 2.18.3 \|\|

*ekāṃte nirmale sthāne kaṇṭakāsthivivarjite \|*  
*kṛṣṇājinaparicchanna upaviṣṭo varā sane \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He sat on an excellent seat in a lonely, spotless place, free from thorns and bones, and covered with hide of black antelope.

## \|\| 2.18.4 \|\|

*kṛtvā padmāsanaṃ dhīro niścalo'bhūddvijottamaḥ \|*  
*vidhāya kandharābaṃdhamṛjunāsāvalokakaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The strong-minded and steady, best Brāhmaṇa, taking to the Padmāsana position, and making his neck firm, and looking at his straight nose, remained steady.

## \|\| 2.18.5 \|\|

*gṛhakṣetrakalatrāṇāṃ ciṃtāṃ muktvā dhanasya ca \|*  
*māyāṃ ca vaiṣṇavīṃ tyaktvā kṛtamauno jitendriyaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He gave up the anxiety about his house, place, wife and wealth, also the trickery resorted to by Vīṣṇu, took to silence, and controlled his senses.

## \|\| 2.18.6 \|\|

*nirāhāro jitakrodho muktasaṃsārabaṃdhanaḥ \|*  
*bhujau padmāsane kṛtvā kiñcinmīlitalo canaḥ \|*  
*manoticaṃcalaṃ jñātvā sthiraṃ cakre hṛdi dvijaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He did not take food; controlled his anger; gave up the bonds of the worldly existence. Holdng \[Holding?\] his arms in the Padmāsana posture, having closed his eyes a little, the Brāhmaṇa knowing the mind to be very fickle, made it steady in the heart.

## \|\| 2.18.7 \|\|

*krameṇābhyāsayogena bhinnāṃścakre sa caikataḥ \|*  
*prāṇāpānavyānodānasamānākhyāṃśca mārutān \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In due order, due to practice he made separate and united the winds called Prāṇa (the first of the five life-winds). Apāna (the life-wind in the body which goes downwards and out of the anus), Vyāna (the vital air that is diffused through the whole body), Udāna (the vital air rising up the throat and entering the head), Samāna (the vital air having its seat in the cavity of the navel and essential to digestion).

## \|\| 2.18.8 \|\|

*evaṃ taṃ hṛdaye kṛtvā gṛhītvā sarvasandhiṣu \|*  
*ānīya brahmaṇaḥ sthāne dṛḍhaṃ brahmaṇyayojayat \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thus having it (i.e. mind) fixed in the heart, and collecting it in all joints, and bringing it in the seat of Brahman, he united it with Brahman.

## \|\| 2.18.9 \|\|

*gṛhītvā pavanaṃ bāhyaṃ yadā pūra yate tanum \|*  
*tadā sa pūrako jñeyo recakaṃ tu vadāmyaham \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. When the external wind is taken in and the body is filled with it, it is known as Pūraka. I shall explain Recaka.

## \|\| 2.18.10 \|\|

*yadā cābhyantaro vāyurbāhye yāti kramānnṛpa \|*  
*tadā sa recako jñeyaḥ stambhanātkumbhako bhavet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O King, when the internal wind goes out in due order it is known as Recaka. When it is suspended it would be Kumbhaka.

## \|\| 2.18.11 \|\|

*pañcaviṃśatitattvāni yadā jānaṃti yoginaḥ \|*  
*mucyante pātakaiḥ sarvaiḥ saptajanmakṛtairapi \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. When the followers of Yoga know the twenty-five principles, they are freed from all sins even committed during seven births.

## \|\| 2.18.12 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*kāni tattvāni ko dehī kiṃ jñeyaṃ yogināṃ vada \|*  
*utpannajñānasadbhāvo yogayuktaḥ kathaṃ bhavet \|\| 12 \|\|*

The King said:

12\. What are the principles? What is the soul? Which is to be known by the followers of Yoga? (Please) tell (me). How would one, in whom knowledge has risen, be endowed with Yoga?

## \|\| 2.18.13 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*prakṛtiśca tato buddhirahaṃkārastato'bhavat \|*  
*tanmātrapaṃcakaṃ tasmādeṣā prakṛtiraṣṭadhā \|\| 13 \|\|*

The Lord said:

13\. Prakṛti (the original source of the material world), then Buddhi (intellect), then Ahaṃkāra (ego sense) that originated from it, the five Tanmātras (i.e. the group of the five subtle and primary elements—this is the eightfold Prakṛti.

## \|\| 2.18.14 \|\|

*buddhīndriyāṇi pañcaiva pañca karmeṃdriyāṇi ca \|*  
*ekādaśaṃ mano viddhi mahā bhūtāni paṃca ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Just five organs of perception, and five organs of action (came up). Know the eleventh to be the Manas (mind), and five great elements.

## \|\| 2.18.15 \|\|

*gaṇaḥ ṣoḍaśakaḥ sāṃkhye vistareṇa prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*caturviṃśatitattvāni puruṣaḥ paṃcaviṃśakaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In the Sāmkhya (system of Philosophy) the group of the sixteen is told in detail. These are the twenty-four principles, and the Puruṣa (the soul) is the twenty-fifth.

## \|\| 2.18.16 \|\|

*dehīti procyate dehe sa cātmānaṃ ca paśyati \|*  
*viṃdanti paramātmānaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ taṃ viṃśateḥ param \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He is called ‘Dehi’ (the soul) in the body, and it perceives the supreme soul. They recognize the highest soul as sixth beyond twenty.

## \|\| 2.18.17-18 \|\|

*āsanādiprakārā ye te jñeyāḥ prathamaṃ sadā \|*  
*yadā dīpaśikhāprāyaṃ jyotiḥ paśyaṃti te hṛdi \|\| 17 \|\|*

*utpannajñānasadbhāvā bhaṇyāste yogino budhaiḥ \|*  
*pūrvaṃ jarāṃ jarayati rogā naśyati dūrataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. The kinds of posture etc., that are what should be always known first. Those who see in their hearts a light resembling the flame of a lamp should be called ‘yogins’ in whom knowledge has risen, by the wise. First old age wears out and the diseases perish far away.

## \|\| 2.18.19 \|\|

*sarvapāpacaye kṣīṇe paścānmṛtyuṃ sa viṃdati \|*  
*mṛto loke naro nāsti yogī jānāti cetsvayam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He, when all his sins have weakened, then obtains death. If the yogin knows himself then there exists (i.e. is born) no dead person in the world.

## \|\| 2.18.20 \|\|

*tadā dvārāṇi saṃruddhya daśa prāṇānsa muñcati \|*  
*puṇya pāpakṣayaṃ kṛtvā prāṇā gacchaṃti yoginām \|*  
*aṇimādiguṇaiśvaryaṃ prāpnuvaṃti śivālaye \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then having restrained the doors (i.e. outlets) he releases the ten breaths. The life of yogins passes away after having destroyed the sins. They obtain such wealth of the (supernormal) qualities like being minute etc. in Śiva’s abode.

## \|\| 2.18.21 \|\|

*anena dhyānayogena bhavaṃ paśyati mānavaḥ \|*  
*manasā ciṃtitaṃ sarvaṃ samprāptaṃ bhavadarśanāt \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. With (the help of) this path of meditation a man sees Bhava. Everything thought of by mind is secured by seeing Bhava.

## \|\| 2.18.22 \|\|

*evamāste yadā vipro vāmano bhavasannidhau \|*  
*gaganādavatīrṇaṃ taṃ tadā paśyati nāradam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. When the Brāhmaṇa Vāmana was thus near Bhava, he saw Nārada, descended from the sky.

## \|\| 2.18.23 \|\|

*vāmana uvāca \|*  
*maharṣe kuśalaṃ te'dya kasmādāgamyate tvayā \|*  
*praṇamāmi maharṣe tvāṃ brahmaiva tvaṃ jagattraye \|\| 23 \|\|*

Vāmana said:

23\. O great sage, are you alright? What brings you here? O great sage, I salute you; in the three worlds you are just Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 2.18.24 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*svarga lokādahaṃ prāptaḥ kuśalaṃ kiṃ bravīmi te \|\| 24 \|\|*

Nārada said:

24\. I have arrived from Heaven. What shall I say to you about my well-being?

## \|\| 2.18.25 \|\|

*yātāyātairdineśasya pūryyate brahmaṇo dinam \|*  
*dināṃte jāyate rātrī rātrau naśyaṃti devatāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The day of Brahmā is completed by the goings and comings of the Lord of the day. The night appears at the end of the day. The deities perish at night.

## \|\| 2.18.26 \|\|

*kā kathā mṛtyulokasya ye mriyaṃte dinedine \|*  
*nabho dhūmākulaṃ jātaṃ devā baligṛhe gatāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. What can be said about the world of the mortals, where (beings) die everyday! The sky is full of smoke. Gods have gone to Bali’s house.

## \|\| 2.18.27 \|\|

*saptarṣayo gatāstatra brahmaṇā brahmacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*hāhāhūhūstuṃbaruśca gatau nāradaparvatau \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The seven celebate Brāhmaṇa-sages went there. So also Hāhīhūhī \[?Hāhāhūhū=Hāhā and Hūhū?\], Tumbaru, Nārada, Parvata went there.

## \|\| 2.18.28 \|\|

*apsarogaṇagandharvāḥ saṃprāptā balimaṃdire \|*  
*utpātaśāṃtiko yajñaḥ kriyate balinā svayam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The bevy of celestial nymphs, the Gandharvas reached the house of Bali. Bali himself performed the sacrifice calculated to remove (the effects of) a portent.

## \|\| 2.18.29 \|\|

*tatraiva gantumicchāmi draṣṭuṃ yajñaṃ balergṛhe \|*  
*sahasramekaṃ yajñānāmekonaṃ vidadhe baliḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. I am going there only to witness the sacrifice in Bali’s house. Bali has performed nine hundred and ninety-nine sacrifices—just short of a thousand by (only) one (sacrifice).

## \|\| 2.18.30 \|\|

*daityānāṃ bhuvanaṃ sarvaṃ saṃpūrṇe'sminbhaviṣyati \|*  
*asāvatiśayaḥ ko'pi prārabdho yajñakarmaṇi \|*  
*dvijātibhyo mayā deyaṃ yena yadyācyate svayam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. On the completion of this (last) sacrifice the entire world will belong to the demons. This is some excellence set in the performance of the sacrifice. I shall myself give to the Brāhmaṇas whatever is asked for by anyone.

## \|\| 2.18.31-32 \|\|

*vāritenāpi me deyaṃ satyamastu vaco mama \|*  
*ātmānamapi dārāṃśca rājyaṃ putrānpriyānmama \|\| 31 \|\|*

*prārthitaścenna dāsyāmi vyartho bhavatu me'dhvaraḥ \|*  
*anena vacasā jātā mahatī me śiro vyathā \|*  
*pratijñāya kathaṃ yajñaḥ saṃpūrṇo'yaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Even though I am warded off, I shall give. Let my words be true. If, being solicited, I shall not give myself, my wife, kingdom, dear sons, let my sacrifice be in vain. By these words there arose a severe pain in my head. After having taken a vow, how will my sacrifice be complete?

## \|\| 2.18.33 \|\|

*bhaṃgopāyaṃ na paśyāmi bhramāmi bhuvanatraye \|*  
*vidhvaṃsakāriṇaṃ jñātvā bhavaṃtaṃ paryupasthitaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*
