33\. I do not see a means to break it. I am roaming in the three worlds. Knowing you to bring about destruction, I have approached you

## \|\| 2.18.34 \|\|

*yathā na pūryate yajñastathedānīṃ vidhīyatām \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Act now in such a way that the sacrifice will not be completed.

## \|\| 2.18.35 \|\|

*vāmana uvāca \|*  
*maharṣe śṛṇu me vākyaṃ kā śaktirmama vidyate \|*  
*ko'haṃ kasmātkariṣyāmi yajñe devāḥ samāgatāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

Vāmana said:

35\. O great sage, listen to my words. What power do I have (now)? Who am I? Why should I do it? The gods have arrived at the sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.18.36 \|\|

*ṛṣayo brāhmaṇāḥ sarve kathaṃ vyartho bhaviṣyati \|*  
*aparaṃ śṛṇu me vākyaṃ brahmarṣe brahmaṇaspate \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. All the sages, Brāhmaṇas (have arrived). How will (the sacrifice) be fruitless? O Brāhmaṇa sage, O lord of sacred learning, listen to my other words.

## \|\| 2.18.37 \|\|

*na kalatraṃ na te putrāḥ kasmātprakṛtirīdṛśī \|*  
*yuddhaṃ vinā na te saukhyaṃ na saukhyaṃ kalahaṃ vinā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. You do not have a wife, nor sons; why do you have such a nature? You do not have happiness without war, nor do you have happiness without quarrel.

## \|\| 2.18.38-39 \|\|

*yādṛśastā dṛśo vā'pi vāgvādo'pi sadā priyaḥ \|*  
*snānaṃ saṃdhyā japo homastarpaṇaṃ pitṛdevayoḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*nāradaḥ kurute cānyadanyatkurvaṃti brāhmaṇāḥ \|*  
*mamāpi kautukaṃ jātaṃ maharṣe vada satvaram \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. Controversy of this or that type is always dear to you. Bath, prayers, repeating names of deities, sacrifices, offerings to dead ancestors and deities—Nārada does these in a different way; Brāhmaṇas do these in another way. I too have curiosity. O great sage, speak quickly.

## \|\| 2.18.40 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*pādmakalpe vyatikrāṃte rātryaṃte śṛṇu vāmana \|*  
*brahmāṇḍaṃ vāriṇā vyāptamanyatkiṃ cinna vidyate \|\| 40 \|\|*

Nārada said:

40\. O Vāmana, listen. At the end of the Night when the Padma Kalpa had ended, the universe was pervaded with water. There was nothing else.

## \|\| 2.18.41 \|\|

*apsu śete devadevaḥ sa ca nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*sa brahmā sa śivo nāsti bhedasteṣāṃ parasparam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The god of gods, lies in water. He is called Nārāyaṇa. He is Brahmā; He is Śiva. There is no difference among them.

## \|\| 2.18.42-43 \|\|

*yadā bhavaṃti te bhinnā stadā devatrayaṃ ca te \|*  
*karttuṃ vārāhakalpaṃ tu bhinnā jātāstrayastadā \|\| 42 \|\|*

*brahmaviṣṇuharā devā rajaḥsattvatamomayāḥ \|*  
*sṛṣṭiṃ brahmā karotyevaṃ tāṃ ca pālayate hariḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. When they become separate, they are the Triad of gods. To fashion the Varāha Kalpa, the three became separate at that time as Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Hara, full of (the qualities) passion, goodness and ignorance (respectively). Brahmā creates the world thus, and Viṣṇu looks after it.

## \|\| 2.18.44 \|\|

*haraḥ saṃharate sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*evaṃ pravartya deveśa upaviṣṭā varāsane \|*  
*kailāsaśikhare ramye maṃtrayaṃti parasparam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Hara withdraws all the three worlds along with the moving and unmoving (objects). Having started like this the chief of gods sat on an excellent seat on the Kailāsa mountain. They consult one another.

## \|\| 2.18.45 \|\|

*trayāṇāṃ ko varo devaḥ ko jyeṣṭhaḥ ko guṇādhikaḥ \|*  
*caturtho nāsti yo vetti sahasā te trayaḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Of the three who is the excellent god; who is the senior-most; who is superior in virtues? There is no fourth one who knows it at once. The three have remained (like this).

## \|\| 2.18.46 \|\|

*tebhyaḥ samutthitaṃ jyotirekībhūtaṃ tadaṃbare \|*  
*kālamānena yuktaṃ tadbhrāmte ravimaṃḍalam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. From them a light that had become united, rose in the sky. Endowed with the measure of time that orb of the sun moves (in the sky).

## \|\| 2.18.47 \|\|

*ahaṃ jyeṣṭho hyahaṃ jyeṣṭho vādo'bhūddharabrahmaṇoḥ \|*  
*dvayorvivadatoḥ krodhātsaṃjāto'haṃ mukhātprabho \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Between Hara and Brahmā, a dispute came up as: “I am the greatest”, “I am the greatest”—O lord, from the mouth of them who were disputing angrily (like this), I was born.

## \|\| 2.18.48-49 \|\|

*kathaṃ deva na jānāsi yaduktaṃ brahmaṇā tadā \|*  
*daśāvatārāste raṃtuṃ matsyakūrmādayaḥ purā \|\| 48 \|\|*

*rudreṇa vāritā gatvā kalaho vo na yujyate \|*  
*tathaiva kṛtavānviṣṇuravatārāndaśaiva tān \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. O god, how do you not know what Brahmā had said at that time? Formerly your ten incarnations like the Fish, the Tortoise decided to sport, and were warded off by Rudra, (saying) “Quarrel does not become you” Viṣṇu did (i.e. said) just like that to the ten incarnations.

## \|\| 2.18.50 \|\|

*kalpādau brahmaṇo vaktrātsaṃjāto'haṃ dvijottama \|*  
*kalahājanma me yasmāttasmānme kalahaḥ priyaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. O best Brāhmaṇa, at the beginning of the Kalpa I was born from the mouth of Brahmā. Since my birth was from quarrel, I am fond of quarrel.

## \|\| 2.18.51 \|\|

*kalpādau sṛjatā pūrvaṃ cinvitaṃ brahmaṇā svayam \|*  
*vedāntinā kathaṃ sṛṣṭiḥ karttavyā'ho hare mayā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. At the beginning of the Kalpa, while creating (the world) Brahmā Himself thought: “O Han, how should I, the follower of the Vedānta (philosophy), fashion the world?

## \|\| 2.18.52 \|\|

*naṣṭānvedānna jānāmi kva vedāste gatā iti \|*  
*pṛthvīmapi na jānāmi kiṃ sthāne kimadho gatā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. “I do not know the lost Vedas. (I do not know) where the Vedas have gone. I do not know even about the earth—whether it is at its place or has gone down.

## \|\| 2.18.53 \|\|

*gaṃtuṃ na vidyate śaktirjalamadhye mamādhunā \|*  
*avatāraistvayā kāryaṃ daśabhiḥ sṛṣṭirakṣaṇa m \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. “I do not have the strength now to go into the water. By means of the ten incarnations you have to protect the world.

## \|\| 2.18.54 \|\|

*jale jalecaro matsyo mahānadyāṃ bhaviṣyasi \|*  
*ādāya vedānvegena mama tvaṃ dātumarhasi \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. “In the water in the great river you will be an aquatic animal. Bringing the Vedas quickly you please give them to me.”

## \|\| 2.18.55 \|\|

*tathā ca kṛtavāndevo matsyarūpaṃ jale mahat \|*  
*vedānsamānayāmāsa dadau ca brahmaṇe purā \|*  
*kūrmarūpaṃ punaḥ kṛtvā maṃdaraṃ dhārayiṣyasi \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. (Taking) the great form of a Fish in the water, God (Viṣṇu) formerly brought and gave the Vedas to Brahmā. (Brahmā said:) “Again taking up the form of a tortoise you will hold the Mandāra (mountain).”

## \|\| 2.18.56 \|\|

*ityukto brahmaṇā viṣṇurlakṣmīstvāṃ varayiṣyati \|*  
*purā citraṃ caritraṃ te mathane dṛṣṭavānaham \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Brahmā spoke to Viṣṇu like this: “Lakṣmī will choose you (as her husband). Formerly I have seen your wonderful act at the time of the churning of the ocean.

## \|\| 2.18.57 \|\|

*yadā rasātalaṃ prāptā pṛthivī naiva dṛśyate \|*  
*brahmāṃḍārthe sthānakṛte tatra sā naiva dṛśyate \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. “When the earth reached the Nether world it was not at all seen. It was not seen when a place was made for the universe.”

## \|\| 2.18.58 \|\|

*vārāhaṃ kriyatāṃ rūpaṃ brahmaṇā preritaḥ svayam \|*  
*mahāvarāharūpaṃ sa kṛtvā bhūmeradho gataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Being impelled by Brahmā himself to take up the form of the Pig, He took up the form of the great Boar and went below the earth.”

## \|\| 2.18.59 \|\|

*uddhṛtya ca tadā viṣṇurdaṃṣṭrāgreṇa vasuṃdharām \|*  
*sa nināya yathāsthānaṃ mustāṃ va dharaṇītalāt \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Taking up the earth with the tip of His fang, He took it to its proper place, collecting it from below.

## \|\| 2.18.60 \|\|

*avatāraṃ tṛtīyaṃ vai harasyāpi manoharam \|*  
*yena sā pṛthivī pṛthvī parvataiḥ sahitā dhṛtā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The third incarnation of Viṣṇu also is charming, by which he sustained the earth along with the mountains.

## \|\| 2.18.61-62 \|\|

*caturthaṃ narasiṃhaṃ vai kathayāmi sudāruṇam \|*  
*ādityā aditeḥ putrā diteḥ putrau mahāvalau \|\| 61 \|\|*

*hiraṇyakaśipurdaityo hiraṇyākṣo mahābalaḥ \|*  
*svarge devāḥ sthitāḥ sarve pātāle daityadānavāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. I am telling the fourth (incarnation) viz. Narasiṃha, the very fearful one. Ādityas are the sons of Aditi; the demon Hiraṇyakaśipu and the very strong Hiraṇyākṣa are the two sons of Diti. All gods have stayed in Heaven, and the demons and fiends in the Nether region.

## \|\| 2.18.63 \|\|

*hiraṇyakaśipuścakre daityo rājyaṃ rasātale \|*  
*manuputrā dharāpṛṣṭhe sthāpitā devadānavaiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. The demon Hiraṇyakaśipu ruled in the Nether region. Gods and demons put Manu’s descendants on the surface of the earth.

## \|\| 2.18.64 \|\|

*vyavasthāṃ tāmatikramya hiraṇyakaśipurdvija \|*  
*rājyaṃ cakre dharāpṛṣṭhe surendraṃ sa vijitya ca \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. O Brāhmaṇa, having broken that arrangement Hiraṇyakaśipu, having overcome the Lord of gods ruled over the earth.

## \|\| 2.18.65 \|\|

*saptadvīpavatīṃ pṛthvīṃ gṛhītvā sā'marāvatīm \|*  
*grahītukāmo bubhuje putrapautraiḥ kṛtādaraḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Having seized the earth with seven islands and desiring to capture Amarāvatī, he enjoyed being honoured by his sons and grandsons.

## \|\| 2.18.66 \|\|

*prahlādapramukhānputrānsa pīḍayati maṃdadhīḥ \|*  
*putreṣu pāṭhyamāneṣu prahlādo'pi papāṭha tat \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. The dull one harasses his sons led by Prahlāda. What the sons were being taught Prahlāda also recited that.

## \|\| 2.18.67 \|\|

*yena vai paṭhyamānena jāyate tasya vedanā \|*  
*bhuvanadvayarājyena daityo devānna manyate \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Due to his being taught that he had pain. The demon did not care for the gods.

## \|\| 2.18.68 \|\|

*tapasā toṣito brahmā dadau tasmai varaṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*amaratvaṃ sa devebhyo manuṣyebhyaḥ surottama \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Brahmā, the Lord, being pleased by his penance, granted him a boon. O best of gods, he had no death from gods and men.

## \|\| 2.18.69-70 \|\|

*kasmādapi na me bhūyānmaraṇaṃ yadi cedbhavet \|*  
*kiṃcitsiṃho naraḥ kiṃcidyo bhaveddharaṇīdharaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*tasmātkararuhaibhinno mariṣye na dharātale \|*  
*evaṃ bhaviṣyatītyuktvā gato brahmā ca vismayam \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. “If at all death is to take place in my case, it should be from none. I shall die not on the earth, being torn by the nails of him, Viṣṇu, partly lion and partly man”, “It will be so”—Saying these words, Brahmā was astonished.

## \|\| 2.18.71 \|\|

*kālena gacchatā tasya saṃjāto vigraho mahān \|*  
*devāḥ kiṃ me kariṣyaṃti viṣṇunā kiṃ prayojanam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. When some time he was going, he had a great battle. (He thought:) “What will the gods do to me? What have I to do with Viṣṇu?

## \|\| 2.18.72 \|\|

*yaṣṭavyo'haṃ sadā yajñai rudraḥ kiṃ me kariṣyati \|*  
*evaṃ hi varttamānasya prahlādaḥ stauti taṃ harim \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. “I should always be offered an oblation in sacrifices. What will Rudra do to me? When such was the state Prahlāda praised that Hari.

## \|\| 2.18.73 \|\|

*yenāsya jāyate mṛtyustameva smarate harim \|*  
*yadāsau vāryamāṇo'pi virauti ca hariṃ harim \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. He recollected that Hari only, due to whom his death was to take place. Though he was warded off he cried: “Hari! Hari!”

## \|\| 2.18.74 \|\|

*caturbhujaṃ śaṃkhagadāsidhāriṇaṃ pītāṃbaraṃ kaustubha lāñchitaṃ sadā \|*  
*smarāmi viṣṇuṃ jagadekanāyakaṃ dadāti muktiṃ smṛtamātra eva yaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. “I shall always remember that Viṣṇu, who has four arms, who holds a conch, a mace, a sword, who wears a yellow garment, who is marked with the Kaustubha (gem), who is the only chief of the world, (and) who gives salvation when just remembered.”

## \|\| 2.18.75 \|\|

*anena vacasā kṣubdho daityo detyāndi deśa ha \|*  
*mārayadhvaṃ tu taṃ duṣṭaṃ gaja sarpajalāgnitaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Agitated by these words the demon ordered (other) demons: “Get that wicked one killed by an elephant, serpent, water or fire.”

## \|\| 2.18.76 \|\|

*prahlāda uvāca \|*  
*gajepi viṣṇurbhujage'pi viṣṇurjale'pi viṣṇurjvalane'pi viṣṇuḥ \|*  
*tvayi sthito daitya mayi sthitaśca viṣṇuṃ vinā daityagaṇā'pi nāsti \|\| 76 \|\|*

Prahlāda said:

76\. O demon, Viṣṇu is even in an elephant; Viṣṇu is even in a serpent; Viṣṇu is also in water; Viṣṇu is also in fire. O demon, Viṣṇu exists in you, and in me as well. Even the group of the demons is not without Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.18.77-78 \|\|

*yadā sa māryamāṇo'pi mṛtyuṃ prāpnoti na kvacit \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśiporvakṣo dahyate krodhavahninā \|*  
*tadā śikṣayituṃ putraṃ mukhāgre saṃniveśya ca \|\| 77 \|\|*

*vacobhiḥ kaṭhinaiḥ putraṃ svayaṃ hantuṃ samudyataḥ \|\| \|*  
*dhiktvā nārāyaṇaṃ stauṣi mamāriṃ stauṣi cetpunaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

77-78. When, though being murdered, he did not meet with death, the chest of Hiraṇyakaśipu burnt with the fire of anger. Then to teach the son, and placing him in front of himself, he, started striking the son with harsh words: “Fie upon you that you are praising Nārāyaṇa, my enemy.

## \|\| 2.18.79 \|\|

*puṣpalāvaṃ laviṣyāmi śiraste'haṃ varāsinā \|*  
*ahaṃ viṣṇurahaṃ brahmā rudra indro varaṃ vada \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. “With aṇ excellent sword I shall cut off your head like a flower. I am Viṣṇu, I am Brahmā, Rudra, Indra. Speak out the boon (you want).

## \|\| 2.18.80 \|\|

*ātmīyaṃ pitaraṃ muktvā kamanyaṃ stauṣi bālaka \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. “O child, leaving your own father, whom else are you praising?”

## \|\| 2.18.81-82 \|\|

*yadā na paṭhate bālaḥ stauti no pitaraṃ svakam \|*  
*daṇḍenāhatya guruṇā prahlādaḥ preritaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*vadaikaṃ vacanaṃ śiṣya dehi me gurudakṣiṇām \|\| 81 \|\|*

*yathā me tuṣyate svāmī dadāti vipulaṃ dhanam \|\| 82 \|\|*

81-82. When the boy did not recite (his father’s name), nor did he praise his own father, the father struck him with a stick and urged him. “O (my) disciple, utter one word, and give me, my fee, so that my master will be pleased, and will give me ample wealth.” (?obscure)

## \|\| 2.18.83-84 \|\|

*prahlāda uvāca \|*  
*praharasva prathamaṃ māṃ kariṣye vacanaṃ guro \|*  
*staumi viṣṇumahaṃ yena trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 83 \|\|*

*kṛtaṃ saṃvarddhitaṃ śāṃtaṃ sa me viṣṇuḥ prasīdatu \|*  
*brahmā viṣṇurharo viṣṇu rindro vāyuryamo'nalaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

Prahlāda said:

83-84a. O Preceptor, first strike me, (then) I shall do as you tell me. I shall praise Viṣṇu, who has created and nourished this peaceful world. May that Viṣṇu favour me!

84b. Viṣṇu is Brahmā; Viṣṇu is Hara; Viṣṇu is Indra, Vāyu, Yama and Fire.

## \|\| 2.18.85 \|\|

*prakṛtyādīni tattvāni puruṣaṃ paṃcaviṃśakam \|*  
*pitṛdehe gurordehe mama dehe'pi saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. He is the principles like Prakṛti, with Puruṣa as the twenty-fifth. He exists in my father’s body, preceptor’s body, so also in my body.

## \|\| 2.18.86 \|\|

*evaṃ jānankathaṃ staumi mriyamāṇaṃ narādhamam \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Knowing this how shall I praise the wicked man that is mortal!

## \|\| 2.18.87 \|\|

*gururuvāca \|*  
*nareṣu ko'dhamaḥ śiṣya janmādimaraṇe'dhama \|*  
*kathaṃ na pitaraṃ stauṣi mriyamāṇo hariṃ harim \|\| 87 \|\|*

The Preceptor said:

87\. O disciple, who is the meanest among men? O mean one, birth etc. and death. While dying why not praise your father (and praise) Hari?

## \|\| 2.18.88 \|\|

*prahlāda uvāca \|*  
*bhojane śayane yāne jvare niṣṭhīvane raṇe \|*  
*harirityakṣaraṃ nāsti maraṇe'sau narādhamaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

Prahlāda said:

88\. He, who does not utter the letters ‘Hari’, at the time of his meal, at bed (-time), in a vehicle (while travelling), in fever, while spitting, in fight, is the meanest man.

## \|\| 2.18.89 \|\|

*bhaye rājakule yuddhe vyādhau strīsaṃgame vane \|*  
*aśaktau vā'tha saṃnyāse maraṇe bhūmisaṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*smaraṃti mātaraṃ mūrkhāḥ pitaraṃ ca narādhamāḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Fools remember their mother, and the mean-minded their father in (the time of) fear, in a royal family, in a war, (while suffering from) a disease, while in union with a woman, in a forest, in weakness, in renunciation, at the time of death, lying on the ground.

## \|\| 2.18.90 \|\|

*mātā nāsti pitā nāsti nāsti me svajano janaḥ \|*  
*hariṃ vinā na ko'pyasti yadyuktaṃ tadvidhīyatām \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. I have no mother, no father, no kinsmen. I have none else but Hari; do what is proper.

## \|\| 2.18.91 \|\|

*ityādivacanaiḥ kruddho hantuṃ daityaḥ samutthitaḥ \|*  
*tadā mātā samāgatya putrasya purataḥ sthitā \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Angered by such words, the demon rose to kill him. Then the mother came (there) and stood in front of the son.

## \|\| 2.18.92 \|\|

*bhrātaraḥ svajano bhaginī bhāṣate mā hariṃ vada \|*  
*ahaṃ mātā svasā ceyaṃ bhrātaraḥ svajano janaḥ \|*  
*yathā saṃmilitairvatsa sthīyate vahuvāsaram \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Brothers, kinsmen, sister (all) said: “Do not utter (the name of) Hari. O child, united with me, you mother, this your sister, these (your) brothers, these (your) kinsmen, you will live for many years.”

## \|\| 2.18.93 \|\|

*prahlāda uvāca \|*  
*mātā me kā svasā me kā bhrātaraḥ ke pitā ca kaḥ \|*  
*svajanaṃ śṛṇu me mātaḥ sahitaiḥ sthīyate sadā \|\| 93 \|\|*

Prahlāda said:

93\. Who is my mother? Who is my sister? Who are my brothers? Who is my father? O my mother, listen. Relatives are those with whom you always live.

## \|\| 2.18.94 \|\|

*yasyāḥ pītaṃ mayā mūtraṃ purīṣamudare bahu \|*  
*sā mātā narako'smākamagre vaktuṃ na śakyate \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. That mother, whose urine, faeces, I drank profusely while in the womb, is indeed a hell. I can’t say any more.

## \|\| 2.18.95 \|\|

*nirmito na dvitīyastu nirmito viśvakarmaṇā \|*  
*tvādṛśastu pumānkaścidyasya no hadaye hariḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Another man like you, in whose heart Hari does not exist, has not been created by Viśvakarmā (the architect of gods).

## \|\| 2.18.96-97 \|\|

*daśamāsaṃ dhruvaṃ manye mūtraṃ pāsyati tarpitaḥ \|*  
*bhrātaro bhrātaraḥ satyaṃ garbhe'pi syuḥ kathaṃ yadi \|\| 96 \|\|*

*yudhyatastānkathaṃ mātā varākī vārayiṣyati \|*  
*svajano dṛśyate vṛddhaḥ pareṣu paṇḍitāyate \|\| 97 \|\|*

96-97a. I think, certainly he, being gratified, will drink urine for ten months. If brothers were brothers even in the womb, how will the poor mother stop them from fighting?

97b. One’s relative, an old one among the kinsmen, become a learned man among strangers.

## \|\| 2.18.98 \|\|

*kuṭuṃbaṃ bhaṇyate kasmādyaśca nāyāti yāti ca \|*  
*baṃdhanaṃ ca kuṭumbasya jāyate narakāya naḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. When one does not come or go, why is it called a family? Binding of the family leads us to hell.

## \|\| 2.18.99 \|\|

*mātā me vidyate cānyā pitānyo bhrātaraśca ye \|*  
*svasā svajanasamvandhaṃ jñātvā muktimavāpnuyāt \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. My mother is someone different. The father is someone different. Brothers also are (different). The sister knowing relation with kinsmen would obtain salvation.

## \|\| 2.18.100 \|\|

*mātā prakṛtirasmākaṃ svasā buddhirnigadyate \|*  
*ahaṃkārastato jāto yo'hamityanumīyate \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Our mother is Prakṛti (Nature). Buddhi (Intellect) is said to be the sister. From that Ahaṃkāra (Ego) is produced which is referred as I.

## \|\| 2.18.101 \|\|

*tanmātrāḥ sodarāḥ pañca ye gacchanti sahaiva me \|*  
*eṣā prakṛtirasmākaṃ vikāraḥ svajano mama \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. The five subtle elements (Tanmātras) born together with ‘I’ are my brothers. This is our origin. My relative (svajana) is vikāra (modification).

## \|\| 2.18.102 \|\|

*eteṣāṃ vāhako yastu puruṣaḥ pañca viṃśakaḥ \|*  
*sa me pitā śarīre'sminparamātmā hariḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. The one that holds these together is Puruṣa, the twenty-fifth (principle). He is my father in this my body. He is the Highest Soul, Hari dwelling in this body.

## \|\| 2.18.103 \|\|

*yadyasau cityante citte dṛśyate hṛdaye hariḥ \|*  
*aṇimādiguṇaiśvaryaṃ padaṃ tasyaiva jāyate \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. If in the mind he is reflected on, He, Hari, is seen in the heart. His position, having the wealth with the qualities like becoming atomic iṇ size etc. is produced.

## \|\| 2.18.104 \|\|

*bhavatā sammataṃ rājyaṃ tanme nityaṃ tṛṇaiḥ samam \|*  
*yatra no pūjyate viṣṇurbrahmā rudro'nilo'nalaḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. The kingdom liked by you where Viṣṇu, Brahmā, or Rudra, or Wind or Fire is not worshipped, is like a blade of grass for me.

## \|\| 2.18.105 \|\|

*pratyakṣo dṛśyate yastu nirālambo bhramatyasau \|*  
*sa eva bhagavānviṣṇurya ete gagane sthitāḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. He, who is actually seen, moves without a support. He alone is the revered Viṣṇu, (so also) these that stay in the sky.

## \|\| 2.18.106 \|\|

*dhruve baddhā grahāḥ sarve ya ete'pyuḍavaḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*te sarve viṣṇuvacasā na pataṃti dharātale \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. All planets, so also these constellation that exist (in the sky), are tied to Dhruva. All of them, do not fall on the surface of the earth because of the word (i.e. order) of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.18.107 \|\|

*kāle vināśaḥ sarveṣāṃ tenaiva vihitaḥ svayam \|*  
*iti saṃciṃtya me nāsti bhavadbhyo maraṇādbhayam \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. He Himself has laid down the end of all (objects) at a (fixed) time. Thinking like this I have no fear of death.

## \|\| 2.18.108 \|\|

*iti tadvacanasyāṃte padā hatvā pitā'bravīt \|*  
*kutrā'sau hanmi tatpūrvaṃ paścāttvāṃ haribhāṣiṇam \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. At the end of these words uttered by him, his father, striking him with his foot (i.e. kicking him) said: “Where is he (i.e. Viṣṇu)? I shall first kill Him; then (I shall) kill you, talking (well) about Han.

## \|\| 2.18.109 \|\|

*prahlāda uvāca \|*  
*pṛthivyādīni bhūtāni tānyeva bhagavānhariḥ \|*  
*sthale jale kiṃ bahunā sarvaṃ viṣṇumayaṃ jagat \|\| 109 \|\|*

Prahlāda said:

109\. The elements like the earth etc. are just Lord Hari. He is on ground, in water. The entire world is full of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.18.110 \|\|

*tṛṇe kāṣṭhe gṛhe kṣetre dravye dehe sthito hariḥ \|*  
*jñāyate jñānayogena dṛśyate kiṃ nu cakṣuṣā \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. Hari remains in grass, wood, house, ground, material. He is known by means of the yoga of knowledge. Can He be seen by (mere physical) eyes?

## \|\| 2.18.111 \|\|

*brahmālaye yāti rasātale vā dharātale'sau bhramati kṣaṇena \|*  
*āghrāti gandhaṃ vidadhāti sarvaṃ śṛṇoti jānāti sa cātra viṣṇuḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. He goes to Brahmā’s abode; he goes to the bottom of the earth. In a moment he wanders on the surface of the earth. He inhales fragrance; he, Viṣṇu, fashions everything. He hears, knows (everything).

## \|\| 2.18.112 \|\|

*ityuktaḥ sahajāṃ māyāṃ tyaktvā siṃhāsanotthitaḥ \|*  
*dṛḍhaṃ parikaraṃ baddhvā khaṅgaṃ cākṛṣya cojjvalam \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. Thus addressed, he, giving up natural compassion, got up from his throne, and girding the loins firmly, drawing out his bright sword,

## \|\| 2.18.113 \|\|

*hatvā taṃ phalakāgreṇa babhāṣe dussahaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*idānīṃ smara re viṣṇuṃ no cejjavalitaku ṇḍalam \|*  
*patiṣyati śiro bhūmau phalaṃ pakvaṃ yathā nagāt \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. (and) striking him with the end of a plank spoke to him unbearable words: “Now remember Viṣṇu; otherwise your head with bright earrings will fall down like a ripe fruit from a tree.

## \|\| 2.18.114-115 \|\|

*no ceddarśaya taṃ viṣṇumasmātstaṃbhādvinirgatam \|*  
*prahlādastu bhayaṃ tyaktvā cakre padmāsanaṃ bhuvi \|\| 114 \|\|*

*vidhāya kaṃdharāṃ netumuccaiḥ śvāsaṃ nirudhya ca \|*  
*hṛdi dhyātvā hariṃ devaṃ maraṇāyonmukhaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

114-115. “Or else show that Viṣṇu coming out of this pillar.” Giving up fear Prahlāda sat down on the ground in the Padmāsana position to raise his neck, and restraining his breath, and meditating upon Hari in his mind remained ready to die.

## \|\| 2.18.116 \|\|

*prabho mayā tadā dṛṣṭamāścaryaṃ gaganādbhuvi \|*  
*puṣpamālā sthitā kaṇṭhe prahlādasya svayaṃ gatā \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. O Lord, I saw from the sky a wonder on the earth. A garland of flowers fell around Prahlāda’s neck of its own accord.

## \|\| 2.18.117 \|\|

*gaganaṃ vyāpyamānaṃ ca kiṃkimevaṃ kṛtaṃ janaiḥ \|*  
*jhaṭiti truṭyati stambhācchabdena kṣubhito janaḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. What did the people not do that pervaded the sky? People agitated by noise quickly fell asunder due to the sound.

## \|\| 2.18.118 \|\|

*dharaṇī yāti pātālaṃ dyaurvā bhūmiṃ sameṣyati \|*  
*patiṣyati śiro bhūmau khaḍgaghātāhataṃ nu kim \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. The earth went to the Nether world; the sky met the earth. Cut off by the stroke of the sword, will a head fall on the ground?

## \|\| 2.18.119 \|\|

*tāvatstaṃbhādviniṣkrāntaḥ siṃhanādo bhayaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*bhūmau nipatitāḥ sarve daityāḥ śabdena mūrcchitāḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. Just then a lion’s terrible roar came out from the pillar. All demons fainted due to that sound.

## \|\| 2.18.120 \|\|

*hiraṇyakaśiporhastātkhaḍgacarma papāta ca \|*  
*na sa jānāti kiṃ kimetaditi punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. The sword and shield fell from Hiraṇyakaśipu’s hand. He did not know what this was.

## \|\| 2.18.121 \|\|

*utthito vīkṣate yāvattāvatpaśyati taṃ harim \|*  
*adho naraṃ sthitaṃ siṃhamupariṣṭādvibhī ṣaṇam \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. When he got up he just saw Hari. Below was the man, and above was a fearful lion.

## \|\| 2.18.122 \|\|

*daṃṣṭrā karālavadanaṃ lelihānamivāṃbaram \|*  
*jājvalyamānavapuṣaṃ pucchācchoṭitamastakam \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. Its mouth was fearful due to the fangs, and it was as if it were licking the sky, The body was bright, and its tail impeded its head.

## \|\| 2.18.123 \|\|

*mahākaṇṭhakṛtārāvaṃ saśabda miva toyadam \|*  
*samucchvasitakeśāṃtaṃ durnirīkṣyaṃ surāsuraiḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. A sound issued if from the great throat, as it from cloud, a deep sigh raising the tips of the hair, unbearable to be seen by gods and demons.

## \|\| 2.18.124 \|\|

*narasiṃhamatho dṛṣṭvā nipapāta punaḥ kṣitau \|*  
*vigṛhya keśapāśe taṃ bhrāmayāmāsa cāṃbaram \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. Seeing Narasiṃha he again fell on the gound \[ground?\]. He holding him with his profuse hair hurled him in the sky.

## \|\| 2.18.125 \|\|

*bhrāmayitvā śataguṇaṃ pṛthivyāṃ samapothayat \|*  
*na mamāra sa daityendro brahmaṇo varakāraṇāt \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. Whirling him a hundred times he threw him on the ground. Due to his having had a boon from Brahmā the Lord of demons did not die.

## \|\| 2.18.126-128 \|\|

*gaganasthaistadā devai ruccaiḥ saṃsmārito hariḥ \|*  
*daityaṃ jānuni cānīya vakṣo hṛṣṭo nirīkṣya ca \|\| 126 \|\|*

*jayajayeti yakṣānāṃ surāṇāṃ so'vadhārayat \|*  
*śabdaṃ karṇe bhujau sajjau kṛtvā tau padmalāṃchitau \|\| 127 \|\|*

*bibheda vakṣo daityasya vajraghātakiṇāṃkitam \|*  
*nakhaiḥ kundasumaprakhyairasthisaṃghātakarśitam \|\| 128 \|\|*

126-128. At that time Hari was loudly recollected by gods present in the heaven. Bringing the demon on his knee and observing after seeing his chest, He heard the words of victory uttered by the Yakṣas and gods. Making His arms, marked with a lotus, ready, he pierced the chest of the demon marked with the stroke of the thunderbolt, and weakened with strokes of bones, with His nails resembling kunda flowers.

## \|\| 2.18.129 \|\|

*bhinne vakṣasi daityendro mamāraca papāta ca \|*  
*tadā saharṣamabhavattrailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. When his chest was pierced the Lord of demons fell down dead. Then the three worlds with the mobile and the immobile became joyful.

## \|\| 2.18.130-131 \|\|

*mamāpi tṛptiḥ sañjātā prasādāttava keśava \|*  
*yadā puratraye dagdhe prasādācchaṃkarasya ca \|\| 130 \|\|*

*hiṇyākṣe punarjātā sā kāle vinipātite \|*  
*idānīṃ nāsti me tṛptiḥ kutra yāmi karomi kim \|\| 131 \|\|*

130-131. O Keśava, through your favour I was also satisfied, when the three cities were burnt by Śaṅkara’s favour, and when Hiraṇyākṣa was destroyed at the (proper) time. Now I am not content. Where should I go? What should I do?

## \|\| 2.18.132 \|\|

*pṛthivyāṃ kṣatriyāḥ santi na yudhyaṃte parasparam \|*  
*devānāṃ dānavaiḥ sārddhaṃ nāsti yuddhaṃ kathaṃ prabho \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. There are Kṣatriyas on the earth. They do not fight with one another. O Lord, how is it that the gods do not fight with the demons?

## \|\| 2.18.133 \|\|

*idānīṃ balinā vyāptaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*pañcamo yo'vatāraste na jāne kiṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*valinigrahakālo'yaṃ taddarśaya janārdana \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. Now Bali has occupied the three worlds with the mobile and the immobile. I do not know what your fifth incarnation will do. O Janārdana, this is the time to control Bali. Show it.

## \|\| 2.18.134 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*tadetatsakalaṃ śrutvā babhāṣe vāmano munim \|\| 134 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

134\. Having heard all this, Vāmaṇa said to the sage:

## \|\| 2.18.135 \|\|

*vāmana uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu nārada yadvṛttaṃ hiṇyakaśipau hate \|*  
*daityarājaḥ kṛto rājā prahlādo'tīva vaiṣṇavaḥ \|\| 135 \|\|*

Vāmana said:

135\. O Nārada, listen to what happened when Hiraṇyakaśipu was killed. Prahlāda, the great devotee of Viṣṇu, the demon-king, was made the king.

## \|\| 2.18.136-137 \|\|

*tena rājyaṃ dharāpṛṣṭhe kṛtaṃ saṃvatsarānbahūn \|*  
*tasyāpi kurvato rājyaṃ vigraho hi suraiḥ samam \|\| 136 \|\|*

*no paśyāmyapi daityānāṃ pūrvavairamanusmaran \|*  
*utpādya putrānsabahūnrājyaṃ cakre sa puṣkalam \|\| 137 \|\|*

136-137. He ruled over the earth for many years. I was remembering the former enmity of the demons; I do not see the enmity of him who was ruling. Having produced many sons he ruled over a vast kingdom.

## \|\| 2.18.138 \|\|

*virocanādbalirjāto bāla eva yadā'bhavat \|*  
*ekānte sa hariṃ jñātvā tadā yogena kenacit \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. Bali was born from Virocana. When he was just a child, he remembered Hari through some means.

## \|\| 2.18.139 \|\|

*muktvā rājyaṃ priyānputrāngato'sau girisānuṣu \|*  
*kalpāntasthāyinaṃ dehaṃ tasya cakre janārddanaḥ \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. Leaving his kingdom and his dear sons, he went to mountain-peaks. Janārdana made his body to last till the end of the Kalpa.

## \|\| 2.18.140 \|\|

*daityānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca bahūnāṃ rājyakāraṇe \|*  
*vivādotīva saṃjātaḥ ko no rājā bhavediti \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. For the kingdom, there was a great discussion among many demons and fiends: ‘Who would be our king?’

## \|\| 2.18.141-143 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*hiṇyākṣasya ye putrāḥ pautrāśca balavattarāḥ \|*  
*virocanaprabhṛtayaḥ santi ye balavattarāḥ \|\| 141 \|\|*

*vṛṣaparvāpi balavānrājyārthe samupasthitaḥ \|*  
*indravitteśavaruṇā vāyuḥ sūryonalo yamaḥ \|\| 142 \|\|*

*daityena sadṛśā na syurbalarūpakṣamādibhiḥ \|*  
*audāryādiguṇaiḥ kṛtvā santatyā cāsurādhikaḥ \|\| 143 \|\|*

Nārada said:

141-142a.The sons and grandsons of Hiraṇyākṣa, who were stronger, like Virocana and others, so also the strong Vṛṣaparvan, approached for the kingdom.

142b-143. Indra, Kubera, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Sūrya, Anala, Yama, did not resemble the demon in strength, appearance, forgiveness etc. They were superior to the demons in qualities like generosity, and in respect of progeny.

## \|\| 2.18.144 \|\|

*śukreṇā cāryamāṇāste yuddhyaṃte ca parasparam \|*  
*amṛtāharaṇe dauṣṭyaṃ yadā daityāḥ smaranti tat \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. Being instructed by Śukra, they fought with one another. The demons (also) remembered the wickedness (of gods at the time) of snatching the nectar.

## \|\| 2.18.145 \|\|

*pītāvaśeṣamamṛtaṃ kasmādyacchaṃti devatāḥ \|*  
*nāsmākamiti saṃnahya yudhyante ca parasparam \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. “Why do the gods give the nectar that remained after a portion of it the gods drunk”. Saying, “This is not our (share)”, and getting ready they fought with one another.

## \|\| 2.18.146 \|\|

*kadācidapi no yuddhaṃ viśrāṃtimupagacchati \|*  
*ekakāryodyatā yasmādbahavo daityadānavāḥ \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. Our war will never cease, since many demons and fiends were intent on doing one thing only.

## \|\| 2.18.147 \|\|

*pītvā'mṛtaṃ surā jātā amarāste jayanti ca \|*  
*devadānavadaityānāṃ gandharvoragarakṣasām \|*  
*viṣṇurbalādhiko yuddhe tadetatkāraṇaṃ vada \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. Gods, having drunk nectar, have become immortal, and are victorious. Tell me the reason why Viṣṇu is strongest in battle among gods, demons, fiends, Gandharvas, reptiles and evil spirits.

## \|\| 2.18.148-149 \|\|

*vāmana uvāca \|*  
*anādinidhanaḥ karttā pātā harttā janārdanaḥ \|*  
*eko'yaṃ sa śivo devaḥ sa cāyaṃ brahmasaṃjñitaḥ \|*  
*ekasya tu yadā kāryaṃ jāyate bhuvane nṛpa \|\| 148 \|\|*

*tasya dehaṃ samāśritya mṛtyukāryaṃ kurvaṃti te \|*  
*brahmāṃḍaṃ sakalaṃ viṣṇoḥ karadaṃ varado yataḥ \|*  
*tasmādbalādhiko viṣṇurna tathānyo'sti kaścana \|\| 149 \|\|*

Vāmana said:

148-149. Janārdana is without birth and death. He is the doer, the protector, the one that takes away. He is alone, is the god Śiva and he is the one called Brahman. O King, when, in the world, the job of one comes up, the three, taking up his body, do the work of (bringing about) death. Since Viṣṇu is the giver of boons, the entire universe is in his hand. Therefore he is stronger, and none else is like that.

## \|\| 2.18.150 \|\|

*pālanāyodyato viṣṇuḥ kimanyaiścarmacakṣubhiḥ \|*  
*indrādyāśca surāḥ sarve viṣṇorvyāpārakāriṇaḥ \|\| 150 \|\|*

150\. Viṣṇu is ready for protection. What is the use of other physical eyes? And all gods like Indra, work for Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.18.151 \|\|

*sṛṣṭiṃ kṛtvā tato brahmā kailāse saṃsthito haraḥ \|*  
*na śakyate surairviṣṇurbhrāmyante bhuvanatraye \|\| 151 \|\|*

151\. Having fashioned the creation Brahmā-Hara remained in Kailāsa. Gods cannot (control) Viṣṇu. They move in the three worlds

## \|\| 2.18.152 \|\|

*jagatyasminyadā kaścidvaiparītyena vartate \|*  
*tasyocchedaṃ samāgatya karotyeva janārdanaḥ \|\| 152 \|\|*

152\. When in this world someone behaves in an adverse way Janārdana, having come (there) destroys him.

## \|\| 2.18.153 \|\|

*tvamejaya mahābāho na mano nāradā'dayam \|*  
*sarvapāpaharāṃ divyāṃ tāṃ kathāṃ kathayāmyaham \|\| 153 \|\|*

153\. O Nārada, do not make your mind waver or make it unkind. I shall tell that divine tale, which removes all sin.

## \|\| 2.18.154 \|\|

*purā vivadatāṃ teṣāṃ daityānāṃ rājyahetave \|*  
*prahlādena samāgatya vyavasthā vihitā svayam \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. When, formerly the demons were quarrelling for the kingdom, Prahlāda himself came (there) and settled the differences.

## \|\| 2.18.155 \|\|

*sarvalakṣaṇasaṃ panno dīrghāyurbalavattaraḥ \|*  
*yajñaśīlaḥ sadānaṃdo bahuputrotidurjayaḥ \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. He was endowed with all (auspicious) signs, had a long life, and was stronger. He performed sacrifices, was always delighted, had many sons, and was extremely difficult to conquer.

## \|\| 2.18.156 \|\|

*na yudhyate suraiḥ sākaṃ viṣṇuṃ yo vetti durjayam \|*  
*saṃgrāme maraṇaṃ nāsti yasya yaḥ sarvadakṣiṇaḥ \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. He, who knew Viṣṇu difficult to be conquered, did not fight with gods. He did not have death in war, He gave everything as present to Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 2.18.157 \|\|

*ātmano vacanaṃ vyarthaṃ na karoti kathaṃcana \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ putrapautrāṇāṃ madhye yo rājate śriyā \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. He never deceived himself in any way. Among all his sons and grandsons he shone with grandeur.

## \|\| 2.18.158 \|\|

*abhiṣiktastu śukreṇa sa vo rājā bhavediti \|*  
*gurupramāṇamityuktvā yayau yatrāgataḥ punaḥ \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. Śukra consecrated him (saying): “He will be your king”. Saying “The preceptor is the authority” he went wherefrom he had come.

## \|\| 2.18.159 \|\|

*tathā ca kṛtavaṃtaste sahitā daityadānavāḥ \|*  
*virocanaprabhṛtayaḥ putrāḥ pautrāḥ svayaṃgatāḥ \|\| 159 \|\|*

159\. The demons and fiends together did like that. The sons, grandsons like Virocana themselves went.

## \|\| 2.18.160 \|\|

*pratyekaṃ vīkṣitāḥ sarve guruṇā jñānapūrvakam \|*  
*prahlādena guṇāḥ proktā na te saṃti virocane \|\| 160 \|\|*

160\. With (proper) information, all were noticed individually by the preceptor. The virtues mentioned by Prahlāda did not exist in Virocana.

## \|\| 2.18.161 \|\|

*anyeṣāmapi daityānāṃ vṛṣaparvāpi nedṛśaḥ \|*  
*yathā nirīkṣitāḥ putrā baliprabhṛtayo mune \|*  
*sarvānsaṃvīkṣya śukreṇa balau dṛṣṭā guṇāstathā \|\| 161 \|\|*

161\. They were not seen in other demons, Vṛṣaparvan also was not like that. O sage, the sons like Bali were seen, Śukra, having observed all, found more merits in Bali.

## \|\| 2.18.162 \|\|

*balidehe'dhikāndṛṣṭvā daityebhyo viniveditāḥ \|*  
*balirguṇādhiko daityāḥ kathaṃ kāryaṃ bhavenmayā \|\| 162 \|\|*

162\. Seeing more merits in Bali’s person, he reported them to the demons. O demons, Bali is superior in qualities; how would the task be done by me?

## \|\| 2.18.163 \|\|

*kenāpi daivayogena baliriṃdro bhaviṣyati \|*  
*yādṛśastu pitā loke tādṛśastu suto bhavet \|\| 163 \|\|*

163\. Due to some lucky coincidence, Bali will be Indra. The son would be as the father is in the world.

## \|\| 2.18.164 \|\|

*pautraśca niścitaṃ tādṛgbhavatīti na cetsutaḥ \|*  
*prahlādastu mahāyogī vaiṣṇavo viṣṇuvallabhaḥ \|\| 164 \|\|*

164\. Certainly the grandson becomes like (the grandfather) if not the son; and Prahlāda is a great devotee, a follower of Viṣṇu, and dear to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.18.165 \|\|

*tasmādvirocane keciddhiraṇyakaśiporguṇāḥ \|*  
*jyeṣṭho virocano rājye yadi cetkriyate'surāḥ \|*  
*narasiṃhaḥ samāgatya niścitaṃ mārayiṣyati \|\| 165 \|\|*

165\. Therefore, certain qualities of Hiraṇyakaśipu (are) found in Virocana. O demons, if the elder (i.e.) Virocana, is enthroned, (then) Narasiiñha will certainly come and kill (him).

## \|\| 2.18.166 \|\|

*muktaṃ virocanenāpi rājyaṃ maraṇabhīruṇā \|*  
*prahlādasya guṇāḥ sarve balidehe vyavasthitāḥ \|\| 166 \|\|*

166\. Virocana, too, afraid of death, gave up the kingdom. All virtues of Prahlāda exist in Bali’s person.

## \|\| 2.18.167 \|\|

*evaṃ te samayaṃ kṛtvā baliṃ rājye'bhyaṣiṃcaya n \|*  
*yaḥ prahlādaḥ sa vai viṣṇuryo viṣṇuḥ sa baliḥ svayam \|\| 167 \|\|*

167\. Having made an agreement, they enthroned Bali, (thinking) he, who is Prahlāda, is Viṣṇu, and he, who is Viṣṇu, is Bali himself.

## \|\| 2.18.168 \|\|

*ato mitrīkṛto devairvigrahaistu vivarjitaḥ \|*  
*ekībhāvaṃ kṛtaṃ sarvaṃ balirājye surāsuraiḥ \|\| 168 \|\|*

168\. Therefore, gods made him their friend, and quarrel was avoided. The gods and demons made complete unity (among themselves) in Bali’s kingdom.

## \|\| 2.18.169 \|\|

*tasyāpi bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā deveṃdro mama maṃdire \|*  
*samāgatā vālakhilyāḥ śaptohaṃ vāmanaḥ kṛtaḥ \|\| 169 \|\|*

169\. Hearing his words, the king of gods came to my house. Vālakhilyas (divine personages of the size of a thumb) came; I was cursed (and) made a dwarf.

## \|\| 2.18.170 \|\|

*prasādya te mayā proktāḥ śāpamuktipradā mama \|*  
*bhaviṣyatīti tairuktaṃ balinigrahaṇādanu \|\| 170 \|\|*

170\. Having pleased them I said: “Free me from the curse” They said: (They will do so) after the capture of Bali.

## \|\| 2.18.171 \|\|

*tavāpi kautukaṃ yuddhe baliryajñaṃ karoti ca \|*  
*devānāṃ nigraho nāsti sarve yajñe samāgatāḥ \|\| 171 \|\|*

171\. “You will also have joy in the battle, and Bali will perform a sacrifice.” There was no restraint to gods; all came to the sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.18.172 \|\|

*sa māṃ yajati yajñena vadhaṃ tasya karotu kaḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ ca vāmano jāto nāradaḥ kautukānvitaḥ \|\| 172 \|\|*

172\. He offers me a sacrifice, who would kill him. I became a dwarf.

Nārada was full of joy.

## \|\| 2.18.173 \|\|

*viparītamidaṃ sarvaṃ varttate mama cetasi \|*  
*tathā'pi kramayogena sarvaṃ bhavyaṃ karomyaham \|\| 173 \|\|*

173\. All this is topsy turvy in my mind. Yet I shall do everything on a grand scale in due order.

## \|\| 2.18.174 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*prasādaṃ kuru deveśa yuddhārthaṃ kautukaṃ mama \|*  
*ekena brāhmaṇenājau hanyaṃte kṣatriyā yadā \|*  
*pitrā proktaṃ ca me pūrvaṃ tadā yuddhaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 174 \|\|*

Nārada said:

174\. O Lord of gods, (please) favour me. I have a curiosity for war. My father had formerly told me: “A war will take place when in a battle Kṣatriyas are killed by a Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 2.18.175 \|\|

*brāhmaṇosi bhavāñjātaḥ kadā yuddhaṃ kariṣyasi \|*  
*vihasya vāmano brūte satyaṃ tava bhaviṣyati \|\| 175 \|\|*

175\. “You are born as a Brāhmaṇa; whom will you fight?” Vāmana laughed and said: “Your (words) will be true.”

## \|\| 2.18.176 \|\|

*jamadagnisuto bhūtvā guruṃ kṛtvā maheśvaram \|*  
*kārttavīryaṃ vadhiṣyāmi bahubhiḥ kṣatriyaiḥ saha \|\| 176 \|\|*

176\. “Being born as the son of Jamadagni, and having Maheśvara as my preceptor, I shall kill Kārtavīrya, along with many Kṣatriyas.

## \|\| 2.18.177 \|\|

*samaṃtapaṃcake paṃca kariṣye rudhirahradān \|*  
*tatrāhaṃ tarpayiṣyāmi pitṝnatha pitāmahān \|\| 177 \|\|*

177\. “On the Kurukṣetra I shall make five deep lakes of blood. Then I shall gratify my sires and grandsires.

## \|\| 2.18.178 \|\|

*puṇyakṣetraṃ kariṣyāmi bhavāṃstatrāgamiṣya ti \|*  
*paraṃ ca kautukaṃ yuddhe bhaviṣyati tava priyam \|\| 178 \|\|*

178\. “I shall make (it) a holy place; you will come there. There will be a great curiosity for the war. It will be dear to you.

## \|\| 2.18.179 \|\|

*brāhmaṇebhyo grahīṣyaṃti yadā kuṃ kṣatriyāḥ punaḥ \|*  
*tadaiva tānhaniṣyāmi punardā syāmi medinīm \|\| 179 \|\|*

179\. “When the Kṣatriyas will again seize the earth from the Brāhmaṇas, I shall then kill them and will again give (them) the earth.

## \|\| 2.18.180 \|\|

*trisaptavāraṃ dāsyāmi jitvā jitvā vasuṃdharām \|*  
*śastranyāsaṃ kariṣyāmi nirviṇṇo yuddhakarmaṇi \|*  
*vihariṣyāmi ramyeṣu vaneṣu girisānuṣu \|\| 180 \|\|*

180\. “Repeatedly conquering the earth I shall give it (to the Brāhmaṇas) twenty-one times. Disgusted with fighting I shall renounce weapons. I shall divert myself in charming forests, on peaks of mountains.

## \|\| 2.18.181-182 \|\|

*laṃkāyāṃ rāvaṇo rājyaṃ kariṣyati mahābalaḥ \|*  
*trailokyakaṃṭakaṃ nāma yadāsau dhārayiṣyati \|\| 181 \|\|*

*tadā dāśarathī rāmaḥ kausalyānaṃdavarddhanaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣye bhrātṛbhiḥ sārddhaṃ gamiṣye yajñamaṃḍape \|\| 182 \|\|*

181-182. The very powerful Rāvaṇa will rule over laṅkā. When he will have the name ‘Trailokyakaṇṭaka’ (Thom to the three worlds), then Daśaratha’s son Rāma, who increased the joy of Kauśalyā will think: “I shall be with my brothers. I shall enter the sacrificial pavillion.

## \|\| 2.18.183 \|\|

*tāḍakāṃ tāḍayitvāhaṃ subāhuṃ yajñamaṃdire \|*  
*nītvā yajñādgamiṣyāmi sītāyāstu svayaṃvare \|\| 183 \|\|*

183\. “Having beaten up Tāḍakā, and taking Subāhu to the sacrifīce-haH, I shall go for the self-choice marriage of Sītā.

## \|\| 2.18.184 \|\|

*pariṇeṣyābhi tāṃ sītāṃ bhaṃktvā māheśvaraṃ dhanuḥ \|*  
*tyaktvā rājyaṃ gamiṣyāmi vane varṣāṃścaturdaśa \|\| 184 \|\|*

184\. “Having broken Śiva’s bow, I shall marry Sītā. Abandoning the kingdom, I shall go to the forest (and stay) in the forest for fourteen years.

## \|\| 2.18.185 \|\|

*sītāharaṇajaṃ duḥkhaṃ prathamaṃ me bhaviṣyati \|*  
*nāsākarṇavihīnāṃ tāṃ kariṣye rākṣasīṃ vane \|\| 185 \|\|*

185\. “I shall first be grieved by the pain due to Sītā’s being kidnapped. I shall render that demoness bereft of nose and ears, in the forest.

## \|\| 2.18.186 \|\|

*caturddaśasahasrāṇi triśiraḥkharadūṣaṇān \|*  
*dhatvā haniṣye mārīcaṃ rākṣasaṃ mṛgarūpiṇam \|\| 186 \|\|*

186\. “After having killed fourteen thousand demons like Triśirā, Khara and Dūṣaṇa, I shall kill Mārīca, who will be in the guise of a deer.

## \|\| 2.18.187-188 \|\|

*hṛtadāro gamiṣyāmi dagdhvā gṛdhraṃ jaṭāyuṣam \|*  
*sugrīveṇa samaṃ maitrīṃ kṛtvā hatvā'tha vālinam \|\| 187 \|\|*

*samudraṃ baṃdhayiṣyāmi nalapramukhavānaraiḥ \|*  
*laṃkāṃ saṃveṣṭayiṣyāmi mārayiṣyāmi rākṣasān \|\| 188 \|\|*

187-188. “With my wife kidnapped and after having cremated the vulture Jaṭāyu, I shall go (to Sugrīva). Making friendship with Sugrīva, and killing Vālin, I shall restrain the sea with (the help of) the monkeys led by Nala. I shall besiege Laṅkā, and kill demons.

## \|\| 2.18.189-190 \|\|

*kumbhakarṇaṃ nihatyājau meghanādaṃ tato raṇe \|*  
*nihatya rāvaṇaṃ rakṣaḥ paśyatāṃ sarvarakṣasām \|\| 189 \|\|*

*vibhīṣaṇāya dāsyāmi laṃkāṃ devavinirmitām \|*  
*ayodhyāṃ punarāgatya kṛtvā rājyamakaṃṭakam \|\| 190 \|\|*

189-190a. “Having, in the battle, killed Kumbhakarṇa and then Meghanāda, and having killed the demon Rāvaṇa in the presence of all demons I shall give Laṅkā, the divine creation, to Bibhīṣaṇa.

190b. “Having come back to Ayodhyā again, and ruling the kingdom void of troublesome elements,

## \|\| 2.18.191 \|\|

*kāladurvāsasościtracaritreṇāmarāvatīm \|*  
*yāsyehaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ sārddhaṃ rājyaṃ putre nivedya ca \|\| 191 \|\|*

191\. the strange acts of Kāla and Durvāsas I shall go to Amarāvatī with my brothers, after handing over the kingdom to my son.

## \|\| 2.18.192 \|\|

*dvāpare samanuprāpte kṣatriyairbahubhirmahī \|*  
*bhārākrāṃtā na śaknoti pātālaṃ gaṃtumudyatā \|\| 192 \|\|*

192\. “When the Dvāpara age will arrive, the earth will be burdened by many Kṣatriyas and will not be able (to bear the burden) and will be on the verge of going to the nether world.

## \|\| 2.18.193-194 \|\|

*mathurāyāṃ tadā karttā kaṃso rājyaṃ mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*śiśupālajarāsaṃdhau kālanemirmahāsuraḥ \|\| 193 \|\|*

*pauṃḍrako vāsudevaśca bāṇo rājā mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*gajavājituraṃgāḍhyā vadhyaṃte me tadā mune \|\| 194 \|\|*

193-194. “At that time the great demon Kaṃsa would be ruling over Mathurā. Śiśupāla, Jarāsandha, the great demon Kālanemi, (Kings) Pauṇḍraka, Vāsudeva, the great demon-king Bāṇa, equipped with elephants, swift horses, will be killed by me, O sage.

## \|\| 2.18.195 \|\|

*kalau svalpodakā meghā alpadugdhāśca dhenavaḥ \|*  
*dugdhe ghṛtaṃ na caivāsti nāsti satyaṃ janeṣu ca \|\| 195 \|\|*

195\. “In the Kali age clouds would have scanty water, and cows would have little milk. There will be no ghee (contents) in milk, and no truth among people.

## \|\| 2.18.196 \|\|

*corairupahatā lokā vyādhibhiḥ paripīḍitāḥ \|*  
*trātāraṃ nābhi gacchaṃti yuddhāvasthāṃ gatā api \|\| 196 \|\|*

196\. “People would be kilted by thieves and harassed by diseases. Though reduced to the plight of waging war they would not go to a preceptor.

## \|\| 2.18.197 \|\|

*kṣudrāḥ paścimavāhinyo nadyaḥ śuṣyaṃti kārttike \|*  
*ekādaśīvrataṃ nāsti kṛṣṇā yā ca caturddaśī \|\| 197 \|\|*

197\. “Small rivers, flowing westwards would get dry in Kārttika. No vow like Ekādaśī would be (observed), and no Caturdaśī that falls in the dark half (of the month).

## \|\| 2.18.198 \|\|

*na jānāti janaḥ kaścidvikrāṃtamapi sve gṛhe \|*  
*daridropahataṃ sarvaṃ saṃdhyāsnānavivarjitam \|*  
*bhaviṣyati kalau sarvaṃ na tatpūrvayugatraye \|\| 198 \|\|*

198\. “No man recognised, even a hero, in his own house. Everything will be affected by poverty, bereft of bath, prayer etc. In Kaliyuga, what did not take place in the former three yugas, will take place.

## \|\| 2.18.199 \|\|

*pitaraṃ mātaraṃ putrastyaktvā bhāryāṃ niṣevate \|*  
*na guruḥ svajanaḥ kaścitko'pi kaṃ nānusevate \|\| 199 \|\|*

199\. “A son would abandon his father, mother and would wait upon his wife. None would be (looked upon as) an elder or a relative. Nobody would Serve anyone else.

## \|\| 2.18.200 \|\|

*yathāyathā kalirvyāptiṃ karoti dharaṇītale \|*  
*tathātathā janaḥ sarva ekākāro bhaviṣyati \|\| 200 \|\|*

200\. “As Kali would spread over the earth, people would be of the same type.

## \|\| 2.18.201 \|\|

*mlecchairupahataṃ sarvaṃ saṃdhyāsnānavivarjitam \|*  
*kalkirityabhivikhyāto bhaviṣye brāhmaṇo hyaham \|\| 201 \|\|*

201\. “Everything would be affected by Mlecchaas (non-Āryans) and would be without bath or prayers. I shall be well known as the Brāhmaṇa Kalki.

## \|\| 2.18.202 \|\|

*mlecchānāṃ chedanaṃ kṛtvā yājñavalyapurohitaḥ \|*  
*bahusvarṇena yajñena yakṣye niṣkṛtikāraṇāt \|\| 202 \|\|*

202\. “With Yājñavalkya as ray family priest, I, having cut off the Mlecchas, would perform a sacrifice with profuse gold (as the gift to Brāhmaṇas) as expiation.

## \|\| 2.18.203 \|\|

*bhaviṣyaṃtyavatārā me yuddhaṃ teṣu bhaviṣyati \|*  
*idānīṃ balinā yuddhaṃ kariṣyaṃti na devatāḥ \|\| 203 \|\|*

203\. “I shall have incarnations and there will take place fights among them. Now deities will not wage war with Bali.

## \|\| 2.18.204 \|\|

*sa māṃ yajati daityendro na me vadhyo balirbhavet \|*  
*sarvasvadānaniyamaṃ karoti sa mahādhvare \|\| 204 \|\|*

204\. “That Lord of demons offers sacrifices to me. Bali will not be killed by me. He takes a vow to give away all his belongings in a great sacrifice.”

## \|\| 2.18.205 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā nāradaṃ devo visṛjya tamathābhyagāt \|*  
*draṣṭuṃ balikṛtaṃ yajñaṃ devakāryaprasiddhaye \|\| 205 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

205\. Saying so, the god, having dismissed Nārada, went to see the sacrifice performed by Bali, with the mission of gods in view.

## \|\| 2.18.206 \|\|

*vāmano nagaraṃ gatvā vīkṣamāṇo gṛhādgṛham \|*  
*brāhmaṇānāṃ gṛhaṃ gatvā bhojanaṃ sa tu yācate \|\| 206 \|\|*

206\. Vāmana went to the city and visited every house. Going to the house of Brāhmaṇas, he asked for a meal.

## \|\| 2.18.207 \|\|

*nityaṃ snānaparo vipro vedādhyayanatatparaḥ \|*  
*vāmano labhate bhikṣāṃ bhojanaṃ dvijamaṃdire \|\| 207 \|\|*

207\. The Brāhmaṇa Vāmana, intent on bathing everyday and on Vedic studies, obtained alms and a meal in a Brāhmaṇa’s house.

## \|\| 2.18.208 \|\|

*catuṣpatheṣu ramyeṣu devatāyataneṣu ca \|*  
*āste parivṛto lokaiścālayanvipulāṃ kaṭim \|\| 208 \|\|*

208\. Moving his broad waist, he, surrounded by people, went to path crossings and charming temples.

## \|\| 2.18.209 \|\|

*śiro vidhūnate sthūlaṃ sthūlaskandho mahāhanuḥ \|*  
*nṛtyate tālamānena gāyatyatimanoharam \|\| 209 \|\|*

209\. He, of broad shoulders and large chin, moved his large head; he danced rhythmically and sang very charmingly.

## \|\| 2.18.210-211 \|\|

*vedānadhīte caturo vāmano dvijasaṃsadi \|*  
*daityānāṃ tanayāḥ sarve brāhmaṇānāṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 210 \|\|*

*vāmanaṃ paryupāsaṃte divārātraṃ manoramam \|*  
*atha taiḥ sakalairnīto vāmano yajñamaṃḍape \|\| 211 \|\|*

210-21 la. Vāmana recited the four Vedas in the assembly of Brāhmaṇas. All the sons of Brāhmaṇas, as well as of the demons, waited upon the charming Vāmana day and night.

211b. Then all of them took Vāmana to the pavilion of the sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.18.212 \|\|

*niścitaṃ maṭhikāsthānaṃ yācitavyo balistvayā \|*  
*tadāsmākaṃ mahacchreyo deśasya nagarasya ca \|\| 212 \|\|*

212\. You should certainly implore Bali in the cell of the demons. Then the great good of the country and the city (will follow).

## \|\| 2.18.213 \|\|

*vijñapto vāmanaḥ sarvairdaityadvijakumārakaiḥ \|*  
*vāmana vastavyaṃ daityeṃdranagare sadā \|\| 213 \|\|*

213\. Vāmana was requested by all the sons of demons and Brāhmaṇas: “O Vāmana, you should always stay in the city of the Lord of demons.”

## \|\| 2.18.214 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*praviveśa tathetyuktvā vāmano yajñamaṃḍape \|*  
*tataḥ kolāhalo jāto dvāḥsthairdvāri kṛto mahān \|\| 214 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

214\. Saying “Let it be so” Vāmana entered the sacrificial pavillion. Then a great tumult caused by those that were at the door, arose.

## \|\| 2.18.215 \|\|

*brāhmaṇairbahubhiḥ sārddhaṃ vedānuccārayansthitaḥ \|*  
*tato vedadhvanirjāto mahānvai yajñamaṃḍapre \|\| 215 \|\|*

215\. He remained reciting the Vedas along with many Brāhmaṇas. Then a great sound (of the recitation) of the Vedas arose in the sacrificial pavilion.

## \|\| 2.18.216 \|\|

*praviṣṭau prathamaṃ daityau daityāya viniveditaḥ \|*  
*draṣṭuṃ samāgato deva brāhmaṇo vāmano'dhvare \|\| 216 \|\|*

216\. First a demon entered (the pavilion). The demon (king) was informed: “O Lord, Vāmana, out of curiosity, has come at the (place of the) sacrifice to see you.

## \|\| 2.18.217-218 \|\|

*bhavaṃtaṃ kautukāttāvaddvāradeśe samāviśat \|*  
*eka eva yathāyāti vāmanastava sannidhau \|\| 217 \|\|*

*nirīho vāmano deva yāvattatraiva kiṃcana \|*  
*vedānāṃ tu dhvaniṃ kṛtvā caturṇāmekavaktrataḥ \|\| 218 \|\|*

217-218. “He is sitting at the gate. Since Vāmana is coming to you all alone, he has no design. He has recited the four Vedas with one mouth.”

## \|\| 2.18.219 \|\|

*balirhṛṣṭo'bravīdvākyaṃ dvāḥsthamenaṃ praveśaya \|*  
*pūjayiṣyāmi vipredraṃ dāsye cāsya yadīpsitam \|\| 219 \|\|*

219\. Being delighted, Bali said: “Bring him in, who is at the door. I shall worship that Lord of Brāhmaṇas, and will give him whatever is desired by him.

## \|\| 2.18.220 \|\|

*smarāmi smṛtivākyāni yāni prāha gururmama \|*  
*kiṃcidvedamayaṃ pātraṃ kiṃcitpātraṃ tapomayam \|\| 220 \|\|*

220\. “I shall recollect the sentences from the Smṛtis, which my preceptor had spoken to me. Someone is worthy of the Veda, someone of penance.

## \|\| 2.18.221 \|\|

*āgamiṣyati yatpātraṃ tatpātraṃ tārayiṣyati \|*  
*yajñe pravarttamāne tu dātavyā dakṣiṇā mayā \|\| 221 \|\|*

221\. “Whichever worthy recipient will arrive, will save me. When the sacrifice proceeds, I have to give Dakṣiṇā.

## \|\| 2.18.222 \|\|

*vāmano na vicāryastu satyamastu vaco mama \|*  
*iti śrutvā guruḥ śukro vārayāmāsa taṃ balim \|\| 222 \|\|*

222\. “Vāmana should not be questioned. Let my words be true.” Hearing this preceptor Śukra prevented Bali.

## \|\| 2.18.223 \|\|

*śukra uvāca \|*  
*dvāri pūjyā dvijāḥ saveṃ dīnāṃdha kṛpaṇādayaḥ \|*  
*badhirā vāmanāḥ kubjā rogiṇo ye tu niṣṭhurāḥ \|\| 223 \|\|*

Śukra said:

223\. All Brāhmaṇas, that are pitiable, blind, poor, deaf, dwarf, hunch-backed, sick, rough should be honoured at the door.

## \|\| 2.18.224 \|\|

*suvarṇarajatairvastrairvāmano dvāri pūjyatām \|*  
*caturṇāṃ tu vṛthā janma vṛthā dānāni ṣoḍaśa \|\| 224 \|\|*

224\. Vāmana should be worshipped at the door with golden, silver garments. The birth of the four is useless; so also the gift of the sixteen kinds is in vain.

## \|\| 2.18.225 \|\|

*aputrāṇāṃ vṛthā janma ye ca dharmabahiṣkṛtāḥ \|*  
*parapākaṃ ca yeśnaṃti paradāraratāśca ye \|\| 225 \|\|*

225\. The birth of sonless persons, so also of those who are expelled from the religious fold, and of those who eat food cooked by others, who are fondly attached to other’s wives, is useless.

## \|\| 2.18.226 \|\|

*anyāyenārjitaṃ vittaṃ na deyaṃ śreya icchatā \|*  
*vyarthamabrāhmaṇe dānamārūḍhapatite tathā \|\| 226 \|\|*

226\. One desiring good should not give wealth (in charity) which is earned unjustly, so also gift given to a non-Brāhmaṇa, so also to one who has fallen after having ascended (the course of morality).

## \|\| 2.18.227-229 \|\|

*saṃdhyāhīne dvije naṣṭe patite taskare tathā \|*  
*guroścāprītijanake pitṛmātṛparāṅmukhe \|\| 227 \|\|*

*brahmabandhau ca yaddataṃ yaddattaṃ vṛṣalīpatau \|*  
*vedavikrayake caiva kṛtaghne grāmayājake \|\| 228 \|\|*

*strīnirjite ca yaddattaṃ vyālagrāhe tathaiva ca \|*  
*parivāreṣu yaddattaṃ vṛthā dānāni ṣoḍaśa \|\| 229 \|\|*

227-229. The sixteen gifts are useless to a Brāhmaṇa: not performing Sandhyā, to one who has ceased to be a Brāhmaṇa, to one that is fallen, to a thief also, to one displeasing one’s preceptors, to one who has turned away from his father and mother, to one who is a Brāhmaṇa in name only, to one who is the husband of a Śūdra woman, to one who sells the Vedas, to one who is ungrateful, to a Brāhmaṇa who conducts religious ceremonies for all classes, to one who is completely subdued by a woman, so also to a snake-catcher; so also gifts given to attendants: these gifts of sixteen kinds are in vain.

## \|\| 2.18.230 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*atrāṃtare balirbrūte naivaṃ vācyaṃ tvayā guro \|*  
*vedānadhīte yaḥ kaścitsa me viṣṇuḥ samāgataḥ \|\| 230 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

230\. In the meanwhile, Bali said: “O preceptor, (please) do not say so. Whosoever studies Vedas is Viṣṇu that has come to me. When a learned Brāhmaṇa has come to (one’s) house, no delay should be done. He should be honoured by standing (before him), by (respectful) words, and by washing his feet.”

## \|\| 2.18.231-233 \|\|

*na vilaṃbastu karttavyaḥ śrotriye gṛhamāgate \|*  
*abhyutthānena vacasā pādaprakṣālanena ca \|\| 231 \|\|*

*yathā śaktyā pradātavyaṃ bhojanaṃ gṛhamedhinā \|*  
*apūjito yadā yāti vāmano maṃḍapādbahiḥ \|\| 232 \|\|*

*tadāyaṃ vyarthatāṃ yāti yajñaḥ sarvasvadakṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*atrāṃtare samānīto vāmano balisaṃnidhau \|\| 233 \|\|*

231-233a. “A householder should offer him a meal according to his capacity. If Vāmana goes out of the (sacrificial) pavilion without being honoured, then the sacrifice in which (even) everything is given as a gift is useless.”

233b. In the meanwhile Vāmana was brought into the vicinity of Bali.

## \|\| 2.18.234 \|\|

*āyāṃtaṃ dadṛśe daityo vāmanaṃ viṣṇurūpiṇam \|*  
*jājvalyamānaṃ vapuṣā piṃgalaṃ sūryasaṃnibham \|\| 234 \|\|*

234\. From within the body of Vāmana, the image of Viṣṇu was shining like the golden sun, when Bali, the king of demons, saw him arriving.

## \|\| 2.18.235 \|\|

*utthāyābhimukhaḥ prāyānnamaskṛtyāgrataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*dhanyo'haṃ yasya me yajñe prāpto viṣṇusamo dvijaḥ \|\| 235 \|\|*

235\. Getting up he went up to Vāmana and said, “I am fortunate and blessed to have the presence of Viṣṇu-like Brāhmaṇa in my yajña.”

## \|\| 2.18.236 \|\|

*vedimadhye samānīto dadau tasyāsanaṃ baliḥ \|*  
*pādyamācamanīyaṃ ca dattvārghyaṃ viṣṭaraṃ baliḥ \|*  
*śrīkhaṃḍagaṃdhapuṣpādyaiḥ pūjayitvāgrataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 236 \|\|*

236\. Conducting him to the elevated ground meant for the sacrificial ritual Bali respectfully received him, made him to sip water from the palms, presented to him flowers and perfumes, put the (auspicious) mark on his forehead and offered him the seat of presiding Brāhmaṇa at the Yajña.

## \|\| 2.18.237 \|\|

*madhuparkaṃ ca gāṃ tasmai satvaraṃ sa nivedya ca \|*  
*āghrāte madhuparke ca vāmanena tataḥ param \|\| 237 \|\|*

237\. Then Bali offered him sandal, a garland, cow and Madhuparka (a mixture containing quantities of five ingredients like milk, honey, curd, clarified butter, and cow’s urine etc.). When Vāmana acknowledged the smell of the same mixture, Bali welcomed him.

## \|\| 2.18.238-240 \|\|

*svāgataṃ balinā proktaṃ svastītyuktaṃ dvijanmanā \|*  
*ahamarthī samāyāto dīyatāṃ vada kiṃ vibho \|\| 238 \|\|*

*medinīṃ dehi me daitya kiyanmātrāṃ dvijottama \|*  
*vāsārthaṃ mama daityendra dīyatāṃ me krama trayam \|\| 239 \|\|*

*vidhāya maṭhikāṃ divyāṃ śiṣyānadhyāpayāmyaham \|*  
*dattaṃ kramatrayaṃ tubhyaṃ gṛhītaṃ vāmano'bravīt \|\| 240 \|\|*

238-240. After his welcome by Bali, the Brāhmaṇa blessed him. Bali in turn asked, “O best Brāhmaṇa! What can I give you? For me, a demon on earth, it is a trivial matter.” The Brāhmaṇa said, “Give me a piece of land measuring three steps only for my dwelling. I will build a hut on it to impart knowledge to the disciples”. Bali said, “I have already given you the land as per your stipulation”, to which Vāmana replied as having already accepted.

## \|\| 2.18.241 \|\|

*mā dehītyavadacchukro viṣṇureva sanātanaḥ \|*  
*hṛṣṭo brūte baliḥ śukraṃ pātraṃ syātkimataḥ param \|\| 241 \|\|*

241\. Śukrācārya said: “Do not give him the piece of land as he is the same old Viṣṇu.” Glad to know this, Bali said, “Then who else could be a greater ascetic than him to deserve this gift of mine?”

## \|\| 2.18.242 \|\|

*savyaṃ kṛtvā balirdarbhānsākṣatāndakṣiṇe kare \|*  
*prayogaṃ na guruścakre na muṃcati jalaṃ kare \|\| 242 \|\|*

242\. Then adopting an upright posture Bali took Akṣata (whole rice grains) along with the sacred grass Kuśa in his right hand. Śukrācārya then pronounced the invocation without dropping the water from his palm.

## \|\| 2.18.243-245 \|\|

*vismitā ṛṣayaḥ sarve hotāro ye sabhāsadaḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇā baṭavo daityā bhāryāputrāśca bāṃdhavāḥ \|\| 243 \|\|*

*dattaṃ gṛhītamityukte kasmāttoyaṃ na muñcati \|*  
*vāmanāya kare toyaṃ vivekāya pradīyate \|\| 244 \|\|*

*yaddānaṃ vacasā dattaṃ karmaṇā nopapādyate \|*  
*vidhāya narake pūye yajamānaṃ na niṣkṛtiḥ \|\| 245 \|\|*

243-245. Then all the sages, priests and other members in the assembly including Bali’s wife, sons and his kith and kin became amazed at the sight as to why water was not dropped from the palm after the very act of giving and receiving of the gift. Water was taken in the palm of Vāmana for the sake of truth and knowledge. A gift given by words of mouth, if not carried out into action, will, as per law, drop the priest into hell and nothing will extricate him from this.

## \|\| 2.18.246-248 \|\|

*uśanā prāha daityendra vāmano harirityayam \|*  
*kenāpi daivayogena tvāṃ draṣṭuṃ samupāgataḥ \|\| 246 \|\|*

*apriyaṃ vā priyaṃ vāpi na jāne kiṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*babhāṣe bhārgavaṃ yaṣṭā śrūyatāṃ vacanaṃ guro \|\| 247 \|\|*

*procyate dānakāleṣu yajamānairdvijairapi \|*  
*ahamindro dvijo viṣṇurdravyamādityadevatā \|*  
*tatkathaṃ na mayā deyaṃ viṣṇave prīyatāmiti \|\| 248 \|\|*

246-248. Śukrācārya told the demon king Bali, “This Vāmana is really Viṣṇu. Fortunately he has arrived in your house and I do not know what good or bad is he going to do”. Then Bali, the performer of the yajña, told Śukrācārya, “O Venerable preceptor Śukrācārya! Listen attentively to what I say. At the time of my giving the gift, the priests and the Brāhmaṇas have been heard as saying that I am as powerful as the water gift-giver Indra. This Brāhmaṇa, the receiver of gift, is like Viṣṇu. The Sun-God, himself is the heavenly substance. So why should I not gift for the sake of my love for Lord Viṣṇu?”

## \|\| 2.18.249 \|\|

*ityuktvā sa dadau toyaṃ vāmanāya kare baliḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kimidamityuktvā saṃsthito maṇḍapādbahiḥ \|\| 249 \|\|*

249\. Having said so, King Bali put water into the palm of Vāmana as a means of invocation. Soon after having said how could this happen, Śukrācārya stepped out of the pavilion.

## \|\| 2.18.250-252 \|\|

*madhye'pi vāmano vipro balimātro vabhūva saḥ \|*  
*dattahasto'surendreṇa grahītuṃ tu padatrayam \|\| 250 \|\|*

*yajamānadvijau haṣṭau dṛṣṭau yajñe surādibhiḥ \|*  
*vavṛdhe vāmanotīva kṛtvā rūpaṃ caturbhujam \|\| 251 \|\|*

*nārado'pi samāyāto babhāṣe ki kṛtaṃ bale \|*  
*śiṣyābhyāṃ sahito hṛṣṭo narīnarti puraḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 252 \|\|*

250-252. In the meantime, the Brāhmaṇa Vāmana also became like King Bali. Accepting the three steps of land offered by King Bali both of them became pleased in the pavilion of yajña which the heavenly beings and others happened to see. Then assuming the body of the four-armed Viṣṇu, Vāmana began to increase in size and shape.

## \|\| 2.18.252 \|\|

*nārado'pi samāyāto babhāṣe ki kṛtaṃ bale \|*  
*śiṣyābhyāṃ sahito hṛṣṭo narīnarti puraḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 252 \|\|*

252\. Nārada arrived at the same time and expressed in wonder, “O Bali! How could you do this!” He also began to dance with pleasure along with the disciples.

## \|\| 2.18.253-254 \|\|

*gṛhāṇa dakṣiṇāṃ deva sabhāryo bhāṣate baliḥ \|*  
*adya kiṃ na mayā prāptaṃ yadgṛhṇāti janārddanaḥ \|\| 253 \|\|*

*sārddhakramakṣayaṃ kṛtvā dharaṇīṃ yācate trayam \|*  
*yadasti tena kartavyaḥ santoṣo madhusūdana \|\| 254 \|\|*

253-254. Along with wife Bali said, “O Sir! accept your sacrificial fee. What have I not got today when Viṣṇu is accepting gift from me! Having walked one and a half steps on the earth, Viṣṇu is asking for only three steps of land. However, as per duty I have tried to satisfy him.” (sārdha-kramakṣayam; obscure) 255-258. Seeing the Vāmana increasing in size, the Brāhmaṇas, the sages and the demons spoke among themselves that the God was rising to the sky. The heavenly beings and the sages said, “O heavenly soul, O unending one, O imperishable one, O Viṣṇu, Victory to you! Victory to you in the form of Turtle, the bearer of the earth! Our homage to you, the Earth-bearer Boar and the Man-lion! We bow down before you, the son of Jamadagni, Rāma, and to you in the form of Lakṣmaṇa. Victory to you, O Lord Kṛṣṇa, O Lord of the universe, O son of Devakī. We bow down to you, O Buddha, O Kṛṣṇa, O one Kalkin.”

## \|\| 2.18.259 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*narīnarti tathā stauti nārado gaganaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*yoginaḥ sanakādyā ye stuvaṃti ca janārdanam \|\| 259 \|\|*

259\. Sārasvata said, “Wandering in the sky, Nārada was engrossed in hymns of praise. The Yogīs like Sanaka etc. were also singing hymns in praise of Janārdana.”

## \|\| 2.18.260 \|\|

*antarikṣe gate kṛṣṇe varddhamāne baleḥ puraḥ \|*  
*ūrdhvavaktrāḥ sthitāḥ sarve nirī kṣante divākaram \|\| 260 \|\|*

260\. Thus Vāmana was seen rising to the sky in front of Bali. Raising their faces, all looked up towards the Sun in the sky.

## \|\| 2.18.261 \|\|

*dṛṣṭacchatrākṛtistāvatpaścādūrdhvaṃ gato hariḥ \|*  
*cūḍāmaṇirivābhāti bhāskaro harimastake \|\| 261 \|\|*

261\. Rising high up, Vāmana was seen in the shape of an umbrella and then the Sun appeared shining like a jewel on his head.

## \|\| 2.18.262 \|\|

*daityairnirīkṣitaḥ samyaglalāṭe tilakāyate \|*  
*hariḥ saṃvarddhate yāvatkarṇe'sau kuṇḍalāyate \|\| 262 \|\|*

262\. The demons saw the Sun-god appearing like an auspicious mark on the forehead of the God and like an earring on the person of the still rising Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.18.263 \|\|

*varddhamānasya ca harerhṛdaye kaustubhāyate \|*  
*iṃdrādyā devatā rudrā vasavo gagane sthitāḥ \|\| 263 \|\|*

263\. The Sun was appearing like the suspended jewel Kaustubha on the chest of Viṣṇu, still growing in size, while all the other Divinities viz. Indra, Rudra, Vasus etc. were present in the sky.

## \|\| 2.18.264-265 \|\|

*ūrdhvaṃ punaryatra harirna tatra gaganaṃ matam \|*  
*vanamālā tadā kaṇṭhe vāsavena niveśitā \|\| 264 \|\|*

*pṛthivī kampate sarvā divisthaṃ sūryamaṇḍalam \|*  
*kiṃ bhaviṣyati daityāste bhītāḥ paśyaṃti bhāskaram \|\| 265 \|\|*

264-265. Now Viṣṇu had increased himself to such a height that he had risen beyond the sky. Indra had put a garland around his neck. There were tremors in the entire earth and in the solar system in the sky. Anticipating with fear as to what was going to happen, the demons were looking at the Sun.

## \|\| 2.18.266 \|\|

*nābhau padmāyate sūryaḥ kaṭau ca raśanāyate \|*  
*evaṃ saṃvarddhito viṣṇurjagṛhe ca padadvayam \|\| 266 \|\|*

266\. Like a Lotus on the orb of his navel, the Sun was shining like an ornament on his waist belt. Growing in size in this way Viṣṇu measured and accepted two steps of land.

## \|\| 2.18.267 \|\|

*sthānaṃ nāsti tṛtīyasya brahmāṃḍaṃ sakalaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*ahardaṇḍo jagatsraṣṭā brahmadaṃḍāyate tadā \|\| 267 \|\|*

267\. Now that the entire universe had been measured and exhausted, no scope was left over for the third step. It thus appeared that the creator of the universe deserved punishment or Brahmā had transformed itself in the form of punishment.

## \|\| 2.18.268 \|\|

*devadānava gaṃdharvamanuṣyoragapannagaiḥ \|*  
*pūjyate caraṇo viṣṇoḥ stūyate cānumīyate \|\| 268 \|\|*

268\. It appeared that gods, demons, Gandharvas, Nāgas and Sarpas and demons all were worshipping the feet of Viṣṇu and uttering hymns in praise.

## \|\| 2.18.269 \|\|

*dharmātmā yatadaṇḍo hi gaṃdharvairgīyate muhuḥ \|*  
*jyotiścakrākṣadaṃḍaḥ kiṃ hariṇā nirmitaḥ svayam \|\| 269 \|\|*

269\. The Heavenly Musicians (Gandharvas) were singing, treating it as a punishment befallen as a matter of moral duty or it could be the punishment of Gods’ own creation like the pervading light.

## \|\| 2.18.270 \|\|

*jitvedaṃ bhuvanaṃ gaṃgā dhvajadaṃḍo'maraiḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*trivikramāṃghridaṇḍo'yaṃ kīrtidaṃḍāyate dhruvam \|\| 270 \|\|*

270\. In any case, the Gods have won the earth and they have created their punishment by bringing Gaṅgā on earth as their flagstaff. In this way, the three steps of Viṣṇu are certainly the action with an eye to punishment.

## \|\| 2.18.271 \|\|

*vegenākṣipya hariṇā nīto brahmāṃḍamastake \|*  
*pādastanmastakaṃ bhittvā bahiryāsyati vegataḥ \|\| 271 \|\|*

271\. It appeared, as if Hari had thrown up the universe on the head with a jerk and this leg had come out tearing apart the head of universe.

## \|\| 2.18.272 \|\|

*tāvadbrahmāṃḍavego'yaṃ virāḍiti hi saṃjñitaḥ \|*  
*sa sarva bījarūpo hi paramātmeti gadyate \|\| 272 \|\|*

272\. The working and momentum of the universe derived from that force is called by the name ‘Virāṭ’ and that which is the seed of all is said to be Paramātman (the supreme soul).

## \|\| 2.18.273 \|\|

*tenedaṃ sakalaṃ jātaṃ pādasyāgre vyavasthitam \|*  
*brahmāṃḍabhedanaṃ kṛtvā na gantavyaṃ bahistvayā \|\| 273 \|\|*

273\. ‘That’ from which the ‘Whole’ with its ‘parts’ is born is there before your feet. Having pierced the universe you should not have come out.

## \|\| 2.18.274 \|\|

*tenaiva saha brahmāṃḍe paphāla caraṇo hareḥ \|*  
*brahmāṃḍaṃ jarjaraṃ jātaṃ pādasaṃkocanādapi \|\| 274 \|\|*

274\. By your feet, the universe has been cleft open and with its contraction it is getting worn out and injured.

## \|\| 2.18.275 \|\|

*bhinne tasminsamāyātaṃ brāhmaṃ toyaṃ jagattraye \|*  
*viṣṇupādodbhavā gaṃgā mastakānniḥsṛtā tadā \|\| 275 \|\|*

275\. On account of its breaking and subsequentally due to the broken parts coming together streams of water have originated in the three worlds. That is how, while originating from the feet of Viṣṇu, Gaṅgā is flowing from the summit.

## \|\| 2.18.276 \|\|

*trailokyaplāvinī devī yā rudreṇa svayaṃ dhṛtā \|*  
*svardhunī pūjyate svarge gaṃgeti gāṃ gatā satī \|\| 276 \|\|*

276\. The river purifying the three worlds was borne by Śiva (on his head). This heavenly river said to be Gaṅgā in the material world is also worshipped in the heavenly world.

## \|\| 2.18.277 \|\|

*pātāle sā yadā prāptā khyātā tripathagaiva sā \|*  
*yasyāḥ smaraṇamātreṇa sarvapāpakṣayo bhavet \|\| 277 \|\|*

277\. This Gaṅgā has also gone to the nether world. Hence it is called Tripathagā (one flowing in three paths). All sins get destroyed by simply remembering it.

## \|\| 2.18.278 \|\|

*darśanādaśvamedhasya saṃpūrṇasya phalaṃ labhet \|*  
*snānamātreṇa naśyeta saptajanmakṛtaṃ tvagham \|\| 278 \|\|*

278\. The fruits of Aśvamedha Yajña (horse sacrifice) accrued to humans by a simple sight of it. Sins of seven past lives get destroyed by taking a bath in it.

## \|\| 2.18.279 \|\|

*snātvā saṃpūjayedyastu devau hariharau naraḥ \|*  
*indralokamatikramya viṣṇuloke mahīyate \|\| 279 \|\|*

279\. A man who after taking bath in the river Gaṅgā worships Viṣṇu and Śiva, attains the highest world of Viṣṇu after crossing over the world of Indra.

## \|\| 2.18.280 \|\|

*viṣṇupādodakaṃ pītvā jñātvā tattvāni saṃyamī \|*  
*upoṣya divasaṃ viṣṇormuktiṃ gacchati dehavān \|\| 280 \|\|*

280\. A self-controlled man, despite bearing the body, obtains knowledge of reality and liberaton \[liberation?\] by drinking the waters of Gaṅgā and following it up with a single day’s fast for Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.18.281 \|\|

*śuddhasvabhāvasattvasthā viraktā janmabhūmiṣu \|*  
*saṃsārabaṃdhanaṃ chittvā yāti te paramāṃ gatim \|\| 281 \|\|*

281\. The detached ones free from attachment for the place of their birth, having pure nature and striving in Sattva-guṇa attain the highest status (i.e. liberation) cutting off the bond of the world.

## Chapter 19 - Dialogue between Sārasvata and Bhoja

## \|\| 2.19.1 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*gṛhītvā dakṣiṇāṃ daityānmahāviṣṇurjanārdanaḥ \|\| \|*  
*cakāra kiṃ mamācakṣva paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me \|\| 1 \|\|*

King (Bhoja) said:

1\. Tell me what did the great Viṣṇu do after taking the sacrificial fee in this manner? I have a great curiosity.

## \|\| 2.19.2 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ stutaḥ surairdevo gṛhītvā medinīṃ hariḥ \|*  
*baliṃ nirvāsayāmāsa saṃpūrṇe yajñakarmaṇi \|*  
*yajñāṃte dakṣiṇāṃ labdhvā saṃpūrṇo'bhūdathādhvaraḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sārasvata said:

2\. After the hymns of praises sung by the heavenly beings for the land-receiver Viṣṇu, he expelled King Bali from the ritual of Yajña. This way the Yajña came to an end after the receipt of sacrificial fee.

## \|\| 2.19.3-4 \|\|

*bhagavānapyasaṃpūrṇe tṛtīye tu krame vibhuḥ \|*  
*samabhyetya baliṃ prāha īṣatprasphuritādharaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*ṛṇe bhavati daityendra baṃdhanaṃ ghoradarśanam \|*  
*tvaṃ pūraya padaṃ tanme nocedbandhaṃ pratīccha bhoḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. With the third step of the God remaining unfulfilled, the God opened his mouth and with the lower lip slightly twitching told King Bali, “With debts unrepaid, bondage becomes dreadful. Hence, you better fulfill my third step or else get tied up to my fetters.”

## \|\| 2.19.5-11 \|\|

*tanmurārivacaḥ śrutvā puro bhūtvā baleḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*bāṇo vāmanamācaṣṭe tadā taṃ viśvarūpiṇam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kṛtvā mahīmalpatarāṃ vapuḥ kṛtvā tu vāmanam \|*  
*padatrayaṃ yācayitvā viśvarūpamagāḥ katham \|\| 6 \|\|*

*yadi tṛtīyaṃ kramaṇaṃ yācase jagadīśvara \|*  
*punarvāmanatāṃ yāhi balirdāsyati tatpadam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*yādṛgvidhāya balinā vāmanāyodakaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*tattādṛśāya dātavyamatha kiṃ viśvarūpiṇe \|\| 8 \|\|*

*bhavatkṛtamidaṃ viśvaṃ viśvasminvartate baliḥ \|*  
*chadmanā naiva gṛhṇanti sādhavo ye maheśvara \|\| 9 \|\|*

*jagadetajjagannātha tāvakaṃ yadi manyase \|*  
*jñātvā balimamaryādaṃ bhavadbhaktiparāṅmukham \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kaṃṭhapāśena niṣkāsya kena vai vāryate bhavān \|*  
*gopālamanyaṃ kurute rakṣaṇāya ca gopatiḥ \|*  
*sutṛṇaṃ cārayanpūrvo gopaḥ kiṃ kurute tadā \|\| 11 \|\|*

5-11. Hearing these words of Viṣṇu, Bāṇa, the son of Bali came in front and asked Vāmana, the cosmic-formed one: “Having assumed the body of dwarf and having asked for three steps of land, how could you be of such a cosmic (massive) form? O Lord of the world! If you desire to ask for the third step of land, assume the form of dwarf. Bali, the king of demons, will certainly give the third step. Gifts can only be given to the form of Vāmana whose feet Bali has washed and not to this being of cosmic form. You have created this cosmos and King Bali lives in this cosmos. One endowed with great power and prominence does not take things by force. O Lord of the world! If you consider this world as your own, then regarding this demon king as having lost honour for turning away from devotion towards you expel him by tying a rope around his neck. Who can stop you? If a master of cows employs another cowherd for protection of his cows then the earlier cowherd cannot do anything.”

## \|\| 2.19.12 \|\|

*ityevamukte tenātha vacane balisūnunā \|*  
*provāca bhagavānvākyamādikartā janārdanaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. After having been told like this by the son of Bali, Viṣṇu, the first creator of this world, said:

## \|\| 2.19.13-17 \|\|

*yānyuktāni vacāṃsītthaṃ tvayā bālena sāṃpratam \|*  
*teṣāṃ tvaṃ hetusaṃyuktaṃ śṛṇu pratyuttaraṃ mama \|\| 13 \|\|*

*pūrvamuktastava pitā mayā bāṇa padatrayam \|*  
*dehi mahyaṃ pramāṇena tadetatsamanuṣṭhitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*kiṃ na vetti pramāṇaṃ me balistava pitā suta \|*  
*balerapi hitārthāya kṛtametatpadatrayam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tasmādyanmama bāleya tvatpitrāṃ'bu kare mahat \|*  
*dattaṃ tenāsya sutale kalpaṃ yāvadvasiṣyati \|\| 16 \|\|*

*gate manvantare bāṇa śrāddhadevasya sāmpratam \|*  
*sāvarṇike tvāgate ca balirindro bhaviṣyati \|\| 17 \|\|*

13-17. “O boy! I am making you hear the answer together with the reasons to what you have said at this time. O Bāṇa! Your father at the very first instance said that he would give me three steps of land and I gave him the measures for the same. Is it that your father Bali does not understand that measure? I have asked for three steps of land for the good of this Bali. Hence, your father will dwell in the sixth of the Seven Lower Worlds (i.ed the ‘Sutala world’ for one Kalpa (i.e.) till the time of the duration of the material world. O Bāṇa! After the age of this Manu will usher in the age of other Sāvaṇṅka \[Sāvarṇika?\] Manu and your father Bali will be crowned as Indra.”

## \|\| 2.19.18 \|\|

*iti proktvā balisutaṃ bāṇaṃ devastrivikramaḥ \|*  
*provāca balimabhyetya vacanaṃ madhurākṣaram \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After saying this to Bali’s son, God Vāmana came near Bali and said in a sweet tone.

## \|\| 2.19.19 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*apūrṇadakṣiṇe yāge gaccha rājanmahātalam \|*  
*sutalaṃnāma pātālaṃ vasa tatra nirāmayaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

The God said:

19\. O demon king! Enter the sixth of the seven Nether worlds for not giving the full sacrificial fee in the Yajña. In that nether world named ‘Sutala’ live free from diseases.

## \|\| 2.19.20 \|\|

*baliruvāca \|*  
*sutalasthasya me nātha kathaṃ caraṇayostava \|*  
*darśanaṃ pūjanaṃ bhogo nivasāmi yathāsukham \|\| 20 \|\|*

Bali said:

20\. O Lord! How can I have a sight of your feet and worship them while staying with happiness in the Sutala world?

## \|\| 2.19.21-26 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*daityendra hadaye nityaṃ tāvake nivasāmyaham \|*  
*ataste darśanaṃ prāptaḥ punaḥ sthāsye tavāntikam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tathānyamutsavaṃ puṇyaṃ vṛtte śakramahotsave \|*  
*dīpapratipannāmā'sau tatra bhāvī mahotsavaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tatra tvāṃ naraśārdūlā hṛṣṭāḥ puṣṭāḥ svalaṃkṛtāḥ \|*  
*puṣpadīpapradānena arcayiṣyaṃti yatnataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tatrotsavaḥ puṇyatamo bhaviṣyati dharātale \|*  
*tava nāmāṃkito daitya tena tvaṃ vatsaraṃ sukhī \|\| 24 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyasi narā ye tu dṛḍhabhaktisahā nvitāḥ \|*  
*tvāmarcayanti vidhivatte'pi syuḥ sukhabhāginaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*yathaiva rājyaṃ bhavatastu sāṃprataṃ tathaiva sā bhāvyatha kaumudīti \|*  
*ityevamuktvā madhumaditīśvaraṃ nivāsayitvā sutalaṃ sabhāryakam \|\| 26 \|\|*

The gracious God said:

21-26. O demon king! I always remain in your heart. Hence, you have the occasion to obtain my sight as I will always remain near you. There will be another auspicious festival of Indra. It will have lights at every step. In this festival the healthy and hefty and well-dressed as well as the best of the kings will honour and adore you with offerings of light and flowers. This festival will be auspicious for the earth and will be called by your name. You will remain happy for years together by this. Those who will worship and adore you with resolute mind and devotion will also continue to be happy.

## \|\| 2.19.27-28 \|\|

*urvī samādāya jagāma tūrṇaṃ sa śakrasadmāmarasaṃghajuṣṭam \|*  
*dattvā maghone madhujittriviṣṭapaṃ kṛtvā tu devānmakhabhāgabhoginaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*antardadhe viśvapatirmaheśaḥ saṃpaśyatāṃ vai vasudhādhipānām \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Having said so, Viṣṇu gave shelter to demon-king Bali along with his wife in the Sutala World and having taken the land came in haste to the abode of Indra served by divine beings. Having given the Heaven to Indra and making the gods get the enjoyment of glory, Viṣṇu, the Lord of the world disappeared from sight when the kings were watching.

## \|\| 2.19.29-31 \|\|

*gṛhītveti bale rājyaṃ manuputre niyojitam \|*  
*dvīpāṃtare ca te daityāḥ preṣitāścājñayā svayam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*pātālanilayā ye tu te tatraiva niveśitāḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ paramo harṣaḥ saṃjāto balinigrahe \|\| 30 \|\|*

*nivāsāya punaścakre vāmano vāmano manaḥ \|*  
*tatra kṣetre svanagare vāmanaḥ sa nyuvāsa ha \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. Having taken away the kingdom of Bali and engaging Indra in it, Viṣṇu outsted the demons from there and made the inhabitants of Hell settle there. The Gods were very pleased with the restraining of Bali. Then God Vāmana made his mood lighter for the residents.

Sārasvata asked:

## \|\| 2.19.32 \|\|

*sārasvata uvāca \|*  
*prādurbhāvaste kathito narendra puṇyaḥ śucirvāmanasyāghahārī \|*  
*smṛte yasminsaṃśrute kīrtite ca pāpaṃ yāyātsaṃkṣayaṃ puṇyameti \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. You have narrated the sacred, the sin-destroying and auspicious birth story of Vāmana, by listening to and singing which, the sins get destroyed and goodness arises.

## \|\| 2.19.33 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*iti sārasvatavacaḥ śrutvā bhojaḥ sa bhūpatiḥ \|*  
*namaskṛtya muniśreṣṭhaṃ pūjayāmāsa bhaktitaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

God said:

33\. “Hearing these words of Sārasvata, King Bhoja honoured him as the best of sages, paid him obeisance and worshipped him with devotion.

## \|\| 2.19.34 \|\|

*tato yathoktavidhinā sa bhojo nṛpasattamaḥ \|*  
*vastrāpathakṣetra yātrāṃ parivārajanaiḥ saha \|*  
*kṛtvā kṛtārthatāṃ prāpto jagāmānte paraṃ padam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Then King Bhoja resumed the journey to Vastrāpatha along with family members as per established practice. There having made his life fruitful he left for the ultimate place,

i.e. the World of Viṣṇu at the end.

## \|\| 2.19.35-36 \|\|

*etanmayā puṇyatamaṃ prabhāsakṣetre ca vasrāpathamīritaṃ te \|*  
*śrutvā paṭhitvā parayā sameto bhaktyā tu viṣṇoḥ padamabhyupaiti \|\| 35 \|\|*

*yathā pāpāni dhūyaṃte gaṃgāvārivigāhanāt \|*
