*tathā purāṇaśravaṇādduritānāṃ vinā śanam \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. I have described the Vastrāpatha region which is a part of the Prabhāsa-kṣestra. Whoever listens to these auspicious words or reads them goes to the World of God Viṣṇu. As the sins get washed away by a bath in Gaṅgā, similarly by listening to the stones in the Purāṇa, sins get washed away.

## \|\| 2.19.37 \|\|

*idaṃ rahasyaṃ paramaṃ tavoktaṃ na vācyametaddharibhaktivarjite \|*  
*dvijasya nindānirate'tipāpe gurāvabhakte kṛtapāpabuddhau \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. I have narrated this secret story to you. Those turned away from devotion to Viṣṇu should not hear it. Sin also occurs by even hearing of it by a Brāhmaṇa-censerer a heinous sinner, one hostile to one’s perceptor \[preceptor?\] and one ever thinking of committing sins.

## \|\| 2.19.38-40 \|\|

*idaṃ paṭhedyo niyataṃ manuṣyaḥ kṛtabhāvanaḥ \|*  
*tasya bhaktiḥ śive kṛṣṇe niścalā jāyate dhuvam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tadbhaktyā sakalānarthānprāpnoti puruṣottamaḥ \|\| \|*  
*purāṇavācine dadyādgobhūsvarṇavibhūṣaṇam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*vittaśāṭhyaṃ na kartavyaṃ kurvandāridryamāpnuyāt \|*  
*triḥkṛtvā prapaṭhañchṛṇvaṃnsarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. A human being who reads it thoughtfully gets his faith firmly fixed upon Śiva and Śrīkṛṣṇa. By that faith a man gets everything. Hence, cows, land, gold, wealth and ornaments should be given to the narrator of this Purāṇa. One who narrates this is poor by one’s own self. All the desires of heart get accomplished by reading and hearing it thrice.

:: End of Vastrāpatha-Kṣetra-Māhātmya ::

## Section 3 - Arbuda-khaṇḍa

## Chapter 1 - A Hollow Near the Hermitage of Vasiṣṭha

## \|\| 3.1.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*oṃnamonaṃtāya sūkṣmāya jñānagamyāya vedhase \|*  
*śuddhāya viśvarūpāya devadevāya śaṃbhave \|\| 1 \|\|*

Obeisance to gracious Gaṇeśa. Now the third section of Prabhāsa Khaṇḍa entitled Arbuda Khaṇḍa starts.

Vyāsa said:

1\. Obeisance to that endless, subtle, pure, God of gods, the creator knowable through the means of knowledge, and the cosmic-formed Śaṃkara.

## \|\| 3.1.2-3 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kathito vaṃśavistāro bhavatā somasūryayoḥ \|*  
*manvaṃtarāṇi sarvāṇi sṛṣṭiścaiva pṛthagvidhā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*adhunā śrotumicchāmastīrthamāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*kāni tīrthāni puṇyāni bhūtale'sminmahāmate \|\| 3 \|\|*

The Sages said:

2-3. O Sūta! You have already described the Lunar and Solar races in a detailed manner. You have also described all the Ages of Manu and the different types of creations. Now, we want to hear about the greatness of the principal places of pilgrimage. O Sūta of great intelligence! which are the auspicious places of pilgrimage on this earth?

## \|\| 3.1.4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*nānā tīrthāni loke'sminyeṣāṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate \|*  
*tisraḥ koṭyo'rddhakoṭiśca teṣāṃ saṃkhyā kṛtā purā \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:

4\. There are many centers of pilgrimage in this world which cannot be counted. Their number has been stated to be three and a half crore in olden times.

## \|\| 3.1.5-7 \|\|

*kṣetrāṇi saritaścaiva parvatāśca nadā stathā \|*  
*ṛṣīṇāṃ tapaso vīryānmāhātmyaṃ paramaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ madhye'rbudonāma sarvapāpaharo'naghaḥ \|*  
*aspṛṣṭaḥ kalidoṣeṇa vasiṣṭhasya prabhāvataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*punaṃti sarvatīrthāni snānadānādikairyathā \|*  
*arbudo darśanādeva sarvapāpaharo nṛṇām \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. Different regions, rivers, mountains and large rivers have attained distinguished and exalted position through the austerities and heroic acts of sages. Among these is a place of pilgrimage named Arbuda which is free from sins, destroyer of all sins and exempted from the touch of vices of the Age of Kali through the influence of Sage Vasiṣṭha. All places of pilgrimage purify by means of offering of free gifts and bathing. But all the sins of humans get destroyed by a mere sight of Arbuda from a distance.

## \|\| 3.1.8-9 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kiṃ pramāṇo'rbudo nāma kasmindeśe vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ vāsiṣṭhamāhātmyātprathito dharaṇītale \|\| 8 \|\|*

*kāni tīrthāni mukhyāni hyarbude saṃti parvate \|*  
*sarvaṃ vistarato brūhi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

The sages said:

8-9. What are the dimensions of this Arbuda mountain? Where is it situated? How could it get the fame by the greatness of Vasiṣṭha? Which are the main places of pilgrimage on this Arbuda? Please explain in details. We have a great curiosity to know.

## \|\| 3.1.10 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ ca saṃpravakṣyāmi kathāṃ pāpapraṇāśinīm \|*  
*arbudasya dvijaśreṣṭhā māhātmyaṃ ca yathā śrutam \|\| 10 \|\|*

Sūta said:

10\. O great Brāhmaṇas! I describe the sin-destroying story of Arbuda mountain, the way I have heard.

## \|\| 3.1.11-13 \|\|

*vasiṣṭho nāma devarṣiḥ pitāmahasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*sa pūrvaṃ bhūtalaṃ prāptastapastepe sudāruṇam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*niyato niyatāhāraḥ sarvabhūtahite rataḥ \|*  
*varṣāsvākāśavāsī ca hemaṃte salilāśayaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*paṃcāgnisādhako grīṣme japahomaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*kenacittvatha kālena tasya dhenuḥ payasvinī \|*  
*naṃdinīti suvikhyātā sā vai kāmadughā śubhā \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. Vasiṣṭha, the son of Brahmā, was a divine sage. Descending on earth, he performed severe austerities. He used to live in open during rains and in water during winter. He used to take fixed food and kept himself engaged in the welfare of all living beings. Undergoing the pain of self-torment under five fires during summer, he used to keep himself continuously engaged in muttering names of deities and in making offerings to fire. He had a wish-fulfilling milch cow named Nandinī with him.

## \|\| 3.1.14 \|\|

*sā kadāciddharāpṛṣṭhe bhramamāṇā tṛṇāśayā \|*  
*patitā dāruṇe śvabhre agādhe timirāvṛte \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Once while wandering about on earth, she fell into a deep and dark cleft affected by extreme thirst.

## \|\| 3.1.15 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu bhagavāṃstīkṣṇadīdhitiḥ \|*  
*astaṃ gato na saṃprāptā naṃdinī munisattamāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Coinciding this, the Sun god set down but the cow did not return to the hermitage.

## \|\| 3.1.16 \|\|

*tasyāḥ kṣīreṇa nityaṃ sa sāyaṃ prātardvijo muniḥ \|*  
*karoti homamagnau hi susamiddhe jitavrataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Everyday in the morning and in the evening Vasiṣṭha, the observer of religious vow used to perform the ritual of offering oblation to fire with the milk of that cow.

## \|\| 3.1.17 \|\|

*atha ciṃtāparo vipraḥ prāyaścittabhayāddhruvam \|*  
*vīkṣāṃcakre vane tasminsameṣu viṣameṣu ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Now worried with the fear of atonement, Vasiṣṭha went in search of the cow in the higher and lower regions of that mountain.

## \|\| 3.1.18 \|\|

*sa tacchvabhramathāsādya bhūṃbhārāvamathāśṛṇot \|*  
*tāṃ provāca muniśreṣṭhaḥ kathaṃ tvaṃ patitā śubhe \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Going near that ditch, he heard the painful voice of the cow. He asked the auspicious cow, “How could you fall down here?

## \|\| 3.1.19-20 \|\|

*ahaṃ homasya codvegānniḥsṛtastvāmavekṣitum \|*  
*sā'bravīdbhakṣamāṇāhaṃ viprarṣe tṛṇavāṃchayā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*patitātra vibho trāhi kṛcchrādasmātsuduḥsahāt \|*  
*tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā sa munirdhyāna māsthitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Becoming nervous as to how offering oblation to the sacrificial fire could be continued, I have come out to see you.” The cow said, “I have fallen down here due to my desire to have grass. Please save me from this difficult, intolerable pain.” Having heard those words of hers, Sage Vasiṣṭha, resorted to meditation.

## \|\| 3.1.21-23 \|\|

*sarasvatīṃ samādadhyau nadīṃ trailokyapāvanīm \|*  
*sā dhyātā manasā tena muninā tatra tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 21 \|\|*

*śvabhraṃ tatpūrayāmāsa samaṃtādvimalairjalaiḥ \|*  
*paripūrṇaṃ tataḥ śvabhre niṣkrāṃtā naṃdinī tadā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*saṃhṛṣṭā muninā sārddhaṃ yayāvāśramasammukham \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. He meditated on the (divine) river Sarasvatī, the purifier of all the three worlds. She on being meditated on by that sage filled the ditch completely at once with pure water. The ditch having thus been completely filled, Nandinī then came out of it. Becoming happy, the cow came back to the hermitage with the sage.

## \|\| 3.1.24-27 \|\|

*sa dṛṣṭvā śvabhramadhyaṃ taṃ gaṃbhīraṃ ca mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*ciṃtayāmāsa medhāvī śvabhrasyaiva prapūraṇe \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tasya ciṃtayato viprā buddhireṣodapadyata \|*  
*ānīya parvataṃ muktvā śvabhrametatprapūryate \|*  
*tasmādgacchāmyahaṃ śīghraṃ himavantaṃ nagottamam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*sa eva parvataṃ cātra preṣayiṣyati bhūdharaḥ \|*  
*yena syātparipūrṇaṃ ca śvabhrametanmahātmanā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tato jagāma sa munirhimavantaṃ nagottamam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā vasiṣṭhamāyāṃtaṃ hima vānhṛṣṭamānasaḥ \|*  
*arghyapādyādisaṃskāraiḥ saṃpūjya idamabravīt \|\| 27 \|\|*

24-27. That great sage saw depth in the middle of the ditch and he, the wise one, thought of filling it up. O Brāhmaṇas! a thought that this ditch be filled up with stones brought from the mountain dawned on Vasiṣṭha and he thought, “Let me proceed towards Himalaya soon. Himalaya will send stones here. This ditch will get filled up by this great soul.” Sage Vasiṣṭha then went to Himālaya. Having seen Vasiṣṭha coming, the Himālaya mountain became happy. Then having received him by washing of feet and making deserving offering he said:

## \|\| 3.1.28-29 \|\|

*svāgataṃ te muniśreṣṭha saphalaṃ me'dya jīvitam \|*  
*yadbhavānme gṛhe prāptaḥ pūjyaḥ sarvadivaukasām \|\| 28 \|\|*

*brūhi kāryaṃ muniśreṣṭha api jīvitamātmanaḥ \|*  
*nūnaṃ tubhyaṃ pradāsyāmi niyogo dīyatāṃ mama \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. “Welcome to you, O great sage! My life has become fruitful today that you, the one adorable to all gods, have arrived at my house today. O great sage! Tell me the job to be done, any job, which I, of course, will do, even by sacrificing my life for your sake.”

## \|\| 3.1.30-32 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*mamāśramasya sāṃnidhye śvabhramasti sudāruṇam \|*  
*agādhaṃ nandinī tatra patitā dhenuruttamā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*yatnādākarṣitā tasmādbhūyaḥ patanajādbhayāt \|*  
*tavāṃtikamanuprāpto nānyo yogyo mahīpatiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tasmātkañcinnagaśreṣṭhaṃ tatra preṣaya bhūdharam \|*  
*yena tatpūryate śvabhraṃ bhṛśaṃ preṣaya tādṛśam \|\| 32 \|\|*

30-32. Vasiṣṭha said: “There is a dangerous hollow near my hermitage. Nandinī, my best cow, had fallen into it. I took her out with great effort. I have come to you with the fear that she may fall into it again. O Lord of the Earth! No one else is able to accomplish this task (of filling the hollow). Hence, O great one, please send any mountain there, by which the hollow gets filled up. Send something like this.”

## \|\| 3.1.33 \|\|

*himavānuvāca \|*  
*kiṃpramāṇaṃ mune śvabhraṃ vistārāyāmato vada \|*  
*tatpramāṇaṃ nagaṃ kaṃcitpreṣayāmi viciṃtya ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Himālaya said: “O great Sage! how does that hollow measure? I will send a mountain after considering the size equal to the same measurement.”

## \|\| 3.1.34 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*dvisahasraṃ tu dairghyeṇa vistareṇa trisahasrakam \|*  
*na saṃkhyā vidyate'dhastāttasya parvatasattama \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Vasiṣṭha said: “Its breadth and length measure respectively 2000 and 3000. I cannot tell its depth.”

## \|\| 3.1.35 \|\|

*himavānuvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ tena pramāṇena sañjāto vivaro mahān \|*  
*abhūtkautūhalaṃ tena sarvaṃ vistarato vada \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Himālaya said: “What could be the cause for the formation of a hollow of such measurement. I have a great curiosity. Describe this in greater details.”

## Chapter 2 - The Acts of Uttaṅka (a Disciple of Gautama)

## \|\| 3.2.1 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*āsītpūrvaṃ munirnāmnā gautamaśca mahātapāḥ \|*  
*ahilyā dayitā tasya dharmapatnī yaśasvinī \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

1\. There was a great sage named Gautama in earlier times, who had practised severe austerities. His wife was renowned by the name Ahalyā.

## \|\| 3.2.2 \|\|

*śiṣyānadhyāpayāmāsa sa muniḥ śataśastadā \|*  
*śrutādhyayanasaṃpannānvisasarja tato gṛhān \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. This sage had taught crores of disciples and he used to send them back home after making them accomplished in the learning of sacred texts.

## \|\| 3.2.3 \|\|

*tasyānyo'pi ca yaḥ śiṣyo gurubhaktiparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*uttaṃko nāma medhāvī nyavasattasya mandire \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Attached firmly with faith in the teacher, one of his intelligent disciples named Uttaṅka used to stay in his (the teacher’s) house.

## \|\| 3.2.4 \|\|

*na taṃ visarjayāmāsa jarayāpi pariplutam \|*  
*uttaṃko'pi suśiṣyatvānno vetti palitaṃ śiraḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Despite old age afflicting him (i.e., the disciple), he was not sent back home. His hair turned grey. But as he (Uttaṅka) was the best disciple, he used to put up there.

## \|\| 3.2.5 \|\|

*jātakāryasamāyukto vidyāpāraṃgato'pi saḥ \|*  
*kenacittvatha kālena kāṣṭhārthaṃ sa bahiryayau \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Proficient in studies and remaining engaged in all activities, some time he went out to fetch firewood.

## \|\| 3.2.6 \|\|

*prabhūtāni samādāya āśramaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*athāsau nyakṣipattatra bhūtale kāṣṭhasaṃcayam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Collecting a heavy load of firewood he came back to the hermitage and the firewood fell down on the ground.

## \|\| 3.2.7-11 \|\|

*kāṣṭhalagnāṃ tadā śvetāṃ jaṭāmekāṃ dadarśa saḥ \|*  
*sa dṛṣṭvā duḥkhamāpannaḥ kṛpaṇaṃ paryacintayat \|\| 7 \|\|*

*dhigdhiṅme jīvitaṃ naṣṭaṃ kutaḥ kāryaratasya ca \|*  
*kalatra saṃgrahaṃ naiva mayā kṛtamabuddhinā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyati kulacchedaḥ śaithilyānmama durmateḥ \|*  
*gurupatnyā ca saṃdṛṣṭa uttaṃko duḥkhitastadā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tasya duḥkhaṃ tathā kṣipraṃ gautamāya niेveditam \|*  
*gautamena tathetyuktvā mṛduvāṇyā sa bhāṣitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*vatsa gaccha gṛhaṃ tvaṃ ca agnihotrādikāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*pālayasva vidhānena patnyā saha na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

7-11. Seeing one of his hair stuck to the wood Uttaṅka became very sad and worried. He began to think, “My life is ruined and has become a matter of reproach! What use has it been left with! As a person devoid of intelligence, I have not got married even. Cursed have I become to waste my life and with my thoughtless action my lineage will come to an end.” Ahalyā, the wife of the teacher noticed that Uttaṅka was very unhappy. As she informed the great Sage Gautama about Uttaṅka’s pain, with a soft voice the Sage said, “O Son! go home and together with your wife perform Agnīhotra \[Agnihotra?\] (offering oblation to fire) etc. as prescribed and without any hesitation.”

## \|\| 3.2.12-13 \|\|

*ityukto guruṇā so'pi pratyuvāca guruṃ prati \|*  
*dakṣiṇāṃ prārthaya svāminnahaṃ dāsyāmyasaṃśayam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*gautama uvāca \|*  
*sevā kṛtā tvayā vatsa mahatī mama sarvadā \|*  
*tenaiva paripūrṇatvaṃ jātaṃ me nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. After the teacher said like this Uttaṅka said, “Tell me the fee which I will definitely give.” Gautama said, “O dear son! You have already served me in a big way and my fee has been paid through the same. There is no doubt in this.” Uttaṅka said, “Of course, you have to take something by which I will have my satisfaction. O best Sage! I have already become proficient in studies with your grace.”

## \|\| 3.2.14-16 \|\|

*uttaṃka uvāca \|*  
*kiṃcidgrāhyaṃ tvayā svāminsantoṣo jāyate mama \|*  
*tvatprasādānmuniśreṣṭha vidyāpāraṃgato'smyaham \|\| 14 \|\|*

*gautama uvāca \|*  
*na grāhyaṃ ca mayā putra santuṣṭaḥ sevayāsmyaham \|*  
*necchāmyahaṃ dhanaṃ tvattaḥ sukhaṃ gaccha gṛhaṃ prati \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ityukto guruṇā so'pi mātaraṃ cābhyabhāṣata \|*  
*kiṃcidgrāhyaṃ mayā mātaḥ santoṣo dīyatāṃ mama \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. Gautama said, “O son! I have nothing to take. I am pleased with your service and I have no desire for your wealth. Go back to your own house with all happiness.” After the utterance of words ‘Service to teacher’ Uttaṅka told the wife of the teacher, “O Mother! I have to make an offering by which I will have my satisfaction.”

## \|\| 3.2.17-18 \|\|

*gurupatnyuvāca \|*  
*saudāsaṃ gaccha putra tvaṃ mamājñāṃ kuru satvaram \|*  
*madayantī priyā tasya dharmapatnī yaśasvinī \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kuṇḍale'thānaya kṣipraṃ madayaṃtyāśca putraka \|*  
*no cecchāpaṃ pradāsyāmi pañcame'hni na āgataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. The wife of the teacher said, “O son! you go to Saudāsa and follow my orders fast. His wife is renowned as Madayantī. O pupil! get the earrings of Madayantī fast. I will curse you if you do not turn up by the fifth day.”

## \|\| 3.2.19-20 \|\|

*ityukto gurupatnyā sa prasthitaḥ satvaraṃ tadā \|*  
*saudāsasyagṛhaṃ prāpa vyāghrāsyaṃ taṃ ca dṛṣṭavān \|\| 19 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā prāha tadā vipraṃ bhakṣaṇārthamupasthitam \|*  
*bhakṣayiṣyāmi vai vipra tvāmahaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Uttaṅka left and reached Saudāsa’s house as soon as the teacher’s wife said so. He saw Saudāsa having the face of tiger. Having seen this Brāhmaṇa, Saudāsa said, “You have arrived for my food. O Brāhmaṇa! I will undoubtedly eat you up.”

## \|\| 3.2.21-22 \|\|

*uttaṃka uvāca \|*  
*avaśyaṃ bhakṣaya tvaṃ māmekaṃ śṛṇu narādhipa \|*  
*dehi me kuṇḍale tāta dattvā'haṃ gurave punaḥ \|*  
*āgamiṣyāmi bhakṣasva mā tvaṃ kāryavivarjitam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*saudāsa uvāca \|*  
*gaccha tvaṃ mandire durge yatrā'ste dayitā mama \|*  
*tāṃ tvamāsādya yatnena jīvitavyabhayāddvija \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Uttaṅka said, “O King! you, of course, eat me up but before that listen to these words of mine. You give me both of your earrings. After giving them to the teacher, I will come back and then you can eat me up.”

## \|\| 3.2.22-23 \|\|

*saudāsa uvāca \|*  
*gaccha tvaṃ mandire durge yatrā'ste dayitā mama \|*  
*tāṃ tvamāsādya yatnena jīvitavyabhayāddvija \|\| 22 \|\|*

*yācyatāṃ mama vākyena sā te dāsyati kuṇḍale \|*  
*tvayā ca nānyathā kāryaṃ yatsatyaṃ dvijasattama \|\| 23 \|\|*

Saudāsa said:

22-23. You go to the temple difficult to approach where my wife stays. With fear of your own life, you go there carefully and ask her for the earrings as per my words, which she will give you. O Brāhmaṇa! you do not have to do anything other than this truth.

## \|\| 3.2.24-25 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*madayantyāḥ samīpaṃ tu gatvovāca dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*dehi me kuṇḍale devi saudāsastvāṃ samādiśat \|\| 24 \|\|*

*madayaṃtyuvāca \|*  
*sandeho'dyāpi me vipra kuṇḍale dvijasattama \|*  
*abhijñānaṃ tvamānīya nṛpasya dvija darśaya \|\| 25 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

24-25. Going near Madayantī, the best Brāhmaṇa said, “O revered lady! Please give me both the earrings as per the command of Saudāsa to you.” Madayantī said, “O Brāhmaṇa! I have doubt whether to give you the earrings. Please show me a token of proof with regard to the identity of the King.”

## \|\| 3.2.26 \|\|

*sa gatvā tvaritaṃ bhūpamabhijñānamayācata \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Instantly he rushed to the King and asked for his identity.

## \|\| 3.2.27 \|\|

*saudāsa uvāca \|*  
*yairvinā sugatirnāsti durgatiṃ ye nayaṃti vai \|*  
*gatvaivaṃ brūhi tāṃ sādhvīṃ mama vākyaṃ dvijottama \|*  
*pradāsyati tato nūnaṃ kuṇḍale ratnamaṃḍite \|\| 27 \|\|*

Saudāsa said:

27\. Go and tell that righteous lady these words of mine: “One without whom welfare cannot be attainable and only misfortune awaits.” She in turn will, of course, hand over to you the bejewelled earrings.

## \|\| 3.2.28-30 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*pratyabhijñānamādāya gatvā tasyai nyavedayat \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tato'sau pradadau tasmai gṛhṇa me kuṇḍale dvija \|*  
*uvāca yatnamāsthāya nīyatāṃ dvijasattama \|\| 29 \|\|*

*ete ca vāṃchate nityaṃ takṣako dvija kuṇḍale \|*  
*sa tatheti samādāya vismayotphullalocanaḥ \|*  
*kautukātpunarāgatya rājānaṃ vākyamabravīt \|\| 30 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

28-30. Having taken such identity Uttaṅka went and communicated it to her. Then having said, “O Brāhmaṇa! take the earrings,” she gave the earrings. She also said, “You must carry these earrings with great care. O Brāhmaṇa! the goldsmith always had the desire for these two earrings.” Having taken these, the Brāhmaṇa became wonder-struck with wide open eyes. However, he was perplexed over the words of the King for which he proceeded to the King again with curiosity.

## \|\| 3.2.31-32 \|\|

*abhijñānānmayā bhūpa samprāpte dīptakuṇḍale \|*  
*vākyārthastu na vijñātastato'haṃ punarāgataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*kautukādvada me rājansvakārye ca yathāsthitam \|*  
*kairvinā sugatirnāsti durgatiṃ ke nayaṃti ca \|\| 32 \|\|*

He said:

31-32. After bringing to notice your identity, I have obtained the two glittering earrings. But I could not understand your statement, for the comprehension of which I have come to you again. O King! I was settled in whichever way in my own work. But I have curiosity to know as to the reason for which welfare or well-being cannot be possible and one is driven towards misfortune.

## \|\| 3.2.33 \|\|

*saudāsa uvāca \|*  
*ārādhitā dvijā vipra bhavaṃti sugatipradāḥ \|*  
*asantuṣṭā durgatidāḥ sadyo mama yathā purā \|\| 33 \|\|*

Saudāsa said:

33\. The act of worship causing pleasure to a Brāhmaṇa brings in welfare while the same act resulting in displeasure causes misfortune as was my previous (old) condition.

## \|\| 3.2.34-35 \|\|

*etāvānmama śāpo'yaṃ vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*tenoktaṃ tvāṃ yadā kaścitpraśnaṃ vikhyāpayiṣyati \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tadā doṣavinirmukto bhaviṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tvatprasādādvinirmukto hyahaṃ śāpāddvijottama \|*  
*sāttvikaṃ dhāma cāpanno gaccha vipra namo'stu te \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. I had a curse of Sage Vasiṣṭha on me, according to which, I would be released from the sins of my vices when someone could only enable an unpressed declaration of this question from me. O best Brāhmaṇa! I have become free from the curse today by your kindness and have attained the sacred Abode. Take leave from me and my due respects to you.”

## \|\| 3.2.36-38 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*uttaṃkastena nirmuktaḥ satvaraṃ pathamāśritaḥ \|*  
*gacchaṃścātikṣudhāviṣṭo 'paśyadbilvaphalāni saḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tataḥ kṛṣṇājine baddhvā kuṇḍale nyasya bhūtale \|*  
*āruroha phalākāṃkṣī sa muniḥ kṣudhayā'nvitaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*etasminneva kāle tu takṣakaḥ pannagottamaḥ \|*  
*gṛhītvā kuṇḍale tūrṇamagamaddakṣiṇāmukhaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

36-38. Thereafter becoming free from Saudāsa, Uttaṅka took to his way swiftly. While on way, becoming intently troubled with hunger he happened to see a Bilva fruit (a wood-apple) on a tree. Then tying up both the earrings with the haired skin of a black antelope, he kept them on the ground and climbed up the tree. In the intervening period, Takṣaka, the Nāga prince, taking away both the earrings went away in the Southern direction of the grassland.

## \|\| 3.2.39 \|\|

*athottaṃkaḥ phalāhārī avatīrya dharātale \|*  
*sarvato'nveṣayāmāsa vegena mahatā vṛtaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Having eaten the fruit, Uttaṅka descended to the ground and began to look intently for the earrings on all sides. He saw Takṣaka, the King of Nāgas in front entering a frightening dark hole.

## \|\| 3.2.40-44 \|\|

*sa dṛṣṭvā sammukhaṃ prāptaṃ samīpaṃ pannagottamaḥ \|*  
*praviveśa bilaṃ raudramandhakāreṇa saṃvṛtam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*uttaṃko'pi bilaṃ prāptaḥ praviśya tamasāvṛtam \|*  
*daṇḍakāṣṭhaṃ samādāya kupitohyakhanattadā \|\| 41 \|\|*

*taṃ tathā duḥkhitaṃ dṛṣṭvā sakleśaṃ gurukāryataḥ \|*  
*vajramāropayāmāsa daṇḍāṃte pākaśāsanaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tato vidārayāmāsa sa śīghraṃ dharaṇītalam \|*  
*praviṣṭaścaiva pātālaṃ kuṇḍalārthaṃ paribhraman \|\| 43 \|\|*

*so'paśyadvājinaṃ tatra sarvaśvetaṃ guṇānvitam \|*  
*tenoktaḥ spṛśa me guhyaṃ tataḥ kāryaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 44 \|\|*

40-44. Picking up a stick lying nearby in hand Uttaṅka entered the hole full of darkness and got engaged in searching. Seeing Uttaṅka to be sad and stressed due to the teacher’s job Indra put the mighty thunderbolt onto the stick and Uttaṅka could dig up to the bottom of the earth very soon. Haying entered the lower region of earth, i.e., hell, he went on moving around with an eye upon the earrings. He saw a horse of superior quality of full white colour there. The horse told him, “You touch my private part and your job will be done.”

## \|\| 3.2.45-46 \|\|

*sa cakāra tathā śīghraṃ tato dhūmo vyajāyata \|*  
*pātālaṃ tena sarvatra vyāptaṃ bhūdhara vahninā \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tataśca vyākulāḥ sarve pannagāḥ samupādravan \|*  
*takṣakaṃ purataḥ kṛtvā saṃprāptāḥ kuṇḍalānvitāḥ \|*  
*uttaṃkāya tato dattvā praṇipatya yayurgṛham \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. Smoke soon spread across there after its saying so. The fire engulfed all places in the nether region including the mountains supporting the earth. Then agitated snakes began to run here and there. Along with the earrings, Takṣaka, the king of Nāgas, was there before them. Then he handed over the earrings to Uttaṅka and after paying his respects left for home.

## \|\| 3.2.47-54 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*athāśvastamuvācedamahamagnirdvijottama \|*  
*yastvayā'rādhitaḥ pūrvamupādhyāyanideśataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*jñātvā tvāṃ duḥkhitaṃ prāptamiha prāptaḥ kṛpāparaḥ \|*  
*sarvathā tvaṃ ca me pṛṣṭhaṃ bhagavañchīghramāruha \|\| 48 \|\|*

*nayāmi tatra yatrāste guruḥ sarvaguṇālayaḥ \|*  
*ārūḍhastasya pṛṣṭhe sa pratasthe hyāśramaṃ prati \|\| 49 \|\|*

*tatkṣaṇātsamanuprāpto gautamasya niveśanam \|*  
*etasminneva kāle tu ahilyā kṛtamaṃḍanā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*snātā cābhyetya bhartāraṃ sādhvī vākyamuvāca ha \|*  
*uttaṃko'dya na saṃprāptaḥ śāpaṃ dāsyāmyahaṃ dhruvam \|\| 51 \|\|*

*śithilo gurukṛtyeṣu sa yadālakṣito mayā \|*  
*tasyā vākyāvasāne tu uttaṃkaḥ paryyadṛśyata \|\| 52 \|\|*

*prasannavadano hṛṣṭaḥ kuṇḍalābhyāṃ samanvitaḥ \|*  
*praṇipatya sa tāṃ bhaktyā kuṇḍale saṃnyavedayat \|\| 53 \|\|*

*sā dṛṣṭvā tatkṣaṇātsādhvī karṇābhyāṃ saṃnyaveśayat \|*  
*svagṛhāya tatastūrṇamuttaṃkaṃ visasarja ha \|\| 54 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

47-54. Now Fire said to the assured best Brāhmaṇa, “I am Agni, whom you had worshipped earlier as per the direction of your own teacher. Out of mercy, I have come here seeing you sad. You sit on my back fast. I will take you to the teacher the storehouse of all qualities.” Then Uttaṅka seated on his back started heading towards the teacher’s hermitage and instantly reached near the abode of Gautama. At that time, after having a bath and getting herself dressed up Ahalyā was by the side of her husband and happened to be saying, “Uttaṅka has not come today. I am determined to curse him. He shows laxity in performing the teacher’s assignment.” Hardly had she spoken like this when Uttaṅka appeared before her with a bright face. He had brought both the earrings and after paying respects gave those with faith. Having taken those earrings, Ahalyā wore them on her ears at that time and then sent Uttaṅka back home.

## \|\| 3.2.55 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ sa vivaro jātastakṣakottaṃkakāraṇāt \|*  
*yathā me ciṃtyate nityaṃ dhenvarthaṃ śvabhrapūraṇe \|\| 55 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

55\. Thus that cleft was caused by Takṣaka and Uttaṅka. Intent upon thinking like this, I am, therefore, for it to be filled up due to my cow.

## \|\| 3.2.56 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ pūraya kṣipraṃ nānyaḥ śakto'tra karmaṇi \|*  
*śīghraṃ kuru nagaśreṣṭha mama kāryamasaṃśayam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Hence, you please fill it up quickly for no one else other than you is able to do this even with one hundred meritorious actions. O Himālaya, O King of mountains, complete my work without any hesitation.

## Chapter 3 - Vasiṣṭha’s Order to Nandīvardhana to Fill Up the Cleft

## \|\| 3.3.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*śrutvā himācalo vākyaṃ vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*cintayāmāsa tatkāryaṃ vivarasya prapūraṇe \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ciraṃ vicārya tamṛṣimidamāha nagottamaḥ \|*  
*ka upāyo nagānāṃ vai tatra gaṃtuṃ vadasva me \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. Having listened to this statement of the great soul Vasiṣṭha, Himālaya began to think how to fill up the cleft. After thinking on the matter for a long duration Himālaya asked Sage Vasiṣṭha to tell the way mountains can be brought there.

## \|\| 3.3.3 \|\|

*pakṣacchedastu śakreṇa sarveṣāṃ ca purā kṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasmādasya muniśreṣṭha kāryasya paśya niścayam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He continued, “Indra had cut off the wings of all mountains since olden times. Hence, O best Sage, make this work certain.”

## \|\| 3.3.4-6 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*astyupāyo nagānāṃ tu tatra netuṃ mahānaga \|*  
*tavāyaṃ tanayastatra vikhyāto naṃdivarddhanaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tasyārbuda iti khpāto vayasyaḥ paramaṃ priyaḥ \|*  
*nāgaḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ khecaro'pi ca vīryavān \|\| 5 \|\|*

*sa vā ūrdhvagatiḥ kṣipraṃ kṣaṇānneṣyatyasaṃśayaḥ \|*  
*līlayā sarvakṛtyeṣu taṃ viditvā'hamāgataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

4-6. O great mountain! there is a way to fit mountains there. You have the son famous as Nandīvardhana. His best friend is of the name Arbuda. He is the best among all bearing life. He is powerful, and roams about in the sky. As one always on the move to higher regions, he must have reached there fast and there is no doubt about it. I have come here having known that all works are his sport.

## \|\| 3.3.7 \|\|

*ādeśo dīyatāmasya duḥkhaṃ kartuṃ ca nārhasi \|*  
*avaśyaṃ yadi bhakto'si tatra preṣaya satvaram \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. You give him orders and do not get worried. If you are a devotee of mine, send him fast there, of course.

## \|\| 3.3.8-10 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*vasiṣṭhasya vacaḥ śrutvā himavānputravatsalaḥ \|*  
*duḥkhena mahatā'viṣṭaściṃtayāmāsa bhūdharaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*mainākastanayo'smākaṃ praviṣṭaḥ sāgare bhayāt \|*  
*jyeṣṭhaṃ tu sarvathā cātha vasiṣṭho netumāgataḥ \|*  
*kiṃ kṛtyamadhunā'smākaṃ kathaṃ śreyo bhaviṣyati \|\| 9 \|\|*

*itaḥ śāpabhayaṃ tīvramito duḥkhaṃ ca putrajam \|*  
*varaṃ putraviyogo'stu na śāpo dvijasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

Sūta said:

8-10. After hearing the words of Vasiṣṭha, Himālaya, affectionate toward son became very sad and thought: “Our son Maināka has entered the sea and Vasiṣṭha has arrived to take away the eldest one. Now what should we do that will be for the good of all of us. There was fear of curse on one side while on the other was excessive sorrow of separation from son. But then separation from son is right while incurring the curse of a Brāhmaṇa is not.”

## \|\| 3.3.11-12 \|\|

*sa evaṃ niścayaṃ kṛtvā naṃdivardhanamuktavān \|*  
*gaccha tvaṃ putra me vākyādvasiṣṭhasyāśramaṃ prati \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tatrāsti vivaro raudrastaṃ prapūraya satvaram \|*  
*arbudaṃ nāgamādāya mitraṃ prāṇabhṛtāṃ varam \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Resolving like this he told Nandīvardhana \[Nandivardhana?\], “O Son, go to Vasiṣṭha’s hermitage obeying my words. There is a frightening cleft there. Fill it up fast. Take along Arbuda, and the Nāga best among your beloved living beings.

## \|\| 3.3.13-14 \|\|

*naṃdivarddhana uvāca \|*  
*pāpīyānsa vibho deśaḥ phalamūlairvivarjitaḥ \|*  
*pālāśaiḥ khādirairāḍhyo dhavaiḥ śālmalibhistathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*suniṣṭhurairnṛpaśubhirbhillaiśca vividhairapi \|*  
*nadyo vahaṃti no tatra duṣṭā lokāśca vāsinaḥ \|*  
*nārho'haṃ parvataśreṣṭha tatra gaṃtuṃ kathaṃcana \|\| 14 \|\|*

Nandivardhana said:

13-14. O Lord! that country is full of sinners. No fruit or flower appears there. Only Palāśa, Khadira and cotton trees (Śālmali), etc. grow there. There is no river there. All inhabitants there are wicked. O King of mountains! I am in no way fit to go there.

## \|\| 3.3.15-18 \|\|

*athovāca vasiṣṭhastaṃ saṃtrastaṃ naṃdivarddhanam \|*  
*mā bhīḥ kāryā tvayā tatra deśe dauṣṭyātkathaṃcana \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tava mūrdhni sadā vāso mama tatra bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tīrthāni sarito devāḥ puṇyānyāyatanāni ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

*vṛkṣāśca vividhākārāḥ patrapuṣpaphalānvitāḥ \|*  
*sadā tatra bhaviṣyaṃti mṛgāśca vihagāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ahamevānayiṣyāmi tavārthe ca maheśvaram \|*  
*tadā sthāsyaṃti vai tatra sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

15-18. Vasiṣṭha then told the nervous Nandīvardhana \[Nandivardhana?\], “There is no need for you to fear or to be affected by anyone’s wickedness there, for there will always be my abode on top of your head. Places of pilgrimage, rivers, gods, auspicious mansions and many kinds of trees having fruits, foliage and flowers will be there. As good signs, there will be deer and birds there. I will get Lord Śaṃkara there for your need, as a result of which along with Indra all gods will shine forth there.

## \|\| 3.3.19-26 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*vasiṣṭhasya vacaḥ śrutva saṃhṛṣṭo naṃdivarddhanaḥ \|*  
*arbudaṃ nāgamāsādya vākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tatra yāvo'dya bhadraṃ te vayasya vinayānvita \|*  
*etatkāryamahaṃ manye sāṃprataṃ dvijasaṃbhavam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*arbuda uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ tatrāgamiṣyāmi snehātte parvatātmaja \|*  
*tatraiva ca vasiṣyāmi tvayā sārddhamasaṃśayam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*kiṃ tvahaṃ praṇayādbhrātarvakṣyāmi yadvacaḥ śṛṣu \|*  
*praṇayānnānyathā kāryaṃ yadyahaṃ tava saṃmataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*mannāmnā khyātimāyātu nānyatkiṃcidvṛṇomyaham \|*  
*tataḥ so'pi pratijñāya ārūḍhastasya copari \|*  
*praṇamya pitarau caiva pratasthe muninā saha \|\| 23 \|\|*

*divyairvṛkṣaiḥ śubhaiḥ pūrṇairnadīnirjharasaṃkulaiḥ \|*  
*madhurairvihagairyukto mṛgaiḥ saumyaiḥ samanvitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*mukto'rbudena tatraiva vivare munivākyataḥ \|*  
*samastastatrānāsāgraṃ gataḥ parvatasattamaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*vimukto vivare tasminnarbudena mahātmanā \|*  
*paripūrṇe mahāraudre saṃtuṣṭo munipuṃgavaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

Sūta said:

19-26. Nandīvardhana \[Nandivardhana?\] became exalted after hearing the statement of Vasiṣṭha. Going near the Arbuda mountain and repeating the same statement he said, “O friend! we will go there. Let there be good fortune for you. I consider this time to be fit for the job related to the Brāhmaṇa”. Arbuda said, “O son of Mountain! with myself originated from mountain, I will come there due to my love for you and will undoubtedly dwell there with you till the accomplishment of your job. But, O brother, due to my love, I want to say something. Till my voice lasts, I am speaking out of love and if you feel I am right, do not think differently. May this place earn its fame by my name and I do not have any other debt.” Then after admitting, and bowing down to mother and father, he left along with the sage getting mounted on Arbuda.

## \|\| 3.3.27 \|\|

*bravīccārbudaṃ nāgaṃ varaṃ varaya suvrata \|*  
*parituṣṭo'smi te bhadra karmaṇānena pannaga \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Possessed of heavenly trees, rivers, fountains, deer and full of the melodious sounds off birds, Arbuda stayed on top of the fissure as per the words of the sage. All of these arrived there and the great soul Arbuda, left all in the fissure. Sage Vasiṣṭha became satisfied with the fissure filled up. He told Arbuda mountain to ask for a boon saying he was fully pleased with his actions.

## \|\| 3.3.28-31 \|\|

*arbuda uvāca \|*  
*eṣa eva varo'smākaṃ yattvaṃ tuṣṭo mahāmune \|*  
*avaśyaṃ yadi dātavyaṃ tacchṛṇuṣva dvijottama \|\| 28 \|\|*

*yaccaitacchikhare hyasminnirjharaṃ nirmalodakam \|*  
*nāgatīrthamiti khyātiṃ bhūtale yātu sarvataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*atraivāhaṃ vasiṣyāmi mitrasnehātsadā mune \|*  
*tatra snātvā divaṃ yātu mānavastvatprasādataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*api vaṃdhyā ca yā nārī snānamātraṃ samācaret \|*  
*sā syātputravatī vipra sukhasaubhāgyasaṃyutā \|\| 31 \|\|*

Arbuda said:

28-31. O great Sage! You are pleased. This is the best boon. However, O Brāhmaṇa! If you have to give something then listen: Let there be a stream of clean water on the peak of this mountain which be renowned by the name ‘Nāgatīrtha’ in all directions of the land. Due to love for my friend I will always dwell there and with your kindness let all humans attain the heavenly world after having a bath in this place of pilgrimage. Let a barren woman taking bath in this place of pilgrimage get happiness, good fortune and children.

## \|\| 3.3.32-35 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*yā vaṃdhyāsmiñjale pūrṇe snānamātraṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*sāpi putramavāpnoti sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*nabhasaḥ śuklapaṃcamyāṃ phalaiḥ pūjāṃ karoti ca \|*  
*api varṣaśatā nārī sā bhaviṣyati putriṇī \|\| 33 \|\|*

*ye'tra snānaṃ kariṣyaṃti hyasmiṃstīrthe ca bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*yāsyaṃti te paraṃ sthānaṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*śrāddhaṃ cātra kariṣyaṃti paṃcamyāṃ ye samāhitāḥ \|*  
*māse nabhasi tīrthasya phalaṃ teṣāṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 35 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

32-35. A barren woman who takes a bath only once in this whole water will obtain a son endowed with all good features. A woman worshipping with fruits on the fifth day of the brighter half of the lunar month of Śrāvaṇa (July-August) will obtain sons despite being one hundred years old. The humans who take bath with faith in this place of pilgrimage will attain the highest place after getting exempted from old age and death. Those performing the ceremony in honour of the dead forefathers here on the fifth day of a month with all strictness, will get the complete fruits of pilgrimage performed in the month of Śrāvaṇa.

## \|\| 3.3.36-37 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ dattvā varaṃ tasya vasiṣṭho bhagavānmuniḥ \|*  
*naṃdivarddhanamabhyetya vākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 36 \|\|*

*varaṃ ca vriyatāṃ vatsa parituṣṭo'smi te'nagha \|*  
*vinayātsauhṛdātsarvaṃ dāsyāmi yatsudurllabham \|\| 37 \|\|*

Sūta said:

36-37. Sage Vasiṣṭha after having given boon in this way came near Nandīvardhana \[Nandivardhana?\] and said these words, “O Son! ask for a boon. O sinless one! I am pleased with you. Because of your humility and good-heartedness, I am giving you whichever object that is difficult to obtain.”

## \|\| 3.3.38-39 \|\|

*naṃdivarddhana uvāca \|*  
*tavāstu vacanaṃ satyaṃ pūrvoktaṃ munisattama \|*  
*sāṃnidhyaṃ jāyatāmatra avaśyaṃ tava sarvadā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*yathāhamarbudetyevaṃ khyātiṃ gacchāmi bhūtale \|*  
*prasādāccaiva te bhūyādetanme manasi sthitam \|\| 39 \|\|*

Nandivardhana said:

38-39. O Best one of Sages! Your earlier statement is true. Your presence be always here by virtue of which I and Arbuda earn fame on the earth. It is established in my mind that all these happened by your grace.

## \|\| 3.3.40-47 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evamastviti taṃ procya vasiṣṭho bhagavānmuniḥ \|*  
*cakre svamāśramaṃ tatra tasya vākyena noditaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*panasaiścaṃpakairāmraiḥ priyaṃgubilvadāḍimaiḥ \|*  
*nānāpakṣisamāyukto devagandharvasevitaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*tasthau tatra muniśreṣṭho hyaruṃdhatyā samanvitaḥ \|*  
*gomatīmānayāmāsa tapasā munisattamaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*yasyāṃ snātvā divaṃ yāṃti atipāpakṛto narāḥ \|*  
*māghamāse viśeṣeṇa makarasthe divākare \|\| 43 \|\|*

*yetra snānaṃ kariṣyaṃti te yāsyaṃti parāṃ gatim \|\| 44 \|\|*

*māghamāse viśeṣeṇa tiladānaṃ karoti yaḥ \|*  
*tilasaṃkhyāni varṣāṇi svarge tiṣṭhati mānavaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*bahunā kimihoktena stānamātraṃ samācaret \|\| 46 \|\|*

*vasiṣṭhasya mukhaṃ dṛṣṭvā punarjanma na vidyate \|*  
*aruṃdhatī pūjanīyā pūjanīyā viśeṣataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

Sūta said:

40-47. The blessed sage Vasiṣṭha told him that it would be like this and inspired by his statement he built up his own hermitage there. Trees like Pansa \[Panasa?\] (bread fruit), Campaka (a tree bearing yellow fragrant flowers), mango, Priyaṅgu, Bilva, three leaved Bela (asafoetida) and pomegranate etc. are there on this mountain. Many kinds of birds also dwell here. Gods and the heavenly musicians (Gandharvas) serve it. Sage Vasiṣṭha dwells there along with Arundhatī. Through (the power of) penances, Sage Vasiṣṭha had brought the river Gomatī here by bathing in which the extremely vicious humans also go to the heavenly world. Those who take bath in the month of Māgha (corresponding to the months of January-February) especially during the period when the Sun remains in Makara (the Zodiac sign of Capricorn), attain the highest status. Especially, a human being making offering of sesames in the month of Māgha dwells for a number of years equal to the number of sesame grains in Heaven. What more to say! One should take bath here. A human being does not take a rebirth after seeing the face of Sage Vasiṣṭha. Arundhatī is worshipped particularly here.

## Chapter 4 - Origin of Acaleśvara (Acala-īśvara)

## \|\| 3.4.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sa kṛtvā svāśramaṃ tatra vasiṣṭho bhagavānmuniḥ \|*  
*tatra śaṃbhornivāsāya tapastepe sudāruṇam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1\. Sage Vasiṣṭha made his own hermitage on that Arbuda mountain and began the pursuit of intense religious austerities for making the dwelling of God Saṃkara \[Śaṃkara?\] on it.

## \|\| 3.4.2 \|\|

*sa babhūva muniḥ samyakphalāhārasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*śīrṇa parṇāśanaḥ paścāddve śate samapadyata \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The sage continued to have fruits for food as per rule. He remained dependent on having leaves for food for two hundred years.

## \|\| 3.4.3 \|\|

*jalāhāraḥ pañcaśatavarṣāṇi saṃbabhūva ha \|*  
*varṣāṇāṃ vāyubhakṣo'bhūttato daśaśatāni ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He spent five hundred years drinking water only and another ten hundred years by breathing air only.

## \|\| 3.4.4 \|\|

*pañcāgnisādhako grīṣme hemante salilāśayaḥ \|*  
*varṣāsvākāśavāsī ca sahasraṃ ca tato'bhavat \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He practised Pañcāgṇi (remaining in the middle of five fires) during summer and stayed under water during winter. He stayed in the open for a thousand years during rains.

## \|\| 3.4.5 \|\|

*tatastuṣṭo mahādevastasyarṣeḥ sumahātmanaḥ \|*  
*bhittvā taṃ parvataṃ sadyastatpuro liṃgamutthitam \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā vismayāviṣṭo muniḥ stotramudairayat \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then being pleased with the austerities of that great sage, the Liṅga of Śiva worshipped in the form of a stone came up instantaneously piercing the mountain. Then witnessing the presence of that Liṅga of Śiva, Sage Vasiṣṭha began recitation of hymns in wonder.

## \|\| 3.4.6 \|\|

*namaḥ śivāya śuddhāya sarvagāyā'mṛtāya ca \|*  
*kaparddine namastubhyaṃ namastasmai trimūrttaye \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He recited: “Homage to you, O holy one! O Lord Śiva! whose sacredness everyone praises, O bearer of braided and knotted hair and the bearer of the image of three gods.

## \|\| 3.4.7 \|\|

*namaḥ sthūlāya sūkṣmāya vyāpakāya mahātmane \|*  
*niṣaṃgiṇe namastubhyaṃ trinetrāya namonamaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Homage to you, having the gross form yet omnipresent through the fine form and the bearer of bow and arrow and the three-eyed one.

## \|\| 3.4.8 \|\|

*namaścandrakalādhāra namo digvasanāya ca \|*  
*pinākapāṇaye tubhyamaṣṭamūrte namonamaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Homage to you, O Śaṃkara holding the crescent moon and pervading all directions! Homage to you, O bearer of the Pināka bow and one having the body of eight forms!

## \|\| 3.4.9 \|\|

*namaste jñānarūpāya jñānagamyāya te namaḥ \|*  
*namaste jñānadehāya sarvajñānamayāya ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O Śaṃkara! You are of the form of knowledge, you are comprehensible through the path of knowledge. You are the embodiment of knowledge. Homage to you- the image of all wisdom.

## \|\| 3.4.10 \|\|

*kāśīpate namastubhyaṃ giriśāya namonamaḥ \|*  
*jagatkāraṇarūpāya mahādevāya te namaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Obeisance to you, O ruler of Kāśī and the God of mountains! Homage to you, O great Lord! O creator of this world!

## \|\| 3.4.11 \|\|

*gaurīkānta nama stubhyaṃ namastubhyaṃ śivātmane \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇusvarūpāya trinetrāya namonamaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Homage to you, O husband of Gauiī, O one of the image of well-being! I bow to you, O bearer of the image of Viṣṇu and Brahmā and the Three-eyed one.

## \|\| 3.4.12 \|\|

*viśvarūpāya śuddhāya namastubhyaṃ mahātmane \|*  
*namo viśvasvarūpāya sarvadevamayāya ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Homage to you, O Great Soul! O bearer of the image of universe and holiness! I bow down to you, O bearer of all images including images of gods.

## \|\| 3.4.13 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etasminneva kāle tu vāguvācāśarīriṇī \|*  
*parituṣṭo'smi te bhadraṃ varaṃ varaya suvrata \|\| 13 \|\|*

Sūta said:

13\. In the meantime a statement issued from the Incorporeal, saying that it was pleased by the gentle behaviour (of the worshipper) and that he could ask for any boon for well-being.

## \|\| 3.4.14 \|\|

*ityuktvā parvataṃ bhittvā tatpuro liṃgamutthitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Having said so, the Liṅga of Śiva worshipped in the form of a stone pierced out from within the body of the mountain.

## \|\| 3.4.15 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*liṃge'smiṃstava sāṃnidhyaṃ sadā bhavatu śaṃkara \|*  
*mayā pūrvaṃ pratijñātaṃ nagasyeha mahātmane \|*  
*satyaṃ kuru vaco me tvaṃ yadi tuṣṭo'si śaṃkara \|\| 15 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

15\. O God Śaṃkara! You please dwell for ever in this Liṅga. I have prayed for the same at this great soul earlier. If you are pleased then, O Śaṃkara! let my words be true.

## \|\| 3.4.16 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*adyaprabhṛti liṃge'sminsāṃnidhyaṃ me bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tvadvākyādbrāhmaṇaśreṣṭha sarvaṃ satyaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 16 \|\|*

The gracious God Śiva said:

16\. I will have my appearance in this Liṅga from today onwards. O best Brāhmaṇa! everything true happens as per your words.

## \|\| 3.4.17 \|\|

*stotreṇānena yo martyo māṃ staviṣyati bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśyāmāśvine munisattama \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Everything true will happen whenever any human sings this hymn with faith on the fourteenth day of the waning period of the moon in the month of Āśvina (i.e. September-October).

## \|\| 3.4.18 \|\|

*matpriyārthaṃ tu śakreṇa preṣitā munisattama \|*  
*mandākinīti vikhyātā nadī trailokyapāvinī \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O best of Sages! to please me, Indra, the King of gods has sent the famous river Mandākinī here, which makes the three worlds holier.

## \|\| 3.4.19 \|\|

*devasyottaradigbhāge kuṃḍaṃ tiṣṭhati nityaśaḥ \|*  
*tasyāṃ snātvā muniśreṣṭha liṃgaṃ me paśyate tu yaḥ \|*  
*sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. As a reservoir holding water it will always remain on the northern side of the Liṅga. That human who after taking a bath in it has a look at the Liṅga everyday will obtain the ultimate place becoming free from old age and death.

## \|\| 3.4.20 \|\|

*acalaṃ bhedayitvā tu yasmānme liṃgamudgatam \|*  
*acaleśvaranāmnaiva loke khyātiṃ gamiṣyati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Having pierced this immobile mountain, my Liṅga has come up. Hence it will be renowned in the world by the name Acaleśvara.

## \|\| 3.4.21 \|\|

*asya liṃgasya māhātmyānna kadāciccaliṣyati \|*  
*sarvathā ma idaṃ liṃgaṃ pralayānte na cālyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The greatness of this (Acaleśvara) Liṅga will never dwindle. Even its greatness will not loosen up till the time of final destruction of this world.

## \|\| 3.4.22 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etāvaduktvā vacanaṃ virarāma maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*vasiṣṭho'pi suhṛṣṭātmā gautamādyā munīśvarāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

Sūta said:

22\. Having said this much, the great God stopped. The great soul Vasiṣṭha became pleased in heart followed up by Sages like Gautama etc.

## \|\| 3.4.23 \|\|

*śakrādayastato devāstīrthānyāyatanāni ca \|*  
*ānayāmāsa brahmarṣistapasā parvatottame \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Gods like Indra etc. were also happy. The Brāhmaṇa sage had brought other places of pilgrimage, temples and mansions on this mountain through his own austerities.

## \|\| 3.4.24 \|\|

*tatastuṣṭaḥ suraśreṣṭhastatra vāsamathākarot \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Now becoming happy, the great God got settled down here.

## Chapter 5 - Greatness of Nāga Tīrtha

## \|\| 3.5.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*arbudasya ca māhātmyaṃ vistareṇa vadasva naḥ \|*  
*kautukaṃ sūta no jātaṃ kathayasva yathā śubham \|\| 1 \|\|*

The Sages said:

1\. O Sūta! describe to us in detail the greatness of Arbuda. We have a great curiosity. Please tell us this auspicious tale.

## \|\| 3.5.2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*purāsīcca ṛṣiśreṣṭhaḥ pulastyo bhagavānmuniḥ \|*  
*yayāteśca gṛhe yātastaṃ natvā cābravīnnṛpaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

2\. Pulastya, the illustrious sage, in ancient times, came to the house of king Yayāti. After paying homage, the king told the sage.

## \|\| 3.5.3 \|\|

*\|yayātiruvāca \|*  
*svāgataṃ te muniśreṣṭha saphalaṃ me'dyajīvitam \|*  
*kathayasva prasādena kathāmarbudasaṃbhavām \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O best of the sages! welcome to you. My life has become fruitful. With pleasure, please let me hear the story of the Arbuda mountain.

## \|\| 3.5.4 \|\|

*arbudākhyo nago nāma vikhyāto yo dharātale \|*  
*tasya yātrākramaṃ brūhi tatphalaṃ dvijasattama \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. There is a renowned mountain by name Arbuda on the surface of this earth. O best one of the Brāhmaṇas! please narrate the sequence of visits to this mountain and their fruits.

## \|\| 3.5.5 \|\|

*sarvaṃ vistarato brūhi tīrthayātrāparāyaṇa \|*  
*tasmādvada muniśreṣṭha yena yātrāṃ karomyaham \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Undertaking pilgrimages has been your principal object. Please describe all in details. Please tell me so that I can undertake pilgrimage in a befitting manner.

## \|\| 3.5.6 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*bahudharmamayo rājannarbudaḥ parvatottamaḥ \|*  
*aśakto vistarādvaktumapi varṣaśatairapi \|\| 6 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

6\. O king Yayāti! this best of the mountains—Arbuda has abundant religious merit. A detailed description of it is not possible in hundreds of years.

## \|\| 3.5.7 \|\|

*saṃkṣepādeva vakṣyāmi tīrthamukhyāni te tathā \|*  
*nāgatīrthaṃ tu tatrādyaṃ sarvakāmapradaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Hence, I am describing only the principal centers of pilgrimage on it in brief. Among these in the very beginning is Nāga Tīrtha which fulfills desires of all people.

## \|\| 3.5.8 \|\|

*nārīṇāṃ ca viśeṣeṇa putrasaubhāgyadāyakam \|*  
*śṛṇu rājanpurāvṛttaṃ yato'tyāścaryamuttamam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. This center of pilgrimage especially grants the good fortune of gift of children to women. Due to this, its ancient history is a matter of great wonder.

## \|\| 3.5.9 \|\|

*gautamī brāhmaṇī nāmnā satī sādhvī pativratā \|*  
*bālavaidhavyasaṃprāptā tīrthayātrāparāyaṇā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. There was a loyal, faithful and virtuous Brāhmaṇa lady by name Gautamī who had made visits to places of pilgrimage the principal objective of life for becoming a widow in childhood.

## \|\| 3.5.10 \|\|

*arbudaṃ sā ca saṃprāptā nāgatīrthaṃ viveśa ha \|*  
*tasmiñjale nimagnā sā snātumabhyāyayau purā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. She had come to Arbuda and had approached Nāga Tīrtha. She had taken a dip in its water with all her mind.

## \|\| 3.5.11 \|\|

*nāyakā putrasaṃyuktā tattīrthaṃ samupāgatā \|*  
*śuśrūṣāṃ sā tastasyāścakre nānāvidhāṃ nṛpa \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. A woman named Nāyakā had also come here with her son for the purpose of pilgrimage. O king! that son had performed many kinds of services here.

## \|\| 3.5.12 \|\|

*sarvopakaraṇairdarbhaiḥ sumanobhiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|*  
*atha sā ciṃtayāmāsa gautamī putraduḥkhitā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He performed service with all paraphernalia. But becoming sad with separation from son, Gautamī began to worry (thinking).

## \|\| 3.5.13 \|\|

*dhanyo'yaṃ tanayo hyasyāḥ śuśrūṣāṃ kurute sadā \|*  
*putrayuktā tviyaṃ dhanyā dhigahaṃ putravarjitā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. “Fortunate is that child always engaged in service. Fortunate is she having a son like this. I am reproachable for being devoid of child.

## \|\| 3.5.14 \|\|

*ahaṃ bhartrā viyuktā ca putrahīnā suduḥkhitā \|*  
*atha sā nirgatā tasmātsalilānnṛpasattama \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. I, a widow, am very sad without a child.” O king! she then came out of the reservoir.

## \|\| 3.5.15-16 \|\|

*vinā'pi bhartṛsaṃyogātsadyo garbhavatī hyabhūt \|*  
*sā garbhalakṣaṇairyuktā sujanavrīḍayā'nvitā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*cakāra maraṇe buddhiṃ jvālayāmāsa pāvakam \|\| etasminneva kāle tu vāguvācāśarīriṇī \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Without union with husband she became pregnant immediately. As a virtuous lady she got ashamed for being enjoined with all traits of pregnancy. Driven by the idea to kill herself she kindled fire. At the sametime bodiless voice arose.

## \|\| 3.5.17-19 \|\|

*vāguvāca \|*  
*no tvaṃ gautami cityāgnau praveśaṃ kartumarhasi \|*  
*doṣo nāsti tavātrārthe tīrthasyāsya prabhāvataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*yo yadvāṃchati citte ca jalamadhye sthito naraḥ \|*  
*cintitaṃ ca tadāpnoti nārī vā nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tvayā tasyāḥ sutaṃ dṛṣṭvā putravāṃchā kṛtā hṛdi \|*  
*tava garbhagato nūnaṃ putraḥ putri bhaviṣyati \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. It said: “O Gautamī! do not enter into the fire of this worry. There is no fault of yours. Your pregnancy is due to the influence of pilgrimage. Standing in this water whatever any human desires (in mind), all those women or men obtain all those desires without any doubt. Having seen the Nāyakā’s child, you had nurtured the desire for a child in your heart. Hence O daughter! a son which has come in your womb will be born.

## \|\| 3.5.20-22 \|\|

*tasmādvirama bhadraṃ te nirdoṣāsi pativrate \|*  
*virarāma tataḥ sādhvī gautamī maraṇānnṛpa \|\| 20 \|\|*

*śrutvā'kāśagatāṃ vāṇīṃ devadūtena bhāṣitām \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā patiṃ vinā garbhaṃ vākyameta duvāca ha \|\| 21 \|\|*

*aho tīrthaprabhāvo'yamapūrvaḥ pratibhāti me \|*  
*yatra saṃjāyate garbhaḥ strīṇāṃ śukrarajovinā \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. Hence, stop worrying. There will be your welfare. O you! having fidelity to your husband, you are blameless.”

O king! then the virtuous Gautamī restrained herself from death. Having heard this statement from the heavenly announcement made by a divine messenger and having seen the pregnancy without husband she said, “The unusual effect of this place of pilgrimage never occurred in my mind where women can bear foetus without semen and Rajas (menstrual fluid) getting mixed.

## \|\| 3.5.23 \|\|

*nāhaṃ kutrāpi yāsyāmi muktvedaṃ tīrthamuttamam \|*  
*evamuktvā tataḥ sādhvī tatraiva nyavasatsadā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. I shall not go anywhere else leaving this best centre of pilgrimage.”

Having said so the virtuous lady Gautamī settled there forever.

## \|\| 3.5.24-25 \|\|

*putraṃ vai janayāmāsa sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitam \|*  
*tatra pārthivaśārdūla kṛṣṇapakṣe 'śvinasya ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

*yaḥ punaḥ kurute śrāddhaṃ tasya vaṃśo na naśyati \|*  
*na preto jāyate rājanvaṃśe tasya kadācana \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. She gave birth to a son endowed with all traits. O king Yayāti! ‘the lineage’ of people who perform the Śrāddha (ceremony connected with memory of the dead relatives in a family) at Arbuda during the waning period of the moon in the month of Aśvina (September) never gets destroyed.

## \|\| 3.5.26 \|\|

*yaḥ pumānkāmarahitaḥ snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ ca pārthivaśreṣṭha tasya lokāḥ sanātanāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. No one in their family becomes a Preta (ghost). The man who takes a bath and performs Śrāddha there without any desire obtains the eternal world.

## \|\| 3.5.27-28 \|\|

*yā strī puṣpaphalānyeva tīrthe cāsminvisarjayet \|*  
*sā syātputravatī dhanyā saubhāgyaṃ ca prapadyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

*niṣkāmā svargamāpnoti duṣprāpyaṃ tridaśairapi \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena yātrāṃ tasya samācaret \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. A woman who immerses fruits and flowers in this place of pilgrimage is blessed with a son. She obtains the celestial world of the gods difficult to attain even without a desire for the same. Hence, one must perform pilgrimage to this place with all efforts.

## Chapter 6 - Greatness of Vasiṣṭha’s Hermitage

## \|\| 3.6.1-3 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchennṛpaśreṣṭha vasiṣṭhaṃ tapasāṃ nidhim \|*  
*yaṃ dṛṣṭvā mānavaḥ samyakkṛtārthatvamavāpnuyāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tatrāsti jalasampūrṇaṃ kuṇḍaṃ pāpaharaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*tasminkuṇḍe nṛpaśreṣṭha vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*gomatī ca samānītā tapasā nṛpasattama \|*  
*tatra snāto naraḥ samyakpātakai rvipramucyate \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sage Pulastya said:

1-3. O best king! thus humans need to go near Vasiṣṭha—the storehouse of austerities—a sight of whom enables humans to attain their objects. There is a pond full of water there which takes away sins of humans. The great soul Vasiṣṭha had brought the river Gautamī in this pond through perseverance. Humans become completely free from their sins with a bath in this pond.

## \|\| 3.6.4 \|\|

*ṛṣidhānyena yastatra śrāddhaṃ nṛpa samācaret \|*  
*sa pitṛṃstārayetsarvānpakṣayorubhayorapi \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. An individual performing Śrāddha here with Ṛṣi dhānya (coarse grain used by Ṛṣis) will be free from the bondage of the ancestors on both maternal and paternal sides.

## \|\| 3.6.5-6 \|\|

*atra gāthā purā gītā nāradena mahātma nā \|*  
*snātvā puṇyodake tatra dṛṣṭvā taṃ munisattamam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kiṃ gayāśrāddhadānena kimanyairmakhavistaraiḥ \|*  
*vasiṣṭhasyāśramaṃ prāpya yaḥ śrāddhaṃ kurute naraḥ \|*  
*sa pitṝṃstārayetsarvānātmanā nṛpasattama \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. The great soul Nārada had sung fully the glory of this place. A bath in the auspicious water followed by a sight of the best Sage Vasiṣṭha is much more meritorious than the Śrāddha, performed by offerings made and yajña conducted with extensive details at Gayā. O King! the human being who conducts Śrāddha on coming to this hermitage of Vasiṣṭha suitably ensures the cross-over of his ancestors along with his ownself.

## \|\| 3.6.7-13 \|\|

*tatraivāruṃdhatī sādhvī vasiṣṭhasya samīpataḥ \|*  
*pūjanīyā viśeṣeṇa sarvakāmapradā nṛṇām \|\| 7 \|\|*

*bālye vayasi yatpāpaṃ vārddhake yauvane'pi vā \|*  
*vasiṣṭhadarśanātsadyo narāṇāṃ yāti saṃkṣayam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*dīpaṃ prayacchate yastu vasiṣṭhāgre samāhitaḥ \|*  
*sukhasaubhāgyasaṃyuktastejasvī jāyate naraḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*upavāsaparo yastu tatraikā rajanīṃ nayet \|*  
*sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yatra saptarṣayo'malāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*trirātriṃ kurute yastu vasiṣṭhāgre samāhitaḥ \|*  
*sa yāti ca maharlokaṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yastu māsopavāsaṃ ca vasiṣṭhāgre karoti ca \|*  
*so'pi muktimavāpnoti na yāti sa bhavārṇavam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*śrāvaṇasya site pakṣe paurṇamāsyāṃ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*ṛṣiṃ tarpayate yastu brahmalokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 13 \|\|*

7-13. Objects of all desires are obtained through the special worship of virtuous Arundhatī after coming near Vasiṣṭha here. All wrongdoings of individuals committed during childhood, youth and old age get wiped out instantly by the sight of sage Vasiṣṭha. One who, becoming aware, lights an earthen lamp before Vasiṣṭha attains happiness and good fortune and becomes a bright man. One observing fasting and having a sojourn for a night here, reaches the ultimate place of the Seven Sages. One who observes fasting carefully for three nights before Vasiṣṭha attains Mahaloka getting exempted from old age and death. Emancipation is obtained by one who observes the ritual of fasting for a month before Vasiṣṭha. He does not return to the river of worldly existence. One who propitiates Sage Vasiṣṭha on the full-moon day of Śrāvaṇa (July-August) goes to Brahmā’s world.

## \|\| 3.6.14-15 \|\|

*vasiṣṭhasyāgrato yastu gāyatryaṣṭaśataṃ japet \|*  
*ājanmamaraṇātpāpātsadyo mucyeta mānavaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*vāmadevaṃ yajettatra yadi śraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*agniṣṭomaphalaṃ rājansadyaḥ prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. All the sins of a human being get destroyed instantaneously when he recites the Gāyatrī mantra eight hundred times before Vasiṣṭha. O king! one who performs the ritual offering to fire with regard for Vāmadeva obtains the fruits of the ‘Agniṣṭoma Yajña’.

## \|\| 3.6.16-17 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena draṣṭavyo'sau mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*śucibhiḥ śraddhayā yuktāste yāsyaṃti paraṃ padam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tasmātsarvātmanā rājanvāmadevaṃ ca pūjayet \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Hence, the ultimate position is obtainable by all those who have a sight of this great sage with all sorts of efforts and with purity and faith. Hence, O King! with a wholehearted devotion, worship Vāmadeva here.

## Chapter 7 - Influence of Acaleśvara (Acala-īśvara)

## \|\| 3.7.1 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchennṛpaśreṣṭha supuṇyamacaleśvaram \|*  
*yaṃ dṛṣṭvā siddhimāpnoti naraḥ śraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sage Pulastya said:

1\. O king! after this one needs to go to the good giving Acaleśvara, a look of which with faith accrues accomplishment.

## \|\| 3.7.2 \|\|

*tatra kṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ yaḥ śrāddhaṃ kurute naraḥ \|*  
*āśvine phālgune vāpi sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Any human who performs Śrāddha (i.e., ceremony connected with death of family members) of his paternal ancestors near the Acaleśvara on the fourteenth day of the waning period of moon in the month of Āśvina (i.e., September) or in Phālguna (i.e., February-March) attains the ultimate passage.

## \|\| 3.7.3 \|\|

*yastu pūjayate bhaktyā dakṣiṇāṃ diśamāsthitaḥ \|*  
*puṣpaiḥ patraiḥ phalaiścaiva so'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The fruits of Aśvamedha Yajña accrue to the human who, while remaining in the Southern direction performs the worship with fruits, flowers and leaves and with due faith.

## \|\| 3.7.4 \|\|

*paṃcāmṛtena yastatra tarpaṇaṃ kuru te naraḥ \|*  
*so'pi devasya sāṃnidhyaṃ śivalokamavāpnuyāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The human who propitiates his forefathers with the presentation of mixture containing equal quantities of milk, curd, ghee, honey and sugar, gets closer to the World of Śiva and obtains it.

## \|\| 3.7.5 \|\|

*pradakṣiṇāṃte yastasya praṇāmaṃ kurute naraḥ \|*  
*naśyaṃti sarvapāpāni pradakṣiṇapadepade \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The human who after taking a round of this pays his homage, all his sins get destroyed on each of his step involving the right turn or clockwise turn.

## \|\| 3.7.6 \|\|

*tatrāścaryamabhūtpūrvaṃ tattvaṃ śṛṇu mahāmate \|*  
*mayā pūrvaṃ śrutaṃ svarge nāradācchakrasannidhau \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O intelligent king! listen to a wonderful thing which had happened here earlier. I had heard that Nārada happened to tell it to Indra in Heaven.

## \|\| 3.7.7 \|\|

*tatra pūrvaṃ śuko nīḍaṃ vṛkṣe caivākaroddvijaḥ \|*  
*gatāgatena nīḍasya kurute taṃ pradakṣiṇām \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. A parrot happened to have made its nest on a tree there before and while moving to and fro to its nest, it used to take a clockwise turn around the nest.

## \|\| 3.7.8 \|\|

*na ca bhaktyā mahārāja pakṣiyonisamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*athāsau mṛtyumāpannaḥ kālena mahatā śukaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O king! it had no devotion due to being born in the species of birds and it was obtained to death as time had approached.

## \|\| 3.7.9 \|\|

*saṃjātaḥ pārthive vaṃśe rājā veṇuriti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*jātismaro mahārāja sarvaśatrunikṛntanaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Later, it became renowned as King Veṇu among the royal families. Having memory of his own clan, he achieved victory over all his enemies.

## \|\| 3.7.10 \|\|

*sa taṃ smṛtvā prabhāvaṃ hi pradakṣiṇāsamudbhavam \|*  
*acaleśvaramāsādya pradakṣiṇāmathākarot \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Remembering that his influence could have arisen from taking a round of the Acaleśvara, he began to take a clockwise turn of Acaleśvara by going near it.

## \|\| 3.7.11 \|\|

*naktaṃ dinaṃ mahārāja nānyatkiṃcitkaroti saḥ \|*  
*na tathā tapase yatno na naivedye kathaṃcana \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O king! day and night, he did not do anything other than this. Neither did he make any special effort as a measure of austerity. He did also not make any offering of edible things to gods.

## \|\| 3.7.12 \|\|

*na puṣpe dhūpadāne ca pradakṣiṇāparaḥ sadā \|*  
*kenacittvatha kālena munayo'tra samāgatāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He did not make any offering of flowers or incenses. He was only engrossed in taking the round. Sages came there after sometime.

## \|\| 3.7.13-19 \|\|

*nāradaḥ śaunakaścaiva hārīto devalastathā \|*  
*gālavaḥ kapilo naṃdaḥ suhotraḥ kaśyapo nṛpaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ete cānye ca bahavo devavrataparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*kecitsnānaṃ kārayaṃti tasya liṃgasya bhaktitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*anye ca vividhāṃ pūjāṃ japamanye samāhitāḥ \|*  
*eke nṛtyaṃti rājeṃdra gāyaṃti ca tathā pare \|\| 15 \|\|*

*balimanye prayacchaṃti stutiṃ kurvaṃti cāpare \|*  
*athāścaryaṃ paraṃ dṛṣṭvā pradakṣiṇāparaṃ nṛpam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*paraṃ kautukamāpannā vākyametadathābruvan \|*  
*pradakṣiṇāsamudbhūtaṃ kāraṇaṃ jñātumicchavaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kasmāttvaṃ pārthivaśreṣṭha pradakṣiṇāparaḥ sadā \|*  
*devasyāsya viśeṣeṇa satyaṃ no vaktumarhasi \|\| 18 \|\|*

*na dadāsi jalaṃ liṃge prabhūtaṃ sumanoharam \|*  
*puṣpadhūpādikaṃ vātha stotrāṇi vividhāni ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

13-19. Nārada, Śaunaka, Harīta, Devala, Galava, Kapila, Nanda, Suhotra, Kaśyapa and many kings were getting the Liṅga of Śiva on that mountain bathed with faith. Apart from them other people were engaged in many kinds of worships and in recounting repeatedly names of gods in their minds. O King! some were dancing while some others were singing. Some were presenting the sacrifice in the form of food while some others were singing praises to god. They were surprised to see Veṇu taking rounds. Filled with curiosity they said, “While doing this act of taking round we must know the reasons behind this act.” The sages said, “O king Veṇu! why are you taking the clockwise turn of this God specially? Please tell us the truth.”

## \|\| 3.7.20 \|\|

*samartho'si tathānyeṣāṃ dānānāṃ tvaṃ mahīpate \|*  
*etannaḥ kautukaṃ sarvaṃ yathāvadvaktumarhasi \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. They continued, “You are not offering water onto this beautiful Liṅga of Śiva. You are neither lighting earthen lamps nor incense nor are you reading out hymns in praise of God. O king! you are capable of making all gifts. Please speak out as we have a curiosity in this matter.”

## \|\| 3.7.21 \|\|

*veṇuruvāca \|*  
*yadahaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi śrūyatāṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*pūrvadehāṃtare vṛttaṃ sarvaṃ satyaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

Veṇu said:

21\. O Brāhmaṇas! listen to what am I saying. This description of my past life is specially true.

## \|\| 3.7.22 \|\|

*prāsāde'sminpurā pakṣī śuko'haṃ sthitavāṃstadā \|*  
*kṛtavāṃśca tadā devaṃ pradakṣiṇāmaharniśam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A bird by name Suka \[Śuka?\] used to stay here in this palace in olden times. Then I used to take round of the God day and night.

## \|\| 3.7.23 \|\|

*kṛpayā'sya prabhāvācca jāto jātismarastvaham \|*  
*adhunā parayā bhaktyā yatkaromi pradakṣiṇām \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. I have become one having memory of one’s family by its grace and influence. I am now doing this act of taking round out of Supreme faith.

## \|\| 3.7.24 \|\|

*na jāne kiṃ phalaṃ me'dya devasyāsya prasādataḥ \|*  
*etasmātkāraṇāccāhaṃ nānyatkiṃcitkaromi bhoḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. I do not know what fruit will accrue out of the influence of this God. O sages! I am not doing any other thing due to this reason.

## \|\| 3.7.25-26 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*veṇuvākyaṃ tataḥ śrutvā munayaḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ \|*  
*vismayotphullanayanāḥ sādhusādhviti cābruvan \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tataḥ pradakṣiṇa parāḥ sarve tatra maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*babhūvurmunayaḥ sarve śraddhayā parayā yutāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

25-26. After hearing these words of king Veṇu, with wonder and exhilaration, the sages said, “all right! all right!” Then all the great sages continued keeping themselves engaged in the act of taking round. They got imbued with great faith.

## \|\| 3.7.27 \|\|

*so'pi rājā mahābhāgo veṇuḥ śaṃbhoḥ prasādataḥ \|*  
*śāśvataṃ sthānamāpanno durllabhaṃ tridaśairapi \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. With the grace of God Śaṃkara, the fortunate king Veṇu obtained that difficult place in comparison with gods.

## Chapter 8 - Greatness of Three-eyed in the Pond of Bhadrakarṇa

## \|\| 3.8.1 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchennṛpaśreṣṭha bhadrakarṇaṃ mahāhradam \|*  
*trinetrābhāḥ śilā yatra dṛśyaṃte'dyāpi bhūriśaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

1\. O best of kings! then one needs to visit the great pond known as Bhadrakarṇa where the bearer of the three lustrous eyes is even visible now-a-days in many stones.

## \|\| 3.8.2 \|\|

*tasyaiva paścime bhāge liṃgamasti pinākinaḥ \|*  
*yaṃ dṛṣṭvā mānavastatra trinetrasadṛśo bhavet \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. There is the Liṅga of Śiva on the Western side of that Bhadrakarṇa pond by seeing which a human being becomes like the Three-eyed One.

## \|\| 3.8.3 \|\|

*bhadrakarṇagaṇonāma purāsīcchivavallabhaḥ \|*  
*tenātra sthāpitaṃ liṃgaṃ hradaścaiva vinirmitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. There was one by name Bhadrakarṇa in olden times who was counted among those dear to Śiva. He had founded this Liṅga and constructed this pond.

## \|\| 3.8.4 \|\|

*kenacittvatha kālena saṃgrāme dānavaiḥ saha \|*  
*yuyudhe purataḥ śaṃbhornānāgaṇasamanvitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. At some point of time, he had gone along with many others to fight the demons counted as dear to Śiva.

## \|\| 3.8.5 \|\|

*naṣṭe skaṃde hate sainye vīrabhadre parājite \|*  
*gatāste bhayasaṃtrastā mahākāle vinirjite \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Being frightened, they all left. Skandha fled away from the scene when other solders got killed. Virabhadra \[Vīrabhadra?\] lost out and the final victory appeared imminent.

## \|\| 3.8.6 \|\|

*balavānnamucirnāma dānavo balavattaraḥ \|*  
*khaḍgacarmadharaḥ śīghraṃ maheśvaramupādravat \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The demon Namuci by name and stronger among the demons ran towards Saṃkarji with sword and spear in hands.

## \|\| 3.8.7 \|\|

*bhadrakarṇastu taṃ dṛṣṭvā dānavaṃ tadanaṃtaram \|*  
*pataṃtaṃ saṃmukhastasya tiṣṭhatiṣṭheti cābravīt \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Seeing the demon coming from the front, Bhadrakarṇa told him ‘Stay where you are.’

## \|\| 3.8.8 \|\|

*chittvā'simasinā tasya carma cāpi mahābalaḥ \|*  
*stanayoraṃtare daityaṃ kopāviṣṭo'hanannṛpa \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. This stronger one cut his spear and sword by his own sword. O king! then the demon got wounded under the influence of anger.

## \|\| 3.8.9 \|\|

*athāsau nihatastena praviśya vipulaṃ tamaḥ \|*  
*nipapāta mahīpṛṣṭhe vāyubhagna iva drumaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The wounded demon then entered the dense darkness (i.e. became unconscious) and fell down on the ground like an axed tree.

## \|\| 3.8.10 \|\|

*vadhaṃ prāptastu daityo'sau natvā haramasau sthitaḥ \|*  
*satye sthitaṃ ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā tatastuṣṭo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then coming near Lord Śiva the hurt demon stood up. God Śiva got pleased to see that the demon was still remaining steadfast on the observance of religious and moral duties.

## \|\| 3.8.11 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*tava vīryeṇa saṃtuṣṭo dharmeṇa ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te nityaṃ yo hṛdaye sthitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

The benevolent God said:

11\. O demon! I am satisfied with your power and especially your adherence to moral and religious duties. You can ask for that specific boon in your mind.

## \|\| 3.8.12 \|\|

*bhadrakarṇaṃ uvāca \|*  
*yanmayā sthāpitaṃ liṃgamarbude surasattama \|*  
*atrāstu tava sāṃnidhyaṃ hrade'smiṃśca sthiro bhava \|\| 12 \|\|*

Bhadrakarṇa said:

12\. O great God! let there be your closeness to the Liṅga I have founded on this Arbuda mountain and you remain fixed in this pond.

## \|\| 3.8.13-14 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*māghamāse caturddaśyāṃ kṛṣṇapakṣe sadā mama \|*  
*sāṃnidhyaṃ ca viśeṣeṇa hrade liṃge bhaviṣyati \|\| 13 \|\|*

*bhadrakarṇahrade snātvā trinetraṃ yaḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*drakṣyate sa tu me sthānaṃ śāśvataṃ yāsyati dhuvam \|\| 14 \|\|*

The gracious God said:

13-14. There will be my closeness to this Liṅga and pond on the fourteenth day of the waning period of moon in the month of Pausa \[Pauṣa?\] i.e. January. One who takes a bath in this Bhadrakarṇa pond and follows it up with a look of Śaṃkara diligently, will certainly attain that eternal place.

## \|\| 3.8.15 \|\|

*tasmātsarvatra yatnena snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|*  
*pūjayitvā ca talliṃgaṃ śivalokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Hence, with all efforts one needs to have a bath there. The man who worships this Liṅga of Śiva goes to the abode of Śiva.

## Chapter 9 - Eminence of Kedāra

## \|\| 3.9.1 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchennṛpaśreṣṭha tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam \|*  
*kedāramiti vikhyātaṃ sarvapāpaharaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 1 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

1\. O king! then one must visit Kedāra—the place of pilgrimage renowned in the three worlds, a visit to which takes away all sins of human beings.

## \|\| 3.9.2 \|\|

*yatra mandākinī puṇyā sarasvatyā samāgatā \|*  
*tatra snāto naro rājanmucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The river Gaṅgā known as Mandākinī has arrived here by joining the river Sarasvatī. O king! the human being, after having a bath here, gets free from all sins.

## \|\| 3.9.3 \|\|

*śṛṇu rājanyathāvṛttamitihāsa purātanam \|*  
*ṛṣibhirbahudhā gītamarbude parvatottame \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O king! listen to the old historical description of this place of pilgrimage. The sages have sung this in many ways in this mountain of Arbuda.

## \|\| 3.9.4 \|\|

*ajapālo nṛpaśreṣṭhaḥ sūryavaṃśasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*saptadvīpavatīṃ pṛthvīṃ sa pāti nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Ajapāla—the best of kings born in the Surya \[Sūrya?\] dynasty was undoubtedly the protector of this earth comprising seven islands.

## \|\| 3.9.5 \|\|

*na hastino na pādātā na cāśvāstasya bhūpateḥ \|*  
*na rathāśca mahārāja na kośāśca tathāvidhāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. This king neither had elephants nor any infantry nor did he have any horse with him. He also did not have a chariot and treasury in any form.

## \|\| 3.9.6 \|\|

*na gṛhṇāti karaṃ rājanprajābhyothādhikaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*rājyaṃ sa īdṛśaṃ cakre sarvalokahite rataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The king never used to collect excess taxes from his subjects. By this, he used to rule in the welfare of people.

## \|\| 3.9.7 \|\|

*jātāparādho bhūpṛṣṭhe jāyate cetkathaṃcana \|*  
*taṃ gatvā nigrahaṃ tasya cakruḥ śastrāṇi tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. If there was any individual committing offence of any kind, he used to go immediately and bring that rogue to book.

## \|\| 3.9.8 \|\|

*evamasya narendrasya varttamānasya bhūtale \|*  
*sukhena ramate loko rājye nihatakaṃṭake \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. People used to live happily and without any difficulty with such a king on earth.

## \|\| 3.9.9 \|\|

*kāmaṃ varṣati parjanyaḥ sasyāni rasavaṃti ca \|*  
*gāvaḥ prabhūtadugdhāśca vidyamāne narādhipe \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. There used to be adequate rains resulting in flow of crops. Cows used to give milk in abundance with such a king around.

## \|\| 3.9.10 \|\|

*kenacittvatha kālena vasiṣṭho bhagavānmuniḥ \|*  
*tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena tasya gehamupāgataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Now the God-like sage Vasiṣṭha came to his house sometime in connection with pilgrimage.

## \|\| 3.9.11 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā pūjayāmāsa śāstradṛṣṭena vartmanā \|*  
*pratyutthānābhivādābhyāmarghyapādyādibhistathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Seeing him, the king got up from seat, welcomed him after paying due homage as per the prescribed rituals in Śāstras, and offered him all goods as necessary adjuctants \[adjunctants?\] of the activity of worship.

## \|\| 3.9.12 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃpūjitastena bhaktyā paramayā nṛpa \|*  
*sukhopaviṣṭo viśrāṃto vasiṣṭho munisattamaḥ \|*  
*rājarṣīṇāṃ kathāścakre devarṣīṇāṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Pleased with the homage offered with highest faith, the good mannered Vasiṣṭha sat down to take rest. Then he started to speak out the stories of all royal as well as divine sages.

## \|\| 3.9.13 \|\|

*tataḥ kathāvasāne tu kasmiṃścinnṛpasattama \|*  
*papraccha vinayopetastaṃ muniṃ śaṃsitavratam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. After the completion of speech of the Sage, the well-disposed king with all humility and in some context asked the sage as to what could be the well-settled practice of religious activity in connection with undertaking of austerity.

## \|\| 3.9.14 \|\|

*ajapāla uvāca \|*  
*atītānāgataṃ vipra varttamānaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*tvaṃ vetsi sakalaṃ brahmaṃstapaścaryāprabhāvataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

Ajapāla said:

14\. O Brāhmaṇa! you know everything—the past, the present and the future through the influence of your perseverance.

## \|\| 3.9.15 \|\|

*kautukaṃ hṛdi me jātaṃ varttate munipuṃgava \|*  
*prasādaḥ kriyatāṃ mahyaṃ kathayasva prasādataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O Sage! I have a curiosity in heart. With grace towards me and pleasure in mind, please explain me.

## \|\| 3.9.16 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*brūhi pārthivaśārdūla yatte manasi varttate \|*  
*kathayiṣyāmi tatsarvaṃ yadyapi syātsudurllabham \|\| 16 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

16\. O king! please speak out everything that is in your mind. I will let you know all those difficult things.

## \|\| 3.9.17 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*kena karmavipākena mamaitadrājyamuttamam \|*  
*niṣkaṇṭakaṃ sadā kṣemaṃ sarvakāmasamanvitam \|\| 17 \|\|*

The King said:

17\. What could be that deed of mine as a result of which this kingdom of mine is running in the best possible manner without any difficulty and with all actions getting accomplished with results?

## \|\| 3.9.18 \|\|

*na dīno na ca duḥkhārtto vyādhigrasto na ko'pi ca \|*  
*vidyate mama rājye ca na daridro mahāmune \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O great Sage! neither there are the poor, the pitiables, the unhappy souls nor are there souls affected with diseases in this kingdom of mine.

## \|\| 3.9.19 \|\|

*nārīyaṃ mama sādhvī ca prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī \|*  
*maccittā madgataprāṇā nityaṃ mama hite ratā \|*  
*anayā ciṃtitaṃ brahmansarvaṃ vistarato vada \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. This virtuous wife of mine is more important to me than even the life-giving breath. I accept that her mind is with me and her life is dependent on me. O Brāhmaṇa! please tell me in details all that she has thought about me.

## \|\| 3.9.20 \|\|

*kiṃ dānasya prabhāvena vratayāgasya vā mune \|*  
*tapaso vā muniśreṣṭha vratasya niyamasya ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O Sage! are these due to the influence of my giving gifts, or conduct of Yajña, or perseverance or due to the observance of rules connected with performance of religious austerities?

## \|\| 3.9.21 \|\|

*janmāntarakṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me \|*  
*kathayasva prasādena vistareṇa dvijottama \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. I have a curiosity that all these may be due to the good work done in my previous birth. O best Brāhmaṇa! kindly speak out to explain me.

## \|\| 3.9.22 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu sarvaṃ mahīpāla vistareṇa ca kathyate \|*  
*na ca manyustvayā kāryo na ca vrīḍā mahāmate \|\| 22 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:

22\. O king! listen in details as I say. Do not get hurt or feel ashamed.

## \|\| 3.9.23 \|\|

*anyadehāṃtare rājañchūdrajātisamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*śūdrajātiriyaṃ sādhvī tava patnī hyabhūtpurā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O king! in the other previous body (i.e., past life), you, were born in the last, i.e., the Śudra Varṇa of the four-fold Varṇa system. So was also your virtuous wife.

## \|\| 3.9.24 \|\|

*kenacittvatha kālena durbhikṣe samupasthite \|*  
*annakṣayānmahārāja sarva lokaḥ kṣudhārditaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. At certain juncture of time in that period, famine had occurred. Everywhere in the world, there was suffering from hunger due to the destruction of crops.

## \|\| 3.9.25 \|\|

*tatastvaṃ bhāryayā sārddhamanyadeśāṃtare gataḥ \|*  
*samāruhya ca kṛcchreṇa kasmiṃścidgirinirjhare \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. At that time you had proceeded to another country. In that country, ascending a range of mountains, you had crossed over a fountain.

## \|\| 3.9.26 \|\|

*tvayā dṛṣṭaṃ manohāri śubhaṃ paṃkajakānanam \|*  
*tatra snātvā payaḥ pītvā pitṛdevāḥ pratarpitāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. There, after seeing an auspicious pond full of an enticing forest of lotus, you took a bath there and offered libations of water to your parental ancestors.

## \|\| 3.9.27 \|\|

*manasā ciṃtitaṃ hyetatpadmānyādāya karomyaham \|*  
*vikrayaṃ yena cāhāro bhavenmama ca sarvathā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. You thought ‘let me take these lotuses and sell them so that we could arrange our food.’

## \|\| 3.9.28 \|\|

*tataḥ padmāni bhūrīṇi gṛhītvā bhāryayā saha \|*  
*gato yatra jano bhūri gataḥ pārthivasattama \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O king! then carrying along many lotuses, you went to a place where many people were already there.

## \|\| 3.9.29 \|\|

*na ke'pi prati gṛhṇaṃti lokā durbhikṣapīḍitāḥ \|*  
*bhramitastvaṃ ca sarvatra śrāṃto vairāgyamāgataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Being sufferers of famine, no individual purchased the lotuses. Moving around in the four directions you got tired and became dejected.

## \|\| 3.9.30 \|\|

*tato dināvasāne tu guhāmekāṃ samāśritaḥ \|*  
*bhūmau padmāni nikṣipya kṣudhāviṣṭaḥ prasuptavān \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. With the day ending you took rest in a cave. Putting the lotuses down on the ground you receded into sleep overtaken with hunger.

## \|\| 3.9.31 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu karṇayoste samāgataḥ \|*  
*paṭhatāṃ dvijamukhyānāṃ dhvanirvedapurāṇayoḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*
