31\. In the meantime, the reverberating sounds of best Brāhmaṇas reading out the Veda and the Purāṇas reached out to your ears.

## \|\| 3.9.32 \|\|

*taṃ śrutvā sahasotthāya jñātvā jāgaraṇaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*padmānyādāya tatraiva sabhāryaḥ śivamaṃdire \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Hearing that you became alert and got up. Carrying the lotuses, you went to the Śiva temple along with your wife.

## \|\| 3.9.33 \|\|

*tatra nāgavatī veśyā śivarātriparāyaṇā \|*  
*kedāre parayā bhaktyā karoti niśi jāgaram \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. A prostitute by name Nāgavatī engrossed in devotion towards Śiva was sitting awake there in the Kedāra temple throughout the night.

## \|\| 3.9.34 \|\|

*tasyāḥ pārśve sthitā dāsī tvayā pṛṣṭā nareśvara \|*  
*devasya purato bāle kimarthaṃ rātrijāgaram \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Then O king! you asked the maid putting up beside the temple as to what for such religious activity of staying awake in front of this God is being performed.

## \|\| 3.9.35 \|\|

*tayoktaṃ śivarātryāṃ vai veśyeyaṃ varavarṇinī \|*  
*kurute nāgavatī nāma rātrau bhaktyā ca jāgaram \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. She said: “This beautiful prostitute Nāgavatī is performing the religious activity of staying up for the night with faith and devotion to comply with the stipulations required for the ritual conducted in honour of Śiva on the fourteenth day of the waning period of the moon in the month of Chaitra, i.e., March.

## \|\| 3.9.36 \|\|

*yaḥ śraddhābhaktisaṃyuktaḥ kurute rātrijāgaram \|*  
*pūjayitvā mahādevaṃ sa yāti paramaṃ padam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Any individual who performs the religious activity of keeping awake in the night and worships Śiva with faith and devotion attains that ultimate position.

## \|\| 3.9.37 \|\|

*kṛtvopavāsaṃ padmairyyaḥ pūjayettryaṃbakaṃ naraḥ \|*  
*sa yāti rudrasālokyaṃ sevyamāno 'psarogaṇaiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. One who observing the religious ritual of keeping awake in the night worships the three-eyed Śiva obtains the service of divine beauties and attains that world of Śiva representing His lower image.

## \|\| 3.9.38 \|\|

*sakāmo labhate kāmāndevairapi sudurllabhān \|*  
*sa tvaṃ padmāni me dehi kāṃcanaṃ ca palatrayam \|*  
*eteṣāṃ mūlyamādāya prāṇādhāraṃ samācara \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Obtainance of desires even of those difficult for gods do materialise. Hence you give me the lotuses in exchange of three grams of gold. Protect your life taking this much as value for the lotuses.

## \|\| 3.9.39 \|\|

*tatastvaṃ bhāryayā cokto gṛhyamāṇe ca kāṃcane \|*  
*na grāhyaṃ mūlyameteṣāṃ tvayā nātha kathaṃcana \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Then while accepting the value in the form of gold, your wife said, ‘O Lord! do not accept the value for these.

## \|\| 3.9.40 \|\|

*upavāso balājjāto hyannābhāvādvayorapi \|*  
*padmairebhirharaḥ pūjyo dvābhyāmevādya niścayam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. ‘In any case, with scarcity of grains, there has been fasting for both of us under compulsion. Today, both of us will worship Śiva with these lotuses with all certainty.

## \|\| 3.9.41 \|\|

*idaṃ tvayā'dya karttavyaṃ tyājyamasyāstu kāṃcanam \|*  
*bhāryāyā vacanaṃ śrutvā taiḥ padmaiḥ pūjitaḥ śivaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. ‘It is our duty today to worship Śiva. Hence foresake the value offered in terms of gold.’ After hearing the words of wife, Śiva was worshipped with lotuses.

## \|\| 3.9.42 \|\|

*śraddhayā ca sabhāryeṇa jāgaraṃ ca śivāgrataḥ \|*  
*kṛtaṃ tvayā mahārāja bhāryayā śivamaṃdire \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O king! along with wife, you performed the religious activity of staying up for the night with faith before Śiva in the Śiva temple.

## \|\| 3.9.43 \|\|

*purāṇaśravaṇaṃ jātaṃ tatra pārthivasattama \|*  
*śivarātryāṃ mahārāja padmaistu pūjitaḥ śivaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. So O great king! having got up after hearing the Purāṇas you the well-behaved in the earthly world worshipped Śiva with lotuses on the fourteenth day of the waning period of moon in the month of Chaitra (i.e., March).

## \|\| 3.9.44 \|\|

*kedārasyāgrato bhaktyā rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*kṛtaṃ tvayā mahārāja ekāgreṇa ca cetasā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. O king! with the mind centered and with faith, you performed the religious activity of keeping awake throughout the night in front of God at Kedāra.

## \|\| 3.9.45 \|\|

*tataḥprabhāte saṃjāte bhikṣāṃ kṛtvā ca pāraṇā \|*  
*kṛtā tvayā mahārāja śivāgre saha bhāryayā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Then when the morning set in O king! you, after begging, had food along with wife before Śiva.

## \|\| 3.9.46 \|\|

*tataḥ kālāṃtareṇaiva kāladharmaṃ gato bhavān \|*  
*bhāryeyaṃ ca tvayā sārdhaṃ saṃpraviṣṭā hutāśanam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Then with the passage of time death obtained you. Your wife as representing your other half entered into the fire along with you.

## \|\| 3.9.47 \|\|

*tato jātā mahārāja daśārṇādhipateḥ sutā \|*  
*vaidehe nagare rājā jātastvaṃ pārthivottama \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Then you got birth as son of king of Daśarna \[Daśārṇa?\], and became the best king of the city of Vaideha.

## \|\| 3.9.48 \|\|

*ajapāla iti khyāto nāmnā ca dharaṇītale \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ tvaṃ ca vallabho nṛpasattama \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Becoming dear to all living beings you became renowned by the name of Ajapāla on earth.

## \|\| 3.9.49 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇājjātā bhāryeyaṃ prāṇasaṃmatā \|*  
*bhūyo'pi tava saṃjātā yanmāṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. It is due to this reason that your wife has been born dearer to you more than your own life. Hence, what has happened, is solely due to you which you are asking me.

## \|\| 3.9.50 \|\|

*tasya devasya māhātmyātkedārasya mahīpateḥ \|*  
*rājyaṃ te sukhadaṃ nṛṇāṃ tathā nihatakaṇṭakam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Hence, O king! it is due to the greatness of the God Kedāra that people are happy in your kingdom and it has been divested of all difficulties.

## \|\| 3.9.51 \|\|

*prāptaṃ tvayā mahārāja kedārasya prasādataḥ \|*  
*yena tvaṃ sainyahīno'pi pṛthivīṃ parirakṣasi \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. You have got this kingdom out of pleasure of the great God Kedāra and it is due to this that despite having no soldier you have become the full-fledged protector of this region on earth.

## \|\| 3.9.52 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sa rājā vismayānvitaḥ \|*  
*gamanāya matiṃ cakre kedāraṃ prati bhūmipaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

52\. The king got into a state of astonishment hearing these words of Vasiṣṭha. The king then made up his mind to visit Kedāra.

## \|\| 3.9.53 \|\|

*sa gatvā parvate ramye pūjayitvā ca taṃ vibhum \|*  
*śivarātriparaḥ samyagvarṣevarṣe babhūva ha \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Then having gone to the mountain and having worshipped Lord Kedāra, the king remained engaged for years in observance of the religious ritual undertaken on the fourteenth day of the waning period of moon in the month of Chaitra, (i.e., March).

## \|\| 3.9.54 \|\|

*putraṃ rājye ca saṃsthāpya tato'rbudamathāgamat \|*  
*prāpto muktiṃ tato bhūyaḥ sabhāryastatprabhāvataḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The king went to the Arbuda mountain after handing over the kingdom to son. Then along with wife, he obtained salvation.

## \|\| 3.9.55 \|\|

*etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ kedārasya mahīpate \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ śubhadaṃ nṛṇāṃ sarva pāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. O king! I have described all this with regard to the greatness of Kedāra. It is an agent of goodness for all and the destroyer of sins.

## \|\| 3.9.56 \|\|

*māghaphālgunayormadhye kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśī \|*  
*śivarātririti khyātā bhūtale'sminmahāmate \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The religious ritual undertaken on the fourteenth day in between the period of Māgha and Chaitra (i.e., February and March) is well-known on earth.

## \|\| 3.9.57 \|\|

*tasyāṃ tu sarvathā rājanyātrāṃ tasya samācaret \|*  
*kedārasya mahārāja prakuryātpūjanaṃ nṛpa \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. O king! You thus need to observe visiting Kedāra by all means on that day. You must worship Kedāra in the best possible way and manner.

## \|\| 3.9.58 \|\|

*māghakṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ yaḥ kuryāttatra jāgaram \|*  
*kṛtopavāso nṛpate śivalokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. By observing the ritual of staying up the night on the fourteenth day of the waning period of the moon in the month of Māgha (i.e., February) and by fasting, O king! you can attain the world of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.9.59 \|\|

*snātvā gaṃgāsarasvatyoḥ saṃgame sarvakāmade \|*  
*ye prapaśyanti kedāraṃ te yāsyaṃti parāṃ gatim \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Those who after taking a bath in the wish-fulfilling confluence of Gaṅgā and Sarasvatī take a look of Kedāra obtain the ultimate passage.

## \|\| 3.9.60 \|\|

*kuṇḍe kedārasaṃjñe yaḥ prapibedvimalaṃ jalam \|*  
*saptapūrvānsapta parānpūrvajāṃstārayettu saḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Those who drink the clear water of the pond named Kedāra, fix the cross-over of seven ancestral generations before and after them.

## \|\| 3.9.61 \|\|

*yaścaitacchṛṇuyānnityaṃ bhaktyā paramayā nṛpa \|*  
*so'pi pāpairvimucyeta kedārasya prabhāvataḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O king! one who hears this story with supreme faith becomes free from all sins. This is the impact of the great God Kedāra.

## Chapter 10 - Pilgrimages in the Arbuda region during Kali Yuga

## \|\| 3.10.1 \|\|

*yayātiruvāca \|*  
*kedāraṃ śrūyate brahmanparvate ca himācale \|*  
*gaṃgā tasmādviniṣkrāntā praviṣṭā pūrvasāgaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

Yayāti said:

1\. You have heard about Kedāra in the supreme mountain Himālaya. The river Gaṅgā has come out of it and has entered the sea in the east.

## \|\| 3.10.2 \|\|

*tathā sarasvatī devī cūtavṛkṣādvinirgatā \|*  
*paścimaṃ sāgaraṃ prāptā gṛhītvā vaḍavānalam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. And the river Sarasvatī has come out of the mango groves. Absorbing the heat of big fires, it has flown into the sea on the west.

## \|\| 3.10.3 \|\|

*kathamatra samāyātaḥ kedāraścātra kautukam \|*  
*sarvaṃ vistarato brūhi vicitraṃ mama bhūsura \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. How could a place Kedāra come up there? This is very astonishing and I have a curiosity. O Brāhmaṇa! please narrate all these strange things in details.

## \|\| 3.10.4 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*satyametanmahārāja yanno'tra paripṛcchasi \|*  
*śṛṇuṣvāvahito bhūtvā yathā jātaṃ śrutaṃ tu vai \|\| 4 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

4\. O king! what all you are asking are true. Listen carefully to the way it has been and as I have heard.

## \|\| 3.10.5-8 \|\|

*gaṃgādyāni ca tīrthāni kedārādyā divaukasaḥ \|*  
*mayā saha purā devāḥ śakrādyā nṛpasattamāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*brahmāṇaṃ prati rājendra gatāḥ sarve maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*sarve tatra kathāścakrurdharmyā nānā pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 6 \|\|*

*samudāye ca devānāṃ sarvatīrthāni pārthiva \|*  
*kṣetrāṇyupa sthitānyeva vanānyupavanāni ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tataḥ kathāprasaṃgena indraḥ prāha caturmukham \|*  
*kautukena samāyuktaḥ papraccha nṛpasattama \|\| 8 \|\|*

5-8. In olden times, centres of pilgrimage like Gaṅgā, resting places of gods like Kedāra along with gods like Indra and others and with other great sages went to Brahmā. All of them conducted many and different types of religious discourses there. O king! all places of pilgrimage, regions, forests and gardens belonging to gods were present in this congregation. Eventually, in the course of discussion, Indra told Brahmā, “O king! this be happened to utter in curiosity.”

## \|\| 3.10.9 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*bhagavanpuṇyamāhātmyaṃ śrotumicchāmi sāṃpratam \|*  
*pramāṇaṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ kṛtādīnāṃ pṛthagvidham \|\| 9 \|\|*

Indra said:

9\. O God! now I desire to hear about the greatness of good. As a matter of proof please tell me about the distinction of ‘Kṛta yuga’ amongst all.

## \|\| 3.10.10 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*lakṣaṃ saptadaśa proktaṃ yugamānaṃ surādhipa \|*  
*aṣṭāviṃśatibhiḥ sārddhaṃ sahasraiḥ kṛtamucyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

10\. O Indra! Yugas have been said to comprise 70 lakh years. From these, one half of twenty eight thousand years is said to constitute the Kṛta Yuga.

## \|\| 3.10.11 \|\|

*lakṣadvādaśabhiḥ proktaṃ yugaṃ tretābhisaṃjñitam \|*  
*ṣaṇṇavatyadhikaiścaiva sahasraiḥ parimāṇitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Twelve lakh years from that stated above is named as Tretā Yuga. In mutual give and take in commercial exchanges it has been measured to comprise more than one hundred thousand years.

## \|\| 3.10.12 \|\|

*lakṣāṇyaṣṭau catuḥṣaṣṭisahasraiḥ parikīrtitam \|*  
*tato vai dvāparaṃ nāma yugaṃ devaprakīrtitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. There has been a Yuga renowned to comprise eight lakh and sixty-four thousand years. This has been proclaimed as the Dvāpara Yuga by gods.

## \|\| 3.10.13 \|\|

*lakṣaiścaturbhirvikhyāto dvātriṃśadbhiḥ kalistathā \|*  
*sahasraiśca suraśreṣṭha yugamānamitīritam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. There has been still another Yuga well-known as comprising four lakh and thirty-two thousand years which is called the Kali Yuga. This is how it has been the established practice of laying down Yugas in thousands of years by the best God.

## \|\| 3.10.14 \|\|

*catuṣpadaḥ kṛte dharmaḥ śuklavarṇo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*na durbhikṣaṃ na ca vyādhistasminbhavati vai kvacit \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. There were four steps of righteousness and Viṣṇu was having a fair complexion in the Kṛta Yuga. There was hardly any famine or disease in this Yuga.

## \|\| 3.10.15 \|\|

*kriyate ca tadā dharmo nākāle maraṇaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*lāṃgalena vinā sasyaṃ bhūrikṣīrāśca dhenavaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. With religious and moral duties being performed, there was no untimely death of humans at that time. Crops could be yielded without ploughing and the cows used to give abundant milk.

## \|\| 3.10.16 \|\|

*kāmaḥ krodho bhayaṃ lobho matsaraścābhyasūyatā \|*  
*tasminyuge sahasrākṣa na bhavaṃti kadācana \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Bad qualities like lust, anger, fear, greed and jealousy could hardly be possible in that Yuga.

## \|\| 3.10.17 \|\|

*tatastretāyuge jātastripādo dharma eva ca \|*  
*cirāyuṣo narāstasminraktavarṇo janārdanaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Then ushered in the Treta \[Tretā?\] Yuga in which there were three steps to righteousness. With people having a long life Viṣṇu was of red complexion in this Yuga.

## \|\| 3.10.18 \|\|

*tasminyajñāḥ pravarttaṃte prāṇināmiṣṭadāyinaḥ \|*  
*na kāmādipravṛttiśca tasminsaṃjāyate nṛṇām \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. There used to be Yajñas as a measure of fulfilling peoples’ aspirations. People did not have the disposition towards enjoyment of desires.

## \|\| 3.10.19 \|\|

*tapasā brahmacaryeṇa snānairdānaiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|*  
*tathā yajñairjapairhomaistatra vṛttirbhavennṛṇām \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. People’s occupation in that Yuga happened to be remaining engaged in austerity, observance of chastity, having a bath as fulfillment of religious activity, making offerings, having a different type of Yajña, making of sacrificial offerings to fire and taking the name of God repeatedly in one’s mind.

## \|\| 3.10.20 \|\|

*tatastu dvāparaṃ nāma tṛtīyaṃ yuga mucyate \|*  
*dvipado dharmaḥ sañjātaḥ pītavarṇo janārddanaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then the third Yuga named as Dvāpara let people little loose. In this Yuga there were two steps to religious righteousness and Viṣṇu was yellow complexioned.

## \|\| 3.10.21 \|\|

*phalākāṃkṣāpravṛttāni japayajñatapāṃsi ca \|*  
*satyānṛtānvito loko dvāpare surasattama \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Repeatedly taking of name of God within one’s mind, Yajñas and religious austerities were all conducted with desire for fruits. People were followers of truth and were equally inclined towards dance (Merriment) and the King was well-disposed during this Yuga.

## \|\| 3.10.22 \|\|

*tatrānyonyaṃ mahīpālā yuyudhurvasudhātale \|*  
*supūtāśca divaṃ yāṃti yajñairiṣṭvā janārdanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The kings on earth at this time were fighting among one another. They used to go to the heavenly kingdom after attaining purity through worship of Viṣṇu by Yajña.

## \|\| 3.10.23 \|\|

*tataḥ kaliyugaṃ ghoraṃ caturthaṃ tu prava rttate \|*  
*ekapādo bhaveddharmaḥ saṃtrasto nityapūjane \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Then the fourth Yuga, i.e., Kali Yuga starts in which there is only one step to religious righteousness. People remain fearful in this Yuga and regular worship is undertaken.

## \|\| 3.10.24 \|\|

*kṛṣṇavarṇo bhavedviṣṇuḥ pāpādhikyaṃ pravartate \|*  
*māyā ca matsaraścaiva kāmaḥ krodhastathā bhayam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Viṣṇu becomes of a black complexion and there is relatively a greater prevalence of sins. So also cheating, jealousy, greed, anger and fear prevail.

## \|\| 3.10.25 \|\|

*arthalubdhāstathā bhūpā lobhamohaśatānvitāḥ \|*  
*alpāyuṣo narāstatra alpasasyā ca medinī \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Becoming followers of greed and desire, people in the kingdom remain occupied with how to gain wealth. The age (Longevity) of life with people reduces and the earth also yields less crops.

## \|\| 3.10.26 \|\|

*alpakṣīrāstathā gāvaḥ satyahīnā dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*tatra māyāvino lokā jaihvyaupasthyaparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Cows give less milk and the Brāhmaṇas become bereft of truth. People cheat and stay assrued under the garb of happiness of taste and sex.

## \|\| 3.10.27 \|\|

*satyahīnāstathā pāpā bhaviṣyaṃti kalau yuge \|*  
*tatra ṣoḍaśame varṣe narāḥ palitakuntalāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. With deterioration of truth, sins proliferate in Kali Yuga and hairs of people get gray at the age of sixteen.

## \|\| 3.10.28 \|\|

*nāryo dvādaśame varṣe bhaviṣyaṃti sugarbhitāḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati kramādvarṇasaṃkaraśca surādhipa \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Women get pregnant at the age of twelve and O Indra! people become of a dirtier and mixed complexion at this time.

## \|\| 3.10.29 \|\|

*ekākārā bhaviṣyaṃti sarvavarṇāśramāśca vai \|*  
*nāśaṃ yāsyaṃti yajñāśca kuladharmaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. All Varṇas and Āśramas become one in this age. Yajñas and the regular rituals followed for ages in a family head towards ruination.

## \|\| 3.10.30 \|\|

*vyarthāni tatra tīrthāni mlecchaspṛṣṭāni sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyaṃti suraśreṣṭha prabhāvarahitāni ca \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. All places of pilgrimage become meaningless due to their coming in contact with outcastes, non-Aryans. Even the best of kings become bereft of influence.

## \|\| 3.10.31-32 \|\|

*etacchrutvā tato vākyaṃ brahmaṇo'vyaktajanmanaḥ \|*  
*tatra sthitāni tīrthāni brahmāṇamidamabruvan \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tīrthānyūcuḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ vayaṃ bhaviṣyāmaḥ saṃprāpte dāruṇe kalau \|*  
*sthānaṃ no brūhi deveśa sthātavyaṃ ca sadaiva hi \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Having heard these statements of Brahmā whose birth is unknown, the centers of pilgrimage stationed there told Brahmā, “You have stated what our position will be in the difficult Kali Yuga. With no place for us O God! please tell the selected places that could always be ours in this Yuga.”

## \|\| 3.10.33 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*arbudaḥ parvataśreṣṭhaḥ kalistatra na vidyate \|*  
*atastatra ca gaṃtavyaṃ tīrthairāyatanaiḥ saha \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Brahmā said, “there is the best of mountains by name Arbuda where Kali cannot prevail. Hence that is the destination for all centres of pilgrimage to have their station.

## \|\| 3.10.34 \|\|

*api kṛtvā mahatpāpamarbudaṃ prekṣate tu yaḥ \|*  
*kalidoṣavinirmuktaḥ sa yāsyati parāṃ gatim \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. “Any individual who, despite having committed the biggest of sins, takes a look of the Arbuda mountain, obtains the ultimate passage becoming free from all the shortcomings of Kali Yuga.”

## \|\| 3.10.35 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā caturvaktro brahmalokaṃ gato nṛpa \|*  
*tataḥ sarvāṇi tīrthāni gatāni ca kalau yuge \|\| 35 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

35\. Saying like this O king! Brahmā then went to the Brahma world. Then all the centres of pilgrimage went to the Arbuda mountain in the Kali Yuga.

## \|\| 3.10.36-37 \|\|

*bhūmāvarbudaśailendre saṃsthitāni kalerbhayāt \|*  
*gaṃgā sarasvatī caiva yamunā puṣkarāṇi ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

*kurukṣetraṃ prabhāsaṃ ca brahmāvartaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*tisraḥkoṭyo'rddhakoṭiśca yāni tīrthāni bhūtale \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. With the presence of Arbuda, the Chief of Mountains on earth, the rivers Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī and even the ponds and places of pilgrimage such as Kurukṣetra, Prabhāsa, Brahmāvarta including all other pilgrim centres, spread over three and a half crore lands went to the Arbuda mountain out of fear of Kali Yuga.

## \|\| 3.10.38 \|\|

*teṣāṃ vāsaśca sañjātaḥ parvate'rbudasaṃjñike \|*  
*evaṃ tatra samāpannā gaṃgā caiva sarasvatī \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. This is how every pilgrim centre could have its place of fixation on the Arbuda mountain and this is how Gaṅgā and Sarasvatī also came there.

## \|\| 3.10.39 \|\|

*tatra śāṃtā narāḥ samyakparaṃ nirvāṇamāpnuyuḥ \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ kṛtvā mahārāja svarge yāṃti ca pūrvajāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. People with their minds bent upon peace attain emancipation from rebirth with all certainty there. All ancestors of a family go to heaven by conduct of religious ceremony there in honour of the departed souls.

## \|\| 3.10.40 \|\|

*śṛṇu tatrābhavatpūrvaṃ yadāścaryaṃ mahāmate \|*  
*ṛṣirmaṃkaṇakonāma sarasvatyāstaṭe sthitaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O king! there was some astonishing happening there. There was a sage by name Mankana \[Maṅkaṇa?\] staying on the banks of Sarasvatī.

## \|\| 3.10.41 \|\|

*tapastepe sudharmātmā kāmakrodhavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*tasyaivaṃ vartamānasya kṣutamāsītkadācana \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Giving up desire and anger that pure soul was engaged in performance of religious austerity. While continuing in that state once shivering with cold he began to sneeze.

## \|\| 3.10.42 \|\|

*pittaṃ prapatitaṃ tatra tacca raktamayaṃ babhau \|*  
*taddṛṣṭvā'tīva hṛṣṭaḥ sa maṃkaṇarṣirbabhūva ha \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. There was some bile lying there. That was appearing like red in colour. Having seen that the sage Mankana \[Maṅkaṇa?\] became pleased.

## \|\| 3.10.43-44 \|\|

*siddho'hamiti vijñāya tato nṛtyaṃ cakāra saḥ \|*  
*tasyaivaṃ vartamānasya jagatsthāvarajaṃgamam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tatra saṃkṣobhamāpannaṃ sāgarā api cukṣubhuḥ \|*  
*gṛhakṛtyāni saṃtyajya sarve vismayamā gatāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. ‘Perceiving (Thinking) that I have become accomplished he began to dance.’ With him continuing in that condition, the entire world both mobile and immobile as well as the seas got excited. The seas began to sprinkle water out. Everyone ceased to attend to his household duties and remained astonished.

## \|\| 3.10.45 \|\|

*tasyaivaṃ nṛtyamānasya sarve lokā nṛpottama \|*  
*nanṛtuḥ pārthivaśreṣṭha prabhāvāttasya sanmuneḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O best king! with his dancing like this everyone in the world too began to dance influenced by the truthful and best of sages on earth.

## \|\| 3.10.46 \|\|

*tato devagaṇāḥ sarve gatvā kāmaniṣūdanam \|*  
*yathā'yaṃ nṛtyate naiva tathā kuru maheśvara \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Then all gods went near Śaṃkara and said, “O Great God! please do something so that he does not dance.”

## \|\| 3.10.47 \|\|

*atha brāhmaṇarūpeṇa śaṃbhunokto dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*tvayā brahmaṃstapastaptamadhunā nṛtyate katham \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Then assuming an image of Brāhmaṇa, Śiva told that best of Brāhmaṇas, ‘Why are you dancing while pursuing the highest perseverance?’

## \|\| 3.10.48 \|\|

*maṃkaṇa uvāca \|*  
*kiṃ na paśyasi he brahmanraktaṃ pittaṃ ca me sthitam \|*  
*saṃjātaṃ siddhimāpanno raktaṃ pittaṃ yato mama \|\| 48 \|\|*

Maṅkaṇa said:

48\. “O Brāhmaṇa! is it not visible to you that my bile has turned red? I have attained that accomplished fulfilment as my bile has already become red.

## \|\| 3.10.49 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇāddharṣāddvija nṛtyaṃ karomyaham \|*  
*evamuktastatastena devadevo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O Brāhmaṇa! due to this reason, I am dancing out of pleasure.” He told in this way to the Great God.

## \|\| 3.10.50 \|\|

*tarjanyā tāḍayāmāsa svāṃguṣṭhaṃ nṛpasattama \|*  
*tatoṃguṣṭhādviniṣkrāṃtaṃ bhasma vai bisapāṃḍuram \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. O virtuous king! Śaṃkara struck his thumb with the index finger of his own and then white-like ash similar to the fibre of lotus came out of his thumb.

## \|\| 3.10.51 \|\|

*tato maṃkaṇakaṃ prāha paśya vipra karānmama \|*  
*śubhraṃ bhasma viniṣkrāṃtaṃ paśya me dvija kautukam \|\| 51 \|\|*

Then he said:

51\. O Brāhmaṇa! look at this feat of mine with all curiosity where white ash is coming out of my finger.

## \|\| 3.10.52 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*taddṛṣṭvā vismito vipro jñātvā taṃ vṛṣabhadhvajam \|*  
*jānubhyāmavaniṃ gatvā vākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Pulastya said, “That Brāhmaṇa got preplexed after witnessing this and then having recognized him as the image of Śiva, kneeled down and bowing before him started saying like this.

## \|\| 3.10.53 \|\|

*maṃkaṇa uvāca \|*  
*nūnaṃ bhavānmahādevaḥ sākṣāddṛṣṭaḥ prasīda me \|*  
*niścitaṃ tvaṃ mayā jñāta etanme hṛdi vartate \|\| 53 \|\|*

Maṅkaṇa said:

53\. You are of course the Great God. I am seeing you directly. Please be pleased with me. My heart says that I have perhaps recognized you.

## \|\| 3.10.54 \|\|

*nānyasyāyaṃ prabhāvaśca tvayā yo me pradarśitaḥ \|*  
*māṃ samuddhara deveśa kṛpāṃ kṛtvā maheśvara \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Whatever you exhibited before me cannot be possible under anyone else’s influence. O Śaṃkara! be kind and rescue me.

## \|\| 3.10.55 \|\|

*śrīmahādeva uvāca \|*  
*samyagjñāto'smi viprendra tvayā'haṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te nṛtyādhikyaṃ yataḥ kṛtam \|\| 55 \|\|*

The great God said:

55\. O Brāhmaṇa! You have recognized me correctly and there is no doubt about it. Let there be your welfare. Ask for a boon as you have already danced excessively.

## \|\| 3.10.56 \|\|

*maṃkaṇa uvāca \|*  
*ye'tra snānaṃ prakurvaṃti sarasvatyāṃ samāhitāḥ \|*  
*tvatprasādātphalaṃ teṣāṃ rājasūyāśvamedhayoḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

Maṅkaṇa said:

56\. Let the fruits awaiting that specific worship in which horses are offered to the fire or the one in which a king makes offerings to fire to win the consent of everyone for his coronation be obtainable by a mere bath in the Sarasvatī river undertaken with undivided sincerity of mind.

## \|\| 3.10.57 \|\|

*śrīmahādeva uvāca \|*  
*ye'tra snānaṃ kariṣyaṃti sarasvatyāṃ samāhitāḥ \|*  
*te yāsyaṃti paraṃ sthānaṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitam \|\| 57 \|\|*

Śrī Mahādeva said:

57\. Those who take a bath in this Sarasvatī with undivided attention will obtain that ultimate position becoming free from old age and death.

## \|\| 3.10.58 \|\|

*atra gaṃgāsarasvatyoḥ saṃgame lokaviśrute \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ kuryurdvijaśreṣṭha te yāsyaṃti parāṃ gatim \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. O Brāhmaṇa! those who perform the religious ceremony in this confluence of the Gaṅgā and Sarasvatī in this world in remembrance of their family ancestors, will attain that ultimate passage.

## \|\| 3.10.59 \|\|

*suvarṇaṃ ye'tra dāsyaṃti yathāśaktyā dvijottame \|*  
*sarva pāpavinirmuktāste yāsyanti parāṃ gatim \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Those who donate gold to the good Brāhmaṇa as per their abilities will attain that ultimate passage getting free from all sins.

## \|\| 3.10.60 \|\|

*ityuktvāṃtardadhe rājandevadevo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. O king! having said in this manner, Mahādeva—the God of all gods disappeared from sight.

## Chapter 11 - Eminence of Koṭīśvara

## \|\| 3.11.1 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchennṛpaśreṣṭha devaṃ koṭīśvaraṃ param \|*  
*yaṃ dṛṣṭvā mānavaḥ samyakparāṃ siddhimavāpnuyāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

1\. O foremost king! then one needs to visit the supreme God Koṭiśvara by having a look of which humans definitely attain fulfilment.

## \|\| 3.11.2 \|\|

*śṛṇu tatrābhavatpūrvaṃ yadāścaryaṃ mahīpate \|*  
*dakṣiṇasyā munivarāḥ koṭisaṃkhyāpramāṇataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Before that O king! listen to one astounding incident that happened there. It was a proven fact that one crore prominent sages used to live in its southern side.

## \|\| 3.11.3-4 \|\|

*anyo'nyaṃ spardhayā sarve helayā'rbudamāgatāḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ pūrvamahaṃ pūrvaṃ prapaśyāmyacaleśvaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

*āgamiṣyati yaḥ paścādbrāhmaṇaḥ śvā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*pāpīyānbhaktirahitaḥ śraddhāhīno bhaviṣyati \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Competing among one another like in a game of play they all came to this Arbuda mountain presupposing within themselves that the sage arriving last would become a dog, and become devoid of devotion and faith.

## \|\| 3.11.5 \|\|

*ityevaṃ spardhamānāste helayā'rbudamāgatāḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sarve yatātmānaḥ samyagvrataparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In this way, playing in mutual competition like in a game, they all came to Arbuda mountain and then in conformity with time they all got themselves engaged in the performance of worship as a fulfilment of some mental resolve made respectively in their minds.

## \|\| 3.11.6 \|\|

*śāṃtāstapasvinaḥ sarve vedavidyāviśāradāḥ \|*  
*teṣāmīhitamājñāya samyakkāmaniṣūdanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. All the Brāhmaṇas were composed in mind, devout in religious austerities and adroit in the learning of Veda. Śaṃkara became eager to know their wish.

## \|\| 3.11.7 \|\|

*kṛpayā parayāviṣṭo bhaktibhāvānmaheśvaraḥ \|*  
*koṭiṃ kṛtvā'tmaliṃgānāṃ tasminsthāne vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Driven by their feeling of devotion, Śaṃkara placed there with great kindness a crore of Liṅgas of Śiva worshipped in the form of stone separately from one another.

## \|\| 3.11.8 \|\|

*ekasminneva kāle tu sarvairdṛṣṭo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*munibhiśca nṛpaśreṣṭha koṭisaṃkhyaiḥ pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The glimpse of Śaṃkara in crores of number could be seen by everyone distinctly.

## \|\| 3.11.9 \|\|

*atha te munayaḥ sarve samaṃ dṛṣṭvā maheśvaram \|*  
*vismayotphullanayanā sādhusādhviti cābruvan \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Seeing Śaṃkara all together, all the sages then keeping their eyes wide open in wonder said ‘excellent! excellent!’

## \|\| 3.11.10 \|\|

*bhaktiyuktā dvijāḥ sarve'stuvaṃste vaidikaiḥ stavaiḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ tuṣṭastataḥ śaṃbhurvākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. All the Brāhmaṇas with devotion sang the Vedic hymns meant for Śaiṇkara. Being pleased, Śaṃkara started to say.

## \|\| 3.11.11 \|\|

*śrīmahādeva uvāca \|*  
*tuṣṭo'haṃ munayaḥ sarve śraddhayā parayā hi vaḥ \|*  
*varaṃ vai vriyatāṃ śīghraṃ sarvaiścaiva pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 11 \|\|*

The gracious Mahādeva said:

11\. O Sages! I am pleased with your highest faith. Now each one of you can have boon from me.

## \|\| 3.11.12 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*eṣa eva varo'smākaṃ sarveṣāṃ hṛdi varttitaḥ \|*  
*yugapaddarśanāddeva jāyatāṃ phalamuttamam \|\| 12 \|\|*

The sages said:

12\. We all wish for a single boon in our minds that the good fruit be received by all of us taking a look of yours together.

## \|\| 3.11.13 \|\|

*śrīmahādeva uvāca \|*  
*na vṛthā darśanaṃ me syādviśeṣādbrāhmaṇasya ca \|*  
*darśanaṃ ye kariṣyaṃti teṣāṃ ca tīrthajaṃ phalam \|\| 13 \|\|*

The gracious Mahādeva said:

13\. A look of mine never goes in vain for a Brāhmaṇa in particular. The fruit of pilgrimage is obtainable for those who have a look of mine.

## \|\| 3.11.14-15 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*avaśyaṃ yadi dātavyo varo'smākaṃ maheśvara \|*  
*ekaṃ koṭimayaṃ liṃgaṃ kriyatāṃ vṛṣabhadhvaja \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yasmindṛṣṭe phalaṃ nṛṇāṃ jāyate koṭiliṃgajam \|*  
*evameṣa varo'smākaṃ dīyatāṃ vṛṣabhadhvaja \|\| 15 \|\|*

The sages said:

14-15. O Śaṃkara! if it is definite that you have to give us a boon please make crores of Liṅgas like this worshipable in the form of stones and by taking a look of which people will get the fruits of crores of Liṅgas worshipped. O Śaṃkara! we desire such a type of boon.

## \|\| 3.11.16 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ saprārthamānānāṃ munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām \|*  
*nirbhidya parvataśreṣṭhaṃ sahasā liṃgamudgatam \|\| 16 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

16\. With the sages making such a prayer together, the worshipable Liṅga of Śiva pierced out of this best mountain all of a sudden.

## \|\| 3.11.17-20 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu vāguvācāśarīriṇī \|*  
*kṛpayā parayā sarvāṃstānṛṣīnvasudhādhipa \|\| 17 \|\|*

*vāguvāca \|*  
*koṭīśvarākhyaṃ me liṃgaṃ loke khyātiṃ gamiṣyati \|*  
*māghakṛṣṇacaturddaśyāṃ yaścainaṃ pūjayiṣyati \|\| 18 \|\|*

*sarvaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ tasya phalaṃ viprā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*dākṣiṇātyo naro yastu śrāddhamatra kariṣyati \|\| 19 \|\|*

*phalaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ tasya gayāśrāddhasamaṃ bhavet \|*  
*tasmādviśeṣataḥ pūjyaṃ mama liṃgaṃ ca mānavaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

17-20. Just at that moment a voice from the bodiless came out and told those sages, “This Liṅga of mine will be famed by name Koṭiśvara in the world. Crore times fruits will be attainable by all those Brāhmaṇas who will worship it on the fourteenth day of the waning period of moon in the month of Pausa \[Pauṣa?\] (i.e., January). Whichever Brāhmaṇa from the Southern country performs the religious ceremony in memory of his ancestors here will get crore times fruits equal to the same such religious ceremony performed in Gayā. Therefore, people should worship this Liṅga of mine.”

## \|\| 3.11.21 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā tu sā vāṇī virarāma mahīpate \|*  
*tataste munayaḥ sarve gaṃdhadhūpānulepanaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

21\. The voice stopped after sounding like this. Then the sages with faith worshipped (the Liṅga) with incense and flavoured oil.

## \|\| 3.11.22 \|\|

*talliṃgaṃ pūjayāmāsuḥ śraddhayā parayā nṛpa \|*  
*pūjayitvā gatāḥ siddhiṃ sarve liṃgaprasādataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O king! the act of worship was done with great faith in this way and all the Brāhmaṇas after worshipping attained fulfilment with the grace of the worshipable Liṅga.

## Chapter 12 - Greatness of Rūpa Tīrtha

## \|\| 3.12.1 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchennṛpaśreṣṭha rūpatīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*sarvapāpaharaṃ nṝṇāṃ rūpasaubhaṇyadāyakam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

1\. O best king! after this go to the centre of pilgrimage with good appearance, i.e., Rūpa Tīrtha. All sins of men go away by a visit here and good appearance and fortune is attained.

## \|\| 3.12.2 \|\|

*tatra pūrvaṃ vapurnāmnā loke khyātā varāpsarāḥ \|*  
*siddhiṃ gatā mahārāja yathā pūrvaṃ nigadyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O king! in a place by name Vapu there was a renowned divine beauty. It is mentioned that she had attained fulfilment there.

## \|\| 3.12.3 \|\|

*purā'sītkācidābhīrī virūpā vikṛtānanā \|*  
*lambodarī ca kugrīvā sthūladaṃtaśiroruhā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Earlier there was an ugly woman having a disfigured face for whom fear was unknown. Having a fat belly and crooked neck, she had such horn-like big teeth that the same appeared as if piercing out of her head.

## \|\| 3.12.4 \|\|

*ekadā phalamādātuṃ bhramamāṇā'rbudācale \|*  
*māghaśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ patitā girinirjhare \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Once she was roaming about in the Arbuda region in search of fruits. That was the third day of the rising period of moon in the month of Pauṣa (i.e., January). She fell off into a fountain in the mountain.

## \|\| 3.12.5 \|\|

*divyamālyāṃbaradharā divyairaṃgaiḥ samanvitā \|*  
*padmanetrā sukeśāṃtā sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In that beautiful and bright reservoir she got enjoined with a beautiful complexion, with lotus eyes, good hairs and with all traits pronounced.

## \|\| 3.12.6-7 \|\|

*sā saṃjātā mahārāja tīrthasyāsya prabhāvataḥ \|*  
*etasminneva kāle tu śakrastatra samāgataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*krīḍārthaṃ parvataśreṣṭhe tāṃ dadarśa śubhekṣaṇām \|*  
*tataḥ kāmaśarairviddhastāmuvāca sumadhyamām \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. O king! the emergence of hers with such a body was out of the influence of this centre of pilgrimage. In the meantime, a King arrived there in the same pronounced mountain for the purpose of playing. But then by beholding such a beautiful sight in that auspicious moment the king got pierced with an arrow of lust.

## \|\| 3.12.8 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*kā tvaṃ vada varārohe kimarthaṃ tvamihāgatā \|*  
*devī vā nāgakanyā vā siddhā vidyādharī tu vā \|\| 8 \|\|*

Indra said:

8\. Tell me who you are like a diamond? What for have you come here? Are you a goddess or the daughter of King of snakes Nāga or are you the embodiment of fulfilled knowledge?

## \|\| 3.12.9 \|\|

*mano me'pahṛtaṃ subhrūstvayā ca padmanetrayā \|*  
*śakro'haṃ sarvadeveśo bhaja māṃ cāruhāsini \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. I have been hijacked in mind by your well-moving brows and lotus eyes. I am the King of all gods. O beauty with a pleasing smile! entreat me.

## \|\| 3.12.10 \|\|

*nāryuvāca \|*  
*ābhīrī tridaśādhīśa tathāhaṃ bahubhartṛkā \|*  
*phalārthaṃ tu samāyātā patitā girinirjhare \|\| 10 \|\|*

The woman said:

10\. I am a woman having thirty husbands and hence fearless. Having come here with the aim of fruits, I have fallen into the fountain in the mountain.

## \|\| 3.12.11 \|\|

*snātvā rūpamidaṃ prāptā surūpaṃ ca śubhaṃ mayā \|*  
*durllabhastvaṃ hi devānāṃ kiṃ punarmartyajanmanām \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. I have got this beautiful and good appearance by dint of a bath here. You, yourself is even difficult to obtain for gods. So what to speak of the mortals subject to repeated births and deaths?

## \|\| 3.12.12 \|\|

*vaśagāste surāḥ sarve mayi kiṃ kriyate spṛhā \|*  
*bhaja māṃ tridaśādhīśa yathākāmaṃ surādhipa \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Having all gods under your control what for are you desiring me? As the Lord of gods, you can have a share of mine according to your desire like my thirty husbands.

## \|\| 3.12.13-14 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*evamuktastayā śakraḥ kāmayāmāsa tāṃ tadā \|*  
*nivṛttamadano bhūtvā tāmuvāca sumadhyamām \|\| 13 \|\|*

*indra uvāca \|*  
*varaṃ varaya kalyāṇi yatte manasi varttate \|*  
*vinayāttava tuṣṭo'haṃ dāsyāmi varamuttamam \|\| 14 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

13-14. After her saying like this the King, i.e., Indra possessed with desire and desirous of winning her over, told her, “O giver of welfare! ask for the boon that is in your mind. I am pleased with your polite behaviour. I will give you a good boon.”

## \|\| 3.12.15 \|\|

*nāryuvāca \|*  
*māghaśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ naro vā vanitā tathā \|*  
*snānaṃ yaḥ kurute bhaktyā prītāḥ syuḥ sarvadevatāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

The woman said:

15\. Let all the gods be pleased by any man or woman taking bath here with faith on the third day of the rising period of the moon in the month of Pauṣa (i.e., January).

## \|\| 3.12.16 \|\|

*surūpaṃ jāyatāṃ teṣāṃ durllabhaṃ tridaśairapi \|*  
*māṃ naya tvaṃ sahasrākṣa surāvāsaṃ surādhipa \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Let the unattainable beauty of gods be obtainable for them. O King of gods! please take me along to the Heaven.

## \|\| 3.12.17 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*evamastviti tāmuktvā gṛhītvā tāṃ surādhipaḥ \|*  
*vimāne ca tayā sārddhaṃ jagāma tridivaṃ prati \|\| 17 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

17\. Saying ‘let it be so’ the King of gods, taking her along left for the heavenly kingdom in a space vehicle.

## \|\| 3.12.18 \|\|

*vapuḥ prāptaṃ tayā yasmāttasmātpā rthivasattama \|*  
*nāmnā vapuriti khyātā sā babhūva varāpsarāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. This is how after having got a pure body while on earth, the place is renowned as Vapu and she has got the same name as a divine beauty.

## \|\| 3.12.19 \|\|

*māghaśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ devāstasmiñjalāśaye \|*  
*snānaṃ sarve prakurvaṃti prabhāte bhaktisaṃyutāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The gods with faith take bath in that pond in morning on the third day of the rising period of the moon in the month of (Pauṣa, i.e., January).

## \|\| 3.12.20 \|\|

*tatrānyā devakanyāśca siddhayakṣāṃganāstathā \|*  
*yastatra kurute snānaṃ tasminkāle narādhipa \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O king! the other divine unmarried girls as well as Yakṣa girls taking a bath there at that time also attained fulfilment.

## \|\| 3.12.21 \|\|

*rūpaṃ ca labhate tādṛgyādṛglabdhaṃ tayā purā \|*  
*sarve tatra bhaviṣyaṃti siddhavidyādharoragāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Appearance is gained over there as she got it completely there. Everyone becomes accomplished there endowed with learning.

## \|\| 3.12.22 \|\|

*tasyaiva pūrvadigbhāge bilamasti suśobhanam \|*  
*yatrāgatya prakurvaṃti snānaṃ pātālakanyakāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. There is a beautiful cave on the eastern side where the unmarried girls inhabiting hell take bath.

## \|\| 3.12.23 \|\|

*tatra snātvā gṛhītvāpo bile tasminvrajaṃti tāḥ \|*  
*tatra vaināyake pīṭhe mahatpāṣāṇajaṃ jalam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. After taking a bath there, they proceed to the cave carrying a bit of water with them. From there they take a bit of water from the stone at the sitting place of Lord Gaṇeśa.

## \|\| 3.12.24 \|\|

*tenodakena saṃyuktaḥ siddho bhavati mānavaḥ \|*  
*gṛhītvā tajjalaṃ yastu yatra yatrābhigacchati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. After mixing both the water humans become accomplished. The living beings carrying that water go here and there.

## \|\| 3.12.25 \|\|

*svarge vā bhūtale vāpi na kenāpi pradhṛṣyate \|*  
*tatrāsti vivaradvāre tilakonāma pādapaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. There is a tree by name Tilaka on the doorway of that cave which cannot be seen anywhere either in heaven or on the surface of earth.

## \|\| 3.12.26 \|\|

*tasya puṣpaiḥ phalaiścaiva sarvaṃ kāryaṃ prasiddhyati \|*  
*bhakṣaṇāddhāraṇādvāpi siddho bhavati mānavaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. All works get accomplished by its flowers and fruits. The man becomes fulfilled by eating or bearing those on the body.

## \|\| 3.12.27 \|\|

*tasminbile tu pāṣāṇāḥ samantācchaṃkhasannibhāḥ \|*  
*tenodakena saṃspṛṣṭā bhavaṃti ca hiraṇmayāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The stones in that cave spread across all directions are like conches. It appears they wish to have a touch of that water through which they turn golden.

## \|\| 3.12.28 \|\|

*vandhyā nārī jalaṃ tatra yā pibettilakānvitam \|*  
*api varṣaśatābdā ca sadyo garbhavatī bhavet \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. If a woman sterile for years and centuries drink the water mixed with sandalwood, she becomes pregnant.

## \|\| 3.12.29 \|\|

*vyādhigrasto'pi yo marttyaḥ snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|*  
*nīrogo jāyate sadyo grahagrasto vimucyate \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. By practising to take bath there, a man suffering from diseases becomes free from ailments and one, afflicted with planetary debilitations, slows down the same affectations through such a practice.

## \|\| 3.12.30 \|\|

*bhūtapretapiśācānāṃ doṣaḥ sadyaḥ praṇaśyati \|*  
*tenodakena saṃspṛṣṭe sarvaṃ naśyati duṣkṛtam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. A touch of that water throws instantly away the afflictions in the form of ghosts, satans etc. \[i.e., Bhūtas, Pretas, Piśācas\] and all bad deeds get mined.

## \|\| 3.12.31 \|\|

*api kīṭapataṃgā ye piśācāḥ pakṣiṇo mṛgāḥ \|*  
*tenodakena ye spṛṣṭāḥ sadyo yāsyaṃti sadgatim \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Even worms, flies, satans \[i.e., Piśācas\], birds, deer etc. will attain the ultimate passage instantaneously by touch of this water.

## \|\| 3.12.32 \|\|

*yayātiruvāca \|*  
*apyadbhutamidaṃ brahmanmāhātmyaṃ bhavatā mama \|*  
*kathitaṃ rūpatīrthasya na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati \|\| 32 \|\|*

Yayāti said:

32\. This very strange and supernatural greatness of this pilgrimage centre as told, has impressed me. It has neither any past nor a future.

## \|\| 3.12.33 \|\|

*kimatra kāraṇaṃ brahmansarvebhyo'pyadhikaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*sarvaṃ vistarato brūhi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. What could be the specific reason about this place so that its supernatural greatness is being remembered? I have a great curiosity. Please describe in detail.

## \|\| 3.12.34-35 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tatra pūrvaṃ tapastaptamadityā nṛpasattama \|*  
*indre rājyaparibhraṣṭe balau trailokyanāyake \|*  
*avatīrṇaścaturbāhuradityāṃ nṛpasattama \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tasmiñjāte mahāviṣṇāvadityā cāsurāntake \|*  
*guptayā vivaradvāre bhayāddānavasaṃbhavāt \|\| 35 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

34-35. In earlier times, with the downfall of the kingdom of Indra followed by the demon Bala becoming king of three worlds, the mother Aditi observed severe penance here. Then the four-armed Viṣṇu descended into the womb of Aditi. Then the great Viṣṇu came out but afraid of the terror of the demon, remained clandestinely inside the pond on the doorway of the cave.

## \|\| 3.12.36 \|\|

*jātamātro haristasminsthāpito nirjhare tayā \|*  
*tasmātpavitratāṃ prāptaṃ tīrthaṃ nṝṇāmabhīṣṭadam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. So that way as soon as Hari took birth, he placed himself in that pond. Due to that the pilgrimage acquired its sacredness and people’s wishes get actualised by a visit here.

## \|\| 3.12.37 \|\|

*na cānyatkāraṇaṃ rājansatyametanmayoditam \|*  
*māghaśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ tatra jātastrivikramaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O King! there is no other reason. I have narrated the truth to you. On the third day of the rising period of moon in the month of Pauṣa (i.e., January) the dwarf Trivikrama was born here.

## \|\| 3.12.38 \|\|

*tilakaḥ sarva vṛkṣāgryaḥ putravatparipālitaḥ \|*  
*adityā sevito nityaṃ svahastena jalaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The tree Tilaka placed ahead of all trees was brought up here like a son by Aditi. She had served it with the auspicious water everyday in her own hands.

## \|\| 3.12.39 \|\|

*etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ tīrthamāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|*  
*sarvakāmapradaṃ nṝṇāmiha loke paratra ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. In this way, I have narrated to you the greatness and goodness of this centre of pilgrimage as mentioned by all. Hence, everyone must make good effort to have a bath there. It fulfills desire of all people in this world as well as in the next world.

## Chapter 13 - Greatness of Viṣṇu

## \|\| 3.13.1 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchennṛpaśreṣṭha tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam \|*  
*aṃbarīṣasya rājarṣeraiśānyāṃ pāpanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

1\. O best king! after this one should go to that excellent centre of pilgrimage situated in the north-east direction established by the royal sage Ambarīṣa famed in the three worlds as the destroyer of all sins.

## \|\| 3.13.2 \|\|

*yatra svayaṃ hṛṣīkeśaḥ kāle ca kalisaṃjñake \|*  
*tasya vākyādṛtastīrthe svayaṃ hi paritiṣṭhati \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. In this place of pilgrimage, even in the time of Kali Yuga, Ambarīṣa himself continued to stay respecting that particular saying.

## \|\| 3.13.3 \|\|

*purāsītpṛthivīpālo hyaṃbarīṣo yuge kṛte \|*  
*harimārādhayāmāsa tapastepe suduṣkaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In old times during Satya Yuga, a king named Ambarīṣa having undergone an impregnable penance, had pleased God Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 3.13.4 \|\|

*tasmiṃstīrthe sa rājendro mitabhakṣo jitendriyaḥ \|*  
*sahasramekaṃ varṣāṇāṃ tata āsītphalāśanaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Frugal, the king of kings Jitendriya survived on eating fruits for one thousand years in this place of pilgrimage.

## \|\| 3.13.5 \|\|

*sahasre dve tato rājañchīrṇaparṇāśano'bhavat \|*  
*sahasre dve tato bhūyo jalāhāro babhūva ha \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then for two thousand years he ate only dried leaves. For another two thousand years more he had only water.

## \|\| 3.13.6 \|\|

*sahasratritayaṃ rājanvāyubhakṣo babhūva ha \|*  
*cintayanpuṃḍarīkākṣaṃ mānase śraddhayānvitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then remembering God Viṣṇu and inclining the mind with faith he lived on breathing air for another three thousand years.

## \|\| 3.13.7 \|\|

*daśa varṣasahasrānte tataśca nṛpasattama \|*  
*tutoṣa bhagavānviṣṇustasyāsau darśanaṃ dadau \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then God Viṣṇu was pleased to come before his sight after ten thousand years.

## \|\| 3.13.8 \|\|

*kṛtvā devapate rūpamāruhyairāvataṃ gajam \|*  
*abravīdvarado'smīti aṃbarīṣaṃ narādhipam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Bearing the form of Indra and seated on the back of elephant Airāvat, Viṣṇu came and told King Ambarīṣa, “I want to give you boon.”

## \|\| 3.13.9 \|\|

*iṃdra uvāca \|*  
*varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te rājanyanmanasīpsitam \|*  
*tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā bhaktisaṃyuktamāgato'hamasaṃśayam \|\| 9 \|\|*

Indra said:

9\. O King! ask for the best of boons as desired in your mind. I have come here after having seen you engaged in the act of devotion without any doubt.

## \|\| 3.13.10 \|\|

*aṃbarīṣa uvāca \|*  
*muktiṃ dātumaśaktosi tvaṃ ca vṛtraniṣūdana \|*  
*tava prasādāddeveśa trailokyaṃ mama varttate \|*  
*svāgataṃ gaccha deveśa na varo rocate mama \|\| 10 \|\|*

Ambarīṣa said:

10\. You cannot give me salvation. I have killed the demon Vṛtra. By your grace, O God! the running of affairs in the three worlds is done according to me. O King of Gods! welcome to you, but you please go as boons do not interest me.

## \|\| 3.13.11 \|\|

*sarvathā dāsyate mahyaṃ varaṃ tuṣṭaścaturbhujaḥ \|*  
*tadāhaṃ pratigṛhṇāmi gaccha deva namostu te \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. By getting pleased in all ways, the four-armed Viṣṇu will only give me a boon. That only I will accept. O King! please go. Homage to you.

## \|\| 3.13.12 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*varaṃ varaya rājarṣe yatte manasi varttate \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇutrinetrāṇāmahamīśo nṛpotama \|\| 12 \|\|*

Indra said:

12\. O King! ask for the boon there in your mind. I am even the Lord of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śaṃkara.

## \|\| 3.13.13 \|\|

*anyeṣāṃ caiva devānāṃ trailokyasyāpyahaṃ vibhuḥ \|*  
*varaṃ varaya tasmāttvaṃ prasādānme sudurllabham \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. I am the Lord of the other gods and of the three worlds. Therefore, ask for the difficult boon with pleasure from me.

## \|\| 3.13.14 \|\|

*prasanne mayi rājendra prasannāḥ sarvadevatāḥ \|*  
*kuru me vacanaṃ rājangṛhyatāṃ varamuttamam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. All gods remain pleased with my getting pleased. Act as per my words and ask for the good boon, O King!

## \|\| 3.13.15 \|\|

*aṃbarīṣa uvāca \|*  
*rājā tvaṃ sarvadevānāṃ trailokyasya tatheśvaraḥ \|*  
*saptadvīpavatī rājā ahaṃ vṛtraniṣūdana \|\| 15 \|\|*

Ambarīṣa said:

15\. You are the king of all gods and the lord of the three worlds. I am the king of land having seven islands and I have killed the demon Vṛtra.

## \|\| 3.13.16 \|\|

*haṣīkeśasya sadbhaktaṃ viddhi māṃ tāta niścayam \|*  
*āgataśca hṛṣīkeśo varaṃ dāsyatyasaṃśayam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O Father! it is for sure that I am a true devotee of Viṣṇu in accordance with perceived ways. You are the Viṣṇu and will give me a boon.

## \|\| 3.13.17 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*dadato mama bhūpāla na gṛhṇāsi varaṃ yadi \|*  
*vajraṃ tvāṃ prerayiṣyāmi vadhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

Indra said:

17\. O King! if you do not accept the boon as given by me, I will apply my weapon of thunderbolt and kill you definitely.

## \|\| 3.13.18 \|\|

*evamuktvā sahasrākṣaḥ sṛkkiṇī parilelihan \|*  
*kuliśaṃ bhrāmayāmāsa gṛhītvā dakṣiṇe kare \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Having said like this Indra took out the thunderbolt weapon in the right hand and moved it around itself like a snake with skill.

## \|\| 3.13.19 \|\|

*tasyevaṃ bhrāmyamāṇasya mahotpātā babhūvire \|*  
*tataḥ parvataśṛṃgāṇi viśīrṇāni samaṃtataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Great disorder began to happen with his circling the weapon around in this way. The mountains including the peaks as well as rivers got affected.

## \|\| 3.13.20 \|\|

*āvṛtaṃ gagana meghairvidhunvānairmahīṃ tadā \|*  
*na kiṃciddṛśyate tatra sarvaṃ saṃtamasāvṛtam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. With the sky covered with dark clouds, the ground below got under its shadow. Nothing was visible as everything got covered with darkness.

## \|\| 3.13.21 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu sa rājā harivatsalaḥ \|*  
*nimīlya locane svīye samādhistho babhūva ha \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. In the meantime that king—the devotee of God sat in concentration with closed eyes.

## \|\| 3.13.22 \|\|

*tatastuṣṭo jagannātha sākṣātpratyakṣatāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*airāvataḥ sa garuḍastatkṣaṇātsamajāyata \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Then becoming pleased, the God of the world came to direct manifestation. Airāvata—the elephant became Garuḍa—the king of birds.

## \|\| 3.13.23 \|\|

*tamuvāca hṛṣīkeśo meghagaṃbhīrayā girā \|*  
*dhyānasthitaṃ nṛpaśreṣṭhaṃ śaṃkha cakragadādharaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Viṣṇu—the bearer of conch, cakra (a discus) and mace (a weapon) told that king engaged in concentration with a deep and vibrant voice like the clouds.

## \|\| 3.13.24 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*parituṣṭo'smi te vatsānanyabhakta janeśvara \|*  
*varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te yadyapi syātsudurlabham \|\| 24 \|\|*

The gracious God said:

24\. There is no other devotee like you the king. O son! I am fully satisfied with you. Let there be your welfare. You can ask for the most difficult thing as a boon.

## \|\| 3.13.25 \|\|

*aṃbarīṣa uvāca \|*  
*yadi prasanno bhagavanyadi deyo varo mama \|*  
*saṃsārābdhestāraṇāya varado bhava me hare \|\| 25 \|\|*

Ambarīṣa said:

25\. God! if you are happy to give me a boon, kindly give me such a boon which will enable me to swim across this sea of world.

## \|\| 3.13.26 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*athāha bhagavānviṣṇuraṃbarīṣaṃ janādhipam \|*  
*jñānayogaṃ suvistīrṇaṃ saṃsārakṣayakāraṇam \|\| 26 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

26\. Then God Viṣṇu. as a grant of boon, instructed King Ambarīṣa about the well extensive Jñāna Yoga that operates as the cause behind obliteration of the world.

## \|\| 3.13.27-29 \|\|

*yasmiñjāte naraḥ sadyaḥ saṃsārānmucyate nṛpa \|*  
*śrutvā sa nṛpatiḥ samyakpraṇamyovāca keśavam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*aṃbarīṣa uvāca \|*  
*bhagavanyastvayā prokto yogo'yaṃ mama vistarāt \|*  
*durjñeyaḥ sa nṛṇāṃ deva viśeṣācca kalau yuge \|\| 28 \|\|*

*api cetsuprasanno'si kriyāyogaṃ bravīhi me \|*  
*lokānāṃ tāraṇārthāya śaṃkhacakragadādhara \|\| 29 \|\|*

27-29. Like a man born leaves the world instantly, the King Ambarīṣa after hearing this properly paid homage to Viṣṇu and said, “O God! this path of Yoga which you have narrated to me is specially beyond the comprehension of people in the Kali Yuga. If you are pleased with me, kindly instruct about the Kriyā Yoga, O bearer of conch, the discus and the mace! This will be meaningful for the people to swim across this world.”

## \|\| 3.13.30 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tatastasmai narendrāya kriyāyogaṃ janārddanaḥ \|*  
*yathāyogyaṃ nṛpaśreṣṭha kathayāmāsa keśavaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

30\. Then God Keśava, i.e., Viṣṇu appropriately narrated the Kriyā Yoga to the king.

## \|\| 3.13.31-33 \|\|

*taṃ śrutvā tuṣṭahṛdayoṃ'barīṣo vākyamabravīt \|\| 31 \|\|*

*aṃbarīṣa uvāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭo'si bhagavanrūpeṇānena mādhava \|*  
*mamāśrame tvaṃ deveśa sadā sannihito bhava \|\| 32 \|\|*

*yatastvatpratimāmekāmarcayāmi vidhānataḥ \|*  
*pūjayiṣyaṃti lokāstvāṃ śaṃkhacakragadādharam \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. Pleased within heart having listened to the same king Ambarīṣa said: “If God Mādhava! You are satisfied with me—the king, let there always be the proximity of the King of Gods with my hermitage. There, I shall be worshipping the idol of yours according to established rules and procedure. People all over the world will be worshipping you—the bearer of conch, discus and the mace.”

## \|\| 3.13.34 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tathokto mādhavenāsau cakāra harimaṃdiram \|*  
*pratimāṃ pūjayāmāsa gandhapuṣpānulepanaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

34\. With Mādhava granting permission in this regard, Ambarīṣa started to construct a temple for Hari and began to worship the idol with offerings of flowers, incense and oil.

## \|\| 3.13.35 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena mahatā bhagavānviṣṇumaṃdire \|*  
*tenaiva vapuṣā prāptaḥ saputraḥ sahabāṃdhavaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then after passage of a long time, the God Himself in His own body along with son and other kith and kin came to that Viṣṇu temple.

## \|\| 3.13.36 \|\|

*adyāpi bhagavānviṣṇuḥ satyavākyena bhūpateḥ \|*  
*sadā saṃnihito viṣṇustasminnavasare kalau \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Even today, in the Kali Yuga, God Viṣṇu, keeping with the truthfulness of words given to the king has permanently positioned himself here.

## \|\| 3.13.37 \|\|

*tadārabhya mahārāja kriyāyogo dharātale \|*  
*pravṛttaḥ pratimākāraḥ kāle ca kalisaṃjñake \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O Great King! from then onwards till the present time in this Kali Yuga, the ritual of making and fixing of idols on the surface of earth has started.

## \|\| 3.13.38 \|\|

*yastaṃ pūjayate bhaktyā hṛṣīkeśe nṛpārbude \|*  
*sa yāti viṣṇusālokyaṃ prasādācca harernṛpa \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Those who worship Lord Viṣṇu here on this Arbuda mountain with faith go to the same world as of Viṣṇu with His grace.

## \|\| 3.13.39 \|\|

*ekādaśyāṃ mahārāja jāgaraṃ yaḥ sadā nṛpa \|*  
*kariṣyati nirāhāro hṛṣīkeśāgrataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*sa yāsyati paraṃ sthānaṃ durllabhaṃ tridaśairapi \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Placing the self in front of Viṣṇu, one who performs the activity of keeping awake throughout the night and that too without food on the eleventh day of a month goes to that place of Viṣṇu which is even difficult for gods to attain.

## \|\| 3.13.40 \|\|

*yatpuṇyaṃ kapilādāne kārtikyāṃ jyeṣṭhapuṣkare \|*  
*tatphalaṃ labhate marttyo hṛṣīkeśasya darśanāt \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The same fruit is obtained by the mortal men by having a look of God Viṣṇu, as is obtained by gifting of the Kapilā cow at the pre-eminent Puṣkara (a celebrated place of pilgrimage at Ajmer in Rajasthan) in the month of Kārtika (i.e., October).

## \|\| 3.13.41 \|\|

*śukle vā yadi vā kṛṣṇe saṃprāpte harivāsare \|*  
*yaḥ paśyati hṛṣīkeśamaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The fruits of the sacrificial activity of offering of horses to fire, i.e., of the Aśvamedha Yajña are obtained by having a look of Viṣṇu on the specific day demarcated for him either in the rising or waning period of moon in a month.

## \|\| 3.13.42 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena pūjayettu vidhānataḥ \|*  
*yastatra caturo māsansamyagvrataparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*abhyarcayeddhṛṣīkeśaṃ na sa bhūyo'bhijāyate \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Hence with all efforts there should be worship of Viṣṇu and with due procedure. One who adheres to the vowed observance of religious austerities for four months and worship God Viṣṇu, does not get rebirth.

## \|\| 3.13.43 \|\|

*ekaḥ sarvāṇi tīrthāni karoti nṛpasattama \|*  
*paśyatyanyo hṛṣīkeśaṃ cāturmāsyaṃ samāhitaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O virtuous king! only one pilgrimage of this kind fulfills all pilgrimages undertaken. A look at Viṣṇu assembles together the vowed observance of religious austerities of four-month period.

## \|\| 3.13.44 \|\|

*eko dānāni sarvāṇi brāhmaṇebhyaḥ prayacchati \|*  
*paśyatyanyo hṛṣīkeśaṃ cāturmāsyaṃ samāhitaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Some people gift everything to Brāhmaṇas. Some others worship God Viṣṇu carefully during the vowed religious observance for four months.

## \|\| 3.13.45 \|\|

*ekaḥ kanyāsahasraṃ tu pradadyācca yathāvidhi \|*  
*paśyatyanyo hṛṣīkeśaṃ cāturmāsyaṃ samāhitaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Some make a gift of one thousand unmarried girls as per established rules and practices. Still others serve Viṣṇu with all sincerity during the period of four months of vowed observance of religious austerities.

## \|\| 3.13.46 \|\|

*sūryagrahe kurukṣetre dadyāddānamanuttamam \|*  
*paśyatyanyo hṛṣīkeśaṃ cāturmāsyaṃ samāhitaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Some make the offering of best of all gifts on the occasion of solar eclipse at Kurukṣetra. Others serve Viṣṇu with all eagerness during the four-month period of vowed observance of religious austerities.

## \|\| 3.13.47 \|\|

*agniṣṭomādibhiryajñairyajatyekaḥ sadakṣiṇaiḥ \|*  
*paśyatyanyo hṛṣīkeśaṃ cāturmāsyaṃ samāhitaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Some worship God Viṣṇu through the Agniṣṭoma Yajña1 followed up with offering of presents to Brāhmaṇas at the end of the sacrificial rite. Some others worship Viṣṇu with all eagerness during the four-month period of vowed observance of religious austerities (i.e., the Caturmasya \[Cāturmāsya?\]).

## \|\| 3.13.48 \|\|

*eko himālayaṃ gatvā tyajati sva kalevaram \|*  
*paśyatyanyo haṣīkeśaṃ cāturmāsyaṃ samāhitaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Someone, after going to the Himālaya, gives up his body. Another individual serves God Viṣṇu with care during the four-month period of vowed observance of religious austerities.

## \|\| 3.13.49 \|\|

*ekastu bhṛgupātena tyajeddehaṃ sutīrthake \|*  
*paśyatyanyo hṛṣīkeśaṃ cāturmāsyaṃ samāhitaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Some leave their bodies aside falling at the feet of Sage Bhṛgu in the Uttana pilgrimage. Other men remain engrossed in the service of Viṣṇu during the four-month period of vowed observance of religious austerities.

## \|\| 3.13.50 \|\|

*ekaḥ prāyopaveśena prāṇāṃstyajati mānavaḥ \|*  
*paśyatyanyo hṛṣīkeśaṃ cāturmāsyaṃ samāhitaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Someone gives up life through continuous fasting for days together. Someone else remains engaged in the service of Viṣṇu during the vowed observance of religious austerities in the four-month period.

## \|\| 3.13.51 \|\|

*brahmajñānaṃ vadatyekaḥ śrutvā jñānavi śāradaḥ \|*  
*paśyatyanyo hṛṣīkeśaṃ cāturmāsyaṃ samāhitaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. One man proficient in knowledge listens to the factual reports related to the Supreme Being while another takes a look of Viṣṇu with care during the four-month period of vowed observance of religious austerities.

## \|\| 3.13.52 \|\|

*gayāśrāddhaṃ karotyekaḥ pitṛpakṣe nṛpottama \|*  
*paśyatyanyo hṛṣīkeśaṃ cāturmāsyaṃ samāhitaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O king! some perform the religious rite connected with remembrance of their ancestors during the period meant for paternal side, i.e., Pitru \[Pitṛ?\] Pakṣa while some others bringing all forces of their minds together within do service of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 3.13.53 \|\|

*cāṃdrāyaṇasahasraṃ ca karotyekaḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*paśyatyanyo hṛṣīkeśaṃ cātumāsyaṃ samāhitaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Some undergo (crores of) the vowed observance of the religious austerity of Candrāyaṇa as per established rules. Some others do service to Viṣṇu during the four-month period of vowed observance of religious austerities.

## \|\| 3.13.54 \|\|

*vrataṃ tapaḥ sahasrābdamekaḥ samyakcarennaraḥ \|*  
*paśyatyanyo hṛṣīkeśaṃ cāturmāsyaṃ samāhitaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Some remain adherents to the vowed observance of religious austerities for thousands of years while some others visualize the opportunity of service to Viṣṇu during the four-month period of vowed observance of religious austerities.

## \|\| 3.13.55 \|\|

*ekastu caturo vedānsamyakpaṭhati brāhmaṇaḥ \|*  
*paśyatyanyo hṛṣīkeśaṃ cāturmāsyaṃ samāhitaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Some Brāhmaṇas read the four Vedas as per rule. Others serve Viṣṇu during the four-month period of vowed observance of religious austerities.

## \|\| 3.13.56 \|\|

*bahunā kimihoktena śṛṇu saṃkṣepato nṛpa \|*  
*ekatastu bhavetsarvamekato haridarśanam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. O king! there is no need for more description here. Hence listen in brief. There are all these things of the world on one side while on the other there is vision.

## \|\| 3.13.57 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena sthātavyaṃ harisaṃnidhau \|*  
*ambarīṣasya rājarṣeḥ sthānake pāpanāśane \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Hence everyone, with efforts must remain close to Viṣṇu. All sins get destroyed by residing in this place of Ambarīṣa.

## \|\| 3.13.58 \|\|

*ekatastu hṛṣīkeśa ekataḥ karṇikeśvaraḥ \|*  
*tayormartyā mṛtā ye ca mānavā nṛpasattama \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. On one side there is Viṣṇu. On the other side there is the line of ‘action/work’. O king! taking shelter under Him is the best.

## \|\| 3.13.59 \|\|

*api kṛtvā mahatpāpaṃ gacchaṃti harisannidhau \|*  
*hṛṣīkeśaṃ samālokya sadyo muktimavāpnuyāt \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. O king! even one going nearer to Viṣṇu even after committing great sins becomes free immediately by a sight of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 3.13.60 \|\|

*puṣpamekaṃ hṛṣīkeśe yaścāropayate nṛpa \|*  
*sukhasaubhāgyasaṃyukta iha loke paratra ca \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. One who places one piece of flower on God Viṣṇu, attains all good fortune in this world as well as in the next.

## \|\| 3.13.61 \|\|

*hṛṣīkeśasya yo bhaktyā kariṣyatyanulepanam \|*  
*sa yāsyati paraṃ sthānaṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. One who massages the idol of God Viṣṇu with scented oil and with faith, goes to that ultimate place becoming relieved of old age and death.

## \|\| 3.13.62 \|\|

*saṃmārjanaṃ ca tasyāgre yaḥ karoti samāhitaḥ \|*  
*yāvatyo reṇavastatra tāvadvarṣaśatāni saḥ \|*  
*modate viṣṇulokastho nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Leaving behind every thing, one who entreats Him remaining engrossed and with an undivided mind, gets liberation immediately by a sight of Him.

## \|\| 3.13.63-64 \|\|

*kārtike śuklapakṣe ca ekādaśyāṃ nṛpottama \|*  
*dīpamāropayedyaśca hṛṣīkeśāgrato nṛpa \|\| 63 \|\|*

*yathāyathā prakāśeta pāpaṃ janmāṃtarārjitam \|*  
*tathātathā vrajennāśaṃ tasya kāyādaśeṣataḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. O good king! one who lights earthen lamps before Viṣṇu in connection with the vowed observance of the religious austerities meant solely for Lord Viṣṇu (i.e., Pravodhini Vrata) on the eleventh day of the rising period of moon in the month of Kārtika (i.e., October), happens to witness sins committed in previous birth and as one after the other sin comes before his eyes, all his sins get effaced from the body at that time.

## \|\| 3.13.65 \|\|

*paṃcāmṛtena yaḥ pūjāṃ hṛṣīkeśe kariṣyati \|*  
*dadhnā kṣīreṇa vā yastu na sa bhūyo'bhijāyate \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. One who employs the mixture containing equal parts of five contents, viz., milk, curd, ghee, sugar and honey in the worship of Viṣṇu or worship with curd or milk, does not get rebirth.

## \|\| 3.13.66 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena hṛṣīkeśaṃ samarcayet \|*  
*saṃsārabaṃdhato rājanmuktimāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. It is due to this that Viṣṇu must be worshipped with all efforts. O King! man attains freedom from the worldly bondage through this.

## \|\| 3.13.67 \|\|

*hṛṣīkeśe viśeṣeṇa karttavyaṃ pūjanaṃ sadā \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. It is the duty ever to specially worship Viṣṇu.

## Chapter 14 - Greatness of Siddheśvara (Siddha-īśvara)

## \|\| 3.14.1 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchennṛpaśreṣṭha devaṃ siddheśvaraṃ param \|*  
*siddhidaṃ prāṇināṃ samyaksiddhena sthāpitaṃ purā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

1\. Then, O best of kings! one must visit the place of supreme God Siddheśvara. He is the giver of fulfilment to living beings. This was founded by a Siddha long ago.

## \|\| 3.14.2 \|\|

*tatra viśvāvasurnāma siddhastepe mahātapaḥ \|*  
*bahuvarṣāṇi saṃsthāpya śivaṃ bhaktiparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. A Siddha (accomplished one) by name Viśvāvasu had practised penance here for many years and had set up the idol of Śiva here.

## \|\| 3.14.3 \|\|

*jitakrodho jitamado jitasarveṃdriyakriyaḥ \|*  
*tāvadvarṣasahasrāṃte bhagavānvṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*tutoṣa nṛpatestasya svayaṃ darśanamāyayau \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He had won over anger, arrogance and all sensuous actions. Then after a thousand years Śaṃkara, i.e., the God having the bull on His emblem came to his sight on His own in the form of a king.

## \|\| 3.14.4-5 \|\|

*abravīttaṃ mahādevo varadosmīti pārthiva \|\| 4 \|\|*

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te yatte manasi varttate \|*  
*dāsyāmi te prasanno'haṃ yadyapi syātsudurlabham \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. The great God Mahādeva in the form of King said: “I have come to this earth to give you a boon. You can ask for any auspicious boon in your mind. As I am pleased, I shall grant you the same even if that may be difficult to attain”.

## \|\| 3.14.6 \|\|

*viśvāvasuruvāca \|*  
*etalliṃgaṃ suraśreṣṭha dhyātvā manasi niścayam \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpnotu prasādāttava śaṃkara \|\| 6 \|\|*

Viśvāvasu said:

6\. O best king! let there by fulfilment of desires of people by the grace of Śaṃkara after bearing this worshipable Liṅga in the mind with all certainty.

## \|\| 3.14.7 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*evamastviti sa procya tatraivāṃtaradhīyata \|*  
*siddheśvaraṃ tato gatvā siddhiṃ yāti sahasraśaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

7\. After saying ‘let it be so’ Śiva then disappeared from sight there. Since then thousands of people have attained fulfilment after going to the Siddheśvara temple.

## \|\| 3.14.8 \|\|

*prabhāvāttasya liṃgasya kāmāniṣṭānavāpnuyuḥ \|*  
*tato dharmakriyāḥ sarvā gatā nāśaṃ dharātale \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. By the influence of the worshipable Liṅga all desires have been fulfilled. Therefore, all righteous actions have disappeared from the surface of the earth.

## \|\| 3.14.9 \|\|

*na kaścidyajate yajñairna dānāni prayacchati \|*  
*siddheśvaraprasādena siddhiṃ yāṃti narā bhuvi \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Neither anyone has any need to perform sacrifice (Yajña) nor has to make any offering as charity. By Siddheśvara’s courting of God’s favour like this, humans on earth can be equally entitled to reach that stage of fulfilment.

## \|\| 3.14.10 \|\|

*ucchinneṣu ca yajñeṣu dāneṣu nṛpasattama \|*  
*indrādyāstridaśāḥ sarve paraṃ duḥkhamupāgatāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O virtuous king! with the uprooting of Yajñas and charity, all gods along with Indra became unhappy.

## \|\| 3.14.11 \|\|

*jñātvā yajñavighātaṃ ca tadvighātāya vāsavaḥ \|*  
*vajreṇācchādayāmāsa yathā siddhirna jāyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Learning about the destruction of the Yajña, Indra put across his weapon thunderbolt as an impediment so that fulfilment could not be attained.

## \|\| 3.14.12 \|\|

*tathāpi saṃnidhau tasya siddheśasya nṛpottama \|*  
*karmaṇo jāyate siddhiḥ pātakasya parikṣayaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Even then, with the place being in proximity of Siddheśvara there, O best king, all actions meet with fulfilment and all sins get destroyed there.

## \|\| 3.14.13 \|\|

*yastu māghacaturddaśyāṃ somavāre nṛpottama \|*  
*śuklāyāṃ vātha kṛṣṇāyāṃ spṛṣṭvā siddho bhavennaraḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O king! One who touches this, on the fourteenth day either during the waxing period or the waning period of the moon in the month of Pauṣa (i.e., January), that man becomes a Siddha (accomplished).

## \|\| 3.14.14 \|\|

*adyāpi jāyate siddhiḥ satyametanmayoditam \|*  
*tasmātsiddheśvaraṃ gatvā natvā yāsyati sadgatim \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Even today also Siddhi (fulfilment) happens there. I have told this truth to you. Therefore, Sadgati (a good or happy state) can be possible (for you) by going and bowing down there.

## Chapter 15 - Greatness of Śukreśvara (Śukra-īśvara)

## \|\| 3.15.1 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tataḥ śukreśvaraṃ gacchecchukreṇa sthāpitaṃ purā \|*  
*yaṃ dṛṣṭvā mānavaḥ sadyaḥ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

1\. Then one has to go to Śukreśvara established by Śukra in ancient times. By having a look of this, a man instantly gets rid of his sins.

## \|\| 3.15.2-3 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā daityānpurā devairnirjitānnṛpasattama \|*  
*cintayāmāsa medhāvī bhārgavastānprati dvijaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kathaṃ daityāḥ surāñjitvā prāpsyaṃti ca mahāyaśaḥ \|*  
*ārādhya śaṃkaraṃ siddhiṃ gacchāmi manasepsitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. O virtuous king! seeing the demons who were defeated once by gods, Bhārgava, the intelligent Brāhmaṇa was prodded to think as to how could the demons win over the gods and attain great fame? Thinking that by worshipping Śaṃkara he could proceed on the path of fulfilment, he began to nurture such a desire in mind.

## \|\| 3.15.4 \|\|

*evaṃ sa niścayaṃ kṛtvā gato'rbudamathācalam \|*  
*bhūme vivaramāsādya tapastepe sudāruṇam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Having decided like this, he proceeded towards the high region of Arbuda and finding a cave in the valley began performance of difficult austerities.

## \|\| 3.15.5 \|\|

*śivaliṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya dhūpagaṃdhānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*aniśaṃ pūjayāmāsa śraddhayā parayānvitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Having installed the worshipable Liṅga of Śiva he got himself intently engaged in worship with incense, perfume and by anointing the Liṅga with scented oil.

## \|\| 3.15.6 \|\|

*tato varṣasahasrāṃte tutoṣa bhagavāñchivaḥ \|*  
*tasya saṃdarśanaṃ dattvā vākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then after a thousand years of nurturing such a desire, the God finally came before him and said:

## \|\| 3.15.7 \|\|

*śrīmahādeva uvāca \|*  
*parituṣṭo'smi te vipra bhaktyā tava dvijottama \|*  
*varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te yadyapi syātsudurlabham \|\| 7 \|\|*

Mahādeva said:

7\. O good Brāhmaṇa! I am satisfied with the faith of yours. You can ask for that auspicious boon even if that is difficult to obtain.

## \|\| 3.15.8 \|\|

*śukra uvāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭo mahādeva vidyāṃ dehi maheśvara \|*  
*yayā jīvaṃti saṃprāptā mṛtyuṃ saṃkhyepi jaṃtavaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

Śukra said:

8\. If Mahādeva is satisfied, the great God may grant me that learning by which I may bring to life the living beings who have met with death in a battle.

## \|\| 3.15.9 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*pradāya vai śivastasmai tāṃ vidyāṃ nṛpasattama \|*  
*abravīcca punaḥ śukraṃ varamanyaṃ vṛṇīṣva me \|\| 9 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

9\. O virtuous king! having imparted him that learning, Śiva told Śukra that he could enjoy and ask for yet another boon.

## \|\| 3.15.10-11 \|\|

*śukra uvāca \|*  
*etatkārtikamāsasya śuklāṣṭamyāṃ tu yaḥ spṛśet \|*  
*tato liṃgaṃ pūjayecca yaḥ pumāñchraddhayānvitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*alpamṛtyubhayaṃ tasya mā bhūttava prasādataḥ \|*  
*iṣṭānkāmānavāpnotu ihaloke paratra ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

Śukra said:

10-11. Whoever touches or worships this Liṅga on the eighth day of the waxing period of Moon in the month of Kārtika (i.e., October), let there be no fear for him or her of untimely death by your grace. Let them all obtain their wishes nurtured in the mind.

## \|\| 3.15.12 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*evamastviti sa procya tatraivāṃtaradhīyata \|*  
*śukropi dānavānsaṃkhye hatāndevairanekaśaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

12\. Saying, ‘it will be so’, Śiva then disappeared from sight. Śukra also got demons killed by gods many a time.

## \|\| 3.15.13 \|\|

*vidyāyāśca prabhāvena jīvayāmāsa tānmuniḥ \|*  
*tasyāgre'sminmahākuṇḍaṃ nirmalaṃ pāpanāśanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. By the power of that learning, the sage brought many back to life. On the head of that Sukreśvara \[Śukreśvara?\] temple there is a great pool with clean water which is the destroyer of sins.

## \|\| 3.15.14 \|\|

*tatra snāto naraḥ samyakpātakaiśca pramucyate \|*  
*tatra śrāddhena rājeṃdra tuṣṭā yāṃti pitāmahāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. A human being gets completely free from sins by having a bath there. O king! the grandfathers become pleased by the performance of Śrāddha here.

## \|\| 3.15.15 \|\|

*tarpitāḥ salilenaiva kiṃ punaḥ piṃḍadānataḥ \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. They become satiated with the water alone here. So the need for making the offerings again in the form of cooked rice-balls becomes superfluous. Hence everyone, with all possible efforts, needs to observe the ritual of having a bath there.

## Chapter 16 - Greatness of Maṇikarṇikeśvara (Maṇikarṇika-īśvara)

## \|\| 3.16.1 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tato gacchennṛpaśreṣṭha tīrthaṃ pāpapraṇāśanam \|*  
*maṇikarṇikasaṃjñaṃ tu sarvalokeṣu viśrutam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

1\. O best king! then one has to go to that sin-destroyer centre of pilgrimage widely heard of and known by the name Maṇikarṇikā.

## \|\| 3.16.2 \|\|

*yatra siddhiṃ gatā rājanvālakhilyā maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*taistatra nirmitaṃ kuṇḍaṃ suramyaṃ giri gahvare \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O king! the great Bālakhilya and other sages had attained Siddhi (perfection) here. The pond they had built up inside a cave in the charming mountain is a remover of sins.

## \|\| 3.16.3 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tatropaviṣṭānāṃ munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām \|*  
*mahāścaryamabhūttatra tattvaṃ śṛṇu narādhipa \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O king! by their taking a seat, a great astonishing event happened there. Listen to that.

## \|\| 3.16.4 \|\|

*kirātavanitā kācinnāmnā ca maṇikarṇikā \|*  
*atikṛṣṇā virūpākṣī karālā bhīṣaṇākṛtiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. There was a Kirāta woman (i.e., belonging to the degraded mountain tribe) named Maṇikarṇikā who was very dark, ugly, having a horrible shape.

## \|\| 3.16.5 \|\|

*tṛṣārttā tatra saṃprāptā madhyaṃdinagate ravau \|*  
*graste ca rāhuṇā sūrye praviṣṭā salile tu sā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Once, with the sun right over head during noon, she became thirsty. She came there and entered into the water. But soon Rāhu had a mouthful of the sun (i.e., leading to solar eclipse).

## \|\| 3.16.6 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu divyarūpavapurdharā \|*  
*munīnāṃ paśyatāṃ caiva viniṣkrāṃtā sumadhyamā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. In the meantime she got a body of celestial appearance. When the sages saw, they found her coining out of the middle of the water.

## \|\| 3.16.7-9 \|\|

*atha tasyāḥ patiḥ prāptastadanveṣaṇatatparaḥ \|*  
*papraccha tāṃ varārohāṃ patnyā duḥkhena duḥkhitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*mama bhāryātra saṃprāptā yadi dṛṣṭā sumadhyame \|*  
*śīghraṃ vada varārohe bālako'yaṃ tadudbhavaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tṛṣārttaśca kṣudhāviṣṭo rudate ca muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭā cetkathyatāṃ subhrūrvinā'yaṃ tāṃ mariṣyati \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. Her husband who was in a hurry to look for her came there and unhappy with the sorrows of separation from wife asked that woman, “My wife had come here. If you happened to see her please tell me fast. This boy is born out of her. He is crying repeatedly affected by thirst and hunger. If you beautifuleyed woman have seen her, please tell. Without her this boy of mine will die.”

## \|\| 3.16.10 \|\|

*stryuvāca \|*  
*sā'haṃ te dayitā kānta tīrthasyāsya prabhāvataḥ \|*  
*divyarūpamidaṃ prāptā devairapi sudurlabham \|\| 10 \|\|*

The woman said:

10\. O my husband! I am that wife of yours. By the power of this centre of pilgrimage, I have got this celestial appearance which is even difficult for gods.

## \|\| 3.16.11 \|\|

*tvaṃ cāpi salile hyasminkuru snānaṃ tvarānvitaḥ \|*  
*prāpsyasi tvaṃ paraṃ rūpaṃ yathā prāptaṃ mayā'nagha \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. You also go and have a bath quickly in the water. You will also obtain that excellent appearance like me.

## \|\| 3.16.12 \|\|

*athāsau saha putreṇa praviṣṭastatra nirjhare \|*  
*vimukte bhāskare rājanvirūpaścābhavatpunaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Then he, along with his son entered into that water for a bath. But, O King! with the Sun coming out coincidentally at that time, he again got back his usual ugly appearance.

## \|\| 3.16.13 \|\|

*duḥkhena mṛtyumāpannastasminneva jalāśaye \|*  
*atha sā bhartṛśokācca maraṇe kṛtaniścayā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. With sorrow, he embraced death in that condition in the pond. On her part, overwhelmed with grief for the husband’s death, she decided to die.

## \|\| 3.16.14 \|\|

*citiṃ kṛtvā samaṃ tena jvālayāmāsa pāvakam \|*  
*atha te munayo dṛṣṭvā tathāśīlāṃ śubhāṃganām \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Having prepared the pyre with selected pieces of wood to bum the dead body she set fire to it.

## \|\| 3.16.15 \|\|

*kṛpayā parayāviṣṭāstāmūcurvismayānvitāḥ \|*  
*sarve tasyāśca saṃdṛṣṭvā sāhasaṃ ca nṛpottama \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O good king! it was a matter of great surprise for everyone to see her courage and her being full of mercy.

## \|\| 3.16.16 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*divyarūpaṃ tvayā prāptaṃ devairapi sudurlabham \|*  
*kasmādenaṃ supāpmānamanugacchasi bhāmini \|\| 16 \|\|*

The sages said:

16\. You have got the wonderful appearance which is even difficult for gods to get. So, O beautiful woman! Why are you following this sinful man?

## \|\| 3.16.17-19 \|\|

*stryuvāca \|*  
*pativratāhaṃ viprendrāḥ sadā bhartṛparāyaṇā \|*  
*kiṃ rūpeṇa kariṣyāmi vinā patyā nijena ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

*virūpo vā surūpo vā daridro vā dhanādhipaḥ \|*  
*strīṇāmekaḥ patirbharttā gatirnānyā jagattraye \|\| 18 \|\|*

*bālako'yaṃ muniśreṣṭhā bhavaccharaṇamāgataḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ kāntena saṃyuktā praviśāmi hutāśanam \|\| 19 \|\|*

The woman said:

17-19. O great Brāhmaṇās! I am a devoted wife always engaged in the service of my husband. What shall I do with the beautiful appearance without my husband? Ugly or beautiful, poor or wealthy, whatever one may be, there is no other way than this singular aspect of having a husband for women in the three worlds. O eminent sages! this boy of mine has come to you as resort. Joined as I am with my husband, I will enter the funeral fire.

## \|\| 3.16.20 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*atha te munayaḥ sarve jñātvā tasyāḥ suniścayam \|*  
*kṛpayā parayāviṣṭāḥ saṃvīkṣya ca parasparam \|\| 20 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

20\. This is how she brought it to the notice of the sages as well as of all others about her decision made with full determination. In return, all assembled there became full of mercy within themselves and began to look in the direction of the body on the pyre.

## \|\| 3.16.21 \|\|

*tato jīvāpayāmāsustatpatiṃ te munīśvarāḥ \|*  
*sadrūpeṇa samāyuktaṃ divya lakṣaṇalakṣitam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then at that time, the great sages brought her husband alive. He was endowed with saintly appearance and with all supernatural traits.

## \|\| 3.16.22 \|\|

*etasminneva kālaṃ tu vimānaṃ manasepsitam \|*
